Cairns International Airport is little more than an oversized bus shelter. Whilst one concedes that it is a low-usage terminal with less than 8 flights per day (excluding mining charters), there is a lot that can be done to improve this airport. There is a distinct lack of working charging ports, noting that the USB ports adjacent to the cafe have been disabled. Tables and chairs are dirty/sticky. There is only one very expensive and oversubscribed café (ie, long queues to purchase over-priced, average quality food). There is one duty free store if that is your thing. There was a business lounge several years ago, but it has been long vacated with no immediate plans to reopen (this might change if there are more flights from full-service carriers in the future). There is no seating whatsoever near the boarding gates. There was no wi-fi coverage during my visit. On the positive front, customs/immigration/quarantine both on departure and arrival are rapid and staffed by friendly officials. It's a vast improvement on the horrendous queues in SYD, MEL and BNE. But as far as I'm concerned this is the only reason to transit through CNS Intl. In short, once you clear customs there is nothing of any interest, and no Wi-Fi coverage. A very drab and uninteresting terminal building with very little going for it.

International airport is just conveniently next to the domestic one. Only one coffee place and another shop to grab a bite. 2 souvenirs shops inside the gate. Considering only a handful flights, I think these are sufficient. There’s one filter water fountain near gate 2. Overall, it can be improved when it gets busier (more flights). Both elevator and escalator were out of order on the day we departed.

International airport is just next to the domestic one. Two coffee shops and 2 souvenir shops. Consider how small the airport is, these are sufficed. One water fountain near gate 2. Coffee from one of the vendors was alright. Both of the elevator and escalator were out of order on the day I flew.

As my wife and I arrived yesterday morning, we called in to Chocolate shop in Departure Lounge. I accidentally mislaid my wallet. When I arrived in Cairns city, I looked for my wallet. Panic set in! My wife called security at Cairns Airport. Some minutes later Anita rang back with good news. The wallet was found. She passed the wallet on to Security Trident in Departure Lounge ready to collect. We drove back. My wife called in to Departure Lounge with a boarding pass and found a very helpful Trident male security officer who despite being really busy with customers, found the time to hand the wallet to her with a very nice attitude. I am writing this review as I wanted to express my sincere thanks to Anita who was on a mission to help us. Big thank you to your staff.

Nice airport, but everything at it is exceptionally expensive. Bought a meal and paid about 2x what I would normally have to pay. Ridiculous prices. anyone would think it’d be cheaper than Sydney or Melbourne but is more!

Very poor transport links to the town and accommodation. Flight was late, luggage took over an hour to arrive. This put a few hundred people outside at 00:30. There were no busses and almost no taxis. The taxi queue was 250 meters long and moved very slowly. At 01:30 the queue was still 100 meters long. All the car hire companies were closed. There was no where open for food or drink. The airport experience gives the first impression of the town, Cairns needs to consider the impression it is giving out. Worst airport service I have experienced.

I was traveling with my 7 months old baby, of course I need to bring some water for the long flight. I didn't mind the security they checked the water and my bags. But the security officer lady was so rude, she sounded like a police officer talking to the criminal. Asked what was my water bottle for, and told me I can't touch my bag. I just carried my little baby to travel and I had been treated like a offender. Cairns airport security is the worst airport I ever seen! Once again I didn't mind they asked me any questions, check everything they needed, but please be nice and friendly. If they want to treat a passengers like a criminal, please be a police or they get the job in Karen restaurant.
The security check staff were unbelievably rude and disrespectful. Nil communication skills and as a result we felt most unwelcome. Not a good look for the gateway to the Barrier Reef.

Cairns Domestic Airport has to be one of the worst airports in Australia. Make sure you bring comfortable shoes as you will be doing some walking. The terminal actually has gates connecting to the aircraft from door, however it does not direct you directly to the terminal, rather than a venture down ramps and semi outdoor corridors eventually into the terminal building. When you arrive with another airline you will need to pick up your bags in a different building, then walk the long way around to the departure building. Then even the runway layout is special, where the aircraft have to turn against the runway then turn 360 degrees, for about a few hundred meters, this means that at busy times you can ensure some stationary time waiting to take off.

This has to be the most inefficient airport I’ve experienced. Countless security checks. Very limited seating which resulted in having to sit on the floor. The cigarette smell looms everywhere in the airport.

Worst airport ever. Long queues for first security screening, the checkin at the counter because Air Cairo doesn’t allow electronic boarding passes, then passport control. Took 2 hours Then another long queue to get into departure gate since they ask again for security screening. Our belongings have been put together with people shoes and fall on the floor, everything then is dirty, even the neck pillow! Not enough staff or proper equipment. Will not go via Cairo again.

Worst airport ever. Long long queues for first security screening for both economy and business, then passport. Took 2 hours Then another long queue to get into departure gate. Lots of bribery to jump queues. Not enough staff or antiquated equipment. Everyone scanned and then patted down Will not go via Cairo again.

Cairo airport has to be one of the most backwards and ridiculous airports in the world. I’ve travelled here countless times and it’s awful every time, whether you’re arriving or departing. The staff are horrid, the services are nonexistent, and the airport facilities are archaic.  If you’re arriving, expect a ridiculous queue for visa, another ridiculous queue for passport control then, for no reason, a queue and security scanner on your way out, where twice now my bag has been damaged by staff. Let’s not mention the taxi trolls on your exit out of the building. If departing, give yourself an extra hour as there is a security measure and scan upon entry into the terminal building, before checking in. Where they’ve destroyed my laptop and broken my bag historically also. Have your passport and your ticket in your hand here, even though there’s no sign or information you need to have it outside your bag. Then expect a queue again and check in and for you to be stressed about missing your flight. Then you’ll get questioned by passport control on your way out. After wasting your time at the most awful outlets, you’ll go to your gate and have another security round where they’ll shout at you, and take all the liquids you just brought in the airport. They’ll then pen you in the gate area with no water, nothing, except one toilet.

Went through Cairo airport during my recent trip arriving from Emirates and leaving to the UK both in terminal 2. Despite the long queues in departure being a bit of a hassle, the coordinators were incredibly helpful. They did their best to address any issues and kept things moving as smoothly as possible. The terminal itself is pretty modern and clean, the lounge is amazing, and while it could use a few more amenities i would say it was an overall satisfying experience, a solid 9 out of 10

What an absolutely terrible airport. By far the worst that I have ever visited. Security is a joke. Security scan your bag, pat you down with an ineffective pat down and don't even check your waist band. Then you get your boarding pass and go to the gate. There's a café there who sell you drinks and food and then claim they don't have change. Then you get called back as there been a cock up with the boarding pass. I will never in my lifetime come back to Cairo.

Departure is very tedious. Our flight got delayed (not due to the airports fault) but it took 3 hours for them to get our luggage back. Most of the luggage returned were wet and damaged.  Arrival however is very quick and easy

One of the best African airports that i have ever been to. I had worries at first before going through terminal 2 but to my surprise the whole experience was stress-free and enjoyable. The airport atmosphere was very pleasant, the check-in was quick and courteous, the duty free shops had some good and reasonably priced items and there were also some decent looking food outlets, the washrooms are well maintained, and staff were friendly despite their limited proficiency of English language.

I have traveled through Cairo airport multiple times before, and my experience this time was a significant improvement. A marked improvement in signage and organization within the terminal itself which made navigation through it a breeze, The check-in process was quicker, wifi stands and mobile charging stations were finally added. the major downside however was the security procedures which were as slow and unorganized as usual and needs a ton of attention. Despite the many areas for improvement i was impressed by the positive changes implemented since my last visit and hope they will continue.

Terminal 2 was fairly good. Despite the bustling atmosphere the staff were efficient and helpful. The terminal isn't very well organized but the clear signage made it easy to navigate. The duty-free area provided a good amount of choices, the terminal's facilities are old but clean and despite the usual rush of the terminal at the time I found a peaceful corner to relax before my flight. Overall it's not the best airport I have been to but it has a good potential for upgrades and enhancement and I can see them trying to achieve it.

Horrible security check staff at the airport, they are rude and have no patience whatsoever. The officers should either learn how to interact with passengers or they should should be fired from their jobs. They don’t deserve to be working in such positions!

Previously Kolkata was one of the worst airports i've experienced but now it has a new terminal which is sufficient in size and clean. It is still not anywhere near to compete even IGI Delhi or Mumbai airport though. I appreciate the cleanliness. I would like to see more restaurants or food courts, and cleaner toilets. Presently there is one food court at the domestic departure, and couple of cafes at the international departure. No shopping plaza. Wifi is poor and only free for 30min, but you need to have an Indian phone number to connect. Staff are slow.

I used this airport twice over the last two weeks. Given the few international flights, the international section was uncrowded. Immigration was quick and hassle free. Security check too was smooth - no need to take off shoes or belts or jackets or pull out toiletries. The business class lounge is used by all the airlines and it is a quiet place with a buffet of Indian and Bengali foods and a tended bar. Limited number of shops and even limited number of eating places. There is a duty free liquor shop just after exiting customs and before exiting the airport with a good selection of whiskeys at prices markedly cheaper than in the city. All in all, a functional airport that is easy to use with only essential facilities.

Calcutta Airport has come up to speed in the recent years and it's about time too! I only used to fly into CCU because it was the closest International Airport to Orissa and cut my journey time by a day. However it was always a tiring and bothersome task fighting my way through the immigration and baggage handling policies they seemed to practice - slow slower and at one stage stop! Flying in wasn't too bad - on a good day I could be off the plane and in a taxi within the hour (depending on the carrier). However departing from CCU was a chore - Immigration then check your baggage tags to bags then Passport Control then a small tussle with Security and Baggage Check then finally the (what seemed like a mile) hike to the plane! However those days are gone if you fly in with BA - they insisted on a proper Gate being constructed and it is now up and running! Much to my delight it's just a hop and a skip to the plane and then you're on your way. Yes you still have to grapple with Security and Passport Control but the last three times I have flown into/out of CCU I have been spared the ordeal of searching for my bags and tallying them up with my ticket tags.

Security is the absolute worst we have experienced. Flew all the way from Armenia and had a delay necessitating an unscheduled overnight in Calgary. Stopped the next day at security “b” and scanned our bags. Security checked manually and questioned a liquid - they claimed that honey sugar (solid mass) was a liquid. We insisted it was not, they asked us to open the sealed container and put it upside down to see if it was liquid and we complied and sure enough it was solid. Then told us “ oh well, it’s a liquid”. Manager insisted it was a liquid even though it’s a solid. They took it saying it was a liquid. No problems at Yerevan, Tbilisi, Frankfurt or Charles de Gaulle. But Calgary has an issue!  Staff not reasonable at all and terrible attitudes. All other staff /volunteers and airline staff we encountered were fantastic!

I am deeply disappointed by the treatment I received while going through security at Calgary International Airport on September 21st. The security staff were unprofessional and seemed to be on a power trip, showing no respect or courtesy to passengers. I was subjected to an invasive pat-down despite wearing skin-tight clothing, which felt entirely unnecessary and violating. One agent threatened to confiscate my iPad simply because it was dead and I didn’t have a charger, which is absurd. Many passengers, myself included, were left concerned about missing connections due to the slow, inefficient process. Furthermore, a female agent exhibited clear discrimination, showing leniency to some passengers while treating others, like myself, with harshness. Additionally, I witnessed an agent in customs speaking to another traveler in an extremely unprofessional manner, once again displaying behavior that felt more like a power trip than proper procedure. This was the worst airport experience I’ve had in all my travels...and I’ve been all over the world. I strongly advise others to avoid Calgary Airport, and I will be doing the same in the future.

What a terrible airport! The worst part of my experience was with the incredibly rude staff member working the oversized baggage for WestJet. She had the entire conveyor belt stanchioned off and wanted me to just haul my enormous bag (hockey bag filled with camping & hiking gear for multiple people) onto the surface directly. She refused to explain where a foot pedal required to operate the ramp to load my bag into the security screening device was even located. She said things like "why can't you just look with your eyes?!" and refused to come and actually show me where this pedal was. When she finally did come, berating me verbally the entire time, it turned out that this foot pedal was just one of many cables under the conveyor and so far back that she had to crawl underneath to pull it out. She asked if I was deaf at one point (she was seated 12m away and was mumbling in the airport noise). There was no one else waiting and no evident reason for her not to just help. This attitude was generally typical of every other airport staff member I encountered, too. Dirty bathrooms, overcrowded waiting areas at the gates, and not nearly enough charging ports for a building in the 21st century to have. I would actively avoid ever travelling through this airport again.

Seating is awful. No place to charge anything, so bring your own power backup. Businesses close ridiculously early. Domestic flights are scheduled willy Milly all across the vast terminal with no rhyme or reason.

I have mixed feelings about this airport. Upon arrival, the check-in process took almost no time at all, and I was on my way in a matter of minutes. Terminal signs pre-security were limited, but easy enough that I was able to find the C security checkpoint quick enough. Security was a different story. The wait was brutal, taking over an hour to clear. On top of this, the staff were not very fast, chatting to everyone about travel plans, flying, etc. Terminal signage post-security was much clearer, and my gate was found quite fast. Departure was also very efficient, and boarding went by fast, and I was departing on time. Overall, this airport has good and bad, but it's one of the better airports that I've been to.
Brutal security lines - super long and not moving. Projected time half hour but already been waiting that long! What is the issue? It was never this bad before! Do better!

The security experience in the Calgary airport was by far the worst. In fact, it was ridiculous. So so slow. Maybe 20 people in front of me and it took 30 minutes to get through. Refusal to open other lines. 3 or 4 security staff just standing around talking. What an embarrassment.

Worst airport I've ever been to. The security screening is terribly managed, long lines, rude staff, no direction. Be prepared to stand in line for hours, and they won't open up any additional Security lines. They are all on a power trip.

Calgary airport is a true embarrassment to our city. The domestic travel experience is horrible if, with perpetual renovations (that never seem to be worked on), stark institutional decor, and reliably long lines at security. The layout of our new international terminal does not deliver much of a better experience. Enough of blaming Covid. Get it together and manage this facility in a world class manner.

Worst experience at an airport I have ever had. I am a casual travel writer and photographer and tend to carry sensitive equipment depending on the project. In this case I was to be shooting a film project and had a few rolls of 35mm film. The day before I arrived to the airport I called both the airport and the company handling security and was assured that my equipment would be hand checked at my request and that they deal with film often enough that they don’t run it through the scanners. Upon my arrival at the security check I was told that they didn’t care what I was told and I was to do it their way or be removed from the airport. The individual behind the scanner proceeded to not only unroll fresh undeveloped film making it useless, but proceeded to treat my gear as unprofessionally as I have ever seen. My cameras were thrown down on the belts and tossed into bins. My canon AE1 now requires fairly large repairs to the shutter and the lens mount. This is a vintage camera so repairs are costly. I have flown through 3rd world countries with better airport staff then what is seen in Calgary. Absolutely unprofessional, unpleasant and overall uncaring. Very pathetic.

Hassle free check in is something unheard of at this Airport. Not even a professional customer friendly staff in the check in counter. Staff treat passengers as some kind of nuisance to their work, they prefer to gossip between themselves rather than clearing passengers in the queue.

This airport has a long way to go. With a lot of airlines not flying this sector thanks to the Runway expansion which has been going on for a long time and still is. When politics is involved, it can take more time. Emirates, FlyDubai do not operate here. A lot of people fly this airport but it is derelict. The maintenance is shoddy, the A/C does not work in some parts of the airport, the toilets are flithy. The airport needs a revamp at the earliest possible time.

Security staff opened and manually checked my bags, normally this is fine however my belongings were showed off to non security personel like a show and tell session. Incredibly unprofessional behaviour that is totally disrespectful. Security was also very inconsistent and had rules that were not advertised, for example I was unable to take sand and stones that I had brought with me from another country in my checked-in luggage (I had never had an issue with this on any other domestic flights I had taken), they also don't allow you to fly with honey.

We misplaced our passport which was very stressful. However Ashley and Phil at the Canberra airport, made sure that we still made it onto other flights back to New Zealand. Their service was outstanding, they were both so helpful, nothing was a hassle which helped to alleviate a very stressful situation for us. We can’t thank them enough.

I recently had an appalling experience at Canberra Airport. A security guard was dismissive and on a clear power trip, telling me, “I’ll take my time then” when I asked for clarification during screening. This was the worst customer service I’ve encountered after travelling extensively around the world. The behaviour of this staff member was unacceptable. I submitted a formal complaint and am yet to receive a response. Extremely disappointed.

The CBR airport security people tried to gas light me. They claimed that I could not take a narrow roll of scotch tape (not gaffer or strong tape but clear tape for wrapping a present). I asked to see where this was listed as a prohibited item. They showed me a card, carefully putting their thumb over the word "gaffer" so I would only see the word "tape". I called them out. Supervisor then backed them up by calling on his authority to prohibit any item -- rather than to admit this was an over-reach and unnecessary. Security should be spending their time identifying harmful items not confiscating harmless items.

Another review from 2021 complained about the wifi, well Dec 2023 it's still useless. Can't connect to flyCBR & no-one to get assistance from. Qantas can't help. Not good when you're now expected to do everything online. Limited & very expensive food choices (of course - airports have got a captive audience). But what do you expect when the people the airport wants to encourage are all members with privileges others don't get. The 'rabble' are to be tolerated not encouraged.

Love arriving in Canberra, perhaps the exit sign could be more obvious though, but it is so easy. Loathe exiting though. I have never not had a problem, I am elderly female and I found it a tad offensive to publicly strip to my undershirt as apparently cardigans are a security risk and I was requested to remove mine. I found this embarrassing, I did remove my coat but seriously...cardigan? Then my knee was an issue with their body scanner and I had to be patted down there. My husbands ankle likewise. I have travelled extensively and I feel Canberra staff are too aggressive and over zealous. Perhaps they dislike the elderly as the young bloke in front of me was wearing a huge bulky jumper but that was OK. There is no consistency between Australian airports, what is ok in Melbourne is not ok in Canberra. I think I will take some calming medication next time. It is way too stressful. Or maybe the manager can man up and watch to see what is going on.

I love arriving at Canberra airport, light and bright. The luggage belt is designed so it’s easy to lift off your bag. Departure was a bit of a mess. You have this spacious airport but the two security lines are too close together which is compounded by the extra line up for body scanning. You have to shove your way through that line up to put your things on the belt then join a line up of 20-30 others to go through the body scanner. Meanwhile your most valuable possessions are just sitting out there vulnerable to theft.
Why is the wifi so poor, couldn’t join, only airport in the world where I have experienced wifi problems. So much for the nations capital, not good enough.

I did not travel today (11/2/21), I am here to pick someone up. They have loud loud music playing like it was a disco in speakers throughout the ceiling so there is no way of getting away from it. I can’t even listen to something on my own phone with headphones as it is too loud. Unacceptable, what are they thinking. I have been through some of the biggest airports in the world and have never encountered this. If people want to listen to music they are perfectly at liberty to do so with their headphones. People should have the choice. This is incredible. I’ve been here 25 minutes and I’m already stressed.

Arriving is easy, everything is close by and there are rarely any crowds. Departure. Well, that was horrid. The security belt is obviously designed for business people on a day trip. Only enough room for a couple of trays. So I was trying to balance three trays in my arms to get them across to the belt with others cutting in front of me. Then my bags went through. I could see the security lady pointing at my e cigarette and battery on her screen, now I know they are allowed in carry ons, however she had a young man search my bag. At no point did anyone talk to me. I told him where these were. Meanwhile, it confused me as I did everything right. I felt like a criminal and I was embarrassed. Finally, when that was sorted I looked for the water fountain to fill my bottle. Gone. So I had to buy water. Sat in the hard seats then and eager to leave this disappointing airport. They have a huge sign saying they want to be the best small airport - they are dreaming. The airport is not tourist-friendly - it is probably best only for business people on day hops
Professional courteous security. Definitely a credit to the management and the leadership team. Well done. Definitely recommend the team for their professional approach and execution of their duties

This review is limited to Terminal 4 only. Terminal 4 is about 4-6 years old and a significant upgrade over Terminal 3. The terminal is very clean, brightly lit and wide concourses. There are dining options aplenty and plenty of seating at the gates. Immigration was a smooth process with biometric screening e-passport line. Took no more than 10 minutes in line. Upon exiting customs/baggage claim, one has to run the gauntlet of the time share vultures. Surprisingly, there are no benches for passengers to sit awaiting ground transportation pickup. Departure experience was very pleasant. Easy check-in with minimal wait times for security and immigration.

2.5 hour to get through customs upon arrival. Our block had 1 agent serving our line compared to 4 agents per other blocks. Additionally we had the handicapped line flowing into our block. We tried to plead with staff that just walked around aimlessly around the blocks, but they would just say that they cannot move customers from one block to another as that is against their policy. One of the customs agents event threatened to take my passport. Fortunately, one of the agents listened from another block otherwise we would have spent another 40 minutes waiting. On my departure Jairo a TSA agent tried to take our food. He also removed sardine containers (that actually came with us from the US) saying they were liquids, and took a frying pan that was light stainless steel (per TSA only skillets are not allowed.

Without a doubt the worst airport, I have had the privilege to use in over 40 years! Arrival Terminal 2 Off the TUI aircraft via the air bridge and been able to find the TUI reps at the other side were the only good thing about the arrival process. Once off the airbridge you follow the signs for passport control and then you hit the queue which then took over 2 hours to pass via the immigration officers who were only interested in talking to their partners has they were working in pairs which meant half desks were closed and there seemed to be plenty of officers standing around with hands in their pockets doing nothing apart from watching the queue growing. Then we got to the front of the queue, and the young female officer had never since a Latvian passport before and had go to show her supervisor has she thought it was a fake! OK not many Latvian go on holiday to Mexico, so another 15 minute delay while she checked the passport with the boss. Then on to baggage reclaim at which some one who must have very if not no experience had decided to put 5 TUI flight on one reclaim so you can imagine the chaos with the baggage from 5 Boeing 787s on one carousal. Any staff standing around doing nothing even when the TUI duty manager was trying to get the problem sorted. Has it appeared that the baggage unloaders had decided to put the luggage the carousal of last aircraft to land first and the first to land last . Once we had collect the luggage we were off to join the queue at customs, the officer who we met at the front of the short queue asked about Electronic Goods and Cigarettes, Tobacco, Vapes and we were waved on past the sniffer dogs who had a sniff of the luggage and we waved on to the x-ray machine other were waved on to the other longer queue for the luggage to be inspected by officers. Once though the x-ray which was very quick on to finding the reps just outside the terminal, and nearly 4 hours later onwards to start our holiday. Departure we had major problem with the check in staff who claimed the cases were overweight we had a 25kg allowance for hold luggage but according them each case was 5kg over despite the tickets showing 25kg? So the TUI rep tried to explain but to no avail it would appear the baggage handlers were refusing to handle cases over 20kgs! so the cases had to be repacked with 5kg been taken out and put into carry on cases. Security was a quick process and we were airside within about 10 minutes but I did have special assistance which I need due to a sprain which I got whilst on holiday. Boarding was fairly quick and painless.

What a difference 14 months make. Second time traveling through this airport. Review limited to Terminal 3. Lengthy walk from gate to immigration area with very long lines. The WiFi was very spotty and I couldn't maintain a connection. Upon exiting customs/baggage claim, one is accosted by numerous time share reps who have set up shop there. This makes for an unpleasant arrival experience. The departure experience marred by overcrowding and very long lines to get through security. Post Security and Immigration, there is a huge duty free shop that you have to traverse to get to the concourse. The concourse and gate areas are very crowded with a dearth of seating. WiFi - unable to connect despite repeated attempts. Signal strength for cell/mobile was very poor. Terminal 3 needs an expansion to accommodate the thousands of passengers.

With electronic boarding pass for a Delta flight to SEA, USA. Carry-on luggage only. Time from drop off at terminal 3 to clearing security, 18 minutes. Delta flight departure time 513pm. Arrival processing time with USA passport, using electronic/automated entry booth which prints your entry document with photo scan of passport and facial recognition scan. Line was long and people were trying to cut into the line, with resistance from people in line. Delta flight arrival at 415pm. Approximately 44 minutes. Waiting line organization could use some work on their part. No contact with immigration personnel. In advance paid Yucatan tourist tax and immigration processing fees/filling out forms. No water stations to refill containers, unreasonably expensive bottled water. Finding a reliable and honest rental car agency prior to trip was difficult and only found using other people's reviews. Required car Insurance costs are misleading or intentionally hidden. Some agencies refused to provide a copy of their insurance policies and prices when requested for review.

The prices for food and drink at this airport are predatory, especially at Terminal 3, used primarily for international departures. There is no free drinking water available, and passengers are required to pay at least 94 pesos ($5.50) for a bottle of water that costs 10-15 pesos in town. Prices for restaurants are double and triple what one would pay in Cancun for a similar meal. The check-in kiosks (where one scans a passport or inserts a credit card) were inoperable for our American Airlines flight. Overall, not a good experience at CUN.
I waited for over an hour to get my bags. The new airport at Tulum is now open if you can try that one or Coxumel. I have travel to Cancun very frequently and it is getting worse.

Scam you out of money. When we arrived we wanted to get 3 strawberry Daiquiris from the coconut bar outside by shuttles. The first red flag was he wouldn't accept US currency. Then 3 young girls kept getting drinks and he would only use their credit card. As I was waiting for my drinks the phone rang was my shuttle was leaving so I gave my credit card. When I got to the room i checked my credit card invoice he scammed me 218 Canadian$ for 3 drinks, no phone number, no email to contact - hoping my bank reimburses me. When going to those places use pesos only, they will rip you off huge

Very frustrating getting to the airport in Cancun. Traffic was horrendous. It took us over an hour to go 10 km. Once we arrived and got in line with frontier airlines, it was very slow, an hour in line with only one agent helping checked baggage for our group, and finally reaching an agent, we were informed that we should have printed out our baggage ticket at the kiosk. if the agent printed our baggage ticket out, it cost an extra $25. Our luggage weighed 43 pounds and they wanted an extra $50 to check it. The airport needs to have agents instructing travelers to print their baggage claim. The airport knows the difficulty due to road constructions in arriving on time and then to pressure you more while you’ve waited so long it’s just bad business. It doesn’t take a smart person to know they should inform their travelers will not be going back to Cancun in the near future.

Worst airport in the world. Bad signage, bad logistics, circle road system. Traffic outside the airport is crazy, took us over 3 hours to get to the main highway. But there’s worse: a local mafia is running the TAXI business outside the airport. They charge you $70-100 just to take you to the hotel area of the airport, which is barely 5-10 min away. More expensive than Paris or London! A complete rip-off!
Airport staff sleeping and sitting in charging booths meant for Travellers. Why are these staff members not working? Bad management. Please see what can be done to make the experience better.

I pre-booked special assistance with Turkish Airlines for my flights. CT-Istanbul-Budapest and Athens-Istanbul-CT. There is no security or special assistance area at the entrance. I used drop and go upstairs. I had to hop to the checkin counter and wait until a wheelchair arrived. The rest was fairly smooth and return trip was prompt with wheelchair assistance to my vehicle.

Firstly the sky bridge was late arriving at the plane. Why? There was only one international flight arriving, is it too much to ask that the bridge arrives on time. Secondly, the e gates were not operational. Why on earth have them if you are not going to operate them. Then to top it all, after collecting our baggage, everyone had to load their baggage onto a manual scanner of which there was only one. I have not seen one of those use in SA ever. Why introduce such an archaic system.

I returned home to Cape Town with my husband, my 69 year old mother and my 3 year old twin boys on June 28, 2023. Our flight landed just after 11am. Passport control was overcrowded, overwhelming and chaotic. There was no queue for elderly people (not in wheelchairs) or for families with young kids. I found this problematic as our kids starting having major meltdowns in the queue that was miles long. We tried to call a staff member over to ask if there was any way we could avoid standing in this long queue with my kids and my mother. The lady told us to come with her to the front (by the counters), but we had to all crawl under the metal bars to get there. After a few minutes, after she had spoken to her supervisor, she told us that she was sorry, but we had to stay in the queue as the supervisor said if he allows it for us, he must allow it for everyone. Shouldn't this be the norm though? Making provision for families with elderly parents and young kids? I found this so hard to understand and felt very frustrated at this point. We had to then re-join the queue, and when I asked if my mother could at least go through a gate, we were told no. When i asked if my mother could sit and wait on a bench until we reached the front of the line, we were told no. So we all had to climb back under the metal bars to get back into the queue. After having lived in many countries and after travelling through a lot of international airports, I have to say that Cape Town International Airport is far, far behind in terms of international standards. Very disappointing to arrive home and to have this experience. I am not looking forward to departing from or arriving to this airport again in future.

Got off a 10 hour flight from Dubai and had a connecting flight to Namibia with a layover of 2 hours of which 1.5 hours were spent at the first passport/Immigration control. Only 2 booths open. Then afterwards the scramble to get to our gate because there is no transit area. You literally have to go out to the exit and back in through the whole Airport to Departure Area then to a Security check and another immigration counter where another hundred people were queuing with 15 min left. We had no choice but to cut into line because other travellers still had plenty of time and then we were still told that we are late by the Immigration Officer. Some of the Staff was friendly and helpful while others were not and just didn't care. Will never use this Airport again!

After 2,5 weeks of touring around South Africa, we experienced nothing but efficiency and kindness from everyone. That is, until we checked in at Cape Town International to fly back overseas. What a total catastrophe CPT airport is - because they are totally understaffed. Six international flights all leaving within 60 minutes of each other, and this is what we experienced: A 30-45 minute wait in front of security. Then 2 hours (yes 120 min!!) in front of passport control, because 1000+ passengers were trying to leave, all impatiently waiting and pushing and getting verbal as they got more and more nervous about missing their flights. There was one passport booth open. At some point a second one opened, and eventually a third, to process 1000+ people!!! I am so disappointed in Cape Town airport, and will avoid all international travel from there from now on, and recommend everyone does the same. What a disaster and actually a huge pity! A beautiful modern city, full of international flair that has such cool vibe, and it has a disaster airport! It just doesn't add up. The few (and for the most part friendly) staff on duty tried to keep things going, but they were so understaffed that things just fell apart.

Absolutely appalling verbal abuse and aggression from the ‘Supervisor’ at the International Passport Control booth when I presented my UK passport and SA passport after travelling from Wales, UK, to Cape Town via Amsterdam by myself — almost two days in transit with train delays, and a crowded KLM flight. I arrived at Cape Town Airport at 11pm, exhausted and with luggage that was difficult to carry. The ‘Supervisor’ was aggressive about my SA Passport status, refused to listen to my reasoning, told me I was ‘just making excuses’, ‘that I was flying illegally’ - and had me in tears when he aggressively shouted at me to ‘go back to where you came from’. How on Earth was this ghastly little man put into a position of such power? I have only ever once before received such aggressive and appalling treatment from a Passport Control Officer — and that was in Johannesburg in 1976 under a SA Nationalist Party Government. This man needs to be retrained in how to deal with the public. Or fired. I am a 63-year old grandmother, and after an hour at the Passport Control booth, I exited the Arrivals Hall at well after midnight into a dark and frightening car park to try and find my Car Rental. I was so angry, upset and shaken by my experience, that I am writing a letter of complaint to the Airport Manager.

Firstly after an 11-hour flight, we were met at the immigration booth by a very aggressive immigration booth worker, we had an issue with one of our family members' passports and he (the gentlemen in the booth) basically threatened us that he would send us (a family with kids) back to our country without even explaining what the issue was or even trying clarify that is a solution which does require such extreme measures. Only after a really friendly immigration officer came to help did we end up finding a solution. So after the passport issue was resolved a few hours later because of help from the embassy, we had to have another situation with an erratic staff customs lady who made a scene claiming to be pushed by us even when no such incident occurred and demanded an apology loudly screaming. When we asked for security to please have a look at the camera footage to see just how absurd this lady was, they did not even want to help us and sided with the customs staff lady. This airport is a disgrace and unprofessional to even have such members working there in such important roles when dealing with people, if it had not been for the friendly staff that we did encounter there a single star would be too gracious. Please check your seats when sitting by windows, they reek of urine.

I arrived at Cape Town International Airport and had to wait for my baggage almost 20 minutes. This was a local flight from JNB to CPT. This is not my first bad experience of the same nature in recent weeks

I find the VAT refund claim procedure at CPT to be a bit of a scam. There are no signs at the check-in or prior to going through security to advise where to go to claim for tax refunds, but as soon as we got through passport control there was a sign and a counter advising about tax refunds. When we enquired, we were told that you have to claim the tax back before you clear security. This desk was just to pick up the card with the amount that you had claimed on it. So now we have to wait until we get back to London, fill in a form and get it stamped by the customs staff, then send it back to South Africa along with all of the original receipts, in order to claim the tax back. If I do that, I can’t insure any of the valuables that were bought as you need an original receipt as proof of purchase and to prove actual value. So I guess this is how they stop people from actually being able to claim the tax back, as people either don’t bother to do it once they get back because of the hassle, forget to do it, come across a problem with the info they were provided at CPT airport so can’t claim, or choose not to if it’s a choice between claiming the tax back or insuring the items against theft etc. Any airport I have been to before, you have to clear security to get to the tax claims desk (I guess to prove you are actually leaving the country?) So I find this a very underhand way to keep hold of tax that visitors have paid and are entitled to get back.

Each time I have flown in and out it has been easy. The lines moves quickly and everyone is friendly and helpful. Upon arrival after passing through immigration you proceed to the baggage carousel and hope that your luggage has made it to your destination with you but don't try to walk away with your suitcase that easily someone will be standing by to check your baggage tag and your passport.

Nearly two years on from the most recent review by A Hetier and much remains familiar at Maiquetia. Entering the country is easy and immigration is quick and friendly. Leaving the international terminal however is a far more stressful experience. The problem seems to stem from the multiple security agencies operating at the airport who often duplicate security checks. So one set of police screened everyone queueing at the check-in desk. Once in the customs/immigration area carry-on bags were x-rayed twice in rapid succession by two entirely different security groups. Then - and this was the real delay - passengers were called from the boarding gate in groups of 5-7 at fifteen to twenty minute intervals to go down to the working area of the airport for hand inspections of their already checked-in suitcases. I was in the penultimate group to be called down for an inspection at 6 PM - for a flight that was supposed to have left at 4:20. Some passengers claimed that TAP (with whom I was flying) and Iberia are singled out for this type of additional security check; others claimed it was common on all international flights though perhaps not to the same degree we were experiencing. I can't verify either of these claims. And even after these suitcase checks our carry-on bags (already x-rayed twice remember) had to be be hand searched in the airbridge by the same police force who had been checking our passports at check-in. These constant overlapping checks can cause significant waits and long delays. It took me two and a half hours to complete the check-in and immigration formalities and after that my flight was then almost four hours late leaving. Do also make sure that you have _more_ Bolivares than you think you need for taxes as all taxes have to be paid in cash. In addition to the airport tax (currently BsF 162.50) I had to pay an additional BsF 30.50 at check-in as the separate departure tax - usually included in tickets - had gone up in August forcing everyone to pay the difference in cash. Several passengers had only brought enough Bs to pay the airport tax and were placed in some difficulty since the ATMs upstairs only accept local Venezuelan cards (in a pinch some of the travel agencies downstairs will reportedly forward you cash; at a price). For all that airside is modern with plentiful duty free and food options - some of which will take a non-Venezuelan credit card - so at least you won't go hungry. I also used the domestic terminal several times in July and August. This is considerably easier to leave than the international terminal and I always found it a pleasant and stress-free experience. Do be careful though if your flight is using Gate/Puerta 5. This is not a standard gate but rather where the buses for smaller planes that don't use airbridges leave from; announcements for boarding are called out by an airline representative and actual boarding does not always match what the airport departure boards claim is happening. You need to pay attention and speak enough Spanish (not a huge amount to be honest) to understand these verbal boarding announcements. Like international airside in the domestic terminal is clean modern and with plentiful food options. The usual warnings about not taking unlicensed taxis from Maiquetia still apply; if at all possible have someone meet you and if this isn't possible only take an official taxi booked from the official desks. The warnings about robbery and express kidnappings from unlicensed taxis should be taken very seriously. Harassment inside the terminal however isn't as bad as some airports I've used. It was less full-on than the old Bangkok airport for example.

One needs more than arriving 2 hours before take-off time for international flights. I would suggest 3. Queues are terrible everywhere (check-in taxes immigration). And why taxes can't be paid by card?! On arrival migration services seem more efficient (search me...) and luggage is delivered efficiently. It is a pity not to be able to get money from an ATM in the international space (only local cards seem to work). On departure when you pass migration you get into a renewed part of the airport with plenty of space totally different from the departure area which is crowed. Duty free shops are nice as well as the food offer. Some don't like the patterns on the floor of the departure area but it's one of the charms of Maiquetía airport. Another one is the take-off and landing especially at daytime. I always enjoy the landscape.

Caracas airport despite many improvements still has a very long way to go to be thought of as anything more than adequate. The mad "tax" system where you pay to get out. A rather surprising total of six separate search points. The woeful queues at Immigration both inbound and outbound. The lack of a covered walkway between International and Domestic terminals. The constant unwanted attention from taxi touts and money changers.
Despite the "new" international terminal ~ give yourself several hours to check-in. It took me 2 hours 15 minutes at American the other morning.

I've been in CCS many times and the improvements made to the airport are incredible. Very friendly and helpful staff. Still it is not a modern airport but manageable considering the amount of passengers. The only bad thing is that they are not paying attention to the security and when you are in the arrivals hall a bunch of people come and ask you if you want a taxi or maybe you want to buy the local currency - I undestand this due to the political situation the country is facing but as I always say it could and must be better.

I agree entirely with Fernando. Immigration staff also very helpful as well as friendly and efficient. Only problem now is the collapsed bridge on the road to Caracas. A diversion has been made but is only two lanes and is operated on a tidal system. Can add an hour or two to the journey.;

I guess Mr. E Bernal hasn't been to CCS Int´l recently. This airport has been totally renewed. since June a brand new arrival area was opened with about 40 desks and very friendly staff. Deplane go through immigration and picking up your luggage takes about 20 minutes. So I recommend you to save those US$ 200 and continuing to fly through Caracas. By the way I did not know that there were flights from Maracaibo to Aruba.

I have flown into Maracaibo via CCS twice this year (both Air France) and after both experiences I have to remind myself to fly via Aruba next time even with the extra 200 EUR of flying KLM (AMS- Aruba). The reasons - All European flights arrive around the same time so you can imagine the line at the immigration counters. Of 10 desks on both times there were only 3 open. First time we queued for 1.5 hours (and the suitcases were waiting outside next to the belt). The second time we risked missing our connecting flight so an officer kindly let us skip the +2 hrs queue at the time we got on the line. The international and domestic terminals are not connected so when transferring it takes a 10 min walk (and carrying your suitcases) under a devil sun. You are not allowed to take the trolleys out of the terminals so the option you have (unless you carry it yourself) is to pay for a porter. I don't know how much it is since we decided to carry them ourselves. Be sure to cool off later on as the AC is barely noticeable inside the terminals. Domestic terminal same chaos as international. Upon departure make sure to check in as soon as it is open - same immigration queues! We were almost the first ones checking in and it still took us more than 30 mins to get through immigration! I must say however it is being remodelled and the new international departure area (before entering secure zone) has a nice food court incl Subway and TGI Fridays. Among others I have flown into Nigeria via Lagos and I must say Caracas is the worst airport I have ever encountered and will avoid it whenever possible. Departure tax is also more expensive than when flying out directly from Maracaibo (nice small international airport).

On my last visit I found many issues which dismayed me regarding Simon Bolivar International Airport. (1) Only 2 ATM's in the entire international Terminal(side by side unsignposted and upstairs in the Mezzanine Level) - both "out of order". (2) Several Bank outlets in the main terminal concourses - closed in the middle of the day. (3) Inability to take luggage carts from the baggage claim area outside the exits into the main Arrivals Hall. (4) Excessive number of "pushy" unregulated (and mostly uninsured) taxi touts. The airport authority regulates (or attempts to) taxis and there is an offical Taxi / Transportation counter in the Arrivals hall. (5) On Departure from the country there is an airport user tax which must be paid prior to security / immigration. The organisation and collection of this farcical and woefully inadequate. In the airport's defense I would say it has one of the better Tourist Information desks of many South American airports but while the staff may be friendly and helpful there are all too few of them. Food selection and outlets are reasonable and shopping appears quite inexpensive.

Through a lack of concentration and waiting to board at the wrong gate I missed my flight to London Stansted. I returned escorted to the checking in counter to get another ticket for the following day. The agent who was available and did place order for the ticket said rather acerbically that it was important to concentrate when going through departure. This is self evident and I resent the comment made as everybody lacks concentration at times and mistakes are made On departing the airport for an overnight hotel stay near the airport I was told the printed boarding pass would be issued the following day, which he then repeated for confirmation. On arrival at the airport I saw the same agent who asked if I had my boarding pass? Now who is lacking in concentration! Another agent I spoke to and who did hand me the boarding pass was courteous and very understanding of my situation and if the other agent was of a similar nature and character I would have given Airport staff 5 stars. On departing Narbonne I had a choice of 2 airports Carcassonne or Beziers. On reflection I wish I had chosen Beziers.

I understand that scanning both luggage and the person travelling is essential at all airports for the safety of all who fly. At a recent departure at Carcassonne airport my bag was cleared through the scanner and showed no items of dangerous content and the all clear given. The bag was then scanned with a hand scanner and opened, items were removed and a hand search made showing the bag again to be clear. At all other airports once the bag has been cleared by a full scanner and the all clear given you are then able to proceed to pick up. When passing through the full body scanner the all clear was given, but I was then given a hand scanner search although no beeps or signs on a screen would have indicated reason for the hand scan. After 55 years of flying this rather excessive scanning of bag and person has only happened at Carcassonne airport Of course acute,precautious judicious procedures have to be made but sometimes they become excessive bordering on paranoia.

A very poor quality airport. No ventilation or air conditioning so it’s always hot. Very few wcs so there’s always a long queue and apart from a very small outside cafe which is good the catering is abysmal. The seating areas at the gates are basic and too crowded.

After spending so much money on the new airport they have forgotten the basics. When you arrive , there are only two toilets, one male, one female, in the main corridor. There are no trolleys for those of us with luggage. The car rental office is over the other side of a busy road. The lift to get us to the underground tunnel and up the other side wasn’t working so we had to cross the very busy road with our suitcases and no trolley. The guy in the rental office shrugged his shoulders when I complained about this. The same happened on the way back and there were still no trolleys at all. What a shambles.

There were no taxis at the airport as our plane, the last of the day, landed at four in the afternoon. I mean, none. I found a card for a taxi company, rang them, to be told it would be at least an hour and my best bet would be to take the shuttle. The shuttle arrived about half an hour later, just one bus and it seemed at least half the flight needed to get on. People were crushed standing in the aisle. The nearest drop off for our hotel was quite a distance for two elderly ladies to drag their suitcases. So, if you are flying to Carcassonne, I recommend that you book transport online from your own country beforehand.

Fine for landing as you get through quickly but lack of facilities, seating shops bar means come with your own food n drink. You can’t buy a beer unless you buy food in the small café before security. There is only a soft drinks vending machine after security. No duty free, and the free airport’s wifi it’s like cracking the enigma code or such to register - time wasting for sure. Okay not many flights in or out but cater for passengers, most seats are outside exposed to the elements.

This is the worst airport I've ever used. It is so small and there is only one shop. They won't let you buy a beer if you're not having something to eat. There is no shopping other than a tiny shop which is worse than a small corner shop. Staff aren't even friendly. Security is so incredibly slow. I've been far and wide and this is the worst I've ever experienced.

We were waiting, on arrival, (on 1 December, on Ryanair flight from Dublin) outside, in very cold weather for about an hour for passport control. We were also "herded" like animals on departure. Returning my hired car was a nightmare, confusing signage meant several passengers didn't know where to leave the car, or where the hire office was. The experience was a good sample of how not to treat people. We pay for service at the airport in our ticket price, but in my view, we should not just get a refund, but be compensated for distress. A chaotic nightmare.

I flew to Carcassonne from Glasgow with Ryanair just when they were having all their major problems about cancellations. Fortunately my flight was pretty much on time with only one drunk man aboard. The flight was pretty standard for Ryanair and was plesent enough. When we landed, we all had to walk a virtual marathon to get to the arrivals hall in the 35 degree heat. Then once we finally made it there we had to wait over an hour in a stuffy baggage hall before our luggage arrived. The next problem I faced was at the car hire depot. I had to wait over half an hour before someone turned up at the desk. A week later when I'm heading home is where the worst part happened. Even though it was only early afternoon half my flight back to Glasgow seemed to be heavily intoxicated and sitting in a tiny departures lounge with only one cafe was quite possibly the worst experience of my life. When I got on the plane we didn't take off for another hour because the cabin crew couldn't get the door shut. The 2 and a half hour flight home was possibly the longest few hours of my life due to the noise and commotion from the drunks. The only thing I got out this holiday was to never fly Ryanair again

Carcassonne airport is about the best example of how France has failed to embrace the 21st century. If ever they wanted to give themselves a funny name a la John Lennon airport, then they should called themselves Clochemerle. The airport is essentially a shack with a runway - as everyone points out in reviews here, the staff are very friendly but friendliness does not overcome crass inefficiency. Ryanair now market "Business Class +" and take money for the "service" but it does not work here. With two flights departing about an hour apart, the baggage drop desk could not cope and the paid for "Fast track" service which is printed on the check in voucher evaporated. It took 40 minutes standing in a crawling queue just to drop off baggage. My advice to anyone wishing to avoid standing in line is to delay baggage drop until they start shouting for passengers for your flight and then you can jump to the head of the queue from the seat where you have been biding your time. For reasons best known to the airport and Ryanair, the return plane parked as far away from the arrivals hut as was possible and passengers were made to walk the length of the runway in the blazing afternoon heat. Mercifully the torrential rain that France endured that week had passed. There is one carousel to serve all incoming flights although to be fair, there are aren't that many. But the carousel holds about 20 bags so they rely of people getting their bags off the belt in order to put more on. The advantage then is that being only a shack, it is very quick to get out. Now we come to the free wi-fi service. I tried to set this up whilst waiting in the bag-drop queue but after 40 minutes gave up until inspiration struck. You have to register with your name and email. But when you try to continue it insists you must accept their terms or conditions by ticking a box which does not seem visible. Finally I tried clicking the box which said I would accept spam emails from them and this worked. Overall, if you want a taste of Clochemerle, this is your airport.

I was booked on the FR9224 service to Faro on the evening of the 4th. Arrived at the airport at 3pm for the 5.20pm flight and proceeded to drop my vehicle in the meet and greet area which was across the road from the Departures entrance. Inside the airport we proceeded straight through security with our cabin baggage and onto the gate. The whole process was under 15 minutes. And an on time departure. Upon arrival it was slightly more disappointing. Immigration being fast. The meet & greet wasn’t. Cones placed everywhere designed for the driver to get lost in an absolute maze and fellow passengers encountering issues exiting the automated barrier. Overall for my local airport and its location being 13 miles from my home, I’d definitely use it again. However saying that I do not think this airport can handle more than 1 flight at a time. Airlines like Qatar would encounter many issues getting their passengers through the short staffed terminal should they choose to return in the future. This airport has potential. Hopefully more flights are added soon so the people of Cardiff & Vale can finally travel without going 60 miles south to Bristol or 200 miles to London’s airports  But that would require staff, expansion and funds.

This airport is very sad. It is like stepping back in tome. With COVID we were made to queue outside the terminal.There were so many officials for 1 flight? I was shocked at the F&B offering and more expensive than I have experienced in Japan If they want to make money from their concessions they need to reduce the price (and massively increase quality) to drive volume. Difficult to take seriously as an international airport. Very officious (rude) security staff too. Shame.

The service there was horrible, we waited so long to check our luggage and when we did we had 2 kg extra which we shouldn't have had, they didn't inform this information to us and kept the luggage and they charged us £50 and when we said we would minimize the weight of the luggage. They charged us this amount for only 2 kg and it was only 1 luggage, they didn't inform us and took the luggage, we clearly said we could take things out to minimize the weight but they said too late. We didn't know it weighed more but we even asked if we could lose the weight but they didn't listen. Overall because of this, I do not think this airport is really good and in the future I will go to a better airport, I do not recommend this airport to anyone and would highly advise people to stay away.

Monday 5th August, 6.25am flight to Corfu. Approaching baggage/security check all we could here was this lady screaming orders out at passengers as she directed them to different counters. Short stocky blonde lady, early 50's take a look around at your colleagues, they were clearly disturbed as much as passengers with the way you were speaking to us. As I passed through the scanner myself, I said to two other members of staff "Why is she behaving like this"? They genuinely shrugged their shoulders. Is this regular behaviour from this lady, if so, someone put her on afternoon shifts as she is clearly not a "morning person". The only positive I can say about her is she is in no way discriminative, everyone got the same treatment.

I’d love to able to write something positive about this, my local airport but alas this isn’t the occasion. Travelling with my son who is autistic but in no way challenging in his behaviour we came up against the most officious security officer in the passenger search area. My son was wearing his highly visible “autism puzzles” wristband which proclaims they are working in partnership with Cardiff Airport. All was progressing well until the officer demanded my son push a tray being used by another passenger forward into the search machine. My son had already pushed his own tray forward and was confused by this brusque instruction and when I interceded the officer’s response was it wasn’t his job to do this. He then petulantly turned on me demanding I empty my pocket as this sharp eyed Sherlock had observed a handkerchief which he insisted must be x-rayed. This experience encapsulates the mountain CWL have to climb to rid themselves of the entitled and self important attitude which is now all pervasive since they were recipients of the ill judged handout from the Welsh government. It is difficult to avoid the conclusion that CWL’s desire to facilitate the travel of disabled passengers is nothing more than a shallow marketing exercise which clearly hasn’t been communicated effectively to their staff.

Tried to book 2 weeks parking in August. Nothing available. This is an airport that is trying to increase passenger numbers, but they have not even got enough parking for the low number of passengers they have got at the moment. Rubbish service, they need to put someone in charge who knows what they are doing. I checked the same dates at Bristol - 4 options available. Wonder where I will fly from next time??

Worst airport experience ever! I was taking a flight from Cardiff to Faro with my two children and husband. When we arrived around 4am for our flight at 6am the airport was the busiest I;d ever seen it, there were about three other flights all going off around the same time as us, queues were massive and people seem very stressed. I went straight to airport assistance as we had requested this for my son who is autistic, Cardiff proudly portray themselves as working in partnership with autism. I was given very bad advice at special assistance, I was told that there was no one available to help me at present and as it was so busy I may be better off just joining the queue unassisted. I did this and when we finally checked in our baggage we joined another extremely large que for security and passport control. During this queue I again noticed a section for special assistance and so I told a member of staff, he then guided me through a gate and placed me right by the queue for scanners, there was only one working and at this point we suffered at least three passengers directing abuse towards myself my daughter and my husband. I have never before been the target of such anger merely because staff were not able to control the passengers and perform their roles adequately, I had to argue with about three people justifying my sons disability. Once I got through passport control I complained to staff who just offered me some sympathy! In Faro airport the opposite was true, I received special assistance from beginning to end with the staff member staying with us through the whole process. I am ashamed to be British and ashamed to be Welsh!

Absolutely horrendous experience! Never in all the years I’ve been travelling have I been so utterly disgusted by poor service in an airport. Queues for an hour at check in! Lady at the desk didn’t have a clue what she was doing. Added to that, never will I fly with Ryanair again! The first and definitely the last.

Rubbish service. Tried to book car park, nothing offered for meet and greet or long stay, only off site with Holiday Extras in August 2019. Do not believe this. Will fly from Bristol next time as they are much more efficient!

I traveled into and out of Cardiff Airport in June 2019. I found the airport to be quite user friendly and compared to some of the reports I've read a pleasant surprise. A couple of negatives the one pound coins needed for the baggage trolleys seems rather tight and petty. Although it's close to Cardiff and the M4 it isn't easy to get to and from unless you have a car. Even in a car there seem endless roundabouts and traffic lights to get through. Check in was fine, I arrived in plenty of time. The security on departure seems over zealous compared to say Heathrow and would if the Airport were busier lead to very long queues. The shopping was okay, toilets were adequate, seating in the new departure lounge was fine, I didn't try the food outlets or WiFi. As I said at the start not an amazing airport but it did the job it is after all a small regional airport.

This airport sucks. It has to be 95 degrees in here right now. I'm about to pass out from the meds I'm on. Asked a worker where I can go and its nowhere. Absolute minimum food choices. Went to check in priority line and some guy started the whole pre check in from scratch. They should have to him to step aside and let others in. I'm talking like 15 minutes. Finally they gave a main seating line to us. Horrible experience.

The airport has to be one of the worst airports I have traveled through. People are very rude and inefficient. Security screening is absolutely horrendous. I saw them make people take bags that would fit through the scanner like backpacks back and have to check them. I was fine but many people got caught up in this. Not sure if it's a scam or what but it's ridiculous that this is a problem. There's not very many restaurant options as well.

This airport is the worst I have seen. One waiting room for all passengers. This one waiting room would be the size of a waiting area of one gate at an established airport for one airline. But all passengers are here, with about four main doors that lead passengers outside onto the tarmac and mechanical scissor steps to the aircraft doors. A small cafe inside the same waiting area that has a small selection of burgers and empanadas as snack food.  One small duty free shop adjoining the checked in passenger waiting area, almost the same size as the waiting area. No stores or food shops in the main entrance to the airport and no places to sit.  Long slow lines upon arrival through immigration. About 90 minutes to clear half of the passengers on my Jetblue flight. One blaring loudspeaker in the waiting area all the time that you cannot even hear when your boarding zone is called.

We arrived on a domestic flight, but heard horror stories about international arrivals. There is no taxiway at the airport - all movement is on the only active runway. When we landed, we spent 15 minutes parked just off the runway waiting for other planes to taxi along the runway to take off. Check in and security were fast, however after you are in the international departures area, the amenities are few. There are 2 snackbars and a shop, and a duty free. There is no restaurant and no tables, so if you buy something to eat, you will have to sit in a chair and hold it on your lap. You can buy beer and wine and sit there, and there is a lot of seating. There are no jet bridges and depending on the number of flights at the airport, you may have a long walk (Copa Airlines) to your flight. There was no tourist information at arrivals. This airport really needs to be replaced by a modern airport with taxiways and jetbridges. It is far too small for the amount of traffic it receives.

The worst airport I've been in my life, 2 hours in line in the sun to enter immigration. They make you wait outside and then another line inside. The airport is very small for the amount of people. El peor aeropuerto que he estado en mi vida , 2 horas de línea al sol para entrar a emigración . Te hacen esperar fuera y luego otra línea dentro . El aereopuerto es muy pequeño para la cantidad de personas

Check in and seating are adequate. There is only choice of gift store and restaurant. Prices are not displayed and service is very rude. Prices seemed even higher than expected for an airport. Security appears reasonably efficient. Rest room was clean.

From the city, getting to the airport by car takes between 30 and 90 minutes depending on the time of day and the attitude of other drivers. Check-in was quite fast although we saw little evidence of a computerised booking system – our seats were allocated by hand and the boarding cards were filled in by hand – maybe this was an airline thing since we were on a charter flight. International emigration was fast and without issue, at security some of us had to surrender our water, others did not. There was no interest in laptops, belts or shoes. One of our checked bags was thoroughly searched once it had left our sight - insides totally moved around but all there when we checked it at home. Airside, the international lounge has free slightly slow but usable wifi, two cafés (no credit cards – us dollars or local), a duty free shop, a jewellery store and a shop selling souvenirs. There are five international gates but only one was used. There are no air bridges. If the building has air conditioning, we did not benefit from it, acoustics are dreadful and it is very hard to hear any of the numerous fast announcements. There is no departure screen showing all flights. Seats are hard, toilets are clean – it is far better than many airports and less comfortable than some.
Strict minimum no much to do no much space. If you can prefer Avianca vip lounge with snacks drinks and wifi.

I did a recent domestic round trip through this airport. Arrival is uncomplicated (no jetways and a short walk to the terminal) although travelers should be aware that the luggage trolleys are only for the use of porters unlike other airports. Taxis await outside the baggage claim. Check-in is more complicated. The first departure area one encounters is actually where ticketed passengers go to reach their gate. The actual check- in is further down the walkway - no signs are provided but employees are quite helpful. The airport appears to be in a state of protracted renovation that is evident at departure - a regular visitor commented that it was different every time he visited there so conditions may change. The security is pretty simple - no removing of watches etc. The gate area is a bullpen and the monitors provide the names of airlines but no departure information. There is a cafe and a small gift shop but little else nearby. Free wifi is provided. Departure announcements are not translated into English or any other language although a large proportion of travelers obviously were foreigners; many from Europe Australia or the USA. Poor acoustics make things difficult even for locals to understand.

The airport has undergone refurbishment in recent years and is pleasant and air-conditioned. Security is tight and efficient. One problem is the availability of refreshments. There is only one major cafeteria - located in the walkway between the domestic and international sections of the airport - but it is a rip-off. If you buy something simple like a soda and a chocolate bar though the courtyard by the domestic arrivals area is very pleasant. When you clear customs upon arriving you need to go to the little taxi services window just outside domestic arrivals to request a taxi to go into town. The attendant will then give you a ticket with the fare printed on it depending on where you go. Do not go straight to the taxi rank nearby as the drivers will attempt to harass you into their cab smile a lot and then rip you off! Alternatively if you don't mind a short 2 minute walk you can just walk straight down the street that leads out of the terminal and get a taxi (or even a local bus) much more cheaply.

The worst airport I have been to. Dirty, outdated, poor signage, lack of staff and lack of amenities. Waited 3 hours for baggage claim. Unloaded on the tarmac and crowded on to a dirty over crowded bus. Once outside swarmed by peddlers who were quite persistent. A very unpleasant experience after a very long flight. If I never go there again it will be too soon. Travelers beware.

Arrival: Lineup at customs was not bad at all. Luggage was fast. I was lucky to find a sympathetic security guy who called my agency for me when my driver did not appear on time. The arrival process was the best of the 3 airports on my trip. Departure. A bit crazy as you have to put your luggage on a conveyor at the entrance. For check-in the signs were not adequate. I had to ask someone. Passport control and security were smooth. I did not eat there. Washrooms were a bit far from my gate.

The airport is all of a 2 1/2 star if that. The airport workers and airline staff seemed bothered when I asked a question, as if I was beneath them. Food court seemed never to have been cleaned and again some of those workers seemed not to care. Overall just a totally bad experience.

Could not find anything vegan, the Starbucks staff were awful, the lounges had nothing. The manager at Cafe Bianca made me the worlds best pizza and a panini with veggies, was able to find soya milk too.

Worst airport I've been to in a while. We came from Marrakech which has a terrific airport. The one here in Casablanca is the opposite. It's run down, inefficient and the staff across the board unfriendly. It needs a complete makeover. My suggestion is to connect outside Morocco if you want to get to one of the smaller airports.

I've flown to Casablanca Mohammed V airports 2/3 times a year for years now and this airport is a disgrace. It's in serious need of modernization. Immigration lines are sometimes very slow. I had to wait 1.5 hours one time for my arrival to be processed all while my family was waiting to pick me up. Hope the authorities do something to improve the main airport of the country.

Arrived at 7am. Check-in slow but efficient. Went to departure gate passport and boarding card checked. Entered the security hall along with thousands of other travellers. Only two points open out of more than 8 and one of those was for people who were about to miss their flights through the delays. Stood in line for over 1.5 hours. They eventually opened another point when there was an undignified scramble from queue jumpers to get there first. No notices whatsoever in Arabic, French or English. One man at the start of the conveyor belt was telling each person what to do, hats off shoes off etc etc. He was also responsible for the white plastic trays which he insisted people put their bags and stuff in. But there were only six available so he kept going to the end of the belt and retrieving the trays.
