Got to the end to be confronted by a policeman who inspected passport and B card again and frisked the males. At the gate every piece of luggage was searched again. This the main airport hub for Morocco and it is a disgrace. Inefficient and a terrible experience. What with all the delays clearing customs on arrival, the stinking toilets on the Royal Air Maroc planes and the time it took to clear security at Casablanca we will certainly not be returning.

Experienced CMN last month arrival from Paris Orly with RAM and continuing to Muscat with Oman Air. Had to retreive my luggage, pass immigration and recheck-in again. All was very smooth and from the time the plane landed, I was outside less than 30min later, very impressive. Agents were all polite and efficient. The secret is like everywhere else: Be patient, respectful and polite and everything will be fine! Will not hesitate to use this Airport again.

I was down with flu and surprised when I checked in and cleared passport, that the airport did not have any pharmacies or clinics inside the airport. This is the first time in a long history of travel that an airport doesn't have these facilities. Very disappointed.

Its the worst airport I have ever seen. Delay in entering airport because baggage is scanned, not necessary. Then at check-in your in the queue for a long time. Then you enter departures and continuously asked if you have money, they are nothing but thieves and beggars in uniform. This causes a lot of delays asking each passenger do you have money, what business is it of theirs if passengers have money? Then your hand luggage is scanned again only for someone to make a fuss and ask for something from your luggage. Then you enter another long queue only to fill out a departure card which is a waste of time. At this point, you've almost missed your flight. They are all trouble makers at the airport. Thieves in uniforms.
A very nice small airport, with all that is needed, except a coffee shop, if I remember correctly. Access is easy and clear, the terminal clean and there is free parking.

Catania Airport is possibly the worst airport. The toilets are dirty and security takes forever. There are only 2 restrooms in Terminal A in 1 restroom in Terminal C. Barely any restaurants in Terminal A, and one cafe in Terminal C. Not recommended because there are always no seats and blaring speakers. Catania is my home airport and they need to improve on such things.

The airport is filthy, the toilets are disgusting, the people working there are rude, no real duty free for travellers outside the EU, very limited options on food and drink, and, if you pass the passport control is even worse! Just an even overpriced kiosk that didn't accept card and of course, no ATM in sight! Hospitality at it's finest (not). You should put A LOT of work to come anywhere near to being a fully operational airport!

It is a shame that KLM/Transavia is in Terminal C which is not a real terminal. No facilities, cafes or shops. I always buy wine and other liquids at the Airport. Not possible here and no facilities to sit properly. Looks like a low cost carrier far away Airport.

I have experience CTA several times over the past few years and only have two complaints, Firstly the size of the lounge is inadequate and overcrowding can be an issue. I have always found CTA to be mostly clean as well that is extremely easy to navigate. The check in area is upstairs, if your early enough you won't experience queuing issues. Security is fairly small but at the same time very efficient. Once past you can try and find a seat, depending on the time you travel the floor may be the only way but this time we found some seats before getting food. We sat and relaxed before passing passport control for the UK bound flight and even there we found some seating to relax, now the seats are hard and not particularly comfortable so you will need to have a stretch before the flight back. Overall I would say CTA isn't the worst airport I have ever used but it is far from the best as well. I would use CTA again for the convenience of arrival to Sicily.

Catania Airport on the 14 May 2024 was chaotic. But what really annoyed me were the toilets, there were only two toilets by Gate 22 and both were very dirty and there was no toilet paper! Also when washing our hands very little water was dispensed and then the hand dryer didn't work. I had enjoyed my stay in Sicily but Catania Airport really lets it down

This was the first time I departed as well as arriving into Catania - previously I had a good opinion of the airport, as arrivals is so efficient and stress free - little wait times at passport control and baggage received very quickly. However this time we were also departing and now I understand why everyone hates this airport. The truth is this airport has too many passengers and flights taking off for the size of the terminal. Terminal A where our British Airways flight was departing from basically a zoo, with too many passengers hemmed into a tiny space after security and no seating to wait. It is so cramped they struggle to even fit in the food and shopping outlets. And lets talk about the food outlets - this is price-gouging on a level I haven't seen at any other Italian airport, just obscene pricing of very average looking food. And of course there is no water fountain because they want to overcharge you several euros for bottled one. Lastly the filth - this airport is filty, absolutely filthy and dirty, it really made me uncomfortable. I will never complain about Palermo airport ever again.

One of the passengers in the group I was travelling with, lost her suitcase on arrival at Catania. We found our way to Lost Property to be faced with a woman behind a glass screen. On the glass screen was some form of map with an arrow pointing to 'REVIEW' which I was told was in the area of Car Park 5. The woman behind the glass screen was obviously extremely annoyed with a contorted angry expression on her face, clenched fists, and actually screaming REVIEW over and over and over again. What was the purpose of that to a non Italian speaker? Not only was it unhelpful but it gave an impression that TOURISTS ARE NOT WELCOME HERE! Catania - clear up your act!

What a way to end a wonderful holiday! Arrived at Catania Airport for my return flight to the UK to find all public places in the departure lounge packed full of passengers. Seating areas were packed - all seats taken and every table used as a seat. So the only available place to sit was the floor - most of which was also crowded with people. My flight was delayed by two hours, and I spent much of that time on the floor in the departure lounge. Eventually I went through to the boarding gate hoping to find a seat in there - the same issue there - so on the floor again. What a thoroughly demeaning experience this was! Having paid what I thought was a pretty high price for my flight, to be treated like an animal at the airport has left me with a very poor impression of this country! NOT TO BE REPEATED!

Appalling! There was a problem caused by fires near the airport, so the airport was closed for 2 hours. However there was no information available whatsoever and passengers were left crammed into the gates with no idea what was going on and there was very little seating (about 10 seats at the gate) and so an elderly lady was forced to sit on an air conditioner. We eventually got information that the flight was delayed but with no departure time. We eventually got onto the plane 3 hours late, after a totally chaotic boarding experience-people crammed everywhere and lots of shouting and arguing. We then sat on the plane for another hour and the pilot announced "the airport is in confusion". Obviously this situation was unusual but it would have helped if we'd been informed what was going on. Security is quite efficient but once you get through the airport is a disaster. There is very little seating anywhere so people sit on the floor, on the steps etc so it's very difficult to move around. There are only 2 or 3 working displays with information and no (or very few) announcements. The whole place is boiling, chaotic and disorganised and also dirty. The toilets are slightly better in some areas of departures but there are only 2 cubicles for ladies downstairs and arrivals is even worse-20 minute queues for the ladies! Overall this place needs reorganising! A very stressful experience.

Possibly the worse European airport I have even flown from - crowded, no seating, no charging, no water, no AC - really lamentable. Check in process was reasonable, as was security but once airside there's nowhere to sit, most people opted for the floor.

As a primary airport for travellers to Boracay Island, Philippines, Caticlan needs serious expansion and upgrading. With separate arrivals and departure terminals (about 1/2 kilometre apart) there is a heavy reliance on cumbersome, unsafe and polluting buses to transfer passengers to aircraft. Arrivals is little more than a big tin shed where passengers are funnelled to taxis, buses etc to transfer to hotels on Boracay. The departure terminal is larger but woefully inadequate. As flights increase, the airport is too small to meet basic needs (but certainly enriches its owners) Security (a joke), concessions (few), direct access to aircraft (none!). Like much in the Philippines, the airport and all of Boracay lacks strategic planning and instead is simply a vehicle to ring out more money for the few families who own everything in the country. Decisions and plans (if any) are reactive with zero planning and strategic integration of the nations needs (that would cost ways too much plus, I want to buy a house in Aspen!). With a feudal system enrich a very few, the PHL and its airports once again falls to the bottom of every measure of ASEAN success.

We were informed that there is a delay in our departure time, it just fine as we had more time to take our last pictures, very good in the part of Air Asia. When we arrived at the terminal for departure in Caticlan (take note: they have different arrival and departure terminals), the state of the area was extremely poor. As if, it is just a huge bus terminal in EDSA. Poorly ventilated, not enough seating capacity. I was taken aback....considering this is Boracay#1 tourist attraction in the country and I can imagine the revenue that it is generating for the country. NAPAKA PANGET NG DEPARTURE AREA. Local E-trike drivers are earning more than 2k or more net on a lazy a day, can you imagine how much is the government is getting form the tourism business and yet the terminal is awful.

What a mess in the transport system. Could the airport or the local government do better. I am proud of Visayas as I am an Ilongga myself, but the airport isn't very inviting. Airports are terminals for tourist and local Filipinos to enjoy the place. But this airport is just frustrating. Planes arrives on time but gosh, the bus transfer and the minutes or hour you need to wait so you can get to the plane is like forever. How can we improve?

Arrival procedures easy and fast. Departure procedures for AF flight: small queue for security checks. Boarding room is too small for long haul aircraft (not enough seats), air conditioning is not selected to a pleasant temperature (it was too hot) and the two small shops opened one hour before take off (OK if you want to buy rum, perfume or whiskey).

Arrival procedures: efficient. Departing procedures: our aircraft had 36 hours delay due to a technical problem. Ground staff have been professionnal and kind with passengers. Embarking area for France: the area is small but enough for one long haul flight, not for several long range aircraft's. Shopping area is too small: only 2 small shops and a small snack. Cleanliness OK.

2nd largest airport in Philippines has 2 terminals. T2 is for international flights. Check-in Level has 4 main banks of Check-in counters A-D, at the back is the Departures area, firstly Passport Control with manned counters and then Security Scanning, both of which were quickly achieved. Main Departures has the usual array of shops and duty free shops and cafes. Some views of the gates and airfield. There is 1 lounge which covers most of the carriers premium customers - it's tired but has a reasonable selection of food on offer and seats with view of the apron. Airport busy but did not feel overcrowded.

We came from Davao and supposedly have a lay over in Cebu before our flight to Hong Kong. But unfortunately, immigration stopped us from entering because we arrived too early and suggested to sit and wait outside for 4 hours, this would make the lounges inside the airport useless because they wanted us to enter the immigration at around 1 to 2 hours before the flight. If this is the case then i suggest they place the lounges outside so passengers with connecting flights be able to rest up before their flight rather than sitting on benches uncomfortably waiting outside the immigation. And also, they should add more airport nap and bath rooms.

The best airport in the Philippines. Brand new, free wifi, seamless arrival and departure and plenty of excellent food choices. The connection between international and domestic is by foot and very short. Connecting flights is so easy.

Arrival was fine, was met by my fiancé. Departure was an entirely different matter. Huge lines trying to get through customs, they really need additional desks and staff. Got through with only 10 minutes to get to my flight, which was already delayed by 50 minutes. Overly bossy check in staff member boarded the aircraft in an incorrect sequence. I was supposed to be in row 7 but was the last person to board. As well as this, there was no room for my cabin baggage. Don't know why, but my fiancé was not allowed to even enter the terminal. Difficult when you are saying goodbye to loved ones.

Cebu Mactan international is a nice airport that was recently redesigned, but people need to be aware that it was hit rather hard at the end of last year by typhoon Odette, and as a result, things are not yet up to 100% again. Airport is still comfortable and clean however, but at this time with a slightly limited number of shops and dining areas available on the departures side of the airport. It is also a strange rule that my girlfriend was not allowed into the terminal to say goodbye to me. COVID rules taken too much to an extreme perhaps? One major issue I had was checking in staff. The entire process took me over an hour, because in the Philippines they have a tendency to train new staff on the job, it appears with no supervision from an experienced member of staff. This can make things very frustrating for the passenger. It took me perhaps 15 minutes to explain to this lady that yes, I had a connecting flight with Scoot to Perth, and yes, it WAS on a separate ticket. I think she was confused by this, or felt that you could not book a flight this way. The upshot of all of this was that she forgot to put a label on my cases to forward them from Singapore to Perth, so essentially nothing arrived in Perth. Fortunately, I reported this to Scoot and received my cases two days later. The Philippines is a wonderful destination, and the people are generally very warm and friendly, but please, give your new staff supervised training.

I was impressed by the cleanliness and orderliness of this airport. Even the porters and staff act professionally. Big space check in counters not cramped. You don’t have the feeling that you’ll be harassed nor cheated. Considering this airport on my future flights.

I would strongly discourage international travelers from using this airport solely due to the attitude and inefficiency of the immigration officers. It took over three hours to get through immigration as only two immigration windows were staffed and the officers made no effort to speed things up. In fact, it seemed as if they were deliberately working as slow as possible. Probably the worst immigration experience I have had anywhere in the world.

Just horrible! Luckily we came 4 hours earlier, otherwise we would have missed the flight. 1st) There is a weird ticket checkup at the entrance of the airport, although boarding passes are given inside. We had to look for tickets in our emails or print them beforehand, you can imagine how difficult that is without internet in a foreign country. 2nd) There is an unimaginable long queues at the immigration desks, both at arrivals and at departures. There are between 3 to 5 officers checking documents for thousands of passengers flying international. Even a 12 year old can do the math and realize that this doesn’t work. 3rd) You have to pay a “scam” airport travel or passenger handling tax (or whatever they want to call it) which is 850PHP (aprox 15€ / 17$). Instead of dealing with the airline for it, they want more money from tourists and create extra queues for this kind of payment. If you don’t have money to pay it, you will basically miss your flight. Keep in mind, paying with credit or debit cards doesn’t work, unless you have a visaCard. My wife had a visa-card and still didn’t work, so we had to go to an ATM, get out of the queues and pay an ATM fee of an extra 250PHP. But they still claim it works with Visacards. 4th. There is no air conditioning. If you never traveled in a packed bus with closed windows in Africa before, well, try to imagine. A great way to start and end your holidays (NOT).

Beautiful and brand new airport! However, this airport needs 4 more immigration officers at the counters. It is very inefficient - long lines! We arrived 2 hours early, and we didn't get a chance to look around, grab a coffee and relax a bit. Meanwhile, booths 11 -14 were empty, and people were panicking as they were about to board.
Unhelpful staff. Long waits. More expensive foods than NAIA. The system is not good. No elevator on domestic gate 25ABC. The security told me the wrong instructions.

When exiting the country, be ready to endure a seemingly never ending queue for the security check. This was the longest wait I have experienced, and airline staff for imminently departing flights were desperately searching for their passengers who were stuck in the line. The duty-free shops were mediocre at best.
This is a really nice airport, the arrival and departure terminal are separate which is very convenient. The airport hotel was amazing.

I arrived at terminal 2, what a pain. If you like stairs, and to walk 20 min to take your train, this terminal is for you! It's brand new, so it's clean, but it's so low cost. I will avoid it at all cost now.
The check in was smooth. Signs in English are sufficient to direct the passengers. The ambiance is great and its facilities are enough to give comfort to its passengers.

Excellent airport, clean, spacious, excellent traveler services, quick luggage check and very friendly staff, easy-access panoramic terrace with 180-degree view of departures and arrivals, restaurants and shops with normal prices, are positioning several low-cost airlines and it is the base of AirAsia Japan, I hope it will increase international connections and always maintain this trend, having for several years won the best regional airport in the world.

The check-in process at Nagoya Centrair Airport was a smooth and pleasant one, with kind staff assisting you if needed. However, the check-in counters opens only exactly 2 hours before departure. Apart from check in, there is an amazing skydeck for aircraft photographers like me to photograph planes free of charge. Also, there are many food options to choose, ranging from Japanese cuisine to Western cuisine.The central security screening was smooth and quick, and I cleared security within 30 minutes. The airside had a lot of duty free shops, vending machines to buy drinks, and a clear view of the apron and runway. Overall, it was a very pleasant experience and I am happy to fly out of Nagoya Centrair Airport.

I have never expected that a small-scale airport can be able to provide outstanding and extensive services to travellers. The airport was very clean and tidy, and everything in the terminal was well organised. Incredibly large number of facilities including an observation public bath. A wide choice of restaurants was available and the prices were reasonable. The sky deck was very large and great for phototaking. Airport signs were very clear and staff were always eager to help travellers. Convenient access to the city centre. The airport gave us a great impression upon our first visit to Nagoya.

Connected through this airport with Delta. It seems slightly older and smaller than Narita. Passing through security was quick and painless. The place is clean and has an open and bright feeling. There are standard airport shopping opportunities if you are interested. The meal options seemed severely limited which would be my only real complaint however I believe it is a large complaint because airplane food is awful.

Good small airport for a short transit. Not as big as NRT which makes it not as daunting. Small shopping selection but pretty good food. Efficient staff and quick security measures makes transit quite painless.

I used Nagoya as a transit airport between Indonesia and USA. Quick arrival procedures. Everything was well signed in Japanese and English. Transfer desk was unmanned but I bypassed as I already had boarding pass for connecting flight. Security was fast and polite. Terminal was clean and orderly. My flight was delayed by 10 hours. Terminal has high ceilings and big windows looking out over ramp providing an open feeling. Clean restrooms. Only 1 restaurant which only takes Japanese Yen and a Starbucks but there are several money exchange booths. I did not find an ATM anywhere. Lots of duty-free and high-end shops but only one poorly stocked news stand. Free Internet throughout airport both via wifi and several laptop stations with Ethernet power plugs chair and light. Lots of vending machines throughout but only take Yen.

When we arrived, exiting the terminal is quick, and our bags only took 10 minutes. Departing is also very efficient, as it’s not a large airport and there’s only one TSA checkpoint. Security only took about 5 minutes to pass through. Although the airport is lacking any duty free. There is a small cafe area to buy some food. Only two gates. Our flight even departed early (At 6 am!). Overall a nice little airport.

The debacle caused by under-staffing at this airport continues. Over 3 1/2 hours' delay in getting through Passport (lack of) Control. Only 2 people checking documents at the airport for all UK flights. We were queuing behind all the people from 2 other UK flights and they too had been trying to get through Customs for hours. As you stand in shivering temperatures in a marquee thing they have added to the Customs area, you can't help but notice the Vinici propaganda posters which indicate that a ton of money has been invested in this airport and how much customer satisfaction has been improved. What a joke. This facility is woefully undersized and understaffed. This issue has been going on for years. The facilities are laughable. Another thing to bear in mind is that the airport is situated low down in a valley and suffers with mist and fog regularly. Our return flight was diverted to Grenoble kbecause of the fog) and resulted in a 5 hour delay. Grenoble Airport is no better setup to cope with the volumes of passengers that are forced through these facilities. I will never fly to Chambery for skiing again. In fact, I will never fly to Chanbery, Grenoble or Lyon for skiing again. It will be Geneva or get in the car Save yourself some grief and avoid this airport at all costs.

The airport is very small so there is a lot of queuing. Check in was fairly smooth once it opened and the check in lady was helpful and efficient. Oversized baggage also taken at the desk which is good when you’ve got ski equipment. There was then a long wait until we were announced to go through security. Waiting area was limited and the food sat in a semi outside area where smoking was allowed. There was a very long windy queue through security. Limited facilities before and after security. There is no lounges available.

This airport physically cannot cope with the volumes of footfall that are common, especially during the ski season. Two carousels for arrivals (which is fine if there is only one private planeful of people, anything more than that, then it poses a problem) and then you walk round the corner and literally are out in the car park, with no waiting area available in between. Departing from there is equally irritating with a minuscule check in where the bags are manually transferred from the weigh in to the conveyer belt, a tiny security area which means that you have to wait until your flight is called up in order to pass through. The facilities available are dismally limited, the seating available while you wait is minimal, and food and drink expensive. Security itself is archaic, with one queue (explains why you have to wait to be called up) and small trays that mean you have to utilise five just to fit hand luggage, coat, phone and shoes etc. It wouldn't be so bad if this airport only dealt with fifty or so passengers over a twenty four period, as that is all the organisational abilities are set up to cope with. Unfortunately it is a key airport for ski destinations, which means the quantities experienced are substantial, and beyond what the airport is built for. It ranks up with Geneva as a horrendously mismanaged and inadequate airport, and that is saying something. The sad thing is, it looks like this is on par with Grenoble, which means any skiing to the Alpes requires being subjected to horrific standards of airport torture in order to get to a nice destination.

Avoid this airport. Our inbound flight was a 4 hour delay and our return flight is currently 3 hours delayed but could be longer. The inbound pilot blamed it on the weather, but this was a lie, and it’s being blamed on a technical issue for our return flight. This is a regular occurrence according to the flight attendant. I will not be travelling here again at any cost.

Check in reasonably efficient despite several flights being due to depart in a short time frame. Seating availability land side very limited. Several people sitting on the floor and maybe over 100 on the grass outside - not possible if raining. Toilet facilities poor - not adequate for volume of passengers. Limited food options. Temperature in airport very hot. I have visited here several times and this never changes. Not pleasant to board a flight dripping with sweat. Security is appalling. I fully respect the reasons for checks but it is the organisation of this area which could hardly be any worse. They have added extra screening conveyors but it is a single tray collection zone behind a solid wall and door to the screening area. Trays constantly ran out as no system evident to return empties other than the sole officer gesticulating in vain through a window in a locked door. Staff on the other side never seemed to appreciate the need to return trays. Having prepared a tray by removing belt into hand baggage; removing liquids in their clear bag, iPad and kindle from bag into clear view it was only when around the next corner (away from tray collection zone) that a different officer decided that everybody had to remove shoes (contrary to the rolling info film before that showed only someone wearing boots having to remove them). Another tray required. A total of 3 trays needed, as the trays are small and officers wanted everything spread out so distinctly. Unlike in Security at more advanced airports (but bear in mind the French have newly designed and created this Security area) trays have to be "self pushed" along a roller belt until x-ray scanners are close but then the tray roller belt does not go into the scanner. Each person has to lift their own tray and carry it across. Maybe 3 journeys. Whilst shuffling back and forth with trays it might be that other people's trays are interspersed with yours going through the scanner and then unexpectedly although checked already to gain access to this area, your boarding pass is required again, so if you have put it in your bag (to avoid objects in pockets) you have to re-extract it. Only at this point officers decide that not only iPad etc had to be out of bags but every charging cable etc as well. Cue general bag unpacking by all passengers just as trays are about to go into scanner. More possessions mixed up in multiple trays, including passport and boarding card. So once all trays come through you might get one full of cables etc and start trying to repack that but other valuables following maybe 5 trays behind. Only enough repacking area to really handle one or 2 trays - not helpful with say, 5 people all waiting in their socks, with trousers falling down, for 2 or 3 trays each arriving in a random sequence with those of other people. For a panicky minute or 2 I had no idea where my passport and boarding card actually were, which one might think would be exactly the opposite of the definition of "security". Eventually clearing x-ray screening I had then lost my wife who I assumed had somehow got through quicker, so I carried on. Long, very slow passport control queue manned by the sloths from Zootropolis! My wife then re-appeared from the underwired bra interrogation zone. 1 min to shuttle bus boarding closure. Buy water! Tiny stall, manned by 1 person, warm bottles. People rushing through, bootlaces not yet re-tied and cursing the staff... “Je suis un passager, sortez-moi d'ici”

Not so bad! Flew from Amsterdam to Chambery and back to use the airport as the port to the snow. Its obvious that it is a small airport not used to a huge amount of people but it all worked well. They have two belts and they use 1 for skis and 1 for the suitcases of all flights. It all went reasonably fast. Its 10 meters from the belt to the exit. On departure it was funny to see how they checked the luggage in, it took some time. At security they made a little mess by opening the wrong door so schengen and non.schengen almost mixed up. A very friendly lady excused and laughed. Staff very friendly and helpful, clearly not used to big groups of travelers. Behind security a couple of guys tried to sell food and drinks. Realy not a horrible place to be, keep in mind that it is a small airport.

This airport simply cannot cope with passenger flow: Arrival-06 Jan 2018. One luggage carousel for 3 arrivals! Had to wait for each to clear prior to loading the next. Only one toilet cubicle was functioning in the male toilet. Seating is grossly inadequate and there was not enough standing room in the arrivals lounge. In effect, passengers were trapped for over an hour awaiting luggage and unable to buy refreshments, sit, or use toilet facilities. Departure-13 Jan 2018. Check in was fairly efficient, with long queues, but moving fairly rapidly, it was good that skis and bags are taken at the same check in point. The experience rapidly deteriorated from then on. In the departure lounge, once again, only one male and one female toilet cubicle are offered within the same room, there are no more, apart from a single disabled toilet. Shared facilities are unacceptable in a civilised country and the queue was extensive with over 300 passengers struggling to find comfort or refreshment with the single, understaffed and overworked small refreshment kiosk. Vending machines only accepted Euro coins and not cards. The facilities are unacceptable in any civilised country, even Kathmandu Airport has better facilities. On the tarmac, the transfer coach to the airplane had a broken door with a sign that stated ‘This door is doomed’ an understatement of the Chambéry Airport experience. This is, undoubtedly, the worst airport that I have visited for toilet and refreshment facilities and I vow that I shall never use it again, even if offered a free holiday.

Travelled here for skiing. My arrival was delayed by about two hours due to fog. When we landed, it was apparent that several other 'planes had recently landed and the terminal was very overcrowded. After a long time queuing to get through passport control (only two officers), I found there were only two luggage belts and the indicator initially designated the wrong one for my flight. This caused consternation for many passengers when luggage did not appear as expected. The error was corrected and I managed to fight my way through the crowds to get my skis and case. Not a pleasant experience. The return journey was an absolute nightmare. Once again, flights were delayed due to fog. Driving the last 15 miles to Chambery was difficult due to the dense fog. Direction signs were few and far between and lacking a Satnav I became concerned I would be unable to locate the airport. The terminal was full to overflowing, people were sitting on the floor, on the stairs, standing wherever there was room. If there had been any sort of security scare I hate to think of the injuries which could have been caused in a stampede to exit the building. The catering business must make a fortune in this airport as there was a massive queue for the whole of the eight and a half hours I was waiting there. Once my flight was called, we were forced to queue in a very small area with tape barriers creating a snake of people waiting to pass the two customs officers. They did their best to move people through, but there was a jam back from the security checking area which is too small with insufficient staff to cope with the volume of passengers. I was becoming concerned I would miss my flight, but I guess they are used to this state of confusion as we were herded directly onto a transfer bus as soon as we cleared security. This airport is just too small for the number of passengers using it. There is no overflow capacity in the event of delays, which I now understand are very common here. Why on Earth build an international airport in an area known to suffer from regular dense fog? Next time (if) I fly to the French Alps, I will go to Lyon. As a matter of interest, if I had chosen to drive to the Alps (as I usually do), I could have made the complete return journey home in less time than it took me by air. Makes you think, doesn't it.

Chambery is a great little airport, the closest to the major ski resorts like The Three Valleys. It's small and gets crowded at weekends, but has a cosy bar/restaurant on the first floor. In 2014 we were delayed 6 hours here due to bad weather and they couldn't do enough to make our stay more comfortable, drafting in extra sandwiches etc. We were on time this year but still had time to enjoy refreshments/drinks etc. Much better than using Geneva or Lyon

Horrible airport and rude security staff. Hoards of people going through 2 x-ray machines and security were unnecessarily obnoxious and arrogant. They made the situation a lot worse by shouting at people when they weren't doing exactly as told. People have the right to be treated with dignity and these people have obviously forgotten that. Once through security there are not enough seats and people just standing waiting or sitting on the floor for long periods for planes delayed due to the shoddy airport and it's staff.

I recently had a disappointing experience with the Chandigarh Airport parking and cab system. I had pre-booked a cab for a nearby location, quoted at ₹230. During my onward trip for the same distance, I had paid ₹170, so the rate seemed reasonable. However, just 800 meters outside the airport, the driver suddenly demanded ₹600, despite the prior agreement. We had traveled across five states in the last two weeks, and nowhere were we charged more than ₹300 for similar distances of around 18-25 kilometers. It’s frustrating to see such unfair practices at Chandigarh Airport. Travelers should be cautious and prepared for possible overcharging. This level of inconsistency and lack of integrity is disappointing and needs urgent attention from airport authorities.
In this scorching heat, ACs don’t work. Travelers are sweating. Even lounges don’t have working AC. Very uncomfortable atmosphere with direct sun rays.

The airport has declined in quality since I last used it. The Plaza Premium lounge has been shuttered and in its place, a bar operates as a lounge on the ground floor, which doesn't take Priority Pass anymore. There are pigeons flying near the departure gates, which pose a health hazard. Food and drink choices are limited. All the shops sell the same type of sandwiches and "burgers," which all look unappealing. The restaurants are horribly overpriced compared to the city. Special versions of drinks carrying high retail prices are sold in the shops to take advantage of the passengers. There is no decent café airside. The only Starbucks is outside the terminal building so that doesn't do you much good. While the number of flights out of Chandigarh has increased lately, the airport is on its way down. It would be better if they'd pay heed and improve the situation after security clearance. At least put back a decent lounge, if nothing else.

Very bad to non existent customer care service. I have been trying to get in touch with the airport regarding a lost bag but have been unable to do so. No one picks up the customer care number provided in the website and no one replies to email. Very poor service.

Extremely poor luggage handling process. It takes so long for the luggage to arrive, it’s almost like they have no staff to mange it or have no training. Took 45 minutes today. As long as it took me to fly from delhi to chandigarh. Cannot call it an International Airport. Need to work on it
Airport was dirty. Dustbins were uncanny and overloaded. Washrooms were extremely unkempt and filthy. That’s not how we expect an International Airport to be.

On 17/11/2020 I was going to Chandigarh. All my journey was good but in the end at the time of exit at Chandigarh airport gate one man was supposed to do the thermal checking. I simply asked him if he could take my body temperature on my hand in place of my forehead. I don't know why he started being so rude.

No free WiFi, poor seating arrangements, cafeteria providers are a joke and serve no value to money spent. Caffe in charge observed talking rudely and in high pitch voice to the counter staff which is totally unprofessional and gives a feel of road side dhaba at the airport- zero professionalism! This is the quality of a so called international airport.
It is very disappointing that Chandigarh airport has no free WiFi facility. It has many free WiFi latch ons but none connect. It may be only international airport without free WiFi.

Even though the International flights to this airport are just a few, the arrival of baggage is a nightmare. IX 188 (SHJ – IXC) landed at 1:45 (delayed by 20 minutes). Baggage arrival 2:40. Why such a delay?

The security check of the airport is so bad. They pass my shoes through the X-ray, leaving me no shoes at all. They don’t provide slippers to me. Despite the overall environment is being improved, this inhuman experience makes me very uncomfortable.

This airport is located in a train station next to it which is pretty cool, but can cause major traffic getting in to it. The inside is clean and well kept with plenty of restaurants. Security is just ok, not many lines open so it can take a long time to get through. The issue I have like most Chinese airports is that they don’t use the jetways much and make you walk out on tarmac and take buses, sometimes to and from aircraft. In our case it was in the rain which made for an uncomfortable trip. Not sure why when jetways were open and they have enough but from what I can tell is that when the plane is not to depart after landing it gets stored over night and if you fly in later at night you will have to take bus, so I try to avoid night flights into this airport.

Very poor for an international airport. Firstly I saw Thai Lion Air's check-in desk and queued only be told I needed to go to a different set of desks for the Utapao flight because I was in the queue for the Bangkok flight, which made no sense because both flights were operated by Thai Lion Air. I therefore had to queue up again, which was annoying. After clearing immigration at around 1.00pm, half of the shops and catering outlets were closed. You expect this very late at night but not early in the afternoon. Also it is not clear how to connect to the Wifi. The only plus side is queues were fairly short at immigration and the terminal was clean and modern.

CZX is a small domestic airport (however a new big terminal is being constructed nearby) with basic facilities (and no milk at a coffee shop). Efficient check-in although boarding is little disorganized as you have to walk to the airplane. Not much to do apart from couple of souvenir and grocery/travel stuff stores airside; there is a smoking room and a lighter can be obtained from the next door coffee shop attendant :) as they will make you remove matches and lighters before allowing to an airside lounge. The airport is quite a drive away from the city. No queues as there were only two flights departing when I was there.

The island is lovely, the residents are lovely. The only down side is the poorly trained passport officials, pretending to read passports and carry out security checks. I have no idea where these people are found,  they need training or firing.

I arrived in Chania from Dublin about 1 hour ago and I am still waiting in a queue at passport control. It is 1.15am. Our flight from Dublin arrived c. 20 minutes after the scheduled arrival time. Everyone in this queue is from the Dublin flight. It is taking, on average, 5 mins to process each passenger at passport control. I am at the back of the queue and expect that it'll be another 30 minutes before I get through. It's absolutely incredible. How can it take so long? I will recommend to friends not to visit Crete because of this. What is wrong with your airport?

Wir hatten Rollstuhlservice gebucht. In Wien alles perfekt organisiert, in Chania scheint dieses Service gänzlich unbekannt. Unter Qualen musste die betreffende Person selbst die Stufen hinunter steigen, keine andere Möglichkeit. Dann mussten wir selbsterklären das es nicht möglich ist im überfüllten Bus zum Hangar zu fahren da keine Sitzmöglichkeit mehr vorhanden war. Ein zweiter Bus ist dann gekommen. Einstieg sehr hoch. Am Flughafen mussten wir dann selbst wieder schauen das wir jemanden finden der uns hilft. Nach einiger Zeit kam dann jemand mit Rollstuhl, vorher wieder eigenständig Treppen hoch. Begleitpersonen wurden dann im Flughafen zum Covid Test gebeten, besagte Person nicht. Diese wurde inkl. 5 jährigem Kind zur Kofferausgaube gebracht. Dann einfach alleine dort stehen gelassen im Rollstuhl!!! Andere Fahrgäste haben dann geholfen bis die Testung fertig war. Also einfach furchtbar und Menschenunwürdig alles. Sogar Ägypten ist hier viel besser. - We had booked wheelchair service. In Vienna everything is perfectly organized, in Chania this service seems completely unknown. The person concerned had to go down the stairs himself in agony, no other option. Then we had to explain to ourselves that it is not possible to drive to the hangar in the overcrowded bus because there was no more seating. A second bus then came. Entry very high. At the airport we had to look again ourselves that we could find someone to help us. After a while someone came up stairs independently with a wheelchair. Accompanying persons were then asked to take the Covid test at the airport, the said person was not. This was brought to the suitcase hood including a 5 year old child. Then just left there alone in a wheelchair! Other passengers then helped until the test was finished. So everything is just terrible and inhumane. Even Egypt is much better here.

Flew into and from CHQ as part of a 10 day holiday. Arrived into a bottleneck at passport control, and the queue went out of the arrival terminal and almost onto the tarmac (only 2 windows open and a number of holiday flights arrived not too far apart). Leaving Chania was an opportunity to see the other side of the airport. Check-in was fairly painless and efficient. However, once through check-in and security checks, it is very cramped airside. Duty free is pretty limited, and food and drink stands are over-priced (nearly €4 for a bottle of Coke). The cramped conditions are made worse by the free-for-all boarding procedures (keep your eyes on the departure screens as they don’t announce flight departures). I am aware that Fraport have invested in expanding the airport, but as more airlines start to use Chania (and the list is likely to increase), space in this airport will be even more at a premium. The airport is convenient re: location, as we were based in the West of Crete, but this airport needs to improve passenger experience drastically in all areas.
Worst experience I’ve ever had at an airport. We were laughed at for trying to find something we forgot on the plane by the arrivals staff. The most unhelpful staff I have ever encountered anywhere.

This is the worst airport I have been to. The staff are rude and inexperienced and provided us with misleading information in regards to the hand baggage and then proceeded to accuse us of ‘tricking them’ just because we did not want to pay an extortionate fee of £170 to send of our suitcases. FYI I based it on the Norwegian Airlines website and thought the fee was £49 however they told me Norwegian rules don’t apply and that the Chania swissport rules apply which are not what the check in lady told us. She was rude and should not be working there and she herself told us it would be no more than £50. Very rude staff and a very haphazard airport, go to Heraklion instead, save yourselves the trouble.
The security stuff are rude, unprofessional and slow. Lines are long and food stalls are much too expensive for this country. Too bad for a nice new airport.

Boarding was delayed by more than one hour. I approached the staff - including the terminal supervisor - to ask them to inform a very long line of families with very small children that the flight was delayed. Believe it or not, I was told by one of the check-in staff at the gate that the flight was not delayed! I asked her to look at the screen where it stated the departure time as 00.05 and pointed out that the time now was 00.40. She scoffed, the terminal supervisor turned her back on me and continued to chat to the check-in staff. Incredibly rude! Incredibly unaware that the airport might need to have passengers to survive and that there is something called customer service. I will definitely avoid anything to do with this airport in the future.

I am sat in a light and airy air conditioned building drinking Cappicino Freddo. The queue for checking in was small but very organised and the whole building is welcoming. Arrival was just as good although a slight wait for baggage due to three aircraft coming in close together. This airport has come on a lot since last year and I recommend it. The indicator boards all seem to be working ok and the WiFi is good. What more can you want. Don’t blame the airport for things they don’t control.

Terrible! Our flight has been delayed for more than an hour, just as our arrival flight and the previous flights from this airport. On moments like this you depend on the information screens on the airport to be able to know when to board. The information screens provided the wrong information and so we had already missed our flight once we got to the gate! According to the staff it was our fault because we had to be in the gate while the screens told there was no boarding.

This was the nastiest public restrooms I have seen in years. Paint pealing off toilet seat, nasty floors, no seat covers and more. The area between B & C concourses was so sad. The choices of cuisine was absurd. Fast food, really?

This is a large airport that is undergoing runway expansion which is very visible on takeoff and landing. For a mid-morning flight, the C concourse was very but not very crowded. Seating at the gates can be a premium; however, we had no difficulty finding seating. The connecting hall has all kinds of restaurants both fast food and sit down. Airport WiFi is easy to connect and fast. The bathrooms are impeccable. There is an attendant on duty who is constantly cleaning the bathrooms after every use. The attendant greets passengers saying welcome to the cleanest bathrooms in CLT. Kudos to Airport management.

The airport was a horrible experience. They are under construction so many areas are filthy. There is staff just lying around taking up space that should be used by waiting passengers. I had to tolerate employees making unnecessary noise while sitting around playing pokemon go. Others were arguing over their schedule's. Language used was very disrespectful.

This airport is a mess and your chances of having a positive experience is 20% gauging from social media posts. The worst TSA I’ve ever experienced, poor infrastructure and non-existent staff/volunteers to assist. J.D. Powers rates CLT as sub-average. In short, stay away if possible from this airport. First, the positive. My experience is with Sun County and Delta 3 times post-Covid. Customer Service Agents were friendly and helpful, both at check in and the gate. Sad to say it goes downhill really fast from there. I have had the good fortune to travel to many airports around the world. From the U.S., Asia, India, the South Pacific, Europe and many more. CLT provides the worst customer experience I have ever encountered. If you arrive or depart by a vehicle you will discover poor signage, woefully inadequate road infrastructure with numerous pinch points where you find yourself in the wrong lane. There has been construction at the terminal for sometime now. Again, signage is either inadequate or non-existent. Absent were any staff or volunteers to assist travelers directing them to where they needed to go. It’s clear from this first impression that governing body doesn’t prioritize a high quality customer experience. It’s NOT the construction, it’s a management, employee/staff problem. And then it gets even worse. You encounter the most rude, unprofessional, demeaning TSA and law enforcement employees I have ever come across. This assessment comes after 3 trips in/out of CLT recently. So, they just didn’t have a one-off bad day. This is a culture that’s reinforced through the hiring and training process. They need a top to bottom firing of personnel and start over. It’s an embarrassment for the fine people of Charlotte and passengers who use this airport regularly. You deserve way better. Once inside the terminal signage is at best marginal. Baggage claim is horrible. I’m not sure if airlines sub-contract this but regardless it’s terrible. Arriving mid-day recently we waited for 1hour after brakes set and chocks in on the plane before the bags started coming into the carousel! And then, god help you trying to find car rental check in. Poor signage and again zero staff or volunteers to guide you to where you want to go. We personally encountered people just like us wandering around to find it. Once we got to the car rental desk employees were helpful, friendly and accommodating. This airport is a broken mess and the overall airport culture, especially the TSA, don’t care and seem to relish in rude, demeaning and unprofessional behavior.  I see on social media that construction is blamed on poor customer satisfaction. Almost EVERY airport has construction! Absent here are adequate road infrastructure, signage, staff/ volunteer assistance that has proven successful in many airports. To top it off sub-standard TSA and law enforcement personnel.  Avoid until they get this embarrassing mess fixed.

Horrible airport. Never again. We had a 2-hour layover. We were on a flight from Europe and we just wanted to catch the next flight to get home. Passport control had two people working for TSA Pre-Check and mobile passport. We stood in line for an hour (give or take). When we finally were next to be called, they allowed another couple in ahead of us. No idea why. When we approached the CBP officer, he was incredibly rude to my husband. He's a permanent resident and instead of instructing him on how to use the machine to get his fingerprints taken, he berated him for not knowing what he was doing. Ok, the man is overworked and under paid, I get it. Up next, we arrived at the luggage carousels where no flights were listed on the boards. Finally, an announcement was made, but barely heard, as to which carousel had our luggage. There were suitcases everywhere and a dog was barking, left in the middle of the floor in an unattended crate. We managed to get 3 of 4 of our checked bags when the carousel stopped. It took maybe another 20 minutes to get someone there to fix the issue. Finally, with our luggage all together, we shoved all 4 suitcases under a rope with little to no hope that they'd arrive at our final destination. We darn near sprinted to security. My husband made it through with no problem and he proceeded to get through TSA. While I waited for security to clear me, a sudden problem with my last name sprang up. Charlotte was our 5th airport and all of a sudden, my maiden name comes up out of nowhere. I haven't used that last name in more than 20 years. It wasn't entered when we booked our flights, it's not on the boarding pass and that last name is no where in my passport. I had to go back to the ticket counter and wait behind 30 people (no complaints against the people working at that counter) to get my name corrected. I was furious! At this point, I was sure that I was going to miss the flight home but the woman at the counter informed me that they hadn't even started boarding yet. I went back to security, cleared that, went through TSA and had an expected issue with my diabetic medication, met up with my husband and we ran to the gate. But we didn't need to. After multiple gate changes and flight delays (the flight was over an hour late) and no place to sit, we finally boarded the last flight of our trip.... angry, exhausted and drenched in sweat. Never again. That airport needs to do better.

This is the most unpleasant experience I have ever had at an airport. Charlotte was our connection to and from Rome. Going was not so bad except the normal gate gate changed and crowds. But returning was unorganized and disturbing. We spent more than an hour in line for Customs clearance; then more than another hour line to get through security. We had to re-check our luggage in between flight's. We are TSA PreCheck, which did not help. Why were we required to go through Security again for a connection. Luckily, our flight was delayed because otherwise, we were close to the time for boarding. The employees we observed were loud and rude!

This is a terrible airport! Disorganized, constant delays, rude employees, the food from the chains is disgusting and of course overpriced. The only positive, the bathrooms are usually clean. It amazes me that places like this are allowed to operate.

Lots of good food and shops. Amazing love piano playing, and fun Wicked Weed food court. However the reason I’m writing is because this place is filthy! I don’t want to touch a surface! I know they’re under construction but that doesn’t account for counters and corners and floors that obviously haven’t been scrubbed in a long time. Gross! Embarrassing! The survey asks if I would recommend this airport, and my reply is mixed. First off, airport choice is pretty arbitrary as it just depends on where you’re going, and also some aspects are great. The cleanliness however is terrible.

In spite of being a large facility, Charlotte was very crowded. Finding a place to sit at our gate was impossible. The restaurants are far apart from one another so if you need something near your gate, your choices are limited. The bathrooms are messy, with broken soap dispensers and stall latches. But really, crowd management between gates needs to be better.

The gate agents and customer service agents from American Airlines are pretty much the rudest and most unprofessional staff I have ever met. They have no manners and are extremely rude to people throughout the airport. This airport also I don't think has ever had a flight take off on time, so it's extremely inconvenient to be connecting through here, I will try my best to never come through here again, as well as never fly with American Airlines. Waste of my time and money.

This is a very nice airport. Pretty clean and very manageable. My only reason for posting a review is there was no functioning water fountain, neither for drinking or filling water bottles, in the concourse. Didn't work when we arrived, still didn't when we left six days later. Drumming up money for the concession stand? Had to buy water for the trip out. Bad look for an otherwise pleasant place.

Departing Chattanooga for ATL to make a connecting flight on Monday, Dec 1, 2019. Previous Delta flight (gate # 3) was detained close to the runway for 30 minutes because the ground crew was not available. So, that delay resulted in almost missing connecting flight in Atlanta to my final destination. Once again, I have experienced another delay and unnecessary anxiety trying to make a connecting flight due to planes not being able to approach the jetway or depart from a jetway on timely basis.

CHA is a compact but efficient airport serving a metropolitan market of about 500000 residents. In the past it has suffered from proximity to major airports in Nashville and Atlanta but today 7 airlines service Chattanooga with a rather rapidly growing number of destinations. The airport is very clean with free Wi-Fi throughout and parking and security is superior. Low fare airlines have joined the legacy carriers so there is quite a nice selection of flights and fares. Sure saves time and headaches of leaving from larger airports.

CHA has the misfortune of being too close to Atlanta. Over half of Chattanooga flyers drive to Atlanta (or Nashville or Birmingham) to fly. However CHA offers competitive fares and I would guess most flights now are regional jet. The airport itself is beautiful with a large copper dome as the facility's trademark (in honor of the city's railroad heritage). CHA is a modern state-of-the-art airport and is where I choose to fly out of even though I live in the northern Atlanta 'burbs.

As a resident of Chattanooga I have used this airport on several occasions. With just 5 gates it seems to be a bit undersized for a city of 160000. However speaking from an architectural perspective it has more character than most airports I have flown through and is very clean besides. There is virtually no chance of getting lost owing to the small size and simple layout. The security checkpoint is neither intimidating nor cumbersome but the agents are thorough and will search your bags if needed. CHA recently added a daily direct flight to Dallas/Fort Worth and will soon follow up with direct service to Houston and Orlando. Other cities with direct service to and from CHA include: Atlanta Chicago Charlotte Washington (DC) Cincinnati and Memphis. CHA really is a connected airport and getting moreso all the time apparently.

One of the easiest domestic airports to figure out. Just a couple of restaurants but each one has great selection of food. They've been getting better flights and it is transitioning to more of a transit type airport. Staff is scarce but ticket counters are fast to check-in and the security line is real quick(5 minutes at the most). I now start my journey to any destination from here.

Because of the coronavirus, there are not many flights leaving the airport, and the airport was almost empty, in general, the airport was clean and quiet, customer service was good, there are not many shops for shopping, and Starbucks coffee was working

This review is for T1. Arrival is smooth and quick as there are only few passengers and many open immigration counters. There are counters for Chinese passport holders, foreign passport holders, APEC, and crew as with other airports. The signs and direction from arrival gate to the immigration, baggage, customs, and exit are all clear. A few steps from the immigration is the baggage carousel and then another few steps is the customs counters and then the exit. There are taxi bays outside the terminal building and a bust waiting area. I am not sure if the airport is connected by a train to the city proper as I did not use nor check it. On departure check-in counters a less crowded as it ws an early flight. There is a security check upon entering T1 and then another one after check-in and then a final and more detailed one after immigration. There was no long queue and so I made it quick and fast to the boarding area. Just at the back of the immigration is Gate 101 which is my boarding gate and opposite it is Starbucks. There are only few stores and restaurants. Seats are not a problem as there are many empty ones. The toilets are clean and well maintained. Directions and signs are clear and understandable. Visa and Mastecard are accepted. The terminal is old but spacious. The thermostat just needs to be adjusted as it is warm and it makes me feel uncomfortable. The wifi si not working as well. Overall, I enjoyed this airport as an airplane enthusiast as it gives me a good view for plane spotting while waiting to board.

Terminal signs and directions are not that clear, we had to ask several people and then got the right desk to check in. The toilet was dirty. We had to wait for a really long time to get through the security check. It was very slow and we almost missed our flight.

Arrived at the airport via the High Speed Railway station beneath Terminal 2 after catching a train from Chongqing. I was needing to transfer to Terminal for my international flight. There was no signage to Terminal 1 from the station. Once inside Terminal 2, there was only a small sign above an exit door on the Level 1 for the Shuttle Service from Door 9 on Level 3 with no direction in how to find Door 9. It was raining heavily and to my disgust, the shuttle service was not under the shelter of the awning but 50 metres short with a 15 minute wait. The staff of the shuttle service even suggested going back downstairs to walk 1km under the raised roadway between terminals. When the shuttle arrived, it is just a mini-bus, with limited luggage capacity and high steps into it. Worst of all, the bus stops 100m short of Terminal 1, requiring a second dash in the rain. As for check-in, it was a standard affair. The line was long through immigration with just 3 desks open with another long line for the security check. Thankfully I was able to board the VIP bus with priority boarding with little hassle.

Arrived at Chengdu on domestic flight from Shenzhen. No problems getting to town on the bus. A dew days later I had to depart on a domestic flight to Jiuzhaigou. Beware there are two terminals both a distance from each other. I got off at the wrong terminal no sign of a transfer bus so I had walk. Not much fun in the rain.

Chengdu Terminal 2 looked new and clean. Despite Air China advice to reach airport 3 hours in advance the check in counter opened only 1.5 hours before departure. Check in immigration and security were efficient and quick. The departures waiting area had nothing of interest even for Chinese travelers let alone foreign ones. There were several shops selling the same souvenirs at inflated prices. The shop girls were standing bored as no customers even entered the shops. There was one book shop selling only Chinese books and 2 restaurants serving standard bland and tasteless fare not the renowned Sichuan cuisine again at inflated prices. The waiting area for our flight was barricaded off and pax had to sit at some other gate. Absolutely nothing for international passengers and it seemed even for Chinese. Even Domestic termini are better.

XIY-CTU-AUH. Arrived from Xi'an on domestic flight in Terminal 3 which was newly opened in Spring 2012. All very clean and tidy with clear signs in Mandarin and English. Quite a long walk to Baggage Reclaim for the furthest gates but not unreasonable. Toilets clean and plentiful with both squat and regular options. For International Departures there are 2 main dining options before Check-in either KFC or local Chinese food. There are a few stores selling various local foods and some souvenirs. Check-In pretty good and Passport Control and Security all pretty smooth. No requirement to remove belts or laptops for security scanning but do enforce the 100ml liquid rules from Europe. In the International Departures no dining opportunities but a couple of coffee-shop options along with the usual array of Duty Free shops. Most departures are from one of the 11 airbridges. Announcements made in both Chinese and English. Toilets are clean.

KUL-CTU-KUL. The Shuanglin terminal is equipped with all the usual amenities. The toilets are clean the terminal is clean. The terminal also has signs in English/Chinese. Going through customs and immigration is a breeze. You can reach the city centre easily by bus or taxi however signs to the bus outside was not to clearly shown.

This is the major airport for southwest China. Flew into Chengdu from Shenzhen where it was quite a lengthy walk from the Terminal 2 gate to baggage claim. This was topped off with a further lengthy walk to the opposite end of the terminal for the taxi rank. Flying out a week later I had time to look at the airport more closely. Terminal 1 is old and definitely looking it's age. Terminal 2 was shiny and modern with three fingers that extend out. Plenty of interesting shops to keep myself amused inside the terminal and the lounges were adequately comfortable. The feeling was light and airy inside with a good view to the outside despite the extra glass screen separating arriving passengers from departing ones.

New airport and far from the city. The airport is new and big, but unfortunately, there are not many shops for shopping or eating, it is almost empty inside and outside. While travelling from it to Hong Kong I was treated badly by the passport officer. After passing the inspection and stamping my passport I found a very small Starbucks café inside the departures hall, and unfortunately the employee who works there treated me in a humiliating manner and refused to provide service to me. When I returned from my trip, the passport officer's treatment was friendly and respectful, and I did not face any problems.

For a thriving metropolitan city, the airport has many features far lower than standard features seen in many busy airports. Entrance security They lack language skills and many don't understand English. They don't understand the ticket's complexity. They are from military so you can't expect too much use of intellectual capacity to understand the time factors. I felt the guys ( twice I travelled in the last 2 weeks) spell each name silently than read the names. Why on the earth a civilian airport is managed by security services that are part of military Ticket counter No clear signs were posted in some places. Seems too many people are working yet very slow process. Immigration was flawless to me both times Security Screening The worst set up and poorly trained people manning the section. Screeners cannot identify the objects through X-ray machine and even after your spread out most stuffs out of the bag, they will search the bag for non existing objects. Literally you have to empty your bag into tray ( very likely you will loose something and high Chance someone may pick some items from your tray . ( Totally a third world county screening).. One lounge only for all airlines, average standards Boarding sequence non existent to small airplane like Indigo. Over all my ratings would be 2/10 ,

On arrival into the airport, there are notices for foreigners to complete the Arrival Card however there were no Arrival Cards arrival for me to complete. I proceeded to the main immigration desk on the advice from a staff member, that perhaps I didn't need one. Which seemed confusing as I am not a national of India and in previous experience, would need the card. On arrival at the desk - for my first time in India - the Immigration Officer slammed my passport down and pointed at a small office and yelled saying 'Go there fill in the card and then come back'. I went to the office and said Good Morning to the two seated inside the office and asked for the card and they practically threw it at me. If the airport was organised, they would of had the cards already presented for people on arrival. In addition, I was told I had to wait for another traveller to finish with the only one pen they had because there are no others. The other traveller and their family also agreed the system was poor. Baggage claim was as expected and no problems to report here besides the fact you get hassled to show you luggage tag to some random person checking the luggage tags. How does one person check all of the tags of people getting their luggage? The main concern is that this is being positioned as as International Airport and there is no WiFi available in the building unless you go the Airport Lounge which includes a cost. I was unable to purchase a sim-card on arrivals and there is no facility that provides one. The taxi system is ridiculous people yelling at you outside. Please book a car with your hotel and spend the money. If you really want a taxi, get an uber. As for the Departure's section, there are no tvs or screens, no comfortable seating, no coffee shops, no food outlets or anything to do for leisure or entertainment and people inside are not helpful. If you have a lay over do not go inside and waste your time. You can only enter the airport for the day you are travelling and they tell you once you go inside the airport you cannot leave. So if you don't have any stable internet connection you are stuck. The toilets were maintained but they are not clean. Staff pushing around a mop pushing the dust from one corner to another, and sitting on the floor under shelves. Why are staff sitting on the floor when there are travellers from all over the world coming here? There are hundreds of people walking around with lanyards on that aren't doing anything productive. Some staff members who are not wearing a uniform so not easily identifiable. I watched people sitting at the 'May I help you Desk' a tiny information desk on their phones having chats with their friends not engaged in providing a full service to people approaching the desk for help. Another member of the 'May I help you Desk' team was napping on the chair next to it? Sleeping at work? Post Immigration where they tell you there is WiFi there is none available. Do not believe them. The duty free was lack lustre, and the food outlets the same. I am appalled by the lack of customer care, service and support for International Travellers. The whole experience in this airport was abysmal. I would not recommend this airport and feel it is important to manage other people's expectations.

My recent experience at this airport was frustrating and highlighted a severe lack of planning and maintenance, particularly in the international arrivals section. Despite having numerous immigration counters, less than 30% were staffed. This resulted in long, unnecessary queues, with travelers left waiting while the majority of counters remained empty. The air conditioning system was either ineffective or nonexistent. Passengers, already fatigued from travel, were left sweating in the stifling heat while standing in line—a basic comfort that any international airport should provide. Bottleneck at Hand Baggage Screening: After clearing immigration, the ordeal continued. With only one hand baggage screening machine operational, travelers faced an additional 20-minute delay. This level of inefficiency is inexcusable. Customs officers use white chalk to mark bags for random checks, which is not only outdated but also damages the appearance and material of luggage. This approach is disrespectful to passengers who expect their belongings to be handled with care. Many trolleys were in poor condition, with misaligned wheels requiring significant effort to push. This made an already unpleasant experience even worse for those managing heavy luggage. Passengers must walk a considerable distance from the arrivals terminal to reach the taxi stand. While there are assistants available to help with baggage, many of them demand tips despite claiming the service is free—a practice that reflects poorly on the airport's management. To top it all off, the airport offers limited direct connections, especially to Europe, making it an unattractive hub for international travelers. Overall, the airport fails to meet even the basic standards expected of an international gateway. The inefficiencies, poor facilities, and lack of passenger care make this one of the worst arrival experiences I have had. Serious improvements are needed to elevate it to acceptable global standards.

I had the unfortunate experience of transiting through Chennai International Airport, and it was one of the worst travel experiences I've ever had. From the moment I arrived, I felt harassed and mistreated. The tax officers were relentless, targeting everyone in a way that felt invasive and unnecessary. The immigration process was equally frustrating, with long delays and rude officials. The lack of basic amenities like WiFi and food options made the experience even worse. You're confined to a small, cramped area with no place to rest or sleep, making it feel more like a jail than an airport. For anyone considering a layover in Chennai, I strongly advise against it. The poor conditions and treatment are not worth the stress. Choose another airport if you can.

We had a very pleasant and satisfactory experience on April 28th Sunday departure. The facilities are international standards. The rest rooms were neat and clean. One Ms Renuka Devi staff in the rest room kept asking whether all okay and she made sure that i felt comfortable and happy. We appreciate all the staff and the officers whole heartedly.

I hope I never, ever have to step foot in Chennai Airport again! What a complete disaster of a place this is, utterly hateful and stressful experience from start to finish! Firstly to gain access to the terminal, you have to get past rude, officious security guards posted at each entrance. They demand to see your passport and a paper print out of the ticket, an electronic version or boarding pass will not do. After much pleading and intervention of Sri Lankan airline staff, they agreed to accept the electronic version of our ticket as proof. Twice we had to go through this as obviously we had no access to a printer being foreign tourists and nowhere did we get a warning this was a requirement until we checked in. What century are they living in when they refuse to accept an electronic ticket/boarding pass? Next the staff at security are possibly the rudest anywhere in the world. Horrid, miserable, angry woman pulled my carry-on aside for examination and just bellowed 'take, take it, take it, take it!' without even bothering to look at the contents. Absolutely disgusting attitude! Why pull it aside if she had no intention of even looking at it? It seemed like the only motivation was to pick a fight. Add to this.... Toilets are the filthiest I have ever seen with excrement all over seats, urine on floor etc. No Wi-Fi whatsoever, paid or otherwise as you need an Indian Mobile number to access it. Shops, poor as they are, are all unbelievably expensive and overpriced, twice as expensive as at Zurich Airport in Switzerland. Needless to say they were all empty of customers. The international terminal 2 departures, consists of vast areas of barren space with a few dirty looking seats dotted around, generally depressing and miserable looking. At arrivals, the border staff are as thick as mince. They kept looking at my expired visa from a previous visit 5 years ago, rather than the current one, even when I pointed it out to them. As such they claimed I didn't have a visa until a senior person intervened and 'found' the correct visa, the one I showed them multiple times. Once you leave the airport expect to be accosted by thousands of taxi drivers trying to scam you into paying £20 to the centre of Chennai. Best arrange a hotel pick up before leaving! We would have flown direct to Colombo if we had known how bad Chennai Airport was, horrible place and the staff are completely devoid of humanity. I feel lucky to have got through the place alive quite honestly, worst airport in the world!

The newly built international airport is dirty, the finish is poor, the cleaning staff are on their mobile phones or chatting, the toilets are dirty, the security is slow and the is manned by disinterested personnel. Overall it is probably the worst airport I have visited in the last 5 years. I hear there are plans to build another airport.

Came from DEL on domestic and departed to FRA from international terminal. Connectivity between terminals is a big pain area, specially if one has luggage to push around. The travellators don't allow for trolleys to go on them, walking all the way is the only option available. Further, international terminal is nothing but a mess and disarray. Gates are scattered far and in between. Too few food options and so called food court is full of pigeons fluttering around. Absolute mismanagement, small domestic terminals are better managed than this.

The worst experience with transfer I ever had. Arrived to T4 from Sri Lanka expected to transit out with Lufthansa with unfortunate layover of 10h. I was left 3.5h sitting in corridor in front of security check with explanation that I have to wait LU staff that will not come earlier the in couple of hours to pass me through despite I had valid boarding pass for my next flight! Moreover in Business class nobody cared at all no information and they even taken my passport for whole this time. Once this nightmare was over I found that behind security its even worse, it looks like after some natural disaster, all shops closed halfway destroyed, terrible lounge with one toilet in sanitary condition that would not allow to enter, never ever would take any transit through this nightmare, god bless I did not travel with kids this time

Very Poor Maintenance of toilets and Cleanliness. The airport didn't even deserve to a domestic arrival. Foreign nationals actually hesitate to step into restrooms or touch the walls. The Air conditioning is also so low and baggage receiving time is taking minimum of 1.5 hours. In such a case Tamilnadu can never promote tourism having so much of cultural spots like old temples and architecture. The toilets directions had not symbols if they are not able to read English they cannot go to the restrooms. The international standards are not maintained anywhere including the people communication skills.

I am incredibly grateful for the staff at Chiang Mai airport! I left my phone in my grab - unable to get in touch with grab due to my phone being in my grab car and details being on the app on my phone so I immediately went to the staff in line.
