She took me to the tourist police by exit number 6 in the international departure hall. They took details such as where I got the grab from, my phone number, the car colour (i couldnt remember the license plate number!). In less than 10 minutes they were able to get in touch with the car driver and I got my phone in the next 5 minutes after that!!!! Thank you so much to the tourist police staff on shift at 10am on 16 Jan 2025. I can't remember the other staff's name that brought me to the tourist police, but i took a photo with her. I wish them all the best and am so grateful for their willingness to help.

The airport is clean and not large. Signposts are clear. Passengers can get around easily. Employees are friendly and helpful. Security check is efficient. The prices charged at food outlets are reasonable.

Probably the most inefficient and waste of time and money with double security screening. Before entering the terminal you are required to screen both check-in and carry on luggage and backpacks. Taking out laptops/tables and mobile phones as if you are about to board the plane. Then after getting your boarding pass you have to go through another security screening exactly like the first one when entering the terminal. Don’t really understand the reason the need for the first security check if they have the exact same one before boarding.

Worst airport and employees ever! Not one person working here spoke to me. Just hand motions that I’m apparently supposed to understand. My friend and I were the only two people in line to check in, and noticed the service counter woman mix up our boarding passes and luggage tags. She informed us of the mix up, and when I told her that was ridiculous and to please fix the tags - she acted as though it was an inconvenience to do her job correctly. Thank goodness she didn’t have a full line of people behind us to screw their stuff up too! Not one person we interacted with at this airport was friendly, helpful, or competent. Avoid this airport at all costs if you can.

Worst airport ever. Arrived for a 1.20pm flight to Hanoi. Have flown domestically out of Chiang Mai a dozen times. Assumed there would be a similar level of food outlets in international as domestic. There is nothing. You can buy 2 minute noodles and a soft drink. No restaurant, no fast food, no bar. Travelling with a hungry, cranky child.

The most unprofessional, inadequate and arbitrary luggage check ever. We were shocked about the way we (and our belongings) were treated when we entered the airport for the first (and overall pointless) check-up. They were focused on batteries and power banks that they unpacked aggressively my whole luggage which I've put before neatly in my bag. I asked them to handle at least a bag with some glass bottles containing my medicine with care but I just got ignored. Then they scanned every bag and some single items they took out of my bag again. They just threw my belongings rudely in a tray. It took my partner and me quite a while to sort this mess out. Thankfully we weren't in a rush. As a criminologist, I'm aware of certain (none-EU) security standards but this action was completely inappropriate and a waste of time. Especially as I could have brought easily a bottle of nitroglycerin with me - no one would have known. Amateurs! Furthermore, food and drinks are even for an airport overpriced. They charged more for a coffee than in London - ridiculous!

Chaotic, lack of facilities and no departure board all make for a less than rewarding experience. Incomprehensible announcements and general chaos. No soap in toilets. No ATM or decent food - avoid this airport if you can.

Left Chiang Mai for Bangkok. All bags are security screened prior to entering the airport which meant a bit of a line outside in the sun. I get the security behind it but it was a pain in the butt. There was a lot of space at the check in counter and security moved well. We had all of our water taken away at security but there is filtered water near the departure gates. There is not a lot of food options after security. A few coffee shops and news stands. Boarding area was not too big for the number of passengers going through the area.

Upon arrival in Chiang Mai, we had to take the bus to the terminal, which thankfully was a quick trip. Customs was fast and the baggage claim was easy. Even as a small airport, there were friendly and helpful employees. It was easy to get around, especially finding taxis. I would prefer Chiang Mai over Bangkok airport, and I will continue to go to this airport.

This is the worst airport I have ever visited - and I have visited many. All flights were cancelled on New Year's Eve - yet foreigners were not contacted to inform of the cancellations of their flights. Both the airlines and airport continued to show flights scheduled long after the airport had been closed (see attached). There were no airline staff in the airport and the information staff were beyond useless, leaving people stranded in the airport overnight, many losing a lot of money on connecting flights. The information staff refused to help and even refused to let people use the phones. We were not offered so much as a glass of water. People from Germany, the USA, the UK were simply told "come back tomorrow". When I asked to speak to a manager, a very rude and unpleasant female member of staff on the information desk told me: "You can speak to the police" and called airport security police. Meanwhile the security personnel were lying about on the floor and across seats. Until this point we have received no compensation for the cancelled flights, nor any apology. Since I have now discovered that Chiang Mai airport frequently closes at times of celebration, citing the reason that planes cannot take off when there are fireworks/lanterns, I strongly suggest you do not go there. They have no respect for foreigners, and are simply interested in taking our cash.

What a great little airport! Friendly staff (in all areas) and, in my opinion, unique system (to me anyway) of scanning the hold luggage whilst you're with it before its loaded onto the aircraft. Domestic departure lounge is small but plenty of seating available.

Flew domestic leg to Bangkok. This is a small regional airport that has become busier but is still under used. It is mainly on the ground floor with 1st floor for International Departures via the Air Bridges. Check-in desks are located at the extreme left end and it can get a little busy if more than 2 flights are operating at the same time. There is a large selection of shops and cafes in the main concourse as there is very little beyond Security. The arrivals is at the opposite end of the ground floor with a separate one for the small number of international flights. Security was very quick, there are two scanners but only 1 in use. There are 3 Departure gates in the Domestic area that lead out to bus or walk on the tarmac. Alternatively there are steps up to the Airbridge if the plane is using one. It was a pleasant experience with free WiFi (the only snag was you needed access to your Emails in order to get the Password to access the free WiFi).

Visited for Songkran this year. Lovely to be met by Thai dancers in traditional outfits. That's where the satisfaction ended. My phone credit had run out. There is nowhere available in the terminal to purchase a top-up. I was being picked up and could not contact my driver. "Information services" suggested I take a taxi into city buy a top-up at 7/11 then come back to airport. How ludicrous? No offer of using the phone. told to try public phone. Refused to give me change of baht 1000 note as that was all I had. No customer service whatsoever.

Very nice small airport easy check in with friendly staff. Plenty of seating in the airport with small selection of shops and restaurants and bars. Parking for cars very close to terminal and with plenty of spaces. Easy access to main roads when you leave the airport. Baggage reclaim very quick. A pleasure to arrive at this airport.

TSA Precheck staff were beyond rude. My husbands pen went missing. I had to put my wallet, by itself, through the security belt. Oh, and they made me take off my boots too. The food options had poor reviews, so we went to the bistro that had the highest reviews. $20 hamburger and additional $2 for fries. I have had better fast food burgers. Gate had way too many seats for the volume of passengers. I will fly to Ohare next time.

I have been flying in and out of Midway for 30 years. I am writing a review about ground transportation. I have always used Midway's parking for almost every trip made, tonight June 21st is the last time. The nice and considerate bus drivers have been traded in for aggressive, rude tip hustlers who need to handle everyone's bag. I fly frequently and this is 3rd or 4th time with this aggressive behavior by drivers and I'm done with it. On to the park n fly for me next time.

How does a modern airport not have shops open when flights are departing? Ever since covid, Midway has been a 3rd-rate airport with almost no options for food. The vending machines (I can attest to this) do not work and every shop doesn’t open until 5 am. Flights are already departing and there is not a single open shop to even buy water. And again, the vending machines don’t operate. My home airport is Austin and a few shops are required  to be open prior to the first flight departing. What is wrong with Midway?

I transit this airport 3 times in one month for my business trip. Getting food is a big challenge. I have seen so many restaurants are closed by 7 or 8 pm. even airports and flights are operating till very late. The second time I been to 5 different restaurants and all had bad attitudes. They are out of items. And if you are vegetarian then it's worst. They don't want to help you make anything vegetarian or even salad. Customer service is not good in those restaurants. Airport authorities need to ask those restaurants to open late and have more food.

A person at a security checkpoint for TSA pre-check told me that my disabled daughter could not go through because she wasn’t prechecked. I explained I didn’t have time to get that for her as she hasn’t travelled in years. She said too bad she’s over 18 she has to go through the regular line. I explained that she is legally disabled and we can’t be separated. She insisted. That’s the rules. I was annoyed that she was embarrassing my daughter like that. I said I am using a walker because I have severe back pain. I can’t go stand in those lines. That’s why I have a walker. She said just go over there and cut in the line. So we have to walk against the flow of people to another station. We get there and they’re like what are you doing? I pointed to the other agent and said she told me to come over here and I can’t stand in the line. Luckily they didn’t argue. The rude attitude instead of understanding treatment is inexcusable!

Super overpriced items in every kiosk. I know the rule is "whatever the market will bear, but the prices at this airport are downright ridiculous. Expect LOTS of attitude from the bored, unfriendly staff.

Awful airport for any type of layover or any restaurant. They tried to “update” Midway a few years back, removing staple restaurants like Harry Carey’s, Potbelly, and even McDonalds. Now, multiple restaurants including Vienna Beef, Cafe Espresso, Bill Goat Tavern, PorkChop, among others, all closed. Weekends and weekdays. Plus, Dunkin’ Donuts, only hot coffee. Zero variety. Employees are angry and overworked. Restaurant Bistro, which replaced a few of the old restaurants is awful. Midway has gone way downhill. Hate it here.

Generally a good airport, but considering the covid, this place is an operational mess! The new security and system for wheelchairs is at a very low level. Customers with ADA accessibility is third-class, they simply are not equipped to handle these travellers. Lines are not clearly marked and wheelchair patrons are left to figure it out on their own. Security is mismanaged, no room for the chair itself. No seating once you get through security to get reset after going through the lines. Additionally, bathrooms are a disaster, no working soap during covid? Who is in charge of operations at Midway, they are not doing the job! No one is cleaning or sanitizing anywhere! Be aware, this management doesn't care, they make it look good in the photos, but actually come here and try to be safe, it's nearly impossible. Why don't the touchless hand sanitizer and towel machines work? Looks like cheap equipment to me, they are either empty or the sensors are poor. Very disappointing and wish Midway would be more serious about being clean, stay away if possible or try O'Hare.

What a dump. Cramped seating areas, bad/slow food, narrow concourse, few 'walking' escalators, tiny bathrooms, short runways that necessitate abrupt, rough landings, very few (and ludicrously small) flight update boards - these are just a few bullet points on a lengthy list, which comprehensively and easily condemns Midway as the worst major airport in the United States. This place is a complete dump, and since Southwest essentially owns the joint, the blame lies squarely on their corporate shoulders. A renovation will not fix this mess - it's time to condemn and demolish Midway.

I had the best custermer experience at Midway airport. I had just gone through the TSA checkpoint when I realized I had left my work binder at the seating area on the way in. I was panicking and I asked a manager in TSA who took his time to walk me back though security and hunted down where I last saw it. There was a gentleman who told us that he saw another member of security take it to baggage claim. He went above and beyond to find the person who took it there and luckily it was descovered. Him and another member were able to get it back to me and I was in much relief. He was then able to help me get back though security so I could make my flight on time. I have never had such great customer service at any other airport.

Terminal 5.  Seriously, turn off the speaker system, unless at one specific gate. Why call out names /departures all the time? Get into the game. People get stress and do Not hear/bother about the messages. And you can spend time and money on other things. Most usb/receptables are broken. Why have only 5 personal screeners in the international security, this is far below par. And this is the bottleneck. Work on it. There are 2 very uncosy and noisy bars.

We arrived from Jamaica here as a layover (2 and a half hour lay over). First the workers, were just rude and yelling. Then we stayed in immigration line for over 2 hours, which sealed the deal on a missed flight. Then it was so difficult to navigate where to go. They were not organized nor did they seem to care that so many purple missed their flights.

TSA employees were very rude. Openly complaining about travelers. Part of what they said was "if we had a giant neon sign, they still wouldn't get it." Then, I have a medically implanted device, so I showed my card. He kept treating me like I was stupid, saying things like did you leave things in your pockets? You probably have a belt on etc. Instead of recognizing the implant card he made me remove shoes and recheck pockets and look for a belt that was never there. Very rude. The woman at the baggage scan was involved in complaining about the people coming through as well.
Security checkpoint staff: Unfriendly, not helpful, and very rude. Traveling can be overwhelming, and having employees that can so easily and audaciously be so rude is disconcerting.

This is easily the worst airport in the country.  I have a 27 minute flight to Grand Rapids and spend more time sitting in a massive line of airplanes barely moving because they don’t know how to get their flights out on time. Such a terrible experience and it’s not just a one time thing. This happens every single time you come to O’Hare. Never again.
Super arrogant and not helpful security staff. Cannot imagine going through security check not being able to understand english. The staff I encountered was the worst person ever!

Terrible experience at this airport! The labeling of the airport transit system is totally confusing. The train stations are labeled 1,3,4,5. What happened to No. 2? Then there is another station after 5 but not labeled with a name! That’s the station we needed to get to but it looked like it was Station 5! Also the parking lots should have different naming system from the terminals. We parked in G lot. But G is also one of the terminals! When riding the train, we thought we should get off at station 4 where G terminal is but actually we needed to get off at the last station, the one with no name! The design of the naming system is a mess!

We found one particular member of ground staff at the automatic check in extremely helpful & friendly as we were having difficulty using it.. Also for my first time I needed wheelchair assistance ( twisted knee). These staff also were helpful thro security and to the gate. Most customers are quick to complain but slow to compliment so I wanted to give credit where it was due!

As a lifelong Chicagoan, I was embarrassed at the lack of cleanliness outside the terminals at O'Hare. Please power wash the sidewalks and paint structures. Gum is stuck all over the sidewalk and its filthy. Mayor Daley would never have put up with this!  I wish I had taken photos.

I’m an international student and I had to stop at Chicago airport to get a flight to LAX and my mom was with me. We needed to recheck in our bags and I mistakenly went to the wrong room. Since I was the only one who spoke the language I went to an old lady to ask her where I could recheck in my bags and then she questioned me and started to scream at me and my mom who doesn’t know the language. Then we went back in and checked our bags again. After I left I went to apologize to her and she told me to “go and learn”! Like I get it that I made a mistake but that does not justify her behavior towards me and my mom

Checked in, sent through passport control no issue. Get to the gate to board and questioned about my residency and how to prove it. E-visa is all linked to my passport now for the UK and a friend with dual citizenship had to “prove” their status. An active e-visa wasn’t accepted but an expired BRP from 2 visas ago was. Made to feel like I was doing the wrong thing when having been to 66 countries I’ve never been questioned like this. If travelling through here - be prepared for appalling treatment

Unprofessional and arrogant staff at the check in. No customer service at this airport. No one helps you if you have a problem. Answering customer's questions with "I don't know", shrugging their shoulders or rolling their eyes with the meaning "what else do you want from me".

The worst customer service I have ever seen. The officer controlling the passports was extremely rude. She had her back towards the line of people, talking with a coworker, then she addressed travelers in a very rude and totally inappropriate manner, for not coming close to her window. Other passengers show a lack of manners and respect also. Everybody is rude to each other. Sorry to say it was the first and probably last time when I used Chișinău airport.

Clean airport, but this is not a priority. The most important thing is customer care, which here in Moldova is in last place unfortunately. I have just had the worst experience going through customs and the personnel were extremely rude. The rudest I've ever seen and I have travelled to over 40 countries. One says don't take your shoes off, the other sends you back to take them off. Why aren't they on the same page? When mentioning that to the guy, he answered rudely and angrily back. Shame!

Chisinau airport is the only international airport of Moldova and sometimes seems to be out of proportion with the growing traffic. But anyway, despite its small size, after the latest restructuration, it became a very efficient and easy to fly from. The ground staff are very productive and manages the traffic with a great dexterity. The number of shops and food choices remains low, but it's not really an airport of transit. The main flaw of Chisinau airport is access to and from the airport, without real shuttle service provided. There is a minibus (marshrutka) route to the railway station, but it doesn't service all night long and you often need to require a taxi (very cheap). Airport is very clean, and staff is very professional.

Chisinau Airport is going thru a massive renovation and expansion. However it is a clean, bright and vibrant airport, with new dining areas, upgraded infrastructure and trained staff. There are regular mini busses linking airport with city, an official taxi service and a lot of "unofficial" taxis (random private individuals offering taxi service). There used to be A bus express line, but I am not sure if it still in service. In the common area there are some restaurants and other airport services. The passport control and security is working fast and efficient. There is a big duty free shop with usual goods - tobacco, alcohol, cosmetics, etc. On the first floor (stairs from the duty free shop) there is a nice cafeteria - Fly Away with good food and decent prices. There is also a nice playground for kids. The waiting area is renovated - looks green and great. Very comfortable chairs, plugs and USB pots for charging your devices and 4 hours limited free wiki. It's a small cosy airport in a continuous development and expansion.

A pleasant experience. The prices are much better be it food or duty-free and the atmosphere is much more relaxed with friendly check-in staff and passport control agents. No shouting in Russian and no high-handed treatment of foreigners. Departures lounge can get crowded at peak times though and the catering options are nothing to write home about.

I was traveling with my family having 2 small kids. Pros: less traffic, since many don't transit. Climate is good. Cons: no proper food outlet, only snacks; airlines doesn't provide any food for long transit. For wifi you need that country cell number.

This is a so-so International and Domestic Airport. I have used the International section 3 times in the past 2 yrs. Firstly Regent Airways is always late opening their lines for international flights to Bangkok and you have to rush. Upstairs you have the customs and security. Not too bad, can be slow sometimes but otherwise you get through. There are no shops and for Business Class passengers there is no lounge facility, if there is it is never open. On arrival it can also be a quick check through security, slow computers etc but staff are nice in the foreign passport line. Bags are quick but no priority bags first, all come at once and then you have to join the queue to put your baggage through a screening area to exit the airport. No buses or transport available unless you have arrange pick up from your hotel. But there is no problem with the airport.

Basically a well designed terminal that requires upgrading. Immigration and visa on arrival procedures are quick as foreign passport holders go to separate counters both for arrival and departure. Luggage delivery is fast but then you will have to queue for at least 30 minutes as every piece of luggage has to go through the only screening machine in the customs hall. No taxi or airport shuttle is available and you will have to rely on touts or on military staff (very friendly) to help you find a vehicle to take you to town unless you have prearranged transport with your hotel. Departure hall is not airconditionned and was infested by mosquitoes. 3 out of 4 duty free shops were closed and the single airline lounge has been closed for a long time. One positive point: all areas including toilets are kept very clean.

Nice international terminal but domestic isn't very spacious. There is a snack bar and a duty free shop in the international terminal and nothing in domestic. On way in the customs is fast longest wait I've had is 30 min. Satisfactory airport but would not want a long layover here.

Airport is a 20 km (9 miles) scenic river-side drive south of Chittagong City Center reachable by taxi or car. No local hotels or serious restaurants available within the vicinity. There are snacks and confections available in a couple of spots on the grounds side within the terminal. Renovated recently the interior is unusually modern and comfortable for a regional airport in a small country like this. The new aero-bridges serve the airport well and efficient and courteous staff make it easy to find one's way through the facility. Toilets are fair to middling but that's expected. Overall not bad at all!

It was the most favorite airport. I mean was and I am writing about terminal 3. But today I am waiting for my flight which departs at H - gates. and there is no place to eat at all! Just Starbucks and Chinese cafe. Before I used to eat and wait for my flight in Burger King, but just a half month later suddenly fence appeared! So there is no food in Starbucks write now, no shops with products and I realize that I still need to wait 2 hours my flight and then spend 9hours in the plane. Why just one month ago there wasn’t a fence and now people can’t eat anything except Starbucks waiting for a flight from H and G gates?? And I am sure many flights are more than 5hours. Now it’s like a prison - no place to go in a huge airport

My incoming flight by West Air was arriving to Terminal 2 at night, and my onward international flight was from Terminal 3 several hours later in the morning. It was easy to find the transit bus stop (there were a few taxi drivers offering their services at the arrival hall, but they weren't annoying as long as they saw I'm uninterested), and, despite my worries, the bus was operating at night and my wait time was no longer than 10 minutes. On the way, the bus stopped a few times to pick up and drop off mostly airport staff in a few places, including the now-disused old Terminal 1, but it took no more than 20 minutes to get to Terminal 3. Terminal 3 is very modern, but looks a bit empty except the departure floor where there are quite many shops (many of which started to open after 6am) and restaurants. I didn't have time to get out to the city at Chongqing, so I picked up some food souvenirs at Mannings supermarket as well as another smaller shop - the prices, while possibly higher than in the city, didn't seem to be overly so. The 7-eleven has some inexpensive foods as well. Wi-Fi is free, doesn't take much hassle to log in, and is fast enough. Check in desks look unusual with those futuristic large machines where all the baggage goes in place of traditional rubber belts. Otherwise, the check in and security procedures were as usual. Didn't have too much time to explore the airside, but it looks a bit empty too.

Chongqing Airport is one of the biggest in Southwest China. The new terminal 3 is just 1km away from the old terminal 2, and is well connected by metro line 10. The airport terminal is very spacious and well designed that incorporates with many new technologies. Mine was a direct flight by Hainan Airline to JFK. The departure area has all sort of restaurants and shops, which makes the last minute shopping possible. Facilities are very clean and well put. My only concern is the long waiting time at the border control.

I was flying alone to Chongqing. The booking process was easy, but I left my camera on the plane. I felt anxious. When I came to the transfer counter and told them the situation the staff were so kind. They made some calls and directed me to the lost and found centre when I found my camera.

Arrived early for my morning flight. Check-in was easy enough but then made a mistake at the security checkpoint. They have introduced Female Only lines, which I think is a nice touch, so I had to change to a male queue. This airport is very thorough and stricter than most, in regards to security, requiring me to surrender a battery pack due to the label sticker worn away and not able to prove the size of the device is under 10,000Mah. My flight is leaving from pier A in terminal 2, so I decided to go down the escalator at the end of the pier and have a McDonalds breakfast. However I was surprised when the staff there claimed that their breakfast menu was not available, it was 8.30am. However I stuck to my choice of a Bacon and Egg McMuffin until they relented and finally made it. They were being lazy in only wishing to serve regular burgers all day. The bonus was ability to order and receive a Flat White coffee made with real fresh milk, not UHT, from the attached McCafe. Upon ascending the escalator, it was almost time for my plane to board, which was handled surprisingly well, with anyone trying to push into the line being rejected by airport staff. Upon my return to CKG, I arrived at pier B and was able to collect my bags and be out of the terminal in about 10 minutes, from the gate to being onboard the monorail into the city. Although this will change with the opening of Terminal 3A soon.

Flew domestically into Chongqing on Sichuan Airlines and for some reason our aerobridge was at the small International Terminal 1. Requiring us to walk 100m around the edge of the terminal concourse and walk down stairs to a shuttle bus to carry Terminal 2 which being winter was bitterly cold especially with the doors opened while the bus waited for a full load. Once inside the proper domestic terminal it was pretty straight forward and standard routine. Once excellent feature was a lady handing out bi-lingual cards listing taxi fare prices to over a dozen destinations around the city to discourage touting and rip offs. For the return I found out the single domestic Terminal 2 is actually split into 3 separate halls A B and C. If you flight is leaving through hall C you can not enter via A or B security points. This also means you are technically shut off from the shops and facilities in the other sections too such as the McDonalds in hall A. However you are able to walk downstairs to the Arrivals level and use the transfer signage to direct you to the other areas making the segregation of the terminal areas pointless. Lastly with the security it was the only place I was asked to take my boots off beyond the X-Ray machine which all passengers were made to do. However with only one seat it meant a longer wait as you could not progress until the person in front had taken off their boots was examined and then re-laced them.

Landed at the newer of the two terminals. Baggage collection was fast and was able to buy a phone card easily on the lower Arrivals level but telephones were only on the upper Departures level. Security was tight with baggage tags checked by airport staff. No illegal taxi touts hounding you and bus into the city was quick and easy. On departing the airline waiting areas were large and comfortable. The food in some places was cheap very cheap. Same as supermarket price for bottle of Pepsi. Had a gate change but was handled quickly and easily. Efforts were made to keep me informed despite being the only foreigner on my flight. New monorail will soon open from airport to city. Airport taxi prices are not too expensive but be prepared for a wild and crazy ride.

The airport has room for improvement particularly around security. Long delays and the attitude of one of the officers was so rude it was almost comical. Think Mr McKay out of the 70s UK TV sitcom ‘porridge’ and you get the picture. Give them a uniform.

Once you have completed check in at the airport - the international departures should also be open - very bad organisation. Instead of having queues of passengers waiting to go thru it would be seamless to have them go through straight away. Perhaps the coordination between check in / airlines/ international departures needs to be sorted - easy just talk to each other. Or perhaps management need to learn a out time management. Without passengers travelling no one would be employed. Most other international airports do and have this all sorted except CHC.

The airport is a complete disgrace, with rude security staff. They don’t even have enough seats at terminals which leaves half the flight to have to sit on the floor. Apart from the terrible service and lack of seats the wait time for boarding is horrible as well. This airport is a complete disgrace to Christchurch and the whole of New Zealand, I highly do not recommend!

After being stuck for cancelled flight for at least 12 hours in this airport, I could not be more disappointed by the food! Only one stand who offers sushi had descent, healthy food. Everywhere else it was the most disgusting food every where: super sweet breakfast choice, and the only “restaurant“ offers the most unhealthy food I ever had. I thought I was in the middle of nowhere in the US. Come on! Christchurch you can do better! And to add to the poor food there is not one quiet, resting area for people who got bumped very early in the morning and wish to take a rest before they next flights. Only the wealthy one have access to a lounge! What a shame!

A quick back story, my wife and myself were moving to Spain, we had previously contacted both Airlines (Qatar and Air NZ) and had been confirmed by Air NZ that they would honor the luggage requirements set out by Qatar Airways. Our flight was 1298 on Thursday 26th of August departing at 14.00 from Christchurch to Auckland. Our connecting flight was with Qatar who obviously have different hand luggage requirements than Air NZ. However as we were trying to get through security and to note "we were the only ones passing through security". The male Aviation Security officer who was supposed to screen our bags refused to let us screen our bags stating we could only take 1 piece of luggage onto the aircraft. We explained that we were actually traveling internationally and had already called and confirmed with Qatar Airways that our carry on was acceptable however he insisted that he was unable to screen our bags as it wasn't the acceptable carry on allowance for the Air NZ flight. He stated we would have to check in our hand luggage so we returned downstairs by which time the flight was already closed and we were told by Air NZ staff it was ok to take our hand luggage and to board the plane. Upon returning to Av Sec, another Air NZ service agent who saw us talking with the agent who had checked us in had followed us up to the Aviation Security and as the Av Sec officer again began berating us and firmly insisting that we must leave behind all hand luggage with the exception of a laptop the Air NZ service agent began to join in stating "Either you leave everything except your laptop behind or you are going to miss your flight". Even with my pregnant wife beginning to cry this continued on with being pressured to leave behind our hand luggage except a laptop each and my wife's wedding dress with the Av Sec officer continuing to raise his voice and at one point even throwing plastic security tray towards me and in a raised and angry tone stating "Don't you know laptops have to be placed inside the trays!". After some minutes of this the Air NZ service agent realized that such actions of herself and the Av Sec officer we beginning to escalate too much and reminded the Av Sec officer that he wasn't allowed to be throwing the plastic security trays around and to be careful in front of the other staff. At this point after throwing out some items from our carry on we were finally allowed to place our carry on luggage through security.

Could security please provide booties for those who have to remove shoes. The floor at Christchurch was covered in food and in general it is a health hazard to have to put dirty feet into clean shoes after having clean socks walk over what everyone has walked in. It is just gross and unsanitary.
Super long queues for passport controls and goods to declare check point. Hundreds of passengers but only 3 officers. Worst airport in Australasia!
Disgraceful toilet facilities, very long queues for both male and female. In male toilets only 3 urinals and 2 stools available for the hundreds of people there.

Very surprised at the length of queues for security checks and passport control, both arriving and departing. In these days of modern airports it seems that Christchurch is behind the times, and certainly falls short of what you expect. Staff very pleasant, but long queues add a lot of stress to the airport experience and I would probably avoid flying into Christchurch again until this has been addressed. Not sure if this is standard for NZ airports though.

Probably one of the worst airports I have seen in New Zealand. Security screening staff was very rude. Seating in a hall and waiting rooms is inadequate to the number of people traveling. My suggestion: avoid like the plague.

A very small airport more like an airstrip. 3 airlines fly there I think: Silkair Air Pacific & National Jets. Departure and Arrival Halls are in the same building and passengers disembark and embark the plane via the stairs and tarmac. For arrival customs clearance procedures are simple fuss-free and then you wait in line to collect your baggage(s) as they are being towed in. There is a large car park outside the Arrival Hall where you can also make arrangements to loan your transport while on the island through a couple of car agencies. There is a cafe and a small gift shop inside the Departure Hall. Checking-in is done manually. The Visitor Centre may have personnel at the airport running surveys collecting opinions and comments with regard to your stay.

Me and a few friends flew to the Dominican Republic in August 2019 and the experience upon arrival was outstanding. The immigration service was fast and most shops where open. The staff help us with our bags and had us out in no time. On our way back it was the same very friendly staff, no delays, food was great on the terminal shops.

Airline staff was friendly and helpful. Thenwe stepped into immigration. When the provided pens did not work, the supervisor became loud and told us to go outside and find one somewhere. Mind you we were guests in the Dom. Rep. so we knew no one. Then he proceeded to rip the non working ones off of the wall they were attached. After this fiasco we headed through security where after searching my bags one of the officers took a hand carved baseball I purchased in the jungle in Puerto plata where artists carve items for sale to tourists. It was a father's day gift for my husband. After saying I couldn't have it- no explanation, no options- she threw it away. Honestly, I just cried. The 2 nice size rocks and the stone lizard in the bag "passed". I proceeded into the uncomfortable terminals where armed chairs, glaring lights and stone floors prevented a nap while waiting 2 hours for my flight. Where I noticed a gentleman carrying 2 large bottles of rum. I cannot quit figure out why my obvious souvenir was taken unless they considered it a potential weapon. But then i ask myself weren't the 2 hand size rocks, stone object and two large glass bottles not potential weapons? So heartbroken.

CVG is my home airport and I have always had a good experience compared with other large cities. However I recently returned from a trip and had parked in Long Term parking. Previously I had only to walk out the door and across the pick up lane to the well marked shuttle buses, and ride to the long term parking. Apparently they have revised the whole set up and there is zero accessible signage to direct you to a brand new pick up spot for the shuttle buses. There should be 1.) a sign at the old spot telling of the new one; 2.) signage in the actual terminal near where arriving customers will see it as they enter the luggage retrieval area 3.) arrows and signage that distinguishes the east and the west pick up areas are for different things eg the East is for Uber etc and the West is for parking shuttles. (note there is a sign for the bus shuttles in the west end only after you have walked about 2/3 of the way there) 4.) once in the line (designated 1,2,3 for different shuttles) there needs to be signage that distinguishes which shuttle lot bus will be stopping where, there are at 3 different shuttles stopping in this lane, and 5.) the bus itself needs to have signage eg “long term parking”. This is such a huge oversight, please correct it so you can maintain your excellent reputation.

Airport was nice, however very long walk from arrival gate to baggage claim. Ridiculous long wait for bags to arrive on carousel. We flew from Dallas to Cincinnati, the flight was a bit over two hours, it took nearly that long (just under two hours) for our bags to arrive in baggage claim. The person at the baggage desk was not able to provide any information about the status of the bags. We had trackers on them and could see they were sitting at a different terminal for well over 90 minutes after our arrival. Talking to other passengers and the Uber driver, apparently this is very common. We were told the airport is expanding operations, without upgrading infrastructure or adding staff to handle the extra traffic. If you have appointments shortly after you arrive plan on being late.

At Arrival, it took an excessive amount of time for my luggage to arrive at the claim area. At departure, there was a minimal line (when we got there) at TSA being funnelled into 2 open lanes (2 out of 10!) . The open lane we were put into hardly moved, as all wheelchairs and ClearPass passengers were moved in ahead of the line, rather than having their own independent lane for scanning & baggage check. Then the luggage machine broke, and we stood there for 20 minutes, until one worker finally decided to more the line over to the next machine. It was very hot in this area and after waiting almost 90 minutes to get through I felt nauseous. It was very unorganized and of all the airports I have flown through, never have I had these issues.
It has been 45 and I am still waiting for my bags to arrive! Never have I waited longer than this at any airport in the United States. This is unacceptable!

Horrible time waiting for valupark. Busses were non existent. When they did come they packed us in like sardines. They claimed it was due to construction but I had seen 3 fast pass busses before I had seen 1 valupark bus. Then when I inquired upon if they had any extra busses with a airport employee. He stated it was due to work being done. Next time go with fast pass if you don't want to wait.

I want to recognize an employee named Karen. I first ran into her while leaving the Thrifty Car rental shuttle & entering the hallway to the ticketing/check in area & she saw that I was crying....she kindly stopped & asked if I was okay...her kindness made my cry more but in a wonderful way, if that could make any sense at all but very true. This sweet girl took my bags & insisted she carry & drag them for me to the check-in, asking if she could do anything to make things better for me or help me in any way, she would. I opened up & she listened, still pulling my luggage & carrying another bag of mine. Who does this?? A super person like her, that's who. Karen went above & beyond in her representation of Cincinnati Airport & I'm hoping whom ever reads this will go the extra mile, as Karen did & find her last name & get this to her manager. It's stories like this that we need to report & in my opinion, as important as a complaint. Please help this get to the correct department so credit is given to this very special employee. Thank you Karen for your kindness.

If you are handicapped and bringing another handicapped person to this airport, make sure you bring someone else to babysit your car while you are getting the other handicapped person into the airport. I am recovering from stage 4 throat cancer and brought my 92 year old mother here for a flight to Phoenix, while taking her in and the car sitting with the handicapped sticker in the windshield, yep they ticketed it after being told by airport personnel to leave it and get her inside it would be ok. But we do understand its all about the money. People do not have a conscious these days, they are greedy here and that is sad.
Why does it take 50 minutes to get bags at the baggage claim for a flight that arrived at 1.05 am? Are they so busy with the one flight that arrived at that time? Absolutely, unacceptable!

I fly from CVG (Cincinnati/NKY International Airport) frequently, for business and pleasure. My airport experiences are typically normal, with few issues, with the exception of the departure traffic attendants. They are extremely rude and unprofessional. They yell and do not give you adequate time to drop someone off and pull out of your parking location. There is no need to be unprofessional and unfriendly. I would not recommend this airport.

Beware of navigating this airport by motor vehicle. The signage is not adequate for those unfamiliar with the airport traffic patterns. The worst violation is the sign at the cell phone exit into the airport. The road consists of four lanes, two for arrivals or departures, the other two for commercial vehicles and exiting the airport. The sign for this pattern is overhead at the exit from the cell phone lot so you just have to guess and take your chances. Navigating out and back is sketchy. What were they thinking?

Abraham González International Airport is a border town airport which only convenience is to avoid paying an international fare for flights within Mexico. Access is complicated and creepy, not a nice area of town. Juarez has gone through hard times with respect to violence and this might make staff look stressed and transmitting fear. Little directions, poor communication, limited services. Not a comfortable airport at all. They claim to offer many services which were not available neither at departure nor arrival. Money exchange bureau closes very early which makes it an ordeal to get Mexican pesos. Had to get an entry stamp on my passport and the immigration officers were not available. Had to wait for over 30 minutes for someone to show up and grant me official admission to Mexico.

International Airport only in name not in service. Departure, toilets, restaurants and other facilities are almost virtually non-existent. Arrival Onehealth pass check is taking an eternity to be verified because of spotty internet connection. They should improve the internet - not for passengers but for their services. The people working at the luggage conveyor are not doing their job properly. Took us 1hr and 45 minutes to wait for our luggage because the workers are having a breaktime. The luggage should have been loaded by the time we arrive at the conveyor because from clearing onehealth pass to immigration - it took us almost 2hours!

Terminal 2 is a smart design but very poorly built. Simply horrendous. The old airport terminal had a 5/10 rating. The new terminal 2 which now handles all arrivals and departures is probably the worst airport I've have travelled to. Firstly when you arrive in the carpark there are no trolleys for your baggage. It would be impossible for wheelchair users due to the steep ramps/curbs. The escalators are not working yet, but up you crawl to departures. There is no signage anywhere and the departure info boards are not functioning. The new x ray machines were not working with them pinging away without any one even being close to them! Long queues for security. The whole place, every seat is covered in builders dust and dirt. There are no lounges open at all and there is only one small kiosk that serves coke, coke, coke or coke. No Airport shops, no Smoking areas, no working wifi, no snack bars or resturant.

This is an International airport but it is very shabby. It lacks many necessary airport facilites such as power outlets, drinking fountains and restrooms. A terminal fee of 600 pesos needs to be paid but the restrooms facilities were either dirty or broken. Hopefully if they charge that much of a fee per person, improvements can be seen to make people's airport experiences better. Really disappointed.

This airport is very poor. The immigration queues were far too long on arrival and not all desks were staffed. The only good reason to fly here is its proximity to downtown Angeles, which is literally a 10 to 20 minute taxi ride away, depending on traffic. On the way back I caught an early flight at 6.55am and other flights were leaving soon after, yet there was nothing open inside the terminal. This is disgraceful for an international airport meaning passengers have to wait until they take off to eat or drink anything. Also attempting to get into the terminal is annoying with staff needing to go through a security checkpoint just to reach the check-in desks yet there are not enough desks or staff hence the queues are long. To conclude, a lousy airport experience, passengers are charged a departures tax upon leaving Clark. Where does this tax go? Obviously not into improving and developing the airport. Overall this is a cheap and nasty airport, which is an embarrassment to the Philippines.

This must be one of the worst airports in all of Asia. Endless queues and waiting required for everything. From the airport entrance security and baggage X ray queue to the check in queue, then it goes to the terminal fee queue (why cant the 600 Pesos be included in the tickets?), then the immigration queue, followed by the security check queue. Then the boarding passes and passports are checked again before passengers are herded like cattle to the departure hall. Philippine travelers also have to pay a travel tax of PhP1,600 before being permitted to check in. That's another 15 minutes wasted. The entire process takes a good one hour, if you are lucky. It also extremely inconvenient and nerve wracking to do this, more so when traveling with children and infants. The airport is not clean, toilets are dirty and staff do not smile, except the immigration who were very friendly. There are no branded shops or restaurants available and no priority queues for premium passengers. Staff at the sales booths appear lethargic. One size fits all - welcome to the airport from hell! Clearly this airport was not designed with any kind of customer experience in mind, rather with a process driven approach which is a complete nightmare. Clark airport has a long way to go before it can provide passengers with a departure experience from the Philippines which is worthy of an established international standard.

Clark Airport is well secured and accommodating for passengers and there are plenty of seats provided in the pre-departure terminal. There are also small food stalls for the passengers who can fill their tummy while waiting their flight to depart.

A good alternative to Manila International airport. Used this airport several times now. Both domestic and international. International flights is very good and fast. It is not spacious enough, this airport has the potential to be good if upgraded. However, domestic the flights I used are delayed but nowhere near Manila domestic. It lacks food options. It is also very basic and hot due to poor air-conditioning. Philippines should make use of this airport as it has the potential to be the best in the northern Philippines.

Clark Airport is now our favorite way into or out of the Philippines. We flew in on Asiana, and 2 weeks later, departed on Emirates. Both arrival and departure were smooth experiences. Immigration, luggage claim, and customs were fast and efficient, and we were meeting our family in just a few minutes. Departing, the security and check-in were fast and efficient, and the staff were professional, efficient, and pleasant. Queues were short, and the gates were all just an escalator ride and a few steps away. The gate area was spacious, clean, and comfortable. Rest rooms were clean and in good condition. Food offerings were quite adequate for a small airport, and reasonably priced (no lie!). WiFi worked fine. Not a lot of shops, but hey, we're flying, not malling. The only concern is that it was difficult to get an adequate cell phone signal at the gate area. Some other passengers were having this problem as well, though I did manage to make my call after a couple of tries. The VIP lounge takes walk-ins for p800 - pretty reasonable. But the main advantage of this airport is location - you don't have to fight Manila traffic like you do going to or from NAIA. If your destination is anywhere north of downtown Manila, this can easily save you the better part of a day! It's not big or glamorous, but who cares? It's clean, comfortable, and very convenient. I'd definitely recommend this airport for any traveller, and especially for families.

Modern airport and very efficient. Upon arrival by taxi one of the porters thoughtfully brought a cart for the luggage. Check-in area wide and modern. No queue at check in, airport security or even for payment of airport charges. Gate area very clean and equipped with a wide selection of dining options. The view of the imposing Mount Pinatubo is something unique.

Clark Philippines Domestic - The Domestic airport (formerly inside the luxurious international terminal) is now an awful tin shed at the side of the airport - it only services a handful of flights to Cebu. One shop selling coffee and no other food (yet Cebu Pacific can be up to 6 hours late when it comes in delayed from Singapore). The toilets are filthy and smell - no cleaners. No Flight Information. The secret is to sit in the Check in zone outside until the last second before entering.

HORRIBLE! This airport doesn't care about their customers. We arrived in plenty of time, but TSA didn't even open until 4:20 and our departure was at 5:30!! We had so many issues with TSA and other staff. We kept insisting we were cutting it close and they agreed but did nothing to help the process! Our party of 11 was left behind along with 16 other customers! Our flight decided to leave early but the plane was sitting there while 27 of us scrambling and trying to make other arrangements. Our party of 11 was split into other flights which took us way out of our destination, we lost our rental cars, and didn't get to enjoy our airbnb. This is my second time flying out of Cleveland and this is my last time. I have had not nice experiences with this airport!

| I fly a decent amount for work so I have gone to the TSA in a lot of airports in the USA yet, somehow Cleveland TSA seems to go out of their way to be rude, obnoxious, and, slow. This last time they confused a portable monitor for a tablet and got annoyed at me for their ignorance, and said I had four laptops. I had just one laptop for work and a small tablet. I have been the TSA at BNA, ATL, GSP, ORD, SFO, ONT, MKE, and Monteray (MEX) with the same gear this year without a problem. Yet Cleveland TSA has got to be obnoxious about it. The Airline ground staff at Cleveland has always been amazing, especially with Delta, and United, friendly helpful, and present, in my opinion, they make up for a lot of the facility's shortcomings.

Flew back in December from Hopkins and spent 90 minutes in line for security. Today, 3/3/24, I checked my bags and saw that the line for security was the entire length of the airport! While we were waiting in line, we were offered “CLEAR” for a faster way through security. We never would have made our 10:50am flight, despite arriving at 8am. So, we spent the large sum of money on “CLEAR” to ensure our vacation was not ruined. The people in security used the excuse that traffic was high for spring break. I didn’t see any groups of young people that looked like they were going to a beach. Spring break is still a week or two away! The problem is poor staffing and planning. I use to fly twice a week through Hopkins for 12 years and never experienced the ridiculousness that I experienced in December and again today. This is the age of “It is no one’s fault and no one takes ownership.” Remember when Cleveland was the best location in the nation? Well, the Plum has worms!
Cleveland airport is awful. Dirty disgusting bathrooms all the time, trash outside and cigarettes. No pride at all. I’m embarrassed when I have people come here as this is my home.
Parking is inadequate and chaotic, understaffed. Late inbounds flights frequently have no gate crews so you get in late, then wait even longer. Very user unfriendly.

Getting in yesterday was ok except for having to walk great distances when my partner and I have hip issues. Being offered a ride on an electric cart that did not happen. Then today we sat in the check in area for more the an hour waiting for someone to push our wheelchairs to our gate. We were taken to the head of the line only to have to wait. But everyone was very nice.

I fly 2-3 times a month throughout the U.S. for work. Every time I go through security at Cleveland is unnecessary slow and some issue with TSA. They are the rudest agents that look for problems and overreact to everything. I fly LAX and ATL frequently with no issues ever. This trip out of Cleveland they wanted to do a full pat down because a coin sized yellow dot came up in my jeans pocket area when I went through the x-ray machine. I asked to check my pockets and go back through and they refused, used intimidation tactics of getting in my face to make me submit to a pat down. I refused and was kicked out. Checked my pocket and a penny had snuck up in crease. You would think professional TSA agents would be able to recognize a coin when they see it and not subject a traveler to be felt up. Other airports wouldn’t have done that. They also wouldn’t allow me to touch my cleared luggage or purse until I submitted to pat down. Complete harassment on every level.
I have been flying again for business and Cleveland Hopkins is the only airport where you can land and sit and wait 20-40 minutes for a gate to open up. It’s ridiculous.

I travel frequently and have found few airports as poorly run as CLE. I would much prefer to use Canton/Akron but end up using CLE when the deal is just too good to pass up. I flew out this past Saturday and watched a bunch of employees walk around with little idea of how to get a crowd through security while employing some type of social distancing. One woman walked around simply shouting "6 feet" and an employee standing in the CLEAR aisle actually argued with a customer about why CLE just wasn't prepared for the crowd that morning. I do not pay for pre-check, but the gentleman in front of me did, and he was irate that there wasn't even a pre-flight aisle open and he was stuck in the same inefficient line with the rest of us. I returned to CLE from Orlando and experienced none of the problems there that I did at Cleveland Hopkins.
We waited two hours for our baggage. The entire flight had to wait two hours. This is absolutely unacceptable. We were so excited to land at 11.06pm and be able to get home a little earlier.

I had to pay another 72 euros because my luggage was a few cm bigger, in fact it was about the trunk of the suitcase that was out of their measurement scale, in the condition that I have been traveling monthly with that luggage for some time and I have never had any problems, from my point of view. Am fost nevoit sa plătesc încă 72 euro pentru ca aveam bagajul cu câțiva cm mai mare,defapt era vorba de toarta de la geamantan care era ieșita din baremul lor de măsură,in conditia in care calatoresc lunar cu acel bagaj de ceva timp si niciodata nu am avut probleme,din punctul meu de vedere.
This airport is a joke. The Schengen terminal is an improvisation without enough seats, without enough air condition, but with a lot of duty free shops occupying half of the "terminal"'s surface.

The airport is currently being reconstructed but this is done in quite an absurd way. All 7 gates are cramped into temporary, low ceiling housing with a way too big duty-free store in the middle. Early afternoon most planes depart, meaning the place is completely packed. Air-conditioning has to be set to the max to keep cool. Definitely wear a facemask to avoid any respiratory illness. The arrival is fine at the old terminal building and is equally outdated either. Passport control and security checks are done efficiently though.

This airport is a disgrace. We have to wait upstairs to get onboard. There was hundred of people there, no windows opened, no fresh air. With increasing Covid cases and seasonal flu the whole place was a cluster of infections.

As usual, the endless airport staff problem. I had an early flight from Cluj last week and it was quite unpleasant that after travelling all night towards the airport. It started when all passengers, including me, were headed out towards the buses that take you to the airplane. 2 of the buses were fully loaded and by the time I got to the apron, the third one was filled. I stopped, together with a few others, waiting for another bus to come and pick us up. Suddenly, this lady comes with a very cold face and yelling to get in the bus. I asked her if she can see any room for us to fit in, otherwise she needs to make room herself in order for us to get in that bus, and again she starts yelling. Some nice people had to literally squeeze themselves in like sardines and we barely got in, overlapping each other. It’s not safe overloading those buses and they always push them over their limits. The staff should take a course for good manners, they are always rude to people. Most of the staff wear no name badges, and this makes it impossible for customers to report this kind of behaviour.

What a horrible experience we had recently in the airport of Cluj-Napoca in Romania. There were 5 departures at the same time in a waiting room that is totally not adequate for such a huge amount of people. People were sitting on the ground, standing, walking around. All the doors were closed and not all the aircon were working. There was nobody form the airport to watch if there were no problems. Our flight had also 1 hour delay. We stayed three hours in hell. One thing is sure, I never go back to that place. I recommend everyone to wait as long as possible to pass security and passport controls. They were very fast and for that reason we were there far too early in the waiting room.

Rude employee and unhelpful. My elderly mum had priority ticket and needs support walking. I wanted to help her boarding but we got sent back queuing because I didn't have priority ticket. I've asked the guy at the gate to help my mum, he replied "she is not my mum, I'm not helping". So we went back to the end of the line. What a disgraceful attitude towards elderlies. This is a young guy who needs to learn how to speak and act with people. Unfortunately he doesn't wear a badge, so I don't know his name.

The very small airport scheduled 5 flights in the morning around 6am all in the same time--the waiting room was so packed that nobody can even move like sardines in a can - no masks or concern for passengers safety. Half of the floor space was taken by some empty stores and café. Totally dysfunctional - management is incompetent and out of touch with reality.

Diabolical isn’t a stronng enough description. 6 international departure gates, 4 on ground fooor, two above. On the top floor there is seating for about 75 people, if you can put up with the high 30s room temperature. With two flights departing an hour (in October) it doesn’t take long for 300 people to get crammed into the small area. And no better downstairs where the situation is similar. I’d hate to be in this place in summer temps and busier flight schedule. My rating is 1 because I can’t select zero.

Is just like an overcrowded two level bus garage, not enough seating not even for 1 flight but imagine 3 at once, shame and disgust but today there were 5 flights all departing from 18.30 to 19.40. Also a smoking area enclosed in the airport! The people were in and out so that the door had all the smoke in all the building. Shame!

Very unorganised airport. A lot of flights were delayed and they change gates without notifying anyone so you have to keep checking the screen. Flight attendants were also rude and unhelpful they just shout stuff at people and the boarding process was worst I’ve experienced. Only positive is the food to be honest.

Cochabamba Airport is a rather small International Airport in Bolivia, which only serves national routes regarding departures. There are international and even intercontinental (Madrid) arrivals, though. I came from Sao Paulo Guarulhos with a nonstop flight with BoA. And returned to Sao Paulo with a layover in Santa Cruz, as there are no nonstop connections leaving CBB. The International Arrival Area is quite small, immigration is done through only one officer. A positive thing is that the airport has air-bridges, which are used mainly for the international arrivals and domestic departures. Domestic arrivals normally get off the plane on the tarmac, where the people have to walk to the terminal, because no busses are used. Regarding Departures, the Check-in Area is quite small, as the airport is only being served by 4 Airlines, of which two are state-owned. The departures take place from the second floor, where there is also a small shop at the gates selling snacks and beverages. There is no duty free shop, which I find quite bad. Also an important thing to note is that there is no Lounge for frequent travelers.

Cochabamba is a very small international airport, some flights of Boliviano de Aviacion arrive from Buenos Aires, Sao Paulo and seaonsally to Madrid. It has enough space for the flights and people who use this terminal. One of the most interesting things about this airport is its food court has plenty of choices and types of food, and best of all if you are traveling on low budget there is a public transport service that will take you straight to town, for almost nothing 0.50 cents. If traveling for tourism or business there is no other choice to get to the center of Bolivia. Wifi runs great and its totally free.

This airport serves both international flights to Brazil and domestic flights with Bolivia with Aerosur. The airport has average facilities for departure however it is with arrival that the weaknesses of this airport shine forth. One small baggage area with an exit for domestic travellers no customs check required and one exit for international travellers with a through customs check result in chaos. The lack of baggage carts and hundreds of people struggling with several large suitcases each all struggling towards the one international exit result in a rugby scrum. When I arrived the one customs agent controlling the gate was also checking the other domestic arrivals gate. I only escaped after throwing my luggage out of the surging crowd and then dragging it back to the luggage area and eventually out. What should have taken 10 minutes took one hour.

We booked a ticket to travel from Ahmedabad to London Gatwick via New Delhi and Cochin airports. When we arrived at Cochin airport our baggage had been unloaded instead of going straight to T3 to the plane for Gatwick. The porters were really helpful in taking us from T1 to T3 and getting the Air India staff to sort out the mess (they were really unhelpful at New Delhi and at Cochin airport) but the porters were expectionally helpful Special mention goes to the porters who took us from T1 to T3 and to Vivek PD who took us to the lounge and then later to the plane.

Why do you need a passport to enter the damm airport and you need a boarding pass. Fun fact they usualy print your boarding pass in the airport. There was no signage to tell me where to drop my bag that's so ridiculous. This guy doing security checked around 1 bag every 2 minutes and before mine just walks off the job. The security is horrible. There is no way I will be coming back to kochi airport your better off just taking the train.

This airport and also some other Airports in India have draconian rules for entry to the airport by not letting before 6 hours. Exceptions are Bombay and Delhi with more than 10 hours. Imagine you are travelling by domestic flights 1 or 2, and need to catch an international flight at Cochin, but you are not allowed before 6hrs. There's no seating arrangements outside rather you are at the mercy of mosquitoes and drenching sweat. They claim to be one of the best international airport but these airports are not managed by keeping in mind about people/travellers rather they want to enforce their colonial inherited rules. I arrived exactly 6 hours before my flight but I was stopped at the gate saying their system has not updated the entry for my flight. He said I have to wait for 10 to 20 minutes outside. When I asked he said to go and talk to the airport manager somewhere in a remote corner of airport. I stood there waiting, then finally he called me and advised that I should have patience and keep shut. Gees this is how their airports are working. Is it appropriate to say shame!

Cochin International Airport is a beautiful, environment friendly and comfortable airport. From the infrastructure to the furniture, the process, the staff, everything about this airport exudes comfort and positive vibes. The airport is powered by solar panels, wooden interiors and well functioning toilet fittings and fixtures make this airport an environment friendly one.

Rude immigration staff. Today i was really irritated with the unprofessional and rude behaviour of the immigration staff. He wanted me to provide a copy of the ID proof of the country which I reside in. I had provided the soft copy ( issued by the govt) which is accepted in all airports.  Not all staff are rude but there are some characters like this who spoil an otherwise good airport.

This is the worst airport in India. I have been to so many airports but never have I been asked to wait outside. I then decided to go to Marriott for dinner, they clearly mentioned come by 11.45 and we shall allow you inside. When I came back it was 11.45 sharp. Then they changed the rules as per their convenience. If I was 6 hours early for check in due to circumstances I had to come early and they asked me at night to wait outside. After coming inside my airline which was supposed to leave at 6.45, didn’t even start check-in which should be done at least 3 hours prior to departure. I couldn’t even go to the lounge. A lady was peacefully sleeping at the counter. The entire staff were rude as if we were asking them their kidneys. I have never in my life had a terrible experience as such. I’m never going to visit this airport ever again. Better to take a train or a bus where you can sleep instead.

Almost all the socket outlets in the food court are not working. Passengers use these points to charge mobiles and this does not serve the purpose. Why do you have them there? To show that you provide service?

Arrival no problem, departure is a totally different matter, the people at customs need to be taught some manners and respect, so rude and obnoxious. Never experienced such people in all of my travels, we will never be going to that airport again. Upset both me and my wife. What an end to what was a great holiday. They don't believe a word of what you say, throw your bags at you and make you feel like a criminal, even though there was nothing wrong. Horrible experience.

Lovely airport, arrivals was a breeze so was departures, my only gripe would be the loud intercom, it’s way too high and becomes more of an annoyance rather than help. Also the WIFI - won’t get an OTP without an active number and receiving OTP is not practical with most international numbers, make your WiFi free just like DXB airport without the number registration process. It was a hassle when my number didn’t work and had to use my roaming data.

Very disappointed to see that you are busy aping the western culture and forget our own roots. As an Indian I am very proud of my heritage and all my traditional food. However Cochin airport is a far cry from that. You will happily serve cappuccino coffee to please a foreigner while completely omitting to serve a traditional Indian masala tea or a nice bru coffee. It is very sad what Cochin airport has come to.

The security are rubbish, no customer service at all, they need retraining or sacking. I was traveling with no luggage, only had my phone in pocket of shorts and T-shirt. They scanned my whole body like I was a criminal. Avoid this stupid airport at any cost, personally I will never ever come back.
Functional adequate satisfactory are descriptions that come to mind. Unlikely to offend but not memorable.

It's big enough for the number of people it serves on a weekday although I'd imagine it would get pretty crowded when the larger Virgin planes come in from Melbourne on weekends. The staff are friendly the facilities adequate for a regional airport of this size the queues managable and it's clean. It just feels like it's missing something. Despite it being refurbished within the last decade or so it feels like it needs a bit of a touch up-and the constant use of that sickly blue colour everywhere doesn't necessarily help the situation. So yes it is a nice airport in regional NSW that serves its purpose and the needs of the people but I just get the feeling that with a bit of money put in (new floorings lick of paint open up the departure lounge a bit more provide wi-fi) it could be have a certain wow factor reserved for NSW regional airports like Newcastle Albury and Dubbo which have been thrust forward into the 21st Century.

What a terrible airport. Minimal staff is not there. AC not there. Mobile charging points not available. Food and restroom tho, just forget about it. If AC cannot be affordable at least put some fans. Power saving mode is ok but it should not effect the passengers .. I have experienced airports in India but Coimbatore is the worse. I suggest you to get into airport just and hr before flight departure. Don't keep any hopes on food here. It is the same menu as we see in the normal veg restaurant. No kfc no burgers no pizzas. Even staff also feeling hot and they too admitting the this is the worse one.

Except the Air India counter staff member, this airport is an absolute nightmare. The executive lounge does not even have WiFi access. Planes are delayed and it's not really clean. To sum up, they call this an international airport, I call it an only-domestic one.

The airport international departure section was very bad. The waiting area is very dirty. The security check will begin only 1 hour before departure and you will have to wait outside until that time. The money exchange there is a loot. They charged us 75 inr for one usd which is almost 10 rs more.

Small and borderline useless. Arrivals is straightforward - plane - bridge - escalator - baggage claims - exit. Being a small airport, baggage arrival is quick. Departure is still housed in the old terminal which is damp, poorly lit, has bad shopping and little food. Thankfully its efficient, so charging points work and there are enough seats to be had. Bus boarding is on the same level as waiting and bridge boarding is in a set of brightly lit corridors on the floor above. All in all an ad-hoc renovated airport that remains small town.
In my opinion airport is not at all up to the mark. Only one aerobridge 2 duty free shop No internet facilities 1 eating outlet. Needs to improve a lot.

This airport is of a very low standard. The baggage delivery is very very slow and not enough departure gates (only two gates are there right now). On the whole this is one of the worst airport in India.

Its a pity - the city of Coimbatore is growing fast at the global level and yet the airport does not cater to international flights except for the meagre Sharjah flight . Yes it is neat and tidy but it is also getting a bit cramped. The Government at the Centre and State could look into Coimbatore as a potential for international flights. The private domestic airlines had success when they were offered permission to fly there. I feel if foreign airlines are given permission to do so they will meet with success too. In domestic flights Indian airlines did not show much regard to suitable travel times to and from Coimbatore In the international side Air India has not shown any interest at all. I feel they think it would be a loss for them to fly there. So since they are not going to lose out on anything foreign airlines or other private airlines of India could be given permission to fly to Coimbatore on international routes.
The airport is tiny! Too many passengers use this airport. The potential of this City is enormous! Government needs to show some care for Coimbatore.

Contrary to what I had expected to find at a small domestic airport the terminal was beautifully clean well laid out with the benefit of some shops friendly staff who helped us through the security and check- in process. Ladies toilets (both Indian and Western style) were acceptably clean. A/C was okay if you were standing under it. I would have no hesitation in travelling through this airport again on future visits to India. Well done to those who maintain the Airport - keep up the good work.

This is the first review on airlinequality.com for College Station's Easterwood Airport. Frankly, I had seen a host of negative reviews on Google, and was skeptical about flying out of CLL. I am elated to report that my concerns couldn't have been any more wrong. First, the parking is ridiculously easy, immediately in front of the terminal. Parking for the first two hours is free, and daily parking is something like $7. Second, it's very easy to get to from Texas A&M (the airport is on university property) or anywhere else in College Station and Bryan, but it feels like you're legitimately out in the country. Third, every single personnel I met, from airline check-in agents (who double up as gate agents since the airport is so small!) to TSA/security to the cashier in the one little snack shop post-security, were quite friendly and professional. TSA Pre-Check also works like a charm there. Fourth, I was impressed that I was able to check my bag in with ease from CLL to southern Asia. Fifth, the terminal has obviously been recently renovated, so it's very modern and clean, and yet it feels oddly spacious for such a small terminal (probably the smallest actual one I've ever been in). As a side note, the airport is so small that to walk from the lower level (where ground-level parking is) to upper level (for check-in, security and departures), one must either walk up stairs or take an elevator. That's right, there's no moving sidewalk or escalator there! This is such a nice alternative from larger, busier airports such as Houston Bush (which typically has good customer service, but is smelly and beyond outdated), and Houston Hobby and Austin (both of which are very modern and clean, but have generally poor customer service).

24 June 2024. Arrived at Airport 3 hours early, check in and security smooth and quick. At boarding, long queue for passport control. 2 flights for UK leaving at same time, not enough police to check passports. Manchester flight, gate was held open till 2 mins before take off, all passengers just about squeaked on.
