Stansted flight, gate closed 10 min before take off time, about 12 passengers inc us denied boarding. Plane sat on tarmac while they unloaded our hold baggage. So plenty of time to have boarded us if they had left the gate open a few mins longer. Cologne Bonn Airport website misleading - says security typically 6 mins - which was true. No mention of very long queue for passport control. No announcements to say 'Go to Gate 60 minutes before departure' to ensure people get through on time.
Most dreadful experience ever! Missed our European flight with 30 seconds due to a security queue of 2 hours! Very impolite and unfriendly staff. Never again.

I just had an appalling experience with passport control on a flight to Heathrow. I had left plenty of time but nearly missed my flight due to a ridiculously long queue. The passport control people were terrible

The woman at the information desk, Terminal 1 near arrivals is a rude person and lacks politeness and empathy, I really don't understand how they choose this specific person for a task that needs some communication skills and some level of politeness.

Car hire drop off and bag drop off was seamless and extremely quick. However, there was a crazy queuing situation to get through security. The line snaked through the terminal just to get to the boarding pass check point - where only one checkpoint was open. The long queue then extended to get through security. In all it took us 1.5 hrs from the point of joining the queue to clearing security. We had arrived early so were not delayed, but it would have been very stressful if it had made us late; the airport staff claimed they could not get anyone through any quicker. There was also a lengthy queue for the fast track line, albeit not as long as the main queue. Mitigations were the staff were very amiable and the queue kept moving, albeit slowly. Recommend factoring in at least an extra hour to clear security, and/or paying for fast track.

Passport control is extremely poorly and inefficiently run. I entered a line which was clearly and unequivocally labeled as mixed - that is, for both EU and all passports. After standing in line for 20 minutes and finally getting to the passport control window, the lady officer rudely told me that the line was only for EU citizens, pointing above her head. I looked up to see that indeed they had just changed the signs after I had waited all this time. She did not care that the sign had just changed or that I had been waiting all this time. She insisted that I go to another line where I had to wait for 45 more minutes.

This airport went from being one of my favourite airports to one of my worst. The quality of security personnel in this airport went from efficient and polite to downright rude, slow and well below standards for a first world airport. From having two terminals, each with its own security gates, the airport now has only one security entrance serving both terminals. This causes extremely long queues to form, and adds to everyone's frustration. The passport control entering terminal 2 is now completely inadequate, and catering and refreshments airside of the passports gate are pathetic. The frequent flyer lounge has been privatised - this was another bad idea. The company running it cut down on service that now is more of a cafeteria with sandwiches and warm beer than a business lounge. This used to be such a convenient airport for me to use, but I now avoid it whenever possible. Sad to see something good deteriorate so markedly.

This is the worst airport experience that I had to go through. And this bad experience is not due to the long queues or the lack of information, but for the incredible rudeness of the staff at the security check. I have never in all my travels encountered such rude people. They basically should not be in contact with the public if all they can do is shout at you. I will do whatever is possible to avoid this airport in the future and will advise any person I know to do the same. This is a first and I am deeply sorry that it has to be about an airport in Germany, a country I have lived in and which I love. But these persons should not be employed, if they cannot show the minimum of politeness.

Mismanaged and understaffed! Atrocious queue management. Had a connecting flight with 1.5hrs in between. Took me over 1 15 minutes to get to my gate; thanks to having only 2 security gates open, and only after jumping the queue. I counted at least 10 flights departing within the following 60 minutes - doesn’t take a genius to count that this is insufficient. To add insult to injury the staff at security, clearly lacking any motivation, had absolutely no sense of urgency. I take about 30 flights a year and flown many airports - this has to be the worst experience I had. Curious and uncommon that even on connecting flights passengers had to leave the secure zone and go through security again. Surely if you’re struggling to manage security, you can reduce all the connecting passengers checks…

Very bad experience, you can easily see the age of Terminal 1 everywhere you look at arrival, it's really quiet hard to navigate to get out of the arrival hall, escalators not working, getting to trains took 20min just walking on departure. Getting to departure hall was ok, not long waiting lines but the experience there was awful my flight was at 21:25 with many other departures around that time or later, but all shops started to close from 8pm, not enough places to sit, people sitting everywhere on the ground, long lines in restaurants/bars/cafes - worst experience were toilets, water everywhere on the ground.

Colombo International airport is a joke. Never had such a horrific experience as a tourist on an international flight. This airport is notorious for ripping you off and charging unconventional baggage fees for carrying a personal item, such as a purse or even food. They weighed our food and charged me over $100 for my purse and food. They even wanted to wear my jacket that I was wearing. I do not recommend this airport, and they are notorious for treating tourist like this, as I was advised when I landed in the Maldives. Sri Lanka in general is a phenomenal country with amazing people.

I had 2 long transits through Colombo airport on the way to Jakarta from Mumbai. I got an amazing deal but this meant two long layovers at Colombo which I initially thought would be alright. However, this feels like an airport which has not been updated for ever and ever. The transit area is just a long corridor along the gate holding areas with a limited number of steel chairs and hardly any charging points. The F&B options are also very limited, anything longer than a 1-2 hour layover would be awful. I had a 6-7 hour layover both ways but thankfully Priority Pass gets you access to the Lotus Lounge which is comfortable enough to spend some time (they give you upto a 6 hour wait at the lounge on a single entry). The food service and the beverages at the lounge are quite good though and there are enough seats to get comfortable in. Unfortunately charging points are limited but atleast there are enough to manage, as long as the lounge is not too crowded.

Everything here is slow, disorganised and so old fashioned. It’s like they don’t care about bringing this airport up to date. Lines are long, staff are slow, inefficiency all round. In the toilet is a sign saying toilets are free. Didn’t stop a cleaner asking me for money. The room after yet another security check you wait to board is inadequate - poor ventilation, not enough seats, no water, no toilets, no communication re delay, nothing. For a country known for hospitality, this airport has none. I can’t recall a worse airport. Sad really.

Airport is badly organised and incompetent. Delayed flight but no information what to do. Bag drop was 1 desk and took hours for small number of passengers. Refused to respect our bought and paid for extra leg room seats. Restaurants very limited. Wifi not functional. Toilets filthy. Not enough seating. Security xray scanning a joke.

What a hot mess. Arriving at 2am there were hundreds waiting for immigration clearance. No real lines, no one to supervise the pushing and shoving. They opened another counter but instead of maybe choosing families and elderly the young pushed through. Took nearly two hours to get kerbside and we had all paperwork in order. They need someone at immigration to control lines and make it fair for all, instead of the free for all it is.

I will never go to Sri Lanka again after dealing with this airport. Forced on to a 12 hour flight with no water, with no warning we had to go through security again at the gate where they take the water you bought for the flight. We were then left in a gate waiting room with no access to water or toilets for several hours, during which time the flight was repeatedly delayed with no announcements being made to customers. Trying to get through the airport is chaos from the moment you arrive. The bizarre check in structure has several additional steps than the standard airport and an unclear order. Lack of signage or staff to help get everyone in the right queue. Lengthy queue’s spiral around the lobby with no structure and move painfully slow. The food and drink prices in the airport are obscene. Wifi doesn’t work. There is nothing good about this airport. Dismal end to a beautiful holiday.

Frequented CMB many times in the last decade and on the whole its ok.  It runs pretty smoothly and in fact has improved over the years, the immigration particularly seems quicker. I do however hate the exorbitant dollar priced food/drink and duty free etc. The contrast between what this cost just outside the door or the airport and the terminal prices must be one of the biggest contrasts in the world. That said its a pretty painless experience to pass through.

First of all they asked me to take off belt, shoe, jacket. There was two lines, when I entered through metel detector no one even checked me on the other side. They were only checking the selected people. After the security screening comes a big shock. Right before where I show my boarding pass comes a person asking for my passport and boarding pass. He then began looking at the pages of my passport as if it was fake. He then demanded my college name, my postal address, how many times I have been to the destination country. As if I was illegally trying to enter Srilanka. While all I was doing was transiting in that airport. After all the hassle, right before the gate of plane a police again asked me to open all my luggage. I had never experienced this in some of the most advanced and far developed countries. No sense of customer service, sympathy.

Airport staff were rude did not listen to customers. Weak WIFI, no information Center, lack of communication skills. No assistance for families who had kids. My transit was for 9hrs so I had booked hotel for one stay. On the arrival, they queue us in transport services for the hotel booking. After that they told us to go to immigration, when we reached there they told us to fill up on arrival card. After fill up the arrival card the line was long have to wait for 20 minutes. On that section they just checked passport number and told us to go in Visa on arrival section. After the queue of 30-45 minutes, they informed us they don't give visa on arrival for Nepal and apply for online visa. I had applied for online visa and came to know that it took 24 hrs for the Visa. And I had roaming around for 2 hrs and end up with no hotel booking. I was by myself and adult still stressed but there was some people travelling with kids and did not get any assistance from staff.

The WiFi is often weak or there is no connectivity at all. I wish someone in charge would get it fixed. Many passengers agree with me on this matter. A good WiFi is imperative for those traveling through any airport!

Their security people and policies are out of control! They have been so strict for no reason. I am a pre-check customer and they found sea salt scrub in my carry on and took me aside to test it. I made it and I could have and offered to eat it. They told me no and then proceeded to take all of my belongings that I had already picked up including my purse, my shoes and cell phone. I find this practice illegal and highly invasive. I had done nothing wrong and because you're incompetent staff was not able to read an explosive test properly (had to call someone to walk him through it), then they inconvenienced me by taking my things and treating me inhumane. For my next flight, I'm driving to Denver. It's cheaper too even with having to pay for parking. Also, when you randomly select people to test their shoes through pre-check, that practice sucks too! You are inconveniencing people that paid to go through security without being harassed.

I have been flying in and out of COS for years, and over the years the TSA acts worse and worse, they act rude and no common courtesy what’s so ever. They stand there saying next, let’s go, hurry up, dont move this or that, you get scanned and they either say move, or I need to touch you more, and then still no kindness at all. They act like they have so much authority. I’ve had senior military leaders who speak better to people. They don’t deserve this position. Hire contractors who know how to speak to people professionally. TSA leadership needs to watch these people. Start treating people with a little respect!
Rudest security staff I’ve ever experienced in years a of travel all over the world. No amenities open to accommodate first flights of the day. Seating is okay but outdated.

I have flown into and out of the Colorado Springs twice a year since 2009. Each time, check in has been efficient and pleasant, the TSA agents have been very nice and observant, the airport has been clean and refreshment options have been pretty good. I was last there in October of 2017 and liked the fact that the piped in music in the waiting area was classic rock. I have a high opinion of the COS airport and don't mind at all flying in and out of it.

Great airport to travel from and return to. No great distances to walk, easy access to check in counters, TSA actually seems to care and think rather than defaulting to lowest level of acceptable service (ie - Denver). Early morning flights are great as the food court has great breakfast burritos and coffee. The only problem seems to be the luggage getting from the plane back to you. Once you have your bags, the rest of the trip out is a breeze.

I have used COS airport several times flying from Nashville to COS and back to Nashville. Each time I have been there airport personnel have been very helpful and friendly TSA security officials have been efficient and very observant and the airport has always been clean. I would highly recommend this airport to other fliers.

The lack of reasonably priced and convenient public transportation options to and from the airport is a major downside to this otherwise attractive airport. Why the city bus system stops just short of the airport is hard to understand without invoking a conspiracy theory involving the expensive and inconvenient commercial bus taxi and limousine services that enjoy a monopoly in this market.

The lack of reasonably priced and convenient public transportation options to and from the airport is a major downside to this otherwise attractive airport. Why the city bus system stops just short of the airport is hard to understand without invoking a conspiracy theory involving the expensive and inconvenient commercial bus taxi and limousine services that enjoy a monopoly in this market.

I highly recommend traveling out of COS if you live in Pueblo Colorado Springs even Denver! COS is a very cozy and convenient airport with easy parking check-in security and baggage claim. It's main terminal has 12 gates so it isn't at all huge but it is a very comfortable size. In the past several years the planes flying into and out of COS have sadly gotten smaller (think regional jets) and the routes served are mostly to hub cities. That said I would personally rather fly out of COS and connect than drive the extra hour and a half to DEN and fly nonstop because it is a lot less stressful. The airport recently purchased new furniture for each gate area and it is a vast improvement. They even have padded benchs in the center of the terminal that you can lie on and sleep before you fly! This little extra is great because let's face it when people come from sea level to 6187 ft it is nice to lie down and adjust to the high altitude. That said one downfall of COS is its lack of shops and restaurants though the variety isn't horrible. The free Wi-Fi throughout the terminal though helps compensate for this shortfall.

If you don't need to go to Denver I recommend COS as the best option for going to Colorado. Small but not too small; clean efficient quick and centrally located to most points in Colorado. Good quick car rentals. I use it routinely to go to Pueblo and Denver. Yes Denver as it can be more convenient and faster to get to a lot of places especially in south Denver. Remember Denver airport is 30 miles east and an expensive toll road from many points in Denver. Also traffic is very congested in Denver but only moderately so in Colorado Springs. Only problem I have is that most often (but not always) the cheaper fares are into and out of Denver.

I entered the TSA area to receive the routine security check. I had on a dress at the time, which I don't normally wear when traveling. When I walked through the metal detector, apparently my "groin area" on the scan indicated an abnormality? I was shown the scan where this region of my body indicated a red color. I was only told because of this, I would need a pat-down. I was pulled to the side and was told to wait for my carry-ons to clear security, so that they could perform the pat-down. The female TSA agent asked if I wanted to receive my exam out in the open or in private. I had a dress on, so I decided to choose the private examination. I was told to move to the side when my items came through security and that I had a couple of items that were problematic. So, I was told which items and that I wasn't allowed to bring them through (a scented body spray, along with a facial cleanser). I had no problems with these items on my departure from California to South Carolina. After this, I was taken into a little frosted glass area where I received the "pat-down". As I've never had one of these types of pat downs before, I was unprepared for what I was eventually submitted to. Another TSA agent came in so that two female TSA agents were present. I am a veteran myself but despite this, I don't normally make it a point to use this as a way to receive special treatment. The one female who put on her gloves and conducted the search was very cold, matter-of-fact and almost callous in her actions. She went up my thighs, pushing up against the sides of my crouch; she brushed her hand down over my pubic area. I automatically moved away from her hands. She had to do this 2-3 times because I kept moving. It was unintentional because my boundaries were being breached, an involuntary reaction. The one agent coldly stated that if I moved again, she would have to performing the action. I am a very tolerant person when it comes to people doing their jobs, but I felt assaulted and triggered. I got angry and teared up but allowed these insensitive, cold agents to finish. I knew that they knew I was upset even though I didn't say anything. I have PTSD, so I feel like this kind of touching shouldn't be allowed. We left the little room, the agents took my items, put them on a table and walked off. No courtesy, no nothing. It angered me. I retrieved my items on the table from the containers and tossed one on the floor and walked off to my gate without looking back. I went to a restroom, changed out of my dress into a shirt and pants. Later on, I ran into another person on my flight who had gone through TSA with her mother, who's in a wheelchair. She also had to go through the same invasive exam. Their experience wasn't long before my experience in terms of time. After, this TSA scenario when I arrived at my gate for my flight, I found out that my flight was delayed. Because I downloaded the app of the airline to my phone I was able to change my connecting flight on the suggestion of my app. While waiting along with other frustrated but resigned people, I kept hearing these announcements over the PA system about one particular flight that kept getting changed to different gates. THEN the ticket agents at my gate kept asking people to check their carry-on bags. Apparently there wasn't room enough on the flight for carry-ons. I had a feeling of a lack of professionalism, despite my personal experience. Thank goodness I won't have to visit SC again.

Returned from vacation to Columbus, OH., May 22, 2024, at 7:30 am. United Airlines. Gate 38. I had requested a wheelchair when booked returning flight. None were available, Agent at desk said they would call for one but it would be several minutes. After a 5 hour night flight from San Francisco, I needed to use the bathroom immediately. Had to walk a distance, without wheelchair, to closest one where I found one with 2 working sinks out of 4. No wheelchair or staff was in sight until food court area. (At the airports in Maui and San Francisco there was always staff available to assist you). Finally found a unused wheelchair (no staff). We then traveled to Baggage Claim area. We needed an elevator to go to lower level. Poor signage of where the elevator was. (sign was on the side wall, none in direst view). At passing the security check point, the entry security line was backed up to the escalator. I am sure many were upset and worried about not getting to their gate on time. Once retrieving our luggage, still seated in a wheelchair, I had to wait for my husband to get our parked car (green lot). While waiting outside, the cars, buses and airport cleaning truck exhaust became overwhelming. I could not breathe and began a coughing fit. With a new proposed airport building, I hope the administration look into these problems and finds a solution to these many problems.

CMH is a nice mid-sized airport. Always enjoy how easy it is to get in and out, as I park in the garage that allows direct access via an underground walkway. It's seldom crowded, though I've had the occasional long wait to get through security. I will echo another reviewer's comments about the rudeness of some TSA agents. The young lady helping us load our trays with our personal items, shoes, etc. on our most recent trip was actually quite pleasant. However, some male agents on the other side of the x-ray machines were harsh and disrespectful to travelers (including myself). One in particular seemed super disgruntled, and lacked basic communication skills to boot. Unfortunate, given the customer-facing nature of his job. On a previous trip, I can also attest to the fact that my wife underwent a pretty intense pat down because she was carrying baby formula through security with our child...maybe this is typical protocol nowadays but I think she was surprised by an agent searching inside the underwire of her bra (something we hadn't seen/experienced when traveling with our first child). Food options, as others have stated, are pretty weak. There is Starbucks available, if you have the time to wait in line a while during peak hours. Overall, I think it's great for flying in/out of my hometown, but probably not much to get excited about for someone passing through.

Terrible experience. The security checkpoint guards were yelling at customers and speaking to them in the most disrespectful possible ways, for no apparent reason at all. Customers were very shocked and upset. I'm from NYC and have never seen professionals speak to customers in any context in such a hostile and unhelpful way. Completely unacceptable.

Decent airport as far as security lines and accessibility, but otherwise just annoying. Pretty much all the restaurants close by 7.00. We were lucky to find a vending machine with a sandwich in it. Baggage claim is also always slow.

I arrived to pick someone up at CMH before 7pm on Tuesday 8/31/21. Not a single store was open. The "Food Court", which consists of one cheese steak franchise, was closed. United had flights coming in and the counter was closed. It looked like it was 2am. I even tried to get a coffee from the one vending machine and there were no cups. The baggage took over an hour because they were short staffed. The airport screamed small town.
Come on CMH, 6.25 pm on a Tuesday evening and not one restaurant on B concourse open? The pandemic is easing and everyone seems to be flying again. We would like to eat!

This is a good airport! The cleaning can be improved, but I do like the layout, it's not a very very long walk but it is long if you ask me. I go here for my vacation flights, instead of having to drive 6 hours to the nearest true international airport. Overall, Columbus has a good airport! Would definitely fly here again.

John Glenn International is a great midsized airport for easy travel. The terminal was recently (2016) renovated and is very clean, bright, and modern. There are many dining options now that weren't present just a few years ago. One of the best things about it is the free WiFi and charging plugs for every seat in the waiting areas. Overall, this is one of the best airports I've traveled through.
Dirty airport with very few direct choices. Always have to connect and always late. Not sure why nay major company would relocate to Columbus knowing that they have a sub par airport.
Easy and pleasant smaller airport. It has all facilities required for a pleasant wait is spacious and never crowded. No wait times at security and very friendly people.

At first I was not impressed by the airport as from outside it looks small and not modern. But, once in, I was happily surprised with the efficiency of the airport both in the arrival and departure halls. The wifi woked perfectly. The facility is simple but clean and fast to navigate through. The airport business class lounge was a great surprise. Beautiful design, very attentive staff, great food and drinks selection. Well done CKY!

Conakry is in no way a modern airport, even quite old. But it's management is stunning. I have been through this airport a great number of times over the years and am always impressed by its efficiency, especially arrivals. In 5 minutes, you get through immigration and then at the luggage carousel, something I've never seen in the possibly 200 airports I know: luggage trolleys are already positioned in front of the carousel, so very convenient. Unfortunately, to leave the airport is somewhat difficult especially for elder people as you have to push you trolley on a pretty steep ramp before exiting the airport. Also departure area needs to be modernized.

rather cold and impersonal although food shop and check-in staff pleasant and I was able to check-in over an hour before departure. Extraordinary use of loud-speaker systems inside and outside the terminal playing a local radio station at full blast. It seems this airport is owned by the local radio station so loudspeakers are used to blast their advertisements at you as you alight from the (Regional Express) aircraft. Beware that the terminal is shut until about an hour or so before an aircraft arrives or departs and one is forced to look for shelter where one can if dropped off a little early. Strange place.

If you sit in an area next to the smoking lounge, the whole area smells like smoke. I even saw people in a nearby queue trying to close the door completely, even though it was already closed. It just smells. I walked from the main hall of the airport to Arena A86, and I started feeling sick because of the smell. Why have such a large smoking area to accommodate people who chose this habit themselves? I found it horrible and hope I don't have to go to this end again.

For a sophisticated and civilized country like Denmark, Copenhagen Airport is a real disappointment. Sure, it is large and modern, but one gets the impression that the comfort and amenity of the passengers was the last thing the designers and operators considered. To begin with, there is a real shortage of places to sit while waiting for your connection. There are broad corridors all over the airport, but they are all lined with stores and restaurants, as if taking the last euro from your pocket was far more important than providing the basic facilities that travelers need. Throughout the airport hundreds passengers were literally sitting on the floor. Some of the ‘seating’ provided consisted of hugely uncomfortable, angular objects as if the message was ‘don’t just sit here, go and spend some money!’ There is practically no seating available inside the check-in lounges where old, frail and pregnant travelers are forced to stand for up to 45 minutes before being able to board. But perhaps the most worrying feature the disdainful attitude of staff to travelers. We were booked on a Ryanair flight that was seriously late, and the holding area was chock-a-block with waiting passengers for over an hour. As one of us had an operation and could not stand, we decided to wait just outside the check-in counter until the holding pen started to empty. To our shock and surprise, we were denied boarding by a very arrogant and aggressive check-in clerk, despite the fact that over 100 passengers were still queuing to get onto the plane. Obviously the check-in clerk wanted to go home and closed the flight before everyone had a chance to check-in. she next called the airport security who showed not the least interest in solving the problem. Subsequent complaints to the airport, and Ryanair were brushed off, and we were forced to spend the night at the airport and pay for a flight next day. This is the kind of thing you might experience in some of the worst airports of the world, but Copenhagen? I think the airport needs to urgently review its priorities, hugely increase seating accommodation, place traveler comfort and amenity above saturating the place with duty free shops, and most of all, get rid of airport personnel for whom travelers are just a nuisance.
The longest, worst and most exhausting airport experience I ever had. Only 3 boarding pass barriers for thousands of passengers before the security check. Took more than an hour in that queue.

Fantastic well functioning airport, all the shops and facilities you need, it took almost no time to get through passport control and security check, friendly staff all in all an exceptionally good experience

Very dirty airport all over. From gates, restrooms to restaurants seems no cleaning. Departing from terminal F, the most crowded terminal, only very few options to sit. Probably less than 1% of passenger can have a seat. Absolutely no charging options. The total airport experience is way below average in Europe.

At this otherwise quite nice airport, there are no charging sockets anywhere to be found. One has to charge one's devices in smelly toilets or hunt for a cleaning sockets somewhere on corridors or other odd places. No chance to sit comfortably while charging, one has to either stand, or sit on floor. There are no sets at departures gates in international C wing. No walkators either.
Another one of these airports for which making money from shopping is more important than traveler convenience. Long distances you have to walk - no walkways, no train, no bus - avoid if possible!
Rubbish, hardly any places to eat at all. No bars in T3 c. Staff utterly miserable. Place was filthy as well. Avoid this airport if you can. Terrible experience.

Really good experience. Security was busy but extremely efficient - I was travelling with far too many laptops locked in security bags (long story) which obviously raised eyebrows. Everything got searched, lots of questions asked but so friendly and professional that it was really no hassle. Could've been awful but was actually as pleasant as it could have been. Great burger (surprise!) at Carl's once airside. Seating around the gates is a bit uncomfortable but it's there and there's enough of it. The gate itself was efficiently managed and there's room without a horrible crush. All in all a good experience, and one I'd be happy to repeat.
It is easily accessible from the city center by metro within 30 minutes. It is clean and modern. Employees are friendly and helpful. Signposts are clear. Goods are bountiful.

Enough space for everyone, didn't seem that crowded. Nice to see fast security checks and fast lines at check in. Also the staff at the AR counter were very nice and professional. Fast and free wifi. Just a bit boring on the boarding area since there is no shopping stores. Only 1 and it was closed.

Worst airport experience ever. Queue for passport control took 2 hours! When you got there, only 4 officers on yet 6 desk areas! And the ones that are in ‘attendance’ (they don’t work hard) … are SO SLOW - could not care less that the departure area is crowded by their inefficiency! Will not be back to Corfu airport.

Very unusual queue system here, somebody needs to go to other airports and bring back a foolproof system of queueing, as there seems to be no system here. Some staff were seen just chatting to each other rather than calling travellers up to check in. Security staff at passport control were chatting and laughing with each other rather than getting, hot, tired travellers through at a fast pace, not much consideration for elderly or people with disabilities were installed in their bizarre queueing system. Water was €6 for desperate travellers. No time to view duty-free shops due to queueing. Such a shame.

Crowded, limited seating, small selection of standard shops, no first class traveller lounge, no BA lounge. Caters mostly for package tourist market. Very poor and few departure board information. No information desk. One of the worst airports

As most of people here state the airport is brand new and clean but they schedule most of flights at the same time, in other words the arrival hall becomes a nightmare. We had to wait airborne for some 40 minutes before we were allowed to land due lack of ramp space. The airport is well connected with buses to town. On departure everything was pretty much smooth, but they let you wait outside waiting on the heat. During peak summer season I would avoid Corfu if I were you.

Impressed with this airport. Quick and easy process for arrival and departure. Yes we had to queue for passport control but they got through the lines reasonable quick. The luggage had still not hit the belts so we would have queued anyway. On departure the line again for both check in and passport control was quick. The food courts were excellent and great choice at very reasonable prices£6 for s/w. What I was more impressed weee the cleanliness of the toilets. Having had the worst experience through Heraklion this was a complete surprise. Well done Corfu. Very clean and modern

We booked a holiday with Tui/Marella Cruises and chose Corfu airport because it was close to the ship port. I am writing this message to warn others to avoid this airport if you are with TUI Marella Cruises and travelling on a Friday to Friday holiday to Corfu during the summer of 2023 for the following reasons: All the chartered TUI flights arrive within minutes of one another over a 3-hour time period causing absolute chaos at this very small and inadequate airport that is unable to support the approximate 2,000 passengers that are about to descend on it at this time every Friday. We waited on the plane for over an hour because we had to wait for passengers from other planes to disembark onto the buses that take you 100 meters. It was very hot and uncomfortable. The queue for passport control was another 2 hours wait standing squashed together - a claustrophobic nightmare! Fortunately, we did get inside the building, others were out in the blistering heat. Our baggage by this time had been thrown off the carousel and we had to hunt through piled-up luggage to retrieve it. I do not think this is the fault of Corfu Airport, this is TUI's fault (I suspect) for selecting a cheap airport and ship port to make more money from their holiday sales. The return journey from this airport could have been catastrophic. I believe that it is a health and safety issue and should be investigated immediately. Again, all the charted TUI flights depart at roughly the same time and the airport doesn't have the capacity. Once at the airport, you will see all the cruise passengers that had disembarked the ship 2 hours before you still standing outside the airport in the blistering heat waiting to check their bags in... and little do you know at that time, you will be joining them at the back of the queue which extends onto the road where the coaches are trying to turn around without knocking someone over. There is no shade. There are large coaches with exhaust fumes adding to the heat. If you are sensitive to sunstroke and heatstroke (like me) it will be hell. I had to leave my husband and go into the terminal. This was very upsetting. There was no space to move inside the terminal. All the departures were mixed up together and TUI staff were trying to squeeze groups through the crowds because their flights were about to leave. A long queue through security and straight onto the plane. No time for duty-free. No time for food. Then told when on the plane that Corfu Airport only has one lift for disabled passengers and we might miss our time slot... we were already delayed by 1 hour.

On arrival we had to wait 30 minutes on aircraft as two were disembarking passengers ahead of us. Once off we had to wait at least two hours to finally get through passport control. On our return flight we were queuing for at least 2 hours, we were advised to wear hats and have water, which I bought from the street food café opposite the terminal. Once inside the departure board told us to go to gate, however we were another hour and a half before we got near a check in desk. Much polite talking to the TUI Reps at the airport did not seem to help as did every bus turning up with more passengers to add to the frustration we were delayed as four people could not get through the check in line any faster. One who looked elderly and frail.

Absolutely the worst airport I've ever been to. Arriving was shocking, sat on the plane for over an hour because we needed a staircase and there wasn't one available, then waited for a bus to take us 10 feet. Queues through security etc were long hot and not very nice, but the way back was something else, coaches were dropping people off every 20-30 minutes or so but the queuess were not going down at all just getting bigger, we were waiting over two hours in 30 degree heat, no shade or water. It was inhumane and absolutely disgusting, its not fit for purpose as it is, it simply cannot cope with the traffic. I'd avoid this airport at all costs and I'm sure the hundreds that went through the day i did (23rd june) would agree, its a shambles. I can’t comment on food, seats or cleanliness because we never got to see it, by the time we got through check in, and security we had to run to the plane which was over an hour late to leave

The vehicles delivering passengers were skewed all over the road and passengers disembarking on the road. Had to queue outside the terminal for an hour. Had to queue for a further 45 minutes to drop baggage off. Then had another 20 minutes for passport control. The Greek staff were generally quite rude in their character. The terminal announcer gave incorrect gate details twice, causing some of the elderly passengers quite a bit of confusion. Once on the plane and delayed by an hour, the Captain announced he could not yet leave due to no ground staff being available to remove the stairs etc. Laughable all the way. Will not return.

Late evening arrival into CFU on the 4th May 23 arriving 10 minutes early from EMA. Deplaned quickly and minimal delay at passport control only due to 200 people disembarking at the same time, there were also several friendly assistants to help manage the queue and answer any questions. Baggage was starting to appear on the carousel as we entered the collection area so again no great delay and straight out to waiting transport. On our return journey, early evening departure 11th May small queue for checkin and baggage drop. Plenty of friendly JET2 staff to assist and pre tag cabin baggage so maybe a 20 minute delay but the queue was inside the building and 4 checkin desks open. Security again was very quick with only about 10 people in front of us, whilst I wouldn't say the security staff were unfriendly they were perhaps best described as efficient. Then into the departure lounge with more than enough seating for all the waiting passengers from various flights with a variety of shops and food and drink establishments available. Again passport control to gates was fast and friendly with no great delay and even at the gates there was food and drink available which looked very appetising. Flight boarded quickly and departed about 20 minutes behind schedule. It has to be said that since the completion of the refurbishment of this airport the experience is vastly improved. The toilets/washrooms are no longer an area to be feared and requiring a bio hazard suit to use. The whole airport is clean and bright with sufficent staff on hand. There is also a greater choice of food and drinks available. So a really pleasant and relaxing experience flying into and out of Corfu compared with previous occasions.

I recently passed through Cork Airport, and I must express my profound disappointment and frustration with the airport's security team. The level of rudeness and unprofessionalism I encountered was nothing short of appalling. From the moment I approached the security checkpoint, I was met with curt and condescending attitudes. The staff seemed more interested in exerting their authority than in assisting passengers or ensuring a smooth and respectful security process. Their behavior was unacceptably hostile, making an already stressful process even more unpleasant. I urge Cork Airport to address these issues promptly and ensure that their security staff is trained to treat all passengers with the respect and dignity they deserve. I sincerely hope that future travelers will not have to endure the same negative experience I did.

Combative and aggressive security staff. Swissport staff were very helpful. My flight was delayed by two hours so I got to the airport later (1 hour before my flight was going to leave). At the top of the security queue - my boarding pass would not scan. The person scanning boarding passes (not sure of his name) immediately said the flight had left (incorrect) and that I had to go down to the Ryanair check in desk to get a boarding pass printed (incorrect). His manner at this time was combative. After I spoke to Ryanair staff who were very helpful they instructed me to return to security where he got more and more combative - coming up extremely close to my face and repeating incorrect information repeatedly. The situation was resolved when a more senior member of security and operational staff instructed him to conduct a manual check on my boarding pass and allow me to pass through security.

The airport is small and easy to find one's way around. One member of staff seemed off hand. She wanted to check my suitcase after xraying so it was opened by her. She picked up items that there souvenirs and held them up to a colleague as though they were something more than souvenirs. This made me feel angry. No explanation was given as to what she was concerned about. I would not travel through Cork Airport again and do not recommend it to others.

My wife was carrying few items which were not allowed due to their oversize (more than 100ml). The officer obviously had to throw them away before she goes through the security. I was very upset to know as these items were medicated and not readily available I called the airport to enquire about the items and was to know, that the items were disposed off in the trash. I again called today and able to talk to the relevant person. He was very helpful and took the pains and advised the supervisor. Within half an hour I was called by the Sergeant who break the news that they found both the items. Obviously I was overjoyed and so grateful to the efforts made by the energetic and helpful staff at the Cork airport.

Really nice clean small airport in terms of actual experience. On arrival my Aer Lingus flight landed slightly ahead of schedule and I was airside within 10 minutes from leaving aircraft door. Immigration was a breeze and quick, and the person checking passports/IDs was friendly and welcoming. On departure security was fast and efficient and staff were relaxed and friendly. The departure area is small but has couple of food options given the size and there was decent duty-free area - although I think greater part of this could be allocated to local products especially food given some of the really great quality stuff I had during my stay in Cork. Toilets very clean and maintained, and gate areas had plenty of seating. The thing I loved though is they sell bottles of water for 1€, which you can just quickly tap and take from a stand - no price-gouging and they have a refill station centrally located if you need refill it before you take off or if you brought your own bottle, much better than Heathrow T2 when I left! The only thing that lets this airport down and why I have marked it down is poor information on its website before travelling (doesn't look like its been updated since covid) and poor transfers from the airport to the city on arrival. Taxis are expensive to the city at €20 given the distance. Bus to the city is regular service bus, not a dedicated airport shuttle, is only every half an hour in either direction, and you need 'Leap card' or euros, no cards accepted. This is inconvenient as international visitors won't necessarily immediately have the either of the former to hand - I was lucky that a kind stranger on the bus paid for me using their own Leap card as the bus was waiting when I arrived, if I had to go to get cash I would have missed it and had to wait half an hour for the next one. Once on the bus it isn't clear when you arrive in the city, as it is neither announced nor displayed on the electronic board, just random street names and the bus runs with the lights off inside so you travel in the dark and it is all rather disorientating. The stop in the city is also a random bus stop not the bus station which also makes it unclear where to get it from when you need to return to the airport from the city. I'm really perplexed why a city that has a lot of tourism has made it so difficult/inconvenient for visitors in this respect and its a shame as the experience at the airport itself was excellent.

I was very impressed by the level of care and support I received at the airport. Having a severe reaction to an insect bite and no Antihistamine tablets with me. The local team and Airport police, went out of their way to help (I wish I had noted their names), they looked everywhere and obtained tablets for me while making sure I was comfortable and relaxed. Thank you very much as the level of care and support at a busy airport was very welcome and impressive.

I have to agree with the review below. The security staff at this airport are extremely rude and aggressive. They seem to take it as a personal insult if you show some initiative (such as dare to pick up a tray yourself) to speed up the baggage scanning process. Move into an area of the conveyor belt that has space for three people but is only being used by one, and you can expect a volley of abuse from a staff member. The angry demeanour and lack of basic courtesy is absolutely astounding. I don't expect much from airport security staff, but these guys - or some of them, anyway - fail to meet even minimal standards of acceptable behaviour.

Overall, I don't mind Cork airport in itself. It's the security screening that annoys me every time. I commute from ORK twice per 9 days and I've done this the past 5 years. The problem is the security staff. Rude, distant and talking to you like you're 5 years old. As you're not allowed to pick up trays by yourself, you're always waiting with your hands full of items to screen separately (laptop, liquids, shoes etc). I aways place the items anyway on the counter in front of the security officer. Standing there with my shoes off and on the table and everything laid out before him, he doesn't even look at it but states loudly "do you have any liquids or laptops?". This happens every time. Last week I was asked to remove my shoes. I work in the airport in Oslo so I've purposefully bought a pair of Chelsea boots without metal in them and I ask why. "Because I need to see your ankles". I'm wearing a skirt with tights and don't see the need, but I comply because I know not to argue with security personnel. The two business men behind me were wearing leather shoes and suit pants that could fit an extra pair of legs in them but they don't have to "show their ankles" for anyone. That's Cork airport security staff for you.

As a regular user of Cork Airport, I have always had a excellent opinion of its services. Unfortunately, this morning while dropping a friend off, I experienced the lowest level of customer service I have in a long time. My friend forgot his phone charger at home and after realising this, I drove straight back to Cork Airport. I was unable to contact my friend who had most likely gone through security. On arriving at the airport, with ample amount of time before flight departure, I asked an employee of Aer Lingus, Ryanair and another company I cannot remember, could they please put a call out over the intercom to call my friend to the other side of security so I could pass the charger through. There is apparently no connection between the intercom system on both sides of security. As it was a Ryanair flight, I asked this specific employee could he please contact a Ryanair colleague at the other side of security to make an announcement so my friend could please get his charger. He couldn't do this. Why, he had no reason. I asked was there any other way, I could go about getting the charger to my friend. He said he couldn't do anything, but if I wanted to try asking security, I could. Of course he said, security probably wouldn't be able to do anything for me. I feel that from a customer service perspective, both by Ryanair and by Cork Airport, there is a complete sense of apathy and disregard for giving the highest level of customer service and simply trying to help your customers. I know this is just a minor example, but one would think in the service industry, employees would try their best to help their customers.

Security check personnel in Cork airport - I've never met the kind in any other airport, there appears to be no accountability and buckets of bad attitude. I tried to lodge a complaint today about a rude girl working there after she snapped at me and made a hand gesture to her colleague about me when I asked for her name (but was refused) and was told there was no facility to complain there. 95% of the employees working in security in Cork are nice and a pleasure to deal with but there are a few bad apples and their management should root them out or train some of them to lose the attitude.

The officer patrolling drop off was incredibly rude. I had two large bags and an Infant. My mother carried my daughter in for me while I checked my bag. There was no line so this didn’t take long. The officer started screaming about the truck demanding to know who it belong to and he said it was black so it didn’t register because it’s a deep navy blue. I was being helped at the desk and I said I’m nearly done it will be two seconds and he demanded now. I requested to speak with a supervisor who told me we were both wrong. I will avoid using this airport at all costs moving forward. No one deserves to be treated like that. I didn’t even get an opportunity to give my mother a hug goodbye. He knows who he is.

Corpus Christi is fine small airport. In remarkably good shape and well kept. Very simple and easy to navigate. TSA security was a breeze, no lines and all staff were actually very firendly. Not much offering pre-security but couple of shops and restaurants post security. Easy to get to just west of downtown.

It looks like a white elephant but what an elegant one! Corpus Christi appears to handle only connecting flights to Dallas and Houston (that's the international bit) with just three airlines operating there. It is light bright airy and wonderfully free of the normal hustle and bustle of a modern airport. Checking in took three minutes; passport control and security about the same - they have new full body scanner. Each airline has its own gate complete with airbridge to connect even to small planes.

Very small airport. Check-in starts 1.5-2 hours before departure. The small cafe on the right is the only place with a clean toilet and AC. When you have checked in there is nothing! It is the most boring airport. Filthy toilets. No info at all about departures - if they are late. You know when the planes are leaving - a lady shouts out. It is a bit of a joke but no waiting time due to the small size of the airport. The AC is not working outside the cafe so it is a bit too hot.

Actually more of a bus stop than an airport. There are no facilities besides a pharmacy and getting through security is pure horror. The whole thing simply looks as if it hasn't had the slightest bit of maintenance since the day it was built.

Modern facade entry and check-in ok though crowed when large planes are scheduled. However behind the easy border post it gets worse. Only restaurant (rather a shabby bar) before the security check. No refreshment facility after the slow security. So don't go to the airport too early (though the airline will urge you). It's terrible to sit more than an hour on very uncomfortable seats in the departure hall (if any available) or in the bar. European airlines have their own security check before boarding. Arrival is chaotic and terribly crowed if arriving on a larger plane particularly at the baggage claim. Be prepared to "fight" you through to the belt while receiving some elbow checks and bruises. Friendly staff.

I live in Valencia and work in the UK and use the round trip service fortnightly and have done so from the beginning with thomsonfly. Although the facilities are small and limited at Coventry this seemed to be reflected in the cheaper flight prices and at the same time suits my needs of a reliable bus service to and from Valencia. But recently I have noticed the flight prices increasing without the offer of discounts for regular flyers with this in mind I have looked elsewhere. Staff at Coventry are polite friendly and helpful but it will be all in vain if you have no customers.

Use the airport regularly and it's great parking facilities are next to the terminal so no need to go on a five mile cross country slog with children in tow nor wait for a packed shuttle boss and try and cram all luggage and children on board. As stated before the airport is small and basic (understatement) but then again I don't use airports to sit in or spend all my holiday money in shops before i even depart the UK something which I think happens at many of the larger airports. A very short walk from the terminal (the interim passenger facility as it is more technically known) to the plane and then you are away on your flight. Coming back is so easy as well the arrivals area is a seperate building from departures. If two planes arrive at the same time then I am under the impression that one has to wait for a short period of time foir the arrivals area to clear. However after disembarking getting through passport control and getting to the baggage claim belt we were waiting for about two minutes and then hey presto the bags started coming through. Again a very short walk to the car park (ever present taxis and an hourly bus service to/from the railway station and city centre are also available) and we were off...home within 30 minutes of landing...at a bigger airport just down the A45 I have been waiting for 30 minutes just for the baggage carousel to start revolving. All in #all it is basic but it does exactly what it says on the tin - it's a building (well two buildings) for passengers getting to or arriving from a city by air - and it does this with minimum of fuss and least amount of time. In some ways it is a good alternative for any inbound passengers wishing to avoid the congested London Airports - the bus to the railway station and frequent trains to the centre of London could have you in the capital very easily. Here's hoping for the new terminal an increase in services and more airlines. I know I shall be a regular user of Coventry Airport and so shall my friends family and colleagues for many years to come.

Flew from Coventry for the second time. We found the trick was to check- in and then go to the café across the road before continuing to departures. (There's nothing there but a little 'shop' and toilets.) Watch out if there's 2+ flights as the limited seating can fill quickly with full flights. No problems with the baggage or staff. Return flight was cancelled however due to 'inappropriate landing facilities' at the airport due to the bad fog. Small airport good in general but could do with some major improvement if there's going to be a big passenger increase.

This was the first time we had used Coventry Airport to travel to Barcelona. Having been used to departing from the larger airports oh how we laughed!! The porter cabin style check in and the cattle shed style arrivals made us laugh and laugh. The coffee shop was like having a cup of tea in your front room. What fun to be escorted to the plane by the same person who checked us in we wouldn't have been suprised if they had flown the plane too! The only hitch was when we arrived back there was already a flight in we were held on the plane while they found someone to escort us to the so called terminal? We giggled at the thought of someone shouting "Stan! Can you leave the loo cleaning and get the next lot off the Barcelona flight?" We will be using Coventry again if only for a good laugh.

I travelled from Coventry to Naples this year and found the airport limited but satisfactory. The checkin area reminded me of the old days with cardboard flight destination signs and this was an area that could be easily changed for the better. The lines crossed each other to the destinations and did cause some friction between customers. The car parking was an experience but again was satisfactory. I do not understand why the local bus companies especially those going to Leamington. Stratford do not call in. On returning the baggage was certainly a LOT better than Birmingham so a plus there. In the departure lounge there was a good choice of food and drink at great prices - no rip off here. Also a small point . The newspapers were out and available from about 0500. Birmingham they are still under wraps at 0600. Good value and friendly. Hope they get permission for the bigger one soon.

Before departure it is impossible to find drinking water or a socket to charge a mobile phone. They extend the airport for Wizz Air but there is no chance to bring Ryanair and provide better prices. Nothing to buy using your card, only by cash.

The flight departure from Paris Beauvais to Craiova (Romania). Is not the first time this company are not landing the flights, meteo conditions, fog. This time the plane landed at Bucharest, where nobody are waiting the passengers, find a solution. The only solution they have is to go back to Craiova in a bus. I was forced to find a solution with my money, to reach my destination. The problem is, the flight attendant knows the plane will not be landing at Craiova, but the plane must go back, and you are informed during the flight. Is the weather conditions in Craiova are not good enough to land safely they have to close this airport. I'll try to find another company.

The airport is very, very small when arriving. However, it is clean and staff are kind. When leaving the check out is done outside and some companies are not as efficient as others but the airport is at no fault. When leaving, there are two relatively small waiting room with limited selection of snacks and duty free. Based to buy souvenirs and keepsakes before the airport. The people are what make this airport pleasant, they are friendly and work very hard.

Small airport but airport location wonderful. Don't have boarding bridge. Ground staff are very fast. No need to wait for a long time to check in bags. I got my bag on arrivals right after reaching the belt - very fast. Staff are friendly. No shops inside airport. 2 taxi counters before arrival gate.

Flying in to Tobago airport you will find minimal facilities with x-ray or your baggage being the norm (you'll wait a while for your cases!). The experience when flying back out was underwhelming. The 'check in' area is outside the main building in the heat long queues and staff who are happy to chat to eat other mill about and lack any kind of customer service. You'd expect that 'departures' is open all the time. Nope. Again you have to wait outside with no aircon - just a ceiling mounted fan just outside the entrance - and wait until the staff decide they're ready/bothered to 'open'. The best I can say is that the grunts of communication were followed up by pointing at what you needed to do and where to go. Appalling and very slow. The departure lounge itself has air con but the plastic seats (part of the airport upgrade!) are shockingly uncomfortable. If you want duty free shopping you're limited to a small shop about the size of a single bedroom with vodka rum and a few bits and bobs a perfume/soap shop and souvenir stall with t-shirts keyrings and beach bags. There is a small counter area where you can buy drinks and snacks (this is not Costa). You may be sad to leave Tobago but the airport will encourage you to get on your flight.

By far the worst Caribbean airport I have had the misfortune to ever visit. Arrived with Monarch unfortunately Monarch Cabin crew wrongly advised passengers with children under 18 they only had to fill one immigration form with the child's details on the back (which is what the form says). Having queued for over 90 mins to be told we needed to fill a form for each person multiply that 10 to 15 times on our flight chaos ensued. One fan in that whole arrivals hall had youngsters fainting after the 9 hour flight. When we got past passport control we got to baggage reclaim with the fastest belt I have ever seen (great that allowed quick retrieval of cases) only to join another queue to get our luggage X-rayed the same cases that were x-rayed at Gatwick as we waited the baggage belt overfilled with the passengers from row 16 back to row 40+ on the plane jammed at the exit door and piled into each other causing a jam with no airport staff to be seen a passenger eventually hit the stop button. We eventually got out after 2 hours the airport maybe be able to handle endless ATR-72s from Trinidad but not an A330 and Monarch have been going there since at least 2005 when I was in transit from Grenada. I love the Island but would never come back through the airport where no welcome was given anyone tourist or resident.

I have been once to this airport as others said the place is tiny I wonder how it looks when BA and Virgin are around. Boarding into small propeller planes is already a mess they search your bags at the boarding area even though you have already had your carry-on x-rayed.

I have used Crown Point airport 5 times over the last 6 years and each time I return I pray the airport service has improved. Unfortunately this has not been the case. Customer Service remains a missing module from the staff training. I can only imagine that much training is dedicated to being rude and unhelpful to the weary travellers. The security staff appear to be on a mission on to be as difficult possible searching everyone irrelevant it the metal detector beeps or not. And the words please and thank you devoid from their vocabulary. On my last departure from Crown Point (and it will be my last) two international flights were due to leave within 2 hours of each other. The duty free had no cigarettes and the alcohol was extremely limited. The cafe (charging inflated prices) had no sandwiches and were ill prepared for the demand. Two staff took 5 mins to serve one person with 1 bottle of water. The ladies toilets has three cubicles and a queue to match a bank holiday sale in Harrods. I strongly recommend the management of Crown Point visit somewhere like Thailand to see how you can be efficient and polite. Crown Point International Airport I think not. Good luck if you use it to depart from you will need it with lots and lots of patience.

Arriving at the airport was quick and easy. However trying to leave the island is difficult is not extremely unpleasant. The few shops in the departure lounge were closed when we got through customs. Even though we had plenty of time and were the only 2 people waiting they would not let us go downstairs and get any food or water. They were rude and made it perfectly clear they were annoyed with us. On top of that they kept telling us to stay on one side of the departure area. Just make sure you get whatever food/drink/souvenirs you want before going upstairs to the departure gate.

Outdated tiny airport. If a large plane is either disembarking or embarking the facilities are stretched beyond capacity. The staff are not properly trained and often rude. The Caribbean Airlines flights to Trinidad can be a hit and miss affair and if one if using Tobago Crown Point to transfer from an international flight to a Trinidad bound flight or vice versa be prepared to be told that your flight is overbooked delayed cancelled.

I flew into and out of Crown Point from Frankfurt once flew out of of Tobago to Trinidad and on two other occasions tried to do just that without success. The airport is very small mostly handling flights from and to Trinidad. There are very few amenities inside but most of the crucial ones on the concourse just outside (ATM fast food etc.). The staff at migrations and customs upon arrival was friendly and helpful but flying from Crown Point proved an utter nightmare on two occasions. While international flights are handled relatively smoothly the staff dealing with the short-haul Caribbean Airlines trips to Trinidad was exceptionally incompetent and unhelpful. Several flights were cancelled and at no point were passengers informed of this fact. Time and again long queues formed at the check-in counter which none of the about ten people standing behind this counter believed necessary to attend for three (!) hours. When asked to provide even the most essential information on which to base a decision staff would still not inform us about the cancellation of the flight. In the end we spent one entire day at this airport without being able to fly. By far the most shocking airport experience I have had in many years of travelling compounded by unbelievably rude and unqualified staff. My only advice is to take the ferry when travelling from Tobago to Trinidad.

Camilo Daza Airport serves Colombia's largest border city, Cúcuta. Access to the airport is quite easy as is moving inside it. Check-in process is fast and hassle-free. Staff is quite professional and courteous. Free wifi with excellent speed. The airport is being remodelled and although small in size, will be more beautiful and pleasant to use. There are just a few shopping choices which is a drawback and the food court is also small and limited in variety. Once improvements are over, it will certainly be a more efficient and agreeable airport.

After the renovation, the airport is nicer, but it is still very hot inside, the terminal is not very clean, there are very few shopping and eating options. There is more seating that it used to have, but it is still not enough. Because the airport is small, the queues are quick. The staff are nice. The wifi is terrible, it is usually fails to connect, but when it does connect, it is very slow. The airport is getting better, but there are still many things to improve.

For the size of Curaçao, the airport is adequate. Its modern aesthetic provides a sense of travel elegance and comfort. The eight-gated facility offers ample dining, snack, and shopping options. Check-in at 9 a.m. was smooth, and security checks were efficient. The following is heavily influenced by a deeply negative experience. I believe I suffered one of the worst injustices a traveler can face. I saw my suitcase for the last time as it was placed on the conveyor belt. It was never loaded onto my plane, nor was it scanned onto any departing plane from the island. Despite the airport having only eight gates and a single conveyor belt—where any fallen luggage would likely be noticed—United took three weeks to conclude it was lost. It was stolen, not lost. Words cannot adequately express the violation I felt. Therefore, I strongly recommend tagging your luggage with tracking technology, such as an AirTag, to monitor its location. Would an AirTag have changed the outcome in my situation? I cannot say. However, it might have provided a more positive impression of Curaçao than I currently have. Additionally, if you are taking a propeller plane for island hopping and it is raining, bring a poncho or umbrella, as there is considerable outdoor walking required to reach the aircraft.

My Mom required wheel chair service and we received superb service, especially on our departure by Devon. He ran to get my Mom as there was a gate change and looked for me as I was getting a snack for her. None of the crew advised us but there was Devon, with his wonderful smile!

The toilets are the cleanest I have seen I'm years. The customs was quick and efficient. I travel every year to Curaçao and was a pleasure to see that they are much better than Schiphol, Las Americas, American airports, European airports.

Be Aware! Arrival at the airport was okay, the immigration line was long but it moved pretty quickly. The airport was clean and looks pretty new. Our main problem with this airport, is the departure security check point, where you have to apparently place all liquids below the authorised limit in ziplock bags. Nowhere in the airport is there a sign saying that all liquids must be in clear plastic bags. The check in agent said nothing, nothing from the airline and did I say no signs. We got to security and were told to throw away our items or pay $1US per ziplock bag. If that didnt feel like an organised racket then I don't know what else qualifies. This type of action is dishonest in every respect, but at that point we had no choice. We've travelled through London Luton and they have the same plastic bag policy but not only are signs of it everywhere, they provide the bags. This felt like a shady scheme and we quite honestly will try to avoid this airport in future. P.S. Duty free alcohol was cheaper in out home country as well.

Immigration reasonably quick and cheerful, baggage reclaim takes a long while. I know it’s a big plane and a small airport but waiting 40 minutes for the first bag to arrive is not really on. Particularly when there appeared to be no other arrivals. Departures worked like a dream. No queues for immigration or security so top marks for leaving.

The security check is very over zealous, threw my liquids away because I had no zip lock plastc bag in spite of the fact that I came back witha zip lock plastic bag bought 1 USD @ at Britshop. I had thus my medicine put in the trash. Is there any frustration from this people? No lounge for business travelers because of construction. A coupon instead, so you can have a beer. Very bad experience.

Arrival was okay, departure was a disgrace. Check-In at the drop-off counter went fast, but then we had to wait 45 minutes in a queue because there was only one person to check boarding passes for hundreds of passengers for two planes (there we two control counters, though, but the second was not occupied). Then we had to wait 30 minutes for the luggage checking (only two rows, one of which closed directly after us, and the last 40 or 50 passengers had to do with only one row. Then another 30 minutes queue at the passport control. We had not even been controlled yet when they already rung the last call for our flight. By the way, buy your Blue Curaçao in the duty free in front of the passport control. They had the lowest prices of the whole island

Departure hall clean, spacious and air conditioned. Well organised queuing system with KLM staff tagging hand baggage in advance to make check in run smoothly. Each airline had their own desk. Security fast, just remember to have your red immigration card. Food outlets fine but limited. Shopping limited as two shops sold the same items. Duty free had a good range of perfume and drinks but beware if you are European, and outside the Eurozone, prices are more expensive for cosmetics than what you would pay in High Street shops. Didn't fully investigate alcohol but you need to look carefully for offers and compare them to a local supermarket. We weren't travelling with children but I didn'notice any play facilities on offer. Seats OK. Arrival Hall just had fans, but didn't have to wait long for luggage. There are toilets in the baggage reclaim hall, these were clean and well maintained. For a small island a really good airport.

Curaçao is an important hub in the Southern Caribbean. In terms of quality of services provided, facilities, friendliness of staff and officials, it doesn't come close to the level of other hubs, e.g. St. Maarten. Although some cosmetic upgrades were made, the facilities are in dire need of modernization. The food courts are a rip off, horrible menu items at exorbitant prices, taking advantage of your misery during long layovers and the usual delays, having no choice, but to purchase inferior nutrition. The air conditioning never seems to work properly and you have to be lucky to even log on to the public wifi. Forget about any business correspondence via email and seeking refuge in the below standard executive lounge. If you can, avoid the airport.

Flew in with AB from DUS. CUR is a small Airport that has drastically improved over the years overall it is looking great for its size. However it is clear the Airport cannot handle the traffic though I suspect This could also be poor planning. IC Flights to DUS and AMS open at the same time. Together with regional flights it's simply too much for the Airport to handle without impact on customer service and comfort. Massive queues everywhere. Check-In Security Immigration Toilets and even at the Shops etc. All because approximately 1000 pax are at the airport at the same time.

Cusco airport is not big, but it is very organized and does have boarding bridges. This airport 3300m high from sea level. Excellent view from aircraft's. This airport is always busy. There are some shops and staff are helpful. However, it does need more seating because I saw many passengers standing up. Free wifi is only available for 10 minutes.

We flew from Cusco to Juliaca recently on a trip to Peru. This airport is kind of odd. It is not an extremely busy airport, but is really too busy for it's size. This may have happened recently because we flew into and out of Cusco five years ago, and I don't remember it being crowded. There isn't adequate seating (many people were standing), the shops and food choices were few, and check in was chaotic. I have read that the airport's limitations have been noted by local officials, and a new airport is being planned nearby but could be some years away. I would recommend this airport because it isn't terrible, and there is really no other choice.

Cusco Airport is another wonderfully crowded and poorly designed airfield in Peru (i.e. Lima, Chiclayo). Byzantine brutalist concrete architecture aside, this airport is by far the worst designed for providing any kind of logical 'flow' for a single-runway airport serving a large metropolitan area. It would seem that nobody in government has looked at what can be done with the cramped space and volume of passengers to try and make a more hospitable, clean and user-friendly facility. Unfortunately, this airport will remain the sole thoroughfare for all international Machu Picchu travelers for the foreseeable future. Maybe Peru can step up to the plate and make some major changes to this facility and take a field trip to Quito, and check out their new airport which is very nice.

We were stranded in line for LAN Peru at the Cusco airport. Due to LAN's incompetence, it took over 3 hours for us to talk to someone. Their customer service folks were not able to rebook us, and took forever to deal with each traveling group. Not enough reps were there either. As time wore on the problems with the airport restrooms became aggravated. No toilet paper and at 8pm, no more flushing or washing of hands. They shut off the water! Not enough seating and they had all the doors open so it was freezing. We couldn't get out of line or lose our places. No food or water available after 8:30pm for sale anywhere in the airport. We couldn't leave until we saw the rep so stuck in the freezing cold. Upstairs waiting area being torn up and not enough seating either.

Large crowds. Information Center gave misleading information as to where to que. Waited 10 minutes in wrong. The 2nd time, she gave us the wrong que and had to double check with her. Long queue for Security Check. Immigration officer rude and dismissive. Not wanting to assist. One of the worst airport I have come across. Almost missed our plane.
Nice, clean but crazy expensive food. 5 USD for a Cappuccino, 7 for a Bánh Mì. Besides that it's a nice airport with all facilities you can expect

Both food and souvenir prices are outrageous, and they are indicated in USD, maybe a better to rip travellers off. $12 to $20 dollars for a bowl of pho, over $20 for Burger King, not even mentioning the drinks. Restaurant offer very limited, not even a proper coffee shop to seat down A very bitter way to say goodbye to Vietnam…

First and only visit to Đa Nang on a transit back in Oct 2022. No complaints overall - easy navigation, not crowded, amenities were up to expectations considering it to be only 3rd largest airport in Vnam. Immigration was surprisingly nice, asked me for a CS survey which I was delighted to do. Staff was also friendly, put me on priority queue to my connecting flight international to domestic. Fast and efficient, everything was done quickly. Would love to fly there again as soon as I get the chance.
Food and beverage are too high in price. It’s not worth. The immigration need to be queued with long line. I really love Da Nang city, so hope the airport could improve it in the future.
