Appalling. Food was exorbitantly expensive, more so than any international airport I have ever visited. I felt like a cow being milked for money during my final hours in this beautiful country. What a disappointing end to my time in Vietnam. Security staff were extremely rude and inattentive. Long painful lines manned by a a single security checkpoint kiosk (all other security kiosks were not staffed). A number of tacky souvenir stores that all sell the same products at rip off prices. Dirty toilets as well. Make sure you eat (and do anything else that may cost you money) before you travel to Da Nang Airport. The international terminal made me feel like I was being scammed.
Too expensive - prices almost like Switzerland. Cannot waiting in this airport with prices so high. One coffee $5 dollars. Customs services so bad and the tax is too much
Efficient and clean airport. Just one tip stop broadcasting on your airport tv’s very loud an aggressive films there are children in the airport and it is annoying noise

Horrible airport, avoid at all cost. The only airport that charged me for my bag after traveling throughout Asia for a month. The prices inside are appalling, more expensive then the airports in the US. Rude customer service and just utterly ridiculous for a Vietnamese airport. Disgusted with the prices the service and fees. Don’t expect any special services.

Terrible airport. Flew with Qatar Airways, terrible queues, security were on a power trip - just awful and the costs inside are appalling - pure rip-off. It's a shame as could be so great with respect and not trying to triple charge for refreshments, or in case of water 5x the price. Not good when water is a necessity when travelling.

I was not very impressed by this airport but I guarantee that it is well run if compared to its neighbors. They use jet bridge for bigger airplanes and deplaning is very quick. Immigration takes forever as every single officer really makes sure they know where you are staying and what you plan to do in the country, with me they were nice, but I saw them being nasty towards other travelers, Senegalese included. The WiFi did not work for me, but on arrivals you can buy a sim card in minutes, ATM's are also plenty and dispense local currency without major charges. The ride from this airport is very expensive for Africa, 40 euros one way as the airport is located some 43 km outside downtown Dakar. Keep that in mind when planing to get to the airport as traffic in this city can be a nightmare.

A brand new airport opened for Dakar in 2018, called Blaise Diagne. It's infinitely better than the old one mentioned in other reviews on this page, which is no longer in use. The new airport is clean and modern, with helpful staff. Once inside, I felt like I was already in Europe. I had no problems with security or checked baggage.

Dakar Airport is old and slow and in pretty bad shape. There are no bridges, it's bus only. Lines at passport control both in an out can get very long. There is only a single security check point on the way out. Luggage delivery can take an extremely long time (60+ minutes) especially when multiple flights arrive around the same time. There is no transit facility. To transfer you have to go through immigration and security again.

Dakar airport has not changed in the last 30 years, still a big untidy mess with busses to go to the planes. On arrival, same old passport booths (you better speak French), but they have started to take finger prints and pictures (like in all other African airports, the capturing of biometric data is totally useless as anybody can get into the country by driving through the desert or bush). On departure, finger printing again on a machine that has not been cleaned for months - disgusting! A new airport has been built 30km outside of the city, but they will only open it when Senegal has a national carrier!

New Year Eve 21.00-23.30 . Standard control and luggage transfer after arrive from Madrid. Chaos and no information about belt. No trolleys. No fresh air. 3 hours for standard control before return flight. 8 passport checks. Police 'confiscating' packed standard AA alkaline batteries left same batteries unpacked. No information in English language. About 30 seats for passengers of 3 flights.

Flew out from Senegal to Madrid. Check in is clean bright and very efficient at the Iberia desk. security was rigorous but very well mannered. Passport control wasn't quick. Airside not too bad range of shops but the cafe sells the worst coffee I have ever drunk. For some reason all European flights take off late at night but save that we took off only 5 minutes late. Been to far worse American airports than this. Promise of a new airport seems some way off but would not be adverse to departing from there again.

Transiting in Dakar airport from Cape Verde to New York. Bussed in from the plane waited for a while at the space marked "Transit" until someone arrived (with some prodding). Then he said I shouldn't go through there (as I had a European passport) I should "faire le tour" meaning go through immigration. Anyway he let us in and then someone came to the transfer desk but said "No we can't do this here you have to 'faire le tour'". So (luckily have a UK passport so didn't need visa) I filled out the entry form queued up went through immigration and past baggage claim then found a queue to get into the check-in area and a monster crowd around the check-in desks. Happily as I was in business class and had no bags to check and was anyway on transfer they let me by-pass the queues to check in and then by-pass most of the amazing queues for immigration to leave Senegal again. But it still took an astonishing 90 minutes from getting off the bus to arriving back in the departure gate and got to the really comfortable business-class lounge.

Flew in from Joburg on a New York bound flight landed at 2am and was the only English speaking person in the air port. Despite my surfboard being lost and difficulties explaining what a surf board is arrival was fairly easy. Airport very shabby and old looking but this is west africa. Customs was virtually non existent on arrival but strict on departing. Beware of the Taxis and the people offering to change money for you. A taxi to Dakar should cost no more than 8 to 10 cfa dont be conned. Look for a cab away from the entrance near the bus stop (across road on the right side) is your best bet. Don't be harassed and don't get into a taxi with more than the driver onboard. Keep your wits about you.

Fresh breeze with a smell of seaweed that you might experience when you leave the plane. You will then probably end up in a long slowly moving queue for the passport control still dressed in your much-too-warm clothes from Europe. Last time we passed there the area beyond the passport control was crowded and rather chaotic. To pass quietly the customs control without any checking was therefore not so difficult. Travellers not used to African conditions will probably also find the taxi drivers quite difficult to handle; have an appointment with somebody beforehand if possible. On departure the main difficulty was to find the right counter; otherwise it went smoothly. Anyway the Senegalese seem to be aware that the situation is not the best possible for a new airport is said to be underway. We flew Air France. As Delta Airlines has a code-share on this flight one would expect check-in staff to have some knowledge of English but that was hardly the case. Should not Delta Airlines demand that their customers can be served in English?

We read the 130 1-star reviews of Dalaman Airport on this website before our trip, and were still appalled at how accurately awful this was. This is by far the worst airport we have ever been to among 20+ countries. Departures- There is only free wifi at the kiosks in the check-in area (good luck finding them), otherwise you have to pay for WiFi. Arrivals- no wifi at all. Yes, you will be arriving in a foreign country without any wifi. Most shocking are the extortionate food prices. A McDonald’s Big Mac meal actually costs £20, water is nearly £4. If it’s in TL, do the conversion with a calculator (as you won’t have WiFi) to avoid the heart attack. Most of the other food places are in EUR, so you’ll already know you’re paying €23 for a doner kebab meal. We winced watching families buy food here- easily £100 gone. If possible pack food at your hotel, and if not seriously just wait to buy food on the plane- somehow it’s cheaper! There are three different security checks. 1) at the airport entrance, 2) after immigration control, 3) at the gate. They are all poorly manned with incompetent staff shouting and grabbing your belongings for no reason. The 3rd security check is the worst of all, as they will pat you down, dump out your bag, spread everything on the table for the whole flight to see, and supposedly swab for drugs with some box on wheels. Everything feels a phony at this airport- they expect you to believe security agents wearing plastic cleaning gloves touching you up and fondling your belongings will find something that the metal detectors and X-ray machines haven’t. In short, avoid this airport at all costs. If you must fly from Dalaman, mentally prepare yourself and your wallet. After being robbed for food, you’ll be treated like a criminal at the gate. Pro: The airport looks nice, very modern and clean.

Dalaman airport has got to be one of the most poorly managed, terrible places I have ever had the displeasure of being. The prices are absolutely ridiculous nearly £2 for a bottle of water. My main issue however is the staff at DLM. during my time there a child was sick on the floor and not a single wellness check was given nor was the puddle of vomit cleaned up for a good 25 minutes despite the fact at least 8 staff members (cleaners included) stepped over said puddle. whilst there we were taken for random searches during this one of the staff members groped my partner complaints about this have been filed with both the airport and airline we flew with but still yet to hear anything back.

Terrible airport, 11 euros for the worst cheese and ham roll you will eat ,wanted 5 euros for a small snickers bar. Security way over the top! Bags xrayed 3 times then singled out for hand luggage checks at boarding gate - everything out the bag, case off tablet and kindle, everything swabbed for drugs or explosives, supposed to be random but Turkish waved through while families who are not a risk are checked excessively!

Worst airport ever. Rude staff at passport control and at security. Cost of food is extortionate, €20 for basic MacDonalds, I paid 30€ for four basic drinks and small snacks. I am well travelled and this is by far the worst airport I have ever had the misfortune to depart from. It has put me off returning to Turkey, I am not surprised that tourism is on the decline.

This is the worst airport I have ever been to. As soon as you are dropped at departures, you are hounded with men pretending to work for the airport to try and get tips for wheeling your luggage to the airport door for you. When you refuse, they will become aggressive. Be advised, some will be dressed in official looking uniforms, others in clothes resembling someone travelling. I raised with airport staff and was met with a vacant stare. Enhanced security checks are in place, I understand this is a Turkey wide thing and not just related to Dalaman. The prices inside the airport are obscene. Be prepared to pay a minimum of €20 for a burger king meal, and €5+ for a soft drink. There are very little places to sit whilst waiting, and then when your gate is called you will have your hand luggage opened and every item spread across a table to be checked by security. This is by far the worst airport I have ever been to.

Scammers out front harassing you right away trying to help with bags that get aggressive when you refuse help. One even grabbed me when I refused to pay and ran away when he seen a police officer. Security then throw your bags through scanners and rush you to collect your things when you have multiple cases. Then the food court is ridiculously priced, I paid £18 for two bottles of water and 2 packets of chewing gum! Total scam and shambles of an airport, you even have to pay extortionate prices for WiFi the whole experience is painful and expensive.

The airport is ridiculous you have to pay €20 euros for WiFi. This is 2024, and you denying humans of the basic necessities. How are we meant to contact family and friends about our arrival without being scammed by Dalaman airport for €20 as soon as you arrive/departure.  I have never experienced this before with tui. This has put me off traveling to Turkey just out of principle.

Arrival was very good, no fuss at all. Bought duty free cigarettes which were very well priced (booze ended up being cheaper in UK sadly). The departures though is just incredibly stressful. I can't stand security at the best of times but it's so over the top here. I do not know if it's the norm for the turkey but the checks before boarding the aircraft were incredibly panic and anxiety inducing. They make you feel like a criminal and do drug swabs all over you and your stuff. I will also mention the prices are criminal and you should 100% avoid spending any money inside this airport. Water and food is cheaper on the plane.

The double security at this airport was not explained to us in advance so that was a suprise. The lady at the gate for the wheelchair access kept us waiting until all the people in the queue already waiting had gone through which we thought was reasonable. She then kept us waiting while she let hoards of people who arrived after us through, then she kept us waiting while no-one was actually in the queue but every so often people would arrive (it was becoming slightly irritating by this point). Unfortunately we don't speak Turkish and she didn't speak any English so we don't know why we were kept waiting all this time while no-one else was in the queue. Her only job would have been to lift the barrier and let us through to the wheelchair access route. We were only allowed through when someone working at the airport arrived pushing a wheelchair otherwise I think we would still be there. She looked really peeved that she had to let us through following after them. In comparison, the security guys in the area we were waiting to get through to were really helpful and friendly.

You don't really have a choice, as this is the only airport in the area, especially if you are going to Oludeniz or Fethiye. But if you can avoid this prison. From your very first steps into the airport you are subjected to x-rays and bag checks that's before you even check in. The staff are about as cheerful and welcoming as what you'd expect when signing into His majesty's Prisons. Once you've checked in... onto passport control and the 2nd bag check. 5 flights leaving in the space of a few hours. So how many gates open? 2 and one for the prison guards... once you've finally managed to get through and you've had your belongings thoroughly checked your through to the Duty Free, which you'll need to remortgage your house and sell your feet pics on Onlyfans to get a bottle of whisky and some sweets for your colleagues at work... Nevermind, the food court can't be as expensive.. Nope double priced meal deals. I could not get my head around the simply outrageous "Meal Deal" from Eat ups! A stale sandwich and small Fanta for £13 pounds... it was even advertised as a "Deal". Oh the WiFi is unreachable as you need a code from the kiosk but no one has it... the paid "super" WiFi work though... shock. And finally when your gate is called and you can escape this prison... you have all your belongings swabbed and yet another scan. Guess it's security and it would stop any potential security threats, but this is too much. Love Turkey, but this Dump leaves a sour taste when leaving. Positives: it's clean.

Flew from Dalian to Beijing on China Southern Airlines. We arrived in good time to check in, along with about 10,000 others trying to check in for their flights. There were 20 desks but no organised queuing system and it was a mad crush until we managed to push our way to check in. Passport control was similar, hundreds if not thousands all lining up to pass through the many desks and lots of people were just rushing up to the front to avoid the lengthy wait. The security checks for hand luggage etc. after we had passed through passport control were quick, organised and incredibly thorough. On arrival at our departure gate, there was another chaotic scene as some passengers for an earlier flight who had been refused boarding were making a stand and refusing to leave, threatening the staff who had left their post to hide behind a locked glass door. Police arrived but just stood there and allowed the rioting passengers to continue with their shouting and throwing furniture around. This went on for some time, until after the departure time of our plane, which was unable to get to the gate because the earlier flight had not left yet. Nobody spoke English and there was no information on the boards regarding our delayed flight. Eventually there was a mad rush to a gate 200yds away, we followed and eventually boarded our plane. We arrived at Beijing three hours late and missed our connection back to London with BA. The hassle we had rebooking and securing accommodation for the extra night would take up many pages, although BA were very good.

Arrived in the domestic section in the evening. Bags out quickly no matching of the bag-tag to the baggage receipt as can be the case in other airports. Left on the international side the following morning. Check-in reasonably quick. No waiting for passport control. Security check also quick though followed up by a pat-down. Once airside the food options are limited. The small smoky cafe served very expensive filter coffee at 38RMB (espresso machine broken) but the Udon noodles at 40RMB were excellent. Shopping limited. The Terminal is bright nice and airy though fairly small - only five gates in the international section. When taxiing you get a nice view of the military airport the closest foreigners will get to seeing chinese airforce planes.

Excellent airport with ample space and good architecture. Check-in very efficient. Immigration officers very friendly because now there is a small machine on the left side with which you can evaluate the service of service of the officer from poor to excellent in 5 grades. It is true that it doubles as a military airport but you could have a rare sight of military jets standing nearby.

Dalian Airport is ok. It is a large “new” terminal now with both the old and new buildings not exactly seamlessly combined. Check in for both domestic and international flights is straight forward. Look at the departure board and go to the appropriate window. Security is also easy. Don’t put your ticket away as they need to see it along with your passport and boarding pass. Delays are common due to the bad weather in the area- seems to me they built the airport in the foggiest part of the city. High winds also cause problems and the fact the civil airport doubles as a military base means there is no prize for guessing who gets priority. Don’t go there hungry or you will have to pay high prices for average Chinese or Korean food. The usual snack shops are plentiful but expect to pay for it. Toilets are bearable but (as with all toilets in China) don’t forget to take some paper from the dispenser near the wash area as there is none provided in the individuals cubicles. I guess they think you will steal it if they leave you alone with it long enough. Despite the smoking rooms provided Chinese still insist on smoking in the toilets so you have to put up with that discomfort too.

Worst airport ever. Be prepared to throw away any duty free items you purchased elsewhere if coming from an international airport and have a connection here. They will also make you go through security again - the worst tsa security, if connecting here. Be prepared to let with any alcohol, perfumes etc if you purchased them at an international duty free. The flight was also delayed. There was no food open at the gate. Very old outdated and big. Will never book a flight with a connecting flight here again.
Terminal E has very few food options. None healthy. No place to get a magazine, snack, book. It's like solitary confinement. Bring food and reading material

Terrible customer service. Wife requested wheelchair assistance, none to meet her on arrival. No one would do anything to assure us that one would help her down the ramp to the airplane. Left us at gate B17 then changed to he gate to B11. She had to walk the distance.

Was told multiple times that our luggage was put on a flight we switched to. MULTIPLE times by multiple people. They did not. They were put on our original delayed flight that overlapped with the boarding of our last flight and they were not moved in time. If we were just told there was no guarantee we would not be so upset. Rude staff and unclean conditions make this airport one of my least favorites.

I'm absolutely appalled by the staff of this airport, first of all the plane was delayed which made me almost miss my flight by 2 minutes. To make it even worse they couldn’t get the jetway to work, it also took 25 minutes to get from the runway to the terminal which is not up to my standards. Me and my family said both the flights were to close. Now the problem that has made me absolutely unsatisfied is that Dallas did not scan 2 of the bags which contained my dads VERY expensive football shirts, all my VERY expensive makeup, dirty washing we need to clean. Overall my experience was absolutely the worst, i’ve never experienced such service like this bearing in mind I fly almost every single year.

The wheelchair attendant verified everything for me! Verified with me, verified with the LYFT driver by asking his name, verify the LYFT ride by licenses plate, verified I felt ok and I knew where I was going. For me, it's humiliating to be pushed in a wheelchair. I never felt humiliation this time. I truly felt cared for. This trip wasn't the greatest vacay I've had but when I got home, I felt great. I want to thank this positive, smart, caring young man. Some ppl have a gift, a few share it in this way. If your lucky enough to meet this young man at DFW Airport, you'll know it's him I'm talking about here.

Absolutely horrible experience! Hardly no staff working the lanes in customs, a line in security closed as people were trying to go through, the entire staff was extremely rude. The airport is also very outdated and set up very inconvenient and confusing.

5 skytrains passed. Lots of people waiting. Horrible! Terminal C to terminal A wasn’t that long but really? One would think it’s efficient and quick- the airport was packed. Was good on the 80’s but more people travel. Time to do a major overhaul. Bathrooms were few and far they are tiny-3 or 4 stalls and 4 urinals so have to wait for someone else to get done before you can Will not be a choice in the future to fly through Dallas anytime soon

What's not to like about DFW. You can park at any terminal and take the SkyLink to whichever terminal you're departing from. Departure from Terminal E and arrival at Terminal A. Parked across from Terminal E United Airlines gates. TSA-Pre took a little bit longer than usual to clear (10 minutes). Both Terminals A & E are spacious with plenty of shops and dining options. Terminals were clean.

Very limited seating while waiting for a flight. In addition it seems that all the flights are scheduled out of the same gate area which causes the congestion. Also has poor information on how to get from terminal to terminal. However when you do figure out how to get to the next terminal the tram is an easy experience.

What's not to like about Dallas Lovefield. The airport terminal is very clean with brightly lit spacious concourses and with plenty of seating. Distances from the security area to either end of the terminal are manageable. WiFi is easy to connect to and fast. Going through TSA-Pre took less than 5 minutes. The TSA officers were polite and courteous. Notwithstanding temporary closure of 2 eateries, there were plenty of other options for breakfast for our early morning departure. On our return to DAL a week later, the terminal was basically deserted with almost all eateries and concessions shut for the evening.

Given the early morning departure, only fast food restaurants were open. The terminal was not crowded and there was plenty of seating at the gates. Terminal is bright, spacious and with plenty of windows through which to see the airfield. There was no line going through TSA-Pre. It took me less than 2 minutes to go through. I have taken several flights from DAL and have always found TSA officers to polite and courteous. Airport was very clean and the WiFI signal was excellent and easy to connect to. On return to DAL a week later in the evening rush, the terminal was very busy and did not appear to be crowded with plenty of space to disperse the crowds at the gates and concourse.

I’m adding to all of the other reviews on the horrible ride share / taxi pick-up location. A poorly signed, disorganized, 15 minute brisk walk (without luggage) from luggage pick-up to the pick-up spot. Horrible airport experience and I won’t come back. Southwest just lost my Dallas travel to United at DFW.

I believe myself to be semi-well traveled and have experienced many airport scenarios in my lifetime (middle aged) and will have to give kudos to Dallas Love Field TSA agents for their remarkable work getting me from the baggage claim area for general boarding all the way to my gate “with time to spare” in as little time as I can possibly fathom. I actually witnessed a family who did not make their flight (one prior to mine but same gate) and persisted by raising their voices that the gate agent should have known they were there but because TSA took so much time, they were late. The truth later came out that they were ONLY in line for one hour, on a holiday weekend. That is exceptional but poor timing on their part. Everyone in the aviation world knows that on a holiday weekend, there is a 2.5-3 hour minimum time preparation period to make your flight. So a free plug for DLF, consider this!! Saying all of this, not only was TSA awesome in their timeliness, but the gate agents kept their cool and handled the situation with excellence.

This airport is horrible. Upon checking in, the tsa people in the front were extremely rude and talked to me like I knew how their machines work because apparently I was standing in the wrong area. They told me to go to counter 5 and the lady at counter 3 yelled at me for not being in her line. They walked around yelling at people standing in line directing them elsewhere even though they told us to stand where we were. There were limited seating once you got in through the screening. The center of the airport was packed and there was no seating when i got lunch. Some of the outlets had no power so you could not charge devices. My flight was delayed due to the tech outage and the lady at the counter was extremely rude if you had asked her any questions. I understand that they can have a bad day but every employee I interacted with either seemed like they did not want to answer my question or just looked like they did not want to he here. I hooked another flight out of here again for my next trip, but I regret it. Don't fly out of this location!

The airport was very crowded for the upcoming Memorial Day weekend. Nonetheless, there was plenty of seating at the gates and dining options ranging from sit down restaurants to fast food. The terminal is bright, spacious and with plenty of windows through which to see the airfield. Going through security was a breeze with TSA-Pre. The Airport WIFI is easy to connect too and fast. The major drawback to this airport is the lack of bathrooms. The bathrooms are small and there are only 3 stalls in each of the men's bathrooms. On a busy travel holiday, this meant waiting times of about 10 minutes. Given the number of passengers that fly through the airport daily, renovating and/or expanding bathrooms should be considered.

TSA and Clear staff are deplorable at this airport! They are incompetent and entitled. I clearly understand how to respectfully express frustration. When faced with incompetence and ignorance. These organizations staff seem to think they are perfect and cannot accept respectfully communicating frustration with their failures / inconsistencies. TSA and Clear fail to train their staff. However, their staff is proficient at being rude, incompetent, and intolerant of being respectfully confronted regarding their rudeness and incompetence!

If you are using Uber or Lyft do not use this airport. If you have a disability or are elderly it is extremely difficult to get to the area for pick up and there is a lack of signage and a lack of personnel for assistance. Use DFW. I used to love this airport but not anymore. Whomever made this decision did not take into consideration, people with disabilities or the elderly.

Flew to FLL 5 days before Christmas. The roadway into the airport and the terminal were beautifully decorated for the season. For pre-holiday travel, the terminal was busy but not at all crowded. There was plenty as seating available as well as plentiful dining options from sit down restaurants to fast food to choose from. The terminal is bright and very spacious with plenty of windows through which to see the airfield. Even though it was night time, one could look out across the well lit airfield and see planes taxing and taking off. Going through security was a breeze with TSA Pre clearance.

The ways they are now making people hike from baggage claim to a garage 15 minutes away is obscene. Especially if you are a business woman wearing heals and toting luggage. What rocket scientist thought having the baggage claim so far away from taxi's etc,? It's the most ineffective, frustrating and idiotic change I have ever witnessed in any airport I've traveled through. Some genius needs to move the options back to the entrance of the baggage claim, duh. I really cannot believe they spent the dollars moving this so far away from the baggage pick up. It's twilight zone stuff...you keep walking and walking and walking.

The airport's renovation seemed to come in handy no looking much more sophisticated. On the way to the airport I couldn't but help notice the new terminal that is in construction. Duty free is excellent with well anticipated manners displayed by staff. The airport itself handles more than Beirut international airport although it is much smaller in size. Restaurants sell reasonable food at magnificent prices. New bars have opened throughout the airport as well as ATMs and other necessities.

I first arrived in Damascus in Feb 1997. Since then I have been back and forth almost 1-2 times a year since then. I am an Englishman who met and married a Syrian girl in 1998. The airport in my view was more relaxed in the old days whereby you could check in and walk back into the lounge/cafe for tea etc with your friends and family.

Our late night arrival was surprisingly easy to manage. After a coached journey to the terminal (some planes use jetties) it was straight into the immigration hall (currency exchange immediately on the right) which had a couple of lanes for “non Arab passports”. The lines moved quite quickly and we were soon into the baggage hall where our bags were waiting. Customs took no interest and one is soon landside where there is an ATM (one of a small working number in Syria) a Currency Exchange and minor shops. We were met on arrival so I cannot comment on ground transport arrangements but there did seem to be numerous “taxi drivers” seeking fares. There are many worse airports throughout the world most of which are major airports.

It is not the most beautiful airport in the world but not the worst! I always found it OK - speed to check-in pass passport control is OK. Shopping cheap and wide range of products - VIP Lounge comfortable but old fashioned. The information system is getting better and friendliness of officials is good.

The refurbishment is finished. Everything looked clean and new. Fast check-in. Information screens were giving correct and up-to-date information. Good catering facilities to have a drink coffee or sandwich. Cheap duty free shops which are not the biggest but still have a good assortment of quality products spirits sweets perfumes etc.

Damascus airport must be one of the worst airports in the world. We were checking into a Saudi a flight and no information was provided on the overhead screens as to which gate was to be used for checking in. In this end one had to push trollys to all the gates to guess where the Saudia passengers were being checked in. At each counter there was a guy loading baggage on the belt and it was expected that we hand him some money. The regulation of smoking in the airport was appalling the whole airport stank of cigarettes including the toilets. The airport was undergoing refurbishment but the experience was chaotic.

The airport is under refurbishment and concrete dust coats everything. Still the only working departure display is in the duty free on the upper floor. The zone between entrance and gates is declared non smoking area with one bathroom size glass cage for hundreds of potential smokers. Consequently the final pre-takeoff-smoke is shifted to the gate waiting room where all passengers including babies and allergics spent half an hour in an air which one could cut out with a knife and use as durable construction material.

Damascus Airport gives an unfairly poor impression of Syria. The arrivals area was basic but immigration was conducted quite quickly if without charm. Departure was simply chaotic. As another reviewer pointed out the check in desks have no signage. We found our desk by a process of elimination by wandering up to each desk in turn checking the small paper sign and concluding that ours must be another one. The queue moved painfully slowly with each check in taking 5 minutes. When we reached the top of the queue we realised why - it appeared that every piece of information on out e-ticket had to be keyed in to the computer. The duty free seemed to house the only departure monitor in the whole airport. Worryingly our flight did not appear. We then noticed that the flight number and time on the boarding passes were different to those on our tickets - I guess due to typing errors. Our flight departed at the time on the ticket if we had believed he boarding pass we would have missed it ! While we passed though several security checks no-one seemed to be checking the magnetic gates and at the departure gate I noticed that a door onto the apron was unlocked and unguarded. I guess the authorities figure they have other ways of preventing terrorist attacks. The departure tax is a swingeing SYP1500 though what happens to this money is not evident - certainly not on the airport facilities. Just treat the airport as an experience and don't let it put you off visiting Syria.

Note that the airport departure tax is SP1500 for over 12s. All taxis from airport are run by private company and are fixed rate. The cost is around $35. All previous comments re chaos at departure. excessive zeal by document checking officials overcrowding etc are still as relevant as ever. A thoroughly depressing experience in what is a friendly generous and wonderful country.

Expect to be ripped off by the taxi drivers taking you into and out of the city. Don't go with any of the people hassling you as soon as they see you come out of the airport for an airport taxi. They would charge you a mind-blowing 15euros to the city. The immigration process was fairly OK even if slow but they could do with some signposting in English. Back from the airport I was ripped off 1000 SYPs by a yellow cab. The check in process is appalling - I don't know for what does one pay 200 syp departure tax. The check in desks are in a severe need for refurbishment. My checkin desk was not even shown on the noticeboard and then a fellow passenger showed me to my checkin desk - indeed it had a handwritten sign stuck with sticky tape to the roof saying 'LONDON'! The duty free section is quite large and varied and one could make a few decently priced purchases from here. One looks forward to visiting the airport when the refurbishment currently being undertaken by a Malaysian company is completed.

I'm impressed with all the improvements made at Dammam Airport. Its easily my favorite airport to fly in/out of in Saudi Arabia because of its compact size, array of services, retail, and food and beverage outlets. Its website and Wi-Fi connectivity are also quite good and easy to use.

This airport has improved phenomenally in the last 1-2 years. Apparently some operations have been outsourced to a private company and gone are many of the inefficiencies we used to run into earlier. Immigration plus custom is now a breeze, and the officials are actually customer friendly. Food services have come a long way. The guys who used to scan baggage before check in are gone, so the check in process is much faster. More helpful signs posted. Bathrooms much better, but need to improve further. Scan of carry on baggage post immigration gets a bit painful at peak hours, but not any more than at Dubai or Abu Dhabi. Since the traffic through this airport is modest, its peak hours (late evening, early morning) do not cause shortage of seats. Parking is a different problem, you might waste a long time trying to find a spot during peak. Ambience is great, helped by sound architecture, bright lighting, vast open spaces.

It can not be worse! Although the airport was almost empty with no flights or passengers, the services were at their worst levels. Security people were totally unprofessional and had the worst attitude you have ever seen! Facilities are outdated and apparently no one tries to maintain it.

We have been sat in Dammam airport watching aircraft (on a 3rd party app) land and take off from all surrounding airports except Dammam because apparently Dammam airport has fog. This is the second day we are facing a cancelled flight because of fog. Here is the problem, we all (7 passengers not traveling together) are all looking outside and there is no fog, not any, no patches of fog, nothing at all anywhere! So why are flights being cancelled because of fog? The airport staff here are so unprofessional, untrained and incompetent that it is a genuinely scary prospect to be flying out of here. Time to move our arrivals and departure airport to somewhere else who actually want aircraft to land and take off.

Hands down one of the worst experiences of flying in just under 20 years. No accurate information for current flights, the airline website does not match the airport boards which do not match the online updated boarding tickets. The airport does not communicate current issues like delays due to weather at all in a 12 hour period of time to customers already inside the airport. The business lounge staff are unknowledgeable and unwilling to assist any customers if it involves doing anything other than swipping a boarding card. The airport is dated and run down and unable to cope with the most basic of adverse weather conditions. We have had to sit at Dammam airport watching (on the internet) flights taking off from all other airports around us but all flights remain grounded at Dammam. I am going to avoid this airport going forwards at all costs.

This airport is old, haggard and unclean. People that work here are lazy, rude and have trouble diverting attention from there mobile phones to actually do there job. The queues were unnecessarily large as there is insufficient staff to operate the customs desks

Worn out airport stuck in the early 90s. Used this airport for a domestic departure and was disappointed at the overall appearance of this airport. Toilets were very old and filthy. Airbridges were old, dark and depressing. The airport had some good retail outlets but it definitely needs a major overhaul in terms of infrastructure and services.

Dammam airport immigration slow and unclear which of the many queues you need to join. The whole process takes much longer than it needs to. At least luggage piled waiting for you, then all baggage (hand and hold) to be scanned before getting to arrivals. Usual selection of outlets, foreign exchange, car rentals. Outside is a taxi booth where you state your destination and get 2 tickets which are fixed price fares to your destination. Departures is on the upper level with various check-in islands (the information board is actually behind you as you get there to tell you where to check-in). Passport control is more efficient leaving the country, after which is security before arriving at the duty free wall. Big selection of perfumes, some tobacco and chocolates but no alcohol. There is a Papa John's Pizza and Starbucks coffee and a Baskin Robbins. The terminal looks out onto the runway and most gates are via air bridges.

The place is awful to both fly into and depart from. Unorganised chaos poor facilities rude immigration staff. Just avoid it at all costs. I've flown into hundreds of airports all over the world and this place is the worst. I would strongly advise flying out of Bahrain.

This airport is probably the worst airport I have visited so far. The seating area seats were very dirty the carpets were completely littered with chip wrappers. I didn't see any cleaners or airport staff cleaning the area. The bathrooms are very in poor state no hygiene whatsoever. The service was poor and unacceptable.

Dane County Regional is a cute little airport lying on the outskirts of Madison, and it has had some of the best services I have ever experienced at any airport. The airport is incredibly clean and attractive on the inside and the outside. This includes nice modern architecture on the outside, and mosaic flooring and stained glass handling lights. It may not have as many stores as other airports, but there is a store for nearly all travel needs, such as a Cafe, a restaurant, a travel store, and a Wisconsin Gear store. I also noted that there were multiple stores under construction. There are hardly any delays and MSN connects to nearly all large nearby airports, which provides excellent connection availability. The best part, was the incredibly fast Wifi, and charger ports in the waiting area.

This is a fairly good airport. Nice and clean, easy to get around. This airport is also very small and therefore has less wait time, thus you can probably get away with arriving only 1 hour prior to departure and still make your flight. On the other hand, there is not very many options to eat or shop.

Very old terminal with which is very hot in summer. Food is on the bad side of average and quite expensive. Staff were terribly rude, unhelpful and seem to severely lack experience. Customs officers seem more interested in chatting to colleagues or playing around on their phones than doing their jobs, overall a terrible experience would recommend avoiding this place like the plague.

Airport tremendously improving. Immigration so easy, relaxed and kind. All sections of airport is now much spacier than pre-corona times. New, marvelous CIP Lounge as alternative to the old, stuffy Tanzanite. Has nice foods, snacks, local craft beers, outdoor areas but lacks curves in design, tarmac windows, champagne, and music.

The service has improved markedly. However visa on arrival takes close to an hour with three queues, paperwork, payment and then entry stamp. The is clearly an effort to improve things and departure was swift and smooth. Hassle free. We had an issue with the airport barrier which failed to work as someone walked under it and the lady did not acknowledge us when this happened and just moved onto the next queue without any explanation. We had to get annoyed to be acknowledged. The guard then came out with a gun and said we now had to wait till the end. How is that good service. If you want tourists to visit - please change your attitude and show courtesy and give efficient service. Remember that visitors expect good service. Generally at the airport a good experience and much improved on previous visits. Nice airport and service showed an improvement. It would help if immigration officers smiled a bit more and tried to speed up a little. Staff at the airport were trained to give good service with a smile. Hope to see things improving on the next visit.

Worst airport experience, ever. The staff is corrupt. I got harassed by a customs officer (with two other watching) for a bribe. Eventually, he openly asked for money. When I picked up my items and walked away, he actually found me in the lounge and openly asked for money. For a country that relies so heavily on tourists, they need to monitor their staff better. I've seen a lot of airports with poor facilities (due to them being in poor countries) but harassment of passengers is something else altogether. I am going to avoid this airport (and this country) like a plague.
Highly recommend getting your visa prior to departing your home country. It is chaos at customs if you're trying to get one there, and it takes close to an hour.

No internet available. Staff rude and unhelpful. For instance the guy at customs stopped had a drink and sent a message on phone then 2 minutes later looked up and took my passport. Customs is slow and unorganised. Even confusing. Terminal is poor.

Unlike an earlier reviewer, my arrival experience was much easier. I had obtained a visa before I left London and hence had not got that issue to deal with on arrival. It was a short walk across an airbridge into the small old airport. Then down some stairs into a rather cramped area where visas where purchased on the right and forms filled in on the left. We did not know we had to fill in a landing card which asked for almost the same information we had given on our visa application. We were fingerprinted, photographed, asked questions for which the answer was already on the form, passports stamped and through to baggage in minutes. Our flight was virtually empty but I would imagine that on a full flight it could be a different experience. Our bags were in the hall and for the first time ever, someone checked my tags against the bags I said were mine. Another X-Ray and then outside. There was the usual melee of taxi touts etc awaiting everyone. I have heard of ridiculous prices being charged ($40 US for a return trip to the nearest ATM because the airport ATM was not working) but luckily this did not apply to us because we were transferring to another part of the airport. This is an old undeveloped airport and it looked as if there was little work taking place on the almost completed new airport so do not expect anything to change for some while. I have been to far worse airports and this was not as bad an experience as I had prepared myself for.

I have used this airport regularly for around 5 years. The airport gives incoming travellers the worst experience I have ever encountered, and that's saying something. For a country which relies heavily on tourism it is a national disgrace to welcome tourists in the way they do. There are plenty of other reviews here detailing the dreadful immigration process etc and the dilapidation of the facilities. Once you are through that you have to deal with the 'official taxi' mafia who produce a 'menu' of charges which is ridiculously expensive. Uber works well in Dar generally, but if you use them at the airport you need to meet your Uber at the fuel station at the airport exit. The 'official taxi' mafia will throw stones at the Uber cars if they come inside the airport! Enough said! For the sake of Tanzania I hope they get the new terminal up and running as soon as possible and implement entirely new systems with thoroughly trained staff.

I may be expecting a little too much but I found this airport to be really poor. We arrived about 4 hours prior to our flight as we were connecting to a different flight through Dar and had to retrieve our baggage in between flights. We started queuing to check-in about 3 hours before our flight, and we only had about 30 mins to spare beyond security before boarding by the time we had checked in and got through security. All just incredibly slow. Incidentally, if we had checked in online it would have been no quicker as the check-in and baggage drop queue were one and the same. Admittedly, some of this may have been the fault of the airline (Qatar). The baggage handling system was none existent. Literally. Our bags weren't loaded onto our plane. The route from check-in to passport control to security just takes way too long. There is nowhere pre security for drinks or anything to eat, and there isn't much more beyond security. The only place to eat is pretty poor and overpriced. The whole airport looked  incredibly dated and in need of refurbishment. Its a shame because Tanzania is a fantastic country and the main access/egress point is poor.

I have to say my second arrival in Dar was much better than the first. First time arrived amid a plague of flying cockroach-like insects that were all attracted to the light inside the terminal. Spent ages swatting them in a huge line for immigration that took over an hour only to then be told I needed a "special" permit and had to pay 200 USD (I already had a business visa). Not wanting to argue I joined the next disorganised line paid my 200 USD and waited another 30 minutes to get my passport back. Notable that everyone in the "special" line was Caucasian. Second time all desks open for immigration friendly hello from the official and a quick stamp and on my way. No "special" permit needed this time for some reason. Bags came out quickly and was out of the airport within 10 minutes of landing. Let's hope that the new terminal will be finished on time and that there will be no more "special" line.

Indigo airport staff are not good. I have travelled a lot through various domestic airport in India, seldom come across airport staff from Indigo or other airlines that talk rudely and asking money for counter check-in of passengers. Argued to pay check-in amount otherwise they were not allowing for check-in. No kiosk check-in available at airport (2nd negative feedback). If airport is not ready why it is being operated. Stop charging illegal amounts from passengers. Better stop Darbhanga airport until ready with standard protocol.

A newly started airport in North Bihar catering large population of North Bihar and even some area of Nepal.The airport is actually an operative airport of Indian Airforce and runway is simultaneously used for civilian service. The Terminal being used is a temporary one and a new terminal will come soon is 2-3 years. This airport should be seen/used for service and facilities but for logistically importance for reaching some of the most undeveloped area in India with ease. Terminal is one of the smallest in India but managed nicely, no parking available, have to park outside the campus on the road, from main gate the terminal is just 2 min walk so not an issue ,trolleys are there, washroom are clean, there is one tea and snacks shop just near main gate in the campus and use that if you need anything, after that wont find anything inside. Hope they construct a new terminal soon. Though cabs are available outside but no option of prepaid or authorized cab inside, better to book cab in advance .

Velocity platinum flyer. Self service check in was poor. No customer service and people queuing just to check in because of 90min checkin timeframes. Security were rushing people through, barking at people to come through. Stopped at the northern common for something to eat and the service was just as average. Overall a very average experience. Would not be in a hurry to come back through Darwin airport again.

The Palms Bar was unclean. Sticky table menu, Bar section sticky where ordering, Power outlets badly positioned because you can't add a usb to your plug, it's too close to the bench top. Bar seat is torn and repairs were attempted with masking tape, but then it seems nobody cared after that, it's come apart again.

Darwin airport self check-in system is useless, 3 times in 1 month used the system as there are no other ways of check-in, the machines never worked properly, always something wrong, and not enough staff to assist, and the staff are not very friendly, very frustrating experience.

Prepare for a headache! Never have I been to an airport where they pump out music (with lyrics) 24/7. Having to wait in the airport for over 3 hours for a flight was bad enough, however, having to listen to someone else's taste in music for that period made it even worse. Had a slight headache when arrived, however, my headache and disposition were in a terrible way by the time we departed. It was incredibly distressing having to sit and listen. Asked if there was a 'quiet' room, however answer was no. Asked staff about the 'music' and one response was 'think of us we have to listen to it all day!'. Even complained when the lounge opened and I could escape it for an hour.

Departed and arrived at Darwin on an international flight from Dili, Timor Leste. As we were the only flight out and then back in (an Airnorth Embraer 170 seating 76 passengers) we had the international part of the airport to ourselves. Darwin Airport has been refurbished over the last couple of years and is now a mid-sized regional airport with good facilities. There are two times of day (around 11 am to 1.30 pm and 11 pm to 1.30 am) when (due to the peculiarities of Australian airport curfews down south) Darwin Airport is very busy. But it still copes. Outside these hours it is quite relaxed with short queues. I find the ground staff and even security to be polite, efficient and even cheerful; and there is an adequate range of food and shopping outlets. Virgin and Qantas have good lounges in the domestic section of the airport; there is a small pay-lounge once you have gone through passport controls, and the usual nonsense of the obstacle course of an overpriced duty free shop blocking the way between immigration and the departure lounge. On this occasion (as previously) from checking in to the departure lounge took about twenty minutes, and a similar amount of time between landing and catching a taxi.

A relatively large regional airport for a small town. However, Darwin is the state capital of Northern Territory. We checked in for the flight, went through security and then waited for the flight to depart. There were no hassles or problems. Everything went smoothly.

Darwin Airport is a small to mid-sized airport. It has limited food options during the off peak times of the day, but is sufficient enough. There are plenty of seats to wait on before boarding, and the maximum time taken through security is about 15 minutes.

Why such aggressive security procedures by airport staff for entry to transit lounge, including targeting individuals in line for special scrutiny and confiscating water provided by airline. Worst experience at an airport. Almost missed getting back on plane on time - Ridiculous!

Arrived at airport to find very little assistance and no check-in staff available despite mid afternoon time. Upstairs in departure lounges are old cracked dirty and missing pieces of vinyl. No bar facilities available again despite mid afternoon time and crowds of people in the lounge area. Very poorly sign posted. Nil star rating if that was possible!

I arrived here on a Jetstar flight from Brisbane with my 85 year old mother who needed a wheelchair. This latter was provided by Jetstar but then we were on our own to travel from the plane to the baggage area not an easy task as signage was almost non-existent and some doors along the way were locked necessitating a rather anxious wait until an official with a key card arrived. The only lift in the main area of the terminal was broken down although there was no sign about this just a loose flapping internal wall that was evident when the doors opened. This discouraged all users including us. In the end we ditched the wheelchair and proceeded slowly down the escalator. There was a total lack of information signage or assistance of any kind in this outdated dirty terminal. I intend to avoid this airport in future.

A sad little airport, with minimal facilities. Reminds me of a old soviet area airport. They charge you P784 as a, terminal fee. There is no option to pay by credit/debit card its hard cash or you are going nowhere. A total scam to pay for what ? A sub standard airport. I feel so cheated by this grubby practice and airport. I don't know why I am complaining as nothing will change

For an international airport, Davao International Airport is really disappointing. There’s almost no variety in shopping or food options—if you’re looking for anything beyond a basic snack, you’re out of luck. It’s hard to believe an international hub can be so limited. The seating situation is also bad—there just isn’t enough of it, and during busy times, you’ll find yourself standing around with nowhere to sit. While the bathrooms are clean, there are only two stalls per restroom, which is ridiculous for an international airport. Long lines and unnecessary waiting are inevitable. Overall, the airport needs serious improvement to meet even basic international standards for passenger comfort.

The worst airport I have been in - this is the 5th time I visited Davao in 2024 and the city has been great. BUT THE AIRPORT IS THE WORST EVER! Not enough seats in terminals, dirty and unorganized! Air-conditioning are not working, flights are ALWAYS delayed and I don't think it's the airlines' fault but how the airport and air traffic is managed. Avoid using this airport both for domestic and international travel if you can.

Worst airport I have ever been. You need to pay a terminal fee, yes a terminal fee just because you flying to another country! Scandal! Terminal fee is 786P and there is no option to pay by credit card and no option to rest cause not enough seats. The roof is leaking! That day my flight was postponed cause of bad weather and heavy rain, so in many places on the roof water was leaking! Immigration officers very rude to me! No WiFi there. Worst experience ever, no wonder there is big corruption in this country, where is the money to fix the terminal? Simple people need to pay a fee for tragic service and fatal condition terminal! Hope my leg will never step again in that place.

Out of 100's of airports I have entered this is nearly the worst. I normally fly through this airport twice per month or more. Because my fiancée and our kids live here. There is inadequate seating. Belligerent staff, baggage claim takes over an hour. In short Filipinos at this airport are horrible hosts!

Terminal was small but efficient. Toilets are smallish but clean. Building looks run down and dreary but noticed significant improvements in the departure lounges. There are still not enough seats though for lounges with wide-body departures. Almost next no nothing F&B and shopping options. Hope they push through with planned expansions, this airport is crying for it.

This has to be one of the worst airports I have ever used, its drab, it lacks any form excitement. Food outlets are poor and dated as is the airport itself. However after reading a 2.7 billion peso upgrade was made a few years back I wonder (well I don't really, because I think I know) where the funds went!

Davao City airport in the Philippines is spacious queues are minimal pre check in. After check in you head upstairs to the departure area pay your departure tax and pass through security. You then find yourself in a the domestic departure area where there is plenty of seating and TV screens. Flight announcements are limited my flight was delayed by 2 hours yet there was no announcement to advise.

From and to Singapore on Silk Air. This is a functional airport which in the Philippines is high praise! Security checks are numerous and slow as everywhere in the Philippines but because of the small number of international passengers moves quite quickly. The same can be said for check-in baggage claim and immigration. Toilet facilities are sufficient and clean. On the downside for those who need shops there is only one very small cafe before immigration and a kiosk selling very basic items in the gate area. All in all a good facility in the Philippines.

International flight from SG. Arrival quick but when passengers started to queue up for immigration the lights in the hall were switched off. The only thing that lit the hall was the sun from the windows. After 10 minutes of darkness someone finally realized they needed to turn on the lights. Departure was ok except for the time consuming queue for x-rays. Basic international airport. There's room for improvement.

Security TSA check-in needs a remodel, non district missing information. A narrow hallway. Seating in boarding area poor. Seats torn, walls in need of "TLC". Entire area needs a new property manager, only nice open - clean area was the car rental area.

What's not to like. Absolutely brilliant small airport. From gate to luggage pick up in 15 min. Airport very clean, ground staff all were friendly, excellent wifi, affordable food outlets and ample seating area. What I liked most were on departure the immigration staff were very chatty, wanted to know how your visit was and genuinely cared that your visit to DAB was enjoyable. All the usual car rental companies were there. I liked Hertz. I was worried that my flight with Delta landed a few minutes after midnight and they close their desks at midnight. They informed me if their system showed a pick up after midnight that they would wait for that person regardless of the time. A fantastic stress free airport.
Its easy to get around very friendly people and easy to get bags and leave. Always a good experience and they have free wifi so never a problem with communication.

This airport on Florida's East Coast is a beautiful little facility! Upon deplaning I was greeted by a small but spacious and superbly appointed six-gate terminal which was quite welcoming. The terminal is remarkably well-maintained and is very user-friendly with nice short distances good signage and a few clean shops to pick up a magazine or a quick meal. The personnel (both Delta and the airport security) were some of the most courteous airport employees that I have seen in a while with an genuine eagerness to serve. The only downside to DAB is the relatively small number of airlines and flight choices; prices are often higher than Orlando or Jacksonville and you will probably have to catch a connecting flight through a major hub to get to your destination. And auto racing fans can catch a good view of Daytona International Speedway (right across the street from the airport) on landing if they are lucky.

A nice airport very clean. Weather is often bad but the airport cant control that. Has a delicious restaurant and a nice little gift shop. The luggage claim was a little slow and they took one of our pieces of luggage to the check-in counter without informing us. Other than that a very nice little airport.

Excellent airport. Arrived at 8.45am on the BA London flight. First time visit to India so I stopped off at the biometric finger print machine - queued for 5 minutes and completed he task in 2-3 mins. Went to border control - There is a separate queue for business class travellers - and they checked my boarding pass. I could have done the finger prints here. The agent wanted to see my eVisa print out. Kind of defeats the object of have an eVisa? But processed and passport stamped and quickly through. By the time I arrived at the baggage claim, my luggage had already arrived. I then exited to meet my pre booked driver. Took about 50 mins from getting off the plane to getting into the car. Departure - had to get a ticket check before entering the terminal. I have checked in online but mobile boarding pass not available. Had to show the eTicket on my phone to get into the terminal - I also had a print out of the itinerary. Check in business class for BA flight to London - only 1 agent so about 20 mins spent. Dedicated business security lane was reasonably efficient. Went to the Encalm business lounge to find a queue - but this was the Priority pass queue - the agent called business and first class travellers to the front. I was then redirected to another lounge Enclam Prive, I don't know what the differences are, but I needed an airline invite to get in. Nice big lounge with a huge choice of food, some cooked to order. Efficient boarding in groups and policed very well. Overall a great airport experience.

A connecting flight on this airport was one of the most anxious and terrible experiences of my life. I initially boarded Air India Flight on Jan 6th in EWR, USA, but the flight was delayed by 45 minutes or so due to inclement weather (snow), and with another half an hour spent getting of the plane in Delhi, it didn't leave me with much time to catch my next flight (Air India) to Mumbai.  I would have to personally collect my luggage, get it through customs, get through all the security checks even though I had a connecting flight (both Air India), the Delhi Airport staff refused to get the bags to the final destination. Even this would have been fine if all the staff had given me a proper answer on time, because some told me that I didn't need to do anything while others told me If I don't collect the luggage myself, I will lose everything. So in order to save my stuff, I went through all the process (very slow lines, most of the staffs just walk away for no reason even if there is a huge line at their station). Getting through all of this had left me with only few minutes to board my plane, so in a hurry I forgot my handbag at the security check-point and ran all the way to board the plane  and got on the plane at the last minute. Only after getting on the plane did I realize that I had forgotten my Handbag at the airport. So I reached out to Lost & Found Department countless times, few calls every day, for every week, sent them all the details they asked for, etc. but no answer or response, agents always delaying the process, telling to call later or call at this time etc. I followed all that but nothing, until the very last week of my stay in India that they provided me with a Bag Number (466220) saying they've found it, but they said they can't mail it or send it to me, I would have to personally come collect it in Delhi Airport! This would have been fine had they told me a week earlier while I was still in India, then I would have been able to solve this issue and get my stuff back.

We travelled through Delhi Airport to go from Amsterdam to Chennai. For this, we needed to pick up our checked in bags from the security belt and go to a check-in counter again. Picking up the bags went smoothly, everything after that was everything except that. We were initially supposed to have an 8 hour stopover in Delhi, of which we managed to spend approximately half an hour not standing in queues. By the time we reached Delhi Airport, there was a long queue at the check in counters for domestic transfers. This queue started in a straight line, but this quickly turned into chaos with everyone trying to push each other all over to get in front of the others. The staff in this time was doing nothing but shouting at people, giving them wrong directions to get rid of people, rather than help them out. After standing in the queue for about 1.5 hours, we finally reached the counter, just to be told that the belt does not work, which was weird considering bags were still moving on it. We knew there was nothing wrong with the belt but they basically forced us to go to a different floor for check-in, promising us there would be no queue. Surprise surprise, what do you think we encountered there? Just when we thought we survived the drama, we ended up in the line for security. Once again, people pushing to cut the line, but alright, this is nothing the staff can do anything about. What they can improve on is not shouting at the people travelling; some people might consider this human decency but maybe there is a different definition of this in supposedly "the best airport of India". The opportunities to improve include clarity in signs for where to stand in queue - not changing the places the customers should go to for the queue - not shouting at customers - attempting to understand customer frustrations that are created by staff - not confusing customers by giving contrasting advice from different staff members

I travel a lot internationally, and the overly complex, chaotic, unhelpful, militant, and unfriendly atmosphere has been experienced each time I fly into Delhi. There are no airports that compare to it in terms of its chaotic, endless, overly redundant processes. While flying in from Chicago, we stood by the baggage carousel for 2 hours  without explanation. Many passengers missed their connecting flights, including me. I therefore had to buy a new flight for the following day as my flight insurance would not cover Delhi’s inexplicable delays. No explanation; no apologies, no interaction at all from staff. It’s basically survival of the fittest, so be warned. In transit to Rishikesh, India after visiting Nepal, after 4 security screenings, the last redundant screening required I unpacked and unwrap all of my healing sound bowls bought in Nepal. Not only did the ridiculous request undo complicated packing, the security guard seemed to take great pleasure in making the process difficult. I had to deal with him for an hour for no good reason. The one Indian who spoke to me with a hint of kindness asked me what my impression of India was so far. “Unwelcoming.”

Every employee except one was rude, dismissive and completely unhelpful. We paid for a hotel stay at the airport since we had a long layover. Airport staff were making us stay in a certain area with no explanation as to why. We explained to one worker that we were currently paying for a hotel, and he was the only one who seemed to care or try to help. Others barely gave a response and put their head down as to ignore us and hope we go away. They kept insisting we needed a different boarding pass in order to go through security, however when we finally could go through, the boarding pass we had was fine. The security personnel was picking her nose before touching me, and did not even say when she was done or that I was free to go. She just walked away without saying a word. After making it through security, other workers we dealt with were very rude. We changed our seats at our gate and I said “thank you so much” a couple of times with literally no response from the worker. Overall, horrible experience. No organization or order and very rude workers.

I had an unfortunate experience with an immigration officer at the airport that left a negative impression on my travel experience. The officer was rude and dismissive, which made an already stressful situation even more challenging. Upon approaching the counter, I expected a professional and efficient interaction, but I encountered an officer who seemed uninterested in assisting me and spoke rudely to me. Their curt responses and lack of patience were frustrating, especially when I had questions about the process. It felt as though my time was being wasted, and I left the interaction feeling disheartened. Travel can be a hectic experience, and having to deal with an unhelpful immigration officer only adds to the stress.

Terminal 2 has the worst system by GMR for security check. Long long queue. No support no guidance . Big harassment even after reaching before 2 hours . Authority should take care & improve the services asap.

I was in international transit with hour and half stay at this airport. First about half an hour was wasted in a bus from the plane to the terminal. Then after getting off I followed the signs for transit when I dint see the sign i asked an official who said go downstairs, after going downstairs there was no transit sign. Then when I asked some officials there said to go transit you need to go through immigration. I challenged this point as I said I am only international transit from one gate to another in same terminal 3, so why why would I need immigration. They said I do and asked me to fill out that foreigners form they ask at that airport. Then when i asked the immigration officer if they are sure about this they said yes as i will need to go out of airport get my bags from belt then turn right. I then said that is domestic, they said yes. I said again my baggage is going to UK i am going to UK. They got confused and then all of a sudden said stop the immigration I need to go back up! No sorry from anyone that they had wasted my time and caused confusion and stress, instead they spoke like its my fault! The after finally getting to international transfer desk checks and security check there were long queues, total disorganisation, people stressing that they are going to miss their flights. Their staff didn't know what they were doing or how to manage lines efficiently. Absolute mess, most of their staff are poorly informed, poorly trained about their own airport and uneducated. They don't listen to people instead they think they are right always, even when they cause confusion. Definitely avoid transits here, its a nightmare. There is a good chance you can miss connections here.

I had a transit flight through Delhi T3 terminal… I had to go through departures to catch my KLM flight to Amsterdam. Had a really horrible experience with security line… immigration process was a breeze but after finishing immigration no one was available from the airport staff to organize the line for the security check … everyone was jumping the lines and it was very chaotic. I asked one of the officers on where the line starts for security and his response was “line starts from wherever you stand” … what kind of irresponsible response was that… most of the airport staff were sporting suits and where busy adjusting their attire to look sharp whereas most of the passengers were arguing about there spot in the line… I will definitely will try to avoid Delhi in my future travels… very ill managed airport.

Security management was very poor. It took more than an hour for security scanning, with very long queues at every counter. The security staff acted as if they had nothing to do with passengers being late for their flights. Even though I arrived at the airport three hours before my flight, I almost missed it due to the long queues.

Denizli Çardak Airport is a small regional airport for the city of Denizli, with flights to IST, SAW and Iran. The airport is quite small, with the ability to hold 4 aircraft at a time. Shops are scarce, with 3 cafes, 2 souvenir shops and one suitcase shop. The main reason people come here is for Pamukkale, which is a natural wonder. The cafes are good for a quick snack, but nothing more. Arriving one hour before the flight should be enough, as security lines are no longer than ten minutes.

Arriving is smooth and easy. Just really annoying with everyone trying to sell you stuff and trying to scam you with taxi rides. Departure is a different story. The airport staff was insanely rude both from the airlines as well as the security (cleaning staff was very friendly). I wanted to assist my mom for checking in as she doesn't speak English but my flight was later that evening and they wouldn't let me assist her to the check-in counter. The airport separates all check in counters and airline assistance counters from the shopping area but still before passport and ticket control, which I have not experienced in any other airport. This makes it impossible to assist people or to contact the airline in case of issues/delays/cancellations. I would not recommend this airport at all (in general Indonesian airports). Bali and Lombok and a lot of other islands are great but the airports are amongst the worst to use. It also took 1h30 to check in the luggage for a flight. They processed 1 passenger every 8-10 minutes, which is incredibly slow.

Specialised tools for camera equipment taken away after being deemed “too dangerous” with no signs for tourists detailing prior to checkpoint. Security’s own rule book is in native language and cannot be ready by English speaking travellers. Brought same tools through the same checkpoint 5 weeks prior with no issue. Would not recommend to travel to this destination to others. Flight over booked by Jetstar after being moved flight for the second time. Forced additional cost of hotel and driver. Would not recommend flying out of this airport. Holiday has been one of nightmares.

Never I have seen an airport where 2 different airlines depart at the same gate to the same destination about at the same time and boarding is side by side only divided by a flexible band for queuing - as I was seated in the front row I usually board after the queue eases. Upon lining 10 min around columns I reached the front of queue and was told it is another flight to the same destination and refered to the adjoining counter 1 m away. When I turned to them I was told the flight is closed even though I was already sitting at the gate and in the other queue for 10 min. First thing I was told to buy a new ticket. Airport authority management refused to talk to me and air asia also told me they do not take responsibility. As a frequent traveler I have never experienced ONE GATE with SAME DESTINATION but different airlines boarding at the same time without having this clearly marked/signposted/communicated. Even those 2 different airline members were talking to each other. Only one board showing the same final destination but different flight nos. Even upon being seated there were announcements for final destination to the same gate. Often flights are code sharing flights though different flight nos. On one board, but not different airlines using one board for 2 different flight to the same destination.

Just wanted to shout out the excellent customer service and help I received recently at Denpasar Bali airport. I stupidly left two bags on the carousal when I went through customs, Airport security were very friendly as the guided me through a secure area to go back behind the luggage area to retrieve the bags and customs did not hassle me for going through twice. Can't imagine doing this so easily in a North American airport. Bali people are great!

Worst international airport, especially the immigration, they work very slow, only 6 counters open for many departures. They make very stupid questions, what will make the que longer and longer. Food and beverage are overpriced and quality not good.
Waiting time is unacceptable. Staff was the slowest and most arrogant I’ve seen. Joke. Visa on arrival 20 minutes. Immigration 1 hour. Get your clearance 20 minutes. Out of airport 15 minutes.
