It is clean, modern, spacious and well designed. The efficiency of security is high. The WiFi connection is good. Employees are helpful and polite.

The airport is big, upon my arrival I passed through the electronic gate and it did not take more than a minute to complete my entry procedures into the country and it was more than wonderful. The treatment of the airport staff is wonderful,  we received our bags quickly and there was no delay. Upon our departure the treatment was also professional, friendly and fast from the staff and there was no delay in stamping passports, security check or check in. We tried two restaurants to eat at the airport and the food was very tasty, travelling through Dubai Airport is a wonderful experience.

The airport police in Dubai are really unpleasant. When I went through security, one officer made me remove my suspenders, even though they were attached to my trousers and difficult to take off and put back on. He couldn’t have cared less. In general, locals in Dubai are not particularly friendly. In Dubai, they probably believe that quality of an airport is the infrastructure, but for me it is people who make the difference.
No air conditioning , it’s terribly hot. Worst airport in my life. The heat is unbearable. I have never experienced something so bad. I do not recommend to do do Dubai just because of this airport.

Me and my husband have really big travel experience, but never had such a bad transit experience as in Dubai! Both times to Bangkok and back our experience was bad! With 1,5h time between our flight to Bangkok we almost missed our flight as AirPort personal guided us to wrong terminal. Information on screens is not sufficient, we did not even find our flight in the screen when arriving. As our connection was in a different terminal you need to figure out where exactly yourself. Also we had to take train and then wait very long time for a bus, Security control - 3 times! On our flight back we had 2,5h between flight - so we made it. Would definitely look for different transit airport if possible next time! Shame on such a rich country to have such a mess in their airport

This a not an airport, it's only a shopping mall. the customer care does not exist. I booked for my parents wheelchair service, due to first flight delay by Emirate airline, they should wait 8 hours in airport. My mother with serious back problem and my father stage 3 lung cancer under chemio therapy. Took two hours to have wheelchair, every time the airport employees were saying takes only 10 min. my parents walked quite long to reach the area of waiting list for hotel and wheelchair. In the way back from hotel although the Hotel employee mentioned several times that a wheelchair must be ready in front of airport, nobody took care. again my parents walked a lot and stay in waiting list. and no place to sit sown. first the wheelchair of my father was ready after 20 minutes for my mother, during this time, they tried to take seat each one 5 minutes to help each other the wheelchairs?  The whatsapp is filtered, you can not make any phone call.

Awful airport. 1 hour trip by bus from the aircraft to the arrival terminal. Then another hour to get through passport control. Automated passport control did not work in 80% of all passengers. Then queueing again for the manual passport control. Worst airport I have ever been.

My mother, who just turned 76 needed a wheelchair so we booked one a long time ago, but when we arrived in Dubai after midnight and after having travelled for more than 12 hours, they did not have a wheelchair for her and just kept saying it was around the corner. She was exhausted and in pain and they kept her walking all the way through security and a little longer, before they managed to offer her a seat. They didn’t even offer her to sit down, when we waited for a car to pick her up. They just laughed when we kept telling them she needed a wheelchair and then they said that we were rude. They kept us without the possibility of getting something to drink or to go to the bathroom for two hours after getting of our plane. This is how they treat an elderly woman who is exhausted, in pain and dehydrated. They also split up families as only one can accompany a person who needs assistance. Even if they were just to walk and not going in a car. I have experienced rudeness and incompetence in other places but never both at the same time in such a degree. And it wasn’t only us. There were others, who weren’t offered a place to sit, when they really needed it.

We landed at Dubai Airport just before midnight following a 6 and a half hour flight from Frankfurt. The Immigration Hall is new, bright and glossy but the set up was confusing as there were 2 sections and it wasn't clear which one to queue in. The process was slow and laborious, and the staff on the desks didn't go out of their way to speed things up. It took us about 50 minutes to finally get through, and into the baggage reclaim area; our cases must have by then done about 20 circuits on the conveyor belt. The Metro had by then shut down for the night, so we joined the queue for the taxi. Queue is maybe a misrepresentation as various people tried to push in, even though there were barriers along the queue. We eventually got to the front, and it was a complete shambles, with drivers touting for business, and people shouting. The whole arrival process, and effectively in the middle of the night was a very bad experience, and created a very poor impression of what is supposed to be one of the world's leading airport.

I would not recommend this airport to anyone, not even for transit. In the wake of the recent flood, it's flabbergasting that a supposed world central airport had no effective emergency response teams who could deal with the situation at any level. 1 out 30 staff gave accurate information. The rest sent hundreds on a wild goose chase because of poor knowledge, understanding and inaccurate information. They raised their voices to repeat information that we later found was just plain wrong. Information regarding compensation information was also wrong. I'd like to know if Dubai Airport has an active, updated business continuity plan, or crisis management teams for different situations? But I would say Never Again, Dubai until you get your act together. A horrible experience.

Definitely deserves 10/10. Nice staff and beautiful sight. I loved how they just fit! I didn't like that there are two gates and you have to wait a while for the second one too. Usually there is only one. The bathrooms were clean and had great terminal seating!

We were flying first class on Emirates. It took us almost 1hour of endless walking and elevators just to get to the immigration area for passport control. We queued for at least 45mins and then needed to continue walking to find Emirates desk to find our driver, who was not meeting us with our name sign. It took us around 2 hours to finally leave this airport!!!! Dreadful customer experience- Never again. They need to send all their airport staff to be retrained in Singapore Changi airport which is vastly superior

Terrible facilities & barely any customer service. We have spent 9 hours of transit today in the airport and we had trouble with buying coffee from vending machine to using the shower facilities. Vending coffee machine only accepts Dirham and Only in 1 Dirham coins! No one is responsible to provide you the coins (you have to magically find some) and no clear instructions. After all the trouble we went through, the coffee was hopeless, I through half of it out. FYI, a very average coffee (which we buy 4 AUD in Melbourne) is 7 AUD in this airport. Shower facilities: there is only 2 showers in each facilities at each end of the airport. One standard and the other one disabled, not mentioning that the guys one were both locked! NO soap, no towels and np shelf for disabled shower. The showerhead was terrible and was splashing water everywhere during the shower. Prices are generally goes to the roof (including food and accommodation), and for any purchase, even a small milk, they would ask for your boarding pass! ( I do not want to give them consent to collect my information, merely because I needed a bottle of milk). I think our 9 hours transit couldn’t be less impressive that this. I do my best not to book my flights through this airport, again.

Went to Dubai for business with my wife and got a flight to Al Maktoum International (DWC). Brand new airport, parts of it still in construction. Much easier than DXB to go through, has less shops though. Not much variety for eating but enough for duty free. Airport staff much more attentive that at DXB, this to be expected though considering the traffic volume is much less than DXB. Only downside is that it is far away from downtown Dubai - if got business there. I would give a high score as it is a brand new airport and facilities are improving all the time. A pleasant experience overall!

It is envisaged, which in Dubai means it will happen, that Dubai World Central will be the principal airport in the Emirate. Presently, however, it has more in common with Bristol Airport circa. 1985 with only a few airlines regularly using the facility, most notably Qatar. Nevertheless, providing you have no interest in over-priced food - there is a McDonalds, Costa Coffee and a small restaurant - and (not) duty free shopping, DWC offers multiple advantages over Dubai's present main airport. Of note: the drop-off is immediately next to the terminal entrance - no long walk to check in, and no queues for immigration or security. One downside is the lengthy bus ride from the gate to the aircraft. Notwithstanding, with few aircraft, departure was fifteen minutes ahead of time. If using Qatar, why bother with the frantic DXB or creaking AUH.

Worst airport in over 100 airports I have been. It is incredible, we spent over one hour when arriving and almost 2 hours (1 hr 50 to be precise) when departing. The staff are awful, they have no respect even for parents with infants or people with disabilities. A young girl in a wheelchair had to wait for over one hour at the check-in counter alone. One reason we will never come to Dubai again is this airport.

I live in Dubai marina and this is a fantastic option to travel from. Small, quiet, check in to boarding in 5 minutes. It's still in its infancy before being ramped up to being a hub but it is a joy to use compared to big, busy DXB. Bags are always office in minutes and you sail through immigration.

A wonderful airport, very cosy and friendly. The only drawback as it is vast it has very long walking distances. The design is very Dubai in style - elegant with an affordable Duty Free. You can buy almost everything in very low prices. Definitely a very nice airport.

Used DWC to leave Dubai to Doha and beyond to Europe. Airport is a very long drive from Dubai's main hotels, unless you are staying in Dubai Marina or Jebel Ali, but also then a 40 min drive. The airport was virtually empty with only 4 flights leaving between 11pm and 7am. Oversized facilities, empty feeling, restaurant and duty free staff just sitting around and playing on their smartphones. Boarding is with buses from the terminal. Will avoid even if no queues, for me part of the travelling is the "buzz" of an airport.

We've used Dublin airport a fair number of times, and it has both positive and negative aspects. Passport control staff courteous. Nearly everyone friendly. Bus info. better than it used to be. Bus areas mostly unsheltered; it does rain here. WiFi very poor, unavailable in several areas. Trolleys unavailable far side of baggage drop / collect; no wheelchairs or child facilities either - Food & Drink poor; nowhere to get coffee / tea except in a paper cup; most food disappointing

I departed from Dublin airport a few times this year, and I was shocked by the aggressive and rude manner in which passengers were treated by the Airport security staff. Maybe it is time to call on the Irish Tourism Board to protect tourists from this type of humiliation and abuse.

I cannot overstate my disappointment and frustration with the treatment I received at Dublin Airport on two separate occasions. Ireland's immigration system is already infamous for its massive backlog of permit and GNIB card approvals or renewals, and these delays are putting people at serious risk of being unfairly denied entry. It is unacceptable that individuals who are deserving of entry—who live and work here legally—are subjected to unnecessary chaos, hostility, and disrespect from immigration officers. Returning from Scotland Despite carrying a printed email from immigration confirming my work permit approval—an email that explicitly instructs individuals to have it on hand while traveling—the officer I encountered dismissed it outright. When I offered to show my expired GNIB card alongside the email, his response was shockingly unprofessional. This level of hostility is absolutely unacceptable from someone in a public-facing role. While he eventually stamped my passport, the interaction left me feeling humiliated and undeserving of such treatment. Arriving from Manila The second experience was even more infuriating. I had been waiting in the non-European line when an immigration officer directed individuals with approved GNIB cards to the EU line. I approached her, explained that my card was expired but my renewal was approved (with documentation in hand), and she told me to proceed. When I reached the desk and handed over my printed documents, the officer dismissed them outright, stating, "I’m not letting you through because you don’t have the proper documentation." I explained that my documents were approved and that I was waiting for the physical card due to delays caused by the government backlog. When I mentioned the other officer's instructions and pointed her out, he retorted with, "Well, I didn’t tell you to do that, did I? Back of the line." I was exhausted but persisted, explaining my situation again and offering my expired GNIB card for review. He begrudgingly looked at it, rolled his eyes, and sarcastically stated, "Why didn’t you just show me this to begin with?" I explained that during a previous interaction, I was explicitly told expired cards were not valid. His dismissive response: "I’m not that immigration officer." After much unnecessary back-and-forth, he finally stamped my passport and remarked snidely, "Well, I guess you’re in." A System That Enables Hostility These demeaning encounters reflect a deeper, systemic problem within Ireland’s immigration process.  Immigration officers appear to have too much power and anonymity in making decisions, with no consistency in following protocols or language guidelines. For a country that promotes itself as welcoming and progressive, this kind of treatment is disgraceful. The first point of contact for travelers and residents should be professional &respectful.

Had an excellent experience travelling through Dublin airport to Miami. The security was efficient We precleared US customs and immigration which took 30 minutes, saving us from having to do it through Miami. There was a good choice of food and drink but very limited once you enter the US zone.

Terrible treatment for wheel chair assistance passenger. I was locked in the lift for 20 minutes with no air circulation and no customer support with me. All passengers boarded the flight before me. Although wheel chair assisted passengers always board first to allow enough time, but no at this airport.  We had to bang on the walls to get the attention of customer service. When we finally boarded there was no space for our bags.

This airport is functional. Not what one would expect of an international Airport. It is NOT a "beacon of luxury" as another review indicated! Obviously a joke. The staff is mostly courteous, some are abrupt and seem tolerant with an air of irritation they keep to themselves. Definitely not friendly or welcoming. I had 6 hours to spend here, let me just say, if you are hungry, get a small snack and hope your flight crew serves you something you can eat. One actual restaurant with a long line and I passed by several times to get a view of the food, understaffed and very long wait times to get a seat, and have food brought to you. I saw several tables waiting about 45 minutes without anything. The souvenirs... mostly cheap junk. I passed. The decor? Missing or dated. Interesting picture of a woman serving tea at the Dublin airport in the 60's, I believe. ATTENTION ENTREPRENEURS! There is a huge opportunity here! Travelers with money and nothing really to spend it on. Food. Souvenirs. Coffee. Restaurants. Even a good bookstore. All modern endeavors would make a killing. There is one decent coffee place. The pastries are not fresh or very good. Save yourself for Italy or France. I don't normally rate things so poorly and i personally enjoy my time wherever I am and enjoy different experiences. This airport though could be so much better with a refreshed management vision. Safe travels.

From the moment you set foot inside, Dublin Airport immediately distinguishes itself as a beacon of luxury, especially noticeable within the sleek and sophisticated confines of Terminal 2. Its modern aesthetic and design set it apart from the majority of international airports, presenting an atmosphere not just of transit but of refined travel experience. The layout of Dublin Airport is a testament to thoughtful design and planning. The check-in areas are remarkably clear and well-organized, making navigation a breeze for travelers. This accessibility extends throughout the airport, with ample space, lifts, and escalators ensuring that everyone, regardless of mobility, can easily move around. Perhaps most impressive is the airport's commitment to leveraging cutting-edge technology for security processes. The advanced systems in place mean that passengers don't need to remove liquids or electronics from their bags, streamlining what is often a cumbersome process. This efficiency is further highlighted by the minimal queues, with most travelers getting through security in less than five minutes—a clear indication of Dublin Airport's effective use of technology and operational management. The warmth and helpfulness of the staff at Dublin Airport cannot go unmentioned. Each interaction is marked by genuine care, making the travel experience exceptionally personal and pleasant. Dublin Airport also excels in its retail and dining offerings. The duty-free selection is impressive, featuring sought-after brands and exclusive products at prices that challenge those of high street shops. The food outlets, including some newly launched ones, offer a wide array of options catering to diverse tastes and dietary needs, all at reasonable prices. For travelers seeking a moment of tranquility or needing to attend to work, the airport provides numerous lounges and workspaces, alongside impeccably clean toilets and abundant seating areas. Navigation through the airport is foolproof, with gates clearly marked and the overall layout intuitively designed. Also has free reliable WiFi unlike other major airports. A unique feature that sets Dublin Airport apart on the global stage is its US Customs and Border Protection Preclearance facility, allowing travelers to complete all immigration procedures before boarding. This means arriving in the USA as if on a domestic flight, bypassing the usual long queues upon arrival—an invaluable convenience. In summary, Dublin Airport is not just a travel hub but a remarkable experience in its own right. Its commitment to luxury, modernity, and efficiency makes it a must-use airport for anyone looking to elevate their travel experience. The seamless blend of advanced technology, outstanding customer service, and thoughtful amenities positions Dublin Airport as a hidden gem in the world of air travel. My advice? Run, don't walk, to Dublin Airport for your next journey. It’s an experience that not only facilitates travel but inspires more of it.

After reading some of the reviews here, I was expecting a real hellscape, but instead I found a functional if not very exceptional airport with no real issues for me beyond all the walking (more about that later). I was arriving from and returning to the US through Terminal 2, using United Airlines, traveling at what appeared to be busy times for arrival and departure. Arrival was uneventful with a quick trip through immigration. The terminal seemed well organized and signed. ATMS will give you pounds, Euros or dollars. I was taking an express bus to Belfast which meant going through a labyrinth of covered walkways in the ground transportation area outside the terminal---despite being able, fit, and used to walking a lot at home, this was more than what I wanted after an overnight flight and the signage could have been better--it was easy to get off track. The ground transportation area looks like an former surface lot repurposed for shuttles, long and short-distance buses, etc. Some areas serve both terminals, such as those for hotels, while others are meant to serve Terminal 1 or 2. Regardless, a lot of walking. Ditto on departure. Departure was easy and went quickly--immigration and security didn't have much in the way of lines. Security had less of the militant hurry up and wait I usually experience in the US and elsewhere. There could have been better spaces for putting bags and gear back together after security, but otherwise, fine. There was less in the way of shopping and food service than I expected. If you live in a place that heavily taxes liquor, you might find some values, but otherwise the prices weren't great, though not as bad some airports I've used. The seating was adequate, although it tended to be toward the end of the shopping area. The currency exchange couldn't change my leftover pounds to dollars w/o converting them to Euros which seemed ridiculous given that there's a nother country that uses Pounds on the island. US Customs is available about 3 hours before your flight. There wasn't much of a line and I didn't have to go through security a second time - I didn't know if this was because of Global Access, but it meant I didn't have to give up my water (yes, they don't let you bring water through this checkpoint). Immigration also was quick, although it was easy to miss the path to Global Access. The US terminal has an abbreviated set of shops and a café, so you can wait until your gate to buy water. I didn't see a currency exchange or ATM. The gates are posted once you pass customs and immigration. The seating was adequate unless you were boarding a jumbo jet. This was the one part of the airport where I saw moving walkways, but the whole process of getting there involved a lot of walking. The general tone of things was more businesslike than friendly which was fine with me. Not a bad airport, overall, but it would be a lot better with less walking.

The place is dirty, uncared for, inefficient and a dump. Clearly there is no pride in this place. All they want is our money. Greedy barstewards. This place needs a serious overhaul. The picture is bird poo right down the wall where you eat.

I think Dublin airport does a very good job of dealing with large number of passengers efficiently and with courtesy. I travel through there at least once a month and rarely come across any issues. I think when they get more of the enhanced security scanners, it will be even better.

Don’t really know where to start. First off the food is limited and is absolute garbage and way over priced. But the thing that really stands out are the staff ! Never in all my years of travelling have I come across such rude and arrogant people. The women on the desks at terminal are vile. Witnessed the one (we were delayed for 3 hrs so watched here this whole time) be so rude to a lot of people. Especially and old couple who nearly missed there flight due to the airport putting gate 20 on screen then changed it to gate 2 (where we where sat) at last minute. These 2 old people struggled to walk. And it’s a long way between the 2 gates. She did call there names quite a few times and once they got to gate 2 she was screaming and shouting at them like they where naughty children. Almost on the verge of bullying.  Once they had gone. She and the others at desk where what I believe to be cursing the old couple. Then laughing about it and very open about it. In the time we sat there we witnessed numerous times things like this happening to customers.

I recently had an extremely disappointing experience at Dubrovnik Airport. Here’s why I would never recommend this airport, and if I could give it negative stars, I would. **Before Security:** - The only store available before security was a small tobacco convenience store with very limited food options. The only food offered was junk food like candy bars and chips, all overpriced by 800%. - The one “cafe” available sold low-quality baguette sandwiches for a ridiculous €8 each! - Seating was extremely limited. This was especially problematic for me as I am pregnant and traveling with a small toddler. The airport is not handicap-friendly at all, and I would never feel comfortable bringing my elderly, handicapped parents here. **Security:** - Security was incredibly unorganized. The priority lanes for handicapped individuals, pregnant women, and parents with small children were not operating. - There were no signs indicating that you needed to remove electronics and jewelry, leading to confusion and delays. - The electronic belt system at security was poorly designed and dangerous. The security guard kept yelling at my toddler to move her hands away from the belt because trays were smashing against each other. It’s difficult to explain, but the design is not customer-friendly and is potentially hazardous. - After the X-ray, most customers had their bags inspected due to lack of proper signage about removing laptops, baby medicine, kids' cups/bottles, etc. Belongings were handled carelessly and just thrown down the belt. This made it easy for someone to grab my laptop and jewelry while my other bag was being inspected. **After Security:** - You are forced to navigate through a cluttered duty-free shop to get to your gate, which is not ideal when traveling with carry-ons and a toddler. - To board the plane, you are then bussed, adding to the overall inconvenience. The entire experience was chaotic and stressful. I was extremely unhappy with my time at Dubrovnik Airport and would never recommend it to anyone.

Very limited food and beverage options. Don’t come to this airport hungry or expecting any fast food chains. Also, once through passport control, the food items increase significantly in price, so if you can get your snacks in the duty free, just after security, do!
Worst airport I have ever had the displeasure of departing from. Food was diabolical and staff were so ignorant. I think I’ll walk the 4000km next time.

My wife put her Passport in the tray to pass through Security but it was missing at the other end. Staff looked, said it was missing and that there was nothing more they could do. Fortunately my wife has dual nationalities and we were able to use her other Passport to get a new Boarding Pass. We tried to report the loss to the Police but was told that we would have to leave the airport to do so. This would have meant missing our flight. Just before we got on the flight we were approached by a Policeman who said that the Passport had been found inside the scanner.

We travelled to Dubrovnik out of season, so unsure what it would be like during the summer season when it is significantly busier. What we did experience was a very clean, modern, state-of-the-art airport that has been built and designed to an excellent standard. It feels premium and polished, not something I expected if I am honest before setting of on our holiday! Arrival was very simple, walked off plane on to a beautiful bright glass airbridge and into modern terminal structure made of glass and metal. Immigration was quick and efficient, not overly friendly but not antagonistic either. We were airside probably within 10 minutes from leaving the plane. There is only one shuttle that goes to the city and it meets each flight, leaving half an hour after each flights arrival and the cost was reasonable. On Departure the check-in hall is bright and airy, and the check-in staff for BA were friendly and helpful. Security was a breeze and staff seemed generally fine - we were the only flight taking off that evening though so it was very quiet. The departure area was clean and well organised, there isn't a lot of shopping opportunities or much to do but it is a small airport so that wasn't expected. Do be aware of the extortionate prices charged by cafés for water (3.50€) - you can buy it cheaper in some of the duty-free shops (2€) at more reasonable cost. Also only 15 minutes of free wifi stingy and charging for more in this day and age is deeply odd. These niggles aside however, overall quite impressed.
Very negative experience at this airport, rude staff, terrible food, unprofessional, not clean, lines suck, ridiculous. Will avoid this airport in the future at all cost.

We had an incredibly negative experience at this airport. It was joint incompetence and unprofessionalism from the airport staff and the airline which is why I write this review. We had an evening flight on Volotea delayed and ultimately cancelled at around 1am after we had boarded the aircraft. I'll start by saying that I understand that delays happen and it isn't the cancellation but the terrible treatment overnight that was the problem here. I have had excellent experiences with cancelled flights at other airports. As we got off the plane, the issues began. We were the only passengers remaining at the airport. Several flustered airport staff were waiting at the gate, giving no information and saying they would make an announcement in several minutes. After 30+ minutes, we hear that there will be accommodation but to wait. We wait and then they say there is no accommodation and our flight is at 1530 the following day but do not tell us where we can sleep in the airport. There is confusion, some people are told to leave and gather bags at bag check. Some say we need to vacate the terminal, leave the airport. No food or water is available. Airport staff is not telling anyone anything. We try to sleep on a bench and are ushered upstairs. After we lay down, a different airport staff member tells us we must leave the terminal and go back through passport check to baggage claim. He says there is a place for us to sleep and once we go through passport control, we ask a pilot where we are supposed to go and he says he has no idea, we can sleep anywhere I guess. There's metal benches only with arm rests to prevent laying down. Older people and family's are in very difficult sleeping positions. Staff all disappeared. Only a dozen blankets and pads were given out to some, we were lucky and got one between my husband and I. Throughout the next day, delays are continuing on our flight and the airline claims its the airport's fault (?) and we keep receiving bad information from staff. Meal vouchers are late and the cafe initially tried to reject it. Communication with us was abysmal. Some were told accommodation would be reimbursed, others weren't, we were moved around the airport all night, only able to sleep from 4-6 bookended by airport staff saying we had to move. This airport is unprofessional and unprepared to handle the most mundane challenges of air travel. Do not fly through here if you can help it and avoid Volotea.

Language barrier and extremely rude security staff. The airport was fairly small, clean and easy to find your way. I did not have to wait long in the queue. Both check in and other procedures ended very quickly to my surprise. Most of the staff at passport check and other parts of the airport seemed nice, but there was one terribly rude lady at the handbag check who -I assume - didn’t know English and therefore thought she could touch me without permission and grunt at me to express herself. There was one wooden mushroom that I bought for decoration purpose in one of my handbags and seemed suspicious to her on the x-ray, she first grunted and angrily pointed my bag. When I started to talk in English, she called her younger colleague to tell me that they have to check inside my bag. Its zip was broken so I had to sew it, so they said they needed to cut the bag open. I asked if they had bags to put my belongings or anything to sew it again, but at the end they cut it. While they were busy opening it, I was so panicked and confused, and I don’t know, I thought they were done checking my other luggages that were apparently waiting in line. When I attempted to walk towards my bags waiting on the conveyor belt, the same lady who didn’t know English raised her hand to push me back and yelled at me. And she and her younger colleague found the wooden mushroom and pulled it up from among my clothes only to look at each other and laugh. Let alone a simple apology, none of them showed any effort to make any explanation until I asked. And during the rest of my time, the lady spent her sweet time lifting the deodorants and some other liquids, which I forgot there, from my bags and grunting at me for each, as if I committed a crime. At least the younger lady tried to explain to me in English, but it was only when I asked a objected to or questioned the situation. I can understand that the security staff has to be very careful with the passengers and and are obliged to implement the rules – but this is not the way to do it. No one deserves this just because they are foreigners, it is important for all of us how to show respect to each other and communicate properly. And since it is a touristic destination, it should not be too much to ask the staff to know English.

Traveled here during covid time. The terminal building is newly built and well laid out. Signaling was very clear and seats, floor etc were exceptionally clean. Security control was fast and easy but seems a mess when they're a huge amount of passengers the same time, as they've only a few lanes. Inbound passport control can take a while as generally only a raw desks are open. Outbound is fine. They've some large duty-free shops. Biggest letdown is ground transportation. Taxis are overpriced and a bus is running at odd times.

Depart this airport for Amsterdam and arrived at this airport from Amsterdam. The airport is a small but quick airport. Security could be quicker, however was adequate for the size of airport. They are no shops airside, but there is a cafe land-side. Toilets are clean, and they are plenty seats & TV in departure lounge. Arriving in Dundee, was straight forward, little walking to the taxi rank as the taxis are allowed right up to the main door.

Excellent airport having recently done a roundtrip from Dundee to Birmingham. It is really convenient for those working in and around Dundee with reliable flights from both Flybe and Cityjet (Air France). If you need to get away from Dundee Birmingham and London are ideal for onward connections and you don't have the hassle of having to drive to Edinburgh pay for parking and the long check in times. Here you can check-in 30-40 mins prior to your flight.

Beautiful views on take-off free long-term parking nice friendly efficient staff and so convenient if you live between Edinburgh and Aberdeen. But does it really have to be so prohibitively costly for the non-business and small business traveler? The dreary trek to Edinburgh by train and bus or even car adds 2 hours but saves hundreds of pounds. When's Easyjet coming to Leuchars? Air France needs some competition.

Dundee Airport provides a convenient link direct to London City Birmingham & Belfast. The airport is small and there are no shops. There is a Costa coffee stall and the airport terminal is modern and comfortable. I would recommend flying from Dundee Air France now provide the Dundee to London City route and Fly Woosh the Birmingham & Belfast services. My only gripe lies with the airlines themselves who do not seem to realise that if they lowered their weekend prices they could cash in on a lucrative leisure market which is put off by the high prices. Dundee to London route is only worthwhile for leisure if booked way in advance and you can fly out with peak periods.

Flew out of Dundee Airport for the first time (even though it is our home town when we are back for the summer holidays). Friendly check-in staff and understanding security staff. Yes it is a small airport and lacks the faciilities of say Edinburgh and Glasgow. But after the 'Glasgow' incident it was refreshing to drive to an airport and not suffer the issues encountered at other BAA airports. The takeoff to London City provides a fantastic view of the Tay. Will use it more often.

Dundee Airport is very small but has a modern terminal building. Facilities are not suprisingly rather limited but the check-in is very quick and easy. Free parking is available. The only route is the Scot Airways service to London City Airport which operates several times daily. The only negative aspect is the lack of public transport links but a taxi ride to the city centre takes only five minutes. The main Aberdeen-Glasgow railway passes the airport - the lack of a station is annoying. Compared to the long queues and delays at larger airports the tiny Dundee Airport is a delight to use and a useful alternative to Edinburgh or Aberdeen airports. The view of the city and the River Tay on takeoff/landing is stunning.

The airport should be embarrassed. A 30 min queue to get through the 1 security station that was open. According to the cafe staff today was a small queue, it’s normally worse. Then everyone herded into an undersized, overheated lounge and flight was delayed, probably due to the queues. This is despite the public announcement 20 mins prior that the flight was now boarding. Please Dunedin airport get somebody who knows what they are doing.

Decided to fly direct from Brisbane to Dunedin rather than via Christchurch then driving. I had previously flown into Dunedin over 20 years ago and the differences were huge from then until now. It is a small airport for a small city, so it is compact but effectively laid out. International flights arrive at an annex that is connected to the main terminal building by a corridor. There are no Smartgates at immigration but it only receives a single international flight at a time, it was also good that all three counters were manned for quick processing. To get to the rental car office, you have to leave the terminal, turn left and re-enter the annex building, which was quite a cold walk on a late night flight. For the return trip, it was a very busy morning with several domestic flights departing near the same time as my international flight, thus international passengers were held in the main terminal area until those domestic flights were processed before being allowed through for screening. However there is only a couple of vending machines at the international gates with a small duty free, so it is better to not rush through.

DUD is a small but efficient airport with everything you need. Landed from Wellington bags out very quickly. The airport is quite far from city centre (30-40 mins) cost nearly 100 dollars by Taxi and 30 dollars by super shuttle. Departure is well organised check-in sufficient airline lounge is located upstairs security check right before you board.

Think it only has a dozen flights or so a day exclusively under the Air NZ banner now Freedom Air is being re-amalgamated into Air NZ. It has been well modernised and seems very spacious. It has the advantages of a small airport with short distances plane to terminal to baggage collection and to car park. We were in the car and off within 10 mins of getting off the lane. On departure there is a great upstairs light and airy waiting/eating/ arrivals area with plenty of space and excellent views. There are adequate drinks food and shop. The only downside was that the hire car companies closed quite early so as we were arriving at 9.00 pm we had to persuade friends to come and collect us.

The pick up area at arrivals requires urgent attention. How can an international airport have a pick up zone for so few cars. To make matters worse it has a boom that has to operate in that connection. Absolute nightmare. Designers rethink.

Why are there no porters in drop off and pick up points to load luggage onto trolleys? Older ladies should be considered when travelling without s male or when being picked up or dropped off by a lady. Luggage is heavy for ladies to lift. There used to be porters it's now no longer a service. Why?

Durban's new airport - King Shaka International - was opened for the 2010 World Cup. It was designed as a state-of-the art regional airport for Durban / KwaZulu/Natal region. The is plenty of space for stopping in the drop-off zone, with direct access to the terminal. There are 3 seperate check-in islands for BA, SAA and Emirates. The departure concourse is spacious, with enough seating for waiting passengers. In the arrivals hall, there is a food court, with a Piazza, some shops, a Woolworths, banks and post office. Also a tourist information office. After security, there is plenty of space. Unfortunately, some lounges were closed due to renovations, but this is only temporary. The domestic terminal has plenty of space, so a quiet corner for reading or working is not a problem. If more international arrivals / departures materialise, then the current 2 departure gates could prove to be a bit underdimensioned in the future.

The long term car parking at this airport is a nightmare. There is not enough and some genius has blocked off the additional parking adjacent to the long term so there are empty spaces there. There are cars parked in places that is not an actual parking bay and also on the pavements, these people are paying to park there when there is no proper space. The airport has also removed the golf carts which transported passengers to the terminal and replaced with a few cars which are rarely there at off peak hours like the early hours which means a long walk to the terminal often in the dark. Other South African Airports offer discounted rates when you book and pay in advance. This one does not so it is expensive to park there and with limited facilities. The security point in the domestic section is often crowded due to not all the check points being open. In international if you get more than one flight arrive the immigration queues can be long and frustrating.

Small regional airport, mostly domestic flights with limited international flights. Was told it was built to accommodate World Cup in South Africa. You can definitely tell the airport interior and parking facility are modern and efficiently laid out. Because it is a small regional airports, you shouldn't expect too much on shopping or dining options. However, for an airport this size, its shops and restaurant/cafe options seem adequate, actually surprisingly many. One short coming is it's dining (food court) area. It was rather poorly laid out, and seem unwelcoming.

A generally good experience at Durban airport. Arrival is quite simple and they seem to keep the touts out of the waiting area. The check-in is well organized and immigration (outbound) proceeded quickly. There are a number of shops and restaurants. The food and the shopping are forgettable but not expensive. Decent amount of seating at the gates. Wifi works fine.

Landed 08H00 from CPT and out in 10mins as no baggage. Long walk as aircraft parked far. Very nice and clean airport. Really like the wide choice of outdoor restaurants in the garden. P/up and go vehicles move fast. Police and security officials visible.
A fantastic new airport that is miles ahead of the old Durban International. Bright spacious and with a feeling of quality.

The new King Shaka airport is roomy airy and thoughtfully planned. There are a dozen or so retail outlets on the ground floor accessible to all and more retail outlets past security on the second floor where check-in occurs. There was an airport shuttle service connecting the airport to downtown Durban (and some coastal points along the way) that was reliable going into town but not coming back. Not sure if this is a regular service or if it was only during the World Cup.

Durban is a very nice airport. I took a connecting flight on Mango airlines to Johannesburg. It was nice clean and well laid out The Spur on the top floor has a great view of the tarmac and runway. Remember that to get to your flight there is no entry ramp but you have to walk outside onto the tarmac to walk the stairs onto the aircraft.

Kazi Nazrul Islam airport (RDP), Durgapur is a new greenfield airport in the the industrial city of Durgapur, West Bengal (Eastern India). It is a growing airport, which holds much promise for improving air connectivity to this part of the state and can become a major player in boosting tourism and business in the area. The connectivity from the city to the airport has improved but still needs more intervention including development of the surrounding areas.
Was disappointed during check-in. Asked for an airport facility fee £6 each even though nothing was mentioned while booking the flights. The lounge and airport were freezing cold despite extra fee.

Customer service has deteriorated significantly since my last trip in Jan. I arrived to catch KL1534 on 27 March 2012. Check-in agent said she could not tag my suitcase through to my final destination claiming that a routing of 4 flights cannot be printed on a single tag. I have taken many 4 flight journeys in the past with a single bag tag printed at the starting airport. I suspect that the real reason is that doing so involves some complication and that she just couldn't be bothered. The airside gents' toilet stank of sewage so badly it was impossible to set foot in there. Finally there was no priority boarding for Skyteam Elite members on the KLM flights: boarding was done by everyone stampeding for the gate queue as soon as the flight was called. If this airport wants to survive let alone continue charging passengers a £6 departure fee which its rivals in the region do not it needs to start running a much more professional operation.

I flew from MME for the first time in almost a year largely because the cost of KLM tickets to a long haul destination have for some reason become more expensive than their equivalents from MAN. This time however there was only about a £60 difference between the MME-AMS-SEA-BUR flight compared to going from MAN and I thought that was worth paying for the convenience and absence of queues that MME offers. On the outward trip at least it was. Apart from the KLM flight I boarded there was almost no traffic at all (I get the impression the loss of charter and holiday flights due to the recession must have hit MME hard) and it remains one of the most stress-free airports I've ever used. There was one irritation. The Iceland volcano business started while I was away as a result of which my return was delayed by four days. While I was away I emailed MME telling them that my car would overstay its paid-in-advance booking in the airport car park asking them not to clamp it or have it towed away and asking if I'd be liable for any extra charge. Don't worry your car is safe and no extra charge came a very quick reply. However when I did return there were no airport staff around anywhere to get my ticket validated and I had to pay an extra £38 in the machine to get out of the car park. I later wrote to the airport enclosing the receipt and asking if they'd consider refunding me. It's now two months later and I've had no reply. Admittedly this is a very minor problem compared to the volcano disruption some people experienced but given that MME must be having real problems retaining routes and passengers (not surprising given how much the cost of KLM flights from the airport have gone up) I didn't find that very impressive; especially given that the volcano disruption would have meant fewer departing passengers and thus my car was not taking up a space that someone else would have wanted and been willing to pay for.

I should report good news. On a recent flight to AMS my pre-printed boarding pass could not be read by the scanner at security and I was dealt with (as were other passengers in a similar situation) very brusquely and rudely by a couldn't-care-less it's-everybody-else's-fault-but-mine attendant. On my return I wrote a letter of complaint to the airport manager received an immediate acknowledgement and within a few days a detailed and thoughtful apology not just a standard half-hearted general fob-off. Excellent PR which I applaud.

I have used this airport much more regularly since my previous comment and cannot fault it as a quick departure/arrival point. I flew in from AMS on Saturday afternoon and even with hold luggage to collect was driving away in my car just 12 minutes after touching down. There aren't many facilities and the staff are willing in a slightly amateurish way rather than polished in PR techniques but who cares when progress through the terminal is so quick and easy? Let's hope it doesn't grow too quickly for its own good!

First time used MME for a holiday charter flight (to Paphos) though used MME many times before as feeder to either AMS or LHR. All very efficient though agree with previous comment about making use of shops and cafe/bar before going thru security. On return baggages arrived in arrivals hall before we did even though B737 800 series plane was full with about 190 pax. At Paphos airport departures still called in Teeside (sic) as do most people me thinks. Signposting at airport could be better during current refurbishments though overall experience superior to NCL.

I agree with both previous comments. Although my most local airport I used it for the first time only this week to fly out to LUX via AMS (with KLM) then back from BRU via LHR (with BMI). I was on the road barely 10 minutes after landing on my return (hand baggage only) but had some trouble checking in at Brussels where the staff still referred to the airport as Teesside then again passing through passport control at Heathrow when I gave Teesside as my destination and was told somewhat sharply (and lacking any humour in tone or body language) by the man on the desk that there was no such place! Seriously road signs must be a real pain for strangers to the area - why on earth can't quick stick-on amendments have been made by now? Overall however a pleasantly small and efficient operation - although like Leeds/Bradford (of which in many ways this is a smaller version) passengers will need to be prepared to get very wet and/or cold when joining or leaving aircraft in poor weather.

I use this little airport for flights between northern England and SE Asia via AMS on KLM. I find it a very convenient feeder airport to the AMS hub and the small size of the terminal ensures that arrivals are swift and painless - I'm on the road within 15 mins of hitting the tarmac in most cases. Staff are generally friendly and helpful. By contrast nearby NCL - which used to be very quick and efficient - is much more hassle with some of the most miserable ground staff in Europe.

Finding this airport can be confusing because it recently changed its name from Teesside to Durham/Tees Valley. Signs on the main feeder roads (i.e. the A19 A66 and A1M) have not all been updated so look out for either. There is a free bus to and from Darlington rail station but it takes a while and is only hourly outside peak times. At the time of writing (12 May 2006) a new terminal building is under construction. The temporary entrance is on the west side of the existing terminal and again is not well signposted. This airport's major strength is that because there are only one or two flights coming and going at any time there are never any massive queues. You'll get through security and (for incoming international passengers) customs and immigration a lot quicker than at NCL or LBA. The long-term car park is significantly cheaper too. There are self-service check in machines for BMI flights to Heathrow and desks for all other flights. If you want something to eat before your flight I suggest getting it at the pub or café BEFORE going through security as the only airside food outlet does pretty grim reheated sandwiches and not much else. Ditto for newspapers/books/magazines - there is a W.H. Smith in the check-in area but not the departure lounge (but it does have a bar and a duty free shop). If there's nothing in it price-wise I would always fly from MME in preference to LBA or NCL because it's a very quick airport to get in and out of; but the facilities are more limited.

Came to Dushanbe airport at around 3am for my very early flight to Istanbul. The new terminal is small but functional and easy to go through. Not plenty to do but the airside cafe is quite nice with good selection and the free wifi was actually quite fast. Duty free shop has the typical selection you see everywhere and some local products. Plenty of places to sit down unless more than 3 or 4 flights going at the same time, it's not a very busy airport.

After going through a nightmare in Tashkent airport I was expecting to face something similar in Dushanbe. I was surprised - in a positive way. Yes the airport is old no facilities but - it took me 15 minutes to get the visa another 15 to go through passport control and once I finished with that my suitcase was already waiting for me. No custom forms to fill out only a short immigration form. Thinking that this may have been an exception I arrived to the airport 2 hours before my departure. 5 minutes for check in no queue in passport control and literally a minute in security check (no one cares about things like liquids taking out laptops etc.). Which left me with more than an hour and half in the terminal where there is nothing to do. A small duty free (expensive) and a small bar are the only things for entertaining no wireless of course. Overall not bad at all. The new terminal building is supposed to be ready this fall.

Welcome back to the 1950s! Soviet era customer service and chaos. Dushanbe only has 2 flights a week from Istanbul (most flights are from Moscow) - if they had more the system would collapse. On arrival it took 3 hours to clear immigration - once I got my visa I had to wake up the border official to stamp my passport! Usual FSU customer service standards - it took 20 minutes from getting to the desk to receiving a boarding card with the check in agent calling her friends and wandering off during check in hand writing passenger details carry your own bag through the scanner etc. They relieved me of $40 exit charge for which I got no receipt so I am not sure if this was simply a bit of Tajik private enterprise or a tax on foreigners. Airside there is absolutely no space - the airport was designed before security measures and you simply have to wait until 5 minutes before the flight before you go through. Duty free closed (with only 2 flights of westerners a week you would think it was worth their while to open it) and nothing at all airside aside from a few plastic chairs. Land side there is a coffee shop selling bizzarely coloured cakes and a variety of beverages but as the Turkish Airlines flight is horribly early in the morning I did not feel up to consuming anything so cannot comment!

This is not the first time flying from and to Dusseldorf, but everytime (and also today) we need to wait extremely long to get our luggage. Today it took over 1,5 hours to get it. I have trackers in our suitcases and I saw that they were already in the back for a long time. Except our stroller, so we now already waiting for two hours for a stroller. Which is one of the first things you need as a parent traveling. It’s really ridiculous! Hire some more people for in the back!

Security staff seems to have been trained to be rude and unpleasant to the extreme. No English spoken and very poor German, if any. Moreover, only two lines out of seven were open, while the rest of the staff, about ten of them, chatted and watched their phones. I guess many passengers missed their flights that evening. Having passed the body scanner, they give you instructions with rude gestures and no words. Even my eyeglasses and pullover had to go through x rays. Toilets are half functioning, dirty and smelly. Gates' directions are highly confusing and long walks. To board the bus to the plane, we had to walk down three floors on outdoor metal stairs with our hand luggage. No elevator functioning and no assistance. We are a 82-year old couple. I have been traveling for decades to more than 100 countries all over the world and Dusseldorf is definitely a bad one.

We landed at 22:00 and went directly to the bagage claim area. There we waited and waited with no information about the delay of our luggage. After 45 minutes they announced that because of a staff shortage the moving of luggage was a problem. We waited another 30 minutes before we finally got our luggage.

When I came into the security area for the check, the staff were aggressive and rude. The woman at the entrance looked and acted like an army member to put it politely (in the worst sense) and then asked me to roll up my trouser leg (I had never had this at any airport in the world up to then). I had brought little luggage and look and act like a mild mannered ordinary man. I heard her muttering to a female colleague 'Englischman' in an offensive manner. I was shaken after such awful behaviour.  Another mild looking man had been harassed simply for having a laptop. Then another security guard checked everything in my hand luggage and claimed I had too much shampoo (it was a tiny bottle). The staff were unbelievably rude and I will never go to that airport again if I can. I will try Cologne, Frankfurt, even go by into Belgium or France to fly back. Then the waiting area had practically no facilities anywhere. One vending machine and one small counter of food/drinks. One small tv screen, for ages no staff to let you through to the final waiting area. Couldn't wait to get out of this small time airport.

The security staff, especially one lady, is extremely rude! I experienced the same rude behavior of this lady before. Most unfriendly and rude security control She Should learn behaviour with older people. Its just the way you tell things to a guest. She yelled at me like a 18 year old school boy who made a mistake, because I put the box with my belongings in a vertical instead of horizontal direction towards the belt. I told her that its not the way to yell at a 65 year old person and she laughed at me, telling me that she only advises guests two times how to put things correctly and if its not done the way she wants it, she would yell.

The staff in the security check point are extremely disrespectful. I wasn’t aware of the rules that all travelers need to take out small liquid bottles and put them in a small plastic bags. In the US, if the volume is below 1 oz, you are fine. They had me take out all my laptop, iPad, Kindle and phones, and put through the system to the other side. When I was taking out my makeup stuff, I asked if they could let me keep all my stuff together, and they said no. What is even worse is that when I asked what I should take out from my makeup bag and put to the plastic bag they provided. The security woman yelled at me “Everything! Have you ever taken a plane before??” I was like “Yes, but never in Düsseldorf. You guys are different.” She yelled at me again “do you have a problem? If you do, take your stuff and leave!!” I was shocked. I’ve traveled to over 30 countries in the past few years and been through many many airports. I haven’t seen any one who are as disrespectful and unprofessional like those in Düsseldorf airport!! That is unbelievable and unacceptable!
Very poor. On a plane from UK and only 40% of passport control booths open. Therefore, long slow queues. Didn't they know a plane was landing? Ridiculous.

As a frequent traveller I would like to express my sadness regarding DUS security staff. 1st of all it’s not acceptable to have airport security personal that doesn’t speak English. It’s a shame in the middle of Europe. Second of all they didn’t accept my support to help them what is wrong with my luggage. They prefer to remove everything from 3 different bags to keep one small bottle of water. It’s too behind to many other small airports located in Europe where the technology used is much better and personal with better knowledge.

We were flying to Larnaca from Prague and had a connecting flight through Dusseldorf. We arrived on time, everything was OK, as we didn't expect anything negative) First surprise was that in order to pass the passport control you needed to take the stairs and no elevator available nearby, so we had to carry our bags.. The passport control was OK, and then we had to take bother stairs down, but we kind of got used already to the comfort provided by the airport. Finally we found our gate and decided to get some snack. The only tiny little counter with brezels and only sparkling water was not working. The coffee machine was out of order too. There was a notice that the next snack stand was nearby, by it was not true - in this area (around gates A57 and 83) it was the only one. There was also a machine that was supposed to be selling drinks, but it was out of order as well. I would not be surprised if the lavatory would be unavailable as well. So we spent 2 nice hours waiting for our connecting flight and I will make sure not to get tickets through this airport anymore. We've never experienced anything like this before. I would be glad to read some positive review about this airport one day. But I doubt it could happen.

I fly an average of 12 times a year and Dusseldorf airport is the worst airport I have ever been to. They stole half of my 100ml liquids because the plastic bags were to big. I always use the same plastic bags for my liquids all over the world and this was never a problem anywhere. They treated us like criminals and were very arrogant. They abused their power on us. And we almost missed our flight. I will never fly from this airport again and advise anyone not to go here. Go to Keulen airport, much better.

A truly awful drop-off and pick up area. Its called a rapid drop off. It's slow chaotic and pathetic. And they have the cheek to charge £5 for it. Which I wouldn't mind paying if it actually was rapid.

This has to be in the worst airport I've ever used in the UK and across the world for treatment by security staff I know there have a job to do but well their ability to deal with passengers is shockingly bad, I took my prescription medication in a separate clear bag with the labels on. As I had been instructed to do at another UK airport, being advised having the prescription labels matching my passport details would help the process. I may as well have been trying to take liquid cannabis instead of anti inflammatory creams. I was repeatedly asked for my paper prescription, I can only assume the staff haven't been ill for a number of years so have no idea the NHS has stopped issuing paper prescriptions; it's all done electronically. After the 10 minutes of interrogation with me finally getting the NHS app working to show them they were actually my prescriptions, I just wondered shouldn't there be more interested that my passport maybe false if it aligned to all the details on the prescription labels on my medicine? And they didn't believe a word of it. More interested in a little bottle of something bigger than you're allowed. Final indignation because they'd messed me around so much before the scanners, I then had a full body search going through. It is the last time I ever use this airport.

Wow, it is some years since we used our closest airport. It was a shock. We knew that EMA was a massive cargo hub but did not realise how much the focus on cargo has detracted from the development of passenger services. To say that time has stood still would be fairly accurate. The post-security facilities are small and desperately overcrowded. Too little seating and what food and drink outlets there were were overcrowded. On our return we disembarked the plane, always stairs here, no investment in air jetties, and had to walk outside the entire length of the terminal to enter what can only be described as a holding shed. From here to the four e-gates. Three aircraft had landed in quick succession so it was all crowed and slow. Walkways to car parks are rough and most passengers walked on the road as these at least were properly tarmaced. I don't know if EMA is the worst and most neglected UK airport but it certainly feels like it.

Ok flying out form this airport but coming back from our holiday we landed at 12.30pm, what a really bad experience. There were 7 in our party, 3 of them were children, it was late at night traveling back, they just don't care. It took us 2 hours just to get though passport control to get to our baggage, only 1 person on passport control and he didn't care. We'll we never go there again.

Pretty lacklustre airport, with just a handful of standard shops like WHSmiths, and Boots. The restaurant choice is pretty poor, between Frankie and Bennies, Starbucks and a burger place. The Ryanair check in desk originally had no staff, until after around 20 minutes one member came to start checking people in. The security process was relatively fast.

Dropped off my daughter today at EMA where they charge a disgusting £5 for a time limit of 15 minutes. I was able to drop her off in a few minutes. However, it then took a further 16 minutes to get to the barrier. I know this because I noted the time. Very conveniently there was only one exit working for 2 lanes of traffic, making it impossible to get out in the allotted time. The problem was compounded by various people struggling with the barrier. A lot of people got out their cars and began to shout at the utterly useless car park staff to do something about the huge que of traffic. They simply looked on gormlessly and then wandered off. Drivers, obviously frustrated as hell, then began to turn on any individual having problems with the barrier. Some poor woman screamed 'shut up' at the top of her lungs to the drivers behind her. A truly lovely experience. Do yourself a favour and fly from someone else.

Flew out of EMA on the 4/05/23 to CFU on an afternoon flight. Pre booked short stay 1 car park online, entrance and exit worked without problem via number plate recognition. Short walk to departures and through luggage drop off with minimal delay. Security was very quick and staff friendly. Used the escape lounge whilst waiting for boarding and this was very relaxing and the staff were friendly and working hard to keep the food topped up, a very good experience. Boarding went smoothly and flight away only 10 minutes behind schedule. On return on the 11/05/23 flight landed 5 minutes ahead of schedule, deplaned quickly and through passport control via E-gates with no delay. Baggage already available to collect by the time we entered the collection area and straight out to the car. So all in all another very positive experience at EMA.

EMA has always been a great airport for me and my family when we fly out of it. Recently I was lucky enough to go to Paphos via EMA and here is my honest review of the experience. Check in was amazingly fast with 0 queues bearing in mind we got there at 12PM. Our bags were took and it’s just a quick stroll to security in which at first the queues seemed long however, moved very fast. I personally had no issues at all and I do recommend if you’re not a frequent flyer or not used to security to watch the informative video provided. It helps makes your and everyone else’s experience faster and easier. Moving on, duty free is your typical British airport duty free with a wide range of products. Leaving it there was 2 main bars to choose from which I must unfortunately say was not the best for accommodating the amount of users at the airport. The queues were huge however the beverages were very nice but if you intend on having more than 1 drink. Order your 2 rounds in 1 go. It’s not worth the wait. The airport signs and departure boards are very informative and give a clear indication on where to go. The walk to the gate is very short and the longest you’ll have to walk is no less than 10 mins at max. We boarded without hassle and the staff were very kind to all of us who flew. One main issue is the WiFi. I did pay a pound for WiFi that was not good at all. Very slow. Thanks for reading and I hope you have a good experience at East Midlands the next time you fly!

Terrible airport. Rude security staff, other staff shouting at passengers. Delays. No announcements. This is my first visit to this airport and am already dreading the return journey. Definitely will not be using again

Great experience at EMA. Travelled out on the 22/04/22 to Faro and returned 29/04/22. Given the recent headlines about problems with departures and arrivals at certain UK airports I was little concerned about delays but this proved unfounded. Parked up in short stay 1 car park without any issues which I had booked via the EMA website. From walking to departures, Checking in at the desk and through security took a grand total of 24 minutes. Staff at the checkin desk and at security were helpful and cheerful so full marks to them. The only slight negative was that we had booked the Escape Lounge which had been due to open again on the 20/04/22 but that was delayed so our booking was cancelled but it only took them a couple of days to refund the payment. On the return to EMA on the 29/04/22 again everything went like clockwork, disembarked within a few minutes of coming to a halt. Security was quite speedy using the E-gates and through to baggage collection which was very prompt and out to the car and departed the car park with the NPR working without a problem. So a thank you to all at EMA for making our first holiday since 2019 a trouble free departure and arrival.

International Airport, far, far from it. Upon arrival you are immediately greeted by a set of stairs that a chairlift would struggle to reach the top off. Walking through portacabins to a large shed , only to be joined by another large flight for immigration checks. 42 mins in a queue to get through the biometric machines. Then into pick up luggage, quick use of bathrooms a total disgrace. Urinals out of order, no toilet paper, water on the floor. Finally to Top it off You must pay £1 to have the luxury of using their luggage trolleys. I’ve not seen this at any airports but I’m sure Glasgow will follow on, just like Prestwick have. Why Tourists want to visit here is beyond me.
Absolute waste of time, an early flight, but no meal deals or yesterdays food sold, WH Smith and Boots quite happy to sell overpriced food, not impressed.

What an awful airport.  Check in - never seen anything like it, tiny scales and then after checking passengers have to take their luggage from the tiny check in desk and lift it onto the conveyor belt. Some people were struggling and no airport staff helped them. Crowded and not enough seats to accommodate passengers. Chaotic and not what I expected of the beautiful country of Scotland. Put me off traveling through this airport again.

Arrived at Edinburgh airport to fly with Ryanair for a 5.55am flight to Alicante. Chaos from start to finish. We checked in at one location then had to drop bags at a different location, which took 25 minutes. The queue to reach security was all the way outside and took 35 minutes to get up the escalator. When up stairs there were hundreds of people with no queue system in place where absolute chaos ensued. There was a lack of staff and systems in place to ensure a smooth transition and to make sure everyone caught their flight. I have never in over 50 years of travel witnessed anything so unorganised and absolute mayhem. We over heard a member of staff saying it takes 14 minutes to get through security' eventually after 45 minutes we asked a member of staff after showing our boarding passes were we hoping to miss our final call she let us skip a bit of the queue but we still had to queue and by the time we got through the security queue the flight had closed for boarding. The swissport staff stated the bus had departed to take passengers to the flight and we could not board despite the flight still waiting for take off. The member of staff was not helpful and directed us to Ryanair check in which we did to be told to go to the Swissport desk, who then told us to go back to Ryanair check in desk. We insisted on speaking to their manager who was helpful and we then had to go back to Ryanair check in who arranged a flight the next day for £100 pounds each. My partner and I had to book an airport hotel that night, this terrible experience cost over £400 more and we lost 2 days from our holiday. My advice is avoid Edinburgh airport if possible, there are too many early morning flights which they are unable to accommodate due to staffing and chaotic systems in place. Shocking service and staff ranged from very helpful to incompetent and those who simply did not care and were uninterested.

I'm ashamed that travellers from other countries have to experience this mess that claims to be an airport. On the plus side the staff we encountered were really very pleasant. However it is disorganised and tatty. Parts are extremely dirty and haven't been cleaned for years (the walkway to the bus stops) Its a depressing way to start or end a holiday for residents and I cant imagine was travellers from other countries make of it.

We have arrived to be greeted by utter carnage due to the Airports poor ability to deal with a bit of snow and slush. We landed at 1200 and have now been waiting over 90 mins waiting for buses. This is Scotland where it snows in Winter right? EasyJet have not offered any water but " hey feel free to use the loo". Fortunately we are not under a tight schedule but many passengers are so we should be compensated in some way. If it was a train we could claim. Very disappointed in our National Airport.

Edinburgh is one of the worst airports you could ever have the misfortune to use, flight arrived no steps, no buses to tranfer to building then wait an age for baggage to arrive, its a disgrace, operates like a third world country, its like they are not expecting a plane to arrive, an embarrassment.

My husband and I arrived back at Edinburgh airport at 16.45, had a transfer booked for 6 pm thinking this would give us plenty of time to get through security checks and collect our luggage. Clearly we were wrong. We passed through security which is always a bit of a shambles, but nevertheless we waited over an hour on our luggage so missed our transfer. There were 4 flights coming through one carousel, which was not great. But worst of all the baggage handlers we spoke were rude and unhelpful. Swissport who were our baggage handlers basically did nothing to help. Worst of all 4 people sitting in the office doing absolutely nothing.

Arrival back at Edinburgh makes me embarrassed for any tourists arriving in Scotland. I've seen better and cleaner airports in 3rd world countries. The weird flights of stairs and narrow corridors before passport control means a huge crowd develops before you can join the queue. Definitely not enough space for arrivals. Passport control queue moved slowly. No decent signage to say where folk with certain passports should go. Ideally UK passports could be a separate queue but you get flung in with the majority of other nationals. Eventually got through passport control and wanted to use the toilet. Did an about turn when I saw the state of the gents. 3 cubicles and 3 urinals is not enough for 4 international flights arriving at the same time. Especially when one urinal is overflowing with urine and 3 of the toilets covered in urine and faeces. Disgusting! Tried a different bathroom after bag pick-up and reversed out again as this was in a similar state. Speaking of bag pick-up - absolute shambles. 4 international flights bags going on to 1 conveyor. Waited for ages for our suitcases. Ridiculous. Road out of Edinburgh is like a 3rd world country road. Potholes from one end to the other. Cannot believe this is how we welcome tourists to Scotland. Avoid if possible. Glasgow airport far better.

A national embarrassment. Arriving you go upstairs downstairs walk a dingy corridor then repeat before arriving at passport control. Home office not known for being efficient but border force here are useless and miserable. Far from pleasant. If I was a tourist arriving and based the country on this chaos I'd about turn and return to my place of origin. And quickly.

This airport is actually very nice. Due to its size, taxiing is kept at a minimum, the terminal design is airy, bright and has warm colour tones. Other notable features: - has well thought of sitting areas including lounge areas overlooking the tarmac, play areas, pet relief areas, good restaurants. - good customer service in the shops, security. Friendly people - due to the size, it’s not crowded.

Absolute mayhem for departures & arrivals. The normal drop-off/pick-up zone is closed to all except the “accessible”, meaning that the normal pick-up/drop-off zone was completely empty while exhausted, bewildered travellers were forced to walk a maze all the way through the parkade to be greeted by a 3-lane traffic jam behind the parkade and try to find their equally bewildered family member in that chaos. There are staff everywhere in safety vests waving wands around and preventing vehicles from stopping for pick-up, which only exacerbates the situation. Surely resources could be better employed. It appears that there is some kind of construction happening, but that is, in my opinion, no excuse. My mother & I have been around the world in much busier airports (such as LAX) and have never seen such chaos. Edmonton: you can do better.

One of the cleanest airports but car rental returns was a nightmare. Sign was car rental instead of car rental returns. No directions how to enter the gate (turn right - press button and obtain ticket. Bar will be lifted). Directions to P4 / car returns not bold enough to see. No employee to receive returns, I wasted 30 minutes and barely got into the flight. If you can do something to improve, it will be helpful for future travellers. I read similar complaints by other travellers but does not look liked any changes have happened.

Liked the airport of Edmonton. Very efficient security and no big walking distances. A nice bright design that make you feel comfortable. Besides, there are a lot of shopping and dining options here. This Airport can be a role model, how regional mid-size airports should be.

The majority of this airport is fine for a Canadian airport except for the baggage management system, which is worse than most other place in the world. Waiting for over 45 minutes after flight arrival for bags is outrageously pathetic. Dhaka in Bangladesh has less wait times for baggage.
