It is far past the time for this airport to upgrade to a modern system.

I am 63 years old, I was pulled aside for an indepth screening - the lady who was screening me told my husband he could go ahead - I said no I wanted my husband with me, she thoroughly went through my bag with a wand - what was most disturbing was how she would just throw my stuff around - not even closing zippers or putting my liquids bag in the pocket it came out. She was not very friendly - my husband and I were shocked to be treated like this. It was quite rude to be treated like this since I am an elderly woman.

The problem was in security the morning of March 27th 2019, the scanners broke down but one, the staff were throwing the tote trays with passengers things in them to the one scanner that was working. It was chaos! We missed our flight with Westjet, no one from the airline came to get us, and they only held the plane for 10 minutes. Many people missed their flights! There was panic everywhere, even tears! When we got to the gate the plane had just closed the door, the Westjet employ was very cold, and not helpful at all. But did charge us an additional $1300 for 4 more ticket home! This is outrageous! No one wants to take responsibility for this, this is not our fault.

❌Not Verified|  Terrible signage. Arriving late at night into the domestic terminal trying to get to the US terminal you are led first to a bank of windows. You cannot get through and next you find signage taking you to a set of doors that is locked all night long. No one in the airport was helpful. Once you figure out how to exit the terminal and go through U.S. security the situation gets even worse. Over 100 passengers were held in a cramped area until 4 in the morning. Finally, exhausted we were allowed to proceed to our gate. I probably could have designed a worse airport but it would have taken a significant amount of effort.

Horrible signage! I returned with my Hertz Rent-A-Car and has no idea where to go! No signs where to go. No signs indicating the terminal and no person to assist. I travel every week for work and have never had an issue navigating an airport. Got inside and stood in security line for 1/2 hour to be told I had to walk half mile American gates. Are you kidding me? No signs when I walked in that I needed to do this! No person checking passports to say this! Security then tagged me and said I had too many liquids, 4 bottles with less than 3 oz? Seriously? Guy took my bag apart and then said, oh, I guess everything’s ok! Horrible experience!

The only way to fly out of where I live, as I do monthly, is to get a connection either through Edmonton or Calgary. My main reason for writing this review is I cannot stress enough how horrible Calgary airport is. Edmonton is well signed, information of gate changes is always available. The staff are almost always kind and helpful. There is food/drinks or restaurants evenly distributed throughout the airport, and not a far walk to get anything I need.

Recently I've visited Ramon Airport for my vacation, The airport is new (opened in January) and modern, The duty-free shops were nice, there are a few before Check-In and the safety checks and after it near the gates. The airport has 8 gates and has a lounge. Airport staff was very nice and the process of Check-In and security checks didn't take longer than 30 minutes. To be honest, the airport is a bit boring, after the Check-in and security checks beside of a few duty-free shops, there is nothing really to do, That's why I don't recommend coming to the airport more than one hour before departure.

As the previous reviewer noted Eilat airport terminal is in the centre of the city and surrounded by hotels: I didn't believe the taxi driver for a few seconds when he dropped us there! Once inside we got a thorough grilling by security and our bags swabbed throughout for explosives. I think we got extra attention as foreigners but the female security official was very friendly and jovial - much nicer that the humourless officials who you normally meet. Checkin and hand baggage checks were quick and easy as the only flight was our 72-seater Arkia departure. There is a shop/cafe on both landside and airside parts but we didn't get a chance to try either. Overall it does the job well - just be prepared for the security.

Poor service. There is no waiting room for passengers who intend to travel in morning earlier we had to wait outdoors in a cold weather we were more than 50 passengers and we couldn't find a room at Tulip hotel so we waited from 11pm until 4am
I missed my flight. Thousands people do too. After more than 3 hours waiting in a shameless security control queue. Misinformation with no help from airport or Ryanair. And finally no assistance

Worst Airport experience ever! Take another option, if you can. Waited for almost 4 hours in the security line and almost didn’t catch my flight. The people right in front of me all missed their flight. Unbelievable!

Waited 3 hours and half in line to pass the security check. Almost lost the plane. My boots and bag were checked 3 times thorough security scan, also other passengers around me experienced the same problem. No danger to be found. The waiting lines started outside the airport and is probably because of these oversensitive scan machine. Hope they will go through serious revision. Terrible experience in this airport.

Closed 11 pm to 4:30 am they put you outside to wait. I had a flight out of Eindhoven scheduled for Monday Nov.28 at 7 am with Transavia. At 11 pm the security guards told us the airport closed and re-opened at 4:30 AM. The reason they gave is that they had to go home and later would be replaced by the new shift.

Staff all very helpful, in particular a lady from the special assistance team. She went above and beyond , what a lovely lady who clearly is very devoted to her job role. We would choose to fly from Eindhoven airport again as our experience was so smooth and professionally handled. Thank you , such a small thing to say , I hope this gets back to the whole team.

The airport is horrible in any term, it's old, ugly without good infrastructure and most importantly the personnel is totally untrained, rude and rather aggressive in order to transfer their responsibilities to the passengers under the name of "security". On instance, I had the bad luck to have a trip from Eindhoven to Athens and there was a security person who saw me sweaty, yes sweaty, and he started asking me "if I am ok and if everything is fine". When I explained that I am ok, just I feel hot and nervous due to the huge queue, he came after me to ask for my ticket just to take a photo of and send it to the gate in order to put it on a standby mode, literally because I was sweaty! Another example of their great lack of training is the fact that an Italian family was talking behind me since they were nervous too that they would lose their flight to Bologna and an other employee told them that "She saw that they are talking too much", only to get the response that they are going to lose their flight and that her job is related to process the screening and not focus on whether they talk too much or not! If someone wants a prison like experience, then that's a great airport, but either they have to improve it or they need to seriously train their employees to learn how to behave and act based on protocols and not based on what they use to watch on Netflix!

It is a horrible airport. I have flown several times. You have to come there hours before the flight, the workers are stressed our and rude, the waiting lines are endless, there is one toilet only at the airport and even that one they had cleaned during the highest flight traffic so we could to go to the toilet. If you don't have to, don't fly with this airport. I never write review and never write negative reviews but this was so bad that I cannot express it enough. I wouldn't recommend this airport to my worst enemies and I feel terribly sorry for everyone who works at this airport. They should close it

Extremely disappointing and disorganized airport! This is the first airport I have seen where the security check queue starts outside of the airport! Usual waiting time before you can reach the security check turns out to be at least 2 hours, no matter what day and time you are travelling (found out from the people around me in the line, as we had the chance to become best friends during these hours standing together). At the same time there were 4 security check lines that actually worked out of 8 in total? There are two older women, who have been appointed with the task to go back and forth the gigantic queue, again, starting outside of the airport, and yell out people for the next flights.. Of course they do that in Dutch and barely speak English when you ask them any kind of a question. The reason why they have these women is that, on top of all, this is a "silent" airport, which means that you don't get any information whatsoever. I am wondering who decided that this airport can support all the flights that are scheduled (usually about 6-7 departures per hour) when the capacity is suited for less than a third of that. (At least with all the accumulated revenue from this overscheduling, the airport could have invested in reorganizing and/or working with full staff and capacity all the time, again, not the case!) Overall: Very bad experience, extremely long queues, unfriendly and solely Dutch-speaking staff, extremely bad management. Chances are you are going to miss your flight when departing from Eindhoven airport.

Bad management at this airport. Booked flight on Sunday morning 25/9 6.55. Arrived on time, more than 2.5 hours waiting - of the 8 security counters 4 closed, one of those 4 still malfunctions, we don't open the 4 closed counters, but are just waiting. We missed the flight! Flight booked with a layover in the evening at 8 o'clock at the destination and 700EUR poorer. Eindhoven airport has beautiful forms to claim damages but everything is rejected with lying excuses! Must have been instructed government policy to limit flying and therefore irritate as many travelers as possible. That worked out great for us! what a gang of crooks that Eindhoven Airport | Slecht management op deze luchthaven . Op zondagmorgen 25/9 6.55 vlucht geboekt . Op tijd aanwezig ,meer dan 2.5 uur wachten. oorzaak van de 8 security balies 4 gesloten, gaat er van die 4 nog eentje defect , we openen niet de 4 gesloten balies ,maar staan gewoon te wachten . Wij vlucht gemist !! vanwege zakelijke afspraak op 26/9 moesten we op 25/9 op plek bestemming zijn . Vlucht met een overstap geboekt . s' avonds om 8 uur op plek bestemming en 700.-- armer . Vliegveld Eindhoven heeft prachtige formulieren om schade te claimen maar alles wordt met leugenachtige smoesjes afgewezen !!! Zal wel geïnstrueerd overheidsbeleid zijn om vliegen te beperken en daarom zoveel mogelijk reizigers te irriteren . Bij ons is dat prima gelukt ! wat een boevenbende dat Vliegveld Eindhoven

Used this airport multiple times for international and domestic arrivals and departures. Nice and clean. Airport staff are friendly. Provides jet bridge at almost every flight. In my opinion, it needs more coffee shops, eateries and lounges. Parking spot is located conveniently, close to the airport entrance.

SVO-SVX-HEL. Arrived mid morning from Moscow on domestic flight. There seem to be a good number of piers to allow access to the terminal building. Airport in the middle of being fully upgraded with building work everywhere estimated to be finished some time in 2014. Arrival was via various corridors that would not normally see passengers but the luggage was on the belt when we got there and then out into Arrivals. Airport not that busy so things seemed to run OK. Early morning Check-in for departure required basic suitcase scanning before Check-in which seemed a little slow. Security Scanning perfunctory - no need to get laptops out and shoes off with minimal queuing. Facilities in Departure Lounge limited but sufficient. Free WiFi available which was OK. Boarding directly via pier smooth.

Used to be very busy in the Soviet times since then reduced the traffic by at least 300%. At the same time the new terminal was built with more adequate waiting spaces. It is rather modern and clean. Food service is kind of slow. Public transportation to the city is not on top: and I used park-n-fly only once.

Modern airport surprisingly efficient compared with some other internal Russian airports. Arrival facilities good baggage on the conveyor without a long wait. On departure check in facilities were good security efficient and the Skyteam business lounge was of a high standard with free Internet connection although all drinks etc had to be paid for.

We left Uyuni on 07Aug24 & transit La Paz to Lima. We landed in El Alto airport at 10:15am. At 10:30am, we went through security check, with our OB746 boarding pass scanned (Lima bound 7pm flight) by the airport staff. There was nobody at Immigration to give the departure stamp in our passport and the security bag scan (second scan) waved us through to the international boarding area. The boarding gate is R18 so we got a coffee at the cafe with the retail shop opposite international flight boarding gates R19 & R20. At 11am, the cafe & retail shop staff turned off all lights & left so we thought she was going to early lunch. At 11:30am, an airport staff (non-English speaking) escorted us out to the public area & asked us to return to security check at 4pm. At 4:10pm, we attempted to go through security checkpoint. Again the staff does not speak English & pointed to the Spanish sign with N3 to N6 (boarding gates for domestic flights). So I used Google Translate to ask when we can go through secutity check & his response was 4:30pm. At 4:45pm, we went to the queue with Spanish sign with gates R17 to R20. We went to that guy manning that queue, only to find out there was a Spanish sign with a QR code which we need to fill form 250 online (inbound to Bolivia, we filled in the paper 250 form which asked for our next destination & is a completely moot point). Utterly frustrated by a total lack of instructions on security check timing, filling in online declaration form & utter lack of communications or English signs, we finally entered the international boarding area at 5:30pm, after we pointed to the confused immigration staff that we had 2 boarding passes staples together by the Bolivian Airline staff in Uyuni as they thought our final destination was La Paz instead of Lima! In summary, the problems we encountered at La Paz El Alto airport: 1. “International boarding area is closed between 11am & 4pm (all shops are closed then) - no Spanish or English sign saying so 2. No departure instructions in English (eg. when to go through security check, what queue to use, online form 250 3. Inconsistent form 250 declaration form (we filled in paper inbound to Bolivia which included next destination, why is there no early instruction to fill in online 250 form for departure? 3. Lax security check to allow us through to international boarding area when they see our Bolivian Airlines OB746 flight departing 7pm!! 4. Embarassed us when we were escorted out through the security checkpoint, when nonody told us we could not enter international boarding area due to 11am to 4pm closure 5. Lack of communication & signs for international travellers - no English signs & English speaking staff - international indeed! 6. 2 queues at security checkpoint for passport & boarding passes - 1 for boarding gates N3 to N6 (domestic boarding gates) and 1 for R17 to R20 (international flight boarding gates - the guy at R17 to R20 queue rudely pointed us to the N3 to N6 queue so he & the R17 to R20 queue were totally redundant. 7. Incompetent immigration staff - they actually questioned us if our final destination is La Paz when there wee boarding passes to La Paz and Lima stapled together! 8. Unable to connect to NAABOL wifi at all - for the whole 8.5 hours duration at the airport! This airport ordeal will utterly overshadow memory of our beautiful tour experiences in Bolivia!

Nice and small airport at El Alto, La Paz. The process to get my bags was average in time and customs was friendly and polite. There are a few cafes and a couple of restaurants I could see. Ground transpiration is readily available by taxi or "minibus". The airport is not a big building but it has wifi, it is clean and has many standard services.

This place should be a model for small airports around the world. They even use airbridges, which are great for avoiding the cold winds. Luggage didn’t take too long but all bags have to be x-rayed because you’re not allowed to bring meat, fruit or plants into Patagonia. Then there are stalls for taxis and tour bookings, and the VES shuttle bus service to hotels is at the stand marked “Bus” - $180 one-way or $280 if you book the return leg at the same time. Tourist staff can speak English. Great views of the Andes out the right side on approach (I think I saw Mt Fitz Roy) and some gnarly winds. On departure, the shuttle bus dropped us at the airport 90 minutes ahead, which was plenty. Check-in staff raced through the passengers, security was fast and friendly, wifi was free but somewhat unreliable, decent cafe on both sides of security, views of the runway and lake, lots of toilets. Probably the best small regional airport that I’ve ever experienced.

Lovely small airport with one of the best views of any I've ever visited. About 20km from the town but generally one plane at a time so queues transport etc not really an issue. Great coffee bar - go upstairs for views to die for (coffee is also good!). Planes can go early and beware of the winds when leaving. Sympathetically installed to harmonise with landscape (as much as an airport can!). Still need to pay in cash a departure tax - about 5GB Pounds. Also don't carry fresh food in hand luggage even if on an internal flight - it will be confiscated on arrival due to some strange Argentinean regulations.

My flights were delayed for many hours due to weather in Dallas. El Paso airport is the best airport to be stranded in! It has an easily-accessed smoking area in a lovely courtyard. It's small enough to get around quickly, but big enough to have decent food. My delays would have been much worse in a larger airport, but El Paso airport made my delays manageable. Staff were also great. Security and the like (especially outside directing vehicle traffic) were nice and helpful, offering extra help or information if I needed it. Love this airport! The only minor annoyance was that it did not have a lot of charging ports in the seating areas, so I had to stand while my phone was charging.

It's an old airport but there aren't any other choices in the area. Terminal is rather dim considering the perpetual sunshine for which El Paso is known. It seems that they're expanding the terminal. Queuing times acceptable. Being a border area may elicit additional screening from the immigration/customs officers no matter how long you've living here. Foreign citizens lawfully in the Country are recommended to take their passports in addition to their IDs. Excellent wifi signal, shopping options are limited but ok. Again, the terminal looks dim and this makes it look less inviting.

I've lived in El Paso for two years now for school and I often use the airport to visit my hometown as well as other destinations. The busiest I've ever seen the airport from the time of walking through the doors checking baggage going through security and getting to my gate was about 40 minutes (Christmas vacation time). I've even got through in 20 minutes. It's a smaller airport with only one terminal that's ever used and about 10-15 gates (so from security to walk to your gate takes maybe 4-5 minutes). This isn't one of the airports you'll need to devote 2 hours in order to get through it. I'd say 1 hour is fine (because you never know even if it does only take 30 minutes to get to your gate) and maybe 1.5 during busy holiday times or if you're going to have to check the whole family (might even be 2 hours for that).

This airport was a small typical airport for a city of this size but it seems to be really under used. Very little planes are seen taking off or landing when driving by this airport. The terminal is quiet and peaceful so don't arrive too early. Overall a pleasant experience. The only problem I had is how there is no shade at the curbside area so be warned about that. Other than that I don't have much to complain about.

Modern new airport. Many hotels nearby almost within walking distance. Fort Bliss borders and shares airport runway with civilian airport. Many military personnel fly out from this airport. Security departing second visit slow planned for 1 hour to get through security and needed it. If you plan to travel across the border to Juarez by car 10 minutes to get to border from airport. Plan one to two hours for return trip back across border because of US custom check. Encounter one waitress in El Paso who could not speak English. Depending where you are in Juarez you can get by with very little Spanish.

Small airport with a southwest theme much like ABQ. All the employees were speaking spanish instead of English so I wasn't sure which side of the Rio Grande I was actually on! The airport is easily navigable and shuttles to hotels were readily available. No problems besides Spanish being the unofficial language.
Worst airport in my entire life, stupid rules, rude people, what ever happened wit El Salvadoreño hospitality. Crowded and lack of emphaty from people without regard for customers

The second security is designed to isolate those waiting at the gates from the general already secured area where there are no seating areas. Instead, there are many Duty Free shops and a couple of restaurants. There are no restaurants or vendors in the waiting areas. Besides an inconvenience, the second security check (shoes off etc) serves to incentivize shopping. If you wish to sit outside the second secure area, you must patronize a restaurant.

A new terminal has been built but was not yet open so I used the old facilities. Arrivals area was a simple open-sided area of the main building. Check-in took place in a single room at the other end of the building. At the x-ray scanner an operator gazed in the general direction of the monitor screen. The main hall had no AC not even a fan and had a very oppressive atmosphere. Baggage handlers man-handled checked bags out through a back door. After checking in most passengers seemed to go back outside where it was much cooler. The waiting lounge had decent seating some air-conditioning unappealing bathrooms and no shops - it was quite full as there were two flights departing. Flying from Ende was an interesting experience but I think the new terminal will remove a lot of what makes it special.

Arrived at the airport only to find long queues outside For baggage screening. We went through all the checks passports etc only to find a further check just for uk passport holders - we had to queue here for a long time only to find no seats or toilets. We had to wait more than 2 hours before boarding. I think this is totally unacceptable and needs sorting out it made travelling from this airport unnecessarily uncomfortable experience.

I've been through this airport several times, and I must say, it's incredibly clean and sparkling, and definitely puts Gatwick to shame. The people of Tunisia are very friendly, which adds to the overall positive experience. However, I have a concern regarding the pricing. While all airports tend to charge fees, the prices here seem a bit exorbitant. I wonder why this is the case. Additionally, I have a personal issue with the height of the walkway that crosses about 300 meters up. I understand this might not be a problem for most, but it would be great if the sides of the walkway could be covered for those of us who aren’t fond of heights. Other than these few points, it's an excellent airport with great service!

Clean, spacious airport in March. WiFi is available, although the signal is weak. Upon arrival you have to queue for longer than necessary (a simple passport check should not take long). Upon departure, there is no online check-in. All passengers must check-in at the counter, even those with only hand/cabin luggage.  I guess the airport (run by TAV) has not upgraded its systems for many years.  There are too many security checks.  Food and drinks are very expensive on the airside, and there are no water fountains. This is extortion.

By far the worst airport experience I have ever had. Yes it is clean, new and modern but these were the only good things about it. There were at least 12 flights within the space of an hour and then nothing for the next 3 or 4 hours, the result, total chaos! I think there were literally 5 or so security lanes serving what would have been probably 2,500 passengers in an hour. We got to the airport about 2 and a half hours before departure and queued for almost 2 hours to get through security! Some people were panicking and trying to jump the queue as their flights were being called, but rightly so the passengers near the front stopped them. It's the only time I've ever had to run for a flight in my life. Turned out they were still missing over 50 passengers on the flight as they were still stuck in the terminal. Consequently Thomas Cook had to delay the flight. The airport shouldn't allow so many flights to go at once if it's totally incapable of handling them all. If you somehow manage to go at a quiet time though I'm sure it would be a very nice airport!

This is the worst run airport we have ever encountered. On landing the queues to get through passport control were totally unacceptable. Five or six planes landed at once and only about 3 desks open. Took one and a half hours from when we got off plane to actually boarding the bus to hotel. One couple we met on holiday with 4 children waited two and a half hours! There was also no air conditioning which made the heat unbearable. On the way back our plane was delayed by over an hour due to the mismanagement of this airport. The pilot explained that we had missed our slot due to the cases being loaded too late and as we were already on the plane we just had to sit and wait. Our Tunisian friend said that the airport is always like this and that he has quite often complained. It is absolutely horrendous total unorganised chaos. p.s. Although the airport is clean the toilets are awful and when you come out someone is holding their hand out asking you for money for the pleasure of using the dirty toilet unbelievable.

This is a comparatively new airport in Tunisia and I have nothing but praise for it. It is clean smart and well organised. Check in and Security were quick and once through to airside a really good duty free shop and a bar. Great views from the glass fronted terminal although the view of some aircraft can be obscured by the piers. Everything ran smoothly and just a pleasure to travel through this airport.

Worst experience ever! The attendants at the KLM airlines checkin point at Entebbe airport were extremely rude and not helpful. They were practically bullying me and wanting to reap me off cash. Secondly, the attendants checking the flight details didn't even know what an IRP card was and she just took me out of the line without hearing me. I was extremely disappointed and hurt by seeing this kind of unfairness and disrespect!!

I am very dissatisfied with the service I got here on the 4th March 2020, the airport staff could not show me where the UN offices were, they were useless and unfriendly. I would never come back here or recommend it either to anyone, poor service.

The worst thing is, after you go through security, there is no water available and no bathrooms. There is nothing but seats. Thankfully they have installed air conditioning. If you don't like security, you will hate this airport, you have to go through security when driving in to the airport. You have to go through security to get in to ticketing and you have to go through security to get to your gate. Outside of the boarding area they have restaurants and shops. It's not a modern airport, so it's difficult to find a plug to charge your electronics.

Baggage reclaim was swift. There was no air conditioning in departures and so we got very hot waiting to check bags as we arrived early. There are very minimal check in desks so expect delays if you don't arrive early. You need to climb exterior stairs to get to the departure terminal and so extra work driving around would be needed for people with disabilities. There is security in the car park, security before check in and security at the gate so expect a lot of waiting around for security checks. The cost of food was very expensive so eat before you arrive. All in all the airport served it purpose and we both arrived and delayed without an issue. Bathrooms were also clean. P.S the Wi-Fi is free and provided by the CAA

Visited Uganda on 12/30/14 and departed on 01/09/15. Both arrival and departure experiences were smooth. Arrival hall is rather large. There is mandatory health screening before one can proceed to visa/passport control. Obtaining a visa is relatively easy. Present valid passport and make payment. Baggage claim appeared to be a rather large area with perhaps 2-3 carousels. At departure level the lighting seems rather deem. There is the mandatory screening of bags before you can enter and check in for the flight. The staff is very friendly. The facilities are clean and the departure hall appears small given the amenities (gift shops dining and duty free). The Karibuni Lounge is excellent. It puts to shame US airline lounges in the USA with its food offerings and amenities. Bathrooms are cleaned frequently by an attendant. Overall no issues with EBB airport. Immigration control staff are very friendly. The only drawback to this airport is that passengers have to be dropped off in the parking area and then make their way around the roadway to the departure level.

Entebbe airport sets good standards for an airport in Africa. Though I do not recommend staying in it for hours it is still a clean safe place. Coming from Sydney it is ok. Its clean and the lounge is amazing. Though having kids with me did make a hassle. Otherwise its a nice quiet airport to go to. Especially when the border security allowed me to go from the back to the front of the line. I like it.
The airport is old. Staff is friendly. The airport is no longer capable of dealing with the large numbers of traffic passing through.

Used Entebbe airport yesterday to fly to Dar-es-Salaam and was pleasantly surprised. Terminal is very small but clean staff are friendly and welcoming and the facilities are fine to while away a couple of hours. One of the best airports I've used in the East Africa region and wish all border control staff could be as pleasant!

I live in Kampala and fly in and out of this airport regularly. It is a rather small and quiet airport clean and modern after the refurbishment. There is not much to do a few duty free shops (overpriced) craft shops and a restaurant. Check-in area can be very crowded especially for BA KLM and Emirate flights. For all other international flights it is sufficient to arrive at the airport 1 hour before departure. The best this airport has to offer is probably the lounge. Clean extremely comfy sofas big TV screens friendly service hot showers internet access and an electronic massage chair.

Inbound they are now taking the passengers thru a temporary barrack on the side of the terminal. At the moment the arrival hall is being upgraded for CHOGM. Anyway it went quite smooth through immigration but the baggage area was very tiny for a A330 full of baggage. Departure was smooth. Remember that all of the airport is non-smoking. If you pass immigration there is really no way back. Lots of crafts to be bought if you have not bought enough already. One restaurant with a ok selection. Need new airconditioning.

Airport has a weird system for departure: 1) You have to go to a security check point outside the airport to be patted down (manually) by security guards while your vehicle (luggage) is sniffed by gaurd dogs. 2) Then, you are dropped off at a terminal for security check (again) this time through electronic devices where you get a special colored sticker on your luggage. 3) Afterwards, you proceed to a shuttle bus (carry your own luggage) that will take you to another terminal (about a 7 minute drive where temperatures reach 45-50 degrees Celsius in the summer). 4) At the 2nd terminal, a security check is done to ensure you have been security checked at the previous terminal (?). Now some of this can be avoided if you have a special VIP pass that skips step 2! And a VVIP that skips all steps! The check in counters are ok, about 10 of them run by Dubai's DNata. Immigration is slow and queues are long. Duty Free is small with tobacco, chocolates and alcohol available. One coffee shop available behind Duty Free. After passing immigration (but before your gate) you pass through another security check point (remove your shoes, belts, etc...) Plenty of seating at the gates plus one coffee shop (although AC is never working in the summer) and no wifi connection through out the airport. Staff are all generally friendly.

I really like this modern airport. It is efficient and clean. Staff are polite and sost can speak at least a reasonable English and in case of any difficulty they would call a colleague. The general public cannot access the main terminal for security reasons. A separate building called "Meet and greet" hosts the first baggage and traveler security inspection facilities. A large free parking for private cars and taxis is available. From here, a bus every 5 minutes brings the passengers (and only them) to and from the main terminal, a few hundred meters away. In the same way, those waiting for passengers on arrival wait for them at a waiting space at the "Meet and greet" building. Only registered "VIP" vehicles (usually diplomats and high ranking officials) can access the main terminal. The terminal itself is modern, clean and spacious, and includes all the expected services. The duty free shop is not big but the choice of articles is good for a small airport. When arriving (I experienced a dozen arrivals in the past 4 years, both during the day and the night), I never had to wait more than 10 minutes for my baggage. While information is always available and efficient inside the airport, the same cannot be said for the website. Here, updates on flight status are unpredictable, sometimes wrong, sometimes late, sometimes correct and on time.

After standing at passport control for over 1/2 hour. It was our turn. Seconds earlier a couple appeared in another queue next to ours. My partner who speaks the language perfectly pointed out that there was a queue. Also someone else in the queue pointed it out as well. The passport officer told us to go back over the red line. And told this couple to come forward. (Not military, not late for the same flight as us). Can't believe that someone should get preferential treatment at passport control.

Small but very clean airport disembarking to exiting airport 20 -30 mins minimal duty free shops on arrival but more extensive on departure area. Very security conscious on entry and exit. All in all a walk in the park no hassle.

Arrived at 2040 on a Sat night along with 3 other flights and went into immigration hall only to find that whilst there were 8 booths only 2 of them were for EU passengers and the rest for Turks /Northern Cypriot people and as a result the queue was back to the door and then back out onto the apron area. Eventually an official told everyone to use all available booths but even then the immigration officials were extremely slow and scrutinised the passports to the point of overkill taking ages with each person. On return we had to go through two security screenings - why ? They told us that it was ok to take bottles of water through the second one. Also why are all the prices airside in Euros or nothing on them ? Surely a last chance to get rid of the Turkish lira.

Nice small airport easy to manage. Reminds me of Luton airport circa 1975. Very cheap duty free shops and security checks on entry to the terminal building as well as the normal checks going thru to airside which possibly only a small airport can deal with. But good security none the less.

It is clean quick and efficient passport control. Landed at 20.10 was driving off at 20.25! My return leg was the same 8 desks open for the 3 flights that were going to London around the same time with CTA. Very cheap cigarettes and alcohol airport staff are friendly and helpful. The chap that said announcements were not made in English is wrong - all flights are announced in Turkish and English. You can hardly miss your flight as there are only 6 gates! A small airport with only around 120 flights coming and going in one week but very efficient!

A very clean airport but with often absent and very rude staff - a trait that we now know to be common in Turkey and Turkish Cyprus. There is a great lack of any English signage or translations of announcements. Hardly qualifies as an "international" airport on that score. On arrival we had no idea which of the bits of paper we had to fill in to avoid the stamp in our passports and on departure we sat ourselves by the gates and watched faces that we knew were to be on our flight so we wouldn't be likely to miss the plane. The duty free is very strange in Ercan - instead of a large shop selling everything there are loads of little shops all selling much the same thing. Despite Turkey and TRNC still having their own currency and being very keen to get their hands on Sterling and US Dollars the prices are all in Euros although mostly there are no prices on anything and you have to ask. This maked it very hard to compare between the various shops. And you also fall foul of a sneaky trick - you never get a price quoted in Turkish Lira - they tell you what it is in your own currency but what you don't realise is that they have converted it using the bank rate which is not at all favourable. Never use your credit card in Turkish Cyprus because they also charge extra and by the time you see the amount on your statement it's likely to be a fair bit more than you thought!! Having said that though if it's alcohol and tobacco you are after the prices are very cheap and even better than in the normal shops. One further warning - beware of the luggage trolleys!! They all work perfectly no wobbly wheels etc. but they give you an electric shock when you start moving them. Heaven knows what is in wheels or in the floor covering but I got a shock on arrival and again on departure. A fellow traveller told us that it happens a lot.

Very clean and security conscious - majority of staff willing to help unless they belong to Turkish Airlines . I found them to be most uncooperative lazy and downright rude to the point of looking at you when you ask a question and then turning around and walking away. So be warned - even the locals told me to watch out for this attitude and like a fool I walked straight into it.

Smart clean and modern north east of Leftkosa (Nicosia). Security conspicuous and efficient check in very efficient immigration slow (form filling !) Arrivals baggage collection was very slow and the baggage belt was to small for 220 passengers. The departure area has two cafes which take a variety of currencies and credit cards numerous small duty free shops (alcohol mainly) all keen for your custom. Walk to the planes - no buses. No complaints.

Exeter used to be a first class friendly efficient and welcoming place. In fact, I went out of my way to use it. Nothing could be further from the truth now! The check -in staff are rude, insulting and ill informed. The security staff could get an award for being the most obstreperous, rude and difficult to grace an airport. They are also wrong on so many counts and semm to enjoy being wrong whilst flexing muscles that they would be unable to do anywhere else. The airport seems to attract jobs worths and is run by a poorly qualified manager who seems to be operating above his ability levels. Many staff in departures, the lounge and duty free ask for travellers to complain formally as they hear so many complaints and there is nothing they can do about it. As they say, they want to protect their jobs and that can't be done if passengers are cross and irritable, not spending money and not using the airport. I actively use Bristol now. That is hardly an example of great practice but at least it is anonymous and busy! Exeter needs custom and it does not go the right way of achieving this goal. I would strongly suggest that the Manager is re-trained and/or the staff are trained at other busy airports where customer service is paramount.

Bar staff very rude, wanted to go home early so told passengers to go to gate as flight had landed and was early. I regularly travel from Exeter and was tracking the flight so I was well aware this information was false. I explained to the staff member who then shouted that she works at airport and knows when a flight has landed. I went through the gate and no sign of the flight just a very rude staff member who obviously has no customer service experience and needs retraining .

Lovely experience through check in and security at around 6:45/7am this morning (6th July 2023). The chap at Tui desk was friendly, professional and helpful. All four members of staff at security were great. Helpful, friendly and professional. Lovely atmosphere. At the café a lovely women served me. Smile on her face. Finally, going through to boarding gate; yet again a friendly, cheerful and helpful lady checked me in (7.50am by this stage). It’s a small airport. The shop and café are small. I’m not here to shop or sit drinking. I’m here to have an ideally stress free start to my holiday. The staff make this place. Thank you.

This review is regarding the security checks and instant irreversible decisions taken by the security staff on items packed in carry on luggage. I arrived at security at Exeter airport and it was not busy at all, I removed my belt and electronics and placed them in the tray for scanning. I had checked the airport website on permissible and banned items from hand luggage and was confident that I complied with all the current regulations. My bag however was pulled for inspection and two rolls of duct tape was removed as banned items. I had checked the website especially looking for the reference to duct tape and saw that it was listed as allowed in hand luggage. Not though at security point, I protested and informed the officer that the web site said duct tape was allowed, no impression at all, they would not even check the website. I did ask why it was banned and was told that you could tie someone up with it. I replied by asking if women's tights were also banned as you can tie someone up with them, ridiculous reply I know but removing an item which was clearly allowed was also ridiculous. I had to get friend who dropped me off at the airport to return to pick up my duct tape which cost time and fuel money. Come on get yourself together either things are banned or not but let the public know.

A very tired and faded airport. Seats in the upstairs lounge were ripped and worn, no bar available upstairs or downstairs, carpet was worn and hadn’t been cleaned. Check in was ok, security efficient, but the comfort and facilities after security were very sadly lacking. Not a patch on what this airport used to be.

Keep an eye on your valuables as you pass through security! My sister and I were late to board the plane departing 1st July at 11.05 am (Blue Islands Airline) to Jersey by about 5 minutes with boarding time of 10.35 am. The check in desk staff were very good. No problem there. The security staff? Woeful! Plainly annoyed, one middle aged woman handling the belongings trays decidedly slappable with her sarcasm while looking down her nose at us. The machine you walk through twice beeped at me, necessitating my watch and bracelets to be placed in a tray. That was the last I saw of my watch. A Rado make so not cheap and a rather attractive black and gold enamel type strap. During the rush of bundling us out of the security hall and across the tarmac to the plane I forgot to pick up my jewellery from the tray. I noticed as soon as I sat down on the plane. I immediately advised the excellent lady steward who instantly asked the captain to radio the security staff to bring my belongings to me. My two bracelets duly arrived to the plane for which I am grateful but no watch. Immediately upon my return to Exeter airport I attended Customer Service desk to be directed to the security hall where I spoke to a tall man clearly in authority. He seemingly went to look at the footage of cctv and returned very quickly saying he could not see anything. I was fobbed off and treated very dismissively by him. Did he really look at the footage of 3 days previously in detail so quickly? My watch must have vanished into thin air. I don't remember any other passengers being present. We were the last to board the plane. Something happened to my watch between being placed in the tray and us boarding the plane. Watch your stuff!

I was booked to travel Club Europe from this airport on 21st August 2021. No dedicated check-in, no priority security, no business lounge. I managed to find a quiet place to sit upstairs in the bar area (the outside seating area was closed). After about 30 minutes an airport employee entered the bar area to inform all of us who were seated there, that the area should have been cordoned off and that we had to move downstairs. Apparently, this was because the floor was unstable. We were told there were plenty of seats at the bottom of the stairs so we went downstairs to sit - which was directly underneath the unstable floor! Very odd - and very dangerous I would have thought. I got the distinct impression that the jobsworth employee just did not want to patrol the upstairs area, so he moved us all downstairs. Because of the danger of the upstairs floor caving in on us we all moved to the main seating area in a windowless room which was extremely busy and required some considerable searching to find empty seats. The area soon became very busy without a seat to be had. All those people sitting so close to each other in a room without a window and all I could think about was Social Distancing. Before long my flight was called and I moved to the boarding gate, Here we all waited whilst the ground staff went into overdrive because they spotted an elderly woman who was reliant on oxygen - and who had a tank strapped to her back. I overheard the member of staff ask of another about how the lady got through check in and security without being challenged about her oxygen. I too questioned this and wondered how easy it would be for a terrorist to get through the airport. This thought soon dissipated when a door suddenly opened and an airport employee shouted 'They're ready for you now' - at which point there was a mad rush for the door. We are all so used to polite announcements made over the tannoy, that to have someone open a door and shout an instruction was quite refreshing - not! In all, a shambles from start to finish. I don't think I have ever been through such an unprofessional airport in my life. And I've been through many airports in some of the most back of beyond places in the world.

One small coffee machine and a tray of muffins at the closed café airside is the only f&b offered at Exeter. The WiFi service appears to have been switched off, and the remote location of this airport also means there is no mobile signal. The management have used Covid to cut costs beyond an acceptable level. Security is quaint, with staff trying their best but appearing to be very amateur. The truly worst part as always is the miserable Border Force staff on return immigration. They are very rude, dismissive and seem to be in a mood that they are stuck at such a tiny little airport rather than an international hub such as Heathrow. Exeter is convenient for my west country house, but I will be adding the extra 2.5 hour drive to Heathrow to avoid this terrible service and fading airport.

I Had the misfortune to have our flight to Manchester delayed by an hour and a half yesterday and was stuck in the departure lounge at this out of date airport. On arrival we purchased 2 decaf coffees and they were drinkable. I then had a look around WH Smith’s (This was the only place available to purchase food) and just couldn’t believe my eyes as there was just cheese sandwiches available. I asked the assistant if they could replenish the sandwiches and she informed me that’s all that’s available, So Crisps it was for my lunch. There was no charging points anywhere to be seen. I did manage to send an email to the airport about my dissatisfaction but as of yet have had no response. I know that things are not going to be back to normal straight away but for goodness sake surely the basic needs of all of your customers is a must.

Departure experience was relatively smooth, an early morning flight on Ryanair so airport was very quiet. Security was well managed, clear markings on the floor to encourage social distancing. However there was no coffee shop open so nowhere to buy a drink or a bite to eat. Arriving back was very quick, there were a number of staff members on hand to organise passengers, no queue at passport control and bags were out within minutes, however this was to be expected due to a very quiet flight and an empty airport. Overall, whilst the airport appeared clean we did not see any staff members cleaning while we were there with no hand sanitising stations available to passengers.

Fairly small newish airport with a few international but primarily domestic flights. I saw no options for dining outside of security and inside saw just two (a bar and a small cafe). There appeared to be just two rest rooms and one was not usable since there was an international flight arriving (I did not understand the connection). Taxis in Fairbanks are pricey (and there is a $1 per person surcharge after the first passenger); fare from out hotel was over $25 for 4 people and Fairbanks is not a large city. If I were to return to Fairbanks I'd rent a car.

Faleolo airport in Apia, Samoa is a small airport. We found immigration, customs etc very quick and efficient, as well as baggage handling. At the moment, the airport is not really pretty to look at, but a new terminal is being built, which should be spectacular when completed. It's really refreshing to be able to walk through the airport on arrival / departure and not be forced to navigate through a giant shopping mall like at Sydney. The airport has done duty free shops (which you are free to go into or not go into, rather than having to go through them to get in / out of passport control, a few small food shops (reasonably priced) and a bar. Parking is $5 Samoan Tala. Staff at the airport are friendly, welcoming and helpful. The only negative side is that there is no air conditioning outside the security areas and check in is a bit uncomfortable when it's humid.

Faleolo is the international airport for Samoa located 1 hour from Apia on Upolu island. A pain for late night/ early morning arrivals and departures but conveniently close to the ferries for Savaiii Apolima and Manono islands. Used Faleolo airport this last weekend as a business class passenger. First pax off the plane to a stretch limousine awaiting at bottom of steps! Together with police guard and band. 100% true but alas this VIP welcome was not for me but for the Samoan Head of State seated across from me on the plane. However no pomp and ceremony for me once inside this basic airport. Immigration was slow/methodical but courteous. Baggage claim and clearance even slower. On return check- in handled efficiently by Polynesian. No lounge facilities at Faleolo provided for premium passengers (only a govt lounge for VIPs). Landside toilets are derelict and filthy. Better to hold your water until you get airside. One rung above Port Moresby airport in PNG - which itself IS one big toilet. Immigration at APW outbound even slower than inbound due to a disorganised pax on an Air Pacific flight - also departing at 4.30am-5.00 am. Once airside an overpriced cafe and dutyfree but at least there's air-con. On the bright side this could be a really good airport with a just little attention to cleanliness from the Samoan Airport Authority (such a contrast to the country itself - Samoa is kept spick and span by its people). Note that you have to pay WST40 departure tax at ANZ/Westpac banks on departure (not incl in ticket).No big deal but for this amount of money (equiv USD 15-20) airport could at least keep the loos clean.

There have been a number of improvements at the Faleolo international airport but I still cannot get over how expensive duty free products are. I travel to and from Samoa at least three times a year and I have yet to purchase anything from duty free. It's just so much more cheaper at other international airports - even taking into consideration the rate of the Samoan tala in foreign countries! Airport taxes are just so ridiculously high it's unbelievable. Look at the departure tax for instance - I remember when they lifted the tax to $30 and justified it to the public by claiming that children under a certain age did not have to pay tax. My husband and I have two children - an eighteen year old and a 4year old we still have to pay $120 which calculates to 'more' - 'much more' than the four of us would have to pay to get out of Auckland International Airport (even taking into consideration the Samoan tala exchange rate!). And I need not elaborate on the many luxuries (100 times over) that are available at the Auckland international airport and NOT available at the Faleolo airport! Once the tax hits the $40 mark you might as well include it in the ticket like everyone else around the world whose departure tax is over $30! We pay tax on our tickets and at the airport ... why not just put them together and leave them on the ticket! That would be one huge improvement - and less hassle when flynig out of faleolo!

Apia's airport has been upgraded and presents a warm pacific feeling. The immigration/customs staff should be taught to smile though - especially after tourists are sold on the idea of a friendly pacific paradise proudly operated by the friendliest people on earth!

On arrival into APW in the evening heat arrived into immigration waiting for 5 minutes as there were no immigration officers to process our docs as if they were on lunch? This was a bit of a shock. Apart from that dilemma baggage was swift & on the conveyer belt pretty fast. Custom officers very polite & efficient. Faleolo airport is very open & spacious. In a hot humid climate tiles are laid through the entire airport. There are no main entrance doors to the terminal as it is one open place but very modern indeed. Departure lounge quite nice with the Tropical Pacific feel to it a big beautiful bar dominates the one huge departure lounge. This would be the only place together with the PH J Class lounge is air-conditioned.

The passenger terminal in Fargo has limited but all the essential services. I used it for arriving and departing to hub cities for onward connections. Taxi drivers were near the baggage belts, soliciting fares. On departure, you check in on the main floor and take escalators one flight up. To your left is a large enough gift shop with the usual items plus North Dakota State University memorabilia. On the right is a food court with a few eateries, including a Subway. The security check was smooth. Once on the airside, there is a coffee shop and a kiosk of a shop - a miniatiure version of the gift shop on the other side. There are quite a few chairs and signage is good. A very easy airport to use and quick to get out of and quick to get in.

We arrived on the 17th October, the passport experience had been very slow, E Gates were terrible, hardly any working and causing huge delays. The staff were sat doing nothing just watching the E Gates denying people access and going out of service. They were also surly and rude when we eventually got through. We almost missed our coach transfer as a result. Departure was even worse, we queued from the moment we arrived all the way to to plane, no time for anything else. The passport queue was huge and snaked all the way from security to the E Gates. Only 3x Gates working and 3x manned gates no wonder the queue was massive. The very few members who were working were making it worse rather than better. One shut the E Gates when we got to the front and proceeded to put everyone in the queue including us back in to the main queue some way back. All around us we could hear people stressing because they would miss their flight. The staff member shouted angrily at people to cooperate and said "everyone will miss their flight" and walked off. This made no sense as there were 3x E gates that were working so why shut them? This whole process took well above 1hr 30 mins if not more, we didn’t time it as we were just so stressed by the whole thing. We eventually made it through and had to sprint across the airport to our departure gate and made it with seconds to spare. No toilet break, or time for food or drink. Less able bodied people would have missed it. There were empty seats on our flight. Worst airport experience ever.
Toilets are absolutely disgraceful, the smell and mess makes you feel sick. The same arriving and departure. I would rather hold my pee in for 10 hours than use these bathroom facilities again.

Disgusted again at lack of any progress in this absolute dump of an airport. Arrival into usual passport queue and égates still not working . Been traveling through here for years and surely the management ought to have been sacked by now . Arrivals hall had marginally improved. Departure was awful again - overcrowded and absolutely filthy catering area and toilets disgusting. Passport control had 2 égates working out of 8 . 2 Booths closed and queues horrendous. Holding area before flight filthy and gate staff unfriendly as always. Faro - how long must we all suffer this before you look at new leadership for what could be a great airport !!

Was expecting the worst after the number of negative reviews but was very pleasantly surprised at how quick, efficient and friendly the service was. Traveling in September probably has a substantial bearing on numbers but we were through check-in and passport control in 25 minutes which is much better than most airports we've used in the recent past. Water is available to top up bottles for free or just €1 from a machine as you exit security, far from the exorbitant prices encountered at other airports. The service, selection and seating area at cafe Soho are excellent, assuming our flight is on time (Ryanair 🤔) it's a five star experience.

Poor airport! Departure worse than arrival. Rude staff, not organized in the slightest it's almost like they are shocked when you ask them a question. Asked for a pharmacy and was told there was not one in the airport ... website states there is. Flight delayed, not the fault of the staff at the airport however no information provided at all. Nobody around to speak with until the the gate was finally out up and then it's just a rush to sling you onto the plane. This is my second experience at this airport and honestly I can't think of a reason to come back.

Awful airport. On arrival was very smooth to be fair but the passport control queue was horrendous for those with UK passports and no accessibility and on departure despite wearing the sunflower lanyard and having booked fast track I was declined at fast track and made to queue for security and with my disabilities I struggle with long queuing. The departure hall was very busy and hot with not many places to sit I had a great holiday in the Algarve but it was tarnished by the atrocity that is Faro Airport on a positive note however the toilets were very clean.

The queues for immigration on arrival at 1040 (local) were long and disorganised (no proper queuing system with “snake” line - zig zag - queue organisation. A free-for-all until you reach the short queuing system near the immigration booths, none of the e-gates were working, and no information). The odd staff member looked disinterested and bored. On departure, the queues after security for immigration through B gate were very long (1hour wait) with no organisation or communication (the only staff member was calling for Irish passport holders, who were able to jump the queue as they had EU passports). I understand that the non-EU passport holders will have to pass relatively slowly through this process, but to have 12 gates with 2 (manned) dedicated to EU passport holders and only 4 manned for non-EU passport holders smacks of discrimination against the Brits on a massive scale. There were 19 flights between 0955 and 1140 on the departures board (in full view of us in the queueing line!) all going to UK destinations. I don’t suppose my family’s decision to change our holiday destination to a country that gives us the impression of welcoming us, will change anything, but it is a great shame as the Portuguese people we encountered on holiday were delightful and would be very concerned that the airport authorities are sending out all the wrong messages. If the consensus amongst the people queuing alongside us are typical, it will not be long before the owners of restaurants, bars, cafes, taxis, hotels etc notice a decline that will not be of their making. The beneficiaries will be such businesses in destinations such as Turkey and Greece!

An absolute joke. Standing here in a queue that goes on forever. 3 passport gates open not an airport worker in sight - what a kip. This is the biggest joke of an airport I have ever stood in, and to top it off, there is no AC working. Do they honestly think people will put up with this? Well I will never go through Faro, nor indeed Portugal ever again.
Terrible arrival experience. 90 minute queue to get through passport control. No queue discipline. Terrible airport staff. Rude and not doing their job. Stressful. Avoid

Waited almost an hour to get through passport control. Holiday season! One guy for three airplanes. People starting arguing as different planes landed and people were shunted into two lanes by some airport worker in a high vis jacket. Exact same experience for my daughter who arrived the following day. What a poor way to be welcomed to the Algarve. Get your house in order. Not good enough.

Flying from Fayetteville to CLT on July 20. The young man at AA was unfriendly like I never seen before. Your ID, put your bag, take your bag were his only words. No greeting, no thank you, no have a good flight. I recently moved to Fayetteville for a job from New York. Flying often. Never flew from Fayetteville, used Raleigh for that. There was no soap in the restroom at 8 am already. Security was okay, did not use thank you or please in their lexicon. I will fly from Raleigh next time.

Northwest Arkansas Regional Airport may be the best small/medium airport in the United States. In spite of being a regional airport in a small state, XNA has direct flights to New York, DC, San Francisco, and LAX. This unparalleled service is ideal for business travelers and those making connections to international flights. Most of the planes that fly out of XNA are regional jets (CRJ or Embraer), but they fly to most of the country's major hubs. The ground services are also above and beyond what is typical of an airport this size, with a large brewpub and high-quality furnishings. I am definitely impressed and would fly from XNA again.

You need to make sure you got to check-in despite already having a boarding pass but there are no signs saying this. We knew from reading previous reviews. The airport is immaculate but the staff are among the rudest airport I have ever come across. During my process to get into departures I was treated like a second class citizen being told to wait behind my partner to go through security, passport control wagging his finger at me and telling me no despite standing at his desk silently (literally no idea what I was being told off for) and then when stopping at a stop sign for passports to be checked again, security summoned me forward by clicking fingers at me! I’m not an animal! I understand security has to be tight these days but why make it worse for passengers by treating them so poorly after we chose to visit and spend our money in their country.

Totally not as bad as all the reviews had us expecting. No printed boarding pass needed. They just gave us one (Ryanair). No long waiting time. Only thing: too cold and no smoking area after security check.

This airport is one of the most weirdly inept airports I have ever been to, even for a 3rd world country. The Moroccan style cafe we waited in initially, in the main airport lounge pre-security check was open but completely un-staffed for a couple of hours until finally, they closed. What's up with that? Then, at the security check in they took from me, and tossed, my silver plated, miniature forks that I had bought as souvenirs, as well as a miniature metal fork that I got on a Lufthansa flight, on the plane, all of these, had prongs no longer than 1.5cm, when up to 6cm are allowed, and I have previously passed through at least 50 airport security checks all over the world without any problem, with my metal Lufthansa fork, last time as recently as a week ago on my way to Fez. Clearly, their security staff are ill-informed and need retraining. Inside the departures waiting area, despite being in Morocco, all the prices were shown only in euros, which makes no sense, since this isn't even Europe, but Africa. This made it really hard what to choose in order to spend the maximum of my last Dirhams. For the boarding then, even though the big screen would read "boarding open", it didn't provide a gate number, and the guy staffing one of the gates didn't know, either. If he doesn't know, who would? Bizarre experience, overall.

Creepy staff and poor facilities! I recently experienced a 13 hour delay, and every staff member simply walked away when asked about flight updates! I could not believe the rudeness. Passengers were asking for water, which was initially refused. During my 13 hour wait, I went to the window to take a photo, and 2 security guards came up behind me and said “no photos are allowed to be taken, except for a beautiful woman like you”. When I replied I was taking the photo to send to my husband, one of the security guards looked me up and down and said the the other “oh, this one is a husband”. Are you kidding me? There was enough intimidating male behaviour in the streets of Fez, let alone having to cop it from airport staff!Bathroom cleaning staff allowed smoking in the bathroom for a handshake payment, which makes the whole terminal smell like cigarette smoke, and after 13 hours waiting, I had a sore throat and stinging eyes from this. Not a single electricity socket in the entire terminal, and wifi cuts out after 2 hours, which is frustrating when you have to spend 13+ hours waiting for a flight - the worst coffee and the minimal food options were horrible and stale. Fly from Marrakech if you can, this airport is horrible.

In May 2017 the new international airport terminal was opened in Fez. It is an enormous improvement and upgrade on the previous terminal with a much more spacious and aesthetically pleasing environment. In departures security can sometimes be a little slow but there is a clear and effective process which is greatly improved as compared to the old terminal. Border checks on both arrivals and departures are much more efficient and swift. There is a lounge available as well as pleasant shops and cafes in both arrivals hall and departures. An entirely upgraded and pleasant experience travelling to/from Fez.

This airport is chaos and a mess. There is little or no information regarding procedures at the airport. Even though you hold your pre printed boarding pass they require you to still use a check in desk first even though you are only using carry on. Security are supposed to stop anyone from getting to passport control who doesn't have the official stamp on their boarding pass but they don't so you queue for ages for passport control only to be sent back to Check in. So it makes pre printing the boarding pass a joke but you have to do it because that's what Ryanair want you to do. Queues are long and slow for passport control but I suppose that's the case for many airports these days. Security is pretty thorough although your not required to remove liquids from your carry on. Gate staff were however very efficient especially enforcing queuing prior to boarding. There's not much once your at the gate area a couple of shops a lounge and a prayer area. It's quite a small terminal so space is tight and if you e got two flights departing close together you'll have to fight for a seat. There's free wifi at the airport but be aware you only get 1 hour 30 minutes over a two day period. So bottom line is if your a regular at this airport and you know their particular requirements then it's not that bad, but for first time visitors it's s nightmare.

A rather small airport serving Firenze. I used the airport in the winter season, so imagine it during the busy summer season. There's bus boarding only and max 12 small gates. It has a abundance of duty-free shops and food & beverages counters. Prices are reasonable. Staff is friendly and efficiently working.

Florence is a joke, not an airport. Passengers are boarded on a bus, under the sun, with no air conditioning, and kept there for 20 minutes. The same happens during winter, where passengers are kept on the bus for long time with the bus doors open and the engine on, so you basically breathe the exhaust gases. Poor airport services complete the picture

Horrible airport, hot as hades. Extremely disorganized and long boarding procedure. We waited 1 hour just to board the plane. Then missed a connection because of the boarding. When we were finally seated we had to wait another hour on the plane for a takeoff time. In total we sat there 2 hours, only to find out when we got to our final destination that the baggage handlers hadn't bothered to put the luggage on the plane.  The bus system from the terminal to the plane sucks, and needs to be brought into this century. My advice avoid this airport at all costs, and carry on luggage.

Not often I have felt so embarrassed as a Florentine living abroad on how my city welcomes its visitors. The luggage collection is a pain (as with most Italian airports, and not only), but the worse is the indifferent and arrogant attitude of the people working there. To top it all is the transfer from the Terminal (tiny and overcrowded) to the car rental. It is a couple of meters, but cannot be reached by foot (especially not with heavy luggage) and therefore there is a shuttle. Instead of driving in a loop, one waits and waits and waits till finally the driver shows up, with cellphone in his hands while driving. While the meanwhile accumulated masses of people try to squeeze in the tiny bus, unapologetically the driver continues the phone conversation and lights up a cigarette. Even when after 30 seconds the bus is filled with people eager to finally move on, the departure for the 2 mins ride is after the driver finishes his cigarette. Don’t think the option of taking a taxi is any better, 2 out of the 3 times it takes an hour to get one as the line is horribly long: if you must be in the centre, take the tram-connection (it costs 1,50 € and takes 20 mins). I have traveled through the whole world, and Florence Airport definitely is in the top ten of the worst.

Had to wait two hours for check inn. Only two counters were open. Baggage drop off didn’t function at all. After entering security. The terminal is way too small for so many guests. Only 20% of the flight guests can sit down. The cafes/restaurants are very small. No seats available. A nightmare.

This airport is woefully short in filling the needs of travelers. It is understaffed and when I was there all of the automatic check baggage kiosks were not working. I waiting in one of the very long lines there with no announcements or information. You are I strutted to strive at the airport 3 hrs in advance for an international flight. I arrived at 8.00 am for an 11.00 boarding but the check in counter for my TAP flight did not open until 9.30 ish. For a major tourist destination this airport is one of the worst I have encountered.
This is an airport, which clearly reached its limits. It is overfilled, facilities are poor and clearly insufficient. Basically it is a small city airport with far too much traffic.

I was having one of the worst times of my life and I went up to customer service balling my eyes out simply asking if there was a phone booth near. The customer service attendants that day were a nightmare they hate doing their jobs. I simply asked for a phone booth and a man pointed to the right and told me there was one over there with no directions. I came back and he was gone. It was only to get me to leave.. no type of humanity or empathy. My flight also left even though we were there extremely early like six hours before our flight because they didnt have enough people for covid testing. But there was this one security girl officer who was so sweet to me I even told her god bless you because she helped me by giving me saran wrap when my suitcase burst open.  I love Italy but that experience was a nightmare.

I was returning to Madrid from Florence on 12 June 2022. This was an utter nightmare. First, the check-in took nearly 3 hours. There was only 1 person at the counter and the queue was moving very slowly. At the stipulated time of boarding and gate closure there was no sense of urgency at all and still a very long line. Secondly, when it was finally my turn they assured me that the plane would wait for everyone (i.e. a delay which was not even announced to anyone at all) thirdly, the flight was delayed significantly because of this long queue. Fourthly, by the time we landed in Madrid, everyone rushed to luggage belt 16 (as announced on the plane) and waited like fools for 1 hour, only for an Iberia staff to appear to usher us to the baggage claim counter. There was no explanation of what was going on. After queueing for 1 hour, we finally learnt from the baggage claim service counter staff that the plane had taken off from Florence airport with not a single piece of luggage. Those with trackers on the luggage have been noted that the luggage is in Florence airport, and yet nothing is being updated yet till today, 24 hours later. I hope you realize what a complete nightmare this is, everyone has important and valuable items in the suitcases and to think we even paid extras to check in our luggage because we were told the flight was full. To all reading this, please never fly off from Florence airport and also be careful about flying via Iberia from Florence airport. There is also no way to contact customer service at Florence airport (only the tourist office picks up the phone), nor is there any platform or email to lodge a formal complaint or feedback. This is why there is probably hardly any improvement, because they just ignore everything. No amount of compensation can make up for the time, inconvenience, fatigue, anguish and emotional stress that something like this is causing. Luggage delays do happen, but if the plane knowingly took off without any luggage they could have at least informed the passengers. (if not at the start, then at the end of the flight) we waited like idiots at the luggage belt what a sheer waste of resources/fuel.

So I write this review mainly as some form of coping with the situation my family is in. We flew into Florence airport 3 days ago. Our luggage was no where to be found. The lost and found office was an absolute joke, under staffed and fairly rude. We were given some paperwork with a promise of a text updating the progress of finding my family’s luggage. Three days later, we have received zero communication. You can’t call because it is apparently open for call for 1 hour a day. Our routine is to Drive to the airport and wait in line with 40 to 50 people with one person trying to help them. We did find 4 of the 7 bags. We are still missing my father in laws heart medicine. When we mentioned the urgency of that situation, the person told him to go to a doctor here. We have been looking forward to this vacation for about a year and it is now ruined by shear laziness and incompetence. We have found out that not one person on our flight from Chicago to Florence got their luggage the day they landed. Please do not use this airport. It is completely unprofessional and a complete disaster.

Forlì airport is very small. The service before leave and after the arriving is very good and friendly. The location is good also because is possible to join city like Rimini Bologna and Ravenna in a very few time. Quite good the service for the disable people.

This airport is so small! First time I flew into It I came off the Plane and was out into the car park in around 1 minute 30 seconds! (only hand luggage with me). This airport is quite a way from Bologna so you need to catch a Taxi to the station in the town for around 12 Euros. Coming back the airport has a couple of nice bars and a cafe. The Taxi driver from Forli railway station to the airport was very friendly. Forli itself is very 60's Italian - don't expect any real culture.

I have grown to hate this airport. First and foremost, when folks are stuck here for hours on end waiting for their connecting flight or rushing to make their connection, the LAST thing we want to hear are your obnoxious and loud recorded messages about everything there is to do in Florida.  God forbid you try to focus on something else or get some semblance of peace because FLL airport will ensure it does not happen. Are you sitting at gate G2 waiting to board a flight? You, too, will hear messages about why you shouldn't park your car in the unloading area! You will not get peace in this airport and must deal with rude airport employees. Very disappointing.

This was the worst airport I’ve been in. We got there 5 hours before our flight so could not check our baggage yet. No seating in this area so we had to sit on the floor - I’m 81 years old so this was quite uncomfortable. When i was able to check luggage in the man was very rude. Told me I should have gotten my luggage tag. i thought that’s what he was supposed to do.

This was my 2nd flight to FLL in 4 months after a 11 year absence. This review is limited to Terminal 1. Arrival was at the A Concourse gates 1-5 which mean a rather long connectors to the B/C concourses common area.
