One huge advantage of FLL airport over the others is the car rental facility which is directly across the airport roadway from the terminal. The renovated terminal 1 is spacious, brightly lit, and has a central TSA Entry point for all 3 concourses. Each concourse offers dining options a plenty. For Christmas Day travel, there was enough seating for all with power ports and USB ports at each gate. The bathrooms are very clean and maintained at regular intervals. Security was a breeze with no wait time for the TSA-Pre checkpoints. WiFi was easy to connect too and blazing fast. The refurbished Terminal 1 is a joy to travel through
Terminal 4 does not have a single chair to sit on. People sit and lie down on the floor, giving the terminal the aspect of a refugee camp. Not acceptable for a large international airport.

Our flight arrived on time, but the airport was unable to receive the plane. We had sit again and wait in the plane. Then, they told us that they had no resources to unload the baggages from the plane and we had to wait another hour. Finally, there are way more travelers than what the customs could manage and we had to wait in the side and then we were moved to the line. Because of that we lost our connecting flight. We had 3 hours between arrival and departure which is normally more than enough for a so small airport. The airport is accepting much more flight than they can manage and the customers are who suffer only. The airport attendants did not care at all. In consequence we had to stay the night at the airport outside the security area with nothing to eat and no where comfortable where to seat. They were not willing to lay anything because they said it was a “uncontrollable” situation. We booked the flight a month ago so they knew how many flights were arriving, it was not an uncontrollable surprise. If I can control it I’ll never fly through Fort Lauderdale airport again.

It's been 11 years since I traveled through Terminal 1. The refurbished Terminal 1 is a world class modern airport terminal. It is spacious, brightly lit with plenty of seating and dining options aplenty. There are oodles of power ports and USB ports at the gates; however, some of the power ports were not working. Bathrooms are very clean. The concourses are wide and directions easy to follow to baggage claim. Security was a breeze with no wait time for the TSA-Pre checkpoints. WiFi was easy to connect too and blazing fast. The refurbished terminal is a significant upgrade to the old terminal 1.

This is a horrible airport to have to travel thru customs at. Literally hours to get through. Last time missed a 3hr connection because of it. Anyway just not good place. Ask question they just look at you? Then answer like you know where your at? Avoid this place at all cost. Especially JETBLUE!

What a Zoo! For Jet Blue, Terminal 3, it was a 2 minute wait for a kiosk for checked bag. 45 minute wait to drop bag. Then, TSA pre-check and regular are in the same line for F Concourse! And regular line is backed up to easily before where you enter TSA Pre-Check. No waiting at TSA Pre-check line! Terminal 3. TSA has the entrance to TSA Precheck blocked off so that you have to wait in the regular line for 10 minutes before you can get to clear or TSA Precheck entrance.

Avoid Ft Lauderdale Airport like the plague. I would give this airport negative 5 stars. I had a flight out of Ft Lauderdale today to Cancun to celebrate my 50th birthday with a large group of close friends in Tulum. It’s been raining in all of south Florida for past three days, and due to this, Ft. Lauderdale Airport has closed for the past two days including today. I can understand weather being a major issue resulting in airport closures, but somehow Ft Lauderdale airport is the only airport that has closed. They are currently close and ironically it’s been sunny all day. All of my friends were able to fly out of Miami International Airport which is a 30 minute drive to the south and somehow Miami International did not close at all. And Miami is extremely prone to flooding as it’s lower than Ft. Lauderdale. West Palm Beach airport which is just to the north did not close either. So needless to say, all of my friends are celebrating my 50th in Tulum without me because the airport will not open till tomorrow with the airline not being able to book me another flight for next three days. Worst part is as we are all sitting in the airport waiting for some news, airport staff had no idea what was going on or when they would reopen. I will never fly out of there, heaven forbid it rains a little again and the airport is shut down for a week. What did Miami and West Palm Beach airports figure out what to do that Ft. Lauderdale couldn’t.

Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport (FLL) is a total shambles. Unbelievable waiting times to park the plane, to access the luggage area and another two hours for customs and immigration. It really is a disgrace to treat visitors like this. I travel a lot globally and this is much  worse than countries the US really does not want to be compared to. In Houston two weeks ago this thing ran extremely smoothly.

One of the TSA Security Guys on C were extremely rude this morning. Lack of proper communication was a huge issue. Please tell me politely to not take my small electronics out of my carry on bag (which has always been the procedure before) instead of yelling the words so quickly that I did not have enough reaction time to process what was being said. Patience and kind words were all that I needed. Please work on this.

RSW is a great airport! The employees are nice & very helpful. The shuttle & parking employees are the best~ especially Theresa! My husband accidentally left his backpack (with meds, computer, & cash) on the shuttle in long term parking today! I drove Back 3 hours later & got it. Everything is there. They were so kind & helpful. Theresa had his backpack in the office. What a relief! So glad there are such good people in the world!

Two staff members were extremely rude this morning. Lack of proper communication was a huge issue. Please tell me politely to not take my small electronics out of my carry on bag (which has always been the procedure before) instead of yelling the words so quickly that I did not have enough reaction time to process what was being said. Patience and kind words were all that I needed. Please work on this.

Staff were extremely rude. Every part from ticketing, to security, to boarding all spoke down to us customers. Very disappointed in the continued disrespect. Security were also beyond slow. I can appreciate good security, but the airport wasn't busy at all and it took forever as they kept just taking their time.

Fort Myers airport is so poorly equipped with bathrooms, enough restaurants, stores that are open, and places to watch TV. There is not one TV in the waiting areas. If there is a delay, there just are no seats available. Breakfast food was not available at 9am. They were out of both breakfast food and coffee by 9 am. The lines for pre packaged food were 20-30 people long. They need to visit an airport like Grand Rapids MI to get it right. Grand Rapids is the same size town and so much more efficient and consumer friendly than this Fort Myers airport. Fortunately, the staff were friendly.

I think everyone can count on more than two hands the amount of rude experiences at an airport that they’ve had but today’s stood out more than usual! My boyfriend and I set our backpacks down after having gone through TSA already to go grab a bagel which couldn’t have been more than 10 minutes. When we came back to our seats there was a guard standing near our stuff with a dog. We didn’t think anything of it and then he approaches my boyfriend to belittle him in front of other people that you “can’t leave your bag unattended” and “it makes people unsettled”. He went on for about 5 minutes and then told us some other people may be coming to talk to us. All for a backpack ?! What is TSA for if you’re still worried about my bag?! Maybe this airports needs to put signs up saying not to leave bags unattended before they belittle their customers for their unwritten rules. Attached is a picture of the dangerous scary backpacks!

We are under a pandemic and I am wearing a mask and gloves, respecting 6 ft distance. Workers at security didn't want us to maintain 6 feet and told me they didn't care if we all got sick. one guy called me sick girl and said you decided to fly, you should have stayed home. This is awful and disrespectful. Security needs to be more aware of the part they play in helping keep people safe. Otherwise, they can stay home.
Small airport, clean and friendly staff. However, they have horrible wifi. Make sure you have a good data plan if you have to sit for a while for your flight.

This airport is clean and welcoming. The problem I recognize is the preponderance of dogs not being carried or placed in a designated kennel. During my last visit, I saw an emotional support animal lying on the floor in the TSA queue. Three dogs on leashes were seen at the Jet Blue gate. Announcements about dog rules and regulations are made repeatedly but are ignored. Signage would be helpful enforcement is needed.

We dropped off and picked up twice in March and went to cell lot to wait. Parking there is a mess! Cars are parked everywhere they shouldn’t be and people can’t move or get out. Has no one ever checked this problem out? Wish I would of known I could of taken pictures and sent in. I will definitely next time!

❌Not Verified|  Fort Wayne airport is so busy trying to save dollars they have created the worst customer service I've experienced in my entire life flying all over this country and several others! I will go to any other city, even if it means driving hours out of my way to avoid flying in or out of this airport. They have all their counter employees going out and helping in the loading departments and because of it they leave before the designated time and then lie right to the face of customers saying, "No we were here until far after it was time for you to be here". The security guards screamed at my entire family (we had children with us!) telling us we should have been there sooner, you were late." They have done this to every professional friend we have. They just don't want to have enough staff to do the job so they fail to provide for those of us spending thousands of dollars for flights out of their airport. Well, never again!

A nice airport except for the parking charges. It's highway robbery. I was charged $84 for 5 days of parking in the Short Term Parking lot. Evidently the word "Short Term Parking" means a short walk to terminal and not the length of time you plan to leave your vehicle there. I would encourage everyone not to park your vehicles at the airport for any length of time. Otherwise you will be robbed by the airport. I know I will never do it again. Shame one you FWA.

How refreshing for an airport free wifi free 30 minutes parking for passenger pickup abundant electrical outlets under seats a splendid Aviation Historical Museum friendly TSA security welcome home free cookies free shuttle to your car long term parking $6.00 per day which is closer than the short term in most airports - even if it costs a little more to fly out of Fort Wayne it is worth it.

After I had already checked in online, I had to wait for a very long time at the check-in counter for document verification. The staff were very slow, impolite and not helpful. I was informed that there is no business class lounge at the airport I could use. As compensation for the missing lounge, I asked for a voucher for a drink at the airport bar and was sent away without any voucher or anything at all, not even a "sorry". Then we had to wait for 45 minutes for the passport control to open for international passengers. Behind the security checks, there was only one single little shop with a very limited choice of food and drinks. What a miserable farewell to Brasil. This airport? The worst I've ever used. By all means, don't come here, if you can avoid this horrible place!

Still a bit of a dump. The airport expansion/modernization project first promised for 2013 then 2014 is now scheduled to be completed in 2017 and even that may be in doubt since a new bidding process may be required.

Still no noticeable changes to increase capacity or comfort in anticipation of the 2014 World Cup. No decent hotel options anywhere nearby. Options to get to the city's beach areas where most hotels are located are taxis and crowded public busses (plus a limited number of hotel shuttles).

This airport has gone downhill in the last couple of years. When we took off in mid-May of 2009 during a steady rain the main terminal roof was leaking in several places and there were buckets placed throughout the terminal to catch the leaking water though there were still several puddles. All airport parking is uncovered and there have been news reports of robberies of people as they leave the lot. The FIFA team that inspected and ultimately approved Fortaleza for 2014 World Cup games did visit the airport - fortunately for the city the inspection did not occur on a rainy day.

Clean and modern when it was inaugurated maybe 15 (?) years ago this airport is showing its age. The large arching windows meant to let in light into the main ticketing/check-in areas are perpetually filthy. Check-in area usually not too crowded especially with the de facto demise of Varig Airlines and de jure demise of Air Madrid but lines can vary widely by airline and time of day. There is one line to get into the boarding area and at times the airport folks will now allow you in until a certain time (which makes no sense since you will just be sitting in the boarding area). Pretty boring airport for a long wait. Food and shopping alternatives are limited and nearly non-existent once you go through security. Competency of airport staff uneven at best. Wait for luggage can vary widely but usually not too bad. I have arrived only on domestic flights so cannot comment on immigration/customs procedures. I departed once on an international flight (with 2 domestic stops en route) and the only difference for boarding was having to take off my shoes (and show my passport).

Mainly domestic airport serving the Brazilian side of Iguassu Falls. Busy airport with a 4 air bridges and some remote stands. Shopping opportunities as you walk from the gate to Baggage Reclaim. Baggage Reclaim is on the ground level and has 4 main baggage carousels. Domestic arrival so no Customs or Passport Checks. Small and busy Arrivals area with parking directly opposite. Small but efficient airport.

Worst airport I have ever been to. The location is terrible, 2h 10mins from Frankfurt reason why I think it shouldn’t be called “Frankfurt airport”. The facilities are few, some are closed. The staff is unqualified, they are blinded by the rules, they are the slowest security checks I have ever experienced. There were like 4 flights tonight, almost everyone of them was delayed (mine included) and lot of people missed their flight. I am 100% that I won’t come back.
Awful staff, worst airport I've ever been to. They don't speak English and don't make any effort to solve any question related to the flights. Very rude. Hated it.

One of the worst airports I've been to in ages.  So bad felt compelled to review - queues were endless, not enough staff, no wifi not enough places to sit, had to walk miles to the plane. And it's over an hour from Frankfurt. Do not fly here.

I have never ever in my life met such unfriendly staff. They were screaming at customers at all liquids should be in one single bag, they weren’t explaining it, thew were literally shouting. They were sneaking into your luggage without asking. Terrible experience.

I never faced in my traveler years what happened yesterday in this airport in Europe. Staff at the gates created a chaos at the control because of cosmetics not in the plastic bag of their choice, obliging people to buy it in a nearest shop or throw it away. Information was displayed on a little monitor not easily readable by all. There were three flights leaving and all left delayed because of this. Staff lacking in common sense, blinded by the rules (even correct), excessive in personal control without good reasons. All these in the name of the safety? Why nobody asked us for an identity card? This is not the correct procedure, I think. They should ask for it together with the boarding pass or not? Identity is not important? Any criminal can embark and what matters is to have the cosmetics in the plastic bag of their choice? So, in my opinion to switch from the Frankfurt Main one is the right choice. Forget Frankfurt Hahn. It is a great discomfort!

The agents are grumpy, on July 6 after a 2 hour flight, I went to gate 13 which leads to B62 to check my bags. When my turn came, they decided to accept people with special needs and let us wait. The lady was not nice, she gave us orders as if we were a herd of animals. No smiles, just cocky looks and sighs as if she hates what she does or hates the people she sees. After 10 min of waiting they sent us to other gates. I chose door 7, the gentleman who was watching the "scanner" machine asked me something in English but I didn't understand him well, he yelled at me saying you don't understand english and he sighed like it was the end of the world. What arrogance and what unprofessionalism. I have often heard that the service in Frankfurt was bad but this time I experienced it. Please teach your agents to respect people. We pay money to travel and not for free. I am very sorry, you are losing customers at this rate.

Poorly guided transfer for incoming flight from elsewhere and then transferring from Z gates to DTW. Dropped off at tarmac, then 2 bus shuttles changes, then 2 airport security checks. Almost missed my flight. Do not take Lufthansa or transfer through Frankfurt airport.
This airport is either totally understaffed or totally mismanaged. The security line took 2 hours, on the arrival we waited more then one hour on the ground. Avoid this airport if you can.

The conditions of the toilets are horrible. Also, they have a single duty free (if you can call it this way) and there is almost nothing. Empty shelfs, dirty bathrooms, the only thing that is nice are the employees. You can’t get out to smoke only if you will pass the security every time and that’s it. The most horrible airport where I had been in my entire life.

Dreadful service from start to finish. Staff unfriendly and unhelpful. Toilets were extremely dirty. Was there early in the morning but don't know when they were last cleaned. Avoid using this airport if you can. Would not recommend at all. Absolutely no redeeming features.

Our flight from Singapore was delayed, leaving us about 50 minutes to get between terminals and to our ongoing flight at Frankfurt Airport. We were told to catch the bus to A terminal at gate 57. When we finally found gate 57 the woman there told us the buses didn't go to A but to Z terminal and redirected us to the train, supposedly up two levels. We never found the train and whenever we tried to get assistance we got contradictory information. After walking long distances and basically being directed in circles- the signage is hopeless- we realised we'd never catch our connecting flight (which would have been the 4th leg of our trip to Budapest) and returned to the Airline gate we'd alighted at. Apart from one woman who seemed somewhat concerned, the gate staff. (airline employees or not) seemed to think it was funny to have two exhausted, hot and anxious senior travellers returning after traipsing everywhere and missing the plane. They arranged for us to go a different airline but that meant changing planes at Vienna, so in total we had 5 flights to get to our destination. They said now that we could walk to A terminal, so I asked how far it was. He asked if we'd like him to arrange transportation for us (my husband and I) so we gratefully said "Yes, please”. We assumed he meant the trolleys we'd seen transporting passengers around. We waited a few minutes and, to my anger and frustration, a man turned up with one wheelchair!!?? I refused to use it. We decided to try Gate 57 again and this time a very rude man told us to line up over there. The bus was packed and the driver showed no consideration for those standing. We were dropped at what we understood was Terminal A, but turned out to be Terminal Z - yes, just different levels of the same place! Walked up stairs where officials officiously told us to keep going up (although it turned out after we'd walked two very long lengths of the concourse that we needed to enter via the entrance we were refused entry to.) We went to the gate on our re-issued boarding pass only to find we needed to back track 8 gates as the flight had been moved. Even if we'd caught the initial bus we'd have still been unlikely to catch our flight as we needed to go through passport control which had a queue- although, strangely, not through security. We have been through many airports but this has definitely been the worst. Signing is confusing, approaching staff for assistance inevitably made our confusion worse and we were given incorrect information and the attitude of most staff was indifferent at best and plain rude at worst. Our worst airport experience ever and we will endeavour never to come to this airport ever again.

While the departure experience is improving thanks to new scanning equipment, the rest is still the same as ever: long ways, poor signposting, ridiculous prices for bad food and worse service. After walking for a kilometre, was surprised to find the e-passport gates working for once- for those with non-EU passports, only two counters were manned. Waited 45 mins for baggage delivery at 6 am. Glad no customs control this time..

Arrival from IAH took an hour to get our luggage. Sign counted down expected in 30, 20 10 and then just saying delayed, please be patience. 1 hour! Rest of the airport is kinda under construction with leaking ceilings, mouse traps and blue fences. There use to be a moving walkway between terminal 1 and the long distance railway station - gone. Out with the convenience and service - in with more greedy retail space.

Worst transit efficiency in Europe and terrible custom officers - very slow, chit chat with each other while on duty and when there is a long line of people waiting - even worse, the officer literally got mad upon our inquiry and said “we are chatting, can’t you wait two minutes?” And repeated "two minutes" several times during his work as if it was such a huge bothering for him from chatting. While not serving us, he also stopped us from going to other officers as if we were already in his possession. The most unprofessional part was that afterwards, the officer left his post, chased us after the custom, and threatened us with words "you'd better watch yourself, be careful" - something I feel expected from a mob member, not a custom officer. Although we do not think this is the right treatment to be received by any visitors (we were not even visitors to Germany, only doing transit), we did not argue with him, so the encounter was bad but brief - because we indeed felt threatened! We have visited many countries in Europe - France, Italy, Spain, Czech, Portugal, Ireland, etc. some for several times, but have never felt so un-welcomed and humiliated as what happened today. We have yet to visit Germany, but now I feel it may be the right decision for my family. Simply the worst people working here to give trash service to visitors, will avoid this airport and go to other hubs in the future.
The area looks is not designed for such a huge passenger number, some of the staffs are rude and unfriendly. The terminal has a nice overview of the taxiways and runways.

Possibly the worst airport transit experience you can imagine. I had 2.5 hours to transit and made it to my gate 5 minutes before the gate closed. First, there was a long line for the one shuttle to bring you from B to A gates. Then, there were multiple baggage cars and vans blocking the shuttle route. Once we got to the other side of the terminal, they made us go up to the Z concourse and walk through to the other end for yet another crazy long line at immigration where there were only 3 agents. The signs were confusing since the arrows pointing to the A gates led to a staff member blocking the escalator to the gates saying that there “is no way to get to the gates from here, you must go to the other end”. None of the staff seemed to care that many of us were about to miss our flights. One staff member responded, “sorry I don’t know” when asked where A gates where and another staff member said “just miss your flight, take the next one” when people were complaining about the long line at immigration. Several of the moving walkways were also out of commission.

I understand that we need security in this day and age but having got off the plane and going through four to five security check points is that really necessary? What I don’t understand is going through security again you have to throw away your water bottles why? You just got off the plane and making a connection, not like you have exited the airport and have done re-entry. On top of all these, just going to your gate there is another security check point. It’s kind of ridiculous to go through many check points. Have some common sense and think how to better check the folks getting off the plane. I would never recommend anyone to use Frankfurt as a transit airport. Talk to one of the agent and she said composing Lufthansa management. Lufthansa being star alliance partner does not even honor the other airline statuses. What good it is. For future I am going to make an every effort to avoid this ridiculous airport.

I'd read the many bad reviews about Frankfurt Airport and approached our transit through there with some trepidation. Well, we flew from Manchester and landed on time. A bus quickly took us to Arrivals, and we made our way to Terminal Z. This is supposed to be a major hub for international travel - but I was completely underwhelmed. After being directed through the inevitable duty free, you're decanted into a very long wide corridor with gates on the left and right all of the way along. On the plus side, the wifi worked, the toilets were clean, and there was at least 1 water fountain. On the minus side, it was very crowded, and the refreshments available I found were at a Bakery, a small shop selling drinks and sandwiches, and some handcarts selling hotdogs, pretzels etc. Very poor. We had a 4 hour wait until our flight to Dubai, and it dragged and dragged. Boarding acomplete shambles! There were 5 airport staff at the gate, and only one of them was dealing with boarding. I felt like taking over and getting them organised, Very glad when we eventually took off.

Plane lands at Terminal 2 and parks at an outside stand. External stairs are provided back and front, but the staff allow only the front to be used until 95% of the passengers have used the front stairs and one bus has left.  2nd bus waits for some minutes with doors closed for some time.  The bus takes the longest way possible to get to the terminal building. On arrival, a long series of escalators and confusing signs to get to the passport control. After that, several signs showed two options in opposite directions to reach Terminal 1, with many folk looking very lost.  Trying to reach Terminal 1, I headed for the overhead monorail service, using 2 escalators taking perhaps 10 minutes. At the entrance to the platform, barriers with a notice: "closed". With no previous information on the ground floor! 5. Returned to the bus stop for buses to and from Terminal 1, which was packed with passengers and luggage. Bus parked 100m away. After 5 minutes, it then moved to the stop, but there were too many passengers. Automatic doors with sensors above "would not let the bus leave until those areas were kept free". Long delay. with no help or airport staff.  Trip from Terminal 2 to Terminal 1 was long with 8 red traffic lights with no preference for buses. At the bus terminal, there was no map or information or Airport staff to indicate where the RMW express buses left from. The entire airport experience was a disaster, very frustrating and with no consideration for passengers. Terrible. Best avoid FRA, if you can..

Lufthansa flight late from Madrid. They unloaded us to buses and we had a slow transportation to the terminal. Many people had connecting flights. The new gate was B46, a very long walk from where the bus deposited us. Very unfriendly and unhelpful staff in terminal. Very slow and mean customs officer. I made my connection to SQ with 10 minutes to spare a sweaty mess before a 12.5 hour flight. I have another 10 hour flight to follow the 12.5 hour flight.

Freetown airport was always a miserable place to be. Even after it was refurbished it only became tolerable. In 2023 a completely new terminal was opened. I have the pleasure of sitting in the business lounge writing this review. The new airport was I believe built by a Turkish company. Sitting here, I could be in another continent. Or perhaps not, since FNA is rather better than the overcrowded airports in Europe. Lots of African countries have built new airports and Sierra Leone is one of the latest and have achieved something remarkable. The airport is not huge of course, but it is modern, very clean, with good facilities and for my Brussels Airlines flight, no queue anywhere. I found the staff to be welcoming, polite and on top of what they are doing. There are a few but enough shops and places to eat. The lounge is a good place to be. Food is more than adequate. Strangely, no beer but the wine is good. The airport must have been expensive but it does give a good first and last impression of Sierra Leone.

Brand spanking new airport. Built and operated by Turkish airport company. Touts and money changers etc all kept outside wich is good. Landing & departure USD25 each tax payment is a real pain and slow and unpleasant experience. Rude airport and security staff. Departure immigration officer ultra rude and very low on skill and job knowledge. Facilities all clean and fresh. Restaurant and shopping still very limited. Business class lounge is good for that part of the world. No beer no ice no sugar free drinks any where in the airport. All things considered its a nice little airport. Staff and officials need some serious training and attitude improvement. Signage is bad. Communication is worse. Why not tell people to pay all taxes on arrival or on arrival at airport, not once you are past the security check points.

Possibly the worst airport of an African capital. And I know very many. Arrival are pretty much okay given the extremely poor infrastructure. But departures are a true mess. Apart from being exceptionally far from the capital on the contrary of most African airports that are usually very close, with a pretty bad road, it is not only extremely old and small but also extremely dirty. Staff are plentiful but only busy discussing between themselves. The tiny business lounge which was confirmed as opened when I checked in was in fact closed for my 3 hours waiting for no reason other than "the staff had something else to do" according to 1 of the local shopkeepers. The only seats are most uncomfortable steel benches. Loudspeakers are impossible to understand. I have been trotting all around the African continent for tens of years so I am comparing apples to apples! The sun everything in one word: shameful.

There are substantial and ongoing improvements to Freetown Airport. They have been rebuilding the terminal building around the old structure for the last few months. Departure and arrival procedures are now quite painless compared with the hot and basic conditions before. The check in area is large and clean and I did not have to queue for long. They could still do with increasing the air conditioning in that area though. Security is good and immigration is using new computers and biometric systems. The departure lounge is now quite big and comfortable. There are a few well stocked duty free shops. The original restaurant is still available as well as a new one upstairs. The new one is not well signposted. Overall a big improvement. FNA now compares favourably with other airports in Africa.

Few improvements to report. Check-in is still slow and chaotic. There are a few more air- conditioners inside so it is not quite so hot. There have been recent problems with theft from checked luggage. Some reports even suggest that bags had been cut open. Definitely do not leave money or valuables in luggage. And do not let airport staff see if there is anything valuable in there. Business class passengers have a better experience because the initial queuing is reduced and the lounge provided some good food.

I have been using the airport almost every month during the last year. Some improvement in arrival procedures has been made. There are not usually long queues at immigration and baggage arrives quite quickly. For departures the entrance hall is still busy and too hot but if you take a fan and pay a porter you can survive. A couple of positives the duty free shop remains good and cheap and the food in the upstairs bar/restaurant is good. The check in area has been improved with modern counters. Hopefully this will reduce the queuing time in the entrance hall once it is fully up and running.

Much better than it used to be - they seem to have clamped down on the baggage handlers and general hangers on trying to extract dollars from you on the way in. On the way out no real problems aside from a few panhandllers trying to take a last opportunity to rip you off. Don't miss the duty free shop - it looks awful from the outside but is really well stocked and cheap.

Back again at the end of March. This time not such a good experience. On the way in baggage was late because the handlers could not be bothered to do their job. On the return we suffered a very long wait in the extremely hot entrance hall. This is caused by the very slow and beauracratic check in procedures. The air conditioning in the main part of the airport is proving totally inadequate and many units do not work. Some of the staff are quite unhelpful. Sierra Leone needs tourism but no respectable tour company would let their customers suffer this.

This airport has improved significantly over the last 5 years. It was badly damaged during the troubles. The only facilities were a partly destroyed hanger. Now the main terminal has been refurbished it is quite respectable. Arrival is easy enough. You will need to be firm with the baggage handlers. They have been clamped down on recently but they will still try there best to relieve you of a few $. If you let them one will carry your bags to the door another for a few more feet etc. Just say no and try not to look as if it is your first visit. Once you have got your bags you have to visit the customs bench. You will now need transport to Freetown which is the other side of a large estuary. There are helicopters a ferry and a hovercraft. Take the Paramount helicopter the other two take too long and are unreliable. It is cheap $37 on my recent visit. You may have to change this into the local Leones before buying the ticket. There is an exchange office which gives respectable rates. The helicopter departure area is the old hanger that used to be the main terminal. It is dirty and hot so try to get the first helicopter. These are old but reliable Russian MI-8's. You will arrive at the Mammy Yoko heliport. Here you will most likely be met by your local agency or whoever you are visiting. If not local taxis are available. A trip to most parts of Freetown should cost no more than Le10-20000. If you do not have accommodation booked go to the Cape Sierra Hotel or Bintumani Hotel which are very close. On the way back the helicopters leave about 6 hours before the time of departure. You then wait outside the Lungi terminal for an hour or more before suffering the long and bureaucratic check in procedure. This is typically African and can take an hour+. The main lounge is air conditioned. There is also a very good duty free shop and a reasonable restaurant upstairs. You will probably not be hassled by airport officials for bribes unlike other countries in the region.

Freetown Lungi International Airport is a small airport terminal building. It recieves very few flights the majority being international. It has so positive attributes like no congestion speedy check in and checkout. A hotel is conveniently located near it. There is a duty free shop and restaurant. There is also a VIP Lounge for the elite and other first class passengers. Beware that the airport is very small. It needs renovations and a series of expansions effort due to its small size. The government is in the works of expanding it to accomodate the international passengers.

The airport is very small with just about 0.5 million passengers a year. The few check-in desks are enough service is fast no queues travel agency's most big car rental company's have a desk and restaurants and visitors terrace with a nice view are available.

FDH is an airport I use quite often and it is generally fine. But facilities at the airport are not geared towards business users; for example there is no business lounge. It was well served by Eurowings from Frankfurt until the beginning of 2005 with 4 ATR72 flights per day each way. But since LH Regional have taken over the service there are only 3 flights per day each way whose reliability timing and frequency are woeful.

A typical Ryanair airport. Small and miles from anywhere (although perhaps suitable for the Alps and skiing access or unless you have relatives nearby!) However it meant that from the plane to the car hire desk was about 50 metres and we were on our way less than 20 minutes after landing. If you need a train the station is literally 30 metres from the terminal door. It's not an architectural gem the seating is limited and hard but it has a cafe and a shop and it's efficient and has what you need. The staff were friendly and allowed us to board first on our return to the UK as my wife had a broken hand in plaster. As long as the plane is on time it does the job well

Going through security I had a pen in handbag which caused problem even though I have travelled with this for 16 years and had no problem before. I didn't mind being stopped for it.. security is paramount...but the rudeness of the staff there was unforgivable... Made to feel bad as I did not understand what was required.. basically through security once more... Just grunted at and very offhand. Chap was going on a break it turned out so that was his problem! Woman who took over very slightly better! Happy going through procedure as should be questioned...but attitude needs sorted...after all we are their bread and butter! Politeness goes a long way! My scoring only really went down because of security..cafe staff weren't friendly either.. Jet2 departure on boarding chap was exceptional really customer focused and friendly..perfect for the job!

Terrible experience. The personnel at the security check is so rude, offensive and unprofessional. They cannot speak English and they pretend you to speak Spanish screaming at you that this is Spain and you have to speak the language if you want to talk to them. We made us waiting 2h in the easyjet plane before taking off. It was the worst travel experience I have ever had.
Ryanair made us wait an hour in a queue with a passengers who had large luggage just to receive printed ticket for visa checks. Annoying ,not fair. We were really dissatisfied and disappointed.

Terrible, rude staff especially with special assistance. I travel with my disabled son and when we arrived at at the desk for check in the woman who served us was so rude. My son isn’t an ambulatory wheelchair user but he walks slowly and we would be happy to get help to the gate. She said if he needs special assistance he needs to sit in a wheelchair otherwise she is going to cancel it. I tried to explain to her that he is fine without a wheelchair but she kept repeating herself not accepting any other answer. My son started to get very anxious and nervous because he thought he needs to be taken to hospital by using wheelchair and finally she said if he doesn’t want using wheelchair chair he isn’t disabled person. Does she have the medical education to comment on this?  I tried to stay calm because my son was stressful enough so I didn’t want make him more feeling stressed, anyway she cancelled special assistance for him. The airport staff having this job only because so many tourists coming to visit Fuerteventura so they should respect that instead of being horrible and making people feel like an unwanted intruder on their wonderful island. Nowhere else have we been treated so horribly like at this airport.

Awful. For an island that relies totally on tourism, the time taken to get through passport control was just not good enough. Everybody should be prepared to accept queues but when you are in a queue of hundreds and there is one person in the passport control kiosks it simply isn't good enough. Is it to punish the Brits for Brexit? Can't think what other reason it could be for as it certainly doesn't put you in a good light. Big improvement required.

Never have I experienced such a hot extremely slow journey through customs. This is unacceptable, only one person checking passports with long queues and no air conditioning. People very tired and hot and babies crying. Absolute disgrace and has put me off returning.

I am a non ambulatory wheelchair user, accompanied by my husband. After prompt check in, I was obliged to wait at least 20 minutes with other disabled, before being guided to another place in departures. I was told that I would be contacted at this point, at least half an hour before departure. We went immediately to a refreshment area to buy a much needed coffee, but were sought out by an attendant who told us that we need to be at the departure gate. I told the attendant that I must first use the disabled toilet, and was pressured by him that I needed to be quick. What a joke. I have never been in such a badly equipped disabled toilet, and discovered to my horror that there were no fixed grab rails to help me stand, to pull myself together. Only one wobbly drop rail. I opened the toilet door, knowing that I could pull myself up, using the door frame. Fortunately a lovely attendant was there, and realising my dilemma, she helped me to pull myself together. I have never been so mortified in my life, but she was very sweet. The impatient attendant was waiting for me in the public area. On the verge of tears, my husband calmed me, as we followed the attendant to the departure gate, where we waited for another 20 minutes. It the door of the airplane, I was transferred to a small loading chair and was dragged on board amongst the confusion with other walking passengers. We have used this airport more than 30, and always rated it fairly, but now, a recently disabled amputee, I am disgusted with the whole departure experience.

Absolutely terrible customer service. Got frisked twice and kept having to go to the back and queue again for the privilege. All my of things removed so fast still on the tray to another place I didn’t know whether I was coming or going. My belongings were gone and I couldn’t find them. Luckily, I asked a man where they could be and they had been taken to lost and found. My car keys, phone, purse, tablet and Apple Watch. Much to my horror. I was spoken to like a fool and he demanded evidence that they were my belongings. I managed to convince him to let me have my phone so I could prove they were mine.

I am disabled and had just been given a cancer diagnosis by my doctor on the phone whilst in Fuerteventura. I had one of the last two flights that night and had been ill all week. I had mentioned this to the team and said I was very weak as a result and needed a bit of extra help. My flight was due to depart at 21.25 and by 21.00 I found myself in the special assistance area with one other couple who were on the other plane leaving at the same time. 2 members of the special assistance team came over and I asked if someone was there for me. I was told to "calm down and that I had to wait my turn". I had asked in a low voice and was perfectly calmly. I waited another 10 mins and when I looked there were 2 other people in the airport, cleaners!! 10 mins until my flight left and no staff or any way of contacting them. Getting distressed and being in pain the cleaner helped me by going to find someone. Last call for my flight had been announced twice already. When the 2 members of staff arrived they were so rude to me I couldn't believe it. I asked why I had been left and they just laughed at me, it got heated and she stopped pushing me and said "Do you want to walk?" ... I mean really?? That's what you threaten disabled customers with when they are unhappy with service?  I tried to get out of the chair  as by now I was so upset and felt so belittled by these 2 women, but she pushed the chair so I couldn't, catching my foot and dragging it.

Very pleasantly surprised by this airport - especially after our "home" airport of East Midlands. Arrived to find airbridges to the aircraft so no busses or walking across the tarmac, baggage didn't take long and easily found a taxi for the short journey to our hotel. When we departed we checked the bags into a check in area with no one queueing (we were a bit, but only a bit, early) and had a drink outside before going through security. This was a bit confusing - got turned away from one security queue as it was for families - could have been a bit better sign posted. The actual proper security was just behind the check in desks - again, this could have been made a little more obvious. But once through the actual departure area was vast, spacious, and light with 2 outside areas, at least 3 children's play areas, lots of different eating choices and quite a few "duty free" options. Didn't try any eating places so can't comment on prices. Plenty of places to sit and wandering down to the end of the hall there were some deserted and very quiet parts. All in all very pleasant and far better than most in holiday destinations.

When I arrived at this airport from incheon, the immigration lines were long. It took me more than an hour to get out of the airport. I headed to Incheon a few days later. Security and immigration was actually fine although I found the facilities a little old. There were plenty of places to shop and relax, but I wished that there were more food choices. Overall, this is a small but functional airport.
Small but good airport, the usual Japanese quality, clean, efficient, good staff. Places to shop and eat, and have lots of charging spots. Its so convenient to reach from the city center.

Never have I been to an airport with staff so keen to help and so lovely. After a baggage mishap at Shanghai Airport I arrived at Fukoaka knowing that my bag was not on the flight that I was on. Upon arrival immigration was a breeze, even with a British passport, and I went straight to the arrivals desk where four people immediately helped me. They were so kind and helpful and sorted out my problem immediately. They reassured me that everything would be ok and even gave me a 5000 yen note to pay for the delivery of my luggage to where I was staying, somewhere around 3 hours away from Fukoaka. The whole airport experience was wonderful in comparison to the rude service I received at Shanghai Pu Dong Airport. Thank you to everyone who helped out a traveler who had lost his baggage.
Long immigration queues are the main factor why the 'Queuing Times' section receives only 2 stars. However, the airport staff were polite and friendly which gives some merits on staff service.

Upon arrival moved swiftly thru immigration. The luggages for all the passengers did not arrive - some malfuntion was announced - it took 90 minutes for the luggage to finally arrive. No announcement during that time. There are no seats in the areas so every one sat in th floor waiting. Upon departure also check in and immigration moved very fast. Went to the Fukuoka lounge - very spacious but very limited food. Soup? Noodles and bread.

Compared to NRT / HND / KIX this airport is left lacking. It is small so should have been an easy one to transfer in but with very little time one had to get out of the domestic terminal and wait for a bus ride to take you to the international terminal. After some 15 minutes ride you get there and it was quite difficult to figure out where to go. Finally getting to departures you had to queue for a long time for both security scanning and passport control. The staff were very rude unlike elsewhere in Japan where one always gets a great welcome. They tried to pull the basket away before I had even put everything in it. No hello. After enduring the rudeness you had the very slow passport check queue which took forever. Left no time for shopping or enjoying the terminal. Grabbing a few items in panic I got to the gate. There was still just the call to go to the gate but for some reason I heard my name called on the tannoy. I presented myself. The gate staff offered no explanation nor smiles looking at my boarding pass and then handing it back to me. It was most odd. The up shot is if you are using FUK make sure you have a lot of time and don't expect the usual Japanese manners. Certainly made this traveler feel most unwelcome.

A very confusing and dirty airport. I've lived in Japan a long time, but this was my first trip to Fukuoka. I was very disappointed with the airport overall. Very hectic and confusing. It was also quite cluttered and dirty, which I was surprised because you don't see that in other airports in Japan. I was looking for a specific shop, but could not find an information counter anywhere on the departure level. I finally went to the bottom floor near the subway station where I found one. The restaurants inside the airport to not have any signage or menus in English, which was also surprising considering the number of foreigners I saw walking around - and yes, they too looked as confused as I undoubtedly did.

Arrived in FUK on Nov 26 and departed Nov 30 from/to Shanghai. Arrival was a breeze. Baggage reclaim immigration and custom clearance were fast and smooth. Staff efficient and smiling. Departure was terrible. Only 1 X-ray machine for all check in bags from 2 flights of pax resulting in long lines looping around the entire check in island. Waited 30 mins before bags scanned and allowed to check in. Then carry on bags had to subject to another check with long lines again. Another 20 mins wasted standing in queue. This was clearly quite unsatisfactory and a pity as the airport was otherwise very clean modern great looking with helpful and friendly staff.

Arrival on 25/12 and departure on 1/1. Efficient and friendly airport staff even the immigration officers were welcoming. It was supposed to be a domestic airport so the international terminal was nearly empty when we arrived. Spotlessly clean no matter the departure or arrival hall toilets luggage claim. Floor guide was very clear. As impressive when we departed from the airport. Before departure visited their domestic terminal. Amazed with their friendly and helpless ground staff and the facilities despite the small size of the airport. Three domestic terminals with good Japanese and western restaurants. Observation deck was amazing that I could actually see planes takeoff and land very closely unlike Hong Kong International Airport where they charged. The domestic terminals were busier but still spotlessly clean and efficient and it is close to the main city and subway station. A fantastic tiny airport.

Great little airport: incredibly close in to the city centre (5 minutes by metro from the Domestic Terminal to the central station) and the international terminal is spacious with comfortable seating by the gates and good value shopping. The only downside is the tedious 10-minute bus transfer to get there from the Domestic Terminal.

Google flights told me that our flight was delayed by 2.5 hours before I arrived at the airport. On arrival we checked with airport staff and they confirmed the flight status was fine. The signs sent us to our boarding gate which meant going through passport control. On arrival at the gate they have not opened it and so nobody is able to sit down. After waiting 30 minutes there is an announcement that our flight is delayed by 1 hour and 55 minutes (just under the 2 hour mark which would entitle us to food and drinks). Google flights still says that our 2:35 flight to Stansted will not be leaving until 4:55. The gate has still not been opened. Very few passengers can sit down. Elderly passengers are standing up in a queue for an unknown amount of time. None of us are able to get back up to the airport where we could by food and drinks. The airport signs still do not show that the flight is delayed therefore passengers will still be being sent down here without warning that they will be trapped. Very deceitful behaviour from Funchal airport and Jet2.

Nice airport pleasant staff and security excellent. Poor check in resources (for a BA flight to Heathrow) took ages for them to set up I think due to lack of staff. Lead lady did the work of 3 people. Lounge nice but on the basic side but I expected this. One staff member officious. Then the horror of having to wait after the gate was called before they would open passport control which was a dour experience. Then a wait to be allowed in the gate. Same overworked lady managing on her own.

I was a disabled passenger on the Tui flight 12/01/24 departure date which eventually took off 15/01/24. All Madeirian staff at the airport were polite, very helpful, in particular the disabled Assistance staff. The poor weather affecting the departure will not deter my family from coming back to Funchal. All the very best for the new year.

I could not buy any gluten free food at the airport. I ended up with a big bag of crisps, (Sem Gluten) the previous shop told me none of the crisps where G/F and she sold the same ones I bought. It was an experience I will not be repeating, the last time I visit Madeira. It is disgraceful that a person is left hungry by greedy cafe owners.

Worst airport experience. Transavia flight TO4851 from Funchal to Porto was cancelled due to bad weather conditions. Since arrival time at airport at 9.00am, I spent 9 hours at the airport for transfer to hotel to be organized. Hundreds of passengers waited like cattle to be processed. Airports announcements unintelligible. No minimum distance kept. In times of a pandemic utterly unacceptable to be forced to queue for hours and risk health with hundreds of other passengers. Unprofessional and unfriendly personnel. No information and transparency whatsoever provided. I was informed by e-mail that my flight was cancelled. It never was shown on screen or announced. I strongly advise flying to Funchal airport - in case of unforeseen conditions be prepared to endure harsh conditions. Madeira, never again. Side note: at arrival to Madeira, very painful testing experience.

Their covid-19 testing team do a terrible job. I felt my brain tickled and stabbed. It is sharp, it’s stabbing - I can’t even really describe the feeling. Ended up with an intense taste of blood in my throat. My legs, of their own accord, not controlled by my brain, shoot up, and start kicking, as if I’m flailing, as if I’m in the electric chair. If it’s done correctly, it shouldn’t be excruciatingly painful as it is, in my case on both times I arrived in this airport this summer. I would prefer to be punched in the nose while leaving the aircraft than going through this again. Both my mother and father felt the same. My question is who are the people doing these tests? Be careful.

It is a very clean airport and very easy to move around. Departures and arrivals are well defined and separate. It is very safe and there are good shopping areas in the departures. My experience at this airport is 40 flights, all without problems at the airport, and the last flight was in January 2020. Nice views from airport, we can see Desertas Islands and the sea, sunrise and sunset.

Going through security screening was a nightmare. I was told I was an "explosive threat" after having my hands screened twice and producing a positive result twice. They said this can happen to people who have used certain body lotions/creams, medications, touched certain items i.e. flowers. I was then escorted (very indiscreetly) by 2 armed police officers to a separate room where I was searched, my hand luggage searched and I was questioned. After all this I had to go through the whole process again, security, hands screened, positive result, by which time I was very distressed. A terrifying experience for a 62 year old woman - I do understand the need to keep air passengers safe but this screening technology is clearly not efficient or sufficient if it can be triggered by ingredients in creams and lotions. I will never return to Madeira.

TSA Combination locks changed by baggage handlers at Madeira airport. My cabin cases were put in the hold by easyJet at Bristol Airport, I handed the two cases to easyJet staff just before going up the steps when boarding as they were concerned there was not enough overhead locker space. No problem, I’ve done this many times before. When picking up the hire car at Funchal airport I needed to access the cabin cases only to find my combination lock numbers had been changed. The hire car reps managed to open the one case but the lock on the other had to be broken open. Apparently this is not unusual at Funchal, this was the fifth time they had experienced it. These mindless pranksters should be sacked. A great start to the holiday. Has anyone else experienced this problem?

I was very excited to land here as this airport is famous around the globe for its risk landings! The infrastrucure per se is very basic, you deplane on the tarmac and then walk to the arrivals, staff were ok, I found people in the Madeira island to be very friendly. Do not come without pre booked stuff as I noticed they inflate the prices for tourists who decided to book on the spot. The airport is clean and security is fast, long lines though. Snacks on the land side much cheaper than air side.

The signs at Fuzhou airport are quite helpful, since available in both English and Chinese. The border security counter has a rating system where you can rate them based on your experience. If you don't speak Chinese it may be slightly difficult to get around. Queue was quite long, and it took quite long to find your baggage. However, it was an OK experience. The staff was very friendly, and friendlier than I had expected.

I have flown here only on private aircraft. The commercial airlines have yet to discover this often overlooked resource. The parking and terminal buildings are great. Reminds me of how Chicago Midway used to be before the most recent spate of reconstruction like a hometown feel. Very clean facilities and the commercial pax I have spoken to all seem to enjoy it. Mostly the lack of a commute to Chicago I think.

I had a terrible experience at Gdańsk airport today at the executive lounge. I arrived too early for my flight and decided to avail of its service. There is a machine in the departures hall where you can buy a ticket which I used. It was a very straightforward transaction. The price of Zl 150 came up. I inserted my credit card and got a ticket. On arriving to the executive lounge, I was told that I could only use it no earlier than 3 hours prior to my departure. The staff member wouldn’t call a supervisor, wouldn’t let me use the service now instead of later, wouldn’t refund the cost and actually told me to leave. She was extremely unhelpful, ignorant and confrontational. She actually enjoyed the situation and her power over it. She kept telling me about the rules, but nowhere on the machine in the process of buying the ticket, did I see any notice about a 3 hours timeframe. The ticket itself didn’t specify it either. I respect the rules but they should be clear, visible and transparent So two major problems, confusing and well hidden rules and terrible staff in the executive lounge.

The Internet connection is timed to 30 minutes and so bad mobile is far superior, there's not enough seats and those that are there are extremely uncomfortable hard plastic with dividers. No quiet zones, low temperature makes you catch cold, and then there's the staff. The service is forced and makes you feel bad for even ordering anything, and dont try resting at any of the restaurants' better chairs - they'll call security even in the middle of the night. Reason? Well, who really knows, maybe they like seeing people resting on the cold floors since there's not enough seats?  There's even a dedicated announcement just to remind there are thieves. If you can avoid, especially if you have to lay over - pay a bit more, and choose one you know to be people-friendly.

The airport in Gdańsk is an absolute disaster. The service is incompetent and rude, and the check-in lines are absurdly long. Virtually every service is poorly organized, from security checks to baggage collection, which takes forever. The terminals are dirty, the toilets are neglected, and the food in the food court is expensive and tasteless. I do not recommend anyone to use this airport - if possible, choose another place to start your trip. Lotnisko w Gdańsku to absolutna katastrofa. Obsługa jest niekompetentna i nieuprzejma, a kolejki do odprawy są absurdalnie długie. Praktycznie każda usługa jest źle zorganizowana, od kontroli bezpieczeństwa po odbiór bagażu, który trwa wieczność. Terminale są brudne, toalety zaniedbane, a jedzenie w strefie gastronomicznej jest drogie i niesmaczne. Nie polecam nikomu korzystania z tego lotniska – jeśli masz możliwość, wybierz inne miejsce na start swojej podróży.

Horrible security staff who went on the power trip. Rude, unprofessional and very unpleasant person. There is no need to act like that. Please do better.  Other staff members at the check in were fantastic.

I am partially disabled with restricted mobility. I have metal in my leg and hip following reconstructive surgery. As a frequent traveller I know I set off the security metal archway detector; therefore, I know what to expect and ensure I carry no additional material which might exasperate my situation. Noting some airports adjust the sensitivity of these detectors. So, back to the Gdańsk experience. Having detected the archway, I am directed to remove my footwear. My trainers are cloth/plastic, no metal. This is the default situation and very annoying. It is obviously not my shoes that cause the alarm. Of course there are no aids, by example a chair, and I am forced to comply or no fly! So, no shoes, but despite my explanations I again alert the archway. I did tell you that would happen - me to the suspicious security person - now a physical search. Remember I am partially disabled. Stand on one leg and show me your sole! I’m +60 years of age and there is no standing support aid. I am then very roughly treated by a security thug who has the compassion and intellect of a slug. Frankly this was probably my worst experience over the years. Shame on you Polish Civil Aviation Authority. Treat partially disabled travelers with restricted movement with more respect and compassion.

I had a very bad experience in this airport. The airport is new and beautiful but you feel you have gone at least 30 years back the way the security system works here. In my arrival we waited ages to get through the security which I would have kept blind eye on it but my departure made me hate travelling here again. From the time I was in the line I think I was singled out cause others were passing through but she kept me waiting behind and then unfortunately having metal clip on my hair made it worse. In other airport if it had made any noise, they used to ask me why it made noise? Do I have anything with metal in it and they used to let me go but here I was checked for explosives!!! which I appreciate it cause I know I’ll be safe on the airplane however why me? It was embarrassing. I never ever had such an experience in any airport and I travelled to many places. I just hate travelling here or even Poland in the future. Never this airport for sure but I read the reviews for other airports before I travel to this country if I do come back.

Airport Security very bad, was a big queue take as more than 1 hour to pass through, no speaking English shouting and screaming all the time with out no reason. They don't let us priorities to catch our flight and we miss our flights. Straight away they remove us from airport with out any help during to rescheduled our flight down stairs.

Horrible experience with security staff. I'm writing this because, sadly, I need to use this airport often, and each time I'm there, already with bad experiences, they still managing very well to climb on new levels of bad behavior towards me and other passengers. They just bark and yell on travelers. Word “please” does not exist in their vocabulary. If you try to talk to them, it only magnifies they bad attitude. My last adventure there was about pants belt, which was not a belt, it was part of pants attached there for good. It was impossible to take it off, and yet they were demanding it. Explaining, showing – pointless. Had to rip out whole thing, and ruined the cloth because of some lady having bad day. Cannot wait next visit there… avoid as long as it’s possible.

Again a negative experience at this airport. Security is of a low level, there is a negligence on the part of the security body. The X-ray control is shameful to see how a policeman, without being well uniformed, rumbling in a chair says a lot about himself. Pressure to pass the trays with hardly any passengers. Workers from the airport without masks in this time with the Coronavirus Rising Up again. Today is 27/11/2021. First flight of the morning with LOT, horrible company too. Don't take except if you don't have other choice.

Health and safety rules are very loosely followed. I was marked for a random check (the one where they check your hands for traces of explosives). The female security worker was not wearing her mask and I asked her to put it on before approaching me. Since then she was plain rude to me and barked orders. The two hand sanitizers that I could locate were empty. When I looked around practically none of the staff were wearing their masks correctly even though it was crowded.

Access to the airport from the underground station is easy to find and well signposted. Due to the high volume of passengers, the waiting times for the check-in and security check were long. There is a good selection of shops and restaurants. The toilets are too few and quite old.

I arrived on Sunday 2nd February to go skiing for a week and from entering the terminal building after getting off the plane to getting through passport control took over two hours. A complete and utter shambolic airport. On the way back on the 9th, from being dropped off outside the airport it again took two hours to get to the departure lounge complete chaos and no one cares. All they want is the money from us for using their airport. My best advice to anybody is to avoid the airport at all costs so you do not get really disappointed and frustrated that I did.

Terminal 2 is an absolute joke, it is akin to a bus shelter. The airport is losing so much money by making passengers wait for bus transfers to the main Terminal and by the time they arrive at Terminal 1, there is no time to eat, drink or spend any money in the shops. You provide 1 transfer bus every 10mins whilst you are checking in 6 flights at a time? This is the worst airport that I have ever travelled from and I have travelled the world. Third world countries can do a lot better than this. Very disappointing.

Absolute chaos departing from Geneva yesterday (Monday 3 February 2025). It took just over an hour to get our passports stamped which was about the same time as the flight to LHR. The queues were enormous as there were far too few staff available. The number of positions open varied from three to five with staff just closing up and walking off. It wasn’t much better for Swiss and EU passengers. Probably not their fault as they would be instructed by management. An appalling experience made worse by airport staff not putting our skis on the aircraft. Overall, a dreadful advert for Geneva and Switzerland.

Third world system. Absolutely awful. The queue to get out of the airport is going to be longer than the flight. Sweating because it’s so hot in the queue. Screaming kids and babies because they’re hot and tired. UK flags covered with white stickers to hide them (just to spite us for leaving the EU (really? Don’t be so petty. You didn’t have them covered when we first left). No markers to tell you how long to expect. No staff to make sure everyone is OK. Lanes not properly marked so people in wrong queue and lots of queue jumping - just a shambles - shame on the Swiss, I thought you were better than this. Arrived in the terminal an hour ago and still no end in sight. Apparently several UK flights land at the same time on Saturday night. Transfer companies know it and expect it so it’s not a one off. Fly to another airport if you can (assuming they’re any better).

Busy and crowded on both Sundays. However queues were manageable. Inbound immigration went smoothly Baggage hall is still a scrum, but more staff on duty to assist Check in was quick and efficient. Food and drink are over-priced. Sufficient seating in boarding area.

Utterly inefficient organisation. Check-in and organisation of security queues were totally chaotic with inefficiency everywhere. On the evidence if this airport, I have no idea where the myth of Swiss efficiency comes from. Also extravagantly overpriced for everything and poor quality food and beverage. Really unfriendly security staff.

Far better experience at Geneva on departure. Check-in queues were long, but moved quickly enough No delays at Security or Immigration, so got the gate. 30 minutes early, despite the long walk Reason being I assume because there were few other departures around that time Shopping area is cramped and crowded

Geneva really must get its act together. Arrived at about 13:30 on Sunday. Queues for immigration were one hour plus for non Eu and 45 minutes for eu passengers. Admittedly three large intercontinental flights had recently arrived together but still unacceptable!

We transitted via Geneva on our way home to Copenhagen after a holiday in Malta. I've flown into and out of Geneva a number of times, albeit not for around thirty years. The airport is poorly designed, with long walks to and from the various satellites. It's certainly showing its age and is in dire need of an update. The most noticeable thing was that the majority of the staff seemed unhappy. With the sole exception of a smiling women at Security all of the staff wore a scowl and ony helped begrudgingly. Unless it's your home or destination, I'd suggest avoiding Geneva Airport.

Everything looked well as we arrived from Palermo en route to Manchester as our bags arrived within 5 minutes and checked in within 5 minutes. That’s where it started to unravel. The security was inept with 2 people checking 3 flights. It took 45 minutes to get through passport control despite Ryanair calling 6 times to get us all boarded. Even when the security guy was told the Manchester flight had priority over the Tirana flight which was an hour behind ours. We just got on board with minutes to spare. More staff needed and better communication rather than a 1970s PA system. Avoid Genoa airport if you can

This airport is small but convenient but also quite dated looking. It looks like it's stuck in the 80s and seating isn't comfortable. Duty-free is readily available and there are a few small kiosks serving food and beverages. Security check is fast and efficient but also looks like how it was done 30 years ago. There are different bus services to the city center.

Flight to Amsterdam was canceled due to the weather conditions, that’s how it was and acceptable. The handling at the airport was unacceptable all over. The help desk appeared ignorant and arrogant to the affected customers. The assisting crew (only 2) at the counters were ignoring our need for help and it appeared as they picked people by names and not from the huge crowded 2 lines. Compared to other airports around the world, this incident yesterday October 11th was the worst I have ever been a part of and the airport should absolutely evaluate the lack of service provided to KLM and the customers involved. Do hope for improvement in the future matters concerned.

Arrival following amended flight from Paris (see CDG report) we went to the lost luggage desk to report our loss but the operative there said we would have to wait a half hour because his computer was down. The fact that we were late for the departure our of our cruise liner did not seem to register. Eventually after help from the marvelous cabin crew from our Air Dolomiti flight he shrugged his shoulders and told us just "Go". On return we went to the same office, aided by the courteous customs and police, where a very efficient lady located our missing paperwork and we were away. Only to join a massive queue of passengers from the liner being security checked using just 2 of the 4 scanners who, in any case missed the liquids which my wife had forgotten to remove from her hand baggage. There were a lot of sweaty bodies flying out that day.

It is a small airport no long queues or big crowds quick check-in and boarding. It has quite good services if you consider its dimensions. It is clean and comfortable. I always start my trips here when possible also for overseas flights because it has good connections with the main hubs: Rome Paris Munich London Istanbul.

Genoa airport compares extremely well with our huge overcrowded and understaffed London airports. It is nice and small with lovely shops and good cafes. There are no long queues at check in or security and staff are friendly and helpful. A pleasure to visit.

I have used the comfortable Cr. Colombo Airport in Genoa at least 15 times in the last 5 years. Small comfortable no crowd no queue security check is not the standard paranoia of the EU just lazy smiles. Friendly staff excellent shop excellent coffee shop (fantastic quality of espresso good grappa and beer - reasonably priced). And not to forget - it is comfortable to rent a car and drive anywhere in the Ligurian Coast easy car return - the Airport is before Genova on the road. One of my favorite airports.

My husband suffers with neuropathy and towards the end of our holiday his feet were very painful which made walking difficult. I did not arrange assistance at the airport and was concerned he was unable to do all the walking at the airport and worse still the amount of walking at Heathrow. I enquired at the help desk and explained my predicament. The staff were amazing and not only arranged assistance at Gibraltar but also contacted Heathrow on our behalf. I cannot thank them enough for making our Journey an amazing experience at both airports which would have been a nightmare their kindness was was very much appreciated and I cannot thank them enough.
It’s an absolute disgrace that all mens toilets and the disabled toilet at Gibraltar Departures have run out of toilet paper. How can that happen? Very unhappy.

My 86 year old mother traveled alone to the UK on December 23 2021 but unfortunately the flight was diverted to Malaga airport. She has to have disabled assistance as she is unable to walk. As per usual protocol, all passengers were walked across the border, in the pouring rain I might say! and into a coach Spain side. The issues with disabled assistance started once outside Malaga airport. All passengers were left to remove their own baggage from the coach hold. A reasonable ask if you are a fully abled person. My mother and another disabled passenger were left behind to fend for themselves. It was a kind and thoughtful passer by that removed the suitcases for them. They then had to make their own way, unaided to the desk. By the time my mother reached the desk, she could barely speak and nearly passed out. This is appalling and these passengers should not have to find themselves in such circumstances when traveling. This needs to be addressed by the disability team at Gibraltar Airport who are usually amazing. I feel that perhaps they are totally unaware that this service which is requested at the point of paying for a flight, totally and utterly breaks down when these flights are diverted. Outside Malaga airport these passengers, who are unable to walk unaided are left stranded and so I felt it is vitally important for Gibraltar Airport and the disabled services concerned to be made aware of it. I have also emailed BA, the airline concern.

I recently slipped a disc and needed assistance at Gibraltar airport. I can't say just how heartwarming it was to be met by the lovely Sam and guided through what can be a pretty stressful experience with genuine humanity and not a few laughs along the way. She's a real gem, as were all other staff involved from check in to departure. Another client asked what happened as we were raised into the transport, and an attendant - who'd had a similar injury - gave some really good supplementary advice as we disappeared. I do a fair amount of travelling and that was a rare experience. Thank you all.

We landed from Manchester about 5pm on the 5 Dec, I went to the ladies but wished l hadn't as they were in a very poor state and smelt very bad. There are not many flights landing in a day so why they are that bad I dont know. The airport management must take the blame as it would not take long to check them and the manager is not over run with work are they. A mop and some bleach go a long way.

Hardly any shops, no good shops, no restaurant with hot food. No vegan food options in the one very bad cafe. Dirty stained seats inside. We were going to pay for the VIP area because it was so bad but were told even that doesn't do hot food or vegan food. Overall very disappointing for an airport experience.

We used the new terminal for the first time this year. The new airport departure lounge is spacious, clean, bright and airy. At around the time of our departure there were several flights scheduled to depart and found that both of the toilets in the departure lounge were closed, one for cleaning and the other due to a blockage. I walked from one set of toilet to the other, being sent to the others which were also closed with the staff not seeming to be aware that both sets of toilet were closed. One of the toilets reopened after me complaining.
