Maybe the airport management should ensure that at least one set of toilets are kept open especially during busy times when several departures are scheduled. I was surprised that the new state of the art airport lacks air bridges to aircraft rather than still needing to walk out to the aircraft and climb steps to board.

I visit Gibraltar airport regularly for trips backwards and forwards to the UK and to pick up friends and relatives who are visiting. I am appalled by the condition of the glass screens on the viewing tower and stairs leading to the viewing tower, the glass screens gave not been cleaned since the airport opened and are now at the stage where you cannot see through them. Equally the stairs are dusty, dirty and litter ridden.

The airport is much improved since I was last here in 2008. Arrivals, not much to say, there was just my flight in, so the baggage queue was pretty tame. Departure, check in was a breeze, even though there were three flights due to depart that morning. There is free wifi and plenty of seating. The new terminal building is spacious and modern, with a nice outside seating area overlooking the runway and apron. Security was also a breeze, with only a very small queue, and security staff seemed pleasant enough. No air bridge though, so if it's raining, you have a couple of minutes walk before you get to your aircraft. Overall, a nice little airport

As per usual security is minimally manned with very long queues. They seem to be surprised by flights arriving and leaving. When I complained that a second machine needed to be opened at security to process people quicker they all laughed and said they were waiting on a break. I think the two crews that were obviously available were rotating around rather than sound security processing. This shows a lack of leadership in an important part of the airport.

Its a pretty bad airport. The airport itself is not bad in terms of cleanliness or anything. But the experience at this airport leaves a lot to be desired. To begin with it is far too small and clearly does not have the capacity to handle a lot of traffic. The lines to go through immigration are utterly ridiculous. The line went literally from one end of the airport to the other. And moved at snails pace. People were missing their flights. Second issue is the rude and just "don't give an eff" attitude of much of the staff there. Nevermind that most can't even speak English. Provided you can even find anyone to help you or that gives a damn about helping you. This is really more like a provincial airport than an actual international airport. I have had far better experience at airports in developing African countries in terms of service. South Korea should be embarrassed by this joke of an airport. I would give a minus rating for the airport staff if I could. But sadly a single star will have to do.

Quite busy airport in South Korea. Arrival went relatively fast, since i arrived from Mongolia you had to fill a health declaration form at the airport which you could do on an iPad or simply write a paper form. Didn't take much time and also the queue to passport control wasn't very long. Luggage was already at the belt after clearing all formalities. Had a 9 hour layover in Busan so wanted to leave my luggage at the airport and upstairs they do have a left luggage office, so that worked nicely. Airport is connected to the metro network so moving around is easy. On departure later in the evening it was quite busy, it was difficult to find empty seat on airside. All seats are cramped in the middle of the corridor surrounded by shops and restaurants, you cannot really get by the window so not a good place for planespotting. Terminal feels more like a train or bus station.

Worst airport ever. Female guard working at the entry gate was rude. She couldn't speak English, so she was mumbling in Korean. People working at international airports should at least speak basic english. She wouldn't let me in because my boarding pass didn't have my middle name.

Worst airport ever for welcoming foreigners. Arrived in the morning and there was a queue of around 100 foreigners and one immigration officer. Whilst the Korean passport holders breezed through. There is a sign which reads “Gimhae Airport, How Korea Welcomes the World”. What a joke.

Staff do not speak English. I received very bad service from the staff that was in the Tax Refund desk beside Peach Airlines. He was very rude with me, shouting at me and he didn't speak any English. I couldn't get any tax refund from him. He was the rudest person I found in South Korea.

My family and I were flying out of Gimhae International Airport to Hong Kong on March 26, 2019. After lunch (around 13:30), we decided to head to the departure gate. I was holding my two year old daughter and my wife was with my six year old son right behind us. We walked up to the airport staff and I handed him all four passports with boarding passes for inspection. This airport staff spoke Korean to me. Me being Chinese, I told him I do not speak Korean. He then proceeded to speak Korean to me again louder and in a condescending tone. I have no idea what he was saying to me. My wife (thank goodness she is Korean) came up to see what the problem was. This person repeated what he said in an even ruder tone toward my wife. At this point, I am extremely frustrated and I said to this person and I asked him if he spoke English. He ignored me and continued to address my wife in a disdainful manner. After a few exchanges, She found out that this airport staff does not speak any English and each passenger had to hold his/her own passport and boarding pass. This airport staff then inspected our passports and boarding passes in the most foul mood, without once apologizing to my wife nor me, and sent us through. Having the name Gimhae "International" Airport, I would assume that the first airport staff personnel any passenger meet would have the basic understanding of English. Isn't it his/her job to make passengers welcomed, greet them with courtesy and respect? I did not see or experience any of that at Gimhae "International" Airport. Gimhae should consider revising/updating its basic requirements when hiring staff. I believe each staff should at least know the English phrase to be able to perform his/her job properly, or maybe I'm expecting too much from Gimhae "International" Airport. Another thing is that there was no signage advising each passenger must pass on their own passport and boarding pass (even toddlers) for inspection. My family and I have been to many airports around and have never encountered this. After this incident, I have concluded that Gimhae "International" Airport is not a family friendly place.

Immigration queue was terrible. Queue was so long for arrival, and even longer for departure. The airport should do something about this. I have no complaints about the immigration officers, it was just the queue that was unbelievable. Could they please at least have dedicated lane for business class passengers? or at least provide a fast-track card?

I cannot praise enough the airport assistance staff at Girona airport. My son has autism and I was wearing the Sunflower Lanyard. Assistance staff saw me waiting and came over to me to make themselves know and offer assistance at check in, security, and boarding the plane. Fantastic staff.

Worst airport I have ever been at. Security staff are so rude and just speak back to you in Spanish. Queuing system for security is ridiculous. You have to put your stuff in a tray way before the belt and then try and walk up with your suitcase and how ever many trays and backpacks. I didn’t beep going through the security yet I was called to the side with no explanation. When I asked for an explanation I wasn’t told anything. The woman was rude telling me to come to the side when I was trying to gather my stuff. She swabbed everything and was so rude asking me to open all my bags. I asked her why and she didn’t answer me. All I wanted was an explanation it was a ‘random check’ I just wanted to know as I didn’t beep. I got told to ‘relax’ then when I kept asking. I have never been treated like this in an airport and I will never ever fly from Girona again. As I said I didn’t even beep and I don’t mind random tests but there should have been an explanation and respect from the security staff. I felt like a criminal and was treated with absolutely no respect or explanation. I highly would not recommend flying from this airport. Avoid and go to Barcelona Airport if possible.

I could not believe how quiet the airport is now Ryanair have decreased their flights checked in with baggage in less then 5 minutes and through security to departures in no time. Once airside there is not much to do but there is several duty free shops a cafe/restaurant and a Subway/McDonalds outlet as well as two outdoor smoking terraces. All in all a nice clean little airport with helpful and friendly staff.

Arriving:-No airbridges but large standing for 6 aircraft in front of the terminal (walk to board) and a further large standing where you board via bus. Ryanair  who base 6 737-800`s here use the area directly in front of the terminal. Passport/Border control can be busy and crowded if more than one aircraft in-especially for UK passengers. Luggage collection hall is large with six carousels but again can get very busy as the Ryanair flights go out together in the morning and return at a similar time at 4-5 hour intervals during the day with final flights about 22.30.Other charter flights are spread out throughout the day and night with  as has been traditional for many years at holiday destinations - a "German day"  a "British day" a "Dutch day" etc.No Customs as such  just out through the doors to a full length and narrow area where Holiday and Car Hire reps. await. Coaches and a car park is straight opposite and since Ryanair arrived there has been a substantial investment by the airport including a new multi storey car park access roads and a new filling station/car hire area. The whole arrival system generally seems to work quite well . Departures- Check in is generally a nightmare the area is far too small for the numbers and Ryanair will not start check in until 2 hours before departure leaving queues of 150+ sometimes snaking out of the entrance doors (and in amongst the smokers). This problem is made worse by passengers repacking luggage at the front of the line to save paying excess.It is also exasperated by the charter companies dropping off their clients 3 hours before making the whole area very busy.There is a large cafe/bar which is again very busy. Once checked in it gets much better and you pass upstairs  through very strict security and scanning to the large and airy departure lounge with views of most of the airfield. Two decent sensibly priced snack restaurantst hree large shops and loads of seating including an open area with bar at high season. There is no executive lounge but with business users using the Madrid shuttle and many leisure travellers now having Priority Pass there is a gap in the market. Announcements and signs are good with departure gates normally shown well in advance  saving the last minute dash. Boarding staff are efficient and motivated for a quick turnaround. Not a bad experience and would give the airport a full 4*`s except for the bad check in experience - has to be a 3* then!

Glacier Park International Airport (FCA) in Montana USA is the best small regional airport I have visited. After a very long journey from Sydney we were cleared very fast. What impressed us was the security guard who stands on arrival exit door greeted us with a big smile and sad: "welcome to Montana". On our return flights we were checked in very fast cleared very fast with smiles by TSA (what a difference after LAX-TSA!). The terminal and toliets are very clean.

A small regional airport with a few flights per day to mostly Brisbane. The airport is always very clean and the security staff are always cordial. The airlines crew are nice but not very friendly. Queuing time does not exist as there is almost a flight every hour. There is no shopping options except two cafes at the airport, one in the departure and the other in the arrival. There is a spacious parking lot and a couple of car rental kiosks. Overall, although you can't even think of comparing this with "real" airports, you can still have an acceptable experience here in the class of the small regional ones.

My benchmark is I travel every month for work domestically within Australia and also internationally. Here’s why Glasgow Airport presently sucks: 1) £5.50 drop off fee for private cars. 2) Length of queue and wait time at security 3) Obvious intent and opportunistic profiteering from services that’d be free at actual world leading airports: paying to weigh luggage, paying £8 for priority security queue (if you were efficient enough there would be no need for anyone to pay). 4) Airport overall tired and rabbit warren like.

What an absolute ripoff. Why are we allowing companies to rob us like this. The government or the Civil aviation authority has got to step in to stop customers from being robbed. So to drop off and collect costs £10. Who are you lot kidding? This £10 gives a customer absolutely nothing. High time that people protested on their doorstop. God help us if other businesses started charging their customers for being dropped off to spend money on their premises. Glasgow Airport get your masks back on like robbers do. Hold your heads in shame.

Glasgow Airport has become nothing short of an organisation designed to part unsuspecting travellers with their money. The drop off fee has again been raised to £5.00, a shocking amount for what amounts to nothing at all. I find the whole concept of drop off charges to be extortion. What other organisation allows people to charge to deliver their customers to their door? On top of all this prepare for further extortion in the bars and restaurants. The Caledonian bar now charge £7.50 for a pint of beer and £1.75 for a dash of lemonade in your already grossly overpriced 25 measure of spirits. If going to the airport my advice would be to bring sandwiches and avoid these highway robbers altogether.

Security alert mayhem, no one knew what they were doing. People with priority pass and Emirates customers allowed to skip the security line, while me and my two boys were held back in the mayhem, missing our flight, connection and part of our holiday. Tried to explain that my flight was leaving to be told “we are all in this together, stay where you are?” Two emails sent as complaints, not one reply. Will avoid in future!

Return flights from Glasgow to Verona. Check in was quick as was passing through security. Facilities were alright bearing in mind our flight was at 6.10am. Boarding was efficient. Return again was stress free other than the automated passport gate refusing to let me through. Baggage was already on the carousel when through security. All in all a pretty good experience.

One of my party fell ill on arrival at the airport an airport attendant was absolutely fantastic - she immediately got a wheelchair. Helped check in luggage and seen us through check in and security and seen us on the flight safely. She could not have done more.

Decent sized airport with friendly staff. Arrivals area was pretty small but the airport itself was well connected to the city with the bus service running just a few steps outside the arrivals. I travelled during the peak holiday season so was dreading departure from Glasgow but I was pleasantly surprised as the security was well managed and we went through smoothly. The restaurants were bearing the brunt of the holiday season with not enough seating but it was still nice nonetheless.

Been using Glasgow airport for decades and my experiences have been steadily declining for quite some time now. The new road layout around the front of the terminal building is very poorly signposted indeed. Trying to pick my way through from the motorway to my hotel it was near impossible to see any signage and was charged four pounds to drive 100 yards through the drop off zone not stopping. Felt like I’d been cheated even before i got anywhere near trying to check in. Inside the terminal building on the landslide its been absolutely emptied out and looks very sad, dreary and like a big neglected shed these days. All the restaurants and eating spots that used to be available upstairs are all gone now. Downstairs theres a solitary coffee shop, an M+S express and a pub called the spinning Jenny that served one of the most dreadful overpriced stone cold meals that I’ve endured in quite some time. On the airside there were at last some more food options available but the prices were absolutely extortionate. The free wifi is only available for an hour and constantly logs you out and good luck trying to grab any rest if you”re waiting around or any length of time now that there is an air hockey table and super loud arcade games in one of the vacant shop spaces without any doors to block the volume. Overall the experience was like visiting a shopping mall months before it goes out of business but with planes parked outside. Management need to sort this shambles out

£4 to drop someone off and another £4 on the way back - for what? Grumpy staff at check in, border control, security, gates. Not enough seating, 10.30 am in the lounge used by Lufthansa and breakfast was over. Cases lost on arrival. Menzies aviation are a joke. I had to go looking for them to inform them. No reference number was given to me and none of my contact details were loaded onto the lost baggage site. A quick call to Lufthansa sorted it the next day. They received my case on the morning of the 3rd Jan and didn't deliver it until the afternoon of the 4th despite it being labelled as rush/same day delivery. Menzies have gone to great lengths to prevent passengers from being able to call them. No phone numbers anywhere, I'll be taking this up with the CAA. I'll be using Edinburgh in the future

Not going to repeat so many other negative comments that I agree with at Glasgow airport however, I must raise the question again as to why the one hour only free wifi business - utterly ridiculous, I’m now on a 10 hour layover in Toronto and free wifi all the way, all day at the airport, why so tight Scotland when other airports are trying to at least offer free access while at the airport but not Glasgow, shame on your stingy offer!

I was diverted to this airport as my TUI flight from Florida to Newcastle could not land due to fog at Newcastle. When we landed we were informed we were to be "bussed" to Newcastle (174 miles away) over 3 hours! After 2 hours sitting on the plane we were informed that fog had lifted & we were to fly back.......plane engine would not start! they were sending an engineer from Glasgow to look at the problem. 3 hours later we were to to disembark into the departure lounge (300 people) after 2 hours we were told to stand in a queue for a £15 food voucher? most people had already paid for a breakfast. The queue was 300 out of the restaurant as only 2 people serving. as My wife is in a wheelchair & I'm 77 I could not stand in line for over an hour I still have my 2 x £15 vouchers! We got back on the plane waited another 2-3 hours (9 in total at this airport) then told to disembark AGAIN! to be told 300 people we to be taxied to their homes! I was on this plane 17 hours plus then a wait for a taxi then a 3 hour trip to Newcastle. The airport did not have enough seats, the restaurant was overpriced almost 316 for a small hamburger . People were smoking in the Ladies toilet. Staff were rude at Passport control & security. I feel sorry for people who have no choice but to use this "airport"?

I'm complaining about the lack of public transport to Prestwick Airport. I have guests from Italy who will fly from Prestwick on Sunday 6th August. The flight is at 9am. Its impossible to get to the airport from Glasgow to catch their flight. The only option is to catch an expensive taxi. Its embarrassing and gives the impression that Scotland is a barely developed country. You need to do better than this.

Security staff were rude and unfriendly. Went through body scanner, all ok, however this guy stops me, before he pats me done I inform him I have a Stoma bag, his attitude changes, telling me, not asking, that I will be subject to a further search, I was furious, treated like a criminal he said "We can search you here (in full view of other passengers) or in a private room", he calls over his mate, I was furious and embarrassed by his actions, in the private room they didn't check any of my luggage, another pat down, a total waste of my time. They didn't even explain why / what they stopped me for. I have used this airport many times before and other Scottish airports and never ever have I been subject to a search, even before I had a Stoma bag fitted.

Staying 20 mins away I love this airport ... might not be many facilities but with fewer flights there's no hold ups, security checks are quick and never experienced long delays. Staff more than helpful, maybe plan a coffee shop for late arrivals but being near to home doesn't really affect me

This is not a family friendly airport at all. We traveled with a 5 month old baby and had to join a general queue to go through security check. This is not acceptable and the airport management should be ashamed of no family lane arrangement. There were also no lifts or ramps on the way to the gates. We had an inconvenience carrying the buggy, car seat together with all our other belongings. No assistance from staff was offered.

The girl who initially was nice to us at the information desk then proceeded to question us at the departure lounge. She looked disappointed when we produced our negative results and examined them very closely. Travelling right now is stressful enough without somebody who is having a bad day create more stress.

Loved this airport, no long queues and you get through security really fast. We only went with hand luggage going to Palma so we arrived 1 hour before the flight and this was plenty of time. We normally use Glasgow airport but would definitely use Prestwick again. Only wish they would do long haul flights to save us having to go to England to get around the world.

In a word horrendous. When you arrive with 2 starving kids and they aren't serving food at 2 in the afternoon. We were told this was due to the food arriving ie delivery (brilliantly managed). The only food place that side of the airport and it's not serving food absolutely genius. Then you go through security and the only food place has no kids options one vegetarian option and literary nothing healthy bar one said salad. Expect to serve your children a bowl of chips or toast not a single vegetable. Just pathetic, absolutely pathetic. Another restaurant is opening but what use is that to me. Its an airport, not a roadside cafe. It also takes 3 days to actually getting your order. Never ever shall I use this poor excuse of an airport again. Don't be swayed by the cheaper flights, they are cheap for a reason. I had to board a plane with 2 hungry kids which has both upset and angered me.

What a shambles at passport control on arrival from Malaga (Ryanair FR 656) last night (7th March 2019)! It certainly did not look like customs staff in attendance were interested in providing a service to the public - only 2 members of staff were employed checking passports whilst 2 others chatted socially at one barrier, another (presumably the senior member) looked on and 2 armed guards observed the situation at the doorway whilst 2 further desks were unoccupied. Consequently there was a bottleneck at the 2 desks in operation and long delays for passengers, queuing in cramped conditions with no access to toilet facilities (after a 3 hour flight). I note from the posters on display that you welcome comments from the public - I would particularly like to ask the senior officer on duty to account for this arrangement and his allocation of personnel.

Food and drink very expensive, 2 or 3 times what you would pay at a normal cafe/restaurant outside. Dirty dishes left lying on empty tables. Quality, so so. Departing was OK, but arrival, around 1am was just what was not needed after a delayed 3 hour flight from Malaga with ~200 exhausted passengers to be met by only 2 security persons on entry. I should add at this stage that I am slightly disabled at present as I am recovering from a replacement ankle operation, so have to use a stick to get around. Also, as my case had been damaged by Ryanair in transit I could not wheel it along so had to use a trolley to get it to Car Park 3. As there was an excalator to get up to the bridge and over to the car park, I enquired of 'Information' how I might get my trolley to the car park. They kindly showed me to a lift which took me up a floor and then along to the top of the escalator where I was met with a notice which declared, trolleys no further! Really helpful! So from there I had to carry my suitcase over the bridge, down the stairs to the station, along the platform, out and down the path to the car park and finally struggle to get it to my parked car, by which time I was absolutely shattered, a real welcome home. I doubt I'll ever use Prestwick again.

Airport staff is not at all supportive. Plus the food is super over priced and doesn't make any any sense. Only thing good is the wash rooms other than that nothing to boast about. Drastic improvement needed.

I had the very worst experience with the airport facilities especially the toilets. They are not keeping the standards of an airport and the staff are not even bothered about the cleanliness or the basic needs inside the toilets. Very worst experience ever had using an airport toilet in Goa.

Probably the worst airport I have been to. Food is a rip off especially beer. A small can is 940 inr which is more than 10 times the price out of this horrible. Dirty, noisy, crowded, not a single place to get some quiet. Kids running around shouting even now past midnight. Security was a circus. They check every person with a hand magnetometer even through there is already another one you pass through. They separate men and women in different lines. Seats are as if I were in third class in a train 50 years ago. People watch movies at full volume. Had to move three times.

I recently visited at airport and was impressed by the impeccable service of staff in Toilets. The attentive and knowledgeable staff ensured that our experience was a memorable one, providing excellent recommendations and ensuring our satisfaction.
Large and fairly spacious airport, unless there’s a couple of wide bodies departing. The terminal is new and smart without being stunning. Good range of shops

In Goa domestic terminal the seating is inadequate at 6 o’clock in the morning, lots of seating arrangement is in very poor condition and badly maintained. For the kind of travellers that are passing through this terminal, national image projection is very poor. This is when sanitation staff (a lady) promptly came over to clean spilled coffee (due to unbalanced chairs set) Seating here is so close that your knees knock. If these seats are unfit to use please have them replaced/removed. Food offered from kiosk turned out to be stale (chicken burger). But was returned thankfully. At the same time, I would like to appreciate courteous behaviour of all individuals on duty.

One of the worst airports I have travelled to. Being a frequent traveller i have travelled to places where airports are virtually non existent but Goa Dabolim airport takes the cake. The rubbish bins near the departure immigration were unclean, the garbage was not cleared and there were flies all over the bin. Dirty and unhygienic. The international departure area had no lounge for travellers to relax and the seats were dirty. The security area where scanning took place was filthy and the trays provided were dirty. Its a shame that GOI is even called an airport.

Arrived mid night from Mumbai in a domestic flight, aircraft attached to aero bridge, in 10 min we were at baggage area, baggage arrived in next 5 min. Washroom were clean, paid porters available, plenty of baggage trolly. No public transport during night ,only option is either prepaid or booking directly with taxi drivers. We took prepaid, going to Utorda around 15 km, paid approx 1200 inr, during night a 35 percent surcharge is applicable, during day time should be around 700-800 inr. Just after you exit the terminal would be surrounded by taxi drivers, prepaid cab counter is inside the building at arrival hall.

Goa is by far the worst run airport I've ever been through. No other airport keen comes close to Goa's inefficiency. I would rate this airport zero if the scoring system allowed me to. It took over two hours to go through immigration and security in a single continuous queue yesterday. In the same queue some people queued for three hours, it's that badly run that people just kept getting missed and they queued for an hour longer than us. Almost unbelievable. Throughout this time there was no information or access to drinking water or toilet facilities. There was no way to sit down. The area where we queued was a very tight corridor with people pushed closely together. Some people were getting angry, others were freaking out from being trapped in the situation (one was even on the floor crying) and I personally felt sick the whole time. It was just lucky I didn't throw up then because I had no place to go and I would have had to throw up right there on the floor. It wasn't even like there was many flights due to depart that morning. It's a very quiet airport compared to some. There seems no reason for it other than an inability of the staff to the run the place like it is actually an airport. How the shops making any money there is anyone's guess. We had no time to visit any of them as we rushed to catch our flight (which was delayed due to the security nightmare) After our trip to Goa my fiancee and I were umming and ahhing as to whether we'd come to Goa again. After the experience we had yesterday we will never go back to Goa again.

2.5 hours to reach gate, standing painfully in 5 different lines (Entry to airport, bag scan, check-in, immigration, security check) with long queues in each line and understaffed immigration and security check is very disturbing. Being an Indian, I feel sad with state of airport with all tourists getting agitated. I doubt if any tourists will ever want to return and will recommend visiting Goa. Very disturbing, considering passengers have to travel in flights ranging 3 hours to 30 hours. Please make their life bit easier.

This is a cheap and nasty airport. When we parked our car, there is hardly enough room to open the door as there is only inches to spare between cars. On one occasion I had to climb through the sunroof to get out of the car. The airport is generally overcrowded and noisy. In some departure lounges customers are all seated or lying on the floor. It’s not too bad on a quiet day, but at other times there long queues even at the toilets. Such a shame that such a beautiful place doesn’t have a decent airport.

Hopeless! Faulty Air NZ kiosk out of bag tag paper. No help there with Air NZ staff. Over zealous customs treatment. No Air con in international lounge. No lounge facilities. We expected Qantas code share lounge as advertised. None in international lounge area. Very poor for on international airport!! Air NZ staff need to be there before 2 hours of departure. Great week in Coolangatta. Disappointed with departure.

The arrival hall is not equipped for the number of people arriving. You are made to line up to use the few arrival card machines. Other Australian airports have multiple units placed along the arrival corridors. Customs staff don’t appear to be well trained and make you open your bags for things you have declared like tea bags.

Free water at Domestic departures is hidden from view with no signage, in a blatant tactic to extract more $ from the travelling public. Almost the same at International departures - free water exists in the furthest location possible with a small sign not visible from the terminal main area. This is just evil corporate behaviour. International arrival experience was poor, long queues. Baggage carousel at international arrivals has a design fault causing bags to fall off, and create bag chaos which passengers need to fix. I will avoid this airport in future.

The new extension at Gold Coast airport is so bad. It’s a big empty ugly grey cavern with no life in it at all. My backside is sore from having to sit on the floor with 100+ other people. There is no wifi no mobile reception. The design is weird with glass walls separating the queue area. There are rows and rows of empty chairs in the old area corridor. They called the flight to board then no staff arrived and all the passengers were stuck in a cramped queue behind the glass walls for over 20mins. Whoever designed this nightmare should be sued. What an embarrassment for Gold Coast and Australia. Reminds me of being in a world country
Upon my arrival at Gold Coast Airport from Bali, I experienced the worst border security treatment. The officer detained me for2hours. This airport has more officials than passengers.

This airport is not capable of handling the volume of passenger traffic. Waited 20 minutes for stairs to disembark upon arrival. Now upon departure the queue for security screening is 100 metres long.

Gold Coast Airport new terminal is a joke. It’s smaller than the old terminal. I arrived on Scoot Airlines, which landed at the same time as 3 other flights. Around 1200 passengers trying to clear Immigration which has enough room for about 350 passengers. I can’t imagine how packed this terminal will be once more airlines start to arrive. Obviously no thought was given to future growth, my recommendation is go through Brisbane Airport, at least you have separate lines for Australians

Could not get free Wi-Fi when logging in inside the terminal. Got directed to the help desk operated by volunteers. Showed the kind lady how I was logging in ad she agreed I was logging in correctly. She directed me to the duty manager who was not interested in helping or getting somebody else to help me. I was staggered by her attitude. What customer service is that ?

Attention Air NZ staff at departure processing 9th October. Gold Coast - Christchurch Air New Zealand NZ0278 OOL - CHC - 18A, 18B A very big thankyou to the team for getting us home. My wife Pauline found she had lost her passport as we were booking in. We were resigned to missing our flight, but staff showed such wonderful determination and commitment in helping us through this crisis and spent such a long protracted lengthy time on the phone resolving our issue, we have only the highest of praise for her and her staff. Heartfelt thanks to you all from two very grateful Kiwis!

Functioning but non-air conditioned air bridge to terminal. Terminal building is easy to navigate and path clearly leads, after heading down escalator, to baggage pick-up. Baggage arrives after minimal waiting time of 5-10 minutes. Many people in terminal besides passengers and employees. Mainly porters. Everyone appears to know everyone else so I guess that security is not an issue. Inside and outside terminal, many drivers call out offering lifts in cars/vans heading to Gorontalo city as airport is 3/4 to 1 hour from regional capital. Fares are negotiable but 200-300,000 is the norm. Bules may pay more. Toilets, ATMs and lower end eating facilities as well as souvenir stalls are easily accessible. Forget having a "drink".

STN-GSE. Arrived on Ryanair. Single runway so only one plane can land/take-off at a time. Very compact with everything close by. A very short stroll from the aircraft to the terminal where 2 Passport Kiosks quickly processed everyone. The Baggage Claim is one conveyor and there are limited toilet facilities before getting to Arrivals Hall. Arrivals is mid-way between the 4 Check-in Desks and the Security Scanning. Outside the airport there is a taxi rank usually stocked with cars for each flight and the bus to the centre of Gothenburg. Picnic tables are still outside on the grass where you can relax. Security is OK and then a smallish Departure Lounge which is very busy if 2 flights are going at similar times. The Duty Free has various things but no alcohol. There is a cafe selling hot and cold drinks sandwiches and similar and a small bar selling drinks. There are 3 Departure Doors of which Gate 2 has Passport Control for non-Schengen flights. NB Whilst Security is quick if there are two flights at the same time the process slows especially as most passengers travel with volumes of hand luggage that need liquids etc removed. It is a good little airport and friendly in size.

Have used this airport twice in the last year and found it very smooth. From plane arriving at terminal only ten minutes to clear border control collect bags and exit airport. Bus to Gothenburg outside terminal to meet each flight and in to city in about 20 minutes - quicker than from the main Gothenburg airport. Adequate facilities in airport and an outside area airside for smokers to sit in the sun with a drink!
Why can’t I use cash/money at this airport? Just want a drink and don’t have a card with me but refused - surely if I have money you have to accept it?

I recently had the misfortune of traveling through Gothenburg-Landvetter Airport, and I was utterly appalled by the inefficiency and lack of professionalism displayed by the airport security staff. Not only did they seem disorganized and ill-prepared, but they also exposed my children's snacks to unnecessary radiation by scanning my bags not once, not twice, but thrice! It's one thing to ensure the safety of passengers, but it's entirely another to subject personal items to repeated and excessive scans without a valid reason. I understand the importance of security measures, but there needs to be a balance between safety and respect for passengers' belongings. The staff's lackadaisical attitude and disregard for my concerns left a sour taste in my mouth (quite literally, considering my irradiated snacks). I sincerely hope the airport authorities take note and implement better training and protocols for their security personnel.

The security staff are too rude. In 5 years of Gothenburg commuting, I have Goosebumps every time I go through security check. The 100ml liquid limit for women is absolutely ridiculous and exaggerated, knowing you can buy tons of liquid after security check. Any other country in EU does better than Landvetter. Today it’s August 25, 2023 and Gothenburg’s airport isn’t keeping up with modern flying conditions yet.

I fly frequently from Landvetter and the staff is just the rudest I've ever met at any European airport. They are often unaware of international rules and I've never experienced such a recurring combination of aggressiveness and blatant incompetence. Airport staff are usually polite and helpful, even at busier airports like Frankfurt or Amsterdam. I'm giving 2 stars out of 10 instead of 1 just because the facilities are very clean and the waiting time is reasonable - it's a rather small airport with very little traffic. Food options are limited, generally unhealthy and expensive.

Arriving, not a bad little airport, very calm and not at all manic. Got through the border quickly and on to Arrivals Hall. There was a delay to the delivery of the bags, but an electronic sign for belt 3 advised at wait time bags would be delivered, and they were delivered at that time! Vintage Volvo sitting on a plinth at belt 3. Departing, terminal was bigger than I expected, and again very calm and not at all manic. However, to get land-side, there are three electric gates, one for Fast Track. Then there is a flight of stairs and an escalator to reach a gallery along which you walk to Security. As I was leaving, escalator was turned off as there were a lot of people going through at the time, and there was a queue on the stairs.This was the only downside. The terminal is being upgraded, but this was only obvious at the Schengen gates 19, 20 and 21. If you are leaving from 19B - do not forget to got through passport control!

Arriving into Landvetter was fine had to get a bus to the other side of the airport to go through immigration. As I was on a non-schengen flight we had to go through immigration. This part is quite small with 4 European check desk and two non-eu that are hidden in the corner and there are no signs to show that the non-eu passport holder check is on the side. Waited in the wrong queue for a few minutes till I had to ask and the immigration office put me right. Immigration was quick with very friendly staff on arrival and departure. I'm the baggage reclaim you can see the bags come out from the conveyed overhead which is cool. On departure airport, queue times were quick with security very quick as well. Gates 24-5 has a small eating area with minimal seating and lack of plug sockets and as you have gone through immigration you can't leave this part. Plenty of food and shopping options very modern clean airport that is nice to travel through.

Excellent small airport - clean, spacious, good restaurant, 2 airline lounges collectively available to a great many airlines. Arrival was to jetway 15. Departure was by bus to plane from gate 18E (the gates 18 uses buses to go to aircraft). The departure flight needed de-icing, since the aircraft was not parked at a gate, it could be de-iced in place before taxiing. Frequent reliable bus service to/from city. Security personnel (on departure) efficient and courteous. Time in security line < 5 minutes.

I think everything is ok but not the baggage claim. It is too long waiting for luggage. When we arrive it said on the board that luggage would be there 20:13. When no luggage was there at 20:25 I went back to the board and it said that it was on the track - it was not. We waited 10 minutes more. So we landed at 19:50 and was out of the building 21:00 That's too long waiting.

I got extremely frustrated by how none of the toilets in the entire airport were suitable for a toddler. My daughter is too old to wear diapers but also too small to use a big and scary adult-sized toilet seat. None of the toilets were equipped with a child-sized toilet seat or even a plastic potty, so she ended up peeing herself in frustration both on arrival and our departure a few days later. The airport is small but otherwise meets all expectations you might have of a modern airport, so I found this particular lack of preparedness extremely strange.

Landvetter airport is a rather small one, well organized and neat. Security checks have seldom long queuing and are generally fast. Lots of toilets are available, very clean, with taps to fill-in bottles with water. So do not hesitate to pass security with an empty bottle. Shopping options are limited as the airport is small but the choice is more than correct. This airport seems well managed!

Chaos in security control, caused by one male staff who was rude and irritated, made people go through security check twice and even three times! The other staff seemed embarrassed of his behavior. This made me feel sad and uncomfortable.

The airport was pretty good actually. However, the security staff were appalling. My wife has Brochietisis, COPD and Asthma combined with fallen metatarsals. Walking is difficult and she can only manage short distances without getting breathless. However, she does her best to avoid using the wheelchair services for a bit of self-esteem. We went to the nearest security gate and were directed to one about 200m further away, which then required another 100m walk then a total of another 390m back to go airside. Despite explaining my wife's issues the staff did not care one jot and when we asked for a supervisor they laughed. Just to add interest today is my wife's birthday. Made a major dint out of a brilliant holiday and ensured a very flat ending.

Bag drop didn’t open until late was meant to open at 18:55 didn’t open until 19:27, for a 20:55 flight meanwhile all flights for easyJet were queuing for just 4 bag drop desks. Security was somewhat chaotic, the instructions have gotten less and less clear, all electricals to come out despite signage saying put small items, watches, phones etc in hand luggage causing significant delays passing through security. After passing security, food choices are extremely limited, there are many concessions offering a broadly identical menu ham and cheese sandwiches or cheese and tomato or ham, some had tuna but looked particularly unappealing on the cheap and sweet local sliced bread. There is also a Burger King but it was too busy owing to the aforementioned issues. Subsequently UK passport holders were made to wait for the e-gates for another half hour, while eu passport holders were prioritised (for the same flights). I have visited Gran Canaria some 20 times in 14 years and never seen chaos like this. And frankly would make me carefully consider whether I return

We arrived early for our flight. The queue formed and we stood for a long time. A lady came over and said our whole queue should move across. Apparently other people had been checking in to our flight at another desk for a long time. Our queue was very slow. It seemed the staff did not care.
Worst airport ever! Queued for absolutely ages upon arrival despite security gates being available. Staff were useless and lazy. Absolute joke of a place!

Arrival was easy and bags arrived quickly, waived through health control and landside within 20 - 25 minutes, departing again no issues although the airport was busy with the evening departures there was plenty of security checkpoints open and plenty of staff, each employee at the airport I encountered was helpful and friendly, once through security there is a excellent Duty Free and several restaurants/bars along with a small selection of shops.

After reading several negative reviews on this page regarding LPA Gran Canaria airport I wish to make a defence. I find the airport similar to many of the Spanish airports operated by Aena in that it handles the volume of passengers proportionately and professionally. Bear in mind the vast majority of passengers passing through the airport are there for leisure purposes, this has always been a difficult balancing act to please the foot traffic. Knowledge and pre-planning are the key to success. Informative information can be found online about the airport, for example https://gran-canaria-airport.com/ is just one example. Especially in this day and age with covid and the uncertainly about travel with changing restrictions, it is paramount that planning ahead to provide a heads up of potential problems and issues is a must.

This is the first time I have ever travelled through Gran Canaria airport and I must say it’s a pathetic excuse for a departure lounge. They are renovating the departure lounge but I am concentrating on the area already renovated. They have no idea what good service is, if they think waiting 40 minutes to be seen in O’learys Or 30 minutes in Burger King is what travellers expect then they must live on cloud cuckoo land. They have made some nice restaurants in the refurbished area, but tended to plan in adequate seating. Really, the airport is a prime reason to never visit the Island, which we won’t be.

What appalling service! Jet2 had everything sorted, boarding was on time, but the airport had other ideas, 30 minutes wait to provide a bus to the plane, and frankly we could have walked a lot faster, then further delays while that bus emptied and returned as there only appeared to be one! They they had the cheek to tell our pilot that as they had made us miss our slot they were pushing our flight time back by over two hours! After a great deal of complaining we were told we might be able to go sooner, but currently are still sat on the aeroplane with no signs of any movement. We always go to Tenerife and this was a change, the hotel was lovely, we said we would return but now I’m not sure. Lots of other poor reviews on here about the airport, Gran Canaria you need to do better. Not to mention that you probably cost the airline many thousands with your lack of buses/drivers and we are still in danger of losing our crew if they go over time. Try harder please if you want tourists to visit you! Nowhere to sit either, not nearly enough seating, and what was there was dirty! Plus way more expensive than Tenerife airport so you lost my custom there too! WiFi didn’t work either.

What can I say that hasn't been said already. All in all its a poor airport from start to finish. From lack of service in food halls, excessive waiting times. It simply causes unnecessary stress. It also misplaced my boarding card and passport whilst going through security. Gran Canaria was ok but I'll never visit again purely based on the departure experience.

Our experience at the Granada airport was absolutely horrible. I am not sure if it was the airline (Iberia) or if it was because of the small size, but the service of all of the workers were completely useless, rude, and incompetent. Judging by the service, I’m assuming that Iberia gives no customer service training. First of all, one of us did not have a valid confirmation number although the payment went through and received a confirmation email. Afterwards, the attendant just sent us to a phone number which was hold and never answered. So we had to go to the Spanish number, but no one would help us to book a ticket or even help us call the phone. When we went to the service kiosk area, they left saying they had to catch the flight that we actually needed to go on. In fact, the flight we needed to book was not available online so we absolutely needed help from someone at the airport, but did not receive help until we talked to them multiple times. When we finally received help, the woman was rude and saying snide comments and only was able to help 15 minutes before. This was an absolutely horrid experience particularly for a very stressful event. We are very upset with the airline, but also at the airport for being rude and making it a more stressful situation (especially when it was not that hard of situation to fix). I hope for the future that this airport will improve vastly in order to be any form of actual competence. Thank god we had a native Spanish speaker within our group, if we didn’t we would have missed our flight and have to rebook for almost 4 times the price.

We got to the airport 40 minutes before the scheduled departure time. Despite this, we were not allowed to check in our luggage in the plane because it was too late, even though the plane was no more than 300 yards away from where we were. Instead of trying to help us, they just ignored us and left us stranded in the airport. Because of this, we had to pay a $650 rescue fee in order to be rescheduled in the next morning's flight and not missing our connection on the next day. I have never seen that lack of willingness to help travellers. From now on, even though my final destination is Granada, I will be travelling to Malaga or Sevilla airport. People make a difference.

Really lovely, small but clean airport. Passport Control was really smiley and friendly and our bags were ready on the cute luggage belt by the time we were through which was quick albeit from a small BA Embraer jet. Toilets were absolutely spotless!

Arrived on the last evening flight from Barcelona tourist desk very helpful and received our luggage within 20 minutes. No taxis available so took the airport bus driver was very helpful and even dropped us a short distance from our hotel.

A very easy airport to use. Arriving on an evening Ryanair flight deplaning was quick passport control almost friendly and the airport bus was immediately outside to speed us to town for only 3€. Return was just as easy the security staff were friendly plenty of seating in both the main airport and the gate area. No WIFI but one rarely gets everything.

GRX is fairly spacious for a regional airport. Very clean marble interior with plenty of seats landside to use without having to buy anything (are you listening UK airports?) and even though it has only one cafe/restaurant - the food is usually great value edible and affordable (lots of tapas dishes too). Long/short stay parking amazingly cheap. Airbus service to city is aways available and there always seem to be plenty of taxis waiting outside. Very friendly security staff too. A good alternative to using Malaga airport.

GRX is a small regional airport. Boarding and disembarking aircraft is usually very quick due to the limited aircraft movements. Passenger facilities are limited waiting areas are small no lounges minimal eating outlets and taxi's are hard to come by (which is surprising for an airport). However some of the nicest security screening staff that I have ever come across always smiling and patient with passengers (UK and US staff can really learn something here!).

It is also worth pointing out that there are no shops beyond the security check at Granada airport. There is only a vending machine which sells water but which is regularly out of order. I suggest you eat well before arriving and buy any duty frees elsewhere. Like Málaga which is far better prepared for this kind of tourist traffic.

Granada Airport is located about 15km west of Granada. Single runway small terminal. Regular buses run into the city. If you arrive late no worries as it is only a short taxi ride. In recent years the number of flights have increased. Mainly to Madrid and Barcelona but with also Liverpool Stansted Melilla. The usual facilities for a small airport so don't expect too much.

Convenient place to fly out of if they ever maintained their flight schedules. My past three flight out of this airport have been cancelled. When I ask why they make an excuse of weather, but it’s not delayed the flight is flat out cancelled. While all the other airports in the near area are fine DSW, MDW, O'Hare. Complete waste of time, no apologies, no alternative provided than roll the dice and come back tomorrow. Airlines used to work to get you out that day or even provide alternate airline solutions. You either rebook on an app, wait on a phone for 2+ hours, or get sent on your way at the counter. Word of advice if you actually want to get somewhere on the original day intended drive to Chicago or Detroit.

Flown into this airport 5 times in the last 2 months, always a issue getting a arrival gate, getting the ground crew to show up and then getting your luggage under 40 minutes after arrival. A joke for this size airport! Management should be embarrassed!! Time for some changes.

Very clean and well taken care of. This airport is served by so many great airlines with diverse destinations. I do think that GRR needs more international routes. At GRR, the airport is not too big so it makes efficient travel. Also, they have a good selection of shops and stores. The airport facility looks really modern and cool for being over 55 years old. The only cons is that sometimes it can get a bit crowded and the staff doesn’t manage high groups of passengers well. Would give an 8.5 if I could.
The worst baggage claim ever. No signs to tell you where to go, what claim you need to use. Crowds just stand around and wait and bags to over an hour to come out. Worst ever.

Terrible management of remodelling and on-property shuttles. I've traveled through numerous airports small to large some under construction, others remodelled. The remodelling of GRR's interior is taking years and is painful to navigate and claim luggage there are 2 carousels for all the airlines and flights. Further, there is no room for all the passengers who have no clue where one's bags are coming. With regard to the parking shuttle - there was too little capacity. As I knew there were more people waiting for the shuttle than its capacity; I started walking to the economy lot. I made it before the shuttle (which I only saw arriving in the lot as I was leaving! The people are nice though.

August 2019 was my first time using this airport and I will never use it again. Security staff is hands down the worst I have ever had the displeasure of dealing with. The most misserable people I have ever met in my life with a goal of ruining your day. I will never use this airport again just because of them. Huge inflated egos with a badge. Avoid this place at all costs, trust me.

I fly weekly for work, and Gerald R. Ford Int'l Airport in Grand Rapids is one of my two home-base airports. It's served by American, Delta, United, Southwest and Allegiant, and has non-stop flights to twenty-something destinations. I primarily fly American, and mostly take flights that connect through Chicago O'Hare or Dallas/Fort Worth. GRR is a larger regional airport, with two concourses of 8 gates each, but not a large airport by any means. I can park in the garage, walk in, clear security (TSA Pre-Check) and walk to my gate within 15 minutes of driving into the garage. I love that kind of convenience. Employees are friendly and helpful pretty much across the board -- at the airline counters, security and at the gates. GRR recently finished a fairly large renovation, in late 2017. They now have one central security checkpoint, and a central area with new shopping and dining, including a local brewpub, Starbucks and a Michigan-themed souvenir shop, There are also new lounge areas, children's play area and a business center, not to mention new, large restrooms. In general, GRR operates on time, which is key for me. Most delays I've experienced have come from aircraft delayed at their originating airport - mostly O'Hare. I'm basically comfortable relying on this airport for my weekly business travel needs.
Great little airport all staff friendly and helpful. Security checks speedy and done with a smile. Could some of the staff be used to show other airports how it is done.

Friendly little airport which stinks of burned toast from a bagel vendor. They really ought to get the vendor to install a ventilator hood. The faux jazz piped in everywhere is also a poor choice. The CNN monitors are loud but not as bad as some. I've been here a while because of the lousy service and rigid rules of Delta Airlines so this is a well-considered review.

Living in South Florida and used to departing from and connecting through massive airports GRR was a breeze. Now the new parking-building is fully functional (and beautiful it is all in a natural colour of brown). The check-in area it-self is nothing to admire and very basic. Than you walk-up to a short-ramp and there you are: Steps away from all the terminals. This area does have a small food-courts with the basic pizza/burger fare. It also has floor-to-ceiling windows bringing in plenty of natural light. GRR had a major problem: its airfare were outrageously expensive: even the discounted ones. However after low-cost Allegiant started servicing Grand Rapids tickets prices dropped dramatically - even last- minute ones! This can only bring more business to West Michigan.

Graz is lovely small airport. From our hotel in town centre it took 30 mins to get airside at the gate, including taxi ride, check-in and security, doesn't get better than that. Friendly staff, a quick service, nice glass walls to view planes, runaway etc from each gate. Cafe, duty free, wi-fi access and not crowded. I guess not a huge selection of destinations to fly to from here is the down side. Overall, a great airport experience!

Graz is an excellent small airport which has expanded in the last few years and now sees scheduled flights to as far as Luxor as well as German and Austrian destinations plus the UK with Ryanair. They have the best answer yet seen to long security queues: they immediately open another scanner: when the queues build up again yet another - sometyhing some of the bigger airports would do well to emulate. A good restaurant is available although once passing through security snacks and drinks are all that is available. They also prove that Priority Boarding can work with buses being used with Priority Boarding passengers be directed to one bus which goes to the aircraft first. Only when those people have boarded do any other buses leave for the plane. The train service has improved greatly over the last couple of years (although still sparse on Sundays) with at least an hourly service into Graz. Staff always seem to be very friendly as well based on around a dozen trips through there in the last two years.

GRZ is a small but efficient and welcoming airport served from the UK by RYR. Arrival was quick and departure pleasant made more so by an excellent meal in the upstairs landside restaurant. Nice views from there and further upstairs - and unusually these days - is a waving area. One thing lets the facility down a little. There is a nearby station but train times are incidental - no real connections - and we thought the station was badly signposted; ditto coming back where you just had to guess where the walking route was.

Had an ok trip using Binghamton Regional Airport - flew from Binghamton to Las Vegas with one layover in Philadelphia. The morning started off rough with a half hour delay to Philadelphia and when we did finally board the plane the grounds crew had to de-ice the aircrafts wings taking another 45 minutes (this is the one April when it was very cold). Had a rough flight to Philadelphia on a Dhc turboprop however the flight attendant was kind enough to announce all departures in the next 30 minutes (of course Las Vegas being one of them) and asked if the passengers would let the people with earliest departures to be let off first. By the time we got off the plane and into the main terminal there was only 20 minutes left and we had to make it to terminal c from terminal f which is a long hike. We were told that we would be better off not taking the bus over to the other terminal so my family of four 2 being young children had to run halfway across the airport. Making it to the terminal in a half hour we were sure we missed our flight however my business company planned the flight and notified the staff that passengers would be arriving late and they held the plane for us. The plane to Las Vegas was a 757 and it is particularly long and of course our seats were in the back so we had all eyes on us as we walked to the back. The flight to Las Vegas was quick and we are very happy with us airways but not with Philadelphia or Binghamton airports as Philadelphia is not easy to transfer terminals and the half hour delay in Binghamton could have been used to de-ice the plane saving time.

This is my home airport. Upon arrival I was pleasantly surprised. I had the entire security checkpoint to myself no other passengers ! This was incredibly lucky on my part. There are no VIP or First class lounges here. Rochester is a place people arrive at or depart from there are virtually no layovers here. This is not an overly busy airport. Taxi times are short and the runway never gets stacked up. I heartily endorse the Red Osier's Prime Rib Sandwiches shop airside too. The only drawback in my opinion is a dearth of ground transportation options taxi rent a car or RTS bus. RTS busses don't run very often and travel through one of the worst neighborhoods in the city on their way downtown.

Small regional airport. With just two terminals it is pretty painless to navigate. Lines at the security checkpoint move fast. I was told that a contractor operates the checkpoints. In my experience staff was friendly and two or more lanes were open. Some restrooms in the secure area were closed off due to renovations in progress. Concessions were limited but there is a McDonald's a Subway a news store and a coffee outfit. Because it's a regional airport many code share flights are operated by smaller airlines flying commuter aircraft. If you're not a fan of turboprop aircraft avoid Piedmont Air operating as US Air Express on DHC 8 planes.

This is a small yet spacious airport, with two terminal piers jutting out in a Y shape. There were ample seating space, plug points to charge your phones, and also an enclosed section with desks and chairs to do any work on your computer. Large glass windows afforded views of the runways and let sunlight stream in. Bathrooms clean. TSA security was thorough. Check in counters are opened a couple of hours before a flight and I found the staff friendly. Car rental booths are in the baggage conveyor belt section and long term parking is just outside the terminal as are the parking lots for rental cars - minimal walking required. Very easy and fast entry and exit into/out of terminal. Driving directions to airport were clearly marked. Only a couple of shops/stores for food and drinks. A selection of Wisconsin beer was available in the restaurant but not my favorite, Leinenkugel! Overall, a very pleasant airport.

It was my first time at this small and beautiful airport. Very well-maintained and nicely decorated airport. The downtown and hotel areas are not too far. Staffs were friendly. Outside of the airport is also environment friendly and green.
Worst ever! TSA took 35 minutes to get trough, such a small airport, TSA workers just standing around, talking and laughing, that's what we pay for? Shame on TSA at Greenville GSP.

It was my first time flying with 2 rambunctious toddlers. One of my granddaughters had her own seat, the youngest would be on my lap. Long story short, l forgot to obtain a boarding pass for the 23 month old and was unable to get through the busy security checkpoint. TSA agent saw my distress, and stepped in with a wheelchair ride for the girls and escorted me back to ticketing. Had it not been for this agent I would have missed my flight. I cannot thank her enough.
Little and very nice airport. Clean, well organized with helpful staff. The way it should be. All in all a good arrival and starting point for any trip.

I fly weekly for business, and flew in and out of Greenville-Spartanburg for the last quarter of 2016 and a bit of 2017. It's a small airport, with only one runway, and one long concourse with arbitrary "A" and "B" separation. The major airlines serve GSP, but flights are limited. I mostly flew on American, which only seems to connect via Charlotte - an 80 mile flight. First - being so close to a major hub like CLT caused almost weekly delays, as my flight was often held on the tarmac by CLT air-traffic control, so we could fit into the traffic pattern. I never actually missed my connections in Charlotte, but did have several walk-jogs across the airport to reach my gate while the final groups were boarding. But, GSP itself is nicely maintained, with super-friendly staff. They offered TSA PreCheck when I flew in and out. I got to know the Avis rental-car staff by name, and they'd give me free upgrades. Best of all, if you use GSP, you have to order a tuna melt from the snack counter on the lower level, outside security. They mix the tuna salad from scratch in front of you, and make the best-tasting tuna melt I've ever eaten.

Greenville-Spartanburg (GSP) is a regional airport in northwestern South Carolina. It gets its "international" name from its customs clearance facility for air freight to serve the 175 foreign companies with operations in the region, it has no international passenger flight (although its 11,000 foot runway could handle them). Greenville, SC has become one of the most dynamic small cities in the US and the airport is finally upgrading to reflect this change of status. Immediate inconvenience comes from a major construction project to upgrade facilities. Boarding areas are comfortable even though services are fairly basic. Baggage claim is very convenient. Outside pick-up and drop-off areas are being improved but can be somewhat cramped at present. The biggest limitation is security, which is totally inadequate during construction and features no TSA Pre-Check.

This is not the worst airport I've seen in my life (and I have seen many). It's your worst nightmare coming true! When we landed (on time) we'd to wait 50 minutes for parking slot. But that was just a beginning. Next Saturday people were waiting in hour+ queques to luggage/check-in desks. Moreover, there is just ONE desk for skis!!! OFC with separate, another 1h long queque. In the airport for skiers! Complete chaos, check-ins and security control still in progress for passengers that were supposed to fly home more than 1h ago. Add absolutely amateur/lame (but friendly) personnel, endless boarding pass/ID controls (stopped counting after 5th, Israelis could really learn from them!) and 2 or 3 toilets for entire airport for complete picture. Never again experience, avoid at ALL COSTS! Fly to Lyon or Geneva, additional time to get to the resorts is definitely cheaper than loss of mental health in this pitiful place.

Absolutely horrendous from start to finish. Delays I can handle and are not the airports problem generally however the chaos on check in and baggage drop etc was unfathomable. Tannoy announcements telling travellers to be at gate now when everyone is standing in a check in queue was not great neither: oversized baggage needs a separate system, not an aisle in the middle of all the check in aisles. Horrendous experience however I feel that things will it change. Cheese in duty free was good hence the 1 score.

Hundreds of people shut outside the airport in the freezing cold, not allowed to enter due to overcrowding. Inside it is everyone for themselves - people everywhere, chaos at check in desks. Baggage belts not working, staff scrambling over desks. Out on the runway, passengers walking all over the place, no concerns for security or safety by staff. Horrendous experience. The time you might save by flying here compared to Geneva is not enough to warrant setting foot in this airport. Don’t do it.

This airport is the most disorganised of any that I have flown from. Some small investments in barriers to organise passengers at check in could make a massive difference. There is a general lack of guidance by the supervisors to transit passengers through the airport. Whilst the transfer to Geneva is an hour longer if you are going to experience close to a 90 minute delay I would say it’s a better investment of time. Rather disappointing given the proximity to the ski resorts

I hate this airport with all my heart and am never coming here again. If you are smart then never come to this airport because you will be highly disappointed in the incompetence of the ability of the airport. Do the right thing and never come to this airport. Never come to Grenoble.

My travel through Grenoble airport operated by Vinci was the worst experience in all my many years of travelling. Having checked the reviews after using Grenoble, as a route to the Alps in February 2024, I see it continues to get the same bad reviews as six years ago. I suspect injuries would be highly likely in an emergency situation, due to overcrowding. We were standing for more than 3 hours to get through security. Vinci have to have passengers standing because otherwise they would have spend money to more than double the size of the departure terminal. There is literally not enough floor space to allow passengers to sit down for the 30+ flights they schedule through the airport on Saturdays.

Astoundingly incompetently run airport - seriously too many passengers for this small airport to cope with - literally teetering on the edge of falling apart if one more thing goes wrong or a couple of staff go sick. No info. on booking in screens (why not, should be an easy fix), so they have extra staff to try and organise this section (45 minute wait). Long queues to Departure Lounge (200-300 people !), where again, they employ extra staff to pull out passengers in danger of missing their flight as they spend so much time queueing! (1 1/4 hour wait) Long queues to get through X-ray security (20 minute wait - insufficient staff/machines), all this leads to no time in the departure lounge/duty free before you are again moved through to the gate - where you are packed in tight ! - and where there is yet another 20-30 minute delay!

The worst airport ever! I had to fly from Grenoble Airport because my flight from Lyon Airport was cancelled and this was the only option available going back to Gatwick at the same date, due to French workers strike action! I carried snow chains for my car, because I drove in the French Alps at high above 2000m, where according to French government you have to have winter tires or snow chains for your car! I carried my snow chains because the rental car company didn't provide winter tires and the snow chains for 10 days was £100 extra. I took my own snow chains, I had no problem taking them in my hand bag from Gatwick, going through Lyon Airport arriving in France. Neither UK border on departure nor British Airways had any problems with me carrying them in my hand luggage because they are only 2.5kg weight and fit into my back pack. However, upon departure from Grenoble, very rude lady at security check confiscated the snow chains with the argument that she doesn't allow these on board, also she stated that Grenoble airport doesn't allow snow chains too. When I asked to show me proof where this was stated and I showed my previous tickets that I flew with them in my back pack, she said if I don't sign the paper that they are confiscating the chains, I will not fly, she took my passport and my phone with my boarding pass! When I asked for her batch number and name and her supervisor too, so I can complain, I was refused the information!
The absolute worst airport in history. So poorly run. Any other airport I have travelled through is better by a huge margin. Any of the other local airports are OK, just avoid Grenoble.

Queue from getting off plane through immigration (without toilet facilities or refreshments) took at least 2 hours. This was longer than the flight time, was very uncomfortable, and nearly caused the cancellation of a v expensive transfer. In short, an appalling disgrace. We will never fly through this airport again.

Nice little country airport with well cared-for gardens. Interestingly busy place with Regional Express flights dominating. Check-in rather odd with no check-in allowed until 45 minutes before departure. No wonder less-frequent flyers get confused when faced with check-in for other airlines and airports closing 30 minutes before departrue (eg Jetstar) and here we have an airport not allowing any check-in at all until 45 minutes before departure. Makes for an interesting rush of people. Pleasant terminal spoilt by a television blaring away in one corner making it difficult to get some work done. Good car rental facilities but beware on driving out of Griffith Airport around dusk watch for big kangaroos in abundance on the airport access road.

This is the only airport that I have come across that does not allow bicycle helmets though security. I got turned back from security because of my bicycle helmet, a large crowd gathered to try and help me but the security people had a piece of paper saying no motorcycle helmets, and had never seen a bicycle helmet before. I am going to actively try and get this changed as checking my bicycle helmet is not an option for me. This airport does not seem to take feedback. This airport does not seem to want to improve their service.
Not friendly or helpful at the front desk and unorganized. They were not helpful when the Volaris airline cancelled our flight and pretty much told us to deal with it on our own.

I hope to never have to arrive or depart from this airport. The staff is beyond rude! It seems as if they were corrupted as well. They send you to the military people to get checked and they charge you extra money. If you ask questions they lead you wrong on purpose. Not one outlet is available, there was puddles of water in various places, gates are far, and the whole place is over packed.

The staff at this airport are always in a bad mood to begin with. When it comes to doing their job as informative employees, they failed immensely. I was ignored multiple times when asking where to find a fill out form. The employees there treat people so badly. My mother flew in from LAX 20 minutes after I did and was yelled at for not knowing what form to fill out on the way out. It was her first time traveling and my sister had just passed. Instead of being treated with kindness and helpfulness she was yelled at. These employees are always rude, unhelpful, and honestly don’t know how to do their job. Please enforce a training for better customer service or hire people that know how to treat people with respect. I would rate a 0/10 but unfortunately I cannot.

They had us waiting in a huge line while our flight time dwindled away. We got out of line at 8.30, pretty much missing the flight if we didn't sprint to the terminal. Worst airport for sure and I travel a lot.

I went through security and explained I had a disability and I needed to go through the priority lane. The lady refused to allow me access. As such, I had a major meltdown and anxiety attack at security. Shame on your staff

At Guadalajara airport the main hallway is completely renovated, but its still very crowded during morning hours as this is the busiest time and lines can be long. Staff are helpful and friendly. There are 4 or 5 VIP lounges - I have used the Aeromexico Salon Premier which is brand new and the Banamex-Citi Salon Beyond, which is the best for me. Many restaurants, many stores and duty free.

Overall I find Guadalajara Airport to be quite user friendly with helpful staff, a decent variety of restaurants, cafes, and shops. Security lines are usually efficient and quick. Terminals clean and plenty of seating space. Several airline lounges and affordable ground transportation options to the city center and nearby areas. One of the easiest Mexican airports to navigate.

GDL - seems to have completed the main phase of its cosmetic renovations but still lacks some of the structural improvements to provide more spacious check-in counters space in the waiting lounge and more jet bridges. Latest development witnessed many international flights still on the tarmac awaiting pax to arrive via caterpillar-like buses. Simply unacceptable for Mexico's second largest city and third most enplaned airport in the country.

Guadalajara Airport main terminal is quite modern however the check in area seems slightly small for the amount of passengers and airlines. Check-in queues were not very good. We waited just under 1 hour to get through the queue for a Delta flight to Atlanta. There were about 3 or 4 desks open and only one MD-80 flight being checked in so it seems as though the service is very inefficient. Security queues were also very long as well. The airport seems to be in urgent need for more contact gates as our plane was on a remote stand and so were many other planes. The car park was appalling- it's obviously far too small and queues to leave were very long and time consuming.
