You also pay when you get to the end of the queue therefore you end up paying for the 30 minutes + that you spend in the queue. Overall Guadalajara airport needs to be expanded quickly!

Wonderful experience, they saved me from missing my flight. I was traveling with my family in China and this airport was my second transit trough this country. My first encounter was with Chongqing airport which was significantly worse because my flight was unexpectedly cancelled and they just barely managed to book another one. I still had a little time but I was worried if I could make it in time. With just 45 minutes left I rushed to find my check in and when this amazing staff found out how little time I had they literally enscorted me and my family to my gate. They were communicating with walkie talkies so we were being preferred throughout the way to catch our flight. The most pleasant staff ever, I will be forever thankful.

Travellers beware. There is not a lot to do at this airport. Security staff are unpleasant as are the staff who inspect your boarding pass and check your passport. Despite being on transit, they check your boarding pass and then stamp it. Security is a standard screen. There are just a few shops and no place to buy water or drinks after immigration ie in the transit area. There are two or three restaurants selling Chinese food where none of the staff speak English and communication is hard but they do try to help you. There is one coffee place and a Starbucks far away near A gate. Wifi is patchy and you have to register your passport on a machine before you can access wifi. Thankfully they do have water dispensers around the airport. If you're in transit here, bring food and a good book and make sure you download movies on your device and be prepared to be bored.
Worst service I have ever encountered in an airport, talked to me like I’m a criminal when I have done nothing wrong. For an international airport in a supposedly tier 1 city, totally unacceptable!

If you are Chinese this airport is adequate. Any other nationality, forget it. Ridiculous necessity to scan a health declaration form, the majority of this form is in Chinese. Also when entering a new country its unlikely people have internet on their phone to do so. The few assistants available only speak Chinese. A lot of the free WiFi stations do not work, the ones that do work have very confusing instructions. Will never fly through China again.
It is clean, modern and spacious. There are many restaurants and shops. Passengers would not be bored during the waiting time. Employees are friendly and helpful. Signposts are clear.

Guangzhou Baiyun Airport is the most impressive airport for me. The ground staff of China Southern Airlines are very warm and have a good attitude. This aspect is much better than many domestic airports! Since I booked the hotel next to the boarding gate, I needed to get the ticket to pass the security check and customs one day in advance. The staff of China Southern Airlines helped me to coordinate with the customs and security check departments, and finally I checked into the airport transfer hotel successfully.

This airport is great. It has all the necessities that an airport should have. I don’t get how it is placed 39 in the world. It should be a top 20 airport. All the staff are very helpful and friendly.

I have used both terminals recently and compared to some other airports in Asia and China this is overall a much better airport. That being said, I don't agree with some of the reviews here and I definitely don't mind to be at this airport. This airport can easily be reached by subway. And even for a 45-minute ride, to the city the cost is only $1. The waiting area at the gate is spacious with enough seats provided, some areas at the new terminal even have massage chairs free of charge. You do need to have a Wechat account though to make use of this free service. Toilets are clean and you won't have issues finding one. Immigration procedure never took me more than 10 minutes, arriving or departing. This cannot be said about some other airports in China. The other good thing when flying with China Southern Airlines is the quick check-in procedure. It never took me more than 10 minutes. So if there are reviews here for long queues at the check-in counters, it is most likely due to the lack of staff of that particular airline. For instance, don't expect a quick check-in when flying with AirAsia. The only 2 minor things of this airport are the security staff and lack of western food options. Security staff can be really intimidating, rude and superior. They don't speak English (well) and they don't have the need to explain something. If they cannot read the specs on your power bank they will confiscate it without explanation. They expect you to speak Chinese and not the other way around (so much for an international airport). However, if these are the only cons I won't hesitate making use of this airport.

Guangzhou airport is not very big. Overall, this is a very clean airport and relatively modern. There is a clear lack of English signage. The shops are not very varied and there are not many food options. In short, if you transit in the morning, don’t expect anything European like for your breakfast. One thing to add: our gate was located in a zone near the smoking area, we were travelling with children and had to to wait there for more than an hour with the cigarette smoke.

Flying from LHR to BKK. Went through additional security check-point smoothly. No big queues. New, clean and pleasant terminal. All information were given very clear. Hope to have such terminals more often in Europe. Glad to be here again.

Modelo in the airport is a scam - do not have food or drink there. We were charged over Q54000 for one glass of wine and one double Rum. The waiter was not overt in providing the price for the wine and charged Q20000 for ONE glass of house white wine. I checked and the bottle is a Q15000 bottle of standard wine. They also added 20% tip without consent and when absolutely not deserved - we had to wait about 10 minutes to get the bill after asking. It is daylight robbery.

Do not visit the Pizza Hut inside the Airport. Horrible service. Staff were rude and do not know what customer service is. I bought a coffee and then asked if I could get some milk or cream and they said that because I did not order a coffee with cream originally that I would need to purchase a new one! Doesn’t make sense. Travelers are tired and don’t need to deal with rude people. That reflects on the airport too.
One of the least efficient airports ever. Security check is a joke, everywhere you have to wait for hours. We almost missed our plane as arriving 2.5 hours before departure wasn't enough.

Small airport with few services. Long enough customs procedures and passport control if you land late in the evening, when there is little staff on duty. However, it offers a good free wifi service, also available outside the airside

Full body scanner was implemented and opting out for an alternative search is not an option. I fully dislike being exposed to technology from which we have no real idea of the consequences, especially since I was not aware of these kind of controls taking place.

15 mins WIFI free, then you have to buy. Wow 3rd world country indeed. Gate waiting chairs / benches are hard as rock. Have the seat dividers so you can't lay down. Loud Speaker announcements are totally not-understandable. Duty free is delivered on gangway, not given to you when you purchase. Was impressed to see food venues open early early AM (4:00). Selections in Duty Free fairly limited. Other mostly touristy knick-knack so so.

I was interested to read a couple of other reviews of Guatemala airport mentioning that random items had been confiscated at security, as this was also my experience and it marred an otherwise positive impression. After X-ray scanning, a guard asked to search my bag and I cooperated fully. He pulled out my small nail file and a pair of safety scissors with 2cm round-ended blades, and confiscated both items. He then added insult to injury by smiling and saying, "Is OK?" as he dropped them through the slot. I'm an experienced traveller and both of the items that were taken had been through numerous other security checks on many previous occasions, including in countries with reputations for being especially strict. The episode left me and my partner feeling irritated and grumpy, as it was so unnecessary. I would never have any problem at all with established security rules being enforced, but La Aurora should ensure that individual officers aren't confiscating people's belongings on the basis of arbitrary and unfounded personal decisions.

This is the only airport where I encountered street vendors positioning themselves outside the terminal building hustling passengers with trinkets and snacks. Departure from this airport was far from trouble free. There were numerous passport checks along the way: at the entrance to the terminal, at check in (naturally), prior to entering the departure hall, at passport control (naturally), at security check, and on my way to the departure gate, I was stopped by a policeman who demanded to see my passport. He ran his fingers over the pages of my passport and then asked how much money I had. This unusual request unnerved me so I asked him why he needed to know how much money I had with me. He relented and returned the passport to me. Then at the departure gate, a further passport check and the emptying of all hand luggage for a thorough check including the lining of the case. I was glad to leave the airport.
It's not a big airport, but clean and good. However, there is not much signage.

The airport itself is nice as others have commented. I travel through here about once a month and the new terminal is very comfortable and pleasant. However the local security is capricious at best. They seem to give security agents very little guidance but a huge amount of leeway. I have had toothpaste confiscated (no pastes they said) a bar of soap (no soaps they said) and the list goes on and on. I am all for reasonable and tight security but it seems like every trip I have a random item confiscated. And it is not just me I see it happen to others all the time too.

I approached a clerk at boarding gate 8 to confirm my gate number since it was missing from my boarding pass. Why it was not noted on my pass is another concern of mine. How is anyone supposedly to know where to board? The clerk knew which gate I was supposed to go to but when I asked she just kept staring at her screen. There were two attendants there but the other was helping another passenger. I even waited about 2 minutes for her to respond. I asked her again and she just ignored me. My wife then caught up and had to literally tap her screen to get her attention. And then with an angry attitude she answered our question. All she had to do was politely ask me to wait until she had a moment to help. This attitude with staff at this airport is common. I am writing this so you can at least try and improve your quality of service. The passengers are paying customers we desserv be treated with respect and dignity.

Guayaquil airport is one of the best around. The building is modern, very functional and easy. The staff who work there always are profesional, and the most important thing is that you always has a feeling of been safe.

We took a TAME flight to Baltra Galápagos. Check-in was very easy with very short queues and very clear instructions given how to get to your gate. For the Galápagos Islands you are required to go through a host of quarantine checks and you are required to pay US$20 per person to receive a certificate. Without such a certicate you will be unable to board nor will you be allowed past the passport control at Baltra. The airport terminal is very organised and gates are well spaced. Great airport. Also when arriving in Baltra, you are required to pay an additional entry fee of US$100.

I was surprised with the cleanliness and efficiency of the airport in Guayaquil. Really modern and easy to navigate. I liked the zen garden at the domestic arrivals which really was a nice touch. Toilets were clean. Passport control very organised and staff are polite, also duty free staff were very helpful. Nice WiFi and view of the runway watching planes goes by. Happy using it.

Everything was great and professional from the moment we arrived. There were two other flights at immigration, one from Europe the other from Buenos Aires and immigration lines was moving fast. When we got there the officer was very friendly and welcoming, she even wished us to enjoy her country, that was very nice. Airport is very modern, has all the amenities to pass by time really fast, free WIFI is available plus charge stations.

Guayaquil Airport is modern and clean but if you arrive on a domestic flight there is no transit. You need to go out and do check-in and security. Arrivals can be crowded and staff are not that friendly. The one smile that I got was from the girl selling chocolates at the store inside.

I've flown through this airport several times this year, and generally consider it a fairly basic, simple no-frills experience. It's close to the business areas of Guayaquil, and normally transit through migration, security, etc is quick and painless. Not however, yesterday, 30/9/2016: the queue for the exit control and security snaked halfway down the terminal building. Even allowing 2 hours to pass the controls was not enough time to reach my gate before the plane left. This is utterly unacceptable, the management company needs to get its act together and provide efficient passenger handling.
Good airport, nice shops and the seating is comfortable, great restaurants, very respectful staff, and flights always on time.

Guayaquil's airport has most of the services that we have here in Australia they even offer jetways into planes. There are restaurants ATM's machines banks coffee shops and entertainment it passed our expectations without doubt.
Friendly of the staff a new huge mall had been opening Mall del Soll. This is the modern and fully functional airport with the biggest mall of the country and four hotels between 4 & 5 stars.

This airport is small. Very small. Arrivals is small and cramped. Departures is similarly small and cramped. Departures is dominated by a way overpriced duty free shop at one end and at the other is a small eatery. In between is a small seating area and toilets. I had planned on arriving at the airport a couple of hours before my flight and am glad I didn't because there is literally nothing to do. So if you are using this airport my advice is to arrive with just enough time to check in and avoid the duty free shop.

I am a resident of Alderney and use Guernsey airport on a regular basis. The customer service provided by G4S (security staff) is non existent. Every opportunity to make your journey swift and courteous whilst carrying out these very important duties seemed totally irrelevant to the staff on duty today (20/01/22). I was travelling with my mother in law who was in a wheelchair after having surgery. The amount of undressing and unpacking of hand baggage was totally unacceptable. After extra body searches with an ever increasing queue of people I retrieved our belongings and started to re pack and get dressed. Unfortunately my mother in law had left some small liquid bottles in her bag. Understandably the items had to be checked. I apologised but was met with a stern look and rather than rescanning the bag had it completely emptied and re searched. I was not alone. This was happening to many others. 2 flights were departing at the same time in an otherwise empty airport. There was no urgency or friendliness. Someone near me said that they felt very intimidated and like they were in Russia! Whilst I have no problem with tight security checks I do have a problem with the lack of customer service. This is a consistent problem whilst leaving Guernsey. I dread going through every time. Why is it such a problem. You’re innocent until proven guilty unless travelling through Guernsey airport! In my opinion the worst experience of anywhere that I have travelled through. I am retired BA cabin crew. In this review I put “no, I wouldn’t recommend this airport” but that’s such a shame because service throughout the Island is fantastic and no way reflects the island of Guernsey.

Flown Aurigny to Guernsey four or five times from Gatwick. Of course, a visitor to Guernsey has no choice...the airline has a monopoly. The flights themselves were only an hour, and uneventful. Aurigny flight team is usually OK. Not rude, but not terribly friendly, either. My last trip, the Guernsey airport staff was a very bad dream. They treated me like a suspected terrorist (I'm a past-middle-aged solo female traveler). Kept me until the plane was completely boarded...I was the last one allowed on board. They opened my suitcase and removed every single item. They turned my book upside down and flipped the pages...looking for who knows what. I fully expected sniffer dogs at some point. Since the trip itself had been stressful (horrendous weather, hotel room robbed), this last insult was so upsetting! I was finally allowed on the plane, but fighting tears. The flight attendant was nasty and gave me a "look" for holding everyone up.

What a very unpleasant end to a lovely stay. I went to the cafe upstairs, asked for a prawn salad, 'we no do them madam', but there's a picture of them in the ladies' toilet, I replied, 'no madam', I asked if they did them in the cafe on the other side, 'we no do them here madam', but there is a picture, 'we no do salad', I did go back into the ladies toilet and took a picture of the advertisement just to convice myself I wasn't going mad! I travelled with hand luggage and had been searched on the way out, my small deodorant and small tube of E45 cream were in a plastic bag on show. However there was a problem so everything had to come out, being of a certain age I didn't give a flying fish who saw all my ladies' accoutrements, the culprit was a half full, or half empty 50ml of tootpaste (so 25ml), but that wasn't enough, everything else had to be examined (except the ladies' things!), the phone charger had to be taken away, and taken to bits for all I know, the deodorant etc all had to be scanned again, surely if they had all passed first time they didn't need to be re-examined, I wasn't bothered as I had plenty of time but it seemed very odd and left rather a sour taste, all the little boxes of pearls and jewellery had to be taken out and examined, I then had to repack everything which I did quite slowly. I can only assume these people have nothing else to do but annoy passengers and being called 'Madam' all the time didn't help. Finally on to the other cafe and yes they had salad, little plastic tubs of pre-packed pasta and stuff, not quiite the delicious seafood I had anticipated. If I ever visit again I'll make sure my hotel makes me a crab/prawn sandwich for the airport because it was all pre-packed plastic food.

I cannot believe the absolutely ridiculous bag search I have just had to endure. The full suitcase was emptied and checked in front of all passengers coming through, underwear and all. Very upsetting and is the 1st time out of many bag checked that I felt violated. The check was completely unnecessary, as I was compliant with all items in my suitcase and removed the items that needed to go through separately. This needs to be addressed because it is very upsetting to flying customers, who should not be treated like criminals.
Lost my phone at Guernsey airport and the security staff on that day, pulled out all the stops to get it back for me: so grateful, a wonder team. Everything else ran like clockwork.

Had 40 minutes at Guernsey airport before sending off my better half. Went to the upstairs bar for a farewell pint. Only 1 person serving but queue only 4 deep. No urgency clearly and over 10 minutes later, eventually served to be told that there was no beer. No effort to rectify the fraught beer supply either. Inflated prices, inflated waiting times, deflated staffing with deflated service.

Check-in would not accept passengers until 2 hours before the flight despite the monitors advising us to do so. Check in person was blunt and almost rude, not acceptable, we are the customers! It isn't my fault she was talking quietly and I had to ask her to repeat every time. Then security, they take possession of my backpack and without comment put it on a unit away from me and left it there. A couple of minutes later another security man came along and started swabbing the bag because I had lots of camera equipment inside. The toilets in departures need a good refurbishment. Otherwise a great little airport, modern, clean, with duty free and so on.

The Airport is really small and the departures lounge is small and unintuitive. The weird door thing doesn't do anything as you could board any plane once out there. Past security the duty free shop is small and is not a world duty free. There is no WHSmith or Starbucks in the terminal. Otherwise extremely good service.

Please please get some training for your check in crew miserable is a mild word. I have travelled to Guernsey twice this year and both times the check in crew seem to be doing all pax a favour. Many years ago in BMI times in Guernsey this would not have been tolerated. All over Guernsey one gets superb service until you get to the airport and check into or ask a question on the Flybe desk. Having worked in tourism for many years(including Guernsey). I feel you are doing Fly be a great disservice. The flight was excellent and on time. Hope next time I will see a change.

Guilin airport is not as big as I thought for the number of passengers - the shopping places are limited and I could hardly find a decent cafe here. Crowded terminal obviously cannot cope with the number of travelers. The goods offered in shops are expensive and water is not provided anywhere as any other airports do.

A fairly small airport by Chinese standards but then again so is Guilin. At check-in they waved me over to check in at the VIP line even though I was flying economy nice of them. Despite being small this airport has a nice decor & is clean. Going through security quite smooth & efficient. My main complaint is at departures gates many people smoking & not much in the way of snacks unless you like strange looking Chinese treats that have no English.

A totally stress-free experience as sampled on a return charter flight from the Tampa Bay area. Just eight departure gates, but ample seating and a friendly bar/cafe. No TSA hassle either. A good gateway to Biloxi, the Mississippi Gulf Coast and even Mobile AL. Close to I-10.

Previous comments on GPT are no longer true. Often GPT is cheaper that New Orleans or any other nearby airport. The presence of AirTran keeps fares very reasonable and service is pretty good in all directions. The new terminal to be completed this year will be beautiful.

The airport is small clean and convineent however very expensive. To fly into or out of this airport makes no sense with the outrageous prices. Better prices available from MSY (an hours drive away from the west) and/or MOB (an hours drive from the east). Note - this information is prior to Hurricane Katrina and may not be accurate at the moment but if and when normal operations resume this information will serve similar to pre-Katrina GPT.

Airport is away from city and not good public transport available, better to use cab. Not too busy most of times so not long queue at entry, check in and security, mostly 30-40 min to complete all formality. Limited food options, needs more, there is one lounge but one of the smallest and least food options i found in India, only suggested if having complementary lounge access. Shopping options is also very limited, only recommend tea shop if didn't got time to buy tea in city which is famous for. Toilets needs to be more clean. Shortage of sitting space on both floors. Free Wifi only for 45 min. This airport need proper maintenance now.

Gwalior airport is very small, although a much larger terminal is being built and should be running by 2024. When it fits it'll be able to handle up to 8 aircraft simultaneously (currently only 3) via airbridges. Until it fits you have to make do with an antiquated terminal with just one departure lounge with barely sufficient seating, no WiFi, and then a sorry walk across the tarmac to your waiting aircraft

Through Goiania on a trip from Sao Paolo. Small regional airport with surprisingly high number of flights on what appear to be only domestic routes. Arrivals experience good walked from plane to terminal and out within 5 minutes of leaving the plane. On departure very straightforward. I would recommend not going airside until necessary there are no facilities at all apart from one snack bar insufficient seating and very crowded (as in fact the whole place was). Easy to find a taxi. There are plenty of cashpoints as well but these are outside the terminal on the kerbside road. Also a small viewing gallery upstairs.

The international terminal of Haikou Airport is a very spacious terminal I have ever seen. The terminal is small and dedicated. The staff of VIP room help me to carry the language when I arrived and welcome me before I check in and keep me company all the way to the lounge. There is a beautiful tropical garden in the terminal. The staff in the airport is professional and dedicated. I want to thank them for treating me so well.

Arrived from Hong Kong and flew out next day to Beijing. A nice little tropical type airport compact and fact to be processed. Clean reasonable facilities and nice staff. A really easy entry into China and would like to visit Hainan for longer enxt time.

Haikou Airport is not too bad but the toilet facilities are a bit dirty. They do not provide toilet paper on the toilets so you'll need to get some paper from the paper towel supply next to the toilets. Check-in gates don't seem to be crowded at all. When I got to security I thought it would take quite long but it had been really fast; 2 minutes to scan my hand luggage. After security there is a cafe bar located before you enter onto the terminal. Now this is where it gets hectic. You simply cannot breathe while you're trying to capture a picture of a plane on the tarmac. The people just smoke and smoke and basically you could just see everyone smoking in the bar. When I approach the toilets in the waiting hall I see them as third class squat toilets. They are so dirty and no one seems to clean them with detergent. This is what is hectic for foreigners but I am Chinese so I would understand this. The waiting hall showing departures do not have English read on them so you have to understand a bit of Chinese to get through the airport as efficiently as you can.

The airport of the provincial capital of Haikou on Hainan Island China. Dominated by Hainan Airlines and China Southern Airlines. The exterior looked a little dated and the interior looked a little yellow with age though the check-in counters and washrooms certainly were up-to-date. Custom and security clearance were done smoothly and efficiently. The main airport lobby was a little dark but it was certainly buzzing with activities. The "International Terminal" serving Dragonair and Air Macau was tucked into an inconspicuous corner and not properly marked. I did not see any signs either in English or Chinese. Touts littered the airport exits. If you do not mind the haggling 50-60RMB should be about right to get you into the city if not go for the Airport Shuttle bus. Cost you only 25RMB and you can grab a taxi from its terminal for only 10RMB to anywhere within the city itself.

Hailaer Dongshan airport traffic is very inconvenient, bus frequency is very few, usually have to wait for a long time. There are only three automatic check-in machines in the whole terminal, which is not very good. There are few queues in the manual check-in office, and the attitude of the staff in the information office is very good! It's not good to go through security only 90 minutes before departure. There is no restaurant after the security check. The price of the shop is very expensive. It's not good. There's free WiFi and it's very fast. The airport signs are very good. The arrival baggage claim area is very narrow, and it is very crowded when multiple flights arrive at the same time, but the luggage speed is very fast. The queuing time of security check is long.

A small modern 5-gate airport. Smiling and timely check-in security and boarding. Pleasant airy shared lounge with good Mongolian and other ethnic items reasonably priced. Ours was the only plane at the airport let alone scheduled to fly around midday but all shops and facilities were fully open and staffed. Only criticism is the lack of a bar which I would prefer to for example the bridal wear store.

Small airport which was about 30 minutes on bus to the city center. Facilities was good and clean. Baggage claim was fast and thoughtful, as at many other Japanese airports. Signs and directions were also clearly noted in English.

Hakodate airport is fairly small but the building is modernised with only two floors. Before the security gate on the second floor a small shopping arcade selling mainly Japanese goods. Like all Japanese domestic airports Hakodate is well organised clean and efficient. It caters mainly for passengers travelling with ANA and JAL two of the major Japanese airlines and Do airline ( a subsidiary of ANA ). If you are staying in the downtown area there is direct airport bus from JAL hotel the Grand hotel and the Hokodate train station to the airport. The bus fare is 600 yens and it takes only 20 minutes.

Not the best but for a smaller city it does the job, if you have an early morning flight you can only get there by cab or someone dropping you off. The transit that is available at the airport at the day time can be very crowded and infrequent. One positive thing is that the airport staff is very friendly and helpful.

The custom officers were mean and condescending. He kept shouting "what's wrong with people these days" and "do you even speak English" while we were being nothing but polite and patient, even after a long international flight.
Nova Scotia is known for its friendly service. But not at this Airport or at least not with Swoop Airline. Hard to pay for a walker for a Child with a disabilities an extra 80 dollars.

A decidedly mediocre airport. Winnipeg and Quebec City are similar in size but are far advanced in terms of services on offer, design and overall experience. What happened in Halifax? Depressing and sad.

The airport is lovely and everything went smoothly for our arrival from Glasgow. Security and customs went quick and luggage transfer was seamless. However, there needs to be regulations put on businesses on the other side of security that are selling products for outrageous prices! The cheapest 2 bottles of water I could find cost me $8! They were 590ml size. Everything in this store was ridiculously priced. Food items way overpriced! Talk about gouging tourists that have little options for items to take on the plane. Airports should take responsibility for this happening everywhere. We came from Scotland and Ireland and thought it was bad in those airports. But here in Canada we witnessed worse.

Why does security screening not separate travellers with connections going to USA and huge families travelling on charters? Stuck behind hundreds of families and just about miss my flight. Easily able to queue travellers not on charters. 300 people for 6am flights and customs doesn't open til 5am. Very bad planning and execution.

Wifi at the airport is so bad that it is not usable at all. First it does not let Linux machines connect, so I have to switch to Windows just to get a connection (and my MAC address registered) before switching back to my beloved linux. Secondly, the connection speed is too low, just less than 0.5 Mb download, even though it's early morning and not many people are in the airport.

The Check-In area was nice, however it wasn't easy finding the Passenger Screening area. The way we found it was by the long lineup into the food court. Passenger Screening was extremely slow and we waited in line forever. When we got in there, they only had 2 out of 6 lines open. I'm not sure what the point of having all of those lines is for if you're not going to open them. I think it's crazy that it takes 6-7 people to man one line. When we got up to departures, the shopping was all cheap junk, no fancy stores or even nice stores. We didn't find any restaurants either, just coffee and wraps, etc. We were leaving from gate 22, and there was literally no seating in the area. The other end of the airport was nice with lots of seating, but the end near our gate seemed older and had minimal seating. We also had a tough time finding any seats with power in them. All of the ones we tried didn't work! Overall the place looked junky, dated, and crammed. Nowhere near a world class airport. The outdoors looked very nice! But get inside and it's a different story.

Flew via Halifax on way from Heathrow to Toronto. As it's a pretty small airport there's not that much to do apart from look at the lobsters in the lobster shop - we couldn't believe it when so many people were boarding planes carrying lobster boxes! There are a few eateries both land and airside which are not wildly overpriced just average food on offer. Tim Horton's provided a decent sandwich. Overall we quite enjoyed the 3 hours we spent there though. If you go up the lift in the main concourse area there's a small viewing platform room which is a calm and relaxing place to be. We watched the few planes that came in and out for 45 minutes before going through security. Everywhere there are plenty of staff to offer help - all dressed in lovely tartan uniforms and without exception totally friendly. There is also free wifi so we took full advantage of that. We did ask one member of staff if we had time to go and see Halifax. She replied in a friendly but blunt way "You'd have to take a bus to get there and there's not really much to see anyway!" It's small but clean efficient and did the job for the few hours' stopover.

Very small but friendly efficient airport. Not a great deal to do and not many shops particularly airside but staff are always remarkably friendly and helpful which makes a change from most other airports I visit.

I came from Bangkok to Doha and transited for 8 hrs, and then to my homeland Cairo. I was frustrated to stay that long transit time but once i stayed there I enjoyed it so much. The internet coverage and speed is awesome. Perfect atmosphere, perfect cleaning, perfect toilets. Unforgettable experience. Thanks to each and everyone who participated at this huge well maintained entity.
This is my second time in Qatar, and the eGate is not working properly. The immigration lane is frustrating, it took 1.5 hours just to reach the counter.

Arrived at the airport and one of the customer service agents was very helpful. He helped me with picking up my luggage, connecting to WiFi, and was very friendly. His name was Houssem. Thank you so much for all the hard work.
Quiet room with reclining chairs are actually very loud since we get very loud announcements on microphones (personal announcements, gate announcements for boarding etc).

Leaving the airport is a painful process. Waiting times for a taxi is unacceptable, while there is a metro line, this is not in use 24 hours. How can it be that a prestigious airport like this does not have uber or a 24 hour metro line.

Flying from Cape Town to Dublin to attend a conference (and later return to Chicago from there). I was looking forward to my first chance to check out Hamad Doha Airport. Qatar Airways was fine, except we arrived late in Doha. We had to take a crowded bus to the terminal, and it took over a half hour. There were traffic jams on the tarmac. I then had to run a long way through jammed concourses and just made my connection to Dublin. On the way, I saw crowds of people, a bunch of luxury stores and chain eateries, and some trees and plantings in one area. Color me unimpressed.
Love this airport but can someone explain the logic of having to throw water away that has just been given on an incoming flight. Doesn’t make sense!

No storage lockers, actually there are but disabled due to health and safety concerns.  There is no option to leave your backpack or cabin luggage if you want to hop for quick tour of the city due to long layover. Food venues are poor in variety of choice and amount of places. e.g. coffee and pastries are everywhere same - no variety. Quiet places are next to the family place so you have a toddler with temper tantrums next to you while trying to take nap or sleep.  Good: On-site gym with treadmill and pool. But not available 24/7. Power sockets are made to be compatible with every plug so you don't need adapters! Something every other airport should follow!

Doha Airport has gone from ok to unacceptable since it’s opening in 2014. While bus gate arrivals/departures were the exception then, it has become too frequent in recent years. I am flying through Doha about 6 times a year, more than half of my flights in 2023 were remote bus transfers. The departures via bus gate are particularly stressful with very limited seating, unorganized boarding and stressed gate agents. The picture shows my latest bus gate departure with crowded areas and inadequate seating.

Transit in this airport both inbound and outbound. The transit time of 3 hours was not enough to experience this enormous-sized airport with a lot of offerings and facilities such shopping mall, indoor gardens, etc. Not the best airport if one is just transferring from one flight to another because it takes time and energy to find toilets, prayer rooms, and gates. But the best for long transit as you will not get bored. This airport lacks free shower facilities.

Hamburg airport security lane on departure experience was not what one expects from a German airport. Staff incredibly rude and unfriendly. We were flying business class on Lufthansa and were asked to remove all creams and liquids from the cabin bag. We had packed these items as required in the plastic sleeved cover, but they removed an after shave lotion and a hand cream as they didn’t fit exactly into the bag. This was the most unpleasant customer experience at any airport!! What makes this even more annoying is that the adjoining security lanes were fitted with newer CT scanners, which do NOT require airline passengers to remove items from their cabin bag!! This newer technology should be operating at all their lanes and would have saved us this unecessary delay and the very rude staff. Australia has this newer CT scan technology already installed at airports, which allows for an enhanced customer experience. Until Hamburg airport upgrades, avoid this place!!

Often hour-long lines for security, and it never fails that one or more members of staff are rude. The airport is quite small and easy to navigate, but the impolite staff makes travelling through here an unpleasant experience.

We took the train to the airport, went smoothly. Its easy to orientate in the airport. Check in was done in a few minutes. Next was security, very long lines, must be many passengers that loose their flights. Since we were a family travelling, with a child, we got a special family line. Not very many in front of us, but the line moved very slowly forward. Some of the security points were closed. The security made a big number of controlling the stroller, they even contacted the police, that wished us a nice trip. Much time used. This maybe explain part of the very long lines. Inside we walked and walked and walked until we reached the gate. With cold wind and rain, it was not nice to wait to board out on the tarmac

Arrived in Hamburg en route to Edinburgh from Istanbul. Expected renowned German efficiency and a smooth transit through airport for final flight home. Complete mayhem with a near miss disaster ensued instead. On arrival all passengers were funnelled along corridor and down a narrow staircase/escalator combo. Unknowingly this was directly into a narrow glass lined corridor with an abrupt disgorgement into passport control. This resulted in a sudden crush at bottom of escalator as there was already a crowd along corridor. Thankfully a quick thinking passenger hit the emergency button on the escalator which prevented a much more serious crush. In addition the glass lined corridor was hot due to setting sun and overcrowding. There were 3 passport control personnel. It took around an hour to move through passport control with no staff available to explain the situation or ease the overcrowding. Total shambles. Once through passport control another blockage occurred at security. Absolute shambles with people skipping to the front due to connecting flight departures. Queues were closed and merged several times due to malfunctioning conveyor belts and overcrowding. Tempers were frayed. Luckily we had just enough time to make our flight but as someone with a spinal issue due to terminal cancer, attempting to run to departure gate was stress I could’ve done without. Absolutely shocking and indeed dangerously laid out and disorganised airport. Never again!

It was a horrible experience. There is no sign telling you where to transit to go at the gate to change your flight, the only person there gave me (and other persons) the wrong information, with resulted on almost losing the flight! I had to pass again all the security and passport controls, jumping people on the queue. I am wondering if they do it on purpose or they just don't know how to do their job or they don't care.

It annoys me this was my first experience with "German efficiency", as it was certainly rude but never efficient. From lost luggage that the airline couldn't communicate with the airport about, awful waiting times followed by being rushed, to having to throw out several items that contained liquid (due to not having the aforementioned lost luggage to store them in, after having to purchase new ones already) and they don't sell any clear one liter bags to carry them in, despite this being a common problem. Judging by other reviews, they clearly don't care and it certainly left an awful impression for me.

Everything B.Gardner of the UK on June 14th and David Cormier (U.S.) on June 13th 2023 said is absolutely exact. We traveled on June 12th 2023, we got to the airport in Hamburg at 8.00am for a 10.55 flight to London on British Airways. After spending 1 hour and 20 minutes to check our luggage at the BA counter (we had E-checked-in the day before) we then got in the security-check line which snaked 1 and a half times the length and width of the airport. One and a half hours later we finally cleared security. Half the security check points were closed. The other half was staffed by rude and overzealous (Kleenex needed to be removed from pockets) personnel who gave the impression of being on a work to rule campaign and did not care that many customers were now about to miss their flights. There were no airport personnel to assist through all of this. I have travelled millions of miles in my life and have never experienced anything this bad. As far as I am concerned, I will never set foot in this airport again.

I travel frequently on business. From the experiences I had in my life, I must say Hamburg Airport is by far, the worst I had the displeasure of using. I live in Hamburg, so I am frequently using the services of this airport, unfortunately and it is rarely a smooth experience. Today I had the worst experience ever: After luggage drop-off I had to wait for more than 90 min in the security queue. There was nothing special this day, it was just another normal Saturday. Later, when I was already inside the plane, all passengers already on-board 5 minutes before the schedule, my plane was grounded for another 60 minutes. The reason? The airport staff took "too long" loading the luggage in the aircraft. The pilot had to call a representative of airport staff inside the craft to ask what exactly was delaying so much the work of the loaders. TLDR: If you don't like huge waiting times and having your flight delayed for absolutely no reason, stay away from this Hamburg Airport (HAM).

Worst airport experience I've had. I have used hundreds of airports around the world traveling for work, and I have never encountered a place so disorganized and staff that are so rude. I checked in to a Eurowings Hamburg - London in one of the kiosks which gave me a luggage tag and boarding pass. Then I was supposed to do a simple "bag drop" of my already tagged bag which is usually easy at many airports. Not here. The only option for bag drop was waiting in a queue, for more than an hour, for automated machines that did not work properly. People spent around 15 minutes to get the machine recognize the luggage tag and they needed to repeatedly try from the beginning. I was not able to drop my bag because the tag was not recognized. I asked for help and the airport staff told me that they cannot help and there is no human-operated bag drop. They told me to go to another part of the airport, re-join the queue and try my chance with other machines. I ended up trying several different machines and after trying many times the bag was accepted by the machine. I was shocked that the answer to my simple "can you please help?" question was "no I cannot". I think it's the only instance in my travel life that some airport staff refused a request for help. The security check was especially awful and it's the main reason I'm writing this review. The staff at the security check were extremely rude, only addressed people in German when many people, including me, were trying to communicate with them in English. One of the security people was making fun of my t-shirt and asking random questions (as much as I understood his German) when I was waiting for him to pat me down. It wasn't a simple friendly chit-chat, it was downright rude. Very unprofessional, rude and inefficient service overall. Pretty minor, but the airport itself is not great and the facilities were not so good. There was no shop open to buy any food or drink in the tiny area we were supposed to wait after the passport control. I'm shocked by this experience taking place in Germany. I would avoid this airport in the future. It's also not a good impression for the city of Hamburg in general.

We had the most horrible experience at Hamburg airport. Little to no signage regarding where to check in. Kiosks for check in did not work and referred us to agent. At Lufthansa that means one agent with long lines. We were then sent to machine baggage check in - half not working. One agent to assist for 30 seconds then leaves. It took 30 minutes to submit 4 bags. Then the 90 minute line for security. Just awful.

Been flying through LBC several times with destinations such as Dublin and London Stansted. I have encountered only once uncomfortable experience with Ryanair flight to Dublin being delayed for almost 6 hours. Thanks to the Eu new regulation I received a voucher for a small meal at the LBC restaurant. LBC is easily accessible from Hamburg City with the direct bus service. The airport condition improved somehow. A new duty free zone has been up and provides wide selection of goods especially perfumes. Unfortunately it is located in the departure hall just behind the security control.

I've flown to and from Hamburg-Lübeck with Ryanair on many occasions (Skavsta and Stansted) and as long as you know what you're getting yourself into when you book it's fine. This is a very much a basic flat-pack airport  but the bus to Hamburg takes about an hour for €8 a pop and deposits you right next to the main railway station so frankly - especially as Ryanair airports go - it's perfectly reasonable. If something goes wrong and you're stranded here all day then naturally you'll start to tear your hair out after a while but - occasional expansions and temporary chipboard flooring aside - it's hard to argue with the place when you're paying beer money for your flight.

If the airport would not be used by Ryanair this place would be as dead as a doornail. Highly unpleasant are the terminal facilities which were situated under a tent construction. If hot bring water or suffer. Bring also a good read otherwise you will bore stiff. The restaurant facilities are okay and adequately priced. Transfer to and fro the airport is pretty easy from town - the bus terminal is in walking distance from the station (even if loaded which is not advisable with regard to Ryanair's regulations). Security could be a bit more relaxed the hired people are overdoing it.

I agree with the other comments the airport is fine. Small and compact but with a reasonable range of facilities. However the contracted-out airport security staff are extremely strict in enforcing Ryanair's maximum baggage weights and dimensions - no leeway whatsoever!! There were a lot of very angry passengers who were told after they had already checked in their hold baggage they would have to check in their hand baggage into the hold as well - for example because the wheels of the bag took it over the permitted dimensions. It's maybe because these security staff are working for a private company instead of the airport or the airline they are so strict. Wireless LAN internet access available at 5 EURO per hour in the departure lounge.

Travelling recently from Lübeck on a Ryanair service to Stansted was a pleasant surprise. This small regional airport placed in a residential suburb south of Lübeck had five check-in counters open for one departure - the staff even smiled regularly - and the new (temporary?) departure lounge is roomy. The walk to the aircraft isn't long so Stansted is beaten in every category!

Air New Zealand representative named Leanne was very helpful when I needed help to check in my 7.ft surfboard, she was helpful when I needed help to print out my boarding pass, exceptional patience and excellent customer skills.

Loved it. Takes no more than 10 minutes from entering to get to the gate. When you depart, 10-20 minutes. It was like heaven compared to Toronto where there are long lines, lots of computers and where it takes so long to get to the gate and where you dread the line-ups getting off the plane for the same reason. It is convenient, it is quick, clean and has a Tim Hortons.

This place is so dirty and all the dam fruit flys are everywhere. There is a woman at security that is so rude not sure how she has this job. I definitely would not come back here for a layover. I have traveled 3rd world countries and this Hamilton is the worst one yet. I am so disgusted with the attitude and lack of cleanliness
Nice small airport. Close, convenient parking. Super fast customs on arrival. Unfortunately the baggage process was extremely slow. It took 30 minutes to get my suitcase.

I am a 22 year old girl and this is my first time using this airport as well as flying anywhere by myself. I arrived and got confused on where to go for my luggage. I asked a security guard for help and he was honestly the rudest person I have ever met. He sounded so annoyed that he had to tell me where to go, instead of listening to me he got mad at me and wouldnt let me speak and began to yell at me. Flying by yourself for the first time is hard enough without the airport personnel making it even harder.

Super small airport, and wonderful if you are meeting someone from Hamilton. Car rentals from site were out of cars and were no help. Cost 40 bucks to take cab from airport to in town car rental agency. Tim Hortons only outlet in airport on arrival side or vending machines. Flying with Flair and can only get tickets printed and drop off suitcases two hours before flight. What we thought we were saving to get to a Blue Jays game in Toronto, cost us more by flying to this back wood airport than what it would have been to fly WestJet to Toronto. Never again, will stick with West Jet - friendly and helpful and reliable. And the Blue Jays lost which made the trip even more horrible.

Hamilton International is a great little airport and very convenient for people trying to avoid the hustle and bustle of Pearson. My family is located in southern Ontario and I always use this airport. The only complaint I would have is the decision of management to serve no alcoholic beverages.

Very convenient to reach from anywhere. I would call it a "no frills" airport. If this airport is to compete as an "International airport" it has to invest money in renovation and updating of the building! In general: I am thankful for the close proximity of this airport.

Very nice alternative to using Toronto. Limited flight destinations but check in for domestic and intl flights is simple. Security clearance on departure and arrival is a breeze. Parking is a short walk. Not much by way of services in the terminal but you also do not need to arrive 3hrs prior to a flight. There are no gates so be prepared to walk to your plane via the tarmac.

Used Hamilton Airport as an alternative airport to Toronto. A much smaller airport than Pearson (a good thing) resulting in much less walking (and waiting) and much easier to get in and out of. A great option if you're visiting Southern Ontario (or Niagara Falls) if you want to avoid the Toronto traffic and is 80 km from downtown Toronto. Not the greatest airport for public transit links to Hamilton and Toronto and beyond likely due to the airports small size. Airport was slightly built on the cheap has exterior siding and drop celling interiors reminding me of a bus terminal and has very limited food/shopping options. Despite these minor complaints overall a good alternative to Pearson for direct flights and would use it again.

We were flying home on 25 July from Hamilton Island. Our flight was with Virgin. As it was pouring rain we noticed at the airport did not have any cover at all. As we noticed Qantas was parked very close to the entry not that far of a walk but still no cover at all for passengers. Very disappointed that every single passenger was saturated getting on to the plane. Virgin did not park close it parked far away. Very disappointed won’t be back

A small domestic airport on Hamilton Island, Queensland Australia very small but tidy and efficient. Check in was a breeze and through security very quickly. Lots of seating and only a couple of gates as planes restricted to daytime flights only. Basic refreshments available and toilets although small were nice and clean. You had a nice view of planes landing and parking close to the terminal and could see bags being loaded unloaded and the plane being refueled. Very small but pleasant airport to wait for your flight.

Checking-in for a 10 seat flight without any other flights at the same time was never going to be busy. Check-in staff (who was also baggage handler flight dispatcher and I'm sure other things) was very friendly and efficient. The small terminal had good restroom facilities car hire drinks and food dispensing machine. Surprisingly large number of security personnel for a tiny airport - I counted at least 4 security staff. Nice experience.

It is a new and clean airport. However, regardless of long queue, there were only 2 officials for immigration procedure and I waited for 20 minutes. What was worse is that when I was shopping in the Hangzhou speciality shop, one clerk followed me without giving me advices, even blocking my way. I felt I was treated like a thief. Very bad experience.

Landed at Hangzhou Airport around 1305 using AirAsia X from Kuala Lumpur. Immigration clearance was smooth and no hassle. I claimed my luggage in just a few minutes. Washroom services are as good as other airports in China. The only lacking is the number of available seats on the departure floor at the check-in counters area.

Arrived from Chengdu and the collection of luggage was straight forward and simple although it was quite a hike from the gate we arrived at. However only after I walked out of the terminal to the various buses that I found out that you needed to buy a ticket inside the terminal. Counter had no English signage and I walked passed it because it was displaying train schedules.

New airport clean and modern design with lots of natural light and greenery. Good choice of Chinese food restaurants for departing passengers Western food is much more limited. China Eastern premium lounge is on the 2nd floor next to security a nice restful place to wait with made-to-order noodle soups available. Free WiFi works but is spotty in places. No train or subway to this airport. It is quite a long distance from downtown Hangzhou and the airport highway is under construction so it will be a long taxi ride to your hotel.
I think it is a great airport compared to most Chinese airports. Today Hangzhou Airport is quite different from what it used to be. It's very large and modern and has good service.

Pretty basic as airports go. Way out of town it is simply ridiculous and taxis are - well keep your belt on and wear a helmet if you have one. The airport sort of works but this is a typical domestic Chinese airport not great not entirely hideous but you know what! If you want to fly to Hangzhou its this or nothing. I can tell you it is heaven compared to the central rail station.
Toilet cleanliness is awful. This new airport could have been better than the old military airbase however it still has long way to go. I will give it a 1-star or no star.

Airport uses a lot of natural light. The design is modern especially the departure lobby the ceiling its so high. The staff in the airport have good manners. The luggage arrived quick and there's plenty of check-in counters too. The bad thing - airline lounges terrible.

Used both domestic and international sections recently. Airport is new airy and modern with plenty of natural light. Walk to passport control was reasonable. Passport control was well-staffed and did not take long. Officers smile! Luggage also arrived quickly. The drive out of the car park is somewhat convoluted under the terminal building and out again and even had locals stumped. Check-in procedures quickly done though why the Chinese Authorities insist in customs declaration upon departure is a mystery to me. All it does add to the scramble for forms and jostling for space on the tables. Once airside there isn't much there. And constant announcements for all flights since int'l and domestic areas are only separated by glass partition. Airline lounges are miserable. In all a fine modern Chinese airport no complaints

New airport opened around 2000 and much better than the old airport at the military airbase. Plenty of check-in counters and smooth handling in security check. First class lounge good. As most Chinese airports it is noisy from continuous announcements.

Hannover ist ein mittelgrosser Flughafen, 5 Mio. Passagier würde ich sagen. Der Flughafen liegt etwa 10 km ausserhalb der Stadt Hannover in Langenhagen. Kurze Wege sind hier ein Vorteil. Die letzten Flüge waren pünktlich, check-in war zügig und auch vor der Luftsicherheitskontrolle war die Wartezeit annehmbar. - Hanover is a medium-sized airport, I would say 5 million passengers. The airport is located about 10 km outside the city of Hanover in Langenhagen. Short distances are an advantage here. The last flights were on time, check-in was quick and the waiting time at air security was also acceptable.

Arrival at this airport was simple, with its connection to the Hanover S-Bahn (suburban train system). Hanover airport is a convenient size: not an overwhelming number of gates but large enough to have plenty of connections. Check-in today with Swiss Airlines went smoothly: we were asked for our destination visa but not grilled and luggage was processed without difficulty. Security checking was slow today (probably because of Middle East tensions) but security personnel were good humoured and friendly. Cafes and shops on the land side closed before 4 pm; there are limited shopping possibilities on the air side but one good cafe.

On Sunday 8th of March returning on the 19.55 BA flight to Heathrow, we had gone through passport control and security. Also passengers for a Turkish arrive were also waiting at the gate when there was an announcement from the Police that there was a security breach and everyone needed to go back to out and wait and again come through security and passport control. There was chaos as those who had bought duty free had to go back and get their purchases sealed. There were no announcements in English so we had to ask people what was going on. Apparently the crew of the Turkish Airlines had gone through without border and security checks. Delays and confusion were not helped by only having two convey belts used as we all had to go back through security once the all clear was given. No formal apologies. No suggestions of compensation from an airport error. Not a good experience.

Flying out with Flybe back to Manchester. Power sockets not working in waiting area before check in but that's often the case in many airports (try Manchester T3 for example). It's taking me 50 min to queue for checkin and to queue for passport control. Still got another 10 min to wait until passport control then bags security check. All because there's only 1 staff on passport control for about 600 people, a real fine mess if you don't check in 2 hours before your flight. I'd advise to avoid this airport in its current state.

Hannover is a medium sized airport with all facilities you expect. Great plus are the short ways, good signage, short waiting times at the check-in, security and baggage delivery. Always very clean. Easy to reach by car, bus or train. They have a good selection of restaurants like high quality Mövenpick or even McDonalds, supermarkets, decent duty free and a great aviation exhibition "Welt der Luftfahrt" and observation deck. When you fly Lufthansa or Star Alliance and have a status you get access to a stylish lounge with great apron views. A nice airport I like to use a lot.

Once again I review my home airport. Its now the third time in a row that I arrived by train and the escalator from intermediate floor to departure terminal was out of use. As I am used to it I know alternative ways, but for guests which are new it is not so easy. This should be really improved, as it is an absolute "no go ". This time check in and passing security was fast. However I recommend everybody to pass security as late as possible as behind security check there is actually nothing other than a small duty free, an expensive snack bar, toilets and a small smoking box. Overall I don't like the departure area, however arrival is usually quite good, average time from leaving the aircraft to get out of airport for Schengen flights is 10 mins only.

I live in Hannover and use this airport quiet frequently. Despite its small size which should make it hassle free every time there is something which annoys me. Either the lift and escalator to the train station is not working, or there are long queues in front of security, the WIFI is not working properly or the power plugs don't provide power. Up to now I have never flown from here without a problem. Arrival procedure is very good, luggage usually comes within minutes. Food and beverage is ok for a relative small airport. Parking a car near the terminal is overpriced for short term, from second day its almost same price then for a week. Airport is easy to reach by train but it would be even better if the lift or escalator would work.

It used to be a nice small airport. Easy lay out and everything is close. Lots of parking is available and a good variety of shops. That means the airport should get a good review. But there is also the human part and there is something completely wrong. None of the staff at Hannover smile. Instead you look into grumpy faces. We wanted to have something at one of the bars. We took our seat and waited for the bar tender. He looked at us and gave the order that we have to come around to his cashier. That was done in such a manner that we left. I do not expect the security stuff to always be smiling, but is it too much just to give a short good morning after they have greeted the passenger.

Great medium sized airport. Travel fairly frequent from Hannover, mainly from Terminal B to the UK. The three terminals are very similar. Good city centre connection with S-Bahn. Fast check-in to gate usually, same for arrival to out of door.

Do not land here if you are non-EU and in transit. The airport is designed such that if you are an international transit passenger you have to enter Germany before checking in to a connecting flight (despite the fact that it is with the same airline and the connection is only 80 minutes). This means you need a visa for Germany even if you have no intention of entering the country. No other airport I have ever been do you need to get a visa just for being in transit.

We were charged $10 for two fresh coconuts at the 'Vietnam Gift Shops next to Departures. This chiseling rip-off is four to five-times the price these cost in cafes in the city. We only paid it because our attention was elsewhere at the time. Beware these obscene costs.

Was in transit from Saigon to Hanoi arriving from International and connection to Domestic. The simple word is Chaos, immigration is slow, unorganized and crazy slow. Keep at least 3 hours for safe transit between flights. While arriving from Cambodia at Hanoi airport just going pass security it took more then 90 minutes and finally reaching gate just nick of time. Completely unorganised, lack of space and very slow process.

Arrival fine, but departure was another story. Chaotic and long security lines made for a frustrating experience. The other problem I found with Hanoi Airport was the inadequate air conditioning, especially airside. Vietnam is a hot and humid country, surely the airport authority must realize this.

The airport was shining, new and clean, with clear signs and directions, both in Vietnamese and English. The international departure was smooth, though queuing time for immigration and security screening was a bit long due to the jam in the morning. Not many duty-free shopping, compared to some other international airports in SEA. Dining was expensive, seemed the restaurant was trying to make money from tourists. Boarding gate was good, with a lot of seats. Toilet was clean.

They’re not accepting e-boarding pass and i have to go to the counter to print the pass, however the counter only can print my ticket 3 hours before the flight time. There are no self check in kiosk, and its very inconvenience, the airport staff also not friendly and not helpful.
The airport is cool, clean, well ventilation and beautiful. The navigation sign is clear, help the customer easily navigate inside the airport. The staff are considerate and thoughtful.

This is the most annoying airport I’ve been to. The shops all sell the same rubbish, the staff aren’t at all interested and all the prices are in US dollars.  That’s like going to Heathrow and all the prices being in Vietnamese Dong! I understand that goods might show a conversion - but to just have dollars is irritating. And the wifi is rubbish.

The new Hanoi international terminal 2 opened at the end of December 2014, excellent and well planned, a big improvement on the old terminal. It only took me a few minutes to check in and pass the security, very efficient happy helpful staff all the way.

Frequent user of the services at Noi Bai airport here, it's one of the worst designed and managed airports in SE Asia. No signage to get you from domestic to international. Airport bus to the city takes roughly 20-30 mins to depart. Food at gates are expensive and taste bad. Restrooms hard to find. Immigration customs occasionally ask you for tips upon arrival. Avoid if you can!

This airport is the worst. The staff were rude, unprofessional and not helpful at all. Barely anyone speaks English, which is a surprise for such an important airport. They mishandled my personal belongings, treated me with no respect and constantly yelling or scolding me in Vietnamese right in front of me. I would not set foot at this airport again.

Friendly ground staff at check-in. Immigration a breeze. Duty free shop limited though. Smoking area present in departure lounge. Some restaurants available for those feeling peckish-at cut throat prices considering the price. VIP lounge looked cozy enough (didn't go in). Departure area great for plane spotting. All in all a clean facility, well run not overwhelmed yet.

The international arrivals and departure section at Harare Zimbabwe airport is a revelation. On arrival all the staff including Immigration and Customs were friendly and welcoming and this contributed to an excellent first impression and a speedy processing. Possibly helped by having obtained visas before flying. On departure check in was efficient and again the friendly staff were most helpful. There is a full range of facilities airside and clean toilets. At present there are not too many international flights but the experience was excellent.

Flew through Harare International several times during a recent trip to Zimbabwe using both the Domestic & International terminals. The current Domestic terminal was the International one until a few years ago - no updating has been done since as the customs & immigration desks are all still there. It was quick to pass through and pleasantly decorated however there was a distinct lack of facilities (only a few domestic flights each day so it probably hasn't been worth their while putting shops etc in) and the toilets were in dismal condition - to be avoided at all costs. International terminal was a much better experience. Opened only a few years ago and built for a much larger number of flights than it currently handles it seemed very spacious. Facilities were all well-maintained with a good range of shops. Food in the only restaurant was also good. Customs and immigration checks both arriving and departing were quick & courteous. Overall a very pleasant airport for international flights but let down by their poorly-maintained domestic facilities.

Harbin airport has two terminals, domestic and international. This airport is a bit old, the government is building a new terminal. Toilets not very clean, and facilities are old. Wifi is acceptable, beside the airport wifi, you can also access to your carriers wifi spot on the airport. You have to queue for a long time for check-in, unless you don't have any checked baggage and your airline has auto check in kiosk. Harbin is a hub city for China Southern, so China Southern occupied half of the entire counters. However, there is a special check in counter and security check path for flights to Beijing. Harbin airport only has 3 baggage claims, so during the rush hour, you have to wait for a long time for your baggage come out.

Despite of being the main international hub of Somaliland, Hargeisa Egal International Airport is small and pleasantly old fashioned. Arrival was uncomplicated and baggage delivery fast. You can buy your local sim card right in front of the only baggage delivery belt. For departing passengers there is one waiting room with optional open-air seating, which is only separated from the apron by a decorated fence. Security and immigration are housed in a newer building on the landside. There is one coffee outlet, a small souvenir shop and two departure “gates”, which are simply different seating areas on the first floor. For boarding, everybody then walks out onto the apron through the same door. All staff, including the immigration and security officers, were extremely friendly and courteous.

Flown in and out of Harrisburg numerous times. A smaller airport with the gates being in a Y pattern so not a lot of walking. TSA is okay but did pre-check for last flight and still had to go through regular check. If you are scheduled for an early morning departure, forget any services being open - restaurants / car rental service counters and even the airline service counters. If your flight is at 6:45 and you arrive an hour before your flight, nothing is open.  For car rentals you have to walk quite a ways to / from the terminal through the parking garage to where your vehicle is located. I have been at other airports where your rental is brought curb side for you. Leaving the airport after dark is challenging if you are driving - signs are hard to read and not lit.

Harrisburg (MDT) is a great airport. Small but connected to many international gateways. Security lines are short. Food options are limited but good. I only wish they offered a NYC area connection. My airport of choice.

There are many different airport choices for this area. Harrisburg (MDT) offers a good selection of carriers (United, Delta, US Air, Air Canada, Allegiant) which does wonders to keep the prices reasonable. Which makes it an appealing choice relative to Hagerstown, State College, Lancaster or Williamsport. There are also only 12 gates in the terminal. The daily parking garage is an easy walk (there's a shuttle to long-term parking), and a reasonable number of places to eat. The terminal is clean, reasonably quiet, and very easy to navigate and use. (Unlike Philly, Baltimore, Pittsburgh, or Reagan National).

❌Not Verified|  Departure ok, but Hartford is awful at baggage claim. When you come from a late or long flight the last thing you want is to wait half hour, an hour or more at the belt. Which is what always happened to me. How hard can it be to improve this, even a little?

Bradley is my home airport. I fly from and to here multiple times a year to visit friends and family. While it isn't as big as the New York airports or Boston, fares are usually among the cheapest in southern New England and southeastern New York, and BDL provides service to all major eastern hubs, such as: Atlanta, Detroit, Cincinnati, Charlotte, Minneapolis, Chicago-ORD, Washington, Philly, and Baltimore, as well as numerous Florida destinations, Las Vegas, Denver, Toronto, Montreal, Cleveland, Raleigh, San Juan, Cancun, and starting later this year, LA and Dublin, Ireland. Concessions are ample and security is usually manageable in under thirty, except some mornings. I nearly always fly Delta and their service out of BDL has been fantastic. Flights to Salt Lake City, Seattle, San Francisco, and Nashville would be ideal additions.

Flew through BDL last week. I like the new set of security lanes open on the US Airways side of the terminals. No line at 5.30am despite a dozen flights departing around 6am. The new arrivals/departures/gates boards are easier to read. However there doesn't seem to be one power port in the US Airways gates even though there's wifi.

Security thorough and lines short - thrilled to find that one of the TV monitors at the Southwest gates showed the local PBS channel - a nice alternative to the usual cable news and sports programming. Custodial staff cleaned gate areas twice in one hour. Spacious naturally- lit gate area was a nice oasis from usually crowded departure areas.

I'm a Connecticut resident and use Bradley a half-dozen times a year. Terminal A is perfectly serviceable - nothing fancy but it does the trick. Luckily most carriers use it. Terminal B which I understand will be closed at the end of 2009 cannot be demolished fast enough. It is an eyesore with next to no services. I guess its only advantage is for people who wonder what air travel used to be like in the 50s and 60s. They can see firsthand in Terminal B! I wish BDL had service to longer haul hubs like DEN and SLC but I guess there isn't enough demand. Nonetheless I'm perfectly happy using the airport. Its smaller size means fewer delays quicker deplaning and some breathing room.

BDL is my hometown airport. I found plenty of kiosks for check-in at US Airways and went through security quickly. On the airside at US Airways gates very limited options in terms of stores and restaurants and the good shops/restaurants are at the other side of the terminal. Upon return finding luggage is easy and the pick-up for valet lots is fast. the amenities are limited but the airport is streamlined and easy to use. I prefer BDL plus connection to a direct flight from BOS or JFK anytime.

As a lifelong Connecticut resident I am ashamed at our one major airport - but then I should remember this is small potatoes compared to Boston New York Atlanta Charlotte. The new terminal is clean and bright and a huge improvement over the old provided you are flying airlines that use it. Security seems totally confused and amateur compared to other airports and after checking in you simply deposit your checked luggage in a heap manned by security staff who seem distracted and uninterested in what you are doing. Worst of all is upon return it takes far too long to get your baggage. On a recent calm winter night we'd all deplaned a Delta flight and it took about 20 minutes before any luggage began to appear at the carousels. About 15 bags came out and then there was another 10 minute wait for 15 bags and then on and on. You can generally plan on waiting at least 30 minutes to get your bag at this "small" airport. This performance is inexcusable.

I am a bit surprised that half the airport is new. It's nice and polished on one side and a trip to the 60's on the other. As a local resident that frequents the airport (about 4 trips a month) I think they could improve the new airport food court section by building a New England type facade over the store fronts seems to be a big empty area that could be utilized for a "New England" feel.

I've traveled through this airport quite a few times due to its location b/w Boston and New- York. Overall its a quiet airport that never seems to be too busy. There's a reasonable share of shops but none too interesting. Flights are generally on time in my experiences and airport staff are helpful although you most likely may never need to utilize their assistance. The signage is perfectly laid out and food cafe's are sprinkled all over. The new terminal and parking garage are super convenient.

Bradley's new A terminal is fantastic. Finally we can show pride in our state's airport and hopefully swing travelers to Hartford rather then Boston or New York. As said before the old B terminal thats serves American and Indepence is really worn down. Signs of TWA and Pan Am still are posted throughout the terminal which is more or less one giant hallway. Security is quick and all the check-ins are well light and clean. New parking garage makes getting to terminal A even easier. Just need to do up B and we can be a world-class airport!

A small Airport. Everything you need is present. But, be warned. Just outside the arrival hall, when leaving the building, there is a table with people selling bus/taxi tickets. It seems that this is an official booth. We got ripped off. We were not brought to the place we asked and checked several times and in the end had to pay more then the double. So please be warned.
