Employees who looks after the airport customer- going above and beyond for others should also be looked after with recognition of their true worth to your operations. All the best Cat in Terminal C, neither will I forget that date.

The staff was relatively pleasant in most places but not all. The Starbucks staff were awful. Bathrooms were less than desirable. To get through TSA Precheck I had to go to opposite side of terminal, couldn’t go through appropriate side, and then had to walk all the way around again and hopefully catch up with the rest of my traveling party. Although wait in TSA line was minimal, definitely a huge minus.

We had a terrible experience at this airport mainly due to the awful attitudes of the staff.  We had orders barked at us and when we didn't understand something or failed to digest things said to us, we were shouted at like we were in a boot camp which I found very intimidating. I has my young son with me too. The staff are extremely unprofessional and when I said to the security worker that its also very stressful for us as passengers, she said "I'm just doing my job". No it's not your job to shout, intimidate and scare people. Its your job to remain calm, professional and give clear instructions. Not shout at ppl which scares them that much they're unable to digest what is being said. If I wasn't so tired & in a hurry to catch my flight I would have said way more and put her in a place. Also the girl checking passports & boarding passes screamed at me that much, her supervisor had to come and tell her to calm down. She didn't tell me what she wanted me to hand over, just shoved her hand out so I gave her passports and passes. She shouted I don't need those stop confusing everything just give me the passports. She was literally shouting at me.  They need to be trained better as I'm absolutely disgusted.

Worst TSA experience ever! 30 booths and only 4 open. Had 2 hours to catch my connection and missed it, because of horrible organization of this airport! Staff kept on saying "everyone has a flight to catch" - well, they were not ones to miss the flight due lack of urgency on their part. Cost me $400 to get a hotel to catch another flight the next morning, not even counting my lost time. Never again will I fly by that airport.

I would avoid using this airport at all costs. It is very dirty, unorganized and unreliable. The planes are always delayed. Surprisingly, the service was very bad here. It makes me not want to visit this country ever again because of this airport experience.

Hua Hin airport offers a direct connection to the resort city of Hua Hin and the surrounding towns of Prachuap and Cha Am, and saves the visitor the relative hassle of a 3 and half hour bus ride from BKK airport and a similar time from DMK, Don Meuang, Bangkok's other airport. Especially if you are coming from Malaysia. The only airline currently operating a service into Hua Hin is Air Asia, God bless them, from Kuala Lumpur to Hua Hin. The route has been a success and rumour has it that other routes will open up from Hua Hin, ideally Chiang Mai to begin with. OK, to the airport review! It's a relatively simple regional airport. With 2 check-in counters, a small snack counter and adequate seating in the check-in area. You go upstairs by escalator to passport control, security and then the departure lounge (again with adequate seating and a bathroom). There is plenty of car parking by the airport, and about 100 metres out of the main gate is a Family Mart (like a 7-11) which sells snacks. To get in to Hua Hin you can catch a taxi, or walk out the gate and catch a Green song-tao (10 baht to town, then another 10 baht if going on in the direction of Market Village and Khao Takiab). One of the pleasures of using the Air Asia service is that as the plane pulls away from the terminal building the ground staff wave you goodbye (Thai gesture of respect), it's a nice touch. Anyway, many thanks to Hua Hin airport and Air Asia for making this route a reality.

Travelled from here to Canada via Amsterdam apart from hideously expensive cafe its always a pleasure to travel from here. Check in and security excellent and baggage pick up very quick its small size makes it virtually stress free.

Excellent airport I agree completely with the last two reviews. I would say to Alastair Finch that he should not worry the airport seems to be holding its own. Having flown from Doncaster recently I was expecting a far better level of service from the UKs newest airport but all I found were closed shops and poor customer service. Access from the A15 and M180 is excellent meaning it can be reached within 30 minutes from all of the nearby population centres. Customer service is second to none and one can be off the plane and through to the car in minutes. The only thing lacking is the range of direct destinations but it seems that is more to do with the economy than the competition. Certainly the KLM service is a godsend and far better than travelling to Heathrow or Manchester for direct flights. I would highly recommend people from the Humber region and Lincolnshire to give this place a try if they haven't already. Given the choice I would sooner travel from Humberside over Leeds Doncaster and East Midlands any day despite living closer to Doncaster.

We live close to Humberside and find it very convenient for onward connections from Amsterdam. Because it is so small check in and security are quick and easy. On arrival back at Humberside we were off the plane and had or case in 10 mins. It would be a terrible shame if it was forced out by the opposition. It is much less stressful than Manchester.

Whilst small and basic it's the perfect option for a frequent traveller. No queues at check in or security. Friendly staff even the security guys are nice. No long walks to find your gate. Arrive 20 mins before departure travel stress free without the crowds and connect to the world via Schiphol. Baggage claim takes minutes. Would recommend this airport over flying via Manchester any day unless you enjoy arriving 3 hrs early and shopping.

This airport is vastly improved since the previous comment. Ideally situated for the catchment area south of the Humber. After nightmare journeys just getting to Manchester Aiport my visits to NZ are now via Humberside and Amsterdam. Minimum fuss no crowding a relaxed start to a lengthy trip. Additional package flights are now offered and the Amsterdam hub is a definite plus. There used to be a direct link to LHR with Air UK but this was discontinued before the demise of the airline and never revived. Although not essential could be useful on occasion. Landing costs I believe.

Very basic airport handling mostly summer charter fights but also year round KLM scheduled to AMS which is a boon if you want to avoid LON or other UK airports. Really quick and relaxed for both departures and arrivals. Really quite under used has a small shop a restaurant a travel agency a couple of kiosks - and quite expensive parking. No public transportation.

This is my home airport and I fly in/out of it 5-6 times a year. Good facilities that are being improved only 10 gates so end-to-end in the terminal is about 3-4 minutes walk baggage service is fair to adequate and security lines can be long (especially early morning) but seldom more than 2-10 minutes at the worst. Still if you're not flying to a hub city you'll have to change planes to get where you are going and 90% of the flights are commuter jets that are tight fits for a 6'2" 250-pounder like me. Overall preferable to starting in Atlanta but make sure you plan for the connection.

The airport is like one huge tourist trap: Although the toilets are free of charge (like inside all airports) the cleaning personnel asked for 1€. Standing in the queue (only 2 toilets for 15 women) I watched how the “cleaning lady” insisted, even when it was evident that the person queuing didn’t have money at hand. The toilets were very dirty (maybe because personnel stands at the door just asking for money). In the toilet in the restaurant area (KFC/Coffee Coster) the cleaner asked for money plus smoked! - In the duty free shop there were no testers of e.g. face cream (never seen this at any other airport) - 3 sales people approached me and almost harassed me, and you’re completely dependable since they don’t provide any testers. - All products are extremely overpriced (even for airports). E.g. 0.25l water for 250egp (5 €) - There‘s no information counter/ tourist police/ security that you could get for help (eg against the toilet personnel).

My worst comment will go for staff. They treat people like animals. As one doesn’t understand their accent, they make fun of you or just ignore that you even exist. If you ask why are you paying something, they look really angry and don’t want to explain. At departure, you fill a form that they don’t even read and so I don’t understand why we need to fill it. I could place there any name and it wouldn’t be checked… I bought a bottle of water and when paying, there was an argument between staff members, and you just stay there waiting for them to stop, to be able to pay. The only good thing is that the boarding areas are good.

I recommend to take American dollars with you in a exchange office in your country. The visa costs $25. You can pay by dollars. As soon as you arrive, you will find a gentleman saying: 'Manchester flights, Gatwick flights, here, here'. Don't listen to him and go where you can pay by dollar. Incredibly, at airport they scam you. That place where that guy tells you to go is an agency and charges in Euros, which they say 30€ (the dollar worth less than euros. Should be 23€ but anyway.) When you say, with dollar, then he tells you quite rudely to go to the other post. Simply, ridiculous. They let the scammer get inside the airport and security. It is just unbelievable. It gives a really bad reputation as soon as you arrive to the country. Take with you a pen for filling the arrival form as they don't have any and you need to ask to the people. Personally, I wouldn't recommend Hurghada airport to the travellers. WiFi is not good. They ask you to provide your tel for a SMS code verification and never arrived

The departure from this airport is unstructured and very chaotic. The containers for the scanning belt were thrown on the ground and you had to pick them up from the ground. Some people, including us, even had to put our shoes through the scanner. You will have to go through the scanner again at a different location. You are treated like animals. Finally through customs, etc. you immediately hear someone from a shop say "cigarettes". I went to take a look and wanted to take this for a friend. The offer was $20 a piece. I said I'll call my girlfriend first to see if she wanted this. I walked out of the store, went to call, and the salesperson stood next to me during the conversation. When paying for 3 slippers, the seller wanted 45 euros. When I said $40, he agreed after a bit of fuss. At Burger King you will find an overheated salesperson who treats both his employees and customers very unfriendly. When I wanted to buy another souvenir and I saw an offer of 2 + 1 free, I wanted to pay for it and I got a completely different price. I drew his attention to the offer, which will apply to a completely different product. When I said something about this, I was answered in a non-friendly tone with "OUT OF MY SHOP!!!". I asked him why and was told that I was destroying his business. Isn't it unbelievable? What a disappointment, for me a reason to never want to go to this country again where showing respect is not really of paramount importance.  Het vertrek vanaf deze luchthaven is ongestructureerd en zeer chaotisch. De bakken voor de scanband worden op de grond toegesmeten en moest je van de grond oprapen. Sommige mensen waaronder wij moesten zelfs onze schoenen door de scanner halen. Je moet op een andere plek nogmaals door de scanner. Als beesten wordt je behandeld. Eindelijk door de douane enz hoor je gelijk iemand van een winkel "sigaretten" zeggen. Ik ging even kijken en wilde voor een vriendin deze meenemen. Het bod was 20 dollar een slof. Ik zei dat ik eerst mijn vriendin zal bellen om te gragen of zij dit wilde. Ik liep de winkel hiervoor uit, ging bellen, staat de verkoper tijdens het gesprek naast me. Bij afrekenen van 3 sloffen wilde de verkoper 45 euro. Toen ik zei 40 dollar ging hij na verl heisa overstag. Bij Burger King tref je een oververhitte verkoper die zowel zijn medewerkers als klanten zeer onvriendelijk bejegend. Toen ik nog een souvenir wilde kopen en ik een aanbod zag van 2 + 1 gratis wilde ik deze afrekenen en kreeg ik een totaal andere verl hogere prijs. Ik attendeerde hem op de aanbieding, zal deze gelden voor een totaal ander product. Toen ik hier wat van zei kreeg ik als antwoord op een niet vriendelijke toon " OUT OF MY SHOP !!!. Ik vroeg hem waarom en kreeg als antwoord dat ik zijn business kapot maakte. Ongelooflijk toch? Wat een afgang, voor mij een reden om nooit meer naar dit land te willen waar respect tonen niet echt hoog in het vaandel staat.

Absolutely appalling airport. Queue up outside for ages waiting to have your passport checked. Security guards will offer you fast track access to the terminal in return for bribes.  Once inside wait in a huge queue to go through security to get into the check-in hall. When you get to the front you will be required to remove everything - coats, belts, shoes, wallets, phones etc - which will go through the scanner. Then you may find out that you are in the wrong queue (queues are by gender but there is no indication of which is which) so you'll join another queue while your valuables sit out of sight on the other side of the scanner.  Queue to check in as per normal. Make sure you have a pen because you'll need to fill in a form with precisely the same details as are in your passport and on your airline booking record.  Queue to go through passport control.  Queue to go through security. Same process - shoes, belt, wallet off, except this time there are no tables so you're doing all this on the floor. Queue to have hand baggage searched. Security staff may confiscate random things without explanation (battery packs seem to be popular).  Fill in your passport details in a handwritten book.  Queue to have your boarding card and passport checked again.  If you're leaving from gates 37 or above, queue to have your passport checked again. At the gate have your passport checked again. Occasionally security staff may randomly ask for your passport while you're just waiting in the airport. If you use a toilet, it nay be filthy and the attendant may 'expect' a tip.  The 'free' 15 mins of wifi may not work. An utterly dispiriting end to a holiday.

Scam like practice at the shop near gate no. 42. I was charged nearly 4 pounds for a bottle of coke. This is the highest price ever I have paid for coke bottle anywhere in the world. Airport needs to do something to stop this corrupt practice.

The whole airport is a disgrace. 5 x body and bag checks before I got to my departure gate. Everyone is out to scam you, from the visas on arrival, to the stalls selling water in the departure lounge. Shady characters all over the place. I saw cleaner toilets out in the desert. It really puts me off returning to Hurghada.

Second and last time I will travel to this country.  5 checks for hand luggage, and at the end you have to take off your shoes and take them through the scanner. At the last scanner I had to hand over my 2 lighters that I can normally reuse, which has never happened before in any other airport, but my half-liter bottle of water and large can of sunscreen fit through without any problems, etc. So they take away things that they can sell. Hygiene is also lacking, and how unfriendly. Everything has to go fast and they shout that we have to go fast, but when everything starts to get stuck they push you back to stand in one line, that more checks are not carried out on this... it's just a shame. I will not step foot in this country again

Departure area has a cold and unfriendly atmosphere. Security procedures are tedious and unnecessary complicated. Personnel is very unfriendly. Bomb Squad personnel kept batteries and sweets at will for their private use. Overall there is a great discrepancy between the warm and friendly welcome on the arrival site (although the building itself is also cold and unfriendly) and the cold and aggressive behavior on the departure site.

This airport is one of the worst in the world, plagued by senseless security checks and disgusting toilets. The toilets are filthy beyond belief, with floors covered in vomit, broken fixtures, and foul odors that hit you the moment you step in. Many toilets are unusable, with no toilet paper, and the sinks are caked in dirt, making it impossible to wash your hands properly. It’s a complete lack of hygiene. There’s also zero respect for women and people in wheelchairs, making this an awful experience. The staff are unprofessional, and shockingly, even in the unsanitary toilets, people are asking for tips. Despite the country relying on tourism, they treat visitors like animals. The atmosphere is hostile, with staff shouting and making rude, degrading comments. After four visits, this is definitely my last trip to Egypt. You have no idea how many people won’t be returning after being treated this way.

My bag was screened for 4 times as the security personnel could not judge the items under screening. it got screened, comes to scrutiny like wise 4 times .... sorry, the same bag was screened with no issue. Finally, all the items in the bag have to put in tray for screening which is very shabby and inconvenient for passengers.
Very slow and frustrating check in process. Toilets are inadequate in number and totally unhygienic. Airports ambience and planning is horrible. Lots of distance to cover to emplane and deplane.

Terrible experience with the security and immigration check , since from the entrance officer who checks passport and tickets works slower than tortoise and shows no respect for passengers no professionalism. As they think they own the airport & immigration officers do not bother to inform about the closer of counter they simply walked out from their designated cabin passenger who are queuing more than half hour haven't got any clue wether someone else going to start the next shift or not. Airport authority need to sent back all the security and immigration officers for hospitality training again.

Travelling from Bangalore to Nashik via Hyderabad. Worst airport experience at Hyderabad Airport.  For domestic transfers, they have single line security check, queue was very very long. Domestic transfers passengers were under pressure of catching next flight, but no one were assisting them. Security staff #CISF people are very rude. Gates are extremely scattered.

I am a frequent traveller and I like Hyderabad airport. It offers a good shopping experience. Has many brands and user friendly. I keep traveling to middle East through this airport as well as various through Mumbai and Delhi as well. I would like to say people are helpful and good easy to understand and very clean airport. I can rate it as one of the best airports in India.
Very crowded airport, not sufficient seating arrangement jut like bus terminal not airport terminal feeling, not proper food stall, vending machine not proper work..

1. Airport isn't organized well 2. Staff at the airport asks for money! (Ladies washroom and buggy operator!!) 3. Mumbai Street Food pav bhaji is terrible in taste 4. Airport cleaning staff are not efficient enough (table) 5. Vending machines sell water for 20 rupees, shops sell for 70!! 6. Zoodles shopkeeper didn't know where the water dispensing machine was! Not did he wish to help us figure it out! 7. Customer service / proactive spirit / pride for Hyderabad is totally missing at the airport.

This is one of the newer Indian airports though unfortunately unlike BLR, BOM, DEL etc you wouldn’t know it. It’s handicapped by a design that was inadequate in size and not well planned. While, there’s a fair amount of shopping it occupied so much space that the passenger concourse feels congested even on a low-traffic Saturday morning. The airport isn’t particularly well maintained. It looks clean but that’s about it. Service standards from the entry to the airport-staffed check in and boarding staff are remarkable by their lack of enthusiasm, lack of politeness and lackadaisical pace of work. If they’ve had much training, it was very inadequate.

Staff at security scanner don't know how to use the equipment. They make you open all the luggage, ask what is this cable which charges phones, open kids toys, open and see jewellery, open wallets to see cash and cards. They even run the metal detector on the boarding pass and kids hair bands. Someone should teach or give proper training on how to detect explosive materials and sharp items via xray scanners.

The services provided at the Rajiv Gandhi International Airport were extremely horrible. Along the way, every single step, from baggage check in all the way to security check were really slow. We came across the WIFI help desk after the security check instead of before. As a result, we could not contact our family. We almost missed our flight. Once the security check was over, we were expected to immediately get onto our flight due to a lack of time. Therefore, we weren't able to access the WIFI services. Flight timings weren't prioritized. Passengers who were boarding later flights were prioritized first for the security check. Despite the numerous requests that we made about our flight, we were assured that we would make it on time, therefore, we couldn't progress forward in the line. Out flight started at 3:30 AM, and we were still in the line for security check until 3:00 AM. The bins for the security check were moving very slowly. Bins were moving in sets of four. Between each set, there was a huge gap. Therefore, the entire line moved very slowly. The airport staff were not cooperative or helpful in this process, especially those who helped with the security check. Could you please look into and improve these services?

The current airport is small but efficient. A new much larger terminal is being build. Border and security control was fast and efficient. All 4 gates are currently in one large terminal with bus boarding only. Staff was acting friendly and speedy. Bus 50 brings you to to city in 30 for only 3 Lei.

The staff in this airport shout at people, get so angry, herding people around like animals. People were doing nothing wrong and getting shouted at in queues. People started reacting as there was no need for this treatment. They appear to hate tourists. I asked a member of staff from Ryanair who was walking by for some guidance on an issue and was shouted at. Never visiting Ibiza again as I do not want to endure such horrific treatment again.

The airport is a bit small for the amount of passengers it handles, that’s my impression. Boarding was through buses and we were travelling with a stroller and two infants and there wasn’t any other way to access the busses apart from stairs. It was actually difficult to carry strollers downstairs.
Shocking level of customer service during our departure on 03/06/2018. I have never seen an airport with so few staff around. The security check in process was shambolic. A dreadful experience.

Love my little home airport, Ibiza, which I fly through a few times a month. Very much the definition of a "seasonal airport." During the summer, it feels like a large European hub, albeit full of tourists and not business travellers, with flights every 5 minutes at all hours of the day. However, in the winter it becomes this sleepy island airport, with no more than 15 flights a day, almost all domestic, with only 5 or so of the 50 check in counters open. The majority of the terminal airside is closed during the winter too. The terminal has undergone a few upgrades over the last few years. It finally got unlimited, free Wifi throughout the whole terminal. A pretty decent premium lounge opened last year, as well as a number of new cafes, with a surprising number of healthier eating options. There was a strike earlier in the year from the cleaners, but that appears to be sorted out. During only the peak summer season of July and August, check in queues can be quite long, however, the airport seems to manage to keep security times down to a minimum, despite the large amount of "unseasoned travellers."

Made our annual visit to Ibiza in September. Some changes some good some bad. The good now a silent airport no plane announcement but the gates are now available on line 24hrs before and put on the boards 1 hour before departure verbal announcements happen if this changes. Plenty of seating in the departure areas and all together a pleasant airport to sit and wait for departure. The bad most arrivals are bussed to the terminal last year and previous it was a 75 yard straight to passport control now they have put in walkways and it is now about 600 yards to walk up and down for old people us not good especially when easy to adjust the straps and cut down the walking distance when little arrival traffic. Getting out similar this year now 3 funnels for customs which feed into each other creating one big bottle neck with those who are leaving it to the last minute trying to push through to the front have made what worked into a disaster. Took us an hour to get through customs and we were nearly the last plane leaving at this time.

I fly in and out of here regularly, and am very impressed. For a small airport, TSA is efficient and does not do a lot of unnecessary screening just to have something to do as at other small airports. The gate crews work very hard to get you out on-time, and luggage retrieval is easy. Rental car offices are next to baggage claim, and other than Budget, are extremely helpful. There is a coffee shop upstairs, as well as a bar/restaurant; everyone is friendly here and pricing is reasonable. Two minutes from I-15. The place seems pleasantly ignorant of airport hassles that have descended upon much of the industry.

The guards on the entrance are so rude, he would even raise voice which was unnecessary, imagine having a super early flight where you still feel sleepy & someone random would shout about the luggages. I knew what to do with it, I fly all the time and there were absolutely no need for him to be so disrespectful.

Waiting area is too far from the entrance, a lot of mosquitos in waiting area as its open, crowded too. My flight at 6:35am and I arrived long hours before my flight in which they decided to let me stay in waiting area overnight and mosquitos enjoying to eat you alive. Please do something.

Worst airport. No working aircons. Seats are occupied by bags. You can see people standing while the bags are sitting and the authorities are doing nothing. Philippines is a tropical country therefore the aircons should be maintained regularly.

Though it is small, it is one of the best efficient and beautifully designed international airports in the Philippines. Been using it when I am visiting for business and leisure, and I’m not disappointed every-time I used this airport. I do hope the government will expand this soon.
Iloilo Airport is one of the best and nicest airports that I’ve seen. Shopping store and a number of restaurants and coffee shops are also available. Really amazing.

I arrived at night so it was difficult to be as observant as during the day but baggage came off the conveyor belt within 15 minutes and I obtained a modern car with a very pleasant driver for the transfer to my city hotel the transfer costing P400 which was reasonable. Overall an airport that delivered for me on this trip.

Used this airport frequently this last year last time September 15. It is a very nice airport small manageable. Cleanliness this time was improved compared to last time facilities are good. True check-in area is rather small but with enough time before departure I could just wander to the counter and check-in straight away. There are rumours that some international airlines might consider direct flights to and from Iloilo I wish nothing more than that just to bypass Manila's terminal 1.

The airport is brand new. It opened in 2007 replacing the old and dilapidated airport in the city centre. The pre- departure lounge is spacious and clean with some pocket gardens. Full of daylight even in rainy season and the windows give a great vista of the mountains. The restaurant serves nice food although I wish the airport authorities would install free WiFi. The check-in counter is getting stuffy and quite small but the queue is still tolerable. Comfort rooms are still in good shape yet needs proper maintenance to keep it looking brand new. The arrival area during high traffic days gets a bit congested. Parking security is not a problem although the toll is quite steep for countryside standards. Accessibility is also not a problem as shuttles and cheaper mode of transportation.

The longest lines in an airport ever. The fact that we arrived 3 hours before departure and had literally not enough time to use the toilet before we boarded was a disgrace. I can't review the food or amenities as there was not enough time to access them. 1 hour in line to check in. 1 hour in line for security and checked our bags because it had a pen in it, they made us re pack our bag once they had searched it. We had to run after being made to wait in line for 2.5 hours just to get to our flight at boarding time. There were many empty check in desks too, not enough signage displaying anything. Disgraceful way the airport has been designed. Will not think about visiting Korea again if this is the airport we have to travel through.

Was subjected twice to a security check during a layover here. Absolutely rude security employees. Their lines were incredibly long and took forever. The terminals also posted easily missed handwritten posters to indicate gate changes. Wi-fi did not work for anyone surrounding me. Did they run out of garbage cans because the airport utilized loose and overflowing bags of garbage out on floors. Incredibly inefficient airport.

We flew from Singapore to Incheon airport and arrived quite late at night about 10.45 p.m. due to flight delay. Everything was OK until we arrived at Immigration counter. There were so many people lined up for a very long queue (may be up to 200 people) and the process was so slow. It took us more than 1 hour to pass immigration which we never experienced before. By the time we reteived our luggage, it was pass midnight as we waited in line for the taxi more than half an hour. We reached the hotel which luckily quite close to airport about 1 a.m. It was horrible experience. We wondered why this airport was rated very high (top 1 or 2). Terrible.

Check in had only 3 counters and they were averaging 20 minutes for a single check in, unprofessional staff causing unnecessary delays. Signs were also useless, had a sign leading to the tax refund station but ended up in front of the departure hall and couldn't find any other signs
I can understand why Incheon airport is one of the best in the world. The airport is very clean and peaceful. There were various seating options and different shops. I definitely recommend it!

The first time through this airport two weeks ago took no time to get through immigration and customs. Today, it took much longer. We had planned to make hay out of our eight-hour layover and visit Gyeongbokbung Palace. Alas, it wasn't meant to be. After immigration and customs, we went to Hanjin Express to store our carry-on luggage, only to be told there was no more space. That was the final decision point -- we were going to kill the time inside the airport. It's no joke -- this airport is only good if you want to buy designer goods and only if you want a limited brand and product selection. I footed the entire terminal from branch to branch and there is nothing that highlights Korean culture in an interesting and/or contemporary way. Don't make the same mistake. If you've got more than four hours go somewhere outside this airport. I hear there are good outlet malls nearby.

Tax refund is very hard, upon reach at counter D, it was closed, so ask you to go counter E, officer will tell you to scan thè receipts, the person there just simply using her mobile phone, you ask her and she will say I dont know and give you a black face, overall its very hard as the steps is very manual, do note that if the refund is more than KRW 80000 you have to get the customs officer to check and stamp your receipt. Most shops and restaurants are closed by 9 or 930pm -airport has a lot of renovations works so its very noisy with drilling etc -airport shops charges USD except the 711 and food court, if you want to pay KRW they will convert it but the rates is too high -ahjummas at thé chocolate shops and duty free will scold you if you ask on the products - staff are unfriendly and will scold you if you ask. Don't ever buy at the airport is much more expensive compare when you buy outside

Insane long lines through security. Very limited food and drink options, huge queues for what is actually open. Forget getting a glass of wine. People jostle over seating and the hospitality staff are anything but hospitable. Horrid place to wait for flight.

Great free wifi, very clean bathrooms, peaceful airport. But strangely rude staff at the coffee shop and Dunkin’ Donuts. I ordered a coffee and asked for a little milk or cream. The barista pointed behind me, gesturing like,“there’s the milk” but there’s nothing there. So I ask again and then he says, “it’s in there” and points at the coffee, but no milk. So I go over to the Dunkin’ Donuts and buy 2 donuts that I didn’t even want, to be polite, and then ask for a little milk or cream, and the lady immediately became quite rude. I said I would pay for it .. anyway, very strange that they’d be a jerk about giving a little milk for their nasty coffee. And maybe learn how to brew coffee that doesn’t taste like its from a gas station.

The on-arrival COVID testing process is atrocious. The app that must be used is completely worthless (in English). The app does not recognize major airports (such as Toronto, or even Canada). The instructors are nonsensical. The Incheon Airport Authority has outsourced the testing to a local hospital which has no experience. It took me 45 minutes to complete the registration. There are no staff to help. Avoid any COVID testing at the airport.

Allegiant Air changed my ticket to wheelchair assistance per my request. Told to call customer assistance in Indy and did to make sure I'd be picked up at curb because of disability. I was to be there by 6:38 and no curbside and sister went inside to get a wheelchair. She told me no one there at desk or for wheelchair assistance. Waited and attendants showed at 7:15. We, disabled customers had to stand in the check in line. Finally wheelchair asst shows and all was well until we had to wait from 7:30p.m. until 2a.m. with 1 snack voucher offered and given drinks.

Nice looking airport with lots of great vendors but TSA security check is a nightmare. TSA PreCheck only available on the A terminal side. Airlines don't make you aware of that or let you know there is a quick path from A terminal to B. TSA checks were very slow so go to your gate early

IND is one of our two main options along with CVG when flying. Both are excellent. Traveling from Indy this week reminded me why I like it. In morning and afternoon there are multiple good choices and most are reasonably priced in comparison to many other world airports, crowds are nowhere near some airports, so it is easy to move around, TSA has always been friendly and efficient unlike some airports, restrooms are generally cleaner than many other airports. We do wish there were a couple of direct flights options to Europe, but for flying domestically we like IND

The directions for the TSA PreCheck are confusing for travelers. When headed to the B concourse gates, the precheck sign points to the right and the TSA Administrative office is on the right, but closed. The sign should read that the PreCheck is on the otherside of the concourse, next to Chick-fil-A. Now, once you get to the TSA Check Point, the sign directs you to the employee entrance because someone turned it around. If the sign is in the correct direction, then travelers would know to join the amusement chains on the left. Indianapolis International, you can do better.

IND is my main hub for the last 10 years and it’s an overall very easy airport to navigate. However, I wait 45 minutes minimum every time I land here. Usually also have to wait 5-10 minutes, sitting 20 yards from the gate before anyone guides the plane in. I don’t understand how this airport continues to get awards when the basics of bag handling and logistics take so long.

5 stars every time for years and years. First time for one star. We are in B section and while waiting for our delayed flight to come in there is construction going on in the closed restaurant located in the middle of the airport. Not a little but extremely loud mechanical tools sawing through metals and wood. Dust coming over the protective walls causing coughing and eye irritation. What were they thinking. Hire a heavy metal band and throw in some flame throwers to match the noise in this airport. There was nowhere to go unless we wanted to not hear our gate screaming over the deafening madness.

Had a flight leaving late. So disappointed that everything was already closed. Ridiculous! The only food available was a snack machine that didn’t work. Thank goodness the bartender at The Fan Zone bar, which should have closed at 9pm, stayed open for a sizeable number of us travelers. No restaurant, Hudson store, candy shop - nothing - open. Can’t one or two places stay open at least until 10pm?

Literally everything closes at 8pm. No food. No drink. I have never seen anything like this. Terrible. I would have eaten before arriving to the airport if I had known this was such a barren wasteland.

8:30 P.M. on a Monday night, no restaurants open (other than fast food). No beer/wine/cocktails available in the whole airport, even outside of security. I just busted my butt working for four days at my elderly parent's yard and flying home sore, but happy to have spent time with them. Four days of hard labor vacation and I can't relax with a beer and a burger.
Horrendous treatment by TSA on March 18, 2022. I would not fly out of here again. Extremely rude, unfriendly and unhelpful.

Arrival at Innsbruck was faultless no complaints. Departure was a nightmare, arrived at the time requested and found one desk open for Easyjet. Waited and got to the front only to be told they couldn't do the Manchester flight, go to the back of the que. Eventually a couple more desks opened and we eventually got through to security. Only one desk open, When I got to the front there was only one male security guy and he was pre occupied with a bloke who had blagged his way to the front of the que by claiming broken ribs (I don't think so!). All males had to wait until the security man finished. Got into the departure lounge, 1 small bar doing re heated pizza and drinks staffed by an understandably fed up young girl. Not worth waiting so went to passport control and waited for ages, got a bus for the 10 yard journey to the plane. I have used Innsbruck airport for over 30 years but stopped because it was under staffed and too small for the flights they are taking. They have learned nothing, I have been using Munich for the last 10 years but Lufthansa have gone useless so tried Innsbruck - never never again. Easyjet to Munich in future.

The common them with Austrian Airports is they are small overcrowded and the shop is an absolute rip off. Innsbruck is as bad as Salzburg. We flew business and yet again the lounge was full. It’s like stepped no back in time. Security slow, passport control was a reasonable pace as there were plenty of border control officers. Birding on a bus to travel 150 yards is a joke. Bad for the environment and gives yet more poor customer experience. Don’t get me wrong I love Austria and the Austrian people, but for goodness sake sort your airports out.

Airport is small but functional. Clean toilets, and security is taken seriously. We could not check in online but went through COVID verification and were questioned if we were staying in another EU country for more than 90 days. The airport police also gave warnings to people who did not wear their masks. Repeat offenders were told they will be asked to leave the airport. This is impressive - first time seeing mask regulations treated seriously in EU. For some strange reason though, we were kept on the bus for quite a while prior embarking the plane.

Small airport we used to fly to ski places. But, the place is too sensitive to weather conditions, and we missed our connection flight in Frankfurt due to long delay in our flight. There are not enough places to sit while you wait so many hours, and not enough places for eating or drinking. My recommendation is to take a train from big airport to the ski places instead of flying to Innsbruck.

The worst airport I have ever experienced! There is no luggage storage possibility, which was not highlighted on the website, no proper waiting area, extremely poor customer service (works more like public administration), poor food and entertainment. Long waiting times at check-in counters, slow security clearance and overall facilities not fit for international tourism. Biggest regret.

Very limited and poor options airside. I would expect a lot better from a city such as Innsbruck. Also the man at the food counter was extremely rude. I do not expect to be spoken to that way, he had no customer service skills.

This airport is one of those that is probably lovely 95% of the time and a disaster the other 5%. Unfortunately I got the 5%. Its tiny and cant handle large amounts of luggage or passengers. An absolute free-for all at baggage reclaim with people standing 6 deep by the tiny carousel and then nowhere for them to go once getting luggage. They eventually opened up the red 'to declare' channel and just let everyone exit out that way to reduce the crowding. On the return nightmare queues to the doors at the limited check-in desks and many people ended up sitting on the stairs blocking them once through security as nowhere to sit. One café air side with a long queue. Its convenient but you have been warned.

Travelled late July. Arriving from Edinburgh late afternoon found the airport quiet. Standing at the back of a long line for passport control I thought we could in for a long wait. But they virtually waved the entire plane load through in around 3 minutes! By which time the luggage had already arrived. So we were out of the airport within 5 minutes. I've never known anything like it. On the way back there were several flights delayed due to a storm. However everything still worked well for our flight and we departed on time. Not a big airport but I was happy with my time there.

Travelled late March/early April. Completely empty extremely clean overlooking the runway walking distance from town check-in queue was non existent for me (travelling to London). Car hire is fine quality food available but all very cosy and empty of huge hordes of people! The best airport I've been too.

Arriving on January 28th no problems. The baggage arrived quickly and we were soon on our way. Nothing could have prepared us for the departure however. It was a nightmare. The baggage check-in took a long time - only 3 desks for an Airbus A332 with nearly 300 passengers. The plane was delayed one hour but that didn't seem to help. It took us nearly an hour in a completely disorganised "queue". The check-in assistants had no sense of urgency chatted amongst themselves and couldn't even manage to put 4 people on the same booking in the same part of the plane! At security it was utter chaos - more than an hour in a crush everyone trying to get to the front and in to one of the two security bay in order to catch their planes. Looking at the reviews here and comments from staff at the airport it would appear that this has been going on for years! It was intolerable and potentially unsafe - one person in our huddle (it could in no sense be described as a queue) fainted. I shall avoid holidays based on Innsbruck airport in the future.

Such a small airport but somehow it was still amazing. The staff were incredibly nice it's not very busy. I do think it does need a few more shops, there was a fair variety of places to eat. I've never really had an issue with delay we have been delayed a few times but not for very long. The flight attendants were kind and the landing was smooth. Overall I personally think that it was a magnificent airport and it is very underrated.

We flew into Inverness on a Monday and were the only flight arriving at the time. The luggage took so long to arrive that people burst into a sarcastic round of applause when it eventually came through. Then on the following Friday our 19.20 flight had an estimated departure time of 20.15 despite being on the tarmac really early. When we queried this we were told by three separate staff that there was no problem and the flight would be on time. Sure enough the bag drop opened early and despite a technical fault at the gate we were fully loaded only a few minutes late. Then, together with two other planes we were held on board until - you've guessed it - 20.15. This was because traffic control was short-staffed and that was the reason for the late departure on the airport screens. Why are travellers kept in the dark and treated like this? No announcements, no explanations and not even the pleasant guy on security seemed aware of what was happening.

I fly into Inverness a couple of times a year, lovely staff in the shops and cafe’s. The security staff, however are a different story, they are rude, aggressive and clearly unable to cope with busier periods. They need customer service training. I understand they have a job to do but there is no need to be rude.

Passing through security I was told to remove my braces, I mentioned that I was using them to hold up my trousers, the man replied that he was not joking, so with some hesitation removed them and subsequently the said trousers fell down. I have done in the past a number of international flights and domestic and have never been asked to do this before. I was really embarrassed trying to find somewhere to put them on again. On having declared that I was using them and also showing them also would be enough! Where is the discretion by the security staff, I felt that they quite enjoy seeing people in uncomfortable circumstances. I do fully understand the reason behind this to make sure the flights our flights safe.

A nice small airport that can be very congested in Departures, fine when it is quiet, a nice cafe in main hall, overlooking the runway, with comfy chairs, and a few nice shops to browse. Worst point - the staff, unhelpful and mean spirited. I had to wait 40 minutes to make a free ticket change with Logan Air because the young lad, on the desk could not sort it out and was very lacking in his customer care and communication. While I was waiting a lovely man arrived late for his flybe Birmingham flight, he had left his bag with documents at home and had to return for them, the Birmingham flight was delayed over 30 mins, a member of staff tried to help by phoning through to departures but flybe / staff refused to help, there was no one on the flybe check in desk, he was told to get a later Manchester flight and travel on to Birmingham. After all this, I got my ticket change, went straight through security as not busy and was gutted to see the Birmingham flight only just being called for boarding, poor man, they could so easily have let him through, it was not at all busy and staff were just standing chatting at the boarding gate, very mean and causes so much inconvenience and extra expense to someone because the staff can't be bothered to help. The beauty of a smaller airport should be more personal care and help, sadly not so at Inverness.

I have travelled through many airports in my life. But never have I been left feeling so penalised, disrespected as I did travelling through Inverness airport. The security staff are extremely rude, they treat you like you're an inconvenience to them. Even after getting past the security part we had to then endure an incredibly rude woman who bullied us about our hand luggage before we got on the plane, I do hope that the inverness management review how they treat their customers.

Very disappointed with the security at Inverness, in fact it soured what was a wonderful trip to the Highlands and Isle of Lewis. We only had carry on luggage and had no trouble flying out of Amsterdam to Inverness but the return was not as good. I had culled my cosmetics before I went and was complimented in Amsterdam on what I had done as they were all well under 100mls. When going thru Inverness was told I should have in clear plastic bag even though my cosmetics bag was see through. When I put in 2 bags was told it all had to go in one bag. When I queried this a supervisor came over and told me I had to comply and throw things out. I did but then I saw I was selected for a full body scan and search and actually saw them talk about me. A women sent me back a couple of times and exaggerated her search. I am a 72 year old. I understand rules are rules but the attitude was what I h ad a problem with. If they thought they could embarass me they did not and really only demonstrated their petty ignorance. The bad attitude of staff should be addressed.

Unscheduled visit to this fantastic little airport. Staff member on the front desk helped me with my bags right through to departures (I have broken my wrist), can’t thank her enough for great customer service. Then through to feel spoiled in the aspires lounge by the host with the most. Brilliant service, I shall definately return to this super place again.

It's always a pleasure to be able to fly into my home City airport of Dalcross. However, on three separate occasions this month my views have changed some what. No suitable infrastructure for the increase in passenger volumes. On two occasions only one security x-ray machine working as the other had broken down (for departing BA, KLM, BE flights) resulting in 45 minute queues with no management of the situation whatsoever. Chaos at check in as they could not cope with the volume of bags being checked in resulting in that breaking down. On arrival into Dalcross on the way home for a visit, bags put on wrong carousel (there are only two in the airport). It's a shame, could be such a nice airport however extemely poor management with no advise or announcements given on any of these occasions, with no taking charge of the situation. Come on HIAL, get your act together!

❌Not Verified|  Departed Inverness airport on May 7th. Queues for security were extremely long because only one scanner was working. We joined the queue at about 11.50am for a scheduled boarding of 12.05pm but were still waiting in the queue at 12.15pm. Airport staff asked if there were any passengers for Heathrow but didn't do anything to hasten our transit through the security. It was pouring with rain but no covered walkway to the aircraft. I asked why only one scanner was working and was told it was being worked on as we speak. Despite the fact that I had already intimated that our flight was due to depart security insisted on testing my carry on liquids. Unfortunately when you live in the Highlands your choice of airport is limited.

Such a poor experience. Quiet airport most of the day then three take offs within 15 minutes in mid afternoon. This Airport cant handle a wave of 500 plus people. Queuing out of the door to pay an "enhance customer experience" development fee of ten euro ? A complete rip off.

Small clean airport - easy to get round, however... you are forced to pay with zero exception a 10 euro per passenger development fee - so travelling as a family you are rinsed for 30 euro so that they can supposedly build a new runway or improve security- however zero work was being done so where does this money go I wonder? Clearly the only airline flying today RyanAir refused to pay and so lumps the passengers with it, I'll not be flying from here again and I wouldn't have flown via here if I knew that when booking my ticket - clearly Ryan Air keep that a nice little secret.

This airport is a rip off, you and all the members of your party will be charged, (including children) will be charged €10 extra at the departure gate in addition to the ticket price. Also it's in the middle of nowhere, and no bus services go to it. Dublin airport for us next time. I'd advise all travellers to give it a wide berth.

This airport is so backward its unreal. Today you get charged nearly three euros to get hot water for your own teabag. You get charged ten euros development fee as you leave. Same as Galway airport ten years ago, six euros to get out (again development fee) now its shut! Last time I flew from Knock the fee was the same. Never went back because of the fee. Now the place has hardly changed, where did that money go. Great idea to put an airport on top of a hill (don't have to come down so far) but hardly a great advert for Irish aviation or Mayo.

What an absolute rip-off! A stealth payment at the point before passing security. I can't believe the airport can legally extort money from passengers like this before they are allowed to fly. Haven't we already paid airport taxes with our ticket? When I booked our ticket, I was never informed about this stealth payment. I asked the woman at the desk why it wasn't already in the ticket and her answer "We are unable to make the airlines do it". What absolute rot. You know how many passengers pass through your airport, if the airlines want to land there, they know the fees. When I again contested the payment, the response was "Do you want to fly?" Its pure blackmail. This stinks of an airport in a third world country or one run by a dictatorship. If they need the money that desperately, good luck!

It's hard not to love this gem of an airport. Everyone is helpful and friendly even the security staff! From touch down to getting on the road can be done in 10 minutes. The only puzzle to me is why there are hardly any road signs to the airport on the roads leading to it, why the mystery? There is a fee to pay on exiting which is a pain but seems to me to be well spent in updating the facilities for passengers

This is the second time I have used Knock. It is a bit out of the way and coach connections are not very good. But the timings of flights suited me better than the ones on offer to Shannon or Dublin so I used Knock. My flight yesterday was the last time ever. They do charge a departure tax of 10 euro which I had no idea about until I got there. Annoying but you can put up with this. This time I had to spend three hours in the departure lounge as coaches were either arriving too early or too late to catch flight. Never mind I thought I can relax. They are doing repair work in the departure lounge which is minute. The noise was horrendous. Walls were being knocked down, sawing, hammering etc. All in a small area and three groups of workers spread around the room. All wearing ear protection so they were really enjoying themselves making as much noise as they could it seemed. I asked if there was anywhere quiet we could sit and a staff member told me "we have to put up with this all day. Try the bar". The bar a small area in one corner. So not much help there. I have tried to find who to complain to but no one seems interested. My point is my flight was the last one of the day: 19.25. So they had many hours when work could be done to not inconvenience travellers. It is a very small area where everyone sits. The food selection is the worst I have seen so all in all a miserable three hours. Never again I have two other airports to use both have been good in the past. Passengers have a choice and my choice is never to use Knock again. I warn anyone else to think again. Staff seem fed up and Ireland has such a brilliant reputation for their hospitality it is a great shame.

Terrible sneaky fee sprung on us at the end. Would never have dreamt of checking if I had to pay to leave an airport. Like other reviewers, I expect to pay everything upfront when I book, and it's not just a couple of quid either, it's £10 per person, which adds up to a very hefty fee if there's a few of you. There were 7 of us, £70 to leave an airport! We're backpackers and we travel on a budget, sneaky, sly fees like this just aren't what we expect. Bus stop is also woefully inadequate in rainy weather. Based on those two things, would not use this airport again and would advise others not too.

I was not expecting that I would be forced to pay extra fees at the airport. Like any other airport I used so far, the ticket included all the charges. This was a nasty suprise, should not be allowed - any airport fees should be part of airport taxes and included in the overall price of flight. Otherwise you are being misled about the flight cost, in my case given we were a family of 5 an additional 50 euros could have meant we decided to fly from Dublin instead. In principal I find this practice very dishonest and will avoid flying from Knock again if for no other reason but not to support sneakiness and dishonesty.

Arrived on Windy Wednesday (19th Sept) and am one of your bus travellers. My experience of the bus shelter is always a cold piercing wind. One has just got to look where it is located within the airport grounds. The construction of glass panels with surround umpteen gaps (like surround sound of howling and whistling) makes for a very unpleasant time! In particular on Windy Wednesday we had to wait a long time because our bus had been held up because of a fallen tree. We were frozen but had to remain there in case the delayed bus arrived. Also, nobody came out to see if we were okay. So why isn't the money we pay to get out of Knock used to redesign the shelter?!

This ugly block is straight out of Stalin's era although a new terminal is going up alongside. The old one is tatty. Two gates A & B. A few little shops a bar and no smoking inside. VIP's are called earlier than other travellers and in my case to a different gate. Keep your eyes peeled. I tried my Skyteam Platinum card on the VIP gate and it worked. The VIP lounge plumbs new depths. Seedy styling and furniture with a peeling linoleum floor and no smoking there either. And you have to pay for everything even a coffee but the range of food and drink is quite reasonable. Still we did get our own minibus to the aircraft and we got on first. To be fair the folks around the place are friendly enough.

Worst airport...unnecessary long waiting time for collection of luggage, take necessary action to unload the plane quickly to facilitate the passengers who are already tired of long journey. Besides this, they need to travel further to reach their final destination. No hope for any correction or immediate action. Futile to raise voice however just write it here in frustration and to show how overseas Pakistani’s are treated in their beloved home country. Keep it up.

The toilet attendants don’t clean the toilets. They are lazy and just want money. A few times they have even stopped putting paper in the loos and handing out sheets this is not acceptable. The plumbing has being done incorrectly as there is a bad smell in the toilets. The mirrors are cracked and the locks on the stalls are ones you would use on an outside gate. Why use cheap tiles when Pakistan is full of cheap marble? No class in this country. Hiring people of low class to clean toilets is a joke they don’t bleach or clean anything because they are so low class. I dread to think how rubbish this airport will be in few years time as maintenance isn’t a word that doesn’t exist in Pakistan. The upstairs lounge is a rip off it has a disgusting brown carpet. The food is a joke the price has been doubled so isn’t worth it at all. There is only one loo which is ridiculous did the people who designed this rubbish lounge never visit a lounge any other airport?
Excellent experience at this airport. Not just departing but upon arrival as well. Very smooth, quick, organised and excellent staff. Look forward to returning soon.

I can't believe how bad the system is at the most important airport of one of the biggest Muslim countries in the world. They airport management should hold their heads in shame as they do not know who to organise a small crowd. How to prioritise different flights. How to train staff. How to stop corruption at the airport which goes on openly in front of your eyes. I was coming back to UK from Islamabad end of March 2022 and got to the airport 3 hours before. There were hundreds of people queuing outside the international departure lounge. There were 4 queues but there were only two doors open where two ASF staff were casually checking the documents and letting people in with sense of urgency. There were no barriers / cones or anything to manage the queues except one man shouting at the back of the queues. Near the gates, all 4 queues were merging into 2 and there were angry people arguing with each other. Some people from the airport staff and queues were coming out and taking "some travelers" to one side and then taking them in from different doors. I waited patiently in the queue for 2 hours before I managed to get inside the airport building. As soon as you get inside, then there were 4 massive queues on the baggage check and again there was no system at all. I was told that there were 4 international flights that night that is why it was busy. But the airport management did not bother to prioritise the passengers according to the times of their flights. Again some of the airport staff were bringing people forward at the front of the queue and their luggage was checked before all of those people who were queuing. After an hour nearly in the queue, I got my luggage through and security check done. But, by the time I got to the check in desk, one man sitting there, talking to someone on his mobile, told me and 20 other people that the check in desk is close and we have missed our flight. I tried to tell him that I have already checked in online and I have the seat number etc but he couldn't care less. People were so upset and angry and he just got up and disappeared somewhere in the hall. Our flight was at 3.05am. We got to the desk at 2.25am and the plane did not fly till 3.45am. Then we were told to go to "Customer Service Desk" if we want to talk to someone and complain. That "Customer service desk" was a joke and nothing else. All of the people who missed the flight went there and the man there, with his arms folded resting on his chair, just saying ok you all have missed the flight, it is your fault. If you all want to complain, here is the register, write down your complain and it would be looked at by someone. In the meanwhile there is nothing I can do to help with your flight. There were some people with children. Some people came from a long distances and they sent their families back home after they were dropped off at the airport because they were there 4 hours before the flight. Now they had to find some kind of transport to take them home at 4am in the morning. I am ashamed that there is so much corruption and mismanagement and lack of humanity in the country and at our airports especially in the capital of the country. I am ashamed that how could they do this to their fellow human beings and still call themselves Muslims. I am ashamed to tell people why I have missed my flight.

It's really an embarrassing experience, as a Pakistani I have no words as to how the staff at Islamabad Airport can take advantage of vulnerable people for a bit of 'extra' money. I may not be the only one who went through this experience. I travelled with my family and we had 2 people who required wheelchair service. Upon arrival to the Departure section, I asked a fellow staff member for assistance to show me where the Helpdesk was so I could get those wheelchairs. This gentleman helped us to check in and showed us the way and as he was about to leave us with 2 other men to push those wheelchairs to our flight, he demanded money for the 'service'. What is this?? Does this man not get paid for his job? And what's worse is that those two men took us to the waiting room and as we waited those 2 men kicked up a fuss and also demanded money for their 'service'? What in the world is going on here? They refused to take my 2 family members (on the wheelchair) to board the flight until we paid them a certain sum of money? This is beyond embarrassing, how can anyone ask a disabled person for money for the service? I am seriously concerned about the staff wage here, something is not right. Islamabad staff all get paid wages so why are they making a fuss for extra money? What is the purpose of their role anyway, I don't think they know. We as customers shouldn't be paying your staff wage money for services. Islamabad please take pride in your service and stop this 'begging for tips' nonsense, it is absolutely humiliating. My family members did not ask for their disability, and if it is an issue for your staff to do their basic job then I don't think they are right for the role. Please sort your Team, Islamabad airport will sink if your staff do not have basic principles to follow.

At last Pakistan has an airport worthy of being a Capital City airport. Very well designed, with excellent drop off points. Excellent flow of passengers although I do wonder if the queues would be very long at busy times as its a single double door entry. All the checks and security are now excellent, with polite and attentive staff and a great spaced out airport. Toilets clean and well serviced. Signs, plentiful and useful. Needs more commercial shops and food facilities but otherwise I loved it.

Worst airport in all respects. Completed recently but very poor build quality with things already breaking down. Floors uneven, wood lamination splitting apart tiles breaking just after a year uncomfortable seats no duty free shop. Felt sad seeing it. Loks like corruption had driven down quality, all work shoddy.

It was an awful experience. When we first landed in Islamabad we went through to the arrivals section which in comparison to the old airport is alot better. We had gone through security despite there being around 9 separate desks but only 2 being open at 1 time. We had our young daughter with us who had a long flight which didn't help. When we got through we went down to the baggage reclaim area and picked up our suitcases. There are no signs to tell you where to pick up prams and after all the passengers had left we had someone come up to us and say prams are down there nearly an hour after we had been waiting. On our way back there were 2 separate security sections which is stupid for what they are doing one after and one before check in. We had 0.75 kg extra which we were made to take out and put into hand luggage despite me pleading to leave this as it would be difficult to travel with my daughter. He insisted it had to come out and had to give it to my family outside and go through this gazillion security screenings. I had taken a vase through security who began questioning me over it as they said it was crystal. In the end they found it was glass so allowed me to take it through. We came to the airport 2 hours and 50 minutes before our flight and managed to get through this whole debacle only leaving us 20 minutes to get to the gate! The immigration lines were huge and we had joked with the immigration officer that 'they keep putting flights at the same time' Again only 2 desks open of over 10. The staff just don't care. They want money from you for nothing so keep you wallets sealed and you'll face the issue I faced but if you pay them then you'll get through. I won't give them a single penny of my hard earned money for their ill gotten gains. I can only summarise by saying if I had no family in Pakistan I would never go back to this country. Honestly I feel ashamed to call myself a Pakistani and be linked to the country and the people of the airport. Just because they have a new clean airport doesn't mean the people have changed.

Worst service I have ever seen in my entire life! Had to wait for 3hrs at the carousel for my baggage to arrive (I'm told workers were slacking off) and didn't see my bags until a senior officer had come to get the baggage moving! Unfriendly staff who don't even wish to communicate with passengers unless you incorrectly use an aircrew term where they are most happy to correct you and then snigger about it and then once again act like you're non-existent. Well, at least that informed me that they are not deaf but clearly ignoring me! Porters in uniform are helpful and kindly directed me too. Beware of Taxi drivers and ununiformed porters; my baggage was forcibly snatched by one these to 'help' me to the domestic flight departures.

Massive improvement in airport and staff. Very clean, public facilities are well maintained. Staff are a bit friendlier now and fewer queues on departure and arrival security/immigration clearance due to having extra staff on counters. Just need a few more shops in the terminal.

Really, really poor, really rude staff. As a very small airport you expect quaint with little service options, but this had nothing. They clearly have no idea about making things covid safe, obsessively sanitising things (which has little transmission effect) but there was no ventilation in any of the rooms and they were forcing people to go through security and into one tidy and poorly ventilated room more than 45 mins than was necessary. Not good.

I flew into this airport on Islay island from Glasgow on a Loganair flight in the morning and returned almost a week later. This is a rural airport, close by the sea, and is extraordinarily easy to use. The SAAB 340 aircraft was parked close to the small terminal building - we picked up our bags that had been unloaded on the tarmac and walked in. The walls were decorated with posters of the many distilleries for which Islay is justly famed. There were also individual displays of whisky bottles and other items from these distilleries. A small cafe provided a good range of snacks and also some souvenirs for last moment purchases. There were ample spaces to sit. A short conveyor belt brought in checked luggage quickly. Across the check in counters are kiosks for the local car hires. I had a car to be picked up. The agent had all the paperwork ready. The car was parked just outside. I was out of the airport grounds, driving on the left, in less than 10 minutes after landing. On my departure, I parked my rental car across the terminal building and slipped the keys into a slot in the kiosk. The check in counters were staffed by Logan Air personnel in their uniforms that sported the easily recognized tartan plaids. Security check was very thorough, including patting. The waiting area after security check had a rest room and was enclosed by glass which offered panoramic views. The aircraft was just outside and we walked to to it. It was a very relaxed experience with a high degree of friendliness and efficiency. The airport is situated midway between the island's two larger communities - Bowmore and Port Ellen.

Absolute shambles. Closed the runway as we were taxying the runway due to staff shortage. Only 1 set of steps which led to a delay loading the plane. I have never arrived or departed this airport on time or had so many cancelled flights. We was looking to move here but until the airport shambles is fixed I'll stay in London.

The staff are very friendly. The queue times for checkin and security are almost always very short or non existent making for a very smooth, fast and pleasant experience all the way to boarding. For such a small airport there are also a good amount of amenities, ample seating and it is always clean.
Security needs a lot of work, staff rude, the queue is longer than in Manchester. Very disorganised and not a nice experience. For a small airport it has no personality at all.

Absolutely appalling, security was a joke and rude, The Loganair reception staff wasn't much better, not only with there " I don't care attitude and the sniggering when they watched an old couple trying to get the correct weight in luggage.

Security agents were extremely abrupt and rude. They screened me for drugs/explosive material residue testing randomly even though every one else went through with no issues. I had my hand luggage swabbed. I doubt I'd come back.

Security was an absolute nightmare, I felt I was treated like a criminal, was told that all my creams, toothpaste, perfume, gels and my medicine had to fit in a 1 ltr bag, I had to put somethings in the bin. Everything in my handbag was emptied out my wallet was went through and even my personal sanitary items were swabbed. My carry-on bag and it’s contents were also swabbed. The security guard was even going to have the prescription medication analysed only for his supervisor to step in, it was a most distressing experience to go through. For all of the public outcry about security in Dublin airport I would give them 10/10 for the way they treated me on my outgoing flight.

Security was a nightmare. We were treated like criminals, bossed around and spoken to in an unacceptably abrupt manner. I've travelled a lot and never been told I was allowed only one plastic bag for liquids: where on earth has that rule come from? And the lady who checked my offending case was a total jobsworth, who took for ever to do the job. No concern for an elderly disabled passenger....I could go on! A disgrace!

Arrived in plenty of time to drop bag and go through security and the airline staff were very efficient. The queue that had built up at security was really long so there was a big wait, still plenty of time. I was really sad to hear how the staff spoke to everyone in the queue and this was topped off by a further "shoe check" (no problem with checks at all) but a faulty machine caused an alarm, which caused a retest and eventually after leaving lots of time, I had to rush through. I'm not normally an anxious traveller but this was the worst airport security experience I have encountered. I also heard another lady being spoken to very abruptly and told that if she missed her flight it wasn't their problem. No reassurance at all. Bit of a let down to the airport as the rest seemed nice from what I saw.

I travel through the airport four times every week. There is a strange combination of helpful efficiency and friendliness from staff, and then appalling rudeness and inefficiency from a few individuals who seem to rejoice in being officious and unhelpful. Today, most notably the gentleman at the entrance to the security queue was particularly obnoxious. with four flights boarding and departing wIthin a short space of time, only 50% of the scanning facility was operating. Delays were over 40 minutes. It’s a shame this wonderful island is occasionally let down by poor organisation and some rude staff.

The airport in general was great with no queues, clean and helpful staff at security. One negative point was the disgusting manners of the shop assistant in the duty free shop. (Sunday lunchtime) After having a wonderful weekend in the Isle of Man with nothing but friendliness this rudeness was disappointing for our way home.

The whole associate i encountered with, was super rude, not helpful. I almost missed my flight trying to figure out where I'm going. Not even anyone had time to to stop and list to my question - ridiculous. I am super disappointed that a whole airport that every country transit can not train or employ people that can speak and understand a little beat of English. It quite unfortunate. This is my second time encounting this situation and I am very disappointed.

Worst airport, even worse staff. Only 4 immigration officers catering to a long queue of customers and taking their own sweet time as if their job is much more important than you.  My parent's arrived at 11.05am. They got out at 2.30pm. Is this even logical?

I'm flying 50-60 times a year in average. This must be the worst airport I've been to. 4 different places to check your bag. 6 times answering same questions about my trip to get safety stamps with just different colour. Queuing all the time, arrival to gate took more than 80 minutes. On top of it, prices for everything are ridiculous, 15$ for a small beer. Really? Staff not very friendly either. Never again.

Ridiculous prices on everything. Tired staff. Will avoid or bring my own food and drink in the future. Tax free more expensive than with taxes for many things. Perfume store without any spray deodorant for men. Generic design. Too bad as flight with Turkish was good.

The biggest trap for the tourists worldwide, one Big Mac 25 euros and a bag of pistachio 76 euros. Staff doesn't speak English, there is not Duty Free Shops. The airport is chaotic and be prepared to walk kilometers. Free wifi is complicated and you cannot access, except if you will scan your passport.

Fast food price is just ridiculously expensive! Went to a fried chicken restaurant only to find out that their price has gone way too much for an average traveller. I checked other restaurants and snack bars to compare prices and their prices have increased. How can customers enjoy the airport when they are prevented from spending due to prohibitive prices? I missed the Old Istanbul Airport when the airport was more inclusive rather exclusionary than what I experienced. My partner also transited here and was surprised that there was no pharmacy inside the transit terminal. Although I love flying with Turkish Airlines, I will probably not do it for a long time as Istanbul Airport has been a rip-off for me.

This airport is luxury and new! However, there are multiple issues that needs to be addressed. The number of toilets for such a busy airport is ridiculously low and more importantly very very dirty! I couldn’t find any clean cabin during my visit which was very disgusting!  The airport staff is somehow very unhappy and angry. Staff should be kind and accommodating. The prices are also very expensive compared to other international airports. I feel that this airport doesn’t represent Turkey well.

Arrived just before midnight with TA from KRK and was surprised with a 5hrs delay of my flight to Hong Kong. The airport facilities are subpar in comparison to Zurich or even Helsinki which I could have chosen as alternative transit for the same journey. So called "nap zone" is far from comfortable when you're drilling the walls past midnight. No matter how many dining and shopping options provided, you can't call it a world-class airport if they don't get the basics right for such circumstances, that is a comfortable lounge with reclined chairs.
