It's all utterly useless and irrelevant to a passenger who transiting at midnight and expecting to spend a whole night at the airport when they are drilling the walls around past midnight. Signages are confusing. Flight status boards displayed in local language only?? Not the way to go Turkiye.

Be prepared to walk kilometers, in an unfriendly environment. Get ready to pay a fortune for a bottle of water or an orange juice. Get ready to cross endless commercial zones looking like Las Vegas. Free wifi lasts only for one hour. Horrible experience. And this is a new airport! Whfy didn't the fire the architects immediately?

Beautiful new architecture doesn’t make up for an airport’s miserable customer service. Upon arrival security officers shooed me away from several busy passport control areas before I found one where I could get in line after a very long walk. Lufthansa lost my bag. Dealing with Celebri, their baggage handler, was a dragged out, exhausting ordeal. I had no communication from them after making lost bag claim for more than 48 hours. Phones were not answered and calls not returned after leaving messages three times. Bag was finally located four days later, when I had boarded ship for Viking cruise but was still in port. The Lufthansa baggage service, Celebri, refused to deliver my bag to cruise ship at the port or release it to Viking representative at airport. Celebri made me return to airport in person to claim my bag. The airport is a LONG ride from town. Celebri is hidden in a secure area and can only be reached by a telephone by an unmanned information kiosk. Celebri employee who answered phone said she was eating lunch and would come out to help me in ten minutes. Multiple other travelers showed up, called Celebri and were given various snarky answers as to when a representative would come out to help us. It was more than 30 minutes later when a surly young man came out and guided us back to the secure area. The only answer I was given for why I had to claim my bag in person was “Customs.” After four days without my suitcase, being forced to retrieve it in person at the airport was an abusive four hour descent into a hell of rude, indifferent Celebri employees in an airport that is already not passenger friendly. They didn’t just ruin my day, they ruined my vacation by treating me like garbage. I strongly advise NOT checking a bag if you are flying to Istanbul.

Likely the worst airport on the planet, I managed to avoid it for several years, but unfortunately had two long layovers here again this year. Overcrowded, dirty, hot and smelly. They probably have a rigorous process in place to ensure they only employ the rudest, most arrogant people for every single position available at this airport. Fancy a 24 EUR lukewarm bottle of beer or a 17 EUR stale croissant while you wait in line at the airline helpdesk where nobody will ever help you? SAW airport is for you then. This place is a joke.

First of all I don't understand how all the airport employees don't understand a word of English, their car parking is a huge scam the sign shows one price however you will get charged almost triple the price if you did not read the extremely fine print in Turkish language at the bottom of the sign. All I can say it an obvious scam. and that's the last time I am using this airport.

From the first minute you will find yourself struggling to breathe, crowded, rude, angry faces, distances between toilets and lifts and gates are crazy.  Incredibly expensive, around 3 euros for the smallest water bottle - food is very expensive, queues everywhere , toilets are dirty, it might look better definitely if less busy.

Nothing inspiring about this airport at all. Dull, overcrowded and expensive. Arriving and transfer to Istanbul. I gather trains and buses are expensive and infrequent. So there's taxis Firstly, like restaurant menus, there is a local price and a tourist price. Get into a taxi and you're snared. The journey to the city centre is some distance and the trip can take anything from 40 mins to 2 hours depending on the traffic, so the taxi driver will be able to 'justify' the cost. We paid €55 for each trip by private taxi organised by the hotel. Seemed reasonable. Top tip. As the passport queues, when arriving, are the usual length (v long) , avoid logging on the airport WiFi to update the taxi people until you're through, as the connection only lasts 30 minutes. Phone package was £7 a day if that's an alternative for you. Departing You have to join the queue to get your bags and self scanned....so you can join the next queue to get your bags and self scanned - again. Not that anyone seemed too diligent in inspecting the screens. Once through, there aren't enough seats and there's no water fountains anywhere. What we thought was enough lire to buy a couple of drinks and a snack each , was actually just enough for the former. Again, the 'free' WiFi lasts just 30 minutes, but there's loads of machines around to buy more time. Don't know how much but lengthy queues at all of them. Expect to be searched and wand - scanned again at the boarding gate

I feel like these people at airport are briefed to be the worst image of the country. I asked 8 people about some information or information desk. All of them gave me wrong directions and some even said we don't know. When I appraised police man at the airport, he insulted me by saying to step away from him and wait 10 feet away until he finishes his call. This made me hate the country and it's people. This is by far the worst and most irresponsible staff I have ever came across. And for Wifi you need to queue at a machine to get a code that works for 30 minutes. I found so many exhausted people and angry people.

Coke at Champagne Prices. I went through this Airport in transit between Sharjah and Manchester. Couldn't find any water fountains so I bought 2 x 500 ml bottles of coke - price £13. I know low cost airlines use this airport, but in some cases the drinks can be more expensive than the flights. Didn't spend long enough in the airport to look around much, but the toilets were grubby and the general feeling was of a 3rd world airport. I suppose you get what you pay for - low air fares and expensive and poor airport infrastructure.

Extremely bad climate control. Bad in many aspects. Crowded Rude and unrespectful security and passport control. Prices in restaurants, free shops and any merchandise price in the airport is extremely high. A simple sandwich will cost you 25-30€ Free shops are charging you much higher than the product cost you anywhere else on this planet. I'm shocked that this is allowed to happen and airport authorities allowing this. Be careful and keep this in mind.

Terrible airport! Slow check in (no machines), slow immigration (& confusing). Food & drunk expensive & not a great selection. Free wifi for 30 minutes only. Worst of all nowhere to fill water bottles; if you’re going to take water away at security at least provide somewhere to fill bottles. I avoid buying single use plastic bottles.
Airport security check is overcrowded, prices are very high. They cut free internet every 30 minutes. City shuttle bus too expensive and not frequent.
One of the worst experience i had. Long queues, staff doesn't speak English and rude behaviour, working slowly. Signs were not that helpful. The wifi doesn't work, boarding gates were too far.

Most northern airport in Finland and in the EU. It serves northern Lapland and nearby Saariselkä ski resort and usually handles only daily flights to Helsinki and some European charter flights during winter time, so terminal isn't very big. It includes couple of shops and a cafe with minimal hassle and quite relaxed atmosphere. Check-in, security and luggage on arrival are all handled fast unless there happens to be several flights coming or going at the same time. You can rent a car, take a taxi or jump into a bus from the airport.

Flying Izmir to Ercan. The International section is Very clean and modern. Quick and efficient passenger service from checkin through passport control and all the way to boarding. It’s always a pleasure to use Izmir Adnan Menderes airport for arrivals and departures internationally. The duty free shops are spacious and have many shopping options. The toilets are clean and stocked. I have no complaints always hassle-free flying out and through Izmir. The Wi-Fi is also a bonus very fast and user friendly to access.

The prices for food and drinks are eye watering. The duty free prices are higher than our high street shop prices. They have the worst WIFI of any airport I have ever been to. You can't get on it for love nor money. Shame really. Its a lovely airport.

I was travelling back to London Stansted on the 10th of October 2020, my mother had surgery in Kuşadası and on our way back she lost her phone. Another passenger handed it to customs and I asked the staff to hold the plane until I got the phone back. A lovely gentleman from Izmir airport ran all the way and got the phone back for me, he was such a lovely person. He was running and I got it just before the doors closed.

I use ADB regularly and I find it daunting. The wifi is terrible and you only get 2 hours. On this trip, I only got 28 minutes. The food costs are pure theft and the money they charge for a small bottle of water is ridiculous. I paid 32 lira for 2 cups of hot water as we bring our own tea bags (we dont like Earl Gray). The airport is modern and should be busier with more flights as Turkey is a great country to visit.

Very nice, big and empty space. Food options limited before security. Check in Agents showed up less then 2 hrs before international departure flight. I'm unsure of the policy at this airport, but seems tight for 2 agents to check in an entire flight. Wifi not accessible with no sim card. Airport Information agent unaware of internet and how to access. I asked how to access, she mentioned there's no wifi. I showed my screen showing black and white where it said free airport access for 2 hours. She still mentioned no there's no wifi at this airport only in restaurants. I paid for lounge access, the agent was kind to explain, you need a sim card otherwise even the lounge wifi will not work. Food options pass security and the lounge is very limited, disappointed despite all the empty airport space available.

Izmir Adnan Menderes Airport seems a bit far from downtown but it has a connection of a local rail system called "İzban" and it takes about 30-50 minutes to reach the airport. There are lots of food and beverage options on the ground. Prices are high in my opinion but you can find something suitable for your budget. It's very clean and safe. Also, there are lots of taxis and buses you can use.

An excellent Domestic terminal, very large and clean. The security screening upon entering the airport for a 11am departure was fast and thorough. Plenty of check in counters, and efficient agents manning them. The food is very expensive, but I don't buy at the airport, so no problem. A very nice airport all in all.

Izmir airport is way over priced for food and drinks. Most of the food outlets were empty and I cannot understand why the airport magagement dont make it more affordable. I would probably use it rather than bring my own food as I will not pay these extortionate prices. The airport is clean and very thorough security wise. Their WiFi near impossible to get as you need a Turkish phone to recieve the special access code they send you giving you only 2 hours of access. The access code procedure was so difficult I couldnt even make out the verification letters even with my glasses on. Their tightness with the WiFi doesn't do them any favours. Very petty on this point.

Izmir-Adnan Menderes is architecturally a very pleasing airport with lots of glass and steel giving it a very modern look. The food and shopping were very good, the restrooms were spotless and clean, and it was very easy to navigate. There is free wifi but only for two hours.
Very very quiet compared to both Istanbul airports. Much cleaner as less people use it. Access to city is decent with local transportation. Much less traffic in every sense of the word.

Flying with Delta Airlines last night and were cleared to land only to have us turn around back to Salt Lake City airport because the visibility was poor. When we got back to the gate we found out that there was not even any observers in the tower at Jackson Hole to guide our landing to the runway because apparently the airport closes at 11pm. What airport closes and more importantly does not have staffing to have an observer in the tower knowing a flight is coming? We flew out this morning only to have the same happen except this time it was them not preparing the runway. What airport does not accommodate for staff to prepare for a runway that has snow on it when the location has snow almost everyday around this time. This airport is poorly managed and staffed and unacceptable.

This is a small airport. Check in and security are painless. Airside there are now 8 gates. There is floor to ceiling glass affording nice views of the Tetons. There is plenty of comfortable seating in the gate area that would get high marks from the people at "Sleeping In Airports". You still have to walk on the tarmac to board your plane. Sadly the food choices are unchanged from my last trip through. That is my only complaint. Still this is a very nice tertiary level airport. As always be sure to book an F side window seat for your daytime flight in.

This is a small airport to say the least. It only has 4 gates and this is after it is being modernized and expanded. Construction is still going on so it can be a bit noisy. Security is fairly painless. There is only one restaurant/lounge airside or curbside. Hopefully this will change when construction is complete. Airside has floor to ceiling windows affording views of the spectacular Tetons. Almost as impressive is the array of private jets lined up toward the south end of the airport. If you fly here be sure to take a daytime flight in and book an F side window seat for a jaw-dropping view of the Tetons on approach.

While I found the Jacksonville airport to be very clean with exceptionally friendly, professional employees, my review is regarding one in particular. His name is Alejandro, a wheelchair provider for people departing and arriving at the airport. I first met him on October 17, 2023 when I arrived at JAX. He was prompt, friendly, and a very nice person. Well, when I left JAX I ran into Alejandro again and he recognized me (after a week and all the people he'd met). He was so pleasant. I have required wheelchair assistance when traveling for over 7 years and Alejandro is hands down the best.

The gate agents are great, but they might have the most inefficient TSA security checkpoint I’ve ever witnessed. It took them around 30 minutes to scan 15 bags and only one was flagged out of the 15. They seem to be the only airport where the analogic machines have actually made the security checkpoint slower, which is wild considering the technology of those things. Everywhere else seems to have competent people to run them.

What a discombobulated mess! I bought TSA pre check to expedite airport security but what I witnessed today was a nightmare. Their new TSA pre check area and process for screening is atrocious. The plastic bins don't go in the same order as the prior who pass through - the person in front of me received his second container after I had received my first and the person after me had a container come through before mine as well. It creates longer wait times and more people standing around waiting for the bins. Lots of confusion causing additional travel stress.
Lousy baggage claim. Actually the worst ever ! And it’s consistently bad. An hour for the baggage belt to even turn on is completely unacceptable - pitiful!

I was checking in my 15 yr old daughter for her flight to Chicago, to visit her father for the summer. She travels as an unaccompanied minor but we still like to walk her to her gate, sit with her while she waits and say our goodbyes before she gets on her flight. I have had minor issues with doing this with other airlines, due to security concerns/COVID/9-11 but this most recent visit, I feel I have to say something about the customer service. We get to the airport 1.5 hours before her flight. It's me, my daughter and her half sister. The ticketing agent was not pleasant from the word go. No greeting, no "hi, how are you", just a very bland "how can I help you". She asked me for ID and I said "mine or my daughter's" - as my 15 year old doesn't have an ID as she doesn't drive yet nor does she have a job. She got a bit of an attitude and was like "hers" meaning my daughter. I stated she did not have one for said reasons above. She proceeds to check my daughter in and as that is going on, I tell the ticketing agent that me and her half sister will need passes to walk her to the gate. She finishes with my daughter, then asks for my ID. I give it to her, she checks me in and gives me a gate pass and sends me on my way. I tell her I need a gate pass for her 17 year old half sister. She asks for her ID and when we told her it was in the car and we weren't sure she needed it, she was like "of course she needs it, if she wants a gate pass, she needs to have an ID". Me, not traveling much, didn't know the rules so I had both girls run out to the car (which was not close), get the ID and run back. My daughter was very distraught at this point and we are getting close to her departure time. I calmed her down, we go back to the ticketing agent where a man took over getting her the gate pass and we were on our way. We then get to the TSA line and it was a disaster. The line was miles long and travelers were stressing about missing flights. The line moved S-L-O-W. We had less than 30 min to get through TSA and to her gate. A lady in front of us asked a TSA employee about the line and what could be done to move it along faster and the TSA employee stated "Lady, a lot of people are going to miss flights today". I know airports are crazy and it was the start of summer but basic customer service has gone out the window. Almost every airport employee we encountered was rude.

Waited 1 hour in line to be checked by TSA. Unacceptable. Poorly run with no concern for passengers. Attitude of staff. For such a small terminal there should be a more efficient way to expedite passengers through and still provide the required safety needed. At least 15 passengers did not make their flight on this one airline due to the inefficiency of TSA. These passengers arrived an hour or more before flight. Totally disappointed.

On June 7, 2018, I was departing from Jacksonville airport on American Airlines to Philadelphia, flight 4705. At Gate C8, an employee who was very supportive and accommodating to me. She was extremely busy; however, took the time to be sure I had a wheelchair waiting in Philadelphia. She also arranged to have me boarded early with someone. She offered to check my carryon bag as I was having difficulty. This woman is a credit to American Airlines. The plane was extremely cold the flight attendant gave me a blanket which I did not know were available. Very good experience.

Unfortunately security staff at airport security check point was very rude, it was a male security officer. I placed my belongings in tray at check in point than on rolling rack and attempted to walk away. He came yelling - “whose stuff if is? Who is watching your stuff? You like you staff than stay there”! He sounded and behaved literally like an abusive spouse. What is this? Boot camp? Who talks like that to people? Most people coming to airport are stressed out already, and last thing anyone needs is a stranger coming out of nowhere yelling at them when only simple redirection is needed. What about being calm and professional instead? Otherwise airport was clean and easy to use, also rest of employees we encountered were very polite. Just this one individual gave airport bad rep for a day.

I go to Jacksonville airport a lot since this is my hometown airport. It is a nice, clean, and small with only 20 gates. Due to the size you don't really need signage at all. Despite the small size there is still a bunch of food options before and after the security checkpoint. There is also some good shops like Brooks Brothers and a PGA Tour Shop. There is also a big pavilion with rocking chairs right before security. It's a great place to wait if you're waiting on an arriving flight. There is also pretty good employees, well besides the TSA people. One time I had to go through the regular checkpoint instead of Pre-Check and they only had one metal detector and one ProVision open. It took about 25-30 minutes to pass through, because of this I got to my gate when they were calling the last boarding zone when I was supposed to board in the first boarding zone. However, a great airport and I recommend it.

This airport is probably one of the best I have been to. Every employee I encountered was friendly and eager to help. The airport itself was clean and efficient. I flew in and out of this airport at busy times of the week and did not experience any problems. When I landed I went through baggage claim quickly and was waiting for my friend in a matter of 10 minutes. When I was flying out I had the same experience. I said goodbye to my friend and five minutes later I was at the gate. What a pleasure compared to flying out of Orlando, and there is free wifi.

Small regional airport, the arrival procedure is fairly quick, 5-10 mins after getting off the plane you are outside (if you’ve no hold luggage) Departures can be a bit hit and miss. I’ve used it twice now and as there are no departures currently between 1430 & 1700 it was empty when I arrived just after 3pm. The second time I arrived about 1230 & security was very busy although I was through in about 10 mins. Gates 1A, 1B & 1C are on the ground floor, M1 on the first and the rest on the second floor. The first floor also has the airports only lounge while the second floor houses a reasonable selection of quick food outlets and shops. Nothing pretty about it but pleasant to use.

Good arriving experience (domestic). Not too busy, not long walk from aerobridge. Baggage arrived fast, wifi available but as most of the airport in India only if having Indian sim, almost impossible for non Indian sim. Washroom were ok, should have better and cleaner. Only one cafe at arrival, not any other option. No public bus from airport, only option is auto or cab, prepaid cab counter is there, also Uber/Ola.

Biggest and busiest airport in Jaipur, capital of Rajasthan. Has all the basic facilities a passenger needs, clean toilet, some food outlets, seating arrangements and some shopping options, also have a smoking zone and a lounge (but lounge is not worth describing, its pathetic). Wifi is available but if having non Indian sim them almost impossible to connect, as won't get OTP even if number is active they should do something about this. Security checks can be sometime time taking during peak hours otherwise ok.

Half of the display screens are off and there is just one or two display screens on where the last row isn't visible due to the start menu of Windows. The staff are not helpful for any information and not even ready to listen to the passengers. The SR cafe does not accept online money and only demands cash even though Jaipur has a lot of COVID cases It's really pathetic to get this experience at the airport. Very disappointed.

They have privatised the airport, so let's hope they improve the service. There are no places where a mother can change her child's diapers. It's a international airport and some minimum standards need to be set for an international airport, also the toilets are not clean.
The bathrooms all over the airport were so dirty, they were like road side public bathrooms. So much of international tourist comes to this city and state. What an embarrassment.

Pros: 1) Small Airport, easy to get around. 2) Friendly security staff. Cons: 1) Poor cleanliness in toilets. 2) No place to change baby diapers. You have make your baby sit between the wet wash-basins and hope that you infant/toddler doesn't fall of while you are putting aside the dirty diaper or when you are opening the new diaper for your baby. 3) Insufficient number of seats in the waiting/boarding area.

The burocratic process in all airports that I have been in India is very disappointing. I would not imagine that the fifth economy in the world would have such bad, slow and burocratic process & services implemented. Starting with the shocking fact that you need to have your boarding pass printed in paper otherwise they will not let you pass. In current days this mandatory paper no longer makes sense since everybody in India has a cellphone with internet connection. That causes delays and more queues in the airport that you could easily avoid. Also India was the only place that I lost a connection flight in my life. Flight was delay and the different airline companies don’t talk with each other and the customer service is not promptly. Very disappointing experience that I was not expected to face.

Parking washrooms are not at all clean. In the name of hygiene all they do is ask for money. After money also it was worst than you can imagine. Not even flushed. When I asked the person to clean, he refused to and said better you take your money back and leave. This is my experience with Jaipur airport.

Staff and facilities are fine i.e. they have options for food, kids play area and enough dustbins. However, I could see pigeons flying all over, at every floor which is very disappointing. It was not hygienic as they were spreading food particles and feathers everywhere and were also scary for kids. Airport management needs to pay immediate attention to this.
It appears that terminal 1A has been forgotten by the airport management; their focus is on terminal 3. Terminal 1A is dark, hot & in need of a thorough rejuvenation.

Terminal 1A is in urgent need of renovation - it is dark, hot & old. The airport authority should invest in making the terminal a better experience for travellers; while terminal 3 might be better, all terminals need to be of the same higher standard

This airport doesn't meet international standards. The air-conditioning is broken, so HOT! The staff are not friendly on the buggy shuttle service, there are double standards with international people. This airport's delay rates are high.

I travel through here about once a month or two, both domestically and internationally. The airport gives a distinct feeling of something new and proud, but a bit under-invested and not-quite well organized. The nice things about it are the staff, ample seating space and many restrooms. The bad thing is often very slow check-in process and the longest ever luggage wait times. At the entrance, passengers with suitcases have to put them through an X-ray machine, and there is usually only one of these out of two that is operational. It takes up to 10-15 minutes just to get inside, and it doesn't help that people habitually cut the line. Signage is okay. I travel once a month on average, and I still get confused looking for my check-in counter, and figuring out the right way to go after check- in. The signs are there, but not enough. There also aren't enough screens with flight/gate information in visible places, like the cafes. Check-in is often slow, even for people who've checked-in online (not sure what the point is if it doesn't save time?). The terminal is quite warm, but not too bad. The cleanliness is good. There's a lot of restrooms in the boarding area. The restroom design is a bit baffling to me - half of the stalls are hole-in-the-floor toilets, and half are normal toilet seats. No one wants to use the former, and the latter ones are always occupied. There is no Priority pass-compatible lounge in the international section of CGK. There is a sapphire premium one which works with some credit cards and premium airline customers. The domestic part of terminal 3 has one-and-a-half sapphire lounges: one dim, small one right at the entrance to the gate area, and another, same brand but a little newer at the far right end or the building. They accept Priority pass, which is nice. Half the time my husband and I choose to go to Paul instead  or some other cafe, because lounge food is basic and unexciting. There are some other food options, mostly Indonesian food and bakeries. The international section has a fast-food court, and a large Chinese restaurant as well. The places that are decent are usually pretty full. The terminal 3 is designed as a long narrow stretch, which often means you're going to take a long walk to get through it. It's pretty meh when you're arriving. Along walk along that endless dim hallway to passport control is not great after 12-hour flights. And then comes the part that gets me the most: the luggage claim. In CGK, you could wait anywhere between 15 and 45 minutes for your luggage, even after the passport control lines. No crowd control there either, so be prepared for people riding their luggage carts right up to the belt and blocking access for others. At the exit, there's lots of opportunities to pick up a ride into town - from metered Bluebird taxis located a bit further out across the street to electric cars. And of course there is an eager crowd of unofficial taxi drivers who will offer their services pretty aggressively in your face. Also, I moved here with my pets, so they had to go through quarantine at the airport. The animal quarantine is located next to the luggage claim in international arrivals. At the time of my move, owners were not allowed to visit their animals, but based on the few videos I got of my pets there it is pretty spartan. Bring your pets here only if they're in good health and resilient, and only if you have no better choice.

Jakarta’s Soekarno-Hatta has been for a couple of years my "home base" for both international and domestic travel. The older terminal 2 has its charm but is clearly outdated and definitely is disorganised, more or less depending which airline one uses. If one flies with Garuda, Citilink (domestic or international) or any international airline the departure or arrival is in Terminal 3. It is a modern building where unfortunately distances can be sometimes a bit of a challenge, especially upon arrival (often it is a true hike from plane to passport control/luggage belt). Both terminals have enough food options to relax a bit or to kill time when you are delayed. Only downside at Soekarno-Hatta is the luggage collection time, regardless of terminal or airline: it requires quite some patience.

I arrived in the airport at night. The airport is surprisingly empty but very hot, it feels like they turned off the ac. Terminal 3 is very huge but feels empty and some of the travelators is not even working.

You can't transfer between domestic and international sections without asking people and the instructions for Garuda lounge was terrible. They showed farthest gate and changed without clear announcement. By far the worst airport I've experienced.

International terminal 3 is a boiling pot.  Air conditioning is a joke in this place. We were drenched in sweat from the walk to our gate. Then sitting there we were sticking to the chairs. Signage is also so poor. Hate traveling through here.

Most of the airport was hot. Only felt moderately cool at the quiet area - which wasn’t quiet at all. It was right next to noisy escalators and on top of an area where staff (I assume they were staff) would congregate and loudly converse. The rest of the time I thought staff were loudly and the airport was nice enough. Lots of restaurants and little shops although most closed at night (I arrived and was in transit for 6 hours). Outlets everywhere and potable water available.

Travelled for business. The airport is still boiling hot. You are drenched in sweat before you get onto your plane which is not fun if you expect to land and go straight to business meetings. The air conditioning near gates 5/6 also now smells like garbage/sewage. The security check system has now became archaic and has made queues much longer. Basically you put your bags/wallet/belt etc on the trays like normal, then men have to go and queue in one line and women in another line to walk through the scanner. This means that you have to walk away from your luggage, and queue with other people. This has created a chaotic system of significantly longer queues and unattended baggage slowing down the scanning system. On a not-very-busy weekday, mid afternoon, this already took 20 minutes (compared to the usual 3-5 minutes). Imagine what this would be like in peak hour. If they don't want unisex patting down of people, why not copy Changi. Let anyone go through either scanner, have a man and women by each pair of scanners. The men go to the man and the women to the lady. It works so much better than what they are doing now.

Jakarta Halim Airport is a secondary airport after Soekarno Hatta Airport, with a lot of Citilink and Batik Air flights. The terminals here were converted from the airport's International terminal, and the result for me is a bit pathetic. No clear signs on what to do on transiting, or where you should go, instead you have to go to the arrivals area and re-enter the departures area. There are a lot of F&Bs and shops outside the terminal but the numbers decreased inside the terminal. The cleanliness is good, Wi-Fi was adequate, signs were adequate, but the airport seating layout was pathetic. There were gates 4-8, and where's 1-3? Overall I do think that this is an adequate airport but it is not recommended for transiting. Staffs were, like most Indonesian airports, friendly and fast.

Airport situated at Jammu city, it has very limited facilities for arriving passengers. At baggage area clean toilets are there, Wifi is there but only if having active sim to get OTP and all prepaid sim didn't work in JNK due to safety reasons so almost of no use for most of the passengers. Jammu airport is the main airport for Vaishnodevi yatra. Now for starting yatra for katra every individual needs RFID card which can be made at airport from Vaishnodevi trust counter. No taxi allowed inside campus to pick passengers, need to exit the terminal and just after exit gate there is a taxi union counter from where can book taxi. Auto are also Available from outside, also few city bus but I didn't have idea about routes.

Nearest airport from Vaishnodevi, situated at Jammu. Airport with very basic facilities, expensive food and no lounge options. Security is very tight, to enter the terminal we need to get our baggage scanned and also 2 times manual frisking, after that again one security check of cabin baggage and manual frisking. Wifi needs OTP but no roaming for prepaid sim in JNK and most people have prepaid sim so no wifi. Toilets were clean and also the terminal.

Janakpur the capital of Madhesi province in Nepal has the IATA code JKR and the provincial government has recently revamped the airport with a total overhaul, new building replacing the old one, that means an entirely new terminal but the same old runway. It may rank as as the best airport operating domestic flights only in Nepal. Belts for luggage handling, big hall with sufficient seating facilities, restaurant inside, and a nice departure lounge. Toilets aren't clean. People are too introvert, security personnel needs to improve on behavioural front. Not long queue for departure. Basic facilities for other things , parking enough for passenger load,

Being a wheelchair user, they won't let me have my own wheelchair at the gate and forced me to use airport's clumsy wheelchair. Then the assistant literally dumped me in middle of nowhere promising that someone else will come and push me to the immigration counters. No on came for next 20-25 minutes and I eventually started pushing myself which was extremely uncomfortable. I saw a couple of assistance staff along the way who refused to help because they were going to assist passengers from another flight. Not their fault because they were assigned a different job. This was the most inhumane treatment I ever received. Very disappointed by the whole experience.
The airport staff was helpful polite and respectful. There was a metro which helped me move around quickly. Schedule boards everywhere. Nice restaurants and coffee shops. Not crowded at all.
The duty free staff especially the fragrance section was very unprofessional. Poor customer service. No please to give feedback. Otherwise the food and airport is good

I have never seen such ill mannered and rude people in my life as there are on security scan of Jeddah Airport. They are reluctant to assist anyone. People look up to them for assistance but the staff male and female both are rude and ill treat people even people of old age.

There was no nursing room provided, water dispenser not working. At departure hall terminal 1, I cannot find any good restaurant for meal, except coffee shops and desserts. So limited choices. Also at arrival only Al baik for chicken option?

Visited through this Airport 2nd time for Umrah in Jeddah Airport North Terminal. The women Immigration officers were pathetic and unprofessional. Always busy with their own business and not doing the immigration work. One of the women Immigration officer asked my partner if she can speak Arabic, my wife replied “No", in response to my wife's reply the officer questions back why not. It is none of her business if my wife could speak Arabic or not. The women officers react as if they are doing a top level job or something extra ordinary, they are not polite at all.

Surprised how small it is and the lack of choice for food. What prompted this review however is the toilet situation. There are plenty and they are clean enough but every single toilet has a bored attendant who will hover around outside your stall, pretending to clean it the moment you enter. Incredibly off-putting and twice I just gave up and decided to use the toilet on the aircraft, where I'd have more privacy and less attention. I will try to avoid this airport in future.

Our journey from Jeddah to Qatar, with a transit stop in Riyadh, was marred by a series of unfortunate events that left us deeply disappointed. As we approached the check-in counter at Jeddah airport, we encountered an attendant whose receptiveness seemed notably absent. Despite our attempts to communicate our situation, she briskly processed our documents and handed out boarding passes, albeit segregating our family onto separate rows. To our dismay, she omitted the essential luggage tags for both our hand luggage and the baby stroller, abruptly departing the counter with her personal belongings, leaving us bewildered and adrift. Our attempts to seek clarity were met with further frustration. A request to summon a supervisor was met with a dismissive response, as she claimed to be unaware of the supervisor's whereabouts. With her departure, we found ourselves adrift, until we chanced upon a more accommodating staff member at a different counter. He promptly rectified the oversight, issuing the requisite tags for our belongings, bringing some semblance of order to the situation. Upon our arrival at Riyadh International Airport, the pre-arranged wheelchair assistance for my mother was conspicuously absent.  In summation, the cumulative experience involving Flynas Airlines, Jeddah, and Riyadh airports was profoundly disheartening. Our expectations for a smooth and accommodating journey were regrettably unmet, leaving us to reflect on the marked contrast between our aspirations and the reality we encountered.

My girlfriend and I stopped over in Jeddah to go to Mauritius (it was cheaper by far). We had an 8 hour layover on the way out and 11:15 a.m. on the way back, both times arriving at 10 p.m. in Jeddah. We were in Terminal 1, which is the most common terminal for international flights. I think the airport is more than adequate, the shops are open all night, the airport is clean, spacious, with seats almost everywhere. I did not find the staff to be rude or annoyed. No one bothered us, you are really quiet there. As soon as we arrived, we just had to redo a check (cabin case, backpack) and then nothing more to do until boarding the plane at the gate indicated on the panel. Be careful, however, because the wifi only worked for us on the way back and not on the way there. So plan something to do in the meantime (download movies on Netflix, board games, books, sleep and so on). I recommend this airport, because it allowed us to pay for our tickets twice as much as normal and it was not death to wait 8am on the way there and 11am on the way back. Also be careful which terminal you are arriving in (like I said if it's an international flight you have a huge chance of being in terminal 1) as my comment only applies to terminal 1.  Ma copine et moi, avons fait escale à Jeddah pour aller en Île Maurice (c'était moins cher et de loin). Nous avons eu 8h d'escale à l'allé et 11h15 au retour, les deux fois en arrivant à 22h à Jeddah. Nous étions dans le terminal 1, qui est le terminal le plus courant pour les vols internationaux. Je trouve que l'aéroport est plus que correcte, les magasins sont ouverts toute la nuit, l'aéroport est propre, spacieux, avec des sièges quasiment partout. Je n'ai pas trouvé que le personnel étaient désagréables ou agacé. Personne ne nous a dérangé, vous y êtes vraiment tranquille. Dès que nous sommes arrivés, nous avons juste du refaire un contrôle (valise de cabine, sac à dos) et ensuite plus rien à faire jusqu'à l'embarquement dans l'avion à la porte indiquée sur le panneau. Attention toutefois car le wifi a marché pour nous seulement au retour et pas à l'allé. Prévoyez donc quelque chose à faire en attendant (téléchargez des films sur Netflix, jeux de société, livre, dormir et j'en passe). Je recommande cet aéroport, car il nous a permit de payer nos billets deux fois moins cher que la normale et ce n'était pas la mort d'attendre 8h à l'allé et 11h au retour. Faites également attention de savoir dans quel terminal vous arrivez (comme je l'ai dit si c'est un vol international, vous avez d'énormes chance d'être dans le terminal 1), car mon commentaire s'applique uniquement au terminal 1.

Their staff is very unprofessional. Queue got long because the boarding staff was busy gossiping and laughing at each others jokes. I had to wait more than I should because of that. Also, they don't know good English if you need any information.

Arrived 0520. Terminal dark except for immediate vicinity of Iberia check-in desks. Check in quick and easy. Security opened at 0545 and was quick and painless. Terminal still mostly dark, including bathrooms. Lights come on and small cafe opens at 0600.

I've come to use this airport multiple times, normally it's not too much of a hassle. They are a smaller airport, so they are not open 24/7 which means if you have an early morning flight you may be waiting outside before they open. Apparently for some reason this airport in particular has an issue with losing luggage. On my recent flight, there was at least 4 other people and myself who's luggage didn't arrive. Another passenger in the same scenario told me this is about the 3rd time they lost her luggage. Only good news about that is she said that it normally arrives the following day, but so far it's the next day and mine is still missing. Cabs are expensive, some staff speak some English, lines aren't too bad.

Small airport, easy to find everything. Overall, a majority of the airport had no issue. However, a single experience can ruin it. In my case, the airport staff at lost luggage was very unhelpful. I had a bag missing, and they had no set-up for an overnight bag. Going through the lost luggage department was like pulling out fingernails. After an hour, they finally open a case number, that you can track online. The number provided to their office would ring for a long time, then either hangs up or is picked up by somebody who knows very little English. While the lost luggage is the fault of the airline, the process in Jerez is painstaking. The taxi prices are outrageous. Mine did not speak English, so have your Spanish handy.

Excellent little airport and the relatively new train stop just a few hundred meters across the parking lot from the terminal building makes it even better. It's a shame more airlines aren't using this perfect spot as Jerez is convenient to Cadiz Capital Sevilla and even Malaga and the Costa del Sol.
I agree with the previous reviewers comments. This is a great little airport. An added bonus is that there is now a direct train link to Jerez centre as well as Cadiz and the surrounding cities.

Andalucia's hidden gem. This is the perfect antidote to the horror of Malaga. Bags arrive within minutes of arrival the staff are friendly and the airport is tiny. Departures likewise are quick security takes minutes and you are a short walk to the plane. Anyone going to Spain between Estepona and Seville should consider this an alternative to fog prone Gibraltar or Malaga even if it means connecting in Madrid as the time lost driving out is gained by the speed of airport service. Only minus is the lack of smoking areas (you can go past security though multiple times without hassle) and airline lounges due to space.

One particular person at easyjet check in was very officious. Going forward, found the security personnel team, abrupt in a manner that was totally uncalled for. We do appreciate their job is essential to keep travellers safe but in the same token, we the passengers have a right to due care and consideration passing through security. Travel, is stressful enough. Have travelled to and from numerous airports and this is the first time I experienced this behaviour. Needs addressed.

Airport on Arrival no problem. We hired a car and having found the car hire desk we were directed to the car pick up point which turned out to be a considerable distance away. No shuttle service. You just have to leg it. If it had been raining we would have been soaked. Can't imagine what it must be like for people in wheelchairs or families with pushchairs plus luggage. Car hire needs to be closer to the terminal or shuttle service provided. Departure was not good. We had to leave our bags to be scanned, go to the other side for Security check which meant leaving our bags and personal belongings unattended. When called for our flight we were herded into a holding pen, not enough seats, stood for 25 minutes while 2 members of staff called out peoples names to re check their flight details, this was done in a very unfriendly and unapologetic manner. Took the shine off what had otherwise been a very pleasant trip to this beautiful island.

A truly horrible airport with a makeshift immigration area that has simply sliced the departures area in half. Unfriendly security staff, and once "airside" there are very limited facilities, not to mention seating areas in abundance. The cafe and bar and shops are mostly all manned by eastern European migrants, and the actual gate areas are a relic from the 1970's, around 40 seats for 100 plus passengers. They extended and remastered this airport shortly after they culled tourism. There once was a lovely open air rooftop viewing area, which then became a glassed in lounge, now even that has gone. Couldn't wait to leave the depressing airport for the last time.

Efficient, frequent bus service from St Helier is a good way to get to the airport, but once there it goes downhill. The first security check (boarding pass) is quick and easy but wouldn't necessarily say friendly. The next, bags etc, despite 2 belts in operation, and at least 12 staff members that I could see, the queue to pass through the scanner took 10 minutes, even though I was number 6 in queue. Some of the staff must be either very new, or unable to cope with, what I would say not unusual circumstances, such as 3 wheelchairs passengers arriving. Even after that wait, selected for random screening (don't mind too much though, as best to be safe), but the biggest bug bear, the public (one and only) bar had sullen staff, looking like they'd rather be somewhere else (wouldn't we all), then for strange reason their bosses have decided to stop selling their best selling drink, Carling Lager, and replaced it with San Miguel at approx 70p more per pint, probably suggesting this was a more 'in' drink. If a nice tasting lager it may be, but I certainly won't be racing to that bar again, somewhere enjoyed a pre departure drink many a time. These airport bar bosses may think they're making more money by selling the more expensive drink, but I know many who will do exactly the same as me, and bypass that bar once they've realised this ridiculous change.
Bar and restaurant staff appeared to be totally fed up and disinterested in their job. Could do a lot better. Rest of the airport was fine and very clean.
Lots of seating. Not enough electric plugs or charge points. WiFi was hopeless - it didn’t work. Tannoy too loud. Staff seem nice enough. Appeared clean.

Very pleasant and helpful staff. With my arm in a sling it was hard to do most things but staff were ready to help and the canteen staff were friendly and professional. Could do with more shops and a better variety.

I don’t know what goes on with this airport but flights are always delayed and staff do nothing to help you with it. Hardly any seating, no variety in shops or food choices. Fast queues is the only good thing.

The arrivals area is pretty shabby but from disembarking the plane to getting on the bus to St Helier took less than 15 minutes. We departed from Jersey late afternoon on a Saturday when it was very quiet and so it was a very pleasant experience. The staff at security and in the shops were all helpful and charming. For the size of the airport the selection of shops and food were decent although there did seem to be a lack of seating after security, however there was plenty at the gate.

I travel to Jersey regularly and am rather underwhelmed with the airport. Arrivals is lifeless, however staff are very nice and even helped me take my luggage off the carousel and onto my trolley. There is also plenty of free tourist brochures and maps available if you want them. Departures is a bit odd. Check in was fast as I used the priority lane, but the security people were very thorough which is fine, except when they are rude as well. There are plenty of shops etc, particularly given the size of the airport. However, the airline lounge is after a one way door. If you want to go back to the shops you can't! I have no idea what they were thinking when they designed that part.

Only 1 entry gate for 3 flights boarding together made a long queue. Without boarding pass you can not enter. No place to sit after security check. No shop for a water bottle or tea/coffee. Not single mobile charger port working.

JMU is located in the far north-east of China approx two hours' flying time from Beijing and three hours' flying time from Shanghai-Pudong. With a single runway doubling as the only taxiway JMU doesn't see much traffic. One has to walk across the runway to the terminal building - no provisions of covered walkways in this single-storey terminal building. Ok in summer but imagine in winter with -25 degrees. And it does get that cold up there - the Russian border is only a few hundred km away. The single belt means it can get crowded when a full China Southern 737 disgorges is complement of passengers. Trolleys are free but in a poor state. As soon as the airport staff matches luggage tag against baggage receipt means you're fair game for the taxi touts. Which is meaningless since they all use the meter. The drive into Jiamusi city is uneventful and mercifully only 50 RMB away. Departing on Hainan Airlines was easy - though the ticket counter accepts cash only should you need to purchase the ticket at the airport like we did. The two check-in clerks went about their job quickly and efficiently. Security was equally quick. The single departure hall consisted of two gates a souvenir shop selling Russian matrioshka dolls and manicure sets (!) and a smoking room. Again boarding was by walking across the aircraft parking bay. My only gripe were the taxi touts filthy toilets and lack of covered walkways.

Nice airport, corresponding to the Chinese standard, no frills but essentials are there. If you fly international, no need to arrive early, as the check-in counter is opened just one hour before flight time. If you arrive early, it is difficult to find a seat. Not very friendly immigration people, but nice lounge with good wi-fi connection and unlimited Internet access. Plenty of outlets, to satisfy the western appetite (Starbucks, KFC, etc.)

Stuck in Jinan airport due to plane delay. Jinan airport on first impression is bright and modern. Yet among Chinese airports it surely must be rated as one of the worst. Passport check was quite inefficient and slow. This due to the security check which not only had very limited space meaning that passengers pile up waiting and bags pile up when leaving the x-ray. The check was unusually strict. As a frequent business traveller I always carry the same items yet here my bag was searched quite a bit and resubmitted for check. Once behind security there were limited facilities. Heating had been switched off so the airport was freezing cold. The coffee shops were simply disgusting with respect to their hygiene while the coffee was amazingly overpriced. Unlike most other airports in China Jinan does not provide free Wifi rather a fee version. Seating became rapidly limited as delays piled up. Lounges are quite grotty as well. No interesting shops at all. Try avoiding this airport.

Pre check in area very disappointing at busiest time of day Lounge - closed Coffee Shop - closed toilets - filthy. After check in much improved small shop bright and clean coffee shop and adequate toilets.

I took a connecting flight from London through JNB to Malawi. We had to collect our luggage and check in again for the connecting airlink flight. The queues for the passport check were very long and there were insufficient staff who were unfriendly. We had four hours for the transit. The monitors with flight details were not updating so we couldn’t find which gate to go to. The staff did not know. Due to long queues at security, baggage and passport we had only 30 mins in the terminal before boarding. That’s about 3 hours waiting in queues. Most of which was in hot sweaty lines with no working AC. Security and passport and flight detail systems failed at different times. Worst and most inefficient experience of a major airport so far. I think we were unlucky to experience multiple system failure but modern airports should have decent backup systems in place.

Sadly this airport is poorly staffed and when there are staff at customs they spend their time chatting and joking. Rudeness which was prevalent is not good for tourism and business either. The Diner restaurant used the same utensils to serve hot meat and then cakes. The whole process was poorly coordinated...with unecessary queues. King Mswati 111 Airport in eSwatini is a much better experience and the Kingdom formerly called Swaziland makes for a fantastic holiday experience which is where we have travelled from.

Someone needs to take better charge of this airport. The airport is poorly maintained, bags take forever to get to baggage claim (1hour) and on departure at this very busy airport there are only 3 passport desks open.  Worst experience.

I've been proud of the overall service and facilities at OR TAMBO. Travelling to SA 5 years later/post COVID, alot has changed..not for the better. We arrived into OR approximately 1am on the 6th of Sept/ Friday a.m. none of the shops were open. It was very stuffy/low air quality. Cleaning staff I groups around the Toilet areas, clearly after tips/denied access to toilets/stating that toilets are out of order. Staff not helpful, just chatting amongst themselves. We had to go to other levels to find available toilets. Toilets were not very clean. On departure on the 14th Sept..a very warm day and clearly the air-conditioning was not working properly. This made for a very unpleasant couple of hours waiting to board. Staff at Indaba and Out of Africa not helpful or friendly..clearly too occupied to worry about a few sales here and there in foreign currency. Staff at security and passport control not friendly or communicative, very robotic and disinterested. Hopefully customer service will be addressed at all levels as the South African hospitality/friendliness and efficiency is missing!

The most unpleasant (and not always effectual staff) I've ever experienced in airports and I travel a lot. Just shy of plain rude with the traveler. A woman at customs upon my return from Mauritius gave me me no eye contact, grunted when I said 'thank you' though she did not deign push my passport towards me but forced me to reach inside the window to get it back. That's only one example. I hope never to have to go through that airport again.

I recently traveled through Johannesburg International Airport and was thoroughly impressed by the exceptional service and overall experience. The airport staff were incredibly helpful and friendly, making the whole journey smooth and stress-free. The facilities were clean, well-maintained, and easy to navigate, enhancing the overall travel experience. From efficient check-in processes to a wide range of dining and shopping options, Johannesburg International Airport truly excels in providing a top-notch travel experience. I highly recommend this airport for its great service and overall pleasant atmosphere.

Travelled through Johannesburg Airport to catch a connecting flight to Dubai. A lady at security was incredibly rude and dismissive of me bringing medicine and sugar through with me. I showed her my medical letters and she did not even glance at them. Told me to stand there and take my medicine now before going through. Shouted across to other staff that I was being difficult. I explained to her repeatedly that I was Type 1 diabetic and that I could collapse. We made our flight in the end with minutes to spare but I had to forego some of my meds as a result.

From being one of the best airports in Africa to travel through a decade ago, Johannesburg ORT has rapidly become one of the worst. On arrival, you will find dozens of immigration desks available but only a handful manned by some of the rudest officials you will ever meet, with lengthy lines as a result. Visit the toilets in the arrival hall and expect the attendant to ask you for a tip for standing there and watching you while you do your business. On departure, expect a single (out of 5 or 6) manned security lane processing hundreds of passengers leading to insane lines yet again. The ACSA staff manning these lanes seem more interested in chatting with each other than actually screening passengers. Further lines at passport control. There’s a security company that mans various checkpoints at the airport called Eagle Eye Security. The staff are thoroughly unpleasant to deal with. My experience on my last trip was not a one-off as I travel through ORT once a month and this is the usual experience. What an embarrassing gateway to one of the biggest commerce centers in Africa.

Awful, unprofessional, uninterested and barely functional. An astoundingly poor experience when international visitors arrive to Johannesburg, with seating frayed or falling apart (ceiling boards too); and that barely mentions the lack of signage. Naturally, the baggage carousel was broken which meant people and some staff started climbing over the broken/stuck/non-functioning carousel to try get their bags. All in all, 75 minutes to disembark, get stamped in, struggle to locate and find baggage before having to redo the whole process again for domestic departures since FlySafair counters aren’t available in the part of the airport where international visitors could easily switch. And of course; none of this is explained or communicated among the dozen broken, glitching screens or dozens of empty booths. Luckily, the actual staff that assist in the airport are friendly, courteous, knowledgeable and kind. Get them into the arrivals area and fix that disaster. Africa’s premier business city deserves much better than the pathetic effort you’ve attempted to throw together.
I am shocked at the state of the bathrooms at terminal A departures. A horrendous smell, and damaged stalls. Embarrassed to think foreigners have to use these poor state bathrooms.

TSA are extremely rude. To the gentleman in the tsa pre line, learn manners if you’re going to be working with customers or work in the back in a dark room away from people. If I’m asking you something, don’t have attitude when responding. I’m asking to know because I don’t know the answer, sarcasm is not needed. Also out of the 30 airports I’ve been to throughout the world this is the first to tell me my cosmetic items were too large. I think it goes without saying priorities need to be shifted and staff re-examined.

John Wayne airport is a nice little small/humble airport good for traveling with kids. It is a small airport with only 22 gates everything in the airport is close by. If you live by John Wayne I definitely would recommend!
Beautiful airport in Orange County with incredible ease to all major interstates. Airport sits off the 405 and is perfectly situated for Los Angeles visitors. Large airport with a small town feel.

The staff here are absolutely rude and unprofessional. I arrived in a timely matter and said goodbye to my family and younger siblings who I have not seen in many years and as I walk up to baggage check in, they say I’m a few minutes too late (despite being over half and hour early) and that no exceptions could be made. They made me pay a fee for a new flight and the lady was extremely rude. This is definitely the last time I will ever fly from John Wayne and instead, will just still to LAX where they strive to please their customers.

I landed with wheels down at 12:05 PM. I was the fifth person off the aircraft and it took till 12:50 to get my bag back. That is horrible! This airport is way too small to justify that laziness and tardiness in a frequently visited area. I am a business traveler from Atlanta and Delta has bags up in 20 min at one of the busiest airports. Get it together and build your quality!

Never had any problems flying in and out of John Wayne/Orange County Airport. It's clean, security is quick and efficient and has that laid back atmosphere that is OC. It's very convenient - even when it comes to flying internationally you can get almost anywhere in the world with no more than one stopover. At times I'll fly out of LAX if I'm not in the mood for that stopover, but OC always offers a pleasant alternative for convenience and efficiency. Because of its curfew, a lot of planes depart first thing in the morning so getting there early is advised. But overall a great airport.

Love John Wayne Airport - it is close and convenient to the I405 and everything in southern California. It is a lot easier to get in and out of than LAX and so much more modern. Flew from here to Portland recently and going through security and checking in the bags was a breeze.

John Wayne Airport is all about efficiency and comfort. This airport has one of the most direct and easy access to the freeway of any airport that I have been to. I took Southwest Airlines from John Wayne to Las Vegas. Checking-in my bags at the airline counter and going through security took me no more than 20 minutes. There are plenty of open seats at this terminal and a variety of restaurants to choose from. Southwest terminal has large windows from which passengers can enjoy views of aircraft taking off and landing. John Wayne also provides free wifi.

This is my preferred airport in SoCal for arriving at/departing from which I do on a regular basis. Big enough to offer connections anywhere in the US for flights to Europe yet small enough offer a quick friendly and efficient service to/from your gate. Drop off facilities outside the terminals needs to be improved but apart from that no real complaints.

The Airport is one of the easiest to get in and out of. The only problem the airport has is in planning and building a convenient location for taxi transportation. This problem did prevail when the airport was built. There was no taxi designated location. The one the taxis are situated now was an improvised one out of necessity. Once again with the addition of terminal C which is far away from the present taxi stand is too far for seniors and others. Something has to be done to improve this.

Juba airport had been rated worst in the world by some passenger surveys, with good reason. However, the original terminal has been replaced with a small but functional new terminal. Arrival and departure procedures are now quite reasonable for a developing country. There is a proper luggage carousel on arrival. Departure is OK. Check-in was a bit slow, but no problems at immigration which is now computerised like anywhere else. There are small but reasonably stocked shops before and after security and cafés too. The gate area is air conditioned, with new seating and TV. You do need a paid voucher for the wifi though. No longer an airport to dread using.

I have been through here a few times in the last year or so. The airport is small dirty and chaotic. No real facilities. Immigration and baggage claim are slow and hot. Departure is worse. Chaos in the check in area as well as for immigration. You can wander out of the terminal once you have checked in and been through immigration. If you have a while to wait you can get some snacks outside. There is a new airport terminal building under construction but it looks like work has stopped or is progressing very slowly.

In Juba (South Sudan) the airport is rapidly increasing number of flights and pax. However it is very old too small and very dirty no scanners working security cumbersome as bags had to be opened manually. The check-in area immigration is basically in one room which at peak hours turns chaotic. No facilities no chairs no airconditioning. No good signage. If granted access to VIP room nearby there is air-condition but one must go through additional security checks. A new terminal is being constructed. This airport is what one would imagine as a typical African airport 60 years ago. If yellow card can’t be presented at check in (to and from JUB) you can neither arrive nor depart.

Juliaca is the smallest commercial airport I have experienced. Because of the size it is easy to find your way around. There is not very much in the airport, so bring something to amuse yourself. The good news is, due to the size, it is a very clean including the bathrooms. There was a "VIP Lounge" that I peeked into. It consisted of a few chairs and a cooler with soft drinks and beer.

I used Kabul Airport both for my international as well as domestic flight to MZR. Comments: 1) There was a TV set in the lounge, but switched off. 2) No digital screens in the lounge, to inform passengers of exact departure or delays. 3) No WiFi connectivity. 4) No information regarding ground transportation (Taxis, buses, etc.) at the airport. 5) Information desk to give advice to passengers. 6) Customs services were professional. 7) Baggage handling was far better than before. 8) I did not see any currency exchange booth there.
Everything was very good. We used the lounge in the airport. The services were great.

Just like winning the lottery there are some things that you just do not expect to do. Giving Kabul airport a good review is one of them. But here it is. I have been travelling to Kabul for many years and have always hated the airport battle. But the new airport is different. If all you want to do is got on and off of a flight quickly and efficiently Kabul airport does that very well. The 2 hour queues at immigration are gone. More like 2 minutes now. Baggage reclaim is as good as anywhere else in he world. It took about half an hour from landing to being out of the airport. No problems with check in either. My Turkish flight left exactly on time. Don't expect too much in the way of shops or business lounge in the departures area but it is adequate. Wifi Internet is working well and free. There are lots of security checks on the way into the airport. Expect 4 lots of X-ray checks and various vehicle and body searches. That is just a part of life in Kabul these days. Overall a good and efficient experience and a big change from the old Afghan way.

Dubai-Kabul-Dubai. The chaos at Kabul airport continues. Still the old terminal is used. However for those travelling to UAE just as you think the hassle is over and you are in the departure lounge you are told that you are boarding. Great. You see the aircraft barely 20m from the gate. But does the bus take you there? No it takes you to the new terminal. In fact to a room in the bottom of the terminal where you are searched again. You have already been searched at least three times already. This whole procedure delays you be 3/4 hour because of the long queues. Meanwhile the aircraft which was ready to go on time is sitting there waiting. Finally you leave at least half an hour late. At least we saw a bit of the new terminal. However it does not appear to be built to the high standard that had been promised.
I agree with Dave's comment. Passengers still use the old terminal. Officials say that they do not have trained staff to run the new terminal this is indeed a big shame!

The new terminal may well have been inaugurated but it is not being used. Maybe it is just for visiting heads of state etc. We were pushed through the old terminal which has had some limited refurbishment. However do not expect any food to be available inside the airport (apart from nuts or Pringles). That and the staff continue to be the airports biggest problem.

A new terminal has been inaugrated to the west of the old terminal. The new terminal has built with international standards. Japan funded the construction of this terminal. The facilities in the new terminal are far more better compared with the old one. From 12 November 2008 the old terminal is used for domestic flights only.

Too much to expect the same standards as they have in Dubai or in the west. Over the last two years too much had been done and is still going on. The existing terminal has been refurbished and looks better then any airports in Pakistan.A new one will be completed by the end of 2008 for international flights.The existing one will be for domestic flights.

There has been some effort to improve the airport. Some refurbishment of the ceiling has got rid of the bullet holes and mess of wiring. There are also a few less opportunities for the staff to collect 'tips'. The upstairs depatrure lounge toilets no longer require breathing apparatus. The new terminal has some of the concrete superstructure complete so there is a chance it will open in 2008.

Very poor conditions no heat light bulbs burnt out luggage conveyor belt was broken exposed wires hanging from the cieling. People including staff very pushy and unorganized all wanted money for accomplishing simple tasks such as retrieving luggage. In short the worst airport I have been in.

On July 23rd we arrived at in Maui due to flight cancelations during a trip to Kauai. Sadly, my wife misplaced an expensive item in a washroom not discovering it until we had passed through security. We asked staff for assistance and the people we spoke to were awesome. They took our phone number as we're only there 1 day but recovered the item before we even left the airport. You guys most certainly brought some stress down on the start of a Hawaiian vacation for us. Mahalo!

All Day long our family reported gate issues. We had 16 people arrive today. All were parked on the tarmac for at least 30 mins. This airport is desperate for some help. If anyone can get me a gate so I can deplane I’d be grateful.

How can you accept planes and not have a gate to deplane? Sat for 45 minutes on the tarmac upon arrival and then was delayed 3.5 hours on departure. Once we boarded, we had to wait another 45 minutes for someone to put gas in our plane. Baggage claim was a hot mess. Multiple passengers getting only some of their bags. We needed to wait for two other planes to unload their luggage before getting our second bag. Hundreds of people waiting for flights that disappeared from flight boards. Lines of customers waiting to speak to service agents that came and left the area without explanation or serviced people outside of the established lines. There was another desk with three uniformed staff members carrying on conversations amongst themselves and a sign stating the desk was closed. Sassy, condescending updates far and few between. TSA line longer that regular check in.

I travel for a living and have been through most of the international airports in the US. Kahului Maui Airport, is hands down the worst of the worst. Visiting Maui isn't worth having to go through the airport here. I'll avoid it for layovers in the future as well. Save your self and avoid at all costs.

Just plain horrible in every regard. Arrival: waited 20 minutes on the tarmac for a gate to open, waited another 20 minutes at carousel for baggage (even after a bathroom stop!). Departure: Absolutely pointless agriculture inspection (agents don't even look!), Long line at security checkpoint, EXTREMELY rude TSA agent at escalator, our gate was not marked in main hallway - had to hunt and peck to find it, boarding agent was nothing short of a jerk, and this is the most rundown airport I have ever seen. In case you didn't get the gist of this review, this airport sucks!!!

The worst TSA experience we have ever had. All three TSA agents were incredibly rude, even to my 9 year old son. They lacked any customer service skills at all. I have never seen such a rude security staff.

My wife I have been coming to Maui each year for 39 years. When we first came, the airport was wide open, no real gates, no real baggage claim. Now, there are buildings but it is unwieldy. As an example, the United counter is at the far right end of the terminal, TSA is then 2/3 of the way to the left. Your first very long walk. No pre-check. Very limited food options when you finish with the TSA. Then what seems like a one mile walk to Gate 1 or 1 mile the other way to gate 39. Very few moving sidewalks especially in the lower gate numbers. OGG really needs updating and a better design. Less walking. More food. Better security checkpoint. The airport is recommended only because there is no other way to fly commercially to or from Maui.

Security line was outrageous. Longest security line ever encountered in my life. So many passengers in the airport missed their flights, I bet it must have set a record. Some airlines like American delayed their departure, but of all airlines, you’d think Hawaiian would have delayed theirs, but no. The airport was filled with passengers who missed their flights on all airlines due to the ineptness of the airport. This needs to be addressed. This is a disgrace! This cost how many people extra $$$ without any sympathy from the airport.

The airport itself was nice but the TSA was horrible. Staff were extremely rude and obnoxious. If you asked any questions about the process they mocked you and made you feel stupid even though there were no signs posted about what you can and can not bring on a plane. I was told by one staffer that bottled water has never been allowed on planes since the beginning of time, which is a lie. The floors where you have to walk barefoot was very dirty and sticky and they treat you like cattle, yelling and pointing at you like a prisoner. They would throw your carry on luggage around like a beach ball. Once you get past that it’s a nice airport.

During covid pandemic huge lines - no distancing in lines or seating or on flight. No mask enforcement. Basically this airport is a super spreader event in progress. Shame on the state of Hawaii, shame on the county of Maui, shame on Maui airport and shame on Southwest Airlines. Understaffed, impatient and rude at all levels Maybe this review should be titled - there’s a pandemic but what the heck we can still milk profits. 600,000 dead - what’s a few more.

I have been using this airport over several years about twice a year and each experience has been very stressful. It is chaotic, not enough space for people queuing either to check in luggage ur just to get through security People don’t know which queue to join and no one helps Once through to the gate, there is only one toilet at gate 2 and it was filthy. The tap was broken. There are three toilets at gate 1 and again the taps weren’t working and it was disgusting. Kalamata airport is getting more and more flights but really needs to get itself sorted out. It is a very stressful experience each time and very off putting. On arrivals one often has to wait in a long queue for the two officers stamping passports.

No information boards. Passport control incredibly slow. Nobody directing passengers as to where they need to be as they have no information boards. Just very chaotic experience. No toilets at the gate and we were delayed significantly.

Kalamata is a tiny provincial airport in Messinia, Greece and serves the Peleponnese - very few flights use it at present. It also has a military connection. Have travelled from here previously. Very fast and efficient check in for the BA flight. Once through security there literally just two departure lounge areas with basic seats - take a good book! Had a small duty free shop and a pleasant enough shop for food and beverages. The BA flight was the only aircraft there, and the airport was full so be aware. Not awful but just....small. It's either Kalamata or Athens with a 3 hour drive if you visit this part of Greece!

This was an awful experience - the queue for passport control took more than an hour. There was only one person checking passports which of course now have to be stamped due to Brexit, as well as examined, and there was no information, announcements or assistance. This led to the flight being delayed as it had to wait for all passengers and some passengers with mobility problems found it particularly difficult. There was only one flight going out at that time so I imagine that It's going to be terrible in the peak season. I suppose that it's up to the flight operators to pressure the airport to improve this so I will be writing to Jet2 and EasyJet to encourage them, although hopefully they will already be aware as it must be increasing their costs.

Shambolic! Small regional airport convenient for Messina but badly run. Despite being only flight to arrive, passport control took over an hour. On departure we arrived 3 hours early and stood queuing for Check-in, security and finally passport control for 3 hours 30 minutes. Others were further back in the queue and so we took off 1 hour later than scheduled. Never again.
