Without a doubt the worst run airport I’ve ever used. Flight at 15.20 on 11/09/2022. In a shambles of a check in queue at 1pm and about an hour and half later started queuing in the security queue. Arrived at the gate at about 15.10. Last passengers boarded at 15.45 and as a result the take off was delayed until 16.30. The evacuation of Baghdad probably went better. No communication and no queue/system management in evidence. This part of Greece is a joy but I will never ever come back to this airport. Disgraceful treatment of customers in the 21st century.

Flew into Kalamata with BA on 8th June and out on 15th June. Tiny provincial airport, typically Greek, in the Peleponnese. Our flight was late landing and was the only flight due in so luggage off of the belt surprisingly quickly and we were away. Returning to UK from Kalamata found that there was one medium sized departure lounge split into to Gate areas with just adequate seating, one small outlet for food and drink and a tiny "duty free" area. Wouldn't want to spend too long here as nothing to do or see once through security - bring your Kindle or a good book. Very few UK flights currently use this airport but this is, apparently, going to change as big investments are being made in this beautiful area, and the airport will be enlarged/redeveloped.

I've used this airport only once for an arrival. I came with a connecting flight from Paris with Aegean Airlines. I chose this airport, instead of Athens airport because it was more convenient and it was closer to my place. This airport is very small, I don't think it can handle more than 2 flights the same time. The good side is that it took me less than 20 minutes to deplane, collect my checked bag and leave. Kalamata airport is mostly use in the summer by European charter airlines. There's taxis available and a limited bus service to town. There's also a snack bar on the departures side. The flights are limited for a connection to countries outside Europe. Overall this airport is not very bad and it's a good alternative instead of Athens airport.

Mainly a military airport with few passenger facilities: in arrivals there is one male and one female toilet but there is more ample provision elsewhere. Snack bar either side of passport control and very small duty-free shop. If aircraft delayed supplies can run out in snack bar.

A surprisingly poor experience. Arriving into a small immigration room that could not fit an entire planeload of passengers a one time.  Immigration efficient, baggage arrived in a timely manner and then a single customs official who checked each passenger causing a long queue.  From customs straight out onto street, no facilities/toilets, nothing. Departing,  confused and crowded, security efficient,  collection of "terminal fee" long queue that merged with check in queues so people did not know who was queuing for what. Into departure hall, very hot crowded, limited facilities and noisy. Flight departure boards, just staff announcements. Rather chaotic. Only blessing was good free wifi - but naturally that was not promoted you had to guess and find it.

Small and old airport. One small ugly terminal with long queues. Once past check in counter and paid 150 php airport fee you are in a waiting area. Waiting area is on two floors with several stalls selling food and drink but nothing spectacular. One small duty free store as this place is an international airport, but anybody can buy in this store. Lavatory's even if not easy to be found are just ok. Gives you the feeling you have been parachuted back to the 1970 this airport but all ended well.

There is nothing good to write about at this airport. You must travel 3~4 hours from Boracay to reach the airport by spending almost 900 Pesos as of July, 2022. It is a tiny airport with almost no facilities. You will be allowed entry into the airport only 2 hours before the airport. If you reach early, either you can wait by sitting on the floor or go to numerous eateries outside the airport and have expensive and terrible food there. There is no free WiFi available at the Airport.  There is no free drinking water available at the Airport. Although you can buy the drinking water from the small coffee shops on 3rd Floor. Please mind that you won't be allowed to carry water into the airport. You would be asked to pay 700 + 84 Pesos as the terminal fees. This is not mentioned anywhere, and you must pay this amount in cash.

What a joke, 700 Philippine peso per person to leave the island that we didn’t know about. Not on tickets, not made clear in airport. Extremely unhelpful and rude staff. Shame, we had a lovely holiday, but the airport was beyond a joke. No facilities and falling apart. Won’t be returning.

Extremely bad experience after leaving Boracay. 4 International Flights leaving at around about the same time creating utter chaos. First you pay 550-650 peso to make your way to Kalibo Airport which involves van to the pier, 15 min ferry ride to the mainland and a 1.5-2hour bus ride to the airport via a company called Southwest. At this point you queue to get into the airport showing you boarding pass and going through medal detectors / x-ray bags. You enter a small room which involves 3 processes which no one explains and you can't even see where lines end or start. You need to 1st queue to get your boarding pass (15-30mins) then queue to pay the "Airport Tax" 700 peso per person (a lot of people didn't have the peso left as most are leaving the Philippines at this point and had to go outside to arrivals to exchange currency and then re-queue to get scanned back in). The last stage is the longest at which you need to clear immigration which is a spiralling queue within the middle of both other queues (check-in counters and airport tax). The immigration line is 5 or six wide of everyone pushing in which funnels into one queue of people getting upset. Got to the airport 3 hours before my flight and boarded the flight 30 mins after the gate opened and 10 mins before the flight was due to leave. I only had carry on thankfully. 6 hour journey in total. Highly recommend flying out of Caticlan which is 5 mins away from the Jetty port to Boracay. Ticket costs can be double than leaving from Kalibo and you need to fly to either Manila or Cebu to exit the country first, however cost factor is not worth the sour taste Kalibo leaves in your mouth after an amazing holiday in Boracay. Total journey time in Caticlan would be 2-2.5 hours. Arrival was fine as I did not have luggage to pick up and could organize my ticket to Boracay from Kalibo while everyone else was still waiting for luggage costing 600 peso in total (Bus, Ferry, Pier Terminal fee, Environmental fee and small van to your hotel). You wait about 30-45 mins before the bus fills up and leaves for the Pier in Caticlan but it allows you to grab some snacks or a fast bite with many stalls and shops outside the airport. I hear the airport has free wifi and shops however I did not get to experience anything other then queuing chaos, needing to board as soon as I cleared immigration. Signage was minimal to none. Arrival was fine, departure was a nightmare.

Power outages causing Air Asia's check in to be an old fashioned manual check in and the flight itself was delayed by 2 hours, resulting in many people being stuck in not much more than a glorified shed with no food and beverage outlets as these were after security. Galling that we still had to pay a terminal fee when nothing seemed to work. Also beware of porters hanging around who will snatch your bag up, carry it 2 metres and then ask for a fee. Next time I will go to Caticlan if I have the choice.

A small airport which got completely upgraded because of the FIFA 2018 games in Russia. On arrival be aware that border control takes 5 min per person. They thoroughly check your whole passport, visa and picture. The airport doesn't have many facilities, only 1 duty free store and some small shops. It's best to use the official taxi service, as there are many scams. A trip from the airport to the city center takes about 30 min and about 700 rubles. Most flights are domestic Russian ones with some international ones. Staff are friendly but don't expect smiles all the time.

This airport gets my vote for one of the worst airports in the world. Services are dismal. There is nowhere to sit. There are maybe 4 functional check in desks in the entire airport. One pair of public bathrooms (filthy). Not a single luggage cart to be found. The construction mentioned in another review seems to have been left unfinished and all the construction barriers are still in place. This means you can't pull vehicles up to the arrivals/departures area, you have to walk a considerable distance from the clogged makeshift parking lot to the terminal. Fine if you have one roller suitcase, not so fine if you have a large number of bags to check! We had to make 4 trips back and forth from the parking lot to check in to carry our equipment. Oh, and the icing on the cake? Customs agents that had to charge a "fee" (aka bribe) to get our equipment out of the country even though we had all the proper paperwork.

Kaliningrad airport is currently undergoing reconstruction so it might have improved after this review. The only way to get out of the plane is by stairs. They use one set of stairs per plane. Expect long queues at check in - usually there is only one desk per flight available. Before customs the airport has 1 bar 1 restaurant 2 souvenir shops and small chemist. After customs there is one bar and a duty free store. Prices are decent but the quality at the restaurant requires a Russian stomach in to appreciate the food. Make sure to use the toilet in the plane before landing after landing before customs there is only 1 toilet. The other toilets before customs are dirty and smelly. There is an information desk but they only speak Russian. There are enough taxi's available - choose a registered taxi (with a sign) to avoid being ripped off. There are no other means of transport (bus lines or trains) to leave the airport. The sound installation in the terminal is lousy. In combination with the poor English of the announcers announcements are incomprehensible. Security is pragmatic and efficient. There is an x-ray and metal detector when entering the airport.

Kalmar Airport is small and get's the job done for what it is. When you arrive it looks like a small red traditional Swedish house, The check-in area is not huge, and I imagine there can be long lines for larger flights. There is a small cafeteria in-between check-in and baggage claim, and this is the only source of food inside the airport (except if you are flying charter, then there is a small bar at the gates), so if you want a bite before flying, eat there. Security is fast and even has a fast track lane, speaking of priority, there is no priority check-in or lounge. The departure area has a bar and shop, but they are only open during charter flights. You can also pick up a free edition of Barometern (the local news paper) at the departure area. Boarding is smooth, but could take time if it's a larger charter flight.

Kalmar is a small regional airport. Only 2 gates, but we have to walk out to the planes the same way. Only a few airlines serve this airport. The staff are friendly and efficient, and the mood is quite cosy. There is actually no stress and the place seem to be very relaxed. There is a small bar and a small tax free shop which is open only when there are some international departures - mainly some charter to Mediterranean destinations. Main airlines using this airport are SAS and BRA for domestic flights mainly to Stockholm (SAS to Arlanda), and BRA to Bromma (BMA). The airport is clean, even the toilets are of a high standard. Even though this airport lacks a lot of things, it is one of my favourites.

Kangerlussuaq is where you enter Greenland on Air Greenland flights, you arrive here from Copenhagen on their A330 and continue on board smaller planes to towns around this massive land. Airport is very relaxed, on domestic flights there is no security check so you simply arrive, check-in your luggage and off you go. The only flight you have security check is the one to Copenhagen. Terminal is very small, it has couple of shops and cafes and also an outdoor terrace where anyone can enter and watch the airplanes. There is only one tiny luggage belt on arrival so when A330 arrives it's very packed and for some reason it took about half an hour for our luggage to arrive. They are now expanding airports in the capital Nuuk and also in the main tourist destination Ilulissat to receive larger aircraft, so future of Kangerlussuaq is a bit cloudy.
The conveyer belt was not working, ground staff are limited and quite unsupportive, no canteen to eat food. But the airport is very clean. Newspaper stand and water filter is well in sight.

This is the primary airport in Kansai area, serving Osaka, Nara, Kyoto, and even Kobe. It is well connected to Osaka via train and bus. Arrival: quick and easy, nothing to complain. Departure: quick and convenient immigration via auto gates. However, the KIX Duty Free area was operating inefficiently and caused a huge congestion. Instead of allowing shoppers to pick what they want, then self-check out and go, they were asked to create an order via machine, then lined up for confirmation and payment, and lined up once again for collection.

A pretty mundane affair, looks quite old and tired especially when you arrive. Departure was fairly swift, no long lines for security and staff seemed quite efficient. Overall a very average airport, but this is my only experience of a Japanese airport.

Cleanliness of Terminal 2 toilets and food section must be improved. Toilets seems to be unattended for ages, floor is full of tissues and stains. Bins are full. Food court, tables and chairs are under the same condition which is quite surprising as per Japan standard. Air Conditioning is not cool enough, seats at 5he waiting area are also not enough. However I still love to come back to visit Japan again.

Japan is totally great, but the only disappointment has been arriving and departing. Kansai airport struggles in almost every department. It is cramped and slow. When we arrived the queues to go through immigration were long and only a few counters open and they even closed others as we waited. Took 1.5 hours to get through. Staff were very slow to process just one person and seem totally disinterested and nonchalant about their job. The public transport options to downtown stop quite early (1030/11pm) so if you're arriving late that will be an issue. Returning to the airport to depart has been equally problematic. Cramped check-in area and very slow. When we were the next passengers in the we waited 10-15 mins to be called to the counter, and we were near the front, there was a very long queue behind us. After that the security area is cramped and crowded and also slow. No water or food/drink shop after security, just perfume, watches and restaurants. Very poor. We were extremely thirsty as we had discarded our water long before the security check. Had to hunt around for a convenience store but had to settle for a vending machine in the end. Prior to arriving I thought Kansai was a leading airport, but the feeling is that it wasn't designed to be this busy. So many improvements could be made.
Very Bad Airport. Queue for almost 2 hours for departure security check, need to improve the security clearance, wasting time just for queueing.

Very poor airport arrangement. Came here many times I'm the tour leader of Malaysia, many time group arrival at the departure parking no Trolley at all, very inconvenient for passengers. The security check point line is more than 45 minutes or more. Can't you do something to improve the waiting time.

Very disappointing offer (food, drinks, stores, showers etc.) to kill the waiting time at the airport.  At the airport, Terminal 1, after the security check (20h00) there was nothing except a small bar and 1 or 2 duty free stores. Very poor! For my next travel to Japan, I would chose to travel by train to Tokyo (2h50) rather and then fly off from Haneda airport.

Total chaos arriving at this airport. The lines for immigration were so badly done that nobody knew where to stand or what to do. Lack of staff to man the various photo and fingerprint machines. Despite already completing the immigration and customs formalities online and getting a QR code it seemed a total waste of time considering how badly everything was handled. Once out of this melee and over to the train station you are met with more chaos and only the actions of the kindhearted and very efficient Trip.com assistant were we able to understand how to circumvent the huge queue for the Kansai express train to Kyoto. It's an experience that really doesn't do the image of a good welcome to Japan any favours at all and left a really bad taste.

The airport was very quiet and relaxing. Security and immigration was a breeze although the process was a little awkward. I don't know how my experience would be in terminal 1 but terminal 2 did not have anything in the main terminal area except a duty free area and a drug shop. Kansai terminal 2 is definitely not a airport to go more that 2 hour early.

Friendly and fast service. Enough toilets, seats and bins. But shops close early and have a extremely poor selection in duty free. If you want anything make sure you get it before coming to the airport

The new airport serving Kansas City is a disappointment. Today, the outbound flight to Detroit was delayed, not due to weather even though we had snow and had to deice, but because the baggage handling system was not functioning and luggage had to be pulled manually off the system and brought to and loaded on the plane. One of the issues that was used by the KC Airport Authority was that baggage handling was an issue (it was). The overall cleanliness is a joke. Within the first month of opening the stains on the new terrazzo flooring were obvious and the number of stains growing. Also the accumulation of dust on the SS ledges by the people movers became pronounced. For a new airport, it will look like a dump unless the Airport Authority wakes up and realizes that maintenance and cleaning is something that needs to be done well and with pride.

The airport has been updated and it’s much better than what it was before, but still doesn’t even have a business lounge or place to go to if your flight is delayed and every time I fly through MCI, the ladies’ bathroom in the Terminal always has a very long line, because the other option is the ALL Gender bathroom, but a lot of women don’t feel comfortable sharing a bathroom with men.

Southwest 4 hour layover on a return trip from Cancun. Airport is quite nice and modern. With enough space to accommodate surges. I'll take this airport any day over an Atlanta Delta layover. Clearly a new addition to the Kansas field (did not experience old terminal). Customs/bag claim, re-check, and re-screen for TSA for the domestic leg was super quick. Really like the glass jetways. Friendly TSA and gate agents. Bag claim and TSA were all quite clean. Gate areas were dirty - and not in the post-rush kind of way. Heavy duty cleaning seemed neglected/deferred. One example that stuck out: Dusty and fingerprints on window area/sills, etc. Bathroom sink areas could have received more attention. Some soap dispensers not functioning. A small gripe: Impossible to get a bottled unsweet tea anywhere in the facility. Every retail business had the exact same drinks in their grab and go coolers. My guess is it is contracted out to Pepsico or something. What's the point of having multiple retail businesses if they all serve the same stuff? Overall, I really like the size and style of the facility. Will look forward to my next layover here, should the time come.

Getting from drop off to your gate takes forever. After you check in with airline they have you walk a country mile to get to security. Than its another country mike to get to your gate which was Delta but God help you if you took Southwest. The old airport was fast and easy. What were they thinking. Poorly designed.
The bathrooms look like they haven’t been cleaned in weeks. Splatters on the back of the toilets, dirty floors, dusty everything. Looks like all they do is refill toilet paper and seat covers
I have waited for about 1.5 hours to enter the gate. It was so disappointed and I haven’t experienced it before in any airport. The worst airport ever.

The old airport was great. Fast TSA, comfortable gate seating, no frills. The new one - not even close. Check in was very clunky, there's no real traffic flow, just a mass of passengers. Horrible, slow TSA (similar to Atlanta). Way too many shops and restaurants. Little to no signage for anything. The gate seating area only sat 55 passengers. More shops and restaurants, why are there any at all? An airport is not a destination, it's a thoroughfare. I attempted to find a bathroom and looked until I saw a sign flat on the door (no hanging sign). Overall a poor experience with something that was supposed to make life better. Next time I'll fly out of St Louis.

The new airport is very pretty but there are some important things missing. The signage is not great. They must have forgotten about signs for baggage claim because they only have sandwich boards in the main terminal area directing you to the baggage claim. We found NO SIGNS for rental car area. Finally got a broadcast on the PA regarding car rental location and shuttle. The TSA lines were very long even though not many people are here. They had the area roped of as if they were expecting a large crowd and didn't bother to shorten the lanes when not needed causing people to walk more than necessary. The new seats are uncomfortable. Our TSA person at the baggage check area was rude and didn't seem to know the rules for people over 75. I realize it is a work in progress but seems like some of these issues should have been obvious to the designers and planners. Lets hope it gets better as time goes by.

Feedback on my initial visit to MCI (new terminal). I am a Kansas City native --- this review is critical, as it should be. Overall impression is outstanding compared to the 1970s era terminals. It addresses the needs of a 21st century Midwest airport with all the modern necessities one would expect as a flying customer. First impression walking in, it's big. It spans wide and the design incorporating natural lighting with an abundance of windows is refreshing. The evening sunlight streaming in through different angles really provides a "non-restricted" feel as you walk about the terminal. The respective airline check-in counter/placements are easy to identify and span the width of the front end of the terminal for easy access. Security access is fairly streamlined and the entire process is able to accommodate large volumes of travelers (non-TSA airport - VMD corp) more natural light as you progress through each arm of the terminal (A/B/C) with interior lighting not overbearing. The walkways are wide and allow for excellent views of the tarmac, exterior gates, and various angles of the entirety of the taxiways and runways. Additionally, the escalators and walking escalators are positioned nicely and push you through terminal in a speedy manner. More shops, etc. at each terminal branch, providing basically anything the traveler would need. The vibe and local venues are all a welcome addition and definitely fulfill the needs of the traveler. Individual gates and structured well and offer comfortable seating and ample wireless device charging. The one thing that seems odd is the placement of the gate flight monitor(s). It is essentially in the seating area of the individual gates. Why not place it directly behind/above the agent booth/desk for easy and quick access and explanation (poor design decision). Boarding the plane, the traveler is treated to long glass jet bridges that allow for excellent views of adjacent aircraft and outside weather conditions. This is a well thought out design that many major airports do not offer. Overall, the new MCI/KCI terminal is a massive upgrade to the Kansas City area. It has the opportunity for expansion and I would expect future modifications to address design shortfalls and customer feedback. We concluded it feels like a mall when walking though the new terminal. Three things need immediate addressing - (1) Men's restroom upkeep and sanitary conditions unacceptable. Need to revisit the options of installing automatic hand blower machines and look at the cleaning schedules to ensure conditions do not deteriorate to the point of being an embarrassment.  Cleaning crews need to maintain a regular schedule on vacuuming the terminal carpet - paper and debris everywhere.  Please explain how the gate flight monitors are controlled by the city? How is this beneficial to the traveler or airline staff? Local control to change/modify the monitors shouldn't even be a discussion. This new terminal is supposed to represent the pride of Kansas City aviation.

Brand new airport that looks pretty nice but housekeeping services are poor in and outside the airport. They tried to make it local Kansas City restaurants only so don’t look for a Starbucks, you won’t find one. Seating at gates is sufficient with work table space as well.

Super nice and wonderful airport! It has so many destinations and the time slots for the destinations are awesome! The airport and airline staff are super friendly and helpful! This is a great gateway to arrive and depart in and out of Taiwan. The queue for security is never too crowded. Best airport in the world!

The ground staff were very friendly and helpful at Kaohsiung Airport, the security was fine too. However, there were only three imigration officials at the counters so it took a long time queing which was very annoying. There were many shops in the terminal but there was only one fast food shop.

There weren't enough airport staff. The security check was efficient but there was a long queue at the passport control with only two staff working. There were many shops but have only a single fast food shop. There were also enough facilities for passengers with different needs.

Always love to travel to/from Kaohsiung airport, very convenient to city center (and Kaohsiung train station) via metro, small airport but got everything you need (cafe, restaurant, duty free), ground staff/immigration/security always friendly and efficient. Both China Airlines and EVA Air lounges are nice, with plenty of food and drinks.

Very nice regional airport convenient access to the city via metro clean and well organized not many shops and restaurants but only 30 minutes away from city and all flights are short-haul who need to spend couple of hours at airport for shoppping? Staff are all friendly and helpful.

Awful airport no facilities at all no stores and the airport is small and old. Very dirty and messy horrible ground services. My flight delayed was delayed 4 hours and I didn't want to spend that at this airport.

I have used this airport a lot over the past two years and find it amazingly efficient and the staff friendly from check-in to immigration and security. It's hardly ever busy and normally you can get from the plane to the MRT station within about 15 minutes even when arriving on a packed A330 from HKG. Sure the shopping and food options are not great but KHH is so close to downtown on the wonderful new MRT that this is not really an issue. All KHH needs now are more international flights!
Kaohsiung International airport are one of the best airport to entry Taiwan. Now with all the transportation by subway which can easy get from Kaohsiung down town to Kaohsiung airport in 30mins.

Kaohsiung International Airport is great but small. There are some shops and restaurants. The biggest point is that the airport is clean quiet and efficient the directions are clear as well. Besides this international airport are really near downtown Kaohsiung. The subway system is partially done recently you can take the KMRT to any place in downtown.

I've been flying in and out of KHH for some time now and I think the airport is quite nice. Not a big one and not a whole lot of flights but compare to TPE airport which is about 1 hr away from downtown Taipei (depending on traffic) it is much more convenient as it is about 10-15 mins away from downtown and if you are visiting the Tainan Science park it is about 50-60 mins away. The airport only has flights to/from Asia so those who are traveling inter-con's will need to transfer at Bangkok Singapore HongKong which serves to/from KHH.

Very bad experience. I thought Islamabad had a bad service but this one is the worst. I reached 3.5 hour before my flight time, at the check in counter very rude attendees, I had a connecting flight Karachi - Doha, Doha to Italy they didn't want to issue my 2nd boarding pass.  I fought but with no results, I had to board my plane at 4.00 and we managed just few minutes before the closing of the doors. Bad service,  bad infrastructure, bad organization, worst management.

Absolutely worst airport ever. No order, no rules. Everyone doing whatever they please. People who have any kind of influence skipping immigration queue. No organisation on baggage reclaim. Worst kind of staff. Completely clueless and incompetent overstaffing. Makes me avoid going to Karachi overall just because of the trauma of this airport. Its sad how we cannot even manage an airport properly, how do we hope to manage the whole country? A city of almost 30 million people and has an airport this pathetic without any wifi.

This airport needs an overhaul. It’s an old airport. The arrival and departure from this airport makes you feel as if you just got out of the year 1989 and landed in some other county where it’s 2021. The state of the airport is in pathetic condition. Too many staff who look busy but are doing nothing. Long queue and only 3 staff on arrival desk, and they are the slowest people you can ever imagine. The rest of the staff are there but I guess they were not in a mood to work. All they did was walk around behind the desk staring at women. They give you the feeling of uneducated uncouth people. You enter the luggage arrival area and 10 porters are already there on top of your head forcing you to hire them because they don’t leave you until you tell them in a loud voice that you don’t require their help. Then there are people standing to collect your baggage tags then you pass through screening machines. If they want to check your bag for anything the scrutiny begins and after that you are left alone to pack your stuff back in your bags. If I was a (white man) oh boy things would have been so very different. All the staff would be saying “yes sir” I could break the queue and jump in line, I could pretend I did not fill out any form and I’d be told “it’s ok sir”. Someone would insist on picking my bag for free. A big upgrading of staff is required. Arrival area is too small and luggage trolleys, please change them.

Karachi airport is a travellers worst nightmare. During the 4 international flights I have taken in the past 3 months I have experienced painfully endless queues, unnecessarily cross checks and confusion amongst the staff. Which has resulted in all my flights departing late. I would attribute the gross inefficiencies to mismanagement by the administration more than any other factor. At the entrance to the international departure there is only one person to check passports for a queue of hundreds of passengers. That is the first bottle neck. As one progresses to the immigration counter to exit the country it takes 45 plus minutes due to understaffed counters and unorganised queuing system. Additionally there are too many supervisors just keep a watch versus multi tasking to process passengers and debating on line management decisions. Without a care for children, older passengers or the less abled. It is laughable that it is quicker to get into the country than leave the country in an era where digital gates are common across airports and workforces are trained to multi-task. What is more perturbing is the obsession with “re-checks” One can expect another 25 plus minutes in the re- checking FIA queue after immigration which again creates yet another bottleneck. The excessive rechecks continue like at a prison facility. In the flight boarding line one person from FIA yet again checks your travel documents. The airline staff checks your boarding pass and as you are about enter the aircraft some ten steps later the same checks are repeated again by another security staff followed by an airline staff. It makes one wonder if the rechecks are required because of a lack of trust in the capabilities of the staff, to keep a big workforce on the payroll or lack of integration between different teams and processes. After two and a half hours later you will find your self physically exhausted and waiting for your delayed flight to take off. I would advise you to please avoid the Karachi Airport if you have any other option.

As a frequent traveller, I notice how this airport's quality has been deteriorating with every visit. Built in the early 90s, the passenger terminal not only looks outdated aesthetically, the processes are as slow and inconvenient as those of smaller, poorly resourced airports from the 90s. The passport control counters are operated by super slow individuals who often aren't updated on visa rules and give you a difficult time. Their computers are often broken too. Baggage is handled without any regard and often arrives stained, wet or damaged. Fragile stickers are useless. It also doesn't look like the airport is cleaned thoroughly. The old and stained flooring needs to be replaced.

I have visited this airport after several years and this time, i found it much more crowded and dirty. The floors were giving a messy look. The air conditioning was not working properly so it was very hot inside. The airport offers very limited shopping (a small duty free shop and very limited food shops who offers very expensive things). The immigration staff was not bad but the lineup for both the Pakistani passport as well as foreign passports were too long and they were not in a hurry to reduce the line quickly. The building needs a lot of changes and renovations as Karachi is one of the biggest cities in the world but the airport gives a 50 year old look.

Even though still functional Jinnah International Airport’s age is definitely showing. No free WiFi, the major shopping areas are before the second security check, and the rush at the front of the airport before the first security check shows that space at the entry of the airport is inadequate and could be a major problem if air traffic significantly increases. The only plus is that I was able to clear immigration and get my luggage in about 25 minutes. The CAA should start to think about long term solutions for Jinnah International Airport.

❌Not Verified|  
Karachi Airport is nice but badly needs renovation as it is some 20 years old airport. Also, they need to work on the satellite concourse as they look outdated from inside and too compact with no space for expansion for retail and neither the gates. Disembarkation bridge is nice and modern.

Needs a proper restaurant. Toilets are not up to the hygiene standard and are very congested. I am muslim and offer regular prayers but call is very loud need to maintain at comfortable listening. Needs further variety of fast food international chains to have a quick meal

Jinnah International Airport is now 25 years old and is in dire need of a renovation. The drab brown and sand color is truly depressing, the departure desk for immigration is now too small and undermanned, the second security check should be moved before the shopping area, and worst of all the free wifi which was a god send two years ago has now vanished. The only thing renovated has been the air bridges which are now all glass and look quite nice. One could only wish the rest of the airport could get a make over like that.

Since my last review Karlsruhe airport has improved beyond expectations. Regular flights to more destinations and vastly improved bus services to Baden and Rastatt. Eating and shopping facilities need to be improved - especially on Sundays when the duty free shop and gate one bar are generally closed.

I use Baden Airport several times a month and it gets better each time - it is growing dramatically. The airport staff are always helpful and polite at check in and security. The airside cafe at gate one is never open and there are no local buses at all on bank holidays to either Baden Bhf or Rastatt (the main rail points for Karlsruhe and further - I had to take an expensive taxi. Rastatt aso has no bus service on Saturday but the airport still has regular flights coming in.

Flew into this airport again in October. The new terminal is now open but with only a handful of flights a day it is a bit of a ghost town. That aside it is now a very pleasant airport to use. Taxis are available it now has a couple of places to grab a drink or something to eat at reasonable prices staff are pleasant and polite. One thing to be aware of - if your flights are assigned to gates one or two you will need to make your visit to the " duty free shop" before you go there once at these gates it is too late.

A small regional airport ex-NATO (Canadian) serving inland flights and European charters (including Egypt). Elegant small buildings fast baggage and security handling very short ways. Hard to find with your own car (road signs? what's that?) and an absolute nightmare with buses (whose drivers sometimes will not even stop for the waiting passengers but just brush past them empty). You spend more time getting there than flying and that's probably the main reason for its lack of success - it is just too inaccessible.

I flew into Kasane International Airport onboard Mack Air, a Botswanan bush airline that principally services safari lodges in the Okavango Delta area. Kasane boasts a nice, new and pleasant airport, in spite of it seeing much more than people arriving to go to or from various safari lodges. Passangers walk from the airplane into the baggage claim area which though not large, is efficient and is air conditioned. As we did not require an immigration or customs inspection, passengers moved directly from the baggage claim area into the main terminal hall. This too is very nice, air conditioned, clean and pleasant and transportation services are available. Airport staff are friendly and there is a small shop where one can buy snacks and drinks. Though small and not very busy, Kasane's airport is a pleasant surprise and is from all I can tell, efficient, clean and staffed with pleasant and helpful folk.

Kashgar Airport is located in one of the most remote corners of China. It is a small airport, handling almost only domestic flights of which most go to or via Urumqi. I spent almost 2 days at this airport due to delays and cancellations on my flight back to Urumqi. The arrival and baggage reclaim hall, check-in hall and departure area are all quite spacious, even when there are many delays. Good overview and orientation inside the terminal. In case of delays the amount of normal seating in the check-in hall is very limited, there are only a few general seats and some seats in the small cafe in the corner of the hall. So be sure to get seated in the cafe when you have the feeling that your flight may be delayed, so you can wait comfortably until check-in opens. The food options in the cafe are limited to only 2: rice with chicken or noodles with chicken. Another option is buying instant noodles at the shop located in the check-in hall and get some hot water at one of the taps located in the hall. During delays there is not much to do at this airport, so take some entertainment. There are no airline staff inside the terminal, so in case of cancellations there is no one to turn to besides airport staff. And they do not take any responsibility and refer you to the airline customers service hotline which is not very helpful either. Utter chaos among passengers is quite common and happened to me 3 times here alone. Check-in process is OK, security screening is strict but not a real hassle. Short queuing times, as it is not a very big and busy airport. English-speaking staff is difficult to find at the airport. F&B and retail options in the departure lounge are very limited. So do not expect to have a nice diner before your flight. They do sell very nice local sweet and dried fruits. Wifi is available, but only if you have a Chinese phone number, which I do not have. Toilets are not clean, and don't be surprised when locals do not close the toilet door. There is no welcomers hall in the terminal, friends and family need to wait outside. I would not recommend this airport in case you tend to stay for a multiple hours. But this is the only comfortable way into Kashgar. Other options are train or bus, which most people told me to avoid at any cost.

One of the smallest picturesque airports in the Greek islands currently with very basic services but located in a scenic mountainous spot on the island of Megisti, also known as Kastellorizo. It is in need of an upgrade that could transform it into a one of a kind airport. Currently this airport is servicing Aegean and Olympic Airways flights from Rhodes in Greece. A taxi service is available (EUR 7.00) to the main town square of Kastellorizo.

Terrible airport, I was supposed to leave Nov 7, I show up to the airport 3 hours early and was told that the airport decided to shut down half of their flights and are no longer doing night flights and my flight was canceled and they didn’t have enough flights going out to get me rebooked and they didn’t know when I could get a new flight. I emailed the airline at the airport and the airports reservations area and they never replied. The airline was good enough to get everybody a hotel until they could get us rebooked which took 2 days. I had to miss work and accrued additional expenses the whole time. I finally get my new flight and checked my bags and went through TSA which was all fine but then we take a shuttle to the plane where they search everybody’s bag again, and then do a pat down again right in front of the aircraft. TSA and security must not be effective if they have to go to these redundant repetitive checks at multiple locations. Overall the airport is very ineffective, will change regulations and restrictions randomly and without any notice.
Very bad arrangement. Not enough seats to sit and wait. All passengers keep on waiting for check in by standing. Usually the flights are Late. It has become a habit to be late

The more the Nepalese government spends on this airport the worse it gets. The traveller-experience gets much worse every time that I use this airport. The process of getting a visa on arrival is frustratingly bureaucratic. The latest press releases from the Nepali government, states that this can be undertaken online and paid online. This is nonsense. You may be able to extend your visa online, but the initial visa on arrival must be paid for at the airport. Even if passengers print off their visa-on-arrival approval, they are sometimes sent to a computer terminal (as I was) to re-apply. This then means queueing up again to pay for the visa. Staff at this counter encourage travellers to pay for their visa in currencies other than US dollars – I was encouraged to pay in British Pounds but others were asked to pay in Euros, Australian Dollars and so on. After paying for the visa, there is then the queue with immigration officers and the queues for non-Indian/Nepalis are usually horrendous. Customs check number 1: Once clearing immigration passengers are met by soldiers in full combat gear who check you and your hand luggage. This check is personal and intrusive. Along with other male passengers my private parts were felt and grabbed. I have never been met by soldiers at any airport in the world nor, been subject to such rigorous personal searches. Customs check number 2: The first suitcase took over one hour to arrive on the luggage belt. Despite our plane having no more than 40 passengers, there was nobody there to place the luggage on the belt. There were literally hundreds of smartly dressed airport workers moving around, mobile in hand, but the person who places the baggage on the belt was not available. When passengers complained, they were told that there was no customs officer airside to check the bags before they were placed on the belt. Passengers having already received the unwelcoming arrival by Nepali officials/Army were getting increasingly frustrated and agitated. Eventually the luggage arrived after 70 minutes. Customs check number 3: Western passengers with other than withminimal baggage are increasingly pulled over by ‘traditional’ customs officers and their baggage x-rayed. This of course is at the Nepalese’ government’s discretion. However, in my view something has changed and for the worse. The international terminal has been reconfigured and upgraded but it is an utter disaster. I have never been in an airport with such a steep floor incline. This means that when passengers have eventually cleared immigration, baggage collection and customs they are met with a downhill floor! Many passengers cannot control their heavily laden luggage trolleys and end up crashing into walls, other passengers, or their trolley runs away with itself. It is a nightmare. Previously, there were long queues for the tiny elevators to take the trolleys to the eventual exit. Whilst placing the blame on a private company the government has installed an additional elevator – which shaves off about 10 minutes getting out of the airport (the airport exit is only about 200 metres from the customs check). TIA – Kathmandu Airport – is the gateway to Nepal for 99% of international flying passengers and is not the welcome that visitors should expect. It is sad that whilst other Asian countries are introducing measures to attract international tourists, the Nepalese government/TIA officials appear to be going in the opposite direction.

On arrival there one of my luggages disappeared. We didn't find it until the following day after looking back at the original point back in China and even going as far as to consult for an hour the airport CCTV of the luggage claim area and carousel in the security area. Only there we found where it disappeared. It was taken away by 'customs', who haven't notified either the airline, me (the passenger) or the ground handling services. No one. When we approached them, even some of their agents didn't knew it was there. It caused a lot of stress not just to me but to the airport employee in charge and almost a whole day loss of time while on the lookout. The security on arrival was extremely hot and chaotic, there was a security screening prior to entering the luggage claim area what i see the first time in my life and which is both stupid, absurd, infuriating and time-consuming. Most officers were rude and ignorant, passengers were fighting between them. On the way out, the airline (Sri Lankan) closed their check-in counters more than an hour ahead of time. They were impossible to be contacted or found. Once contacted, they promised they'll come down, they never did so i missed my flight eventhough it was delayed and took off two hours later. I purchased another ticket and i won't mention the chaos, overcrowding and extreme heat/absence of a/c, dirty toilets and absence of seating in the airport that everyone talks about. What infuriated me the most is that on arrival i found both my luggages not only damaged but opened and that someone scavenged through them looking for God knows what. Everything was spilled out and taken out of its purses and pockets, all clothes were messed up and small items were thrown out all over the place. I've neve witnessed something like that. I don't know what were they looking for but that doesn't happen at any airport worldwide. Maybe they were digging for some valuables which fortunately after the previous incident i took out of my luggage, for not to risk a repeat of a similar scenario. Internet doesn't work in most places without a Nepali Sim card, which, if you have one, you probably don't need public internet anyway. I witnessed more dirty and aesthetically unpleasing airports, but in terms of operational effectiveness and customer service, this has to be one of the worst in the world. Avoid at all costs.
Dirty Toilet, seats also very dirty. It is also very smelly. I never review any airport ever in my 16 years of travels. Only now because I am unable to use the toilet as it so smelly.

My experience with the security staff at the departure security checkpoint was absolutely terrible. They pulled out every single item from my bags and if an officer liked any item, they simply kept it, claiming it wasn't allowed on the aircraft. Even after bringing airline staff to confirm the item's validity, the security officers would just laugh and still refuse to return the item. This was a very distressing and frustrating experience, and I would strongly recommend avoiding this airport if possible. Their behavior was unprofessional and unacceptable.

Simply a terrible airport, the bad experience starts with a long queue at the passport control at the arrival, then you end up in another line for a totally useless security control before collecting the luggage, which obviously takes a while to arrive. But the big problems are at the departure. First useless security check when entering the terminal (useless because they didn't really check anything, but yeah, that's a waste of time). I queued at the online check-in line, which is usually faster than the normal one, but not there... I literally queued for 40 mins, despite there were no more than 15 people in front of me. Considering that it took only 30 seconds for me to leave the counter, it means that other passengers did NOT check in online but nobody cared that they were in the wrong line. Another 30 mins waiting at the passport control and you finally reach the small terminal, but here comes a new bad surprise: the shops and even worse the lounges are all BEFORE the security check... it means that you can't relax in the lounge until the boarding announcement, because you have to consider another line that could be just 5 mins or half an hour... so, if you stay too long in the lounge you don't arrive at the gate in time, and if you fear about it and leave the lounge too early, than you have to wait long time at the gate where you can't find absolutely anything but dirty seats and an useless shop (guess what? yeah, to buy a bottle of water and spend the few rupees I had, I obviously had to queue for another 15 mins). Obviously the airport is dirty as everything in Kathmandu, but one thing was really disgusting: at the security check the trays were horrible as people are forced to put the shoes on the same trays where you also put your belongings, jackets, laptop and so on... I really wanted to throw up when I realised it. Last point about the Horizon Lounge. Finally a positive point: the staff was really good. But the food, despite a big choice, is definitely not what I was looking for. I could eat only cheese, as all dishes were spicy and/or mixed with vegetables.

Security staff are completely inappropriate my bag was pulled to pieces with every item being tipped out and on to the floor. My underwear was pulled up in front of me for everyone to see and there was clearly no reason to inspect this. They were very rude and laughing and I felt very violated. After a overly thorough inspection, I was allowed through. It seemed they were just picking on tourists. Also, the airport is disgusting with bird droppings over the seats. Don't bother buying a coffee either, it must be the worst coffee I have ever tasted, it was so bad that I had to pour it away after a few sips.

Honestly this is the worst ever airport I have ever seen. This airport is dirty, the staff are all useless and rude always hungry for money. Everything in this airport is just unimaginable. Worst in everything, the cleanliness, the workers, the environment. The airport is like a zoo, bunch of animals, no sign board, no clear instructions on where we should go. It’s like a jungle.

The worst airport I’ve ever experienced. Appalling immigration. They don’t have good customer service. Their check point disgusting. Employees act like they are helping, but they start pulling your luggage and asking for money in front of all the airport staff. I have never seen this at other airports. They don’t have signs and they don’t have good customer service even at the customer care front desk. According to international airlines policy, customers have the right to carry two pieces of luggage under 28 kg. But they charged for both pieces of luggage. I feel like all the staff are just only looking for money.

Literally the worst airport experience I’ve ever had. My plane arrived after a 6 hour flight. Passport control took 2 HOURS! Three plane loads of people came into the hall and they had four members of staff working! Even the EU passport line was going out the door and took hours. Never, ever using this airport again. Added to which, when I eventually got through security, trying to find a clean seat to rest for a while before my journey home was impossible, filth everywhere on almost every section of seats. Bad management is the cause of this. How can you expect 4 border control staff to deal with such huge queues? Awful.

I am from EU, so I should not care. Terrible experience for non EU visitors passport control waiting time. Do something with that… It is shame to have airport like this in the middle of Europe with feeling like 3rd country airport. How you can keep complete empty windows for EU travelers and let few hundreds of non EU people wait in line of 4 windows for hours. It is not about capacity, it is about organization. Small change can have a great impact. Please reconsider it

I was rather disappointed by the lack of knowledge from the staff and security control. I suffered a Sudden Cardiac Arrest in April 2018, and due to no cause for this incident happening, I was fitted with an Implantable Cardioverter Defibrillator (ICD) later that month. This is a small metal device, wired up to my heart that acts as a failsafe, if the situation arises that I was to have another Cardiac Arrest. As this is inside my body, it is near impossible to take it out. Due to the nature of this device, I have been advised not to go through metal detectors, as it could trigger my device into action, and as such I contact the airport before flying to do so, explaining I will be carrying my Patient Identification Card on the flight, which gives the information in English, French and German. This normally is suffice information, and when I inform a member of staff at an airport, they allow me to come round the side of the metal detector to be searched by a member of staff. However, when doing so at Katowice, I was rather rudely told to put my Identification Card in the tray with my bag, while I was trying to explain to another staff member what it was and why I couldn't go through. I was told to go through anyway and it would be fine. As expected, my device did set off the metal detector, and I stepped aside to be searched. On being searched, the staff member felt where my ICD was, and asked me to take it off, despite it being inside my body. I explained how it was inside my body and couldn't be taken out, and while he seemed to understand this, my body search seemed a lot more rough than normal. I felt this was a very inappropriate comment for a staff member to make, and I was very disappointed at the way I was treated by the staff, almost with suspicion. While I am fine with flying now, the first few times I did so I was very nervous, and grateful for the support given by staff members who I explained my situation to. My worry is, if someone else travelling for the first time was treated like this, they may have a panic attack at the airport and be reluctant to travel by plane in the future.
Avoid if you can. This airport is a joke. No organization at all. Spend over 3 hours at border control on arrival from Liverpool. What a lack of professionalism. What a waste of time.

I cannot believe what unprofessional customer service we received. Most staff is making very unpleasant comments especially for those that don’t understand Polish language. They have no idea who they are checking and how many people they are checking for the passport controls even though they were given all the passports, checking every possible luggage even for those who are travelling with small children, repacking backpacks as they were over the limit by 3 cm. I found the airport staff absolutely useless.

The worst security screening I’ve ever experienced. They are creating their own rules and give you a small plastic bag(one per passenger) for your liquid cosmetics even these are properly packed in see through cosmetics bag. The comments workers make are unprofessional and offensive. I’ve lost very expensive and not replaceable items because I had to make a choice which will fit into their bag.

Departure section totally unprepared to safely operate during Pandemic State. Heavily overcrowded departure section of the Pyrzowice Airport (Aug 1 2020) with long lines of passengers awaiting for check-in and security control (with only two positions opened) with no chance to respect any physical distance required during the pandemic state. No reaction of the airport staff to passengers wearing no masks or using them incorrectly, let alone to stinky restrooms. The whole track from the arrival at the airport until boarding the aircraft under tremendous risk of potential infection by coronavirus. I wonder how such an unprepared airport was allowed to operate during the pandemic state. So much surprising, the airport is located in Silesian district, the then epicenter of COVID-19 in Poland.

Airport was absolute chaos this Sunday, the security line snaked through pretty much the entirety of the terminal with no clear beginning or end and took well over an hour to navigate. Once I got to the departure area in Terminal A, I took the escalators down to the bottom floor however the room was so crowded, I couldn't actually properly get off the escalators as the whole floor was blocked. Because the whole area was so busy, there were no real clear lines to see which queue people were in for which flight. The temperature was 32 degrees outside and there seemed to be no AC in the building too which caused the very long wait to be very uncomfortable too.

Staff apparently does not understand the principle of (paid for) Priority Boarding. First, they mixed up the gates, switching from Priority to Non-priority back and forth, causing confusion and causing people to run from gate to gate, pushing each other and annoying each other from losing their spaces in line over and over. The duty free shop in Terminal A cannot be classified as functional as they told me they do not have 10 grosz to return me from 9.90 purchase (when I paid with 10 Zloty). Very hard to believe since there are 3 cash machines in the store. In addition, staff hardly knows any English and the safety control staff once regarded my Nintendo game console (released around 2015) for a dangerous device - could use an update on recent technology. Despite the many negatives, there are some positives about the airport worth pointing out. These would be: functional phone charging stations, plenty of seating, piano in the waiting area. Nevertheless, many aspects to improve in.
Massive lines for non EU citizens. Bad experience! Some officers were doing nothing. Many counters were closed. Not recommended for traveling if you want a great experience.

Absolutely awful experience at passport control, people are treated very unfairly. Staff shouting at people no respect at all for travelers. Very poor trained staff not confident at all. Surely need to be retrained or SACKED for that sort of behaviour. Traveled round the globe and this is worst experience for sure. Would even like to make an official complaint to authorities. Staff needs to be shown which is right way of working ethics. Such a shame that sort of people still exists. Very very poor.

Horrible behaviour by the passport control staff. This woman at passport control took my passport and kept on repeating "open!" "open!" like a parrot. I am asking what am I supposed to open? She literally starts yelling at me in Lithuanian, luckily the gentleman behind me was Lithuanian and opened the finger print scanner cover for me, I had never seen a scanner like that before, and why was it covered in the first place? She never asked any questions, not even the basics. I thanked the guy behind me and left. I mean being strict at passport control is different but this sort of behaviour is disgusting and totally unacceptable.

I am writing to express my deep dissatisfaction with the service I experienced at Kaunas Airport on August 18. I was scheduled to fly with Ryanair to Copenhagen at 13:00 and arrived at the airport more than an hour before departure. While waiting, I frequently checked the screens for updates on the gate status, but it remained unchanged, leading me to believe there was a delay. When I eventually noticed a line forming at the gate, I joined it about 10 minutes later. Upon reaching the front, I presented my passport and boarding pass to the staff, only to be informed that the flight had already departed, and the gate was now being used for a different destination. I was shocked and confused, as no final call or announcement had been made. A staff member offered to assist me in understanding the situation. However, both she and her colleagues informed me that, as a small airport, Kaunas Airport does not announce final calls or provide updates. Frankly, I find this explanation hard to believe. Having traveled through numerous airports worldwide, I have never encountered such a lack of communication or unprofessional service. To make matters worse, I was told there were no available flights to Copenhagen (or any airport in Denmark) that day. This was extremely concerning, as I had an important meeting scheduled for the following day. Despite the circumstances, the staff insisted it was my responsibility to have boarded the flight and informed me that I was not eligible for a refund or any assistance. They offered alternative flights from other airlines, scheduled several days later, with multiple layovers in different countries, costing more than 200 euros. This was simply not feasible given my schedule. With no support from Kaunas Airport's team, I had to take matters into my own hands. I booked a last-minute flight from Vilnius to Warsaw, followed by another flight from Warsaw to Copenhagen, at a personal cost of over 300 euros. In addition, I had to rush from Kaunas to Vilnius to make the connection in time. After a long and exhausting day of travel, I finally arrived in Copenhagen at 23:30. This entire experience has been, without a doubt, the worst travel experience I have ever encountered. I am deeply disappointed by the lack of professionalism and support provided by Kaunas Airport. The following email correspondence with Kaunas Airport was unproductive, as they failed to take any responsibility for the issue. I strongly advise others to avoid this airport to avoid similar disappointment.

Absolutely terrible, bad experience, people treated like cattle, after check in and passport checks, waiting in queue for bording..stuck for over an hour outside, after 11 pm, frail and old people, people with small children forced to stand for very long time, no explanation, no seats, no toilets, waiting outside in cold and wet weather. Several times I flew through Kaunas it was the same- small, cramped spaces, not enough seating, they can't cope with any numbers of passenger flows. Rude, inpatient staff, arrogant and unwilling to provide information. I will avoid this airport at all costs.

If you are in a hurry to get somewhere never travel with this airport especially in the evening. Your flight will arrive on time but you will spend hours waiting in queue to get your passport checked and getting out. Absolutely no information about why no personnel is working. Waiting in the queue for 2 hours white the line not moving at all, people at the booth to get passports checked are standing in 1 booth for over 10 - 15 minutes. They accepted 2 planes landing at the same time and absolutely no staff to get people checked out. I understand if it was a big airport and multiple plains, but even there you have movement in the queue! I normally do not leave reviews but this experience was absolutely atrocious.
Very nice and clean, no problems at all. It is very small but it was still a very good and modern airport. One of the cleanest airports I have been to.

This is the worst airport I been travelling to. There is a long waiting time to go through passport control. Toilets are dirty. There are no places to eat, only a bar. I wanted to rent an automatic car. Four companies were closed on a weekday, another three said they had no automatic cars to rent and another said it is only possible with advanced booking. Customer service skills were poor in all cases. I decided not to take a taxi as the price of driving into the town was too high - 25 euro for 10-15 min drive. There is only one bus connecting to the town. It was filled to the brim, yet the driver was stopping every 3 min trying to squeeze in the commuters on top of the people traveling from airport. It was 30 min drive from hell. I got off at the bus garage and called eight companies to high the car - there was not a single automatic car in the whole town!

Truly awful service. Woman working at security was unbelievably rude, and continued to hassle me even after my luggage was successfully screened. Luckily, the airport is small so getting to the gate without checking luggage took about 25 minutes. At the gate, there were about a third as many seats as people, so many were standing / sitting on the ground - but it's being renovated, so hopefully this is soon to improve. Flying from Kaunas could be a comfortable experience, but the cosmetic improvements are moot when the staff have no respect for passengers. Did not expect such poor treatment when the country actively tries to attract tourists - would rather drive to Riga airport than fly from here again.

It's a small airport. No toilets close to check in or when waiting for check in. No sign to the check in place. Bad English skills. Unfriendly personnel at security. Two young security guys started to argue at me not asking for a explanation from me, trying to irritate me.

Kaunas airport is small and modern. Arrivals is super fast, especially if you don't have any checked-in luggage, you can be out of the door in 5-10 min. Super tiny bathrooms. A bar, kiosk and souvenirs in the main hall. Departures are compact. Staircases to go up to security and down to the gate. Another bar, kiosk and a small duty free in the departures side. Once again stairs to go to the plane. Overall it's fine, wouldn't mind using it again.

This airport serves Cappadoccia, a major tourist attraction in Turkey. It really needs an upgrade. The whole process in and out is one of utter chaos. There are no updates on gates no place to wait since there are very few seats. With crowds milling about waiting to board with the staff unable to control anything.

Small airport, badly organized not able to simultaneously accommodate many travelers (it is the main airport of Cappadocia, so there are often large groups of travelers). Chaotic and slow security checks, no seats in the small area in front of the gates. Poor services.

It is a small airport, but very modern, easy to get to. Plenty of shopping available and some food as well. I came across the nicest security ladies ever, which is good for a change! Sockets to charge the mobile are a bit limited and wifi did not work for me.

I traveled to Kazan for business purpose and was surprised to see that this airport is rated as 4-star one. This does not correspond to other airports I am familiar with. Access is only by (expensive) taxis. Space in the international area is very limited. Refreshments almost missing. Security area very limited and uncomfortable. The only positive feature I found was cleanliness.

Flew in on a domestic flight (from Moscow SVO) and exiting the aircraft getting luggage and leaving the airport took no longer then 15 minutes. No checks at all though (due to it being a domestic flight I guess). Because of those 15 minutes I didn't get a chance to check the airport in itself. During departure though we needed to wait for 20 minutes in the terminal or what you can call a terminal! Had a small bar and some seating areas. There was 1 TV broadcasting a russian soap and that was about it. Coffee was good though; and again boarding the aircraft was relatively quick. It is definitely not (as also stated in another review) a place you want to stay for hours. Luckily boarding and exiting goes really fast and I had no problems at all doing both. Overall impression is Fair.

Kazan Airport has two terminals but T2 a square shaped building some 50m from T1 seems to be used mainly as a VIP facility. Terminal 1 is a small rectangular building with separate sections for international and domestic services. Most likely it is the international section you will encounter on the regular LH service from FRA that arrives / departs in the very early morning. To say that Kazan has few facilities for departing passengers is rather an understatement a preliminary baggage scan leads immediately to a few check in desks and a very short walk to immigration control and a further scan for hand baggage. In the small waiting area there are some hard seats in a small waiting room and a bar. The business lounge has a few soft seats a fish tank and a television. Drinks here even coffee are to be paid for nothing is free apparently. There are no shops banking or change facilities at departure. They bus you the 20m to the aircraft of course. On the plus side this very small facility is a pleasant change from the corridors of FRA but not a place to linger to arrive too early or any place to be delayed either. It is a reasonably long way from the city but linked by a good road so it does not take very long to travel to the city. At that hour of the morning the roads are empty also. The domestic area from one glance does not seem to have much to offer either.

Arrived via DME from LHR and MAN with S7 airlines and same route return. Probably the fastest ever transit through an airport I have ever experienced even if it is only a small provincial one. Had to return the day after I arrived and with the assistance of friendly helpful staff collected my late luggage. All in all a great little airport if a basic one.

I flew in on Lufthansa's twice weekly flight via Samara no February 1st. They are the only international carrier. Apart from immigration refusing to acknowledge the computer generated form from the Russian Federation's London Embassy (which meant I had to fill one in by hand) everything was fine. I was in and out of the airport inside half-an-hour.

A nightmare is the only way to describe it. The airport infrastructure is too small to handle more than one plane at a time and you will be made to stand on the tarmac in the sun either to board the plane or to have your passport checked on arrival. You may also be halfway through deplaning when the ground crew stop you, while another plane taxies out. Tip - get the crew to shut the doors quickly or all the fumes from the departing plane will go through yours like a dragon's breath. Our skipper lost his cool with the tower when it happened to us on arrival. The temporary baggage hall is literally a joke; the bags keep jamming the belt as they enter from outside due to poor design and expect a wait of 45 minutes while the luckless lady on duty tries to sort out the mess. At the end of your holiday, when you go to leave from the newly built terminal building you will discover a number of things - there may be four flights getting ready to depart, but there are only 25 seats in each of the four gate areas. The duty-free shop is too small and the snack bar usually has a queue around 20 people long - tip - buy your food on the way to the airport. When you do go through the gate and down towards the ramp you may well have to stop for 10-15 minutes while the ground staff do their thing - it does not matter if you are old, ill or young, you will all be made to stand there without any shade. Still, it's a nice island when all is said and done!

The arrivals building is still inadequate for handling more than one incoming flight at a time. We were warned towards the end of our flight from Stansted that we might have to queue for quite some time outside the building in direct sun, and that we should consider buying extra water or juice to keep us hydrated. Whilst this was probably a good sales pitch I think that this could be good advice for this summer..have some water on you! We arrived at 13H30 and there were three more holiday flights on the apron.. Tui, Norwegian and Easyjet. We deplaned by steps and walked across the apron via a narrow concrete path (not particularly evenly laid) to the new escalator leading up to arrivals - thankfully it was working. Parents with small children were able to get their buggies/strollers at the airport steps, which was useful because it wasn't a particularly short walk if you had had to carry them. Passengers requiring special assistance had to wait onboard as there is very limited capacity on the ambilift, and very few wheelchairs. It was suggested that those accompanying wheelchair requiring passengers meet them once they arrived in the baggage hall. Passport control was swift, and we entered the baggage reclaim hall which has only one baggage belt. The baggage is brought up from the aircraft on trucks - one at a time, so it can take up to 40 mins to offload the baggage from a Boeing 737. Patience and good humour are good qualities at this time. There are toilets just before passport control, and just outside the baggage hall landside, but there were noticeable queues ;.. so go on the aircraft before arrival! Once you have your baggage it's a very short walk to 'outside' where the car rental desks are and the tour company representatives. This can only get better ... work is in progress to provide a new arrivals hall and they were certainly working on it on a Sunday!

The airport is mid being rebuilt, arrivals still in progress, but departures all complete. Departures was very quick, no check-in or security queue, it was a Tuesday but our plane was fairly full. Great clean toilets, friendly staff, the only major fail is despite it all being brand new there is nowhere near enough seats, expect to be sitting on the floors, also not much food on offer if you cannot eat wheat-based food groups.

Kefalonia Airport has a new hall, which is big enough for 200 passangers waiting. The queing went fine although there are not many desks. The toilets were new and clean. Coffee and sweat breads are in the hall. In de waiting area is a small shop. Personnel was very kind and helpful.

This airport is really tiny but can be chaos depending on how big the arriving plane is. You will deplane on the tarmac and will have to walk to the terminal, it gets messy as there is not enough space for everyone! I remember there was only one luggage belt and people will crowd around it! Make sure you pre arrange your transportation because taxis here are a rip off! Such a beautiful island but the infrastructure is terrible.

Arriving at Kefalonia wasn't too bad, luggage came through quick and we were off the plane and out within 30 mins. Departing was another story - chaotic check in queing, only 3 desks, signage is appalling, you have to weigh your bags at check in then fight through the throng to get them on a X-ray machine belt. The chap checking passports was plugged into his iPhone, the food from the overpriced kiosk in the departures lounge was woeful, the toilets were appealing with doors that didn't lock and toilet paper on floor. The departures area is too small with inadequate seating and poor public information. All in all, a complete dump, needs some severe investment.

Flights to Kefalonia from Athens. Arrival smooth with reasonably quick bag delivery. Departure less good. I felt sorry for the people stuck in a long queue waiting to check in for their charter flight. Olympic Air was fairly speedy. Terminal facilities are basic at best. One shop/cafe before security. The toilet facilities are dire. Very poor signage in the airport - domestic departure lane was closed with no instructions to join the long international queue and no gate information once through security. However, as there are only 3 gates, the guess was easy. Such a shame that Greek islands have such poor airports for really wonderful places!

Full concurrence with the stream of negative comments below. I can actually live with the fact that the airport expansion hasn't kept up with the rapid expansion of Icelandair and WOW (but they need to get on with the expansion ASAP) but the lack of communication and organization around what's happening around luggage arrival (on arrival) and departure times is worst in class.

Queued outside for 45 minutes (with Thomas Cook Airlines) then again indoors. Two check-in desks only. We were stood for 2.5 hours. Unsmiling passport guy and one baggage scanner only. Once through to departure its tiny - no smoking area, a tiny kiosk with over-priced snacks and nowhere near enough seats - people are stood, sat on the floor and on tables. Power kept going off as did the departure screens, there is no tannoy so the staff have to yell. If only I were exaggerating - honestly I'm not - the worst airport ever.

Kefalonia airport is really too small. Although it was quiet when we travelled and we were able to get through to departures quickly, I can see things might be very different if there are more than 3 flights departing. Once through the lack of seating was evident and the facilities very scant. There is a small duty free shop with a very limited stock. The only refreshment facilities consist of a small kiosk with not a lot of choice of anything and rather expensive. There was a huge queue for it. My wife reported the ladies toilets as "appalling", with no means of drying her hands after washing them. I can vouch that the facilities in the gents were distinctly insalubrious. It was a relief to get on the aircraft to depart - even for this we had to trail hundreds of yards across hot tarmac in the heat of the afternoon to get to it.
Extremely disorganized! It is a cluster of an airport specially at the gate where there is not enough space for seating and the lines to on board get quite overwhelming.
