What if they have to do maintenance to the train to the City instead of few hundred meters satellite train at Klia?? Moreover, every morning the airport register some delays officially due to "heavy traffic"!! It doesn't seem KLIA airport is on the top 20 for traffic! It was a fantastic new modern efficient airport years ago! The solved the problem of very long queuing on arrival now! I spent hours queuing there in the past. That's good!!

Absolutely very bad and unfriendly staff at counter J3-J5. Been waiting for a wheelchair for almost 20mins and yet to come. Promised by 10pm but still yet to come until 10:20pm Completely disappointed with the attitude of the staffs in spite the flight is at 23:45 to Istanbul. TK0061.
The whole airport air conditioning is NOT working—10 PM and I am sweating! Batik Air staff were very helpful, but I must say that the airport is one of the worst, with not much seating area.

No help staff at AirAsia luggage drop off machine. There were two security checks performed before reaching the boarding gate, which seems unnecessary and redundant, but causes more troubles to passengers. Third, the carry-on luggage weight limit of 7 kg is measured strictly. The customs officer asked me if I had used the same US passport to enter and exit. I said of course, and told her that she should see an entry stamp on my passport. She looked very unhappy. I felt unpleasant too by her unfriendly attitude.

The setup is poor and unable to handle large numbers of travelers. The flow is chaotic, the officers sitting around chit chatting, very few counters are open and the space is small. We went thru the custom scan with all our purses/bags, carry-on luggages, jackets, and everything in our pockets. There wasnt any officer managing the traffic so we had people cutting queue left right center. By the time we got to the other side of the custom scan, we realised that our belongings fell on the floor due to the short conveyer belt (why would any airport make a conveyer belt that could only fit 2-3 bags?). Before we could pick it up, we got scolded by 2 officers and said that we were too slow. She sat in front of the monitor screen and could’ve paused the conveyer belt before our belonging fell on the floor but instead she only paused it afterwards to get a chance to lash out on us. After we collected our belongings, we heard another yelling by the same officers aimed towards the travelers behind us.
Nice and very effective Airport. With an Business Class Ticket your within Minutes at the Lounge. The Security Check also Works smooth. Great experience.

A nice looking airport and on the surface but boarding was a complete mess. Rude staff made the procedure as difficult and uncomfortable as possible. You have to complete baggage check at the gate. The line is long and the staff are inattentive and bark commands at passengers. You can take drinks you bought in the airport onto the aircraft either. Then, once you pass through that ordeal, you are cooped up in a lounge with little aircon. Next, to add insult to injury, they got the gate wrong and we had to move to a different gate and go through the whole procedure again. It’s a shame that a nice airport physically is ruined by incompetent staff who just don’t care.

As a Malaysian on arrival only 4 immigration auto gates were dedicated to Malaysian's arriving. This lead to a long queue. As the remaining AUTOGATE’s were for foreigners which also had a long queue. Being a Citizen the airport need to sort out the long waiting time and line.

Koh Samui Airport was in general very cool! This was because it was completely outside. Although this is cool, it was really hot throughout the airport, which made it uncomfortable. The airport was also dirty and the toilets were also dirty and very smelly. The WiFi was also very poor. Overall, cool airport, just the cleanliness isn’t the best!
Brilliant little airport with thoughtful touches such as free snacks and water. Only downside was the open air departure lounges so no air conditioning i.e. humidity very high

Security staff are extremely rude, one threw my luggage in front of me and demanded that I open my luggage. When I removed the lighter from hand luggage he threw the lighter past me and started shouting. I’ll be taking this matter much further as it was a very intimidating encounter.

Koh Samui Airport is a lovely little airport and probably the most attractive airport I have ever travelled through. Check in seemed to be very efficient and no long queues. There is a large number of shops and restaurants available outside after you have checked in. Toilets were ok and reasonably clean but quite a lot of insects buzzing around! As many airport in Thailand they mix passengers on domestic flights through different parts of the airport and therefore passengers with international departures clear immigration and board the flight through a different gate to the domestic passengers on the same flight! Seems a bit odd but they have a system and it works!

The airport is pretty clean. Though it's small, it's pretty cute, like a park or resort. This uniqueness suits the vacation vibe of the beautiful island of Koh Samui. Different types of seating areas are available. there are a few shops, diners, and a café. Check-in and immigration were both very efficient. A courtesy corner full of snacks and drinks is available for free to all passengers. However, I wasn't able to connect to the airport Wi-Fi.

Cute little airport, everything functions as it should. No big lines, it's nice and clean and organized. It was very easy getting into a shuttle after landing and getting to the hotel, a great price too. I'm always a fan of getting to a new place and not having a chaotic mess of people trying to rip you off on transportation, that was definitely not the case in Ko Samui.

From the first step of the airplane at Koh Samui Airport I felt that I was in a tropical paradise. It was not a standard airport bus but a train of small wagons painted in bright colours. Airport is a complex of many small buildings in Thai style connected by open galleries. A lot of open space just covered with roof from rain. Many trees and flowers. Even an aquarium in WC. There are minibuses for transfer to Samui hotels and of course you can take an individual taxi with fixed price.

Koh Samui is usually an excellent airport; the tropical ambience, laid back staff, garden setting and impressive views of the planes make this a quirky experience. The recent floods and mass cancellations have, regrettably, brought this airport to it's knees however. Under normal conditions I thoroughly recommend this establishment.

I've been coming to Koh Samui for over a decade but my first time since they expanded the airport. The airport is spread out with quite a distance between departure gates and check-in counters. The security counter staff member was rude but nothing compared to the baggage security staff. I was asked if I had a power bank in my backpack and I said yes, then asked to show it, but was trying to put my belt back on. The woman kept saying hello, hello, hello mister show me, and I said can I put my belt on first, stopped and showed her the power bank to stop her carrying on. I must say the way she carried on was very unprofessional and rude to say the least.

Koh Samui is a real unique airport, almost everything is open-air. As they dont have any air bridges all passengers will be carried by little unique trolleys from and to the planes. They do have a roof on most parts of the airport but no walls, a very airy experience and a fine contrast to the usual.

The worst airport that I have visited. The checking process is slow, security check did not even have trays and was so slow that I almost missed my flight. The food was full of garbage on tables that no one was clearing. The whole experience was awful.

On arrival, the arrival hall and the taxi queue was stinking. My taxis was filthy. While departing, every part of the airport was dirty from washroom to waiting area. Overflowing dustbins, cats within the airport, stained toilets what do I even start with. I am pained to see the gateway to my own city like this.  Leaving this feedback hoping it catches someone's attention and necessary action is taken.

I arrived early in the morning from Singapore. I had trouble locating my suitcase at the baggage claim as someone had taken off a color identifying tag that was wrapped all around it. I had to wait for over an hour before noticing it as the last one left. The worst experience was at the security check. There were no lines and nobody to ask questions. It was a major struggle to find trays, but I finally managed. After waiting for a good 20 minutes, the personnel just closed the security booth. The passengers, including me, had to find another booth. The security personnel were downright obnoxious. It was a nightmare.

Kolkata Airport is a complete mess. The security process is unbearable, not due to long lines but because of utter disorganization and a total disregard for queues. The pushing and shoving in lines reflects a severe lack of discipline, contributing to an unnecessarily prolonged and chaotic experience.
This is a surprisingly filthy airport where the majority of the seats were dusty or stained. There are hardly any restaurants post security. Creates for a very poor travel experience

Rude behaviour from the security guard at the entrance. Travelling with my wife and daughter, a mixture of New Zealand and UK passport holders. The man could not speak English or Bengali and could not understand Qantas bookings or boarding passes (codeshare with Indigo) nor had no idea what an OCI for my wife was. Had difficulty reading the English names and then took out his frustration on my wife of Indian origin who kept saying ‘speak in English or Bengali only) and kept telling me in Hindi I presume to stop showing him my phone with two names in one booking (my daughter and myself). Then the worst most shameful behaviour was shouting at my wife’s cousin in Hindi and asking him to leave because he had no ticket and obviously had no confidence to stand up to this staff member. Airline staff could say or do nothing as they explained it was another jurisdiction. My wife finally had the last word by saying we have international passports this despite this man’s threat he could detain us for ‘time wasting’ he of course could not. This is not the first time we have seen such inefficient and jobs worthy behaviour from a domestic airport in india but today was the worst most unnecessary form of communication. Thankfully checkin, security and boarding staff were clear and polite with their communication and behaviour. I have no doubt if I had not been a white man, then my wife and her cousin would have received even worse conduct from this so called security official in a faux uniform. Please could these staff be trained in English, foreign passports, foreign name-reading and understanding code share or international airline boarding passes on a smart phone app before they are given such jobs - and how to behave with fellow human beings. Quite clearly he was biased against younger men and women of his own ethnicity.

Of the many airports that I use frequently, Kolkata Airport is one of the worst. Seating: many bus stations and railway stations today provide more comfortable seating. The seating area is very unclean. No cleaners are seen. Toilets very poor indeed.  Today, 14th Nov, the temperature was terrible. I had the misfortune of many early morning onwards travels from Kolkata... today, I am fortunate there are better airline connections. Dread to spend night hours here.

Biggest airport of East India, can get AC bus from different area of Kolkata to Airport. Queuing was small, 5 min to enter and 10 min for security. Few eating options before security and multiple options after security with 2 food court. Not much shopping options but can get souvenir if need to buy. Clean toilet, just one smoking zone which is very small. Wifi for 45 min. Sufficient chairs near gates to wait.

This is the worst airport I have ever been to. I have travelled across so many countries from a number of airports but Kolkata airport has to be the worst of all. Starting from cleanliness to the processes, from security processes or their knowledge, the airline executive knowledge, the airport managers knowledge and their incompatibility to address issues or guide the passengers. This airport and the management is clearly deserving negative ratings if available. I definitely won't recommend this to anyone. Also would like to tell them that go and see how Mumbai airport has been performing and serving the passengers.

We arrived from Bagdogra on IndiGo GE534 arriving around 1755 and transferred to an Air India flight AI 023 bound for Delhi with the UK as ultimate destination, scheduled to depart at 2030. We had to collect bags and then book in again with Air India; this went without any issues. Air India book-in was operating very slowly until one member took it upon himself to call all Delhi passengers to one counter, which allowed bag drop to complete more quickly than normal. We were not advised to skip the visa check however and stood in a queue for 40 minutes until advised to move directly to security. Here the queue was horrendous and moving very slowly. We spent an hour in this queue. There were insufficient baggage scanning machines, the security personnel were oblivious to the problems of overcrowding; those close to missing their flights were barging to the front of the queue - in sum it was an utter shambles. The head of security made a fleeting visit, made no attempt to resolve the problem and left again. There was no coordination between airline staff trying to get their passengers through security and onto aircraft and the security detail, consequently several flights including our own were delayed. We are used to travelling through Indian airports and know security can be difficult, but this was not only being run very incompetently but there were also insufficient resources for the number of passengers due to catch flights.

It's mainly a domestic airport. Internal sign and direction system is clear and well arranged. Immigration check procedure is efficient. The Japanese officers are well organized. Public transportation from Komatsu airport to city downtown only relies shuttle bus. The schedule is not frequent. The time interval is often more than one hour.

I've been using Kona Airport for over thirty years (from back when there were no luggage belts but instead bags were put on a large wagon and wheeled in). It's generally a good little airport, except twice per day when the major airlines have their flights arrive and depart - around noon and at night. At those times the airport is overwhelmed. If the airlines would stagger their arrivals and departures better (especially since they are now using larger planes) it would function a lot better. The renovation might make things better, but the aesthetics airside have suffered.

Probably the worst airport I have ever experienced. Disrespectful staff, very rude people in the restaurant, flies and bugs everywhere. They always wanted to kick people out if you do not order enough food even if we have ordered and we have a toddler with us. They asked us to parked our stroller outside even if there are other people parking their stroller in the hallway. They made me want to puke. If I could I would rate negative stars.

I have flown in and out of this airport several times and it is by far the worst airport I have experienced in the USA and throughout the world. There is no air conditioning or adequate seating. When it rains propel are huddled under limited cover. There are no walls or physical buildings but a series of open air pavilions. There are too many slights arriving and departing for the airport. There are limited restrooms. As an inter island airport it might be adequate but this is an international airport serving 777s, 787 and 767s. There are no jet ways, no cover to protect from heat or rain. A disgraceful experience.

The worst airport that I have experienced in 34 years of travel. Even worse than airports in developing countries. It is dark, dirty, brown, low ceilings, no functioning toilets in the gate area (!), there are almost no services, food, shopping. Scarce electrical outlets for recharging. There are two souvenir shops, and the "restaurant" was in disarray, old, uninviting. Seating in the gate area is restricted to wooden benches. Big 737s deplane and board from the tarmac. It took over 30 minutes for the handicapped and disabled to be hauled up ramps by the one porter on duty. Staff were friendly, and tried to reassure people, but we were late leaving because how long it took them to deplane, clean, and load people in wheelchairs. If you have to fly to Kona, plan things so you can spend as little time as possible in the airport. I can't understand how a state that prides itself in beauty and tourism would want this airport to be the first thing tourists see, or the last thing they'll remember. Perhaps there are plans for a new airport to be built, and so they are not spending anymore on the old one? Who knows. But there is no excuse for dirty and a lack of facilities in the gate area.

There are no physical gates but apparently some plane was using our gate so we couldn’t get off the damn plane even though they just need to bring the ramp over for us to get off. Had to wait an hour after landing because they were being dumb and just having us wait for our gate to clear up instead of trying to actually fix the issue and it made me go insane because it’s not like I can just leave, I am physically trapped in the airplane.

Horrible. No air conditioning. Ridiculous agricultural inspection happens twice. Twice. Why? The seating is uncomfortable. Everything is outside. It’s hot. And the buildings block any natural breeze that could provide relief. I’ve traveled to several “third world” countries and all of them have better airports. Not sure I would recommend coming here unless you get an evening flight out. And eat before you get here.

This is without a doubt the worst laid out airport I've ever visited. We found it incredibly confusing to navigate since everything is choppy and spread out without proper signage. The bench seating is incredibly uncomfortable and with multiple flights going out you're packed into the gates like sardines. You have to clear agriculture twice, why it can't be once I don't understand (is this an American thing or specific to Hawaii?). Once you have cleared your bags you can't actually take them with you to use the bathroom without rechecking them. And yeah, you actually somehow do not have bathrooms past the bag checkpoint so for travelling alone it's a massive headache. The security people tell you to have your travel companion watch your bags so you can use the washroom without re-scanning, but why can't they just add restrooms by the gates? Once at the gates there are no food options and even the snack/souvenir store closes well before the flights finish for the night. The open air may be good for protection against COVID but given how many people were only half wearing masks and some not at all, the staff need to enforce proper mask wearing is still required. The signage for catching rental car shuttles is also missing, which caused a lot of confusion.
Do not come early. They obviously do not want you to be comfortable. Alcohol only inside the restaurant, but zero chairs to sit in. You have to stand. Ridiculous.

This is quite literally the worst airport I have ever been to. Our disappointment began the night before when we attempted to check into our flight and could not. We sat on the phone for 3+ hours with no help given or even answer to our calls. Upon arrival to the airport to attempt check-in we were demanded to weigh our carry on bags even though we did not ask to, then since they were 2lbs over, we were forced to open our luggage (my underwear exposed to the entire airport) and move some clothing from our carry on just to our personal items (our backpacks). After that fiasco, we were met my incredibly rude and aggressive TSA staff that split my husband and I up and threw my husband into a line with no bins to put his electronics in and then proceeded to yell at him for not moving fast enough, which he couldn’t due to not have any bins provided to him! This airport also made us get a covid test after landing which made no sense after we just paid $280 to get one in order to fly here so their decision making process is basically not there. Again, worst airport I have ever been too and will not be coming back and suggest to anyone to fly any where else!

This airport, besides being completely dated, gives visitors a horrible impression. The 'restaurant' in Terminal 1 is a bad fast food facility. Why not provide healthy food instead? There are also insufficient seating areas in the pre USDA boarding area, and in those available there is no social distancing observed. There are also vacant buildings that instead could house a lounge, which this airport is also lacking. Lots of room for improvement!

Worst possible experience in any airport I have ever travelled through. The queues we have had to stand in tonight are absolutely horrendous. People with small children standing for extremely unreasonable amounts of time. We had such a fantastic time in Kos but will never come back.
The Chaos is unspeakable. Complete queuing chaos hundreds of people locked in narrow space, little Aircon and dirty toilets, really a shame for the airport operator.

Shocking! Massive queue on arrival, 2 staff on passport control going very slow, other planes arriving and bypassing passport check and straight 2 baggage claim, (our rep used the word “Brexit”) waiting ages and ages for cases, no carousel number so pot luck if you were at the right one. Departures unbelievable, queuing outside 2 get in then more queues, then back outside to queue again to go back in 4 passport check, hundreds of people going nowhere, once in departures words cannot describe it, hundreds of people in one small room - well that’s all we could see as you literally could not move, boiling hot, no seats, will we return - no!

The staff were completely incapable of managing the check in queues. We were moved from one queue to another and waited in line for one hour or more. It was a total chaos. I asked the staff what was the procedure to make a complaint and they were not able to tell me the steps but all they said was "sorry". Worst experience ever and I've seen many airports until now.

Absolutely disgraceful service, this airport can obviously not cope with the amount of people, it is just not equipped to deal with so many coaches arriving at the airport. The departure lounge is not big enough so they just keep you queuing in an unreasonable order of time, an unacceptable situation because they have nowhere for you to go and information given is appalling and you can’t understand even when they speak as the tannoy system was terrible. When we talked to the TUI reps they were not interested as they informed us this happens every Saturday night and there is nothing they can do to help anyway. I will not return to Kos, even though I had a lovely holiday I could not go back until this airport is refurbished. It can’t happen soon enough, I am so amazed that nobody is willing to advise their passengers what is to be expected for your departure even some seating or access to water a unbelievable experience for 2019.

Worst airport ever. Arrived to be told to queue to get into the airport, inside was chaos with no air conditioning. All seating was taken (I’m disabled), dreadful public address system unless you were Greek. I eventually got a seat thanks to a woman much much older than myself or I would’ve collapsed. The staff talked to one another constantly while they were supposed to be dealing with the customer. I was looking forward to going back to Kos but until the airport is upgraded to something more comfortable I will never return.

Queue to get into the airport. Queue to check-in. Queue to scan hold luggage. Queue to get hand luggage checked. Queue to get through passport control. All told, a 90-minute experience so leave yourself plenty of time. Also, I've never been to an airport where areas to sit on the floor are at a premium.

This airport is currently undergoing construction however the problems with the flight departures is a disgrace! One or two people to check passports for hundreds of people is ridiculous to say the least, I was still having my passport checked 10 mins before my flight was due to take off!

Total disgrace. One man at passport control. Hundreds of people queuing right out of the building. Disabled and parents with young children stuck in a hot room for approx 3 hours. No water supplied. Staff even closed the doors making it very hot. I understand renovation work is underway but that is no excuse for one man at passport control. No duty of care whatsoever.

Absolute disgrace and the worst airport I have ever visited. Six flights and one person on immigration. Total joke, disgrace and completely unorganised chaos. People are queuing to get in and buses cannot stop. They should hold their heads in shame.

Few years ago a new terminal was built. Although it looks relatively good for a small airport it is hard to get anywhere from here since it is expensive for airlines to operate here. There are only two small duty free shops with limited offer and enough place for sitting. If you are flying outside of Schengen area you will go through the old terminal that looks terrible.
Small but very pleasant. Nice staff and decent facilities. Better than any of the larger airports.

Arrived to KSC on a SkyEurope Airlines domestic flight from Bratislava on one of the last days in March 2006. The airport was modern but at the same time still very small - the baggage reclaim area was just a short walk away from the aircraft you could easily follow ramp activity and your luggage on its way from the aircraft through the large windows and you didn't have to wait long. There is a bus service to downtown Kosice but I don't think that they connect with arriving and departing flights - I took a taxi to my hotel instead. On the landside I noticed that - despite the size of the airport and the relatively small number of flights handled - the car rental desks were staffed (and not just equipped with a direct-dial phone to some downtown office or so). I would not hesitate to use Kosice airport again.

Quite simply an awful airport for its customers, considering that it is an international terminal; immigration and security staff are brusque bordering on rude and appear to express great delight in confiscating power banks, mine was only a few months old. Terminal is modern, toilets were very clean, with paper and bidets. However, air-side there is only one Starbucks and a noodle shop and a guest lounge that closes at midnight (I arrived there at 2315 and they wanted 36 USD for 45 minutes) and most of the few shops close at midnight. Flights depart regularly throughout the night but the facilities are not there if you have a departure in the early hours. The seating air-side is sparse. I'll never use this airport again. Oh, and you can not buy alcoholic drinks anywhere in the facility.

Shame on Kota Kinabalu Airport For a basic necessity such as toilet, you can’t even manage it properly! Airport toilets are filthy and no toilet paper Can you update toilet bowls with installed bidet? Train your janitors how to clean toilet properly? Have more frequent cleanings. Really Shameful even shopping malls toilet are cleaner and dry.

I'm in transit to this airport before continuing my journey to Kuala Lumpur. The cons to this airport is the boarding gates are shared between two airlines. There are two queuing lines in front of the boarding gates (6A & 6B) and the boarding room was full and hot. It's a mess when both passengers queuing at the same time. Other than that, this airport had basic services and amenities for the people. The toilet was clean. There are plenty of shops and food.

It's a fine airport however for International travel they scan the luggage twice, the first time at the entrance of the International Terminal and no outside water is allowed as per usual. They then after being inside the gates check your carry luggage once more, after you have filled your water in the terminal and at this point they make you dump your water again and then of course there is no water from that point on. The. you have to purchase water onboard. Makes no sense.

Honeymooning in various resorts in Borneo, so visited Kota Kinabalu several times during our trip. Check in area busy and crowded and Air Asia check in process a bit confusing, but staff very kindly helped us out. Rest of airport very well laid out and signage very helpful with ample seating at boarding gates.

Such a disappointment that a basic neccesity as such can't be provided for the comfort of the visitors. Toilets were smelly, wet with no toilet paper. Rubbish and sanitary pads were thrown inside a cubicle with the bins not cleared. Obviously no cleaner to maintain the standard of cleanliness. If one do not show that standard it is difficult for others to do their part in respecting the use of such amenities. Please do something about it and let visitors leave with a good note.

Third time transiting in this airport (Terminal 1) and was not satisfied with the quality of service from the staff around the airport. Staff were not professional and lacked basic etiquette. Airport is empty and has hardly anything to do. Immigration and immigration staff are not professional and lacked basic communication skills as I was told to wait for 4 hours without any notice or information before being able to exit through the immigration. Once I went through immigration I was shocked as the airport looked very untidy, unclean and old. The toilets are also very unhygenic and unsanitary as it reaked of waste and the floorings were all wet. The only good experience that I had whilst on my transit was eating McD. Would not recomend transiting through Kota Kinabalu, better to transit through Kuala Lumpur or Singapore.

A modern medium size airport, with ample space airside, got plenty of outlets at the departure area and efficient check-in counter. The airport is near to the city centre, and it is easy to reach by taxi and private transportation. Once through the security check, you will be greeted by an airy airside with an ample seating area near to the gate, and due to the design of the terminal, the distance of the gate is really short and gave ample time for the passenger to catch their flight.

Terminal 1 is modern, clean and spacious. Arriving 0130hrs there were several Immigration Desks open. No Landing Cards required and fingerprint scan for ID purposes. A few minutes wait for bags and we were landside within 15 minutes of landing. Taxi's are a fixed price of 45 MYR to the city. We departed late at night and there was a burger place open landside but everything was closing around midnight airside. Good security, quick and efficient check-in and Immigration. Not much comfortable seating air side.

Relatively a modern mid sized airport located quite near the city. Arrivals and departures were fast and hassle free with polite immigration. Several food venues with OK prices and a gift shop and as usual selling post cards but never the stamps! Even if the city is very close by taxis still charge 30-50MYR for the ride which is 16USD which I find rather high seeing that I pay the 30MYR equivalent when I return to Bangkok to the city. The former's distance is less than 8km and the latter is around 40km including tolls!

Krabi airport underwent a recent renovation and extension. The old airport was well organized and kept. The new one looks already old and rundown within a year after opening. Toilets were dirty with no hand dryer or tissues to dry. All air bridges were available at time of my departure. Both flights departing at that time were handled simultaneously at the sole bus gate number 7. it was total chaos because the holding area is not suitable for so many passengers. There is no loudspeaker system and the gate agents were shouting and screaming at the passenger, equally frustrated having to handle two flights at the same gate. It’s !

Small airport, arrival was smooth half hour queue at immigration but bags waiting for us..on departure ten minutes from check in to be sat at the gate on comfortable seats and soft carpet...airport is very clean and did not come across any rude staff...in fact they were very polite.

Extremely unreasonable and rude staff. They took away my astringent and toner bottles with just 20ml liquid each. No one till date has done that. They are seeing the bottle size and not the amount in them. Disgusting treatment of tourists

A very pleasant experience. Its a small airport, with limited number of flights being operated daily. 1) Very clean Airport. 2) Very trained staff. 3) Clean washrooms. 4) Nicely organized being small in size. 5) Few no. of shops not exorbitantly priced. 6) Waiting area also very smooth. Overall a very good experience.

The rudest staff I have ever encountered at an airport. They must do a roaring trade in Power packs. I too was advised that my power pack needed to be in my hand luggage. Then when my hand luggage was checked I was told I could not take it as they could not read the capacity on it. I offered to look details up etc but nothing I said was of any interest to them. This is the first time that I have encountered this at any airport with the same power pack. Again as others, I explained that I had been allowed to take it on the same airline to arrive in Krabi. There was no previous warning of this. When we suggested that we destroy the power pack (rather than hand over to them) I was told this was not possible. For such a small airport, in such a lovely place, this is such a strange rule and very unfair as it left me without the ability to re-charge my phone. As stated previously, even when we complained, I was told that I could not take the persons name, and could not complain to anyone! The other staff just looked on giving us dirty looks! To be honest their attitude was disgusting and the supervisor we spoke to, just shrugged and put a piece of paper in front of us saying that all Power packs should be in hand luggage, then pointed to the small print of the capacity needed to be visible! Pretty useless advise if you are not advised in advance by the airport or the airline we were travelling with.

As expected Krabi is a small airport. We had no issues with the arrival, however the departure was a whole other story. Staff were extremely rude and dismissive from the start! They wouldn’t attempt to communicate and explain why I could not bring a power bank (even though I brought it into Krabi via Bangkok) just kept showing me a card to read. Annoyingly the wattage was no longer viable and they just kept saying ‘no prove’ even though they could clearly see the power pack was very small and was nowhere near the wattage limit. I even pulled up the official product website to show them to which they just laughed and said 'no'. I wouldn’t be so annoyed if there was signage showing they aren’t allow or if staff had attempted to communicate why it wasn’t allowed rather then just laugh and put it in the bin.
Absolutely the worst aiport in whole Thailand. The most rude staff ever. Especially ladies who check lauggage at the gates. Try to avoid it as much as it's possible.

This is the worst airport I’ve been to and I travel often. The staff are completely rude and have no sense of customer service. When you try to speak with them it’s like talking to a wall. They took my portable cell phone charger with no reason. They assumed it was over 32000mvh which a monkey could tell that it isn’t that powerful. They also let another person keep theirs, so they are quite biased and not consistent. I have a lot of friends traveling to and through Thailand and I’m advising them all to avoid this airport completely. They should either completely shut down or hire competent staff members. If I could give negative stars I would.

The staff are extremely unfriendly from the beginning, they treat you with no respect and bad manners, I have never had such a bad experience with all of the staff of an airline before. They are disorganised and they do not understand English.

The worst airport ever. An International airport with some employees that don't speak English, they are rude and do not allow water for a baby and baby food also thrown. My power bank which they didn't make an effort to check or to know the capacity after years of usage and travel all over the world with no problem suddenly got thrown by a lousy airport like Krabi.

Very bad Ryanair ground handling staff picking fights with passengers. Please beware of this while traveling. I paid for extra luggage at the gate and requested the lady at the gate if I can carry the bag with me instead of putting it in hold. She took her time to check and then finally confirmed that I could indeed take it with me. At the ground a guy who called himself "team lead" repeatedly called me aside and asked me to handover the bag. I told him that I have paid for it now and she told me I can bring the bag with me. To which he responds, "you can't take it, i am the team lead, and you should listen to what I say". He then pretends to make a call to the gate and then tells me , "i spoke to the lady, she doesn't know anything, if you want to board this flight then you have to handover the luggage to me". I then asked him if I can go under a shed and take my laptop out and then return the bag, he says, i don't care how you carry your laptop, carry it in hand or however. I then finally take it out and handover the bag and start walking to the back entry, he again follows me saying that you can't board the flight, i don't like the way you gave me the bag, i am calling the police. At that point, (me clearly irritated ) told him to bring the police so I can also describe how he is harassing me for something so petty. My boyfriend then apologizes to him and explains that we specifically asked her to check because there was a laptop and she confirmed it was okay. We are sorry but we are also stressed with all of this. To this the guy immediately switches and allows the bag in. He then responds that just because u apologized I am letting this bag in. She should have requested me from the beginning and I would have let the bag in. Instead she started telling me that she has checked with someone inside and paid for the luggage and all. I deserve respect since I am the team lead and she needs to know that she has to respect me! " Why am I writing this review? I wasn't sure why I was harassed at the ground despite of following all rules and paying them whatever they asked for and waiting until the airport authority at the gate confirmed? It is a shame that the airport doesn't look into the mental health of their employees who clearly were taking out frustration on what they believed were "easy targets". And then they think they can just bully people by threatening to call the cops, just because he can ( i believe). He was clearly upset that he wasn't getting enough respect (in general) and I urge the Airport to review this behaviour. No one wants to really engage in an argument while on a trip but situations like these that are created for no reason just ruin a good holiday.

Arrived on time at 19:20 thanks to Ryanair. Deboarded by 19:32. Airplane parked directly in front of terminal, physically less than 100 metres from actual baggage hall. Luggage took 25 minutes to appear, what a time waster. Not sure if incompetent management or lack of staff

As a frequent traveller and also working in the travel Industry I would say this is probably the worst airport in Europe when it comes to customer service. Arrival to Kraków: only one person at the information desk, she was so unmotivated and reluctant to help we ended up buying the wrong tickets for transport to the city. No staff to help us around the terminal and poor signage overall. Departure: security completely disorganised, rude & aggressive towards passengers with unnecessary shouting especially in front of children. Strange layout to gates and little choice for shopping. Queuing before boarding the plane was chaotic, with little information from staff. Needs to improve.

The worst airport I've ever been to, both in Poland and abroad. Rude, impudent staff who think they are unknown. On Thursday, March 2, 2023, I flew with my 11-year-old autistic son from Balice to Dublin. Around 7:30 p.m. we were checking in at the conveyor belt where luggage and clothes are put in baskets. A staff rudely said to my son: "Take off your jacket", my son stood motionless, I said her that he has autism and needs a slightly different approach, to which she directly, verbally replied that she is ignoring it. The son began to get nervous, circling and repeating her words. it ignores She got my son to a point where he beat his head, went around in circles, repeated her words, finally cried. After 6 years of therapy, he has not been in such a state for many months.

I use the KRK airport about 4x per month for commuting and this for already a period of 3 years. From my >100 visits I can state that the KRK airport is very consistent in its ability to provide poor service. You could almost call it an achievement how practically everyone who works in this airport and interacts with customers fails to have any basic understanding of how to treat a customer. This mainly valid for the ticketing offices - the check-in desks - the duty free shop - and especially in the business lounge.

Unfortunately the experience of my transit at Krakow Airport was terrible. We still have covid and the airline/airport decided to load a full plane of people in one single transit bus to get us from the plane to the arrival terminal (we were all in each other's face, not exaggerating here, and I was squeezed by the bus doors on the ride). Absolutely terrible. The officers there smirked when they saw me hesitating to enter and signaled me to enter from a certain door in the bus too which I very reluctantly did. To add to this first bad impression, upon arriving to the terminal, they did not allow transfers directly through arrivals, but also they had no information and the signs to follow the "transfer" route were still there. Then two other soldier-dressed officers passing by me (while I tried following the transfer route) ironically remarked that "Can't you see where the others are going?" and continued while I stopped and said "But I am self-transferring and the transfer signs show to go this way". They never turned around and just continued on. Lines were not respecting distancing rules again in the PLF check points and everyone was extremely rude and simply had the attitude to get it over and done with you. Similarly inside the departure gates, the security check was very poorly situated with very short-length benches, and with the security talking in single words and rushing everyone remarking it is a stressful experience. All in all a terrible airport with terrible service and treatment. Only the food was good from the restaurants.

A small decent airport as an entry point to Southern Poland. Staff is friendly and acts efficiently, food and beverages aren't too expensive. Seating isn't the best as it's made of hard plastic. Overall a good experience.

The worst experience ever. I flew with my two children only. The check-in people from Ryanair and the security guys from passport and baggage check were so rude and aggressive. Disgraceful attitude and so much unnecessary stress. Already made a official complaint to the airport itself. This wasn't my first time there, but definitely the last one! Not recommending there, avoid if you can.

Absolutely worst place never check in your bags you will be robbed. I didn’t want to give my luggage but they forced me  they forced me and few ppl to give away their bags. Don’t recommend this airport.

My family and I experienced a great time in Kraków and thoroughly enjoyed our stay. We met some wonderful people and the service anywhere we went was exceptional. Unfortunately we had a bad experience at the airport when we were leaving the country. The security staff were extremely rude and almost barked orders at everyone. What a shame! A bad end to a great holiday. I really do feel the behaviour of these guards should be looked at and reviewed.

I have been surprised to learn that Pobeda does not feature on-line checking for the flights from Krasnodar Airport. Consequently, you end up queuing in an ugly, soviet time like terminal which is very small and overcrowded. Navigation in the terminal is not very easy given all signs are only in Russian. You cannot even connect your notebook, because WiFi authorization has to be done by the call from your mobile. The only seating in the terminal is in two coffee shops. Moreover, Pobeda is checking the size of the each single piece of cabin luggage, so the whole process of check in is very slow and unpleasant. No Priority Pass lounge. Airport is unfriendly, messy and mismanaged.

Left on domestic flight at height of summer season. Very long check in queues and staff worked hard to try to get people on their flights. No dedicated bag drop counter so no real advantage from on line check in. Terminal and number of counters inadequate for demand. Terminal was not very clean. Regular announcements re flights etc.

Easy access by bus or taxi. Two terminals - International on the right Domestic on the left - as you face them but only 20 metres apart. Signs in English as well as Russian although all announcements are in Russian as you would expect. How many of the staff speak English may be a good question - one who does is the AviaNova manager. Easy layout to navigate in domestic terminal although there is not much space for the check-in queues so they snake around the room. However the staff (for my flight anyway) were very efficient and the queue moved quickly. Security check was quick and easy. Airside has an expensive cafe and coffee shop as well as a news-stand and gift shop. Plenty of comfortable seating. WiFi is available - good signal but every site I tried came up with "Security Certificate not issued by Trusted Source" so there's possibly some bug in their software (I didn't do any more than just log in). Bussed to plane - only complaint as with so many of these airports is that you go upstairs to a departure lounge and then have to walk back down for the bus!

Kristiansand is very small airport just one story. Apart from being very small I have never on my few trips had any problems. No long queues (in fact almost none at all) speedy check-in quick baggage claim. Since the airport is so small you're almost out of the airport before you're inside. This may fit KRS particularly well since more than 50% of passengers are business travelers. Anyway my last trip KRS-OSL and OSL-KRS: Arrived well in time for check-in there had been rumours of cancellation and not surprisingly SK222 was more than three hours late - luckily with a seat for me 5-10 minutes before the flight departed. Total time at the airport was less than 15 minutes. When arriving back three weeks later we parked just at the baggage claims - had to wait five minute before the belt was moving then right in the car. Total time at the airport was 10 minutes.
Kualanamu airport is very good. Check in counters are good, the waiting room is comfortable and clean. But the toilets are not too clean, but no problem. The airport staff are good.

The staff were extremely unfriendly, not professional and not helpful at all! I had a quite big piece of luggage and they asked me to put the baggage in a different place from where I was checking in, I was struggling to put the baggage on the X-Ray and the staff just stood watching me. Not helpful at all. I'm quite petite woman and the male staff member just stood there watching.

Staff and service are unfriendly. Trollies aren't provided on arrival. Waited quite a long time for baggage and we were supposed to rush home for family matters. Service was not professional. If visitors from international countries sees services like this it would be a shame. Other than that I think the airport quality was good.

Used Kuantan airport last week flying Firefly from Singapore to Kuantan return. It is a small single storey domestic airport which has 6 check in counters 1 eatery outlet before immigration and a special holding area for Club Med guests. Bought a taxi voucher from the airport to Hyatt Hotel for M$40. Taxis in Kuantan are non metered and reasonably priced. Once passed immigrations (there are only 2 immigration counters) there is a small shop and a eatery outlet. Prices were 2 times higher than the malls. Only the arrival hall and boarding areas were air conditioned. There are 4 scheduled flights a day between Kuantan Singapore and KL.

The international departure airport needs an upgrade to attract more tourists and international visitors. It should include amenities such as cafes and shops in the international departure hall. As an international visitor, we are unable to use the airport's premium lounge because it is located in the domestic flight area. This is poor planning, as most visitors would like to use the lounge. Please consider improving this situation; it will benefit your tourism industry.

There is nothing after immigration for international departures. No shops, no cafes, no drinks, nothing. Also, no business class lounge. The business class lounge is in the domestic side. Terrible flow arrangement. I highly recommend everyone to enter immigration at the last possible minute. Otherwise, you will be bored out of your mind, and suffer from dehydration. Pro: straight forward flow from immigration to security to waiting area. Coz nothing to do. It is just one straight corridor.

The worst airport experience ever. Imagine heading early (4 hours prior) to check in for international flights, yet check in counter do not start operations until 2 hours before departure. So the waiting game of 120 to 160 minutes start. After check in, similar occurrence at departure immigration side. Not even able to cross over to Travel Club lounge. Rejected entry till the eleventh hour into departure hall. So another round of time wasting. As such, never recommending travel to East Malaysia ever. Above mentioned never ever happens in Kuala Lumpur or Penang. Quite disappointing to have the capital city of a state to have such operation standards. Conclusion. DO NOT come to Kuching if you're an international traveller. DO come to Kuching if you're a domestic traveller, i.e., within Malaysia.
Still no facilities in international departures. Airport management say there are too few passengers - it will stay that way if you don't provide basic amenities and signage.

I suggest Kuching Airport to improve their amenities inside departure halls. Our flight was cancelled for few hours, and there is no convenient shop to buy drinks, food. There is food court, but the prices are ridiculous. Souvenir shops are around but limited common food supply, 2 vending machines with exhausted supply, coffee bean shop, marry brown, famous amous cookies, sox world, cosmetics shops.. what happen? No varieties, please improve !! We were left hungry because not enticed with the food inside. Learn from KLIA2 at least...

Completely nonsense with the international departure. I have travelled to so many places and no airport is like this. When you check in, they require you to scan all your bags, not just the luggage but all the bags. Then when you get into the international departure, there is nothing. They won't even let you into the departure hall where all the food and drinks are because that's for domestic until you get through the gates. You have to wait until closer to flight time for the gates to open. No travel comfort or customer service at all. This is worse than the airport in underdeveloped countries like Vietnam or Cambodia. Their airports are better by a mile. Malaysia airports overall need a serious rehaul. Maybe go learn from Singapore their neighbor who got Changi Airport right.

A small and modern international airport with clean facilities and adequate staffing. There are reasonable shopping options, KFC and Starbucks until you go through passport control. If you are on a domestic flight the options look good. However on the international departure side you are in a deserted shiny new hallway with no chairs. A major negative. This leaves you wishing you had waited on the other side. Free WiFi works, slowly.
Airport is quite small and toilets are not so clean. Not much to do while waiting for your flight but for a short wait the experience is not that bad.

I have travelled through Kuching many times in the past (even before the current new terminal) although this was the first time in 3 years. The airport has become very grubby especially the general waiting areas post immigration/bag x-ray. The toilets were in an appalling state. The air conditioning is set far too cold (even for a westerner). My Malaysian wife also noted that the airport had deteriorated since she last passed through. Not a good advert for tourist arrivals into Kuching!

Having gone through so many different airports around the world Kuching Airport is definitely one of the better airports to use. Airport workers here (check-in counters security immigration etc.) are generally fine but can be improved especially on the level of professionalism in their communication with passengers. The airport may look very new but there is a need to improve some facilities such as seating areas especially the terminal Air Asia uses at one end of the single terminal and the automated passport gates at the arrival hall. Cleanliness can be improved as well particularly on the toilets. Overall Kuching Airport is a good and hassle-free airport to use.

Looks nice but that's all. On arrival they broke my luggage. It seems to be happening often at Kunming airport. Nobody, absolutely nobody at the airport speaks English, even the main information desk. There are people spitting on the ground everywhere so although the airport is quite new the floor is already very dirty. Passport and security can be extremely long, gates are far with no travellators and very poor signage. They seem to have some obsession about lighters, they take away lighters even from checked in bags! The worst of all, Kunming airport doesn't have a transit service. Meaning even if you connect with the same airline, you will need to collect your luggage, go through immigration, passport and security control once again and have potentially valuable stuff taken away. It's not worth the risk, coupled with one of the most primitive and disgruntled airport employees in the world.

The airport itself is OK for transfer (domestic to international). The lounge for (China Eastern) business class and Skyteam elite members is very disappointing. It is almost empty, without warm foods. The personnel there explained that the cook does not like to work in the evenings, such an excuse appeared on some websites two years ago and the airlines/airports have not taken any actions to improve?

I had to pass through Kunming airport on my way to Thailand. It was simply for a layover flight, but our layover was 13 hours. Given that the purpose of our vacation was not China, we didn’t wish to deal with the hassle of leaving the airport. We assumed that being in an airport for 13 hours, there must be some place to sleep, right? Well, we discovered the “rest lounge” on the bottom floor, it was full of uncomfortable chairs that do not recline and cannot be moved. I did not wish for both me and my partner to be asleep in an unfamiliar airport and country at the same time so stayed awake away while he slept. Our 13 hours was from 6pm-7am the next day - so the middle of the night. The rest area was filled with visitors who were loud all throughout the night, very hard to fall asleep. We moved to some chairs that were actually more uncomfortable than the first, but we could move them against each-other and actually lay down. Well that worked, until the literal police awoke us at 12.30am as they came towards us on segways and yelled at us and made us move the chairs back. We drifted upstairs in search of refuge. We found a sleeping lounge, I gladly was ready to pay money for a wink of sleep, they would not let foreigners use the sleep lounge! You would think that at an international airport they would have an option for foreigners to get some sleep in a situation such as ours. All of the kiosks were closed, we couldn’t figure out how to use the ATM which was fine, our fault, but when we asked restaurants if we could use our cards they yelled “no!” At us and turned away. When the kiosks did open up, they sent us from one counter to another for about 2 hours. Never giving us a straight answer, we were very sleep deprived and simply trying to get answers. Finally we got an answer as to where we could check-in, and then they changed it on us 3 different times. We ended up sleeping in restaurant chairs guarding our things until we were able to check-in. I understand the airport is located in China, but for a foreigner at an international airport I was very displeased and baffled by the quality of service. Will definitely never be scheduling a flight through Kunming airport ever again.

Kunming airport was terrible. I traveled though Kunming on my way from Nepal to South Korea. Since this is China, even though I was only in airports, I still had to go through entrance customs, annoying but a country wide policy I believe. However, airport staff were unbelievably rude, condescending, and confrontational. I'm an American citizen, but a student studying in China. Apparently I filled out the wrong card, for even though I was only traveling through China in transit from Nepal to South Korea, I needed to fill out my an immigration card because I had a residence permit. Oops my bad, but holy hell the response. The woman walking between arrivals checking information shouted at me to go back and get another, implying I was a complete idiot. When I was back in line, there were a number of people who had the information on their phones, but it had gone missing. (Probably they had it open in a browser that had timed out). They had no internet and were frantically trying to figure out what to do. They were international travelers too, so of course they had no working sim cards and airport Wifi begins after customs. The woman started shouting at them too, "Hurry up! Get over there! What are you doing? Where is your itinerary? No, no WIFI!". I couldn't believe it. Shouting in Chinese culture is incredibly rude. I walked over to them and told them I had a sim card for China, let me find it. We stepped out of the way of the flow of people to one side. As I rummaged though my bag it didn't take long before the woman noticed us. She marched over and demanded to know what I was doing. So I told her, "They need internet to get their itinerary, I'm going to give them internet." She just glared at me, how dare I offer a solution or any help to these people? "No, you over there! Hurry up!" "They have no other means to get it, what you want them to do?!" Finally infuriated and annoyed, the woman let them through without the itinerary! Apparently it was just too much of a bother, and all of the information they had to have, staff decided they didn't need and they let all them through anyway. The way they treated me, and especially the tourists from Nepal, left me so infuriated I was shaking. It took everything in me not to start shouting at the staff and cause a scene. I have never been so horribly treated, nor seen someone else so horribly treated at any airport or anywhere else in China. To top this off, the rest of most of the airport staff could not be bothered to be helpful. I arrived between 8pm and 9pm, and had to stay until 7am the next morning. No one could be bothered to help me! All I needed was information on when the ticket counters would open in the morning and where I could find the WIFI machine to get access (turns out my sim card was out of data). However airport staff just waved me away and wouldn't talk to me. I speak Chinese! It definitely was not a language issue! The best employees were the cleaning people who helped me find bathrooms, the elevators, and didn't bother any of the guests sleeping in the restaurant chairs at 3am. Those women were a godsend because I was exhausted after my flight and customs. Otherwise, the airport was a bit dirty, saw a number of cockroaches. However, the bathrooms were nice and had toilet paper and soap. Anyone traveling to China should know that often public bathrooms expect you to bring your own and while airports are better, they can still be hit or miss. Always carry your own.

Worst customer service, rude staff, not helpful at all. It's an international airport, at least learn some English and manners. Why do I need to collect the luggage and check-in again even it was just for 3 hours transit? Why so long process for checking passports manually? While handing over passport, at least read out the name on passport, don’t ask who is this? Custom police and security are very rude. No shops in the whole airport accept dollars, just accepts Yuan only. No display of airlines on screens. This would be my first and last travel via Kunming airport, Guangzhou is far better.

This airport is quite the improvement from the previous one. The old airport reeked of different terrible odours, was terribly under capacity and badly designed. This new one has addressed some issues. Firstly, the terminal architecture is impressive, albeit I find it unnecessary. There are very few widebody departures yet the airport is extremely large. Unnecessarily large. I like airports in Europe because they tend to have shorter walking distances. The check in hall is very confusing. It lists the airlines, and on the Thai Airways website it literally just says "Row H/J/K" And my tour guide says that what that means is that some days it is row H, some days it is row J etc. This is really confusing, as I went to row K only to find Cathay Pacific. Security seems to take forever and is such a weird practice, the screening is done in small rooms. I don't like this at all as if you get separated from your companions you literally have to wait for them to emerge from one of the rooms. One thing that bothers me is the immigration. There were no automatic passport lanes for Chinese passports, which meant half the lanes for foreigners were taken up. It was a rather long wait at passport control. Staff can barely speak English. The only English proficient staff member I met was the Thai Airways station manager. For an airport which is served mostly by A320s and B737s I cannot fathom why in the world would they deem it necessary for such a large terminal. LAX has the gates close to each other which is very convenient for walking. My mum did not enjoy the long walks especially having to rush to the gate, as she has knee problems. All business class lounges are operated by the airport itself, none of which (at least in the international wing) have a window. They at least have some hot food and various snacks. Also, seats by the gates only come in the form of cheap massage chairs. To sum up this airport in a word, it's designed improper to its purpose. I think this airport is really a bit of a design failure, and without bringing too much ethics into discussion I believe it is designed to awe passengers than actually function as an airport. Unfortunately all the large airports in China have this problem. Luckily with my next destination, Guangzhou, I can use Hong Kong airport which is by far one of the best airports in Asia.

Nice, modern, clean airport with plenty of check-in rows. Food options fine with a McD and noodle shops. WiFi not always present. The only nuissance in this airport on departure is the number of times you have to show your boarding pass and passport, 5 times, yes 5.

A very modern building and a large terminal but very long walks to and from gates. Not very clean including the toilets. The persons cleaning the toilets would keep the toilet rooms locked and you would have to request him to open it up. The security and immigration staff are very rude and disorganised. I stood in a queue for immigration security staff were shouting and screaming at passengers. My hand bag had already been screened and cleared and just as I was about to go a lady started screaming at me 'Check Check" and wanted me to put the bag through again. Their systems were clearly not organised much like our Indian airports. The worst experience I had was when I had arrived the previous night from PVG at around 12.30 am. Not a single airline counter was open in the arrival or departure hall and there were touts openly moving around the arrival area soliciting people for hotel and taxi. I will avoid this airport in future.

A very long walk between gates and between terminals. Little in the way of eating we could only find one restaurant that was opened and this was 10 in the morning. A very disappointing place and I will try and give it a miss when flying out of Chengdu.

On arrival a very large new complex. A long walk from arrival gate to baggage claim area. For a new complex it looks old. Dirty windows and patchy paint. I will have to wait and report on the departure process in 3 weeks time.

Rude and uprofessional Staff at Kutaisi Airport. Terrible experience with my family at Kutaisi Airport. The staff were unfriendly, unprofessional, and wrongly took my dry honey despite it being allowed. Worse, they were rude to my child, making our experience stressful. Poor service and zero professionalism!

Beautiful and good looking airport but there are not enough public transport options to leave. I had to wait 5 hours for a bus to leave the airport. The trains also run 1 or 2 times a day which is useless.

The worst airport I've ever been to. Very disorganized. The staff is unfriendly and terribly unprofessional. I wouldn't advice travelling through Kutaisi airport to the wheelchair-users, because the staff shows no respect and gives almost no attention to them. I travelled with my son, who is wheelchair-dependent and I was told by the airport-staff, that I had to "carry and transfer my 20 -year -old big son myself from his wheelchair to the plane-seat, as they had only one assistant in the airport ". Unheard of.! This airport should be avoided by travellers!

Kutaisi airport is probably the worst I have ever been to. Having read the reviews on the internet (2/10, on average), they have ended up convincing me that I am not crazy. Basically it is a small airport, like the Bratislava one, f. i.. But this does not have to be bad in functional-proportional terms. First of all, from the outside, at the infrastructure level, the airport is new, modern and even fancy. When you get inside it is, however, chaos. To start, there is a single screen the size of a low-end plasma TV in the center of the room, where you have to get within two meters of it to see the check-in or boarding announcements. To make matters worse, there are no places to sit, but 10 meters further back, where there are, in number, 6 metal chairs and a bench with a cut edge edge where you slip when sitting. The rest of the seats (perhaps the architects thought there would be too many), in the arrivals area, consist of wooden steps as a ladder, so that your backrest is the legs of the fat man behind you. Consequently, I have been on my feet for 3 hours and 30 minutes waiting. Secondly, although the size of the place is very small, probably like Bratislava or even smaller, the signs are situationist or utopian. For example, an "exit" sign points with an arrow to the WC, while the WC sign has an upward arrow, as if to go pee you had to ascend to heaven like the virgin. But these were not yet the worst and my fears predicted that the saga would continue. Exclusively, there are only 7 desks, which are for both domestic and international flights. However, instead of opening check-in for other flights for which there is at least 2 hours difference with the flight boarding, 5 of the desks are empty. My flight to Brussels, scheduled for 06:40, opens check-in at 04:40. As there are not enough desks and the organization is terrible, an absurd queue of people begins to form that, at most, would reach 100 people, adding all the passengers on the 5 flights there were. 1 hour waiting for check-in. But it's still getting worse. When it's time to go through the controls, we wait 1 more hour in line for the scanners. The problem is not the lack of personnel (I counted 20 staff for three scanners and more or less 100 people). One of the controllers makes me open my backpack and takes away the plastic fork (it's not even metal, it's the set of cutlery that you buy at the Carrefour for a snack, which although they are painted metal, they are not), and the guy takes it back from me saying that it can be considered a knife. In the end, when it comes time for the passports, I see a team of about 10 police officers (10!), all of them in their early 20s and I could swear that some of them are 18 or 19. The job of the guy who must be 18 is very simple, namely, to indicate: "Georgian nationals to the right; ohter nationalities, to the left". I go to the one on the left and then staff stops me and tells me to go to the right. An argument breaks out between the 20-something window police and the staff (even though the international desk was empty of people. Then another 20-something girl from the staff calls me to go to her desk, which is for Georgian nationals and I tell her that I'm not Georgian and the tips starts banging on the table and yelling at me that it doesn't matter and that I should go over there for the check. Anyway, I was very angry about everything, service, infrastructure, staff.

The most unorganized airport I've ever seen. At first, all passengers waited for an hour in line in front of the passport control, as the airport service was changing shifts. A bunch of employees just stood around, grinned, talked to each other and often went to smoke. Then we sat on the plane for the next hour, as the airport didn't give permission for departure, because they wanted to put 4 passengers from another flight to whom migration service didn't give permission to enter the country.

Modern terminal with efficient security. However there are not enough check-in desks during busy times, they don't accept digital boarding passes, food and drink is relatively overpriced, WiFi keeps kicking you off, prices are confusingly in both on GEL and EUR, there is only one small departure board screen in the entire terminal, before security cigarette smoke from people just outside fills the terminal, not enough capacity for people using women's bathrooms.

This airport is completely mismanaged. I arrived on Saturday morning and there were two Wizz Air flights arriving. There was such a long line for immigration, that people had to wait outside the terminal. Out of 14 desks for immigration, only 7 were in service. The whole process was very slow and inefficient. Unfortunately, I have to use this airport frequently and I cannot see any improvements or even any attempt to improve the matters.

Terrible experience. A very long queue at check in desk. Completely chaotic. No priority for priority passengers. Than follows security check with even slower queue. They operate only two lines, and this is despite an overwhelming number of security staff. The whole process is not managed, complete mess. No business lounge. Crazy price charged for any snack. Toilets are dirty. Duty free is charging for wine the same prices like in the normal shops, but in EUR rather than in GEL.  The cars are parking everywhere alongside the main road, because the airport parking is insufficient to the demand.I am using Kutaisi airport for many years. Never every service was good, but I feel rather than improving they are deteriorating.

Modern building but huge waiting lines to practically anything, just one plane arriving and you wait for over an hour at passport control, when you try to leave they let you stand in line to print your boarding pass again on the airport paper even though it has the same information as that one you just printed. Even if it’s some weird regulation they could provide kiosks or something instead of letting you wait in line with hundreds of other people - or at least a sign "please first go here before security check".

The worst airport I’ve been in last 20 years. It is visually nice but the organization is pathetic. Expect 1.5h waiting times at security/registration points. You can’t use electronic boarding passes.

No one should transit in Kuwait like me. They dont give u a chance to charge your phone here anywhere or smoke for free beside if you pay 40$ then u get 4h access to a lame buffet and some chairs and a smoking area. Could'nt even find a charger there while I sat in their expensive smoking room. Food was okey but not for 40 dollars and it was like nothing. Some dry fika, desserts as bread and stuffed sweet bread and only rice and like two salads and two different pot foods ... with chicken and potatoes. Machine coffee not good quality or taste. And its only men here.

Overall very pleasant experience. Landed in Terminal 4 (Kuwait Airways). Holding on to a Singapore passport and it took me just 5 mins to have my e-visa stamp. Very efficient. Custom clearance done under 10 mins and luggage out right on time. I was out of the airport in 20 mins! Departure from Terminal 1 (Qatar Airways), fuss free. Few DFS stores and cafes. Not much options but all good.

I had the unfortunate experience of departing from Kuwait Airport, and I must say it was nothing short of a travel disaster. The airport seems to be stuck in a time warp, with outdated facilities. The terminals are cramped and claustrophobic. The worn-out carpets and dim lighting only add to the overall dismal atmosphere. Navigating through Kuwait Airport is a challenge. Poor signage and a lack of clear directions turn what should be a seamless process into a confusing maze. The waiting areas have uncomfortable seating and a noticeable absence of any decent dining options. The duty-free shops offer a pitiful selection of overpriced goods. Security procedures at are a nightmare. The staff appear disinterested and inefficient, causing unnecessary delays and frustration. It's alarming how little regard they seem to have for passenger comfort and timely departures. The Wi-Fi is abysmal. Trying to stay connected for work or simply pass the time with online activities becomes an exercise in futility. I
I was traveling from Jeddah to New York and had a transit at Kuwait airport. Security guys at the security check are horribly rude. I was stunned by the rude behavior.

My flight arrived around 4 AM, and next flight was to depart at 7:40 PM. So, I had some time to check-in for my next flight. As my next flight was carried out by Jazeera Airways, I thought I could check-in online. Unfortunately, their website didn't provide the check-in service, and the app missed my country from the list. So, I found the information center and asked their help on how to check-in. They kindly pointed me towards the Transfer Desk. I asked the same from them, and they said they will help me to check-in. But then they noticed that I have more than 6 hours to my next flight. They told me that I cannot stay in the airport terminal for that long, and I have to book hotel right away. I argued that I cannot go outside of the airport because I don't have a visa. They replied I can book a room in the airport hotel. I managed to find the hotel's website, but the booking was impossible because the feature wasn't implemented yet. So, I went back to the information center to ask about it. Of course then we went back to the Transfer Desk where they told me they will organise the transportation to the hotel within half an hour. That half an hour wait turned into 2 hours wait before they had time to deal with it. Also, I had no more information about my check-in. So, now they deported me to the hotel and I have to pay for my stay myself. It was 8 AM by the time I walked into the room, having been no smarter about my check-in, nor what and how long was I supposed to wait in there. I thought that 6 hours before the departure of the flight would be a good time to leave. Around 2 PM I went back to the lobby to ask about how much longer should I wait for. The reply I received was: "Someone comes to pick you up around 5:30 PM". So, I went back to enjoy my room. At 5:30 PM I came down to the lobby, the receptionist's first reaction was: "Somebody will come to call you!" Then I pointed out to him that it's about 2 hours until the departure of my flight. So, by that time I had been in that hotel over 9 hours, no meals nor no place in the vicinity where to buy something edible. And now I was getting anxious about them making me miss my flight. So about 75 minutes before the departure of my flight someone came to pick me up, to transport me to the doors of Jazeera's terminal area, but I still didn't had my boarding pass. Luckily, from this point on everything went smoothly. I booked my flight via Kiwi.com who stated that they don't have any information, neither from the airlines nor from the airport that they are not allowing the passenger to stay at the airport for more than 6 hours. In conclusion, the experience is definitely worth something. I wouldn't recommend anyone to stay in Kuwait International Airport for longer than 6 hours if easy transit is a priority.

They are rude, they don’t care about other country people. When I get my emigration seal on my boarding pass she just throw away my boarding pass after seal it. That lady shout at me without any reason. Is how you are treating the people who visit your country.  Kuwait is my worst experience ever

The transit has few Duty free shops and only 1 coffee shop. The air condition is very strong and is freezing. They have 1 lounge that you have to pay $40 just to access it even for just 1hr. Then the prices of the beverages and snack are very expensive. I Don't think they can ever compete with the airports in the same region. I hope I will not have to transfer here again.

For one of the richest countries this airport is bad at all fronts. Not organized, rude security staff, below standard lounges & services. This should be compared to Doha or Dubai Airport but they are light years behind even compared with the smaller yet much better airports in Muscat or Bahrain.

The worst experience in my life time. Limited number of toilets and with long standing queue just to enter. Worst internet connectivity. Try to avoid the airport. Not spacious and congested everywhere.
