Worst airport. The bad airport service - they are dropping too far from gate and the facility. There was very bad toilets, seating, stairs, everything worst. They have the moving stairs but they are closed you have to walk up by stairs all over.

The new Terminal C is a significant improvement over the old Delta terminal. This is a spacious terminal with plenty of light from the floor to ceiling windows giving views of the airport runways/aprons and CitiField and Arthur Ashe Stadium. The walk from gate 75 to gate 97 was rather long. Restrooms are plentiful and clean; however, in some locations they could use more stalls given the number of passengers who traverse this terminal. Dining options are placed conveniently. I had a delicious lunch at one of the restaurants. The airport WiFi is very fast and worked flawlessly.

High marks for LGA new Terminal B. The building is spacious with plenty of light. Long walks from check-in to the gates and one has to walk through the  shopping mall to get to one's gate. Arrived on a Thursday at 7:00. Went to the TSA PRE line. There were about 20 people ahead of me but, with 4 stations open to check ID, the line moved quickly. Found myself in a too-slow security lane. People, why do you wait until you get up to the scanner to remove your watch, belt, jewelry, etc. Especially if you're in PRE, you know who this works! Still and all, I arrived at 7:00, checked luggage and was through security by 7:15. Not at all bad for this newly refurbished airport.

Absolutely no signage to speak of for Frontier, very hard to figure out where to go amongst all the Competitor airline signage, very difficult to find the terminal to go to, and the ticket agents and bag person was rude. The only thing going for this terminal was the security desk, they were nice, and the person behind the screener checking the people images was sort of funny, other then that everyone else i dealt with was rude.

While arriving to La Guardia Terminal B from JFK after an international flight, we were too early to check in. There is no restaurant to relax in without going through security It was too early to check bags therefore could not go through security but had nowhere to have a drink & food & relax. Very few seats Those that we’re provided were backless benches. After a renovation it seems someone should have thought to provide food service for those arriving too early to check in. Horrible experience

Terrible signage, inefficient layout, understaffed. Its bad reputation is well earned. Not much else to say. Ridiculous that they are trying to renovate the airport but simply better signage would go a long way.
The new Delta Terminal C is elegant, convenient and modern. Restaurants, gate areas, and restrooms were all immaculate. Check-in went smoothly. Keep it up.

I had a flight scheduled to leave a 6 in the morning connecting in La Guardia. Several delays and flight changes later, I finally managed to get on a plane, and then had to wait in the plane for another hour because La Guardia had shut down airspace. I will have to figure out another connecting flight because of this, and they made me check my carry on so God knows where that will end up. This has been a complete nightmare I will never fly through La Guardia again.

This has to be the worst airport I’ve ever been too. Not only is every terminal a 20 minute drive but the ‘shuttle service’ drops you half a mile from terminal C. Wait it gets better, you have to walk another mile once you get through security to get to gate 67 because they refuse to open a closer security checkpoint site. This is a pathetic excuse for an airport and honestly should be shut down.

I hadn't flown from LGA in years and was very impressed with the new Terminal B (home to American Airlines and others). Beautifully designed, spacious, and easy to navigate with abundant dining and shopping opportunities. Check-in areas are spacious and efficient. Great rest rooms. The new terminal is unrecognizable and a huge improvement!

We flew from Dallas to New York where we had a lay over and changed planes before going to Portland Maine. We thought! However our flight to Portland was delayed several times and then cancelled late at night when shops closed. There were elderly people and handicapped people and some medical issues. No assistance was offered. The passengers stuck together and tried to help each other as much as possible. Had to ask for snacks and water but no wheelchairs, no blankets, no directions, just a lot of rudeness. We spent the night on the floor freezing in the airport, then next morning when trying to leave nothing but rudeness everywhere. Security screaming at deaf boy because they wouldn’t calm down long enough to realize or listen to us trying to tell them he was deaf. Eating places the same way. Don’t mind taking your money but don’t care if you get what you pay for and rude to boot. Check in very inefficiently run.

Overcrowded and no consideration for passengers. Arrival was chaotic, and we had to wait as computers were reset for British passport holders. There were no organised queues, just an overcrowded room with no explanation for the delay. We come here every year to the island, spending our hard-earned money on our annual holiday, but we feel we are no longer welcome. Departure was even worse. We were herded like animals from a large crowd in the main concourse where we couldn’t even find the end of the queue. We waited with crowds all around us for at least 20 minutes while the new passport machines seemed not to work at all. Eventually, we had to present ourselves to officers behind glass, who checked our passports manually. We then spent 20 to 30 minutes in an overcrowded lounge with limited seating while waiting to board. We are in our seventies and found this experience extremely stressful.

There were no drivers for wheelchair passengers. We waited and waited. In the end I went to desk twice The young lady on the computer was very irritable and no help. I, as a very old lady, was beginning to panic as my flight EZY2274 to Luton was due to depart in half an hour. I think they got a lady staff from Security to wheel me to Departures. I was nearly the last to board my plane. Come on Palma Airport = you need to improve organisation of Special Assistance. The lady that wheeled me to Departures was lovely and helpful.

I was absolutely disgusted to reach this airport to find that I couldn’t check my bag more than two hours before my flight. This gave me grave concerns and anxiety relating to getting through security, and whether I’d be able to afford the plane on time. To be asked to arrive at an airport three hours in advance and not check your bag for an hour is ridiculous and I have never experienced this in any other airport. Furthermore if the signage had directed me to this fact I would not be so disturbed, having already waited half an hour to check my bag.

First impressions count, so as a result of the UK not being part of the Schengen agreement, we are the ones who have to wait nearly an hour for the single passport control staff member to scan everyone's passport on arrival. Not a good start, but our cases looked a little forlorn as they were the last ones on the belt. The airport is small and well designed, and kept very clean. There are plenty of seats. When it came to leave, the signage in the lift doesn't make it clear that the departures floor is not the same as check-in floor. Nice lift, if you don't mind riding up and down a few times. Next, easyJet tell you their check-in is open 2 and a half hours before departure. Not here, an hour's wait in line until an hour and a half before any staff appeared. Passport control for departures was much faster: still only one staff member, who was cheerful and polite, but only a perfunctory glance at each passport, no scanning. The airport is functional. When it's busy, I imagine it would be bedlam, as it doesn't have large spaces for more than one full flight at a time.

La Rochelle airport is tiny and small, however is efficient. Arrival: EZY8995, 17.05 (17.37), 28th July. We arrived 32 mins late into La Rochelle however got off the aircraft and was out of passport control in 5 mins, however you did have to wait outside in the pouring rain. The walk to the car hire facilities was long and there was no undercover path. Thus we got sodden. Departure: EZY8996, 12.35 (13.25). We got to the airport 2.5 hours before to drop off the car and then walked the very long walk to the terminal building. Once there the security opened earlier than usual so was in the departure lounge early. Unfortunately the duty free lounge didn't open and one of the vending machines was broken. The services in the departure lounge are poor and there needs to be consistency on when the duty free is open. Boarding began before the plane arrived and we were off quickly 50 mins late as expected. Overall La Rochelle needs to improve its walk to car hire and have more services in the departure lounge.

This airport is bad. It has to cope with several Ryanair/Easyjet/Jet2/HOP!/Flybe flights in the summer and doesn't even take the opportunity of opening up the duty free store. The check in opens far too close to the flight which causes massive queues and the 2 security channels open 15 mins after check in starts. Then you sit and wait
for 15 mins until your all called to queue up for your flight that hasn't even arrived yet. However upon arriving it was quick but now you have to wait outside for immigration. The staff however are fine (except when boarding) and the airport is maintained to a ok standard of cleanliness. Travel here every summer with Ryanair or Easyjet.

Traveling through Murtala International airport in Lagos, Nigeria is an experience. Staff are generally friendly and smiled a lot. My documents were repeatedly checked. I counted ten checkpoints altogether. At five of them, I was asked if I would hand over some money. They weirdest situation was that the customs officer asked how much money I carry, and then after hearing the honest (as he was a customs officer) answer, asked me if I would give him some of it. The airport is quite run down and processes are not streamlined. Boarding was rather chaotic with passengers placed on different coloured seats after the boarding passes were scanned.

An unsupervised, unregulated embarrassment. There's one bottleneck after the other for departure, including "sanitizing" luggage at entrance, two luggage weightings, and two window visits for passport control. All along the way are unauthorized touts trying to "help" you, and staff asking for bribes despite all the anti-bribe signs hanging in the terminal. Arrivals are hit or miss with passport control lines (can take up to two hours), and sometimes after a long wait you still wait for your luggage. And dealing with bribes and touts again. Gates are a mess and can't come close to accommodating the number of passengers for a flight, and there are useless security checks and a pat-down - again, with the occasional fishing for a bribe. It may be the worst airport in the world.

This was my first time visiting my homeland and my experiences both on arrival and departure were disappointing. The staff were all asking me for bribery starting from the carrier staffs till the immigration officers. What baffled be was on my departure time the purposely didn't tag my luggage leaving it behind, had to send my sister to retrieve my bag.

I travelled home from holiday in Lagos by myself with my two little daughters (1 and 3 years old). At immigration I experienced hostility, rudeness, lack of understanding and the most intimidating behavior by a female immigration officer. Traveling alone with two children is already difficult but when you are treated this way at immigration leaving the country on a European passport on a flight to Europe, it comes close to harassment. My husband is Nigerian and he has never been treated like this when travelling on a visa or with his residence card to/from the UK or to/from my native European country. I felt like the immigration officer tried to put a fault on me, constantly saying that she had been about to let me pass because of the children but the way I was talking to her would make her not to let me through. During all conversations I was most polite and even when using 'please' and 'madam' several times when speaking, she was still insisting that I was talking to her in a bad way. Most disappointing and daunting experience I ever had which made me feel that she was actually looking to be bribed. I was so happy when I was finally on the plane and I highly doubt I will ever fly to or from Lagos airport again. Just horrible.

A bit chaotic but not as bad as some of the reviews I have seen lately. We arrived and queued at the non Nigerian queue which was short. Had to queue and try to complete the landing card at the same time. Why can't we get this on the plane? Then immigration checks the passports. If you travel in a group then one person presents all the passports while the others wait to one side hence the chaos as several officials now begin to ask the rest of the family, where are your passports. I think they were asked 3 times! I presented the passports to the 1st chap, then I had to move across to the other chap next to him. He checks it again! Then he says to me, have you got something for me? In other words money. A bit aggressive and unfriendly. I give him $4 and go on my merry way. Then we wait for the luggage. Well! That took about an hour for our bags to arrive. And thats my biggest gripe. I will be travelling light next time. Out of the airport was just as chaotic. Touts everywhere, asking if you want to change money or a taxi or a trolley. Best thing is not to make eye contact and just walk away. Getting out of the car park was just as chaotic, that took an hour too!

So as always when arriving it is hot, one surprise the escalator was working. The staff were very rude at immigration and customs. When we got out people everywhere trying to "help you" but when they do they expect you to pay them and their friends. Once you finally get out of all that its fine. Not a very good first impression for newcomers.

I arrived at the Arik Air domestic terminal (having taken an internal flight from Abuja) and departed on BA from the international terminal. Arik Air use remote stands and bus you to the terminal. Business class passengers get their own mini-bus, which is more than BA offer when they occasionally use a bus at LHR. The terminal is in a decrepit condition but quick to get through. Fortunately I didn't have baggage to collect. The worst part of the experience was the chaotic taxi "queue" area outside the terminal. Fortunately, I was with a Nigerian business partner who knew the form, but I wouldn't have wanted to navigate that on my own. I departed on BA from the international terminal. I had heard the horror stories about Lagos traffic so allowed plenty of time to get to the airport. In the event the cab ride from Victoria Island was only 40 mins so I was very early. I checked in online and printed by own boarding pass so by-passed check-in. The terminal is in a bad condition (although not as awful as the domestic one) but there were no queues and it was actually quite efficient. As I had checked in online I didn't know about or have a departure card. The immigration officer filled in it for me. I think he was expecting a "tip" but I just smiled and walked away. The BA lounge is like something from the 1970s, but plenty of seats and a reasonably good selection of snacks. The priority boarding procedure was a bit chaotic but not too bad. They let "infants" board first, which seemed to include kids of up to about 15 years old! All in all, not as bad as expected.

The procedure in the Lagos airport was to irritate and inconvenient the passengers. First, the airport did not turn on the air condition even though they have the unit in the hallway walking up to the departure gate.  Upon entering the airport building, you must weight your luggage on a scale. Then wait in line. Before you get to the airline counter, you must go thru a screening to produce your printed itinerary and show proof of the credit card that purchase the ticket. Then you wait in line again to the counter. The luggage must be lifted up a meter high onto a stainless steel table and opened to have an officers to hand search. At the checkin counter, you check in the bags and get your bag weighed and your boarding pass. They give you a yellow color departure card to fill out and specify exactly how much foreign and local currency are with you. Time to change the currency (4 to 5 different booths). Before enter departure area, the passport and boarding pass was checked by a guard, then queue up to the immigration. Before you get your immigration stamped on your passport, you get to have someone check your departure card boarding pass again. Then the immigration stamp on your passport and collect the yellow departure card. However, I saw the immigration officer looking into my eye, the right hand holding onto my passport, and the left finger were thumbing or playing with his left fingers to signify handling over money. I looked at him and smiled and shake my head. Then, I went thru the security line with shoes off and laptop out on to the x-ray machine. Everyone get padded down. And I got my shoes back and walked away towards the Duty Free store. Going thru the store is the only way to the gate but there was no sign. I hesitated and stopped, an officer called me to halt. He wanted to know how much money I was carrying and whether I can spare some change. A Nigerian lady behind me just passed Niara 200 into his hand and quickly walked away (because I was in the front and delaying the line); while I had to explain to the officer that I had less than N900. I took out my billfold showing the Nigerian money and count in front of him. He was satisfied and let me go knowing there is too little money to extort from me. I went to the end of the hallway at gate #44 and waited in line to have the boarding pass scanned by the airline staff. Directly behind this airline staff about literally 2 feet away, sat a lady and wanted to see my passport and boarding pass. Then, I walked up a few meter in front, all items in my carry on bag were taken out, placed on the stainless steel table, and every pockets of the bags were checked. Then had me to take off the shoes to have body padded down again. Finally I sat on the chair in the hot room and wait to board the plane. One thing for sure is that all of these checks reduced the chance of terrorists bring in any weapon but what an experience.

Lagos Airport cleanliness was horrible. Check-in time was outrageously long. Check-in hall was not air conditioned. Lounge was fine. Customer service was fine, not great though. WiFi is not secure. Flight info boards are incorrect. when I flew South African Airways last year our flight was late but the board said "On Time" - overall airport was poor.

Transiting through Lagos to catch a United flight to Houston was an unmitigated disaster. Immigration sent me to baggage claim to look for my bag even though it was checked all the way to the US. Took my passport. 8 different people will tell you 8 different stories or people to go talk to. Finally with my passport located I was escorted to the gate through Duty Free, security checkpoints etc. At the gate, my bag was checked, scanned, and rescanned and rescanned as the scanner needed re-alignment. In 15 minutes, I was checked 5 times by the same security staff even though I was just standing there the whole time. What possibly could have changed every 3 minutes requiring a check? The airport itself has no air conditioning, poor seating areas at gates and is highly disorganized and dysfunctional. I have been to many similar airports with infrastructure and organization that isn't close to the circus in Lagos. Avoid this airport if you can connect elsewhere.

The slowest check-in process I have ever seen. The ticketing officers keep chit-chatting with each other meanwhile the the queue is extremely long. No sense of urgency at all. All of a sudden the officer missing in action for almost 15 minutes.

Very small considering that it serves such a large city but a clean airport. There were very few options for food inside the departures lounge. The burger meal at Mr. Cod was decent considering we didn't have much options. However the escalator to the CIP lounge upstairs was non-functional and the outside of the lounge area itself gave the feeling that the lounge would be closed. The arrivals terminal was also very small but no complaints there since we got luggage quickly and were able to exit.

We arrived well in time for our flight, and stood in line for terminal entrance. During our time in Pakistan we have been guided to the front of lines quite a few times, so were not surprised that this happened here as well by 2 members of airport staff. We gave a small tip when inside, but soon they asked for big amounts of western money (we gave 4$, which is quite a lot for Pakistani standards, they wanted 40€). We ripped away our luggage and walked away. They dripped off. Once inside, long lines for passport control, lounges closed but a decent departure hall with enough seating.

Nice airport but needs modification.  I have been travelling through this Airport for some time and it is not the best, but it is being upgraded and work is going on right now so hopefully it will be a very nice and beautiful Air port with a lot of new facilities. Airport need better management in dealing with multiple flights and improving the cleanliness.

Make sure to have a printout of your visa to Pakistan and of your boarding pass. Without the latter, you will not be allowed into the building. They request to see the visa into Pakistan in one of the many document checks. Officers are not pleasant. Very ugly, old airport. There is the option to pay 15 GBP to access a lounge that does not have much to offer regarding drinks and food, but you have access to a comfortable seat and wifi.

I am a frequent domestic traveler. The route usually I take is LHE to KHI. When you reached Lahore airport you can always sense negative vibes. Poor management, poor hygiene, seat comfort level at the lounge is at the worst. When you will land at KIHI airport it seems a bit high end in terms of infrastructure and glass bridges.

When arriving, you can see the agricultural beauty and the city of Lahore and the country of Pakistan. The airport is very nice. Immigration is busy and crowded. Staff were vigilant and happy to assist with any baggage related queries and baggage also arrived on time. The washrooms are very wet and needs improvements. The airport needs more duty free shops. WiFi and connectivity are fast and quick to connect. The check-in is a bit slow and there is always a big line.

The airport is very nice and average. The check in is a bit slow. Be at the airport terminal at least 4 hours prior to the flight. The arrivals is busy and crowded. The washrooms are wet and needs improvements. The airport needs more duty free shops. The WI-FI and connectivity is very fast and quick to connect.

Arrivals lounge was very tidy and we reached baggage claim without a hassle. Staff were vigilant and happy to assist with any baggage related queries and baggage also arrived on time. Departures lounge is very small and the CIP lounge which was on the upper level was closed due to some unknown reason. Lack of snacking options was visibly noticeable. Otherwise an OK experience.

Lahore Airport has received poor reviews. I think it is important to establish a basis of comparison, you can't compare it with Singapore, Amsterdam and such airports, compare it with airports in the sub-continent. Based on this, it is not too bad in terms of speed though the lighting, toilets and othere areas leave a lot to be desired. When I landed on Oct 23 night by Thai Airways flight TG-345 on Oct 23, I was through Immigration and Baggage Claim in less than 20 minutes, granted I was seated in the front cabin of economy and the gate at which the aircraft parked was very close to Immigration. A couple of porters asked me if I neede their services but there was no hard-sell. I was more worried about Departure after having read some of the dire reports on this forum. Remember they won't let you in until 3 hours before flight departure as the check-in counters for the respective flight do not open more than 3 hours in advance. If you arrive too early you will have to cool your heels in the public area and that is not so inviting, in fact it is hard to get a seat. Once you do enter the secured area after having passport and ticket print-out (doubt they will accept a mobile ticket) checked by Security, you put all your bags on a belt where it goes through the X-Ray machine while you go through a security screnn and get frisked. Then you walk to Customs but foreigners are not questioned, just have their passports and boarding passes checked. Then, as is normal, airline check-in desk, Passport Control and Security, and you are done. The whole process didn't take me more than half an hour, no doubt it could be much longer at peak periods. Contrast this with my experience a month ago at Berlin airport, where checking in and going through Security for a domestic flight took 90 minutes.

The current airport consists of two buildings. The first houses the security scanners and the second an open air thatched building the manual check in. Very pleasant for small groups. A new terminal is being constructed and should be ready in a few years. Like most things in Lamu this is a simple functional relaxed airport. From the terminal you walk 200 meters to the fast boats for the 10 minute ride to Lamu Town or to Shela Beach.

Not a large airport, my wife and I found this one more like ones we are used to in New Zealand. No airbridges, but airstairs do the job well, especially at smaller airports. Arrival was good, a lot of taxi touts which is not unusual in Malaysia, we used a coupon taxi for transport to our hotel. Did not visit the shops or toilets here, had a long wait in departure lounge for our flight. Met our needs, staff helpful.

Arriving was a breeze. You have to use stairs though. Everything was fast, luggage, hire car, easy. Leaving was not as nice. I advise that you buy any snacks before you go through security, Airside it is very tight. Nearly all the seats were taken, there is just a small cafe selling a very small array of snacks which looked unappealing, and a newsagent. That's it, The toilets were the worst I have ever experienced in any airport, the smell was horrendous. The fan going in there did nothing to make it better. My husband is a smoker, nowhere to smoke airside. Our flight was delayed and this is not a place to spend any time in if you can avoid it.

Arrived at Langkawi International Airport at 1.00pm after my AirAsia flight. No aerobridge here so we had to disembark the plane by stairs. First impression of the airport was good because it was clean and simple, perfect for an island airport. Toilets were very clean. Baggage reclaim area and customs come just after we enter the terminal, very convenient. Small airport so not many shops and restaurants. At least there is a small lounge there. Lots of seats for you to relax. Found this airport really nice.

Small airport, no sky bridges so you walk from and to the plane. No problems arriving at immigration, line not so bad. Bags arrived in reasonable time. Toilets in the baggage claim hall are awful, rather use the one on the plane before landing or wait until you get to your hotel. A lot of car hire firms in the arrivals hall, loads of taxi touts and taxis, cars and mini buses blocking the drop off road. As for changing money, everywhere on the island the rate is poor $1 = MYR4.10 rather change in KL, there we got $1 = MYR4.40 On departure, no line at the Tiger air check-in, but a long one at Air Asia. There are shops, McDonalds and a Starbucks before going airside. Security and immigration, no lines. Once airside there is only a very small takeaway coffee kiosk and there are no smoking areas so be warned. Tiger Air left on time, Air Asia which was meant to depart before us, also to Singapore, was delayed.

Small, functional airport which is a bit drab for a holiday destination like Langkawi. Clean, but a bit rusty. A decent common hall with shopping and eating before check in / after baggage claim, but next to nothing to do on the airside. Still more pleasant than KLIA 2 or Subang.
No boarding bridges. But views are very nice. Not much wait for luggage. The ground service is good.

Small airport only serves a couple of airlines. Landing process was pretty fast seem the airport does not have air bridges. Bags delivered pretty fast. Check in at airport was fine many dining options. Security check was fast. Not sure about transportation options because we were picked up and dropped off by our hotel. It is a very sufficient regional airport.

Lovely airport and great shops for an airport of this size. Paying a the counter for taxi's removes the touts that descend on you in other places. Food options are limited but then who would want to spend too long checking in too early and getting hungry when on such a lovely island

Used this airport recently. It is nice and efficient. Managed to retrieved luggage within 10 mins. There are about 3 belts at the arrival hall. We booked a taxi at the taxi counter for M$24 for our 30 min journey to the hotel. At Langkawi there is no meter in the taxi they offer fixed prices unlike KL. Check in at Air Asia counter fro flights to KL was quick. Passed through immigrations within minutes. They offer an "only lady" immigration as well. Plenty of Arabs in the airport and was told that it was their peak (holidays) season. There is a number of shops and food outlets. Overall its a nice airport.

It's always a pleasure going through this airport. It is clean spacious and easy to navigate. Immigration and customs are always fast and efficient. There are a good number of duty-free shops although not as many food outlets.

After 2 years of making an attempt to improve this substandard airport things are no better. Parking in the long term is lacking. Exits to the terminal from the parking if you have the good fortune to find a space are often blocked. The lighting at night both entering and within the car park is less than adequate. The road leading up to the airport is not lit making it dangerous. If you Uber they charge a surcharge to be picked up and dropped off. The parking is expensive in comparison to O R Tambo. At O R Tambo there is a facility to pay for long term in advance which makes parking easy and reasonable. The facilities within the airport are minimal. It is stated that Lanseria is convenient for Fourways and Sandton whoever said that hasn’t tried to leave Lanseria first thing in the morning. The traffic congestion is terrible. All in all I would not recommend the place at all.

Don't use this airport if you want to park, there is limited parking particularly if it's long term and expensive and a total rip off in comparison to OR Tambo where you can prebook and pay in advance or a reduced rate. There is construction going on to build a multi storey car park, no thought has been put into how to deal with the parking issue in the interim. Customers have to walk near a construction site and some pathways and exits to the terminal have been fenced off. If you are using this airport at peak times good luck with the traffic and the roadworks leading to the major centers such as Randburg and Fourways. Any advice? Stay away from this Airport for at least a year to give the construction and roadworks chance to be completed. There are limited facilities in the terminal and at peak times queues at security are long. Would I recommend this Airport? No definitely not

Really pleasant and convenient airport. Minimal queues and pleasant staff. A really nice touch is the free coffee tea and newspapers for all passengers in the departure lounge. I just wish that the runway was long enough to permit direct flights from the UK to land here.

I understand I’m in a foreign country, but I do not expect to be screamed at in their language while going through security. Obviously, I couldn’t understand what she was screaming about. I have MS and have had strokes, etc. Apparently, it was my bracelets she wanted me to remove. She then continued to rant as I walked through. It was not a pleasant experience. I also had priority boarding and my grandchildren’s boarding passes on my phone. I didn’t need to pay for luggage for them, as they are 3 and 5 years old, yet she refused me entry.

This was the worst Airport we have ever been after visiting many places. Very dirty and very unpleasant! No respect and empathy to pregnant woman. The only positivity is a lot of restaurants and food select on such a small place.

Myself and my wife were on our first visit to Lanzarote and my first time as an assisted passenger. The team who took care of us were excellent friendly and so helpful. This made our holiday so much more enjoyable. Thanks to the team, well done assistance team at Lanzarote airport Thank You.

There is no food available in this airport after 7:45 pm - The only option normally is Fast Food but incredibly they all close at 8pm. So in an airport full of people taking 3,4 and 5 hour flights there is no option to eat for adults or children only crisps and sweets. This is absolutely ridiculous - you could not make it up. If you don't want to work, put signs up and tell people so at least the people there at 7:30 would know about it. No person from any other location would believe a business would close at 8pm and both deny people a service and deny the business the income- incredible but a reality - bad end to a great holiday.

Absolutely disgusting help with special assistance. We had two assistants screeching and shouting at both myself and husband, and then I was just left dumped at the gate when everybody else had left for the plane. I have serious heart problems and was so upset my heart rate went sky high. I'm seriously considering never going to Lanzarote again, as this completely ruined our holiday. Have some respect please. If you don't like your job, leave, then don't take it out on the disabled

What a joke of an airport. Starting with the check-in process, which was shambolic. An extremely rude member of staff shoo'd away around 100 people in such a rude manner. The crime that us and all these people had committed well it was queuing at the desk that was stated on the board. After creating this chaos, she soon re-opened the same desk and told half of the already frustrated people to re-join, which caused anger when we didn't move as they couldn't figure something out. Lots of angry punters voicing annoyance at such impotence committed by the rudest person I've ever seen at any airport, let alone an employee. Security was fine though. Next up was queuing for boarding, my god, what cretin designed this airport. You had to queue to cutting across the main concourse of the airport, blocking everyone up and next to toilets. Next up is the bus, now the bus doubles up as a waiting room. A hot, nasty waiting room. Eventually we all boarded and were told it would be 50 minutes until we go anywhere. Awesome news. Why board us then you complete cretins. All in, the worst run, designed and run airport I've ever experienced.

Told to board and then kept in a boiling stairwell. No help for mother and babies who after nearly a hour needing to feed and go to toilets. Apparently not enough bus drivers. The ones we saw where busy joking around. This caused our flight to miss the a lot and we are delayed by about a hour. Still sat here on the 14th January. Really disgraceful service from a poorly run operation. Cattle get treated better than this place! Terminal not enough seats and not attempts to queue manage on any gates, so the terminal just got blocked up.

Since I last visited this airport they have replaced most of manual passport control with E-gates which families with young children cannot use. This is a bad error of judgement considering how many families with young children come through this airport. We queued for over half an hour for passport control. My daughter needed the toilet and there was access to none because they had barriered them off until you got right to the front of the queue. We then missed our transfer as were it took an hour to get through the airport. The E-gates were only being used by about 20% of travellers and staff were walking down the queue trying to find travellers who could use them. What a waste of money installing them or so many of them.

This airport is one of the worst airports I have been into in my life. Disability with my mum pushing me in a wheelchair, no help whatsoever .. they could see us struggling and just say staring at us but helped everyone else. Didn't help us get the bags or anything.  Airport is tiny, crowded. No room to do anything especially with a wheelchair. Gates are all squeezed in with the restaurants and cafe so your standing next to people getting food while their in a queues at their gate number. No food available for allergy sufferers.  Special assistance people have to wait until the whole plane gets on first then they get on last even though your put at the front to get on first? Makes no sense. There's a reason why it's called special assistance. Jet2 woman did not care at all that we were distressed, stood there like a wet lemon. Not sure why she was there. Absolutely no staff to look after the ones needing special assistance.  Very unorganized and unprofessional. Won't be returning back to this airport.

This is actually a pretty good airport. It is very spacious and there is plenty seating if you walk to either end. We found it to be clean. The check in for Jet2 was excellent and security was very quick and friendly. There are plenty of options for bars and cafes once through security - there are also two outdoor seating areas which are great to catch a last bit of sunshine. Staff are all friendly - we never experienced any rudeness described by others - after all, it can be a two way thing. The duty free area is good with excellent variety.

Flew from CKG-LHW on Sichuan Airlines, a pleasant enough flight. We used an airbridge in the older Terminal 1, while the booking hall is now closed, the baggage hall and arrivals remain the same for Terminal 1. The high speed railway has been completed, so I decided to catch the train to Lanzhou West railway station. The train station is a short walk to the left from the exit of Terminal 1, opposite Terminal 2. There was only a short queue for tickets in the Ticket hall, to the right of the station entrance, about ¥‎22 for First class on the very next train. Travel time was about 40 minutes. All in all, it was much better than slow airport bus and ¥‎200 taxi options.

Having travelled via this airport several times before, this was the first time using the new Terminal 2. Access to the airport is still painfully long and slow from the city, with no advantage over taxi and the airport buses, however progress can be seen on the high-speed railway to cover the 70km into Lanzhou. The new terminal is light and airy and much better than the concrete lifeless box that is Terminal 1. The multitude of check-in counters are a big improvement on the old terminal. Security check is typical of China with little space actually given for the lines of people trying remove laptops and metallic objects. The choices for food and shopping has also greatly improved both on air and landside. My gate was still within the connected old Terminal 1 which required a very long walk with no travelators available. The old terminal check-in hall seems to be closed and mothballed at the moment, awaiting renovation after the opening of the newer terminal. The airport staff were fantastic, when they gave me their personal phone to call my destination hotel, after it was apparent that my flight was to be delayed. All in all, it is a much nicer experience flying through here.

A very small regional airport. Up to 4 flights a day, all to Manila. Single storey building with Check-in at one end with Departures and Arrivals at the other end. 2 Check-in Desks, a single Security Lane and 4 doors in Departures to walk out to the aircraft parked outside. Single runway with no taxi-ways. A very small friendly efficient airport, Check-in and Security. NB had to show ID and Ticket/Boarding Card to get into the airport. In Departures a lot of seating, small cafe and toilets. A number of screens showing news, promo information but no departure information. A very small, efficient airport. Similar set-up for arrivals.

Small airport with basic but sufficient facilities. Upon arrival airport staff welcomed passengers and provided a small bag of local snacks which was a nice touch. Outbound processing was fine with courteous and friendly staff in security. Check-in queue took a bit longer than normal for a regional ATR flight. Room for improvement on this but ground staff very friendly and helpful.

The airport has introduced a screen check at passport control on departure. EEC passports go through in 5 minutes. British passports took about 40 minutes when I departed on 1 March at 6.30. You need to either build this into your schedule or avoid the airport and use Paphos.
Massive queues everywhere and staff rude arrogant and ignorant, manners cost nothing, perhaps staff training in manners could be introduced. Very poor experience at this airport.

Appalling organisation at the airport, took 1.5 hours to get through passport control and security with no one knowing what was happening. Then delayed and no communication at all- stuffed in hot room. Clearly committed to too many flights and not enough capacity. Need to get it together and provide a better service

Having done online checkin the day before, 65 minutes before departure we were denied handing in the bags and boarding the flight. There was no Bag Drop counter, either. Two days and hundreds of euros in rebooking fees later, we arrived early, only to go through three hours of sheer pandemonium, with football-type crowds at checkin, passport control, security, everywhere. No time to sit for 5 minutes and a have a coffee. Just a mad dash.

Absolutely terrible experience on all levels! The staff is unprofessional and unhelpful. The check-in took a little less than 2 hours while the counter opened 2 hours before the flight so the whole process was unexpectedly stressful. The tax free agents are not centralized so you need to go to different parts of the airport to complete the tax free process. The wifi is extremely weak. Again, absolutely terrible. It is unfortunate that a country who relies on tourism has this airport as its main airport.
A lot of noise. They were talking all the time on the speakers. The food on Burger King were not fully cooked. nice staff, but irritated by all the bilde on the speakers!

I left on early BA flight and was very impressed with the helpful staff in the airport, check in 3 hours ahead, fast empty security and border control. Nice airy feel and clean although some cafe prices shocking; cost me more than Scandinavian airports. 4 euro for potato chips. Generally modern and relaxed despite a number of early morning flights and there was a machine where robot gives you jelly beans. I like distractions in airports, takes your mind off stress. BA gate staff helpful and whole experience was stress free compared to disgraceful regional airports in UK.

Awful airport experience from start to finish! Was the nail in the coffin of our exploration decision. Immigration staff, including the police were extremely rude. Their queuing system was frankly chaotic and their speed of dealing with people was slower than a turtle having a nap! Airline lounges were all closed for refurbishment with no alternatives provided and no explanations. The departures lounge was dirty and crowded with insufficient comfortable seating. There is no airport information desk in departures to help when you have a query. We were here in Cyprus to assess whether to invest more than EUR 100M into the Ayia Napa economy (assessing against another option) and have just decided to go with our other option purely on the basis of the appalling attitude, attention to detail and service experienced in Cyprus and the airport! A backward place that if they don’t improve they are doomed to remain the third world of the EU!

The airport is a relatively small international airport that is easy to navigate. The checkin lines are a gamble as some airlines have short queues and some are ridiculously long. The passport control and security check was a relatively quick process, even though the security staff is one of the most unfriendly I've experienced. The duty free area is large, however the prices, especially for food and drinks are very high (even for an airport). The seating area is relatively quiet and there are usually enough seats available with bathrooms and kiosks in walking distance from the gates. Due to the small size of the airport even the bus journeys are not long to the plane, although we had airbridges on both departure and arrival. Besides the indifference of the staff, the only really bad thing at the airport are the sometimes very long wait times (30 minutes+) at the luggage carousels. This is especially the case during off peak times when it should actually go quicker. This time, however, it was a relatively quick process and the bags where already there when we arrived. I think the airport is nice small airport without any thrills but also nothing that makes me hate it.

Quick and easy security and immigration at departures (weekday afternoon). Departure terminal is overheated. All the food outlets are overpriced and a total rip off. All the "duty free" goods are expensive apart from tobacco and cigarettes. Announcements are too loud. The terminal carpet was absolutely filthy.

The most disgusting bathroom I have ever used in an airport in any major city and I’m usually not picky. I had to change clothes, so I wasn’t even using the toilet to go to the bathroom. If I did, I would have had to probably search for an hour to find something I would possibly use. Urine and feces on the floor in multiple stalls. I didn’t see a place to mark “please clean “, but I did mention it to a worker that was coming in. Not sure if he understood what I was saying. I just got a glazed over look from him. It was in C gates. I had actually come over from B because it was bad there too.

I am a elderly woman who requires assistance. I asked to have a wheelchair to get me straight to passenger pickup. The woman they sent to wheel me through the airport consistently asked me to get out of the wheelchair and walk the rest of the way after taking me off the plane. She was rude and constantly mentioned how heavy I was. She wanted to take me out of the chair and have me walk the whole way. She did take me even though she didn't want to, however, I don't appreciate someone judging me for my weight. I am always trying to lose weight. I don't ever want to fly out of there again. They were the worst part of my trip. Please hire someone who can do the job and maybe has some lessons in etiquete.

I am only writing this review because so many things are off about this airport. I definitely expected more, as it's a huge airport with tons of revenue from the gaming here. 1. The companion care restroom was locked, as someone who needs this restroom, and cannot use the other ones, I was waiting for about 30 minutes. I knocked several times. After 15 minutes, I called the courtesy phone operator, concerned that someone was in there and unwell or unconscious. No one responded, then another person called on his own volition, and still no one came. This is a HUGE security concern. After 30 minutes, a line was forming, so I flagged down a lovely custodian who unlocked the door and discovered, thankfully, no one was inside. He explained, "It was locked in the night to prevent people from sleeping in it". The fact it was not un-locked during the night in the morning, means this airport was not ADA compliant, and the fact that no body came after 2 security-related calls were made to the operator, means this airport does not have quick response to security concerns. 2. It's filthy, there's food crumbs, coffee, dust, and crud on every surface and many chairs. 3. The charging stations barely work (at least in the A7-A15 terminal) and nearly all of the USB direct ports are full of grey putty, while the ones that aren't full of putty don't charge and are loose and broken. The staff here are lovely, but the facilities are dismal and frankly this place is a security nightmare. As a bay area resident, I will never fly through here again and will never recommend this airport, with a definite preference for connecting CLEAN & SAFE airports like Denver, IAH/Hobby, Atlanta, or Chicago.

I have TSA pre check. I stood in the pre check line 10 minutes without it moving even one person. Meanwhile, people were going through regular TSA with NO WAIT. How on earth is that? So I switched to regular TSA where of course I had to take off jacket, shoes and remove laptop. Then as I’m standing in bare feet, suddenly the long line of pre check people go flying through? What’s the problem with your pre check?

I can’t express enough how grateful I am for the exceptional help I received from Hilary, the gate check agent at Spirit Airlines. I was in a complete panic after losing my cell phone at the airport. With no way to contact my family and let them know when I’d be arriving, I was extremely stressed and worried that they’d be concerned about me. Hillary noticed my distress and went above and beyond by offering to let me use her personal phone to send a quick text to my family. Her kindness, thoughtfulness, and willingness to help me in a moment of crisis made all the difference. Thanks to her, I was able to let my family know when to pick me up, and I could finally breathe a sigh of relief. Never did find my phone but there was a silver lining. Hillary truly saved the day for me, and I can’t thank her enough for her generosity. Spirit Airlines is lucky to have such a compassionate and dedicated employee. Thank you, Hillary, for turning a stressful situation into a manageable one. You have no idea how much your help meant to me!

This airport is disgusting. The bathrooms are filthy with urine and unworking flush mechanisms. Floors throughout terminal 1 appear to rarely get swept or mopped. Im amazed the airport can pass a foodservice inspection. We ate breakfast at the wendys and the seating areas and tables had spilled drinks and food all around the dining space. Trash overflowing. It seems the cleaning crew are non existent or inept. Avoid this airport at all cost. Tsa was friendly and efficient but the rest is a zero.

Review limited to Terminal 1. Arrived at the D gates. The D concourse appears to have more amenities which appear to have more amenities than the B concourse. The concourse is bright and spacious. Departure was from B concourse. The B concourse has only 2 restaurants and lacks amenities. Slot machines take up most of the space at the gates which makes for a very crowded gate area. I didn't notice any in seat USB and/or power outlets. The B concourse needs major renovations to align it the modern and spacious terminals you see at other airports. There is no lounge at either B or C concourse. Free Airport WiFi is fast. We dined at PGA restaurant. One of the worst meals we've had. Our meals were comped (fish & chips) as it was not up to the restaurant's standards.

God bless the amazing lady from Flint Michigan. I can’t remember her name. I threw my back out the day before my flight. I was hunched over and could barely walk. She got a wheel chair for me and took me though security and all the way to my gate. Waited for my plane and rolled me down the jet bridge. I don’t know what I would’ve done without her kindness! I hope she knows how much she’s appreciated!

The TSA employees were very rude! TSA Pre Check was closed! The airport is one of most unclean airport’s I have ever visited. Seating at Gate A has no charging ports on the seats. The experience at LAS makes me extremely grateful to go back to my home airport #BNA.
Sitting area is disgusting! Trash under chairs, carpet very dirty and bathroom were not clean. Water was all over the bathroom ladies room and it was dirty and nasty.

I just want to have an explanation for why I was charged .18 cents on top of the purchase for a glass of Chardonnay when paying by card - savings account. The bar’s preferred method of payment is card. There should be no eftpos transaction fee for use of card when this is their preferred method of payment. This is wrong and your airport personnel need to address this issue especially when dealing with COVID19. I would like an explanation.

I was transferred to a later flight and couldn’t check my luggage in as it was too early. I decided to wait in the restaurant shopping area and have a coffee. Well I had to take my large suitcase through the security area. I am an older lady and had to get someone to help me lift the suitcase up onto the X-ray carousel. I had to first take my nail scissors etc out. It was embarrassing and no one was able to help me and the staff were unfriendly. There is no other entry to the shops etc but through the security area. It is ridiculous. I am so stressed and upset over the whole episode.

Travelling in and out of Launceston Airport proved a pleasant experience. Since the terminal is still fairly new everything seemed to be in very good working order. Facilities were very good having 2 large coffee shops and 1 well stocked souvenir/gift shop selling real Tasmanian and Launceston branded items. Check in and customs were hassle free. No time lost waiting for luggage or taxis.

Good airport with facilities to cater for the number of flights. Slight delays on arrival due to fruit and vegetable quarantine but no problem. (read the notices and listen to the announcements makes it easy). It does the job.

Pleasant little airport in Tasmania with limited flights and destinations. But easy to trot through and all staff most pleasant. Beware do not bring fruit from the mainland. Do not rent a car from "Lo Cost" they take a $750 charge (Damage deposit?) off your credit card and I am still working on having this refunded. Limited facilities.

Launceston Airport has seen a large redevelopment program completed over the 2008/2009 period. At the northern end of the terminal are 12 checkin counters for Qantaslink Jetstar Virgin Blue and Tiger Airways which has created more room than before. Southern end of the terminal has two baggage carousels added with car rental counters opposite for Avis Budget Europcar Hertz Thrifty & Red Spot. New upgraded retail outlets are provided in the central section of the terminal which are Newslink Long Bar and Hudson's Coffee. This central area has been expanded with a greater amount of room making it easier when more than one flight is in at the same time. New security area directs passengers downstairs to new roomy departure lounges which are now at the lower level. Windows at the central section and the departure lounges give visitors and passengers great views of the mountains east of the airport. This redevelopment has made Launceston Airport a lot more user friendly than previously.

Launceston's airport is rather small with two distinct gate areas one for Qantas/JetStar the other for Virgin Blue. On the plus side it means relatively short queues and a short walk from the plane to the parking lot. The secure area is glass-walled from the non-secure area so non-passengers can still watch their friends and loved ones get on that plane something you can't do at many airports today.On the minus side it means a lot of things we take for granted at other airports are missing. There are no jetways so boarding is the old fashioned way via stairs. A minus in poor weather and for those with physical ailments it can be a plus depending on airline and aircraft as you can board via two doors simultaneously. There's only one small cafe and I don't recall any shops if you want a last-minute souvenir of your Tasmanian holiday. Another minus is that like many of its bigger cousins the rental car facilities are off-airport and not onsite like you'd expect for a small airport. While the major chains like Hertz Avis Budget etc. all have counters within the terminal their offices are located on the main road into town. When dropping off my Hertz car (I rented it at Hobart) the clerk who accepted my car also drove me in the same car to the terminal! I'm not sure if it's the same for incoming passengers or if a shuttle bus exists like at other airports with off-airport rental car offices. A really big minus is that because the airport dates back to a more innocent period in air travel the toilets (as well as everything else) are outside the secure area with none inside. I got there real early and noticed that people didn't enter the secure area until starting about 30 minutes before their flights. However that causes the non- secure area to get quite crowded at times. Again due to the low passenger numbers security queues are relatively short compared to large airports.

The airport continues to disappoint and only succeeds as it is a main Jet2 hub and it's locality as a hub for West Yorkshire. On our most recent visit we had booked Fast Track, We entered the dedicated lane and then found there was no fast track security, the dedicated lane just merged with the standard queue to the just two scanners in operation. When I enquired where the dedicated Fast Track scanner was, the reply was that they did not think they were busy enough to have one today. Fine, return our payments please. Secondly, we entered the lounge using our Dragon Passes. The lounge was uncomfortably warm, mainly because it has approximately halved in size since our last visit. I asked a member of staff if the air conditioning/climate control was working and was told, 'The airport staff have turned it off' and that was the end of that conversation. As soon as Doncaster reopens, LBA should receive a massive wake up call as the airport is very poor.

Atrocious airport that not only needs a rebuild but an almost clean sweep recruitment of staff. Lazy, lethargic behavior topped off ‘we can’t get the staff’. Alcohol Drinking from 6am. Unbelievable. Over priced with poor shoddy ill thought out product. Whoever runs this eye sore, needs the license revoking.

Once again the check in desks struggled for over 30 minutes to sign in and queues for security are going outside. Paid for fast track but waiting longer and longer due to pushing late flights through. This airport really needs to spend some effort improving its service as it’s getting worse.

Having travelled extensively, it should be welcoming to travel from a local airport - not so, Leeds. The car park is rough and disorganised, the departure areas unclean, with overpriced food and teas etc, and the staff unhelpful. Thankfully, Jet2, the airline are different and great ambassadors for their airline. Arriving back into Leeds was worse, with a cold walk along a third world shelter, into a building with filthy walls and floors, that looked disgusting as a first impression for visitors to Yorkshire. On attempting to leave the car park too, the ANPR cameras were not working, creating huge queues, with one camera taped with packing tape and plastic . Quite frankly, it was embarrassing, having flown in from the pristine cleanliness of Barcelona. Unfortunately, Leeds Bradford Airport is a sad reflection of a lack of care, lack of interest and lack of respect for itself.

Set off from my home in Pudsey on the morning of my flight and was in the duty free shop within 40 minutes. Check in with Jet2 was a doddle. Security was reasonably busy but staff were efficient and polite, new scanners were in use. Used the Boots store - perfectly fine. Made use of the Starbucks - great coffee. Used the toilet facilities. They were clean. Boarding the plane was swift, had the luxury of an Airbridge which was great (but have used the much maligned "bus shelter" walkway on many occasions and had no problems - kept dry in wet weather - does what it was designed to do). I have flown from many UK airports and my experience of this small airport is up there with the best. Wish I could say the same in respect of my arrivals experience at Malaga Airport and an hour long wait at passport control.

A small airport that is a bit tired and shabby but convenient due to it's small size. Generally security is quick, 5 to 10 minutes. It can get a little crowded at times so you might not have somewhere to sit. I regularly use this and Belfast City airport as alternatives to Dublin and Manchester (bigger airports, more crowded, longer security queues etc.) and this airport is nowhere near as nice as Belfast City. In particular the lounge in Leeds is quite poor in terms of food / drink offerings & cleanliness. However if I have the choice between Leeds and Manchester for a flight I'd choose Leeds because of the faster security. But they could make it cleaner and put more into the lounge experience.

Leeds Bradford is an awful airport. Security is like a cattle market with you herded through a small hot security room. Things only get worse from there as once through security you find the airport has few facilities and even fewer sets. If you want an alcoholic drink expect at least a 20-30 minute wait. The return journey was just as bad as they had a problem unloading the planes, which resulted in a delay of over an hour after we landed and got through passport control. Which led to thee plane's worth of passengers crammed in to the very small baggage collection area, with the entrance and exit next to each other so the whole place became gridlocked. To top it off our daughter had to move from the 1 hour free parking, missed the turning to the medium stay due to the lack of lighting and poor signage, she had to reverse back a few feet to get in but got a £100 penalty notice for stopping. Clearly Leeds Bradford airport expect you to do hand brake turns if you miss the entrance to one of their car parks.

I don't know what all the fuss was about. Bad reviews about security, dirty airport, unfriendly staff, no seating? I experienced none of that. In view of the negative reviews, we arrived 3 hours before take off, and were through security in five minutes. Very cheerful, efficient and friendly staff. Bought some items at duty free, and the lady there was extremely pleasant and helpful. Plenty of seating. Good food and drink offers, and both the airport and toilets were very clean. Boarding process straightforward and stressless. On return, our plane landed about 40 minutes behind schedule. This unfortunately coincided with 3 other flights landing at the same time, so passport control was very busy, but it only took about 20 minutes to get through. The staff there were smiling at 22.00.  I understand why passengers complain, but it's also useful to get positive reviews sometimes. I hope my next experience of Leeds Bradford will be as good as this one.

I had no complaints on departing from the airport but on arrival, compared to Alicante airport, the toilets were grim, there was even rubbish on the floor on the way to passport control. Going through Nothing to Declare the area was filthy, dust and fluff everywhere mixed with hairs and dirt. It is is embarrassing. Please pay for a cleaner.

My wife and I flew out of LBA on Friday 15th Sept. After queuing and passing through security we found that there was no available seating in the terminal. The terminal was very warm and the air stale. There was no way of getting any cool or fresh air. We queued in a corridor after being called for our flight and again the glass corridor was very hot and no fresh air. Not good for somebody who is still recovering from a severe heart attack. Very poor for 'Yorkshires Largest International Airport" that they advertise. More like Yorkshires Largest Embarrassment. On our return, it got even worse. Our plane landed and we were informed that there were no buses available (only 3 buses in use for what turned out to be approximately 500 passengers) to transport the passengers as two other planes had just landed, and then a third turned up. We were held on the plane before a bus arrived for a 30 second trip. Then, only to find out we could have walked 150 feet to Gate 9 and then to the terminal. When we reached the terminal entrance several passengers complained and the bus driver was extremely rude. The Jet 2 reps were all but useless. It took us 45 minutes to actually get to the terminal from landing, and then we were forced to queue in the rain and cold and then endure a further 45 minutes before reaching Passport Control. No toilets or fresh air. Passport Control was struggling. Why? Why must British Citizens endure the wait for Passport checks when the electronic Passport Control allows EU residents through and not British Nationals into their own country? Surely, it should be the other way around? Upon visiting the gents toilet in the baggage area I found it to be disgusting. The area smelt considerably and appeared to not have been cleaned for several days. The fixtures and fittings were very old and worn, and can only be described as disgraceful. LBA should be ashamed. Upon getting outside it got even worse. Because LBA have decided to close the road to any vehicle other than Arrow Taxis that have to be booked and paid for in advance for at least £10 more than other taxi firms charge, there was a very long queue as one would expect after four aircraft had just landed. It was pouring with rain and the temperature was 9 Deg. I managed to book a taxi from another company to pick us up at the only drop off point, but only after being soaked through to the skin, literally. We understand that the original drop off areas at the front of the terminal have been closed because of security concerns in the past, but why has it not been re-opened. Why not? After all, every other airport in the world except the UK does not do this. Even in the Middle East. I know, I have been to most of them. Could it be the security excuse allows the profit to be too large to stop it? When LBA has been asked in the past why there is a charge of £6 (increase of 100% since 2016) to drop people off at the drop off point, we are told that the money is used to improve the airport. Where exactly? There has been no visible improvement to LBA since Jet2 erected their check in building years ago. I have travelled extensively around the world on business regularly and the two worst airports I have visited are Manchester and Leeds Bradford. They are both old, tatty, smelly and out of date. We live in the countries largest most beautiful county but we are served by the one of two worst airports in this country. LBA should be ashamed of themselves.

This was a quite different airport altogether from what I have seen to date. When you look from the outside it is surrounded by beautiful Himalayan mountains and blue sky. Me and my husband were flying back to our home after a 10 days 'best ever vacation' of Laddakh. Our experience of its Airport though was not very impressive. The security check was different from a normal airport. After submitting the luggage we had to claim it once again before boarding the flight. The flight management didn't seem to be very punctual and professional. We were allowed for boarding the flight 1 hour after boarding was announced. Announcements and actions were completely out of sync. Food served were not fresh. When asked she told me samosas were made 24 hours earlier. Quite to my surprise there was hardly any airport shopping! Airport authorities should take serious measures to amend these shortcomings as Leh - Laddakh is becoming a favorite holiday destination for people all across the world.

Leipzig/Halle is my home airport. I like the short distances and the good accessibility with public transport (long distance buses, commuter and long distance trains). Parking is comfortable and the number of direct connections is acceptable for the size of the metropolitan region Leipzig/Halle. Waiting times at security checks are usually predictably short. It seems like they usually give me priority access with my Lufthansa frequent traveler status. But there were times when I was standing with 15 other business people at one check point for 20 minutes whiles less than 5 tourists were quickly checked at two other open check points. The bathrooms are terrible and need a renovation quickly. In combination with the fact that you have to leave the Lufthansa lounge to use them I avoid using them in all circumstances. The Duty Free is very small and I can not remember that I ever found something worth buying it. There are plenty of seats in the public areas. As soon as boarding starts you have to move into a hall that is connecting the gates. If boarding is delayed then you have to stand in the line and there is only a hand full seats in front of the gates. My standard LH Business and Senator lounge is one of the most boring LH lounges I have been to. No daylight, in Senator lounge things like prepared Bratwurst or Leberkäse waiting on a cold plate until somebody is hungry enough to take it. Very low food standard. No own toilet as described above. One really good thing in Leipzig is the quick baggage service at arrival. I never had to wait more than 10 minutes after arrival before the belt started to rotate. Sometimes when I have to take the bus from a small airplane to the terminal the suitcases arrive before the passengers. All together I would say that I like the airport for quick services and short connections. Some details need improvement.

Leipzig is a wonderful city but difficult to reach from the UK. Flew from Manchester via Dusseldorf. The airport is huge but seemingly deserted for much of the time though most facilities are there. There is a long but under cover walk to the railway station to catch the hourly connection into the city. (6 euro) Here lies the problem. There was no indication as to which platform the train departed (it was No 2 ) nor were there any staff to ask. Eventually with the help of several other bemused travellers we worked out the ticket machine and the train eventually arrived. A great little airport with friendly staff but for international travellers the rail connection into the city needs a bit more working out.

Leipzig airport is a new modern airport but not very user friendly. A major advance is the direct train connection right underneath but the layout is an odd one. After check in  the passenger has to walk a long distance to the security and passport control. This can be a headache of you have to stamp your papers for VAT tax refund as you need to show it to customs. It is located at one end and the check in at the other end. Good facilities present and staff are very friendly and polite even though not very conversant in English.
Easy to get to with car from the Autobahn or from Leipzig with the train. The airport is large but not confusing or crowded. Security was a breeze. All the people seemed nice.

Huge airport serving the cities of Leipzig and Halle and good connections to Berlin as well (roughly 1 hour by express train). Oversized shiny modern. Due to its huge size one has to walk quite far through the whole airport to reach the rail station (oversized as well) which is located at the opposite end of the arrivals / departure hall. Good and fast connection to the city centres of Halle and Leipzig but very unfairly calculated fare - they let you cross several fare zones so you have to pay more than for comparable distances in that region. Because of new restrictions for landing and taking off after 11 pm - interestingly there are NO restrictions for cargo flights - many budget airlines have cancelled their services to this airport and now only few major European cities are still served by non-stop flights . Very sad since the alternatives now are Altenburg Airport or one of the Berlin airports. However having to go there first from Leipzig or Halle increases the overall time of your journey massively.

Leipzig/Halle (LEJ) is modern with shiny terminals and state-of-the-art information systems. Travellers might wonder why the whole facility is so grotesquely oversized. The answer is simple - after Reunification the German government spent billions on new infrastructure in the East and Leipzig got a huge share of this. Too bad in a way for what could have been an efficient regional airport with sleek operations and short distances turned out more like a ghost town leaving the traveller with long walks through deserted buildings and sitting lonely in ridiculously large lounges. Ground staff usually is very helpful – especially the check-in staff by GlobeGround is always friendly and pleasant.

A very easy to use and convenient airport. Arrival was quick and easy to pre-pay for taxi to Guanajuato - 360 pesos was the cost. It's less than 30 minutes to Guanajuato. We arrived at 9:45 for 12:05 departure - much earlier than necessary. No line for CO check-in and no line at security. The snack bar was affordable and there are a couple of decent shops. Even though the airport has jetways they apparently don't go low enough for the regional jets that provide most service so you have to walk outside. Just before boarding there was an additional pat-down security check.

The service to get from airport to the centro district to Guanajuato is too expensive! No options. Just get on the taxi. Last fall it was around $37 usd. This is an 18 mile trip which takes 20 minutes. The bus from Guanaujato to San Miguel is about a one hour drive and cost about $8 usd. There should be alternatives at your airport. Maybe a bus into town?

I've flown in and out of BJX a half dozen times and have no problems. Take along a book or knitting as there are only a couple of souvenir shops (but they are colorful and reasonable). My destination has been San Miguel de Allende the art colony that's popular with US citizens).

This is a small and nice airport. I've landed and departed from this airport before and it has changed a lot. I don't know why it is called Leon Airport if it is closer to Silao Gto. I landed there a few months ago my destination was Romita Gto my mother's hometown. This airport is very convenient for us since it is only about 25-30 mins away from Romita. Also this airport is not very far from Guanajuato city. I recommend people to visit Guanajuato this is perhaps the most European style city in Mexico.

It's a small airport, so getting on and off was easy. They ask for a tourist tax when you arrive. It's not a lot of money. There were lots of taxis, and a cheery driver took to me to Tabatinga. The fare seemed very reasonable. For departures there's a few shops and cafes, but once you go through security there's nothing at all except the toilets. There's no AC but the biggest ceiling fan I have ever seen. I didn't see any information screens.

Bluegrass is an amazing airport that I have flown into and out of numerously with nothing but positive experiences, until this July, 2019. To start, I'll tell what all I like about Bluegrass. Firstly, pickup, drop-off, and parking are almost a joke, they're so easy! Absolutely no hassle, ever. Secondly, the terminal was fairly modern to begin with even before the remodel about a decade ago, and now it's a "well-flowing," well-organized airport (as if it already wasn't). Thirdly, while there are very few shopping and dining options, and they're really only open during peak traffic volume hours, this is to be expected for such a tiny airport, what options are available are of pretty high quality, plus Dunkin' Donuts (at least last time I checked). Fourthly, baggage claim is efficient even by tiny airport standards. (That said, if nothing is open pre-security, there's a piddly little coffee and hot chocolate machine that doesn't seem to work and when it does, it doesn't seem to work right.) Fifth, personnel from airport check-ins to security, to gate agents to store staff, are usually very friendly, attentive and kind, it's like Bluegrass is a sort of big small town. Sadly, however, when I flew out in July, there was an exception to that friendliness. When I flew out, the TSA Pre-Check line was closed, so I had no choice to go through the regular TSA line. Okay, fine, but the guy who checked my driver's license barely even moved his eyes. The officers at the scanner were more pleasant, but still made me take almost everything out of my backpack, thankfully, I didn't have much to take out, but I don't remember having to empty out so many little details from my bag while flying anywhere around the country or world. It was just a bazaar experience. Thankfully, security are still efficient and the gates are only a 2-3 minute walk from security, so I still made my flight in the nick of time, but that particular experience was just aggravating. Overall, Bluegrass is a fine airport that sets the gold standard for what tiny but very functional airports should be, but I sure wish all of its TSA folks understood the concept of Pre-Check.

This airport is great. Always clean, lovely staff, few delays, and good food. The information desk woman was very welcoming, and we had a lovely chat. Wi-fi access was good. As small airports go, Bluegrass is pretty much the model of what a small airport should be. Shopping options are limited, but you have a nice bookshop and a good bar after security, the car park is a minute's walk from the terminal, and the surroundings are well kept. In years of traveling through Lexington, I can think of nothing negative to say about this airport and its staff. Even the TSA security check has always been pleasant.

I have flown in and out of this airport on several occasions, although I don't live in Kentucky.  I mean, it is a small airport serving a small city, so don't go expecting any big city amenities other than just a couple of sit-down restaurants, a Dunkin' Donuts and a small store.  But it is surprisingly spacious, extremely clean and very modern.  Signage is clear, staff and security are friendly, the terminals are small and manageable, and there is even complex and beautiful artwork on the floor in security honoring the region's thoroughbred horse racing heritage.  Lastly, where else can you park in the parking garage, that is only around 100 feet from the terminal? The ease, simplicity, and friendliness of this airport makes it one of my favorite airports in the world, and I've been all over North America and Europe.

Whenever I travel I try to avoid having to go through Toronto or Newark airports, two places that seem designed to discourage people from travelling. I've just added Liberia to that list. It clearly was not built to handle the traffic of increased tourism and both arriving and departing reflect that fact. Clearing Customs takes time as the lineups can be long and slow moving, in a hot, humid building.
