Departing is also an exercise in patience, as waiting passengers are jammed into an area designed for a fraction of their number. Seats are cherished items, boarding lines are more like boarding scrums and the prices for everything in the building are beyond ridiculous. Water can cost $10US a bottle, basic burgers $19, and fries $9.50. Last minute souvenir items are similarly overpriced, even by airport standards. There is nothing appealing about this airport other than the fact it's bright inside. A necessary evil if it's by far the closest airport to your destination but one to be avoided if you can arrange to go through SJ.

Immigration systems went down and executive director of security wouldn’t answer his phone for manual overload. Made us wait in very first security line for at least an hour so far, hundreds of people. Sheer incompetence and stupidity.

Used Liberia Airport to depart on JetBlue to New York JFK. It's mid-size compared to other airports in Central America yet it seems more crowded and things are more expensive. They have the usual airport shops but on a smaller scale and less organized. Travelers are scattered all over confused with no clear indication as to where a line starts and ends. Staff make no real effort to make things more efficient. As a matter of fact they barely speak English. There is a lack of seating both in departure and arrivals areas. You have passengers standing around before boarding their flights. Bathrooms are large but still a lack of facilities for the number of passengers. Boarding announcements are done with a microphone, often times speaking on top of each other which made it hard for me to understand. Lots of confusion. Food and drinks are overpriced. It's located about 10 miles from city center and taxis overprice at $20-$35USD on average. I stayed about 2 miles away and was still charged $12USD. When considering this airport calculate prices to see if you’re actually saving money when you add in higher prices for transport, food and accomadation in the area. Would fly from here again if savings outweigh the stress.

We use this airport at least 3 times a year as we have a residence there. They have been increasing the number of flights in and out but the new terminal was built too small to handle the additional traffic. Seating often fills up and people are forced to sit on the floor and wait for a flight to depart to free up some seats. Check in is slowed by immigration and security agents checking each passenger's papers before you get to the airline counter. Security lines can back up since there is only two lines. If you didn't prepay your departure tax you can wait a long time on a line to do that at the airport as there is only a small office counter to handle this. Food is very limited and very expensive. Arrivals are the best part as the immigration and customs people are efficient and courteous. All in all the new terminal is better than the old one but it already too small and inefficient.

LIB aka Daniel Oduber International Airport is the second main airport of Costa Rica. The current terminal opened within the last year. Bright cheerful facility with windows viewing the runway etc. Security was tight - shoes belts etc to be removed. Currently 5-6 flights a day (Sunwing TACA United American Delta and Westjet). Adequate ground transport. Only issue was the food concession - US$18 for a bottle of water and a chicken wrap. Our flight was the only one Monday morning (other than a small TACA regional plane). The other 4 all leave within the 1-2pm window.

Libreville Airport is certainly not the worst airport in the region but not the best either. Staff very civil servant minded with a lot of arrogance vis a vis passengers. A good point is that on arrival luggage is quick to be on the belts. A bad one is that air conditioning is not efficient at all and we are in a tropical country.

This is a well-laid out and efficient airport. On international arrivals passport control was efficient as was the luggage claim. On international departure the various formalities (check-in immigration security) were all adequately staffed and efficient. Facilities are plenty before security though minimal after clearing immigration and security - a few duty free shops selling alcohol perfume and cigarettes and a quite limited bar. The domestic part of the airport is more or less the same though the facilities after security is even more spartan limited to a vending machine for water or soft drinks. Notably there were no restroom facilities in the waiting lounge.

ADD YOUR COMMENTS Very pleasant and open design. Arrival was easy and there was absolutely no hassle once we cleared the secure baggage area. Marked taxis were available outside. Check in was conducted in a secure area which you cannot leave once you enter so ensure you are not hungry because nothing other than a small cafe and some duty free stores are available on the gate side. Compared to other airports in the region this one is very good.

Because its a very small airport 1 flight per day, the controls are strict, unpleasant, formal and questionable. 50 ml crème and a Tape were taken because of procedures so they argue. No coffeeshop open no restaurant open, nothing open. Very unpleasant.

A modern building a short distance from the departure hall to the gate. No hassle airport. There is however no train or tram connection to the city and the city bus is not equipped for passengers travelling with luggage. The bus times are not electronically indicated and it is not clear what route the bus will take. If you don't know the city or if you don't speak French finding the optimal ground transportation might be difficult. Recently (Spring 2015) a list of new destinations was added to this airport (non-charter flights).

I agree with previous post Liège airport with the new terminal is a good alternative of Brussels. Staff is friendly and we had quick check in. Some shops and restaurants helps us to wait departure time. This airport is also the European Hub of TNT.

This is a small airport but the new passenger terminal is great. Fast service helpful people and clean. This is a good alternative of Brussels airport. We like it and for sure if possible we will try again.

It is a small airport, so time to get to the gate isn't long. There aren't a lot of shops, but enough to eat and drink something. The Wifi is good, but only free for 15min. There aren't enough spaces to sit when you wait at the gate, but I can understand that there isn't enough space.

I chose this airport for my summer holidays back in 2016, as a familiar airline started operating a scheduled summer route and provided very appealing promo prices. It seems that is airport is mostly used by charter and low cost airlines, providing all-inclusive offers to leisure destinations. However, you can still find some scheduled international routes operated by bigger European airlines throughout the year (such as Air France of course), but the prices usually go through the roof, meaning, you can buy a train ticket to Paris and fly from there at half the price. The current trend is that bigger European airlines will use this airport just for a couple of months per year, mostly for the summer season. That being said, the airport is very small, but on the other hand there is also not much traffic, so it is as big as it should be I suppose. It is very easily accessible from anywhere within France or northern Europe. This is because Lille is a train hub in northern Europe, you can use the Lille Europe train station in Lille to reach multiple European capitals. There is a bus shuttle from Lille Europe train station to Lille Lesquin airport for 10 euros aller-retour, or 8 euros single journey, not very cheap, but not expensive either. The airport is also very nice from the outside and the inside, and you have perfect view for landings and take-offs while waiting in the gate for your flight. The airport has a very informative website, a facebook page, and a twitter page. There could be more adequate toilet facilities, in the gate I was waiting the was a single facility with just one or two toilets inside, I do not remember correctly. On the plus side the facility was spacious and appropriate for people with mobility issues (e.g., wheelchair).

This is a lovely little airport, with few flights, but try to avoid the midday rush when 3 aircraft arrive and depart within an hour, as queues can be bad then. Immigration and issue of visa's is efficient and politely handled, and delivery of baggage is swift. The bus transfer to/from the terminal and the aircraft steps is a bit of a joke, as it is only about 200 yards. There are lots of banks, cell phone companies and a post office on the arrivals level. However there is no easily accessible public transport to the city centre, so it is best to try and share a taxi with a fellow traveller. Departure is also an easy operation, there is a nice pay-to-use lounge off the departure area. Otherwise few shops or eating places, which is hardly surprising given the small number of passengers.

Manageable and friendly this feels like an airport from the 80s. Coming in and going out immigration facilities are fairly efficient. Going out after immigration there are a few shops a bar/cafe and a sitting area. The layout is semi-open and you can watch the planes land (not that many do - this is an airport with very few international flights daily). You go through another security when heading to your gate where you can have your last beer before leaving the country. Overall a good reflection of the country: unpretentious clean friendly and relatively efficient.

Kamuzu Internation Airport (KIA) LLW is a small but pleasant airport. I left at night and had some problems with a taxi not able to find my house so I finally arrived at the airport 30 minutes before take off. No problem at all. The luggage scanning machine was broken so had to open my bags and everything was thoroughly checked but all was in order. Then went past immigration and it's so small up there and the shops were closed at night so couldn't buy anything. There is no smoking area after you pass immigration so keep that in mind if you smoke. All in all fine airport friendly staff one cannot get lost in here like in western airports.

Modest airport staffed by cheerful smiling people - typical Malawian experience. Took about 15 mins to get through immigration and another 15 mins to reclaim bags. Most people's bags are opened at customs for a cursory examination. On the way out check in was a bit Heath Robinson systems were down and bags/boarding passes manually processed. Only downside was the check in agent tagged my bag through to LHR using a handwritten tag and told me unconvincingly it would be fine. Just as well that I took the precaution of checking at Johannesburg as the bag came out on the belt and I had to check it in again. Overall a satisfactory experience.

Lilongwe airport (Malawi) takes you back to some of the delights of 70's travel - no announcements so you have to listen carefully when the staff shout which plane is boarding. Fortunately it's a small and quiet international airport so you can't go too far wrong unless you're asleep! There's enough shops to keep you entertained for 10 minutes there's a cafe and you can watch the planes from the outdoor balcony - and there's not much else. But what it needed to do it did so efficiently and pleasantly - nice to be aware from the security paranoia of LHR or other big western airports. Note - the duty free doesn't come in sealed duty free bags so you do run the risk of losing it all if you transit to somewhere else as we did. A shame as the prices were really ok and I don't know anywhere else outside the country that you can get Malawi gin!

Which airport can be worse than Lima International? There is always line in women’s bathroom, because each women’s bathroom has three toilet stalls and four think. They let you keep water bottle at security, to enter the gate area, but at the gate they have 6 agents who check your carry ones and personal bags and confiscate all liquid, including the bottles of water which we just bought at duty free area. I’m a diabetic and need to drink a lot of water. So I was thirsty all 6 hours of flight. Little cups of water which flight attendants give is not enough.

Despite arriving at the airport three hours early for the first time ever, I almost missed my flight. First, there was a long line to enter, followed by baggage screening. After that, another lengthy line awaited to speak with an immigration officer. Just before boarding, there was yet another line for additional bag checks, as if the machine wasn't enough. Plus, you can't bring drinks or snacks bought outside through security. I didn't even have time for shopping due to the delays. The airport staff was unhelpful when I explained I was about to miss my flight, they asked to wait like everybody else.

Security was super helpful! As we were passing through security someone stole my wife’s Apple Watch from the box after we went through the X-ray. We immediately notice it was missing and reported it. Security checked the cameras and found the thief. Using the image from the cameras they tracked down the passenger and recuperated our watch. All this within 9 minutes. Amazing!

Flew both into, and out of, Lima airport. Arrival was a swift process with immigration taking about 15 minutes and then the bags arrived shortly after. Met my driver and it was a v short walk to the car. Departure was also a breeze: quiet LATAM premium check in and then through security and passport control quickly. Staff were friendly and helpful. The Sumaq lounge was pleasant with good options for food and drink. Boarding was on time. I’m sure the airport could do with some modernisation but it worked perfectly for me.

After many years (since 2007 +/-) I frequent this airport I have seen NO improvement. My last visit was on JAN 2023. Why? - Almost no place to sit unless you are in a restaurant - bad choice of restaurants, even if the food is fine in a very few of them - Crampy and not comfortable bathrooms - No airport WiFi - Complicated and lengthy lines at customs (but here there is another responsibility too). In conclusion: it reminds me of a bus station instead of an airport.

It was an airport official with a drug dog that sniffed me. He needed to search my backpack. I had a carry on and a backpack but he was only interested in the back pack. He opened it and started to empty it, I had smaller bags with things in it that he didn’t look at. I the back compartment I had my money belt with money that I didn’t wear yet because I was still good my to go through security for a domestic flight. He dove in to the backpack, opened the money belt and took my money into his sleeves. Luckily a face mask got stuck in the zipper so he could only open a small part of it and take some Costa Rican pocket money (was going there after Peru). Terrible that you cannot feel safe at the airport.

It was the worst time lost in an airport queue that I ever experience in my life. It was about two hours to clear customs, a huge queue and just a few employees. I am very hungry now, although I do have money to spend on the airport and I thought I had time for a breaksfast there. But I ended up in a customs queue for two hours. Now I am inside the plane, I needed to run to be on time inside, even though I arrived 3 hours before my flight! You guys need more staff for the number of people in the queue.

I have never had to give an airport review. This one was so bad I felt the need to alert other travelers. I will never come to Peru again as a result of Lima Airport. Over two hours to clear customs entering. Two and a half hours leaving.
Worst experience within LA. Spent 95 mins to go through immigration. No one could guide us through afterwards and luggage took another 30 mins to come out.
97 minutes to pass immigration. No one monitoring the line. Complete chaos. I was then sent to wrong luggage carousel. Twice. Officials kept disappearing from their desks at immigration.

As no taxis were available from 5pm to 8.15 pm, at least 30 passengers from our flight were left stranded at Limoges. It was 31 degrees. There was no shelter, no vending machines for food or water. The staff were extremely unhelpful. When all the staff left, we were all still standing outside in the heat. There were elderly people and children amongst us. In the end some people walked towards Limoges. Others begged lifts and in our case (last three standing) my sister, whose birthday we were attending, and who had already been driving for 5 hours drove another 5 hours to collect us. I have been in many small airports around the world but this was the worst experience I have ever had at one. Neither I nor my traveling companions will be flying to Limoges again.

This is one of the friendliest airports I've travelled to or from, the staff are super good, in good cheer, helpful and you get the impression that they enjoy working together which shows in their happy service to the customers. Its a small, efficiently run airport. It can get very busy with tired grumpy people who refuse to speak or learn to speak French but the staff are polite in return. My husband and I use this airport regularly at least once every month, to fly to the UK, we are both Australians who love Europe (yes I know UK no longer is in Europe but it is to us Antipodeans!) There is a small news / sweet stand, a good café/bar a nice restaurant, outside and inside seating, seating around the main airport area. Loos flight side and departure / arrival hall. My only negative point otherwise would be a 10 is there is no food available for Vegans, there are 3 in our family 2 vegetarians and 2 meat eaters, some choose for all would be great. Thanks in advance.

I travel from Limoges to and from Paris. The terminal is a little bit small but it is very clean. There is a not a very long queue time and the staff were very proactive. At this airport there is one bar and one restaurant but there are no lounges or duty-free. The boarding area is very small and there is not much seating. This is a little but very efficient airport.

Linz is a very small airport. Cheap bus ticket (€3) from city centre. Nice rooftop terrace - but nothing to look at from it. A closed bar in connection to the rooftop terrace. Not much to see or do except wait. Good WiFi, but no charging spots except a random plug here and there. Nothing on the inside of security control except a duty free shop. This place does its job, not more, nor less. Tip: Do not arrive any earlier than needed. Plus: Short waiting time and distances. Rooftop terrace. Minus: Nothing to see, eat, shop or do.

Linz Airport is not great. Nothing here. Officious, overzealous staff. Probably nothing else to do apart from deal with Ryanair flights. There is a little cafe near the entrance to departures. If you fancy a tea / coffee or a pretzel get one there before you pass through departure. There is a small duty free shop and a small grotty bar at the gate. Nothing else. For a small Airport you'd have thought it would be better organised.

It was by far the smallest airport I have ever been to. Actually I wanted to go to Austria, and I found a ticket a this city so I booked and stayed there a couple of days. The airport handles only a few flights per day so nothing is really professional. We got off the plane, walked to a hall immediately, and then it was the exit and taxis were waiting, I guess all the way from the plane to the taxi was less than 100 meters. Hopefully, it was a flight in the schengen area, otherwise, as I took a glimpse, the border control would be a bit of a nightmare.

For a small airport the organisation is almost unbelievably poor - when passing through here twice last week it took an eternity to exit passport control because of the officiousness and dead-slow working speed of Austrian immigration staff. On the way back there was chaos around the boarding gate area as two (yes two!) flights were boarding simultaneously through adjacent gates (leaving 8 others empty) and no attempt was made to direct queues or instruct passengers to wait for their number sequence for a Ryanair flight. A useful airport yes - but as poor as other contributors have said.

The airport is tiny the shops are few and expensive even when compared to other small Austrian airports such as Salzburg. The opening times are poor by western standards (this is a general trend in the country). There is a departure room at Linz where once you have gone in you cannot go out . There is no prior warning of this fact there are armed police there to stop you leaving something to do with international law depends where your destination country is. It is literally one room before the runway with one drinks machine (poor) and one food machine (poor). The airport is terrible but it may still be the best option if you want a cheap flight to that area of Austria.

The airport is ultra-small. I arrived some 3 hours early and found myself trapped in an airport with nothing. There's a duty-free shop a cafe and if I remember correctly nothing else. There isn't even a TV (well I don't understand German but at least a TV gives you something to watch). Those 3 hours were the worst part of my trip to Austria. While the airport itself is obviously under-used certain facilities simply have to be provided to make the life of the handful of users easier.

Linz is indeed a very small airport however it serves it's purpose. Facilities are limited and flying in at 4:15pm I found the few shops were almost all shut. The hourly bus is excellent value for money at 2.20EUR (compared to the £14 I paid in London approx 18EUR) and only takes 20 minutes non stop to the city centre. Beware there is only ONE medium sized duty free shop after passport control.

Linz is a really small airport! It is only a few kilometer away from the city but to go to the city is either expensive or takes a lot of time. The taxi costs EUR 2200 from the Central railway station to the airport (for this distance it is a lot!). The Bus costs around EUR 200 but there is only 1 bus an hour. I won't spend their more time than necessary because there is nothing! one or two shops and cafes but not more!! It's ideal for Ryanair but otherwise I would try to bypass this airport.

Chaotic! First time we missed the flight after traveling for thirty + years. Avoid this airport. Beautiful country but terrible management of airport. People’s shouting because everyone is fighting for time.

Sparse toilet facilities on arrival. Disinterested staff (grumpy jumped up security/cleaners with headphones oblivious to others). Information desk unmanned. Seating areas packed. Wifi hit and miss. Lane separation unnecessarily long at departures - difficult for the elderly and infirm.

You often have to wait on a remote parking slot for buses to arrive, flights have narrow time windows to land or take off which leads to delays both at the origin and destination. Can definitely be better managed, Geneva airport model would suit it perfectly. It is extremely central and convenient. You almost arrive on the historic zone of Lisbon.

Once again, I have the displeasure of using Lisbon Airport. We arrived on time, but by the time we reached passport control, the line was unbelievable. Only five officers for hundreds of people — it was chaotic. Many passengers missed their flights, creating a lot of drama. The city desperately needs the new airport, which is only expected to be completed in ten years. Poor Lisbon deserves better. I would never recommend this airport. For those reading this review, you might want to consider Porto as your entry point into the country.

After a late departure from Manchester we arrived at Lisbon airport with just under an hour to transfer to our flight to Funchal, Madeira. Passport control was a joke. Our party was separated by the "helpers" as we had a 3 year old who couldn't use the electronic passport controls. They were directed to priority line which was slower than the normal line! Horrendous and very stressful experience Avoid Lisbon at all costs, especially if you have a connecting flight!

Lisbon Airport is one of the most crowded airports to fly from. The queue at Terminal 1 was extremely long, and EasyJet did not help the situation as they were slow in attending to the earliest passengers. The security control at the airport was particularly inefficient, with only a few security processing lines functioning out of many available in the terminal. This caused long queues at security, and the processing of passengers took much longer than expected. As a result, the five of us missed our flight, despite having already checked in. Although we reported this issue to EasyJet and called to explain our ordeal, there was no assistance offered. It was apparent that they were already aware of the chaos at the security control, yet the airport's management did nothing to improve the situation. Passengers were left to bear the loss without any accountability or remorse from the airline or the airport authorities. It is unbelievable that we missed our flight after arriving at the airport two hours in advance.

Arrival was very efficient but departure was stressful. Very cramped. Inadequate signage. Endless pointless chicanes for non-existent lines. No seating presumably in very old airport. Totally inadequate for today but improved signage would help a lot. Eg we were told at check in that we had to go to Security but there was no sign to security. We were given the impression that it was extra and not part of the route to the departure gates. Everyone exasperated and short tempered. Not a good experience. Allow loads of time.

Surprisingly good experience departing Lisbon Airport Terminal 2 on a Sunday evening with only hand luggage. Far less crowded than I remembered from previous visits (maybe I was lucky?) and security was a breeze. The duty free area has been updated and toilets were clean. It still has the low cost look and feel and does not have very attractive departure lounge or places to plug your phone and laptop, but overall pretty efficient.

Not a good experience. Staff seem to be purposefully unhelpful. Passport scanning machines only seemed to work 50% of the time after which you are sent to an even bigger wait line. When I told the staff I would miss my flight he told me to take it up with the airline which made no sense at all. Very little seating in the airport, wait for ever to use restrooms and no way near enough staff. I only made my flight because people let me jump the line at passport control after waiting 2 hours. Would give 0 out of 5 if possible.

Humberto Delgado Airport (LIS), avoid if you can or you’d have to arrive at least 4 hours before your flight, they lack staff at customs (2-3 officers for 700 people). We’ve missed the flight in October half term as the queue at the customs (after Security check) on 29/10/2024 between 6-11pm, was over two hours there are no staff on the ground and you’d be refused help if you’d ask to be fast tracked or given priority even if you could still make it to your flight. If you miss your flight you’d have to queue again for over 2hrs to get your stamp cancelled. No matter if you complain no one will respond, assist or help you. Airline staff say it happens all the time. Airport can’t cope, people are welcome to raise a complaint with highest authority (custom police) but do you really want to risk it and possibly get locked up?

A delightful regional airport set amongst the lush valleys and hills of the Northern Rivers District of New South Wales. Nice well designed terminal and with more convenient flight schedules with Regional Express down to Sydney than nearby Ballina - which handles mainly tourist traffic. Lismore Airport is close to town and has all the usual car rental facilities - and is only 30 minutes to the coast Byron Bay/Ballina etc. Only downside is as is usual at most airport terminals in Australia blaring televisions all around the terminal causing a racket and breaking the pleasant peace of this delightful place.

Small & quiet regional airport with small turboprop aircraft from a single airline. There is no separate security screening & staff have always been exceptionally helpfull. Late arrivals for departures are handled efficiently. The cafe is an offshoot of a nice respected cafe in the city serving exceptional coffee. There is little point trying to fly from the bigger airports of Ballina or the Gold Coast. The planes might be bigger there but flight times to Sydney are the virtually the same & you are less comfortable waiting in those bigger airports. Mother nature is the only downside with early morning fog causing some concerns but has never really affected me when I have wanted to travel.

One of the nicest and  cleanest airports I've experienced. Thoughtful touches are everywhere, from the piano in the food court, to bags for wet umbrellas, to a cart of peanuts and pretzels from Delta (identical to what they give out in flight) at the baggage claim. Bathrooms are spotless! And clocks throughout the airport.

Simply put the Little Rock Airport has to be the nicest smaller-sized airport that I have ever used. It is very easy to access from downtown and elsewhere. Everyone who I encountered there was extremely friendly. The TSA folks were all nice and they did their best to move folks through the line as quickly as possible. For an airport its size it has a great variety of restaurants.

Little Rock National Airport (LIT) is one of my favorite mid-size airports. It is on par with the Bob Hope Airport (BUR) and Ft. Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport (FLL) in that it is easy to get in and out of the airport complex the location is close to downtown and the presence of low-cost airlines keep overall ticket prices among the lowest in the country.

The facelift is complete! After years of construction everything appears to be complete. LIT is smoke free so smokers must cross security and go to a covered outside area. Several coffee shops and a mini food court were added however while several open early for early bird flights most close long before the last flights arrive. A couple of little news stands and a book store was added but the gift shop is not on the secure side. So if someone one that has a lay over must cross security to shop. Free wireless internet has be added that can be accessed from almost any where between gates 1 & 12. Overall not bad for a small airport.

I have been to many many airports all over the world and Little Rock is one of my favorites. It is small but modern and clean. There are never long lines and the personnel are always helpful and friendly. After being away from home for months I always look forward to the simplicity and comfort of LR airport. I like that baggage claim is after you meet up with the people waiting to get you as well.

As an Arkansas native I have flown in and out of LRN several times. LR National is exceptionally clean and easy to navigate. For an airport with only 12 gates there is plenty to do nice places to eat and even a museum. The airport just underwent a $170 million overhaul which gives it a nice modern flare. It has also recently added a three-level parking garage which is reasonably priced and has easy access to the terminal. LRN is now undergoing construction on their baggage claim area to make it more "user friendly" (although a little burdensome in the meantime) and there is also some landscape work being done to the main entrance to get ready for the opening of the Clinton Presidential Center in November '04. Easy transportation to city (downtown is only 4 mi. from LIT). Also cheaper fares than nearby MEM!

Our plane landed at about 5.45pm. Once we left the plane we had a lengthy walk, in bitterly cold weather, to join the long queue for passport control. We were queueing outside, in freezing temperatures, for well over thirty minutes before our place in the queue reached the inside of the building, where we queued for at least another thirty minutes. The walkway outside, interspersed with glass tunnels was totally grim: dirty, unpleasant, unwelcoming and unfit for purpose. The intense cold and wind made it incredibly uncomfortable and, whilst the tunnels provided slight respite from the biting winds, for a huge part of the time there was no protection at all. Thankfully, it wasn’t raining! There appears to be a complete lack of any consideration for the welfare of customers. I can honestly say our arrival into Liverpool was the worst we have experienced in over forty years travelling around the world. If the airport buildings cannot support the number of people arriving at any one time, then something needs to be done! The current situation is totally unacceptable.

On the 17th of October i arrived at the airport with a Uber rider. Shortly after i left, i noticed i left my phone in the uber who has driven off. My flight was 1 hour and 30 minutes away from departure. I tried asking for multiple people within the airport for help if they had the uber app to help me contact the driver, as i would not be able to check in to the flight without my phone. The kind police security gentleman by the name of Chris kindly helped me contact uber, let me use his phone to call the uber driver and, with only 30 minutes left for depart, kindly helped me through the security queue. Honestly a life saver and I couldn't be more grateful for finding this man this day, and i would like to once again thank you if you ever read this review.

At present I am at my departure destination (Majorca) but fell so aggrieved at Liverpool John Lennon Airport that I feel I have to submit my review now. Arrived at Airport in torrential rain. No continuous covering from dropping off area to domestic arrival. Restaurants in domestic arrival dirty (pigeons flying about depositing droppings). Security staff totally unresponsive when asked for routine help. Departure side restaurants poor value and abysmal food.

This is my home airport and I hate it. The traffic controls and parking options are an absolute scam. Terrible, trying to make revenue and dressing it up as safety. I always choose to drive to Manchester since Liverpool Airport stole £100 from me with their lying and manipulation of video evidence. Disgrace to the city.

Myself and family travel via Liverpool Airport two to three times a year. It remains our first choice since we began using it ten years ago where previously we tended to travel via Manchester. Liverpool is smaller than most international airports but this has it's benefits, less crowds, less queuing and easy access. The staff throughout the airport are friendly and ready to help. The signage is easy to read and well proportioned. Lifts are available. Liverpool recognises the Sunflower scheme. Our experience has been, security is strict, but quick and friendly to get through. Prices are typical airport prices (£1.99 for a small bottle of water) reasonable I suppose when considering the ridiculous prices airports are allowed to charge where ever you go.. I can only presume it is down to airport owners and the high rents they charge? The only shops I ever see that are really busy are the food, beverage and drinks outlets. Again our experience has been food is fresh and well prepared. The one downside are probably the toilet facilities, a bit smelly, and like most airports today no free drop off zone. Why airports, in the name of security, are allowed to charge astronomical prices for parking I have never understood? Captive audience I suppose. All in all I would give Liverpool Airport 9 stars out of 10. Freshen up the loos, be the first actually run an airport for the passengers benefit in pricing and parking and you get a 10.

It's a long while since I have posted a review here, but I have not changed my opinion of Liverpool Airport: for my wife and myself it is always our first choice. It is never crowded, we know our way around and we have never had a negative experience when passing through. About three years ago we had to switch to Manchester Airport when our flight was cancelled and we hated the crowds, the queues and the struggle for seats. In comparison, passing through Liverpool is a doddle. We've never had any problem at security which is light and airy compared with the claustrophobic equivalent at Manchester. It helps that we travel hand baggage only, so we can bypass the queues to hand in hold bags and don't have to wait at baggage reclaim on the way back. We're not interested in buying food and drink prior to our flight and we know that even if we are delayed en route to the airport we'll still progress through the airport to the boarding gate with time to spare. Passport control can be a bottleneck on return, but even that seems to have been speeded up in the last year or so. As long as it does not over-expand in terms of flights, we will be content to use Liverpool Airport for as long as we continue to fly.

Upon arrival at Liverpool Airport it was just a disaster the moment we sat foot on the tarmac in the pouring rain. The young lady with the Swissport vest organising our movement was completely out of her depth. We were told to wait in the rain for 15 to 20 minutes before we were moved to what I can only describe as the luggage train area. Once there we were told to move here there and everywhere while the polite baggage handlers drove their luggage carts in between us all. At one stage a young man arrived wearing a health and safety vest and showed no initiative in any way, so he seemed completely pointless in holding this position. Another time elapsed as the passengers could not enter the building for whatever reason. Once in the arrival building all baggage carousels were stopped and it seemed everyone for themselves to wonder around when we found our luggage at an area where they had just been thrown about on the floor and belt that was not on. It was a complete fiasco and the staff need to be trained properly and professionally and to be informed that if they do not want to be in the position of employment then they need to be told to seek employment elsewhere. They were extremely unprofessional and extremely poorly trained for the positions they hold. I will fly and arrive at an alternate airport in the future. In my employment I have been in and out of airports all over the world and due to the serious lack of knowledge and professional of the staff at this particular airport I would rate this ‘international airport’ as one of the worst airports I have experienced.

My review is that the service at this airport is the worst I’ve encountered for a long time. I would not recommend it to any traveller wishing to get home. It took more than one hour to provide baggage at 2 am with only 100 passengers in the whole terminal. Give it a wide berth at all costs, travellers.

This place has quite the worst airport signage that I have ever seen at a so-called International Airport. I went to Liverpool John Lennon Airport to pick up some friends arriving from Spain. The signage was so bad at the airport terminal, that they went the wrong way and took 43 minutes to find me. The free parking time was 40 minutes. Ka-ching! Eight pounds straight off the mark for being three minutes late, entirely due to the lack of your damned signage (a sign saying Drop-off 2 this way and another sign at the car park saying Drop-off 2 is all that it would have required, with the same for the other car-parks). If you want to drive into the airport, the signs are adequate (I wouldn't say they gave drivers much warning of the turns) but if you actually want to arrive to meet someone, particularly if you've never been their before, the place is dreadful. Of course, you can always open your wallet and say after me "Help Yourself" and pay the extortionate charges to drop people off, but then airports have always been completely immoral in the extent of their charges. Needless to say, we didn't stop for coffee!
Dirty and smelly public washrooms. Good food and beverage options. Long queues at security screening. Cramped baggage reclaim area and long wait for baggage to be delivered to the Carousel.

Lovely airport, but for some odd reason there’s 2 security checks, which all goes to creating queues. No airline lounge, yet there seems to be plenty of lounges on the first floor, and most un-used. On arrival, the immigration process was long winded, can’t understand the need for a manned diplomatic line, Livingstone can’t be getting many not being the capital, though on the plus side, Zambian Immigration now allows you pay for your visa with a credit card.

Terminal is very small so if there are plenty of passengers or more than one plane arriving/departing at the same time it will get packed. My own experience was a good one though and it was a breeze to get the visa collect luggage and get out. There is a new much larger terminal under construction next to the current one.

Long lines await you when you arrive and need to visa to enter the country. There are only two counters: one for visas and the other for travellers who do not need visas. The arrival hall is small but the waiting drivers etc are gathered respectfully outside the terminal building. The airport is not far from the town.

We arrived at lunchtime from Jo'berg to find the arrival queue out the door. Despite huge ads for Visa credit cards throughout the airport by the time we waited 30 mins to get to the passport counter to pay our visa entry they only accept US$ 50 each. The airport only has 2 atm's one displayed a 'virus detected' message the other was temporarily out of service. Departure was just as slow and chaotic with the queue out the door.

Arrived on the only SAA flight into Livingstone a fairly basic operation though there was a mad scrum to fill out the visa form out as there were no pens on hand. This slowed everything down as people were getting their $Dollars out to buy the visas (you have to have Dollars in cash as well). About 20 mins after the BA flight arrived to add to the lines so thankful I flew SAA. In the past the flights into S Africa used to dish out visa forms on the flight before you landed they should do this on this flight too.

A small, pleasant, and friendly airport. All the staff are really nice, and now even the younger staff at security are very friendly, which wasn't typical before the pandemic. The procedures are very fast. However, during peak times, there is absolutely not enough space around the café and duty-free shops in the Schengen section, even after the recent terminal upgrade. I really miss the newspaper stand in this area. I would especially like to praise the staff at Little Slovenia in the Non-Schengen section. It’s truly a small oasis of kindness and well-being.

They have removed all the ceiling tiles that might have deadened the sound so that the bare concrete is exposed in the departure area. As a result it’s like being in an echo chamber and the announcements are impossible to understand. It’s very unpleasant. Also there are very few seats in the check-in area even though there is plenty of space, so people end up sitting on the floor. Finally the taxi drivers have a scam where they add all sorts of illegal charges so that a normal 35 EUR fare for a ride to the city center costs 85 EUR or more.
Convenient because it's small. The only toilet at the Schengen departures is horrible. The offer of food and beverages is limited. Overall, the new terminal looks unfinished.

Ljubljana airport is very practical for passengers and all procedures are carried out quickly. There are not many flights and passengers in the morning, so the experience is even better. The employees are professionally friendly, but not much more (very, very few smiles). In the duty-free shop, some Croatian products are offered as Slovenian ones, which is probably an unintentional mistake. The coffee at the bar is excellent. The toilet, which was otherwise clean, smelled of nitrogen compounds, probably due to insufficient or absent ventilation. In the waiting room in front of the bridges to the plane, at least some of the otherwise comfortable seats were torn. It was also possible to see through the windows into neglected, closed, and abandoned rooms, which they probably do not know what to do with. The airport is a very important point of entry to my beloved country, so even some seemingly trivial carelessness is out of place.

Ljubljana Airport has undergone a major update over the last few years and has increased in size quite substantially. Line of sight signage is good making navigation around the airport very easy. Arriving from a Schengen country results in a very fast entry procedure to the country. Departing was also a breeze with very friendly and efficient staff, we were checked in through security, customs and in the lounge in very short time. Waiting area's are comfortable and duty free shopping and other outlets well staffed and spotlessly clean.

Lovely airport, amazing views of the Alps. Check-in was ok. Wizz airline desks were poorly managed with long ques but the rest of the airlines seemed fine and so was security. Shops were a bit lacking but overall a good airport.

Excellent little airport. A bit tired cosmetically but everyone was friendly and everything worked seamlessly. Don’t rush through security unless you’re desperate to look at aeroplanes as there’s not much else to do. There’s a little smoking box that takes 4 people after security next to gate 4 upstairs. It’s free and the ventilation works well.

Terrible airport - could not check in for ages and nowhere open to eat or buy food/drink until we had gone through security. The food available after security was ridiculously expensive and tiny portions. We got our water filled up but the woman told us she wasn’t supposed to allow people to have free water and when I pointed out the cost of plastic bottles on the environment she said that the airport didn’t care about that and just wanted people to spend as much money as possible. Avoid at all costs, Slovenia is an incredible country but I would advise coming via Croatia, Italy or Austria instead!

Avoid at all costs! This used to be a reasonable airport, nothing special but at least flights were punctual. This seem to have degraded in the last couple of years. Queues at this airport resemble a rock concert. I have been to many airports around the world but have never had to wait 2 + hours for a simple baggage check (and, sadly, this is the rule rather than exception). Flights are almost always late and frequently cancelled. Absolutely no care for passengers' itineraries. If you are planing a trip, try to avoid this airport, particularly if your itinerary involves connecting flights.

Upon leaving Europe back to Los Angeles my flights had me departing LJU to connect at CDG for my flight to LA. For some reason my travel agent had booked the two flights separately under two different confirmation numbers. while in Slovenia I had called the airline, and even the hotel's concierge did as well, and we both found out only the gate agent can make sure and both flights are listed as one continuous trip, mainly for the sake of routing checked luggage all the way through. The gate agent, with the assistance of a co-worker easily got this done and I was only charged $35 for an extra checked bag (my initial flight was in economy, while my connecting flight was in business. Thankfully both flights were on the same airline, in the end everything went smoothly. Upon arrival at LJU I was amazed how much of a small town airport feel it had. You could walk through the entire airport in 15 minutes. There were only about four check-in/ticket windows and no one was in line. Proceeding to security there were about three rows to enter through, and once again, no one else was in line. My time initially at check-in took about 10-15 minutes (to get my flight/s worked out and to pay the extra checked bag fee) and then within ten minutes I was through security and enjoying a drink near my gate. A very laid back and friendly experience. Sort of a calm before the storm I would have at CDG in three more hours.

The check in area is too small and overcrowded. The escalator is never turned on, forcing a necessary wait for the elevator. Security is a nightmare. Some staff are pleasant, some are plain rude. Machines stopped everyone and they physically searched each and every bag / personal item (so much for a random check ? More like check everyone). Nothing meaningful to do, limited shops and restaurants. Wifi is poor and unsuitable. Not enough seats unless you go early morning. There is no lounge  (shocking for a so called premium airport.) To board, there are no jetways or boarding ramps, they make you queue in the freezing cold and board by stairs. Too bad if you have bags as the gates have no elevators. Also gate 21 has poor lighting. The arrival was so much worse as well. Arrived at the last gate (10) so this caused a 10 min walk to immigration. Avoid E gate number 6 as it didn't work. Was forced to wait in line to see officer Only 1 baggage collection unit was used as opposed to the two available (by the way the screens told me to use reclaim 10 which didn't even exist). Suddenly they changed our reclaim to reclaim 2 which caused a mad rush in such a tiny space, too few toilets in the arrival hall as well. One cubicle is not enough to serve the arrivals hall (international). This caused queue jumping in the small restroom leading to arguments. This entire ordeal took 40 mins of my time To conclude, dirty toilets and arguing passengers and on top of that, faulty equipment and on top of that my bags took ages. If this is the first thing a first time London tourist saw, I don't think they would want to visit this beautiful city again. I advise people to use Heathrow and Gatwick, or even Stansted instead

Awful from start to finish. Used to be great years ago. At the moment - a long security queue, dirty lavatories, no accurate information about the flights, very long wait for the luggage after the return flight, nobody makes any real effort. Is anybody managing this airport please?

Waiting for my flight 15 minutes before departure. The plane clearly isn't even in the gate, the LED screen still shows it on time and boarding. Not one message over the public address system. Terrible communication.

A small airport right in the east of the city center, with a convenient metro connection readily available. The terminal itself is small but well organized and has enough small shops for food and beverages. Security queuing times late in the evening were non-existent, border control (only inbound) was equally fast. Best airport if you've to be in London itself.
The toilet facilities are disgustingly filthy. Shopping experience is rubbish too. Some of the seats in the waiting area’s are not very clean, this is the worst UK airport I have visited.

This used to be a great airport. I have no choice but to use it regularly. Today I have arrived 20mins early which can't be helped with the train service at the moment. I have arrived much earlier previously and been able to check in, today I have been told to go and get a coffee then come back. I don't want a coffee plus refuse to pay for one down here then go upstairs to get one. The only seating is in the coffee shop I am a pensioner plus have disabilities. So I am now standing with a crowd of people whilst I would like to say the check in desk is empty. This has really set me up for going through security where they have adopted the same puffer jacket bouncer attitude as Stansted airport is an embarrassing

The most awful airport. Have not used for 10 years or so. Used to be a great airport which was quick and easy to use. Now has terrible snaking queues to get through security. Much worse than Heathrow or Gatwick. Avoid if you can.

Crowded as ever. Security was OK (no longer than 10 minutes), but once inside (@1800 admittedly) it was hard to find anywhere to sit. The airport is a brilliant idea, but the concourse areas are too small for the size of aircraft they are now handling. Not enough toilets, e.g. One positive: with the Elizabeth Line now in service, a transit from LHR can be done in under 90 minutes via Woolwich and the DLR, station-to-station (I managed it in 70).

Avoid at peak times, security is a mess. Gone are the days of the 15 minute check in and smooth easy journey. This used to be my go to airport due to the ease of transit. Such a shame they have added so much flight capacity and not matched it with security.

Do not transit through this airport! No direct transfer path, have to pass through immigration, no airline lounges (even BA). A godforsaken 4 hour wait in a miserable little airport. Truly a third world experience in the heart of London.

Gatwick is, above all, an experience. An experience for the eyes, nostrils, and hygiene that might not exactly be considered favorable. Bear in mind, I come from the US. We have some excellent major airports, but also some rubbish ones. Gatwick would easily be considered to be among the worst of what I'm used to in the US, and it's the worst major airport I've seen yet in Europe (other than possibly Otopeni in Bucharest). The only nice part of Gatwick I saw was the train station upon exiting the national rail. Otherwise, the check-in areas are depressing and run down, like a throwback to whenever Thatcher was prime minister yet without any good cleaning since that time. The check-in (as well as gate) personnel with Norse Atlantic Airlines were honestly surly - professional, but surly. The security process is a hot mess and lines are incredibly long; at least I had paid the 8 pounds or so for expedited security. While I made it through security quickly, I still had to swiftly pay attention to what was going on. Walking through the south terminal, there were very few places to sit and eat. At least the employees at the Pret were nice. The floors were dirty and sticky. The toilets and accompanying sinks looked like they were also from the Thatcher era. The terminal had a pervasive damp, dank, flatulent-like odor to it (not sulfur, but still odd and gross). Final point, I usually like British people for their politeness, but Gatwick is a place to see some of the worst in British people. In closing, if you have to come to London, fly to Heathrow, as at least some parts of it feel like a proper airport, or to London City, which is very small and easy. Very clearly, the privatization of many British airports has not served the British traveler well at all.

Arrived today and was disgusted by the cleanliness of the airport. Dust which looked like it had been there for days. Floors old but no excuse for not giving them a good clean. Moving walkways with piles of muck around them. Hopefully will never need to use Gatwick again.

Gatwick North terminal is not big enough for the number of passengers. We are treated with contempt by the airport. There is nowhere to sit, nowhere to get an alcoholic drink - all outlets were absolutely heaving and no bar space or tables available. Passengers have to beg for some service. Travelling on my own and I had to walk the terminal 3 times to find a seat at a bar.

This airport is very small for the number of passengers and airlines it is serving. Everywhere seemed to be crowded and felt cramped. I thought they needed more space for better facilities and customer service. Transferring from the train coming from London to the terminal, and between terminals was very easy and well signage. The prayer room is available and well-maintained, and the toilets are clean. Not a pleasant experience for shopping and dining as there are too many people in a cramped space.

Average airport. I've been here many times since I live in the UK but my experience never really changed. There are a lot of shops which I find good and the food is meh. I do often see some rubbish on the floor and wet floors with no wet floor sign which is quite dangerous. If you come here I do recommend to go to the lounge since it is relaxing, you get tasty food and a view of planes taking off. The flights are always massively delayed but overall a pretty average airport.

I was impressed with my trip through LGW south terminal, I experienced no issues with my journey. I went to check in and was done within 2 minutes, Security was fast and easy as well. The departures area is well kitted out with shops and restaurants. Seating outside of these areas is limited however so be aware of that. The walk to the gate areas is extremely long so book assistance if you struggle with distance walking. Overall, mostly clean only issue was a few dribbles in the toilets but when I asked a cleaner he was more than happy to have a look. Really cannot complain even on arrival the experience was smooth and without issues.
Lousy air traffic control. Flight on-time yet they delay you onboard citing busy half term. Over an hour to wait on the aircraft. No wonder Gatwick lost the runway competition to Heathrow.

Long distance walking doesn't suit everyone with mild mobility issues, and the South Terminal, complete with non working escalators assists with this. Added to which, poor signage directing you one way to passport control which resulted in a blocked exit, only to be followed by being rudely shouted at (as if we were an unwanted problem) by an official wasn't acceptable either. It was a surprise however to find the scanners were actually working!

We arrived on a delayed flight which deposited us in the South Terminal at around 2am instead of our normal 9pm. As all hotels at the airport plus a 16km radius were listed as “no vacancy”, we had no choice but to settle in for the night. As you are not permitted to check baggage until 2 1/2 hours prior to the flight, and our flight was not until 11am, we couldn’t even cross into the better post-security gate section. Be that as it may security gates are closed then anyways. Seems this airport hasn’t even considered this as a possibility from a human being perspective. There were close to 100 of us in the same situation. The couple dozen comfortable seats were long gone, occupied by the long-since asleep. The rest of us were forced to curl up on tile flooring or leaning against walls and pillars. The toilets were disgusting. The fact that airports don’t consider that people can arrive at all hours for all sorts of reasons this long into the air travel game, boggles my mind. But some do it well. Gatwick doesn’t even attempt to make this comfortable at all. The stewards of this airport need to spend a night in their own airport as an eye-opener..

The only things that seem to have changed since the last time I flew through Gatwick is that the prices in the food court have somehow gotten even more expensive. £6 for a small, lukewarm, flavorless and inedible breakfast wrap is a disgrace. The staff at security screening are still unsmiling and unfriendly barking orders at passengers and the holding pen/waiting area is still a cramped and poorly laid out mess where the departure boats are impossible to see from the seating areas. The whole place feels dirty and in need of a good clean and it needs quite a bit of maintenance. It’s convenient for getting to the south coast but I always feel like I need a good wash after being here. A pretty poor overall experience again I’m afraid.

Terminal 2 has poor seating and overpriced restaurants. Security has improved as they now have new body & shoe scanners. Toilets are not well serviced. Getting from train station to Terminal is a long walk. Getting from hotels to Terminal is chargeable.

Domestic passenger. Arrived at and departed on from Terminal 5. No issues disembarking. Having staff there to ensure passengers with baggage to reclaim don't inadvertently leave without collecting it is helpful. On return, it took a while to clear security. With a number of airports across the UK now using the new scanners, meaning liquids can stay in hand luggage, it's a pity Terminal 5 had not restarted this. Good range of shops and restaurants in departures, with clear signage and ample seating. Flight pushed back on time but there was a wait of about 40 minutes as it sat in a queue for takeoff clearance. From previous experience, excellent for international travel as most major cities across the world reachable with a direct flight, but Gatwick remains my first choice for regional travel.
The arrival immigration process was very slow. We had to wait for so long. All the queue was full and not moving. It is clear that the is not enough staff for the passengers.

A complete mess of an airport. Chaos, queues and ineptitude at every turn. Security has different rules every time you travel there. Boarding zones mean nothing, horribly busy, expensive, dirty and tired looking. Toilets were messy, corridors had buckets catching leeks. Staff are obviously fed up and act accordingly.

They made me throw away a small Benadryl bottle for my Allergic child. The manager was belligerent and nasty when we explained why we needed the medicine. I am also pregnant and once we got to the gate I couldn’t use the bathroom. I asked the staff and they said “you can go but the gates could be closed on the way back”.

Drove to the airport to meet a visitor. At the barriers was met by multiple and confusing signage that proved irrelevant. The barrier machine itself was confusing and the enquiry line was unanswered. Finally got the barrier to work. Terminal 2 is looking dated and the lifts were slow and crowded. Inside the terminal the men’s toilet was grubby and stank of urine. Hand washing water was a trickle. All in all this relatively new terminal and the airport approach and layout is third world.

We use the BA lounges here to avoid the horrendous crowds everywhere in the terminals. This airport needs at least two more terminals to offer the space and experience many of its rivals offer. When we landed at Terminal 3 we had another interminable wait for our luggage. Not a great experience again. I'd recommend it only because it is better than the other London airports

Arrived from Saudi Arabia expecting wheelchair assistance, but none was provided. I was directed to a buggy at the gate, where a rude employee refused to let my wife join, citing space. Forced to walk through Terminal 4’s maze, we arrived at customs only to see the buggy arrive with four empty seats. Confronting her, she showed no empathy, refused to apologize, and argued even more when I asked for her name. A shockingly poor welcome back to the UK compared to Asia's service-oriented travel culture.

We were lucky enough (or unlucky enough) to use the Fast Track in Terminal 3 on leaving the UK from a holiday. On entering the line was blocked with a mother with infant in a pram with no effort from security in getting her to move to the side while looking for something. On entry through the doors all 5 security staff were looking at 1 bag ignoring all those waiting to get their luggage screened for more than 10 minutes. What is the point of having modern 'faster' equipment for scanning when there is no one manning them.

I used to like Heathrow because it was nice and expansive with a variety of shops. Our recent experience with connecting at this airport was a complete nightmare. We got dropped off at Terminal 5 and had to haul over to Terminal 3. We were already on the verge of missing our transcontinental flight and we were dealing with highly incompetent and indifferent airport staff. After taking the bus between terminals, we had to run another 2 miles inside the airport to get to our gate, also having to go through another needless security check. They were almost going to change seats on us even though we paid extra for more legroom. One egregious staff member even poked his head in the middle of another staffer trying to help us, just to chime in and tell her to drop our itinerary if we are arguing about seats. A very entitled bunch. I will never again go through this airport, whether it be for connecting or otherwise.

Really disappointed by the way in which Stansted has changed. Will definitely fly from Heathrow next time. No Wifi, unless you pay, (free doesn't even work). The recharging stations in the waiting area just don't work if you have a USB connection. Passengers desperately looking for a wall socket to recharge. Shockingly bad service for an airport serving London.

I used to love stansted airport. Conveniently close to my parents and fast. Sadly I have to emphasise "used to" because year on year its getting worse and now I would rather drive an extra 2hrs from Heathrow and save all the pain. Very long security check queues are now standard and rarely less than 1 or 2hrs. And when you get through the have lots of new shops but absolutely no waiting / seating space. The waiting areas are extremely overwhelmed as are the bars and restaurants. Even staff are grumpy and sometimes rude and the toilets are filthy. Sad state and a poor demonstration of what uk can do. Not a good example. Why have they changed for the worse?

The experience at the airport was a humiliation ritual. We arrived at the airport 2 hours before the gate closure. We didn't have any baggage. There was a 6 lane colossal queue towards a narrow gate that goes towards the hall where security check starts and people were packed like cockroaches getting pressed under a hydraulic pressure. The security check was a complete disaster, engineered to maximise the chances of having a stress-induced stroke and missing your flight. Despite the crowd, security insisted to go through everything single procedure in a slowest possible way. It took us 2 hours to get through the security and when we were over with it, we've tried to reach the gate running like crazy on a result of losing our flight. 15 people lost our same flight and so on with other Ryanair's flight too. We've tried to talk with customer service and to staff and the answer was always the same saying that we had to arrive at least 4 hours earlier, in a really rude way. That was easily the worst airport experience. Understaffed airport and such a bad organisation.

I am convinced that anyone that has anything bad to say about Stansted is either paid, delusional, or a banker that hasn't got anything positive to say about anything. I've travelled to 56 airports, so, not quite as many as some people, but I've been to enough to say that Stansted is bloody marvelous at what it does. It's simple, clean, efficient, has a beautiful single terminal building, some of the fastest security queues I've ever seen no matter how many people it's trying to push through. Stansted is quite simply, operationally, one of the best ever and I've never had to wait more than 10 minutes departing. Even arrivals moves ridiculously fast, and while sometimes you can wait in a queue that looks lengthy to enter the country, it never takes *that* long. The people working at Stansted know how to move! It's an absolutely marvelous display and it always astounds me whenever I go. It's a well signposted airport, very easy to navigate; the quiet area is fantastic, loads of shops and food options. My only MINOR criticism is that it can sometimes be difficult to find a place to sit down upstairs, but other than that, it's absolutely a class airport.

Worst airport I have ever experienced mainly because of the staff and the security process. It was incredibly disorganised and the staff were beyond rude. Only allowed one small plastic bag that had to seal. If you couldn’t seal it then just told ‘you’ll have to throw away whatever doesn’t fit’. I’ve used a clear plastic wash bag at many airports recently with no issues (including the return flight of this journey through Budapest) Not Stansted though, and because the small bag they gave me would only half seal I was told with a shrug of shoulders ‘better choose what you’re throwing away’ . My bag then got pushed over for further inspection which took approximately 20 minutes of waiting for it to be my turn. By the time they got to my bag it was re scanned and I was told there was nothing in there that needed checking. She swabbed some of the items in the small plastic bag then proceeded to struggle to seal it up again. To which I said ‘don’t bother I’m transferring it back into the wash bag now’ . She said ‘I’m sorry I have to, it’s silly I know’ So I watched her seal it, pass it over to me, where I unsealed it and put it all back in the original bag. Pettiness to the extreme. Return journey (through Budapest) no issue with plastic wash bag, had a little look through and a lovely chat about our trip. A completely different experience. I feel embarrassed that our country is like this

I have travelled widely around the world in my 68 years on every continent, and Stansted Airport is about the worst airport. I have travelled through Stansted airport many many times, and it continues to steadily deteriorate, and has now reached the level of a third world country. There are no working jetways at the airport, instead you have to climb down a steep staircase to get out of or into the aircraft. Then once you are out of the aircraft, walk across the apron tarmac, then you have to walk up two flights of steep stairs, with no elevator available. Third world stuff. The last straw on my latest trip was the complete lack of adequate toilet facilities, for men and women. We stopped at a couple of loos, one in the domestic baggage claim area and another in the rental car village, men and women's side. They were all filthy, lacking in toilet paper, and had few if any working stalls. The majority of the stalls were not working at all, i.e. were out of order, and in the rental car village there were no working male stalls at all. The Hertz guy at the rental car village told me there was a male stall somewhere, but I was not able to find it, and there was no signage supporting that man's claim. Overall Horrible, filthy, disgusting, and a total disgrace. Welcome to Britain!

If you like rude staff who shout at you and give instructions inconsistent with every other international airport, this is the place for you. I was shouted at for using the same clear plastic bag for liquids that I’d used at Gatwick in both July and December 2023. The man threw a tiny bag at me and then turned his back on me. Subsequently my bag was rechecked at security by another man with the type of manners that any parent of a toddler would be embarrassed by. Having endured this, I then discovered that half of the ladies’ toilets were unavailable. During peak travel season? A dreadful experience - I’d last flown from Stansted 10 years ago and am in no hurry to relive this demeaning and inefficient experience.

The entire STN experience was a humiliation ritual. We arrived at the airport 1 hour before the gate closure. We didn't have any baggage. We acquired our boarding passes pretty quickly but the horror started at the security check. There was a 6 lane colossal queue towards a narrow gate that goes towards the hall where security check starts and people were packed like cockroaches getting pressed under a hydraulic pressure. The security check was a complete disaster, engineered to maximise the chances of having a stress-induced stroke and missing your flight. Despite the crowd, security insisted to go through everything single procedure in a slowest possible way. It took us 30 mins to get through the security and when we were over with it, only 10 minutes left for gate closure. Then, a marathon started because of the distance between gates and shopping corridors. We ran through maze-like corridors and made it to our gates exhausted and stressed. That was easily one of my top three worst airport experience.

Good public transport connections via bus/coach. Lack of seats before security. Long wait at security. Airside is a vast overpriced shopping centre. The only reasonably priced food outlet is Wetherspoons. Toilets are disgusting and stink. Floor was covered in urine. Sinks were filthy. Uncomfortable wooden seating in departures area. WiFi is terrible. Only free for an hour then you have to log in again. Overall a badly run overpriced airport that could be better with competent management.

What a filthy dump of an airport. Outbound was bad but the return beggars belief. Toilets are absolutely revolting, floors and carpets look like they've never been cleaned, totally inadequate seating all over the airport, hostile, rude, argumentative ground staff. Arrived early from Pisa with Ryanair and connecting to Glasgow with easyjet. Was not allowed to check in as I was too early. Nowhere to sit, customers in the same boat were sitting all over the filthy floors. Check in staff both at the main bag drop and gate area were downright unpleasant at best. Boarding was total chaos. Customers being held in a freezing cold stairwell without seating for over 30 mins prior to boarding. Everything about this place is lacking. As the owners and management have very little pride in their airport it's high time that the civil aviation authority stepped in and forced them to clean up their act or lose their licence. I'm sure all of the other airports in the region will manage to pick up the slack. What an embarrassment for the country when foreign tourists arrive here and this is their first taste of the UK. Filthy, embarrassing,disgraceful. The owners of this dive should hold their heads in shame. The CAA should be sending inspectors to investigate this rip off and totally unsuitable, badly run outfit and revoke their licence until marked improvements are made.

Long Beach Airport is one of the nicest airports to fly in and out of without hassle or delays. However, if you intend to park your car with the Long Beach valet service, don't expect the complimentary car wash to be a car wash. It was the most pathetic car wash I've ever received. A toddler could have hosed it off better. The cost to park was $24 a day. I was gone on a business trip for 24 hours and when I returned I expected a nice clean car. I was wrong. Don't park your car with the valet expecting a decent Car Wash. Thank you.

I fly out of Long Beach airport whenever I can, business and personal travel. My friends and family choose to do the same. I've only had good experiences until today, 8/14 while picking up a friend and her family. The bad experience was related to a Long Beach police officer monitoring vehicles curbside. I was approached by the officer as I was opening up the back of my SUV for loading luggage. He asked me to move my vehicle twice, even after I told him my friend and her family were walking over from the luggage area outside of the airport. His demeanor and tone were aggressive and he didn't care to listen when I said my friend and her family were approaching the vehicle. He raised his voice and came very close, it made me uncomfortable. Fortunately, my friend and her family walked up, greeted me and asked what was going on. The officer just walked away. The officers conduct was unprofessional and not appropriate.

This airport is highly recommended. Many of the reviews below are pre-2012, which is when the facility completed a full upgrade of terminal and gates. I would discard any pre-2012 reviews as "irrelevant" to the current condition. Long Beach Airport is a well-designed and pleasant experience compared with LAX and to a degree John Wayne. It's a smaller but more efficient facility, with competitively priced parking within an easy walk of your gate. The TSA Security Checkpoint is relatively fast compared with other airports. The facility boasts two outdoor seating areas for two of its restaurants, a comparative luxury in this age of airport design being little more than shopping malls with airline gates. The central area between the two terminals is an outdoor seating area allowing for a retreat from the madness at the gates. One of the unique aspects of LGB is the lack of jetways. Walking out onto the tarmac to board a plane is a fun and different experience which adds significantly to the charm of this facility. Long Beach doesn't have the cold and sterile feel of most modern airports, and that is a welcome aspect of flying here. There are a number of restaurant/eating choices available, though the shopping is a relatively weak area. In general, Long Beach is easily my favorite American airport and is qualitatively far better than the vast majority of facilities I use.

As you pull into Long Beach Airport, the parking structure is conveniently located right across from the terminal. Check-in and security screening took less than 10 minutes in the afternoon hours. Long Beach has an open, natural, and airy terminal. You will find palm trees, small birds, and abundance of sunshine on this terminal. There are enough seats for you to sit and relax. Dining options are very good. Free wi-fi also works well. This airport does not use jet bridge, so you will enter and exit the aircraft using stairs or ramp. Baggage claim area is small, but appropriate for an airport with a vintage look.

I fly to LGB twice a year or more to visit family. I really cannot say enough good things about this airport especially after the remodel a couple of years ago. The place is beautiful. It is well laid out, it is small and so very easy to deal with. I fly Jet Blue and it is almost always on time. The restaurants in that terminal are quality and very reasonably priced. This was one of the first airports to provide unlimited free wifi. I love that you can board and leave the plane from both the front and rear. It is so quick. If you have to fly to So Cal this is the place to fly too.

I've always enjoyed flying in and out of Long Beach Airport but this time was a big disappointment. They used to have remote lots for long-term parking at a reasonable price but now those have been shut down. At this point the only option is the short-term parking which is a bit of a walk from the terminal with a cost of $2/hour maxing out at $17/day or $19/day depending on which building you use. That really adds up!

At first I was concerned seeing the long lines at JetBlue's curbside check-in and at the check-in counter on my way to the upstairs restaurant to eat dinner before my flight. Restaurant is good but not cheap but not outrageously priced considering portions and food quality. Was through security with minimal wait less than 10 minutes. No jetways here so you have to walk on the tarmac to board your plane via stairs. Only complaint is terminal building is too small considering the number of people that pass through. Still I would continue to use LGB to avoid LAX every day of the week and twice on Sunday.

This is such a convenient airport. Reminds me of a small mid-west airport where you park close by check in and at the gate so quickly. While not a lot of fancy amenities like the larger international airports this airport is such a breeze.

It is simply an airport and not trying to be a shopping mall or anything else. Very quick passage through the airport if you're only dropping off bags; TSA efficient but thorough; bit of a crowd in the north portakabin as JetBlue DL and AS had simultaneous departures but as you can turn up so close to departure it's not a long wait.
