Restaurant upstairs is good as well though not cheap and it would be good to have more of the balcony given to non-eaters (maybe it's busier midweek than on a Sunday afternoon).

Long Beach is a great little airport. It has the most efficient TSA checkpoint I have ever seen with the longest line ever being about three minutes and I fly through here quite often. While the south concourse is the only gate area I have used I am sure the airport is the same throughout the terminal. The staff is great and friendly and you can chat with everyone. The gate numbering can be a bit confusing but so long as you don't immediately exit the terminal to the left you should be fine. They even give you an umbrella when it rains to walk onto the plane.
❌Not Verified|  Courteous and friendly staff. Flight left early by about 10-15 minutes, when it was confirmed all planning to fly were on board. Crew was great. Seating was great.

Islip to Baltimore with SWA. A hidden gem in the NY area for local flights terminal is clean and spacious with good facilities all round. A much better option than the scrum at JFK or LGA particularly if you are out of the city and have a rental car.

ISP is an excellent alternative to LGA JFK or Newark! I've flown out and in to there at least 10 times and I have never been delayed! The makeover they gave the airport is great too! It would be nice to see ISP expand a little bit with some more airlines going out of there.

While it is beyond the reach of New York City taxis ISP is five minutes away from Ronkonkoma railroad station in turn a 1h20m train ride to Penn Station. This may seem very inconvenient for Newyorkers used to La Guardia airoport but it isn't so bad if compared with JFK. The airport is small and efficient. There are little or no delays on the ground. This field is used primarily by Southwest as its gateway to New York. Southwest partner ATA is another visitor while some legacy carriers only offer regional service to their respective hubs or focus cities. For those passengers who don't like turboprops be advised that Piedmont Airlines operates from this field with DHC8s for Us Airways express while Colgate uses tiny Beechcrafts on flights for Usair express and Continental (I find those tiny planes charming but many passengers complain). Overall a very pleasant passenger oriented airport.

Very nice airport closely situated to New York City and very convenient for all travelling to/from Long Island. Decent selection of shops easy to navigate and not crowded at all when I flew threw both times. Local hub for Southwest airlines.

Just recently MacArthur Airport here in the middle of Long Island recieved a makeover. The makeover included a big new concourse added terminals and new concessions. Its beautiful! It is a big relief to see the airport go from old and small - to new and bigger! The new concourse was built and is now primarily owned by Southwest Airlines! The layout of the airport is very simple and easy to navigate! As soon as you walk in the main entrance you can either make a right to get to the check-in counters or make a left to get to the carousels and pick-up a friend that just arrived. Security is fairly fast. There are a number of concession stands as well as souvenir shops located before & after the security check-point. The following airlines service MacArthur Airport - some of the airlines may use a codeshare partner for some flights. Southwest Airlines Delta Connection Continental Express US Airways express Brand new concourse terminals & concessions!

The addition of the new Southwest wing has been a good improvement for all those who enjoy flying on this airline. Flying out of this airport has been very convenient because of its' location for many Long islanders especially those living in Suffolk and eastern Nassau counties. The one drawback to the Southwest facility expansion is the distance from their new gates to the baggage claims area.

A great airport only one hour from New York City that is still a secret! A major stop for SouthWest it is a welcome relief from the congestion at La Guardia or worse JFK. Nice new buildings with convenient parking for locals or access to a train station with links to all of long island and NYC.

An absolute terrible experience every time I leave and land out of LAX. The roads leading to the airport are two few with the amount of air traffic scheduled so getting there is awful. I live 9 miles south and it’s not uncommon for it to be a 1 hour drive at the drop off or pick up terminal point. The last 3 times I have flown I’ve been delayed an hour due to too many flights scheduled and airplane traffic. I’ve been at the gate for an hour or even away from the gate for an hour. Returning is no better. After arrival you taxi for 30 min and end up off boarding in some remote part of the airport that you need a bus to take you to the terminal. It’s adds another hour just to leave. There are too many flights for the infrastructure in place so it makes for a terrible experience. If departing or landing on time is important to you, LAX will fall short every time. A really terrible experience.
$10 for this rinky dink breakfast sandwich that has one paper thin small piece of ham on it to call it a ham sandwich. This is just highway robbery!

To be a premium passenger at Tom Bradley Terminal is deplorable for 2024. The line for a $12k ticket in business class is always horrible. They need a separate line so passengers can enter and start spending money! You lose so much revenue people standing in a line and not buying food or drinks Or retail. Some things just never change and keep LAX in the bottom of airports on the world.

Arrive at Alaska air terminal and walked to international. Underground tunnels let you skip shuttle bus. These are very narrow, long and drab and you need bag on rollers. Signage is sparse. International terminal very crowded and seems duty free oriented. Food is limited to very expensive fast fare. Enough seating but few places to charge phone. Not a great to spend 5 hours, but I’ve had worse.
As usual gate changed twice necessitating walking between terminals. Happened every time visited this airport. Most restaurants shut down at 9:30pm which means no food on internal flights.

My family had a stopover in LAX a few weeks ago. My elderly father is disabled and also has a cognitive disability. We told a female LAX employee he can't walk on his own. She offered to drive him on her cart but told us we (my mom, my aunt, and I) we couldn't go with him. Then she drove off without telling us where she was going to drop him off. After we went through security, we did not see my father. We started to panic and frantically looked for him for him all over the airport. We asked a few LAX employees where we could possibly find him. They shrugged and acted like they didn't care. None of them got on their phones or walkie-talkies to communicate with each other. We also informed a customer service agent behind a glass booth and told him we couldn't find my father. He was unhelpful and wouldn't go on a public speaker to page my father. After over an hour, we randomly found my father at an Alaska Airlines counter. The airline we were supposed to fly with was Air Canada. LAX, this is unacceptable. You should let family members travel with disabled passengers and train your staff to communicate with each other and with passengers.

It's a few years since we last landed or left LAX and things have changed, for the better. Ahead of the game, LAX has installed new scanners so passengers do not have to remove liquids from their bags, liquid sizes seem to be the same as before. Body scanners are widely used and seem to indicate things in pockets or concealed regularly. On entry and leaving it said there was something in the groin area (something unusual that is) causing me to have a very thorough frisking around that area. A few more shops and refreshment options airside now than before. The Star Alliance lounge for my transit and the One World Lounge coming home are okay. Seating was easy to find and the buffet and drinks were plentiful, if simple.

After enduring the crazy night traffic of LAX, there was a TSA worker who was very rude and disrespectful, causing a verbal spat between a couple and myself with my mother. We were instructed, by another TSA agent, to find any open space for the bins and use it. A couple in front of us obviously didn't know how this TSA worked, and neither did I, in addition, to taking their time and holding up the line. In the mean time, the older women TSA agent wasn't paying attention and was making small talk with the couple. I had already placed items in 2 bins, and stacked another because she wasn't paying attention and her male co-worker was giving my mom (who was unable to move bins because of surgery) instructions to put a heavier suitcase in a bin. The way the luggage line is set up, there is a divider and the TSA agent has to pull the bins from the customer side to allow them to move toward the xray area on their side to create space. I attempted to maneuver the bins and then waited, but there was still no space in front of me, so I took one of the two spaces that the  couple was not using, because the older TSA agent wasn't paying attention. The TSA agent then gets an attitude with me and tells me that I took the white woman's space that was in front of her; but, the woman of the couple had 2 spaces without bins and she was holding up the line and I needed to get to my flight. So I proceeded to tell the TSA agent that I was helping my mother because he coworker was instructing my mother to put items in a new bin and rushing her along and my mother wasn't able because of her arm, and I asked her, since she wasn't moving the bins in front of me to create space, what did she expect me to do, and she stated to "hold it (the bin)!" Really?! I attempted to explain to her that her coworkers instructions and her instructions were conflicting and that I was trying to help my mother. She continued to go back and forth with me. The male coworker was apologetic after we told him of my mother's condition, but the older agent continued to be rude, which caused me to also respond. This could have been resolved if the TSA agent was paying attention and moving the bags along and instructed the female to place her items in one of the spaces and allow me to place my items in the other space. The couple continue to talk about me and the situation and my mother became upset because they were saying I was mean and inconsiderate but that couldn't have been furthest from the truth. The situation only escalated after the couple, along with the TSA agent, continued to be inconsiderate of others trying to make their flights.

I was well on my way to missing my connection flight from Cancun on United to Brisbane via LAX on Qantas. The Cancun delay of 1 hour 30 had changed my connection time to one hour. Usually an impossible task. I was in luck and was travelling using disability services due to a broken foot. The disability services had been arranged for each leg and when I mentioned my predicament the staff were just absolutely amazing. Firstly the lady who name I can’t remember got me through customs and bag pickup in minutes, handed me over to a waiting disability transfer van she had called ahead for. Once in the international terminal a gentleman by the name of Lyn made a personal effort to get me through all the check points radioing ahead to let all staff know he had a passenger whose flight was boarding. Once through all checks he got me on a golf cart and raced me to my gate. Without the tremendous kindness and effort of these staff members I wouldn’t have made it. I made an extra effort to be courteous, kind, thankful and called everybody by name. It’s amazing how far people will go if you are actually thankful and polite. The bus transfer lady and I had a lovely conversation whilst getting between terminals. I’m forever grateful to those individuals. Thank you LAX for giving me the experience I never thought I’d receive.

Not inclusive to folks that need assistanc - I waited over an hour before my flight started to board which they never showed up. If you travel to LAX and need assistance don’t expect help here. I actually hurt myself worse because I could not get a wheelchair

Louisville is actually one of the nicest airports in the United States, pound-for-pound. In fact, Louisville "on steroids" gives you an idea of what more of our true international gateways should look like, but don't (I mean, Detroit and Minneapolis are good, but LAX and JFK?!) I'll start with the good about Louisville: Parking is easy and reasonably priced. So easy, in fact, that it's literally at the back door of the terminal, and nicely covered for all those inclement weather situations. The airport is super clean. The personnel are above-average in friendliness; some of the security and restaurant staff could learn to smile, but it's hard for me to recount any particularly rude experiences with personnel. The terminal is very Louisville- and Kentucky-themed, making the airport an unmistakable part of the state of Kentucky's cultural identity. Security is usually a breeze, even if you don't have TSA Pre-Check (which I have). It's almost immediately next door to the state fairgrounds, 10-12 minutes from downtown, and 15-20 minutes from serene natural areas like Jefferson Memorial Forest. The terminals are straightforward and well-signed. The public art is very local-specific and -themed, and attractively positioned. As a bonus, the airport is UPS' primary North American hub, so it's neat to see the massive cargo planes regularly flying in and out of there. The real drawbacks of flying into and out of Louisville are that baggage claim takes a little longer than it should for a relatively small airport, and you have to pay close attention to signage right as you're driving off the property to access the freeways and fairgrounds. In summary: It's hard to go wrong with flying in and out of Louisville. I've been doing it for years and it just feels almost like putting on a comfortable pair of shoes.

Louisville Airport is a great airport, very clean and improvements being made all of the time. Arrived from Chicago off of the aircraft and by the luggage claim within 10 minutes. Local staff are all very helpful and polite as well as being professional. For some passengers there were some issues with delayed or lost luggage but the American Eagle ground staff were very professional and sorted out their problems quickly.

Departure from Louisville was excellent, the First Class check-in was efficient and fast with great service from the American Eagle ground staff. Security was quick about ten minutes to line up and go through the security, they are using the new body scanners now which improve and speed up the process. The TSA staff as polite and very professional and ensure that your time with them is minimal as well as ensuring standards are kept. After security the Lounge is good with excellent views over the runways & aircraft. Boarding areas are clean and airy with plenty of seating for passengers.

A very pleasant experience both arriving and leaving this airport, the terminal is well designed with some good places to eat and purchase last minute items too.  There is a business lounge which is a great oasis to relax and catch up on business for a $5 fee which offers drinks and food. Baggage collection was fast and was on the
reclaim by the time we had walked from the arrival gate to the reclaim. The customer service and information is very good and professional as is TSA who all appear to go the extra mile to assist passengers departing.

Airport was much better than expected. In the general area are a few food options - incl coffee shop ; ice-cream, bar, and a few fast food choices. They even have a small duty free We were in the TAAG lounge - called the Pearl lounge . Clean, comfortable with basic drinks & food . Staff are very friendly . Did not see showers . Internet is available but weak . Other than internet this lounge is better than many US lounges I have visited . I was expecting something much worse

Looking forward to our holiday in Portugal, we decided to book TAAG as this would be the quickest flight. This is the first time my family and myself have flown using your airline and I can honestly say it will be the last. We departed Johannesburg on Monday the 26th June. We had a short layover in Luanda, whereby the plane should have left at approximately 11pm. Come boarding time, the board read flight boarding, however, we were told by staff that there was no plane for us and we had to wait. The wait took until 2:30am after there being another mess with the boarding pass machine (written boarding passes were made - for what I don’t know as all the info on the written pass was the same as the printed pass. We thought this was a one off problem, however when we returned to SA (18th July) we were met with the same confusion at Luanda Airport. No plane available to accommodate us and another long wait of 4 1/2 hours and not much information was given from TAAG staff. I find this unacceptable. The flights cannot be faulted however the airport and ground staff need a lot of work. If you are booking flights surely planes should be available and not this hash up.

What a horrible airport. First off there's no proper ventilation. It's stuffy as hell. Secondly, I tried to buy a beer at a bar and was told they only accept Master Card not Visa. Then I went to the food court to buy a juice and was told they only accept local cards.  This airport can definitely not be classified as an 'international' airport.

Wanted to go out and explore Luanda. Staff at the airport lied to us and said visa was necessary, kept us busy for an hour with no feedback. General poor communication. No charger ports in the lounge area, not properly cleaned.

I have travelled all over the world including countries of lower economic standards such as Indonesia, India and parts of China. I have never seen such a horrible airport. Came to airport, can’t tell where to go with nobody to help or any signs. Wait through lines to get boarding pass. Then wait at immigration. Immigration decided to take a 1 hour break for which nobody got through. Afterwards they take all your Angolan currency as part of a government regulatory requirement but don’t warn you until there’s only one thing to do, give it to them. Ticket said plane departs 3.15 and I can board 3.30. Screen says board at 4.40 on time. 4 comes and nobody knows anything. People are rude, food should not be called food. I liked Angola more than I thought I would but for this airport dismal would be a understatement.

Luanda Airport: This is hell on earth. An abomination. It's hot with no proper ventilation. It's dirty. It stinks. The staff are not just downright rude, they actively show their disrespect for travelers in every possible way. They are wholly incompetent and disorganised. They dont inform anyone of what is happening, they merely bark or shout orders at you as if they are herding slaves onto a ship destined for hell. There is no kindness, grace towards - or understanding of - the weary traveller's plight. They charge exorbitant prices for no choice of food or drink. You can't even buy, at a high price, a bottle of water anywhere. I will be writing to more authorities about this. And the airline TAAG will lose custom because surely anyone who savours their sanity will do everything in their power never to have to spend another minute in Luanda Airport. Shame, shame, shame on you, Angola. Your main port and transit point is so atrocious, one can only wonder at how awful a visit to your country must be. As a gateway, your airport should be the example you want the world to see. How utterly lamentable that you should allow this despicable place to continue operating at all. Absolute hell.

One of the worst airports in the world. People cutting the line, no control from the staff. On the way out, there were people just going through the "nationals" line, since there's no control. Lines for immigration on arrival and departure, take over one hour. Also for security check on departure, another hour, in the evening. Toilets are dirty, air-conditioning does not cope with amount of people, staff are rude and often do not understand English.

Although shabby and expensive, I have to give credit where credit where it's due. While waiting to board my flight, I was asked for my boarding pass, then told that my suitcase had broken open and that I was to go with them to verify that my belongings were all there! I followed the man into the bowels of the airport, to find that the suitcase was not mine. It belonged to someone from Sao Tome. Our luggage numbers were similar. Thanks anyway Luanda Airport, Obrigada para a sua atencao!

I flew TAAG Airlines from Johannesburg to Lisbon via Luanda. Arriving at Luanda Airport the luggage scanner was out of order therefore all luggage was opened by hand which made people impatient and moody as this was early in the morning. On my visit to the Ladies toilets I was met with dirty floors, no toilet paper, no soap in the soap holders, no paper towels cubicle door was stuck with old, yellow masking tape, only one water basin tap working, cubicle door handle broken off, toilet seat missing. Just the most awful toilets! I went looking for the janitor and I asked a young girl dressed with a cleaner uniform if she knew who was the responsible cleaner which she replied that she was the cleaner for the cafe and didn't know who the responsible janitor for the toilets was. I then went looking for the janitor or a security guard and there was one in sight so I returned to the Ladies toilet to find the cleaning lady spraying toilet spray in the air and making the floor wetter and stickier. I politely asked her to get me some toilet paper and hand soap which she rudely stormed off sighing. On her return she placed the toilet roll on the basin and walked out. I then returned to the corridor seat to wait for our delayed plane, there are very few seats and I noticed a young family sitting on the floor with their child sleeping on their lap (these were overseas tourists). I also happen to notice a Cleaning Service employee with a ladder and a cloth in his hand he put his ladder next to the widow and with a dirty cloth proceeded to wipe the window and after 2 wipes he left without the ladder and was never seen again. The air conditioners filters are so dirty that is the reason why they not functioning properly. When finally we were asked to board go down to Gate 4 (the one and only gate) they then realized that the Botswana flight was to go down first before our flight and they had made a mistake. Now the ill and elderly people had to climb up the staircase as there is only one escalator and its going downwards. To date we still don't know the reason why there was a 3 hours delay. There is definitely a lack of communication and professionalism within the staff. Finally I got to sit on the plane (TAAG) where the seat was soiled with old food and a cockroach walking across it, the lady seated next to me was ready to jump when she saw it.  In this day and age I can't see why Luanda Airport needs to be so inferior when they are such a wealthy country? They should invest in training staff and getting supervisors to watch over their outside contractors, if not they might as well not function at all.

The worst airport I've ever seen. Everything is expensive (as is in Luanda). The only place with air conditioner is the duty free shop. Not many things to do. Bathrooms are awful smelly. But the worst thing about the airport is that all of TAAG's flights board through the same gate (number 4). So there you are, crammed in the boarding area with passengers of 2 or 3 other flights, waiting to go to the bus that takes you to the plane. No Wi Fi that worked. In every flight we saw boarding there there was at least one passenger that didn't make it in each flight. So there was this weird constant scene of people shouting that they were not late and that it was the airports personnel fault.

One of the smallest airports I've ever encountered. Due to required visas for Laos, there was a bit of a hold up at immigration but staff were thorough. Luggage made it off the aircraft in an efficient manner so waiting times were minimal. The whole arrivals area was so compact, you could see the baggage hall from immigration and visa versa. Interesting as the chaotic arrivals hall had all doors continually open and once you left the baggage collection area, you could easily go back. Our arrival was an evening one so most retail outlets were closed and, inconveniently, also the money exchange. Not a bad little airport, but renovation and refurbishment needed.

Everyone working at the ground services at LPB airport gave us excellent service. We somehow missed that we could not board Laos Airline flight to Vietnam without proper documents. We had read we could get on arrival visas in Vietnam. A staff member helped us considerably, instructing and helping us get emergency visas. I think we might have missed our flight if it was not for her. Just wanted to acknowledge her excellent service.

I had a problem with the immigration. I somehow missed the immigration check after my evening flight from Hanoi to Luang Prabang, my responsibility of not having checked if I had a stamp. The next day I went back and they charged me 100$ on top of what I already paid, made me sign a paper written in Laos, not a copy or a picture I was able to take after I asked. I paid as there were no other option. They were not nasty but not kind, they kept telling me it's my fault for not checking. No sharing the responsibility or acknowledged that they might have not done a proper job on their hands. So check your stamps before you leave (there are 2 different separate lines to do: one for the visa the other for the immigration stamp) and be aware that they can play the game they want. At the end all is good you pay and you have your passport back with a big smile from their side.

Appalling rip off of 36$ (35$ posted on notice board then an extra 1$ inexplicably demanded) for visa was expected but nevertheless galling. Welcome to Laos, give us some money for no good reason, and if you’re Canadian it’s 40$! Who knows why. Taxi drivers are raking in the cash. You pay 6$ for a taxi ticket into town. Then it turns out you are in a minibus with 6 other travelers. This means the driver is making 42$ for a 20 minute ride into town. That’s a fortune in Laos. Appalling.

Absolutely terrible. 3 very long queues for immigration on arrival (deposit passport for visa, collect passport with visa and actual immigration). Took us roughly an hour, lots of empty, unmanned booths. Terribly organised. Upon leaving we waited approximately 30 minutes. We were told to change queues by staff and once we got to the front we were told to change again which meant starting at the back of the queue. Which was very long. Lots of people missing flights. Terribly organised and understaffed. Why are we paying all this money to immigration for visas if they are not hiring enough staff? An embarrassment to the country. An otherwise lovely trip scarred by the shambles that is Laos immigration.

Luang Prabang Airport arrival was late at night, so almost everything was closed. It was a little hectic, with long lines, probably because I was arriving on a larger international flight and everyone, self included, were queueing for visa on arrival. It was fine once I stood around, very informal. No one is pleasant or unpleasant. The taxi stand drivers did rip me off, but only by $2 (it's a set fare, which I didn't know). Leaving from Luang Prabang was lovely. I arrived about two hours in advance. Check in and security was a breeze. It was about noon, and everyone was friendly. I was glad to have a glass of wine in the bar and some excellent lunch, surprisingly good honestly, and the WiFi worked too. I even did a bit of shopping in the small stalls since amazingly, the prices were not all that marked up compared to other parts of Laos (I was there long enough to get a good sense of "real" prices). They even had a small bookstore, and I got tons of cheap snacks, and some duty free Lao Lao to bring home. Everything about this airport, while not the cleanest in the world, or with the greatest signage, was easy and fine. I liked it overall very much. It was self-explanatory.

Luang Prabang International is a small and pleasant airport with a decent selection of amenities and relatively good service. Upon arrival in Luang Prabang, immigration officials will direct you to the relevant desks for passport checks (if you don't need a visa you will be directed straight to the passport control desks). The airport has a money changer located right outside the arrivals/departures area where the US dollar rate is relatively similar to the rates quoted in town. There is a desk to order a taxi for 50000 kip per person, or if you prefer a cheaper ride, you can try to hail a tuk-tuk from outside the terminal. Check-in was very quick on my flight departing Luang Prabang, and I cleared the immigration check within 5 minutes as my SilkAir flight had few passengers. Inside the airport there are some shops selling local crafts and duty free outlets, though they weren't very interesting. Anyone who's flying Bangkok Airways will be pleased to not that they have a waiting lounge in this airport. There was plenty of seating in the gate areas and boarding of my flight was very efficient. All in all, this is a good airport to use - if you ever have a chance to use it and if your flight isn't full.

Not a good impression on entering Laos through Luang Prabang airport. On the flight you are given some forms. You queue in the visa on arrival line, then you are told you should get another form from a desk in a corner, with no information. You queue again in the visa on arrival. You pay inflated prices in Thai Baht unless you happen to carry dollars. Then you queue again in another line with the first form you completed, which has same info as second. Staff were grumpy. Feels very bureaucratic.

Arrivals worked well with friendly staff, quick bags, and an efficient visa on arrival system. My flight was lightly loaded but there might be a significant delay with a full flight. Departures were a little unusual. Check in, emigration and security all worked well but the airside facilities are a little unusual. The departure lounge is on two levels, the lower level has a small cafe with limited food options and two small duty free shops. Upstairs there are a number of shops selling tourist gifts plus a large outlet on a third level which has most of the items you find in Luang Prabang's night market but not at the same price. When I visited there were no catering facilities in the upper lounge but there was a massage parlour with six passengers all having a foot massage! I would have been happy with this small airport whose terminal is a couple of years old but for the fact that some 42 bags were not loaded on my Vietnam Air flight to Hanoi due to a "Technical Problem". I don't know whether this was the fault of the airline or the airport.

A very small airport, ours was the only plane there when we landed, so visa, immigration and luggage was quick, though I doubt if they could manage with more than one plane at once. Departure, check in quick and efficient. The airport is clean with a number of duty free shops (bit tacky).

The staff are helpful and the airport is so user friendly. I accidently dropped my Aadhaar card somewhere maybe in the flight or the airport without me knowing. They found it and gave it to me in the shuttle bus. They saved me so much trouble.

There is no jet bridge at Lucknow airport, so you have walk down the stairs from the aircraft and board a bus. Overall, the airport is very small so there isn't much walking to do. During my return flight, I arrived at Lucknow airport 3 hours before departure (standard practice at many US airports). I was told to sit in a waiting area and check-in 2 hours before departure. Check-in bags are screened before you visit the check-in counter. Once you clear security, the boarding area is small with limited seating.

Travelled into and out of here on a LCY-ZRH-LUG long weekender last summer and look forward to doing the same again this year. Incoming as smooth as expected outgoing return complicated by a fault on the outbound plane - but didn't miss my London connection as a result and the small but civilised departure area (think those few Ryanair routes that involve local airports that aren't hastily assembled wooden shacks) offered a well-stocked duty free shop and a sporadically manned bar. Shops/bars available outside the airport for departing passengers and accompanying friends and family - no problem with one final Swiss beer before checking in at short notice. All in all a very pleasant experience.

Lugano-Agno is a little airport (maybe the smallest in Switzerland) but I think it's the most efficient. It's commercial says: "You'll be in the air in 20 minutes" and it's the truth. I think it's a great airport.

Arrived and departed from Lugano Airport last week. It surely is one of the smallest airports I have ever seen. Passport control is extremely fast baggage reclaim too. (SWISS does not yet recognize priority labeling from other Star Alliance members.) Regular shuttle service to and from Lugano city centre is timed to match arrivals and departures from and to Zurich. There are a few shops and restaurants outside the airport. Check-in on departure is very swift too. The staff are highly motivated and efficient. They managed to have our luggage checked through to final destination although our onward flight from Zurich was not booked under the same reservation code. (Yet again no priority labels.) You then go through security control and are in the waiting area about five minutes after entering the terminal building. Only downside there is not much you can do after passing through the security control. But then it is only minutes from arriving in the departure area to boarding.

Incredibly poor and unsafe customer service: In the departure hall at the gates I cannot find hand sanitizer anywhere! They have bottles of it standing at each gate, but behind glass and only for staff use.

Small but good airport. I visited it two weeks ago and I found it to be clean. It's true that there not many people - principally fligths of SAS and Norwegian - but I liked it, especially the "after control" zone, where two bar/restaurants. The check-in zone is clean and well organized with an active information point. Positive general impression from this airport.

For international flights Lusaka now has a brand new airport and it is considerably better than the old airport which is now only used for domestic flights. The new airport is spacious and currently clean and well maintained and well ventilated. Check in is usually quite speedy. Airside there are a few shops and cafes and currently a basic lounge though another is opening soon. My only criticism is limited use of the airbridges but I was told that the airlines need to have a correct tow bar which some have and some do not hence some planes parking and passengers walking to/from the terminal. In rains you can be bussed. Lots of immigration officers means it is quite quick to enter Zambia now.

Small airport with helpful staff. In the arrivals hall there is nothing special. On departure you can enjoy your time on the 1st floor snacks bar with some good choices. The view to the apron is good from the departure hall. The only negative side is that the air conditioning system is not good at all.

We passed through LUN briefly on two occasions in September and found it to be a pleasant small airport with a couple of interesting features. The first one was that when disembarking from a domestic flight one is led into the terminal building but the door to the main terminal is always closed so the person leading you has to knock on an adjacent partition wall to get someone's attention to come and open the door. We thought that was cute. The second feature was the presence of a coffee/cappuccino wagon in the terminal area dispensing a variety of freshly brewed coffees as well as freshly squeezed orange juice. We thought that was a very civilized touch and considering there didn't appear to be any restaurants or cafes available (that we could see) at least that simple option was appreciated.

I have recently been in Lusaka. The airport is old but clean. The departure lounge is quite big but it lacks more restaurants and more tax and duty free shops. It would be advantageous to change this situation. The immigrations officers are polite and easy-going which is a further plus.

In the last 2 years Lusaka International Airport has been going through a re development programme which has seen an upgrade in its infrastructure. The old 70' style check in counters have been replaced and updated. The airport has received new ground handling equipment escalators and lifts. Having been invited on a press tour of the facility i got to see first hand what is happening. The airport is very clean cleaner than some more 'developed' airports I have seen in my travels.

Considering this is an airport in a poor African country Lusaka Int'l Airport isn't that bad. The arrival hall is rather small en dark but it is possible to leave the airport only 20 minutes after landing. The immigration officers ( I've only seen female ones ) are kind and easy going and I can say the same about the airport staff in general. The sanitary provisions are old but clean. The departing hall is more modern ( from the late '70s ? ) and there is more space and light. There's one bar and one shop. Just be aware of some huge leaks in the roof during rainshowers : at some places mini-waterfalls come into being.

Horrible airport! Almost no seating available. If you want to sit, you have to sit at a restaurant and that means you’re required to buy overpriced junkfood. Airport staff is almost invisible. Was traveling with my family, but a staggering lack of facilities for baby care. I had to do some work on my laptop but there was nowhere to do that. The gate was old, did not show accurate information and also didn’t have enough seats. In one word: appalling. Never using this airport again.

We had a really good experience at Luton. Started well with the official meet & greet parking in Car Park 1 -- this is clearly signposted and we were met by a very pleasant and helpful gent ... quite a contrast with our rather dismal Heathrow experience in May. It was a short walk to bag drop in the terminal, which was also done quickly, and on to security. This was a real stand-out, with short queues and friendly staff. No need to remove liquids, computers, and so on, and they do a full-body scan for everyone that saves the palaver of being 'beeped' by a standard gate and going for the full scan. My bag was selected for extra checking that was swift and polite. It took about 30 minutes from car park to airside, where we found plenty of decent options for breakfast. All in all, a very positive start to our holiday.

I had a bad feeling as we queued for the temporary drop off zone at Luton airport as I had heard horror stories of this airport in the past, but I went into the journey with an open mind. We flew out with Ryanair and check in was an absolute breeze with no hold ups at all. Security was very busy but we had FastTrack purchased and cleared the lanes within a few moments, the staff were very friendly and helpful to us as we passed and even were open for a laugh. The departures area can feel a little claustrophobic with low ceilings till you reach the main area. There is good choice of F&B as you pass through with a nice selection of shops to spend some money. Seating is decent as well outside the F&B areas so there is space to take a load off. I spotted a nasty spillage on the floor and spoke to a cleaner who told me she would attend to it straight away. The gate are for Ryanair and Wizz was a little cramped down the corridor with limited space but if you time it right you won't be there long. Overall a very surprising experience at LTN and one I didn't expect
Giving up on Luton. Parking is so ridiculously expensive, we’re picking Gatwick or LHR from now on. All good other than that so not much else to say.

Luton Airport always used to be a joke and it still is as far as queue management is concerned! As you approach Security old, young and infirm are forced to walk up and down unnecessarily for miles between taped barriers, even when there is hardly anyone waiting to go through Security! Staff, with ironically "I'm here to help" yellow tee-shirts stand aimlessly around and rather than helpfully opening and closing the queuing lanes (as demand dictates), their job seems limited to shouting at anyone who has the temerity to duck under a barrier (even when there is no-one in front of them)! When challenged one of the staff unhelpfully stated "if you don't like it you can buy "Fast Track" i.e. pay more to avoid walking needlessly backwards and forwards - clearly this is the managements intention to make life difficult for most passengers! Awful customer service - come on Luton Airport, time to up your game!

Horrible filthy airport with vile rude staff. Special assistance is virtually non existent, I cannot express enough how rude the staff are, its clearly allowed and the organisational culture of Luton must be very very toxic.

Arriving on a cold wet after Midnight flight I was delighted to see a shuttle bus to take us to the pick up in the Mid stay car park. So we sat on the coach and after about 15 minutes we moved off. Down the road about 300 yards it stopped at what I assumed were red traffic lights on the main road -no that was the end of the journey. We then had to haul ourselves and luggage up the hill into the car park. This was made worst by the pick up point being located at the far righthand corner. What a waste of time. Whilst operational difficulties due to the fire are understood, the arrangements are very poor.

What an absolute shambles is taxi drop off and pick up. They are now at the mid-term car park where one is PROMISED a shuttle bus that doesn't come. On Wednesday the 21st of February at 10 pm, there was a queue of people waiting for the bus. It simply didn't come. I had to make it by foot (a good 15 min walk if not more) with a toddler and luggage to where our taxi was waiting. The whole arrangement is chaotic and confusing. The whole thing is in disarray. Same story when we arrived at the airport, but it was raining so we had the privilege to walk to the terminal on the rain, suitcase, children and adults got soaked in the process. I bet the CEO of the airport doesn't get to experience this. What a mess this is. I would give them 0 stars if I could.

The worst of the London Airports by far. I have used this place for some 40 YEARS now, and all it's done is take one step back for every step forward. They save money at the expense of the traveller by simply putting too few staff on Departure checks and even at 6.30am on a late October morning they only had a handful of overworked checkers (and MANY empty booths) yet a long, LONG line of travellers getting more and more anxious as the time frittered away. ON top of that they have progressively expanded the ridiculous farce of making every one waste time by being "FORCED" to go through a serpentine 'retail experience' with no chance of any short cut. It may be the easiest for us to get to, but in future I will travel the extra miles to Stansted - and I recommend others in East Anglia to do the same! A Cheap and NOT Cheerful Airport to use. Be warned!

I got to the airport two and a half hours before my flight was due and joined a queue to check in (as I couldn't do it on line) and put baggage in hold, after queuing for nearly an hour because there were not enough desks open, was told to go to help desk (definitely not helpful) to pay £42 each to check in, then go back to the first check in and get boarding passes. Then had to take luggage to yet another area as it was a large case, so yet another queue! Then it was on to security and that was another massive queue, where nobody new what the other was doing and due to the time we had to spend there the gate for our flight was closed and we were unable to fly. When asked for help was told we would have to buy another ticket for a flight that wasn't for another 12 hours and go through it all again.  The staff in every department, from security, airline, help desk and Airport are all agency staff and they don't want to take responsibility for anything. Over £600 on Flights, Luggage, Parking and Transport to and from Airport and I never got to leave the country. I beg anyone reading this, do not use Wizz Air or Luton Airport as they are unfriendly, unhelpful and unprofessional.

Awful experience. Lufthansa informed me that my luggage was at the airport, however none of the personnel had the capacity or the patience to locate it, especially the lost and found service that they could not complete their job since they were supposed to leave at 2200 (Lufthansa informed me that the luggage was as the airport at 21.38), despite my pleading and informing them that I had important stuff such as some pills.

This Airport (if you can call it an Airport) is the worst place i have ever been and it gets worse every time. Unorganized, crowded, expensive, filthy, no food, no service. Avoid this place at all cost!

The security team at this airport is rude, inefficient and unfriendly. You'll always have problems. You can be totally ok (same bags and clothes) at other airports yet in Luxembourg they will find something. The security staff is rude and speaks with travellers in a non respectful way.

Shockingly poor airport. Checking border passes on a screen visible to the public (security and GDPR breach). No border police at border checks until after the queue has stretched well into the duty free and pilots were delayed. Eventually one police officer appeared, their e-Gates remained closed.

We were very unsatisfied with our transit experience at Luxembourg airport. To just change the gate (make a transit) you need to leave the airport and go through all the security again. So if your connection is less than 2 hour, I would think really carefully about choosing Luxembourg airport as a transit. Employees are very slow, huge unorganized queues everywhere, no staff available to ask questions. The queue at the security check is especially annoying, the plastic bags for liquids are not provided in advance, they are given right near the machine, which makes the security control x10longer. We were very hungry and wanted to have lunch in the boarding area (were all the gates) and its the first time I see an airport without any restaurants with proper hot food, only sandwiches and chips available, take it or leave it.

Whole airport poorly organised. Queues for both check in and security were huge. We arrived 2 hours before our flight and were still in the queue for security 30 minutes before take off. We had to get called forward to skip some of the queue or we would have missed our flight and this was the same for a lot of people. Clearly can’t hire enough staff however they could hire two men on stilts to dance for a very bored and frustrated crowd. Ridiculous! Also the only food place when we eventually got through to the gate refused to serve us saying they were closed?!

Terrible security experience! I'm a frequent flyer and this is my first bad review ever but I need to share. I had a new ziplock 1l bag bought especially for this trip, all my liquids were there. The woman then told me it's not 1l even though it clearly was and told me to throw away half of my stuff including medicine 10ml (!) and a stick deodorant. She didn't listen to me, I calmly explained that this is not a liquid and I flew with it in different EU countries with zero problems. She arrogantly stated that 'in Luxembourg it is a liquid' but she had no clue what that was.  I wish I asked for her credentials. Avoid her at any cost, she will ruin your experience. I want to add that my friend had the exact same bag and products and a different guy had zero complaints about it. Plus the airport has no smoking area.

Nice design and spacious. However thats where the good news stop. Security totally outdated and badly organized despite high staff number. Outdated scanners, no body scanner no scanners for liquids; outdated tray management. Constant showing of ID needed, no automated gates Wifi is crap and almost instantly saturated. All in all not the most pleasant experience in fact a bit outdated. Shame for a country which wants to be one of progress and innovation

We are currently at the Luxembourg Airport, flying with three kids and are not allowed to enter the waiting room for the departure gate as it is "too full" - although you are able to see that there are still seats left. So, the kids have no access to seating, rest rooms or beverages / food. The security / police let certain passengers pass but is denying access to all other passengers. No information at all, no signs, no info, no spoken info. Nothing.

So painful to go through this airport, every single thing took long queues and waiting time. From the counters to check in and most importantly the border control with few people having to check luggage of hundreds of passengers. In summary, not a nice experience.

Weak and inconsistent security. Bell’s restaurant & cafe no prices on display. After persistently asking the “manager” the shop assistant eventually grudgingly produced the menu prices (pic) from behind the counter. Rude and unhelpful

I recently travelled through the airport to London on MS0761. Although better, I would still describe security as a farce with some people able to go to and fro at will, even if they do work in security. But the main problem is the number of checks and the (lack of) efficiency with which they are carried out. You get checked on entry, but staff seem to be able to walk in a side door un-checked. At least I could see no sign of any checks being carried out when I looked down the corridor. Once upstairs, you go through another check once your flight is nearer time. Two operators manned the walk-through door, but had to hold people back since many of those already through were standing just inside, awaiting their hand-luggage - a much longer conveyor is needed after the scanner. There was one operator manning the screen and also carrying out searches if he saw anything in people's hand-luggage. While he was doing a search, the queue just stood still since no more scans could be conducted. I admit, the passengers did not help - they seem to think 1.5L bottles of water will get through unnoticed. Another staff member would speed things up, but the longer conveyor is needed. My camera bag was searched and 6 x AA batteries removed. I was told 'Batteries not Allowed' These 6 batteries have been in the case for the last 4 visits to Luxor. Ignored were the batteries in torches, spare camera batteries and the battery in my camera. When did this change in the rules come about? Or did the guard just need batteries for his torch? Then you get a hand-swab, then to get into the gate you undergo another hand-luggage check to make sure laptops, pads, cameras etc. work. On the way out I used Edinburgh and London airports - there was only one security check to be negotiated in each. Maybe security staff should be sent to other airports abroad to see how it can be done? Our plane took off nearly an hour late. I have no idea if there was a technical issue, or it was late arriving, but even if all had been perfect, the queue would not have been processed in time, anyway, so it would have been delayed. If Luxor Airport wants to have any reputation other than 'It's a joke', could I suggest that a serious look at security is required before Luxor Airport can consider matching normal international standards.

Why is it that the customs officers in the arrivals hall are still targeting older people and lone women travellers and asking them to open their luggage. They have even asked people to open wrapped Christmas presents. What are they looking for when the bags have been checked at London Heathrow and Gatwick airports with the most sophisticated equipment on the planet. The security forces would be better employed guarding the planes due to leave to make sure nothing dangerous is put on board.

Arrived at the airport from Gatwick. Was pestered by touts selling visas. Went to the visa / bank kiosk and got the visa there. Queued at the passport control for it stamping. then went to collect the baggage. They are supposed to be random baggage checks but the customs men singled out the most vulnerable to look in their cases. By that I mean the elderly and women travelling alone. They take all your carefully packed stuff out then leave you to put it back. They are rude.

We flew into and out of Luxor as international passengers. Landing at the airport all flights are transferred to the terminal building by bus. Once stepping inside the terminal it is possible by get a visa at any of the banks before going to passport control where the visa is check and landing card (as previously issued and filled in on the plane) is taken. Immediately after this there is a staff member who checks your visa has been stamped. Never ceases to amaze the level of irrelevant check. From here to baggage collection/ customs and then out to face the scrum of touts. They seem to be keener as there are far few flights. The return trips was much the same but in reverse. Touts scanning checking/ bag drop exit card (given at checking and need filling) in before getting to passport control. The lounge is quite large with four duty free shops one on each corner and in the centre a gloriously named 'food court' with quite a poor offering of food but expensive. To the gate. No announcements but numerous displays on screens but very slow security checks. As to why with 10 staff they didn't open a second channel to deal with hit is beyond me. Not many people there only three international fights listed for departure that day. Previously used the same airport many years ago and it is a vast improvement on what it was. One really good thing is the authorities seem to have got rid of the toilet touts so more selling loo roll and trying to extort baksheesh.

Arrived at 3pm for a 6pm flight. Long queue for security (just as you walk in the door - before check in). I accidentally left more than 100ml liquids and my laptop in my bag but they didn't detect it in the chaos. My wife's belt set off the security metal detector alarm but the security staff were busy looking elsewhere in the chaos and didn't notice. Check in lines were another long wait. Passport control only had 2 staff on so another 20 min wait there. My son wasn't visible to the passport control officer but that didn't stop his passport being stamped by an officer clearly in a hurry. The policeman/officer who checks that you have a passport stamp before moving to the next stage couldn't find my stamp but the queue was so long he just waved us through not checking any of our 4 passports. There are more (duplicated) security checks to get to the gates but this was equally lax and might as well not have been there. The fellow supposed to be watching the xray screen was talking to his mates. We had 15 minutes to rest at the gate before boarding. It looked like a modern airport but in the chaos and queues we didn't get to see it. Tip: get there early expect chaos and with that in mind you can't be disappointed.

The airport building is much better maintained than Cairo with shops and cafe. However like Cairo there are very bad touts particularly on the forecourt. I haven't experienced the ones at check in as others have but this may be because of my flight time. Domestic check in is extremely chaotic and disorganised for departures with conflicting information. Arrivals (international) is similarly chaotic for people who have no organised visas in advance with long poorly organised queues for both visas and immigration (both with a shortage of workers). I recommend international visitors get a visa in advance as this will save a lot of frustration at Luxor as arrival is very disorientating with guides touts and unhelpful staff giving conflicting information. Beware the taxi touts outside and be sure to have small denomination notes upon arrival for a bus into town.

We used Luxor airport both for internal flight to Cairo and international flight to UK. On both occasions it was clean and airy with plenty of space to sit. We were allowed to take our water with us so no problem in buying drinks. Yes there was someone 'selling' us toilet paper despite the notices saying this was not allowed but by then we knew their standard of living and if you can't spare the odd pound when we have spent so much on a holiday what does that say about us? We were protected from harassment by 'helpers' by our rep. Altogether I thought using Luxor airport a pleasant experience

When we arrived at Luxor airport & got off the coach all I can say was what appeared like a pack of wolves were waiting to 'help' with bags. Now I'm a 6ft 17.5 stone bloke so am well capable but even despite this I ended up almost having to wrestle my bag away from a very eager 'helper' who all the time was whispering under his breath "drink please" interspersed with "something". It appeared as if there was a supervisor or someone that they didn't want to hear their 'requests' - if so - they were spectacularly unsuccessful in stamping out this sort of over-aggressive 'help'. Having managed to wrestle free of the initial wave of 'helpers' & get inside the building once again there was another 'helper' to lift bags onto the x-ray belt. This time however as he didn't have any English phrases apparently the 'helper' was saying something in Egyptian (again whispering) while showing me an Egyptian 10 Pound note folded in the palm of his hand as a 'prompt.' Having now managed to get through these 2 levels of 'assistance' there was of course another 'helper' at the other end of the x-ray machine who was equally 'helpful' in taking the bag off the belt & similarly looking for money! Next up was the check-in desk itself & yes - you have guessed it - there was yet another 'helper' at the head of the queue to again lift the bag onto the check-in conveyor. There is a sign on display at the desk stating that all baggage 'assistance' was free of charge but this was clearly not having any effect on the various 'helpers' that have to be negotiated/overcome. Finally - naturally there is the customary 'help' in the toilets where even though I am at 46 yrs of age well capable of washing & drying my hands I was presented with some toilet paper with the by now customary demand for money. All in all - never again!

I would agree with the above comments. The only smoking areas are the restaurants where you are obliged to buy at least 1 beverage and at £E17 for a really rough coffee we felt a bit ripped off. They were also charging £E13 for a kids lollypop which would cost 25p in the UK. On check in there was a guy lifting hand luggage onto the X-ray machine (you had no choice in this) then getting stroppy because all I had was a £E10 - the equivalent of £1 Sterling for 2 seconds work!

Spotlessly clean airport! Fantastic cakes in departure! Travelling to and from Kiev for Champions League final from Liverpool via Venice and Lviv. Very smooth transit through Lviv Airport both ways. Cakes were more memorable than the game unfortunately.

Lviv airport, modernized for the 2012 Euro football championship is a modern airport with all the european standards of comfort, security and ergonomy. Staff are very attentive to passengers needs, especially at the security and passport checks. It seems a bit cold anyway, with very large spaces empty of everything, and terribly lacks of lounge services such as cafe or bars once you pass the security check, especially for the domestic flights. Well served by local transport, it is very close to the city, and even a taxi ride won't be expensive. A good point in this airport is that you won't be glued by a patch of taxi drivers upon arrival like in Boryspil or many Ukrainian airports.

Very modern terminal, which is a lot better then the old one. It is spacious and clean. There are a few cafe's, my favourite one is the "Ciao!" which offers lots of tasty food, snacks, deserts and coffee. Going through the passport and security check doesn't take much time. The Airport has 2x Business Lounges one for national and one for international flights. There is also free wifi which is really fast and available throughout the whole airport area. The staff there are very friendly and ready to help you.

Flew WAW-LWO-WAW last week. The airport is very big and airy and clean. No problems going through passport control either way and no issues with security. The airport is quite empty but it has a duty free section some places to drink a coffee or have something to eat both inside and outside the departures so quite satisfactory. With the huge fall of the Hryvnia the prices in the coffee shop are reasonable the gift shop (Baltona) is not a bargain as they quote in Euro. Travelling to the city is about 80 Hryvnia by taxi which is now about 3 Euro. There is free wifi that worked fine for me. I would not hesitate to fly through Lviv again.
Once again I used Lviv Airport four times in August 2014. Very satisfied with facilities and staff who work there. Definitely beats many USA airport who have a lot to do in order to improve.

Very modern terminal which improved a lot since last year and is far more superior that some airports in Europe. Air bridges free Wi-Fi and excellent staff customer service. I certainly recommend Lviv airport and definitely would fly there again.

The new terminal is very spacious and it was apparent they were putting in additional shops and services but was under construction when we departed. Very clean and modern. One thing I miss about the old terminal is that it was right on the end of the electric tram line. So you could walk out of the airport to a tram and pay about 2 dollars for a ride into the city. You can still get to the tram but it's an awkward walk. You have to walk about 15 minutes to reach it. Also the kantor/currency exchange was outside of security so after we had gone through passport control I couldn't exchange money. So hopefully they'll fix that. There was free internet near a cafe but couldn't easily find power. So most people had to run off of battery. There was a nice hotel we had used in the past (affordable and clean) but it was closed for renovation. Hope they don't raise the prices upon reopening. They really jazzed up the airport and city for the world cup.

Extended and refurbished runway is so much improved. New Terminal building constructed for Euro Cup 2012 is really nice and well designed. With lots of space very clean and spacious. When I arrived on the flight from Warsaw we were coached to the international arrivals where all 80 or 90 of us cleared passport control in under 10 minutes. Baggage was on a belt also in about 10 min after we disembarked. It was a pleasure to use such a lovely little airport and o much improved.

A brand new airport which is large and spacious but lacking in facilities. Our gate was in an area where there is no catering and no access to a part of the airside where we could even get a coffee. Staff are not all that friendly here but it seems to be efficient with little queuing (though not all the many flights either).

The new airport is a large airy and often empty building. Flew to KBP and connected to RIX on Friday morning and we were the only flight for 4 hours. Although there was no other plane at the airport instead of parking the VV ATR 72 by the gate they parked it over at the far side of the old terminal necessitating a long and completely unnecessary bus ride. Check in was quick and so was security. There was a small cafe after domestic security and nothing else. Oddly the signs pointing to domestic gates didn't match the number of the gate shown for our flight. Looking to the terminal from the front domestic gates are to right international in middle. A cab to the airport was about 20 minutes at 8.15. If you take the trolley bus I think it drops you at the old terminal so you'll have a walk of a couple blocks.

The staff at this airport were rude, unhelpful and uninformed. Both security and passport control were extremely slow. We arrived 2 hours 20mins before departure (would have been earlier but the signage to get back to car hire drop off was poor/confusing) and still nearly missed our flight. Security was a shambles, badly laid out with bottlenecks that slowed the process down. Passport control was obviously understaffed with just 2 desks open. There was a large queue downstairs to get to an escalator that took you upstairs to the passport control hall where there was another large queue. Passengers were being held downstairs to prevent overcrowding upstairs. Our gate had already been announced by the time we cleared security so we went straight to the back of this first queue. We were still in this first queue when our flight status moved from “boarding” to “closing”. When we asked the staff holding the queue in place what we should do we were met with shrugs and a “what do you want us to do about it/we don’t care?” attitude. Worried about missing our flight, we found a lift that bypassed the first queue and got up to the passport control hall where one of the desks was being used to “fast-track” certain flights. We made the flight, and had to wait for other held up passengers, so the flight was delayed. The BA crew were great and apologetic even though the situation was beyond their control. It sounded like parr for the course for Lyon. I’m surprised BA and other airlines put up with such a terrible airport that treats their customers appealingly…
Staff working on security incredibly rude! Threw my bag towards me. I think it was intentional! There was confusion around the taking out of liquids (not required on outward journey).

A beautifully decorated small airport located near the city of Lyon, France. This airport is not too large but it has all international facilities available. Very neat and clean. Luggage collection was faster. However there are very few chair to sit on for waiting. Taxis are available.

This was our first time travelling to Lyon rather than to Geneva and I wouldn’t so so again. Took over an hour to get through passport control on arrival as only two people checking passports. On our return journey home the queue for check in with Easy jet was horrendous and very badly organised. We paid to fast track security as the queues were so long and then queued for one and a half hours to get through passport control. All the easyjet flights were delayed due to the issues getting through check in / security and passport control including ours. Will not book flights to Lyon again based on todays experience.

Not great. Easter Saturday and only two people on passport control - almost 1 hour wait. Hot, stuffy and toilets not working near passport control. Bags came out on the wrong belt - shuttle to car hire wedged with nowhere to put luggage - but of a third world airport to be honest - compared to the slick check in and security at Gatwick

I had a connecting flight here to London and Montreal. First off, the WiFi here doesn't work. I was in the airport for hours and would maybe have WiFi access for a minute or two at a times until it disconnected again. One small plane of people took customs 30-40 minutes to clear through. Then I had to walk through and extremely long series of hallways to try to get to my flight because the door that led to connecting flights was locked. It was completely empty and the lights were off in a lot of sections of it. I felt like I was trespassing at times, it was so quiet and eerie. After a while signs didn't point to connecting flights anymore and just said exit. I had to walk around and try to find someone to ask for directions. Then after finding the terminal it was a task to find the check-in counter for my flight. I walked around for quite a while trying to the counter and couldn't find it anywhere. I gave in and asked an employee at an information desk where it was. She looked at me like I was an idiot and told me that it says on board next to the flight. I went and looked and it said something like 10.26 or something. I had no idea what that meant. I tried to find a different employee who could help me find the check-in counter, couldn't, gave up and went back to the lady. I asked her again and she said she would look it up and then told me that it's at 10.26. I still don't know what that means. She says that it's downstairs, past all the shops on the other end of the building. I get there and they said that check-in had closed five minutes earlier. I ended up having to book another flight back to London because all the flights that week were over a thousand dollars. So I had to deal with this archaic check-in system. After waiting half an hour in line I found out that you don't check in with the airline, you check-in for that specific flight. Just because you're in the right line for the airline doesn't mean you're in the right line. I had to walk over to the other side and wait in line again. Luckily security was fairly well streamlined and finding the gate was pretty easy. Though, since the WiFi doesn't work, I had no idea that the flight was delayed 15 minutes. It didn't say on any of the signs and they didn't announce it.

No food or beverages options after 9pm, everything is closed. This is an international airport? Literally everything is closed, not even the the relay shop so can’t even get a sandwich. I think this is appalling

It is unbelievable how French authorities at Lyon airport seem to have fun by creating difficulties and causing passengers to waste time at passport control. It makes absolutely no sense leaving e-gates unavailable, even for EU passport holders, asking all passengers to queue and wait quite long time because there are only 3 or 4 officers available.

Appalling. Computers broken so couldn’t get through passport control. No AC trapped for more than an hour so far. Very very very rude staff. Indeed shouting stop complaining loudly when no one was. We were too hot to say anything whilst sitting on the floor wondering when the hell would end. Preference of course for the French at the back of a huge queue once things started going. Update. Now through after an hour and luggage still not off plane. Toilets a disgrace. Found it very difficult to find shuttle bus for car hire but made it in the end. Full marks to Enterprise car hire though. All sorted and through in a few minutes. I gather it’s worse coming back.

After some bad experiences whilst the new terminal was built I thought I would give it another go. I will not be making that mistake again. Arrived 2 hours before flight home on 16/4/23. Got to gate 2.hours later - thankfully plane had been delayed or we, and pretty well everyone else due to travel, would have missed it. Inadequately staffed and managed and thoroughly unpleasant end to our holiday. Oh, and Wi-Fi not working.

Fort de France Airport is small, but heavily decorated. There are very few amenities at the airport. We found the restrooms to be surprisingly clean! Sometimes flights seem to change gates without electronic gate screens reflecting that, so better ask staff wether the gate is correct. A lot of seating was provided for such a small airport.

There is no smoking area in the airport and very little waiting room space. If your plane gets delayed as it happens to me and you smoke - you are stuck. Personnel here not going to help you anyhow, they will just be "sorry for the inconvenience" and smile. Also you can't buy any normal food here, just some bread with cheese. People working here extremely slowly, while having just 2-3 planes in the day. Horrible experience.

Only 2 immigration counters for all arrival passengers at Maastricht Aachen airport and over 200 passengers from 2 planes queued. Few shops in the airport and I could not find something hot wto eat. There are no real restaurants in this airport and only a few small shops. The transportation is awful. Only 1 bus route is operating and it is under a sparse schedule. Nearly 100 people waited for a bus. Some of them could not take on the bus, and had to wait for next departure 1 hour later. You have better to rent a driver if you land in this airport.

Customer service representatives are extremely rude and will yell at you for no reason. Everybody’s cutting the line. If you’re a foreigner, prepare to be unable to buy anything, they only accept Alipay or local cash at this airport. The first time I’m having such a disappointing experience, avoid going here at all cost!
Very poorly designed and managed airport. Not worth flying out of this airport compared to HK international airport due to a guarenteed bad experience.

I had high expectations for Macau Airport, none of which were met and Macau has neglected to bring an int'l standard of quality to its airport. Poorly lit corners abound in what amounts to three levels of cramped mediocrity. In the whole terminal is a lonely 7-11 down the hall. There's the obligatory McD's upstairs for finer dining, but not much else. Seeing the jacked up prices in these places turned me off from them. An unforgiveable oversight is the lack of standardized mobile device charging. Fully expecting to plug my phone into a USB port, I still can't fathom what the airport admin was thinking by installing very non-standard 3-prong charging ports, what they dubbed as 'wireless charging'. To use these, you're forced to buy the local solution in the form of an adapter. No worries, for the 7-11 has 'em for $100 MOP.  Kudos for removing the use-anywhere, conveniently 'universal' of the USB. That took a special effort. The personnel at MA could also use some rewiring. Most obvious, the airport overstaffed its confines with too much security. Here, there & everywhere you'll meet the Blueshirts who, you can bet, have an eye on you.  I interacted with a warden-esque washroom attendant who let me know my time was up by rapping the stall door & barking admonitions. On the way out I fingered him to take the matter to admin for further assessment.  Macau Airport is not merely a scaled down version of its counterpart across the pond. More than that, it's a featureless, frustrating area where you'll be in a hurry to not just catch your flight but to escape the pains of being in the place.

My 2nd experience of a Macau departure and it was consistent with the 1st. Very small compared to other airports in the region but nonetheless did not feel cluttered. Check in not very efficient with an ineffectual security check sticker placed on the zip of my bag. Otherwise it was a pleasant public area with good duty free shops. Annoying that my flight required a bus to get to the aircraft but not unexpected.
Macau Intl airport is spacious. Security was efficient and fast. Check-in counter queues not long and fast. Staff at the counters were good and friendly.The boarding gates were big and not crowded.

To start off, the immigration staff are the worst I have ever seen. They are unhappy people who just toss your passport at you. When I said hello in Mandarin and English, they didn't even look at me! Across the border in China I met friendlier immigration staff, even though typically Macanese people are very friendly. To add to this bad immigration staff, the food is extremely overpriced. I got a "coconut egg tart" (which had no coconut in it) for 18 Pataca. Outrageous. A bowl of noodle soup for 70 pataca, and bottled water for 20. There's two positive things I can say about this airport. One, it's very light and airy, and two, other staff are very helpful. I would visit again if it weren't for the bad immigration staff.

I came to Macau many times before. This time I arrived early afternoon transferring to HK. I expected to catch an airport bus to the ferry terminal to HK. I went to the information counter and there a member of staff gave me the travel info. After I left to the bus stop I realised that I had no Macau coins to pay the bus fee. I returned to the information desk for help. The kind staff searched her bag to find the coins to exchange with my HK notes so that I could take the bus to the ferry pier. This little effort means so much.

I arrived at Macau from Beijing on the way to Vietnam (layover of 6 hours). I found the staff who were waiting by the luggage were unable to understand me and so finding out whether I would have to collect my luggage or not became a huge issue. I then went to the currency exchange who were not rude, but extremely utilitarian and peeved that I did not wish to change a larger quantity of money. Exiting the airport throws you out onto a road where roadworks are being undertaken making it difficult for you to walk. On returning to take my onward flight, there was no order as to where I (or anyone else) should go to queue to check-in and no-one understood enough English to explain. The guy blocking my entrance to the customs area made an enormous issue out of me not having a slip of paper (that I did not need!) and held me up for ages. The teenagers who were undertaking the customs search and bag check were extremely rude, the x-ray area was very busy with people grabbing, pushing and snatching their items from the outlet of the x-ray. I refused to leave my personal effects (where literally all my money / phone / passport) was all piled into the same plastic box in order to walk several metres away out of sight of my bag in order to be searched. The agent shouted at me several times to go over to be searched and I refused repeatedly (I'm not normally pushy, but gut feeling was all wrong here), he continued to shout and point "camera, camera, camera" until eventually he snatched my bag and dumped it on the floor by the area I was to be searched in and then snarled at me "Happy now! You happy now?" I politely replied that I was happy now and he shouted / pointed / talked with the rest of his colleagues who basically kept their heads down, not even looking at him. Drinks and food were expensive in Pacific Coffee and the staff at the Information Desk unhelpful when asked about my delayed flight - they didn't seem to know which gate it had been altered to board at or when. From there Macau Airport was less eventful apart from someone disconnecting my nearly finished charging bank to connect his mobile phone to it (the charging bank). If I hadn't been stood directly behind him at the the time, I believe he would have stolen it. My flight was also delayed but I'm guessing that's nothing to do with the airport.

This airport is decent. It's not that bad but it's not that nice either. The comfort rooms are nice. The duty free only has a few shops. What I don't like about this airport is that the salesladies are just rude.
