They speak to me in Chinese because I look Chinese but I don't understand Chinese, I asked them how to use their product and they just say huh? I've encountered many of them and almost all that I've encountered are the same. They speak in a rude manner knowing that I'm their customer who spends a lot on things. I guess it's their loss that I didn't buy from them. The airport is neat with only little trash.

Not sure if this is one of the busiest times of the year but there was quite a line thru security check. Mortified that they asked me to actually drop my passport on the tray to go under the scanner. T'was still fine until I was waiting to get my things from the belt when I was ushered away to do a body check. Understood it might've been because I was wearing a jacket but it took too long that I was afraid for my handbag and passport left on the tray while a lot of people have already passed through the security check. Good thing my mom recognized my things and grabbed it. But it was frustrating and left me feeling annoyed until my flight arrived.

I arrived at Mackay airport at 5.30pm for 6.15pm flight to Townsville. I went to the bar and got a drink, and then at 5.45pm I went back for another, only to be told the bar was closed? There were still incoming and outgoing flights, and other people were also wanting drinks. There was no signage to advise of the closing time. I thought this was very poor. On the start of a long weekend, we could not even enjoy a couple of alcoholic refreshments to start our holidays.

Was transiting between fight from Brisbane to flight to Townsville with wait time of three hours. Boarding areas large enough for amount of passengers. Lots of windows with views over runway. Shops and eateries limited but probably appropriate for airport this size. Check in area clear. Security staff friendly and talkative. Noted the airport has a new Ibis Airport Hotel nearby and looks rather flash. Had a pleasant time while at this airport.

Outbound the transfer was fine. A quick security check, no passport check, and then on my way to the gate. Inbound transfer was slow and confusing. Despite much shouting it wasn't clear to most people which line (EU/non-EU) they should be in. Ironically the non EU line was quicker. Long line at security, though it did move quickly - then another passport check. I travel a fair amount and I've never experienced two passport checks before. The signage could have been better as well.
It is a shame that the people at security do not speak English. This is an international airport. For the rest it is okay, food is good and it is reasonably clean.
Sorry, but this airport is such a joke. It is old, dirty, chaotic, there are barely any seats or lounge areas. This just can’t be an airport of Madrid - capital of Spain! Such a shame.

First and foremost, the charging stations here in T4 are nothing more than horse posts. Zero USB terminals I tried worked. Ninety percent of the plugs did not work plus, they are shoved on a wall so only 2-3 people can use the ones that do work. MAJOR inconvenience. I suggest charging tables with 10-12 stations and access to both sides in multiple locations throughout. Second, different restaurants. Not sure how many variations of a club sandwich one can experience but that seems to be the theme here. It’s sad when McDonalds is your best choice. Other reviewers are correct, who decided how many seats were required in the gate area? It’s more like a commuter airline in a mountain town with 3 gates. Add more. Lastly, Iberia needs to add personell. At least at the Customer Service desk since most of their inbound flight misconnect. Two employees to take care of 50-60 customers an hour is cruel. On a positive note it is a very clean airport. Cleaning staff gets 5 stars.

The airport itself is easy to get to by public transport and generally clean. Airport staff are helpful.  I arrived at 8am, toilets were clean, used them again at 9.30 and they were disgusting. One blocked sink and dirty toilet paper and pee on two toilet seats. Quick and easy to get through security. Most annoyingly there is a woeful inadequacy of seating at the departure gate. Left from gate 28 and there must be less than 80 seats for 3 gates. There's a lot of floor space so I don't know why so few seats are provided. For that reason I can't recommend going to your gate early. So many people were sitting on the floor.

Two and a half hours standing up and inching along in the non-EU passport control queue upon arrival in Madrid Barajas international terminal on Sept. 17, 2024. Of 18 available non-EU stations, only 2-4 stations were staffed during that time. If Spain wants to discourage international visitors, this is the perfect way to do it!

It's alright. It is good since it is a massive airport but it didn't meet my high expectations. They had a few places to eat, a good amount of places to eat. The staff were not the best when it comes to kindness but good enough. Queues for security were ages though and it took about 5 minutes to scan 4 passports. Overall though it was alright. If you go to Madrid you should go here because the nearest airport is probably Barcelona.

Traveled through MAD 3 times in June and July and it has been a chaotic experience. Train between main T4 and T4s disruption with up to 10 min between trains (imagine the mess), queues for non-EU passport so long for T4s departure that they take the entire train platform (luckily I have a EU passport and could bypass that), Fastrack system malfunction not recognizing boarding passes, lines of cars to the terminal block shuttles access, and remote stand boarding procedure assuming everyone can use stairs ... not a smooth operation. Outside of that MAD T4 design is great but that does not help with travel experience.

Worst airport I have ever had the misfortune to use. No thought whatsoever for passenger. On arrival from a transatlantic flight I had to walk nearly 3km to get to the gate of my connecting flight, some of this on uphill ramps. Between the aircraft and passport control on this nightmare there were no seats to rest, toilet facilities or water fountains. The queues at passport control, check in for connecting flight and security were long and chaotic with thousands of people not knowing where they should go. The overall signage was inadequate and I had to keep asking the way especially in departures. I was exhausted, I had not asked for assistance as I had no idea how gruelling the experience would be, never ever again.

Security were extremely unpleasant and it appears that they are employing those behaving inappropriately on security. Avoid a rude lady in the VIP security lane of T1 if you don't want to be examined over and above that necessary for the understandable purposes of security. If you try and complain you are directed to information whose computer is "down".

A small airport with few flights. Single storey building with Departures at one end and Arrivals at the other end. Some international flights to Dubai & Colombo. Busses across the tarmac from aircraft to terminal. 3 Baggage Belts (1 international Belt with Customs/Passports). Usual selection of car rental and other booths. Car Park directly in front of the terminal building. Very quick in/out. Nice airport.

A small domestic airport in Taiwan. Fast and friendly staff. Surprisingly many shops. Looked very clean. Because this is a military airport too, you can spot military aircraft taking off and land, taking photos is forbidden though. On time non-chaotic boarding, and the plane took off in schedule. Recommend.

Off the plane in under 5 minutes of arriving, no queue at passport control at either ends, bags in 5 minutes, no queue at security, duty free is reasonable (not WHSmith). Buy water at the vending machine as it's only 1.20€ and not 3.40€ as it is in the shops.

Upon arrival, we were herded into two huge queues in passport control. Plenty of people to herd you but only two actually processing passports. After 45 minutes one of the "herders" pointed the remaining twenty or so people in our queue to the automated passport machine. She then promptly walked away. Unfortunately , no one bothered to walk through them as you could simply walk around - so we all did. Spain has no record of me entering its island. Arrivals is like re-visiting the 70s, it all needs replacing. Departures by comparison, was like a different airport, well managed, very short queues and modern. Toilets are very clean.

On arrival at the airport on the 4th May we kept waiting at security for one and half hours, due they said by a new system. On departure day 11th May, the queues for the check-in were horrendous. Only two desks were open initially and eventually a further four. By then the queues were very long. Two desks then became priority desks for people in wheelchairs. The airport did not have a one-queue system which would have been a better idea. As it was people were just crowded in one place. It would have taken them a few moments to sets up a channelled system which would have been a lot fairer.

On going through security at Mahon airport we were met with security staff who could clearly see we were traveling with a young baby. Never encountered this type of bad attitude before, no respect, rude and complete lack of care. There is no need for this attitude.

What a pleasant airport, easy check in, good facilities, cool and well organised. As enjoyable as an airport experience can be. This was in complete contrast to our "home" airport of Bristol, UK. Everything seemed so well organised and customer focused.

STN-MAH-STN what a fantastic airport clean quiet and easy to find your way round. I know this airport is much quieter than some but why can't they all be like this. Even had outside smoking areas in the departure lounge and it wasn't all retail retail retail like most UK airports.

We arrived on Monarch which was a great flight from London Gatwick on arrival to Mahon we swiftly disembarked into a very cool air conditioned Arrivals lounge where bags took no more than 5 minutes to reach the conveyors. Everything else went smoothly and we proceeded to car rental so all in all I estimate we were on are way to Villa less than an hour of arriving. On the return had no problems at check in had a polite and friendly check in lady Aircraft was on time. All in all a very good experience of Mahon airport from start to finish.
Great airport. Excellent shopping facilities. Very clear directions. Very helpful staff. A cut above the rest of the small airports I have visited.
Mahon is clean light and airy with reasonable shopping facilities and bars the seating area is particularly good with a view of the airfield and runway and plenty of space.

Due to the major construction work going on at Mahon we flew out on 20th September 2005 and were extremely disappointed that the international departure lounge was shut. No duty free no retail therapy nothing. We were told that they did open it on a Saturday when all the flights came in and out but not during the week. We flew out from the internal lounge which has nothing in it at all! My advise if you are travelling mid week is to get all your duty free goods from the resorts.

Arrival was not too painful. The queues for immigration were not too long. The longest queue was for the lady with a digital thermometer who was doing the Ebola check. Bags arrived fairly quickly. I needed a taxi which was not readily available. I had to ask on of the locals to show me where to go which meant leaving the airport and finding a car on the road outside. Departure was also not too much hassle. There is very little in the way of facilities so do not arrive too early. The business room is just a room with some comfortable seats. Someone did come round who offered drinks and some basic snacks.

Small but new building. Departure: check-in can be chaotic (especially on routes within Africa) but the international departure gate is spacious. Note there are no services (duty free or refreshments) air-side. Arrival: hyper-strict security. Prepare for long delays and numerous passport finger print and visa checks. Unlike other African airports however there is no hassle once you get out of the secure area. There are not many taxis available and most are unmarked. It is assumed that a foreigner will have already arranged for a drive. The ride to the city centre is a quick 10 minutes on a new highway.

I was in a group of 14 people who required Special Assistance to travel across the airport at Malaga, on a TUI flight & cruise package. The experience at the airport was absolutely deplorable. Only two people eventually arrived to help us. It took almost 1.5 hours to transport us all through the airport to our transport to the TUI cruise ship. There staff were very disorganised, very stressed, under resourced, lacking effective wheelchairs and other transport, poorly supported and poorly trained. The organisation was chaotic, with no confidence that people would make their connections. I would like to say things got better, but our experience was even worse at Tenerife airport, where I would say treatment was almost abusive, with several passengers in tears due to the treatment received, the stress and shame and support staff in tears at the experience. The complete disorganisation, and the way we were treated as second class passengers was absolutely shameful. I would not advise anyone needing assistance to travel to, or through, Spain. Upon our return to France my treatment, along with other passengers was exemplary.

Absolute disorganised nightmare which spoilt the overall holiday. Queue for passport control on departure over a kilometre leading to flight being delayed. I will never go back to this airport. Absolute no respect for travellers treated like cattle. Gatwick baggage on carousel for their flight landed after us so our bags couldn’t be loaded while they were still in passport control. Waited one and half hours for baggage handlers to figure this out and the squeezed in Cardiff baggage a few at a time crushing Gatwick baggage. Do not use this airport.

I arrived at the airport 12 hours before my flight (I live in a small town which has 2 buses a day) so didn’t have a choice. Was told by a very helpful lady I could not go through security until 2am, arrived back at 2.30am to be told 6.30am. Actually waiting looking at the security who are ignoring me right now.

I wanted to share what an unorganised chaos it is at departures. Especially security. No communication what to take out. All we got asked 'randomly' is if we had any babies. We didn't. But then the mayhem started: everything out of the bag: including the last small items - what a mess. Clear signage and loud/clear guards should communicate all this beforehand and not when the bag has gone through. Unfortunately that was a very poor performance, if not the worst in 25 years of flying. No customer service, no help just blunt sending is back. Any assistance in putting the trays back was too much. Is this Spanish customer service? I'd say: avoid this airport.

It seems several flights have arrived at once and immigration is not geared up to deal with so many passengers even though Malaga is now the 4th largest airport in Spain. So far we’ve waited 45mins and it’s still a long way to go. No information provided over the speakers and no staff to explain why the delay.

Today, I was dropped off at 08:25 for my 10:55 flight to Glasgow. To check our bag in we waited in a queue for 1 hour. We waited about 20 mins for security and then 1 hour for passport control. It was absolutely chaotic and airport staff just shrugged their shoulders. People were running everywhere fearing they would miss their. Something has to change in this airport.
What a nightmare. It starts with the fact that they do not try to speak English and if they can do it it's very bad. Customs certainly don't know what they are doing - all in all very bad.
Excessive queues - 1.5 hrs to get through passport control.
Worse airport I have ever experienced. Staff (at least what staff was there which was very little) were completely ineffective in handling queues. Passport control a nightmare.

This is the worst airport I have ever been to. They are unprofessional and not helpful. They lost my luggage and still haven't delivered it to me even if I see on worldtracer they my luggage had been Found. I called every day and they just don't bother. Not a good experience for me.

As soon as I arrived to the Airport immigration, immigration staff was very rude and shouting at me for no reason. I asked politely was that can I go out of the Airport for few hours as I had about 8 hours transit for the next flight. I hold British Passport and filled out their landing form already online. He could have politely mentioned, it wasn't possible. Instead, he was shouting at me. Then I was asked to wait for 30 mins in a narrow corridor to enter into the transit hall.  I never ever had this kind of very bad customer service at any Airports !

The experience at Male airport is horrible. This time I had the opportunity to experience both the international and domestic terminals. First the international terminal is really small for such a major tourist destination, though the staff are quite pleasant and helpful. The arrival experience is bearable but the departure experience is not very positive. The Airport WiFi is very spotty and finding a spot where it works is tough. The toilets are tiny and the food prices are sky high for even basic pick-up foods. The only good thing I would say is that the runway views are stunning to watch from the first floor of the departure and if you are a plane spotter it is a good way to spend time. Coming to the domestic terminal, it is even smaller than the international terminal, there are no facilities once you cross check-in except a toilet. So if you want to eat, better do it before going through security outside the terminal. The arrival area is also similarly a single largish room.

Upon entering Male the customs agent was quite professional.  Carts were easy to acquire as our luggage arrived fast and in poor condition (possibly due to GOFirst). One airport employee impeding our path to the exit was eagerly ready to stop us and ask ridiculous questions as if he was the actual customs agent. Annoyed that we were the only tourists stopped, we impatiently waited for his ego to be satisfied so that we could meet our arrival team and proceed with our holiday. While awaiting our boat we noticed how unbearably hot the airport felt and how few shopping/dining options there were. We tried to seek service at the local bank where we were met by a rude employee. Fortunately the duty free shop kept me busy. Upon departure we were fortunate to have a hotel escort. Onsite covid testing was quick and painless. Despite holding both a valid visa and boarding pass in my possession an agent appeared requesting to see each document that was painstakingly loaded into the online system for web check in. This agent then proceeded to photograph our passports.  After listening to his excuses for almost 10 min in this insufferably hot airport the man instructed the check in agent to continue checking our luggage. Mind you this airport is the size of a shoebox. It cannot be this hard to manage people and processes. The island is beautiful but this inappropriate behavior is no boost for tourism. I would not recommend this island for the stress of entry and exit (despite how much you plan to invest in your holiday).

We used the airport facilities both for international arrival/departures and domestic (sea plane). The international part was no so bad at all; the Covid Clearance was fast and correct, luggage arrived within a reasonable time and all worked pretty well. Not really first class but not as bad as some reviews should indicated. Staff was courteous and friendly. The transfer to/from the sea plane terminal was bumpy (literally speaking) and luggage handling somewhat chaotic, but somehow it worked and with a bit of positive attitude, we really found it pretty good and quite amusing. The business class lounge was not the most modern and delicate one, for sure, but had what we needed and was quite comfortable. Check in "Qatar" was very well organized, friendly and correct in every way. Same for immigration and document control. We give the airport good marks, not need to worry when going to/from Maldives.

Very rude staff, absolute chaos on entering, security staff very rude and do not follow Airlines baggage policies, handled inside our bags without sanitising or changing gloves, tried to tell us we could not take Mosquito spray in our hold suitcase, took our umbrella off of us got safety issues, zero customer service here!

Horrendous lines for the first bag check and temperature check before you enter the terminal, need around 30 minutes. Absolutely chaotic boarding, no seating, no separate lines for Business Class, no covid19 distancing at all. The boarding by busses needs 1.5 hours because they simply don't have enough busses if 5 aircraft's depart at the same time. Around every 15 minutes came one bus per Gate which only be load a maximum of 40 people due to covid19 restrictions. Holiday in Paradise but departure Airport is Hell.

Very slow, running late on our arrival and departure, nearly missed connecting flight back home because of slow progress at Male airport. Lovely Maldives, you are amazing but please step up your services and speed at the airport!

Horrible security airport service who has over redundant security check points, demanding customers to take on and take off stuff frequently. Disgusted by airport security guard who could not distinguish between being professional and being rude to boarding passenger who has forgotten to take off a belt while passing the metal detector gate. Just a command “take it off” is all that was issued and a chin upwards tilt to signal the passenger to start the security scan all over again. No please, no words. Absolutely poor customer service.

Second visit to Male airport in 7 years and this airport goes from bad to worse. Arrival was reasonable, even though we had to disembark the plane and walk around in airside with no guidance which terminal door to use to get into the airport. Then the bags get x-rayed on arrival, more queues there. No air conditioning and wifi requests your phone number and email address. Regardless, that was reasonably okay. Departure was ridiculous - you have to go through security twice, first queue was 30 min, then check in queue 20 mins, then another security queue 30 mins, then you reach the "duty free" that are more expensive than the hotels. The only cafe in the departure lounge had one guy at the cashier and one guy making coffees, and they also provide table service with that staff. Then you go to the gate and there is no seating, because all departure gates are in a single large room. Wifi requests your phone number, email address, and after capturing that, doesn't work. Disgrace.

Male is a small but reasonably clean airport. You won't be able to find any interesting things to do here. It is fine to be a small airport, but the service of some airport employees is terrible. They were extremely rude and asked us to move our luggage outdoors only a few minutes after we finished our meals and are still waiting for our flight. Also, when I used the U.S. dollar bills that I received from an island resort, they asked me if I have a U.S. dollar bills in brand new condition and refuse to take the older bills. After I asked why, they reluctantly took the bills.

Time warp but in a positive sense. I guess this is how a small town airport must have looked and felt 40 years ago. Sleepy atmosphere old building completely unorganised staff but friendly and quick. We got through immigration baggage collection and customs within 10 minutes all without any "tips". Enjoyed the experience. Return flight: check-in was quick no hassle. The best airports are those in which you don't spend any time. If it wasn't for the complete lack of any facilities I'd give it four stars.

This airport is the worst I have ever seen and I recommend avoiding it if you can. The security staff is absurd and rude. Although I was within the limit of 1 litre in a maximum of 10 recipients of 100 ml each, they made me throw away several products because they did not fit their mandatory plastic small bag. When I made the point that my liquids did not exceed the above mentioned limits, a lady with called another colleague who threatened me that if I continued (preserving my rights that is), they would let the pilot know. At this point, I had to accept what they did in order to be able to fly out and when I was recollecting my trays from the band, some of the other staff asked me why I was crying (the frustration got to me after such humiliation) and one young lady from the security staff even hugged me. One of them wanted to throw away a face cream but I explained it was of 100 grams not ml, and although she was not convinced she let me keep it, which makes me think that what they do there is incoherent and they apply some stricter rules if they want to whom they want. I am preparing an official complaint also, but I hope this review may be useful for other passengers.

As a frequent traveller I can truly say that airport security is horrible! Rigid when it comes to liquids, strange double checks of my hand luggage every time I'm flying out of this airport. On top of that the staff has an most unwelcoming attitude. Unbelievable that this has been so for at least 10 years. If you want your trip to start in a good way - stay away from Malmö Airport for sure! Choose Cph instead.

The most unfriendly staff. They did not allow us to pass through security with more than one bag for liquids which is stupid. Had to throw away some of the liquids from our hand luggage, no explanation nothing. In 24th of April the still check IDs for Schengen flights as well.

No service at all, what is on the information screen does not match reality at all. Don't understand what the staff is up to. Shouldn't they inform travelers about flight times? Thanks for missing the flight, it doesn't matter if you're already there in good time. No one cares to help/inform you.Ingen service över huvudtaget, det som står på information skärmen stämmer inte alls med verkligheten. Förstår inte vad personalen har för sig. Ska de inte informera resenärer angående flygtider? Tack för missat flyg, spelar ingen roll om man är redan där i god tid. Ingen bryr sig om att hjälpa/informera dig.

We where traveling mid day, and wanted to get a small lunch before boarding. The only two cafes were closed, and in the only place to get food was at the tiny kiosk. They had hot dogs, but that’s it. They are supposed to sell vegetarian options as well but they had nothing. We had to resort to a bag of chips and a bottle of water.

Very bad experience at security. I am a very careful traveler and even though my bottle had 60ml written on it and it fit the special bag, security decided that they will not allow it. In my opinion this is not going by the rules. I do not recommend this airport.
Very annoying smell of tobacco smoke at the gate. There is a closed area for smokers, which should either be properly isolated and ventilated or removed altogether.

This is not a very friendly airport. They should tell you what they define as liquids at the ticket counter (toothpaste, gel, other toiletries that are not liquid). It was really irritating to have to throw away things that I've never had to throw away around the world. And I used to work at an international airport. Then you could put those things under before they are taken.

I nearly missed the plane to Romania due to extra passport check (required apparently only for Romanian passports). Moreover as it turns out it was not a passport check at all. I basically had to wait in line with all passports, all destinations just to get a hand made sign on the boarding card, when I had no baggage to drop, and my check-in was done online. It was extremely irritating and time consuming - no one knew anything as to why or what was behind it, and it made no sense whatsoever.

Well, I have only one reason for complaining, except the most obvious one, that the Malmo airport is actually Sturup and is not close to Malmo as one might think. The issue that bothered me was the fact that even though I had checked in before coming to the airport, I was denied entrance in the airport based on the ground that I had to pass Wizzair desk for confirmation. I had no cargo luggage, I had my ticket with me and the idea of going to a queue for no reason whatsoever was mind blowing. So I went to the desk, the lady wrote something with her pen on my ticket, then I came back and the lady that denied me in the first place made an ok sign with a marker and then I got to security check. It seemed like a stupid, unnecessary check since there was nothing to check in the first place. So there you have it, beaurocracy at its best.
Fast security checks, great food court with wide selection of healthy and affordable meals and also fast-food. Overall a great experience. I can recommend this airport.

Malta airport was busy during October 2024-however I have to warn anyone who thinks that despite landing on time they will be on time to meet up at the other end. The Passport people are beyond rude, and blatantly taking their time. In a 25 minute queue! just to look at my passport, and despite some kind of high tech looking machine right next to the box office where the man is inside, he looked as if someone had seriously offended him, and took each passport, riffling through the whole book, only to them ask a series of questions to nearly everyone in the queue including old ladies. He then proceeded to slowly and reluctantly stamp the passport. The whole queue was chatting about it after a while as we had all noticed by then. The rest of the staff were also slow but not half as bad as this one individual who clearly wanted no one to enter! This individual made us late for our transfer pick up, and really took his time. He was inefficient and clearly had a problem with everyone in the queue.

The only international airport of the tiny island of Malta. The building isn't the most modern one, its renovated but doesn't offer enough seating or space at all, especially during peak-times. Security was fast tho and they use the latest equipment. There's the usual food & beverage (all British shops) and some duty-free. Malta has a huge bus-network and the airport is served by several bus-lines too. Staff is friendly and speaks fine English. Don't forget to bring your British-style power connector, because European ones are hard to find.
I would like to thank Alessandra at the customer services desk for the phenomenal service and friendliness she has provided me at the airport. She is an absolute gem.

Great Airport. We travelled from Manchester and from landing to leaving the airport, it only took us 30 minutes. For the return flight, we checked our bags in 5 minutes, and took just another 5 to get through security etc. The departure lounge is bright and welcoming, and boarding just took a few minutes. Good experience. I wish more airports were like this.
Great airport, no time waiting. In 15 minutes we were out with our check in luggage. Professional personnel. Thumbs up. Signage very good and easy accessible to everyone

Absolutely shameful. No water stations after security. They have large advertisements for reducing plastic but when you bring your own bottle there is nowhere to refill because they intentionally disabled them (only place anywhere I know that has done this). You are forced to pay for overpriced plastic water bottles. I asked for a refill at one of the bars for water but they refused. Had to pay. This airport doesn't even stand true to its advertisements which promote themselves as being green. Please take note of this complaint and notice the hypocrisy.

Airport Security Staff and police were really rude and in bad moods. Always trouble with them, at no other Airport in the world will you be treated so badly as a tourist. Always a really bad start and end of an otherwise so beautiful trip to this wonderful island and the friendly locals.

Ok, Coronavirus made everybody extra vigilant however, the down turn is the very small number of people travelling. The airport operates ok however the Duty Free ship! A queue about 12 deep, staff in/put without opening another desk and having an argument between themselves. It took longer to be served than choosing 5 items, probably a good part of 20 minutes just to be told that check out only accepts cash. People, get your act together. You are within the service industry and have to sharp up your act.

Passenger assistance is the best we have experienced, very polite, helpful and well organised, thank you very much, airport clean, good to see it as drinking water fountain, also impressed free bottles of water on arrival on inbound flight.

International arrival hall is small, immigration is crowded, does not provide much facility except 1 toilet and 1 carousel. With its size, luggage come very quickly and most passengers only need to spend 15-20 minutes from gate to pick up area. Once you get out of terminal, there are plenty of food shops, coffee shop including Starbucks on ground floor, and food center on the 2nd floor. For Departure, facility is much better. Check in area is large, clean and modern. Departure hall have a lot of shops, cafe and restaurant, but International departure need to make sure to reserve enough time to pass immigration, which is at the farthest end of the airport and no more shop beyond that point.

For a small town scale, Manado airport is pretty good. Has several places for check in. Several lounges equipped with internet access and good food. The lounge area is quite spacious and has good service from Avsec. This airport is set as the transit airport for Raja Ampat (another greatest diving spot in indonesia, located in Papua), and also has an international direct flight like Singapore etc.

Manado airport is one of the best in Indonesia. It has a small delay rate and has a very good view from the waiting room. The airport terminal faces east of Manado and oversees the beautiful nature and mountain ranges with the planes taking-off and landing.

Arriving in Manado from Singapore by SilkAir is always a good experience. The greenery around the airport was beautiful and the short walk (less than 2 minutes) from the plane to the immigration counter is a relief compared to the 10-15 minute walk I used to have in Changi when rushing from immigration to the gate. The terminal building is quite clean and adequate. The only downside is the crowd outside the arriving gate exit. There were lots of illegal taxis touting arriving passengers. The lack of seating area outside the terminal is also a concern as it was hard to find a proper place to sit while waiting for someone to arrive.

I had to travel to this airport because I had no choice as it is the only airport in Manado. The queue for check-in was incredibly unorganised! There was hardly anything at the airport and the worst thing is that there was no air-con well if there was then you wouldn't feel it. I had to run and pay to wait at the airport lounge to avoid the busy waiting area.

A small airport with quite decent facilities. So many small shops restaurants and cafetarias to be found with reasonable prices. However I was disappointed when I saw no escalator from arrival hall (1st floor) to baggage claim carousels on the ground floor of the terminal instead we have to use the one and only stairway. Thankfully there was an elevator dedicated to person with disability. Plenty of metered-taxis available however each taxi company seems to have different per kilo meter rates. The downside of the airport is the toilets. Departing area was good 21 check in counters available no long queue on check in desks still lack of international flights. Garuda Indonesia has a very decent lounge here with wifi available for free. Overall the airport is considered above the average of the rest Indonesian international airports.

Sam Ratulangi Aiport is a small international airport at Manado in the northern tip of Celebes Island (Sulawesi) Island Indonesia. I was using this airport as the entry for my trip to Manado. I surprised to see a relative small airport in Indonesia (which currently only serves few international flights to Malaysia Singapore and The Philippines) as a world-class airport with its modern facilities efficient and friendly staffs and spacious lounges (the VIP lounge is great and very comfortable place to spend some times before the flight). It deserves more international flights in the future since some international destinations in the past such as Taiwan had been terminated.

Even though Managua International Airport has a small terminal, it is very nice and well maintained. It needs improvements since it was last remodeled in 2006. I hope that after the arrival of Iberia, the government invest in improving the runway and taxiway as they are both too short. The terminal needs to be modernized. They announced that the terminal was supposed to have 7 bridges but they only installed 5. There is a need for more screens providing departure and arrival flights information. Overall, I think there is a nice choice of food and drinks and also duty-free shops.

Es una aeropuerto pequeño pero moderno tiene todo lo accesible que se necesita para un viajero, es rápido en lo que es migración las malestas llegan rápido al recogedor todo limpio hay WiFi gratis conectores por muchas partes muy amable el personal buena seguridad lo Malo son los precios de las tiendas todo esos precios desorbitados pero en lo que respecta al aeropuerto muy bueno anunció de vuelos pantallas todo modern. - It is a small but modern airport, it has everything that is needed for a traveler, it is fast in what is migration, the baggage arrives quickly to the pick-up, everything is clean, there is free WiFi, connectors for many parts, very friendly and good security personnel. Bad things are the prices of the stores with those exorbitant prices but in regards to the airport very good announcements with modern screens for flights.

A small airport with about 6 gates, half of which were closed for construction. Not a bad airport-has reasonably spacious gates, shopping, and dining, although most of the dining is before immigration. Immigration and security go quickly. They claim to have wifi, but I couldn't find it. There is a post office, so you can get stamps for postcards, but they have no stamps for collectors despite having a display and book with with current collectables. The shops are staffed by people who will jump on you like vultures if you show casual interest. The duty free sells coffee for more than twice what I paid at LaColonial supermarket and that sets the tone for most of the pricing. Most people seem to browse without buying anything. When you arrive internationally, immigration is reasonably efficient. Your bags get stamped as you exit and you need to pay a $10 fee which is more or less a visa fee. Once you go through the X-ray, you exit into a scrum of taxi drivers. Airport taxis appear more functional than the ones on the street, but will charge more. There's a $2 air departure fee, but it was not levied on my international departure and seemed inconsistently enforced for my domestic flights. Security for incoming baggage on domestic flights into this airports consists of bringing in dogs to sniff your bags. Overall, not a bad airport-easy to get around, but not great for shopping and related services.

The airport is small. Only 6 gates I think. When you arrive from overseas there is a ten dollar fee per tourist for a visa. They scan your luggage with a scanner. If you have anything that they need to take a look at they will pull you over but didn't hassle me a lot. When you leave in the pre-boarding area there is a food court which has free wifi. But I didn't find free wifi in the terminals. Lots of places to plug in along the walls to charge your laptop or iphone.

Small but perfectly adequate airport. On arrival we were through the airport within 20 minutes of touch down though don't forget the US $10 tax taken at passport control. On departure we found the airport was shut and locked with lights off until 4.30 am - for departures that started at 06.45 however it is modern enough with self service check in quick but thorough security with plenty of space in a light and an airy atmosphere. There are now screens for departure information as well as the usual unintelligible tannoy calls and the only downsides were the exorbitant prices for snacks and drinks. Duty free was a bit better but not particularly cheap either. US $3 for a coffee was 3 times the price in the Best Western Hotel across the road.

I was very surprised to see how this airport works everything is clean and well kept but as people said here there's lack of technology no departure boards or wifi available immigration is a breeze come with changed money because you need to purchase a tourist card on arrival taxis will demand from 20 to 30 usd 10 usd is the market price.

Both arrival and departure from MGA was problem free. No crowds. The only short queue was immigration on arrival. If not included in the air fare there is an entry charge of $5 (US) and a departure charge of $35 (US). The facility is modern and clean. Shopping here is not cheap - but the quality and variety of merchandise is excellent. Eating is much more expensive than outside the airport - but prices compare favourably with European equivalents. The waiting areas have ample seating and are cool. Unlike many other airports there is a lack of electronic information boards. But it has the charm of some of the once small manageable airports we once had in Europe!

It is a nice and small airport for a poor country. The airport itself is not ugly at all but it still needs to get a little bit more modernized. After the 2006 renovation the airport looks much more modern than it used to be but still they could work a little bit more on it.

Very friendly clean and organized. Still in need of more modern technology but above all for being in a poor country it delivers a good service nice food court and souvenir shops although the latter are pricey. It has something for everyone.

The rum and pretty well everything in the duty free stores costs double what it costs in a grocery store in Managua. Rum is about US$5 in a grocery and $9 in the "duty free" in the airport. A pound of Case de Cafe coffee is about $8 vs. about $3 in the grocery store. However the duty free shops are the only place to buy legitimate Nicaraguan cigars as total production in the country is for export. They are very good and very high quality but to be honest at times in the USA they cost less. Random luggage searches on departure are almost always for locals rarely tourists. The airport is really quite advanced for Central America currently departures are a bit of a hassle with the construction of that area arrivals are a breeze and rarely does it take more than 5 minutes with immigration and customs both especially for tourists vs. visiting/returning Nicaraguans. Taxis to the city are clean and controlled if a bit slow vs. a regular taxista and cost US$15 with the drivers in the red shirts. However if you walk to the street about 100 feet the fare is around $7. If you can negotiate in Spanish that is.

Other reviews are clearly outdated, so don't put much stock in them. My arrival was around midnight, and was fine - incoming passengers were separated into Brazil nationals and all others, and as a non-Brazilian I was quickly processed. I found it odd that passengers exiting the terminal were forced to go through the duty-free shop, but this may have been a result of the late hour. The departure was fine also, scheduled for 1 am. It was confusing to check bags because only some of the check-in counters are visible when entering the terminal - others are in a second row behind the first. My carrier opened their counter 3 hours before the flight and security opened about 2 hours beforehand, so I had a few hours before checking in. There weren't an abundance of seats, but few people were inconvenienced. I didn't see any lockers to store baggage. Even at this late hour (9-11 p.m.), several shops were open (like a news stand, a snack bar, a chocolate shop, and a cosmetics shop). Beyond security there was only one small news stand (with a few snacks and water), but it was also open. There was abundant seating here. All in all, this airport is just fine.

Optimal infrastructure, parking is good, the check in is very fast, thoughtful attendants, the security is good. The airport has a lack of restaurants that is somewhat annoying, but has a good service and good wifi.

A provincial airport that seems a lot bigger than it needs to be. The immigration officer may well be the most bored person on the planet - 'Next!' (scowls at passport), stamps it 'Next'. When catching your flight, make sure that you stay focused - the tannoy announcements are completely unintelligible (even if you speak Portuguese), and it all seems a bit gloomy which tends to send you to sleep. Airside faciliities are OK but nothing to write home about.

A dreadful place. The only airport I have visited where the check-in desks are in a controlled area to which access is restricted until around 90 minutes prior to (domestic) flight departure. This setup means that if you have a few hours to kill you are saddled with your luggage and unable to make the most of the (overpriced) shops and facilities on offer. Internet cafe must be in the running for worlds most expensive at US$15 per hour. Its slightly more reasonable once through security (but see above - you will not have much time to use it). For reasons unknown the entire area beyond security control smelled of vomit. A taxi for the fast 7 mile/12km journey to town costs an extortionate US$30+. As a point of principle you can avoid this by turning right outside the terminal and walking 100m to the bus stop where services are quite regular and a much more reasonable US$1.50.

No avoiding this place if flying to Manaus which is worth a visit but the airport is in need of some significant help. My flight was to MIA and the check-in area was a small space cut off from the lobby. There were only 3 positions available and the process took quite a bit of time. Once past security there was a single big room with trinkets kiosk a book kiosk that eventually opened and a snack bar. No lounge or any other space available. The staff were friendly but the facility was deficient for an "international" gateway.

Had to change planes here on our way from Fortaleza to Miami. Looks like an older airport with added security equipment for international flights thrown in at random. When we left our first flight we had to exit the secure area find our way to the new departure area and then go through security again (there was a total lack of signage or personnel letting people just making connections know that they did not have to stand in the longest line with others just starting their trip there). Waiting area rather confined with a couple of small shops and one concessionaire selling a very limited selection of food and drinks. I would hate to have to spend several hours in this airport which is getting increased numbers of international flights.

MAO is an old airport far away from the city but with good and cheap connections! They have a lot of security food is expensive so come prepared - a simple burger will cost you 5 dollars or so and internet 9 dollars one hour! Tourist information center is very friendly and helpful.

Traveled to Manaus many times found the airport good with easy access to car park. Staff nice security not too long a queue shops etc are standard airport stuff. Would recommend early arrival and double check all documentation you need to travel. Stop to look at the turtles outside the terminal in their own pond.

On my first trip to the Amazon in 1998 Manaus airport was a nightmare. On my second trip the airport had been much upgraded. The entire building had been enclosed and was air-conditioned many shops some with quality goods.

I know terminal due for closure but do it now. Whole departure experience appalling. Easyjet now confined to the basement. Scanner rejected both carryon and no reason. The exit doors for security closed and no one around to alert to the issue. Most of duty free was closing up at 6pm, departure gate, again in the basement with a flight delay.

Horrible experience checking in and bag drop for Qatar at T2 which Qatar staff say is MAN management insistence. Arrived 3 hrs before departure having tried to checkin on line 48hrs before but it won't let you. You then arrive with your bags and have to stand for 40 minutes, I timed it, to go to one of the self checkin terminals for luggage tags but then have to queue for another 10 minutes to actually drop the bags. The queue behind us was even longer when we got through and everyone was complaining. If this is the future then it's a backward step. As an aside, the security checks were quick and smooth so that's something. I accept the place is undergoing redevelopment but new systems need to work from day 1 for the airport, the airline and most importantly the flying public.

As echoed by many, Manchester Airport is a thoroughly depressing travel experience from start to finish. Where to start? Outdated, incredibly tired and in many areas, downright filthy. Having travelled extensively, I can honestly say that it is really the worst of the worst!  Staff on the whole, especially security personnel, are rude, unprofessional and at times boarder line aggressive in the manner in which they treat and speak to passengers. They bark out their orders, adding to the general sense of passenger misery, add to that chaotic snaking lines, that staff seemingly have limited control over (by not using clear and friendly direction) and you have in a nutshell MAN T1! Sadly, none of the time spent at this airport is pleasurable, nothing makes you (as a paying passenger through the airport) feel valued or relaxed in any way. The waiting areas at gates are cramped, dining options are limited - being generally grubby and tired, both in their decor, food options and overall haphazard appearance; often with long queues and miserable staff plus the kicker, the toilets throughout are horrendous. Surely we can and should do better! If similar budget was spent on passenger areas of the terminal, as clearly the more ‘preened’ areas of ‘duty free’ for example we would be somewhere near acceptable, but I guess it’s all about money extraction, rather than passenger experience. I always wonder what overseas visitors must think, their first impressions must be awful! Would I recommend this airport? Absolutely not! Should higher management be ashamed of its running and maintenance? Most definitely!

I recently flew out of Manchester Terminal 2. A great experience from leaving the car at the pre booked car park. No queues at bag drop off or security even though I had bought a fast track pass. The terminal is clean bright and well appointed. Within 15 minutes of arrival I was eating breakfast in San Carlo. My return trip was as efficient, within one hour of landing I had collected my car and was at home. Terminal 2 is a revelation after the dire experiences of Terminal 1. Well done from me.

I thought it was great. In the past I've been very critical of Manchester Airport, but credit where it's due, my recent experience was very good. As always, we parked in Jetparks3 and got the shuttle bus. I hadn't been through Terminal 2 for about 20 years, as all of my recent flights have been from the dump that is Terminal 1.What a refreshing improvement the expanded Terminal is. The check-in area is bright and clean, passport control was a doddle, and it took just 2 minutes to get through security, albeit this was at 04.30 in the morning. I had a wander round, bought some duty free, and sat and relaxed for a while until my flight was ready. It was a bit of a trek to the departure gate for my flight to Frankfurt, but no real problem. Boarding was via the airbridge, so thank goodness no messing about with buses to far flung areas of the tarmac. And our flight took off exactly on time. My return flight was a week later. Again an airbridge was available, and the arrivals gate was fairly close to Immigration. One of the 2 travellators was being repaired, but in a couple of minutes I was through passport control, and amazingly my bag was in the first batch- then straight through customs and out through Arrivals where the JetParks 3 bus was waiting. All told, 25 minutes from the plane to my car. So, Manchester Airport can be a smooth and stress free experience.

We let Manchester for Melbourne via Dubai. The passage from check in, bag drop and security was all smooth. The infrastructure coped well with the small number of passengers. However, our experience on the return journey on 08/11/2024 was exceptionally poor, the worst we had over the period of a 10 weeks abroad visiting a number of different airports and cities, and indeed, the worst we've had ever a Manchester. The aircraft was an A380, and on finishing taxing, the flight deck informed us that "due to the fact that there is no airbridge available at the moment to take such a large plane, we were parked at a remote stand and would require bussing to the terminal. Welcome to Manchester. We were on the upper deck of the aircraft, and there were no steps available to reach from the apron, prompting internal, cramped, potentially dangerous disembarkation to the lower deck to the exit stairs to the tarmac. When the bus arrived my wife was told extremely rudely by one of your employees to " get on the bus, now" She explained she was waiting to board with me, I was 2 or 3 people behind her. He repeated his rude remark. Welcome to Manchester. The bus took us to the terminal but parked in such a way that disembarkation was only possible from the front doors. Again, more delay. On entering the ground floor doors, we realised the escalator was broken meaning lugging up luggage to the top of the stairs. No help was offered to families with young children, buggies or the elderly. Welcome to Manchester. We then arrived at Immigration. What a farce. 23 snaking lines of queueing arrives, once you got to the beginning of the snake ! The automatic passport readers were malfunctioning so badly the people assisting on the queues had to intervene, slowing the lines down even further. And so to luggage retrieval. Two incoming flights with baggage on the same carousel, £1 trolley fee, 35 minute wait. Welcome to Manchester. Nowhere in the world compares

Early flight with Easyjet from Belfast to Manchester. Smooth experience - then Fast Track through Manchester to Geneva. Quite the worst experience we have had in years. Five "footmark" spaces at security with only one allowed to be used. Officious, unpleasant staff, who actually reorganised every single tray before letting them go through the scanner. They used SIX trays for my wife's hand luggage and FOUR for mine! Bearing in mind that we had just travelled from Belfast with two trays each being used, laptops etc. this was unbelievable. I was told by the agent that I had breached security because I reached across the rollers to get a tray. Then the luggage was pulled for inspection. At this stage many people were complaining. I asked, politely, to speak to the manager, who, when he approached me told me to "Stand back"! He was quite the most ineffective manager I have ever encountered - many staff standing around doing absolutely nothing with no supervision. Then my cabin bag had to be emptied and the lining unzipped because the scanner had detected something - the handle of the case - an £800 Montblanc which I have travelled with weekly for the last 2 years! By this time the manager had scampered off somewhere, ignoring the chaos. All lounges full, food offering poor elsewhere. Unfortunately not a forgettable experience but one which, thankfully, I will be able to avoid in the future. All in all a shameful offering.

Terminal 1 is the area I am reviewing this trip. We used the short stay car park as you can walk, undercover, into the terminal. Very easy, although not the cheapest option. Finding the Aer Lingus check-in was simple and as we stood in line the single check-in operator asked for passengers for Belfast to come forward first, which was great. The airline uses T1 for short hops to Belfast and Dublin, the main activity for long haul is in T2. Security was very quiet and efficient for those of us who understand and stick to the rules. One family was annoyed at having to surrender much of their liquids and cosmetics because they did not know the rules. My partner's bag was sidetracked for search. Apparently, her paperback novel attracted their attention. Mine, thankfully, did not, so go figure! Once through we ran the gauntlet of the "Duty Free" maze and found our way to the Aspire Lounge, included with the economy-flex ticket. Boarding was simple with the ATR72 aircraft having only 72 seats. Returning, the aircraft was parked very remotely for some reason and we were bussed to the terminal, at times I thought we were on an executive all-areas tour! By the time we got there, the bags were on the belt and we were away.

Terrible experience. Arrived 2 hours before a short flight to Newquay. On arrival we found it very confusing to find T3 departures, after a few wrong turns we got to easyjet check in along with about 700 others. Easyjet had two desks open hence it took us well over an hour to check in. Security was chaos, the dingy room was packed and staff were screaming out orders like it was a prison camp. The xray machine was rejecting every other bag, we had to plead with one of the staff to check ours otherwise we would miss our flight, we were lucky I met a guy in the throng of people waiting for their bags to be checked who told me he was autistics and was feeling overwhelmed he'd already missed his flight and didn't know what to do with no staff interested in helping. We had to sprint to the gate only to have to go through more security here my partners passport wouldn't scan and staff again didn't care and were unhelpful. We fly to the UK and then on to Newquay or Dublin from Australia regularly, this was the first time we have enter via Manchester and will be the last.

Travelled through all 3 terminals at Manchester over June/July this year. Experiences as follows: 14 June. Arrival into T2 (Singapore Airlines). No waiting for gate, immigration fast and efficient, bags delivered promptly, taxi waiting to take us. 17 June. T3 departure Ryanair. Early morning rush, busy terminal. Security brisk and efficient. If you are prepared then there should be no dramas. Departure Lounge a zoo with limited seating. Eventually got a table for breakfast. Many, many people drinking alcohol pre 7 am. Not an issue to me, it made flight to Majorca interesting…. Unlike any airport/flight I have ever encountered! Boarded by aircraft stairs. 24 June 8.25pm. Returned to T3 Ryanair from Majorca. Day after power delays caused disruptions. Arrived early, slight delay getting onto stand. Disembarked via steps. Straight through immigration with no delays. Evidence of huge “snake” queuing system that may be used at busy times I guess. Hand luggage only so no comment there. Waited 15 minutes bus to car hire (Green Motion) but picked up car very quickly. Courtesy buses to car rental village and other parking came and went. Overall good arrival experience. 3 July. Terminal 1 EasyJet departure. Awkward getting lifts to check in area. Very busy check in area. Left suitcases at Left Luggage. Hand luggage only again. Passport control again automated and swift. No queue for security once again. Staff brisk, efficient and polite. One bag (out of 8 for our party) pulled for further inspection. Clear explanation as to why this was the case. Busy terminal. Got very good seat at “Giraffe” eatery, right by window. Surprisingly good food and excellent service. Boarding by stairs. Had to wait a while in light rain before boarding. Departed 30 minutes late but only arrived into La Rochelle a few minutes late. 10 July. Arrived back into T3, 2 hrs late (weather in Europe), straight through immigration again, no bags to collect, walked to Radisson Blu for overnight. 11 July. Depart T2 (Singapore Airlines) No queue at check in. Straight through security. Polite staff, no shouting etc. Clear explanation as to why bag was selected for secondary screening. 1903 lounge very pleasant. Once renovations complete this will be a very good terminal. Overall, while Manchester Airport is no Singapore Changi, our experience across all 3 terminals was perfectly satisfactory. As long as you turn up on time, well prepared and organised you should be fine. It’s not the hell hole some of these reviews would have you believe!

Forget your TSA pre-check here. You are still required to take you belongings out of your bag and go through that disgusting equipment that is almost as bad as being felt up. Add more time to your departure if you want to make your flight on time.

The airport is on the smaller side which usually means shorter TSA lines, especially during non-rush hour times. The airport also tends not to be too crowded but can feel a little tight around the Southwest gates due to their large presence at the airport, but overall the terminal is not very crowded. I have TSA-Pre check and on my last trip through the airport in October of 2018, it probably took less than 2 minutes from when they looked at my boarding pass to when I picked my bag off of the screening belt. Talk about efficient! The parking is also cheap with always plenty of spots available. There is also a small rental car location as well which is more than adequate for an airport of its size. The terminal and the bathrooms are also kept very clean and I've never had too much of a problem. There is also some restaurant variety past the security checkpoint with there being a Starbucks, a sit-down restaurant, Burger King, Dunkin Donuts, Hudson News, and a small bakery. Overall, the regional airport is a nice cheaper option rather than going to the congested Boston Logan airport and is super convenient for anyone living in the Seacoast area. The only downfall of the airport is that most flights are going to have to be connecting flights since they only fly to major hub cities and the planes tend to be smaller regional jets so I recommend to bring a very small carry on or just a backpack since it will have to be gate checked when boarding.

Dunkin donuts coffee shop closing at 6pm on a Saturday night. Ridiculous! Flight gets delayed 1 hour and nowhere to go. Just wrong. You can get alcohol no problem. Wonder why there are issues on fights? There it is.

Mandalay airport is not very big, so is very easy and fast to go around. The ground staff are very friendly, like all the burmese people. The airport was clean, lots of light and good air-conditioning. There is a smoking area inside. There are also some souvenir shops and a few places to eat. To get the stamp at customs it took a lot of time as there werent many desks open, and many flights at the same time, so many people started to stress a little.

Modern small airport, bright and clean with good signage. On arrival it is a short walk to the terminal. Toilets better than expected but all modern and clean. All the facilities you could want not busy and not overcrowded. I think I was expecting a small outdated airport building but obviously its a tourist hub so they have made it pleasant.

This was my first time going to Myanmar. We landed in Mandalay International Airport. An airport clearly built a long time ago, awaiting the prosperous times ahead. The immigration control took a bit of time since there was an aircraft arriving from China Eastern at the same time as ours. Airport staff directed some of us westerners to the Diplomat's counter, which cut the waiting time at immigration substantially.  At the airport the currency exhange rates offered for US and Euro were best at the Farmer's Bank.

Mandalay International Airport was built at the turn of the 21st century. It serves both domestic and international destinations and is designed like many airports around the world, it just works slightly differently somehow. Arriving on a domestic flight you are bussed into the single terminal building where you walk passed unmanned Passport Control Desks to one of 3 baggage carousels before having your baggage (hand and hold) scanned and into a large Arrivals Hall with the usual selection of booths and a small café/shop selling bottled water. There are TV Screens showing which flights are coming or going. Marble floors and air conditioned. Departures start with the need to scan all you bags (hand and hold) before going to Check-in Counters which are clearly numbered in 4 banks A, B, C and D. After this is the a boarding pass check and into the Departure Hall which is upstairs (Check-in and arrivals are on the ground floor). There is a large selection of shops and a couple of bar/cafes, not all of which are open for domestic flights. Security Scanning is done at the gate and Gate 6/7 seems to be where all the domestic flights leave from via a pier down to a bus. In the Gate area there are no shops or toilet facilities just rows of seats looking out on to the apron and in the distance the runway parallel to the terminal building. The airport is larger than the current traffic levels so it does not feel crowded or too busy but it has a "new" feeling that none of the other airports in Burma (Myanmar) have.

Despite more international flights the terminal still has the feel of a ghost town. After a very speedy check through security all domestic passengers are directed to a largish departure area and bussed out to their aircraft. The colour coded badges all passengers are required to wear ensure no one gets left behind or attempts to join the wrong aircraft. There are more food outlets than my last visit a few years ago sadly the washrooms and the rest of the terminal show no sign of having been properly cleaned since then.

After the splendour of Yangon Airport (International - not Domestic which hasn't been updated since easily the 60s) Mandalay Airport is reminder of what could have been. Coming in to land the airport looks deserted. We were brought to the larger looking terminal by bus and instantly I recognised the Japanese design having lived in Japan for several years. Aside from the outstanding design nothing else was even close to Japan. Most of the lights were off immigration desks looked abandoned and one of the panels of glass separating the baggage and arrival halls was badly smashed. Still service is efficient if only because there is no one to serve facilities mostly work and taxis are plentiful. If the reforms continue to improve Myanmar this airport could be a real gem. If you need to fly to Mandalay - and domestic flights are not as scary as they sound - it will do just fine but let's hope for better days.

It seems very under used airport - comparing the facility and the passengers go through here. It's all new (a couple years old - with very long runway). Arriving from CNX on Air Mandalay's prop plane seems odd on this runway. It's located pretty far out from Mandalay city center. The airport seems deserted after all passengers left.

I have been flying from Mangalore International Airport domestically for a very long time. I'll be honest, the check-in, baggage claim or the security is just literally the same like any other airport, with less people. The airport is calm and clean. Restrooms are provided. The only drawback is, there is no source of recreation and entertainment here. We have a couple of eateries, but very, very, very limited. Wi-Fi is provided. But when we speak about shopping! Don't depend on Mangalore Airport, it has nothing! Trust me, nothing! The last time I visited, there was a food stall at the ground floor and an umbrella/raincoat shop and a metal item store at the first floor. That is it! No clothes, no alcohol, no Mc.Donald's etc.. But all in all, its a good airport, I mean it's catering for the needs of Mangalorians. Arrival also went very smooth.

Never seen such a laid back airport as Mangalore. I had a flight to Mumbai at 10:40am and I reached the airport by 8:30am only to find out the check-in counters are all closed and open at 9am only. There were many passengers like me waiting for check-in. After staff for Jet Airways arrived the counters opened and I got my boarding pass, again was made to wait for security checking to open. The counters of security checking opens only after 9:30am - all employees were seen gossiping, having their tea and so lethargic. And there were so many passengers waiting, even passengers with special assistance. Never came across such a lethargic airport.

This is no longer called Bajpe airport since the opening of a spanking new terminal building at the end of the new(ish) runway. The new terminal has aerobridges that are used for passengers disembarking from the front end of the aircraft. While I was there passengers could also disembark from the rear end using air stairs (this for a B 737!) The airport is clean and spacious not particularly stylish but nice. Mine was the only flight that came in at the time so the bags came quickly. Cars/Taxis park outside where they're not supposed to so getting out took longer than it should've. On the departure side there are shops before you get through security (which is opened only about an hour before the flight) but once you get through there's only a small coffee and snack stand. The restrooms were clean.

Very small airport with very limited facilities. I am amazed that this is an international airport. If you are stuck in this airport for a few hours there is nothing to do!!. However check in and security a breeze and seems very organised.

Main airport to Philippines. 4 terminals squeezed round 2 runways. Terminal 3 International Arrivals has airbridges and a shortish walk to Passport Control. Important to get your eTravel declaration done before passport control, usual baggage reclaim and customs check before getting out of the airport. Very busy arrivals area with many taxi' offering their services and congested parking directly opposite. Terminal 2 is mainly Philippine Airlines with a domestic and international section. You have to show your passport and ticket/Boarding pass to get into the terminal and get all your bags scanned. Check-in Desks and a few other amenities before going through security. The Departures Lounge is for domestic flights and separate to the International one. A small selection of cafe and similar and 9 gates/air bridges. Limited seating means it can get very busy if a few flights go at a similar time. There is patchy WiFi.

Worst airport I have ever visited. Less comfortable chairs for the passengers to rest - worst is many are with long hours transit. You will see many passengers sleeping on the floor along the walkway to the departure gates. Foods are pricy & with limited choices. Luxury stores are with less items on display. WiFi is not strong enough. Internal looks old and a bit run down. The airport has to be upgraded to preserve the image & dignity of the country

Worst airport I have ever seen. No food selection available, only a scarse choice. No place to take a seat to eat in terminal 2. Very old and outdated airport. Also arrival was very chaotic. Taking a taxi is an adventure. Sim card for Internet is at extortionate rate. Security do not follow international rules set by Civil Aviation Authority but they have their own rules. Be ready to have unexpected issues when going through security. I travel the world and can confirm thst Manila Ninoy D'Aquino is definitely the worst airport in the world.

I have never experience such chaotic and overcrowding lines to Terminal 1 check-in counters of PAL. Four lines waiting for our turn to have our luggage x-rayed by One machine. Average wait is about 2 1/2 hours. Then another average 2+ hours in line to check-in luggage. And all this waiting is just to check-in on one airline PAL. Even at LAX Tom Bradley terminal with more Passengers coming and going is never this chaotic.

Waiting for our luggage ... took me 1 hr 17 mins to wait for my luggage to show up as most of us passengers did. The fact that only there was only 2 airplanes that has arrived. Immigration officers were as efficient as they can be.

I have never see anything like this. They scan your carry on bag, it is ridiculous. They scan it again before entering the plane and after you pass customs. They sit you behind the a gate like a bunch of animals, if you go to the washroom just beside your seat but the other side of the blue ribbon you have to go in the line up again. It is my last time with Philippine Airlines, never again.

I fly almost every month abroad for work and sadly always end up in Terminal 1 of NAIA. If you're departing from the terminal, there's only 1 restaurant before the immigration so if you arrive before your check in counter opens, sadly you won't even have anywhere else to sit. Always crowded and since the check-in counter area is pretty small, the lines between airline counters can get confusing esp when the terminal is busy. Arriving in the Terminal 1 however is much worse. There are I think 5-8 electronic counters open and most of them don't work properly. Other than that, there are only 3 manual counters where those who can't pass the e-counters (coz they don't work) all fall in line at. There is an "electronic check-in supervisor" booth beside the e-counters but they don't even assist the passengers who have a hard time passing through. And don't get me started on baggage claim. It'll take you 30 mins - 1hr to get your luggage.

Manila is a very crowded and busy airport, I have been through here a number of times. It's sad that in this day and age you have to lug your bags to a bus to get a connecting flight to Terminal 2. Still, I guess it is what it is. Bus was crowded and very hot, I guess this was to be expected, as this was a very busy time when I was traveling. Signage has improved a lot since my last visit; I was able to find my way to my gate very quickly. Always crowded here, I feel that they could perhaps improve the air conditioning a little. Aside from that, little to complain about.

Manila Airport should be avoided at any cost. Last three times I have been there, Airport lounges are fully booked and can not accommodate passengers? Dirty, unorganized, ridiculous cues at immigration. There are no smoking zones at the airport, and if you’re a smoker, better avoid this airport and Manila itself. Food will be served with plastic cutlery, so you can imagine cutting a piece of meat. Philippines has been such an awesome place, warming, welcoming, affordable and reasonably priced, foreigner and tourist friendly. Unfortunately, not any more. Next time, I am flying via Singapore, irrespective of cost. Simply, avoid Manila at any cost, if you care about your dignity, and you value your money. Thank you

Eventually helpful staff but they are all transfixed on to mobile phones constantly, so fairly hard to get their attention. Departure area is an uncomfortable, chaotic, hot, very old area with absolutely nowhere to buy water or a coffee whilst waiting for your counter to open. I had to stand for 3 hrs, with no water, as my previous domestic flight to Manila arrived 5 hrs before the next. Be careful when transferring from one Terminal to the next, very tricky and a lot of scammers everywhere. There is WiFi in the airport but it is the slowest WiFi on earth. All in all, not a good experience at all

Arriving and departing from this regional airport is far less stressful than dealing with the airports in Cancun or Mexico City. There are fewer passengers of course, plus the airport is well organized and clean. Check-in was fast and easy, and security was well organized, courteous and fast. There are several places to enjoy a snack or meal before takeoff. The waiting area is spacious and uncrowded and offers great views of planes landing and taking off. Wifi was free and worked well.

This is one of the worst airports I have experienced and in stark contrast to the wonderful people of Mozambique and their gracious hospitality. I used this airport 4 times this month. My arrival experience almost turned into a catastrophe, the immigration is so disorganised that it is not funny, they are all over the place and no one seems to have any idea what they are doing. They first had some issue with printing out my visa, which took almost 20 minutes to sort, then they pasted by visa on the passport of another person and handed it to me, I took it and walked a few steps and realised that this is not my passport and returned to the counter, at which stage, there was a frantic search to find my passport, then the immigration officials removed my visa which was pasted on the other gentleman's passport, tearing the page in his passport and then proceeded to stick it in my passport which was finally found lying buried under other papers at the immigration officers table. The worst part is the constant demands for money by the officials at Maputo Airport, at departure. After a few days, I returned to Maputo for a domestic flight and the policemen outside the airport stop tourist cars and ask for drink money, the same thing at security check and this happened again as I was heading for my flight out of Mozambique. Thankfully by now I had learned how to play dumb, On the domestic side this airport is small and there is not much there to write about and on the international side its a bit bigger and there are a couple of shopping outlets but hardly any plugs to charge your phones or laptops, but the infrastructure is still manageable but the harassment by officials who should be doing their jobs is just insane.

Having visited over 212 airports worldwide, I've heard tales of corrupt security practices, but my recent experience at Maputo International Airport has left me genuinely shaken. The entire process felt intrusive and intimidating, leaving a lasting negative impression. My taxi was stopped at the airport entrance, and police officers searched through my belongings. While I understand the country's ongoing conflict with rebels, this level of scrutiny seemed excessive. After passing through the initial security check, I had to wait for a green light from the police before proceeding to check-in. The check-in area was minuscule, serving only a handful of airlines. The air conditioning was barely adequate, and the overall ambience felt cramped and uncomfortable. A few souvenir shops and snack bars lined the waiting area, along with two VIP lounges. The real ordeal began after checking in. As I ascended a staircase, two security officials approached me in a forceful manner, demanding to know how much cash I was carrying and if I had any local currency or USD.
