I explained that I primarily used digital payments and only had around $5 in cash for purchasing a snack. Despite my explanation, they insisted that Brazilians are wealthy and should have more money. They proceeded to rummage through my bags, scrutinizing my belongings with an aggressive attitude. I remained calm throughout the ordeal, reiterating that I only had the clothes on my back and some cosmetics. Their search yielded nothing, and they eventually gave up, appearing visibly frustrated. This unsettling experience left me feeling deeply intimidated. I noticed that the security officials worked in groups, making it clear that travelers should never attempt to pass through security alone. The entire encounter left a sour taste in my mouth, and I sincerely hope to never return to Mozambique.

Maputo airport is very close to the city centre. It consists of two vast glass buildings [domestic & international], totally of proportion to the small number/of flights/passengers. However check-in area was quite busy, security was rapid, and air-side was bright and airy. A few souvenir and duty-free shops and a number of airline lounges, most of which were closed Airbridges looked tired and rusty!

Arrival at Maputo Airport is via air stairs to the ramp to the terminal. There is no covering that I could see in the event of rain. Inside the arrival area is what seems to be a mass of confusion at the desk where one collects his visa, unless you are one of those coming from a country not requiring a visa. Following issuance of the visa, one then has to clear immigration to have an entry stamp put in his/her passport. This is a slow procedure and one is frequently asked where one will be staying - so best to keep a copy of your hotel confirmation with you. Customs is simple enough, where all baggage is screened in an x-ray machine. Following this, you are finished and can exit the terminal. Note that there is presently no air conditioning in the terminal and it can be hot. Also, lighting is rather limited. Departure is likewise slow. I arrived 2 hours before my flight time and had to sit and wait almost 1 hour for the counter to open. Again, the terminal lacks air conditioning (the story being that the system is under repair). Following check in, one takes an escalator to an upper floor where one processes through immigration which oddly enough is a fairly fast process. The departure area has a few shops and some airline lounges, but is otherwise fairly devoid of anything. Flights are called over a loudspeaker system and one descends again to the ground level and proceeds out of the building, across the tarmac to his/her plane. The very worst part of utilizing Maputo Airport is the arrival where it seems that confusion reigns, mostly due to the matter of issuance of a visa and having it applied to one's passport. This occurs even if one has acquired the pre-visa on line and involves paying the fee for issuance of the visa. Note, the visa fee can be paid by cash or credit card (Visa, Master Card only). If you have secured the online pre-visa, be sure to bring a print out of it to show to the visa issuing clerks. There are some countries that do not require a visa and apparently this number has just been expanded - although the expansion has yet to be implemented as of this writing. If you have not secured a pre-visa and are from a country that requires a visa, you can be delayed by this process for as much as 2-3 hours. In my case, I asked the tour company with which I arranged my bookings and tours in Mozambique, to arrange a meet and assist service for both arrival and departure at Maputo Airport. This was a good investment and I tipped to man who assisted me with US$10. I highly recommend this type of service for a first-time visitor.

Nice new Airport. I have been travel through his airport for last one year and it is very nice and good airport overall. It is relatively new but still there is a lot things which can be improved like Air conditioning and bathroom cleanness etc.

Flew out of Maputo up the coast to Inhambane. Found it to be clean well organised free of queues and with fairly friendly staff. We used the domestic terminal which was largely devoid of facilities apart from a couple of shops but also virtually devoid of passengers. A surprisingly pleasurable experience.

One nice feature of Maputo Airport is that it has one of the few remaining exterior viewing terraces so you can stand outside and take in arrivals and departures. A worse airport on arrival than on departure with the slow waiting around for visas on arrival be sure to have exact change if you can and the relatively slow delivery of baggage which may or may not have items missing or delayed if your transit was via JNB.

A pretty basic airport but seems to function fine. At customs people needing visas need to line up in the "visas" line - if you line up anywhere else you'll just be told to go to the visa line. It's a bit confusing as the booth is slightly behind the others. Visas are US$25 cash there are no change facilities so be prepared. They take your money and passport and then walk over to an office near the baggage claim where the visas are processed. Everyone has to stand around and wait in front of the office until an immigration official walks out with a stack of passports and starts calling out names at which point they will give you back your passport with the visa inside. In the meantime you can collect your bags the carousel is literally 2 metres away. Plenty of taxis right out the front you can't miss them. Barclays ATM also just outside so easy to get local currency. Outbound the check-in is pretty straightforward though I would suggest getting there a bit early as it looks like it would get mad in a rush. Public toilets on the second floor a little bit away from the action but nice and clean. Not much past customs other than the ubiquitous bar but nice to have one last Laurentina premium before leaving.
I am not sure when you went to the airport in maracaibo but things have change a lot. Prices are not as bad and there is lots of choices to eat and drink very reasonable.

Maracaibo city is the hottest city in Venezuela and so is its airport 40 degrees or more it would appear that the air conditioner system is not working at all. This airport itself and its staff is another story compared to Caracas Int'l. I spent 4 hours in Maracaibo's airport and I found nothing but rude and careless staff all around the airport. My flight to Miami was delayed apparently for some problems with the jet bridges that at least I did not have the chance to see or walk through to get to the airplane. The prices are extremely high in restaurants and stores. I just can't understand why Maracaibo being such an important economic centre in Venezuela since it is the heartland of the oil has such a dull and unfriendly airport.

The worst airport experience ever! Security check after security check. Police is performing racial profiling, selecting anyone travelling from a non EU countries and taking fingerprints. Signs in the airport are extremely confusing. Check in personnel are lazy, chatting among themselves rather than working. No fast food in the waiting lounges, just some extremely dry sandwiches.

The Cleaning ladies in all toilets at the airport remove the toilet paper from the cabins and if you ask for paper, they ask for a charge! I think its really mean and it should not be like this! Toilet paper should be provided for free.

Men working at passport control middle booths, 5pm 10th Jan 2025, were cruel to my autistic daughter and disrespectful to myself and younger daughter. One of them shouted at her to hurry up, my husband explained she is autistic and that made him more angry at both of them. Before myself and youngest daughter could approach they pulled two males, can only assume they were friends, out of the queue behind us to go in front. When we did approach, I was asked to confirm I was a housewife, I stated I was a Doctor, they then proceeded to ignore me and laugh with each other for 5 minutes whilst we stood there. Horrible, sad, cruel men in positions of authority where we just had to stand and be disrespected. Will not be visiting Marrakech again. Gave 2/10 as the man working at the easy jet check in was very supportive and understanding towards my autistic daughter.

Our experience at Marrakech Ménara Airport was an absolute nightmare. The check-in process was a complete disaster, primarily due to an apparent shortage of baggage handlers. This caused a massive backlog, resulting in an unreasonably long line that moved at a snail’s pace. Passengers were left stranded and stressed, with no clear communication or guidance from airport staff. It felt as though no one was in charge, and the lack of organization was appalling. What should have been a straightforward process turned into an ordeal that left us scrambling to make our flight. For an airport that serves as a gateway to such a vibrant and beautiful city, the management here is a glaring disappointment. If you’re traveling through Marrakech, prepare for frustration and delays. Truly one of the worst airport experiences I’ve ever had.

The airport building itself and the internal infrastructure are good, but the entire process that passengers go through upon arrival or departure is incredibly inefficient. All the queues move very slowly, and it feels like passengers are deliberately made to wait unnecessarily. Every step is unnecessarily repeated: first, your passport and visa are checked when issuing the boarding pass; then there’s a massive queue at passport control. After they stamp your passport, you immediately face yet another queue to check whether you got the stamp. Staff members who are supposed to simply verify your booking number and issue a boarding pass, or customs officers, work incredibly slowly. In every case, they take a long time discussing something with their colleagues—when there’s clearly nothing to discuss—or they spend an absurd amount of time examining every document, double- and triple-checking them as if they’re solving world-scale problems. Plan to spend at least an hour and a half going through all the queues before departure and at least an hour upon arrival.

Marrakesh airport off season is a breeze and my opinion may be different if I was arriving/departing with the European holiday crowd. My biggest focus when traveling business class is an airport than can offer differentiating services for that class of service. It was not clear on arrival if we had access to Fast Track and could not find much information about it but with the limited number of passengers queueing at immigration we just went with the crowd. On departure we had a better experience. Getting inside the terminal requires queuing with all passengers but we obtained access to Fast Track for security and immigration following our check-in at Air France business check-in counter. There is a chocking point following immigration where all passengers converge but it was fairly quick considering the slow season. Great shopping and an amazing little Royal Air Maroc full service lounge made the rest of our airport experience enjoyable. One really concerning point: The free airport Internet was not working well besides the light crowd … I cannot imagine how bad it gets during the busy travel season.

After reading all the poor reviews I really readied myself for my arrival and departure. I had to leave this review because I actually had an ok experience. I’m a regular traveller and have been to many airports!! Arrival… yes it took about an hour to get through and out the airport. I didn’t need to collect luggage and sat at the front of the plane so was first in the queues. If I was at the back, I expected it to take 2 or maybe longer hours to get through. Deparute had me most worried. I was flying out at 3pm so arrived at 12:40 (it took 40 mins to transfer from centre of the city to airport, the driver said it or Ally takes 15 mins tops!). Yes there was a queue to get into the airport but we spent about 10 Mins waiting. It’s a simple X-ray machine and the time it rakes it just the time it takes people to push their bag through. There was no messing around. You have to check in, even if hand luggage only. There were about 5 checkout outs ope. For jet2 and and I was through in about 5 mins. Next is security which again was fast, no people, took 10 mins or less!! Passport control was straight after and again, hardly anyone there so it was through in less then 10 mins. Overall it was a normal experience… with only the arrival taking long and potentially causing a problem. Overall this was not as bad as I thought it would be. Maybe I was very lucky. But if you are revelling too, just expect a long arrival. And give plenty of time to depart.

This airport at best is absolutely atrocious from the moment we arrived we departed the aircraft and thought this should be a quick experience, how wrong I was, the short walk from the aircraft to immigration was short however once you get to the that point the enjoyment of starting your holiday is shattered the queues were horrific a lot of staff but doing nothing, we joined the queue and I decided to time how long it would take and it took just over 2.5 hours and talking to others who have used the airport have said they waiting over 4 hours once you have stood and waited for all this time you think that’s it queuing has been done how wrong could I be, once you have your entry stamp you join another queue to make sure that you have the stamp you literally just received. Once through that hurdle you’ve been at the airport longer than the duration of your flight there, baggage reclaim once you’ve waited all that time your baggage to find is a hunt around and find it yourself as your flight is no longer on the board after a good 25 minutes we found our bags just left on the floor by the belt which is a risk in itself as anyone could have simply taken it. Once you’ve got your baggage and absolutely exhausted from the shambles that is Marrakesh airport you join yet another queue so your baggage can be screened and once you’ve waited there probably another 20 minutes you are to customs which was the only quick experience. For departures the airport does not improve and is in fact probably far worse, before you’ve even got into the terminal the queues begin, everything is screened before entering the terminal which I have no issue with but as per everything in this airport is so inefficient this can take 20 minutes and the queue is outside which can mean standing in extremely hot temperatures dressed to go to a colder climate, once you’ve waited negotiated this, you enter a nice beautiful natural light terminal which is misleading for how shambolic this airport is, next is check in which despite having a little queue the staff seem far more interested in anything other than doing their jobs. After this you have to exchange any currency left you had as you cannot take Dirhams out of the country this again is another queue with terribly inefficient staff, next is security again, a relatively small queue but again terribly slow as the staff are inefficient, they don’t keep people moving and when they need to screen a bag they hold everyone up by doing it immediately as it comes out the x ray allowing passengers behind them to not collect their bags and move on, once you passed another slow and inefficient process you get to passport control and you guessed it another queue this time can be up to an hour or longer which the entire time you are wondering will I make it in time for my flight, after all this stress you are funnelled into a small corridor where yet again the stamp you just received is checked yet again in another queue, after this you finally made it to departures where if you are lucky you might have time to get any duty free or food and drink however as you guessed it all the staff there are also very slow and seem interested in anything other than you. We barely had time to get anything not to even go to the bathroom. Once at the gate there is yet another queue not just for boarding but to have your exit stamp from passport control checked yet again. Overall the experience was horrific from start to finish I don’t recommend.

Really poorly organised with loads peple doing nothing. Queue after queue check after check and people q jumping and nothing done about it. Once you are through if you had any time left the shops looked ok but allow up to 2 hours to get there. The tannoy system is so muffled that no one can understand a word of it, wifi awful.

I visited your beautiful country with friends in mid-October and I really enjoyed my stay. I would love to return but the big negative was the experience at your airport in Marrakech. It started already on arrival. Upon arrival we were greeted by an incredible line at passport control. We joined your queue system and waited there for 1.75 hours! After an hour, when your staff started to see the panic of some passengers, they started to guide the new arrivals through the Fast track, which legitimately annoyed everyone who was only halfway through their waiting experience. It should be added that we were so called head to head in the queue, after an hour you get thirsty or wish to use the toilet, but somehow this is not possible. All the excitement of reaching our destination was gone. Moreover, when I got within sight of your officials after an hour and 40 minutes, I understood why everything takes so long. The two officials who were ahead of me had other priorities than checking in tourists quickly. One was chatting and the other was even talking on the phone to someone else while checking in tourists (from the nature of his cheerful speech, I gather he was not talking to his supervisor). This is the ultimate in unprofessionalism. Our departure 6 days later was the same, just split into 4 queues. We arrived at the airport 2.5 hours early. First we stood in the baggage drop line, where it was very difficult to get information on how to handle passengers who don't put their luggage in Cargo. Why did they have to stand in the baggage drop queue in the end, believe me it is very misleading. After dropping off the luggage and getting the much needed stamp, we were faced with another long queue in the area before entering the security check area. Here we reached the first gate after half an hour. Beyond the first gate was another long queue for the security check. Your very sharp security staff herded us like a herd of animals into a queue that had no space, i.e. people were crowding each other and panic ensued. I cannot imagine how mothers with children feel in this queue. After about 1.5 hours we went through security and were again faced with an incredibly long line for passport control. By that time most of the people were overstaying their boarding time, i.e. there was a panic when half of the people who came to the passport control hall demanded some faster check-in (some fast track). I understand them. Your staff just stood by and watched, or occasionally let someone get halfway through the line. So there were people who stood in line and a few lucky ones who were able to beat half the line. We got to the plane at the last minute. If it hadn't been late, it would have been gone by now. Your airport has three major problems. It is not at all equipped to handle the number of people you are handling (capacity of arrival and departure officials), it is very poorly organized, and your staff is completely ignorant of the situations that arise.

Absolutely appalled. We were informed by a lady with ID that we could, free of charge, use the awful lounge and have speedy boarding. We clarified this with the lounge guest desk, to be told it was free as a trial, being a fairly new airport. We then were moved to another lounge to be told it was a free service. Appalling not edible food, choice of 2 drinks. Lounge like a waiting room at GP surgery. How can Egyptian authorities allow this to go on. It is absolute theft and needs looking into. Have complained to Priority Pass and AMEX, as she implied this service was free from the providers.

I've been in lots and lots of airports in my life, this is by far the worst, incredibly poor. We booked vip longe £27 per person and for that we got a cup of tea and a cold slice of pizza. The staff where charming but not very helpful. Because we where VIP we were speedily passed through a security check, this only took 1 hour? We were stopped at 3 desks to check our small hand bags, after every stop and search I told security we've just been checked he answered in Arabic, I'm bored and my boss is over there. I bit my lip as I understand limited Arabic but I knew they were playing with an old English couple. By the third check I asked in English this is third check. He smiled, this quick you VIP check. Then I answered in Arabic to see his boss, our bags where swiftly zipped through with an apologetic statement and a shy smile. I called over the police security man and told him in Arabic what was going on in his hall. He apologised and rushed us the right way through. This spoilt our holiday immensely, paying £56 to be played with and 2 cups of tea and a cold slice of pizza? Was going back to Marsa Alam in February. Not again will I step inside this circus of an airport. Hargahda airport is head and shoulders above. Never again in Egypt, sorry.

The departure from Marsa Alam was very unsatisfactory. Security procedures were slow, queues were long and personal was very customer-unfriendly. It took 2 hours from entering the airport to getting to the gate (check-in time was just 5 minutes though). Passengers are treated unprofessionally.

The airport has not changed since I was last here two years ago. On arrival we collected our visa from the "bank desk" (cost now $25) which was very slow because everything done by the teller had to be checked by the person watching him. Only one of the six passport desks was open (although there were a lot of staff around watching the queue) for the rudimentary non checking stamping of the passport followed by two more staff (independently) checking it had been stamped. Baggage arrived quite quickly. Upon departure all our bags were X-rayed on entry to the terminal (queue 1) then we queued (progressing very slowly) at the only two desks open to check-in (queue 2). Then we queued (3) to go through passport control passing through clouds of cigarette smoke from those watching the queue. Airside facilities (cafe food etc) nothing has changed including the erratic quality of the free WIFI and the attempts of the toilet attendant to get a tip of £1 or €1 for use of the free toilet. Queue 4 (relatively short) was that for the airport bus. As airports go this is better that any other Egyptian airport I have been to it would be superb is those watching the queues or watching others do their job would work as well.

Despite the difficult situation in Egypt this airport has got no worse since I was last here two years ago (neither has it got any better). It was clean and it had adequate facilities for the reduced number of passengers now using the airport. Duty Free prices are ridiculously high and therefore not as well used as they could be. There is free wifi but I could not get a reliable signal. Baggage delivery on arrival was astonishingly fast - a quality for other airports to copy. The longest queues were those going through security at the front door of the airport other security queues were quite short.

Arriving passengers are bussed to the terminal where visa stamps are paid for / or collected. These are not visas in the traditional sense but a tourist tax of $15. Immigration simply involves having your passport stamped (there seemed to be no checks) and this was done speedily. Baggage delivery was very quick on a fast moving belt and you are soon outside of the terminal building. Departing passengers have to endure a number of queues to get into the terminal but once through check-in is reasonably quick. Luggage weight checks are very thorough and they seem disappointed if your luggage is within limits and recheck it a few times in the hope it gets heavier. Departure forms are completed after check-in air-side there are the usual range of caes (some offering free WiFi which is really great) and things you never knew you wanted. Buses take you to your plane. This would be a good airport by European standards and is an example to others in Egypt of how it can be done. The one thing that annoyed me was that in the Gents Toilets (supposedly free) you were hassled (even whilst occupied!) for a tip by the attendant â€“ he did not get one.

A very new airport with few flights. Lots of parking and an outdoor cafe. Check-in easy because it is not very busy once past security the gate area is small but with plenty of seats. Duty free is expensive (priced in US$) costa coffee pizza ice creams and a cafe provide more food than at many airports. Toilets are clean. Free WIFI is good and fast. Buses to the planes (no airbridges at all). Very good for an Egyptian airport.

Long queue for passport control, although arriving from a European country member of Schengen area. This is disrespectful of the European agreement. Moreover, the automated border crossing called "parafe" is often out of service, which worsens even more the problem. Big waste of time for nothing. A shame.

This airport is almost third world in many ways. Terminal T2 has a staff of immigration which is woefully understaffed, rude and inefficient. It need more staff and also machines that work would help. T1 immigration can be even worse. Toilets are closed, the restaurants are expensive (as most airports) and often do not have much choice. No seating after security in Terminal 1 (if you remove shoes ), queuing is inefficient at security. The airport Terminal 1 is modern (ie. a shopping centre) but the staff are not well trained. Baggage handling is slow and slovenly, sometimes waiting 45 minutes for bags. Management needs to look at operations. This is a busy airport with an increasing number of destinations, it needs to update services.

This review is solely for T2. We visited Terminal 1 as there was no where to sit in T2, literally 20 sits all taken, T1 for larger carriers is good and plenty of seating, so if you arrive early for check-in I'd recommend going to T1. T2 on the other hand, is the worst airport I've been to, and I've been to Basrah during conflict! As mentioned pre check-in seating is poor and the whole venue is like some poorly put together art piece, concrete floors and walls. Really nasty place to be. Once you check-in you then have to walk your bags around to another location for your baggage to go be scanned and loaded - first time ever for that!! The security are rude and abrupt and in one case verbally aggressive but for legal reasons I cannot divulge the details! Then once you get through it's like a cattle shed, hot and stinking, with a lack of resources, so after spending €55 on some sandwiches we were ushered to the plane, where once again, there was no seating, just some planks of wood to lean on!! I only gave 2/10 based on the time it took to get through the airport to the plane, which to be fair was swift - thankfully! Avoid where possible!!

Where to start! On arrival it appears to be a temporary structure converted for use as an arrivals hall. Two flights landed at the same time and we were herded into an endless queue for passport control with only 2 officers. The electronic passport control was no better as only 2 of the 5 lanes were working. As bad as that was departures was even worse. Again, endless queue for a bag drop as no designated line for that, got stuck behind a huge school group who were all checking in bags. Then once you finally reach the end of the queue they give your bag back to you to go around the corner to enter another queue to hand your bag to a porter so he can check the tag against your birding pass and put it on the conveyor belt. Next ANOTHER queue for security, this one actually wasn’t too bad. On to duty free, not bad, but not enough seating. There are apparently 2 lines to go through passport control. But they don’t tell announce which line is yours until the last minute, just so everyone can make a mad dash to the line only to find out that both sides lead to the same place. We were directed to the electronic passport control (EU passports), only 1 out of 5 were working but it was still quicker than the other queue. We then entered a corridor leading to the seats at the gate. But the door was locked and we had to queue AGAIN until somebody came to open it and check our passports and boarding passes (100m past the actual passport control). There is a sign at the entrance stating Terminal 2 was inaugurated in 2006, but it really feels more like something from 1976. Avoid if you can. I’m giving it a rating of 1 out of 10 only because the website won’t let me give 0.

Terminal 2 is like a cattle shed! It's like going back in time to a provincial airport in the outback. There is no order in the queuing system, staff were chatting and cutting their nails. There is no room to sit down once through security- which is stressful for a family with small children. It's unbelievably primitive. Contrastingly Terminal 1 where most of the domestic and most European flights depart from is everything an airport should be - modern, spacious, efficient! It is like a 2 class system airport. Most disappointing and disturbing.

We entered terminal 1 where we dropped a friend off to their flight. Terminal 1 was lovely. Air conditioned and seemed like there were no queues. Then we walked towards where terminal 2 was; this was where our flight was leaving from. There were queues outside the airport for what we thought was the baggage drop off was. We queued for over half an hour before realising this wasn’t the queue for the easy jet flights. The signage was atrocious, there was nothing to say that this was the baggage checkin for Ryan air!! We then went into the building knowing we had wasted over half an hour. On entry to the building we were greeted by yet more queues. We queued for about half an hour just to get the bags weighed, only to be given our bags back to then queue again with our bags. This next queue was like the herding of cattle into a milking parlour. It was horrific. People were so squashed together now trying to funnel through a small space like sand in an old fashioned sand timer. We then queued for another hour to place our bags about 100m from where they were weighed. By this time we had only 30 minutes to get to our flight and we hadn’t even gone through security yet. Thankfully the rest of the process went more smoothly, if it hadn’t we wouldn’t have made the flight. The whole experience was stressful and a horrible end to our lovely holiday. Shambolic. The staff were overwhelmed and couldn’t help. The system was archaic and reminded me of family holidays over 35 years ago. Appalling.

Over years I have experienced bad airports but must say this one hits the top of the worse, mountains of space to create something better specially to those who need to stay overnight for early flight however they decide that having the most disgusting dirty chairs. Regarding charging phones, computers etc, disconnected plugs, USB available but not working and all the chairs have no charges, what they expect you to do for hours and hours on end, if these people were to go to Asia and have some lessons on how a airport should look please do so. I understand an airport is not a hotel but nevertheless there are people who have no money and lying on the floor to charge a phone in possibly the 5/6 plugs you have available that is disgusting. This airport should be demolished and able competent people made in charge of making it more welcomed specially in a place where thousands of visitors pass through On a daily base.

I came by taxi to the airport, and it felt like the airports doesn't have a nice place where the taxi could stop. Inside it felt confusing with two different security checks. In the security check to the left in 2nd floor one young man was kind but the others seemed to have get bored of their job long time ago. So far this is minor flaws, but the real reason behind this review is to let go of some frustration related to the almost total lack of providing something to eat - except some dry sandwiches and just a little more.

This airport is a mess, and whilst they are expanding the terminal, the present areas are poor. The shopping and cafes / restaurants are very limited, and poor for what calls itself an international airport. Toilets are a disgrace, filthy and poorly maintained. Boarding gate areas are overcrowded, hot with very poor aircon, dirty carpeting and no sight of a cleaner anywhere. WiFi is non existent, and the handful of charging points are almost inaccessible for most. For what is effectively a state owned airport, Marseille Airport is an absolute disgrace and needs private owners to come in and make it fit for purpose.

Its beautifully located airport in the outskirts of Marseille and next to the sea. Good public transportation from Marseille city center to the airport (Bus after every 10 mins). Airport structure is lacking a good maintenance, although, big part of the airport is going through major facelift renovations that could really confuse the departing passengers as the signages aren't very clear or bilingual to guide passenger towards a right direction. Waiting area and washrooms temperature is warmer than outside temperature. Passengers were literally sweating bullets and kids were crying, its just too hot. I enjoyed the tarmac view though and also like how they let people to board either by jetty or just walk to the plane. I will review it again once all the  work would be done and hopefully, airport would be in much better shape.

I was there at 1 am to catch a flight to Istanbul. It wasn't crowded but the airport simply lacks basic facilities which appear to be a problem when it gets crowded. Very few shops after the passport control were open and there weren't any restaurants at the International terminal (or I didn't find one open). The airport is clean. The passport control is fast, but the security guards are not very friendly. Actually if you have to travel to Mashhad, its not that bad. Even comparing to the airport in the capital city (Tehran), it is so-so.

I was in the airport international terminal around 1 am. International terminal is quite newly built and not completed. No food or snack or shop available. Passport control fast and efficient. Not enough seats after passport control. Check in area is very crowded when there are two three flights. It is better to be at airport at least 2 hrs before departure time. Normally you do not need more than 30 min from the city to airport but in some seasons and for some events it may take more than an hour so check with hotel reception not to miss the flight.

Tiny yet functional airport which serves this remote South Pacific Island with regular flights by LATAM from Santiago and Papeete. Airport is only open when these two flights arrive. The terminal is a single storied structure, very user friendly. The airport has all the ambience of a tropical island - palm trees, open structures, walk across the tarmac to disembark and board the aircraft, even a moai - a specimen of the island’s iconic stone statues. Before the baggage claim area is a stall where one can buy the National Park ticket in Chilean pesos or by credit card or US dollars. On exiting the baggage claim area, you find you hotel pick drivers waiting holding up your name. There are also taxis. The town is so close that you can even walk to your hotel if you have light luggage. On departure, the terminal hall becomes a bazaar with many stalls selling local souvenirs. There is also a cafeteria. Bathrooms are clean. There is an “exit” check by the security services where they collect the stamped form that you have fill out before boarding the flight to IPC. Rules limit stay on the island to 30 days for both foreigners and Chileans. There are also souvenir stalls, restaurant and bathroom beyond the security check. The covered “gate” area is open and you can watch your plane getting readied for your flight. All very relaxing!

My fiancee and I flew in from Cape Town and had a 2-hour layover at this airport prior to taking our next flight to our first bush camp in Kanana. So we strolled outside to do some souvenir shopping and get some refreshments at the cafe just outside the airport. On the way there, I stopped at the smoker's hut and had a cigarette. Obviously I pulled my mask down in order to smoke. When I finished, I threw my cigarette butt away in the provided trash can, and adjusted a few items in my backpack .. about 10 seconds had passed b/w my throwing away my cigarette butt and that's when Maun airport police officer approached me. He rudely asked "Why are you not wearing your mask?" I replied, "I just finished a cigarette." He even more rudely said to me "And that is your defense?" I replied "Well, it is my reason." I pulled the mask up, he scowled at me. I expect this sort of behavior when I go to the post office, or to renew my driver's license, but I would imagine the city of Maun, the airport, and definitely the many bush camps in the region largely benefit from tourism that comes to the area and those tourists do have a choice. One disgruntled man's actions will harm an entire region and people, and that would be a shame.

I arrived at Maun on a flight from Cape Town. Maun airport is a relatively simple and small airport with almost no conveniences and no air conditioning. We had to walk from the plane to the entrance of the airport, although the distance was short. Just before entering the door, we were stopped and asked where we were coming from and several passengers had to produce their Yellow Fever vaccination records. No one had given us immigration forms on the plane and thus we had to complete these in the small, hot area just before the immigration desks. At the time I was there, only one officer was processing passports, so there was some delay. However, the lady immigration officer was pleasant and processed me promptly. From there I went to the baggage claim area and while there used the restroom, it was not pleasant. I collected my baggage without much ado and simply walked past the customs inspector, who ignored me, and was then in the main terminal area. A few steps past that and I was at the desk of Mack Air, the airline I was to use to fly to my safari lodge. The Mack Air people processed me promptly and the next stop was a luggage scan before entering the pre-boarding holding area. The security folks used a scanner but also insisted on opening my small bag and having a look-see. My feeling is that the scanner is not really very good. The pre-boarding area is simply a non-airconditioned room, hot and without much in the way of creature comforts. Although Mack Air gave me a bottle of water, I could see no facilities for purchasing drinks or anything else. My impression is that Maun Airport, though an international airport, is dated and seriously needs some upgrading. At the time I arrived, another flight was arriving and it appeared that this was the time of day when almost everything happens at the airport. Still, it is stretched to capacity and seriously needs some upgrade as it handles most of the transiting traffic between international carriers and the smaller shuttle airlines (such as Mack Air) that move passengers to and from the various safari lodges in the Okavango Delta. Thus, whether one recommends Maun Airport or not, it is a necessity if one is going to the Delta and its only plus is the friendliness of its staff.

Both sets of ladies toilets that I used during our recently transit through Maun (early November 2009) were horrible. Several sinks were broken/hanging off the wall some toilet mechanisms would not flush taps were out of order and facilities for the disposal for feminine waste had clearly not been functional for years (although the toilets were kept as clean as their poor state of repair would allow). I know that Botswana is currently having a particularly hard time given the global downturn but maintenance of these facilities must have been neglected for a very long time to get into their current state. Botwana has unequivocally positioned itself at the high end of the tourist market: if so then it must be prepared to deliver service and facilities commensurate with this market niche. This applies not just to the camps but also to airports which are the gateway (and first introduction) to the country. Given the parlous state of the diamond market and the beleagured US economy (from which it apparently attracts the majority of its tourists) Botswana should be placing even greater emphasis on delivering quality facilities and service to attract visitors from the diminished pool of tourists who have the money to be able to afford to visit which is undoubtedly a costly travel destination. Otherwise the airport is fine for a small regional airport in the developing world and thankfully the air conditioning works well! The use of golf carts to transport passengers and luggage to and from the planes is also an excellent idea both in terms of passenger safety and comfort.

Travelled twice from/to Jo'burg. Very small airport used mainly and maybe only to reach Okawango Delta. A couple of flight per day to South Africa and Gaborone twice a week to Namibia. However it is usually quite busy because all small airplanes leaves from here to all airstrips in Okawango. Security control also for internal flights with these small planes!. One "gate" you walk to the airplane. There are no facilities inside only one toilet and no food and shops one check-in desk that open 2 hours before flight but the queue is reasonable. It is a safe airport quite clean but not the place where you'd like to spend more time than necessary! Nice shop and honest food just in front of the airport.

Just landed, and I didn't realise I had to fill in a form umtil I was in the customs queue. Once I knew, I immediately started filling in my form and once at the counter I was asked where i would be staying, how long etc. all the usual stuff. He then asked how much cash I had? which I found extremily unusual especially holding an Australian passport. When I told him he seemed alarmed and consulted his workmate next to him. It was then they told me I needed to have such and such a day being in Mauritus. Internally I was laughing thinking yeah of course I have money in the bank to cover costs while here, I just had little cash on me at the time. Anyway this is what really annoyed me the most, theres no train, no bus services etc to the airport at least not after 4pm (so I was told) so the only way was via taxi. Their taxis have no meters, so it seems like their all working together to rip off every potential customer. They have one head guy with a taxi badge, he says it will cost so and so amount, you think to yourself thats a rip off considering what my dollar is worth compared to yours. I can't believe their government allows these scammers at the international airport, what a joke coming to a small island and having this happen as your first or second port of call.  I think something so simple as metered taxis need to be implemented.

We weren’t informed during the flight that two forms needed to be completed on arrival. It took 1.5 hours to get through passport control. Simply there were not enough staff to deal with the number of passengers.

This is a quite modern airport and serves the country well, after that being said, I felt the airport is terribly connected to the other parts of the island and it makes you rely heavily on taxis or hotel transfers. On arrival they will ask you for the "Mauritius all in one form" if you do not have it they will send you to the end of the line so that you can fill it online, the airport provides free wifi for that, then they will ask for hotel accommodation and return tickets, make sure you have then handy or this will delay you and everyone else standing in line. The staff seem to be friendly, specially if you speak French. Bathrooms were clean and after immigration and security on departure there are plenty of food options including global fast food giants. I would say that I enjoyed my time while using this airport.

Overall, a great airport with great facilities and ample outlets to eat/drink/shop. The only issue about this airport is the queues at immigration and security, which is serious. For instance, immigration at arrival took 40+ minutes although there were only ~15 people in front of me and this was because only 3 windows were open for processing.

No bookstore or magazine stand. Our flight was delayed and except for the ridiculously priced shops, there was nowhere a person could buy a book to read while waiting for the delayed flight. I find this unacceptable as most flights with Air Mauritius will be delayed at some point during your trip, so please assist passengers that are not glued to their phones and would actually like to purchase a book to read.

The airport is well-organized, secure, and clean, with nearly all services available. The crew at Air Mauritius is extremely professional, and they go above and above to execute their jobs in a courteous and professional manner. Nishi, the travel consultant/passenger service, is amazing in terms of customer service and taking care of passengers with a smile and enthusiasm.

A pleasant airport. Our flight arrived at 09.30 and even though we had to do a COVID test at the airport we completed all the formalities and left the airport within 40 minutes. On departure the flight was at 21.50 and at this time there were a reasonable number of international flights also departing, however the check in and security checks were quite quick. After security there is a large duty free shop as well as some smaller shops and food/beverage outlets. The terminal was clean and tidy. Obviously the airport is not yet operating at full capacity but our experience was fine. Only letdown was the poor WiFi.

Probably the best island airport in the Indian Ocean. Well designed structure, the only challenge is the long queue in the immigration hall. The authorities need to arrange extra officers during peak timings.

Check in was slow but this was the airlines responsibility and not a reflection on the airport. Signage around the airport is good and the terminal was nice and clean. There is no smoking anywhere inside the airport. Smoking is only permitted in designated areas outside the terminal building. As I was a business class passenger, I used the fast track through passport control and security and I was pleased I could, as the queue to use the normal passenger route was very long indeed. Security screening was as efficient as it could be, and the only delay to the process was passengers unpacking items which needed to be screened separately. It still amazes me that passengers still don’t know how items need to be separated for screening and what items should be removed from the body, belts, coins, watches etc. So passengers slowed the process and not the screening and security staff. There is a good amount of seating available in the departure lounge. A good range of shopping and food and beverages is available in the departure lounge but there is no electronics shop. 3 hours free WiFi is available and while speed isn’t fantastic, it’s sufficient.

I was extremely impressed. My flight from Paris arrived at 05:35 and there was a bit of a walk from the arrival gate to immigration, but there didn’t appear to be any other arriving flights. There was no queue and I was processed within seconds of arriving at immigration. On arrival at baggage reclaim my bag was already on the carousel. I think it’s safe to say I was out of the airport within 20 minutes of arrival.

I must say I was quite surprised with this relatively new airport. It is well designed and all check-in, security and boarding processes were very efficient. The free wifi connection is probably one of the best services I've experienced so far. The choice of dining and shopping are also very good. The airport itself is quite far from the city but there is a train service to the city.

First time contributing to this thread, and I must say: Kuala Namu International Airport looks pretty modern and roomy indeed, something I truly want to see in a functioning airport. I mean, yes, it has opened recently, yet, I saw in the pre-opening photos a lot of modern features, from streamlined check-in desks and a variety of shops (I'm surprised I saw a branch of Cotton On at the airport), to modern jetways and small plants placed along the waiting areas near gates (I wonder if those are actual palm trees).

The airport of Medan has been moved from Polonia to Kuala Namu International Airport (KNIA). KNIA is now the most advanced and the second largest airport in Indonesia. It is also the first integrated airport rail link in Indonesia. The whole area is free from smoke (means that they provide and manage the smoking area well). The baggage claim area is well-designed. Restrooms are always clean and have no pungent smell.
This is a well designed airport. There is no hassle from porters and taxi operators. Checking in is very fast and efficient. Arrival luggage handling is very good.

Kuala Namu International Airport is it is the second largest airport after Soekarno-Hatta International Airport but the first airport which has a direct rail link to Medan city the capital of North Sumatra. Kuala Namu is the most comfortable and the most modern airport in Indonesia.

Finally the new Medan Airport opened after a few years delay and it was just 2 weeks old when I touched down at Kuala Namu. The terminal building itself is stunning a combination of Suvarnabhumi and KLIA with lots of daylight. The gate holdrooms are huge with comfy chairs and you can see the tarmac clearly. Airside and landside shops and restaurants are not entirely opened but lots of interesting shops and restaurants will open soon. Check in area is also airy huge shiny and modern. This is the first airport in Indonesia with a direct rail link to the city and the train station even though its not entirely finished also stunningly designed. Arrival areas still has a lot of things to be completed as the airport is just soft opened. Hopefully when its officially opened in September all the facilities are ready.

I and my wife travelled via Medan Polonia Airport twice in December 2012. I lived in Medan for over 10 years in the past and have relatives still living there. I'm trying to review this with appropriate comparisons against other airports I've visited by taking into account their relative sizes and passenger movements. I think Polonia airport was still terrible. As soon as we stepped outside the arrival terminal taxi drivers approached us making us feeling uncomfortable. The taxi was unmetered. We were charged IDR50k for a short travel. On the departure we arrived earlier (3 hrs before flight) and had to wait until the Garuda check-in counter was opened. There was absolutely no single seat or chair anywhere from the entrance up to the check-in area. We were forced to sit on the trolley and on the floor. The check-in process was messy. Some people stood in between 2 queuing lines. Some people blocked the queue although they did not intend to check-in. When I compared Polonia's today with Polonia 10 years ago I absolutely saw almost no improvement except for a renovation that followed a fire disaster a few years ago.

I have used Polonia six times in the last four year both international and domestic arrival and departure. No problems with taxis overcharging just as for any airport do your research. Be affirmative informed and polite.

The state of Indonesian airports is sad. This hub is dank and dirty. Wait until you're on the plane to use the restroom. If you're just arriving you will be besieged by porters who will grab your bags without asking then hustle to the exit. Just say no with a smile and that should do the trick. The airport uses a taxi voucher system which will charge you a flat (tho grossly inflated) fee depending on your hotel. Expect to pay IDR55000 easily double what you would pay on a meter. Not the best introduction to Indonesia if this is your first port of call.

It’s a small airport with limited resources, however I’ve flown into Medellin several times. Their international arrivals terminal has a disproportionately small immigration section, with even fewer immigration officials. It simply does not meet standards I’ve seen at other airports I’ve gone through. I would really hope they can give themselves more resources for this as Medellin continues to grow as a destination.

There are 2 airports in Medellin - the international airport in Rio Negro, MDE, and the in-town airport, Olaya Herrera, or EOH. We arrived at MDE and left from EOH. The passport queues at arrival at MDE were not clear about which line was for foreigners, and the lines for foreigners were long. Otherwise, it was a fairly standard arrival. The EOH airport is right in town and used for some domestic flights. The look is very 50s/60s, but the airport is very functional. Oddly, they made us buy disposable masks to go through security, but otherwise there was nothing unusual. Check in and security were quick, and there are several cafes both before and after security. There are no jetbridges, and you'll walk through seems like a small botanic garden to get to your plane. I would recommend this airport for a domestic flight if possible.
The airport services were very attentive to the plane, we arrived at 3:30 local time, when we left the plane the luggage gang was already in operation and the suitcases were in very good condition.

It's an airport that is showing its age and needs urgent remodelling. Immigration, security checks and customs were relatively fast, but there are certain peak times when many international flights arrive and this may cause things to slow down. I couldn't believe my ears when asked where the elevator was and they told me that it was out of order. When travelling with heavy bags this isn't what you want to hear. Wifi, provided by Airplan, was good but tends to get slow during hectic hours. Medellin has seen a recent increase in the number of passengers, international flights and could be an alternative to the nice Bogota International Airport but a lot of effort (and work) has to be done before this materialises.

Arrival: Clean and spacious airport. However the luggage/baggage arrival area appears small and congested. Taxi counters are available near the exit. Departure: Checked in online and print ticket using the kiosks available in the airport. Thumbs up. However, upon entering the departure gate, the officer who are on duty, did not recognise the ticket (ticket from kiosk is thinner, more plasticky compared to thicker ticket from the counter) and questioned me of having a fake ticket! She maintained her politeness though, but still, how come your own staff didn't recognise ticket which you own airport (albeit kiosk) produce. Otherwise, the rest of the experience was good. Spacious and clean airport with abundant seats. A bit too cold.

We were flying to Kuala Lumpur from Madinah airport through group reservation on Feb 22, 2020. The check-in counter staff separated all of us. When we wanted to exchange seats with fellow group members the crew were not really helpful. All the havoc could easily have been avoided had the check-in counter staff been more accommodating when seating passengers according to their family groupings. Do not assign seats according to your mood or whims and fancies for that day. It is very unprofessional. Next is the passenger security scan. Ladies and men security scans were separated. At the scan, even folding chair cum walking stick was confiscated. How do you suppose the passenger is going to walk to the gate when the walking stick is taken away?  My 87-year-old mother wears a lumbar support waistband. She was told to remove it and go through the scan again. How to remove without privacy at that scan area? Security lady can easily be more sensitive and take her to a more private place.

First time arriving in this beautiful country together with wife for umrah. Arrived by Malaysia Airlines A380 and departure with same aircraft. Facilities well kept. staff welcome us with a smile. Easy flow for arriving and departing.

❌Not Verified|  Bags didn’t arrive with us. Jeddah staff were probably responsible for this mishap. Didn’t issue a receipt for luggage. Medina staff were very efficient and tracked and delivered bags a day later. However, they still kept on calling us back to ask if we received bags. Staff at check in counter not efficient at all. Didn’t return our passports. We walked off only to realize that it wasn’t returned to us and returned to fetch passports. Check in and departure were delayed. Most disgusting of all was the foul smelling toilets below the beautiful mosque outside the airport.

Convenient location - only 15 mins from the Mosque. Excellent modern facilities. Nice simple elegant layout with steelwork reflecting date palm trees. Convenient location of cafetarias, toilets and prayer rooms. Friendly staff and security personnel. Clean and tidy. Ample seating facilities

TSA at terminal A, Jetblue is the worst, screaming at you to hurry up. Then when you do, they don’t touch your bags to push it through. I had to beg for my bag to be brought forward. EWR TSA, you should go take lessons from Orlando on how to be courteous to your customers.

Airport cant cope at off peak February morning. Some are being transported by bus to the arrival terminal from plane. E passport check are just hundreds of people long. Baggage collection ok but chaotic as a least 600 people are waiting in a small area. Custom queues formed 200 people long looping around baggage claims belt, all looking confused and heading different direction. The Goods Declaration and No Declaration signs too small hidden and people cutting queue. Only 1 officer managing the long queues and instructions vague and incoherent. A horrible welcome to visitors. An embarrassment for Victorians. Total mismanaged to the max.

The airport is incapable of maintaining basic facilities and cleanliness standards.  One if the two water fountains in the international gate area adjacent gate 9 not working. Seems to have been broken for some time. Windows in the gate 8 area have clearly not been cleaned for days. The grime and hand prints were terrible. Car parking exit wayfinding signage at the new T4 terminal carpark is plain absent in some areas. It all about greed.

Bad attitude from airport staff in bag checking. Refuse to inform all people to push the tray into belt. He only selectively help some, and sarcastically told some passengers that we need to push it into tray. Is it that hard for u to tell upfront. Not all passengers understand what you want. Shopping here is great, except that they do not offer any plastic packaging for any liquor purchase

What a joke, I am embarrassed to be Australian. Immigration machines not working, just chaos. Picked up luggage, then one more hour before we got out. What a disgrace, understaffed, poor organisation. Long queues just for the ridiculous declaration card. Watching the people from other countries wondering, what is this? Better service at third world airports. Whoever is in charge of this mess needs to resign, couldn't run a chook raffle.

On 28th September our plane from Dubai landed at 6.30am. On exiting the plane we found toilets very small and run down men's toilet with just 2 cubicles & ladies toilets hidden some distance away around a corner - totally inadequate for hundreds of people disembarking. Massive queues starting well before the duty-free area. Electronic passport checking - initial set of machines were randomly refusing to issue tickets to many people - about 50%. No border force staff monitoring the machines that were malfunctioning. No clear directions as to how to queue having been rejected by the machines. Hundreds of very tired people milling around trying to figure out what to do next. After progressing for about 30 mins border force directed us to the non- resident's queue where overworked staff processed us quickly once we reached the counter. Arrived at baggage carousel and many bags had still not arrived, including ours, 90 mins after disembarkation. Finally picked up our bags and found another huge border force queue snaking around the carousels with one staff shouting directions from a distance. Finally, that queue seemed to speed up, and we finally emerged 2 hours after disembarkation. Followed signs for taxi rank and discovered Uber has taken over the original taxi rank and we had to walk right the furthest queue after the buses to find the taxi rank .

Another terrible experience arriving at Melbourne International. Queues at passport control and customs. Baggage took forever to come and kept changing carrousels, and they put so many flights on the one carrousel even with others empty. So dumb.

This is probably my most visited airport, been here over 30 times in the past 14 years, flying domestic and international. Nothing changes, but that's not a bad thing. Some check in areas are hard to find, and queues are always long and very congested in the international terminals, it's not big enough for the amount of foot traffic, it used to be adequate, but it's become a more popular destination as years have gone by. On the other side of the coin, domestic terminal seems too big for the amount of passengers checking in. No smoking areas after going through to departures, but that doesn't really bother me, good excuse to quit. Darwin does though...? Getting dropped off and picked up outside is always mega-chaotic, and there's a lot of works going on now, which makes it even worse. Shops, bars and restaurants are all good, before and after departure gate. Arrivals is usually speedy and quick baggage claim. From stepping off the plane to walking out the doors with my suitcase, its usually only 15mins max, which is always satisfying after a long flight.

Our family and I flew in from Bangkok via Thai Airways arriving Melbourne Airport T2 on last Friday 21 May night. We travelled in Business Class with Priority Baggage handling with Priority tags attached to the luggage's baggage tags. However, we waited 30 minutes for our bags at the baggage claim area after the first non-priority bag was delivered to the baggage claim belt. Our bags were among the last few ones coming from the belts, almost after all Economy non-Priority bags were delivered. During my observation, I could not see many 'Priority bags' appearing in the baggage claim. The Business Class was full. Our friends travelled from Dubai via Emirates arriving Melbourne T2 on Sunday morning on 23 May. Their bags also had Priority treatment but also experienced the 'delayed' treatment by the baggage handlers. Their ones were also among those last few bags coming out after most of the Economy's non-Priority ones. I do not believe these are isolated events. This happened to me in December 2023 as well. It appears that either the baggage handlers do not follow 'Priority bags' protocol or they deliberately mistreated the 'Priority bags'. It took me 25 minutes from the plane landing to receive my bags in Paris CDG a week before and about the same time in Istanbul Airport last year. Even at Heathrow London 3 weeks ago, it took me less than 35 minutes to get my bags from landing time. Last Friday, it took over 1 hour to get my bags since plane landing time. However, Melbourne Airport's baggage services is far below the world's standard. I have not even compared this with airports in Singapore or Hong Kong, which are among the most efficient ones in the world. I tried to use the Airport's online complaint form to submit a complaint, but the form does not submit and does not work!

Melbourne International arrivals hall is very poorly designed and chaotic. It is a disgrace that this terminal is so congested, poorly signposted and lacking any natural daylight. All the immigration and customs staff should be re-trained in order to provide a more friendly and streamlined service to all arriving passengers. The very long delays and queues at this terminal are unacceptable and create an unfavourable impression, in particular for international travellers who are visiting Melbourne for events.

The airport is very poorly organised. I was transferring from international flight to domestic flight by Qantas and there was absolutely no signage or directions of which terminal should I be going. Despite from long waiting time of my luggage, I have tried to reach out help from the T1 terminal staff and Qantas staff because of the limited transit time. However, they are not helpful. I have talked to them about my situation and my luggage could not be checked in because of the machine issue. The self check in staff referred me to the economy queue staff and then to the special assistance staff after a long queue. My domestic flight was missed.

Not too bad an experience for a small airport. Not busy so my problem at the bag drop was quickly solved. My big gripe was that we could not refill our empty water bottle at a bubble. Could not find one after checking in. We were forced to buy a bottle of water for $4.20. Yes $4.20 for 600ml of water how idiotic is that?
I flew AirAsia into here from Kuala Lumpar. A friendly and efficient airport, the connecting bus had me in Melbourne in about the same time as to Tullamarine as there was no jerking about.

Worst airport experience in Australia. Long queues, incorrect baggage tagging, checked me in as a different person and worst of all, the discriminating attitude of the custom/immigration officers. Look a bit international, then you'll be a prime candidate to get abusive questions from different officers.

Avalon is a small airport outside of Melbourne. As it is small it is quite quick to get through immigration (on exit) and security. The best option is to get a bus from Southern Cross station and this helps as it meets the plane so you can get to Avalon with plenty of time. The new international departure area is big but with a few shops and a bit pricey. Not too bad with more international it may improve a bit.

Writing on behalf of dad who called me from within the terminal. My parents took 2 hours to come out. My dad was unable to locate a trolley and there was no help on the ground. He was unable to approach anybody and he also received no help to push my mother who needed assistance with a wheelchair. He was not able to push mum who finds it hard to walk due to a knee surgery, and pull their bags. After a long wait they finally walked out as they had no choice. There is a reason for one to request for wheelchair assistance. If support cannot be provided then don't provide the service.

I have never experienced such strictness in regards to carry on luggage. I had not only my partners laptop bag but also my hand bag. Has anyone ever had such ridiculous money grabbing methods used on them? Not only will I never fly to Avalon, I will never fly jetstar. Very disappointed!

Living in Geelong this airport is great! 20 mins from my parents place and traffic is rarely a problem. Check in is quick (quicker with no bags - check in online the night before) stroll through security and a short walk onto the plane. Only criticism is that the airport is small (3 gates) and only 1 bar 1 cafe and 1 newsagents. Hopefully with the new International terminal they're cleared to build they'll upgrade the domestic terminal too!

In my experience ground facilities showed little improvement. There is nothing to do unless you want gaming machines the food shows little imagination and is very expensive and you have to check-in long before departure. Then you have to climb up steps to the aircraft - difficult for someone with disabilities.

It's small and it's clean and it's easy to use. On arrival from the stairs hitting the plane door to my driving off in a hire car took me 12 mins - and that was with checked luggage. You can deal with the hire car people while waiting for your luggage and the car-hire parking spots are 30 seconds' walk from the terminal. Driving into Southern Melbourne took maybe 10 mins longer than it does from Tullamarine: it's further but the traffic's better. and you don't have to deal with the toll roads. On departure there were no queues and no delays. Food choices are limited and you have to pay for Wi-Fi access: those would be my only criticisms.

A very basic terminal. More like a tin shed with temporary stands for business counters. While it serves its purposes I hope that they improve terminal facilities and appearance given the increased levels of traffic. It can't be that hard to install proper car hire counters and have some coffee shop facilities in the arrivals section. When Albury airport has a better terminal facilities than Avalon you know it's time to improve!

Very small airport in Spanish African city of Melilla. Service seems to be limited to flights to Malaga, Madrid or Granada. In April, only eight departures all day. Choice of airlines was either Air Europa or Iberia. Exceptionally easy to check in. The two airline counters for Air Europa were staffed for the upcoming ATR flight to Malaga. As such, maybe 55 or so folks would be expected, even for a full flight. Check-in took all of two minutes. In the end, only about half the flight was full. Prices to Malaga were about $85 a person. Airport had a small cafeteria, shop and some related businesses. After check in, one security gate to navigate, then to a holding room for both airport gates, and then a walk out to the tarmac. No fuss, on the plane within 3 to 5 minutes.

Terrible security treatment. I took houmous with me. Security forbid me to take it with me. I offered to taste it, to show it’s real. She refused without any valid reason. Then she threatened to call the police and prevent me from flying. Absolutely unbelievable.

I booked a flight from IASI to LONDON. My two children, aged 3 and 11, and I arrived at Memmingen airport around 15:30. I attempted to communicate with airport staff, but unfortunately, none of them made an effort to assist me. This experience has been incredibly humiliating, unlike anything I have ever encountered before. It was a new country and I was just there to change flights, nothing more. Somehow, I managed to find my way to Gate and attempted to settle down there with my children. After arrival, we reached the check-in section following a 3-hour delay. There was staff who attended to me and my kids during check-in. Has displayed extremely disrespectful behaviour towards my son and then towards me. He was speaking in Germany, and I politely asked if he could speak English because I was leaving for to England. His behaviour was incredibly unprofessional. He made the offensive remark that I don't need to speak English and should instead learn German since I am in Germany. I mentioned that I didn't come here to visit; it's just a connecting flight. And I assume the same applies to the other people who were on the same flight as me. Later, he charged me for extra luggage, but I paid without any issues. Then, purely out of spite, he demanded that I pay for my backpack. I was surprised when I realised that I've been using the same backpack for all my travels in Europe, England, and even Turkey. I was never asked to pay for a bag for the flight. After witnessing my struggle, a fellow passenger behind me voiced the same concern. We all have identical bags, so will you be charging everyone? The staff confidently stated that he is fully capable of performing his job and should be allowed to do so. Since I provided him with suggestion on how to speak professionally with customers as well as interact correctly with children. He became furious. His colleague sitting beside him also advised him to relax. It was incredibly disheartening to experience such rudeness from someone, especially as a single mother with two children, who had been waiting for three hours in a new country where it seemed like no one was willing to offer assistance or communicate in English to help us. I am extremely frustrated with the behaviour of particular staff members who show a complete lack of respect for their job and the customers they serve. especially children.

Unfortunately this airport turned into a real nightmare over the last couple of years. The good thing first: -They are still able to attract airlines to open direct routes to various places, so you could technically save some time avoiding a stopover at a hub. -They offer free german newspapers for everyone. -Public WiFi is a bit slow, but straight forward and actually quite ok. -Very close to a highway, so it can be easily reached by car. The bad things: -Public Transport is probably one of the worst in the world. The connection to the train station is not meeting the demands and only runs at limited times. The transfer to Munich is done by a single operator with a very unreliable schedule, expect to depart Memmingen within 60 minutes of the scheduled departure time, the operator always waits for all booked passengers to arrive as there's no regular service and instead of expanding the service to accommodate delayed passengers, they just wait without any information. Why to blame the airport operator? Because they must be aware of it and they always have the chance to break the monopoly and allow a competitor as an alternative. But my guess is that the airport wants to focus solely on non aviation revenue and they dislike people who don't bring their own car, -The terminal is way too small to handle the amount of passengers, I don't know why the airport hasn't been facilitated by the german flight plan coordination office due to it's limited capacity. Obviously the management isn't really pro-aviation or into the seamless travel concept of the international aviation business. -Due to the amount of PAX handled at peak times, the terminal quickly turns into a dump yard, cleanliness is for sure a big issue here. -The airport doesn't even try to create a pleasant experience for the customers, the whole process is chaotic and I can recommend to arrive earlier than you would do at big airports like Munich or Vienna, as it consumes a lot of time to struggle through the mess. -Hotel availability is also very limited, they should focus on attracting some competitors, a proper Hilton or Accor branded hotel would be a blessing, also with the highway next door, as Memmingen is a little village and hospitality isn't their business. -Secondary airports always surprise when they come up with a night curfew, they prefer cancelling flights over waking up some cows or donkeys (it's in the middle of nowhere, there aren't many people living in the vicinity). Luckily it never happened to me as I avoid flights around the curfew, but sometimes you see passengers from the day before around the airport still waiting for their last days flight. -Staff is ok, but I think they have a lot of stress and need more patience and training, it's seems like most of the people do the job only to avoid unemployment benefits, not because they are good at what they do. To sum it up: If you can, pay the 100€ extra and choose a full service airport like Munich or Zurich with outstanding reliability and comfort. If you need a quick connection to a more remote place, Memmingen is an unavoidable option.

Literally one of the worst experiences in my life, never again. I never even thought that an international airport can be closed at night (23-3am), so that is also way I arrived late at the night ( with the trains is also hard, countless delays and no trains during the night to the airport...at the end it is really to be all night outside the airport or at the train station, yet I don't know which is better). So at the end everyone is waiting in the cold outside. For luck at least there is a toilet outside, so I guess it could have been worse. Still no security, no police, as a woman that makes you really unsure, for luck we (the women) just form a group and wait together, even when we don't speak same languages, just trying to make us feel more secure. I had a flight really early in the morning and it would be impossible for me to reach in time, when there are no trains in this direction at night. The hotels are full , also with the hotels around Memmingen is risky since you have to depend on the Deutsche Bahn, witch is not always a good idea, bc of the countless delays or the train not arriving at all.  I wouldn't recommend the airport especially if you have an early flight and couldn't find a hotel next to the airport. The hygiene in the toilets in the airport is really not the best, for example the toilets outside were cleaner and smelled better. Otherwise if you have a night or afternoon flight, I guess it is fine.

Arrival was satisfactory, maybe because we were the only aircraft at that time Departure was different. Check-in was quite quick and the agent was helpful. The queue for security was all across the building and took over an hour. Immigration was slow but acceptable. Airside lounges were very crowded, hard to find a seat. The airport is too small for the number of passengers. There used to be two aircraft stands, but now four (two remote), however the terminal has not been expanded in any way. A rather unpleasant experience.

This airport is way too small to handle so huge amount of passengers in its peak time. Security checks may take 2 hours easily. It doesn't fulfil its main purpose - to make travel fast and easy. Avoid especially if flying with connection here. You may get stuck.

Airport is simply not fit for the level of flights crammed I into a short window. The queue goes out the door along with any chance of getting to your gate within 90 minutes. They park the aircraft remotely and use a bus to transfer from terminal- so those that manage to make it through the queues just after the 30minutes cutoff literally “miss the bus”. No chance if any assistance from airport staff. Worth avoiding.
Bad and poor service. Staff with low experience and intelligence on how to spoke with passengers. Security with poor standards. Not recommend to anyone this terrible airport.
Very poor service and staff attitude. I do not recommend this airport to anyone. Arrogant and powerful staff. Dirty rooms and terrible internet speed.

I have used this airport for over 15 years as a regular visitor to family in Landsberg. Staff on reception desks, security and passport control were excellent. Unfortunately the Fellowes catering operation on the 1st floor is appalling, I submitted a complaint regarding filled bagels on my last trip in December 2018 regarding dry, tough bread, unbuttered chicken and avocado filling devoid of filling. Unable to complain at time as take away for flight. Complained to Chief Exec Customer services and still awaiting a reply.

Yesterday, 5/14/24, we arrived at Memphis airport at 4:55am for 6:05 am flight to Philadelphia.
