Upon receiving our boarding passes at the kiosk, we noticed a long line of at least 500 passengers waiting to pass through security. The line seemed endless, and we later found out that the airport only had four security checkpoints for over 12 flights scheduled to depart between 6am and 7:30am. When we inquired about the delay, TSA claimed they were not responsible, despite the airline attendant mentioning that TSA's understaffing had been an ongoing issue for morning flights. Due to the long wait, we missed our flight by 11 minutes and were rebooked on a connecting flight to Philly via Charlotte. Shockingly, 70 other passengers (fact) also missed their flight to Charlotte from Memphis. My advice to others is to arrive at least 2 1/2 hours early for flights departing from Memphis. The understaffed TSA seemed indifferent to the chaos, and there were confrontations in the line. Many latecomers appeared distressed, and there was even a member of the Memphis SWAT team present to maintain order before passengers entered the security checkpoint. Good luck! Side note: Huge shout out to Rejoice, the Gate Attendant at American Airlines, for having the patience of a SAINT and getting us on the next connecting flight to Charlotte!

Great MEM airport. This airplane has been here for hours. We’ve been loaded for 30 minutes. Waiting for fuel. Apparently they only have one damned small fuel truck. He fuels a commuter jet and has to go back to the farm before he can do a second one. Fantastic. Crew had to wait 3 hours last night for fuel. Somebody needs to fix this place. Nice terminal but management and operations suck at their jobs.

The airport itself is tidy and seems pleasant. Being a solo traveler with hidden disabilities, I am very pleased with the staff who were able to assist me. They were helpful and kind. So far on my departures, the ques haven't been too long a wait or crazy, timely manner in my experience. Look forward to coming back again as I'm a frequent flyer to this airport.

Appalling Covid prevention measures at the airport. Crowding at security with new rules about food, slowing the process because of confusion about what needs to be removed . No social distancing guidelines at gate and no mask enforcement. People sit wherever they like and pull masks down. I am truly shocked at how Memphis airport operates at the times when there is a mandatory mask mandate in place, and all good businesses work toward social distancing. Would not recommend flying out of Memphis any time soon.
Check in staff was very rude. Team Sports food service was horrible. Lost my order and did nothing to apologize. Time is a factor but they apparently don’t care. Do not go there!

Memphis is always the city I depart whenever my family decides to go on a trip. The service has always been pleasant along with the low-cost airlines it has been adding, though, after the KLM flight to Amsterdam ended along with Delta dehubbing, Memphis, MEM, has been on a downslope with direct flight routes and still is. MEM urgently needs a new international flight, although I think MEM could potentially surpass the Delta/KLM days by its amazing service. Keep it up MEM.

A very friendly team of airport workers overall. Southern hospitality goes a long way. Would like to see more dining options and shops that are not all identical in product choices. Overall a very good experience. Would definitely fly to Memphis again without hesitation.

A very friendly team of staff overall at Memphis Airport. Southern hospitality goes a long way. Would like to see more dining options and shops that are not all identical in product choices. Overall a very good experience. Would definitely fly to Memphis again without hesitation

Departure from Memphis. The airport was ok. I regard it as the best airport I experienced during my trip - much better than Newark (EWR) and better than Chicago O'Hare (ORD). The stores and restaurants was plentiful, but the airport is quite small. The staff was friendly and efficient. It was also quite clean, much better than the other airports I passed through this trip in the USA. It was easy to navigate through too. Many small airports are better than their reputation.
his airport offers easy entry and exit for domestic flights but lacks a Priority Plus lounge. Car rental is on the airport site - the most convenient (for Alamo) I have ever found.

MEX consists of two terminals, with Aeromexico, Delta, Copa, and LATAM taking up the newer Terminal 2 and everyone else essentially taking up Terminal 1. Terminal 2 is definitely more user-friendly, with Terminal 1 being well over capacity. This honestly I don’t think will change given that it’s proximity to the center of Mexico City makes it quite convenient in spite of it’s shortcomings.

Word of advice, if you plan on purchasing anything whatsoever after you're awaiting your flight by the gate (after security/baggage check-in), do yourself a favor and keep some of that Mexican currency. Naturally, to save time you may opt to hit the first window, to get your native currency exchanged back before going through baggage & security on the way to your gate. Here's the con. It's common for you to want a beverage, snack, etc to bring on board, right? The businesses are purposely giving you less than the exchange rate, when you pay them in your native currency (USD for example). One employee at the Le Pain Quotidien flat out admitted it to me like it was normal! It's a double dip into your pockets with that and the fact that airports charge more money for items than they would on Wall Street. Be a better person to your pockets and just eat a big meal beforehand because they're not going to tell you there's another exchange on the other side. It makes sense considering the efficiency of the airport employees is seriously something to be desired.

I’ve been through this airport a dozen times, and it is a disaster. It’s hot, dirty, disorganized and always late. They broadcast the departure times on screens that have dozens of advertising so you have to wait you til the carousel finishes advertising to you before you can run to your gate. I have never taken a flight here that has arrived or left on time. Having traveled to 60 countries in the world and at least 10 airports in Mexico, this one is the absolute worst.

I’ve traveled all around the world and this has to be one of the worst airports I have traveled through. Customs is a mess, there are no boarding screens to determine your gate when you arrive, and though they have charging stations everywhere, not a single one actually works. I did the math- there are over 240 charging ports that do absolutely nothing. It’s also just incredibly saturated- all times of day, it is packed with people. Additionally the diesel fumes are poignant throughout the terminals. If you’re able to travel through a different airport, it’s probably worth it; this is certainly not a favorite airport of mine.

This airport is the worst place l ever been to. People in security, immigration and mostly everywhere are rude. There is no AC, it stinks, there is no water to flush the toilets and it is so unorganized. Really disgusting. Basically security people make their own stupid rules if they want to keep a duty free product you have acquired somewhere else. I will start buying tickets where l can do transit at a different airport

The worst airport for transit and rude personal! We had to transfer in Mexico city airport and it was a pure disaster. First, we had to do immigration which makes no sense and waited over 1.5h in line. After you had to pick up your luggage, go through the scanner. The lady by the security scanner said something to me in Spanish and I didn't understand, for what she replied very rudely "You are in Mexico, why you come here if you don't speak Spanish" - in an he international airport! And I don't even go to Mexico, it was just a transfer! We were traveling with kids and have car seats, well, apparently if you have car seats or any oversized luggage you have to carry it upstairs and do the check in again! Isn't it crazy? And then again to go through security check one more time. Most of the personal treated us very rudely without explaining what needs to be done. No clear signs, no directions. Never again!

Has to be the worst airport ever. Unhelpful, rude security staff making heavy weather of pointless checks for transit passengers. Why do we have to go through passport control on transit, Europe and Asia do not do this. Insufficient seating. Just grim. Fortunately I won't be back

Unhelpful, Disorganized Was on a layover from Amsterdam to Toronto, Canada. I arrived through KLM airlines, but my luggage didn't. When I asked about my luggage, the luggage staff said they transferred it to my next flight, which they don't do, and my itinerary said "baggage not checked through". When I left luggage collection and went to the check in area, I asked a staff member if they could confirm it was sent through and they said with certainty that they would not have transferred my luggage and to go check again. I went back to check again, but security would not let me back into the luggage area. I told them the story and without even looking at my flight itinerary said it was transferred to my next flight (I had no contact with this security officer before, nor did they know anything about my situation prior). Now to be clear, it's almost certain that KLM lost my luggage, and it's not the luggage handlers' problem. But for them to just lie about it to get rid of me is unacceptable. They could have said it appears it didn't arrive and that's fine. I can't blame them for that. But I just essentially went back and forth between people in the airport not knowing who was telling the truth, or who knows what they're talking about. I don't expect Mexico City airport to be the best airport in the world, but to be an international airport that essentially has no centralized information center, and to have employees who just lie to get rid of you is really unacceptable (I'm sure they don't get paid the most and I get that).

The rude security check by an entitled, inexperienced, careless, rude, extremely poorly trained young man who seemed too bored and just wanted to humiliate and degrade an old person completely, ruined my nice two week holiday in Mexico City. First he touched every single item in my suite case including my personal hygiene items and underwear. Then he had me take out ALL the contents of my carry on bag without providing me with adequate bins. My stuff was all over the place. He wanted to check the lining of the suitcase, even though it was very evident that there was nothing in there. He ran the empty suitcase through the x-ray machine again and he was still not satisfied and wanted to humiliate me further. A couple of his colleagues who were older female Security Check personnel were wondering about his behaviour. I think he was just bored and wanted to get a kick from humiliating and upsetting an older person. This incident has made me reconsider my good opinion of Mexico and makes me extremely reluctant to ever want to go there again. Why can't they provide some training or have a responsible surpervisor who can control the disgusting and hurtful actions of these out-of-control personnel who only want to humiliate and degrade travellers. It appears that no one in Mexico City Airport cares about the conditions of the airport so I am only writing this to warm other travellers to expect the worst experience of their lives when leaving the Mexico City Airport.

Unquestionably one of the world's worst airports to transit in particularly of you have to change terminals. I came into T2 on AM and flew out of T1 on AF. It's so poorly conceived it's beyond belief. Why they'd have AM in T2 and all of the SkyTeam partners in T1 necessitating an absurdly long, difficult transit is simply absurd. You need to clear customs then recheck your bags, walk one football field to get the train to T1. Once you get to T1 it's another 2 football fields to get to your airline check in desk and then 2 more to the gate. Complete nightmare. Once in the terminal you can find plenty of small bottles of water for USD 5 and Mexico world cup kit for USD 125 , all well above market prices in most of tye world and certainly in Mexico. This place is a shameful disgrace and avoid at any cost.

How is this the airport in one of the most expensive cities in the US? Wifi didn‘t work, there were only two  food options and one of them didn‘t even have a vegetarian option and in a lot of gates people were sitting on the floor!

Absolutely no seats, at 1 gate there was an entire space of nothing. So many people were sitting on the dirty floor. Long lines everywhere, not any good food options, and it wasn’t even that clean, rather get re-routed! Avoid Miami Airport.

One of the security guards at H7 went out of her way to delay my flight by removing my things from the queue just because I asked a question to understand one of the steps she mentioned we need to follow. The job could be hard and requires thick skin as she may have to explain the same things again and again all day, but from it would good to have someone a bit friendly in location where they need to interact with customers.

The airport was dirty, floors with food everywhere. One restaurant in the entire area after you get through security and the food was terrible. Not enough seating in terminal areas and seats on terminal were dirty as well. Security process was fast

When we arrived on Thursday afternoon none of the elevators were working or the walking escalators. Nothing is well labeled so we couldn’t find our badge terminal and ended up at international baggage. When you ask staff no one seems to know where to find Alaska. We stopped for a burger at Burger King and had to wait for staff to finish their 5 min conversation. Then had to wait till she completed the line that had formed before she loaded our food which was cold by the time she got to it. Then after we finally found our baggage we had to find the rental car shuttle. Nothing labeled easy to find so we had to go up and down stairs multiple times to find it. Again no one who works at airport seemed to know where we needed to be to get rental car. Finally found it then found shuttle. Then when we got to the rental car area not well labeled what shuttle stop is for our rental car place; Priceless. The exact same miserable experience was when we returned to go home that following Monday. No walking escalators working. No one knew where our gate was and no one knew where our lounge was. We asked 5 different people who worked for airport one of whom was a TSA agent. Nothing well labeled and no helpful staff. Tried to find a filling station for our water and again none to be found by restrooms and again no one knows.  You know it’s bad when security check was the only smooth spot in this airport.

The layout is laughably stupid and pointlessly confusing. The terminals have far too few chairs. The TSA security check is quite literally at a 45° angle downwards so, when you are waiting in line (staring at the repulsive floor with litter and zyn packs scattered about), you are forced to struggle with your suitcase to keep it from rolling away. Once you struggle to get to the screening area, it is hideously disordered and the bag collecting area has room for 3 people max. When we had recently arrived at the airport, the security officer we asked for directions (due to the aforementioned pointlessly confusing layout) informed us that because our flight was not for quite some time, we would not be able to go through the TSA check and therefore had to stay in the "front area." (I put it in quotes because the layout is so stupid I cannot in good faith call it the "front"). This was, as we later found out, false. While maybe another officer knew better then he, we could not find another that spoke English.  All in all, sufficient to say, we will never return to MIA and I recommend you to do the same.

Arriving at Miami International Airport to return to Rome, we had the invaluable assistance at the automatic check-in before the Air Canada desk, so I don't think an Air Canada employee, helped us so much to understand how we had to make our boarding passes and what to do with our luggage. Thanks to him the passage through this airport seemed delightful.

A lot of staff were aggressive, rude and condescending, even those who are in the restaurants! Signages and Instructions for the queues are not available. Not enough seating areas. Wifi is good, though.

Miami Airport is hands down the worst airport experience I’ve ever endured. From the moment we landed, it was a nightmare. The staff are shockingly rude, with a special mention to the police officer at immigration—condescending and unprofessional, he treated us as if we were a nuisance rather than travelers. The airport itself feels neglected and outdated, as if it’s been stuck in some third-world time warp. Broken facilities, confusing signage, and chaotic lines create an atmosphere of constant stress and frustration. The inefficiency is staggering, with painfully slow processing that leaves you trapped in what feels like a never-ending maze of incompetence. If you’re planning on flying through Miami, be prepared for an absolute disaster. This airport is the definition of a travel nightmare, I wouldn’t wish on anyone. The staff would get zero stars if that were possible.

For a large international airport it seems very badly run, the places needs a lot of TLC. I had watched YouTube clips 5 months before using airport and I was naive and thought that the travelators which were broken in the clip would be working when I arrived 5 months later!! no such luck. We were flying out of J section and there was a huge queue for passport control which we queued in got right to the front to be told by the lady there it was closing and to use another one at the end of the building!! so had to go to that one. I suffer with bad hips and knees so all this walking was beginning to take a toll on me. What a shambles, will not use again.

When waiting overnight for an early flight it is cold, dirty and unfriendly. There are no comfortable seats to relax on and staff keep waking you up and moving you around for no good reason. The toilets are situated downstairs forcing you to use the escalator. Why can't soft, lengthy seats be provided for the many travellers spending the night there waiting for early flights?

The security person that checked me was so rude. I went through the body scanner and it beeped which it was not a surprise, it was always happens to me for some reason and she shouted for me to take my shoes off and go again through it. Then during the search done by hand she even lifted my top up without even asking, resulting in me being almost half naked in front of everyone. I would not recommend this airport at all as I never had such a bad experience in any airports I have been to. The pros are that the food is generally good there and there are lots of shops, so if you have time to kill, it is a good airport for that.

Baggage arrived 50 minutes after the flight arrived. Security personnel would not prioritise me as my lay over was 80 minutes only and time was running out fast. When I arrived at the gate, the ladies did not let me through as they said the gate was closed. At the same time people we still boarding the flight - many hours wasted and I had to pay with my time, plans and money.
I had special assistance booked here. The check in staff were incredibly kind and helpful and the assistance staff were fantastic. Could not fault my experience.

An airport for shopping and not for people. Departing July 21 all planes delayed. People everywhere and no seating capacity; travellers had to sit or lay on the floor. Absurdly there was a man playing a piano in a large room with no seats at all. Avoid this place when travelling. The total neglect of needs of passengers and especially those of children and elderly travellers is appalling.

Twice I have traveled through this airport with my mother who needed a wheelchair as she cannot walk the long distances to the gate without getting out of breath and risk of heart issues. Our flight was leaving at 7 am so arriving at 4 am is useless as the Sala Amica staff do not start until 5 am. The totem where they ask you to register to request assistance also had no one answering so it was very worrying for Mum and frustrating for me. The staff were friendly but it's ridiculous to have flights coming and going with no Sala Amica staff available. Mum had to walk with us helping her from the car to the check-in desk which was a ridiculous distance when someone has difficulty. As her carer, it was possible to ask to go with Mum, and agreed. Bergamo Airport please review how you support people with reduced mobility so you are available 3 hours before flights leave otherwise you are putting people at risk physically and psychologically. Also there is no time for passengers using the Sala Amica to get Duty Free shopping or use the facilities such as toilets and cafes. This is an added stress and also reduces potential sales for the airport and the travel experience is poor. It's good the cafes are open all night at least.

While waiting for passport control I felt very hot and dizzy. I asked a make member of staff if I could have some water. He got me through security, got me water and made sure I was ok. Very helpful and I wish I knew his name to thank him.

I am a disabled lady travelling with my husband who is my Carer. We arrived 2 hours before our flight as advised by Ryan Air. We sat and waited an hour before help arrived. One lady pushing two wheelchairs for different flights. We passed thru check in, security and then arrived at passport control at the gate where my husband was told this is as far as you go with your wife, now you go to the gate and you will see your wife on the plane. We said he should be with me as my carer but was advised this was not allowed at Bergamo. I was whisked away to a lounge which had a large room and a small room. I was put in the small room in my wheelchair along with many others, a tv was blaring away. The staff were stretched out in the larger room watching tv! I needed the toilet but my husband wasn’t there to help so had to struggle my way to it. When I came out I saw my flight was boarding, in 10 minutes I was told. My husband phoned me and said he was on the plane. I was then fetched and was pushed and shoved to the lift outside, then had to wait while they fetched other disabled passengers. Then was again shoved and pushed on to the lift. I felt degraded. There were four of us for different flights. We got to my flight who was waiting just for me. My husband was frantic wondering where I was and what was happening. We were so late he thought the flight was leaving without me!! I have never been treated so inhumanely!!! It was a disgrace, you do not treat disabled people like this in the modern world. I had no idea what was going on, I rely on my husband for all things and you removed my only support!! I was in tears. Bergamo and it’s staff need to improve 100%.

Absolutely shocking service. My daughter queued for 45 minutes at McDonald’s only to be told they had sold out of what she wanted. No idea of customer service or using common sense like managing the queue and letting people know they were on limited stock prior to entering the queue

This is a "3rd world" airport not an airport in EU and "capital of fashion"! Bathrooms are very dirty, everything is dirty, few stores with old perfumes for example, few restaurants, few cafe, not organized...really I saw stalls looking better! Just transit but never again! Few years ago I was in Napoli....guess Italians are the same as their airports.

Upon arrival, we attempted to check in our suitcases. The lady at the desk refused to let my husband check in a suitcase with a laptop in it, she attempted to verify this by showing him a laminated piece of paper explaining what you are allowed to take in your hand luggage and what must be checked in. What she also attempted to do was hide the laptop icon under her thumb under the heading 'items allowed in hand luggage.' When my husband pointed this out she became somewhat indignant and refused to admit she had made a mistake. She wasn't able to verify her point, but out of consideration for the queue behind us he took out the laptop and put it in his hand luggage. Only then were we allowed to check in our bags. At security I had problems getting through as staff didn't know what a freestyle libre sensor is (for diabetics). I showed the lady, at the magnetic scanners, my sensor and explained going through an electromagnetic port could damage the sensor making it impossible for me to check my blood sugars. She was very understanding and went to discuss this with a male colleague, who refused to let me be checked by hand. It was only when I threatened to hold him personally responsible for me not being able to check my blood sugars, should the sensor be damaged, that he allowed me through. Another female employee checked me and let me through, she was very understanding and helpful! In the departures lounge we wanted to test some perfumes. What we noticed was that staff were uninterested in helping people willing to shop, if anything we got the feeling that we were' not important enough' to be helped. They were clearly too busy chatting amongst themselves to actually do what they are paid to do. Staff were arrogant, lazy and quite honestly they didn't have a meaningful function in the duty free lounge. We wanted to eat something before we left, this proved to also be quite a challenge. We wanted to order two sandwiches, instead of being helped we got told that the till was closed... and that was it. No explanation of where we could pay, as the self service portal was also out of order. The lady that told us that the till was closed simply walked away and continued to chat with her colleague, ignoring paying customers. At this point our tempers were staring to bubble up a little, I ended up asking in a somewhat agitated manner where on earth we were supposed to pay then? In the end we got our food. At this point we were do fed up we decided we were done with Milan Linate airport, we will fly from Malpensa next time. Our overall impression of Milan Linate airport was that staff were rude, disorganised and unmotivated. By far the worst airport experience we have ever had. The two ladies that helped me at the security check were their only saving grace.

Security was good because you didn’t have to get liquids or electronics out of your bag. Airport was clean and spacious. My one huge complaint however is the service in Autogrill Italia. The staff member asked me if I would like to pay 15 times without putting it through to the card machine. She would just point at it and then say “PAY?”. There was a language barrier but I feel there may have been an intelligence barrier because I stood there for 3 mins wanting to pay and not being able to.

The best thing of this airport is that it is incredibly near to the city centre. Normally it is a breeze getting there or arriving, as in no time you are at destination if you need to be in Milan or get on a train (or arriving) at Milan’s main station. Only thing really weird is how on departure, after the security check, they guide you by all shops: you really have no possibility to take any shortcut.

If you are thinking of making a transit at Milan Linate, think again! There is no dedicated transfer route through the airport so you have to leave the baggage hall, find your way upstairs to Departures and go through security all over again. On Monday we arrived 30 minutes late from Naples. Stopover time was scheduled at 1 hour 5 minutes, so catching our next flight to London was still possible..at a pinch. We get ferried from aircraft by bus, go through baggage hall, take the escalator up to Departures and find a long, long queue to get through Security. Fortunately, we had booked Fast Track. No queue, but problems with the boarding pass scanners. Ran through the newly extended Duty Free obstacle course and made it to the Gate with two minutes to spare. The airline had held departure for ourselves and two other passengers. So, we made it, breathless and stressed. I see that there have been previous posts here about the lack of an easy transit route. It's bonkers that the airport authority still hasn't managed to provide one. If we'd not had a Fast Track booking we wouldn't have made the second flight. Be warned!!

My glasses were broken on security line and i was rejected a reimbursement! On the security check we were asked to put everything (including the sunglasses) in the basket. While the basket was inside the machine something went wrong and my sunglasses got stuck inside. The head of security guard took broken sunglasses out, apologised and promised that we are gonna receive the reimbursement. We filed a form but customer relations declined their liability (though it was confirmed by the head of security) and ignore our emails!

Sneering, lazy rude staff, rancid food, no English, dirty, no charging points, rubbish shopping, no information, inadequate seating, no ambience whatsoever. Staff have clearly never done a days customer service in their life or it didn’t work. In B gate area I was sold a rancid fruit salad, I took it back got given another rancid replacement I took it back again. She carefully hid my discarded fruit salads out of public overflowing trash bin sight. The rest will be still on sale for the next year as far as I know. Would be closed down in the UK. Got espresso coffee given to me as compensation. I would have preferred a cappuccino but never mind.

As a single female traveller, to be intimidated and shouted at by security is terrifying. Luckily, a male passenger on my flight care to my rescue. I still don't know what I did to incur the wrath of this security guard who came up and started shouting at me ‘what are you doing? What are you doing? You idiot? Why did you do that?’ His colleague was standing there laughing. I still have no idea what he thinks I did. Traumatic. And complaining to the airport afterwards will get me nowhere.

We arrived at the check-in at 9.50. We finally checked in at 10.20. Firstly the "computer was slow", then it broke down completely. Our flight was at 11.20, so by the time we got through security and grabbed a cup of coffee people were already boarding. While still sipping my coffee I had to run to the toilet. We were up at 5 am and left our hotel at 6 am. This airport is a joke.

Miserable security experience with surly underemployed staff. One undersized table available at the end of each queue to repack your belongings once they pass through the scanner. Combine that with poor shopping opportunities and food outlets and a generally oppresive environment makes for travelling through Linate one of life's must miss experiences. As someone who used to travel very regularly through Linate I can safely say there has been no improvement (or investment) in the airport and facilities over the last 10 years.

Awfully rude and highly aggressive airport security personnel. What is a simple relatively quick body search after putting your clothes and laptop into the trollies turned into a highly aggressive pantomime act by one of the personnel who was conducting this. I took offense to his behaviour and informed him of this to which he became even more aggressive to me. In the end one of the managers had to be called. Only happened to me in this airport. As a result I won't ever come to visit Italy ever again.

Just wish to say that the check in and wheelchair assistance at Malpensa was really excellent and one of the best that I have experienced as a recent wheelchair traveller. Staff were very helpful and efficient. The only issue that I would raise is the state of the toilets.
Not enough seating for eating or at the gate. Bathroom facilities woefully lacking. Not enough and lacking in hygiene. Not impressed compared to other European airports.

This airport is a complete disgrace. There are a very few seats for passengers, a tiny number of toilets and therefore large queues. Information is difficult to find resulting in going through passport control more than once and the whole experience is an ordeal. At the gate we were standing there for an hour waiting to board. Why are there so few seats, there is plenty of room? I would give it 1 out of 10.

I was afraid about leaving just before mid August, in the peak holiday season. Instead everything was fine. Security checks were really fast, and for passport control we waited 10 minutes. All in all a smooth experience, and plenty of places to have some snack or drink before boarding.

The rudest agents I have ever seen. I asked a lady who was standing and clearly had a badge saying “agent”, where the Air Canada check-in was and she yelled “Oh My God! I’m not information!!!” Another walked away as I approached her and I said “excuse me! I’m a passenger!” She turned around, rolled her eyes, sighed, and said “yes?” These people shouldn’t be working with the public.

Malpensa Airport is not International enough to call it International Airport. The first time losing my luggage happened here with NEOS airline. And can’t seem to find anyone knows what’s going on. We finally reported to lost & found.  On our departure date, we experienced how indifferent the airport staff are. We almost missed our flight, the line to security is at least 1.5 hrs long. And since we had a Young Child with us, we had to go through all passports instead of the quick line for no visa access.  I tried to communicate with the lady and the gentleman working on the quick lane, we are missing our flight. They didn’t seem to care at all.  At the end we had to talk to all the passengers ahead of us to skip the line. God bless all these nice ppl. and the lady staff stood at the security glanced at my bag from duty free, made a comment that “you had time to shop in duty free”. I mean who are you the judge if I bought a few boxes of chocolates for my daughter? You didn’t help me and i don’t need your judgement now! Not impressed by the airport staff’s customer service if there’s any at all.

Each time I come back to Milan Malpensa from other airports I long for the quick and modern security checks installed here. I left on the evening of a small holiday period and there were thousands of travellers. Despite this the security checks (at Terminal 1) handled the crowd without problems, we waited about 12 min for the whole process. Being able to carry liquids, to leave computers in the bags mean really accelerating the flow and guaranteeing a quick check. After that the airport is nice, there are seats to wait before boarding, a lot of shops and restaurants; possibly some more gates should be added.

No seating when you pass security control, everyone sitting on long steel pole, plenty of room to put seating in place, no idea why management have not thought of this, terrible for people waiting. Also water filter would be useful like most airports.

People don't know what service means. We have been waiting in the arrival hall for an hour for our bags to come. No one in charge no information. Οι άνθρωποι δεν ξέρουν τι σημαίνει εξυπηρέτηση ...Περιμένουμε στη αίθουσα αφίξεως εδώ και μία ώρα για να έρθουν οι ταξιδιωτικές μας βαλίτσες... Κανένας υπεύθυνος καμία ενημέρωση.

Airport staff very friendly and helpful but airport is actually the modern building with a minor older satellite terminal from where a low cost company exclusively operates. It needs better - highlited signals.

Mildura Airport is the 3rd busiest airport in Victoria (Australia) and is serviced by three airlines: Virgin Australia, QantasLink, and of course Rex. It has three gates, a great bar, really clean check in and the people are nice with the perfect amount of seats. They do not have aerobridges (obiously) a really modern airport, its just great.

Airport was clean and great but would like to complain about the customer service of check in passage. There was problems with my check in and although I understand that it's not their fault, their attitude just stuck into me. Really offended when they ask me if I have a business black card and when I say no, they just gave me customer service card and told me to call even though I was right there. I understand that it may be useful to some situation, but the way they handle and the tone is just really unprofessional. I saw several people just standing behind the door seemingly free and on purpose trying to avoid me. Not even mad, just disappointed.

Busiest I have ever seen the airport. TSA, with a huge line of people, closed 3 lanes creating a major backlog and then no agent directing people about the policy of the day - laptops in or out, etc. Only one scan machine so even once your bags went through security you were stuck behind 15 people waiting on the scanner. Walking through Concourse D they removed all water fountains and replaced with vending machines. One water fountain in the entire concourse. Couldn’t find anyone who works there to help find a water fountain. Busy weekday late afternoon/early evening and more than half of the vendors are closed so everyone goes to the same few, causing service lines out onto the concourse and subsequent traffic jams. Essentially they were ill equipped to handle the volume of passengers.

I cannot say enough positive things about the staff at the Delta part of this airport. I had badly hurt my knee at Logan and I was to have a wheelchair to take me up the ramp to the luggage return. When I got to the walkway there was no wheelchair. The flight attendant called to the desk who apologized and said they would get one to me asap. Within a minute, literally, the manager on duty was there beside me. He was absolutely wonderful! He was on the walkie talkie, tried to help me get up the ramp some and we both gave up. The flight attendants and even the pilot were attempting to help me get to the terminal. Finally biting the bullet, the manager got me up there just in time for another young man to arrive with the wheelchair. He was sweet, friendly and so very helpful. We had an Uber coming and he got our luggage and took us to wait for the Uber. These men and women are to be commended for their kindness and dedication to the passengers! Kudos to all!

Milwaukee is a great airport to spend a couple of hours in. Decent food selection, a great in-terminal aviation museum and the most incredible airport (used) bookstore I've experienced. Wish I had brought another carry-on bag as I could have filled the thing with all the great books at reasonable prices I wanted to buy.

BOS-MKE. I have flown to and from Mitchell countless times. I grew up in Milwaukee and moved back here in June. I agree with other reviewers that it is a clean, friendly well-run airport. What stuck in my mind was how swiftly and well the baggage is handled. I flew Southwest and sat fairly far forward in the cabin, walked directly to the baggage claim area, and by the time I arrived, my baggage was already on the carousel. This is something of a record in all of the flights I have experienced over the past few years (at the other end is Copenhagen Kastrup in July, where I waited close to 45 minutes for the baggage to arrive, with my own valise arriving some 10 minutes later). There is also a rapid bus to downtown, with the stop now just outside the baggage claim area, now that renovations of that area are completed. There are also a couple of good Bartolotta restaurants on the concourses (Piccolo Pizzeria and Nonna Bartolotta's), which I have enjoyed on previous departures. All in all, Mitchell is an excellent airport. Now, all they need is more non-stop flights.

Big enough to serve all of your needs yet small enough and easy enough to get in and out of. What a contrast when compared to Kansas City and Atlanta where my journey originated. They have a children's play area, great local restaurants, beers, coffee etc.  It is about the same airfare to fly into Milwaukee often times as it is to fly into Chicago with a lot less hassle.

Loved flying into Milwaukee. We flew in from DC with AirTran to attend our daughters naval bootcamp graduation and what an excellent airport. It was a short 40 minute drive to North Chicago. We even loved the enterprise rental car pick-up/drop-off. I highly recommend this airport.

General Mitchell is a breath of a fresh air. It's clean friendly and efficient. There's actually a classy little used book store and a museum full of model planes and blimps and whatnot. If you get lost it is your fault my friend. The whole place is like one of the models in the museum - accurate well labeled and miniature. Everything is right in front of you. There's an Amtrak station a block away - 90 minutes and $24 to get to Union Station in Chicago is hard to beat. This airport is tiny but it's the easiest one I've ever dealt with.

This is possibly one of the nicest airports I've flown through. Staff were amiable the terminals were clean and well-maintained and everything was well-marked. Security was a breeze and the baggage claim system is both swift and efficient compared to other airports.

One of my favorite airports to make a connection through. I've flown through MKE maybe 30 times or so and never have had to wait in a line to go through security. There is also a very nice bookstore decent food options nice play areas for kids and an aviation museum. The airport is also fairly stress free for making connections.

Upon arrival at MRV, discovered a new arrivals hall since my last visit in October last year. Baggage very quick into hall. Outside, a pleasant array of kiosks should you need anything food wise. Departures hall is spotless and some nice Caucasian shops to spend your Rubles in. Security quick and easy and departure lounge has a nice cafe and a few more shops. A pleasant experience before the hassle of Domodedevo.

Horrible experience! The Delta airline did such a great job getting us 15 minutes earlier so we can get in time to our connecting flight, but MSP airport didn’t have the ramp ready, so we got off late, the agent at gate said the cart can take us to the other side of the airport, well the cart driver said it wasn’t his problem, when asked what is the best way to get there faster, he said he didn’t know, the other cart driver who again refused to take us, sent us the wrong way. You gotta do much better training your employees to first treat travelers with a little more kindness and compassion because a lot of us travel in stress and and really would like to see a little more help from the people who supposedly should know at least how to navigate through the airport. The worst part was to see the same cart driver took other people to the same flight as we (me and two of my underage daughters) were approaching the gate in sweat and almost tears … this was extremely frustrating to see that, even harder to try and explain to my kids why this unjust thing happened. This is completely unacceptable MSP. Please do better job at getting your employees to be a little more helpful and kind, or at least fair. If you reject taking someone to the other side of the terminal, please don’t go ahead and just take the next (completely healthy and not old) family to the same place where the first ones are heading.

Our Amsterdam flight arrived at time precisely. 1.5 hours wait on the tarmac because of the gate agent, because of other reasons. In the international arrival hall > 500 people, 3 officers to check passports, > 2 hours waiting. In civilized countries, usually helpers are asking passengers about tight connections and help them through to catch their flights. The assistants here were few and could not care less about us. The luggage’s checked in and out for customs - the re- check points with other assistants (watching their phones) directing passengers how to put their luggage on the right position - not helping or moving a finger in the process. Security - same rude treatment: we supposed to push our bags through the tunnel - at the flashing red light - who would know? workers standing there and screaming at us, not helping at all. I had to run like crazy to catch my flight and I would have never be able to do it without the help of a kind fellow passenger. Shame on the management to allow this to happen. “Welcome to the USA “ was written on monitors. It was a mess and a far cry from anything welcoming. I will try never to go through that airport again.

TSA line was long. The wait said it was 25 minute but it was 45 minutes. TSA security check didn’t say a word to get the process moving. They don’t tell anyone to take off their shoes or about electronics to be prepared. Everyone was upset because they didn’t communicate which made the process longer. One person was yelling at someone in a wheelchair.

You be prepared to walk a lot. Then at the Arrivals/Baggage Claim the cars are double, triple parked and will sit there for 20, 30, 40 minutes blocking traffic and making it impossible to load your car. We saw some cars just sitting there for over an hour while our man went to get our rental car. Security is non-existant, we never saw a guard until some dude threatened us while we were trying to back our car in to load, then one slow-witted airport security dude shows up, and basically does nothing because "that's always how it is here...and I'm supposed to be on my break." Eventually four real police arrived to deal with a situation that never should have happened in the first place. Try double parking at LAX Arrivals for longer than three minutes and see what happens. Stop letting people quadruple park at Arrivals before someone gets violent, because it will happen eventually if it hasn't yet. This airport is obviously poorly managed, and security is lazy.

I normally don’t review, however my experience at the Minneapolis airport was the worst experience I’ve had at any airport I’ve traveled to. I agree with other reviewers, if you can fly somewhere else, do that. The rudeness I encountered from the staff made me feel belittled, unwelcome, and left me shocked. We pay a lot of money to fly through your airport. And then, if you do try and say anything to any workers, about how awful they're treating you, your in the wrong because they work there. That’s not right.

So getting checked in and boarding is easy. It's the customs that can't get things figured out. You know how many planes are arriving, and how many people are on each flight, then you should have enough staff to move people in a timely fashion. Yet the simplest jobs your in a 3hr waiting line. Go somewhere else if you can.

We are on a layover from Cancun to Portland, the deboarding, customs area had one, filthy gross restroom. The Delta wing of the airport has very few restaurants choices or shops to browse/entertainment while stuck here. We ate at Mill Tavern, although the customer service was great, the food was not, very few choices and very over priced. They offered to remake my burger as the first one was too raw, the second was cooked done, it was just wasn't good, fries soggy and flavorless. Airport restrooms unkept, poor food choices and/or restaurants with comfortable seating to waiting. Hope I don't have to visit this place again!

Security is a big deal, and everyone just wants to get though the most efficient way possible, but I have never seen such a disrespectful, ill-tempered employee ordering passengers about as I did today at Security checkpoint 1. I witnessed an extremely elderly couple arrive at the TSA que. They were traveling alone and obviously had trouble getting around. They did not have the correct boarding documents, but instead of showing compassion, or helpfulness, the airport employee yelled at them and told them to get out of line & go back to the ticketing counter. The elderly woman asked if her husband could wait there ( he had a very hard time walking) but the grouchy employee said,” No, you have to take him with you! I don’t have anywhere to stash him!” Like he was a piece of luggage or something. Next she ordered me & my family to a TSA booth that didn’t have an agent manning it. We stood there briefly, looking to see if an agent was coming. Next we stepped to the next agent to show our ID & boarding passes. She charged over to us and told us to stay where she put us! I pointed out that there was NO agent where she sent us, and she proceeded to start stomping around barking out orders. My husband just told her we were staying in the line we stepped to because the TSA agent was already processing my daughter.

Having traveled extensively in my 59 years, I have to say that MSP is one of the most ill-designed and unfriendly airports in the world. Yesterday I walked 2+ miles to my connection, the moving walkways not operating. Every single time I’ve flown to/from/thru MSP in the past 30 years there has been an issue. Entering the States from Europe several times we were detained in security for 3 or more hours, our kids taken to the other side of the room while we were interrogated. Never has this happened at any other airport in the world on our travels. Last time we waited for 20 minutes for a French translator to come to read the label on a can of foie gras to determine if it contained pork.  You need to do better MSP! And get better transport from C20 to F15 (in example) - no one should have to walk miles (literally) to get to their connection flights!

MSP Airport does a great job with stores and restaurant options and recently completed some moderate improvements in aesthetics to terminal 1. They currently offer a total of 15 electric parking spots which are spread out across 3 sites! It appears the planning team completely overlooked this aspect of the customer experience.

A modern, stylish and clean airport with good facilities but rather small. The check-in area in terminal 1 was rather crowded as were the departure gate areas. Immigration was rather slow and unnecessarily complicated. Customs were simple. There wasn't enough seating in the gate area and the restaurant was busy. There were plenty of Duty Free shops and in fact too many. All in all, a very nice airport.

First impression of Minsk airport was given by it's exterior grand Brutalist, Soviet-era architecture. Very impressive. Inside the terminal doesn't feel grand and impressive. I was in transit only, so I only saw the arrival gates, transfer area and the airside departure areas. The arrivals area is a bit of a maze and signage not that clear. So be sharp when looking for the transit area after arrivals. The transfer area was old fashioned, with worn fake-leather couches that seem to taken from a landfill. Queuing time at the transfer area was OK (around 5-10 minutes). After boarding card check, passengers process through security, which was a bit of a joke as passengers are not checked at all after passing the walk-through metal detector. The departures area with its shops is a bit of a maze and the gate waiting areas are very small. There is not a lot of choice in shops (what I saw was mostly liquor) or food and beverage outlets. Seating in the gate waiting areas is limited, but on the upper level of the departures area there is sufficient space to take a rest on one of the seats. At the upper level there are also seats on which you can recline, but these seats are quite hard and not very comfortable to take a good nap. There are also sleeping cabins here. Wifi works great, login via SMS. Terminal and toilets are clean, especially at the upper level where not a lot of people go. The terminal it not really fit for PRM passengers as there are a lot of stairs but not escalators and just a few lifts. They did install stairlifts at the gates, a rather silly solution in my opinion but is works. This airport is fine, when you have a short transfer. In case of a long transfer it can be boring and F&B options are very limited.

Minsk Airport was recently renovated and even though the layout may be outdated it looks brand new. The airport is easy to get around and there are plenty of signs and directions for the passengers. I did not experience any queues at all, neither at check-in nor with the security and passport control, it was all very quick and professional. The terminal is extremely clean just like the city is, which is almost surreal at times given that it is the place where thousands of people pass through every single day. Food and shopping options seem standard for the airport of this size, there is a duty-free shop, a souvenir shop, fast food restaurant and a few cafeterias. The only problem is that I haven't seen any money exchange offices. Airport staff are very professional and efficient. When it comes to wi-fi there is a 15 minute free connection, however one can buy a very cheap wi-fi service for several days which also works in the city. The main downside of the airport is the fact that it is so far away from the city and that there are no low cost options.

We flew from Minsk to London on 3 Jan 2016. MSQ has been refurbished following the hockey world cup one year ago (ish). Check in area is bright and efficient. There is even a nice play area for children. Signage is generally clear and in two languages. The terminal is very clean. Arrival was also smooth and passport control was quick. Security was reasonably fast as it was passport control. Gates (as the lounge at the upper floor) have not been renovated, thus still look a bit obsolete. there are few shops (with prices in Euros) and few bars for the last cuppa before flying off. there are not many seats by the gate, meaning that it might be difficult to find a seat if two flights are departing simultaneously from two adjacent gates. Overall a good airport.

I pass thru Miri airport at least once a month now that I work here. It is nice and clean and all counter staff courteous and efficient. do visit the lounge as they accept paying walk in customers. Also a recent addition that is quiet welcome are the massage chairs.

The new airport in Miri is a blessing to all of us frequent travellers. Although it is small it is efficient clean and cool. If anything needs to be imroved on is the charges we have to pay for a small cup of coffee or a meal. The charges are much too high for a domestic airport.

Mobile Regional (MOB) is honestly not a bad airport, even if it's showing some signs of age. The signage leading to anywhere a passenger needs to go is mostly straightforward (except for signage to short-term parking for some reason), though some of it is older and fading. Parking is easy and relatively cheap compared to airports in larger metros. The entry into the terminal is one covered passageway. Checking in luggage is painfully easy at one of three small counters. Going through security is easy with small lines, and painfully easy if you have TSA Pre-Check. There are only seven departure gates total and 2-3 stores post-security. One of those stores is one that almost everyone has to walk past or through on the way to their gate: Hudson News pairing up with a tiny restaurant and bar, equipped with cafeteria-style seating. It looks like the set of the old TV show "Wings," or perhaps a miniature version of a 1990s mall food court. This makes the airport so small that it's quirky. The personnel working in this airport are sweet and warm - yes, in an airport! As for the drawbacks, some of the ceilings post-security are quite low, with the lighting dim. Only some of the pre-security area looks like it's seen any renovation since the 1990s. The signage from I-65, and most of Airport Boulevard until you reach the airport, is almost nonexistent. MOB's location is so far out in the western suburbs that it's really quite inconvenient, whether you're coming from Mobile or other Gulf area cities in Alabama and Mississippi. Mobile Downtown Airport is expected to open in 2024 and should be a vast improvement in terms of modernity and accessibility.

It is dirty, hot and uncomfortable. No possibility to charge mobile devices in the waiting area. Gastronomic offer not reasonable (e.g. dried bread rolls) and overpriced. Ants everywhere. No drinks sale at the gate (at over 30C) but WiFi works. | Es ist dreckig, heiß und ungemütlich. Im Wartebereich keine Möglichkeit, Mobilgeräte zu laden. Gastronomisches Angebot nicht zumutbar (z.B. vertrocknete Brötchen) und überteuert. Ameisen überall. Kein Getränkeverkauf am Gate (bei über 30C) Wlan funktioniert aber.

The airport is in desperate need of an upgrade. It looks old and is falling apart. It certainly does not look like an international airport. There is also no proper coffee shop or restaurant. The basic coffee shop serves really bad coffee. They should have a coffee shop such as Java or Artcaffe for the discerning traveller. I also went to the small shop opposite gate 5. The lady in there was just busy watching something on her phone with the volume up. She was really cold towards her customers. I also noticed that she was not issuing receipts and that the shop had not name displayed outside. Not issuing receipts is illegal. I hope the airport authority looks into this. On the bright side, the toilets were clean and had a nappy changing table.

I used Terminal 1. Passenger processing at this airport is very fast however the terminal building is in need of an upgrade. Boarding of my flight was slightly delayed and no announcement was made. Also, no FID screens at the boarding gate. It was quite hot and there is no air-conditioning. As I had arrived early, it would have been nice to have a shop and café of slightly higher quality although the 1 hour free wifi kept me busy.

Domestic arrival and departure at Mombasa. Walk across the tarmac on arrival but an airbridge on departure. The airport is beginning to show its age, but more than adequate for the current passenger numbers. The approach road is truly appalling, and the main road as bad with seemingly never ending road works. There is no air-conditioning [except in the business lounge], cooling being done by the fairly constant breeze. Minimal delays in passing through arrivals or departures. A shop and café airside and lots of little kiosks on arrival for car hire money exchange etc. A pleasant enough small airport.

Used Mombasa Airport late on Mon 14th March 2016, on a local flight, very quiet (about 100 pax) only one plane departing in the hour, security good, even picked up on detectors a small piece of lava we were carrying as souvenir from the lava field of Tsavo West. Café simple but adequate. Ample seats and clean toilets.

Typical African airport. After you go through the first bag security there is a long hot wait to get checked in. When you make it to the check in desk be prepared to be ripped off my advice is ask to see a supervisor or ask for the test certificate of the scales. Don't waste your time thinking you can go have a smoke in departures as they charge 400 shillings to get to the smoking room after that just another security check and a bag search. Bear in mind once through that there are no toilets either. Kenya has so much to offer pity they can't get it right.

Arrived from Nairobi and flew to Amsterdam on September 2nd 2012. Baggage arrived quickly from our domestic flight couldn't immediately find international departures but were helped friendly at the outside service desk. Security went fast but that could be attributed to the fact that it was a very quiet day (only 2 international flights departing after 3 pm) and we were early. Enough available power sockets for charging. Check-in opened a little over 3 hours before departure once again we were helped by a couple of very friendly guys. Staff on the lower floor overall was kind and helpful but we asked 3 different people if there was either a Burger King McDonalds or KFC at the airport and none of them gave us a straight 'no' answer they all directed us to the small sandwich counter on the second floor. On the second floor staff spoke poor English. Passport control went fast but was arbitrary they asked for my entire right hand (4 fingers + thumb) to be scanned while my sister and father didn't need to have their thumbs scanned. Free wireless internet of fairly good speed but very limited reach. A dozen or so of duty free shops. Half the ceiling fans were broken but since the second floor is not entirely walled up the fresh wind from outside cooled the waiting area down enough. No power sockets at gate 3/4 no toilets either if you need to go you can just walk right back. After asking very politely and kindly if there was a way I could charge my laptop for the long flight (13 hours) they agreed I could charge it behind a desk at the security check where I left it out of sight for over half an hour and I'm happy to say my faith in humanity remains the same it was right there where I left it when we boarded right on time.

Traveled in Feb/March 2012 and fingerprints are now scanned upon arrival slowing down the process considerably. From a departure perspective check-in and passport control were abysmal. Flew Thomson from the UK who add additional layers of security checks not 'enjoyed' by our German or Italian neighbours. Upon arrival at the airport we stood queuing continually for check-in security passport control and beyond that a second baggage/passenger scan and finally a hand luggage search/body search. In all we stood queuing for 2 hrs 45 mins.

We travelled back to the UK on 28th October - when booking in our hand luggage was weighed which increased our allowance (other passengers didn't have theirs weighed) we were informed we needed to pay £30. I offered to pay but was told someone would come and collect it thought this a bit odd but in a foreign country so did as requested. In departures just before our flight the same check in person approached us and asked for the money - I asked for some paperwork or a receipt but he said it was between us and he would have to get a supervisor. I told him I was aware he was putting it in his own pocket and he was very concerned that I would report him. I stupidly gave him the money to get rid of him as he was rather intimidating and our flight was due.

We have flown in and out of this airport nine times and have found it chaotic. Upon arriving there are not separate queues for those with visas and those who have to get a visa. Everybody is in the same queue. There are not enough staff on duty to organise queuing to make it more efficient. Hence you arrive in sweltering hot temperatures and it takes over an hour to get through to collect baggage. Can somebody not do something about this. It is also pretty bad for departures too. Very long unorganised queues and it takes forever to check in.

I have used Monastir Airport now for 11 years and whilst the queues at immigration can be slow at times I think the other facilities and friendly staff more than make up for this. Transport links are excellent if you are an independent traveller.

Arrival at the airport tainted the whole holiday. It took 2 hours to get through passport control in a very hot and sticky environment. There was a complete lack of organisation and the "officials" were no help at all. Surely a more efficient regime could be implemented (eg a queuing system). We understand the need for security however would feel happier if a fairer system was put in place. Unfortunately despite a fabulous holiday we will probably not return to Tunisia

First time I have travelled to and from Monastir airport and I don't want to do it again - ever! We travelled back on a Sunday morning at 10am and it was horrendous. The check-in area was packed to the rafters and because the check-in desks were set out in an 'L' shape each queue was queuing through each other and it was impossible to move. In just the queue we were in one woman had an asthma attack and another one fainted. Luckily the travel reps were on hand as no medical staff could have got through and they managed to get her into a wheel chair. By the time we got through this part and then queued for passport control we had been on our feet for well over 2 hours and only sat down when we got on the plane. Most of the people on our plane said they would not go back there again.

Nice little airport which I use regularly. Queues for passport control can be horrendous as has been said but staff are mostly friendly and facilities are good. Plenty of places to eat and drink and you can use dinars in these (though not in the Duty Free).

We travelled through Monastir Airport and found it to be pretty good for a small airport. The queues coming in were fairly smooth and on the way out of the country everything went smoothly as well. Facilities are perhaps a little limited but it's only a small airport comparatively and at least it was clean!

I agree most strongly that passport control is a nightmare. I could not believe the length of time it takes to get passengers through and especially when the airport is so hot and lacked air conditioning. I have visited this Airport twice now and hope that in future they can implement a more effective way of getting through control. The rest of the airport was fine and even homeward bound found it was comfortably set out with refreshments and enjoyed a last encounter of some traditional Tunisian retail shops.

Good airport but the passport control is ridiculous. Each name is introduced into a computer and only when a green screen with "Rien à signaler" ("nothing to mention") flashes the passport is stamped and you can walk through. Even the same procedure when you are leaving the country... I traveled with my 4 children (one of them is a 6-months old baby) and for each of them even the baby the same procedure was applied. The queue was so long that suddenly they realised everybody was going to be late for boarding so a lot of people were suddenly rushed through the luggage control without screening of X-ray. This made me feel worried as I think this control is far more important than the passport control.

Impressed by this airport apart from the queue at Passport control. It took ages - once through to Departures everything was fine. Duty Free was reasonable and plenty of places to get a drink or something to eat.

I showed up to MLU for my morning flight. I was there in plenty of time and I have flown out of Monroe multiple times. A family in front of me was buying tickets for a flight tomorrow. I waited and waited. Apparently, the woman at the counter, (the only one working) thought I was with the family. Once she realized I wasn't with the family, she tried to get someone to help me but no one was there. I waited long enough to miss the time to check a bag. Finally, a man came to help, but immediately gave me a spill about being on time so I can check my bag next time. I was polite, but I've done this many times. Let's just say the woman working was not happy with him. She tried to help me and I don't think it was her fault that no one was there to help her. I had to wait from 9:40-4:30 to catch the next flight. I guess it is a small airport, so there's not many staff. I think the problem could be prevented.

The airport is one of the worst I have encountered, so I am unsure how it continues to win awards. Competitors must have equally low standards. There are no food options before you check in and go through to the departure lounge so you could be starving for hours without respite, if they are it is poorly signed bring food people. The airport is small and has staff who clearly dont want to talk to you, rude and unwelcoming especially the women. The toilets are disgusting, both in the check in area and post security. The doors are not high enough to ensure privacy, many times they are not working causing long queues. Food options in departure lounge is PATHETIC, no authentic Jamaican places so resigned to Wendy's at a rip off price. There needs to be much more and branch such as Taste, Island Grill, Starbucks ets Seating area in departure lounge is dirty and needs repainting, shops close too early and do not align with flight times.

To be 100% clear - MBJ is destroying tourism in Jamaica. Absolutely the worst airport I’ve ever come through. Rude, lazy, incompetent and impossibly slow staff. I’ve been through this airport about 10 times and it’s consistently bad in both directions. If you upset any of the security staff (real or imagined on their part) they will slap your boarding pass with the dreaded SSSS and they will aggressively screen you for extra security during the boarding process. Seen it happen to many travelers multiple times. Todays’s latest debacle was the ground crew filling the plane with fuel in the WRONG tank causing a lengthy delay for the flight since they had to call the plane manufacturer for a procedure to fix the issue. It would almost be funny if it wasn’t so consistently BAD. If they fix it we’ll be back but we’ll be spending our vacation dollars at other locations until they fix this mess of an airport. Not holding our breath though!

The airport is fine and clean, food was good and getting through the security was fine. However the so call duty-free store is another matter everything was, way over priced. For example the Local Rum Appleton 8 years old was over $40.00USD. That is very expensive to pay that kind of money in Jamaica for local rum on a duty-free, when you can buy the same in Ontario Canada one of the higher liquor tax jurisdictions for under $30.00USD All of the products on the duty-free were way over-priced! You can get the same rums in the USA at the supermarkets for 30% less from the duty-free store of Montego bay airport! I purchase a Cuban Havana Club 7 year old, in Havana on December 15 2024 for 15.00USD.
Slow, slow. Some of the laziest airport workers I have ever experienced. Hot and humid. Packed us into the jet ramp to await boarding. Unheard of

What an absolute joke of an airport! Young people working there are disrespectful and absolutely clueless in regards in what needs to be done. Upon arrival we saw families with young children who had been queuing upwards of 5 hours. Jamaican culture as a whole is one of laziness and nothing better typified that than the “carefree do as little work as possible” by their immigration staff. After asking constantly where we should go I decided to open up the self scan passport queue and help the additional passengers reach through immigration as the staff their refuse to do so unless you make commotion - as I did. If you’re lucky enough to have a good experience going through this airport you’d certainly be in the minority. My advice is avoid this airport altogether and go to an island where you will be shown respect like Bermuda or St Lucia. Will not be returning ever again
The luggage team was absolutely incompetent and delusional they are so laid back it is ridiculous,. They really do make Jamaica look bad and unintelligent.

Customs is a mess. Airport can be a 20 minute walk between terminals with few walking escalators working. Employee was screaming that everyone must go through customs I don’t care if you have connecting flights. Made me rebook to a later flight and then I still got to original gate and could have boarded but they forced my ticket to be changed. Avoid this airport at all costs.

We got to the airport around 10 am for a flight at 1:25. The place was so chaotic, so many people standing in line that we were in an overflow area. There were 6 kiosks for our airline with only 2 employees working. Eventually they added a 3rd person but that was only when we were near the front of the line and there was still a lot of people behind us. So unorganized. We were told to stand in the overflow area and wait by one person, then another employee came and told us to move to the other line. There were quite a few people that were ahead of us, but we did what we were told. Then another person came and told us to move back to where we were. Needless to say there were a lot of angry people that were ahead of us. Just total chaos. We ended up waiting for more than 2 hours to get through, so not a lot of time to shop in duty free and we didn't have time to eat anything. It would have went a lot faster if they had just had enough employees at the desks. So frustrating! We were told it's like that every weekend.

I've been to Jamaica 10 times over the years. This last trip through Sangster Airport was the worst I've ever experienced at any airport anywhere in the world in over 50 years of air travel. The utter lack of organizational skills, the bedlam, the sheer chaos, produce nothing but frustration and anger for visitors. The hallmark of Sangster is abusive disregard for arriving passengers who actually have had to pay for "service" fees slapped on to ticket prices. We felt mistreated , far from welcomed and we will never return to Jamaica as a result.

The most disorganized and bureaucratic airport I have ever seen. I have been there a few years ago but things have changed. First we had to line up for an hour to go through the computer kiosk, then 3 other line ups to see different custom officers who asked the same questions on the computer printout! Total 3 hours later to get out of the airport. It seems like they have layers of bureaucracy to keep people employed.

The biggest plus for Monterey Airport is its size. This is probably the smallest airport I have ever seen. What that means is fast airport screening. Curb to your gate, including clearing security, is less than five minutes. Got it? Less than Five Minutes! On the negative side, the airlines treat the airport as a step-child. Until recently United used to fly its throw-away planes here for the Pebble Beach class masses. This is slightly unusual as there are a hell of a lot of big wigs from Fortune 500 coming in for Golf and right now the Centennial celebration at Pebble Beach. Up until this month, nearly every airplane you flew on was sketchy, dodgy, a throw away plane from once upon a time, long long time ago. That is the class of airplanes coming in and out of here. Not very good. The Airline personnel on more than a few occasions were nowhere to be found. Just not there. And you look around and it looks like a ghost town in there. Really - no body there. The On-Time in bound and out bound is about - lets just say - add 1 to 5 hours to your scheduled departure or arrival. Its very obvious Monterey Airport is not a priority for the major airlines. My guess is that they are thinking if you really are a Big Wig, then you really shouldn't be flying commercial. Fly your own Jet. The services at terminal itself is - well - lets just say - it looks like an 8th grader set up a Lemonade Stand. There is one gift shop. Next door is a 7 Eleven type of place with hand made signs all over and evidence that its a one person operation. There is basically two terminals. You go left or you go right, from the scan stations. And both of these terminals are very dark. What fluorescent lighting there is here does not add to the mood of it being very dark. It sports a couple of dated TV's hanging way too close to the roof. Its a little strange - the terminals. It could definitely use some better Feng Shui. Some art perhaps. Something to make it seem more human, than "Here is a terminal, you wanted one, here it is. It's up to code. They have lights." The restaurant upstairs looks like it could use a renovation. Its furniture and carpet look very 1980's. I'd put money on it that the furniture and carpet is at least a few decades old. Definitely not new. Its important to note, it is not inside the gate, but outside it. The parking here, for a small airport, is pretty steep. About $13 / day long term. $20 - 25 / day Short term. Yes, that is steep. For a tiny airport flying with the average one flight per hour. This airport definitely could use some sponsor subsidizing. Bring in some of the Golf companies. Advertise it as their lounge. Why not? Thats how all the majors work. Sponsorship. Make this thing look a charming, cozy, Tiger Woods world class than midwest airport hick woods class. Clearly the airport has some negatives. Usually at nice airports you want to arrive early and spend some time in there because its such a joy. This is not one of those Airports. You want to be here only to leave. Why am I giving it 7 Stars? Its tiny and convenient. And if it ever were updated with better airplanes and facilities, it would get 10 Stars easily.
The smoke detectors all have low batteries and keep chirping. The announcements are loud and never ending. The ambiance is like that of a prison, but even less nice. In short, I would never return.

Staff very unfriendly. Not willing to help. United Airlines policies assume all passengers must have a credit/ debit card (staff doesn’t take cash a form of payment). Staff doesn’t approach customers friendly to help find alternatives. United Airlines staff doesn’t help passengers to do the check in process. Again, the personal expectation is that ALL passengers know how about technology. Age or social status might be an issue regarding use of electronic devices.

The airport is really compact so the distance to walk between the gate and the curb is small. The departure and arrival processes are really fast! On the other hand, because The Carrasco Airport has a small Terminal, the commercial and service options are really limited and there are just a few options to eating, drinking or shopping. The immigration and emigration services are efficient. There is an electronic system to verify passport (e-gate) that makes really agile the process of documentation verification. The Security area (x-ray) needs better attendance. When I was passing by the Security inspection (X-ray) there was one senior couple slowing the only one row available. The security officers did nothing, neither helping the senior couple, neither opening an extra row and x-ray equipment. The baggage claim works well and is efficient! In this travel time I had one normal luggage plus one special sport equipment (bicycle) that arrived to the baggage claim area earlier than me. The Wi-Fi is good when you find an antenna to connect, but you will need to search the signal, that is not available in all the spaces. The signal is better on the second floor (checking area), but it did not works well on the ground (arrival and curb), so if you need the signal to send messages, chat in WhatsApp, or call Uber or taxi, it will be difficult.

Very good. Clean, minimalistic and very nice. Its quite a small airport so its impossible to get lost, very well constructed and new. The only drawback is the duty free, very little choice and what there is is expensive.

Sitting and overlooking the abandoned runway at Carrasco International in Montevideo waiting for the mysterious fog to disappear makes you imagine what the world will be like without people. The airport closed due to fog and to help with the delay there will be a strike in the fog that got few passengers stranded and roaming this modern, but today useless building. However, the lights are glistering bright on the far side of the runway and you can't help think that South American mentality is taken much further in Uruguay than the rest of the continent.
