I wish I could upload my photo of the massive visible concrete slabs and the runway lights chasing away airplanes completely shying away from their function. I think you can even see the new Peñarol football stadium they recently completed in the distance and luckily it doesn't snow in Uruguay.

I have been in this airport many times over the last three years, and it is by far the best airport I have experienced in Latin America. It is clean and new and easy to get through with no long queues, only a little when waiting in immigration after transatlantic flights. Everything is very open and there is many different things to buy in tax-free.

If you fly Premium classes and get off the plane first you will be lucky enough not to queue too long with immigration and passport control, which is not too unpleasant. They seem to be friendly. Then directed to customs but through the Duty Free Shop, which is the cheapest in S.A, you can buy up to 500 US dollars of alcohol (bubblies, and wines and beers and 3 liters of white spirits). Customs are nice but tough. Do not change any cash inside the international no zone area, the exchange shop, who are expensive with high commission will give you vile rates. There are cash dispensers outside. Taxi service to town at one price only but expensive though. Do not take any taxi just airport ones that are of a beige colour. Check in facilites are good. Very few international airlines fly to Montevideo. Security is vile and long queues done by a division of the air forces, who are rude and not at all polite. Immigration on you way out are rude and unfriendly. Then again lounges after security and after Duty free (yet again convenient prices) you will find the lounge, just the one, for all F and C classes) ok though. Lovely little airport.
Very new very clean lots of natural light. Easy and fast arrivals process. Departure area spacious.
Flew in and out of here on flights to and from Sao Paulo. A striking modern terminal with reasonable facilities. Very pleasant.
Brilliant Airport - new clean clear spacious! Shame so few airlines do fly into MVD.

Spacious clean well located well serviced bright naturally illuminated airport. Large halls with folk articles shops and chemist money exchange bureau and wrapping baggage service. A breeze! Fine areas for check in and spotless lavatories. Once checked in fast track to security and immigrations available. Smiley faces all over the airport. Excellent Duty free shop! Very good VIP lounge.

Landing in Carrasco is a nice experience if the plane approaches the tarmac overflying the nice beaches and architecture. Immigration did not take more than a few minutes and luggage was efficiently delivered - it is necessary to go through a duty-free in order to reach the hall where the conveyors are placed. After customs the main lobby is very illuminated with natural light and spotlessly clean. Taxis are abundant and comfortable and the airport is located about 30 minutes from downtown. However some of the car-hiring companies are not located in the terminal but there is an efficient shuttle service to their offices.

Montgomery Regional Airport (Dannelly Field) has been completely modernized and is one of the most attractive small airports in the US. Check-in in close to the curb and security is efficient. Food and drink groundside and airside is basic. Deplaning is easy and baggage claim is close to the street. Parking is reasonably convenient unless you are travelling mid week. It can be a longish walk to the terminal.
Montgomery AL is currently renovating the terminal and will eventually have up to 6 Jet Ways once construction is completed. They currently have 3 carriers serving the community.
Check-in for the flight was on time, the reception by the staff was excellent, confidential space. The control is efficient and fast, the boarding lounge comfortable.

Small airport, clean and easy to navigate. The airport is very basic, no major queues as there are no many flights. Waiting area is clean, not many places to recharge iPhone/iPad and laptop. I was not expecting too much but at least a decent taxi experience. When I arrived there were no taxis at all outside the airport. I had to call a number that I accidentally found at the taxi rank . A taxi driver replied saying that he would have arrived in 5 minutes. No one turned up. After 15 minutes another random taxi showed up. Bearing in mind the experience (taxi drivers are totally unreliable) I booked a taxi on my way back well in advance as my return flight was at 6am. The taxi driver did not turned up (!), impossible to find other taxi drivers as no one was answering (also the hotel reception could not find anyone) and I missed the flight. I travelled all around the world and I have never missed a flight in my life. It's like this place is stuck in 1930. Rent a car, maybe the experience is better.

A small yet very convenient airport in the south of France. From the plane to the exit takes no more than 5 min. Signaling, shopping etc is all fine given the size and role of the airport. It's not the most modern airport but everything is well maintained. There's a convenient bus service to the city center.

We visited the Airport Restaurant Le Terrasse. The rudeness was unbelievable. We were ignored for over 30 mins while 5 tables who arrived after us were served before us. When the waitress did arrive I ordered a carafe of wine in French. She literally jumped down my throat to say she spoke no English and only spoke Spanish as an additional language. Wow! Such prejudice in the assumption that we would not speak French. She had not listened to the fact that the initial order was in French! As a Head teacher I raise my students with good manners and question those who have not taught so by their parent. What the three waitresses do not understand is that they make themselves look bad. Why do they want to carry themselves in such a negative way? It takes energy to be rude. It is less stressful to be polite. They really made themselves look bad. As we travel to the airport frequently, I have a home in a France, it would be good to see a change of attitude. After all we are paying, they are not doing us a favour.

Montpellier–Méditerranée Airport is a tiny but nice airport. Facilities are clean, some computer charging desks are available, reasonable amount of seats can be found at the gates. Shopping and eating options are according to the size of the airport. The airside area also features a lovely terrasse taking advantage of the sun! 2 drawbacks however: 1) The terrasse does not offer a direct view on the movement area and 2) it's the spot where all smokers end-up. Bagages delivery on arrival was a bit long, especially for such a small airport. Traffic right outside the terminal can be abot messy as the pick-up / drop-off zone seems to be on the street, so cars are jammed. Wifi connection procedure should be simplified and streamlined.

Better to arrive at than to depart from. Baggage reclaim was quick and efficient and decent transport available (shuttle bus and taxis). Taxi to centre of Montpellier less than 30 Euros so not too bad as four shared the expense. Departure was ok but with a "Duty Free" shop saving very little and just one snack bar the place is one not to be delayed in. Fortunately we weren't but the departure gates are designed poorly and there is confusion especially when the priority boarding is progressing. I would welcome a ticket system where those first into the departure gate area are guaranteed to be the first to board the aircraft. This would enable the latecomers to risk having their cases put into the hold and those with regulation size bags would be able to use the gauges and thus make boarding a little more civilised.

There is a frequent direct bus from the city centre to the airport which only costs 1.50 euros and only takes 15 mins. The building is large and modern and air conditioned inside. We had no luggage to check in so went straight through security which was speedy. We had 2 hrs to wait and I was dismayed to find the international departures area is very small with a single tiny coffee bar and one small shop selling duty free perfumes and local products. Seating also very limited although thankfully the airport wasn't busy. I don't think there are any air bridges so all departures mean walking down outside stairs onto the apron. Nice if its sunny.

A very pleasant quiet airport no queues clean organised polite friendly staff and compact. No fancy facilities just the basics but what there is in terms of a couple of shops a snack bar and so on are good. A few minutes off the motorway and well signposted. My only complaint is that the Wifi (which some airports in France now offer free) is charged at EUR 6/hour but after 10 minutes use I was unable to reconnect. Not really a big deal and there is a customer service number to call but I suspect that calling it from a mobile would have cost me more than the original EUR6.

People here need to learn how to do their job! I got so much wrong information on where to go and about where my suitcase is that I ended up in the border control queue to leave the airport even tho I just had a connection flight! Since I came from Colombia they saw me as suspicious and I had to go through SO many security controls that I missed my flight to Europe!! Throughout the whole process I got zero information on where to go and where my suitcase actually is which also made me loose a lot of time! They also take ZERO resonsibility if you miss your flight! Horrible experience, was treated like a criminal. Wifi would constantly disconnect!

I avoid Montreal-Trudeau YUL at all costs. In this case, I had no choice. Half of the moving-walkways and escalators do not work. I had to hunt for a USB port to charge my phone. I found six, four of which did not work. Personnel were generally unfriendly and not helpful. The waiting-areas are filthy. I had to brush muffin crumbs off a table and chair. The worst part was, when I reported an unaccompanied bag (security-concern), it was seemingly ignored.

Had a layover at YUL montreal airport, for 8 hours. The gates to come to Edmonton wing was where we had to stay for this period. The lounge area had decent chairs without arm rests that you could sleep on, that was ok. The amenities, coffee shop Starbucks and Java U plus Urban food. The price gouging for food is out of this world. JAVA U $14 sub sandwich heated with ham and cheese. The URBAN RESTAURANT, We had a meal of smoked meat sandwich, (boring) with fries and a burger and fries, one coffee and ice tea. $69 and the waiter expected a tip on top. Mediocor warm fries and crappy sandwichs. Absolute rip off and you get it all in full french, only one person spoke in broken english. This country is biligual The French want special treatment in Alberta and recognition of their language yet English people arent given the same considertions in Montreal. Never gonna fly into YUL if i can avoid like the plague

We flew Air Canada Frankfurt to Montreal and final destination Quebec City. When arriving at Montreal airport we tried to follow the ‘In Transit’ signs but at one point we could no longer see them. We asked an airport employee for directions and he gave us the wrong answer as did a second employee.(We had the feeling we bothered them!) After wasting 15 minutes we finally ended up at Security (the second time here!). The overall impression of the airport is that its management is unable to handle the very heavy flow of passengers. There are not enough places to sit as we saw passengers sitting on the floor. Even the security staff appeared overwhelmed and stressed apart from the lack of English fluency. No way to eat in a restaurant as there were waiting lines. We have experienced at least a dozen or more airports and this was by far our worst experience. We will avoid in future!

It is dirty and nasty. First stop was the bathroom after going trans pacific for 10 hours.  The toilets all had poop streaks and water or urine seemed to cover every inch of the bathroom. There was no toilet paper or bassinet and dirty sinks without hot water or soap.  Imagine all the people in the airport who haven’t washed their hands. The customs staff were smart mouths and wanted to strip search me because of my premium katmandoo adventure bag which apparently had marijuana concealed because its a katmadoo.

The airport is dirty and disorganized. Westjet staff at this location were rude and not helpful. I was returning to Canada from an international trip and had to remove my luggage because I was switching airlines. My luggage could have been moved for me because it did not get re inspected. I had to wait at a WestJet booth which was not open to allow the transfer. I was not directed to a drop off line and got in with a crowd of new Canadians checking in and weighing multiple bags. Staff knew I was just dropping off and refused to help me. It was hard to find the drop off area because of signage. I went through customs twice. The waiting areas were dirty and crowded, seats were comfortable and it was a nightmare. Shopping areas looked ok but not many accessible from my gate area.

This airport has been going downhill since the last few years. Many international flights as well as some new carriers came (one of them went backrupt), therefore there's not enough plane stands, gates, check in counters to accomodate them. As a result there's often congestion on the roads around the terminal as well as a lack of transportation options. Not to mention the endless waiting times to clear security checks point or immigration and customs inspections. There use to be another airport in Montreal area Mirabel airport that was suitable to serve and accommodate the current demand. Unfortunately this airport was closed to passenger flights and Dorval airport is a mess and unpleasant to take a flight or work there.

Arrived in Montreal 5 hours late from my original flight from London. I was very worried I would miss my connecting flight to Ottawa. I had to pass through customs and make my way through what seemed one end of the airport to another. The signage was confusing and inadequate. I tried to get directions and information from airport personnel. I was brushed off almost every time. I was given incorrect information which delayed my progress. Some even told me they did not know where I could find a particular gate. People were treated like cattle being moved along with no time to even give a word of explanation. The moving conveyor belts were not working. I had just come from Heathrow and although that airport is huge, it is well organized and the signage is clear. If I can avoid this airport I will. Rude staff, poor layout and signage are its characteristics.

We arrived here from Narita Japan for our connection flight to the US. There was a long line for security and employees just wandering around. The security staff weren't just rude, they were MEAN. Screaming at people for absolutely no reason. Told me to empty my pockets which contained my passport and boarding pass just to be screamed at down the line that I didn't have my boarding pass in hand even though prior to that I had to show it to 4 different people already. I watched them scream at a Japanese man to remove his shoes even though he already did. He was trying to explain that he already did and they just kept yelling at him. Then, we were in line for customs, only 1 employee working it seemed. The guy in front of us was upset because his connecting flight was boarding and they kept letting other people skip the line. An employee was rude to him and told him "they have to board 100 people you have time" Not all flights board 100 people. Ours was a very small plane and if his was as well he definitely missed his flight. Then in the waiting area it was filthy, the bathroom was disgusting. I absolutely will be avoiding this airport at all costs going forward.

The airport is filthy, washrooms out of soap and paper towels, bunch of morons changing gate number every two minutes sending travellers back and forth like yo yo's. Never ever again, done with Air Canada and YUL airport.

Newly refurbished airport, an exhibition of antique cars etc - the money wrongly spent, wrong priorities in my opinion. On my arrival to Moscow via this airport I used a ladies bathroom and found it cramped, poorly and cheaply refurbished, smelling of sewage and no soap to use. Not what you expect in a country's capital international airport. Newly refurbished! Even worst experience departing from the same airport. Most check-in kiosks not working. Ok, not a major problem, I checked in using the desk. Had to wait for my flight for about 6 nocturnal hours overall of which about 4 hours before I passed through departure gates. I witnessed a female airport worker walking around the seats telling people to put their feet down as passengers not allowed to sleep on the seats or even lift your feet to relax them a bit/change posture. She was trying to appear polite i.e. say "good evening" and "please" however still looking and acting like a teacher mentoring her under-aged misbehaving pupils. "such are airport rules", she said, "check it if you like". How about introducing lounges like in many other airport across the world? Or to teach airport staff some customer service skills at least? Rude staff in "EDIM LETIM" cafe; saw me coming over to check what's available and abruptly took display sample dishes I was interested in (Asian soups) away from the counter right in front of my nose: no apologies, no smile, no offer of another type of meal, nothing, so I left. Tried to use wifi on a British phone: I registered as requested, should have received a confirmation message but never did so was no wifi for me. To conclude my review there were not enough seats at departure gates. Unfortunately, I will have to fly via Domodedovo again this summer as non-refundable tickets already been bought but will try to avoid in the future.

Please avoid this airport, very rude staff and lack of mannerisms, full of youngsters at the passport control and don’t know how to treat tourists and they truly don’t realise that they are the face of Russia and how important their job role is. I will never ever fly to Moscow no even for a stopover and you all should do the same. I travelled with a British passport and they almost tore my passport by doing some silly checks.

The airport itself is good, but the design looks simply ok. The airport is big, it has old and new parts, the new part looks better. It has many check-in desks, fast security check, and very nice that they have priority security check and priority passport control. Some nice business lounges and good duty free.

Overall, it was a bad experience. Quite a breeze through the fancy terminal, fast passport control and good-enough baggage check in counters. But once you reach the departure area, it's the worst modern airport ever seen. The airport staff was rude and did not allow anyone to sit anywhere in the already crowded place except the chairs. Not good for those on delayed flights, common in Russian winters. Also, this airport has the worst choice of shops and food court. There are no fast food chains, no good duty free (except perfumes and alcohol and souvenirs) and nothing else. The AC was medium, although it was a bit on the warmer side. Even Vnukovo airport and Sheremetyevo airport (Moscow) is 100x better in all respects. Overpricing is also a major issue. An espresso was rarely found, and when found in Shokoladnitsa (branded coffee kiosk), it was prized at 300 rubles, higher than in Vnukovo (230 rubles). (Prices obviously subject to change). Every other thing was certainly costlier as well.

Probably the worst airport in Eastern Europe and the world. Only, huge, fancy terminal building. Inside , very congested and outrageously expensive. Traveled through here twice, in the winter and the summer. I had to wait 3 days for my flight, as there was no seat available for my destination, so I had plenty of time to see what kind of lousy, torture like facility it was. Huge terminal with planty of space. But, the most shocking thing was that the Airport staff did not allow passengers to rest, or sleep - they said it was rule set by Airport management. Thousands of people transit here plus many delays on domestic destinations. It looked like prison, with Airport staff approaching passengers and waking them up every 20-30 minutes! Even if people slept on the floor. No matter who, young, old, tourists. Can you imagine this nonsense? 24 hours a day! The air conditioning system was terrible. In the summer only departure check-in area was properly air conditioned. While, level 2 , where passengers await their flight was like sauna! Was very hot and suffocating. The entrance area, to the Terminal is very crowded and badly arranged. I have never seen such an lousy planning. Passport control takes long time. Avoid this airport if you can. Sheremetyevo Airport is much better and less crowded.

I can't say that Domodedovo is very good airport, staff is ok, good business lounges, the standard Russian duty free (Cosmetics and snacks). I think it is nice because of business security check and passport control.

I read some scary reviews here, which made me leave for the airport more than 5 hours before my flight. But after a very good journey on the excellent Aeroexpress train, I have nothing to report. DME is no Changi for sure, but it is a completely average airport. No big queues, and from checkin to lounge it took me 20 minutes max. The bulk of it spent with a slow passport officer, who did not speak English and was confused by my dual nationality and me living on a third country. But the rest of the security measures (X-RAY of all luggages on entry, second check of boarding pass and passport) are on pair with other (specially Asian airports). Granted this is a Sunday afternoon, so things could get busier during the week. But this is it - just an adequate airport. Not one of the modern Shopping Centers you find these days, but just a regular place to wait for your next flight. Maybe the view from the lounge is different, but I learned long ago to not leave home without my Priority Pass. Contrary to some of the reviews here, the airport does offer wi-fi and it does accept any international number. Maybe this is one of the benefits of traveling after the WC 2018.

Having arrived very late (23.00) at Domodedovo, we wanted to leave ASAP. The queues aren't long at passport control but they do take forever to verify everything so we waited about 10 minutes at the desk. Baggage arrived very quickly. The arrivals hall can be a bit dodgy with all the illegal taxi drivers etc and the car park is a good 200m walk from the terminal (you can imagine in Moscow at this time, it's ~-2). On departure, everything is quite well signposted. The security section is a mess with only two lanes open with lots of people and baggage. Passport control again has very short queues but it takes forever to get through. The Duty Free is ok but far from cheap. There is WiFi if you have a Russian number, but if you don't, prepare to sit there, bored. There is Wifi just outside the S7 lounge on the top floor if you really need it but not next to the gates. There isn't much seating but the airport wasn't too busy so it was ok. Overall, the airport is a bit of a struggle and I will look to travel to SVO in the future primarily due to location, but it's ok if you really need to take a flight from it.

The Immigrations process took the longest ever. What a waste of time. Fortunately, we stood in front of the line. Otherwise, we wouldn't get to the Aeroexpress train in time. All the staff should consider learning to speak English fluently since they have to deal with foreigners every day. Some spoke to non-native speakers of Russian and got upset when they didn't understand what they said. This wasn't civilized.

Most of the staff were very helpful and friendly, icluding the border control officers. Shopping is OK there and so are the seating options - at least in the lounge I visited using my priority pass. However, when I entered the airport, I asked the security clerk whether my suitcases passed the check and are OK. They were, but he answered rudely in Russian " Njet, njet, njet, Davaj" - which means "No, no, no, move it!" I had done everything orderly, so why must one be so rude and not even answer a simple question? WIFI is available. Unfortunately, the activation code you have to get by SMS never arrived - but this is not necessarily the airport's mistake. All in all, I like the airport.

Wait at Check-in lines are way too long - had to wait almost 2 hours. Personnel’s are too slow and rude and not enough staff at the airport. If you are exchanging/buying tickets or paying extra for whatever reason at the register - they are handwriting most information and takes so much time. Navigations are not too clear, even for Russian speaking people. Improvements needed!

Transfer from international to domestic flight and back last week. My flight from London arrived into Terminal D and transferred to Terminal B for the domestic departure. Efficient experience overall, clear signage but some long walking distances from arrival to the shuttle train. Terminal B has a nice, interesting design and plenty of seats with chargers. Nice selection of lounges for cardholders. Overall, recommended.

I flew into and out of Moscow Sheremetyevo Airport in December 2019 for the first time and was quite impressed with arrivals and maybe a little less so with the departure process. Arriving and clearing customs and security and getting bags was all pretty straight forward and easy enough and efficient. Signage for me was great and easily navigated to the bag carousels and also found an ATM before exiting to take out some cash. Plenty of food options once exiting and then I easily followed signs to the Aeroexpress train from the airport to Moscow Belorussky, about a 5min walk through terminal.I bought my train ticket online prior and scanned the bar-code and all worked fine.So transport to and from the airport is easy, on the way back I took a Yango ride and it pulled up easily right in front of terminal. On the way departing security is pretty tight but to be expected, you go through two screening stations and again check in pretty seamless, except for the fact your Departure Terminal indicated on the board may not be the one you finally need to go to as I found out. Ended up having a fairly decent walk from one terminal to another. Once that finished then we headed to the aerobus as is common in Europe to be driven to the plane, waited for about 15mins with open bus doors for late passengers in Moscow winter..then the drive started and instead of a couple of minutes, it turned into about 15 minutes, driving from one aide of the runway around the end and over to the opposite apron to the plane. But for me all an adventure, but just be prepared for a bit of a walk and maybe an extended bus ride. Overall a nice clean airport that was very functional and not overly crowded when I went through and easily accessible and a good range of eateries and amenities.

I had the unfortunate experience of transiting through this airport. The passport control and security scanner issues caused us to miss our flight, we were left to book our own overnight accommodation and flights home the next day. We were careful to gather evidence and recently took the airline to the small claims court for the accommodation, food & flights. We won the case and were awarded 50% of expenses.

We (travel group) had transit connection in Sheremetyevo on the way from Hanoi to Tel Aviv. We tried to get through "short connection gate" - because our first flight was late. We came to the security check gates: huge crowd (probably several flights were late). All being late people really broke through to get a stamp with the security lady - to pass to screening - with screaming and pushing going on - it was chaos. There was only one security lady and 2 screening machines against the crowd. I do not recommend this airport (for transit at least).

I never thought I would experience such a horrible transit in an international airport! I had 3 hours for a transit onto another and I just made it to another flight on final call. I saw people that were supposed to be on the same flight but they never made it. I'm not going to repeat what other reviews say about the lines for passport checks, the heat, etc., because it's absolutely horrible! Never again.

The worst airport that I never want to pass through again. This airport makes me never want to visit Russia, a country I always was interested in. International transfer areas are atrocious - at a time of the global Wuhan coronavirus outbreak, hundreds of intl passengers were trying to cram into a single gate for passport control. Zero attempt from airport staff to organize the chaos. The transfer area was unsafe: the proximity was perfect for transmission (ridiculously lax safety measures when compared w/ how other airports try to prevent any outbreaks), and people were suffocatingly close to each other. We were barely moving, cramped next to one another from all four sides, for over two hours. If you miss your flight because of these delays, don't expect Aeroflot to compensate. "That's the airport's problem, not ours," is their standard reply as they ask for your credit card for a new ticket. Don't expect airport staff to be helpful or even kind. They are incompetent and utterly shameless about their incompetence. They view customers as a chore, and don't hide the fact. So ridiculously rude that their attitudes aggravate bad situations. I found one kind staff at an info desk who didn't make me feel bad for asking questions.

This was our second and definitely last time at this airport. The international transfer area is disorganized beyond belief. The area is inadequately signposed, very congested, there is no queuing system in place and the crowds of passengers are trying to make their way through two/three transit doors (the other four doors are closed) and then there is even more queuing before you reach security check. The staff are incredibly rude and keep shouting at passengers. Nothing has changed within the space of five years! To be avoided at all cost (and if you really have no choice I would suggest allowing plenty of time between flights and a bottle of water).

Wifi is super hard to connect, and will almost guarantee to fail at some point. Stores sell the same stuff again and again. Staff start creating fences around where I sit for some reason without telling me at all, and then they yelled at me because I was sitting inside (not even in proper English. The lady just scream out some Russian words then said "out". How rude!). But the worst thing here is the restrooms. I swear they are the dirtiest of all airports that I have been in (20+, some in third world countries. They all have cleaner restrooms). Overall would never come here again.

Just want to support recent reviews of this airport. Despite the acceptable and good amenities provided at the airport, the immigrations / security check is a total nightmare. The limitations to just two check points with security scanners and multiple cues squeezing into these zones, you can not even speak of queues. This is like in the middle ages with no system nor concept at all, just everyone pushing trying to get to the end of the line while constantly travelers keep jumping them. Although I'm more than happy when inside, this makes it so inconvenient that it is an unacceptable situation for me, definitely first and last time using this airport. Aeroflot can not make the flights into Moscow cheap enough for me to consider Sheremetyevo for transit ever again. Ridiculous really, because this issue could be easily solved with simple measures.

Went through Muenster-Osnabrueck for a commuter flight to FRA. Due to the not so many flights, there isn't much to see or do at the airport. For example, there is only one place to get food after security, with not much choice. There are countless places to sit down though, and you have a good view of the apron (where not much happens) through the large, glass windows, and from the visitor's terrace. Because of two cancellations in a row, we had to spend 8 hours at the airport, and it quickly got boring. On the other hand, it's really easy to find your way, and queuing times are minimal, even just before a flight leaves, thanks to the very efficient security personnel. Wifi was free, and reasonably fast.

A long way by bus from either Munster or Osnabruck. And with 7,50 euros a rather expensive bus ride. There is an expressbus (S50) departing in front of Munster railway station every hour (35 mins) and a slow one (45 mins) also every hour. But apart from this, FMO is one of those regional airports where you experience a relaxed departure. A late morning departure resulted in a very quiet airport. You get out of the bus and are literally meters away from luggage drop-off. Security was a breeze and I even noticed friendly security agents which is a rarity. Free wifi, short walkways to the gates and quick boarding. A small airport means short taxiing and no waiting for departing planes as well. All in all: very good. It was my first departure from FMO and I hope it won't be my last. Downside: not many flights and flying via MUC or FRA on Lufthansa is usually much more expensive than from DUS (why LH?).

Good transport connection via BAB 1. Moderate parking-rates close to the terminals. Check-In only 30 minutes prior to departure. Short distances. More than 10 daily flights major Star Alliance hubs MUC and FRA and direct flights to holiday destinations. Daily low-cost flights to London (STN) Vienna Rome. FMO is a good choice for travellers in northern NRW western Niedersachsen and eastern Holland who want to start their journeys (business travel as welll as holiday travel) relaxed and in a friendly atmosphere.

It's development in the last 10 years is rather impressive. More than one million passengers now use this airport each year for a regional airport this is rather much I think. I like she short distances the easy and quick checkin services the nice environment and the very close parking facilities. I you arrive at this airport you have to wait never longer than 3 min. for the luggage delivery.

Nice clean and efficient regional airport which I have used regularly over the years. Never had queues at check-in. Living in the Eastern part of Holland FMO (the official abbreviation of Münster-Osnabrück) is a good alternative for me to Amsterdam. Provided that is (1) you have a car-- public transport connections to the airport are not simple and not fast and (2) you find a good and not too expensive flight--especially flights with connections in major hubs Frankfurt or Munich can be rather expensive.

I travelled with my mom, who is a senior citizen to Mumbai. We arrived in Mumbai at approximately 2:30 am on 30 January 2025. At customs control there were no ground staff to supervise and assist passengers as to which lines they should queue in. They ran out of the customs forms and the print quality of the forms was pathetic. After collecting our luggage we proceeded to the exit. Since the wifi does not work for foreigners (Foreigners must be made aware of this as it is a risk since one has no way of contacting the hotel/driver), I left my mom near the exit with our luggage and proceeded to exit the terminal to look or our driver since there was no way of contacting him. When I tried to enter the building again to collect my mom, I was rudely chased away by a security person stationed at the door. I tried to explain the situation and he rudely and aggressively told me to leave. Fortunately my driver located me and I explained to him what happened. He tried to intervene and speak to this person but the official disgracefully refused to listen. Eventually the other official who was standing there intervened and told this official in vernacular (have compassion - she is a female). The officer then accompanied me to my mom and produced our passports and boarding pass. He tried to defend the actions of this colleague stating that its their job. My response to him was, do your job, but do it properly with respect. My question is, is this the modern age Indian values of how guests are treated in the country? Basic courtesy, respect, patience and understanding was lacking. It is shocking that this calibre of staff are appointed to represent the face of the airport and to some extent the country. Foreigners must are made aware of just how disgraceful; ill mannered and disgusting some staff at the airport are.

The coach service was horrendous. It takes longer to transit from one terminal to another than flying in to Mumbai. Possibly the airport operator wants the passengers to take Taxis Hope someone will notice and provide sufficient buses or some inter-terminal train to make it fast & smooth.

This is my third visit since 2022, and if I could give 0 stars I would. This Airport boasts a world class facility but unfortunately, is literally like a hub of scam, systematic loot, and fleecing of passengers. Free Wi-Fi is a scam - they have made accessing Wi-Fi deliberately difficult by requiring PIN and Phone Number only because of some  rules, and at only 45 minutes, following which travelers need to pay for a Wi-Fi Pack that lasts for 1-7 days. This is deliberate inconvenience to international passengers. Honestly, the Adani Group is getting a Return on its investment by such kind of pathetic service. Shame on them. They’re not world class operations, they’re third class.  Furthermore, for security, personnel ask to remove charging cables and adapters, considering that just laptops and iPads are not sufficient enough. Even Chicago Airport is better when it comes to basic facilities. At the same time, Customs lines are long, baggage claim is a time consuming task, Terminal cleanliness on the outside is horrible because of broken wall times at the elevators upon exit, stray animals, defaced walls with Paan, and of course, no proper ventilation even in winter. The poor A/C settings makes the airport feels like a sweatshop.

The wheelchair assistance at Mumbai Airport was exceptional. From the moment my parents landed on an early morning flight, they received excellent support through immigration and luggage collection, ensuring a smooth and hassle-free process. A special thanks to the young gentleman (whose name I unfortunately can't recall) for his kind assurance and attentive care. Truly appreciated the respectful and seamless experience. Highly recommend their service!

Mumbai Airport never fails to impress me from the dedicated drop off options or the overall efficiency. It is my favourite major airport to travel from. I am more impressed with arrival facilities but even departure is as good as it gets. Only fundamental issue is its very overcrowded.

The staff is probably overworked. The sentry / security at the gates are rude. At the security area they speak to you rudely asking you to remove your watches, put your bags in separate bags etc. I think a lesson in speaking politely is needed. We understand you deal with an immense load of people but this is hospitality sector.

Do not transit at this airport. The security people at transit who were doing nothing when was was escorted to transit as nobody else was stupid enough to transit in this place. As instructed no batteries were in hold luggage but in my carry on none of them connected and all uncharged. They went through my entire bag and stole several vapes which I need to continue to stop smoking. They said I couldn’t bring them into India. I wasn’t entering India! They then said three rechargeable batteries were for vapes and confiscated the lot. They even tried to steal my CPAP medical machine. Only when the Vistara ground staff translated my medical note do they return it. Thieves all of them and there were 3. I have never faced this at any other airport in the world. Never going back to India

By far the worst experience ever. I have never seen and airport weighting bags and specially handbags by the gram. When i said this to the person who did my check in, his answer was: 'we follow the rules'.  If you want to follow rules, be regular, not only where you can exploit foreigners.

Chatrapati Shivaji Airport’s T2 terminal is absolutely the worst airport terminal I have ever visited and I have been to many global airports. The digital sign boards are broken with many having paper stuck on it for instructions. The transfer from international to domestic terminals is an excruciatingly painful process with no signs or helpful people telling you how to do this. The worst thing is you have to come out of the international terminal, and take a bus or taxi to the domestic terminal, which you would need to do under extreme eye watering pollution. No worthwhile airport in the world does this - terminal transfers are easy and comfortable. Other people’s comments on rude behavior of staff and immigration officers is spot on. There is no “how may I help you” counter. Never again will I fly to this airport.

We travelled via Air India on and are a frequent flier via Mumbai usually with no issues. A recent return from Bangkok to Bangalore via Mumbai had a slight issue wherein there was a delaying the primary flight, and we had some unforeseen delay on top of that. We didn't find the right exit terminal quick enough. Inspite of a heated discussion that took place between my family and few of the official, they did their best in the given circumstances. They sent a staff to expedite our transfer they kept said staff updated via walkie about how and where to go. And the staff also ensured we reached with all of our belongings intact. Kudos to that.

The airport is airport looks sleek and modern but the staff members are unfortunately inept. It was neither overly busy nor were the people running the airport understaffed. I had to wait an hour in a line to go through security. And another 50 minutes to get through passport security. Our flight was delayed leaving because so many people were held up waiting in the queues. Much improvement is needed

Every time I come here there is always a situation with baggage claim. Either they lose my luggage or it take an hour for them to unload the luggage from the plane. The baggage situation here has to get better it’s the only airport I’ve experienced any of this.

At least half of all escalators were down, including the moving floors. Airport staff were unhelpful in every regard. By far the most helpful people were complete strangers, as nobody could help us understand the train system. (S1 splits in half on the way to airport?)  We had to go thru three separate security lines, the last of which was between us and our gate, and we are still waiting to be let thru to our flight ad this is being written. Its been over an hour. One of the employees here was rude to us and told us to sit down and wait. If you can possibly avoid this airport, do.

Terrible airport. Terminal 1 passport control is 500 meter walking from security check. Not enough seating in waiting area. Most travelers have to stand. Prices in duty free shops are way too high. Definitiv NOT a world class airport

Worst airport ever. Everything about both Arrival and departure were awful. Nearly 2hrs in passport queue after arrival, with 3 staff spending 5-10 mins each person. People queuing up the stairs. No water provided in the very hot waiting area / queue. Many people were asking why the delays, but the staff were all very rude and unhelpful. 2 passport agents sat with nothing to do as they were supporting the EU only queue, and were told not to help alleviate the c.200 person queue. This 2hr delay meant we could not go and visit Munich town as planned as we waiting in queue past 9pm. Then no food outlets available either. Arrival was bad enough, then we had an equally bad experience when departing. The supposed Fast-track queue, had around 70 people in it. One person was looking after both this and the main security queue. The non-fast track queue had around 200 people in. Another long wait for us, but even worse for other people. Then passport again was a big delay. This is by far the worst airport we have ever been to. Everyone in the arrivals queue would also agree.

One of the worst airports I've been to, and I've travelled quite a bit to third world countries and all over. The x-ray staff had no idea what they were doing, were only serving 1 person at a time, took ages. Then passport control to leave, was a huge queue and they only had a few counters, half of them walked off smug and arrogantly, leaving a queue of 100+ people to be served by 2 people! Absurd! Terrible airport, avoid it if you can.

In the past I've been very happy with Munich airport and have recommended it to other travellers for being well-organized and relatively peaceful, for an airport. But that opinion is no more, following our experience of almost missing our flight to Toronto due to super-slow security lines. My husband has Star Alliance gold status, which in the past has entitled us to a faster trip through security. However, yesterday the security agents told us no Star Alliance gold card holders or business class travellers could be processed through a faster lane. (Usually buying a business class fare or being a Star Alliance card holder does give one that benefit.) We were at the airport nearly 3 hrs before our flight, having been concerned about slowdowns on the S8 line to the airport. But it was the security at the airport that let us down: we made our flight by only 5 minutes! Spending that much time in lines for security, wending our way through arbitrary crowd control gating, is unacceptable for anyone, let alone frequent travellers.

On arrival following signs to customs took us down a corridor where a lady asked us, and everyone following us if we were looking for the exit, she then walked us out to another sign, and chastised us for not being able to read just as another group of passengers entered the corridor, it was clear she does this all day, when everyone is confused you have a design flaw. On arrival with no bags to check and using business class lines it took us an unacceptable 90 minutes from door to gate. There was an abandoned backpack in the passport control line. Multiple passengers brought it to the attention of the customs agents who seemingly did not care to address it as a security issue or lost property. Once in the gate area, the only retail options were two vending machines, one pit of service, one with only a few skittles packet in it. Around the corner was a small pretzel stand manned by one person, all of this is an enclosed gate area with a few A380s going out so hundreds and hundreds of people. The way-finding in this airport in unnecessary complicated and confusing, the staff (airport not airline) were rude, unhelpful and patronizing, the retail and food offerings airside are essentially non-existent, restrooms trash cans and other services seem almost intentionally designed to be hidden and inaccessible, and the wait times at the three separate checkpoints are wholly unacceptable. Wifi was down during our time at MUC.

We found Munich Airport to be an excellent airport, very well laid out with two level gate system that seems to work very efficiently. Very easy to follow signage, good seating. Check in and baggage drop off was well managed by friendly staff at Singapore Airlines service desks. Gates and boarding in designated assigned groups seemed to work quite well. Well presented airport.

In terminal 1 there are no drop off zones where you can print labels for baggage yourself. Longest queues for security I have experienced here in Terminal 1. Too few lanes and not even all open. 1 hour wait is simply unacceptable in 2024

Worst airport I have ever been in. Every single gate labelled with incorrect locations and times. They had people running back and forth across the terminal for hours with little to no information about what is going on. When a correction was made it turned out to be wrong again repeatedly at several gates. No organisation, absolute chaos.

A wonderful little airport! So impressed. While it was busy at the peak of the holiday season, everything moved quickly and efficiently. The shops airside, while small, have a great selection of Spanish specialties like olive oil. I hope the new airport that opens next year keeps up the same high standards!

What a pleasure. We arrived into Murcia on the 2nd June and greeted by cheery ground staff, straight to passport control, a little queue at passport control, nice and polite customs officers. Went to baggage belt and there were a few others in front of us but 10 mins at the most wait for our baggage, Through the exit and outside in under half an hour, how amazing was that. The return journey went just as smoothly, I was blown away by this efficient, friendly and calm airport, staff are amazing.

Arrived 18/08/2016. Departed 05/09/2016. Pleasant, small, regional Spanish airport. No air bridges but the aircraft parked on stand just outside the terminal building. Breezed through Spanish border checks. Collected bags. On our way. On return, short queue for Easyjet bag drop manned by pleasant, english-speaking staff. Quickly through security checks. Not much post security in terms of shops. A few small shops selling the usual expensive items. A few places to eat. Plenty of seating in departures. Toilets were clean. Departure gate staff (same as at bag drop) were pleasant. Departed a few minutes ahead of schedule. Would happily use again.

We have been using this airport several times a year for the last ten years. Over the years the facilities have progressed. From a field for a car park to a proper hard standing area with security. The terminal is up to scratch for a small airport, generally very clean with all facilities. We particularly like the short walk from the arrivals entrance through security to the gate. Announcements are clear and there are plenty of arrival/departure screens. We don't use cafes or shops in any airport but they look to be appropriate for the size of the airport. Car hire and baggage reclaim very easy. Plenty of taxis usually outside but can be a queue at peak times. This is our favourite airport - hate Alicante and Gatwick.

A pleasant small airport, very useful for southern Spain. A minus point would be being held in the sun before boarding a plane, this is quite unpleasant. Announcements are very clear. Very good airport

Great airport small and friendly. Not too bothered about duty free shops its an airport for quick in and out (like most should be) - flights seem to be moving to Alicante but lets support this little airport and its staff. Car hire very easy.

I fly through San Javier about 16 times a year and generally it works fine. My only complaint is the boarding process. Because there are no seperate gate lounges people queue in the departure hall. All pretty chaotic especially if one has paid for priority boarding as it means fighting through crowds to get to the front and in the process putting up with mindless comments from people who don't seem to understand the concept of priority boarding! The ground staff do nothing to help.

Not a bad little airport but I can only comment on the departure side. It was however the last Saturday in August so possibly one of the busy days. Bag drop (for Ryanair) speedy. Queues for security almost non existant. There is a cafe and a small shop landside (the shop sells English papers). Also a very pleasant open air kiosk on the traffic island ourside. The car hire drop place is reasonable close although it appears the procedure is (at least with some companies) to drop the key at the desk in the building. Beware there is no petrol station site to top up your hire car. The nearest we found was on a roundabout in the very centre of San Javier about five minutes away. Airside there is plenty of seating a cafe a Subway and a duty free shop. The prices in the cafe were very high as everywhere so better to bring your own food.

The Airport is fine as it is small at the moment so luggage is retrieved fairly quickly and the car hire section is easy to find. However the duty free is virtually non-existent and shuts at nine. So does the cafe area. So if you are delayed and you dont organise your food before nine its a case of hard luck.

On arrival: Very long queue for passport control (over an hour). They have plenty of staff but processing time per person is simply very long. On departure: queues were fine. We were told to arrive 3 hours in advance - which meant waiting doing nothing for a long time! There are no restaurants after security (just a few fast food options). Also WiFi only works if you can receive an OTP by text (ie you already have data). Clean and pleasant but some of the details could be thought through a bit more.

On arrival the airport was very clean. There was water fountains and music. It was very peaceful. When we departed check-in was so easy and security was simple. There were lots of shops and duty-free. Overall, One of the best airports in the world.

My wife and I had a two-hour transit at Muscat between flights with Oman Air. Our time in the airport was unexpectedly pleasant. The terminal building gives a new and modern appearance, but with features of traditional Arabic architecture. The total effect is aesthetically very pleasing, and supported by mellow background music. Travel through the terminal was not onerous: although distances between gates and other transit points were long, most of it could be covered by moving walkways. Security check was painless and efficient, with short queues. At the departure gate, there was a nice separation between boarding pass check and seating in the waiting area. There was plenty of seating in the gate, and we appreciated the boarding procedures being separated by zone. One negative: there was no obvious place to get a coffee in the transit areas we passed through, although signage pointing to another part of the terminal suggested eating and drinking options elsewhere.

The airport has definitely improved and it looks a lot more modern than it used to be before. They have a decent duty-free shop with a good selection of items. I really liked the sports bar that they had there which was also showing the Fifa World Cup games live and the food was good too. The airport staff is very friendly and welcoming and there are also stalls where you can get a massage. There is also enough seating if you are traveling in transit.

Very nice designed airport, clean and big but they have the worst type of airport staff, from salesmen at the duty free, to airport staff walking around to assist you. You feel that they were forced to work and you can see that in the way they behave.

The staff at the information desk by the exit was rude and disrespectful to me. I asked a few questions for directions and about the airport WiFi, and they didn’t help me. They were looking down at there food and eating. Not welcoming to me or interested in answers my questions. Acted like I was bothering them!

I visited Oman first time in 2015 and used this airport. It was then very a small and unorganized airport. Now, the airport has become huge with many other facilities. There is a museum with Omani architectures. There are many handicrafts shops with very high prices of commodities. There are KFC and McDonalds that offer food at an affordable price. There are Muslim prayer room and toilets as well.

I visited Oman first time in 2015 and used this airport. It was then very a small and unorganized airport. Now, the airport has become huge with many other facilities. There is a museum with Omani architectures. There are many handicrafts shops with very high prices of commodities. There are KFC and McDonalds that offer food at an affordable price. There are Muslim prayer room and toilets as well.

The airport staff have a real attitude problems. Most of them are careless and do not show respect or support to passengers. In addition to their lack of knowledge about rules more quality and performance control should be in place to ensure effeceint performance. Toilets dirty and the cleaners are just standing and chating.

Staff is not supporting, first they have to listen what passenger asking for and how to revert the . When we ask for services they excuses that our shift is different, so its their duty to check email and satisfy customer. Even they did not confirm and check not even try to search out.

MSL is 30 minutes from my home instead an hour twenty to HSV. The staff is beyond exceptional up to and including the TSA employees. Over the years I have had less problems with connections in Memphis than any other hub in the southeast. Two years ago we dropped our 16 year old daughter off for a flight to her grandparents. We left for parts far and wide before the flight departed as we knew she was in good hands. This wound up being one of the occasions when mechanical problems caused a delay. The staff called me on my cell phone and explained the options to get my daughter to her destination. We chose to allow her to stay and wait for the next flight that afternoon as her arrival time would not have varied much had we turned around and put her on a flight out of HSV. I asked that they make sure she was fed since her wait would go over lunch time. Long story short when we checked to see how she accomodated the staff insisted my daughter accompany them to lunch and picked up the tab. She was provided vouchers for the 2 hour layover in Memphis and the staff explained in detail how to use them where the eating places were located in Memphis airport etc. She was treated exceptionally well and other than the long day actually enjoyed learning about the pitfalls that face air travelers at times first hand. The same smiling faces that helped my daughter two years ago are the same ones that greet you at the counter today. My only complaint is the limited flights don't allow me to fly out of the shoals as often as I would like.

MSL continues to be a good alternative to larger nearby airports. Flew to see family in Late Nov. and Early Dec. of 2005. NWA continues to have 2 flights a day to its Memphis Hub. As with my previous experiences traveling through MSL the NWA and Airport Staff did a great job in taking care of their passengers. Again a job well done by the MSL Airport and Airline Staff. Also the New Marriot Hotel and Spa has opened the Robert Trent Jones Golf Course is also open for the avid golfer both of which are just minutes from the airport. My round trip flights were flawless and running at or ahead of schedule outbound and inbound from the North West Alabama Airport.

Being a resident of Muscle Shoals the Muscle Shoals airport (MSL) is very convenient; I can walk there from my house. However my experiences with MSL have almost always been unsatisfactory. In June 2005 I flew round-trip from MSL to Houston TX (IAH). The pilot would not land at MSL on the return trip because of a problem at the airport so he flew over the airport turned around and flew back to Memphis. The problem was that the VOR was not working and claimed the pilot it was too hazy to land using VFR (Visual Flight Rules). The pilot told us seven passengers all on business that he would not have left Memphis had he known about the problem at MSL. The MSL staff said that the VOR had been out for a month and that other pilots had been landing without it. The MSL staff told my wife who relayed the information to me that if my plane the first of the day could not land then the second plane last of the day would probably not be able to land either. None of the passengers including myself was willing to take a chance on Northwest Airlink (NWA) being able to land the second plane. I rented a car from Avis at a cost of over $170 plus gas for the two and half hour drive from Memphis to Muscle Shoals. This is not the first time I have had to rent a car to get home because of NWA and MSL but it will be the last.

Flew out of MSL for a trip last month. (June 2005) Booked on the morning flight and was scheduled to arrive at my destination in the early afternoon on Northwest Airlink. However due a mechanical issue the morning flight was canceled. Northwest Airlink(Operated by MESABA) called me at home and already had me booked on the late afternoon flight to Memphis getting into Arkansas that evening. When time came to catch the connecting flight we had a gate hold due to severe weather over the airport in Memphis. Finally arrived at my destination about 40 minutes late. I have to give the MSL Northwest crew a Job Well Done. They showed excellent customer service and did everything they could to make my flight out as pleasant as possible. Mechanical issues come up from time to time and the weather tends to throw a curve ball at us causing one to adjust travel plans. This is to be expected. The return flights operated on- time from gear up to gear down from Arkansas back to Memphis on into Muscle shoals. Weather: Clear skys and mild temps during the trip home. We even arrived in Muscle Shoals about 15 minutes ahead of schedule. As Mentioned in my previous comments MSL is a good alternative to other nearby airports. Parking is just 2.00 a day and if you book 2-3 weeks ahead you can get fares lower than at the other larger nearby airports. Granted flights are limited and experienced some challenges on my last two trips out of MSL. Will continue to utilize the airport for future trips. One additional fact: Avis Rental Car does have a Rental center adjacent to the airport terminal building. They Do Not have a counter inside the Terminal only Enterprise Rental Car does. If North Alabama and Southern TN are in your plans check out MSL as an alternative to other nearby airports.

Flew out of MSL in December of 2004. Small airport with 2 flights daily to Memphis on Northwest Airlink Saab 340 Aircraft. MSL is about 70 miles west of HSV International Airport. Experience was good. Saved about $ 90.00 in parking and airfare from MSL. The Saab aircraft was a pretty nice plane for a commuter. Drawbacks: Limited flights with 2 a day. Positives: Parking is $2.00 a day compared to 8-10 a day at HSV. Fares are usually lower if booked in advanced. I could have flown out of HSV but found MSL to be a better deal. Will try to contact the Airport and pass on my experience and ideas to improve air travel in the area. Finally If your a Golfer MSL is 15 minutes from the New Robert Trent Golf Course their in Northwest Alabama. Also a new Convention Center and Hotel will open soon. If flying to North Alabama MSL is a alternative to HSV. Even though flights are limited. Enterprise R-Car is on sight.

Hell on earth! Despite the airport being modernised and made bigger by Fraport, my experience on departure was nothing short of hell. On arrival, the air conditioning in a heatwave was not working. The departures/check in hall was packed full of travellers. Long queues of people waiting because there were not enough check in staff for all the flights. BA had only one lane for check in, no business lane. My flight was late leaving because of this. Eventually another line was opened but still no line for BA Club Europe. It took nearly an hour to check bags in, in sweltering heat. Fraport have really got it all wrong, hopeless management and clearly understaffed.

Very quick visit through this airport - it's small and gets very busy but I did not encounter any issues. Bags arrived on belt within 10 minutes, was out in 20 mins. Check in efficient, small duty free shop, kiosk airside, security staff polite. Am embarrassed to witness how rude some passengers are when using this airport. They don't use bins for their litter, talk rudely to staff and have an air of arrogance. It will never be Changi but it works for the short time you are there.

Abrupt and rude staff. Departure lounge has 1 person serving in the cafe. She makes the coffee, gets the food, takes the cash. A guy smashed a bottle of wine and she went to mop it up. Hence extremely slow service. Rubbish place

You know an airport has major problems when the number of "welcome assistants" exceeds the number of check in staff. If I am going to hell when I die, Mykonos airport reminded me what I can expect. The new private owners give every indication of wanting to milk the profits without considering passengers at all. It was completely unclear where to queue to check in and I wasted time where you hand your bag over and had to queue again. Several people made the same mistake. Departures horrible. No spare seats, 30 minute queue just to get a cold drink. No vending machines.

Considering that Mykonos is a small, hilly island, this little airport does well. It is small so transit through from disembarkation to exit is really quick and not far to walk. Arrived on connecting flight from Athens on Aegean at 6.30am. Bags were out in around 10 minutes. Return flight back to Athens a week later. Afternoon flight so busier as 2 flights departing together. Check in was busy, big queues but efficient check in staff. Small coffee / sandwich counter and gift shop airside and small duty free shop, toilet facilities and snack bar with hot drinks once passed passport control and security. It's not the Business Lounge at Changi but it does the job for the short time people are there. Good job.

This place doesn't even deserve to be called an airport. Nothing I've recognised from 30 years of air travel is present here. Certainly nothing that's made travelling easier. It's total chaos. Badly designed and totally disorganised. From arriving to boarding the flight I was stood in any of four different queues for two hours. Checking in on advance saves no time. You have to queue out of the airport at a desk which has no sign so you just hope it's the right one. People push in constantly. After an hour of that once you've it a tag for your bag you have to queue again to deposit your bag because the scanner is before the check in desk conveyors. Then queue again for passport. Then stand in a packed gate area in another queue until you board. We got in a bus that left us near the wrong plane and had to walk across the Tarmac. Stressful, chaotic, tiring and a massive time waster.

Absolute chaos. Very little staff to help, no television screens to advise on passenger travel information. People were queuing at the wrong places thinking that they were queuing at the check in desk when in fact they were queuing at the departure security area all due to the fact there isn't the staff and no clear signs to be seen anywhere. The toilets are terrible, dirty with no proper facilities for passengers. Only one small cafe in which I had to queue for 30 minutes to buy a bottle of water and a juice. There is inadequate seating with passengers having to stand for lengthy periods of time. Mykonos Airport needs a complete overhaul to ensure its passengers receive a good service. The island has a lot of tourism so come on mykonos airport do something about this situation.

The worst airport we have ever been to, it's an absolute shambles from the minute you walk through the door both coming and going. There is no organisation. You queue to check in then queue in an even bigger queue to drop your bag then another queue for security. There are no computer screens so you have no idea about your flight times etc or delays. No air conditioning. The toilets are disgusting, no tissue, never been cleaned by looks of it. Not a nice experience which is a shame as Mykonos itself is absolutely stunning but the airport would put us off coming back.

Probably the worst airport I've ever been through. Woefully understaffed, poorly laid out and even more poorly organised. Dirty, with even dirtier toilets with no soap and the longest security queue ever. Mykonos is a beautiful place but this airport means I may never return.

Avoid this airport if you can. When arriving at Mykonos airport the 1st August, in the peak of the holiday season, 3 flights were leaving at the same time and only 2 check in desks were open. It took 2.5 hours to check in one luggage. No effort has been made to speed up the process. There was not a single information screen or announcement to tell about delays and no staff was visible. The checked-in bags security is made manually by the passenger and you need to go through the other queues. It's very messy and disorganized. The departure lounge is small and very crowded. Our flight was delayed 2 hours simply to allow private jets to land and our plane was not supplied with water. The service provided by the airport is unacceptable. Mykonos has been a popular destination for decades but their airport is beyond any acceptable standards.
Needed a wheel chair because of an injury, people were so helpful and caring. A special thank you to Damian who pushed my wheel chair. So grateful! Thank you

For a small beachside city developed as a getaway destination for North Americans, this little modern airport did not disappoint me. Getting through security was a breeze (very friendly TSA), and compared to other airports I've been to, navigating is easy enough. If you are someone who goes to the airport not just to fly but to shop mountains of stuff this airport might not be for you, granted it has somewhere between 15 and 20 gates total, and there is no gargantuan walkway of duty-free shops to be found. The terminal is very modern and clean. For some reason, despite being first in line for takeoff, it did take us about 15 min to get off of the ground. Lots of general aviation, so this might be a regular thing. Bottom line, would I fly here? Absolutely. This airport is all about convenience and efficiency.

So upon the approach of my gate for my first departure, (5 minutes after boarding time), none of the flight details in the entire airport had been updated to inform me that my flight was delayed. This is Spirit Airlines that I'm referring to. My flight had been delayed over 2 hours due to the lack of crew. I know this is a small
airport, but it is not hard to update your information in the airport, the terminal, the gate, or online in order to inform your passengers before potentially going through security. On top of all of the inconvenient change of plans, the lady at my gate attempting to inform us of all that changed was quite possibly the most incoherent person I spoke to on my 4 day stay here in South Carolina. I will never connect here or fly Spirit again. The only bit of accommodations or considerations I received was a free upgrade to vacant exit row seats. I didn't receive a voucher for breakfast, no help trying to find another airline that could get me there sooner, or a voucher for a future flight for satisfaction. Had it not have been for the pilots coaxing all of us passengers and explaining what she apparently was incapable of, there would have been an outrage in Gate A.

We were delayed for 2 nights due to bad weather on the 17th and 18th January 2016. The staff at Mytilene Airport in Lesbos were excellent, they kept a smile during a very difficult time for them. We were given a voucher for food and drinks each time our flight was cancelled, 4 times in all, and they sent us to very good hotels both nights. In addition, when we asked if they could extend our journey for the days that we had lost, they did with no problems.

The worst airport I have ever departed from. From the seriously bad acoustics to the constant announcements screaming incredibly loud. The announcements were literally yelling, we could not speak among ourselves it was an awful experience. They also unnecessarily confiscate all Water purchased once you are past security. We had no water when going through security. We spent $29 On water to have to throw it out at the gate. Why ? I have travelled all over the world and have never had water confiscated at the gate. Horrible airport.

Noise announcements My flights had been delayed today It’s now more than 5 hours that I’m still waiting I’m right now at the airport (gate 8) Not sure if i’ll get my flight But my disappointment is for the amount of repeated announcements. I’ve been counting: it’s less than 40 seconds between announcements and they repeat over and over the same message. This must be the most noise airport I’ve ever been (and I’ve been to big ones) I love Fiji islands. This has nothing to do with the numbers of repeated announcements they do.

International layover - international transit queue was slower than customs. Security check required but never left secure zone of the airport. Had a lady behind me, have her sealed duty free purchases taken. She purchased from her last location and was given no opportunity to access her checked bags. Based upon experience and other reviews. It's a nice airport, friendly staff, with absurd and antiquated policies blindly followed by staff. Do not recommend.

Staff are friendly, facilities clean, but was quite annoyed that when I deboarded and went through the transit area security checkpoint, 3 bottles of perfume I bought in the departure terminal of LAX immediately prior to the flight to Fiji were confiscated and destroyed because they were just over 100mls (even after I showed them the receipt proving I had just bought them in LAX). The most annoying part, apart from wasting my money and no longer having a gift to bring back to my daughter, was that immediately after you leave this transit lounge security checkpoint, you proceed straight into a shop that sells bottles of perfume that are over 100mls, meaning that you will need to take those bottles in your carry-on back for your next flight anyway, so what is the point of destroying my bottles? Not impressed. Airport security team needs to be sat down to explain how they justify such an absurd policy.
I found very good customer service by each and every worker at the airport whom we dealt with. Wifi facilities were excellent with no interruptions. Overall it passes the required tests

Airport itself is fine. Simple. Easy to get around and not too large. There is a Tapoo shop and Burger King check-in side. Once through security there is a couple more eating places and 2 bigger duty free shops as well as a WHSmith. There is a very weird rule that you have to carry your Toiletries in a ziplock bag for check-in. This is OK except they want to charge you for one. It seems a very pointless rule for rules sake. But then after you've gone through the gate things get strange. Water and stuff you've bought in the departure lounge also has to be under the 100ml or in a duty free bag. They check all your bags and so I had a small bottle of unopened water just for the flight and had to throw it. The shops should tell you this or everything should be put in a duty-free bag. (tho that's a bit useless for water) It's a weird rule, and completely pointless since no other countries do it. It ruins all the rest of the experience if the airport. The staff also can't tell you why they are doing it.

Nadi airport was very busy when we arrived. We had to use steps to exit the plane and then walk a way. Three international flights landed so immigration was very crowded. Many people with children and elderly having to line up for some time. It was very slow. Some passengers must have had issues as some were with agents for a long time. Shame these are not dealt with separately. Bags were already there by the time we got through. Then we headed towards car rental to get our SIM card. F$49 card saw our whole trip through. (digicel). Departing was ok. Note there are only two options to eat landslde but far more airside. Also if you buy water airside they will bag it so it is ready as you board the flight as your bags get searched before boarding.

Nadi is a fine airport in some ways, and an airport in need of even more significant improvements in other ways. After flying in and out twice, I'm glad to see this small airport mostly modernized (at least the lobby and check-in areas), and looking very beautiful. This is a reflection of the success of Fiji's tourism industry, and the welcoming face that Fiji wants to portray for tourists. Check-in was not a challenge at all. Going through customs and immigration, leaving the airport briefly, then going back through security pre-gate were no problem. The signage to shuttle buses, taxis and public buses could still stand to be improved, but the airport was so small that I found where I was going. A bus pass can be bought for $5 (Fijian dollars), and a bus can be taken into central Nadi for less than ($2 USD). Connecting to your next flight should be no issue, as, like I said, going through customs is no problem (as long as you don't have anything significant to declare). Now, there are some cons. First of all, there's only one gift shop thingy I can remember post-security, and their prices are as high or higher on some products than you'd pay in the USA, Australia, or New Zealand. They have a monopoly! Second, staff in said gift shop don't seem to care if you fall over dead, as long as they get their money, as that's obvious in their attitudes. Third, security personnel have this stupid policy where they check carry-on bags AT the gate as planes are being boarded, without warning. They don't want any "unauthorized" liquids to be brought on, which means that even your carry-on-friendly toiletries better be in Ziploc bags (thankfully, mine were), and they'll confiscate your $4.00+ drink bottle that you bought in that unfriendly gift shop for "security reasons." Yeah, I echo the sentiments of some other travelers who have posted in saying, "That's stupid!" Fourth, their Wi-Fi ranges from pathetic to non-existing. In all, I'd far rather fly into and out of Nadi than a lot of major hub airports in the USA, but for an otherwise very welcoming Fijian people and culture, this airport doesn't have a lot of the "Bula!" spirit.

The custom security was ridiculous! Traps everywhere! Started with the custom security who was asking for the little zip bag for small items, where we only had a lipstick. The security was very “nice” to advise the bag cost 50 cents from the shop next to the checkpoint. When we went there to buy, we were told there was a minimum spend of $5. Walked around the shop, nothing is $5. Then we bought the cheapest item of $7.95, plus the 50 cents, plus 2.5% transaction fee, ended up spending almost $10. No other country’s security actually have this kind of requirement. Fiji is the place for tourism to be 'shaved' by the locals. Be careful!

Arriving into Nadi airport was no problem at all however departing was quite ridiculous with the rules they have in place and procedures. Before checking in, we were stopped by a security agent at her post, who wanted to see our passports and ask us some TSA questions which is fine! However she asked if I had an itinerary for the both of us which I had luckily printed but didn’t expect for it to be needed at that time as all you usually need to check in to any airport is a passport and she wasn’t even a check in agent. So that was a hassle and waste of time? Check in process was fine once we were done with the security agent. However going through security screening was annoying!
