They had pulled me aside for a small hand sanitiser I had in my bag and a roll on. I’ve travelled through so many airports where it is okay to have these items not in a bag as well as a lip balm. But these guys just seemed bored and wanted to make it a big deal. Luckily there was a little toiletry bag attached to my suitcase that they put it in but it was very unnecessary and wasted my time. I’ve also read that they won’t let you take duty free products through from another country even if it’s in those security bags provided in other countries? This is the only airport I know that does this and it is ridiculous! This is the worst airport I have travelled through.
Air-conditioning was not working on the first floor. Too hot and suffocating on first floor. Airport staff should monitor the temperature regularly. This is the bare minimum standard.

Absolute worst experience with the customs officer. I had arrived from Sharjah with Air Arabia, and customs wanted to check the baggage of each and every passenger. Slowed the exit process. Even though the signage says green channel and red channel, they force all passengers to go through the red channel by checking all the bags and questioning them on any electronic device. I was moving to India for good, and by law, I'm allowed to carry my personal effects. They made pay for my 3 year old camera and 2 year old gimball. The person from the bank who is supposed to validate the receipt, wasn't there on duty and came almost an hour late. Despite complaining to the customs department, no serious action was taken. I will never fly into NAG and will never recommend anyone else to fly into NAG. Unprofessional staff who rob you in broad daylight.

It’s a smaller airport compared to Mumbai; not a problem actually. Some toilets on the arrival hall are not good. This airport has more shopping options now and it’s enough actually. There are spa and lounge facilities available here. The lounges are okay. I have never experienced any delay to date. Overall an above expectation feel. It gets my job done.

This airport has improved a lot as compared to my previous journeys. The areas that needs improvement are announcements quality and sound system. This system lacks clarity and speakers as well as waiting hall ambiance are not designed to hear announcement clearly. The baggage carousal requires some maintenance for the area around it. Some of the building materials are not good quality and total area looks like a amateur work.Just after the security clearance please put up a clear signage where each gates are. Which gates are upstairs, where is the lift location etc. Similarly clear signage for assembly point and first aid kit.

It's really shame how the facilities are at this airport. Authorities seriously need to look into certain issues, if this is to be called an international airport. A. There was no snacks or refreshment counter in waiting area open past 22:30, which is extremely inconvenient as there are some flights scheduled past 23:30-00:00 hrs. PVK Bar is open though. B. The waiting area was not clean, and it looked as if the maintenance guys left sweeping work halfway through. Air conditioning was not working properly it seems. C. Lighting is extremely dull. D. It's good to use TV screens for entertainment purpose, but at least a few can show flight updates as well.

It is sad to write a negative review about the airport of my home-town. But it is so inconvenient to travel from here. Now Nagpur airport is called as International airporr but it is shameful that they do not have wifi facilities at the airport or ask for Indian numbers to get the code. Not a single telephone-coin box to call in case of emergency. Staff are so unprofessional and slow. They have no idea about the airline they are working for with flight timings. Please make basic arrangements so that we don’t have to feel awkward when bringing foreign travellers with us.

I visited Nagpur City in August 2017. I flew from Sharjah to Nagpur. The experience of Nagpur Airport is one of the worst I have had. The staff are unprofessional. Customs officials present at the airport are the worst, they will check each and every passenger, their way of checking is to treat you as if you are a thief or a prisoner. Second worst thing is the luggage belt, it took one and half hours for my luggage to arrive on the belt. I advise everyone to avoid this airport as much as possible.

Nagpur is the worst and most inconvenient airport I have ever visited. The luggage x-ray at the entrance is still followed which has stopped almost in most of the airports. Even after we got our boarding passes for the flight we had to wait for 30 min for another security check in. This is inconvenient to the passengers who had to stand and Wait for so long. There was no genuine reason for the delay. The security was filled with staff and sitting talking and reading news papers. I'd rather prefer traveling by train than use this airport. Extremely disappointed. Where other cities are developing so fast when it comes to roads, airports etc Nagpur has a long fight to win to even get to a decent place. You are also using tags for the cabin bag security which is ancient and had been curtailed in other airports.

We have used this airport in the past, there is noticeable improvement in the facilities and services. The check in are is spacious with adequate seating and few shops. The check in process was smooth and the security swift and friendly. After security there is a large waiting area with free newspapers and view of the apron, the separture lounge is upstairs and they have 2 aerobridges. A good regional airport if you want to go to see the Big Cat (Tigers).

Nagpur is the largest city in central India and the second capital on Maharashtra. Nagpur Airport (Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar International Airport) is a small airport located 7km from the city centre. The airport is very small in size and also in the amount of destination it serves, so it is difficult to judge. Given its capacity it can handle max up to 3 aircraft's at a time and anything more than that there will be congestion and the flight will be delayed. The airport is clean and the staff can be rude at times.

A truly awful airport to fly from in so many way. We had to pass through 4 stages of security starting outside the airport which was so cursory it was meaningless. Then we had to go through 3 full-on get undressed security stations one within yards of actually boarding. I wouldn’t mind if it made you feel safer but it didn’t. There was zero signage to find the Premium Plaza lounge that BA use, and staff sent us in 3 different directions. All in all a depressing way to end a great holiday.

This airport is horrible. The staff are unfriendly and rude, they are close minded, do not respect airlines priority boarding! Painful to check in and even to pass through control check in. Very disappointing after a nice trip to have to deal with frustrated employees.

I am a Business Traveller and have Sky Priority. The Sky Priority queues in Nairobi are never monitored and are always a free-for-all. Why can't there be staff to man the queue? The chaos causes delays every time. When you speak to staff they ignore you. I dread going through Nairobi. Boarding the plane, Sky Priority is ignored. Everyone gets up and you have to push your way through as a Business Class passenger!

Always the same. Coming off a long haul flight and transiting through JKIA. Even as a business class traveller the queue for the transit security check takes at least an hour. Total chaos reigns. Only two gates are open. Security staff totally overwhelmed. This is by far the worst airport to transit through

Due to a late arrival of our international flight we needed to stay overnight in Nairobi. Though we had a great stay at the hotel, it was really short because all took so long at the airport after landing. It was confusing and messy. As I was traveling as a mum alone with 2 young children it always a challenge in itself so late at night. (Landed around 11.15pm if not mistaken). My children’s boarding pass was printed but not mine, so staff took my original boarding pass and went to print it, so I ended up totally at the back of the queue. Despite asking I was not allowed to shift back forward with the children. I showed them my Tz residence permit while I was in the queue so I was told I didn’t need to fill in a form. But 10 minutes after completing the immigration check I was called back to fill a form anyway. Immigration officer was very insensitive by - yet again - asking out loud and in front of my children « are these your children ». When I commented that he should be more sensitive with this question in front of the children he refused to stamp our passports. Then he went to watch some video/movie on his phone. We waited really long, both in the immigration queue as well as downstairs. WiFi was not working (there had also been no WiFi in the plane, so had not been able to notify anyone). Nobody of the staff provided much information. We were « dumped » in another queue downstairs not knowing what was meant to happen. We waited a really long time for the hotel pick up with no info. Six weeks ago, we also passed through Nairobi airport, and both going and return we (a small group of passengers) got lost in transit, up and down stairs. It took a while to figure out where go. Both building and staff are the most disappointing I have ever encountered in any of my trips. Will do whatever possible to avoid this airport in the future. Kenya. What a missed chance to shine.

Very expensive compared to any other airports that I have used. Facilities are very basic. The inflight information board does not update making it difficult. The announcement is also done in a local accent that is not clear.

Baggage collection-I discovered that staff in Nairobi attempted and managed to break the zip for one of the bags, because the padlock was too hard to pick. I could not tell if anything was taken but if anything was taken, it is not that important as I could not tell what it was. Return journey, staff dealing with baggage managed to uncode my bag and removed items of clothing which again we cannot tell what they took as we never count what we take on holiday to wear. Our bag was 3kg lighter by time we collected it in London. When we were collecting our bags from the airport, we immediately realised the Zip was open and there was a huge space showing either dirty clothes had been stolen as we did not have any valuables. Our suitcase weighed 21.9kg when we weighed it at home and it was 22kg when weighed at the check in counter in Nairobi during our return journey. After noticing the zip had been opened, we immediately spoke with Customer service at the London airport who asked us to put any claim online. We didn't know what was missing but we weighed our bag and it was 19.1kg and not 22kgs as it was when we checked it in. So we know about 3kg worth of dirty items were taken but we can't tell exactly what they took. So by process of elimination, we know locks and padlocks are being broken in Nairobi by the bag handlers. Whoever manages these staff handling bags at Jomo kenyatta international airport Nairobi; you and your staff are giving Kenya a bad name breaking people's bags which is a violation of their privacy. The last time I was in Kenya, I had my sunlight bar soaps stolen from one of the bags and I think it is time to bring this to the attention of whoever manages these people. Stealing dirty clothes! Most people carry valuables in hand luggage so stop with the embarrassment. Going forward, I will never take check in luggage to Kenya. Everyone travelling there, double lock your bags with as many locks as you can, or just have hand luggage as this problem appear well entrenched in Nairobi. I cannot see it going away unless they have CCTV cameras to deter these thieves masquerading as paid staff. Brighter side, the staff at the first check as you arrive at the airport as well as those at the main entrance are brilliant. Appear very cheerful and give guidance so I will be rating 2 just for those staff. Also staff at the passport control and those checking and providing boarding passes are brilliant. After that, everything is down hill and gets worse !

Worst airport I have ever seen, in all my travels: boarding started way too late, for all documents (incl. COVID) to be checked. Same documents have been checked at 3 queues, till boarding. No priority boarding for business. No social distancing whatsoever! The plane is a Covid timebomb, sadly. No seating available at check-in area. No one to ask anything at the multiple airport queues I had to endure. My plan was to come back to Kenya, but to pass this airport again, that would be an ordeal. Better to visit other African countries, maybe they work better than Kenya which is a mess.

This airport is horrible. The staff are unfriendly and rude, and also corrupt looking for every chance they can get to take money away from you. I had a flight which allowed 2 x 23 kg bags per person, I had one bag of 25 kgs and my partner had one bag of 11kgs. The staff refused to give me my ticket until I paid 50 USD for the 2 extra kilos. I had exactly the same weight coming from Cape Town and this wasn’t a problem.  The guard at one of the scanning stations also tried to ask for a bribe because we had beer in our luggage (which we checked and double checked beforehand that it was indeed allowed). I’m so disgusted by this place and the staff here. Kenya really needs the tourism industry yet doesn’t care at all about the tourists. I will not be visiting again and will encourage anyone else thinking of coming here to steer clear and rather support any other African country more worth while

This airport is a complete disaster, it looks like an abandoned warehouse, there no information center to ssk for any informations, no one knows what there doing because everyone I did ask about the information, they didn’t know anything. Staff are just busy on their chats, for example at Gate 6 for TRANSIT INFO DESK. No one was there for a good 5 hours, I’m like what are they being paid for if they can’t be present for assisting passengers. I can’t express enough bad the experience was, and how on earth the Toilets don’t have water? Really are you guys out of your minds. I’m so sorry for those who have to use this Airport as their main point for traveling. There’s no restaurant or cafes for passengers or lounges and it is by far the worst airport you can go to.

This is a small airport in a small exclave of Azebaijan. It looks neat and clean especially from the outside. Very few tourists arrive here. Arrival and immigration was smooth. A curious thing about this airport is that on departure, you first need to go through immigration first. There was only one immigration officer on duty. Check-in was slightly chaotic with local passengers breaking the queue. There are no proper duty free shops inside. The only shop selling local products was staffed by a single, bored assistant. There is not much to do in this airport.

This typical Thai regional airport is surprisingly busy. Perhaps also due to the presence of the Chevron offshore helicopter base. There are about 10 flights a day to-from Bangkok. Facilities are limited, so it's not an airport to linger in. That said, the land side restaurant upstairs has a nice view of the apron so you can have a beer until you see your plane landing before going through to the departure lounge, where seating is limited. The car park is always crowded, which is due to people using it as a "park n ride" when they fly to Bangkok, it being free of charge.

Terminal 1 of Nanchang Changbei airport is horrible and a complete embarrassment to Nanchang and China. It is supposed to be international but I've seen small town bus stations in a better condition. They seem to be forever renovating the international terminal meaning that when passengers arrive to check-in they must stay in a waiting area that is tiny and becomes very cramped. Furthermore there is no heating or AC in this part of the airport so you feel uncomfortably cold or hot depending on the weather. Check-in desks only open 2 hours before and once you clear immigration there isn't even a restaurant just a "shop" that sells limited confectionery and duty free products. Finally you can never get a taxi at the international terminal. If you're lucky a tout might appear but you will get ripped off or you can walk across the car park to the domestic terminal and if you're luckier still, you might get a metered taxi but they are reluctant to use the meter. Overall a pathetic excuse for an airport and I always dread flying out of here as travelling from Nanchang Airport, especially the international terminal, is an ordeal.

The airport is very new and modern. I have flown through this airport multiple times, but this is the first time at the new terminal. It is a lot larger than the original terminal. There was finally free Wi-Fi and it was pretty fast considering the internet in China. It was mainly based off of Shanghai Pudong (the airport I was actually flying to) and had the identical announcement system that PVG terminal 2 had. Although there were a few foreigners (including me), it felt very open and very welcoming.
Awful experience. Airport handling makes the communications only in French. We had a flight canceled and the management of the situation was terrible. Nobody seems to know what to do.

Worst airport. Security control took away 3 “hard cheeses” claiming food cannot exceed 100g a piece. Also took away a climbing carabiner that I’ve traveled 50+ countries with. Never seen such ridiculous rules, implemented in the rudest way possible by the staff there. For a flight within the EU. Apart from that, airport is very old fashioned and not very clean.

Worst airport experience ever. We arrived 2.5 hours before departure and there was no check in or bag drop. Check in finally showed as opened (less than 2 hours before our flight) but we had to stand for over an hour in a confused crowd of hundreds of people as the three check in staff tried to first funnel through all passengers for a flight that left just 10 minutes before ours - without having separated the two flight queues or directing the two flight queues to separate desks. The result was chaos, queue jumping, confusion and bad tempers all round, including an extremely nasty check in lady screaming at passengers and insisting on measuring people's carry on handbags even as the situation around her descended into farce. We waited for an hour and 20 mins before we could finally drop off our bags (that were already checked in online!!!) before having to race through security and passport control, we didn't even have time to go to the toilet before having to board the plane. Security and gate staff were either stressed and rude, or oblivious and standing around chatting instead of helping. Security and gate staff were totally unaware of what passengers had been through in the check in hall - or maybe they simply didn't care. I saw one staff member at passport control scolding passengers for being late, the same passengers who had been stranded for hours trying to check their bags in. There wasn't a manager or supervisor in sight all morning. Everyone on our plane was upset, furious, or stressed, especially those travelling with young children. Other delights included no luggage trolleys in the drop off zone, broken vending machines and broken lifts and escalators - we helped one single parent carry their baby's buggy down two flights of stairs because none of the lifts worked and no staff wanted to help. Avoid this airport at all costs, it's a horrendous experience.

Feels old and outdated. Outside is chaotic, confusing on a first visit. Inside feels cramped and old, lighting (all artificial, barely any outside light entering in the areas before security. No matter, it's not meant for you to stay anyway, there are barely anywhere seat. The waiting area is really small, with low ceiling that would need a good cleaning. Finally some natural light, but not a view still. Only thing to see out the window is the large bridges with people disembarking. A place to go through, not to be enjoyed.
Worst airport we have ever been to! Little seating, chaotic security for domestic flights and not even a cafe open!! Go via another route if you can.

Judging by the other reviews here I am not alone in my disappointment. In addition to everything others have mentioned I will add that I was flying with a well traveled backpack on which I had a 10cm long section of bike chain attached to it (impossible to take off without a chain tool or to cut the pack itself). Not even enough to put my fist through. It was used to pick up the pack and secure a lock to. I've traveled far and wide with this chain on the pack - even to the USA where Homeland Security is notorious for its scrutiny of such things. Well at Nantes at the security checkpoint they considered this small piece of bike chain to be able to be used as a weapon! They said I either needed to check the bag (EUR40) or cut it off. As the pack is not worth EUR40 I told them to cut it off - after giving them an honest, if not perhaps sarcastic, comment on how they operate their airport. After more than 20 years coming through this airport to vacation in and around the surrounding areas I am calling it quits. I will go elsewhere as all of my experiences over the years have added up to enough negativity that I no longer wish to spend my hard earned money in this region. Farewell!

I felt this is a sort of makeshift airport, a lot of missing and confusing information and works in progress, very, very limited seats, after I cleared security, which was quick, I felt I was on a war scene, with dozens and dozens of customers seating on the floor, some of them even playing cards or having snacks, seems they are used to this kind of situation. Gate is confusing the announcements in English are very poor and one can almost not understand anything, the only very positive thing from this airport is that public transport is free on weekends, both ways. Tip: local cafes serve the same quality cafe latte and snacks for half of the price if compared to international brands!

We had thought of a walking holiday but we got one free courtesy of this airport. After walking a long way to the departure portal, at the far end of the building, we had to walk another long way on the ground floor, up stairs and back along the same, but reverse route to get to security. The officers there were anything but friendly and it was obvious that they escalated their searches and arrogance if one responded with anything other than utter compliance. Not a smile or a 'please' or 'thank you' in sight. They all wore identity badges but would not allow me to inspect these. Utterly the worst goodbye I have ever had from anywhere. After more walking, we were directed down to the waiting area on the ground floor, which just happened to be adjacent to where we left our hold baggage. The signage is abysmal, amazing us that anyone got on the correct flight. Then more walking across the hardstanding and up yet more stairs to board the aircraft. Both my wife and I are over 80 years old and were completely exhausted by this pre-flight activity. We were so looking forward to using this airport - but found it abysmal, soulless even hostile.

An embarrassingly poor airport. The largest in Western France and a choice of six sandwiches and a couple of cakes from a buffet bar. The bread was frozen and the sandwiches were disgusting. Nothing else apart from a small duty free shop barely larger than a Proxi. With trains on strike, gilets jaunes blocking roads and this standard of service this is a country that knows how to take the mickey. As I am in the hospitality industry I reassure myself that this is the quality of the competition in France.

The worst experience ever. Very poorly organized and very poor quality. Lack of staff and lot of waiting. If you transfer remember that you have to go out and do the security check again which takes ages! Security are very grumpy and unfriendly. If anyone is planning to carry on a skateboard forget about it. Mine got confiscated due to the airport rules, even if I haven’t had any problem anywhere with this and I have been traveling with my skateboard for last 12 years. Avoid this airport!

It is so poorly organized that even if you tried to design a more inefficient system, you wouldn’t surpass them. Not to mention the staff constantly chatting with each other and treating you like a burden. Being an Italian myself, I feel ashamed about this airport.
Having read the previous reviews Naples did not disappoint. Rude staff even in the shops they couldn’t have been ruder. The place is  filthy and unorganised. Hope to never visit again

Tax free department is very disorganized. No one in the office. Called the number posted and no one shows up. You have to check in the luggage then carry the luggage to their office and still no one there. Called the number again and they said to go the machine to do it. Of course the machine is not working then went back to their office, still on one there. Called them again. She said well we need to see your luggage still no one is available. I talked to the lady in the front of the airport they said tax free department is very dysfunctional. In the end we DID NOT GET OUR MONEY. so many people had the same experience. This is one of the worst airport to steal others money without any regards. What a shame for the Naples airport because of this department.

Despite booking special assistant for a severely disabled 87 years old lady there was no assistance available unless we had to wait two hours in which we would’ve missed out on the flight. We travelled with British Airways but the service provided is by Naples airport management which is absolutely ridiculous. Disgusting I would avoid coming here at any cost if you are disabled.
Worst airport, too few seats for so much people and just a few toilets. Totally crowded. All flights are delayed, mine to Vienna they are still postponing, now more than 2 hours and 23 minutes.
Confusing, chaotic, dirty toilets, lack of seating. There's no logic to it's layout. I'd find an alternative next time. I love Italy but this is the worst airport ever!

Lives up to its name : no signs, chaos, rude airport staff, overflowing rubbish bins, 80% of flight delayed, and no aircon - but great food. Unless one wants to fly to Rome and drive not many options to visit Campania, and it is worth visiting so just have to roll with it and accept it.

Naples Airport. Welcome to chaos. As usual (I have arrived at this airport about 8 times) the time to get off the plane and to baggage reclaim via an airport bus was 45 minutes. It seems to take forever. The baggage reclaim area is too small to handle multiple flight arrivals. It becomes a scrum, with insufficient space to negotiate the identified belt, the one exit point, and the hordes of people with their luggage. And then there’s the minimum 45-60 minute wait for your bags. It’s painful. The experience gets better as you then have to get out…past the reception committees. And into fresh air…..no, wait. Here we go again. Exiting the airport means inhaling lungfuls of secondhand cigarette or vape smoke.  So, I survived the experience again, but wait for the return. It’ll be the same painful process, but in reverse. The takeaway. This is a small and congested airport surrounded by vehicle drivers who use their horns to communicate, Last time, earlier this year, I couldn’t drive back to the airport and went around in circles, despite having a Satnav, before eventually working out how to get to the hire car return. Enjoy, it’s a bumpy ride!

Horrible experience. Many of the people on our flight did not receive our luggage. We spent 4 hours being given vague advice by lost luggage and information (often contradictory) and which involved being continually sent to different carousels. Finally we gave up as for many of us, we were at the point of missing connections. Despite the number of times we had queued and been sent away and despite our time running out for making connections, we were forced to queue for another hour as there were many people who had arrived much later than us also missing luggage. The staff were indifferent and uncaring to our situation, even to the point of letting us have a pen to fill in their forms. The arrivals lounge was full of unclaimed baggage. It’s 10 days into our holiday and our baggage has not arrived. I feel genuinely upset by the uncaring attitude and unhelpful mess of the staff. It felt like they would say or do any old thing to get rid of us. I would never use this airport again

Please ever fly out or in to this airport. It is the absolute poorly run, least efficient, and incompetent out of all Ive been to. There are only 2 buses running for all of the gates. Our flight was severely delayed and will miss our connecting flight!

I would like to say a very special thank you to the security staff that helped my friend and I last week at Naples Airport. A friend had travelled earlier that day and inadvertently left his iPad behind in security. We only had a short time before our departure to try and retrieve it for him. The staff were fast, efficient and located the iPad within minutes! After running through some security checks we were able to take the iPad home, back to its owner, saving everyone a lot of time and energy. I don’t usually write reviews but the service we received from the security staff was first class and deserved a mention.

We arrived 3 hours early to check in and it took us 3.5 hours in line to actually check in. People were fainting as it’s June and the air conditioning was broken. Then the ticket agent said she wasn’t sure they would hold the plane - simultaneously- the tracking system for checked luggage broke down. It was a nightmare experience - there were so many people going to Dublin for connections. They ended up holding the plane because no one could get through to get on it. I’ll avoid Napoli airport like the plague it is.

The airport has a quick checkin counter right outside where you arrive with the taxi. This led to a checkin time for our Delta flight (including one checked in luggage) of just 4 minutes after I got out of the taxi. Security was fast too never experienced such a comfortable on boarding on any flight.

Friendly little country airport in Australia. Quiet clean terminal building with enough space for passengers using the frequent Regional Express Airlines Saab 340 services. This airport is well positioned between the towns of Narrandera and Leeton and has easy access to the main road to these centres. It also has rental car services. Best of all it was quiet and peaceful so one could do some work while waiting for flights (no blaring television in the corner as is often the case these days). Pleasant airport check-in staff at Regional Express as well.

Its been decades since I last traveled through Nashville. The transformation of this airport is amazing. The international arrivals facility has Global Entry but no Mobile Passport Control. Give yourself plenty of time (at least 2 hours) to make connecting flights. The lines care very long and the distances from the gates to Immigration and Customs are very long. The terminal was very crowded however with wheelchair assist, we were able to breeze through Immigration. The only drawback is that one has to exit the secured area and go through TSA security all over again with very long lines. Once you're through the security, one is met with wide open, very clean and brightly lit concourses with dining and shopping aplenty. Restrooms were very clean. The free airport WiFi was easy to connect to and very fast.

I'm not sure what ultimate plan is for gates C4- C11 is, but in its current state, its awful. I have never walked as much as I have in an airport as I have here. The shuttle bus process is really bad. Driving in a fully loaded bus with NO air is un excusable. The two tiny windows that were letting a tiny bit of air were not enough. We ended up sitting on the bus for a good 4 or 5 minutes while we waited for 3 Southwest planes to pass. When the last jet went by and started throttling up we got a nice HOT blast of the smell of jet fuel.  I can't say that I won't be back, but we may change airlines so we don't need to endure the poorly planned annex wing.

Shuttle between terminals to get to bag claim takes forever. Very poor design has shuttle bus.  Absolutely no controls at ride share pickup. Ubers double parried everywhere created 15 minute traffic jam delay. If you come to Nashville airport plan to wait. Everything takes three times longer than required. Poor design and poor governance.

Worst experience arriving to an airport. Have to stand in extremely long line waiting for shuttle to take you to main terminal to then get your bags and rental car. Took over 15 minutes standing in line with no official information from the airport staff. All information came from locals who were also in the line. Worst experience, arriving in a city. No soap on the ladies bathroom. Finally get on the shuttle to stand on the runway waiting for planes to taxi in and out. So now on a crowded shuttle watching planes move all around and still not to the terminal. Absolutely ridiculous and a miserable introduction to a city.

After having stood in line with my family for an hour and finally reaching the check-in counters for our airline, we were told to wait while while another 20+ people checked in before us, causing us to wait another 30 minutes. We were the only ones going to a separate state, so it would have been so easy to just check our 2 bags when we first got to check-in. So because adults couldn't plan ahead and get to the airport with plenty of time for their flight, we were the ones that had to stand there and wait for them. We finally made it to our gate with 10 minutes to spare. To say I was angry and frustrated that the employees had zero sense, is an understatement.

Had a great experience. Going through security was fast, had no wait time. They had great local beers on tap and even a smoking section. It costs 10 bucks to enter, but considering I haven't been in an airport that had one in 15 years it made the wait SO much better. 10/10 will layover in.

I am writing to complain about the cost of long-term economy parking. I have lived in large cities around the country and long-term economy parking is around 8-10$ per day. This airport has continuously raised its long-term parking fee over the last few years to a now astronomical amount of 18$ per day! That is unsatisfactory and unacceptable. There have been no improvements to the parking lot and there are not buses running more often to them. Why the unreasonable raise. The traffic at the terminals themselves is also horrible. People will be waiting for almost an hour to pick someone up around the holidays.

Getting in and out of the airport is now a real problem. Traffic does not flow around and is backed up constantly. New design has added stop lights which just backs up traffic even more. Years ago, BNA built a parking deck, then 2 years ago tore it down to do the new terminal and parking. Now everything is worse than was before. Even the shuttles to the parking areas are affected and now take forever to go to and from the pickup/drop off areas. Parking spaces are blocked off, constant construction. Cell phone lots have moved off site causing drivers to “Park” on the road. Traffic cops at arrivals do not enforce people from parking and moving on causing traffic to back up all the way around the short term parking area.

Flight 1101. Dec 23 12:23AM: We have been sitting on the tarmac for 2 hours tonight. Yes there was some snow here. We were told there are no open gates. Get the other passengers off the planes at the gates if they aren’t going to fly out. There is no reason for planes to stay boarded sitting and blocking the gates. Ridiculous. Very very dissatisfied.
Fantastic. Ample and clean restrooms. Great restaurants. Napping rooms available to rent. Everyone was kind and assisted as needed. They asked me if I needed help. Super customer friendly service.

I have flown with Bahamas air to Nassau at least 12 time. It was the first time we flew on a two engine prop plane. The plane was not the issue. It was boarding the plane. We entered the normal location then had to decline 20 stairs. The problem was with our carry on baggage, There was no attendant at the top of the stairs. I saw a shoot beside the stairs and placed my bag on the shoot. I had not looked to the bottom and had not realized someone was removing their bag at the bottom. I trust the sound of my bag travelling down the shoot caused her to look up and remove her arm before my bag slammed into hers. She looked up and was not happy. There needs to be attendant at the top to monitor when a bag can be place on the shoot which also runs very fast and could damage items in the bag. On our return to Tampa we departed on the ground and walked to another staircase which would take us the normal departure level. From prior experience I knew it was 20 stairs to the top. I am 78 with a heart problem and my wife is in her 80's. I was not going to carry our carry on up 20 stairs. There was no attendant present. I told the security guard I was not going to carry the bags up the stairs. The guard tried calling someone without success. There where two ground crew standing by the plane which she approached and one came to take the bags to the to the top.

Last week (January 25, 2018), my wife and I flew out of Nassau, Bahamas. We arrived at the airport two and a half hours early for our Delta flight to Atlanta, Georgia. I along with about 20 other passengers was randomly selected by the U.S. Transportation Security Administration (TSA) for extra security screening. My wife went through the regular security screening. The security screeners took an unbelievable 15 to 20 minutes to screen each passenger in the extra security line. There were eight passengers in the extra screening line ahead of me. More than two hours passed before I was screened. As a result, I missed my flight and had to re-book another flight to Atlanta, and also re-book my connecting flight to Baltimore-Washington Airport. My wife, waiting over two hours for me to be screened, chose to not get on our scheduled flight but to wait for me. Almost all the 20 passengers in the extra security screening line missed their flights.

Probably the most difficult thing is to get to this airport. If you are not staying in the hotel but in private accommodation as we did and you are far from Nassau downtown you will hardly see any taxis around. There is no bus going directly to the airport. You might ask the driver of bus route 12 to drop you off at the nearby roundabout and then walk around half a mile to the airport. The airport itself is divided into three different section. You must have in mind that you cannot just ask from which terminal your airline departs as that also depend on your destination. The US departures have a separate terminal.

This is a very nice airport. Very clean and modern. Airport staff are courteous and helpful. It is definitely the best airport I have been to in the Caribbean and definitely better than some airports in the US, especially Miami where you are not even offered free WiFi. Nassau airport has complimentary WiFi everywhere. Selection of popular restaurants inside the US departure lounge. There are some shops, but mostly expensive souvenirs. A great experience, hats off to everyone at NAS.

Nassau Airport has extremely over priced shops and restaurants. A pasta dish for over $35 in one of the restaurants I tried. Funny thing is that the airport speakers don't stop telling you to enjoy the 'excellent customer service and affordable prices'. Customer service is average to bad to be honest. Staff is moody, they know they get tourists any way so they don't care much. All shops closed down at 6pm without a place to buy a bottle of water. Not good when your flight is at 7pm and gets delayed for 3 hours. Overall, it was a bad experience and I don't recommend anyone to fly to the also overly price island. There are other Caribbean islands with more reasonable prices for sure.

This place is clean and efficient. Lots of room and well staffed airport. Both the international/domestic terminal and the USA pre clearance terminals are modern and the lines are usually moving very quickly. US Customs is exceptionally efficient and considering the volume of persons traveling the process is smooth and the staff is excellent and friendly. US citizens get to experience an even smoother passage with the automated terminals. Just make sure you follow all the rules because some of them might seem unnecessary but if you have had a big win at the casino declare it or loose it after a night in a terrible local lock up and a visit to a magistrate back in town the next day if it is not a Friday.

This airport has 2 terminals, one for USA flights and one for non USA flights. Not big airport. Inside is very clean and staff are very helpful. However, there are long waiting times at immigration and customs. Customs has no scanner machines so they have to open all bags for checks. Needed almost 2 hours to finish immigration and customs. When departing it is very quick. Inside the airport there are only a few shops.

Arriving: Lines for immigration lasted 45 minutes; US$18 charge for 4 minute (no exaggeration) cab ride that the hotel had said would cost no more than $10. Departing: airport merchants ready willing and able to rip you off if your guard is down for a minute.

This review is for International arrivals and US Departures. I've used this airport in December 2009 and then again in March 2013. In general a much better experience this time around. On arrival sufficient immigration desks were staffed and customs was quick enough so that I was in my hotel within 25 minutes of touching down. On departure the new US Departures terminal is much improved from the older version. Check in and security is quick and efficient. The only place where there are lines is the US immigration pre- clearance. Airside the terminal is quite pleasant with lots of shops restaurants etc. While the main restaurant (Kafe Kalik I think is pleasant with outdoor seating I would not recommend ordering food there unless you want to risk missing your flight - they took 45 minutes to bring our food.

My children ages 16 and 11 and I went to the Bahamas in June 2010. The airport was not bad at all. Yes the airport is smaller but it got me to where I was going! I did not run into one rude airport employee. Some were quite nice actually. 3 hours doesn't seem to be necessary but why chance it? There are a few places where you can get something to eat. One small restaurant dunkin doughnuts and subway. Also there are some local wares you can purchase and a convenience store. The bathroom is large enough and clean.The screening process went easily and quickly. Just be prepared. You know they want all of your documents out and ready so do just that. You know that you have to put everything through the xray machine so make it simple. Wear flip flops and keep your bags to a minimum. We didn't even check in any bags and had no problems. No different then any other airport.

The worst place to go if you're in a wheelchair - waited three hours to get moved from arrival to my gate. They just leave you setting there with all the other people with disabilities and ignore you till they have to move you before you miss your flight. Worst experience at a airport and I fly all over the world for business. Avoid if you can.

ANYN (Nauru Int’l Airport) is a small 2 story building and does not offer free wifi like most international airports. An air conditioned cafe had just opened recently late 2017 that’s got couple paying massage chairs, few selection of non-alcoholic beverages including instant tea and coffee, few choices of snacks, Asian food, ice cream etc.. Check-in counter and the cafe are both on lower level and departure lounge (air conditioned) is located on the upper level. VIP and business lounges are also available and seperate however I think VIP lounge had been moved downstairs outside. According to other local travellers it was Nauru’s government order to close down the smoking room. Toilets are better upstairs at departure lounge although can still be quite uncomfortable. There’s no ATM machine available.

A beautiful airport. All of you who remember how airline travel was in the sixties and seventies would recognise Ndola. Originally built as a R.A.F. airport during the second world war it has continued as the airport to service the Copperbelt region of Zambia. I arrived on a domestic flight and departed international to Johannesburg. Everything is so laid back and friendly. I doubt if there are to many airports that have straw thatched tables for your final beer before departing and straw thatched toilet blocks. I love this airport and I usually have tears in my eyes on arrival and also on departure.

Due to a mechanical fault, the plane that landed was too small for all of the passengers, So the ground staff at Nevsehir had to work really hard to deal with about 30 people who could not fit. The 4 staff in this small office tried so hard to identify the most urgent passengers who had connecting flights, then they prioritised everyone. The staff were faced with 30 passengers who all thought they were the most important person in the airport. We did not have a connecting flight and were lower priority. So the team arranged for about 20 of us to be bussed to nearby Kayseri airport, our flight was going to be 8 hours later than expected. So the ground staff refunded the cost of our flight, not once but twice. We were able to collect the money from a counter at the airport immediately, then we were upgraded to Business class, which meant we were able to sit in quiet and cool comfort while we waited. Then on the flight we were very impressed with the food and service and priority baggage service. I know the fault was not due to the ground staff, but they really tried hard and were very successful at getting people through to their connecting flights and what they offered us really helped ease the pain of our delay. I am really impressed with the 4 people in that small office, I wish I da their names to thank them personally. I highly recommend flying with Turkish Airways after this experience.

Worst experience in an airport I have ever had. We flew out on Monday, Dec 9th.2024 and every single staff we encountered at the security check point were rude and even disrespectful. Multiple people in our party of 10 experienced this. The lady who was suppose to be helping guide people (since there was no line yet a mile worth of taped off barriers) literally told us, " That's it I'm sick of you people, find your own way." Then the lady who was checking the IDs was worse than her with her negative comments and rude demeanor. These people acted like they hated their jobs. This is ths statement I made to someone in our oarty and then was mocked for it once I approached the ID counter. The staff in the bathroom were on their cell phones when multiple stalls were out of TP. I will always attempt to fly in or find a connecting flight elsewhere from now on. I will def. Not be using this airport again.

My experience with United Airlines at New Orleans' Louis Armstrong International Airport was ramping up towards a masterclass of poor professional service and lack of customer empathy. When a delay came up for my initial flight, I spoke to a remote agent who ultimately said, "tough luck" and didn't provide any options. There was no empathy and no discussion of any options to make it home safely. You can imagine I was scared and anxious when my flight to return home was nowhere in sight. Luckily, at United's desk, the representative Anna, who also worked at United, was present. She is the epitome of the perfect professional. She used critical listening to understand my concern and problem-solved on the spot. She gave me an option to return home safely. This wasn't a testament to United training, because it seems like the rep prior routinely told me "tough luck," but it showed how much of a true professional AND good person Anna is. I am grateful for being helped by Anna at New Orleans' Louis Armstrong International Airport, who works at United Airlines. If any problem arises, and she is present, best believe she will give you the most ultimate and efficient service.

It was first time at Louis Armstrong New Orleans International Airport; it was is one of the nicest and biggest airports I have come through in the USA. anywhere in the world. This multi level airport has many boarding bridges. There are many shops and restaurants. The staff were friendly and welcoming. The airport is well-decorated and well-maintained and easy to get in or out. Public areas are a huge, clean and bright.

I've traveled all over the world and probably been to close to 100 different airports. I can confidently say that in terms of international airports this place is probably the worst. There is nothing whatsoever to recommend it. The location is bad. It's been under construction for more than a decade, resulting in the removal of the limited seating and amenities they formerly had in the outer areas where you wait and pick people up. Staff are uniformly rude, uninformed and/or just plain incompetent. It's badly organized and unattractive. There's very little to nothing in the way of assistance for things like ground transport, rental cars and the like. And they don't have that many flights. So the only reason to use this airport is if you absolutely have to go to New Orleans. If you're flying out, including overseas, use Gulfport or somewhere else and avoid this dump.

Was departing New Orleans two days after jazzfest. Had no problems with queueing anywhere. Had some time to kill before my flight and sat outside in a cool spot close to where buses depart. Spent some time chatting to n airport employee. Absolutely delightful, polite young man.

Disgusted by the employees and customer service here. Traveled with someone who left their purse (with identification and the whole nine in it) in a bathroom and we were sent on a wild goose chase to find someone who was even willing to help us retrieve it. We were met with horrible attitudes and treated like a bother by everyone we encountered and were even told by multiple employees “I can’t help you with that”, and after being sent to them by another employee at that! If it weren’t for the law enforcement office we would not have received any help at all. Not being able to help is one thing, but being rude and completely unwilling to help is another. Do better.

Nearly everything is wrong with this airport. But special disdain goes to the rental car location (30 minutes away!) and that the shuttles drop you off at baggage claim for departure. Then there is a long brisk walk and 2 escalators to get to check in where there is a line all the way to the door. We slipped outside and did curbside check in. (The only nice person in the airport was at the curbside check in for Southwest). TSA is very nasty here too, and not empathetic at all. There seems to be tons of wasted space and open areas and very little space that is actually useful. The MSY airport had been remodelled after Hurricane Katrina and it was quite nice back them. Why ruin it for this poorly thought out billion dollar fiasco? It has a very generic look. There is barely any seating except at the terminal. The restaurants and shops are like mall kiosks. For a brand new airport there are few modern conveniences. I feel huge sympathy for anyone elderly or with a disability, this airport is not for you! Really its not for anyone

This is the worst airport experience I had since I have been traveling. All passengers have to go through big lines, it’s only one way to get to all gate access, one hour+ is an average wait time just to get by the security check and another 30 to 40 minutes for the security check. Most ridiculous set up I have ever seen. I hope I would never have to come back here again. I still at the line writing review … it’s been an hour, I hope I won’t miss my flight. One more thing to add, if you are retiring a rental car that you picked up from another location good luck with that, add some extra time, you will not know where to drop, you be be lost, your phone GPS can be your best option.

Wish I had taken pictures. Words just cannot describe how poor this airport design is. It is almost like a real life experiment on the way an airport could be designed to make customers walk the most, be disorganized, crowded in little walkways that go to plain ugly open spaces, have to be jammed up tightly to retrieve luggage, have a terrible time finding a restroom. Customers with bladder issues need diapers because there will not be a conveniently located restroom. Perhaps they should include a vending machine for them. It is really scary that it isn't an experiment but a new facility, opened November 2019 at a cost of 1.3 billion dollars. If I could rate a negative number I would.

The wait for the rental car bus is unbearably long. No organization. This airport is a total chaotic mess. The rental car situation adds at least an hour on to your trip whether you are arriving or departing. They need to get their act together.

Worst airport ever, specifically Terminal 8. There aren’t any restaurants unless you eat Dunkin Donuts. No bars. No Priority Pass lounge. Trash on the floor. Dirty tabletops. Disgusting. I have a long layover & there is nothing to eat!

This is simply the worst airport I have ever visited. Departures are an absolute shambles. Terminal 8 6.30 am., joke. You do all your pre boarding checks online, passport photo, boarding pass all of that. You then go to drop your case, takes forever, check in and bag drop all in the same line. They then take your case and yep print you a new boarding card to add to the two you already have. Then you get checked again with some random person, then you go through security and it's a free for all. Lines all over the place, constantly moved out of one line to another and at the end of it, yep another photo taken. Oh and then photo machines break and you go to a guy who puts your passport through a checker in a second, Why not just have these like most normal countries. Then you bottleneck again whilst the TSA staff shout at each other for who is doing the least amount of work. Absolutely horrendous. Then after what seems like forever you want something to eat, good luck with that, one small concession place selling an sandwich. This is supposed to be the gate way to and from the leading country in the free world. It's no better than a market bazaar . The USA should be ashamed of such an incompetent, useless and inefficient airport.

One of the worst airports I’ve been to. I’m at terminal 8 waiting for an international flight  .. no services, very limited food choice and personnel at the shop (La Villa and duty free) extremely unpolite. The security controls are so slow and so disorganized that you can’t tell you are in New York!

Just had this experience with tsa, a 20 something kid with braids in t5. Was in line for security screening and noticed 2 people going through metal detector. I asked the agent if I could go through. He said “nope!” Condescendingly and slammed the sign/barrier back down without explanation. I called to him, “I’d like to opt out of the x ray” and he ignored me. I was shaken up. To be ignored? His abrasiveness. There was no one else around and begrudgingly went through the x ray. He was at the end and I asked him why I couldn’t go through the metal detector? He called out “SUPERVISOR! She’s bugging me!!!” And a 250 lb man comes over to me. I explained what happened and he proclaimed “nah my guys would never deny someone the metal detector.” I explained that I was denied it, and he became elevated when I shared why I wanted to avoid it, including asking “ARE YOU A DOCTOR? Are you a doctor!?” I told him I did not want to cause an issue . By this Time I couldn’t hold back my emotion and was about to cry. The way they handle human beings is horrific. I have constant exposure to radiation with treatment and was trying to avoid a small dose more. If you hate your minimum wage job, quit.

I was passing through security at JFK terminal 4 on Saturday Sept 28th 2024 between 8-10pm. I have never seen a more incompetent and dysfunctional group of airport staff in charge of security in my whole life. The staff was rude, lazy and by far the slowest group of people I have ever seen put together. It’s clear that they all hate their jobs and they want nothing more than to pass their misery to everyone around them. It was such a bad experience that I vow to never fly through JFK ever again.
Avoid like the plague. Waiting for 3 hours with 2 people processing the entire queue. Absolutely ridiculous. Asked why it takes so long and all I got was. It’s like this everyday. Sort it out people

Was going to security with me husband and son, appreciate all airports have there own way od doing things, but the girl at the conveyor bell was extremely rude raised her voice when my husband put his shoes in tray instead of putting them directly on belt, I then said in a raised voice also will admit that ok we heard her, she was passed off that I had spoken up, call another lady over who then asked Mr where all the luggage mine I said no, she asked my husband were we together he said yes , then she looks at me and said so these are all yours, I said nope that my husband had his luggage and I had mine, it wasn't even that hard to explain, it was her attitude over the whole thing, even at check in no acknowledgement no please or thanks, I work in customer service and to say I'm astonished by the customer service at this airport, never again will I use this airport, and I've been to many but my god this was the worst airport I've ever been in, customer service so low.

Due to flight delay, we were very tight for our connection flight. Using JFK on connections, we were forced to leave the secure area going from T5 to T7. This required us to recheck in at airline and go through the security screening process a second time. Airline facilitated us, but security were the rudest, uncaring, belligerent staff I had ever encountered. They simply barked to get to the back of the queue, which was huge. Avoid JFK at all costs.

The airport staff very rude and like it is not enough the trauma we have to go through with the checking time; we also need to experience the TSA staff rudeness and lack of emphaty. It is just sad how horrible we are all turning to be as human.

It is specific for Delta Airline Check-in process staff at JFK airport! My flight was to Seattle on July 1, afternoon, ~4:00pm. I checked-in online before I headed to JFK Airpot and so I did not have too much time before departure time. In security check point, the officer told me that, the birth date in my ticket (My son booked the ticket for me. It is his/our fault, I know.) is not the same as that in my driver license. So he asked me to go back to the check-in point for correction. The waiting line in the check-in (Maybe most of them are for checking in baggages while I do not have.) that day is super long. If I lined up from the end, I probably I will miss the flight. So, I talked to staff around the check-in area. It was so crowded. Someone said, you go to there, pointing. Totally, I talked to 5 difference people around that area. Still no one is responsible for my issue. They were saying differently. It seems I have to line up from the end. In the end, I stick on one lady. She said, I understand your situation. I can do nothing about it. She hinted me I have to line up again. Finally, I have to cut into the line by some people's kindness to allow me to cut into the middle of the line. I am OK to line up, even it is long, if I did not check in online. I would leave more time to do that. My question is. For this kind of special situation, should Delta Airline have some specific rules to handle??? would you like the custom to miss their flight? Thanks!

Last time I visited Newark, my review was overall very bad. Since my last visit, the quality of service has improved a lot, especially with the TSA staff at security checks. The United Airlines staff also provided good service. The airport was clean, and the transportation system between terminals was efficient. The only negative part was the long queue at customs due to a lack of CBP officers - a point to improve.

Regular airport check-in staff have been almost fully replaced by kiosks. Prepare for a truly terrible experience if you do not have a boarding pass ready to go and no checked bag. Any issues or mandatory travel verification's leave you at the mercy of the rude staff. Airlines purposely employ almost no humans to perform tasks needed to even enter security. Your experience is likely to be frustrating and you also get to witness large amounts of individual missing flights due to the airlines choosing to leave customers with inadequate assistance.

Poor direction within the airport for travelers. When coming from international flight to Term 1 headed to Term 2 and gates for B were clearly marked, but it was not clear on where Gates A/C where located. Then gate was a significant distance away, which took us outside the airport causing us to re enter the airport, on a tight schedule, having to go through airport security again. Not only is this very inconvenient it puts people in a bad mood which then alters the encounters with airline workers. Very frustrating process. It could definitely be streamlined and made more convenient for travelers. I give this airport a D rating.

The ladies at the United bag drop off were great, they communicated well, were very polite and helpful and the bag drop off was simple and speedy. Pity the security staff were so offensive doing their jobs. Of the six security staff encountered 5 were rude and had minimal idea of any service to the client. Poor instructions were mumbled with a gesture to go elsewhere or do something, when clarification was asked "sorry I'm not sure where you mean I should go, could you please tell me again" was met with a glare of disdain and a repetition of the same mumbled, incomprehensible directions, with a very offensive level of attitude. The security staff ushered through 4 or more airport staff with little more than a cursory glance of ID's, the opportunity for fake ID's being presented was breathtaking. Meanwhile people catching flights were left standing in line while airport staff basically ignored them. I have never seen such a poorly managed security system.

I was traveling to Orlando Florida from EWR flight #1213 departing Newark at 2:53pm Sept 16. I was taken to gate C132 via wheel chair, the wheel chair person dropped me off at gate c132 and said the wheel chair would be ordered from the gate to take me to the plane. We asked the gate attendant about the wheel chair she told us she had ordered it. It never came so we again asked to no avail. I finally had to navigate as best as I could, we were boarded last. I asked the flight attendant on the plane about the wheel chair, she checked and told me it was never ordered.

This could be a good airport, despite the fact it's locked in the middle of an urban area limiting its expansion and infrastructural upgrades. However the worst part is the staff: Rude! and unnecessarily so, immigration officers have a terrible attitude, I was treated like a liar. My identity had to be investigated beyond what is done at the passport control booth, and the way I was told to proceed was humiliating, everything was completed in less than two minutes and I was allowed to got home, the rudeness was a totally unnecessary extra that only eroded the expected professionalism of those officers. I hope someone will notice this problem and require them to take etiquette training. Being rude and nasty is not a synonym of efficiency.

Customer service is so rude. I approached a rep asking if where a flight was due to arrive as it was delayed and I was given a stock answer. I tried to clarify the issue i was having and was met with hostility. The agent was dismissive. Instead I was able to get my answer online using the free wifi .. staff very unhelpful.

Fix your lane system. Waited for hours to check in. Slow service for checking baggage in.  15 minutes per person in the queue. The US and especially Newark Airport has to fix their organizing systems. Shopping was boring,

I never thought I would find myself reviewing a TSA department but I felt compelled to after my recent positive experience. My family and I were unexpectedly transiting through Newark on June 2. We had several mishaps happen beyond our control after an extended travel day (>20 hours). The TSA department at Newark airport, in particular a man named Fontaine, helped greatly alleviate our stress and help expedite us through the security line and airport, correcting the mistakes of our airline workers. I cannot begin to tell you how appreciative I am for their help, empathy and services.

Every person I encountered there was extremely rude, but the the TSA employees were by far the worst. Super rude and disrespectful yelling at customers. Something needs to be done about the unprofessional employees there. I will not return to this airport.

Newcastle is a small airport which always delights. It's not the most modern or breathtaking, however, it's well organised and functions well. Check-in zone is excellent and plenty of space, clean (despite dated) toilets and some generic shops/eateries. The renovated security area is very modern with high-tech equipment, meaning the check is very thorough despite being completed in under 5 minutes without priority. This of course makes the airport feel very safe, however, security staff aren't the most friendly I've got to admit which surprised me. The departure lounge is spacious and has plenty of room, with no awkward 'no return' sections. Shops are overpriced which you'd expect for an airport but there's plenty of choice. There's also a newly renovated lounge which we didn't visit on this occasion but looked fabulous. Despite this, the area leading to the gates is quite dated and needs upgrading to make the whole experience seamless. Arrivals are also great, very fast and friendly border agents. It took approximately 15 minutes for us from leaving the plane to outside the airport, which is simply excellent. Despite the excellent terminal, one thing that really disappoints me with Newcastle is the parking arrangements. Extremely expensive and the shuttle system to the long-term car park is a nightmare, never mind the technical issues and problems with closed car parks. I'd try to arrange alternative transport to the airport if possible, as the drop-off zone is good.

I used Newcastle Airport in Feb/March for my recent trip to Chicago, and all was great apart from security. Check-in was a breeze and there was no queue, there were 2 staff on the desk checking people in and as we were part of a group, they both checked us in to make it quicker. I was looking forward to travelling through security as I knew they had brought in the new security equipment that would speed up the process, however this was not the case. Upon arrival to security, there was no queue which was brilliant but we soon ended up being stuck at security for quite some time. When travelling through Newcastle I have never had to take my shoes off but as soon as I went through, they swabbed my shoes and made me take them off so they could go through the scanner. Every bag that went through the scanner was rejected and had to be swabbed/checked, and they only had ONE person doing this, with staff even looking confused as to what they were doing/what was going on. The whole purpose of this new equipment is for passengers NOT to take their electronics out, however every bag that was rejected had to have the electronics out and swapped/checked which defeats the whole purpose of this equipment. In total, even though there was no queue, we were stuck a security for around 15/20 minutes which has defeated the purpose of what this technology aimed to do.

My wife was having trouble getting her handbag through security. After much rummaging by the security officer, he pulled out a penknife. My wife was mortified. The knife had belonged to her brother, a farmer, who had died some years previously. She became visibly upset and the officer got quite concerned. He said not to worry, if we would go to the shop, get an envelope and stamps he would post the knife back to her. Got home from the holiday to find the knife duly arrived. What a kind and considerate man, thank you very much.

Terrible airport. Not enough seating before check in. Once checked in not enough seating and bad loud music like in a nightclub. They need to announce gates much sooner as most gate seats empty as everyone is kept piled in the noisy pub area. Not a pleasant place.

The female security attendant was unnecessarily rude and impatient with my 82 year old mother, totally unacceptable. Attitudes and behaviour like hers will make travel very difficult for older / infirm passengers. What amazes me is that the North East has to be one of the friendliest places on the planet. This is absolutely not reflected in airport staff at this airport.

Over 24 minutes to get through passport control. Travelers and staff looking cold and tired as midnight passes. 4 flights luggage all coming onto 1 carousel. 2 others silent and still. It was an opportunity to shine and it wasn’t taken- even a hot drink would have made it more bearable. No explanation for delays given by any staff
Luggage belt was broken down so they asked us to leave all luggage by the counter, as expected we arrived to our destination to find that one of our luggage went missing.

Contrary to all of the recent negative press about airports and their staff, our experience flying and coming back in was seamless. Given the pressure that all airport staff are under, they are doing an amazing job and are doing it with a smile. We travelled down to Newcastle from Scotland and stayed in the Premier Inn the night before. I would have no hesitation in using this airport again. Well done to all of the staff.

I suddenly needed to use the special assistance service at Newcastle airport in order to go on holiday in May 22. I had seen in the media the chaotic scenes at some uk airports and in addition the issues for passengers with disabilities. I never expected Newcastle special assistance service to contradict the horror stories but it certainly did. To put it simply they excelled and you should go on holiday via Newcastle with absolute confidence. What an amazing service. They have some of the most friendly helpful and professional staff who cannot do enough to help you and put you at ease. They explain what is happening throughout the transit process in the airport. To and from the aeroplane. Through security to baggage collection even right through to getting in the taxis home. They get you through.

My husband and I have never used Newcastle airport before but I though we would give it ago and this time I need special assistance as I'm waiting for spinal surgery and loosing the use of my hands and feet. I booked it easily enough with Ryanair and the special assistance was easy to find and I found the staff very kind and courteous and nothing was too much trouble. We arrived the 3 hours before we travelled as per the warning message from Ryanair, so the special assistance man took us through the process of X-ray and boarding cards so easily and left us for a drink and they came back when they said for me and everything was perfect except the food area was slightly dirty but the special assistance people all I can say thank you for making my travel easy and you all were brilliant.

Very nice to have more flights at a local airport, but still lots of improvements are clearly required from a passengers point of view. Bad signage in airport, the security queue blocks the main entrance. All sanitizer stations were empty, no signage to show customers that there were two security lines so many left standing waiting unnecessarily. The flight info displayed was late and the gate opened after it was supposed to have closed. The bag measurer was littered with half full cups of drinks. Non priority passengers were told to go to the left, many went left to the next desk, but were not meant to, actually only had to stand at the door, where we already were, not go left where pointed to. On return flight, we disembarked the plane and were left standing on the tarmac in the pouring down rain because the rain shelter is far, far too small for the amount of passengers on a plane, most passengers including elderly and babies left absolutely drenched and shivering in the rain for a very long time, the airport wasn't ready and no staff were there nor were the doors even open, we could all hear the staff on tarmac radioing to others to say you need to open the doors because everyone's waiting in the rain as the security staff were not there ready for the passengers, yet alone had opened the doors. Once they eventually arrived and opened the doors they were so slow that majority of passengers had a further 30 minute wait outside (yet plenty of empty corridor space if the security point was further back). No shelter between airport and parking areas. Lack of signage in car parks or any staff to ask for guidance, also not enough car parking spaces even though we had paid weeks ahead. End of the holiday ruined by this experience and now all have colds from standing shivering in the rain for so long. Although most staff were polite, there is clearly an issue with organisation or seeing potential issues from the customers point of view. I really hope in the future this airport can improve, the issues are all very simple things that can easily be corrected without any cost. Just having staff there when a flight arrives would be handy and is completely necessary. It's no good putting sings at the start of the queue after people have already been queueing for ages, people cannot see that from the back so it only causes problems for the airport and the passengers.

When arriving at the airport in a taxi I was met by a very nice viewing point for people to watch aircraft's taking off and landing. My flight was from NQY to LHR when Flybe was still alive, when I entered the airport there were check in desks and a café right there so not at all difficult to find them when arriving with only 2 hours of sleep at 5.30 am. I had already checked in online so I went straight into security which was very conveniently in the next room. It took about 5-10 minutes to get through security and into the Airports Lounge. On first impressions it was quite small with not really much to do but what more can you expect for a local Airport. There was only 2 places where you could buy stuff in the departure lounge which was a café and a Cornish shop that sells Cornish alcoholic beverages and other snacks and the café sold quite a few things but I only got a water bottle which I think was around £2. There were also toilets which were kept to a reasonably well standard and we boarded our flight with no problems and took off about 10 minutes after departure time.

Very poor experience. Flight delayed by over two hours obviously not the fault of the airport, but we were then obviously a nuisance as it was the last flight of the evening and I guess they wanted to go home. Cafe more or less ran out of food and the pulled pork bap served to two of our party caused sickness the following day. It was barely lukewarm and in hindsight we should have rejected it. Having settled down for a two hour wait, plus the two hours you have to allow, we were called to the boarding gate and made to stand for forty minutes ... the incoming plane for our flight had not even landed! Children were exhausted and crying ... we had been happy enough playing cards. Returnin luggage belt ridiculously small for 100plus cases, and no covered walkway in wet weather. Exeter for me in future!

This airport can’t cope if something goes wrong. We flew out on the 29th June 2019. There had been a number of flight delays that day. Our flight was not delayed and we arrived within plenty of time for check in. Check in was chaos, not enough desks and a queue that never seemed to move. Staff were not prioritising passengers to get to their flights in time. The information desk had a huge queue, it was impossible to speak to anyone. We were lucky to find a member of staff who then rushed us to the front of the queue. We were then told the flight had closed! After voicing our opinion on this incompetence, the flight was reopened (for us and all the others stuck in the queue). We were then given a personal escort through security, I didn’t get her name but she was very helpful and professional (the only professional staff member we encountered). After all this, our flight hadn’t even landed when we got through to the gates! If travelling from Newquay, allow lots of time for check in as the process moves at the rate of a snail.

This review regards the parking at Newquay airport. I have just booked parking for 3 days at this airport for a trip to London Heathrow. I am astounded at the exorbitant cost of £40 for three days, by comparison a recent booking at Gatwick airport is £48 for 11 days in the official long term car park for the North terminal. Cornwall council, I believe runs Newquay airport and they want us to use the airport as the gateway to the west. There are no shuttle buses from Truro or St Austell also no trains, the only way to get to the airport is by car or Taxi (very expensive). To charge these parking costs is both greedy and short sighted by the council, especially as the one thing they are not short of at this airport is space. I for one will not be using this airport again, I can drive to London for less cost in fuel!
Newquay airport is excellent apart from the abysmal state of seating in the main departure lounge. Seating all torn and very scruffy. It has been like this for a long time. Unacceptable!

Whenever I depart from this airport it seems that the planes are always delayed for silly reasons and for a very lengthy amount of time. It’s a very nice airport and nice staff - they just don’t seem organised- “routine maintenance” that occurs when the plane is supposed to fly? Surely you would plan the 2+ hours it takes on another day.

Security staff asked me to remove my belt and leather bracelet which a female member of staff took from me. Upon retrieving my luggage after the security scan my bracelet was missing. Staff started 2 look on the floor and were unable to find it. Just as my blood was about to boil another passenger found it in his personal items. Needless to say I was not impressed with the security staff who clearly had no respect for my personal items. Very disappointed.
