Recently travelled with a broken ankle. The staff were very helpful getting me on and off the plane. The special waiting area was a nice touch because I was scared of getting knocked by other passengers.

❌Not Verified|  Super small airport. Arrival was swift off the plane and into the arrivals section. Only waited 5 minutes for the case. Car hire is literally just outside the terminal with cars in the car park nearby. Departure checkin was easy, spaces to wait outside with picnic benches. No queue at security at all with friendly staff. Very small departure lounge but straight onto plane that was parked outside.

Visited nice airport upon transit to Doha. A very long stopover which I will not do again but couldn't be helped. Landing and disembarking fairly routine and swift. After clearing passport control I was expecting to see a sign where I could wait in the transit area. Only there was no transit area. Just an arrivals lounge and free reign to leave the airport. Airport itself is functional and basic. Nearby hotels are expensive, so if you're only going to be around for a short while, you can try it and slum it on the waiting seats scattered across arrivals. Or not. They are immensely uncomfortable and you'll find other travellers bending their bodies around seats , lying on 4 chairs just to lie flat in the desperate hope of getting some decent shut eye . Information counter closes at 10 so if you land after that you're on your own. Plus side local supermarkets like Lidl are 30 mins walk away if you're put off by food prices inside the airport. All in all an ok airport i guess, not recommended for long layovers. Designated quiet rooms with chairs for resting like they have in Doha would be ideal. Fantastic Mediterranean sea air outside the airport. A solid 7/10 from me.

Worst Airport in the world, arrived to check in, then security on baggage. Then Passport machine,  thought great all good. Walked through Duty Free then a mile long queue to get through to B gate (BA is B gate). Poor shops, nobody could shop or eat unless you had got their 4 hours early. This queue apparently is normal and is called the new 'fast track' what a joke. One person in a box checking passports again! Run to B9, hundreds of people standing there, no way could you board in Groups ... just a free for all. Again with one woman at the gate before you got on the coach to the plane -  still coaching you out to the plane. She was checking everyone's passport again. Why haven't they upgraded this system by now and built satellite gates off the main airport? Not going back there.

Been living here for 10 years. If you ever park you car in the airport parking, be sure for remove any important items from the car. I have had my car broken into twice in during parking while on business trip. It is simply the worst airport in Europe in regards to parking security, and the airport police are doing anything to help or enforce security. Apart from that, service is generally pretty French, as in none existing.

Please can someone improve the signage when you leave Nice airport to go to the motorway to Monaco. We always end up going round and round roundabouts, looking for the sign to Monaco/Genoa and end up going through parts of Nice and joining the motorway at a later junction. If we take the train to Monaco from St Augustin Station the signage from the airport to the station is inadequate. Please can the airport management arrange to improve the signage to and from the airport to the station and Monaco. One wonders, does anyone care about the customers at Nice Airport? For example, the BA check-in desk is substandard with unfriendly staff. The whole experience at Nice airport is not a pleasant one, If senior staff at Nice airport read this review one wonders if they are bothered to do anything about it! We live in hope!

I was waiting, with my fellow traveller to board my BA flight on September 22nd 2023. We were hoping to have a glass of wine and something to eat at Bellota Bellota where we usually stop. However this time, there was no one to be seen, I and several other travellers waited for 10/15 minutes to no avail. I walked just inside the area to check if there was a notice, computer, till, wines, food etc were all open and unsecured. I turned by the unsecured opening and an enraged and shouting female demanded what I was doing I explained, she said that there was no one to cover for her and that she was entitled to a break.  I returned to my seat and this female came 'screaming' over to me, seated with other passengers, asking if I had photographed her as 'I had no right'. I hadn't. I am an older female and found this altercation, embarrassing and humiliating and not up to the high expectations of wonderful Nice Airport. I have been using Nice since you could walk to the plane!

Appalling airport. Extremely rude, borderline aggressive staff, who throw your stuff around and scream at you for no reason. Passport control is an absolutely joke, they have one officer for the whole non-Schengen area and you have to queue for ages. No proper food or drink - not even water fountains - just a shabby Starbucks once past passport control and it closes at 10pm so if you a late flight you can just go to hell. Toilets are disgusting. Shops - the lady tried to close her shop while I was still in it. Just ignoring me. Rude. At arrival, there is only one vending machine for the tram which means you have to queue hours to get a 1 euro ticket. Couldn't it be done online or on an app, in 2023? Please. No explanation no signage, car rental is located in the most absurd place possible and everyone around is so damn rude, barely speak a word of English and it feels like they're all just out of prison or something. Avoid at all cost this ridiculous airport.

I can only agree with all of the other reviews regarding poor staffing and long queues. The lack of staff in the baggage drop and the passport control areas meant that I queued for nearly all of the two hours from arriving till my flight, along with hundreds of other people even though I had fast track boarding passes. I hate to think what other people experienced. I witnessed some people walking to the front of the queues and pushing in, using physical intimidation of generally older people to get their way. There was no-one to manage these issues. It was a completely unsatisfactory and unacceptable situation. To have only two people on passport control to deal with hundreds of people is extremely poor. A number of people around me were late for flights or had to ask staff (when available) to help them as they were minutes away from missing a flight. This was the worst experience I have ever had at an airport.

At T2. Checking in was ok and so was security screening. Walked into the departure area and it was filled with a queue for passport control. I set my stopwatch and 53 minutes later was finally through. The 4 biometric readers were out of action so everyone had to use the human inspection method. I have never experienced such poor management.

Rude, chaotic, loses passports! Nice airport is the worst I've ever seen in all my years of traveling internationally. Do not fly out of there. The staff are rude. The check in counters are nothing but chaos. No airline has their own and we spent 20 min trying to figure out which line we needed. A French woman on our flight even said "c'est ridicule". And even once you find your line, the desk people are disorganized and very slow. At security, a man stands at the conveyor belt, shuffling everyone's stuff into other bins and combining different peoples stuff together. You have to be vigilant to watch what is happening. At the end, my son's passport was lost for awhile until some passenger found it. Who knows where. They checked 2 of our bags thoroughly - every inch. The woman was so slow - like her movement was actually barely moving sometimes. She spent 15 min per bag. My husband said "looks like they've hired the sloths here". Took us 45 min to get thru security and the line wasn't that long. Avoid this airport if you can.

Nothing to do. Old airport, looks like some maintenance is needed. Not a lot of shops or seating. Toilets not clean at all. No ventilation in terminal, humid. Definitely not what I would expect in Nice.

I am writing this because we are currently having a bad experience of Nimes Airport. This is the worst airport experience I've ever had. The main problem is the lack of basic logic used in relation to the queuing/check in system. In very small writing, one queue is marked as 'bag drop'. If you mistake this for the queue to go through to security (which many did) then you get turned away by a disinterested staff member and told to join the other queue. Even if you do check in luggage, you can't go through the door to security. Instead of utilising the many potential entrances, they were determined to make everyone in the airport form one queue (and not for lack of staff). If the airport read this then I would suggest letting people go straight through at that point? And make your signs clearer? Once through security you are welcomed with a lovely waiting room. Phew.

I've been using Nimes Airport on and off for 12 years and never found anyone working there particularly friendly or helpful maybe it's because most of the interior is painted black! During my last visit (26 Oct 2012) I was subject to a new rip off they have devised. They advertise parking deals which have to be purchased in advance so I asked to buy the 6 month deal for the advertised tariff of 340 euros. The guy took my money wrote out my receipt and prepared a little plastic 'credit card' for me to use for entry and exit. When I asked why my expiry date was shown as '31st March 2013' he explained that all parking contracts have to start on the first day of the month so despite the date of purchase being 26th Oct my pass had to start on 1st October. Furthermore there was an additional 20 euro fee to issue the card! My other memory of Nimes is the airport restaurant. Service there was so sloppy and slow that despite having nearly two hours available it was never possible to eat all of your rather poor quality overpriced 3 course meal without missing your flight. Other gripes - The little newspaper / book shop closed in 2010 and has only recently reopened I would say in summary that I only use Nimes Airport if I have to. Nearby Beziers is a much better option if you have a choice.

A very small quiet airport and with only a few flights a day check-in is very quick and hassle- free. Probably one of the easiest airports I have ever used as long as transport to and from the airport is planned in advance or is directly connected to your flight. Between flights a great silence descends on the place. In the main hall there are several car hire desks one cafe stand (offering good quality hot sandwiches) and a small restaurant upstairs for those needing a traditional large French lunch. There are no shopping opportunities either in the main hall or in the departure lounge (a small cafe stand there). The main point is that because there are so few flights passengers are easily organised and you are unlikely to spend much time at the airport and what could be better! When arriving you need to rent a car OR pick up the ONE shuttle bus service linked to the flight that will take you into Nimes city OR have a friend collect you. There is a taxi rank if you need to leave at a time not linked to a flight but taxis seem very infrequent we once needed to leave the airport at a time not connected with a flight and waited half an hour for a chance taxi to arrive as there is so little activity apart from the few flights a day. The rent-a-car car park is directly across the road from the airport main exit just a few steps. Most customers seem to use Hertz because it is advertised with Ryanair but there are several other car desks and it would pay to plan ahead and find the best deal regarding rates and maybe avoid the problematic and hefty supplementary insurance fee that Hertz offer unsuspecting customers on arrival. Going back to the airport after a stay in Nimes there is just one shuttle bus per flight. Don't miss it. There are four points in Nimes city centre where the shuttle can be picked up and the main hotels have the timetable. The hours on the hotel timetable were slightly different from the times displayed on the bus stop but the hotel timetable seemed to be the correct one. The time allowed between shuttle arrival at the airport and last check-in time seemed too close for comfort but in fact it was fine just right and things work smoothly because there are so few flights. Going back with a hire car the airport is very close to exit 2 on the A54 autoroute very easy access. Hertz (and perhaps the other companies) also have a base in Nimes at the railway station where a car can be collected or left as an alternative to the airport.

Nimes is one of the most pleasant airports I've experienced. It's quite small is a favourable alternative to Montpellier for those of us whose eventual destination is in the Herault area not least because of its close proximity to the motorway and (current) absence of major roadworks. It is a place to relax and stroll about while waiting to meet incoming friends and carparking is a doddle. The flight to and from Liverpool with Ryanair is direct.

There is also an excellent restaurant on the mezzanine floor overlooking the runway. It opens at noon which gives adequate time for a good lunch before the departure of the Luton flight at 1435. Information on bus transportation to (and within) Nimes is at: http://www.tcn.fr

Great Little Airport easy to find just off the motorway. Departure Lounge only has seats toilets & 1 drinks machine but allows own food. Reception is again sparse of amenities but has small cafe. souvenir shop of camargue items at a hefty price. Car park is literally opposite. Disabled passengers have 1 toilet & share toilet with baby changing. No disabled lift to & from aircraft local fire crew manhandle wheelchairs down stairs - very scary!

Modern airport, medium in Chinese terms. Incoming, by bus from runway, efficient and fast, very simple to get your bearings. Outgoing, fast, very clear information, very efficient check-in, good facilities. About 30 min, from city center.

Nice small low cost but very aged airport, needs full reconstruction asap. Everything looks like the 80s but not nice way. The floor was dirty so they need to improve cleaning as well. Restaurant was closed so there was nowhere to even get a coffee. Staff were kind and helpful. Will fly there again as FR and W6 operate nice cheap flights, otherwise no chance will be back!

I have been flying out of/into Norfolk airport my whole life and have always had a pleasurable experience with it; this time was no different. The Southwest check-in agent was very friendly, as were the TSA employees at the checkpoint. My bag got flagged as a possible explosive, but luckily they figured out it wasn't. A major plus ORF has to offer is its new bathrooms, which were installed less than a year ago. These are sleek, modern, and well-maintained by airport staff. The terminal itself reflects the era it was built in, with smaller windows and lower ceilings than, say, SEA. Instead of inducing claustrophobia, though, it gives the entire a building a more "cozy" feeling. New seats at the gates with electrical outlets are also a major plus, allowing you to charge your phone while you wait for your plane. One downside of Norfolk International, though, is the WiFi. It is very hard to connect to and hardly works. Aside from that, though, this is a small, practical, no-frills airport that is impossible to get lost in and is located near the Norfolk Botanical Gardens (another positive).

As someone who's travels constantly for business, Norfolk Airport is honestly the worst airport I have ever been through. I have traveled through here well over a dozen times and not once had a pleasant experience here. The ticketing agents are rude. The TSA are frustratingly incompetent. The airport is dirty and falling apart in many areas. If you have any other option of airports I suggest you use it.

This airport was dirty and dilapidated. The terminal I was in was in the middle of an update, but they didn't do much to try to make it look okay in the interim. There are very few food options (for some reason they are all outside the terminal so, so you'd have to eat before going through security if you want something edible. The person who gave me my lackluster bagel was very rude and mumbled the whole exchange. The prices at the food places are even more exorbitant than expected. The check-in, arrivals, baggage claim, and security were mostly fine, but once you're passed security, don't hold your breath for good service.

It is a second tier (non-hub) airport so traffic is lower. As others have noted it is surrounded by a botanical garden so the setting is beautiful. Recently all of the food options were significantly upgraded. Security moves quickly and efficiently. The arrivals area is large and conveniently located next to the parking garage for a quick departure. Rental car counters are right in the arrivals area. Which brings me to the only negative -- waits for checked baggage are noticeably longer than almost any other airport. Figure on a minimum 30 minute wait. Would recommend getting your rental car while you wait on your bags.

Over the years have had the pleasure of travelling through this airport surely the best planned facility of it's size anywhere in the world. Maybe all would-be new airport planners should pay Norfolk a visit to see what a well designed airport should look like; and that's not even mentioning the surrounding beautiful botanical gardens a very pleasant change from the usual grimy industrial areas adjoining most airports.

Norfolk International Airport (ORF) in Norfolk Virginia is one of the best airports that I have flown into or out of in the past year. The airport itself is set in the middle of a beautiful botanical gardens. It is great to wonder through the grounds of the gardens if you have several hours to kill between connections. The airport has a variety of resturants that are very reasonably priced and the food is excellent. Access into and out of the airport is easy. Parking is great with a well lighted attached parking garage. The new arrivals terminal which was recently completed is huge and baggage retrieval and rental car pick-up is a breeze. The only thing lacking at this airport is direct access to the Interstate highway system. After leaving the airport property you have to travel through a residential/commercial neighborhood to gain access to the Interstate.

Departed yesterday to Canada. Inside the airport was like a sauna where you go to burn off excess fat, it was unbearable, last July came air-conditioning wasn't working in some areas, this year it's worst, there's no way this could happen at Sangster international airport, it a shame, people were almost half naked trying to cope. Stripping down to accommodate the heat. And on top of that the airlines wouldn't even do their progress much quicker. Very disappointed as a Jamaican. Please do better, those fans that look like propellers not cutting it, was so sorry for the staff. Please you can do better.
Stood on Burger King line for over 20 minutes to place an order then stood on pick up line for an additional 20 minutes then had to stand up on the boarding line so about 20 minutes.

The airport is so peaceful and clean, the staff at the airport are so calm and friendly. The duty free shops are so easily accessible and the food at the airport is so tasty. The announcements of the arriving or departing planes are so clear and the sings and directions are so bright.

CPH-NRK and quite satisfied with this regional airport. Only a few flights per day so baggage reclaim understandably very quick. Bus line 116 connects with downtown Norrköping every half- hour - travel time is 20 mins and costs 20SEK. Beware that bus drivers do not accept cash any more - the only option is the self-service machine inside the terminal or to purchase a SMS- ticket. Check-in efficient and hassle-free - online seat pre-selection is available. Security staff very friendly. Boarding area is limited to two gates and rather cramped - do not go airside too early. I recommend the airport restaurant which serves tasty and hearty Swedish meals.

Arrival on a rainy day looking forward to breakfast, ours was a lunchtime flight and we arrived in good time, not much queueing to check in which was a good start. However, the restaurant stopped serving breakfast at around 11am stating it would not be ready in time for the flight, the attitude of the people behind the counter seemed annoyed that I would be asking for breakfast at 10:45am, I don’t quite know what they were going to cook on that would take so long to produce a breakfast, the only thing they were able to provide was tapas for breakfast! I think Norwich Airport ought to reconsider their choice of restaurant provider as they don’t appear to be able to provide basic food quickly which is what you need at an airport , bearing in mind they already know how many people will be coming though the airport every day. The choices after that were also limited both food providers stopped providing food around midday and then the only thing available were sandwiches, which was ok for my husband but I am gluten intolerant and so this was not an option for me, the best I could find was a packet of crisps and chocolate bar, not such a a great breakfast. This was such a disappointment for the start of our holiday. Flight went on time. Our return flight from Crete was delayed by a day and TUI dealt with this very well. When we finally arrived back at Norwich airport late at night, I was amazed to the see that the same old creaking, held up by plywood, luggage conveyer belt was still there, the same one I remember being there many many years ago. The noise was deafening squeaking, you could see all the passengers looking at each other wondering if the luggage was going to make it up the onto the conveyer belt. It does make you wonder what all the airport tax is exactly being spent on. The experience at Norwich airport has not inspired me to use the airport again, I do understand the delayed flight was not directly their fault however he size of the airport played a role in the ability to replace the flight. But I don’t think we will be flying through Norwich any time soon.

This is the first time in over 10 years that I have used Norwich airport. So easy and quick with friendly staff. WH Smiths was as normal for airports overpriced, however, Flour and Bean cafe was reasonable—also Plenty of seating in departures. Security was so fast and I was from check-in to departure in under 10 minutes. (I am used to Stansted and Heathrow where it takes an hour from check-in to gate.) The airport was clean and had a free cold water dispenser. Overall impressed and I estimate saved me 8 hours overgoing from London. The only let down is the limited amount of shops though you expect that with the size of the airport, duty-free was cheaper than London and destination airport.

Where does the airport development fee go? Its certainly not on retail outlets or staff training! It’s certainly not used to enhance passenger experience. The check in staff were rude. My bag was 1 kg over weight and I was advised that there would be a 65 pound charge. I asked why. I was told it’s a safety issue. However if I paid the 65 pound I didn’t need to remove the weight indicating it’s a money making scheme rather than safety. I removed the 1kg and put it into my backpack which is going onto the same plane! The security staff at the metal detector were rude and disrespectful and quite hostile. I had to remove my shoes, stand on a box and lift my toes so they could look under them with a mirror. I have never seen this before in my life. They emptied my carry on bag to check the contents and just walked away when finished leaving all of my belongings on the counter. Poorly organised and limited airport with backwards practices. This is the worst airport I have ever had the displeasure to travel from!

Just had to leave this review. on 17th May returned from Rhodes and my flight was delayed two hours. Just after midnight left baggage reclaim to go to my car. I had a flat battery and was unable to get into my car. It was exceptionally cold and all I was wearing was shorts and a tee shirt. I returned to the terminal where I met the staff at the parking desk. At this time the terminal was empty and they were locking up. The staff came out and helped me gain entry to my car but I had a two hour wait for the Green Flag breakdown. The staff waited with me almost an hour and had to go home leaving me alone in the car park freezing cold but not before he returned to his office made me a hot cup of tea and brought it to me in my car. A beautiful act of kindness and one I will never forget.

The security staff at the metal detector were rude and disrespectful and seemed to enjoy humiliating and embarrassing people; they did not ask if you were suffering from any serious health conditions. They lacked respect and had been poorly trained. Ghastly, stressful experience, as it deeply upset my partner, who having recently nearly died from heart problems and having undergone a heart op burst into tears! Awful experience as the security guard put them through a ridiculously long and drawn out inspection - all in public view. The exec lounge was a joke! No breakfast items and no gluten free options. Coffee was cheap and nasty. £40 for two vile coffees! What a rip-off! Worst ever. We will never step foot in this airport ever again, despite living 16 minutes walk from the check-in! Never!

Where do I start? I travel with a folding mobility scooter. I usually fly out of Stansted with no problems. But the staff at check-in did not have my scooter registered with my ticket, they said it was the first time they had to check in a mobility scooter. After a long procedure, they finally got me checked in with a lot of help from me. Next was security. As I had no check-in luggage I had my toiletries in a plastic bag in my cabin bag. I was rudely told that my plastic bag was not the correct size. I said that unfortunately, Tesco does not supply airport plastic bags. She just scowled at me and produced a plastic bag that was a little smaller than mine and said I would have to take my items out of my plastic bag and put them into the other plastic bag. Unfortunately one of my items would not fit, the deodorant, which she said I would not be able to take onboard. Finally getting through the security I saw a convenience shop and popped in to buy some juice, I then noticed a shelf of travel-size toiletries, so I bought deodorant and just to stick it to the airport security I also bought some hand cream. I put all the items into my original plastic bag and boarded the plane. On my return flight, the security at Amsterdam Airport did not even bother to question my larger-size plastic bag. The security staff at Norwich Airport has this inflated sense of their own self-importance. I had booked a taxi to pick me up on my return and as it was raining I wanted inside the airport terminal until I received a text from the taxi letting me know he had arrived. I walked out of the terminal but could not see my taxi. I walked back inside and asked the girl in the office where do the taxis pick up and was told I had to walk down to the car park. After paying that 10-pound airport improvement fee I had to walk down to the car park in the rain? absolutely appalling! The only reason I flew out of Norwich Airport was because I was going on a short holiday to Amsterdamt. Worst airport in the world and I have traveled through airports in developing counties

Great experience using Norwich airport. Efficient and cheerful check-in personnel. Compact WH Smith outlets land and airside. Fast, friendly and helpful security people. Sweet little duty free. Great hot/cold snacks/drinks areas. Lots of seating with airfield and runway view. Downside was no ‘development’ fee spent on arrivals. Walk from aircraft (hoping it’s not raining) then queuing under draughty, plastic-covered outside waiting area before clearing customs. Not good. TIP: On arrival, phone whoever is picking you up to let them know you’ve arrived. it’s best if they wait for you away from the airport. Most planes arrive late so the 30-minute £3 parking fee becomes £10.

I fly from Amsterdam to Norwich and back regularly. The airport is always a breeze. Check in never has a queue, security never has a queue. You can arrive 30 minutes before a flight and it's never a trouble. Staff are nice and friendly. There isn't a massive selection of things to do airside, but you wouldn't expect there to be. The development fee is bizarre, but certainly not unique to Norwich. Go to a small airport, get a small airport experience. Norwich appears well run and is always a pleasure to fly through. If you want a big airport experience, go to a big airport. I'll happily take shorter waiting times and friendlier service and stick with Norwich.

Poorly organised and limited airport with backwards practices. The first issue is that the long stay car park is not signposted, you are funnelled into the short stay with no way to back out and the contact on the exit barrier then acts surprised at your mistake, even though others were doing the same just for the short time we were there. Next is a 'Development fee' that all adults are required to pay on check-in at around £10. I was aware of this before attending but it feels like a rip-off as there are no modern amenities to speak of - it's the sort of scam you expect in a banana republic. We had to wait 9 hours for a replacement aircraft as ours had a technical fault and, although this is not directly the airport's fault, I can't help wonder if the issue could have been dealt with at a better-equipped airport? There are lots stories about the issues caused by the fact the airport closes over night. Our return flight was affected by this, not because we travelled late but because a delay to our aircraft because due to this from the early morning where it had to divert to the midlands! Then final point and the one that left the bitter taste in my mouth (and the reason for this review) was that when I went to leave the (prepaid) carpark, 3 hours late because of our delay, I wasn't allowed to leave until I paid a £15 fee for the overstay. With the fact I paid them £100 for the parking and the development fee, this felt like daylight robbery and the man on the barrier intercom simply told me it wasn't his problem and to contact my airline. Overall a poor show Norwich. Stansted is slightly closer for me and friends laughed when i said I would try Norwich - that it would be backwards and not fit mof the modern age, unfortunately you proved then right!

August 2022. I swore never to use Norwich airport ever again after using it in Sept 2019 but, because of the chaotic departure experience at Gatwick earlier this year, my partner has sworn off using Gatwick so that leaves us with Norwich - which I’m dreading. Where does the airport development fee go? Straight into the pockets of the owners? It’s certainly not used to enhance passenger experience. No shop landside, expensive and minimal range of refreshments airside. Upon arrival airside, passengers are still expected to wait in a draughty, open-ended bus shelter outside the building before clearing customs. That is just an insult. Norwich, a beautiful city, deserves more than this travesty of an airport.

Arrival: fast procedures and quick luggage delivery. Departure by night (11.00pm): not an long queue to ckeck in and to check immigration procedures. After that, a small shop and a small bar/snack are not sufficient to waste time waiting the aircraft.

Pretty boring airport. Not much on the way of amenities or food places. Lack of working power plugs and comfortable places to sit. Rude cleaning staff. Staff at S7 lack basic English competencies. Only recommended for short layover (~3 hours or less).

Novosibirsk airport was renovated during last two years. Now the building looks modern and clean. But when you enter, the hell starts. No customer service at all. Airport staff are very rude and unhelpful. Currency exchange does not exist even in International terminal. So you come from abroad without Russian currency, you cannot even pay for taxi. Restaurants are so overpriced and the food is terrible. Avoid this airport.

A friendly airport if you just want to watch the planes from the viewing area, but not passenger friendly, poor layout. Up a lot of stairs for passport checks when you arrive. Had to go through security the past twice on departure the both times they claimed I had "passed through a public area" after the first check. Security pat-downs are embarrassingly intimate.

Having walked up and down several flights of stairs, and then left standing on them, to get to Passport control. If any accident had happened, we would have been stuck on the stairs. Health and safety measures need to be examined there. Passport control at this airport was extremely slow. Queues of people, with no toilet facilities was very disappointing. They need to get their act together.

After a pleasant stay in Leipzig I travelled to Nuremberg for my flight home to the UK, I arrived at security at Nuremberg Airport and placed all my items into a tray as directed. Then had the misfortune to meet the most rude, obnoxious and officious female member of staff I’ve ever met, anywhere in the world. She was barking orders at everyone in supposed English. Problem is she was using the wrong words and was confusing everyone. Shouted at me to remove a jacket, when it was already in the tray. Actually meant “jumper”. Was very aggressive to everyone and needs to learn some manners, and retraining at the very least. Needs supervision as she obviously has a big problem. Would not recommend Nuremberg airport to anybody

Nuremberg is an amazingly convenient and fast airport. You get there easily by public transportation, from the metro station to check in it’s not even one minute walking, and you can be at your gate within 15 minutes of arriving. Baggage delivery is quick, mostly your baggage is already at the conveyor belt when you get there.

Extremely ignorant staff particularly a female on the gate. She was the cause of patient passengers awaiting an explanation becoming upset and feeling mistreated. She waved her finger in one person's face. She 'shoed' another passenger away with both her hands. She stood with her arms folded grinning. Her manner is appalling and perhaps would be more suited in a prison. The gentleman on the desk downstairs however was the complete opposite. He was understanding and compassionate. The row of employees downstairs knew who I meant when we mentioned this female to them. 'It is not the first time' was one comment. Another passenger has witnessed her vile behaviour on a previous trip. This one employee is the reason I will never return to Nuremberg airport. The security process was good. The food was very poor. No warm food just sandwiches and pretzels. The airport was clean. Transport to the city was quick and easy.

Public transportation to and from the airport is great. Easy access to the city center and local attractions. However, the employee’s that work at the gates are by far the rudest I have ever encountered as a traveler. If the job is that stressful then maybe customer service is not for them. Carrying on a personal conversation while passengers are trying to ask questions about the gate or delay times of a flight is probably not the right thing to do.

It always a good experience to fly from / to Nuremberg airport, because you have short ways. It is connected with the metroline U2 so you are in 15 minutes at the city centre. You can eat some local stuff. The staff is friendly and helpful. The most important to the end - WI-FI is free.

Update to the review 5 years earlier: Since more than one year the new security check between the Terminal 1 and the Terminal 2 is now in operation and has improved the security check in respect of speed and capacity. Since I had some flights last year to Turkey I have unfortunately to confirm that the passport check at Nuremberg airport is a nuisance. It was opened late and the waiting area in front of the check is small and uncomfortable. The check is slow and the personel at the check can easily improve in friendliness and speed. Since most flights to/from Nuremberg are in the Schengen area, this is a minor item. In summary: the airport is still efficient and fast. Security check improved, passport control has room to be improved.

It's always very relaxing to fly from / to Nuremberg. It's a really small airport, but everything works so easy and uncomplicated. You can get there easily by train (a subway station is directly in front of the entrance) or by car (you can park just 1 min walk away), check-in is very fast and boarding, too. There is no shopping and not that many food options, but when you just want to get relaxed and easy from A to B, it's perfect. And the staff are nice, too - even the security staff is always good-humored. More airlines should use this airport.

Due to the relatively low number of flights planes don't have to wait circling around in the air or on the tarmac. The airport itself is perfectly connected to the inner city and the central station (trains from there take you to Munich WÃ¼rzburg and Regensburg in about 1 hour to Frankfurt and Stuttgart in 2 hours) by a 12 minutes metro ride. Passport and security checks as well as baggage handling are a breeze. Staff is very friendly and helpful.

Bagan airport as most westerners will know is a small domestic terminal, all very efficient as they do not seem to use computers. Bags are weighed at check in, luckily as a group of 7 they just calculate all the luggage together which in my case was good as I was overweight. Again usual screen luggage before entering departure lounge which is small with a café for Tea or Coffee and rows of plastic seating again unable to hear announcements but they give you a sticker to put on your shirt so they know who is on which flight.

Often referred to as Bagan Airport rather than its formal title of Nyaung U Airport. It is a very small domestic airport between Yangon (Rangoon) to the south and Mandalay in the north. It is primarily used by tourists visiting the country than by local people. Arriving aircraft make a 3 point turn on the runway before taxiing to a stop near the small terminal building. You are then bussed between the aircraft and the terminal. Luggage is wheeled on large flat carts into the "Arrivals" Hall and is taken off by the passengers. There is no baggage carousel, but there are toilets available. In the public part of the airport is a small café selling coffee, cold drinks, bottled water and the like. Outside the gated compound which doubles as a short stay pick-up point, is a hut with tin roof which provides more of a full café service. For departures there is a row of Check-in booths for each airline. Bags are weighed on communal scales and loaded onto the flat baggage trollies that are then passed via the large scanner and then manually pushed out to the aircraft to be loaded. No computers seem to be used with boarding cards manually completed and baggage tags hand written. As a passenger your hand luggage receives a quick scan and then you are in the lounge which has rows of plastic seats where you sit until a person comes in with a board which is held up with the departing flight details. There is nothing else in the Departure Lounge. It is a small functional airport very much operating as many airports did 40+ years ago, relaxed atmosphere but chaotic at times.

What a dump. Arrived in the morning, only 2 coffee shops open and each had lines out the door. No other food options. On the return trip layover, I made the mistake of stopping by a Mexican restaurant. The menu was limited and food tasted like re-heated frozen food. The layout is poorly thought-out. The queues for the airlines spill out into the walkway. Anytime a flight is about to take off, you are unable to pass through the area. Worth avoiding if possible.

Compared to SFO, SJC, and SMF? OAK is a total dump. Food selection is really poor. The airport closes food vendors, and the walls stay up for years. The terminal is very small. The location, and weather at OAK are good, but that’s it.
3 hours at custom check point. That never happened to me before. One person helping over 500 people. Will never go to that airport again for an international flight.

A security agent found some old coffee in a mug in my carry-on and refused to dump it in the garbage can right next to us but made me exit and go all the way through security again. Extremely discourteous. There is no valid security reason to inconvenience someone this way when there is a garbage can right there. They order everyone through in a hurried rush but apparently don't care about increasing traffic and passenger delay by doing this. I tried to submit this complaint to the Oakland airport through its website but (surprise!) complaint messages aren't going through.
If given the choice I will always fly into Oakland over SFO. It's small, efficient, and flights are most of the time on time. With the new BART connector train it's super easy to get to!

The baggage service for incoming international flights is deplorable. I thought I would try Oakland instead of SFO because it seems like it would be more efficient since it’s 1/8 of the size of San Francisco’s airport. No wonder. I have been through immigration and I’m still waiting for my bag an hour later. How ridiculous. I will never fly into her from internationally again.

Extremely friendly wheelchair assist personnel! I am disabled and was being moved from gate to gate and since I had some layover time I decided that I would like to get a snack at one of the fast food shops. The wheelchair assistant not only took me there, but he helped me get my order as well! The people everywhere were friendly. Cleanliness wasn't top grade but adequate.

Flight DI 7073 landed at 4:15 and waited 45 mins for a gate at 5pm. After clearing immigration at 5:15 there were no bags. It as 6pm before we exited the airport - 1:45 after landing! Someone wasn't doing their job. That delay for bags, on top of lack of gate capacity, is unacceptable service. This isn't a one off. Other family members had a similar experience on June 26 for the same flight where they waited 15 minutes for a gate again and weren't allowed to deplane for another 15 minutes due to a backup in the immigration hall. Departing OAK June 8 was another exercise in lack of airport capacity. Check-in took an hour. The gate had people sat on the floor everywhere due to lack of space for the size of the aircraft. OAK isn't equipped to handle the number and size if international flights currently using the airport. There are similar reviews from a year ago. Clearly Oakland Airport management don't care about customer service.

We arrived and departed on the BA flight from LGW. Arrival was amazingly quick. It took less than half an hour to deplane, go through passport control and collect bags. Being a Club World passenger undoubtedly helped but even so we were pretty impressed. There was almost no queue to go through security at the time of departure (lunchtime midweek), so the process was painless. Again we were lucky that it was so quiet. A new business lounge has just opened by Gate 8. It's rather small, but has good food choice. Getting to San Francisco is a cinch using the BART connector shuttle to Coliseum and thence onwards to downtown San Francisco. In fact the whole experience is much better than at SFO. And because of the competition between BA and Norwegian fares from the UK are very reasonable at present.

Typically the best airport to travel from in country. I travel out of Oakland 15+ times per year. Today, however, they've changed their queuing and the wait times are 30 minutes plus despite only about 100 people in line. Miultiple agents checking IDS at A-List queue with no one in line. Agents are insulting if asked a question. Is this a sign of Oakland airport taking a turn in the wrong direction? Hope not.

In Odessa airport two of our suitcases were missing. In the Odessa airport Baggage Service we were told that there were no lost luggage delivery services at UIA. The only way to reach or leave the Odessa airport is by taxi as there is not a bus / public service to there now. So we had to pay for a taxi plus taxi waiting time. But on UIA site we can read: As soon as your luggage is found, we will contact and inform you about delivery.

As we speak, the new terminal is only used for arrivals. Departures still go through the old, dated terminal. My first complaint is that there are no baggage trolleys at the parking place. Very uncomfortable. My major complaint is about how departing passengers are transported to their waiting aircraft on the platform. A bus waits outside the gate and is so crammed with passengers that I worry some elderly people or children may become unwell, especially in the summer heat. A second bus is waiting behind. It's an absolute insult to passengers that this second bus is rarely used. Odessa Airport, you are treating passengers worse than pigs.

Firstly poor info: there is no airport map/plan nowhere on internet let alone on their web site. The good info should also include that the trolleybus 14 / minibus 177 works from 5 till 22. So the airport is OK and the queuing times are good. At the arrival one waits up tp some 15 min if there are no other plane's passengers coming. The taxi people are annoying but bearable. The airport is practically in the outskirts / suburbia and well communicated by minibus also one can walk some 25 min to the nearest tram line 10 if they wished. [trams work till 2330]. There is a 24/7 kiosk with food and drinks plus a freezer with icecream. Several exchange offices rates are a bit worse than those of the city centre. [27.50 vs 28.90 per euro]. No shopping in departures is rather a pleasant surprise.

A truly awful airport, old metal seats in departure lounge number 2, disgusting toilets that stink. The whole building is old small and not fit for purpose. The ground staff are over zealous on hand baggage size, one guy actually carried a tape measure and small scales to catch passengers out. My bag was the same size and weight as the outward trip, the airline staff at Kiev Borispol had even seen and said yes it's fine as hand baggage. Not at Odessa departure terminal. So £48 charge later and would I fly there again - no way. Yet the arrival x terminal is very modern in fact it's still being finished off. Just knock the old terminal down think 1950's design because that is it.
Arrivals to “new” terminal, departures from old one. Heavy congestion could be at customs, especially if there are >2 flights there at the same time. WiFi is unreliable.

This airport is called an international airport, but in general it only matches a 1970 Soviet local bus terminal standard. The building is old-style and dirty, the seats are arranged in a very awkward way and the number of seats are not sufficient. No air-conditioning before the security check, WIFI signals are very weak and unstable, meanwhile in a very slow speed. Electronic boarding pass is not allowed so everyone has to go to the counter to check-in. The staff there are rude and do not really want help you, they can speak very limited English. There is almost nothing after the security check, a very shabby bar only. Odessa International Airport is the worst airport I've ever experienced. I will not come to this place for sure.

Infrastructure lacking, excellent welcoming courtesy. Plane from VIE landed on the one runway, turned around, and taxied to a parking area, from which we descended staircases promptly rolled up to the front and rear doors. This airport does not know the concept of "gate." We walked to a huge barn of a building and all joined the line of non-Ukrainians. At this point, some passport control official undertook a mental exercise called "thinking" -- let's open the other line (for Ukrainians) for these passengers. That immediately cut the wait in half (my wait was 4 minutes). The passport official who stamped my passport smiled (note to US CBP agents: that's when the ends of the mouth go up) and said "Welcome." Then enter the other half of the huge building, with a currency exchange, a clean bathroom, and not much else. Overeager taxicab drivers were in abundance, but I (and many of us) took the Viking bus to our river cruise ship.

They opened a new terminal but old airport rules remain. Like airport entrance door closed! Even in Ukraine, haven't seen such idiocity in any other airport. As we landed on December 20 and got out of the aiport bus, we stopped near closed entrance door and stayed there in cold for at least 10 minutes. People were amazed and couldn't understand what is going on, since there was nothing to do some started smoking. An airport employee started yelling that it is not allowed. We asked if at least standing is allowed. She said yes, standing is allowed but not smoking. She also announced that she informed about our bus arrival and she's standing there much longer than us without smoking. And accused passengers in having no patience. Annoyance from the very first steps on Ukrainian land. Welcome to Odessa. When we finally got in, we waited forever in border control lines and then for our luggage delivery. Border guards were all over armed and watching us like we were not travellers but some criminals. With a few airplains a day in that airport they manage to do everything way too long! New terminal was cold just like the old one. Toilet cabins had no hooks to hang a purse and toilet paper was on toilet cleaning device instead of normal place.

The most horrible service I have experienced. Staff are rude, ambience is stressful and not organized. Even domestic flights seem like a nightmare as staff do not know how to be professional and organized. Big attention to people who will travel from October 2017, if you don't have a printed ticket the airport has a right to charge you 20$ (which is ridiculous). How is it possible nowadays to charge for what you have already in the system.

I travel for business every week, so clock up a few miles and experiences along the way. 3rd time through Odessa and I can say it doesn't get any better. The airport is tiny and you would at least hope their process and procedures would be top draw. Well, you would be wrong. Poor process compiled with staff who don't give a damn about the pain passengers are suffering just makes it the worst airport I have been to. The staff don't realise they are in a service industry, so do not smile and are surly and rude. How can Kiev get it so right while this big holiday city airport can't. 3 times I have had to experience this coupled with the poor Turkish Airlines service, that means I missed my connection today and write this from my hotel room in Istanbul. Honestly, I would trust these people to run me a bath, let alone an airport.

Absolutely tiny airport but great at the same time; has a lot of character. Lacking service stalls but that's due to the scale of the airport and the expectations of people derived from visiting larger airports.

Ohrid "St. Paul" international airport was, in terms of size, like a trip with the time machine. The aircraft is parking literally in front of the Arrivals door, where passengers are directed to the Passports control. There were only 2 desks working out of 4, which for an airport with 1-2 flights daily can be considered a good performance (!) Nevertheless, despite the size, the airport is well organized and clean, showing the travelers how flying was, at the past times when holding an airline ticket was considered a luxury. As an improvement for the administration, I think that a shuttle bus from airport to the city (roughly 20 km. Distance) would be to consider, synchronized with the flying schedule.

Slow service at international counter. Domestic quite smooth but international very slow, check in counter only open 2 hours prior to flight, and it took 1 hour to check in Jetstar to Singapore with only few counters open. Slow service and staffs that I need to change to different counter to get it done. Slow service at the passport control area. Everything is slow and took more than 2 hours.

Check in efficient, long wait at security, took almost an hour to get through. Boarding unorganized despite 6 gate agents. This was the first time that I was not satisfied with a Japanese airport in 40 years of flying to Japan

Naha airport has undergone some renovation and expansion, it keeps improving each time I go there. Being a small airport, arrival is easy and luggage waiting time is not too long, customs are also friendly and easy to pass through. There is a major improvement in check-in areas for international flights (and some domestic). Used to be in a cramped little area, now it's a lot more spacious. There is also a big improvement in food offering (before immigration). Once passed international immigration, you will be left with very little choice. I believe they are still undergoing some major facelifts for the departure gate areas, maybe more stores will be added soon. Overall, this is a charming little regional airport which is easy to move around.

It was 2 years ago I used this airport, and wow so much has changed! The check in on 2nd level had moved to a much more spacious 3rd level! It made the experience totally different, in a positive way. No longer does it feel cramped. Staff are friendly and signage are very clear. The only thing that still need improving is the variety of shops available (air side), and food options. It is still pretty basic at this stage. With more and more airlines flying to OKA, they can be more ambitious and open up more shops and restaurants to cater for us.
This airport is small. Traffic is quite convenient, and the number of stores is small. The airport is very clean and tidy, and the waiter is polite.

Arrived and departed as a domestic traveler between Tokyo Narita and Okinawa Naha. Small and basic area for both arrivals and departure check in with only one small shop selling some souvenirs and cold drinks and a hot coffee stand but no actual food for lunches etc. On departure the waiting area again has very limited food options with one small souvenir shop only offering some anaemic looking ham sandwiches. There was one actual food stand but the sole employee was working at such in incredibly slow pace that after 40 minutes waiting without being acknowledged that along with another 11/12 passengers I had to give up waiting still hungry as my plane was now boarding. A nice and easily navigated small airport with very friendly staff but I recommend bringing your own food with you!

The international terminal of Okinawa, compare to the domestic one, is a lot smaller. Like all other airports in Japan, signage is clear, clean and very organised. Be warned the, early birds for flights may not get the worms, what I mean is, due to its small size and limited counters available. Very often an airline will only open its counter for check in at 2 hours before the departure time. There is no benefit to arrive early, as you can't check-in yet, plus very limited number of seating and restaurants. The number of gifts shops and food stores after immigration, is also very limited to a scanty few. It is a little underwhelming, so just don't expect too much, it's nothing like Osaka or Tokyo.

Okinawa Naha Airport has 2 parts, International and domestic. This review refers to the international departure. The building is separate to domestic, it is relatively smaller than the domestic counter part. Very limited seating (before immigration) and small numbers of check in counter, result in carefully timed and limited use by respectively airlines. If you arrive early you often have to wait patiently for the check in counter to open. Things improved after passing immigration and security. However, very limited number of shops available for that last minute souvenir hunting. There is a small but functional lounge upstairs for use by premier customers. As an international airport, Naha is functional but small in every way.

It appears that conditions at Naha have changed somewhat in the two years since B. Walberer commented on it. While I haven't been inside the domestic terminal the international terminal was small clean and efficient. There are two restaurants in this terminal now. The number of retail establishments is still limited but that wasn't a problem. While I had to board a shuttle from the plane to the terminal upon arrival an airbridge allowed me to board the aircraft directly on the return flight. One thing Naha could improve on is the waiting time to go through immigration upon arrival.
I live here and fly regularly. New terminals are open airy and plenty of seating. Limited but appropriate shopping. Nice cafe/restaurant selection for a small airport. Security swift and courteous.

Excellent modern airport that is 2/3 complete. There was a complete redesign and now it consists of 2 concourses (West and Central) with the East Concourse still to be built. The facility is modern and airy and nicely designed for post 911 with lots of shops and restaurants post security. Presecurity it is very tight particularly because people waiting for arriving passengers congregate at the two TSA checkpoints (see CHOKE points). For the passenger flying into or out of OKC is a breeze.

This is a smashing little airport - friendly well laid out and very well run. Because of its location very attractive to fly in and out of too - always a big shock returning to Gatwick! Good ice cream too.

A true surprise and real gem of an airport. Superbly clean and tidy nice array of shops to suit all prices and bar/cafes also serve good food. Staff pleasant seating comfortable and good signposting. Only downside was that internet charges too high and not always available.

I rarely have anything negative to say about an airport as I travel frequently. I understand the airport in a small town like Omaha is small. However, when I overhear TSA agents badmouthing passengers that were just in their line to the desk agents, you know something is wrong. I guess moral of the story in Omaha, keep your head down and mouth shut.

Absolutely terrible customer service again with Delta! Could not locate my flight and made my employee late for his flight today, twice in one day, once at Omaha and once at Minneapolis. Both employees were there 2 hours before flight time and still didn't make their flight because of the incompetent employees at the Delta check in. Flights were rebooked at no charge because Delta was at fault but I am not reimbursed for the time lost at the job site for these two employees. Will not be using Delta again.

Easy in and out airport. Decent selection of food outlets and shopping options for an airport it's size. Flew in for a day trip to visit and old friend and had no issues whatsoever. Security screening was a breeze, less than 5 minutes. Flew in and out of the B concourse.

Small and easy airport. Plenty of food options. Extremely clean terminals and toilets. Only 9 out of 10 due to parking. Signs are a little confusing when using quick parking option...the signs do not inform if you have made it to North terminal.

I was brought to the airport by a friend. There is both adequate paid parking and also free (15 minutes) for drop off and pick up. The terminal building is a little dated but it functionas well. There were a couple of flights being checked in while I arrived and there were sufficient counters open so that queues were reasonable. The security check was fast and worked well. You then went upstairs where there is a lounge and cafes and space to sit. Boarding in my case was on a bus but no problems.

It's inconceivable that ONT International airport has to delay flight until the sun melts the ice off wings of planes. Frontier Airlines should have left at 5.45 a.m. and they could not de ice their plane ruining everyone's connections. Still sitting waiting for the sun to rise and maybe melt ice despite temperature will be the same at 7.32 a.m. Incompetent and typical for California

I love flying Ontario Airport. It’s convenient, never busy like the LAX nightmare. It’s small fast and convenient. They have China Airlines flights but not many International flights. Popular flights to Las Vegas Hawaii and Seattle. Nice and clean.

This is the rudest airport I have ever been to. Nothing but issues. Issues with going through security with a 1 yr old and all they did was yell and did not seem to understand or even help. I will never fly to or from this airport again and I will be letting family and friends know how the experience was. Also the place is very dirty and disgusting.

Well, obviously no one reads this or even cares about it as nothing happens and my issues are similar to the ones everyone else is having. Staff are extremely uncooperative and using language that is not understandable. A person just said, “You alarmed” as if we were supposed to know what that means. Next thing we know is that they need to check our hands because we could be hiding something on our hands. Next thing they say it’s just lotion or something. Does the advanced technology that we use not tell the difference between harmful substance and lotion? I know nothing will happen from this as no one even cares, especially those from the airport, but someone does need to care.

I have flown into this airport several times and have consistently experienced long waits for rental car shuttle buses. The buses are sometimes too small to handle the waiting crowd and are never timely. The airport apparently doesn’t know how to update what baggage claim bags arrive into also.

They are restricting Uber/Lyft but there should be a Cab at Airport. We have to call a cab to go to the Airport which is ok but when we arrived there was no cab. We tried to call several cab companies but they would not come to the Airport. There should be phone numbers listed so it would be easy for Arriving passengers. When we got a cab the driver told us that due to some reasons no one wants to come to the Airport so there are very little cabs available. We travel lots so used John Wayne, LAX, San Diego Airport but this one was the worst experience on getting transportation. How you can develop airport without proper transportation?

At 6am on a Monday morning there were literally hundreds of people waiting to go through security. Clearly everyone is frustrated with this idiocy. I travel for a living and I can tell you this is unacceptable and incredibly incompetent to be so understaffed and unprepared. Foolishness.

Incoming flight to Ontario was good, departing flight no lines and we had a TSA PreCheck. Staff member at security spoke poor English and we could not understand what they wanted us to do, made us take off our shoes even with the TSA pre-check. Not very clear for giving instructions. If you work in the United States you should be able to communicate clearly in English.

Red eye to Dallas on American. Easy drop off, but it's a ghost town. Absurd that you can't bring drinks or food through security. Every single vendor was closed. Hadn't flown out of Ontario in over ten years, I use LAX, SNA, and Long Beach. Don't see me using Ontario again any time soon.

One of the easiest airports to access both inbound and outbound that we have ever experienced. Staff on the information desk in Terminal 4 were extremely pleasant and helpful when we asked for assistance. Public areas very clean and well kept. Plenty of seating for passengers. Great food outlets and some interesting local shops as well. A real treat to travel through this southern California airport.

The largely renovated and rebuilt MCO airport is absolute class. Clean, well organized from the signage to the drop-off to security, and aesthetically pleasing in most areas. Returning to the US, the new international arrivals area and post-customs area (so, arrivals really) is just gorgeous. If you have Global Entry, you breeze through in 60 seconds with courteous officers that speak English and Spanish. That alone is unique for a large US airport, where many passport control officers are known for their power-tripping belligerence, but Orlando pleasantly provided the opposite of all that. The signage to trains, rideshare, and hotel shuttles is granularly specified, such that it's easy for anybody to follow (at least when leaving terminal C/international). Leaving MCO the next morning, arrivals at terminal A had clearly been renovated and was looking quite sharp. CLEAR/Pre-Check in tandem reduced security from a 30 minute wait to a 3-minute one. The shuttle tram facilities between gates and terminals are showing their age, and the terminal A gates area is also showing its age (and could also use some more and better seating throughout), but I wouldn't necessarily consider them dumpy. I suppose that MCO will get to renovating those facilities as they can. Truly, MCO seems to be running like a well-oiled machine that is geared to leave visitors to their city with a first and last positive impression.

Arrival it took over 2 hours to clear immigration 4 people working at the immigration gates. Departure 2 hours to get through security 7 gates not open. We were on an international flight so had to be at the airport 3 hours before due to poor reviews we arrived 5 hours before our flight. Once through immigration food and drink availability horrendous Will never use this airport again

This has to be one of the worst International airports in the US. This airport is overcrowded and understaffed. I have been routed through this airport on 3 trips to Jamaica. Customs and immigration are understaffed which makes this airport a disaster to get through! I would rate this airport along with Miami International Airport. Both failures when it comes to International flights.

Leaving travelers sitting in the tarmac for over an hour when there is no weather on site after a cross country flight is not acceptable. We can see the weather now rolling on meaning this hour will be extended further escalating aggravation onboard. The airline was quick to clear us as landed in their system to give the facade of a timely travel experience but that is a complete fabrication of the truth. MCO needs to improve the quality of the experience for a city that is supposed to be welcoming of its travelers.

Why is MCO getting worse with each passing week? As a frequent flyer, out of all three terminals, across several carriers, this airport is pathetic. Between the sheer lack of on site parking, the lack of employees that speak English and unimaginably poor ground service, I loathe this place. I will do anything I can to avoid checking a bag because I know I am in for a minimum of a 30 minute wait at baggage claim. That’s on a good day. The wait for a gate to taxi to, the wait for a jet way brought to the plane, then the incredible, inevitable wait at baggage. Carry on only isn’t always an option for me. As one waits, the announcements are made at times only in Spanish, but when they do make it in English, usually secondary to the Spanish, it’s incomprehensible. Listen at any baggage claim, you’ll hear passengers complaining about them. After a ridiculous wait, when you finally get your bag, it’s smash to bits. Every.Single.Time. Of every airport I travel, world wide, my home airport, MCO, is a disaster.

The TSA women are horrible with no manners. They should be saying “thank you for visiting, come back again”. Instead they tell me this is not Universal this is Orlando International Airport when I’m going through the scanner. They speak harshly to some and are nice to some. Second time departing Orlando and they tell me I have something between my legs. They told me either they feel me all over in front of everyone or they take me to a room to strip down. Mind you I’m traveling with a small child. They really need to learn courtesy and be more polite. Is this how they are being trained? This is the Jet Blue TSA ; one had gray hair and the other had red short hair. They picked up my sun screen in my carryon but not the big Fuji bottle in my son’s bag smh. So much for checking and security!

My wife arrived on Flight AD8706 arrived 6PM sharp and my wife only left the luggage's/immigration at 7:50. Between the airplane get the finger, luggage available, it took 1 hour and 40 minutes. Immigration was quick. Also the terminal does not have enough parking spaces for it's current operations. This was the third time parking A and C where closed and I had to park elsewhere. Luckily I learned how to park at train station and walked 20 minutes to airport C, avoiding a 30 minutes walking from B parking to C.

This airport has a extremely large number of visitors. Ground transport and flow to and from are fine. Concessions facilities and restaurants are far and few between 1 sit down bar restaurant for many gates waiting lines everywhere, all facilities both male and female have long lines. Very far behind the times, would rather fly to any other airport in they area.

I live in Orlando, so use this airport frequently. I don't know what is happening but it continues to get worse and worse. I flew internationally for holiday and returned last evening (April 15th). I left out of Terminal A and returned to Terminal C. I parked in North Lot. Apparently you can take a shuttle from C to the South Lot but not the North Lot. WHY? So I had to take a shuttle to Terminal A to then take another shuttle to my vehicle in North Lot. The shuttle took forever to arrive to C. I saw other shuttles (Mears, off site parking etc) circle two or three times while I waited for the shuttle to take me to A. When it did arrive, me and other other 3 passengers all informed him we were going to A, however he dropped us at Terminal B and told us that was his only stop. So I then had to drag my luggage across the airport to get to Terminal A to catch the next shuttle. That shuttle arrived slightly faster, however the driver didn't even get out of his seat to help any of the passengers board. He just sat there staring at us. A nice passenger helped me load my luggage onboard. I had asked a couple people in the airport how to get where i was going and one girl actually told me "it wasn't her job to answer that question". When I did get to my vehicle and went to pay and leave the attendant couldn't have been any more annoyed that I was trying to pay her. She barely could extend her arm to take my payment and seemed severely pissed off she had to actually perform a function. I traveled to three countries and therefore three airports and am sadly embarrassed how our city is represented with regard to our airport. After customs and retrieving my bags, it took me 2 hours to get to my vehicle last night which is horrible. Why is there no shuttle to North Lot from C? Why doesn't the shuttle that is supposed to take you to A not actually take you to A? Why are the workers so rude and unhelpful. Really poor on MCO's part.
Worst wheelchair assistance experience ever. Attendant assigned to me did not speak enough English to understand my needs, ended up parking me off to the side and walked away!

Traveling to Florida with friends for a cruise, our arrival was fine. The departure was not! We arrived at the airport around 11am, our flight did not leave until 7:30 pm. We were fine with this and tried to make the best of it. The airport was clean but there is limited food selections prior to going through security. The employee at the registers was extremely slow and not very friendly. When you pay $27 plus for a burger and fries you would expect better service. The Allegiant desk representatives were rude. I asked how soon before our flight could we check bags. I was told 4 hours which was great but the representative didn't look at me, smile or ask how can I help. The absolute worst was the TSA agents. extremely rude and arrogant. They were demanding and extremely unfriendly.

I would like to share a positive experience I had with airport staff on December 1, 2024. I came back from a weeklong trip to find that my car battery had completely died. We called AAA but it was a long wait time due to the holiday weekend. A very nice gentleman in an airport pickup stopped by to check on us and offered to jump start the car. He was respectful and courteous and saved us quite a bit of wait time. We will forever be grateful for his kindness and professionalism.

I was wondering why you do not have signs outside for departure and arrival areas that depict location? Like at least, A,B,C or D. When your pick up person arrives you can't give them any notice of your location to pick you up because all the signs say the same thing.

This airport does not have a designated line for Clear customers. Instead, Clear employees walk their patrons to the front of TSA lines cutting in front of travelers waiting in line. This is especially problematic in the lines closest to the Clear checkpoint. Our line was stalled for at least 30 minutes while well over 30 people were allowed to cut in front of us throughout our wait. It took me a while to fathom why my line was not moving anywhere near as efficiently as other lines. Rather than spread this inconvenience equitably throughout the TSA screeners, the Clear employees used just the closest line and rarely the next few. They were rude and clearly unconcerned about the inconveniencing other travelers waiting in line. This elitism may be tolerated at Disney World but is shameful at a public airport.

If you like large airports with lots of shops, restaurants and people then Sanford is not the sort of airport you would appreciate. However, if you prefer a small regional type airport that you can pass through quickly both in and out, without stress then I strongly recommend Sanford. We now look at TUI flight options first simply because they use this airport. The staff are friendly (including immigration and security) and yet its only about 30 miles north of Orlando and roughly a 45 minute drive to the Disney resorts. We haven't been here since 2014, but I can confirm from the time we started queuing for immigration, to collecting baggage was only 25 minutes. Compare this to Orlando International where you would probably be held in a holding area due to congestion.

TSA agent asked if I was over 65 years old and they would allow me to keep shoes on. Being 56 and not overweight or gray haired, I feel quite upset about this. Instead of picking out "old" folks, they should have a sign and recording about the shoes. Do not individually pick out people to ask. It's a horrible experience.

Absolutely love this airport. Easy in and easy out. Not jammed with people like the zoo at MCO Orlando. Adequate places to get something quick to eat and comfortable seats to wait. Only 15 min from our place in Oviedo. I just wish more domestic carriers other than just Allgiant flew into SFB. Maybe international travelers don't care for it because it's not a large airport but it;s great for us and I do recommend it.

When trying to find Gate 4 at 5.30am, all passengers were walking in circles as area was poorly marked that all Gates 1-5 enter through same gate! I started playing hostess so passengers could stop dragging their bags around! Should be an easy fix with an extra sign or staff directing traffic.

Very poor. Would definitely choose Orlando international next time. A lot of security staff, trained to a very basic standard which is quite worrying. Looks good, but hard work to discuss anything with them. Queue in and out was quite long. Clean and tidy, but outdated. So looking forward to getting back to the UK.

My sister-in-law, sister, and 83-year-old mother flew into Orlando Airport last night. I picked them up. The flight was on time but my 83-year-old mother is unable to walk. A young man came with a wheelchair to help us get her to the parking area. He rushed ahead of us and got on an elevator as others crowded into the elevator behind him. We were unable to get on, so my sister jumped on the elevator with him with barely any room left for her to fit, and my husband told him to wait on the second floor for us. The rest of us got on the next elevator. The young man took my mother and led my sister somewhere other than where we requested. It took us two hours to find them and the airport staff were little help. When we would ask anyone for help, they'd just quickly tell us a location and go back to what they were doing. By the time we found them we were all very stressed out as my mother's health is not good and she suffers from Alzheimer's disease. I will not recommend this airport to anyone again.

90Very very poor experience. A Wednesday middle of the day and there were two passport booths open. Absolutely huge queues. Waited over an hour. You expect this in poorer countries over the world. You do not expect this in one of the supposedly most civilised and wealthiest. Really unacceptable. Spoils things a lot. Not good Norway, not good at all.

Badly organised, extremely chaotic and long passport queue. For a country that manages exceptional feats of engineering and superb tourism all around the country it is extraordinary that it fails to organise such a basic airport function leaving millions of air passengers with a really negative impression of the country as they depart. The Oslo airport building itself is modern and impressive - this is simply a case of bad management. With a decent plan it could be fixed - if they can be bothered.
Poor signposting of amenities. The Information desk was closed in arrivals. I tried to find the walkway to Radisson Red but only found it by accident.

There was one entrance for two gates. Also there is no display in front of the concerned gate, for which airline / city the flight is flying to. As they give more importance to Norway language (and the slang of the English), it is very difficult to go through the gate by simply assuming.

Avoid this airport if you have a wheelchair! I travelled through Oslo airport with my 95 year old disabled mother yesterday. We flew in, collected our 4 suitcases and stood in line to re-check our bags on a British airline. We had three hours and plenty of time to check in. First the woman at the check-in was told by someone in Cargo that they wanted a photo of the battery. Then they asked for some obscure information about the battery that we did not have, and told us we could not fly unless we somehow produced a paper with the information. My mother has been disabled for 40 years and has flown several hundred times on flights in Europe and the USA with the same model of wheelchair she still uses. It's a well known brand. We have only ever been asked for the weight and dimensions of her wheelchair, and the type of battery (dry cell) and how it turns off (by key).
