After standing there for an hour and a half another check-in person finally found some information on-line and we were told to go as quickly as possible to the gate. I asked for help getting there as it was 15 minutes before the boarding time. I pleaded with the check-in person to get our suitcases on board (they had been taken off the plane half way through this incident). No help was given as we had to negotiate security, the length of the airport, and passport control by ourselves. There was no time to use a disabled toilet (which we knew from our trip through Oslo a week earlier had a broken seat and was dangerous) which resulted in my mother not being able to use a toilet for 12 hours (she can't walk to use the ones on the plane). This was a nightmare experience which only got worse when we landed at the next airport.

Could have been quite nice small airport but some things has to be improved. Its always understaffed - security, passport control, cleaning and maintenance. Especially on holiday time Its always the same - management forget to check the calendar for holiday or peak times. For the cleanness and tidiness looks like management fired everyone, hired some incompetent externals and never leave their office chair to walk around the airport and check how nasty it looks.

This was my second trip to Oslo this year, but I have never experienced such an interrogation by Norwegian Immigration during my previous visits. You would think that coming from a country with one of the most powerful passports in the world would help. I’m not trying to sound arrogant, but one would expect that Oslo, Norway (Immigration) would have done their due diligence regarding passengers arriving in their country, especially given the high number of tourists. As someone who travels frequently, the officer would have seen that I have visited Norway numerous times before and would have access to intelligence regarding my background. Instead, I felt subjected to an interrogation with questions about what I was doing there, how long I would be staying, my return flight, and the address where I would be staying. This unnecessary scrutiny made me feel as though Norway does not welcome visitors and treats everyone like a potential criminal, especially if their flight originates from Istanbul. I understand the necessity of conducting checks on visitors, but there is certainly room for improvement in their level of security and scrutiny.

We were travelling through Oslo on the way to Manchester. We had our 10 year old son with us who is autistic. We had fast track access to security as SAS Plus customers. Our son was wearing a sunflower lanyard which is the recognised symbol of a hidden disability. When my son walked through the metal detector, which is no easy task for him, it immediately sounded and he was selected for secondary screening, with the girl pointing him towards the full body scanner. She stated that this was a random search. At this point he had a total meltdown which is something that autistic children have. He did not have any concept of what a random search is. The girl who was at the scanner smiled but gave the impression of being totally disinterested and again pointed him in the direction of the full body scanner. Following with my son having a total 'meltdown' screaming and shouting two supervisors appeared and swabbed my son. However, by now the fact that he was in this agitated state was a distraction to others and would have certainly affected the ability of employees to carry out security checks. I believe this led to the security lane being closed. This situation could have been easily avoided had the girl on security taken notice of the lanyard and taken my son and myself to one side and explained the situation or as is acceptable used some discretion or offered alternative methods of screening. As such it must be questioned the level of training as regards hidden disabilities and autism that the security staff at Oslo airport have and their understanding of issues caused by going through security for autistic children as ACI EUROPE guidance, “Assisting Passengers with Non-Visible Disabilities” outlines. Lastly it should be noted that in all of our travels through numerous airports in Europe and the USA this is the only time that my son has been treated without compassion for his hidden disability has not been addressed. Hopefully, someone from Oslo Airport will take note of this and implement changes to training and protocols.

Check in procedure was absolutely a terrible experience. Staff seemed very tired and frustrated. Very few people working. No staff checking how people put their belongings in the trays in the first place (before entering the scanners), only checking this carefully after the trays go into the scanners causing them to be returned back into the machines causing further delays and items getting lost. In that procedure one of our ipads got lost causing further stress and anger, even more anger when staff show no empathy at all. Lines of people waiting and nothing moving. Staff not helpful at all and not pleasant to deal with at all. Very disorganized and this experience was totally unexpected from Oslo Airport. It seems that very few people work over there in these types of jobs which could easily be replaced by more intelligent machines. These staff members clearly seem to be tired, frustrated and show lack of motivation to such a routine nature or work. Our experience in Helsinki airport in comparison was wonderful and smooth. They had super intelligent machines which did not require us to remove one single thing from our handbags and staff there were cheerful and very helpful.

The staff in the Security check was horrible, i have diabetes and my mother prepared the trip so I could have it easy when entering the plane. But when we where going to put everything in boxes, we clearly Said ”we can’t put our cmg (wich is a sensor that measure blood sugar) through the body scanner, and that I can’t go through one” they obviously didn’t understand. A man came and started to explain things and made us look like fools. He also threw my things Down with a aggressive tone. The staff Said I could go through a different machine instead, and I thought that they probably know more Than me, they broke the cmg wich made a mess. Clearly the staff has no idea.

I had terrible experience in this airport. First of all there is nothing, no cafe or shops, nowhere to wrap your luggage. But the worst are the hand luggage control - they may take ANYTHING they want from your carryon, they don’t bother to explain you why they take it, to be honest I doubt that they actually spend a little time learning what is allowed to the cabin and what is not, they just assume that they know (if one of them doubts, he just look at his colleagues and they together decide). They won’t show you any paper or instructions they just take your staff from your bag and say it is a rule. And I am not talking only about cheese (they love to take cheese from tourists, you can see that smile and definitely can say that they enjoy their tiny power to take your things that you spend your own money on), they can practically take anything! Food, cosmetics and more, ones they took my tape). If you dare to tell them that you disagree with them they become extremely rude and disrespectful! They definitely won’t try to find a way to save your property before you come back, because people who use this airport usually leave the country forever and this is a reason why they think they can act so. They know that none of their supervisors will hear about it, they know that the tourists don’t have time to argue about their things, passengers don’t want to have any problems and miss their flight and this is why the workers of the airport can do whatever they want, laugh to your face when you cry about your things that they take. I am curious, does anybody check what is in that blue boxes? Does anyone check what this workers take from people?

A small airport where you can go from the luggage check-in to the gate within 15 minutes. There were enough places to sit down and the WiFi is good! If you want to eat something before the security, there is a restaurant with enough food (price/quality top!). After the security, you can also drink or eat something. Boarding goes quickly.

A small airport with a modern purpose-built terminal with direct rail-link from the city. With only one flight to serve on a Sunday afternoon, service all round should have been and was excellent. Plenty of seating, although that in the bar was a bit utilitarian.

Ottawa is my home airport and given the population that it serves it's very convenient. It is not very large so it may not have some of the amenities larger airports will have (showers, multiple lounges, etc.), but it's fast, clean, and provides an acceptable amount of food choices. Whenever possible I like to clear customs in this airport vs. doing so in Toronto or Montreal.

This is an extremely clean and well maintained airport. They do updates regularly as needed. Its very easy to get to and from. Parking is pretty cheap compared to a bunch of other airports I've been to but not super cheap. They're already planning out the new rail connection to downtown that will be running by 2021. Currently there is a bus service as well as Uber and taxis if you don't have someone picking you up. (Lyft on its way to the city). Its very easy to get around and if you come in from an international destination the customs is very quick. What I do find bothersome is the lack of airport lounge in the US departures area. The only lounges in the airport are Air Canada and Porter, both on the domestic/international departures area. The food selection in the airport is pretty slim, but you wont go hungry, it's just really limited in the US departures to one so-so restaurant and a tim hortons. Shopping is even more slim in all departures areas. But does anyone really go shopping in an airport? This airport is miles (or kilometers) ahead of those in a lot of US airports I've been to despite all the drawbacks.

Ottawa Airport is one of the best airports I travelled from. The security line is fast, the airport is clean and you don't have to wait one hour just to get to your gate. Its a well made, good looking, fast and efficient airport.

Small, simple and clean, everything you want in an airport. Love coming home to this beautiful airport. Pros: - extremely clean - efficient, great signage - short wait times - never any traffic (to and from) and never any plane traffic Cons: - no lounges - not a lot of shopping, very limited food choices - things close early - a bit far outside city centre - parking can be pricey.

High marks for YOW. Transited from USA to international. There is no sterile transit area. One has to enter Canada and then go through security again, but the process was fast. I was number 2 at passport control. Service personnel uniformly nice and helpful. Reasonable number of shops and eateries for a small airport. Well done, Ottawa.

I really like this airport, it is small and not complicated. It is really clean and they have a small but nice section for kids to play. Just wish there were more restaurant for the US side. There are usually no delays. The airport is a bit far from downtown, so a bit expensive in taxi, but hey, they have Uber and lot of parking space.

A good airport to fly in and out of. Lines are not long and staff are friendly. While it is outside of the city there is OC Transpo service via busways directly to downtown. The only down side is that there aren't many food options past security.

Arrived from London and agree with other reviewers about airport size and lack of walking needed to get through immigration and baggage claim. Found immigration hostile to my wife (US citizen) but OK to me. Inane questions and suspicious attitudes are unwelcoming. Little choice of food in departures when returning to UK but interesting architecture and layout - rivals new T2 at Heathrow.
Wonderful! Right size efficient super clean reliable in all weather conditions and wonderful ergonomics.

We (2 adults 2 kids) came here about a year ago (YOW-PUJ) nothing bad but nothing good. Very clean and a lot of Sunwing! Workers are nice and there is a great viewing area for kids! But the downside is long waiting times for everything! Otherwise it was pretty good and we will be using it again on Mar 22 for a flight to London UK then Warsaw Poland and back. Will review it again then.

I fly this airport several times per year. The name and location sounds like a bigger adventure than it actually is. The airport is small so boarding an A330 is already something that keeps everybody busy. However there are not that many flights, ground staff are friendly and helpful.

A fairly typical African airport. I was not hassled for bribes or other payments. Immigration and baggage reclaim were not a problem on the way in. Departure was a bit confusing and facilities limited on the way out. They are rebuilding the airport at the moment whilst it is in use. So it is in a poor state but looks like it will be very good when complete. No business lounge at present. The airport is very close to the centre of Ouagadougou so no long drive is required to get anywhere.

As a small airport on a poor island in a poor country so I did not expect much. Previously I had arrived at the same airport. As expected, check-in was disorganised with locals carrying too much luggage in the form of large cardboard boxes. Customs carry out a pompous but cursory examination of my old backpack. Immigration checks fingerprints and take your photo after a bit of form filling. After immigration you can go back outside the airport because security has not opened yet! Security consists of a cursory search of the cabin bags. You then enter the dismal departure lounge with only ceiling fans for cooling. There is a decent toilet and that is about it. At boarding there is another security check and the guy asked me to raise my leg so he could see the sole of my shoes. I am not sure what that visual search achieved. Later I saw the same "security" guys helping the aircraft to taxi. If you want to see Anjouan, you have no choice but to pass through this airport. Keep your sense of humour!

Second busiest airport in Finland after Helsinki, now really quiet thanks to covid. Terminal is reasonably big and has 4 jet bridges so you don't need to go outside while boarding unless it's a small turboprop like we had, which cannot use jet bridges. There are couple of shops, a bar and a cafe, and just like most other airports in Finland there are rocking chairs where to relax and even a piano anyone can play. Check-in, security and baggage claim went smoothly and fast since there were only a few passengers. Airport is well connected to the city by buses and taxi.

The airport is very small. Only 4 airlines go there Northwest Airlink United Express Midwest Connect and Comair by Delta. There are only 9 gates at the airport. I flew there on Northwest Airlink and the guy that was at the check in desk also carried the luggage onto the plane. Only CRJs go there. There are very few shops so if you have a delay you dont have anything to do. The nice thing about it is since that it is small you get through security very quickly. Overall try to avoid it but if you have to then use it.

It’s a small airport yet compatible with the island size and visitors received. Security personnel is on the edge considering treatment for visitors, there is no need for being so uptight about using cell phones in the baggage area. It’s common practice nowadays and it’s time to adapt. Organized taxi service. Duty free personnel were rude to me except for the Hispanics and Asian descent employees. As a Black woman I was treated with indifference by people of my race / locals. Sad mentality. Uncomfortable seating area for such rich island. Never again.

They are extremely rude at the airport in their customs. I have been asked numerous times why I’m flying alone, and then because I asked what’s the problem, my luggage had to be searched. I talked to the rude and unprofessional “manager” who condoned the staff’s rude behavior. This place is a joke and not equipped nor do I think they want tourists here. Say less, I’ll never be back here!

My experiences with customs and immigration have always been exceptionally pleasurable. Over the past year, I arrived in Cayman a dozen times to meet with immigration lawyers on the basis that I will move here. The officers greet me warmly and I am processed efficiently. I usually try to fly in in mid-week when it is less crowded. However yesterday I arrived on Saturday. This was an interesting experience because the airport was almost full to capacity, causing long lines and delays. I suggest any traveller to avoid arriving or departing on a Saturday or Sunday because there can be many flights arriving and departing. The airport is safe, clean and convenient. Everyone is friendly and easy-going. I love it here. I suggest everyone come visit at least once in their lifetime. This is paradise (an expensive paradise though).

Awful airport. Not at all equipped to handle the number of people travelling through it. Our plane was in queue to land and had to reroute to Jamaica because we were going to run out of fuel while waiting to land. Two or so hours later, finally landed. Immigration - 2 hours of standing in line to get through! Fast forward to departure, again huge lineups and long waits to get through security, no WiFi at the airport, shopping is lacking, food court is too small - super long queues for every stall, not enough washrooms - again long queues for the 3 small ones that are there, not enough seating for all passengers. The place feels crammed and overcrowded, hot and miserable.

Been coming to GCM for 15 years. Yes tourism has increased based on reports by almost 100% over last 10 years, which is fantastic for this beautiful Island. But, the airport although complete remodelled is poor at best. Aesthetically pleasing, it is too small and very uncomfortable. Why go half way for something inadequate from the start. Fortunately, the entire staff are awesome and eased the pain. Suggest a change in schedule of when flights arrive may assist even by 20-30 minutes. Two recent issues I dealt with. The runway pothole was a total screw up. From accounts in paper it appeared that new asphalt from night before was destroyed by a jet blast. Asphalt needs to cure. Second, and personally involved is that our plane needed to wait one hour after everyone was boarded for maintenance to return a log book. This made our connection for our next flight impossible with all the inconveniences associated. How can you allow this calamity to occur is still not sitting well with me. If you expect tourism to continue to visit your beautiful Island you need to improve.

They are not equipped to handle large crowds. We arrived on a Saturday afternoon with 6 other large flights. It took 1/2 hour just to get inside to the customs area and 2 hours from the time we got off the plane until we left the airport. No air conditioning, no offer of water and no seating while lining up for customs. For an island that depends on tourism they should be ashamed. They are not equipped to receive air travellers.

Arrived into Grand Cayman from Miami on Saturday night. Immigration took 10 minutes and bags were already off the belt when we came into baggage hall. Only recommendation is a larger canopy by car pick up point as needed during heavy downpour - we got very wet. On departure - took 15 minutes from arrival to check in and clear customs check. Limited seats at gates but more seats to right hand side as you enter departure lounge. A bit warm but not too bad. More space needed by desks at each gate as gets crowded. Food and shopping limited but sufficient. Few restaurants and duty free but food items very expensive. Boarding is via walk to plane which is great if weather is good. Passengers were crowding the gate before Boarding Zones were called. All in all a good airport experience at a small airport.

It is extremely unfortunate that the residents of the Cayman Islands paid such a significant amount of money for this airport remodel. We departed Grand Cayman on Saturday March 30, 2019 and it was absolutely horrible. No place to sit, waited in line for 45 minutes for a bottle of water. There are currently no restaurants or bars to have a drink at before departure. The departure hall was packed wall to wall. The air conditioning was obviously not size properly for the building and the amount of passengers. We had a similar experience on our arrival. We stood in line for over an hour to get through customs and immigration. I have to say "bring back the old airport" it was actually better.

The airport was recently rebuilt and opened. The design is terrible - no place to sit, very hot, waited in line 45 minutes for two bottles of water. There are no restaurants just a concession stand. We will not return to Grand Cayman next year. This airport is one of the worst airports I have traveled through. Time to go back to Aruba or St. Thomas.

Horrible security experience. The random security checks were one in every 4 people. There was not enough staff to tend to security checks on a very busy day. I stood waiting for a long time without my shoes, as they were part of the security check items. The guy checking took forever as he slowly emptied and scrutinized every single little item in my purse! My children and husband waited for me at the gate as it took nearly half an hour just to get through with a random security check! Worst security check experience ever and I travel often.

Paderborn (PAD) is a regional airport supporting the OWL area. PAD is mainly used for charter flights and has limited and unreliable access to other larger airports mainly MUC and FRA. Overall I like my little airport but the Customs Officials have issues with foreigner and international travelers. The Customs Officials are very unprofessional, rude and enjoy bullying. Their treatment will definitely spoil your vacation. I am sorry, but I cannot more recommend PAD for foreigners and international travelers.

The airport and their airlines offer a wide range of European and North African leisure destinations, but also large German cities such as Frankfurt or Munich. Nice little shops and restauants/cafes. Staff are very friendly and the waiting times as well as the walking times are unbeatable. Love flying from/to the Airport.

Great regional airport. Friendly people and some little shops. It is nice and clean, everything goes fast, I have never waited more than 20 minutes. The flights to Munich and Frankfurt gives opportunities to travel from there and the flights to Antalya and other vacation destinations are great too.
Great regional airport. Min check in time for Lufthansa flights is 30 mins. Good connections via MUC to international destinations. Reasonable amenities at the airport.

A first class airport with a good range of facilities. There does not seem to be the usual hectic atmosphere of most airports bringing back the pleasure into flying. Decent food at non "rip-off" prices particularly recommend the cafe/restaurant on the mezzanine floor.

A regional airport with very modern facilities catering mainly for leisure travel: Lots of travel agents a decent check-in area restaurant/bar glass-walled departure area airbridges in use. There is a modest charge for parking near the terminal (incl. multistorey car park) but car parks located a bit further away (still just a few minutes by foot) are free of charge.

Small, but efficient little island airport. Quite possibly the cleanest terminal building I’ve ever been in, a small team of cleaners were walking around constantly dusting, vacuuming, polishing and looking for any litter the whole time we were there. No fuss, no overly loud announcements, friendly staff, obvious sign posting and a nice selection of shops which had very reasonable prices and unobtrusive sales assistants who didn’t attempt to force anyone into buying things. I really like this airport a lot, the only thing I’d mention is that try to remember it’s a tropical island so be careful where you leave your bags. While waiting outside for the shuttle bus to take us to our rental car centre I saw a huge spider the size of the palm of my hand scurry into someone’s luggage! Probably not the best start to that persons vacation but thankfully we managed to arrive and depart without any extra passengers with us!

PKZ Airport is a small regional airport that is served mainly by Lao Airlines. It has an international connection to Bangkok but mainly to other airports in Laos.  Small single floor airport with Departures at one end and Arrivals at the other end. There is a Cafe/Viewing place upstairs which provides very good views of the
runway and apron where you can watch the few planes come and go.  In the main part of the airport is a Money Change booth and a couple of souvenir shops selling gifts, books, postcards etc and a Lao Airlines Office and the Airport Security/Information.  The Check-in Counters are in a room off the main Departure Entrance which has some
seating just by the Passport Control/Security which lead into the Departure Lounge which has a very small but stocked Shop/Duty Free (No alcohol or cigarettes on sale) which has some last minute souvenir opportunities.  There are also toilets in both Departure and arrivals areas and the main part of the airport.  Processing times very quick as flights are typically ATR72 sized (less than 70 people at a time). The airport is very user friendly and things work well.

Very small airport but there still are jet bridges which was surprising. Everyone I met was so friendly and welcoming. The bags were out very quickly. Just remember to arrange the transport before arrival.

I visited this airport last May. Arrival here was a breeze with some improved facilities, baggage claim was not chaotic like Jogja. Departing from this terminal we're welcomed by entering a narrow aisle, however inside the terminal, it was very big and less-cramped. There were some shops along the way to the departure lounge. Staffs were friendly, but the terminal seating was a bit cramped and the Wi-Fi here was just so-so. There are still some construction works at the time so it was a bit inconvenient. Overall not a bad airport at all.

Travelled to Palermo over the holiday period. Whilst there has been some effort in improving the airport, the place does feel quite tired at times and processes are less than smooth. Staff generally don't speak English, including alarmingly at immigration which is concerning at an airport which is an international gateway. On arrival, if you are held at immigration expect no explanation why and no attempt at communicating, just silence and a blank stare while they hold your passport and keep scrolling on their computer. Toilets apart from in the major departure halls are old, dirty and not maintained - although the ones in the main departure hall airside are now ok and seem to be regularly checked. The ones through the non-Schengen area are quite traumatic to use and are filthy. There have been concerted efforts to improve and modernise the shopping and food but this remains pretty poor. General shopping is very overpriced compared to the city and the food poor value and of poor quality. You would think as the last point to make a memorable impression of Sicily and also sell the island, this would be a good opportunity to showcase the amazing food the island has to offer and also make the effort selling souvenirs but apparently not. Gate areas are shabby and lack seating. Not the worst airport but not a comfortable or pleasureable airport to go through.
Great airport. Easy to park, easy to get to terminal and fast security. Beats almost every other larger airport I have been to. Not much to do but you won't be there long anyway.

A fine small airport, great personal service, clean, well decorated, easy parking, simple and efficient signage, has a luxury feel befitting the Palm Beach Clientele. Food selection adequate and reasonable. Parking is a breeze. Always many security personnel and queue times very short. A pleasure to travel to or from.

What a mess of an airport. From TSA to space for waiting and eating. The open airport area may be nice in the spring and fall but is not practical and dangerous during rain, heat and/or colder times. Whoever thought this was a good idea maybe was ok many years ago but it’s not practical nor safe with huddle and bustle and people trying to get between gates and terminal’s quickly in the rain. TSA is also not appropriately spaced and or staffed for the current passenger load. Then, try to grab a bite to eat and you are out of luck with the 1 1/2 hour wait to get in and order food in the 1 very small restaurant. This airport needs a lot of work to safely and comfortably accommodate the passenger load.

The 3 baggage claim carousels had incorrect labeling about which flight they were serving There was a hoard of people waiting for all the rental cars. We had checked in online but there was no way to utilize this

Great little airport. Everything in one location - baggage belts next to car hire desks and you walk out into the car park and collect your car. Will be my preferred choice now rather than coming in via LAX or SAN and facing a 2 hour drive.

PSP is a great little airport. The 60's style terminal is fairly well designed but with the advent of security screening areas its a bit harder to negotiate. Rental cars are right outside the door from the baggage carousels. The weather is seldom a problem so flights stay pretty close to their schedules. Parking is reasonably priced and convenient to the terminal.

PSP is a beautiful airport in the "secured" area. However the check-in to the security point is a long walk for the many retired people that travel through this airport. The open air feeling is great in this warm climate. The biggest negative is that when there is poor weather and those times are few is the lack of technology for pilots to land. During a rain storm and low visibility we were delayed 30 minutes while circling and then continued to Los Angelos then bussed back to Palm Springs.

I arrived at PSP from SFO. I have used the airport from time to time in the past. It is quite capable of coping with its traffic but has experienced one major improvement whereby hired cars can now be collected on site. This is very welcome especially when the heat is high.

Check in desk queue was ridiculous flying with Tui queued for over an hour only 4 desks open for all tui flights. Security staff very rude, made joke about my appearance and the fact that I had large breast jokes made by a female staff member. The only good thing was the assistance service but they basically gave my husband a wheelchair and pointed us in the direction of passport control and the gate but they were super friendly unlike the security staff. Not my favourite airport. Toilets were dirty no toilet roll no soap or towels. Every cubicle was a mess near to gate A10 a total disgrace

As a disabled passenger I’m puzzled as to why disabled access is so far away from the entrance. People like me who are unable to walk far, like me will find it a struggle to get to the access and feel management need to relocate the access for disabled closer to entrance like many other airports.

The total experience at Palma de Mallorca was next to armageddon for us! We arrived in good time 2,5h before departure, at 3:30 am. First we tried to return the car rented at Record which is at level 1 at the Parkinghouse. You would expect to follow the few signs and arrive at the rental parkinghouse level 1, where you first picked it up and where the keydrop is. NO! You will arrive at the parkinghouse see P1, P2 etc go up there just to find that entering level 1 is closed and blocked. Ok you think, and go to level 2, you can always drive down a level…noop you can not! You are shuffeld out in the wildernes again not knowing what happend. After that we arrive at the driveout. The man in the servicephone finally managed to say “exit in turnabout at the number before seven (exit at the 6th exit that is)”. This car happening took more than an hour (and not only us, about 10 others were in panic) and we realize we have to run for it, with our 20kg bags. Thankfully I hoped, since we were checked in and just had to bagdrop at Ryan Air that would be a quick story. NO! There was no bagdrop, just a line with 200-300 pers going at all directions in the world. Now we realize that we may miss the flight, but still 45-50 min we had. Finally our turn, check in is closed! But they say run, and go direct to gate, D76 as i recall, with your suitcases…oops. Well at security they got angry, bringing our suitcases, but after consulting each other in spanish they remembered that there is a security check to the very left for big suitcases. Bad for us since many thinks allowed in checked luggaga is not allowed at security. Lost quite many things there and many souvenirs, still screaming about why we did not check in below…impossible to communicate. I speak English, German and Swedish unfortunately not an expert in Spanish. Perhaps a good idea to be able to speak english when you work at an international airport? Running to gate after that and Ryanair did not wait for checked in passengers, but closed gate early instead. Never RA again! Luckily we probably got the last two tickets to Copenhagen that day from the only man able to understand our situation. We nearly missed that too but this time Norwegian Airlines kindly waited at least for the scheduled gate close and just a bit longer. At the neat sum of 950 euro well spent in this case we arrived in Copenhagen and then later Sweden. Our mistake was to underestimate the time needed at this airport. On the other hand they should reorganize their logistic. Mallorca is lovely island, but from now only visit off-season.

My wife has mobility issues in that she can't walk further than about 50 metres without resting and can't stand for long periods either. This is our second holiday in Mallorca and both times we have booked Passenger Assistance. In May 2023 we travelled through Palma Mallorca Airport and it was the most traumatic part of last years vacation. In summary, the experience is like a chain with each link being a section of your journey through the airport, however, the links don't appear to be connected or communicate with each other and so you keep getting surprised. To make matters worse we travelled home on 19th July, the day of the IT Outage. Firstly, it didn't appear as though anyone knew that she needed Passenger Assistance and so after checking our bags we had to check her Walker into a different check-in desk and that's when the disconnect started. We were asked why we were waiting when just ten minutes before we had been told to wait there. I asked to borrow a chair so my wife could sit and was told 'no' and then someone else said 'yes'. Then we were asked why we were waiting in that chair and that our name had already been called. Then we were collected and walked through to security without anyone asking whether my wife could walk that distance and without telling us where we were going or why. We were then left at Security and told that after security we would get a Buggy but that didn't happen. Our luggage got separated from us but we caught up with it and were then seated in an area after Security. About five people came and asked what we were doing and each took my wife's Boarding Pass somewhere to check something but we don't know what or why. After about twenty minutes a young lady with a wheelchair arrived and then she wheeled my wife to the departure gate and left us but taking the wheelchair with her. When boarding was called we went through the Gate and then had to stand in a corridor for about 90 minutes. Why weren't we left with a wheelchair? I did ask if we could go back into the waiting area or just borrow a wheelchair that was stood close by or a chair but was told 'no', My wife was in a lot of pain. Other people had arrived in wheelchairs and were in that passageway too but still in their wheelchairs, why not my wife too? Then she had to navigate stairs and get on a coach to the plane.

I've got to admit that our recent trip to Palma has been the worst airport experience I've had in a long time. Sure, high tourism makes things difficult but I much prefer UK/French airports. Arrivals was dirty and worn, essentially also resembling a half-finished construction site which it has been for years. Toilets are disgusting with uncleaned waste on the floor, and no effort of assistance from staff. Extremely long queues at border control, little organisation and very little officers working. Those working were arrogant and rude, going as slow as possible and laughing at building queues. Definitely not a great start to a vacation! Baggage reclaim is okay. Departures are just as unclean and unorganised, despite our check-in being good. Security was fast, however, I did question if their checks were thorough and an agent didn't even look at the screen while I went through the scanner, much worse than UK airports. The departure lounge is also disappointing, extremely busy and no organisation, stores shutting unexpectedly and large amounts of individuals messing around. Walk to gates also showed the age of the terminal with tiles from floor missing, making it look like out of a third world country. Despite this, the area near the gates was modern and comfortable despite little temperature control, meaning it was a relatively nice send-off. However, the airport issues have put me off returning to Majorca voluntarily, really disappointed!

Departure zone A still has no free drinking water access. Each time I fly out of Palma I am told it is because of construction work! It is a legal requirement across the EU that free drinking water should be accessible to passenger yet for some months it has not been.

Upon trying to board the plane we were told that our carry on bags were too big and forced to stop and wait until the plane boarded and then pay extra to plane side check our bags. Upon booking our tickets we pre paid extra for assigned seats and for carry on bags, to then be charged more money upon boarding to check bags that are certified as carry on bags. We have flown for more than 15 years with our bags all over the world and have never been told they are too big and can not be carried on. Also the treatment, the customer service was horrible, we felt taken advantage of and robbed. We were threatened with sercurity pulling us off the flight and to top it off our daughter was with us and was scared and confused. Both the Palma airport and the airline Vueling are horrible, the gate agents should not be allowed their jobs.

Confusing as to where to check in. Went to EuroFlight area only to be directed to British Airways check in area. Long walk. Queued there for about 25 minutes. Bags taken and given boarding pass. Then upstairs to shops, shops and more shops had to walk through large concourses of over-lit shops selling perfumes, cosmetics and jewellery. Both aged 80+. Nowhere to sit. Our tickets allowed us to use Customer lounges, but closed. Very long and confusing walk to Area A from where our flight took off and not well signposted. Eventually reached appropriate area. British Airways Heathrow flight delayed. Sat for about an hour  before boarding. Further delay over luggage loading before our flight eventually took off. Oh, dear! Have spent very many decades travelling but this was the worst airport experience ever.

My husband has airport assistance. At 9.30am after going through security we we taken to an area and told to wait to be taken to the gate, there were no toilet facilities in this area or anywhere to get a drink. Our flight was due to take off at 11.20am. People who were on later flights than us were taken to their gates, upon asking when we would be taken the reply was you will have to wait. We eventually were taken to the gate and when we got to the lift to go down to the ambi lift the man driving the truck said oh you won’t have time to go to the toilet now and laughed, we eventually boarded the plane at 11.16am, we were totally stressed and as a result will never visit Majorca again, the way we were treated was disgraceful. On a note there were about 8 people dealing with the assisted travel it was totally disorganised and they spent most of their time standing around, there was not a lack of wheelchairs or staff.

Really excellent airport! I flew to and from Palma De Mallorca airport for a weeks holiday. There was absolutely no queues! But it was 2am so it was expected. But even when I arrived at about 12pm, the queues were short and went very fast. Definitely a great experience! No delays or inconvenience, except for most of the shops being closed on departure but as stated earlier, it was 2 in the morning. Highly recommend!

Main hub in Northeast Colombia. Although small, the terminal is clean and tidy. Tends to get crowded during peak hours. As many airports in Colombia, renovation is taking place. Most of the terminal is air-conditioned, immigration and customs was fast as was luggage delivery. The airport has ATMs, some souvenir shops and a small observation deck. Flight arrival and departure announcements need improvement with regard to acoustics as information can barely be heard while waiting in the food court (airconditioning will be more than welcome in this area). Let's see what the airport looks after renovation is completed. Pleasant experience. Wifi connectivity was very good.

I don't know what they call it an "International Airport" because it doesn't look like one. It's a small airport and the only positive thing that I can say is that it was clean, the rest is all negative. 1) People doesn't speak English. 2) The customer service is really bad, they weren't friendly at all, the people were mean and rude. There's no restaurants just two coffee shop and one kiosk and two ATMs. According, to New York Times Panama is one of the best destinations for tourism, and I agree that it is a beautiful country. However, they need to work on the facilities, customer service, and improve their languages skills because they could loose tourists and clients just for these points that I mentioned before.

Easily the worst airport of the 20 countries I’ve been in. You have to hop from restroom to restroom to hopefully find soap. They have you fly into/from one terminal but pickup/dropoff bags in a different terminal. They don’t give you a warning that they sometimes have a second wave of security/searching outside of your gate, so you don’t realize you need to allocate extra time. Overall, not enough seating, not comfortable, not free wifi after an hour.

Like many airports food and drinks are much too expensive. I do therefore I also do not want to buy water. It is not allowed to take bottled water through customs so most airports have free tap drinking water . Also this airport. But they are all disconnected. I find this outrageous. To have access to drinking water is a right.

This is the worst airport ever.  Security controls every 100 meters. Even if you get a bottle of water in Duty Free area they will take it at the gate. All security officers are with a strong attitude, rude and don’t speak English.

Airline messed up and we had to spend the night in Panama. Annoying but nothing major. The security checks when we got back to the airport were horrible. Two grumpy staff who shouted in Spanish at people who clearly did not understand, and rummaged through bags in search of anything to shout some more. Apparently mosquito repellent that is allowed everywhere in Europe and South America, is a good reason to shout more and throw it away. Wonderful, when you're travelling to a malaria infested country. They would not even let you say a word, just shouted. They did this to me, kept a couple (who had gone though the same screening the day before) there for ten good minutes, shouting at them not to touch anything (again, they did not speak Spanish) when their gestures said otherwise. Terrible. Very few places to eat, no seating. Even the paid lounge is a waste of money. Glad I'm not passing through on my way back home.

Airport is disgusting. Filthy. Trash everywhere. Gross bathrooms. Stains and sticky material on the seats. Lot of people standing around "working" but doing nothing. Horrible layout. Can't hear anything on the announcements.

Not great, this airport. Consumerism rules - there are shops upon shops upon shops, and literally no where to sit, not even at the gate. The gates have about four rows of seats, which obviously isnt enough for all, and other gates are guarded off by staff. Instead of having hundreds of shops, this airport would benefit from having some SEATING or LEISURE areas for passengers.

It is very discouraging that an airport that calls themselves the bridge of the Americas provide such poor service. My husband and I had to change planes in Panama in our trip to South America and stopped here twice, in our way down and back up to the US. The service is terrible, the technology sucks, the bathrooms we bad, the people very unfriendly, the employees who checked bags right before we board the place towards Orlando were very young and unfriendly ladies who do not take their job very seriously and did not consider older people who needed help. It is sad since I liked Copa Airlines, but I will try to avoid Panama airport as much as I can and I hope their management reads this and does something about it and put some money to bring this airport up to part, make this airport a real sample of technology and service that truly deserves the name you so proudly call yourselves but do not show, you have a lots of room for improvement and all areas and aspects

The worst airport I have been in. It's crowded, hot, they charge for wifi after 60 minutes, there are no water fountains, not enough restrooms, security just before the gate that makes you toss all your water. You can't take a drop of anything to drink on the flight with you. If you have a long flight, tough... I hope you like being dehydrated. Everything is expensive by airport standards. You may have a really long walk between gates because there aren't any moving platform and it's spread out.

I never thought I'd review an airport, but there is a mix of staff that hates being there and some willing to be friendly. The wi-fi is horrible. Sometimes it connects and other times it doesn't. I would even if you paid for their faster service, reliability would be the same. Food selection is similar to a mall's food court that is somewhat deserted

I'm really disappointed in this international hub. There are very few amenities other than Duty Free (which inexplicably and aggressively pushes Kylie Jenner products) and the beer selections are abysmal. Panama's local beers make me long for a Budweiser, which is a beer I normally eschew. I paid for 24-hours of wi-fi service in the terminal (my flight was delayed and it was pouring rain so I didnt know how long id be there) and only got 1 hour. With one notable exception, the staff was woefully under-prepared for international travelers. I did not understand what the person at the bag scanner was telling me, to the point where I had to literally say "I genuinely do not understand what you want me to do." I'm very comfortable traveling; I know the routine. My belt, shoes, and carry-on were carefully placed in appropriate bins. Even after she waved me through the scanner I was unclear on what she wanted me to do (I still don't know, and she must not have either because she just stopped trying to communicate). I strongly suggest avoiding Panama City as a stopover if you can.

Arrive at the airport for check-in/bag drop to discover all passengers waiting in lines outside the building as this is where check-in is located. A bit like a shop in a rough inner city area, steel shutters cover all the desk area and these are only raised when it is time for your flight to check-in. This was only two hours before the flight rather than the recommended three for long-haul destinations. Consequently an hour in hot, humid temperatures with the occasional rainfall. There is a canopy over the wait area which offers shelter from rain but nothing else. The airport is pretty basic inside with nothing very much to recommend it. The business class lounge had plenty of seats, a very basic buffet area, reasonable drinks, and self-service. Access to all aircraft is steps because there are no air jetties here. Consequently, passengers are refried on the way to the aircraft.

The Papeete airport (PPT) has to be experienced to appreciate how fortunate we are to have competent, well-run, modern airports throughout the world. It’s not third world. Worse. It is an astounding perfect storm of incredibly slow TSA, total indifference, indecipherable in so far as where to go, how to get there. The one happy experience we had was the people, the airport service employees (I’m in a wheelchair), they were friendly, helpful and made up a little for the amateurish functioning of PPT. Our larger issue was United Airlines. They cancelled our return flight at 3:00 am-5 hours after departure time-and immediately a wheel chair attendant showed up to deliver us to two of a few hundred cots—no blanket, pillow, water—in a warehouse near the airport. I looked at a picture of a prison cell and the bed was superior to what United provided for us. We never saw a United person in the multi-hour process. Never again will we fly United OR go through through the Papeete airport (PPT)

This airport is THE worst! I’ve traveled to many places globally and I’ve never been to a more disorganized airport. If you get there earlier than 3 hours before your flight you will find everything is closed so there is a line full of people waiting for the ticketing agents. That line was well over 2 hours. Thankfully the 1 of 10 ppl who asked to see my passport allowed my partner and I to move over to the priority line which meant we stood in line for an 1 hour. Note the whole time there is no AC so your standing in sweltering heat while you wait. I had asked one of the airport workers where customs and was because we needed to have our receipts stamped in order to get a tax credit for a pearl necklace I bought. They told me I had to do that once I went through security. In security I got asked about 2-3 more times to see my passport and boarding pass. Then I go to the information desk to ask where customs is. Oh it’s on the outside before you go into security and I was told the wrong information. Too bad so sad I can’t take care of my tax stuff anymore and will now need to mail in all this info to get my $80 credit. Now I we wait to start boarding. They had like 4 international flights all leaving within 15 min of each other and it was utter and total chaos! It’s frightening to think the people running this airport are in charge of your safety because they are so disorganized and nothing they do makes any sense. They never told us our flight would be boarding late and it wasn’t until 10 min before our flight was supposed to take off that they finally told us they changed our gate. They had 2 different LAX flights going out which caused confusion since we were at gates right next to each other. People were standing in a very long line and waiting to board because Air Tahiti doesn’t have the common sense to have boarding groups. Then they eventually call rows but they aren’t in order so that creates more chaos. Everyone is blocking everyone because they were all standing in line in front of the gate. So we’re standing in another long line waiting. They obviously can’t handle all these flights going out at once so no clue as to why they wouldn’t even do that instead of staggering them by 30 min or an hour. They also ask you for your passport again 2-3 more times. No exaggeration I had to show my passport 8 times. I will never fly to this airport or on Air Tahiti ever again.

I have been using this airport for close to 20 years and can honestly say it has become a complete nightmare. The day we departed the had 4 International Flights set for Departure at the same time and the airport was a complete disaster. They are in no way equipped or handling 4 flights simultaneously. They seem to have missed the fact they are the size of a municipal airport and trying to have the appearance of an international airport. We arrived at the airport 3 hrs. early as directed and they entire time was spent in the security line. There were 3 passport control employees as the line was wrapped around the building and down the sidewalk to the rental car lot. The workers, while friendly didn't have a care in the world that they were holding up a thousand people from boarding their flight in a timely manner. Their TSA was also the slowest on the planet, taking their sweet time to look at everything and ask the same questions over and over again. We walked on our flight at final boarding and our plane was delayed 20 mins due to more people stuck in the line. They also had a side door at passport control that they allow people to continuously cut in line because their flight was in final boarding, or they seem to know the people working at the airport. We must have had 100 people jump the line in front of us during our 2 hr. 45 min wait time. This airport needs to re-evaluate their procedures and limit the flights departing at the same time as they are in no way up to the standard of being able to work in this manner.

Definitely will not be returning via Papeete airport Tahiti. Departure is a real nightmare. Flight left around midnight and it was there 28 degrees outside and inside. No AC, but fans that skew corridors on the ceiling. When the VAT line opened there was only 1 employee for a flight of almost 300 people. However, security left something to be desired. From check in to after the rx check it took almost 2 hours and a half. Security just laughed and asked those stupid questions, like where do you fly on arrival in LA or did you leave your hand luggage alone, no right. Don't think it's possible in 2023! Toilets without AC. After a very nice holiday in Tahiti, employees, airport security and the airport itself tried to ruin the holiday.

Definitely will not be returning via Papeete airport Tahiti. Departure is a real nightmare. Flight left around midnight and it was there 28 degrees outside and inside. No AC, but fans that skew corridors on the ceiling. When the VAT line opened there was only 1 employee for a flight of almost 300 people. However, security left something to be desired. From check in to after the rx check it took almost 2 hours and a half. Security just laughed and asked those stupid questions, like where do you fly on arrival LA or did you leave your hand luggage alone, no right. Don't think possible in 2023! Toilets without AC. After a very nice holiday in Tahiti, employees, airport security and airport itself tried to ruin holiday. I was very happy in the morning when we land in LA.

This airport, like much of French Polynesia, does not have air conditioning or modern amenities. 75% of the restaurants and shops you encounter before security at the airport are always closed for some reason, and the places that are open are very expensive. If you are flying domestic or international there will be one restaurant selection past security. When we had a domestic flight, there were long lines at the “Snack Shack”, I can’t comment on the food quality because there was no power. When I flew international, the one shop selling food was not making iced beverages but was selling hot coffee and sandwiches of rancid meat and cheese. They are probably rancid due to the lack of roper refrigeration in this hot and humid climate. The two upsides are that staff are very friendly and the airport was very clean considering it is all an open space.

The airport is located just west of downtown Papeete and is on the sea front. On arrival at the terminal you note that the front of the building totally open. This means that the waiting/check-in area is hot and humid as there is no air conditioning. It also means that the waiting/check-in area is not as clean as some would like. The ticket counters are located a few inches behind doors that roll up and down. The airlines only have their check-in counters open (the rolling doors in the up position) about 3 hours before the flights depart. Food service and shopping are both limited in the departure area before the security check point. After passing thru the security check point there is additional, and better, shopping but even less food service options. All food, both before and after the security check point, is expensive. Seating in the international departure lounge after the security check point is also limited. There are no bridges from the terminal to the planes. Passengers need to walk on the tarmac from the terminal building to the plane and then climb a set of rolling steps to enter the plane. The terminal, while workable, needs to be updated to meet modern international standards.

Papeete airport is dreadful! It has no air conditioning and no fans either in the check in area or the international main departure area. It was extremely hot and humid so I was dripping sweat as were others who stank from the heat. It was very crowded, body to body as all the international flights to the US (and to Europe) go out in the late evening. The good thing about so many bodies is I only got a few mosquito bites while waiting to check in (I had none before getting to Papeete airport). It was a very long wait to check in and they didn't have the counters clearly marked as to what flights each counter person was working. Because of the heat and the long wait and the confusion about which counter did which flight many people were in the wrong lines. The only place with air conditioning on the lower level was the stinky bathrooms which I stayed in for a while despite the stink because I felt like I was going to faint from the heat in the main checkin area. Almost no chairs were available either in the check in area despite many, many people having to wait hours to checkin for all the international flights leaving between the hours of 9-11:55 pm. The main departure lounge was little better. No air conditioning except in the duty free shop. Not enough seats for the many people waiting for their flights. The islands of French Polynesia / Tahiti are beautiful but I would likely go to other South Pacific island countries just because the Papeete airport is so awful.

Will not return to Tahiti unless this airport changes. The absolute worst airport I have been to. Departure was a nightmare. Flight departed at 10.50pm, arrived at the airport at 5.30pm. 88 degrees. No fans turned on, of course no AC, not enough seating for people already there. When the VAT line opened, there was only one employee, 15 people in line. One lady fainted from the heat. It was so hot that the back of my shirt was dripping. McDonald's was just closing and get this! They came out and collected all of the trash cans and stacked up all the chairs and took them away, making even less seating in the terminal. We have a lounge pass which let us in to the Air Tahiti Nui lounge. Still, we could not get to the lounge until they opened the gates at 8.15pm. There was only one employee to be found, and that was a lady at the information desk. Felt sorry for her having to take the wrath of mad customers. Also the bathrooms had AC. Go figure. This experience pretty much ruined the end of our vacation. Which ever country runs this airport-shame on you!

Arrived to find large ques at immigration. Grunted at to use police E gate. It would not read my new passport, an airport immigration official ripped the passport out of my hand and put it into the machine, after 30 seconds it eventually read my passport and took my photo what was next to blank. The next gentleman behind me had the same issue but this time the machine would not read his passport so the immigration official shouted that it was is fault due to Brexit.  Duty free at departures is more expensive than the UK high street. I have been using this airport for over 30 years and every year it seems worse the staff now have seemed to lost there ability to speak English, (must be the Brexit effect.)

Small airport totally unfit for purpose when you consider the amount of pepple passing through. Had 2 desks open. Waited until the queue reached Paphos harbour (joke) before they opened a third. All in all over an hour of standing until we got through. The eateries were all overcrowded with limited seating. The info screens were very few and so small they were almost unreadable without a telescope. Then we were sent through a gate to wait in a holding area in 38 degree heat for 35 minutes whereas we could have stayed in the cool. All in all poor experience. Would give it no stars if possible

strong>Not Verified| Departure obviously embarrassing. Disgraceful! Workers need a sacking did nothing wouldn’t answer questions made us wait for 7 hours to then cancel our flight when they knew it wouldn’t be going into the air. To then have the audacity to leave straight away and go to the smoking area to laugh and joke like they haven’t just ruined hundreds of people’s plans. Outrageous will never be flying from Phaphos ever again. Wish I had the names of the ludicrous deluded staff that were as useful as a water paper towel stuck to the toilet ceiling. After they cancelled our flight tonight they then told us to wait another hour to see the next steps I.e hotel we would be sent to. Left with no food no water. Waiting for this service was like waiting for grass to grow in a desert. Had more chance of finding water in the Sahara then finding any useful information from the incompetent staff.

A simply awful experience and not what you expect from a popular tourist destination. The staff are miserable, rude and unhelpful. A more unpleasant bunch of people it would be hard to imagine; do they train them that way or are they specially selected for their negative, hostile attitude? All in all it’s a great shame as Cyprus is a wonderful place to visit or live and this lack of humanity and friendliness in people who are supposed to be ambassadors for the country will inevitably sour the whole Cypriot experience for many. Apart from all that the food is dull and like everything else at the airport (apart from parking) horribly overpriced. Items from “Duty Free” are actually much more expensive than in local shops; for instance, a bottle of Methy wine is €16 in Phillipos in Coral Bay and €26 at the airport, Toblerone is €4.99 in Phil’s and €11 at the airport. Not good enough!!

After 6 wonderful weeks in Cyprus, my husband and I flew back home to Tallinn. As this was our 3rd trip to Cyprus, we were well prepared and everything went quite smoothly until we arrived at security. I happily greeted the staff in English and began placing my things on the conveyor belt. A middle-aged male security guard approached me and began to make his demands in Russian. I can understand Russian, but my English is significantly better, especially after 6 weeks in an English-speaking environment. I asked him to speak to me in English because I have already answered him three times in English and I don't speak Russian. The official got angry at this and said in Russian that you are taught Russian at school in Estonia (in fact, the first foreign language in Estonian schools has been English for 30 years) and that the Russian language is not to blame (in what, he didn't specify). I told him that he was attacking me by talking like that. Then he turned to my husband, still in Russian, that they usually call the police in such cases. My husband silently listened to the threat and we managed to leave. I really didn't know that I had to learn Russian to pass the security check at Paphos Airport.

I wasn't very impressed by the staff. The two woman on duty did not appear to be helping visitors much. Several of us didn't know which queue to join to go through passport control. When I finally got there, it was like 20 questions. They made me feel like a criminal. "Is this your first time in Cyprus?", "Do you have house here?", "Where were you in 2009?" As if anyone can remember that! I assured them it was my first visit to the island. After some discussion between two if them, they eventually stamped my passport and one of them slammed it down onto the counter. I know they have to do their job, but it wasn't very welcoming and they didn't have to be so rude!
Bad service, very small airport with a lot of travellers, overcrowded, I don't recommend it, prefer to travel from Larnaca.

On the morning of 04 April 2023 I transferred through a sweltering hot Paphos Airport on my from Amman to Athens. There was no electricity at the airport, as a result the airconditioning did not work. Because there was no electricity, the ticket scanners after check-in malfunctioned and a very rude lady opened a gate for me after interrogating me, my boarding pass and my passport as if she was the border patrol official. Hundreds of people trapped in a sweltering hot airport building which, at best, resembles a garden shed the size of a football field. The business class lounge was not open and the corner where it is is located at stinking of sewage because it is situated next to the toilets. No coffee available and no working credit card machines at any of the restaurants. Long queues as people rummaged through their handbags for coins to pay cash at the cashiers. I settled for a lukewarm cold drink. And of course there is always that one airport employee that makes you feel as if they are doing you a favour. Thumbs up though for the new biometric scanners at immigration. Five stars for the efficient immigration staff. One star for the overall experience. Use this airport only in case of an emergency.

There were several very rude staff at the ticket barrier, where most of us passengers were having trouble getting our tickets to scan successfully. They hung back, didn't offer assistance even though it was obvious there was a scanning issue and when help was requested, barked at us like we were the most stupid people in the world. If anyone is using this airport, seemingly you have to hover your ticket bar code above the scanner rather than place it directly on it (not that this is remotely clear). The staff are rude people who seem to hate their jobs and hate customers. They shouldn't be public-facing. Terrible customer relations and service. Unhelpful, impatient and rude. Other than that, the airport is small and unhectic in the quiet season, so quite pleasant.

The lack of organisation and laid back attitude of staff at this airport is letting the whole of the holiday industry down in this area. After touch down last night we were through customs and waiting for our luggage within 15 minutes. It took another hour for our luggage to arrive on the carousel! Two of the carousels were working but neither of them had the correct flight numbers on so you were not sure where your luggage was coming from! Our flight number never came up on either carousel. There were was one member of staff trying to assist handicapped passengers and that was the only staff member I saw. This was a very frustrating start to a 2 week holiday. The holiday industry in this area is relying on the staff and organisation of this airport to survive. At the moment it is giving a very poor impression of the island.

Very slow service at the immigration and at the luggage belt. We spent 2 hours in the airport after arrival. This is really bad given that here is like 3 flights a day only. Airport is old and falling apart.

Very dirty, noisy with boomboxes, inefficient procedures, outdated equipment. Leaking roofs, no proper waiting area before you enter immigration, immigration is not permanently manned. Avoid by all costs. Very limited food sale. Only positive are the very friendly people who handle the flights.

Small airport - check-in was quick and big smiles and friendly check-in agents. Security took forever - slow process and flight was early (6.15am departure) so maybe that is why.  I can't imagine when KLM has a 747 here and they are clearing 300 people compared to a 737 on Surinam Airlines.  Gate area is small and there are quite a
few shops - some were closed this early but when they are all open there are plenty of options.  No jet-bridges so you get the experience of walking on the tarmac to your plane.  Toilets clean and prices in the shops reasonable. Arrival is slow with immigration but bags were delivered quickly.  Plane parked close to the terminal and it was pouring with rain - no umbrellas provided but wasn't too bad.  Airport is 45-60 minutes from Paramaribo on a road with many speedbumps - that is the biggest negative about the airport - especially when your flight arrives at midnight and you don't get to your hotel until after 2am.

I haven't experienced Terminal 2E until today when I had my flight to Japan. I was in airport 3 hours before flight and I was in passport queue 2.5 hrs before my flight and 1.5 hr before boarding. It was understaffed. Our queue wasn't moving at all when they opened a separate queue of people way behind us and opened a new customs booth to let them in. We waited for 45 mins when I interrupted one of the info people saying our queue hasn't moved in last 30 mins and that they took people from behind, I was told "this is not a restaurant and these are police" when police has nothing to do with managing the queue and I was angry at the staff. I nearly missed my flight (if it wasn't for inefficiency of onboarding) I was in L21+ gate which you have to take another train and find your gate and security checks too, it takes 15 mins.  I am in France as expat and I rarely came across this behavior, I find French lovely but this behavior in airports is only off-putting and repulsive.

Worst experience ever. Waiting time for security over an hour, unfriendly and not really helpful staff. We had a long layover which saved us. Its a maze with bad signage. Next time I pay the extra and fly over Amsterdam.

We were in transit on a Sunday night in January (arriving into Terminal 2 and connecting from Terminal 1) and absolutely everything proved an obstacle. The first flight was slightly delayed and we knew that we didn't have time to be too slow, and had to change terminal to catch our connecting flight. This included a train ride and a trip by bus. The layout of the airport is pretty bad, but the real problem is the lack of proper signage and the rudeness of the airport staff. We tried several times to ask for directions, but were met with shrugs, "not my job", no English.  We were sent through 3 security checks. We ran but to no avail. The gate closed before we got there, and the staff said that they couldn't help us and left.  We had to spend the night in the airport with overpriced vending machines.

It is disorganized and poorly laid out. Signage is contradictory and confusing. Do not attempt to get a ride share from the airport, it is nearly impossible. Following the detailed ride share directions to the pickup area will not yield a positive result. The food options are abysmal and overpriced. The airport layout is so random and lacking cohesiveness that it’s absurdly easy to miss connecting flights. Security was a mess and you could expect it to take much longer than it should. Also expect to have hand baggage weighed. Even the WiFi sucks.

This was probably one of the worst airports I’ve experienced in terms of organization. The issues started with the luggage drop-off process, which took us 1.5 hours. We had to navigate multiple queues and deal with belt malfunctions that brought the line to a complete standstill for a significant amount of time. Before security, something I’ve never encountered before—they weighed our carry-on luggage. If your bag was even a few kilograms over the limit, you were required to check it in. In our case, this could have easily been avoided since our checked luggage was under the 23kg allowance. It felt unnecessary and poorly communicated. The queues for passport control and security were long and tedious, though I suppose this is typical of large international airports. Still, the overall lack of efficiency made it even more frustrating. After all the stressful queues and delays, you’d hope for a chance to relax and grab a decent meal. Unfortunately, the airport offered very few places to sit down and even fewer options for proper food. Most eateries were limited to snacks, and there were almost no places to enjoy a real meal. I’ve traveled through many airports, and this was one of the poorest in terms of seating and dining choices. Overall, the lack of organization, poor communication, and subpar facilities made this one of the most frustrating airport experiences I’ve ever had.

By far the worst airport experience I have ever had. I will avoid this airport in the future at all costs. On my way to Bangkok I nearly missed my connecting flight because of all the chaos at every checkpoint. The signage is terrible and just trying to find your way around is a nightmare. On my way back to the States I unfortunately had a 16 hour layover here and paid $220 for a closet with a bed in it at the airport yotel (hotel). The food selection was no better with only 4 or 5 restaurants, if you can call them that. 3 of them all had the same pre-packaged, soggy sandwiches. I honestly don't see how a city as popular for travel as Paris could have such a terrible airport. I will fly through Amsterdam next time and take my chances!

We arrived into the non-Schengen area of 2G and left the plane at 11.35am, which was a late arrival. We had to catch the flight to Oslo from 2B/2D (D68) at 12.15pm. Based on our experience, it is normally possible to make such connection in other big airports (e.g. Heathrow, Frankfurt, Schiphol) if you follow signs, walk fast and make an effort to skip lines at the passport control / security using short connection as an excuse. The 2B/2D transfer signs in 2G quickly brought us to the security check and then onto a shuttle bus, which took us on a 30-minute journey with the following itinerary 2G-2A/2C-Terminal 1 and finally 2B/2D. When we left the shuttle bus, we still had hopes, but our optimism started to fade when signs guided us to the second security check after the border control. In the end, we had made it to the gate by 12.20pm (it had closed 2-3 minutes prior to that) and missed the flight. It would have taken us up to 70-75 rather than 45 minutes with normal walking pace and no cheating in the lines. Now, the most important thing: 2A-2F are all connected by pedestrian corridors, which would allow you to both skip the ridiculous shuttle bus journey and reduce the number of security checks to one. If you walk fast, you will then make the connection. Having said that, you will never figure it out unless you are very familiar with CDG. Don’t repeat out error. Don’t trust the signs.

Transited twice in November, without problems. Signage is good, distances are large even within terminal 2e No problems either time, though timings were circa an hour and a half Security check each time, but fairly fast and efficient

Used T1 this time for both departure and arrival. I fancy this strange facility with flavor of 70-s after its recent refurbishment. Overall clean and well looked after, with all lifts and escalators and travelators working, with meaningful food options, bearable security queues and convenient transportation access via bus and monorail, it does the job and does not irritate. Well done.

I can't believe the absolute nightmare I just endured at CDG Airport! I arrived a whopping 3.5 hours early for my flight, checked in without a hitch, and then made my way to customs immigration, only to be met with utter chaos. The lines were insane—thousands of people from all over the world jammed into a disorganized mess. At one point, there were only TWO customs agents on duty! Are you kidding me?! The so-called "customer service" people were running around trying to manage the queues, but it was all a pathetic display of incompetence. I've traveled by air for over 20 years and have never seen anything as ridiculous as what I witnessed at CDG. This airport is supposed to be modern and efficient, but it was anything but! The organization was a complete joke, and the customer service team couldn't have been more useless if they tried. I barely made my flight with just 10 minutes to spare, while countless others were left stranded, missing their connections. And to top it all off, I watched the staff LAUGHING at the mayhem around them, like it was some kind of twisted joke! Oh, and let's not forget about my arrival—another hour wasted at passport control with hardly any staff on duty! I can't stress this enough: DO NOT transfer through this airport if you can avoid it! My flight on November 12 from GDG to Manchester was ruined by this disaster, and I will NEVER forget it!

Initial security was okay. They did a good job in speeding up checking bags. But after getting to the gate the experience wasn’t nice at all. The airport is very hot. Checking at the gates could be improved. We have stood in the line for 45+ minutes before entering the airplane! There’s no good food options, basic cold food.

The worst airport I have ever travelled through. I’m writing this because every time I come here, the staff are impatient and unnecessarily rude. This time I actually fell flat on my back being abruptly stopped before going through the security scanner after another person told me to move forward. The process is chaotic and the staff had the audacity, as I lay on the ground, to yell at me! I’m not surprised that the average review is so low.

One of the worst experiences ever in a major airport. There was no one in the immigration at gates F, Orly 4 building, 1h30 of waiting to have a single policeman for 3 or 4 flights departing from this hall and of course, they had to start with passengers with priority, so 30 additional minutes of waiting. Never in my life, I could imagine an airport with no immigration officers, even in the worst airports in the world. Once the immigration passed, gates area is still under construction, no wifi and very little number of electric plugs. So if you are unlucky and have a flight departing from Orly 4 hall F, take everything you need in advance.

Absolutely terrible experience at Orly in September 2024. Until it improves I would advise people to avoid. Upon Arrival the transfer from plane to Terminal and the ability to enter the correct Terminal for the transfer flight was a disaster. Delays at every point in the journey. Construction seems to have made a mess of airport movements. Upon Departure the Security queue is quite simply HORRENDOUS.

Was supposed to be transiting to Istanbul, welcomed by a rude staff member upon asking for directions. Pointed me to the exit queue which resulted in having to go through the passport control and security control once again and missing my flight!
