Absolutely unhelpful and unprofessional staff - felt outraged going from one terminal to another, trying to find an info desk only to find out two hours later that there was no information desk.

I had the most horrible experience with your airport, travelling at terminal 3. Firstly, the airport layout is terrible, no signs, so for Transavia drop-off luggage there’s a queue of people where Transavia signs are, just so you get told to go ab print a label before coming back and then, if you’re lucky to be at the right queue area for your flight (there are 2), you can continue. The worst part is the security check: staff completely unprepared and unfriendly. I had my laptop (Airpad) out from my laptop bag, one beside each other on the tray and the staff took it aside because they wanted it in 2 different trays, but I was never told and kept waiting for 5 minutes for my tray that never came. In any other airport, you are not asked to do such thing, as long as your laptop and bags are beside each other it does not matter. Then I had to go back and separate from tray myself and got caught to do random sampling- even though I had already gone through. The security staff was awful and did not listen to the fact I had been already gone through and should have not needed to go on control again. Too many people working inefficiently, unfriendly and unprepared.

The staff was very unfriendly and unable to explain why we had to move our liquid items to another plastic bag when they already were in proper transparent bag of appropriate size. Staff members don't make any effort to speak other languages! Moreover the toilets (terminal 3) were filthy and unacceptable in any airport. Hoping this review helps you to improve your standards.

No facilities were made for disabilities and our party was split up as apparently 4 people with disabilities don't travel together.  We had to find evidence to show that we were infact 4 special needs and three carers in the party. 2 of which were under 6. When asking to be together we were sworn at by a female member of security staff, and when we asked for an apology by another member of the security team, she walked off swearing again, after denying swearing at us. No staff want to speak in English and what they do use is rude, and each member of staff we encountered bar one, put their hand up to stop the conversation. After travelling through many airports this one is by far the worse and staff need to be retrained in customer relations!!

I arrived in good time to check in at Orly airport. I was directed by a member of staff to Area 1, and to check in at No. 11 or 12, which I duly did. As I received my boarding pass without a boarding gate I enquired, at what Gate I was due to board at. I was advised it was D12, which I duly proceeded towards. On approach the gate I made further enquiries, conscious that I didnt speak French to ensure that all was in order, which I was reassured of. However, by the time I learnt I was at the wrong gate it was too late and I missed my flight! On arrival at the correct gate, I was advised as was another person who missed their flight due to prolonged checks at security, that an attendant from the airline would be with us shortly. However we were advised that the attendant was new, was stressed and had poor English. Not quite the sort of thing one want to hear while stressed after missing a flight. The attendant lead us for some time without appearing to know where she was going. Eventually she departed and advised to proceed some 150metres to meet with the Concierge! However on arrival it was a dead end. We didnt know whether to laugh or cry. We were eventually directed to an office by the airline. We didnt know whether to feel more sorry for the staff member or ourselves. Such carry on is a regular occurrence, we were informed. There was no member of management from the airline to speak with. There was no section within the airport to get a bit of sleep with a sense of security or safety. One of the worst ever, not even near a pass grade. Please take note management, airline and all concerned.

The check-in is chaotic and not safe in the manner it works. First they wanted to separate our Children from us (the little one just 4 yo). The corpulent security lady begun to shout instructions in French and was outraged, because we did not understood. Our items were separated in time and space following her orders. A small bag positioned as ordered by her on top of all our belongings, fell down, got into the conveyor belt. It was damaged and is just garbage now. The service personel noticed it, but just went on. Later they put this bag back on the belt to check it properly. To perform this they put the bag together with the baggage of another person, and we both had to explain what happened. To summarise: 1, Check- in took us like 30 minutes although there were just a few passengers 2, Items of different passengers were mixed together which gives the question of safety - it would be hard to explain if a bag with illegal goods some of the staff packed to my items is not mine. 3, Staff only able to scream commands in French (which later proved to be wrong due to the law of gravitation) should not work in an international airport or get in contact with customers that are also human beings.

Arrived in Paro airport at 1pm. There WERE 2 flights that had arrived. Immigration was quick and the staff were very polite. We got our bags and we left the airport in less than 15 minutes. For our departure, check in took 5 minutes and immigration another 5. The departure lounge is small but adequate. Lots of craft shops and a few places to eat. Very casual airport and the staff are very friendly. The cafe food was however awful but the coffee was nice. Wifi available but kept disconnecting. All in all a charming little airport for this stunning country.

Paro International Airport is located 2335 meter above sea level so flights can only fly in the morning. I took a Druk Air flight from Bangkok and the other time I took a flight from Kathmandu, I prefer flying from Kathmandu because I could see Himalayan Mountains if the weather permits. Paro Airport has very basic amenities because they have two carriers flying in and out. It replicated Bhutanese traditional architecture and it looked very beautiful as I was walking into the airport.

Leaving aside the airport which is impassable, the ground staff can be defined as one of the worst ever encountered. The only people who are not kind and who do not know how to work on the whole island. I highly recommend the ferry from Athens so as not to spoil your holiday.

First visit to this brand new airport that replaced the old one, the longer 1400m runway facilitates larger aircraft than the old airport, which is a good thing for tourism and the economy, and can expand even more. The problems are in the modest terminal that can facilitate current passenger volumes but is ridiculously small for a brand new airport. Will need significant expansion to facilitate any growth. Arrivals hall is literally a small room with two doors, one facing the road, the other facing airside. When passengers arrive from a flight, anyone can easily cross the (already open) automatic sliding doors from the road and reach the apron without any security barrier or officer monitoring. There is very little room for parking and after just one year of operation the benches in front of the terminal are already corroded.

Passenger wise India's 13th busiest airport but infrastructure wise one of the most smallest airport in India. When flight lands they don’t even provide bus to arrival’s but needs to walk from aircraft to terminal via on tarmac. Arrivals is very small, only 2 baggage belt in a limit spaces but baggage can take more time. Toilets are just ok, should be more clean. Prepaid cab and also uber have pick up point just after exit, no issues finding them, at the same time many taxi drivers will approach you offering ride. Airport needs proper management, new terminal is under construction and hope that it is better managed.

Terrible staff at the passport control! The woman was yelling at me and calling me names for no reason! So much for "the country of smiles". The area after passport control has no money exchange, so I have to take local currency home. Also there are a lot of flies in the airport and air conditioning is weak. I will never use this airport again and will think twice about visiting this country again.

Twice I’ve flown into U-Tapao airport now and twice had to face the longest immigration queue I’ve ever known bar MIA. Absolutely pathetic to have 5 staff manning the immigration when three flights have all landed at the same time. Over an hour into the queue and still nowhere close to getting through immigration. Had this been a one off, I wouldn’t have wrote this review, however as this is the second time I’ve faced the same immigration queue hell after both flights. I feel this needs highlighting. It’s pathetic and you’re made to feel no better than cattle. Sort this shambles out!

At last our local airport features nonstop rotations from Europe, operated by TUI UK, using B788 dreamliners, routes are : BHX, LGW & MAN. Unfortunately the embarking & disembarking passengers still get transported by bus to & from the plane. Let's hope that some more airlines will open up this airport to more intercontinental & domestic destinations. As for public transportation, very little has been done in that respect, due to some taxi/limo lobby wanting to draw the blanket to itself. There is however a manned booth of BH Rayong bus Co, alas the agent speaks no English and, discourages foreigners to travel on their buses, thus mostly Thai people know about this cheap transit system to : Rayong, Trat, Pattaya, Si Racha & Chonburi.

This is a tiny and very old terminal. There is a new domestic terminal next door. Walk 10 meters to check in desks and a further 20 to immigration control. The lounge looks onto the airfield and was partly full of very noisy Chinese tour groups. Once they left the few passengers to Doha were free to spread out and relax. A small kiosk sold packaged snacks and canned drinks. There was a small kiosk selling Thai Airforce caps and things - this is an army base. Quick bus transfer to plane. All in all a relaxing experience much preferable to either of the huge impersonable Bangkok airports. As a resident of Pattaya City only 35 minutes travel time. Really appreciate Qatar Airways opening services to this port.

Flight FD 204 with AirAsia from Singapore to Utapao, Thailand arrived on time. After leaving the plane was transferred by bus to the arrival hall. Then on to a line of about 180 passengers outside on the airfield in three rows in front of six immigration desks. Only four immigration officers of six possible were operating. Waiting time 90 minutes from 3.30 pm to 5 pm. No explanation, no excuse, only stupid announcements, nothing related to the chaos in front of the immigration desks. This airport is to avoid in any case.

I've flown in and out of Pau several times. It's a lovely airport with a pleasant "smallness" about it. The only downside for me is that from the UK it is only served by Ryanair. On principle I will no longer fly with them. If any other UK carrier starts using Pau I will happily fly there again.

Clean little province airport with efficient and friendly staff. The only drawback I can think of is the traffic jam on certain hours of the day when you try to join from downtown. One of the best small airport shops I've seen when it comes to local wine and edible goodies.

A lovely little airport. Ample parking right in front. I was happy because I could find a seat in the waiting area no small matter. Toulouse is closer to the area where we vacation but the trip (peage/major highway) makes travel easy and fast and the national and local roads are good too.

What a fantastic little airport - after leaving Paris CDG behind (and all its filth) it was such a welcome sight to arrive in a clean modern organized airport. What a shame that more airlines don't fly into Pau. The staff in the airport were also extremely helpful and polite. Much nicer airport than Toulouse which is not far away.

For an airport which only had 2 flights in and out on the days I travelled through it is amazing. It has a large waiting area shop and small cafeteria. The only down side is that you are made to queue between 2 glass walls while you wait to get to the plane. On the very sunny day I was there this became an oven even though we were only there for 10 minutes.

We were departing on a domestic flight and overall a positive experience. Check in at Malaysia Airlines was very quick. No queue at security. We used the Plaza Premium lounge which is OK, but nothing special. There are a couple of places to get refreshments and a few shops. What we were most impressed with was the boarding process, they had set up four separate lines for each boarding group, clearly signed and it worked, no scrum with everyone trying to board at the same time!

I am going back to my hometown. The airport staff broke my suitcase and asked me to give it to them for repair. After the repair, they asked me to come to the airport to get my suitcase back. Isn't this a waste of my time? They broke the suitcase and still waste my time. The staff's attitude is not good either. I am very disappointed!

I’m not sure which airport is worse, KLIA or Penang (which is classified as an International Airport) ! Malaysia have introduced a Malaysian Pass which is supposedly required to enter Malaysia. What a waste of time on the travellers part. After having issues downloading and finally doing so none of the Immigration officers even looked at it. After departing for Thailand and returning I didn’t even bother showing the downloaded pass and wasn’t asked for it. My friends I travelled with had the same experience. Penang Airport lacks everything, places to eat and rest before outward flights. As for KLIA it’s even worse.
Standing queue of 3 hrs with back problems. Very bad for tourism industry. This happened in KL in 2015, I thought Malaysia might have improved over the years

Staff were very helpful. Both of the officers help me get my phone which I lost in the airport. They managed to contact me to retrieve back my phone although I am already departed to my destination. Thank you so much!

Poor airport management. Immigration, baggage claim, luggage security check, signage all have outdated management and queues are long, customer and staff unsatisfied. I could easily improve the system by 10-20% by optimizing the service, in order that restaurants and shops receive more customers and businesses would be improved. I am surprised that this is not possible in 2024, learning from other airports how it works.

My boarding time was 10:35am and I was at the departure immigration gate at 10:20am. When I entered and saw the clearing immigration queue was so long I proceed to ask one of the female staff standing near my queue. She scolded so loud and ask why came so late and told me I am not supposed to ask her. She shouted to me asked me go ask one by one who are in front me. I am so surprised that an international airport have this kind of non quality staff which can stand at frontline to facing tourists. I admit I have my mistake as I am late but without listening to me or giving any solutions for tourist an airport staff attitude sure will bring down the image of the airport.

I was with my family as one of the last ones coming to the border check but by the time we got to the front of the queue, everyone had gone. Now we could have gone through with out doing the necessary security checks but we waited for someone to show up, which after searching for about 20 minutes we finally got someone to do the passport checks, only to be met by disdain and just a could not care attitude from the staff. Would not recommend this airport if you need to go to Malaysia.

Terrible immigration officers, there was no queue at all, and several officers were in the counter with lights flashed as “red”. No counters were in green and I was the first in line. I walk to the officer to ask if he can stamp my passport. He was frustrated and told me that I should wait till a counter turned green. I was already at the queue waiting for sometime.
Horrible! Waited 3 hrs+ to clear customs. Poorly organised and no one was their to take charge. Reflects badly on the airport and customs management. Will definitely not return to Penang anytime soon

Pensacola isn't a fancy airport, but it's fine, functional and beautiful. Even the exterior architecture greets travelers in a way that reminds them of the waves and big skies of Florida. This is also a better alternative, in my opinion, to flying out of other Gulf Coast airports such as Mobile, Tallahassee, and Gulfport/Biloxi. Pickup and drop-off are a breeze. Check-in is hassle-free. Security is a breeze, and even more so with TSA Pre-Check. Dining and shopping options aren't ample, but do get the job done nicely, remember, PNS is a small airport! Boarding the flight is easy. Pensacola is just a very modern, efficient airport, one that reminds me a lot of other smaller airports like Louisville (however, no small airports in this country set the world standard like Wellington and Christchurch, both in New Zealand, do).

Pensacola International is a terrific and convenient airport for the entire Emerald Coast/Pensacola Bay area. Flights are rarely delayed, airport staff are friendly, and the terminal is clean and easy to navigate. TSA lines are usually short, and there is absolutely no need to fear for safety, as the Pensacola Police Department, TSA, Escambia County Sheriff's Office, and United States Military Police (due to the extraordinary amount of military bases and armed forces personnel in the area) all patrol the airport and its grounds. Walking distance away from several hotels and recreation areas. Only about a 5 minute car or bus to Cordova Mall, and Sacred Heart Medical Center. As well as a ride to 10-15 minute car or bus ride to downtown, and a 20-30 minute ride to Pensacola Beach (depending on traffic on the Bay Bridge). Being a local to the area, I would also recommend taking the 40-45 minute ride to Navarre/Navarre Beach, which is usually quieter, with a healthy choice of restaurants and hotels, and still a relatively convenient distance to the airport.

I live in Fort Walton Beach and every time I need to fly out I drive over to Pensacola. I prefer Pensacola Airport over Eglin AFB because of the wide selection of flights (Over 90 a day!) and more non-stop destinations (15 at PNS vs 5 at VPS) and not to mention the lower fares! It's worth the drive every time.

The airport is new and clean, however it is already overstretched. For departures, there are only a couple of snack bars and small shops in the departure area, and for an international departure, there's only one cafe. Although your plane may be parked at a jetbridge, you may not board from the jetbridge, but rather have to go outside and use stairs. Alternatively, you may board at gate 4, but then walk in the arrival corridor to the jetbridge at gate 2. Check in and security were easy and fast. At arrivals, the tourist information office was closed. There is no area for rental car return - you will have to go in to the building to tell them you have returned. Signage on the roads to the airport is not very good, and it is tricky to reach the airport from any direction other than downtown. There is construction at the airport entrance and perhaps that will address this issue. The airport makes a good arrival spot for the Eje Cafetero. Arriving with Easy Fly our bags arrived almost instantly.

I would not advise anyone to use this airport as there is no shuttle bus to the train station. If you are in any way feeble or have young children I would advise you to get a taxi as the no 7 bus that services the airport stops in the middle of Perpignan and it's a 15 minute walk to the station carrying luggage. The taxis are like vultures waiting to overcharge you. €25 for a few miles. Maybe try hiring a car but here again the weekly charge for a modest car is overpriced.

Inside the terminal was fine but outside appearances were unkempt and lots of the concrete surfaces - kerbside and actual walking surfaces were unsafe if not dangerous. Bushes and other attempted adornments neglected. Even the car parks looked dis-organised. The check-in facilities were opened too early and closed too soon. This inconvenienced and upset four of my fellow passengers. This was the fault of the young female administration staff who need better training and courtesy. The elderly male security staff are too severe giving the impression that you are entering/leaving a third world former communist country. Totally unnecessary to treat fellow EU citizens in such a manner. In conclusion this is not an Airport but a Aerodrome. I shall revert to using other airports in the region.

There is no shuttle bus anymore. Connection to the town is by scheduled bus #7 which is much more reliable. The shuttle to town frequently left before the flight so you had to get a taxi. The departure lounge contains a shop selling local goods at 'special' prices. The prices are about three times what you'd pay for the same elsewhere. Likewise coffee at the coffee bar is more expensive than anywhere else. Service is of the usual surly type. I have on occasion rented a car from Avis here and being a preferred customer was told I would have speedy service with no forms to fill in. This was not the case - there was endless form filling to be done. Note also that although your flight may arrive early it won't do you any good if you have a hire car to pick up. Whatever time the plane gets in the hire car form filler turns up some minutes after the scheduled arrival time so you don't get away any quicker than you would have done otherwise. Downstairs the public toilets are clean but the cubicles are of such microscopic dimensions that it's almost impossible to get in whilst in possession of a piece of luggage and neither me nor my luggage are particularly large. Leaving is one of the few pleasures here. The security people are relaxed and sometimes even polite when they forget themselves. Presumably this is because they're glad to see the back of you.

Never travel to Perpignan on a Sunday if you can help it. There is only one bus no 7 which goes about twice a day from the airport and shuttle buses which used to take you to Perpignan station no longer run at the moment (I travelled in June 2012). You would have to check on this but they were not running when we were in Perpignan. Be careful with taxis they run on a meter and are quite expensive. We paid over 100 euros to get to Collioures about half an hour drive we shared the cost with two other people who were going the same way. During the week buses are much more frequent and perhaps the shuttle buses work during the peak season. It would be easier to fly to Carcasonne transport seems to be better from there.

A tiny regional airport but conveniently located. Due to prevailing northwesterly winds final approach is usually quite bumpy. Baggage claim is very quick. A shuttle bus awaits each incoming regular flight - travel to the city centre takes 20 mins and costs €4.50 one-way. The same bus leaves Perpignan roughly one hour prior to each departing flight. Check-in is hassle- free. ID check takes place upon boarding but also at the security check. Do not go airside too early as the small boarding area has few seats frosted glazing and no toilets at all!

A sweet little airport and very fast getting checked in and through security. A bit peeved that there were no facilities in the departure lounge and windows were frosted. Suggest you leave it as long as possible before going through to this lounge. I arrived in Perpignan at the bus station where I found a shuttle time table (2 that day). Plenty of time and I ended up at the railway station where there was no sign of a timetable. Found the 'Navette' stop but a bit worried hen departure time arrived and I was the only when there and no bus. Then noticed it across the road and I was the only passenger!

I commute regularly between Perpignan and Manchester and it is my favourite airport.It only has one cafe and one shop but these are conveniently situated and adequate for the number of people there. I can walk 10 yards to check in there are rarely any queues and there is no need to rush through security. The place is small but that's its charm no hassle no long walks and friendly and helpful staff. To fly from most airports you need to allow a good two hours to get from a drop-off point to check in and then to a gate. In Perpignan 40 minutes suffices.
Shuttle bus to town only runs to coincide with plane arrivals. If you miss it be ready to fork out for a taxi as it may be some hours before another plane comes in.

Very small provincial airport close to town but out in the scrub. Not a bad airport when arriving plenty of taxis but departing is pretty grim. Facilities limited to one small cafe bar and one small newsagents shop plus vending machines. There are very few seats. The facilities after passing through the baggage security checks are practically zero - fewer seats and not even any toilets plus all the glazing is frosted - you don't even have a view! I have experienced airports in many third world countries in Africa India and the Caribbean but departing from this airport is not enjoyable.

Awful toilet situation (one single gents’ cubicle with no water in the tap; one single female cubicle that was out of order; a parents’ room with no toilet) - serving 4 gates (gates 50-54) and surrounding cafe and shops! Woefully inadequate. Furthermore: it was raining outside and we saw luggage for Gate 55 uncovered in the rain on the tarmac waiting a long time to be loaded. Surely it’s not right for passenger luggage to be soaking wet before being loaded on flights. Otherwise the airport is modern and works fairly efficiently.

The operators need to be embarrassed. Absolute shambles. Conveyors not working. Delays delays. Ridiculous boarding process. Facilities broken and filthy. Charging Power points with no power. Plugs lying on the follow not plugged in.

We travelled overseas and was returning from Philippines. We are residents here! We are law abiding citizens and the way that the arrogance is flaunted in our face when providing our passport and coming thru immigration is nothing short of disgusting behaviour! This behaviour needs to be culled!

1) need to vet the security screening personnel, very rude and abrupt. Cannot understand what some are saying 2) can only use a card in the international departures. And to top it off they then hit you with a card fee for purchases and on public holidays throw a hefty surcharge on top of the bill. 3) went to JB Hifi duty free and bought a JBL speaker, check on internet and the price was $15 dearer than Myer normal price. Management and the government should be aware that Perth Airport is the first and last place international tourists see of our country and from what I hear overseas I. My regular trips is that the reviews are not that good

My biggest complaint is the actual building design. I cannot believe how poor the design is, whoever the architect was they had no foresight to the future. How can you build an airport when arriving and departing passengers are exposed to the weather, particularly in winter. If you are being dropped off or picked up you have no protection from the elements, if it is raining you will get wet entering or leaving the drop off points or trying to get or being dropped off. It is an unbelievably poor design. The whole building needs demolishing and a 2 story building built, the upper level for departing passengers and the ground level for arrivals, whilst all under cover for pick up and drop off points. The car park should be a under cover multi story. It is time Perth Airport actually built a modern and feasable airport that will look to the future, not just the next 5 years. Wake up Perth.

Again, very long lines and delays due to the inefficient way passengers are jockeyed through border control. Seems that there are never enough staff working. Was told by one member of staff that I didn't have to remove my belt and watch, only to be re scanned for the same thing by another staff member not even five metres away. Scanned for explosives AGAIN, even though I work for an airline! They claim that they don't profile, but they must do. I want to formalise a complaint, but not possible to find out who is in charge.

The worst airport especially the security screening through the virgin domestic terminal. Staff are rude, arrogant and are on a power trip that is totally over the top making for a miserable experience. I wear a sunflower pin which is globally recognised except in Perth where they seem to think it gives them carte blanche to cause you as much upset as possible asking your medical condition which they should not do. Not wishing to go through the body scanner due to the health risk of being microwaved but being willing to endure a pat down requested politely saw their behaviour be very aggressive and threatening to prevent my partner from flying. They appeared to enjoy seeing the distress that it was causing me. You don't get treated like this on a bus or train in fact the train from Melbourne to Sydney is an example of great customer service at a reasonable price with decent food also sensibly priced. Sadly flying is pretty much to only way to get anywhere when leaving Perth as if there was an alternative we would take it. As for the rest of the airport - the food is crazy price and poor quality.

I have had a few pretty poor experiences but my latest one this morning kinda tops the rest. Due to a mix between drop off queuing, airport security and Qantas tomfoolery I managed to miss a flight. I left home this morning at 0357 for my 0515 flight to Karratha. The average travel time to and from the Airport is usually around the area of 45 minutes. I arrived to the drop off queue for my 0515 flight at 0442 this morning leaving me 13 minutes to do the above things and arrive at my boarding terminal for boarding at 0455. No bags to check in so in "theory" plenty of time. Queuing several flights causes huge waves of congestion particularly around 6AM/9AM and 4PM/7PM. I was expecting that my earlier flight may have missed that window but I was wrong. Managed through the queue departing the car at 0446, dashed for airport screening and managed to get through to the scanners relatively fast as they where hurrying people through that had flights boarding soon. The queue, de-bagging myself and body screening probably took about 3 minutes. Upon scanning my bag they identified a grease coupler fitting, due to the fact that the the fitting while clearly viable due to the clear plastic was still in the clearly labelled original packaging. The identity and use of such a tool eluded the security staff, and required a manager to inspect it. The screening procedure, checking 3 other peoples baggage took 14 minutes.  I dashed up the escalator and made the short trip to gate 8. All in all about a minute from the scanners, I checked my phone to bring up my boarding pass and noticed I missed a alert from Qantas that boarding had began early. 2 minutes early. I arrived at 0505, 10 minutes after boarding was supposed to start. Yet they closed the gates 1 minute prior as they "only allow 12 minutes for boarding." I was both somehow two minutes spare and two minutes short to board my flight to Karratha this morning. Qantas was unable to change my flight to either of the couple that would leave leave this morning. Also quick review about the Terminal, Parking is expensive, the stuff in the "mall" is expensive, airport screening staff is an acronym and it's self describing of their competence), the pick up and drop off needs far more work not just overpriced boom-gates if it takes longer than 6 minutes to get around and public transport needs work, takes almost 3 hours for me to bus and train to from my home.

Things just go from bad to worse at this airport, mostly by border force and security services. I intend to make a written complaint to Border Force after I have completed this review. They state that they do not do profiling but every time I have departed this airport, I have been pulled aside and checked for explosives.  For reference, I've never had a run in with the law, I'm a 57 year old IT Professional currently working IN aviation. So why do I keep getting pulled aside? Somebody this morning tried to tell me it was coincidence. This morning's arrival back to Perth was even worse. After checking in to the airport electronically with my passport, I was asked about explosives etc, even asked about my passport and who provided my ticket.

It starts with the T1/T2/T3/T4 roulette - international except qantas domestic, domestic except qantas, does your head in; badly-signed roundabouts etc. Long term parking and bus seems logical though. Self-check-in - nobody around to assist, most people struggling with the bag tag sticker puzzle, some people just not familiar with the system, but a human would be just the thing to ease that confusion, or so you'd think. No bins for the label backing strip. So zero points there Perth. Bag drop - one man in hi-vis, looking blankly at a screen while sitting on a stool, ignoring the elderly ladies trying to work out where to drop and how to lift their cases onto the conveyor. They had sent one of their number to seek help elsewhere. I helped them in the end. I called out in frustration to the empty void where people could be that some human help would be appreciated and that whoever worked there was a lazy dog. Surprisingly, a woman soon sauntered out with as much enthusiasm as one. Hi-vis guy was totally ignorant. The bag drop pass reader that shows "scan here" on the left while the scanner itself is on the right. When I asked the hi-vis guy for help with this he was annoyed and not helpful, "Read the sign" and stormed back to his stool. Zero points here again. Gate 53 bar cafe Haymark. Staffed by three people having a yarn on the cafe side where there were no customers, while two people waited at the bar. One of the three staff came thru and saw the bar customers, said nothing, turned around and went back to the cafe side. Same guy came thru to the bar side again a few minutes later and didn't say anything until my lady asked him to serve her. "Oh" he said, "I thought you were being served"! By whom I wonder, as his two colleagues were still next door. Perth airport has no drink bottle refill stations after security. There is a drink tap designed for slurping from, hidden around in the toilet lobby, with more poor signage. So to refill a bottle you are blocking access to the toilets, as well as having to half fill a second container and pour that into your bottle. Auckland and Queenstown airports both had multiple, well-signed drink bottle refill stations. Absolutely the worst experience, I'm a regular Perth airport user since i live there, and that was the one that broke the camel's back. Shit all the way. Only gets a 1/10 because I can't leave the slider at zero. 30th December 2023, QF176, 7pm departure.

I fly in and out of Philadelphia International Airport twice a week from Terminals B and C, and I have nothing to complain about. The layout is well-designed, making navigation easy, and there are plenty of food and shopping options. Security lines are usually efficient, and the overall experience is smooth. As a frequent traveler, I know what bad airports look like, and PHL is definitely not one of them. It’s a great airport that provides a convenient and pleasant journey every time.

Bathrooms were closed at a peak time (6:30 pm) with 20 people in line. When they did open, they were dirty, several doors did not lock and there were no paper towels and the dryers were broken. The phone charging stations had limited usage/availability meaning they were not working. There was food caked in the carpet at the E gate and the chairs were worn and dirty.

I found Philadelphia International Airport very confusing to navigate. Fortunately, we had requested wheelchair assistance for my mum who has limited mobility. The guy Cordell who helped us was friendly, approachable and kind which made our experience so much more pleasant!

I was subjected to a very intimate search three times by two different TSA agents. The scanner was obviously malfunctioning. How do I know? Well, I was clean but it kept saying I wasn't.  Then, walking on the tarmac to the plane, a baggage handler insisted that I had to "valet" my carry-on bag. Once inside, seeing the mostly empty luggage bays, I complained to the flight attendant. She went and brought the bag to me with apologies Arrival was okay, but the I had to follow a "bread crumb" trail of corridor, stairs and turns -- all with inadequate signage. Eventually I arrived at two luggage bays and was (at first) relieved to see my flight posted as "unloading." But it turned out that we did not get our luggage in hand for 1hr 50mins. No information from the uncommunicative employee in the Baggage Office. She said they were trying to find the agent to "see if he has any more bags." (I'm being generous here). She told me to scan a lost baggage claim code -- which did not work.

They play non stop super LOUD ads at the gates while you wait. That with the combination of fluorescent lights, It creates the absolute worst atmosphere that you can imagine. There’s no peace or calm between flights while you wait.

I have been waiting in terminal b gate b8 since 4pm 8/19/24 for a flight which has been delayed 4 times and by 7 and 1/2 hrs. No information given over the speakers as to any changes. We have to constantly check the app. No airline attendants at the gate at all to ask any questions. (This is for aa flight 437). The lounge air was freezing and people were not prepared for that. Also the food areas that the airport offers in this section have no prices in the menu and he. You look it up online who the heck is paying $25 for a burger. Not even in London airports are they that expensive. And the cleanliness of the gate was atrocious. No one came by to clean up the trash all over the floor. It just seems like the airport did not care enough to provide good customer service. And the airline was a joke in giving us current information over the speaker system. I am rating this a 2/10 and that is generous!

Over an hour wait for a gate. Seems like it happens every time. Apart from the wait - the condition of the public restrooms and general cleanliness is embarrassing. The Philly airport aligns with Philly’s nickname - Filthadelpehia - why can’t we be better than this? Ideas - larger bathroom stalls so an individual traveling by their self can enter with their luggage? Warm water and soap to wash hands. Sensors that actually work and stay on while you are washing. Better coordination of empty gates. Clean more frequently. Power wash the exterior - gum and cigarette butts everywhere - yuck Ban smoking within 200 yards of the terminal Plant flowers

Specifically Terminal C: ladies rooms were filthy dirty and smelled terribly. Gate lounges were dirty and no trash picked up. Quick food place by gate 19 had gross looking sandwiches behind case, husband saw worker touch garbage then pick up slices of ham without washing his hands. Workers, including stores, restaurants, airline workers had bad attitudes, some not even acknowledging you spoke to them or asked a question of them. I have honestly never seen such deplorable conditions at an airport, hope basic manners and cleanliness return soon.

My first impression of this airport was the huge queue for passport control. I counted three desks open for hundreds of arriving passengers, it took around an hour to get to the front where I was greeted by a surly immigration officer. No smile, no "hello", just barking demands. Once I was through that I needed to change terminal to get my connection to Knoxville, which led to another problem, a distinct lack of signs. Eventually I found the shuttle bus and proceeded to security where a female employee was screaming, actually screaming at passengers. I overheard another employee ask her to dial it down but she ignored him and continued the screaming. Brilliant. Eventually made it to my gate only to find there was a distinct lack of seating, with people standing here there and everywhere. On my return trip I was heading to LHR on an AA 787, and was shocked at how few seats there were at the gate. Overall, it's a big airport with the staffing levels and seating provision of a small airport which also assumes passengers know the airport inside out and don't need signs to get where they need to be.

Me and my son arrived from Doha via American airlines on April 20, 2024 at 2:55 pm. We had a connecting flight Air Canada same day at 4.35PM. We had to pick up our bags and go thru security check again. They sent us thru a second Agriculture security check. We begged them that we are Canadian citizens but they would not allow us to bypass the queue for inspection of bags. We missed our onwards flight. We dropped of our bags after security and bags left for Toronto on April 20 and we were left behind. We check into a hotel as there was no night flight, bought new American Airlines tickets and left on April 21 at 8.35am.We lost $1600 for no fault of ours. Worst airport, worst service and very rude staff. Avoid this airport if you can,

Very modest airport that clearly cannot handle a high volume of flights. Check in is very modest and slow and people speak very basic English. Undoubtedly, we are facing a country that urgently needs tourism and foreign funds to improve the quality of its infrastructure. Fortunately, the new international airport in Phnom Penh will open in a few years and I hope they will be able to guarantee the cleanliness of the space, a better quality of service, increase the number of places where you can sit and also the spaces before boarding.

To say this airport is disastrous is a major understatement. Staff are the most incompetent people I’ve had to interact with at any airport. They are lazy, moody and rude and they spent more time on their phones scrolling through tiktok than trying to help me check in. It is also excruciatingly difficult to have a quick and easy check on when none of the staff speak more than 10 words of English and they blatantly ignore you. There was 1 tall lanky man in a grey suit working for Vietnam Airlines who came right up close to me and coughed on me with no mask on and proceeded to push my trolley with my bags away. He is just one of the pivotal reasons why I hated my experience at this airport.

We came on a domestic flight, everything was fast including getting our big check in bag. We should only stay 24 hours in the city, so we wanted to store the big bag in the airport, but 'sorry sir, we are renovating that area, no lockers!' Outside the wolfs are waiting, ready to help you with a taxi to town for 15 usd. There are busses going to town, but three different routes, so you need to know up front, which one. We read that they have train service also, but when you ask outside, they just shake their heads. We booked a grab tuktuk for 3.5 usd. Completely ok, if you only have one big bag.

Upon my departure from Phnom Penh International Airport, I was turned away from the transfer point and required to pay a $30 a tourist visa entry fee for a 4 hour layover while flying from Vietnam to catch my international departure flight from Cambodia. A waiver was not considered even with documentation supporting ongoing travel. The process of application requires a cash payment and is terribly inefficient. Additionally most vendors refuse to accept credit card payment in the arrival terminal. If you are considering travel to and from south east Asia, I would avoid Cambodia as an entry and departure point.

Airport is brand new after going through modern reconstruction. Airport surrounding has also gone through a modern reconstruction. Signage was seen throughout the airport, passport control and security is upstairs, accessed through an escalator. Pens used to fill out a departure form, were running out with no other pens in the surrounding area. Passport control was quick and so was security (despite there being a long line, it soon disappeared). Couple of food shops, Chinese dim sum, Khmer etc. Overall, the airport has been refitted to a modern state, gates, shops etc, were new and staff were friendly.

Nice airport. Fairly modern. The washrooms were clean and well maintained. It’s a fairly small airport. There seemed to be a lot of security around the day we departed. Airside international there is not much choice of food, however I noticed across the road seemed to be popular with locals. There was a coffee shop, ouch $5 for an iced coffee, also some food there, very expensive. Going through security etc you go upstairs via escalator. The oddest sight, all booths open for both security and immigration yet we were the only ones there. First time that’s ever happened and I suspect last. There were a few places to eat or drink airside and they seemed ok although we were not hungry. Definitely liked this airport. A very positive experience.

Absolute incompetence from security. Overweight and undertrained "passport control" waved me to back of the queue to answer personal call. Seems to take three individuals to do the work of one person. Airport management need to seriously evaluate this part of the airport staff, both in training and general intelligence. Top marks for Cathay Pacific check in and the friendly and helpful duty free staff. Pleasant and clean terminal and good facilities otherwise but prices are ridiculously high in some places.

In November, Phnom Penh air travelers started using a spacious new terminal equipped with 50 percent more check-in counters than now, twice as many immigration counters, and three times as many X-ray machines for carry-on bags. In Cambodia’s largest airport expansion ($100 mil) in a generation, the new airport terminal will seem like an upscale shopping mall. There is a large food court, twice as much floor space for duty free, and a host of new food and beverage vendors never seen that far west on Russian Boulevard. Last week the VIP and Premium lounges opened and are as good as any in a terminal this size. It all looks very clean and organized though I have yet to see the new terminal when there are great numbers of people arriving or departing.

Ground service is not very good, except the fact that the process is slow because of the small space. Soon it will be okay after the terminal expansion. The waiting room is good as it has some restaurants and some entertainment. However, I would suggest that they have more stores, especially conveniences stores or more duty-free stores.

Phnom Penh airport is a small airport, albeit there is construction to make it bigger. The departure hall can be crowded with limited seating. As one can walk in and out of the building with virtually no security checks, it can be easier to walk over to the arrivals area if one has to wait a longer time. There it is much quieter and there are a few restaurants. Prices here are (much) higher then in town. The airport is located only a few hundred meters from the main road from Phnom Penh to Sihanoukville. It is therefore possible to get off a bus from Sihanoukville right at the airport. The airside is somewhat bigger with enough seating and some electrical outlets too. There are a few places for food and drinks. There is also a smoking room and obviously toilets. On arrival, one has to pass the visa on arrival circus which all in all works pretty smooth but you will spend some 15 minutes there. Getting a taxi is also pretty organised as you buy a voucher for transport to the city. It does help if you know where you are going because these taxi drivers did not pass any Knowledge.

This is the worst airport I have ever traveled in the world. When you are in terminal 4 there are no signs to get to the sky traxs to terminal 3. I must have had to stop to ask 10 people only four knew how to get there. Most of the people were very rude. Also with having CLEAR they put us in regular TSA security lines

Encountered 3 very rude staff. Terminal 3 is confusing and disorganized. When asked for directions was spoken to disrespectfully twice. The layout so very odd and the signs are confusing, things are not where the signs indicate. The restroom by Egates was not kept up, out of paper towels.

Forgot my identification. TSA usually gets a bad rap, but I'm here to tell you they were awesome today. I was taken to the side where an alternate route of id verification was sought. I was treated promptly and with the utmost in professionalism. Thanks TSA - I made my flight.

Phoenix is the easiest of all major US airport to get in and out of. I picked Phoenix as my home based in part because I needed a reliable airport considering how often I fly and PHX does not disappoint. The new terminal 3 is really excellent and the improved lounge situation at Terminal 4 is really appreciated.

Easily the worst airport I have ever traveled through. To transfer from one US flight to another flight wholly in the US you have to reclear TSA. They don't have free wifi, Anchorage Alaska can manage free wifi WTF Phoenix. The airport is so spread out and disconnected forget getting something from another terminal.

"America's Friendliest Airport" is false advertisement. Phoenix Sky Harbor is anything but and fails to live up to its false moniker. From baggage claim, it is impossible to find the Rental Car Center on your own because the signage for such could not be found. At 10:30 PM, I could find no airport personnel to help and an airline employee whom I was able to find seemed genuinely annoyed and displeased that I was asking him for assistance. Upon my return, the rental car return was extremely confusing and nobody from the rental car agency could be found to assist me. I just dropped my car and prayed that I had left it in the right spot and wouldn't incur any additional charges. Once I arrived at my terminal from the Sky Train, signage initially directed me to ticketing and check-in, but then the signage abruptly stopped when I reached the escalators and a four-way intersection. I looked all over and there was no more signage to tell me where to go. Another passenger saw my confusion and directed me where to go. Once I received directions, I looked for additional signage in the direction I was sent, and could find none.

I truly believe that the woman at Passport Control saved my life on Thursday, July 20, 2023. After being the last to disembark from a British Airways flight from London, I mustered up what little strength I had as I approached Passport Control. The woman at the entrance to Passport Control took one look at me and said, "You are having a medical emergency. Come with me to the wheelchair line." She whisked me to the front of that line and waited for the EMT staff to wait on me. I was taken to the Banner Medical Center via ambulance where we discovered I had an acute case of Pulmonary Embolism. I was going to try to push through my final flight to Tucson and get tomy home city. Had she not recognized the acute state of emergency I was in and taken me to get care, I may well have died. I will never forget her.
One of the worst airports I’ve been to. Surly employees, no bars only cheap food in overpriced chain style beer pubs or family grab and go’s. And not one place to get a drink in Terminal 3.
Terminal 3 restroom across from gate 6 was filthy and there wasn’t any paper towels to dry your hands. Half the restaurants were closed, not enough choices although it was only 6:30pm.

Phoenix Sky Harbor is not set up up to accommodate people with injuries or disabilities. I flew in and out of there in January and February with an injury and had bad experiences. In January I had to walk long ways to get from rental car return to Sky Train and then waited 40 minutes for wheelchair assistance. In February walked long distances again. There needs to be assistance provided from rental cars to airline ticket desk.

I went there and they did only not notify about my flight being canceled, but when I got there they told me that my flight was moved to the Phoenix Sky Harbor Airport. First things first, Allegiant does not fly out of Sky Harbor and I found that out the hard way. I went back into the Mesa airport and yelled out hello very loudly. A lady came out and said she's new and In training as well as the other guy I spoke to. I ended up coming from Tucson Arizona. So I ended up traveling well over 250 miles and all they had to say was sorry we are "Under Staffed". I could care less what's going on. Do your homework and job instead of making excuses and lies for something you know nothing about! I asked for a Hotel and shuttle for the inconvenience and they also said it's out of our control and this happens sometimes. Very unpleasant experience. Absolute disregard and care for customers.

It has everything you need for a small convenient airport. One of my carry on bags flew off the top of my Jeep on the way to the airport, I found a nice selection of ones to replace it in the shop and the food in the restaurant was very good, all the service there was great. I had my service dog, the security was educated on what documents was needed to prove he was a real service dog. The added bonus was they have a small Pet rest area. What a gem, instead of fighting all the Skyharbor hubbub.

Smooth arrival (domestic) in the new airport. It is the only airport that I have arrived at that there is actually free onwards buses (to most of the tourist resorts north of the airport)- about every five minutes. I did not know about this free service but if passengers have lots of luggage they need to be mindful that it could be a long haul from the bus stop in their resort to their actual hotel. I took a taxi from one of the three or four tax agencies outside arrivals - they were actually half the price of taxi-hailing apps! There were some nice airy restaurants in the arrival area and presumably these are available to departing passengers. Five stars from me.

The airport was small and has very basic amenities. But the worst thing is the rude staff, from checkin counter staff who work very slowly, to security check who are extremely rude, lack professionalism and give unclear instructions. Be careful with pickpockets and loud crowds.
Small, but modern and well equipped airport. Check in and security check are fast. There are some stores and food shops also. Clean and well . Minor point is no free wifi provided

Travelling there in April was awful. It is brand new but loads of problems. 1) Upon arrival it took two hours to get through visa control. 2) Leaving it took two hours to check in. 3) Four coffees in departures US$25. Hardly anything to buy - no tobacco and spirits more than in the UK!

Very limited F&B selections and the food is pricy and charged at USD between $10 to $20. Would recommend taking your meal before going to the airport or order in-flight meals. All other parts are fine.

Phu Quoc Airport was built and completed in 2012 which was one of the newest international airports of Vietnam. The queuing times were not too long and the terminal signs were easy to follow. However, there were only some seats in the waiting room. The wifi connection did not work.

New airport building with good facilities. Minimal airport food facilities and retail outlets other than jewellery. Good facilities for vehicles to pick up at ground level and drop off at first floor level. Excellent toilet facilities and very clean throughout with good air conditioning. Construction of second runway in progress together with airport buildings to cater for expected increase in tourism. Downside was that there was no wifi facilities other than those offered by fast food franchises.

Very disappointing experience at Phuket Airport. Our flight was delayed with barely any updates or explanations.  The airport was overcrowded, chaotic, and poorly managed. Security clearance was disorganized and stressful. At one point, we were kept on the shuttle bus for almost an hour with no communication at all — it felt like no one knew what was going on. Overall, the experience was frustrating. Phuket is a beautiful destination, but the airport needs serious improvements in both service and infrastructure.

Almost every very store in the airport I purchased souvenirs, was a very unpleasant experience. No one smiles, they are talking to you like you are a criminal. No explanations, no thank you. They all stand behind the counter like soldiers with uniform and their heads covered. Very unpleasant experience. We were group of 6 friends, we simply stop shopping after going through 4-5 different stores. Bad business. I would change the system or management to make the experiance more pleasant and exciting for tourist.

Phuket airport was one of the most horrendous experiences. I was travelling with my 2 year old daughter for a holiday. The security checking officers were extremely rude. At one point the lady pushed and shoved my 2 year old when doing a body scan. She didnt even let me hold her. If there was a way to formally complain against her and an accompanying male staff i would. Will not want to travel to Phuket again!

Extremely rude staff at passport and boarding pass entry before hand luggage security especially to Indian travellers at approximately 1pm not letting them through the queue with evidence of their flight boarding telling them to get to the back of the queue, I let them in in front of me as I have been delayed myself and been late for flights. Horribly screaming at everyone to get their passports out, totally unnecessary and unacceptable. The duty free shop staff at gate 15, were standing about not helping customers, I asked where the Samsong would be and they casually pointed to the whisky section, they must have seen me frantically searching before boarding but just stood there. I asked a young man and he told me they didn’t stock it, thankfully he was very helpful and apologised for the women’s attitude. The staff in general in all the shops didn’t seem to care about being helpful or interested in doing their job.

Terrible airport. The aircon didn’t seem to be working so it was really hot. Even the staff in the shops were sweating. Not nice when waiting to depart for 2hrs. Also, the notification system/alerts from airport staff to passengers is terrible. You cannot hear anything the announcer says. I’d definitely suggest having their mouth slightly further away from the microphone but also turning the volume up!

Being greeted by rude staff especially one lady out of the plane being told I have a power bank with me. I looked at her confused and explained I don't have a power bank. We walked down and I had to open all my bags. Once I showed them that the power bank was not a power bank but an external hard drive. The one guy just grabbed 2 of my collectable Zippo's! The same rude  lady gave me this paper and said sign. I said no. Sign for what. She replied sign for lighter. I explained that it's a Zippo and not a lighter. No pressured gas. I've emptied all Zippos with no flint. No fluid nothing and it's impossible to cause any danger. She continued sign.  I know that lighters and power banks are not allowed as it's not my first rodeo. Once again very disappointed as the staff couldn't even explain and show me what they where doing. It's like stealing from people. Very disappointed.

We arrived at the airport 14.01.23 at 13.30. We had a shock from the work of the yellow taxi service . One service worker took the money very quickly, she promised a taxi in 15 min, we waited 1 hour, the women didn't answer questions, she was rude, then refused to provide a taxi at all and refused to give her name, no badge. This attitude is unacceptable. Airport is not her private service.

Great experience at arrival. Very friendly staff welcoming all the way. Quick check of Thailand Pass with no waiting time, as smooth through immigration. The bags already on belt when we came to arrival hall.

I had a shock when I landed in Phuket Airport. Was looking so much forward for this trip, but started not the best way. Just for having the Italian passport, but living in London for 4 years and haven’t been back home in Italy for over 2 months, I’ve been so much discriminated and treated badly. I haven’t been given the chance either to explain, some policemen came shouting at me and so rude attitude. They didn’t wanted to let me talk or explain something, then after being taken to the medical center for check up like being told "we don’t care what you want to say or where you live, this is because you have Italian passport”. Our country never treat Asian citizens this way. The police men used bad words toward me, shouting and so much attitude, I haven’t seen never in my life. Security staff very rude, using loud tone while speaking. Still in shock. This is not the correct behavior.

Phuket Airport is purely money minded, no one is helpful infact they are very rude. They ask for money for direct immigration, one policemen said give me 200 baht I will give you a direct and quicker immigration. I will never suggest anyone to go from Phuket International Airport. One policemen used bad words towards us as we did not have sufficient money in our pocket, it was in our luggage. Later we converted INR into Thai Baht, this is not the way to treat tourists.

A ghastly customer service experience. I lost my passport at the airport. I attribute this in part to the endless bureauocratic nonsense at this airport. Everyone here is on a mini power trip where the greatest pleasure is taken in saying things like, "Ma'am, please stand behind the line" or "You missed question 47 on the immigration form" Totally uninformed, lacking manners and quite pathetic really. I took my passport out a total of five times. I am quite sure that the incidence of lost passports occurs regularly. They need to streamline their operation, cut out about 15 meaningless steps and place their focus putting the customer first. They are a long way off from this in my opinion.

At other airports in the world duty free alcohol is a set price and every merchant is mandated to sell at the same set price. Not so in Trinidad. After purchasing duty free alcohol on the lower level, passengers are directed upstairs for security check and access to the gate area. In the upper level, other duty free merchants are selling alcohol at lower prices than downstairs. At this point I have already gone through security and cannot return downstairs. Some price are significant lower. A real disappointing experience and feeling of being ripped off.

In transit gate closed. Passengers made to queue up standing for more than 30 minutes. Even business class passengers not spared. Callous answers. Made to undergo baggage check again in the restricted transit area - a new security procedure never seen in any other airport. The security check involved belt, shoe removal etc even you are in a hurry to catch your next flight. The security personnel are robotic. No one takes responsibility for customer complaints. Caribbean airlines is world-class but not the airport. One is advised to avoid this airport even if it is expensive to try another route.

Arrival: the immigration staff are very rude, unprofessional, uneducated, self-centered, unmannerly, ignorant and just plain lazy. Getting through immigration has always been a terrible experience when visiting Trinidad. Piarco immigration approach is always hostile and abrupt. They do not want you to talk, and when you do talk they always cut you off. So rude and frustrating. The worst airport immigration team I have encountered in my years of traveling to many other countries. Departure: Can someone please explain the reason for airport security going through your bags and patting you down after your bags have gone through a scanner and you have walked through a metal detector? They randomly call your name and have you stand in front of all the passengers while they conduct this search again. Is security not competent enough or just plain insecure or being extra cautious? We will never know! Because if you ask any question to the security personnel, they either ignore you or give you senseless answer.

I found the airport, world class standard, But immigration officers, ground staff, even the airline personnel I Travelled on United airlines seem to hate everybody, Immigration seem to think they are doing us a favour by simply stamping our passport. Don't even try to ask any questions. You have some gruff answers like, "I asked the questions, you don't". The airline employees were even worst, they closed out the flight an hour early, told me I was late, and I would to wait till the morning. I had to wait, no choice. I Will give the thumbs up to workers in the restaurant, they were all welcoming, kind and treated me with respect. I have travelled to at least 16 different countries, and was never treated as badly the Trinidadians. This the country of my birth So it pains me even write this.

This airport is clean and seemingly well managed. My complaints is your immigration officer I was travelling with my niece, The officer seem to take a real dislike to my niece, She ask for the phone number of the person I was staying with, I pulled my phone out to get the number, she screamed at me to get off the phone said I was putting her life in danger. Now tell me how in the hell was I doing that? Please do some training on your people I have travelled quite a bit, and Trinidad immigration is the worst.

I would have to say as a flight attendant with a major airline the security system at Piarco airport is beyond horrible. This is not my first encounter at this airport with security (AATT), also my fellow colleagues have experienced/witness this unpleasant behavior leaving from this airport. Something has to be done with the manner the security speak to pax! I understand sometimes pax can be difficult. However, I asked a simple question in the most polite way. Shocking! Well not so shocking because it is Piarco airport where apparently no one can ask a question without security being hostile! The response I got from the male security was in a very passive aggressive tone! This left me with an awful taste and feeling, we’re not animals/ prisoners passing through Piarco airport for departure, but human beings simply trying to arrive at our destination safely.

Terrible airport. Rude staff, who outright lie. Ridiculously long immigration queues, even for those with an onward boarding pass. I was last here in March 2017. Missed my connecting flight because immigration queue was 1.5 hours (1.5 hours!). Tried to speak tomorrow staff. One lied to me and said that the connecting flight was also delayed - not true, as it turned out. One simply looked at me as though I was crazy and said "I don't know" when I asked her a question, and walked off. I have gone out of my way to avoid this airport since, but was forced to use it again. Sincerely hope that this proves to be a better experience. Puts the country to shame, unfortunately.

On arriving, travelling with my Trini wife and child, I was met with a substantial queue to immigration. There was this very empathic and helpful immigration lady ushering people along. She saw our plight, along with other families with children and expedited our movement through immigration. On return, at check in, this positive attitude to assisting passengers was also evident with the handling clerk (we also had an internal Caribbean flight during our stay and the check in staff was exceptionally helpful, as we had left an important document at our accommodation and had to get a copy whatsapped over). My only criticism is the system whereby a trolley is available free from the baggage area, but you are only permitted to use it as far as the entrance/exit to the airport, after which one must either carry your baggage to the transport or pay a trolley porter $8 US to move your baggage perhaps 20 meters. It's nice that in the Departure Lounge one can obtain such essentials as Royal Castle Pepper Sauce and Mudder in Law Chadon Benni pepper sauce. It would have been nice to see a fast food outlet in the departure lounge itself, though some people had little difficulty bringing food through from the food court by the entrance. Security was efficient, no issues there. Loud speaker announcements were entirely incomprehensible and impossible to understand (this must be a trait in airports).

Generally the airport is fine except in the past couple years. I travel to Trinidad 1-3 times a year to visit my family. What had me most surprised is that there is now a separate line for men, even when traveling with a family. All women and children go through a separate line. You can imagine which line is ridiculously long while men sail through or security at the men’s line just hang out. Is this the Middle East? We just went back a few steps in equal rights. So much for being a family friendly airport! Don’t forget the usual Trini rudeness of the security staff.

GSO is a very convenient and nice airport. Parking is super convenient right next to the terminal which makes it nice when picking up people. It is a nice and clean airport that I try and fly out of whenever I can. I only wish that I could get more direct flights out of there.

Piedmont Triad is just a jewel of an airport. Friendly staff, polite and helpful TSA Officers, who seem genuinely pleased to have the opportunity to chat to travellers. Add to this outstanding wi-fi connection which comes free of charge, with no time limit, and comfortable, clean and stress free surroundings. We fly here frequently from Glasgow with a connection to NC at Newark. Not as many shops or food concessions as larger airports, but at least the staff are friendly. The difference between Newark and Greensboro is really quite startling. My wife and I love this airport.

Worst airport I've ever been. The employees are incredibly pedantic and rude and barely help you at all. The airport is so small and it's very hard to move around with large luggage, and employees don't even consider helping you in any way. There are aren't many cafes or restaurants, and worse thing is some are closed even in the afternoon. Food is more expensive than in other airports,

Absolutely overcrowded, old infrastructure, tiny despite the number of passengers (which are basically forced to sit on the floor everywhere). Who is responsible for the state of this toilet of an airport? This is Pisa, not a third world country with huge socioconomical difficulties.

An utter disgrace! Probably the worst of the worst in Europe, definitely in Italy. Absolutely no place to sit, people sitting on stairs as solution, poor sales of food and drinks, simply unacceptable. Filthy too! Incredible they get away with it, basically one should claim back the airport tax, as one gets simply zero service. Second time in few months I have been fooled by this horrible place: don’t care how convenient it is to my travelling schedule, will avoid this inferno by all means and make a big big detour.

Overcrowded, filthy, tiny airport. No seats whatsoever. People forced to stand on lines for hours. Ridiculous. Absolutely low-grade in all respects. I will do all I can to avoid this filthy trap in the future.

Pisa airport is the worst airport I’ve ever been to and I have seen many airports. It hasn’t been updated since the dawn of time with two officers reviewing passports while there are hundreds and hundreds of people waiting. Honestly shocking how awful it is.

I have been in many airports Across the globe and I can honestly say Pisa International Airport is the worst airport I've ever had the Misfortune to take a departing flight from. It is clear the airport is vastly oversubscribed and has never updated its infrastructure to cater for the increased capacity overtime. Once you arrive at departures, there are no seats, with customers fighting over the few seats available while others stand in every available nook and cranny or sit in the floor. There are only two places to eat in departures which is also full of seat hoggers. Toilets are also disgusting. How anyone could think this is acceptable in this day and age is beyond me. Will never be back to this airport.

Shame on this horrible airport. Miserable organisation, filthy, overcrowded: one of the worst Italy has on offer. Not a single good word to spend. Going through security takes hours and the queue starts already from outside the terminal. Mind you, this isn’t because of too little personnel, rather it is the absolute incompetence reigning in this airport! To be avoided by all means.

Poor from start to finish. Poor signage for drop off (in fact, no real area to drop off) and a long walk in the heat from car rental (shuttle is very infrequent). Check in doesn’t open until 2 hours before take off. And then there are long queues. Tax refund service is before security but we were told it was after (and no-one else had even heard of it). Arrivals cafe gave my wife and two kids a tummy bug that lasted 4 days. On departure - once you go through passport control there is one manky cafe and not a single duty free or other shop (bizarre given only those after passport control should be entitled to duty free). Post security and pre passport control can only be described as a zoo. No seating, so everyone crowding around standing. Toilets are a hygiene risk Avoid if you can.
All the toilets are disgusting, so smelly you can't even breath. There are no drinking water fountains. Water prices are extortionate. Seating area is very small and crowded.

Lots of issues with this airport. It is not big enough or well equiped enough to handle the amount of traffic that is currently going through it. I've arrived here several times and have had to sit on the aircraft for up to an hour waiting for a parking space. There are not enough stairs for arriving aircraft and not enough working ground generators. leading to huge delays, Try sitting on an aircraft in august on the Pisa ramp without air conditioning and you'll know what I mean, Security queues are huge and slow. Once through security, passport control is nothing short of scandalous. I've never seen more than 2 desks open. The escalator going up to passport control is an accident waiting to happen. The queue can back up onto it , I've brought this to the attention of airport management several times and they are just not interested. If you are checking in hold luggage, 2 hours is not enough time to get to your gate before it closes. As in all airports the prices are daylight robbery. I did notice that there were no testers for perfumes just before and after Christmas, I wonder why? If you arrive in winter you will invariably get soaked walking from the aircraft to the terminal and God help you if you have hired a car. I've had to wait ouside in the rain for 5 minibus trips before getting on, Queues were huge. There are no baggage troleys at the car hire area so you will struggle if you have more than one case. Boarding is chaos, Either the airport or the airlines think it's OK to keep customers packed into a staiwell for up to an hour before departure in freezing cold or swealtering hot conditions without anywhere to sit. On arrival in Pisa be prepared to wait for anything up to 2hrs for your luggage and don't even expect it to come in on the belt that it actually says on the screen. On arrival there is some guy directing the 2 lines at passport control. He seems to take great pleasure in saying Breeteesh is not Europe anymore, It might be worthwhile if someone told him that there is a difference between Europe and the European Union. If you have a choice don't use this Airport, I've found staff to be rude and offhand, queues for everything, filthy toilets,outrageous prices for anything that you buy. It's not a friendly airport and it certainly isn't customer friendly.
The worst departure ever! Arrived early per recommendations only to be faced with a security line that was outside of the terminal! BarEly made boarding time.

I have flown from Charlotte NC to Pittsburgh many times in the past 14 yrs. Today I lost my wallet. I was very fortunate to be called informing me someone had turned in my wallet. They kindly sent an employee up to gate B32 to return it to me just minutes before my flight took off. That is excellent customer service and I will be forever grateful for their kindness. I will never forget this. Thanks for such a wonderful and caring staff. You guys rock!

The line to go through TSA security checkpoint was literally outside into the tunnel. It took 45 minutes to get through security checkpoint alone. Considering it is 5 am on national turn your clock forward day with only a handful of flights, there must’ve been three dozen people in line complaining that they were going to miss their flight. I missed my flight, because of horrible personnel management. There were plenty of individuals standing around they could’ve very easily opened the optional check point.

Overall PIT is a good airport. Given that it was built for much higher traffic everything is far under capacity. However the Delta flight from Paris continues to be very inconvenient and the process of arrival is designed in a very poorly thought out manner; after our first time on this flight we decided not to do it again but we broke down because there was a rare deal on this route. One would think that PIT's only flight to Europe would be outstanding. It is excellent to CDG. Upon return one goes through customs and immigration as expected but then stupidity gets inserted into the process. The mammoth design flaw is that one must recheck bags and go through security in order to LEAVE THE AIRPORT. This is standard procedure for connecting flights but not if your final destination is PIT. I have traveled numerous airports on three continents regularly and never seen anything as as poorly designed as this process. Third world countries do better. Imagine you purchased some duty free booze in CDG Paris. You cannot bring them through security and they need to be placed into your baggage. Our first time on this flight we were not told to put the liquor into our bags. Several people forfeited very expensive wine because they already checked their bags. They do a better job of warning passengers now. Additionally Delta seems to have some problems with baggage. We rechecked three bags after clearing customs for pickup at the baggage claim so we could leave the airport. One bag arrived fairly promptly about 20 minutes after checking it. The other two bags showed up more than 45 minutes after the first (so it took an hour). All were deposited on the conveyer belt at the same time. They only had to move the bags from the gate to the "landside terminal". Delta told me that they have three flights arriving very close together and there are only so many baggage handlers.
