These three flights all came in on schedule. They knew the planes and passengers would arrive - no mystery regarding the required tasks. The international arrival area was designed when security was far more lax than it is now however there are solutions. Why not run buses? European and Asian airports are always loading passengers into buses. Why not move the international gate to the "land side terminal"? It is simply not worth the trouble to get a direct flight. We intend on driving to another airport to do international flights or simply connecting elsewhere in the U.S. to go abroad. Clearly PIT management and facilities are not competent to handle international flights.

I am embarrassed to admit that this is my home town airport. My family flew in and out on Delta's new direct flight to Punta Cana this past week (12/28 - 1/4). Departure was fine but it's pretty hard (without de-icing debacles) to screw up a departure. Our return was another matter. A de-icing debacle caused the flight to Punta that would return us to be delayed almost two hours. How difficult is it to manage a de-icing operation? Obviously at Greater Pittsburgh it is. Our flight to Pittsburgh was on it's way and accurately tracked by Delta and flight tracker. Greater Pittsburgh should fully have known not only that it was on it's way but when it would land (down to the minute). We land and of course the gate is not ready. We wait and finally pull up to a gate. Of course there is no staff to service the plane at the gate so we wait almost an hour. Finally we depart the plane. Anyone with a connecting flight missed their flight. We go to customs. Two desks were staffed. For almost an hour and a half it takes two desks to process the plane. Stamp the passports. We then go for our bags. And surprise surprise we wait again. Add another 30 minutes. We then have to re-check our bags for landside baggage claim. Then we have to go baggage claim and wait another hour for our bags. We have now spent more time at the airport than we did flying from Punta Cana to Pittsburgh. Avoid this airport for any international travel.

Pittsburgh International is a modern well-kept airport but it has been sad to its usage steadily decline over the last 15 years or so. The US Airways hub is no longer and the airport has had a difficult time with the transition. Unfortunately this has meant plenty of vacant gates and ticket counters. For the passenger PIT offers free wifi though the signal is really only active near the Skymall McDonald's right in the centre of the terminal. Security lines are well-organised. While I was joining the line an employee suggested to a group of us that we use the "special annex screening gate" which had no waiting. That was really good advice which had all of us through and into the secure area in no time. Overall it is still a clean comfortable airport. I just really miss the days when so many more people used it on a daily basis.

This airport is just sad. It is such a beautiful facility that goes largely unused. Largely abandoned by US Airways most of the stores close early now so that any travellers coming into the airport in the evening find virtually all food establishments and other retailers closed. Many of the gates have been walled off as not necessary. It's all just very disappointing for the Pittsburgh area.

This airport is well organized. All arrivals and departures come to one common terminal. This has a lot of advantages in terms of dropping / picking up passengers. ANd it is very easy for anyone to find their way in this airport. Plenty of restrooms all over. Food court / shopping is very decent and neatly organized. And help-desks for visitors in airside and landside! You have to take a train between airside and landside. This adds a few minutes to your travel.

Agree with all the positive comments - only in transit at Pittsburgh International recently and found it to be a very pleasnt experience due in large part to the variety of shops and restaurants. An uncrowded spacious lay-out adds to the comfort level. Also agree with a previous comment regarding the downside of this airport being the near monopoly of US Airways; a greater presence by competing carriers would be a real plus!

When I compare the Pittsburgh Airport to my most frequented airports (Denver Chicago O'Hare Washington Dulles Orlando (MCO) LAX) Pittsburgh wins hands down. The airport itself has good signage to get you on and off Route 60. The terminal is also easy to navigate although the security procedures are more intense than any other major airport that I've seen. Show your boarding pass and ID when you get in the security line. Show your boarding pass and ID before passing through the metal detector. Show your boarding pass and ID AGAIN before leaving the security area and getting on the train to the gates. Once off the train and up the escalators there is ample shopping and many places to eat. The gates branch off of this main area like spokes on a wheel. There is an added bonus for computer users: FREE wireless internet access is available in the food court area. Get a bite to eat check your email catch up on the latest news. Other airports have wireless available but they use clients like T-Mobile or AT&T who charge $9.99 for a couple of hours use. I was able to pick up a mid to low wireless signal while sitting at my gate. Surfing the web made the time go by a lot faster. The major city airports like O'Hare Dulles and LAX could learn a lot from Pittsburgh Intl.

A small airport, about 10km from the city center, and played as the gateway for Pleiku and Gia Lai. Signs and information were clear and easy to navigate. Taxi pick up and drop off were right in front of the terminal. There were couple of shops and restaurants but please do not expect too much since it is a small airport as mentioned above. Security check was ridiculously slow and wasting time. No priority lane at security check for business class passengers.

Unpleasant experience: the airport is small and not connected with the city centre. The staff are extremely rude and not prepared. Be ready to pay for a taxi to go to the city centre, no buses at all. Taxi drivers will try to ask you an higher price. Average price to get to the city is 10/15 Leva (5/7 eur). Be ready to get a cold and rude welcome from the police that are checking your Italian ID card. We spent 1 hour waiting for police control, even in Paris I spent less time waiting for the security check. On my way back, they stopped me because of some water in the bottle. In front of everyone they took out everything from my back, even the dirty underwear. A clear violation of my privacy and without any authorization from me. Horrible experience! When I asked to speak with the airport manager to ask for an explanation, the staff member said "Shut up, put your things in and go!" Plovdiv is a nice city and worth a visit but be prepared to pass by this airport.

Plovdiv is a small domestic airport. It doesn't have any lounges. Check-in is okay. Not many staff, so the lines are long. There are very few flights, some days even no flights. The little bar next to check in is good. However, the airport is nice.
Parking in front of terminal is not free anymore. However the first 15 minutes still are. Distance to the center of Plovdiv is about 20 km. Plovdiv taxi's are reasonably priced.

Modern clean and efficient airport. Only a few flights per week. Airside after security and passport control there is a kiosk for food and drinks and a souvenir shop. For Ryanair flights you walk between plane and terminal so the priority boarding works. Parking in front of the terminal building is free.

Stunning new terminal friendly staff pleasurable experience only thing missing was the airlines. One scheduled flight to Moscow once a week and winter charter flights is not justified hope to see the scheduled operators move in soon.

Plymouth is a nice little airport with friendly staff. Not much point in arriving too early - the check-in does not open until an hour before your departure. The cafe is just by the check-in and there is a further landside lounge with the aforementioned free internet. There is just the one airside gate so if there are two flights at once you have to take your turn. Once through security there is a soft drinks vending machine but no other catering. All the seating areas have views over the apron. Everything seems to happen efficiently and with that personal touch that is lacking with other larger airports.

Nice clean and quiet little airport with good cafeteria. Also the departure area has free Internet if you need to check your e-mail before boarding; I thought that was a nice touch. We flew out of Plymouth on an Air Southwest flight and their staff are wonderful. The only downside for us was an over-zealous security officer. That aside Plymouth has a lovely little airport and a super airline in Air Southwest; will certainly fly with them again.

An excellent regional airport with good updated facilities including it's super cafe which will provide you with coffee and toast for that early morning departure. From car park to check in takes just a couple of minutes and baggage return the same. Air Southwest staff from check in flight deck and cabin crew are exemplary. As a regular traveller with them I recognise so many friendly faces. I find flying with them and from Plymouth a pleasure.

The main problem with this airport is that it is becoming too small for the traffic it tries to handle, especially the terminal. The positive point about the ramp area is that, without docking on a jetty, a plane can taxi off right from its parking position without the help of a tow truck. The arrival and departure halls airside and landside are too small and crowded. Check-in staff was unfriendly. No hello, no comment, no thank you nor any sort of "have a nice trip". Boarding pass scanning to get access to the departure hall took 30 minutes (I have knee trouble and had to stand in a crowded line, had to wear a face mask to stay safe bacteria-wise). The line was single file, one of two scanning positions was not staffed. A lazy employee took the boarding pass, scanned it herself (a thing that is done by the passenger normally, and takes a couple minutes) and handed it back with no thank-you. Little seating room in the waiting area, but at least there was a coffee shop. Boarding started late, and with no particular system. Everybody just tried to get thru. The employee at the gate (walk-out boarding in any weather), when asked why there was no priority boarding for business class, snapped: "First here, first go!" Unfortunately Austrian Airlines seems to have no control over the pathetic lazyness and utter indifference towards the paying customer.

This is the hottest airport I have ever encountered. I suppose a combination if poor design - too much glass and inadequate air conditioning. Today was only 17° - in Summer it would be an absolute furnace.

The two women who were supposed to be only scanning boarding passes have literally destroyed the reputation of this airport and even of Montenegro as a country, for anyone who has spent little time there. They created a line 50 meters long and waits of 30-45 minutes for no reason. We nearly missed our flight despite arriving with plenty of time. These woman should be instantly fired, should have their pay docked, and should have to write a handwritten apology to every passenger they delayed for absolutely no reason. Their jobs should be given to someone who actually cares and wants to exchange with society. They had one of the easiest jobs on planet earth. All they had to do was scan boarding passes and let people into the line to have their passports checked and go through security. Yet they managed to delay each person by up to several minutes, by fussing around, having long conversations and making people wait, sometimes allowing people to cut in line, other times arguing with people for a long time about cutting in line (and holding up the rest of the line), stopping to slowly drink water and take their sweater on and off, etc. There was no urgency or care to allow people to move through the line and catch their flights. In fact it appeared that they were deliberately slowing people down as much as they could so that they could miss their flights. To scan a boarding pass and let people through takes 5 seconds at any other airport. Not at Podgorica airport - there it takes several minutes per person and the line that should be the fastest is actually the slowest - 30 - 45 minutes for absolutely nothing.

Flying as a silver frequent flyer member on a full plane. One of the perks of having the membership is the promise of having hand luggage on the plane with you. Not according Podgorica staff you don't. They make their own rules. Not only that. They threaten you that if you take the hand luggage with you, that they will take it on board with no tag. Honestly, I am speechless. In the days when European airports are begging the people to travel with hand luggage seems like in Podgorica they only aim to make the customer experience the worst possible. They should all be retrained in all areas of customer service, luggage handling. Especially the supervisor who are responsible for the ground handlers.

A small airport for the tiny capital of Montenegro, so that means big queues for border control, no online check in, hardy any shops or food and beverages. Staff were friendly and correct. Best to pre-book a taxi in order to get to town, which will be around 8 euro.

Canadian passport used on entry and despite having valid visa I was still required to show a letter of invitation from someone residing in the Congo. Next you have your Yellow Fever certificate inspected. Luggage arrived in good time but all bags were manually searched by officials before exiting arrivals. Arrival hall was very crowded with 2 aircraft's having arrived within 20 minutes of each another. No functioning air- conditioning. On return thereafter came another security check passport control another security check at X- ray screening line and only then access to departure lounge. To enter boarding area from departure lounge area you again have a passport check as well as another table where you have your carry-on opened and inspected. If you happen to need a bathroom visit after having entered the boarding gate area you must proceed back to departure lounge.

The first thing that struck me was that there was AC units along the walls but none of them was turned on. It was quite hot but that didn't seem to disturb the airport staff. Got a bit surprised when the staff started to manually carry the luggage inside. The luggage band did not work. Had expected it to be more of a fuzz to get inn. Remember that there are not many english speaking staff at the airport. When going home used about 2 hours to get through safety. Had to show passport 10 times before being able to enter plane. As the safety check was not that thorough Air France had their own safety check when entering airplane. (The Congolese safety check was rubbish) It seems the airport only employs security guards in uniforms and no maintenance personnel - half the lightbulbs was working. Also toilets (some without sink and toilet paper) was rubbish.

The airport is small and modern. It has both local and international flights (Air France). Arrivals are no problem and there is not far to walk from the aircraft to the airport exit. There did not seem to be to many people bothering passengers. Departures is also straight forward with modern check-in desks. There are not many shops in the departure area and only one basic cafe. There is adequate seating and the air-conditioning works well. Overall a very good experience compared with other African airports.

I visited Guadeloupe in 2014! I found the airport stuck in the 90's! A little old, mixed with modern glass. Immigration was quick and no questions! (I travel on a Brazilian passport). Everything very expensive, and cleaning conditions can be filthy, even on food carts! Taxis charge average 20 EUR to get you to downtown, public
transportation only if you walk to the main road outside airport zone.

Looks as if the dreaded car parking charges are about to be introduced at Poities airport after upgrade work completion. This is planned from 1st February '07. Like me a number of people have enjoyed free parking while leaving there cars at Poitiers. Getting information about parking fees penalties etc (for those whose cars where left at Poitiers pre 01/02/07) is proving extremely difficult. Does anyone have contact details to ensure cars are not towed away post 01/02/07. Many thanks.
When I was last there about a year ago it and free parking. Makes a good alternative to Bordeaux if travelling to the North Dordogne. Facilities minimal.

Ridiculous behaviour of customs at Azores airport. Checking in 2 persons with 2 identical travel-rods and having 1 refused as hand luggage and forcing the traveller to pay an additional €65. Since when do the rules change from the flight towards flight leaving. Colleagues even tried to correct the lady because they did not agree, but she refuses to correct her mistake.

Such a small airport. But perfectly sized for the amount of people and traffic. Nice staff and very clean facilities. Just need to ensure there are some drinks and food available past security, as the drink vending machine was broken!
Very convenient airport, as it is not very large. Signs are clear, getting to and from the airport is easy too. Shops are available, post office included. The terminal is clean.

Excellent small airport. Arrived from JFK and departed to JFK (homepoint DTW). Arrival: It was raining, so as a courtesy, we were bussed to terminal (ride 2 minutes). Passage through passport control took 3 minutes. The passport control officer smiled and welcomed me. Ample shops landside; I was able to buy postcards and stamps to mail them to friends. Taxicabs to town do not have meters; rate is fixed at 10 euros. Careful driver, clean taxicab. Departure: 4 minutes at security; 2 minutes at passport control. Passport control officer smiled again (why are US CBP personnel so unable to master the skill of smiling?). Airside, only 1 tiny snack shop. Lovely sunny morning, so we walked a few feet on tarmac and up staircase into airplane.

Small airport, well organized and easy to get around. The staff are not even remotely nice and not very fast at handling all the procedures. The terminal is nice, clean but lacking heavily on options to eat, specially after going through security. Not enough places to sit and waiting areas are small.

Airport is small and fairly organized and clean. There are not sufficient places to park to leave or pick up passengers and Public transport is terrible, close to non existent. You have the usual taxi service, you have a very small bus that connects to some hotels but if you live in the city or if you just want to commute to the city centre to then take a bus an hotel out of town, you are out of luck. It is absolutely shameful that you need to insert a coin to get a cart, you do get it when you return the luggage cart but if you don't have local currency with you, you are out of luck. Staff are friendly enough. Almost no places to eat or drink anything, very bad in this respect. The lines for security were far too big and took far too much time for such a small number of passengers. The waiting area is clean and nice but it is far too small. Luggage delivery usually takes too much time and I can't say things are well organized. Decent place but nothing special.

This is a very small airport but it is clean, convenient and easy to get around. Passing through security was a breeze, no big queues to wait at. The waiting room was easy to find and it was nice, clean and comfortable. There isn't many places to eat or shop but I really don't care for that. Airport staff was ok, they aren't the friendliest out there but they weren't rude either. It is a shame there is no public transport access to the airport except for a mini bus that links to the major hotels but not to the city.

Well, this a small airport, reasonably well kept but small. Arriving was easy and dropping off the luggage was a fast process as well as paying for excess luggage and going through security. The airport was clean and it looks nice but there are a quite a few problems with it: Foods and drinks are expensive and the offer is small. Waiting rooms are very small, not much in terms of shopping. Don't know any other airport that requires you to insert a coin to use the carts/trolleys. And finally, at the arrival, it was terrible. There were just 4 flights at that time and still people had no place to be while waiting for their luggage, I couldn't even get an eye on the convier belt and it was very hard to notice my bag let alone get to it. Some people couldn't even get a trolley for the luggage as they weren't nearly enough. It was very bad to walk amongst that people in such a crowded place with the luggage and I must confess I have been to much bigger airports like Frankfurt, Haneda or Kansai and never felt so crowded. People working in the airport were professional but not much in the way of nice. They could do so much better.

The airport was a bit crowded and it is small but everything was clean and organized. Boarding was simple and easy. One negative aspect was the security officer at the X-ray machine, he was quite rude and unprofessional. I had forgotten my swiss in my carry on and instead of asking me to remove it, he insisted in opening my bag and going to all my belongings himself. I offered to find what he was looking for, another security officer remembered him that it would be better and faster if I did it but he insisted in going through my stuff. I am not sure but I would say this is incorrect and probably illegal as the security officer should never go through the belongings of a passenger. In every other airport where my bag need to be check, they always asked me to open it and to remove the items so they could watch it. It almost seemed as if the security officer was enjoying going through my stuff and exposing it to everyone.

Ponta Delgada is a small airport. If you have to stay for more than 1 or 2 hours you are out of luck. Almost no places to spend your time, few options to have a drink or something to eat and no wifi. Staff aren't friendly nor are they efficient or helpful. Check in and boarding takes abnormal amounts of time for such a small amount of passengers to take care and sometimes people don't even respect the check in queues and the staff don't care. You are on your own. Waiting rooms are small and with inadequate seating. Cleanliness could be much better and strangely I couldn't find any place to place my suggestions. To get a luggage cart you need to deposit a coin, this is not practical as many flyers don't have local currency on arrival and there is no place to exchange your currency for the local one at the airport. I have travelled a bit and never found another airport where I had to deposit money to have a trolley, this is even a bit offensive, not sure if they are afraid I might steal their carts.

I traveled with 20 people from NYC. We entered the airport and had no problems coming in. Pretty fast service with immigration and getting our bags. Outside was rather chaotic. Too many men standing around to carry bags. They should control them better maybe like cabs take turns as requested. On the way out we found the airport entrance very clear. Our bus pulled up and emptied better than it could in JFK. It was comforting to see the UN security team right outside. The building was well air conditioned which was great. The ticketing area was easily accessible. We found that there was a ton of security checks not sure why as it seemed to be for baggage mostly. We had our ID's checked 4 times and our bags screened twice. We were told at the ticket area that once inside there were no rest rooms. That was not completely true. There is a rest room area inside TSA but before the final jetBlue secure gate area baggage screening. Also the signs for the duty free shop inside could have been better/higher to see. Overall it was not horrible but just a little cramped in feeling and the double check of the bags while offering a feeling of security sent red flags up as to why they were doing that. It seemed like a jetBlue thing as Spirit did not do that. Also the place was clean.

This January was my fifth trip to Port-au-Prince and my first since I flew in on a DC3 just after the quake. While the airport is essentially the same the service coming and going is very much improved. Customs and security well organized. Staff courteous. Best of all the road and parking lot outside are way better controlled. I was impressed at how much has been done without new buildings. Cleaner more efficient and quite friendly. Big compliment on the effort and results. I returned to Canada via Fort Lauderdale which was a bad transit experience.

The worst service of a small airport. The men working reception where rude, unhelpful and couldn’t really explain or help with anything I asked of them. Port Augusta airport would have to be the worst in the state

Arrived 1pm from Cape Town and walked across tarmac to terminal. The terminal was a bit chaotic as far more arrivals than usual because of World Triathlon Championships. Our flight waited at nominated luggage belt and watched same luggage go around and around for 10 minutes without any being picked off, then we, and those passengers on the next belt, were told to swap belts and surprise, there was our luggage. Out the front door after picking up a handful of tourist brochures and maps and Avis was 50m away. From flight landing to driving away it was about 50 minutes and the airport is 5 minutes drive from the beach front and city centre. At any other time there would not have been the confusion but thousands of competitors and visitors arriving strained the services a bit. We drove to Cape Town so can't comment on departures.
Changes made for the World Cup have improved this airport from small and efficient to small and very slick. New access to departures security is welcome.

The Port Elizabeth airport is compact and well laid out and it is very convenient to the Summerstrand beach area. Car Hire is in a separate building across the entrance road which is close to the terminal but requires dodging traffic with everything in tow. Baggage retrieval seemed to take an extraordinary long time considering ours was the only arriving flight and the plane was sitting on the tarmac 50 meters away from the baggage claim but these things happen. Check in on return was polite and efficient and there is a modest selection of shops to pass the time waiting for departure but only on the street side of security.

Port Elizabeth airport is small and friendly. Best thing about it is that it is so close to the main seafront area - you can be on the beach about 5 minutes after leaving the airport if you want! Slight disadvantage once you are on the beach is that planes go right over your head! Also very close to CBD and the pleasant suburb of Walmer. PE known as the Friendly City and the airport gives it a good introduction.

It deserves the rate of passengers through this airport. It was not air conditioned and I was stopped 7 times and was asked if I can give a donation: 1. health officer, 2. Immigration officer 2 x, 3. custom officers 2 x, 4 officer after security check 3 x, 5. Security body search before boarding. The custom officer ask whether I had cash then and I had to open suitcase as she found some cash you have to donate it or you can wait long before you can go.

Among the 120 airport I've been in my life Port Harcourt is the worst by far. Arrival is not in a building but in a tent. Departure is a mess (like all other airports in Nigeria). I feel like I'm  in an airport of 60s. Electrity shorcuts. No flight information display (like others in Nigeria). Impolite employees. Security processing poor. Never took a flight on time there.

Avoid departing from here if you can possibly avoid it unless you want your passport checked ten times your bag emptied three times your body scanned three times and be forced to declare your currency even if it is within the legal limits. All this is accompanied by the intimidating and constant query of: 'You have something for me ?'. Utterly and shamelessly corrupt.

Port Macquarie Small airport that serves its purpose. It only gets flights from Sydney. The arrivals gate is a gate (much like one would find around a pool to keep kids out) and the departures lounge is comfortable and air conditioned a new add-on as a result of changing security laws. All the staff friendly and personable possibly because they don't get many people through in a a day. Whilst the number of people in the terminal was comfortable around my flight times it wouldn't go astray for the owners to speed up on expanding the airport facilities as it was getting a bit on the crowded side as there is only one taxiway connecting the apron to the runway. There's also a nice viewing area for all members of the public outside near the arrivals gate where all planes can be seen arriving and departing.

The more I travel the more I appreciate Port Moresby's Jacksons International Airport. Whilst the speed at check-in is dependent on the systems (sometimes it takes longer but usually it's quite fast), it's always a breeze moving through this terminal from check-in to security to immigration and into the departure lounge. The lounge itself has great seating, with good food options and drink options as well as shopping. POM isn't Changi, but then again Changi is matchless.

Having previously written a review that was positive about the Port Moresby experience arriving from Australia, I have now flown in several times from Asia and I have say it is very different. The flights generally arrive early morning and some days you will have flights from Tokyo, Singapore and Hong Kong arriving at the same time. This means very long queues at immigration - if you have a domestic connection, tell the staff and they'll put in a shorter queue. However, then you get your bags and join the customs queue. The reason the Australian flights are easier is that the passengers rarely get searched, whereas these Asian flights are targeted for customs checks. So when I got to the front of the queue, I was waved straight through despite declaring food, but it took me half an hour to get to the front of the queue - there were 5 search counters open but only one person checking everyone's declaration card. So if you're flying in from Asia, be very careful about connections - for me, a 3-hour connection turned into a mad rush to the domestic terminal.

Domestic arrival was good, canteen facilities are reasonably priced. Toilet was clean in arrival hall. International departure - 2 money exchange facilities available. The security check was not particularly friendly - boarding was smooth via gate 3 with Virgin Australia using an air bridge.

After a few trips through the airport, this is what I think: International arrivals: Remarkably smooth when there’s only one plane arriving (the 767 from Brisbane). Efficient and well-marked immigration queues – I spent just 10 minutes in the “already have visa” queue but if you’re rushing for a domestic connection, try using the “visa on arrival” queue on the right, which was very short (if you need a visa on arrival, go to the separate booth to buy it first). Baggage collection and customs was fast with very few bags checked. There is an ATM by the baggage carousel and an ATM and money changer in the main hall along with a decent café. If you’re connecting to Air Niugini domestic, you can use a transfer check-in desk in the international terminal, then walk over to the domestic terminal. International departures: Also smooth with fairly fast check-in and immigration lines. Airside has 2 cafes (better than the one in the main hall), a bar and duty free shops. Basically just like a decent small western airport except that the bathroom was dirty and had no soap. Paid wifi only. Domestic terminal: Things get a lot worse here. Compared to international, the domestic terminal is a madhouse, especially at peak times like xmas. You have to pass security on entry, and maybe show your ticket, then you might have to deal with a huge pack of people (some of them very stinky) at check-in. Make sure that you’re in the right queue, as the lines aren’t always straight and people are often diverted to other counters. Check often with the staff and other passengers (middle-class PNG citizens generally speak English well and can be very helpful). Make sure to check-in early – at least 2 hours during busy periods – due to the queues and to the fact that locals check-in huge amounts of luggage, which leads to late arrivals being bumped from flights due to the planes reaching their weight limit (frequent weather delays and cancellations can also mean that late arrivals are bumped in favour of passengers from a cancelled flight). Then you have to go past a single person checking every Air Niugini boarding pass for all flights and then more security – once I got through here very quickly but the other times there were long queues. The departure area is OK when it’s not crowded and has a couple of basic food shops. Pay attention to boarding announcements and check with staff at the gates because it’s not always clear which gate you’re supposed to board through. Then you have to walk out to the planes – most of the way is covered but you will get a bit wet if it’s raining. Ratings below are for the international terminal, where you shouldn't have any problems. I rate the domestic terminal a 3 and advise you to plan ahead.

Very little queueing times in both the domestic and international terminals. Jacksons International has just undergone some big renovation work and is looking excellent, with great shopping and cafés. Jacksons Domestic still needs a bit of work especially in the departures hall but I understand plan are afoot. A pleasant airport to transit.

I find that boarding and getting out of the plane is quite fast. However if you're travelling Virgin Australia their planes do not connect to the gate so you'll have to come out and walk to the terminal. As off 25th September 2013 - all tourist visas are now free. Passport queues always take a long time and it gets stuffy. I arrived on 26th to find out that I now have an extra K100 in my pocket. There is a BSP Bank branch by the carousel but also inside the general terminal area. I carry around my digicel simcard with me so I buy phone credit as soon as I walk out with my bags. You don't have to go and wait outside as there are people around. I feel safer waiting inside and looking out the window for my pick up to arrive.

Arriving late at night from Brisbane on a delayed flight we were quickly off the plane and through customs without a long delay for baggage - but remember PGK100 for a visitors visa! Security is fairly tight due to the general problems of PNG and only passengers with tickets are allowed into the terminals. The domestic terminal is somewhat more crowded and more confusing with limited facilities but is relatively clean. Returning from outside POM you may well find that there is no international baggage transfer - you need to walk the three hundred or so metres between the terminals with your baggage - but it is a covered walkway with lots of security staff everywhere. After check-in there is then a wait (with few available chairs) until customs is opened about an hour before the flight. Once through things go fairly smoothly though there is not much airside apart from the small Air Niugini lounge which is pleasant enough. For the size of Port Moresby a reasonable enough experience though more seating would be good.

The arrivals hall at the international terminal is clean and tidy but does not cope well with any more than 2 large aircraft arriving at the same time. It can take over an hour to clear customs and there is only one baggage conveyor. The only ATM is after passport control and you will need PGK500 if you wish to purchase a visa - so it pays to have your currency ready before you depart for POM. The departure lounge is also very clean and tidy and customs and immigration are efficient. However if you wish to do shopping there is only one very small duty free shop and an even smaller cafe after customs and security.

Things have improved a little - arrival is chaotic if a large plane (eg 767 from BNE) it took an hour from arrival to leaving. The money exchange was open you still pay for your visa. Check-in was very efficient . There is still one shop pre customs and some food available afterwards. You do not have to get wet anymore when boarding. Domestic more challenging when checking in. You do walk to the planes although some covered walk ways. Was quick delivering checked bags from internal flight.

Harry Bauer lounge at Port Vila Airport is located airside after passing through Immigration and Customs. We travelled Business Class on Air Vanuatu and were handed lounge invitations. Its best kept secret that this lounge is also a pay as you go Lounge, so anyone (Economy Class passengers as well) can actually access the lounge on paying a fee when the lounge is open before each departure. I didn't ask what the fee was, but did notice they accept credit cards by way of a credit card machine, contrary to some reviews some years back stating they only accept cash. The lounge is air conditioned, very welcoming after walking through the non-air conditioned public waiting area. There is a refrigerator with non-alcoholic drinks/sodas as well as a selection of local beers. Minimal snacks are on offer and comfortable seating with views out across the tarmac and runway. A quiet haven to sit and relax before the flight. There is sufficient seating for some 40 or more people, so not a small lounge but cosy enough. Sure beats waiting in the public area where there is no air conditioning.

This airport really needs a major overhaul. Vanuatu is becoming very popular with visitors from the south Pacific region so an upgrade to this airport is badly overdue. No WiFI no Qantas Club and very slow check-in facilities. The airport could also benefit from providing air conditioned comfort instead of over-head fans.

Portland's airport feels slightly dated, not run down by any means, but still pleasant and functional enough. A lot of construction taking place at this time in the check-in area, I guess in an effort to modernize the airport and expand passenger capacity. The terminals themselves, again, are a little dated, but still nice enough and functional. TSA Pre-Check operates smoothly here, even where there are a lot of Pre-Checkers in line. Personnel, whether they're working at check-in, for TSA, in a restaurant, or at the boarding gate, are usually super bubbly, but still professional, helpful and polite. PDX is neither stellar nor bad, it's above-average but with a lot of potential. And, it's better than Sea-Tac!

A quiet afternoon at PDX. Short queues to get through security with efficient and helpful staff. As the space allocated for security was fairly small, I can imagine at that at busy times there could be problems.

We were pressed for time so we didn't stop and eat, our plane was scheduled to leave at 9.15pm. We arrived an hour and 45 minutes early but nothing was open except a place across from gate E11 and they only had drinks and chips. I realize there is a labor shortage but if you look at the chart that depicts the busiest time at this airport 9pm is the busiest. Wouldn't you think that would be the best time to schedule staff?

I used to think the PDX was an ok airport, and after tonight’s security fiasco, I am changing my tune. 10 people got through the security line in 30 mins. She said my neck pillow, which had grains in it, could be explosive. She swabbed it on the outside then took out the sealed insert and swabbed the inner layer. And said “people try and take explosives, it could be explosive” my response was. “It's a neck pillow” if those weren’t allowed to take on flights, then put a sign up! The arrogance of the TSA staff is ridiculous. 30 minutes to let through 10 people! The two families with small children in front of me are not security risks. They’re now super stressed out single moms! Because you took apart all of their children’s things and made them wait in a line for no reason. It felt just like they were being mean and literally searching through every persons bags. It was the worst security experience ever, and I’ve flown through JFK and it’s not like the other TSA agents were doing anything, at least 10 of them they were just standing around talking about their weekend. Flying can already be stressful, there’s no need for the drama over neck pillows. It was ridiculous. Portland International Airport should really get their act together and maybe use some more common sense in the hiring of their TSA agents.

This is my local airport and not a bad little place. Yes, at times TSA slows things down to a crawl, but the TSA workers here seem to actually have a sense of pride and a sense of humor. I have a steel hip and this has caused numerous delays in other airports but either they know me by now or they have their collective ish together. Food offerings are decent and the Powell's Bookstore is a great place to grab a book for your flight. My only bummer is that it IS a smaller metro airport and thus fewer international nonstops.

Arrived at the top deck outside the ticketing counters to pick up my college-age daughter (American Airlines Flight 6088) after waiting near the airport to receive a text telling me she was approaching the exit. Airport traffic was light with several empty spaces for cars to pull up to the curb. I had been there no more than 2-3 minutes when a military-looking airport security guard suddenly started pounding on my passenger window. "Get out of here!" I rolled down the window to tell him I had waited for notice my passenger was available and he leaned all the way into my car and shouted, "If it was alright for you to be here, would I be talking to you?" I pulled my head back so fast I smacked the driver's door. He was completely out of control and shouting as if a major emergency were happening. I sincerely thought he was going to hit me or continue striking my car. I saw my daughter out of the corner of my eye and was immediately afraid for her safety. I pulled away as fast as I could so he wouldn't realize she was connected to me. I'm 62 and a small woman. Portland International Airport doesn't deserve all the high ratings. This isn't the first time I've had their airport personnel act like they enjoy menacing people. Whoever trains their security people needs to be trained themselves.

What is wrong with this place. My flight is leaving at 12.30 am and literally nothing is open here. You can get nothing here after 10pm apparently. Utter nonsense. They call themselves an "international airport"? Get real-it's a parochial bastion of complete boredom with no libations.

The international arrival system sucks. There are about 15 machines to verify your password and to answer customs questions which worked great, but then you get in a very slow moving queue with 2 customs officers to ask the same questions you just answered. Do the math 15 machines then down to two agents guess what happened ... we all got through the machines quickly just to get stuck in a slow moving line for the worthless additional step. Then you grab you luggage and yet another agent only one this time checks your customers and passport again. Then you get on a bus to take you to the main baggage pick up area, why can’t you just walk like the rest of the airport access. And yes there was another line for the bus. Seriously PDX you can do better ... lovely carpet only goes so far.

TSA is horrible at this airport. I don't hear well, but I'm well versed in the procedures we are forced to go through. Staff kept screaming something at me, I had no idea what, but I knew what was expected so ignored him and was just waiting my turn to go through the screener; he actually grabbed me by the shoulder and pulled me back! I am nearly 70 years old, female, I jerked away and he pulled me back and screamed at me to empty my pockets! I do not have things in my pockets, good grief.  Got to my boarding area, Southwest C12, and sat down to read and wait ... looked down and the metal bar between the seats was covered with filth. It was so thick you could run your fingers through it. So disgusting, I got up and looked for a clean seat, and they were all filthy, so I just got some exercise and walked for two hours. I cannot believe how filthy it was.

40 minutes to get through security. 25 in line and then the worst was the arrogant attitude of all TSA when my bag was pulled to be checked - it sat there for 5 minutes. 4 workers stood right there within 3 feet of it talking to each other. After 5 minutes another woman walked nearby and I went to her and said my bag has been there 5 minutes - she had an arrogant attitude as well and said with an annoyed tone - someone will get to it. I waited another 3 minutes - 2 of the 4 talking walked the other direction and 2 still talked a minute or more - I tried to get their attention but was ignored. I saw another man standing around and told him my bag had been there almost 10 minutes - same attitude - “someone will get to it”. With an attitude a minute later a still waiting - I saw a woman who I complained to and she said same thing with an attitude. Meanwhile a TSA man had gone to the next row over and started checking 2 or 3 bags that had come out way after mine - mine was only bag for a full five minutes at least. It took 15 minutes. Rude people that don't care and think they are god because they have so much power over your life and you can’t do anything about it. I hate this airport.

Bennett at the TSA first check point was so incredibly sweet to our son and his attitude was great. I'm sure everyone that works for the TSA feels this way on the inside but he was clearly showing it to us on the outside. Keeper.

Terrible airport and one I sadly had to wait in for my delayed flight! Seating is limited, and many people had no other choice than to sit on the floor. 5+ minute wait for the toilets, which are not clean. 10+ minute wait to order food or coffee as the options are so limited. The only positive was the music that was playing, I believe it was live but I was hesitant to leave the seat I found and then be faced with sitting on the floor. This airport is not built for, and cannot accommodate a vast amount of people.

A surprisingly large and spacey airport given the size of Porto. Boarding times, security and seating were all great cuz of the practical layout. Even during peak season there's plenty seats available. Prices at the foodcourt were lower than you're used to in Europe. There's a convenient metro connection to the city center. So all in all a hassle free airport.

Awful airport. Puts me off visiting Portugal again, which is a wonderful country, Check in was chaos, 2 agents for trying to check in an Air France Hop flight to Paris, and a KLM CityHopper flight to Amsterdam. We stood in this queue for 1 hr, no queuing lines, just pushing and shoving and we saw one altercation in the line. One checkin agent then started calling people forward who were on the Paris flight as they were in danger of missing it, Both of these flights were fairly small aircraft, dread to think if they’d used larger aircraft. Overall checkin was a horrible experience. Security line was huge, but moved really quickly and staff were very polite. Departure lounge hardly anywhere to sit and heat was unbearable. Overall a horrible little airport, apart from the security team, and I’d never fly from here again.

Their wifi doesn’t work at all (I tried for 2 hours at different spots) and there’s no mobile signal either! Also, due to their massive glass panels, several gates are as hot as greenhouses! So, if your flight is delayed, be ready to be in a sauna without the possibility of writing emails, calling or texting someone, doing any online work or watching any videos or streaming service either. If it were possible to claim a refund of airport fees, I would.

So, if your flight is delayed, be ready to be in a sauna without the possibility of writing emails, calling or texting someone, doing any online work or watching any videos or streaming service either. If it were possible to claim a refund of airport fees, I would.

After passing the boarding area I noticed that water is either free or a bottle costs €1, which is acceptable. Going down one floor, water stops being free and costs €2.10 per bottle. The number of seats available in the waiting areas is absurd, 50%. You can hardly hear anything when they announce flights over the microphone, especially if you are Portuguese/Brazilian.  Depois de passar a zona de embarque reparei que a água ou é grátis ou uma garrafa custa €1,aceitável. Dencendo um andar,a água deixa de ser grátis e passa a custar €2.10 por garrafa, um roubo ! O número de assentos disponível nas áreas de espera é absurdo ,50%. Não se percebe absolutamente quase nada quando anunciam os voos ao microfone, em especial se for português/brasileiro.

Nightmare! On a domestic connection, Portugal to Portugal, they Force you to go through a security check. So, when flying from Lisbon to Madeira, you run through the entire airport, go through a security check, and then run through the airport again! And they have no smoking section.
Terrible place. No useful signage. Boarding shambolic. Can’t hear any announcements. Flight after boarding procedure and standing for forty minutes. Will avoid in future.
Terrible and lazy security. Not helpful and wasn’t even willing to listen to what i had to say. Experienced so many airports and this is the worst I've been to.

Most areas were closed and no one was helpful. We were transiting through the airport with the same airline. Security was closed, passport control was closed and being disabled we had organised help at the airport. We were advised because we were transiting and we had been issued our ongoing boarding passes we would be taken to departure gate via passport control negating the need to go though full security. The security area was closed for cleaning meaning we had to go through departure security again before being left in wheel chair for hours waiting for passport control to open. Take care when booking flight and requesting help at Porto as clearly they tell you one thing but do something completely different

Very good airport, clean, little queue times, wi-fi works well and there are many options for eating. One thing that I liked very much about this airport is that on the third floor there are many food options. This airport is not very big, but it's space is very well used.
Only one word filthy! Toilets disgusting Floors filthy - weeks of filth. Coffee shop at the front filthy. Needs a deep clean as filthy.

This has to be the worst airport I have flown from. And I am travelling around the world on a regular basis. Lack of food options, the only two extremely expensive. Disgusting unclean toilets, no cleaning to be seen, over flowing bins rubbish spilling onto the floor. No air conditioning in an over crowded terminal with 35 degree heat. An awful airport be hard to get any worse. Terrible just terrible.

The airport itself is small and easily accessible. The downside is the airport security staff. The staff who greeted us first were pleasant and friendly but the ones conducting inspections and overseeing direct searches of people and luggage are gruff at best and grumpy at worst. I think they need some training on how to be polite and respectful to passengers. This isn’t the first time that we experienced this kind of behaviour on the security line. The washrooms are limited and in need of cleaning and an upgrade. They could also use at least one area for passengers with pets so the animals can relieve themselves, as seen in many other airports.

The queue for the border was moving quite fast, the border guards were working fast. The toilets in the baggage reclaim area was clean although there was a queue to them, one of the two urinals wasn't working. The toilet would be better if they were bigger albeit they were quite clean

I picked up the horribly long waiting time for the luggage after almost an hour of waiting (there were no other flights at that time). It is worth improving the cleanliness and smell of the toilets. The entrances are full of cigarette butts and the stench of cigarette smoke - despite the information about the possibility of smoking in designated places, the staff does not enforce it from passengers. Very high prices in bars.
The check-in and security were very quick. One bottle of water was quite expensive. This is a very nice but quite small airport and there isn't much choice where to go but it was OK for me.
When I got out of the plane, there was no bus shuttle to the terminal but this is understandable because of the Coronavirus. Border control was fast and my experience at the airport was pleasant.

One of the worst experiences - disrespectful behaviour of the staff is a standard. I fly in and out every two weeks and do a year now I can recollect any pleasant experience. staff responsible for a fast track- every time I am “greeted” with questions do I have a right to use the fast track - and that’s even before I show my status card. Flying into Poznan airport is fast and completely fine. Flying out is a drag! The security check is always busy- if two gates are open, consider yourself lucky- queuing takes a lot of time and is completely inefficient.

Staff a bit typically surly which doesn't bother me but upsets the Mrs and others at times. Pretty fast and straightforward although they could do with showing the world cup match on a screen in a bar etc somewhere. In departure lounge the gents toilets were disgustingly filthy with the urinals all near overflowing, with a lot of urine on the floor and 3 cubicles for a dozen terminals a huge queue of men constantly. Utterly ridiculous. Free WiFi with ambiguous marketing terms seems a con.

We arrived from Rome with Ryanair bussed quickly to the terminal which is new bright and clean. Luggage arrived almost in a blink of an eye. Easy navigation to the exit with a stop in a clean toilet several ATMs very convenient. 15 mins from the moment we landed to the car pick up. Highly recommended airport nice experience.

Staff appeared blunt and rude - unwilling to help. Lack of smiles and kindness within. Security checks is at the gate, therefore you cannot relax knowing you have to go through the stress of checks after getting to the airport. At the security checks, staff are once again blunt and demanding. For example, shoes have to be taken off if wearing anything other than trainers. No toilets past security checks, therefore you have to try not to wee on the floor. When asking if I could go, as this was not described prior, was told I would have to be escorted there. This adds to the already uncomfortable atmosphere of the airport. Unfortunately you have to fly to and from here to experience Prague, but overall, a very unsatisfied customer.

I flew from Prague to Rome Ciampino on Ryanair. I prefer using public transport Metro + the very comfortable Trolleybus 59 combo especially during rush hours. The 'AE airport express' is risky using very busy roads. Both Terminals 1&2 are modern, easy to navigate and especially love the large supermarket (charging regular prices) with fresh pastry, bread and fresh fruits. The mornings are busy with many flights departing but security in T2 was very fast. I had no luggage to drop-off this time. The air side is getting better with various shops and eateries. I still think the gates and corridors (Gates C) are a bit bland with more seating needed but that's just a personal taste. I rarely had any negative experiences flying from or to Prague with arrivals equally easy. I appreciate the Uber reservation kiosks with clear instructions for those taking a car to the city. My only big criticism is that I strongly advise against exchanging currency here due to lack of 'choice'. Some minor works on the exterior of T1 causing mininal disruption. Looking forward to seeing the planned green transformation of the areas Infront of both terminals with greenery and trees on the surface & traffic below.

Queue for passport control took an hour despite not a huge amount of people to handle. Only 3 open for non EU and 13 including machines open for EU. Most the guys on EU had a nice hour break. Bags on time but you expect so after an hour delay.

Rudest member of staff I have ever encountered in security. She screamed in my face "madam, I asked if you had any liquids, open your bag!" She saw a jar and said "what is that?".. it was a candle. She didn't have the manners to apologise and left me highly embarrassed. I returned to Dublin where I was greeted by friendly staff, which should be customary when visitors your country. We were then left waiting in a bus to our airplane for twenty minutes in 31 degree heat without any explanation. Then a further 10 minute wait when we got to the plane.

Terminal 1 at the airport employs a dated security setup, with individual security checks for each gate rather than a centralized system, a system long abandoned by any modern airports. Upon passing through security, I discovered that my flight was delayed. The inconvenience continues as any attempt to access refreshments or restrooms necessitates leaving the secured area and undergoing security procedures once more upon return—a frustrating and time-consuming experience. This approach requires an excessive number of security staff and technology, resulting in consistently long queues and an overall sluggish process. Additionally, the lack of a predetermined wait time at security means passengers must factor in a contingency for potential delays at security, adding to the overall inconvenience. Regrettably, this airport's shortcomings extend beyond its security procedures. Upon arrival, passengers are facing queues at passport control and wait quite some time for checked luggage. Nothing is working properly. The airport is inefficient and unfriendly.

Disgusting. Terrible queue, complete mess. The airport is featuring this distributed security control for each individual gate. Looks like they are not capable to match the capacity of the flight with capacity of the security check. Unfortunately, the long queues everywhere is a sort of normal for Prague.

Very clean airport, arrival and departure very well organized. Lots of places to sit with a view of the runway in the departure hall. The Billa supermarket located in the airport terminal is a good choice. Transport from/to the airport very easy.

I've read some negative reviews, but had a good experience myself. Arrival was smooth (the parts inside the airports control). A short queue at customs and easy to find my way around. Departure was overall good. Not overcrowded like a UK airport, with good eating/shopping options and family/kids areas. My flight was delayed so took a couple of hours sleep in the airside hotel which was good value. The only let down was a pretty long queue for security and lack of seating post security - then my airline had delays/drama, but no fault of the aiport. I'd fly here again.

Airport staff were unfriendly, unhelpful and rude. Flight was delayed and no information was transmitted, when asked they simply said “look at the board” of which was not actually on show. The boarding gate was B10. When asked to make an announcement as other passengers on the flight were still waiting under the belief that that flight still had another one hour delay the said “we can not do that” aka they could not make an announcement to passengers? Will not be returning through this airport so substandard disgusting service.

My flight had been delayed so I arrived later at the airport however check-in had closed (as check-in times had not been amended!). The security team were really helpful in scanning my bike box and ensuring it got to the gate to be loaded on the plane. The team were very friendly and supportive with a great result. Thanks!

My son, who is epileptic, had a seizure during the security check in. We had already requested Special Assistance at the desk, and the airport team were incredibly helpful and took us to a quiet room to wait until our flight was called. They checked on us every 15 minutes, and arranged a wheelchair and preferential boarding once the Gate opened. They also ensured that the crew were aware of our situation, and forwarded the request for assistance to Gatwick.

My wife, my daughter and I were waiting at the gate to fly to Vienna. Suddenly a man in charge of the security wanted to control again the identity of my wife and ask her a lot of questions probably to make that her passport was not falsified. It took 20 mn. She was the only person controlled among at least 200 passengers waiting, she felt very uncomfortable and finally discriminated.

Airport with the slowest and least professional staff ever. Greece is beautiful, I love its rhythms ... but here we are absurd. 3 planes in one day, and the ability to wait 2 hours to check in your baggage. Once I got to the check-in desk I was asked to wait a moment. 8.50 am, flight at 9.15 a.m. I waited 5 minutes and asked what the problem was and the lady told to go to a colleague at another check-in desk. Slow, disorganized, unprofessional staff. Bad experience.

Queue, queue, queue. It's all you do at Preveza Airport in Greece. If my next holiday to Greece involves flying into this airport, I'll change my holiday plans. On arrival we were met with extensive queues outside the terminal building; two-and-a-half hours later we still hadn't checked in! But it didn't stop there - once we had checked in and had our luggage weighed we then had to queue up for another half hour with our luggage to have it scanned and taken off us. More queues for security and toilets airside left a really bad taste in the mouth and I would advise anyone against using this airport if they can possibly help it.

This is a very small airport on an island. You have to get a ferry and a bus to reach it both free of charge. It is in a lovely setting surrounded by trees. The facilities are very limited with only one very small cafe no shops but that is all part of the charm.

Been coming here since 1993. The airport has grown, been destroyed in hurricanes and now 3 years after the last hurricane it is starting to recover. However in the new and improved departure area (gates) there is only 1 bathroom. 6 toilets in the women’s and 2 family toilets. This is crazy. All kinds of fancy new fixtures but the hand dryers don’t work. Worse the staff is rude and doesn’t care. They are too busy chatting to each other. Despite the repairs the airport is still dreadful.

American Airlines to Miami. Check in was quick and smooth - I had multiple segment flights (on one booking) - Miami - Madrid - London - Manchester, and my luggage was checked all the way though to Manchester. The check in opened at 11.30, 3 hours before flight and there was a priority lane for business class and One world status customers. Although the general queue was small. I was there at 11.45. Outgoing passport control also very quick. Security efficient - shoes and belt off, but iPad and electronics remained in my carry on. There are 2 lanes - so this could get busy if travelling on the Air France or KLM widebody flights. The departure area is still being rebuilt - but it was pleasant non the less. Large fans in the first (upstairs) seating area kept the place cool. A couple of sandwich outlets including Dominoes. I had a large Turkey and Cheese panini (hot) and a bottle of coke for $17. Small duty free kiosks as well. Down a ramp to the gate area - a lot of seating and not crowded, despite the KLM flight waiting as well as my AA. There a large central bar area - I didn't buy anything so cant comment on price. Boarding about 40 mins before departure. If you are travelling with hand luggage and have not had to check in, make sure the gate agents check your passport before attempting to board. We walked along the apron, passed the KLM A330 to our plane - boarding front and rear. Boarding completed well before departure time. Left early - unfortunately we took off towards the sea - so we didn't see the tourists on Maho beach preparing to get sand blasted. Overall a great experience - much better that I envisaged

Arrived with no issue. Bags were delivered in a timely manner, rental car booth was easy to find, and plenty of restrooms available. The departure was another story altogether. The line through immigration was a bit long, and then security was even longer. It kept moving so it wasn't terribly bad. The airport has been renovated and the shopping area inside the terminal is new and very open. The "restaurants" in the outer area before security serve their purpose, but nothing fancy. We were departing from gate B2, located on the lower level of the terminal. We walked down the stairs into utter mayhem. There must have been 700 people all standing around waiting for their flights. Then the announcements started - this airline looking for Mr and Mrs So and So. Then that airline looking for Mr. Such and Such. Then that flight being delayed until whatever. Then, all the while we heard nothing about our flight. The scheduled boarding time came and went and finally the pre-board announcement was made. We were sitting, but all the people around the gate started crowding in. All the while the PA announcements kept going on and on. We noticed the gate agent saying something and another surge from the crowd to the gate. No announcement and we wondered what was going on so we walked over and found out that our section was being called to board. Again announcements for every other flight in the airport - not ours. We got through and made it on to a bus to take us to the waiting aircraft only to sit there while two more boarding groups were called. Total chaos mishandled by Delta.

I only have one experience (departure) from this airport but not so good. The problem is that they are unprofessional - the border police probably never saw my eu resident permit and wanted to prove that is fake, I lost more than 1 hour and I needed to run to airplane with a small child. However they had no reason to think it is fake. Some police don't know or want to speak English. Check in - from 3 counters, 2 were not working, many people in row. Security checking - good.

The biggest problem with this airport is unprofessional and inconsistent service. Rules are being arbitrarily enforced, business check in desks are used by economy passengers, mobile boarding pass would not work so even if you have no bag to check you need to queue for 30 min to get a paper boarding pass. The biggest problem is the lack of professionalism.

Small, clean and efficient as some of the previous reviewers have said. Outside of this, the customer service needs major work in terms of communication between the customers and internal steakholders. Had a flight delayed for over 5 hrs, for 4 of those hrs there was no info on what fhe status of the flight was or anyone to talk too in regards to the flight. Was stuck in the terminal with no way to get out.

Since the new modern terminal was inaugurated traveling to Pristina has become more convenient and a more pleasant experience than before. All needed facilities are here in a minimum amount of space. But it feels very fresh and airy though. The new terminal really is great and pretty much everything has improved since the old terminal isn't used anymore.

Travelled from Göteborg Landvetter Airport to Pristina in July and returned to Göteborg in August. The airport of Pristina is very compact and small. It has a restaurant in the check-in area and some shops. In the departure area there is a duty-free shop small but has some good stuff in it. When arriving to Pristina we had to walk all the way to the arrival hall which in my opinion looks very old. Baggage took a long time to get to the baggage carousels and they were on the wrong carousel. They were on the carousel for a Swiss flight instead of where they should've been. Staff were very helpful helped us to take the bags down from the carousel and explained to us that there was a misunderstanding between the staff. But one bad thing is that they didn't bring baggage carts so we had to carry the baggage all the way to the car waiting for us but the walking distance to the parking is really short so frankly it was not a big deal. When departing there were enough baggage carts and the whole check-in process and everything worked pretty smoothly and fine. They're currently on the final phase of building the brand new terminal which can be seen from the runway. Hopefully when I arrive and depart next time it will be from the fresh and modern new terminal.

No change in Pristina airport. It continues to be small and efficient. The staff are polite and there is not much queuing. On arrival the baggage arrived quickly. The bar before the passport control is still the best place to wait. Wireless internet in the departure lounge is free and works well. There is a small but smart duty free shop.

Small clean efficient. The departure terminal is well run there's a nice bar though the windows have been covered with some coloured adhesive plastic preventing from a view to the runway. Everything is so simple and hassle free that one does not need to arrive hours before departure time. Very nice indeed.

Back to Pristina in February. The airport now has a proper baggage reclaim and is looking a little more finished. The departure lounge has another shop and increased size. It is still best to use the bar before immigration. Overall this is still a good little airport.

The great thing about this airport is its size. It is small. And that means a short walk from the aircraft through the building and out. Baggage reclaim is basic - you take it from the baggage truck outside but that is efficient and quick. The arrivals area appears unfinished. Check in and departure are also quick and easy. If you want a drink in a nice bar use the place before the immigration. After that there is only a small bar. The duty free shop is cheap and quite well stocked. There is wireless Internet at the airport but it does not work.

The airport has a capacity of 1 million passengers a year. It has two terminals passenger terminal and cargo. It is a nice small airport. There is a bar in the waiting lounge and also a restaurant a place where you can buy newspapers At the terminal it also a new Restaourant lot of airline companies has their offices in the airport building including British Airways Adria Austrian Airlines etc. You can not sleep in the airport is closed after the last scheduled flight at 22:00 pm Pristina center is very close as there is a Motel Aviano located 1.5 - 2 km from the airport. There is no buss service from airport to the city but the majority of travellers use taxi to get to the town. The price is usually 25 euro.

What's not to like about TF Green Airport. It was recently ranked the 2d best airport by Travel & Leisure readers. Its newly remodeled bathrooms are like those of a 5 star hotel. Going through TSA-Pre was a breeze. Cleared security in less than 5 minutes. Distances from security area to either end of the terminal are manageable. WiFi is fast and worked flawlessly. This used to be my home airport before I relocated to the Dallas area and it remains one of my favorite airports to fly through.

This airport is consistently name among the best small airports in the USA. Shops and eateries that were shuttered because of Covid have now reopened. The airport is in the process of adding more amenities and concessions. The newly renovated bathrooms are amazing. They're brightly lit and significant improvement over the pre-existing bathrooms. Security was a breeze. There was no line and I walked right up to the TSA counter and cleared security in less than 5 minutes. The distances from the security area to either end of the terminal are manageable. WiFi is fast and worked flawlessly.

There is a reason why this airport is consistently named among the best small airports in the USA. Thanks to COVID, some shops and eateries have shuttered and not reopened to date. Security was a breeze. There was no line and I walked right up to the TSA counter and cleared security in less than 10 minutes. There is a spill over of passengers from the gate area to the concourse, nonetheless, there is enough space to navigate the concourses. The Escape Lounge is a welcome addition to this airport.

Terrible wait times and lines. This is my 3rd experience with an unacceptable wait in the security line at this airport. Many people around me were within minutes of missing flights due to the incredibly slow, understaffed security lines. Be careful flying from this airport.

This is by far the worst experience I have ever had with an airport. I arrived an hour and 30 minutes ahead of my flight and missed my flight due to a failure with TSA. It took over an hour and 30 minutes to have my carry on bag checked and to go through the detectors. Also, the workers were very rude about the whole process. I overheard many people asking “what do I need to do if I miss my flight?”, “I have somewhere I need to be at a certain time what do I do?”. The response to these questions was “you’ll just have to book another flight” and “take that up with your flight provider.” I understand that things happen and technology fails and situations occur, but I was very disappointed with how the staff handled the situation. I was also told “just leave and come back before your flight.” Well, not everyone lives around this area and not everyone is able or capable of leaving for 12 hours and coming back whether that be due to funds or time constraints. Due to my experience here at Providence airport, I more than likely will not be returning mainly because of how unprofessional and how indifferent the staff was. I hope that no one else has this experience.

There is a reason why this airport was ranked among the top airports in the country. Its very easy to navigate, the facilities are very clean and there is free wifi for 30 minutes. Security is a breeze with the lines moving very quickly. The TSA staff are pleasant and friendly. There are several food options here ranging from fast food, coffee to sit down restaurants. Wolfgang Puck's and the Providence Oyster Bar are highly recommended. There are also a number of retail shops with Brooks Brother among the more prominent ones. Plenty of restrooms which are not only clean but maintained at regular hourly intervals.

I was extremely impressed with Providence TF Green Airport. It is high up on the list of my favorite small airport and here’s a lowdown on it: The Terminal: It is all very straightforward, with everything well signposted and not complicated at all. Security is efficient and the multiple times we’ve gone through there wasn’t much line at all. After Security, there is a decent selection of Shops and Dining. The shops include the standard souvenir and news shops, plus a few interesting clothes and accessory shops. Food-wise there is a small but good variety of places to eat, ranging from a Dunkin Donuts to an Oyster Bar. The seating in the terminal is comfortable and regularly equipped with charging outlets. The Wi-Fi is nothing special, free for 30 minutes, but at least it’s there. Connections: Norwegian Air advertises the airport as Boston/Providence. While Providence isn’t too far from Boston it is still a good hour driving. The RIPTA bus service passes reasonably frequently and is a good way to get to downtown Providence. I recommend that or the Peter Pan Coach over the MBTA train as that passes infrequently and only works on weekdays. To get to Boston using Public transportation I would recommend taking the Coach as the train not only rarely passes but it takes forever as it stops at every station along the route. And there it is. A nice little airport, clean and with good amenities. The main problem is the lack of connections, especially late at night, which might make an uber the only option. I really recommend it though, even as a low-cost alternative to Boston.
Very nice airport. Small, short ways with quick check-in, short TSA waits, short Gate walks and free wifi for 30 minutes.

Flew in from Baltimore on Southwest. What a great little airport! Easy to navigate spotless facilities fast wifi and good options for coffee and snacks. A great alternative to Boston for access to Cape Cod.
Quick lines through security and it is a better option than flying out of Logan with the longer lines. Airport restaurants/bars are limited but OK for all the longer that you will be there.

Worst airport ever. Long lines, no seating and not helpful staff. Unbelievably unorganized and constant delays. Avoid at all costs. We had a perfect trip other than this airport. We will not be back due to this airport. Again, avoid this airport.

Absolutely atrocious staff, management and handling of any airport I have ever been to. Someone needs to take this airport over or they will ruin their tourism industry for TC. Airport is run down, dirty, and cannot accommodate their travelers. It’s obvious that air traffic control is incompetent at this airport. I’d venture to say all departments lack management, service etc.they will scream at you until you comply with whatever it is they want you to do. Upon arrival, we were screamed at for getting a rental car inside the rental car area. For no reason. We had hour long lines both times we checked in for no reason other than disorganization.

This airport is in dire need of demolition and reconstruction. Arrival was not bad thanks to TCI Fast Track and departing wasn’t bad until you are done the process and in the terminal which is dirty, outdated, crowded, uncomfortable. The men’s room toilets were overflowing, the air conditioning was pretty much non existent, seating areas are lacking both downstairs and upstairs. For such a beautiful island I would think the government would spend a little money making their airport more modern. As much as I love traveling to Turks, the airport is awful and unless you are staying at a resort the rest of the island needs some serious cleaning.

This is by far the most screwed up airport I have ever been in, and I've been in plenty! They seem to care nothing about visitor's comfort or convenience. I can hardly believe that they treat visitors to their island so poorly especially considering the high cost of staying there. No place to sit or wait other than an overpriced bar (yes, even for an airport), or a restaurant which is also overpriced with terrible service and unbelievably awful food - it's like no one cares (which is the same vibe we get from just about everyone on Grand Turk as well). Lines of people extending out into the traffic flow - no place to sit and wait.
