We were not even allowed to stand outside the airport on the pavement to wait for a family member arriving on another flight. We didn't quite know what to do as there was no seating inside either. The very rude airport personnel outside didn't help any either! I have been to Turks and Caicos 4 times now as I love the water and the excellent snorkeling but am now considering elsewhere, at least until they get their act together with their airport. Not worth spoiling the start and end of a vacation by having to deal with this airport!

TCI is a beautiful, welcoming island with fabulous accommodations, great beaches, wonderful restaurants, plenty to do, etc.  However, the government obviously has a policy of treating visitors terribly upon arrival and departure. This was my wife’s and my third visit, and it has only gotten worse. Evidently their desire is to cut down on the large number of tourists visiting by making arrival and departure tortuous, you have succeeded. Upon finally boarding our plane back to the US, my wife turned to me and said, “We need to consider other options for our next trip, I can’t afford the mental cost of coming and going here”. I readily agreed and our plan for a fourth visit to TCI was quickly moved to the dustbin. I strongly recommend that anyone considering a trip to TCI consider other destinations until this airport is improved.

The airport customs are very long over an hour long and it is very hot. The departure was the worse when you arrive everything is fine until you get to security they take again over an hour. Once you get into the airport has some small shops, barely any seats and the floor is dirty old carpet. Their is a nice outside plane spotting area though. No WiFi. Though this place sucks you can't avoid it if you want to go to Turks and Caicos because it's the only international airport on the island.

Turks and Caicos is a very nice place, but the airport is very bad. Coming here was bad, we had to wait over an hour to get through immigration. Place was understaffed, only three people working, and there was like 8 booths open for visitors. Baggage took 15 minutes also. Coming back from PLS was even worse. Our flight was an hour and a half delayed due to "weather", but it was because the ATC was offline for an hour, according to an American Airlines captain. To make matters worse, we had a connecting flight in Charlotte, NC (CLT) that goes on to Austin, TX (AUS). On top of that, seating was awful. There were no seats, so we sat on the disgusting ground with my kids for 2.5 hours. There was no air conditioning on an 85 degree day. We were able to make the 50 minute connection in CLT (originally had 2 hours 35 minutes) only because the second leg was 20 minutes delayed and we had to sprint from security near Terminal E to Terminal A which is on the other side of the airport. Thank the Providenciales airport & staff, because they totally caused this to happen. Also we didn't get luggage at final destination, but is on the next flight from Charlotte.

My wife and I had a great time in Turks and Caicos Islands. I was selected for a special search at the gate upon departure. My wife was ordered to board the aircraft but refused. She was informed that she would also be searched. The female employee was very rude and abrupt to her. I contacted the tourist website. I was informed via email that this is a common complaint from visitors. The gentleman wrote that he personally has been subjected to rudeness at this airport. He asked for permission to forward my communication to the TCI airport authority where it will no doubt be ignored. Turks and Caicos Islands is a beautiful place with wonderful people- and a pitiful airport.

The airport at Turks and Caicos is the worst airport I have ever experienced. Turks and Caicos Islands are among the most expensive islands, the require travelers to purchase insurance policies before arrival and then pack people like sardines in an unairconditioned airport. I’ve been to this island several times but will not return until they do something about this airport. Absolutely disgusting!

Totally understaffed, much too small to handle the traffic. Everyone was crammed in which is very unsafe in covid times. The staff are apathetic and rude. They are intermittently enforcing mask rules if they see someone they want to pick a fight with. Others including their own employees are left maskless no problem. Security guard has her mask on her chin and she was supposed to be the force enforcing these rules. What a joke. They don’t enforce social distancing at all. They squirt cheap cleaning fluid on your hands and think this is a safety measure. There are hundreds of people in there and one tiny restaurant to feed them all. It was over 80 degrees in July in this place. This place is unsafe and needs help. But they can’t seem to help themselves as they are so mean to the tourists bringing in the cash. I’ll not be going back.

Cataratas del Iguazú International Airport (IGR) A small regional airport specifically to allow tourists to access the Iguacu waterfalls on the Argentinian side. Check-in on the ground floor with a small number desks which open about 2 hours before a flight. Security up an escalator and were very quick. Opens into a small Duty Free type shop followed by a cafe and a business lounge and then a Hard Rock Cafe. Some seating by each of the 6 gates which quickly get overwhelmed when A330 sized aircraft are on stand. There are some work benches at the far end with stools and electrical plugs for charging. All felt small but efficient and friendly. Restricted view of the runway and apron through some frosted glass. Boarding via airbridges relatively quick. Runway small so take-off quick so as not to block the runway/taxiway.

Puerto Maldonado airport serves those who travel to the Amazon. It's small airport only 3 or 4 airlines operate flight daily. Very organized. Inside there are some shops and also there is one lounge for priority pass. No boarding bridges. Also they don't have luggage scanners. They check all luggage by hand after you give your check-in baggage. Overall good service.

That airport is very close to downtown Puerto Princessa and is located around a green area. Airport looks quite new and it was efficient to use. Got my luggage within 10 minutes. Check in was also efficient. There are some souvenir shops in departure hall and some simple food stalls. After security check you find a waiting hall, on second level is a coffee bar and a food stall in the departure level some shops which are not too expensive. Overall a no thrills airport which is easy to use in all regards. Free Wifi available.

The Puerto Princesa International Airport had just opened its new terminal. The terminal was clean and brand new. The airport terminal had no jet bridge or ramp stairs so we had to deplane via an old fashioned staircase at the mercy of the weather, thankfully at that time it was already dark. The airport lacks formal transportation to the city center although the city streets is just a mere 10 minutes walk away. Definitely one of the best provincial airports in the Philippines if you consider dirt runways the norm.

It does not have water fountains or water bottle filling station. There is no seating area before check in if you come a little early. Otherwise nice little airport, easy to get around and small line up, easy security. We didn't eat or shop around so can't rate that.

As we know PV has become for so many of us a wonderful holiday escape destination and/or many of us are living here now! Great 6 millions + coming through the PVR airport (new records of last year) but they truly have to improve their arrival at PVR as it's quite pitiful now after you try to get out after going through immigration and claiming your luggages. We accept the fact that they have a right to really check all luggage now via security scan but PLZ use ALL of your scanning machines as when I came in, only two were used and the rest were sitting idle when the lines for waiting were just impossible! It's not they do not have the facilities or staff as many of them were just standing there and talking between each other... For me, it's a real lack of organization and I don't know anyone who is really happy facing arrival at PVR as most of us it's really mostly the opposite! Why can't they get better organized as the flow of tourists arriving daily is on the increase (they know about it) but this funnel style of checking us to get out truly needs much more attention as it should be much smoother and less frustrating. It's getting to be now one of the worse airport to arrive, totally frustrating when you see they have the techno to check our luggage via X-ray machines, but they only use the minimal of them. I just don't get it as PVR is NOT fun at ALL when you get there.

Clean airport but there are no drinking fountains and asking for a small amount at the food courts was refused. They will sell you bottle water for $8 . Refused to pay that and found a cola for $5 dollars. I guess it is the last fleecing of airport guests before you leave.

This airport is passable if you're the passenger. Have been through many times. Problem is if you are waiting for someone to arrive. No seats anywhere! Pricy food choices, super high taxi prices. It is clean though.

I love the PVR (Puerto Vallarta) airport. It is clean and well organised. It is reasonably well air-conditioned all-though a few areas might be considered too cold. Security is quick and efficient. Walk ways and waiting areas provide plenty of space and there are work stations with plug-ins. Directions are clearly marked and the airport is not huge. There is a good selection of restaurants and shops. My only complaint is that all the restaurants in the departure lounge close around 6 pm. That is unfortunate especially when your flight is delayed. It is interesting considering that most people in Mexico do not go for dinner till about 7 pm. You also would expect them to stay open longer since this is an international airport and there are plenty of late flights. This is by no means the only airport that has that problem though. 3 stars for food and beverages just because of times open. The quality is great.

After arriving you are assaulted by a phalanx of timeshare sellers and taxi and tour companies that descend like a plague of locusts. When you finally manage to be able to leave through the doors there is another school of hungry piranhas who descend on you offering you highly overpriced taxi rates or tours. Just exit to the left walk up the stairs and cross the pedestrian bridge to hire a taxi at one fifth the price. Leaving isn’t much better, don’t be surprised to pay 5 dollars for a bottle of water, or ten dollars for a crappy slice of pizza. This place should be bulldozed and build something not controlled by crooks.

As far as arriving, expect a long line to Passport Control. The wait was approximately one hour. However, the agents were very fast and efficient. I believe they were so glad to finally get tourists to Mexico that they sped up the process inspecting passports. At Customs, you are required to press a button on a "traffic light" device. If green, you may proceed. If red, you will be approached by a Customs agent. Once leaving Customs, be prepared to be approached by people trying to sell you time shares or offering you transportation. It's best to have your transportation prearranged as once outside the airport, it is a "madhouse." As far as departure, it can be hard to find a drop off point as traffic is very heavy. Security was fairly fast and staff were pleasant. Not a bad experience.
The airport is hot and sticky. They have AC but only use it to keep the temperature at around 26 degrees. There is a serious lack of information about flight delays and gate changes.

Waited 1.5 hrs in line for Sunwing to check us in. There were 10 people outside with the buses but only 3 at the check in! Numerous flights to check in people with only 3 attendants, not good service. Westjet beside our line moved very rapidly.

After being treated in a rude and abusive manner by some local person who decided he could hold up an entire Air Transat flight from Calgary (February 28, 2018) by slowly and methodically reviewing every passport supposedly looking for v entry visas, knowing the flight originated in Canada, we then had to depart today March 11. Going through security, they confiscated wooden knitting needles that my wife uses for intricate design. Old and very difficult to replace. We had already confirmed with the airline that we could fly with these on-board. Also, my wife flies internationally as an Executive VP of a major energy company. Every flight, every security, around the world did not have a problem. These incompetent people at security would not listen to our explanation, used no common sense. With these experiences, arriving and departing, that's it for Puerto Vallarta in our future travel plans!

If you arrive at Pula Airport and you want to park your car it looks like a normal parking. The first 15 minutes is free of charge, one hour is one euro that they didn’t write what it cost for a day. This is unbelievable because I was asking two police officers and they didn’t want to answer me and when I go inside to the information office, they only loss and say hello this is Croatia. That means that you pay €24 for one day of parking.

Pula is one of my favourite airports to arrive to (it takes sometimes 15-20 min to get through). I travelled to Pula in July and return experience was as usual, quick, swift and enjoyed the upstairs open space. Arrival in September was the same. The problem was the departure in September. Transavia and Ryanair flights were one hour apart causing moderate number of passengers at the airport. I arrived 2hr 15min prior to flight with hand luggage only and tried to pass the security. There was nobody in the queue. I was refused entry since the flight was not "loaded on the system" and asked to wait until 2h prior to scheduled departure. This created surge of people at the exact time causing a queue at the security check without any social distancing measures. At the ticket check after I had my boarding pass scanned I was asked to present UK Visas and Immigration document (self isolation declaration) to the airport staff. There are two issues here and I hope somebody from the airport team is reviewing these comments. As a healthcare professional and on the front line of COVID-19 I am trying to distance myself. The airport queuing system is doing exactly the opposite - they are preventing a free flow of passengers and creation of queues. I think this is a very poor practice putting at risk staff and passengers with large numbers of people without any good reason. Another issue is being asked to present UK Government document to the airport staff. I am following the rules and have paperwork ready but this is nothing to do with Croatian authorities and feel this is inappropriate invasion of my privacy. 5/10 I am afraid, I hope this is a one off and next year we are back to normal.

Worst airport in Europe I have ever visited. Although the staff at the check in desks do their job, they firstly don't do it with much of a smile, but once checked in thats when the problems start. We departed on a Sunday, that had about 4 flights departing roughly at the same time, and it was total chaos trying to get through Security. They only have 2 conveyor belts trying to cope with about 1500 people all trying to pass through security at the same time. The queue to get to one of the check points was about 40 mins and it snaked around departures so much that eventually airport staff had to take charge and make the queuing line zig zag to avoid blocking the doors and check in desks. Eventually, because they knew that people would actually miss their planes, they then started taking people out of the queue who were on the next flights, and moving them to the front of the line. Once you got to security the staff were rude, with one security man physically shoving me out of his way so he could get to talk to one of his colleagues. They snatch your belongings off you as you try and put them in the trays to go through the x-ray machine, and shove your trays through before you have even finished trying to put your stuff in. Awful place. I'd rather fly in somewhere else and drive!

Really small airport but everything went fine. Fast check in and fast security check. There’s only one coffee shop - 17 kuna for a cappuccino and 14 kuna for water is a decent price. People speak English and are friendly. The WiFi works fine but you have to get the password from the personnel (I asked a girl from the duty free shop). Taking 2 points away only because the WiFi password is not available somewhere and you have to ask and there are no nice seating areas.

What chaos. As others have said there is poor customer relations at this airport. Queues for security and passport are horrendous, taking 1.5 hours as there are so few people working and then staff seem to spend time talking rather than providing a service. No monitoring of other people jumping queues even though staff were standing around. If you have to use this airport then allow loads of time. Can not comment on any of facilities airside as we had to run for our plane after getting through passport control

I've been flying in and out of Pula Airport at least four times a year for the past ten years and have witnessed the rise of passenger traffic back to its late 1980-ies levels. Since this small regional airport caters primarily to tourists, crowds are intense in peak summer months, quickly outstripping the airport's capacity to fluidly handle passenger flows. Outside of that period, it provides a really pleasant and refreshingly uncomplicated experience. For its small size, there are plenty of car rental agencies to choose from. Resolving formalities of a rented car, checking in and going through security takes no more than 30 minutes. Arrivals are similarly straightforward and if weather allows, one simply walks the apron from the aircraft to the terminal building. Services are basic, with a coffee shop in the entrance hall, another one in the departures area, a well-stocked duty free and a tiny business lounge. There is plenty of room for improvement, particularly in the proactive assistance to passengers and providing up-to-date flight information.

Terrible customer service. We needed help as we missed our flight. The staff just shrugged and said I don't know what you do and were very rude. Needs a lot of improvement and staff need to be taught how to talk to people with respect. Will not be returning.

This must be one of the worst airports I have ever used. Arrival from the UK aboard a BA flight was fine, although the queue through passport control was substantial. The departure was a painful affair. Long queues through security which is not geared towards catering for families (was travelling with an 18 month baby), one cafe post security, charging extortionate prices even for the most rudimentary sandwich, one chaotic duty free shop and no waiting area to speak of: tired and frustrated passengers were all herded together in the departures hall, with the lucky few who managed to find a free seat carefully guarding it for fear of losing it if should they leave it for a second. Free airport wifi does not work. Airport staff unhelpful even if they see you struggling with a toddler and a pushchair: you need to go down a flight of stairs to reach the plane and there is no help provided (as soon as the gate opens there is a mad rush to reach the airplane and it is not possible to safely descend the steps whilst carrying a baby and a pushchair). There is no baby changing facilities! A horrid airport experience, will not be using this airport again.

Arrivals fine, landed and out in about 20 mins. Departure back to UK horrendous, queued for 2.5 hours to check in and passport control. No aircon, kids fainting. 2 scanners for hundreds of passengers, seriously needs updating. Leave plenty of time.

Bearing in mind that the arriving / departing passengers here are enjoying a holiday in Istria the welcome is not a good one. Packed buses to the terminal when there could be an option to just walk the few yards to it? Steps and more steps up into the terminal with no directions to a lift for the less than fit to use. After that all OK except the airport staff please smile! You are welcoming people to spend money in your country and first impressions can cloud the overall experience. Departure has horrendous queue's to check in, crowded departure lounge. I did appreciate the outdoor space there though. Once again no smiles! It was all quite officious and why I had to be called back to have my boarding pass checked twice I have no idea, I'm an almost 70 grandmother. Again steps and more steps, crowded bus, no option to walk to the plane. The words "Customer Care" come to mind. Could do better!

This is a very small airport serving the island of Pulau Redang in Malaysia. It resembles an airstrip more than an airport and serves only one airline - Berjaya Air. There is also only 1 building with separate arrival and departure halls and 2 small commercial shops selling souvenirs. There is no air-conditioning. The baggage crew will collect the baggages from the plane and trolley them to the arrival hall where you would have to claim them. There are no baggage belts. Coaches would be waiting right outside the doorsteps once you clear immigration to transport you to your pre-booked resorts. Journey is about 10-12 minutes from the airport to Berjaya Redang Resort where most people travelling via Berjaya Air would end up.

The airport resembles a fanciful but tired air-strip. Situated in Kampong Tekek and near the ferry jetty the entire airport is open-air in concept. There are separate arrival and departure gates all housed in a wooden building with 1 small souvenir shop and 1 duty-free liquor shop and washrooms in the middle. Baggage trolleyed from the plane to the baggage claim area where passengers must step forward to collect before clearing customs. Resort coaches will be waiting at the arrival gate to fetch guests.

I had one of the most worst experience on Pune airport. Security staff is so rude and bad. They took my moisturizer and face wash on the name of extra liquid. I have travelled through many airports but no other Security staff even never faced such thing at such a big Delhi airport which is international. Security staff think themselves as boss. They are so rude. I have paid extra for my baggage and still took my stuffs.

Incompetent security, very slow hence people have to wait in long queues. Then poor infrastructure, On 1st floor (near gate 8) no air circulation is happening, no proper air conditioning is there. Entire sitting area is full of mosquitos. We are spending huge money through tax and govt is just looting our money.

Most unfriendly and unorganised staff. Why can't someone check-in 3 hours befor the flight? I came from a nearby city to take a flight and had to wait as the counter opens only 2 hrs before. No facilities, unclean this place is.

Incredibly incompetent staff, almost missed our flight because they had "error in system" and they wouldn't care less to fix it, took them 1h to give us boarding passes. Please consider Mumbai, Taxi to Mumbai is not that much and will save you nerves and possibly missed flights.

I'm a resident of this city and I can honestly say that this is the worst airport in India. It is a defence airport but the state government has repeatedly shown their unwillingness to build a new one and that too from at least past 20-25 years. They simply hike the prices of land and then the subsequent govt cancels the proposal and bring in their own proposal to earn money. Pune is a base to big MNC's and educational institutes and I firmly believe that it deserves far better than this!

Very bad experience at Pune airport. Since we had a connecting flight they had not updated on the screen and also the boarding gate. Very disappointed with the services. It was nothing more than a bus stand. Secondly, there is nothing to eat and there are few shops which take double price and not at all worth.

Very poor quality of services, there is no lounge and no canteen for a meal or decent options to eat dinner. There are small vendors charging double price for water and similarly for tea in a tiny cup and that is also half full. There is no inspection or quality check for any shops. Too many ad-hoc changes at the airport from pick up to car movement and random rules. Now passengers have to walk far outside for a cab with a bad walkway to pull heavy suitcases outside. Pune is a big IT, pharma and auto hub but the quality of facilities and service are very poor.

Although capacity has been enhanced and facilities are relatively better, overall cleanliness and passenger comfort e.g. Efficiency of air conditioning is still far from satisfactory. I live in Pune and would want this airport to be one of the best in the true sense. Customer experience must be top class at such an important airport. There is a lot of room for improvement.

The Aerobridge 5 and 6 at Pune airport are really dirty and full of bird mess / pigeon droppings. As you get out of the plane or board it, one is stepping on pigeon droppings and this is very unhygienic and unaesthetic. Please make sure that birds are not allowed to nest in the Aerobridge and dirty the entry point to planes. Kindly clean these urgently. Also Belts at baggage arrival have the same problem and are full of bird droppings. No passenger wants their bags dirty and touching bird droppings while collecting baggage. Kindly address this serious hygiene issue urgently!
Not clean, not many shops open during the night. No maintenance at all. It's not lively. No professionalism. Hence I would not recommend this airport.

Probably one of the worst experiences that I have ever had with an airport. It was nice to look at but it seems few now what to do. I was traveling with a group of 30 and over 20 of us had problems getting to our departure terminal. It seemed like all needed to have our luggage opened and checked, that in itself was not bad. The process of checking was terrible. The agents had to constantly called some one else check to see if they were doing it. Four in our group made it within minutes of take off. You have a beautiful country but you will have join to the modern world in moving passengers. I’ll probably give you a couple of years to get it together and until then go back to Jamaica. They got it together. Maybe you should check them out and learn how move crowds

vSay what you may, but I have seldom had an issue with this airport. In today's world of checking in online, just pass the long lines at the check-in desks if not travelling with bags. Customs and immigration were quick and professional...no surprises. The check-in at both terminals is now air-conditioned. Duty-free was typically overpriced. Just smile and move on! I departed from Terminal A, and enjoyed a few overpriced airport beers, prior to boarding. Hey...it's an airport! Boarding the flight was painless with the bus to the plane. I did note, however, that the staff at the gate were a bit perplexed when I handed them my home-printed boarding pass. All good though. On the return flight, again, through immigration and customs in no time at all. Please remember, that if you are a citizen or a resident, there is a separate aisle for you to the right side of the arrivals hall.

This airport was very well-run when me and my family were here. We were going to Punta Cana for a family vacation through jetBlue. We were able to get through security smoothly and the customs and shuttles were fast! The food court provided a wide variety of foods for me and my family to choose from, and everything was very modern. The bathrooms were clean enough for usage. The only con about this airport was the lack of the jet bridge. It didn't help that it was raining upon our leaving Punta Cana. We experienced torrential downpour and had to quickly get onboard, and we were drenched by the time we were on the plane. But, there were also many good things about this airport and I would not mind visiting it again!

Hundreds waiting in one large room after a 9 hour flight. Immigration asking stupid questions like "why are you here' and "what's the purpose of your visit'.  We were  lined up on the tarmac whilst dogs individually sniffed us. Absolutely ridiculous. On leaving, I think we went through 5 or 6 Passport checks and an x-Ray. I've known nothing like it but, Mexico comes close.

We were departing Punta Cana on February 16, 2023 after a 7 day vacation at a resort in Punta Cana. We had a very bad experience during check-in for the following reasons: The AT check-in counter the clerk did not seem to know how to check-in. She needed her manager's assistance and did not speak very basic English. Her manager knew a little better English and when I reached out to him, he was rude. My wife was in a wheelchair and there was no consideration for expediting her check-in. The check-in agent did not seem to differentiate between normal person check-in and a disability person check-in. Although we reached the airport 3 hours before departure the check-in process took well over 2 hours leaving no time to charge my wife's portable oxygen concentrator. Air Transat services at Punta Cana airport needs improvements which is well under Air Transat's jurisdiction. Air Transat needs to ensure that the check-in personnel have better basic English competency. Due to the ordeal we went through we do not plan to use Air Transat services to Punta Cana in future. Please consider the above feedback so other future travellers do not have to go through the frustrations we experienced.

The worst experience of an airport I have ever had. Arrived two hours before a flight to JFK. Informed at check in queue that the desk was about to close (not true). Asked for COVID certificate - not a problem, it was on my phone. The WiFi in the airport was so poor it took me 15 minutes to login to the app to get the certificate. Next we were asked for our immigration certificate. The one I had completed was inbound only, even though it asks for your departure date, and we needed to complete a new one. The same problem with WiFi - my phone couldn't connect using WiFi to the internet to fill in the form. Neither at this point could my wifes. The lady from ServisAir behind the counter very kindly did it for us. We've now wasted 25 minutes due to poor WiFi coverage in the airport. Went to first line - about 100 metres long to have only our passport and boarding pass checked (not immigration, just a couple of airport officials). Was sent through a barrier to the left and had our passports and boarding passes taken from us - no explanation. We figured out we needed to head after our boarding passes and passports so got in line for the x-ray machine that had no trays. My wife went to find trays whilst I held the line. Through x-ray, had to ask an official where our passports were and was told we needed to get in another line - about 12 people in front of us. Two more airport officials were checking bags, unpacking clothes and swabbing for trace explosive elements. The line moved slowly (35 mins to take off) with one person working at the slowest possible speed whilst his colleague wrote down on paper the outcome of each bag check - welcome to the 1950s. When we eventually got the front, after my wife complaining to three different officials we would miss our flight, they simply logged our passports on the piece of paper, stamped our boarding passes with a blue 'e', and waved us on (No checks undertaken). I should add at this point that whilst in the line we had both been sniffed by a sniffer dog - presumably for drugs / explosives. We got ourselves fast tracked through the next line at immigration by showing our boarding passes and then ran all the way to the gate. The gate was closing and we made it with about 3-4 minutes to spare. We were then sniffed again by a second, different, sniffer dog. Onboard there were about 6 people behind us so close to being last on. Our connection at JFK was a dream compared to this place. i genuinely think it has put us off going back.

My home airport, thus I use it a few times a year. Check in has been as easy as anywhere else I have flown with similar wait times. Terminal A can get busy mid-day, but I have always found a seat. I never expect in any airport to find food and drink at bargain prices, thus not shocked. I see some talk of $6.00 coffee. I had a coffee for 150 pesos which is under $3.00. As a resident, I can bypass the hoards that arrive mid-day when entering the country. There is a lane set up for residents and citizens to the right of the concourse. I always feel a little guilty but, hey, I am a resident! Best try to get flights that do not arrive between 1-4pm. The baggage handler I had assist was obviously in cahoots with the customs official who tried to intimidate a "propina" out of me. He told me to leave it with the baggage guy. I left him nothing. The airport does need more capacity to process those arriving, or perhaps an automated system that is often found these days.

People that work here seem more preoccupied with talking amongst themselves than paying attention to customers. Although immigration has improved its processing of passengers, there are still quirks. Security procedures here are not lined up with US guidelines, they took a pair of nose hair trimming scissors from me that had a round tip and not even 1/2 in blade. Just absurd. Shops are expensive. 6 dollars for coffee from an automatic machine seems excessive.
This airport is just a joke. Queue for hours. Too small. Not enough seats. Worst business lounge ever. Disorganization at gates. Wifi very slow. Third world airport.

One would think that after 50 years PUJ would figure out how to operate an airport. Whoever runs the place has no clue with respect to airport operations or management. It is definitely a 3rd World airport. Customs and Immigration is ridiculous and laborious. Staff are extremely rude given it's a tourist airport. The departure lounge has maybe 200 seats for 5,000 travelers and 1 restroom. The worst part is the PA system won't tell you when aircraft are boarding until the last call. By then, you are scrambling to get to the plane. Check-in counters are open-air with no a/c. They think their thatched roof and open-air are cute but we want a/c when we get to the airport on 90 degree days. We've had enough sun and heat and don't want to sweat all the way to the plane. The coup de gras is some idiot thought it was a good idea to put a pool by the departure lounge so you can swim while waiting for your plane. Good news though. There will be a new airport in Bavaro to compete with PUJ. Should go a long way to put PUJ out of business. The new airport investors seem to know what they are doing and how to run a good airport. We will see. My advice is to fly in to Santo Domingo and get transportation to Punta Cana and avoid the hassles.

While this is a very attractive airport with few flights off season transfer between plane and terminal can be hazardous to elderly and infirm passengers. A bus with very high steps caused my wife to hurt her leg and later she needed medical attention. We witnessed other elderly travelers and children finding the bus steps difficult. On our return trip to Buenos Aires the Pluna station manager alerted by our hotel concierge arranged for a golf cart transfer and early boarding to the second row of the all economy jet. Why the Airport authorities don't operate a more customer friendly vehicle is a mystery. The airport departure tax at $29 each for the 40 minute flight is way out of line considering Ezieza in Buenos Aires charges $18 for long haul flights to the U.S. Once through the first of two security checkpoints travelers find themselves in a sizable duty free considering the size of the airport. For those heading to and from Punta del Este and other nearby Uruguayan resorts PDP is certainly the most convenient and is an hour closer to those towns than Montevideo Airport.

Long lines. Unable to hear employees calling for flights that need passengers to skip to front of lines that are 1 hour long. Missed my flight because they can’t communicate with passengers. I was literally there in line. I got a call asking if I was going on the flight. I confirmed I was but was waiting to check my bag. She told me check bag time for the flight ends 45 minutes before departure and it was too late for me and to find a representative. I cut everyone in line and spoke with a lady at the counter who said they announced for all people on my flight to go directly to the counter ahead of the line. I told her no one in line can hear anything they are saying. She said that’s what she’d been telling her coworkers. After she confirmed I couldn’t get a new flight for 2 days I sat and waited for my ride to come back and get me and I then witnessed an employee walk around and shout the names of 3 destinations whose flights were needing to have customers go to the front of the line immediately to check in. I was furious because had it been done sooner I could’ve been on my way home with my seven year old who was sobbing because he couldn’t go home to his dad. I will never use this airport again. I am so frustrated.

Very small airport which is not necessarily a problem. The problem we have every time we travel into or from PGD is that they have inconsistent rules nearly every time. We have TSA pre-check which we paid to obtain. At all other airports this allows us to leave our shoes belts and light jackets on as well as laptops and ipads in our bags. Not at PGD. Even though they hand us a piece of paper that identifies us as TSA pre-check travelers we have to remove belts, jackets and laptops/ipads nearly every single time. It is as if the TSA agents at PGD went to completely different classes than every other agent in the country. Not to mention how rude some of them can be about it as well. I really try to avoid this airport as much as possible.

They should spend more money on putting gates in the airport instead of a multi million dollar resort. Plus there isn't any place to eat and minimal places to sit. When a full plane comes in and you have to stand for a minimum of 1 hour it gets pretty bad - at least for seniors.
Excellent also it is not as large as other mainly international airports it is the largest airport in Shandong province. There are many attractive airlines and aircraft's in this airport.

Pretty good facilities. The negative side of this airport is the bad customer service from the custom officers. I had to fly to Singapore and lacked one of the documents that was not required from previous trips the custom officer told me that I was not allowed to pass immigration and confiscated my boarding pass. No more help was given other than telling me that someone from Singapore had to fax me or mail me the document. They left me hanging there. One of the young custom officers tried to help but was immediately directed away by his superior. If there is one thing to improve about Qingdao airport it would definitely be the level of service provided by the custom officers. At the end of the story the document they "required" can be printed within 2 minutes and was not required of course I missed my flight.

One of the smaller airports by Chinese standards but a very positive experience for the passenger. Good signage short distances to walk from plane to baggage carousel and a mere 10-minute wait for luggage to be on the belt. Good public transport to greater Qingdao region including resorts area by the sea. Beware of taxi touts go to the official taxi line where you get a taxi from a dispatcher who registers the ride and also hands out a complaint info card - just in case. When departing from Qingadao don't come to the airport too early. Check-in (also for international flights) is 120 min. before scheduled take-off and there is not much to do in this airport. Just some shops and two so-called coffee shops with a limited choice of snacks. Found out too late about a "VIP-lounge" which is hidden in a corner to the far right of the international departure lounge. Access charge is 100 yuan but had no time to use it. Friendly airport staff quick security check plenty seating at gates one restaurant one coffee shop and one airline lounge airside duty free and souvenirs. Facilities clean and well maintained. All in all a very positive impression.

Not a bad little airport. Plenty of space and seating if you need to wait a while. But like all most Chinese airports the departure shops are terrible and expensive. Bring your own snacks drinks or something to read. Nothing to see there but it is comfortable enough.
Not as big as Airports in Beijing and Shanghai that it is hard to navigate. It is very efficiently run and very clean. It is the best mid-size international airport in China

Really nice facility. The Olympic games in that city I am sure modernized the facility. Nice waiting area at departure area to wait with friends before immigration. Immigration was fast but was surprised by the friendliness and the "I hope you had a nice stay in our area" of the one person at immigration check with excellent english skills. Nice. Food selection and shops acceptable. Over all a good experience.

Nice modern airport. Efficiently run. Arrived here on an international flight from ICN and was bussed to terminal despite most finger docks being empty. Immigration was a breeze and luggate was efficiently delivered. On outgoing domestic flight to SZX our flight (Shandong airlines) didn't appear at all on the departure screens but was correctly displayed at the gate. Flight delayed and no announcements made. Good selection of outlets. Pleasant environment waiting for the plane - big bright airy. About 30 minutes drive out of Qingdao.

We flew out of YQB UA 3659 on Tuesday October 22, 2024 at 3:01 pm. I became very disabled after a bad fall in old Quebec Clty on Monday, October 14, 2024. After going to the Blessed Sacrement emergency, and having much pain due to pelvic fractures. After much pain, we had to delay flight plans back home from Oct16. I contacted UA for disability help. I was assured we would be taken care of at the car rental area and throughout the airport terminal; also YQB website assured they are very proud of their disability service. Fortunately, after Avis personnel refused to help, an airport employee saw us struggling to manage our luggage, walker and wheelchair and offered to help get us to Avis. Sadly, I had to beg for help because the response was, “Our airport is too small’ Finally, at Avis a young man behind the desk said, “I will help you.” And then took us to the UA Ticket Counter. He refused an offer of a tip. Then after getting baggage etc taken care of again we asked for help to go through TSA and boarding area. At first the response was again, “Our airport is too small,” Fortunately, a young woman said she would help. And she did with kindness and refused a tip. She dropped us off at boarding area after letting us get some food at a vendor and stopped so we could use the restroom. She said she would be back to help us get our boarding pass and onto the plane. SHE DID!! We are giving an excellent rating because of the people that did take the initiative to help us despite others refusing.

Still a well organized airport. We use the new international section. Clean and simple to use. Good staff (security and customs). Just expect that more international flights will be available soon from Québec.

Very rude and impatient security personnel. It wasn't very busy which was good. However, making sure instructions are enunciated and understood before being rude would be better served. The attendant that was supposed to be instructing you to enter metal detectors was more concerned with personal conversations than directing travelers and proceeded to yell at me advance, move! She was so far away from the metal detector I had no idea she was referencing me. Bad ending to an otherwise excellent trip.

We have traveled to many countries including throughout Europe, China, Russia, etc., but the Quebec airport is truly the most disorganized we have ever experienced. First, you can't check your luggage in until 2 hours prior to departure which means you have to drag your luggage everywhere until that time. We were coming off a cruise and were there 4 hours ahead of time. There were so many people, there was no where to sit. Then, when it was time to check in, it was huge lines with representatives giving out conflicting information, kiosks not working properly, etc. Once we did get ourselves checked in and went upstairs, the few food locations they had were jammed with very long lines. Maybe flying into this airport would be okay, but I would discourage anyone from flying out of this airport. It is utter confusion.
The Aéroport international de Québec is a good example to follow concerning quality of service and infrastructure. It's clean, well designed and the staff are professional and customer oriented.

Quebec City airport is very clean and comfy. Free and fast wifi with no submission or forms to fill or emails to wait for to validate the access. The whole terminal is bright and welcoming. The seats inside the departure terminal are new and very comfortable. The check-in area is very well organised and neat. The toilets are very clean. On my arrival, everything was easy, and in the end the only little improvement this airport could make is for the luggage delivery time. Apart from this very small detail this airport is just perfect.

Excellent airport. Well organized. Airlines and security staff are friendly and professional. Good customer service. The airport building is very clean and modern. Good parking indoor and outdoor next to the terminal. Easy to go around. In conclusion, a place were it's pleasant to go.

Small airport dealing mostly with flights within Canada and USA. Security was quick and easy (no language problems either) and we were through into the departure lounge which only has a shop and cafe but does have good free wifi to give you something to do while you wait. A good experience.

Arriving from the U.S. was easy and fast. No long walks not monorails no buses. You get off the plane go to customs get your suitcase change some money and grabbed a taxi all with a minimum of traipsing around. Most efficient arrival anywhere. Departure not so good. Airlines staff was late opening checkin lines. Baggage check man ridiculed my attempts to speak French and the woman operating the X-ray was rude to passengers. Furthermore the airport offers little in the way of food for purchase and duty-free items.
Love Quebec's airport. Small but offers all of the facilities in a big airport. Not too much people.

Security screening a nightmare! One person on one screening lane checking bags for 4 flights. A spare station was not staffed. Can’t be that difficult to roster staff on. Stood in line with other international visitors for over 1.5 hours! Not a good look for tourism New Zealand. It’s like saying well thanks for spending your money here but no you are leaving your dead to us.

Seriously wanting! Facilities airside for international departures are very poor: food and beverage is practically non-existent, seating is woeful and there are no charging ports. I can forgive the lack of an airbridge (in summer at least - I hate to think what it's like in winter!) This isn't helped by Virgin Australia not having any international lounges and the terminal barely large enough to cope maybe a new airport at Taras wouldn't be such a bad idea.

What a strange decision to place the new security gates across the entrance separating Air Espresso from the domestic lounge. I have to store my bags in the lockers given my transport time from the airport. So I go through, put my bags in the lockers and have to pass through security to get back which, by the way is always a hassle compared to departing AK. A cleaning cloth in my pocket is an issue?

Worst security queues and management. The security team were either poorly trained or had poor equipment as my bag went thru 3 times and found nothing. It seems that the domestic market is not important and this maybe an airport management decision as international passengers had no queue while domestic passengers queued for 30+ minutes. Not good enough.

It is unbelievably customer unfriendly. Baggage took over 30 minutes to be off loaded. There were no taxis waiting for passengers that arrived. There was no one calling for taxi service. There is very very limited shade. Lucky it was a hot sunny day but imagine arriving on a wet winter night. It's not rocket science. This has to change. Absolutely disappointing experience.

The worst airport experience ever. Travelling domestically and seriously couldn’t wait to leave. 6-8 staff all in the security area and most of them were standing around - the amount of staff did not equal efficiency or cut down waiting times. So slow moving people through the queue. Not only that, I was asked to remove my shoes because they covered my ankles (despite every passenger around me wearing pants that covered their ankles) and there was no signage or notes anywhere that this was a requirement - again for domestic travel. After passing through the X-ray machine, majority of our travelling party’s bags were opened and searched, despite all our packing and contents being exactly the way they were when we departed from Auckland airport a few days prior. The reasonings for checking our bags were useless, if we even got a solid answer. Staff were dismissive of our queries and just said oh because we have to. Queenstown airport is honestly the worst part of Queenstown. A wonderful trip otherwise soured by your horrendous staff. If you’re counting on tourism to pick up, your staff either need more training or replacing because I can guarantee I am questioning whether to ever come back after that treatment so I’m sure there are others doing the same. Your staff were useless in the security area, had no customer service and portrayed themselves as better than us. We were not the only ones verbally annoyed either. We had several other passengers complaining of the incompetency, lack of speed and general interactions of staff with us. Not only that, this experience left me shaking and with extreme anxiety. Worst staff, worst airport, worst everything. I will be telling everyone I know about how bad this airport is. If I could rate it and the staff a zero, I would.

Departing from here is like a form of torture. The departure gates all face the sun and it streams into them without any blinds or sun shades. The gates are therefore like little greenhouses filled with a hundred or so people all getting hotter and sweatier. Only two rows of priority seating are in the shaded area, the rest of lounge is entirely bathed in sunlight. It could be helped with some air-conditioning but sadly, no. There seems to be no cooling at all as I sit here quietly roasting. To top it all off, the sound system is tinny and like something from the late 90s which makes even The Who sound like a poor high school band. Horrible - can't wait to Board and get away!!

There is a need for some chairs and a table to sit and reorganise after the security check. This is especially important for people with knee / other implants requiring putting on the shoes. Cannot do this in standing position. I kept the bag on the only one table and was putting on the shoes in standing position. One security lady officer showed her displeasure and asked me to remove the bag from the table. Not very helpful.

Oh Queenstown Airport. You folks really let the side down coming and going. This ex-kiwi visiting family with her partner had a 40 minute queue for biosecurity coming in (I fully support protecting NZ flora and fauna but how about some more staff?), then a 50-minute wait simply for bag drop on departure (again, where are all the staff?). No apology at any stage either. You need to do so much better.

At the international check in the senior staff member assisting in loading items onto trays was incredibly rude, assuming I was of a foreign background that could not understand english, she was pointing at the empty tray, in which I was going to put my jacket into - I did not understand what she was trying to communicate to me. She then yelled at me saying “put it in here, put it in here” - I felt extremely offended and I was appalled by how I was being spoken to. I was completely lost for words, in this day and age to be spoken to like I’m an idiot when she was unclear as to what she wanted, expected me to understand her as she was pointing at the tray. In the end what she wanted was for me to separate my laptop from my iPad. She was a senior lady with short grey hair and classes, I was served at 2.55pm. I just cannot believe how rude she was to me, obviously thinking I could not speak or understand english. It was just disgusting and disgraceful.
Worst airport ever. Immigration had no people working and everyone waited over an hour and some 2 hours. It's like they had no idea flights were arriving
It was perfect. I love everything about thr airport. It was quick and has good staff. Good food and it's modern. Just love it but I dont like the national airlines like TAME.

Quito is a clean airport which I used for both domestic and International flights. Great security, free internet. Shopping and dining is expensive for a Latin American country. Check-in works fine with modern equipment. They have an annoying system of paying 2 dollars for a trolley.

Small airport and with almost no seats before airline check in. Counter check in / line only available to ticketed passengers. Be ready to show passport and boarding pass physical or electronic ticket or Web check in. Space for queues is limited so it could be crowded especially if there's another airline during check in process in the same area. Restaurants for general public in another building outside the airport. Almost nothing once you clear security and emigration. Only one very simple paid lounge. No courtesy lounges for Airlines.

When you get off the plane at Quito Mariscal Airport, you are greeted with a stunning view of the mountains. The staff are all very friendly, and the airport itself is quite modern. While there aren't tonnes of bars and restaurants like the airports at home in Britain, it doesn't matter. Because the facilities are satisfactory, and the staff behave the way staff should. I arrived in Quito after transit in Panama (which was a total dump with extremely rude staff) so to arrive in my final destination (where I now live) and to be greeted to my new country in such a friendly manner by immigration and customs was lovely.

Quito is a really nice new airport about 45km from the city - there is very little available around it. The airport has free wifi, which is always a bonus. As it seems with all airports now the prices of small things like coffee etc are expensive. My experience with the new airport was excellent - not so though with the employees of American Airlines at Quito Airport - beware.
New facilities in the national arrivals/departures concourse, very nice modern terminal, new roads from Quito recently finished so the trip to city is quicker and easier, overall great airport.

We only used the airport for arrival so can't comment on departure related matters. The arrivals hall had all the facilities one would expect of a modern airport but was let down by very long immigration queues. We had to queue for just over an hour. There were two queues one for nationals of Ecuador (plus nationals of a few other South American countries) and the second for Foreigners. There simply weren't enough desks open for Foreigners but there were plenty open for Ecuadorians so they never had to wait more than maybe 10 or 15 minutes. This really needs to be rectified and also there needs to be clear signage as to which queue to join. In front of us was a couple from Peru who could have used the short queue had it been clearly marked. On the day of our arrival (3 Sept 2014) the new road from the airport to Quito had just been opened that very same day so the journey to the centre took us just 45 minutes even though it was a busy time of the day. Shame about the immigration queues as immigration staff were pleasant enough and this should otherwise rate as a good airport.

Still not in full working order March 2013. One hour for bags to arrive from international flight. Immigration fast and terminal clean. The worst part is getting to Quito. The traffic is terrible and there is only a one lane bridge across the gorge. Try to arrive on Saturday or Sunday when you can do the trip to the city in about one hour. Otherwise it can take you 2.5-3 hours.

Tale of 2 different airports arrival was horrible. Stood in the immigration line for 2+ hours. Heard similar if not worse stories for arriving passengers for the next day. Departure was fine. Check in was fairly quick immigration was painless. Appeared to have many stores/food options available but went to the lounge to wait. An additional inspection was required to get into the gate area-be warned you are not allowed to bring in bottled water even though obtained post security. Airport is very close to town (10-15 minutes to hotel) new airport appears to be about an hour+ drive.

A new airport terminal has started functioning now but it is a shame that after spending so much money the facilities and services have not improved. The aerobridges do not function and come cold rain hot winds one has still to walk to the planes. Families with young children have been suffering immensely. No serving airline has a courtesy coach to take passengers to the planes. The lounge itself is shabby without proper lighting. In the evenings/night it feels like a ghost house. The staff of the airlines are rude. The food courts have not started and the few stalls functioning charge exorbitantly. Outside the airport they charge you even if you have come for a pick up or drop. This is irrespective of your parking the vehicle in the parking lot. The prepaid taxi counter is a big cheat shop with flat rate of taxi charges irrespective of which part of town you are going. There is a bus stop and a bus is supposed to be parked during the flight timings but never ever seen it. When I enquired they told me that to reduce congestion in front of the terminal it is parked far away they expected me to carry my luggage to the bus. All in all a big airport terminal with the worst services.

This small airport was a model of efficiency: clean cool organised with a friendly restaurant serving Indian and Western food. The Kingfisher Airlines ground crew were excellent. The short walk to the plane will sadly end when a shiny new terminal is soon completed.

Rajbiraj is an airport limited to domestic flights in Nepal, that too one flight a day(X2) operating from the capital Kathmandu. The facilities are very basic. Ground handling is all manual. Baggage delivery was delayed because of manual handling only. Seating is not enough. Cleanliness is a concern. No WiFi, no restaurant. The surroundings also is not like that of a airport. In summary an airport which is to be used in absence of other better options. Janakpur is a nearby airport and better one. Biratnagar also is not too far.
The pre-TSA agents are extremely rude. They yelled front of everyone that I didn't go to school because I tried to ask why toothpaste is considered a liquid and not soft solid. Very poor service.

The TSA in this airport is incredibly rude. I came in with a fractured ankle, and nobody was helping me. They were screaming at me. I managed to take a picture of that rude person, who wouldn't even tell me his name and covered his tag so I wouldn't catch his name. Embarrassing. I hope he and the other rude people around gets fired. This is terrible. No one deserves to be treated like that!! Thank you Shanon and Cameron for be the only kind and professional people at this airport.

The airport itself is nice and clean but the staff were awful! I consider myself pretty easy going and let a lot of things brush over but the way my daughter and I were treated was completely uncalled for. It was myself and my 5 year old learning disabled daughter traveling home from a vacation visiting family in North Carolina. TSA yelled at and berated my daughter for struggling to follow exact instructions scaring her and made following instructions that much harder. It turned our already stressful day into a nightmare. I understand millions of people move through the airport and there are protocols that need to be followed for everyone’s safety but I can say with absolute certainty we will never fly into or out of Raleigh again. Experiencing one moody/rude person is easy to pass off as they are having a bad day but literally everyone! Staff really need to get in touch with how to treat travelers like human beings not prisoners. Chicago O’Hare TSA/staff are top notch and were so kind for our trip flying out making our experience this morning that much more shocking.

This airport is fine, but the TSA agents (terminal 1) are rude and condescending. I frequently fly with small children (my 12th flight with 2 two-year-olds) and have never had a worse experience with TSA practically berating me over stroller. Most airports have you breakdown the stroller and run through machine. NOT here. If you don’t want to be harassed, do not break your stroller down. I would suggest you refrain from asking either because they will make jokes about you in front of everyone. They are slow, unhelpful and unprofessional.

Being fed up with the chaos at many ports of entry into the USA from Europe (as a non USA-citizen), I thought to try out a new way to enter the USA with less wait, hassle, stress and frustration. I flew the non-stop AA flight from LHR into RDU. Even though I was in business class and was among the first to disembark, I believe all passengers entered the USA (border control), in 15 minutes or less. It took me 3 minutes from plane door to curbside.  Also, the airport is modern and clean, really nice staff. With just one or two daily incoming flights from Europe, I don't think there is a better way to travel into the USA from Europe. I connected the next morning on a very early (5 am) departure. Staff told me there was a 'morning rush', so I was a bit nervous about TSA opening only at 4 am. Arrived at 3:30 am, and soon after that TSA started processing passengers. Again, lovely kind people all around. What an exceptional airport!

I fly every week. RDU is always the worst airport I have to use. And this is saying something since I have to fly out of NYC airports. The security check point is horrible. Regardless of time of day - even 5.00 am. The line is so long it spills out into the baggage drop area. And it's ALWAYS this way. The staff are so rude. They obviously enjoy harassing people. Then, should you have enough time for food or coffee, the lines are huge for these too. Don't even think about Starbucks unless you get to the airport 3 hours before your flight.

I had a Frontier flight that was scheduled to depart at 9.46pm and found out it was delayed. Upon hearing that I was ok and figured I could just enjoy some of the restaurants and found out that every bar and restaurant closes at 8pm. I was told by an employee that when flights are delayed they are supposed to receive a memorandum that will keep the restaurants open until those flights have departed. There are too many people that pay good money to fly and there are no accommodations to keep them comfortable and entertained until their departure. I strongly recommend the hours change from 8 to 10pm for closing time. I understand these places open up at 4.30 or 5am but you still have fliers who take flights late in the evening. These little stores that stay open does not meet the demands of customers. I am extremely dissatisfied.

I have flown to/from RDU 4-5 times now at different times and hours during 2020-22. I must say that it is one of the best run mid-tier airports in the country. Beautiful and thoughtful design, airy and welcoming, extremely clean and efficient. The security wait times have always been under 10 mins. Decent food and shopping options too. It's hard to fault this one, just needs to step up when it comes to wifi and entertainment options. Otherwise, it's a great airport.

The Terminal 2/AA/Delta etc arrival area, where most airlines come in, is the most poorly run pick up area I have ever been to. Twice this summer I had to experience the gridlock of cars attempting to pick up people at this terminal. There is no way to pull over to pick up people, even when they are right there waiting out front. The security officers yell at you to keep driving around, adding to traffic issues and do not give you a chance to pull over. My 80-year-old mother was stepping across several lanes of traffic to try and reach me and the security officer was yelling at both of us. I had already circled around 3 times! The poorly run arrival area looks like a COVID hotspot. If they would let you pick up passengers, there would be fewer problems. They should redirect rental car buses to another location or spread arrivals out so there are fewer people trying to be picked up at the same time. The security officers should get off of their Segways and try being helpful instead of yelling at elderly people and those picking them up.
Remarkable that they speak several languages over the loud speaker but have no free internet available. A disgrace to the travel industry. I will rethink coming through RDU ever again.

The woman taking care of boarding was very rude and overbearing. She made me pay $50 for a carry on bag. I have a small under seat bag that I use all the time and went under the seat when I sat down. I asked a flight attendant if the bag was alright there and she said yes. I was told that she is not well liked by Allegiant staff and I can't imagine why she is employed by Allegiant. I fly Allegiant all of the time but usually go out of Grand Island and they are wonderful. I will not fly Allegiant out of Rapid again. According to passengers this happens all the time.

Personally Rarotonga airport like most of the Cook Islands is a little over-rated. Had to stand for 30 minutes in a queue to check in on a concrete floor while we waited for the check in desks to open which they did 10 minutes past their advertised time. After checking in we were told we had to pay a $55 departure tax which I was told is not part of the airline ticket price. Customs and immigration not that helpful and my wife had to give up some perfume we had just bought or they would not clear us. Limited shopping there but the toilets were clean. Blaring music non stop which made it hard to hear the announcements so at times you were doubting you were at the right gate. Not overly impressed.

Raro continues to provide the friendly and low-key facilities I so enjoyed years ago (visited 2000 and as commented on here in 2004) however there's a whole new terminal building that with a whole four shops and a cafe at departure is positively massive compared to what went before. It's been nicely done and they have continued the live music for welcoming and departing with custom songs depending on where your place is going (eg. 'Pub with No Beer' for the flight to Sydney). The cafe does a good coffee and there's enough seats to cope with a plane-full. The staff here actually care about their customers and that's what makes it such a pleasant experience compared to almost any other faceless oversized airport with security gone mad as there is almost everywhere else. Thoroughly recommended.

Half the terminal has been demolished to make way for the new terminal under construction. Bit of a shock on arrival but should be fabulous when finished. Befitting a gorgeous island such as Rarotonga. Previously RAR didn't separate Arrivals and departures - bit of a problem for the once weekly flight to/from LA. No airbridges in the new terminal planned from the renderings I could see. So still a bit of a problem to/ from aircraft when a tropical downpour arrives as it want to do. Reason being this is such a tiny aerodrome with short runway of approx 2300m ( just enough for a 777). Accordingly turnaround and parking area for aircraft precludes a fixed airbridge. New departure area will still have the outside garden area so you can have one last look over the airfield to the beautiful mountain peaks before boarding. On another note duty free no longer the stupendous bargain it once was. Still pretty good compared to many big airports around the world. Happy to see such a new terminal being built but also a shame that Raro is geting all grown up! Hope the new terminal can retains its 'island' feeling.

Small airport by international standards. Immigration and customs smiling and welcoming. Departure easy with only one aircraft. $30 departure tax has to be paid and quite rigorous security procedure but done with typical Cook Islands good nature. Walk from terminal to aircraft across tarmac necessary. Could be a wet one in a tropical downpour.

Ground side is good with adequate food sites. There is no shop to buy magazines and the bank machines are not reliable making it difficult to withdraw cash. Security is well organised but they don't supply plastic bags for liquids in hand baggage, you have to exit and purchase one in the pharmacy. This is ridiculous in an international airport. Airside is hopeless, a small cafe with limited range of eats and a small dutyfree shop and the card machine was not working when I passed. Overall: poorish

The airport might be nice, small and clean, but there is a big BUT: 2.5 hours before departure the queue/line was already going all the way through the airport (that means the double length of a normal full line) - but the check-in counter was not open. They didn't work. I am sure you had to queue for more then 1.5 hours with that airport service. I am sorry, but the airport is not modern, since they don't accept boarding passes on a smartphone - they make you to go back in to the line to get the boarding pass printed. Since I did already the check-in online and had no baggage, I could go to the fist class line and skip the 1 hour check-in line (otherwise I would have been very upset and angry with the Recife Airport). Also not perfect: It is a bit complicated to store the luggage inside the airport and it's very difficult to find it (you have to ask a person).

Recife Airport is definitely the best airport I have been through in Brazil. The scenery coming in to land is impressive. The architecture of the building is very modern and excellent use is made of natural lighting. There is an excellent observation deck on the second floor with a good selection of restaurants and shopping outlets. The first floor is departures and the ground floor is arrivals. Selection is good landside and even airside there are enough options for an early flight including a 24-hour coffee shop. Security is extremely tough. Be prepared to take off belt shoes wallet etc. Check-in machines strategically placed and few queues (although my departing flight was at 3.30 am maybe the situation is different during the day) - I arrived at lunch time though and no problems either. Excellent connections into Boa Viagem and downtown via bus 042 (Aeroporto Opcional) passes in front of airport very frequent (daytime only). Taxis are also readily available a trip to Boa Viagem Beach shall be about R$ 20 which is about USD 8. The airport deserves more international traffic as Recife is a major tourist hub. Current flights only to Frankfurt (Condor) Panama City (Copa) and Lisbon (TAP). A tip: if you are flying out of Recife be sure to take some "bolo de rolo" with you. It's a local delicacy a kind of guava cake.

The airport terminal was built from scratch beside the old building currently closed. It has a huge skylight from end to end making good use of natural light that reaches all floors through an atrium. Many sculptures are integrated in the project which gives it an interesting touch. Facilities are good enough. The local delicacies stores are surely to be visited. Totally sets itself apart from most Brazilian airports whose problems usually begin at finding a parking spot and extend through all possible aspects up to the boarding ramps.
Very good array of shops ahead of security. Very modern very clean. Far nicer than the other airports that I've encountered in Brazil.
One of the best choices in Brazil. The airport is very modern pretty and clean it can be considered an architecture beauty. Way better than São Paulo and Rio.

One of the nicest most modern airports in the country. Decent array of shops and restaurants. Not a large selection between security checkpoints and departure gates but that is typical and here it is still far better than at Fortaleza a city of similar size. Airport is close to town especially beach areas so transportation is usually easy. How many agents are actually working at the check-in counters can vary widely but I assume that is the responsibility of the airlines.

Redding Municipal Airport: Newly Remodeled with Same Shortcomings: Not Ready for Prime Time: For years using the Redding Airport (RDD) has been an exercise in frustration. Much of the frustration stems its primary sub-par 'I don't care' airline (United) and pathetic staffing levels. Here's the truth. Redding Airport is treated like an inconvenient afterthought as connecting airports regularly delay inbound planes not once but at least twice. You have a 4.00 pm flight, no worries, count on departing around 4.45pm. You had better hope your connections are not too close lest you miss them. The new remodel has helped speed up what typically was a 30-45 minute wait for checked bags for the one and only plane that has landed at the airport. Now you wait about 20 minutes for arriving guests to get their luggage. Want something to eat while waiting? Need to speak to a gate agent? Looking for professional and knowledgeable advise? Look elsewhere. The lone restaurant (Chu's Too) is rarely open to attract customers to the bar while waiting for a plane. Ticketing is a ghost town until 1.5 hours prior to flight so you better have your phone app at the ready and have your carry on bag packed like Bear Grylls with snacks and other necessities if you need assistance. Need a car rental to escape the lack of services in Redding to drive to San Francisco in hopes of catching your connecting flight? Not in Redding, rental agencies are consistent in their underwhelming inventory, no one-way rental availability and exorbitant rates to rent a roller skate. Redding airport is great if you have lots of time built into your itinerary for frustration, delays and intentional understaffing and lack of assistance, otherwise make the drive to Sacramento Airport (SMF).

This airport is too small and outdated for a region serving 3/4 million people in ten different counties. It is definitely worth the drive to Sacramento or San Francisco to get better flights and many people around here don't want to make that long cumbersome drive. The terminal hasn't been updated since 1998 but all that was remodeled restrooms and new seats and carpeting. We desperately need a larger airport with more flights and parking options.

Regina International Airport is viewed by many as a municipal airport, as they only have domestic flights and their only international flights are during the winter holiday season. The airport is trying to expand, but with the loss of transborder flights, it’s limitations to serve the global network are seemingly smaller. That being said, their amentities pre-security include a full service Tim Horton’s, SubWay, and a restaurant alongside a Relay. In the departure lounge, there is a Tim Horton’s express, a cafe, a bar, and another Relay. The airport would benefit from a lounge such as Plaza Premium. Departure and arrival are very quick as the only delays are due to the inbound flight, or the de-icing of an aircraft.

With family in Brittany I'm a regular user of Rennes St Jacques and have seen its traffic grow significantly in volume over the past decade. What a shame that the airport itself has not been able to keep up. The only passenger facilities are a small café / gift shop and once you get beyond security there's a pop-up snack stall (closed on Sundays) and a vending machine. No shops, eating establishments or even the token Duty Free. Generally I pass through the airport quickly, so this isn't really a concern, but if you are unfortunate enough to be delayed, it's not fun. My main issue is with the speed of check-in, which can only be described as glacial. When there are two or more imminently departing flights at the same time, the queues barely seem to move, at the risk of passengers almost missing their plane. I speak from experience here. Staff are pleasant and bilingual but absolutely inefficient at processing large volumes of passengers. I want to like Saint Jacques - it's clean, friendly and has a good bus service to the city centre, but it hasn't really done enough to move with the times and comfortably accommodate its passengers. If it had a choice of amenities, expanded check-in with more staff, and a better departure lounge, it would be pretty much the perfect regional airport.

HORRIBLE Customer service. The TSA lady was so rude over an honest mistake and she’s yelling at me and my daughter. She was so hyper-focused on pushing everyone through like cattle that she sacrificed basic customer service. Yelling, barking at customers, making comments while walking past me without any regard for my response. AND she barked at a fellow co-worker in front of everyone. Really set the whole mood for our trip. Thank you TSA.

The personnel are rude everywhere-from check in areas to security to everyone except janitorial. The management must be terrible for it to be so pervasive. Very slow day at airport so it’s not overwork issues. Example. At head of security line signs tell you to await next green light. Then agents yell (for 10 minutes I saw) what do you think my arms that long or hurry up-when their lights are red. Which federal rule do you break? Should you be harangued and abused just because you’re politely following signage?

Upon arriving home after a lovely Thanksgiving trip, I patiently awaited my luggage at the Southwest baggage claim. My bag is very distinct and when it didn't come through, I knew it was elsewhere. I took my baggage claim sticker over to the office and the staff were absolutely wonderful. He kindly assisted me and had a genuine demeanour that reassured me my bag would arrive later. He told me where it was and when it would arrive. Later in the afternoon, he called me right at the time he said he would to alert me of my suitcases arrival. When I went to pick it up, he was so kind and polite to me! I appreciated his enthusiasm and positivity. He is truly a wonderful example of great customer service. I wish all airport staff were as welcoming.
