3 hours early and needed a wheelchair but was told i would miss my flight if i waited for one. Walked through security and was treated like a criminal. This is not the first time this has happened.

Great airport. Very easy to find everything, spotlessly clean, and nice decor. The TSA employees were very efficient and friendly. I was flagged at TSA precheck for my bag to be hand searched because of a binder in my bag. The agent looked through the binder and repacked my items. I was still through the security fast. They have helpful announcements periodically. TSA called people over the loudspeaker when someone had forgotten an item at security. One announcement was for a granola bar left behind. One of the best airports I have been to in a while.

Flew in and out of RNO on Southwest. The terminal layout is compact and easy to navigate. There are plenty of slot machines but unlike LAS there aren't so many that they take up too much floor space and leave not enough room to walk past. Smoking is also not permitted anywhere inside the terminal which is a nice change from LAS. The food/beverage/shopping options in the gate areas are limited but there is a nice food and shopping court in the main terminal area before you pass security. The rental car facility is just across the street from the terminal so there are no time-consuming shuttle rides. The airport is only 3 miles from the city centre and traffic to/from the terminal is usually light. The TSA screening area however is too small and understaffed for a 25-gate airport. If you're travelling at peak times expect long lines and delays.

Yet another airport that does not provide fresh drinking water free of charge airside. Having had a discussion with the security people at passport control they assured me there was no provision for potable water. The only option was to buy a plastic bottle of water or use a tap in the toilet but that was not recommended! It makes a mockery of the 4 dustbins for recycling different items and that are scattered around the airport - see picture. It should become mandated that airports provide water free of charge. Any claims to be "green" are otherwise total garbage.

Can't fault this airport at all, the staff are very friendly & helpful. I found the experience of arrival & departure stress free. It's nice & clean & one of the friendliest airports I have ever been to on my holidays abroad.

Awful airport. Very few staff for a great deal of passengers. Queued for nearly an hour to check in with 3 staff. No water fountain facilities as is standard everywhere else. Staff in restaurants unwilling to help (but you can definitely buy water). It’s 30 degrees outside. And the air conditioning is terrible. Announcements are poor. Fraport are more interested in making a ton of money. That’s what happens when there’s no competition around. They’re making a bad impression of the great country of Greece.

Absolute carnage, huge queue at check-in but in fairness had 10 desks open so got through fairly quickly , security pretty quick as well then the problems begin. On entering the departure area there was extreme over crowding , No seats, people sitting and standing everywhere, the limited food venues totally full with large queues, passport control was reasonably quick which takes you to the non Schengen area departure area which was also extremely busy with the same overcrowding. Too many tourists in too small an area, Not sure if always this busy but beware of potential overcrowding.

Absolute chaos. Boarding queues stretched the length of the terminal, back to the duty free section. Constant Greek language tannoy announcements. No guidance offered at any stage. Delayed an hour and a quarter.

Just one small step above cattle barn status. This so called Airport is not set up and unable to accommodate the hordes of tourists that pour in an out of Rhodes. Shengen flights are delayed beyond anything I have seen anywhere else. There are not enough seats, except if you fly non-Shengen. Great advertising for Europe incapacity to treat with a minimal decency travelers spending their cash in this island. The spectacle of people and children laying everywhere in the floor in overcrowded rooms with no or not enough AC feels like being in a third world country hospital after a disaster. Official airport staff will explain that it’s much worse in other places. I think they should be allowed to travel. This place is despicable. Stay away by all means.
The staff are rude and doors are locked at departure lounge and the place is a sweatbox. You can't find a tour operator on the upper level to help if needed.

Extremely crowded and doesn't feel like there's air-conditioning at a time of year that you can barely breathe. Floors, bathrooms and chairs are dirty. People are sitting on the floor because there isn't enough seating. This very moment a family has surrounded me in an effort to be near the grandfather that is seated. No regard for covid or personal space. However, there is barely space to move around so they don't have a choice really. There aren't enough options to sit and eat. The bathrooms have a toilet roll device that doesn't work. I literally open all doors to find one where it is still functioning. About 30% of flush buttons are missing leaving holes in the wall. Lovely island but this airport is hell for my long layover.

We had a weeks holiday in Rhodes so arrived and departed. Our arrival at approx 2300 local time was easy and quick. We were off the aircraft, through passport control, baggage collection and customs within 45 minutes. Our departure was longer and check in queues were lengthy with over an hours wait- however I believe that is the responsibility of the airline, not the airport. All staff were courteous and cheerful. We had a snack whilst waiting for our flight, the quality wasn't good and it was very overpriced, so whilst I wouldn't choose to eat in the airport again I would be happy enough to use the airport and look forward to visiting Rhodes again soon.

One member of our party has special needs and requires the special assistance service. The airport ground staff were exemplary. We travel regularly. The assistance, kindness, efficiency and responsiveness of all the ground staff we encountered was the best that we have experienced. I would recommend Rhodes airport as an airport with staff that genuinely assist those with special and additional needs.
TSA pre check is so slow. It’s supposed to be faster than general boarding, that’s what I’m paying for. The lady doing the check in appears to be new or just slow. She needs help. 7am, 5/16/22.

Never had a problem til now. TSA was extremely rude, they were pushing everyone around, not just me. Speaking to me as if I were a child. This was 8th June at 6 am. No respect whatsoever, very unprofessional. It was obvious they were abusing their authority

This was the worst airport I have ever been to. The people are extremely rude and short. It seemed like common behavior from the TSA agents to the store/restaurant clerks. Seems like the pre requisite to work here is you have to be rude. I will avoid this airport at all costs in the future.

Airport is clean and seems to be efficient as airports go. However the food service is dismal. There are no brand fast-food which is what we needed in order to catch a bus out to a conference center. The only offering was some place called Cheeburger Cheeburger (yes a dated reference to an old SNL staple) which food was neither fast nor flavorful. Fries were greasy meat was half-cooked and the service was slow. Certainly an "international Airport" can do better.

My experiences have always been pleasant. Security lines are extremely short and there is a lot of open space. Checking in is never a hassle-we have been able to pass by the check-in desk in 20 minutes or less on the worst of days. Bathrooms are clean and there's always a cafe or news store open. Delta seems to have the largest concentration of flights at the airport most of them being on their regional affiliates running under Delta Connection. Overall the airport is very good clean and friendly.

Richmond International is a new stylish and perfect sized airport on the outskirts of Richmond. 9 major air carriers serve RIC flying to over 22 domestic and international destinations in the USA and Canada. The airport is medium-sized and easy to find your way around. The security lines are short and hassle-free. The airport atrium has a large glass roof giving the airport interior a very "open" feel. A restaurant in the atrium has a large window with a full view of the apron for all the plane spotters. Travel into and out of RIC is always hassle-free and fun.

Richmond is a medium size airport that has recently been extensively renovated. My experience flying in and out was very pleasant – RIC is a “human sized” airport so it is easy to get around. Baggage recovery was fast and painless with our checked bags appearing only about five minutes after we had arrived at the carousel. The rental car desks are conveniently sited and the rental car garage is a two minute walk from the terminal. Our total time from landing to driving off in a rental car was less than thirty minutes. The airport is well connected to the adjacent Interstate highway so the airport is easy to get into and out of. On departure check-in and security was quick and painless. There is a restaurant in the secure area offering a view of the ramp a pleasant thing for the travelling aircraft buff. Overall I was very impressed with Richmond airport and would use it again anytime.

It hard to understand where to go, and staff are the worst especially those who are check in. They used 30 minutes to find something wrong with you bag by checking the weight multiple times. Not me but an other lady. And bunch of people had to wait for only that one lady. They could at least open one more check-in. When I asked a question staff was annoyed by me asking if it is the right gate. My experience is not good at all. Felt stressed. And I had 2 hours on me at least.

The worst airport I have ever seen. No overview where to find, I found myself in a labyrinth of parfum shops I was looking for a Restaurant run up and down. There are no  acceptable signs only fast food or bad convenience shops. No quiet place where I can make my work and make a phone call with a customer. There is rock music everywhere. No noise reducing walls etc. Security check absolutely overdone.

Been to 20 airports and this was hands down the worst I've ever seen. Waited over 40 minutes to get my passport checked. Beyond embarrassing. You could tell it was bank Holiday Friday, the staff weren't bothered. Wish I could put 0/10

A pretty average airport, quite dated and gloomy especially landside. Going through security was no problem, airside things are slightly more bright and modern. The prices in shops are an absolute rip off, even by the standards of an airport.

I was very impressed with the experience at Riga Airport. So fast through security and no problems with my Japanese hair sticks which look like weapons on x-rays. Pleasant staff too, which makes a real change. Wish I could say the same for UK airports. Good range of shops and helpful staff, but some of the cafes are very expensive just for coffee and cake. Slightly let down by toilets and desolate area C after passport control but generally, very impressed compared to some nightmare experiences in the UK.

Absolute terrible airport, outdated security protocols, expect to be frisked and berated for things that are normal in every other airport on this planet (couldn't bring in 1 lighter even though there is smoking rooms inside?) Guess they need to milk the travelers for every cent they can. Terrible eating options, only 1 place to sit and eat with garbage overpriced food, only decent things are the beers which will be needed to drown the sorrow of being in this sorry excuse of an airport. Overall experience 2/10 (2 points for the beers), would not recommend for anybody to experience, it's almost as if they want to make sure you're suffering when traveling from or have a layover at Riga International Airport.

We were in transit through Riga Airport. We have three children one of them four months old. We were having a baby stroller which we handed to the ground crew before boarding the plane in Milan and no other luggage. When in Riga we have asked one of the ground crew to give us the stroller, which was five meters from him, telling him that we are in transit and we don't have any other luggage. He refused us telling us that is not his problem and he don't care.We have asked couple of times, after he just turned his back and left. We have asked two other ground crew and they have tell us that we need to go to pick up the stroller from the luggage hall. We have asked inside the airport four different staff members and received four different answers of how to proceed none of them making sense. In the end we have exit the airport, retrieve the stroller, going through security again with three children just because they don't "care". None of the staff members were nice, but the guy on the ground crew was very rude. We have traveled a lot of countries but never faced this issue. If you could avoid this airport, I will recommend you to do so.

Great experience! Early check in possible and done quickly, staff super friendly. Security fast and let's you go faster with a baby. Nice tax free zone that you can actually enjoy as the check in and security is done quickly. At least two amazing playgrounds for children, great cafes, everything clean.

Good check-in and boarding, excellent lounge, but a disappointing experience with an unfriendly and ignorant worker at the security check. There were only a few passengers at the airport, no queue at the check-in counter. The lounge was impeccable, with a friendly staff, a very good choice of snacks, drinks and reading material. The only negative moment was in the priority security line, despite that there were no passengers in the line, right after 8 am. The worker who checked my passport and boarding pass sternly told me that next time she would not allow me to use the priority security line if I don't present my Silver Finnair Plus card (?!) The “Priority Security” note was boldly printed in a big font on my boarding pass which she was holding in her hand, so I'm afraid to think she could not read English. RIX, in general, is a good airport but the management has to teach priority security line workers to read and understand at least two words in English: “Priority Security”.

Never been to another airport where the staff won't empty your reusable bottle for you (nor let you empty it yourself on the spot, you have to go to the bathroom facilities with all your hand luggage). I poured it into the trash container and they told me off and threatened to call the police next time. The security control is also really slow although there wasn't any queue. The containers are provided individually by the staff, so you can't lay out your stuff while they're checking another passenger. I can't say I don't recommend the airport - but you have to be prepared for how the security control is handled.

Use this airport only as must. Once you are through the passport control, toilet use is done only in group excursions. So god forbid you have human basic needs. Beautiful touch to this regulation is you will be called to the gate at least two hours too early!

This is the 5th time that I flying to this airport. The café after security is so disgusting. A lot of cigarettes on the floor. The tables are always dirty and uncomfortable seatings. Food supplies is poor and bad service.

Its a small airport at an island (abt 30 km from Rijeka). Checking in and out goes quite fast (at our experience). Some staff members in the shop are kind of grumpy. Nevertheless, we are very happy with this airport how they have arranged a 5***** hotel in Opatija for our group when our flight was cancelled all of a sudden in the evening. Our flight company Transavia told some people to find and book by themselves a hotel, but the airport arranged bus transport and a luxurious hotel, so our compliments.

It is a small easy accessible airport with a huge unexpensive parking lot, where you can easily drink a coffee outside while waiting for your check in. But after check in the true horror begins: There was just one girl who checked the passports before security check and we had to wait for 30 minutes in a small very hot alley. The alley had no AC but a glass roof it was incredible sweaty to stand in a pushy crowd just to get your passport checked. Around there were kids, mothers with babies and older people heavily breathing. Who builds a glass house in a sunny country as waiting area? At this moment there were just two middle sized planes boarding and the people were almost rioting, because of this horrible situation.

MUC-RJK-MUC. We arrived at Rijeka Airport on Croatia Airlines twenty minutes ahead of schedule. Ours was the only aircraft in service at the airport. The off-loading of the hand luggage went extremely quickly. After immigration control, there is only one conveyor belt for all arriving aircraft. It took quite a while before baggage delivery started. There is no money exchange at the airport, so you should have a few kuna with you for the taxi or the bus. The check-in for our flight back started two hours before departure. There were two counters open for only 44 passengers. Boarding passes were only available for the first segment. After security and passport control, there is only one snack bar with limited products and a duty-free shop which can only be accessed when the aircraft is ready for boarding. On the plus side, a very nice terrace where passengers can sit in the open and wait for the arrival of their aircraft.

Rimini Airport is highly recommended as a way to access the Adriatic Riviera. This smaller than average airport is located on the edge of Rimini MiraMare and is well connected to Rimini and the train stations by coach and a local tram service is not far away either. The negative aspect is that the lack of clear signs inside the airport for ground transport could be very misleading for newly arrived passengers and lead the newly arrived into the hands of very expensive taxi drivers. Rimini Airport has some nice shops and is well set out. I highly recommend this airport.

We arrived at Rimini airport for a flight with Ryanair to Stansted. First of all the check in queues were not organised. People were pushing in and not queuing correctly. No one was there to organise this. Once through security we could not find a seat anywhere. We managed to find a couple of chairs outside but the backs of them were broken. All the tables covered in rubbish. The bins were all over flowing with rubbish so no one could put anything in them. The shops and bar had large queues - it was horrible. We then went to our gate and the queue for passport control was very long. People were pushing in. The Russian flight was called forward all the people pushed us. They then had to call our flight as it was 22.00 and the flight should have been taking off at this time. Again more pushing and shoving! This airport needs some organisation. I have never been to such a poorly run airport.

I fly into Rimini Airport at least 4 times a year to visit family. It is a small airport and the restaurant and shops are expensive. I love this airport. You can't get lost and the best bit is you can go outside on a very large balcony and watch the planes land take off etc. Also great if you smoke! You are allowed to smoke only outside. I would recommend this airport it is still small and friendly.

Flew in and out of Rimini Airport recently. A very small airport that can hardly cope with the amount of passengers who use it. Were brought by bus to the small "Schengen" arrival hall. The forty passengers of our flight were almost too many for the luggage vonveyor belt. I wonder how they manage aeroplanes of the size of a Boeing 737 let alone an Airbus! In the departure hall they have approximately ten check-in counters which seemed quite enough for a Sunday afternoon. The "Schengen" departure lounge after passing the security check however is hardly adequate. There were only two departures at that time an ATR 72 (70 seats) to Munich and a Boeing 737-500 (120 seats) to Luxemburg. These two were already two many for the few seats they have in the departure lounge. Moreover there is almost nothing you can do. There is an overpriced restaurant a an equally pricey souvenir shop. You cannot look onto the apron as all windows have frosted glass. In short there is quite a lot to improve at Rimini airport.

Galeão International Airport. The primary airport for Rio De Janeiro. International arrivals can lead to long walk from most distant pier but Passport Control relatively quick - no paperwork needed. Baggage Reclaim no problem and arrivals hall has usual selection of food and drink leading out into the parking area. Domestic Departures a bit more chaotic with lots of Bag Drop machines beyond a check-point for tickets etc. Security up on the next level was efficient. A selection of shops and eating places along one wall, opposite glass wall looking out onto parts of the apron and one of the runways. Different lines at each gate to gather before boarding.

This is a small airport. Single terminal concept. Security was quick and since my flight was to Sao Paulo it is internal and there is no passport check. All the gates are in a single long corridor. Distances to walk are short. The shops and cafes directly face the gates so you can drink a coffee and see when your gate is boarding. The free WIFI was excellent. Good stress free experience airport.

Dumont airport - terrible service by GOL. The queue has not moved for over 1.5 hours. Nobody speaks English for an airport that's full of passengers flying to and from overseas. We don't understand why is there a delay, nobody speaks the language and none of the staff are bothered. From what we understood, some people fought with the guy who looks like the supervisor and they were pushed in front? What a joke! Enjoyed Rio but won't be back, thank you!

The airport was renovated in 2016 before the Olympic games, it looks like Miami International Airport, nothing special, good duty free, some good lounges, all in all, good airport, with some problems with queues and not so friendly staff.

Awful airport. We went one terminal to another 4 times. Also seating in waiting area are made for only one people so you can't stretch at all. Passport control had only 3-4 desks for more than 600 people. Nobody speaks english. They change gates pretty often. No smoking area.

Flew in and out of Rio Galeao airport in October. Terminal was quite clean and quiet, and quite a lot of shops, but not too many, which is neat. The walking was a lot though, and there were no conveyor belts to speed from the security to my gate (all the way at the other end of the airport). This is one of two points that could be improved. The other one is is that some employes doing reaserch and statistics about client satisfaction were walking aroud the gates to get info. No problem there. But there are far too many. I got interupted almost every 10 minutes, and I think that the airport can/could relax on that. An otherwise great airport.

Much better now that they inaugurated the new pier. More shops, restaurants (although some are overpriced) and seats available. Good staff and cleanliness.The restrooms are very good and clean. One problem is the distances between check-in and boarding.

Rio De Janeiro is a good aiirport but was very crowded during the Olympics. The new terminal is awesome, but GOL VIP lounge is poor - the Plaza Premium Lounge is better. The duty free is good, but overpriced. Customs and immigration officers are quite sympathetic, and the airport is clean.

This must be the worst international airport I've flown out of. Much worse than São Paulo. We arrived at 4.30am for our 6.30am TAM flight to find a long queue for check in with only one person working and no priority check in queue at all. Once through most of the very small rubbishy shops were closed. Couldn't even get a coffee. The lounge was also closed. The seating is uncomfortable and impossible to sleep on, which I really noticed given my kids had to be up at 3.30am to get there. Power points are not easy to find and I couldn't even by a charge cable for my phone. I could go on.

By far the worst airport I've ever experienced. Nowhere to get a meal, very few shops and the main duty free shop prices everything in US dollars. Not much use for someone wanting to use their remaining Brazilian Reals. You could, in fact, use them but had to convert the prices to see how overpriced things were and if you could afford it. The few other small shops were all closing during the evening so missed out on trade. Had to queue approx 1hr 50mins for a midnight flight even though it appeared that it was the only flight due to depart. Only 4 check in desks open which became effectively 2 when two sets of people were there for over 20 minutes. No attempt was made to open more desks by the time we'd checked in the shops were closing. Not a good end to a holiday.

Small airport closed at night, not practical, fortunately the staff and police are benevolent otherwise the time would be long, few shops and hot spots but it's small so... Singularly lacking seats.. FR: Petit aéroport fermé la nuit, pas pratique, heureusement que le personnel et les policiers sont bienveillants sinon le temps serait long, peu de boutiques et de points chauds mais c'est petit alors. Manque singulièrement de sièges.

I have arrived with pretty bad expectations after reading the reviews here but every single person was so kind to me that I had to come back to leave a positive review. Absolute pleasant surprise, correct exchange rates that I'm not used to, clean, easy to navigate, staff super kind and respectful. I am happy that my experience was different from others.

A supposedly international city airport, and in the huge transit area the managers don't even manage to install a few water fountains for cool refreshing water, for tired and thirsty travellers, especially those with children. What an appalling omission. It is a shame really, as in most other respects, the airport is very pleasant.

Very unfriendly to westerners. We asked for help and we were in a rush to take our next flight. They only shouted to us: “sit down”. Also we where the only ones that had to go to a special security and they didn’t want to tell us why. Some people looked very angry at us. It was an very unpleasant experience. Also the signs where very bad. We followed a sign and came on a closed area. Some guy helped us but he was very angry. We have been to many countries but this was the worst ever…

I am quite shocked with the extreme poor condition of Terminal 2, the bathrooms are very dirty, smelly. Both the lounges were extremely poorly maintained as well and the air conditioning was not working while the outside temperature was over 45 degrees C, when we asked the workers there, they said it has been over a month that the air conditioning is not working. The drinks at the lounge were hot as the refrigerators where not working either. While doing the boarding, one of the workers was literally shouting on people with zero respect. The terminal doesn’t have any proper food and beverage places, no restaurants, inexistent entertainment.

Flew DXB - RUH - CAI. Taxied for about 10 minutes after landing and then on top of that had to take a bus to the terminal which took another 10 minutes. On departure, also had to take a bus to the aircraft and taxied for a lengthy time again. The airport staff are deplorable. Everyone I came across was rude. No one wants to help, or acts like asking them something is a huge inconvenience. It’s the opposite of what I’ve experienced in other GCC countries. Saudi is lightyears behind UAE and Qatar when it comes to service and treating people with respect. I would not recommend anyone transiting through King Khalid International, Riyadh.

The staff in Riyadh International Airport (departure) are very rude. I drop my son in airport because he is going back to the US to study while we are waiting my son just to pass the immigration I was crying looking at him from a far because as a mother I am going to miss him but one staff guy rooming around shouting, yelling at me to go away he was very rude, ill-mannered, disrespectful creature I’ve ever met in my entire life. How can Saudi Arabia attracts tourists if the people are impolite and discriminate expats? Calling out the management in International Airport in Riyadh hire a professional, educated and well mannered staff.
Riyadh airport is a nice airport. We had to transit from there and were surprised to see that how beautiful is even their domestic terminal.
I arrived in Saudi Arabia for a layover for 8 hours. When I got there, they asked me to pay for visas to stay in the airport. I didn't leave the airport and was not informed of this earlier.

Saudi immigration officials and airport staff are unpolite and rude in general. I was travelling with my 3 young daughters and my wife on Saudi airline. We had 19 hours of layover time in Riyadh airport. My plan was to get transit or tourist visa and stay in some hotel near airport during my connection or layover time. I was told by Saudi airline earlier that being an American citizen, i can apply for tourist visa on arrival on the airport on arrival. But my plan did not work. Saudi immigration officials would not grant us tourist visa or transit visa. We got stuck inside the airport for 19 hours. My wife and daughters had to sleep on the floor during night time. Make your transit or layover time is as short as possible.  If you need tourist or transit visa, make sure you have it before you get on the airplane.

This airport is a total scam. We arrived on a Wizz A Mir flight from Vienna. Even though we had no intention entering Saudi Arabia they made us and hundreds of other passengers pay for a visa just to go from one Terminal to the other. Cost $130 per person. Staff rude and unhelpful. Total chaos. Free wifi sign up page only on Arabic.

The rental car area is appallingly signed. It is conveniently a short walk from the terminal but there is only an initial ramp and then there is no path for suitcase dragging people to go to the next row apart from the gaps between the cars. The different companies have small signs and it is impossible to know where to go. If one is unlucky then you need to walk back and forth to find your spot. Returning is the same problem to drive around and find the spot. I am writing this as I spoke to the rental company and it appears everyone complains but the airport will not do anything about this. Maybe this publicity will help them improve.

The security screening at this airport is the worst I've ever experienced and I fly a lot. They insist you place liquids in a zip lock bag at the screening, they don't supply them. Just leave anything like that in your bag and you'll have no issues. If you don't have a clear bag and put your liquids in the tray they throw them away, obviously telling you it's their policy afterwards where they fail to tell you any of this before security. I'd put a 75ml face cream in the tray and he threw it in the bin after the scanner then sarcastically told me it's my own fault as liquids need a clear bag. Contradictory to his comment he had no issues with the toothpaste, nasal spray and lip balm being in my bag. His colleague prior to this told me the stuff I had would be fine. They literally make this up as they go along.  My partner took their few liquids out and into the tray the same as me and was told they could keep them. They have zero logic at this airport.

After a wonderful time, we encountered the most rude and unprofessional employee at the airport in St. Kitts. She clearly was unhappy with her job. Being a TSA employee, we expected a certain level of professionalism and courtesy, as we have always experienced in the past at many different airports. Since tourism is the main source of income for this island, we expected better. Her behavior would not be tolerated at my company; therefore, we shouldn’t have to tolerate a rude and unprofessional employee while on our vacation.

I left this airport on 15/10/2017 and was thoroughly disgusted at the way the staff behaved. They were rude, aggressive and unprofessional towards passengers who had been delayed by the tropical storm. They did not even help the situation by processing the passengers quickly, instead they wasted time arguing with them and shouting at them for being late for the flight, which was through no fault of their own. No passenger should have to endure this kind of treatment and the airport should dismiss these staff and replace them with staff who are trained in Customer Services skills. I would recommend the international community to give St Kitts a miss until they do this as generally people respond to an impact on their bottom line. St Kitts if you don't value international visitors, find another industry as tourism will not survive. Thankfully, this was not a similar experience at the hotel and within other island tourist venues but the first impressions count. The airport facilities are very limited (no ATMs or exchange facility, limited food and drink), customs is very slow and unfriendly, no special assistance for disabled and elderly passengers despite long queues. Having travelled to other Caribbean airports, this is better elsewhere e.g. Antigua, St Lucia, Barbados, Dominican Republic etc so no excuses.

Since there is no other airport that you can go through to get to this place I have to recommend it. Staff were friendly and nice. There were no long lines at departure I was taking AA flight in the afternoon and there were some people waiting for BA flight. At arrival I went through immigrations and customs with no hassle. Lady at immigration even said Welcome to St. Kitts; I never hear those pleasantries in the US! I heard they are building a new terminal. So I hope they could have more services at the new terminal.

Tiny but well kept airport different design not too many flights but departure lounge seemed chaotic. Immigration is friendly but takes a long time a few shops you need to pay attention to the counters to find out where you're going to check-in. Overall experience fair.

Arriving here is a potential nightmare especially at the weekends. They are just not geared up to handle more than one jet the size of 777 at a time. Queues at passport control can stretch almost out to the tarmac and although very friendly and courteous they are so slow. Baggage reclaim takes forever and it is just a scrum to try and get through customs. On the last trip we were in a queue for customs clearance and the officer in charge of our line just disappeared. We had to start all over again!
$7.40 for a 10oz Coffee is price gouging at its worst. If you are hungry at this airport, be prepared to sell a kidney in order to pay for anything. Probably the most expensive coffee in Australia

Lovely and clean little country airport offering frequent flights to BNE. Short and long term parking in front of the terminal is free. Restroom facilities very clean and in good working condition. Airport has 4 gates but they are pretty 4 separate doors right next to each other leading on to the tarmac (no air bridges). Security staff well mannered and friendly. Free Wifi in the terminal. Only one fast food type of restaurant with very average food and rather expensive prices. Seating in the terminal is rather uncomfortable (hard metal type of seats) so suggest you buy a coffee or chocolate bar and find a seat at the fast food restaurant. Overall a very friendly and efficient environment.

The worst experience I have had at this airport. On Thursday 2nd September I had a flight to London in the evening. I live in the south of England and for this flight I had a night in a hotel in London before taking the train the next day to Portsmouth. So I spent 3 days with my parents who live in Aurillac, they had to drop me off early at the airport that day by car to avoid going back in the night because they are old and it's still an hour and a half drive. I spent the afternoon there waiting to do my check in, of course with the restrictions in England, I had done my test 3 days before without really paying attention to the time and I had also scheduled an appointment in a clinic near my home for the test 2 days later. When I was boarding, the agent told me that my health pass had expired by 2 hours and that she couldn't let me board.  I told her that I didn't know, that I had done it within 72 hours and moreover I had my 2 doses of vaccine, but she wouldn't listen. The solution that she proposes to me at 20h00 for a departure at 21h25, it is necessary to contact the police station so that it allows me to open a pharmacy of guard to make me the test in 15 min and then to return to embark. When I had no transport in the middle of nowhere, she had no shame in offering this solution. This kind of service is pathetic, I found myself alone trying to find a solution. I waited for a taxi for 1 hour outside as there was nothing around to get me to Rodez, then found a hotel room at my own expense. As there were no more flights to London until Sunday in Rodez, I had to find a pharmacy that could give me a hygienic PCR in 15 minutes, take another taxi to the train station to go to Toulouse. Another taxi to Bagnac airport and then an easy jet flight to London. In total I paid 200 euros out of my own pocket plus the hotel room I lost in London 100 euros. The staff in this airport is miserable, no help was offered, no solution, you find yourself alone in the middle of nothing.

This little airport is very nice and adapted to the demand and number of passengers. There was only one cafe but with nice food and drinks. Because of the small numbers of passengers traveling through that airport, there was absolutely no waiting. I would defenitly go there again.

No long queues no hustle and bustle easy parking adequate facilities. This is an airport where you can be sitting in your car ready to move off into the beautiful French countryside 20 minutes after landing! This is how air travel should be - civislised!

A small little provincial airport can be a touch uncomfortable in hot weather as the large glass windows absorb the sun as you wait in the departure area. One small cafe serving reasonable food and drink. Check in quick and car hire points convenient to main entrance. Good main road access to the town of Rodez and Tarn and Tarn et Garonne etc.

United Airlines flight 301 supposed to depart at 5:35am. We are currently still waiting at 6:07am because MFR is using a new 3rd party crew with only 1 person qualified to load luggage. Unacceptable! We pay good money to fly with an airline that makes you feel safe. Now, at 6:19 am were waiting on another company to deice the wings. Flights are made months in advance. The airport and airline were aware that trained ground crew is needed to load a plane along with de icing planes. This is ridiculous!

I love the Rogue Valley but thumbs down to this place at the moment. They are building a new terminal to replace the dark and depressing thing they have now. Unfortunately the parking lots and rental car lots are quite a long walk with all of the construction going on. I struggled in 90F+ degree heat to take my bags from my rental car to the old terminal. They do provide a rental car shuttle for rental car patrons. One has no idea where to wait for the shuttle and he drove right by me. The TSA staff seem to think they are running some sort of Vegas-style comedy act the way they talk to you. The restaurant is horribly overpriced--get something to go at one of the many fastfood places on the way to the airport. By the way the roads around the airport can be confusing and so are the signs.

A small provincial airport serving Bangkok DMG. Two airlines serve the airport, NOK Air and Air Asia. Avoid using Air Asia if I were you. A couple of food outlets selling snacks and water. Well set up and very efficient. I have used the airport on many occasions. I get collected when I use the airport so not sure what the Taxi connections are like.
A small but friendly airport which is quite central. The facilities are adequate for the size of the country. It is clean and tidy and the staff are helpful.

Very bad experience I faced in Reunion. 13 hour flight delay. No one responsible in airport. No proper food. No proper lounge. No proper WiFi. Airport shopping is very costly. Ground staff don't answer a single question. And in between they don't know English.

I have visited this airport numerous times over the last years. Arrivals, departures and transit. Air Austral, a very good airline in the indian ocean is using this airport as its hub, unfortunately this is the most awful airport, even compared to all other African airports I have visited. Transfers If you are on a transfer flight, be prepared to ring a bell to get through security, and wait up to an hour before they open the door. Departure They are trying to set record in the longest check-in process ever. I have experienced 4 times that the check in number has changed while in line. Expect to use 1 hour to check in if you have just carry on or already checked in online. Not much to do while you are inside the airport after security. A small taxfree, and kinda a restaurant and a few stalls. Free internet, if it works. Usually it does not. You have to check screens to know your gate. It is not a lot of gates, so it do not require many steps. English is not spoken in stores or restaurants. Arrival: Buses comes if they want, usually no taxis, or wait forever. One atm, if it does not work, you do not get euros. Very unorganized airport, bad service. It is a shame since the best airline in the area uses it as a hub.

Arrival on Sunday morning (22 Apr): Good airport, quick luggage delivery, clean airport. Departure on Thursday evening (27 Apr): Check in correct - no air conditioning, very hot temperature (more than 30°C on the evening), very crowded due to small boarding lounge and not enough seats. Only one small bar in international area for more than 3 large aircraft (B777) departing at the same time.

A quick visit to Rome from Prague on Ryanair. The airport location close to the city is great with a painless connection via Airport Link Bus + Train. The entire trip easily purchased on the Trenitalia app for only 2.7€ to Termini. The airport terminal itself is large enough to accommodate 3-4 flights at the same time (could be stretched to capacity with more traffic). Boarding and disembarking on foot with some shops available. Staff was curtuous so our departure was on time. The proximity to Rome is a strong selling point when comparing to FCO.

Currently standing waiting for boarding in this airport. Too small, dirty, no air flow, not enough seats for the masses of people that are of course here because people fly to places. Too hot, poor staffing, overcrowding, avoid this airport.

The airport was clean and the the personnel kind and professional. Bad transfer service if you arrive late at night. The taxi service outside the airport is highly dishonest. I think it is dangerous for lonely woman. If you don't have choice book it from a website and take the name of the driver and the number of the cab. But better to avoid. So good airport but not to arrive late at night for the quality of transfer service.

Atrocious! Staff rude, airport dirty, and when your airline asks for incorrect paperwork and bars you from your flight in error (dealing with that separately) allowing you to book the next day meaning you must stay at the airport, airport management bring in the police to force you out of the airport and make you sleep outside in the rain. No access to the airport between 11pm and 4.30am. After costing us nearly €400 unnecessarily can’t afford a hotel. No sympathy from the airport, vending machines outside but no access to toilet facilities and refuse to wee in a floodlit car park! Cold, wet & in need of the toilet. Writing this at 3am on a bench outside the airport.

It was terrible. We arrived at the airport at midnight and the airport was closed. It was very cold and rainy, we were wet from the rain and sat in the cold stairs with many others for hours until 4:30 am when they open the doors. It was crowded and all of us didn't expect that the airport was closed especially in a big city like Rome.

I’ve been to some small airports such as London City, and generally had a reasonable experience. This airport is overall poor. It is very poorly equipped in terms of facilities. Only 2 small cafes with minimal seating, perhaps 10 stools maximum in the “food hall area”. Quite rude staff at the coffee shops, not surprising given the environment they’re having to work in. In addition to inadequate food & drink facilities there is just a general lack of space for the number of people. The airport’s location is closer to Rome city centre than Fiumicino however it takes about double the time to get into centre of Rome by public transport. In summary, totally naff airport with poor public transport links to city centre. Choose Fiumicino.

Absolutely appalling airport. Barely any seating, places to eat, or toilets. When the airport gets busy, the whole place comes to a standstill. If possible, always fly to/from Rome Fiumicino as it is much, much better.

This airport has much potential, but its so badly managed that it totally destroyed the customer experience. The queues to board the plane were horribly long, with no attendants to manage. The busses were slow, and actually ferried passengers for a later flight prior to ours which was 10 minutes to boarding. There were no seats for everyone. The staff were rude and unfriendly. Overall one of the worst airports I have seen. Very surprising for an European country.

Hate this airport. While getting to Fiumicino is as easy as hopping on a direct train from almost anywhere in Rome that leaves very regularly, getting to Ciampino is perhaps one of the hardest ways of getting to any airport that I've ever been to. It is impossible to take public transport to this airport and make your flight. Period. Sure, a taxi will cost you 40 euros, but that's cheaper than the 100 euros you'll inevitably have to pay to buy a new flight when you miss yours. I've left for this airport 3 hours before my flight and missed it. Just now, I arrived at 7:10 pm and wasn't home (in trastevere) until 9:45 pm. By the way, this airport closes. If you're waiting for a flight, they literally just kick you out in the cold. Writing this review has made me realize how every single experience I've had getting to or being at this airport has been terrible. It might be the worst place in the world.

This is the most ridiculous airport I have ever found. While the seats inside the airport are completely empty and a security man is guarding an empty space, people are freezing outside, praying for the time to pass faster. From 12 to 4 am everybody gets kicked out of the airport. It’s not like they are completely shutting down the airport, the lights are on, the heat is working, the place is guarded, etc. They simply choose to not care about the people who are clenching their teeth outside their door because of the cold. On 2 degrees celsius and quite powerful winds, no discrimination will be made: there were parents with small kids, older people, injured etc. There is no explanation that can be given in order to justify such a cruel way of treating anyone.

It is clean, modern and spacious. It is easily accessible by the Leonardo Express from Termini about half an hour. Employees are friendly and helpful and can speak English well. The WiFi connection is stable. Signposts are clear.

Worst airport experience in my 20 years of flying as an international journalist. The entry for global, non-EU travelers was a chaotic, massive maze of lines that never ended with only ome counter open. I waited two-and-a-half hours in a line with no chance of using a bathroom or water. Staff, if you can find them, were extremely rude and aggressive. I missed my business appointment and never have I felt so degraded as a traveller. Rest assured I will make sure none of my future flights stop in this torturous cluster-mess of human misery.

The minimum connection time at this airport is dishonest and not doable at all. It is technically 40 minutes, and ITA sells itineraries that meet this requirement but more than likely you will miss your connecting flight if you are transiting and have to go through passport control - we only caught our connecting flight to London after landing from Palermo due it being delayed. The e-gates which I am allowed to use as a British citizen don't work most of the time, I noticed several British citizens being rejected and sent to the manual desks which are understaffed with only half open despite a massive snaking queue full of transit passengers of various nationalities from morning bank of flights. I only made my flight after pleading with staff member and showing my boarding card that I was connecting with a short connection time. Lastly what doesn't help with connecting efficiently is the constant use of remote stands for planes instead of the many empty airbridges - you have a long wait for buses to arrive to pick everyone up from the plane, which then idles for ages, before taking long circuitous route to the terminal to drop you off. It's madness to do this in this day and age and with so many empty airbridges that could be used, not to mention the issues for less able passengers with diminished mobility.

The airport is very big, so you better arrive early if you have international flight. Immigration queuing might take more than an hour and duty free is very far away from lounges and gates; so you might have to choose between duty free or visiting the lounge. Staff are generally friendly even under pressure

I want to thank to all the staff at this airport for helping me find my luggage which was lost because of Zürich airport. The medicine of my mom were in that suitcase and all your team helped me a lot to locate and find it as soon as possible. Very warm hearted people and extreme professionals. They didnt skip any official procedure so that they kept the security conditions but did their best to help me. Unfortunately I do not remember their names but I hope this message will find them and make them feel appreciated. Thank you, wish you all the best and God bless you.

Arrived at 8:00 from Tirana. Flight from Tirana took 75 minutes approximately. Been waiting at passport control for 90 minutes where out of 24 control booths, only 4 work. Horrible airport who looks like it tries to be completely irritating to travelers.

I've never been part of something so beautiful but disorganized or met so many unhelpful and rude staff at an airport. They take their time with everything and have no shame about it, there is no rush to get anything done, the airport is beautiful got great shops amazing shopping experience, terrible airport service, staff cant be on time everything is late everything changes me and a few people where running around for an hour and a half staff was just confusing us more than actually helping. Seems like they are focussing on making it a mega shopping mall instead of focusing on basics of an airport. Currently 50 mins behind schedule of even taking off. Avoid this airport if you can, Rome is beautiful. Unlucky , that the reception of it is so low.

Absolutely horrible experience at the airport. Waited two hours in the queue for passport control. I had several heavy bags one which my bag was broken the wheels were off. Got screamed at in front of everyone, was humiliated by it all to come get my bag , pointing at me saying all my fault. I had a bad accident prior to my flight and also was carrying this heavy luggage for hours i said i couldn’t physically carry it anymore and was in a lot of pain was then shouted at again- the women said I dont care. All your fault, all your fault and shouted at me to get my bags and leave. Will not be back. Was really upset how I was treated so badly.

I was scammed by a taxi driver. When there is a taxi service with regulated queue's outside of an airport, one expects a degree of safety. I don’t care how beautiful an airport is, or how many shops it has, if I don’t feel safe - it doesn’t matter. Before getting into the taxi, double check that they have a card machine and don’t get in if they say it’s cash only. Very upsetting to have this happen on the day I arrived in Rome.

Leonardo da Vinci  Fiumicino Airport is a huge, well-designed, well-decorated airport with clean and huge facilities. I waited there for 5 hours as the check-in, security check and immigration were completed early. However I spent good time as the airport facilities made easy travelers to navigate and browse for shopping and restaurants. Airport staffs were good. They speak English well. Only bad thing is that, travelers have to walk long to get into the boarding bridges.

Old worlddescribes this airport in Southern Russia. As with most flights in Russia passengers arriving on my flight were bussed to the terminal even though it was less than 100 metres across the tarmac. Let out and straight into the main hall to meet and greet where we had to wait until the luggage had been put on the conveyor then into a side room to collect our things. As with all Russian airports (and I seriously think this is a good policy) you have to show your matching luggage tags before you are let out of the room. Taxis are available (of course) or you can catch a bus to the eastern suburbs or just walk across to the main road (it's only 500 metres) if you want a bus in the other direction. Didn't use it for departure so can't comment on things like check-in.

There in December 2013 Jan 2014 and Mar 2014. 3 times very quick handling of luggage etc. comfortable waiting area and free internet. No queues for Immigration desk. One point that is minor if you don't know where the bus to Rotterdam centre is located you may have a problem however I took a taxi and then it takes only 5-6 minutes. Its much more agreeable than the big airports like Toulouse Orly JFK or even Schiphol (also in the Netherlands).

This is a very pleasant airport especially compared to Schiphol. It's efficient staff are friendly and the decor resembles a hotel lounge rather than the average airport look. At peak times when a lot of leisure flights depart it can however get quite crowded. As this airport is labelled as Rotterdam-The Hague Airport there has to be a public transport link to The Hague. This is inadequate consisting of a small shuttle bus connecting the terminal with the nearby metro station where you need to change. It's all a bit of a hassle as the minibus is often too small for the number of passengers and baggage and runs infrequently outside rush hours. The schedule should rather be adjusted to the arrival and departure times of flights. Better still would be a direct public transport link to The Hague.

An airport geared towards business travellers it's in excellent condition and has very appealing decor - feels like a hotel lounge. There is also free Wi-Fi which is welcome. There are very few queues are the majority of travellers are going onwards to Heathrow and New York which made for a pleasant change with Transavia than flying through Eindhoven. Very clean and security methodical. However the food prices are extremely high even by airport standards. But otherwise this is an excellent airport the most impressive I've used.

I flew to LCY from RTM in the middle of the day when it wasn't busy. The only way to get there by public transport is the bus from the city centre. Had to ask staff at the ticket counter to open bag drop. Security staff were more interested in chatting amongst themselves than paying attention to passengers. Food options poor with shelves barely stocked. Toilets (air-side) smelt revolting and needed a deep clean. Staff in the duty-free shop were eating their lunch at the counter also chatting amongst themselves while 'serving' me. Overall the staff throughout the entire airport didn't seem to care. The plus side is it's a small airport and the queuing was almost non-existent. In summary I would only use this airport if I were living near to it.

I travelled from London Heathrow to Rotterdam on 2 February 2013 and returned the following day. On the outward journey I was through immigration/passport control in less than a minute. Arrivals area contains an information desk which provided useful information on onward connections and provided me with change for the bus travel recommendations and a complementary city map. Bus number 33 leaves from virtually outside arrivals and takes approx 20 minutes to reach Rotterdam Central. It costs 3 euros at the time of writing and the driver has limited change. On the return journey there was no queue for check-in and virtually no queue for security. This is a small airport but there are decent airside facilities including a duty free shop cafe newsagent and an upstairs bar (which has an outdoor seating area and viewing platform). If you are travelling with BA there are no lounge facilities but you are allowed three complementary items from the airport cafe (for which you will need to complete an information card). Clear information throughout the terminal and announcements in English and in Dutch. Free Internet in departures which was fast and required no password. Overall this was a stress free experience and I was impressed with Rotterdam Airport.

As I live nearby it's a convenient airport for me especially because of frequent flights to London and Southern France. You can make use of free Internet. Parking is cheap. Connection to Rotterdam City and Port area is good and quick. Hardly any queuing you can arrive 10 mins before departure without any problems. Whenever possible I make use of Rotterdam-The Hague Airport.

Looks like a tin shed for starters. Immigration could not comprehend that I was Asian- Australian and held me up for ten minutes flicking through pages of my passport back and forth back and forth. I was the last one on the flight allowed through even though I was one of the first off the plane. I can understand that the Netherlands may have a problem with illegal immigration but a quick conversation with me would have revealed my fluent English with an Australian accent. Assuming that someone who isn't white but travelling on a Western passport is probably illegal is just racist.

I just flew into this airport and not out so I can only say that the bags arrived very quickly and efficiently. I will also say that walking from the plane to the terminal and night it seemed as though we were the only people on earth in the middle of nowhere. I've never been to an airport that was so quiet. It certainly seemed bereft of planes!

Good shopping for such a small airport. Clean and clear. Cheap car parking compared with Schiphol. When arriving plane parked in front of terminal and was outside the building with my checked bag in 5 minutes!

Rotterdam airport is small but very easy to get to as I live only 10min away. People are very friendly and helpful. I travel on average 1x per year sometimes more normally I only have hand luggage and have only once encountered extra checks and body search. I find check in and arrivals no problem and never had to wait very long. I do think it could use a few more shops and especially as I fly early morning it would be nice to have some kind of breakfast that is not too expensive.

This airport is clearly not equipped to take the number of pax departing after the winter break. Check in was too crowded, so we had to wait on another floor. Conveyer belt at check in blocked by heavy usage. Boarding never indicated on screens, but was only announced via PA system. Shambles. Shame, as we had such a great time in Finland.

The airport of Santa Claus, it's only 2km away from the arctic circle and Santa Claus Village which is a major tourist destination and during winter holiday season there are a lot of charter flights coming here. Terminal is not big with 8 departure gates in total, so I can imagine that space is tight during holidays. Now it was smooth since there were no other flights departing. There are few shops and cafes after security to get some last minute souvenirs and snacks. The city of Rovaniemi is not far either, so it's easy to get there by taxi or by bus.

Efficient security, although very nit-picky about rules. There is no water for cheaper than 3.40EUR once through security!! I could not take my medicine. Water should be a human right, most international airports offer cheaper or free water.

We got to the airport early and were one of the first through security. Should be quick, right? Unfortunately, no. The security staff were very rude and abrupt and decided to go through every piece of everything in the suitcase even before it went through the scanner. My wife was practically in tears because they told her they were going to confiscate all her toiletries until they finally let her take everything except a $50 bottle of oil used for a skin condition. I had several camera batteries and a portable charger "confiscated" from my checked luggage and was told these have to be in my carry-on. Interesting because I went through Frankfurt airport and Helsinki airport without a problem. Apparently the safety monitors in this outpost airport know more about security than the big airports, or they needed camera batteries and chargers. Had I taken them in my carry-on, they would have been confiscated because they should have gone into my checked luggage. Overall treated very poorly. Such a sad representation of this country, the people and the culture. Especially for an area that relies heavily on tourism. Everything else was uneventful. Oh, and the airplane needed to get a jump start because we were told the starter (in airplane terms) wasn't working. This delayed us 20 min.

An excellent small but well equipped airport. Clearly built to service the Santa charter trade I went through off-season when it was quiet. The security staff are probably the most pleasant anywhere saying thank you and smiling and for that alone it deserves a recommendation.

This is my idea of an Airport. Minimum of fuss checked in through security in mins ready for plane inside 10 mins. Leaving well from "Secured to stand" to exit to the main road 4 mins including collecting luggage. Queues there were not any to measure by.

Very nice small airport located outside Rzeszów, easily accesible by the bus from the city center, inside the airport was not busy during the time of travel, took less than 5 minutes to go through security. A duty free shop and a bar available, however a very good lounge is avaiable too at a very good price around 50PLN, with very comfortable waiting area and very good selection of drinks and snacks. Overall I recommend going from this airport.

Shuttle service for rental cars is getting worse and worse by the day. I have been traveling weekly to SMF and I can say the shuttle service has gotten worse by the day in the last six months. It used be couple of minutes wait to now it is over 20 minutes of wait with 100s of passengers waiting in shuttle line. At this point, I am seriously not renting car from the airport and just catch Uber ride to downtown rental agencies and it would be cheaper and faster.

Plan on waiting 50 minutes for the rental car shuttle from terminal B or use airlines that fly out of terminal A. Worst shuttle service ever out of Terminal B. Tons of business travelers needing to get to rental cars and the wait is inconsiderate to those of us who use the airport for work.

This is the worst airport to arrive with luggage. The airport is tiny and they managed to take more than an hour to start releasing our luggage. It is absolutely the worst airport in Northern California

Budget lots more time for this airport, horribly inefficient. Taking the more difficult option of public transport (rental cars, etc.) is penalized by drop-off area furthest from each terminal. Rental car center requires dragging bags across lots, through building and then long wait on huge bus, only to be dropped off on outer land furthest from check-in! Maddening. If you miss turn-off to your terminal (no sign, only colors) be prepared for long delay as you drive miles to other terminal and terminal return. Why a smallish regional airport needs to be spread out over miles of terminal is difficult to comprehend. It’s one thing to have to significant transfer between terminals at London Heathrow (giant airport in urban area) it’s quite another at small regional. How about putting terminals together and allow passengers to access them without driving all over god’s green earth. Sorry for the rant but dragging heavy bags for 20 minutes at 5am needlessly requires some decompression.

Worst airport in a decade. The gas station on the drive in is great, but getting out was awful. No signs! And dark red Jersey barriers in the middle of the road impossible to see which is bad cause 3 of us were driving around trying to find an exit. No signs. Then one tiny sign across the road, no lighting to direct you to the airport. Can’t see in dark and fog. Drove the wrong way, it is a two mile trip to a dead end to get back to the airport. Signs to rental cars as bad. Can’t see in fog which is common this time of year. Another 2 mile misdirection. Rental rental requires a bus. Train to terminal B ok but just be warned. Marginal food choices. Coffee stand closed at 07.00! I have been in 3rd world countries with better quality. Take extra time. Be warned!

Was easy to get to, however after I checked in my luggage, I never got them at the final destination as they never made it there! Every time I fly from this airport I have an issue! for both Domestic or International flights!

I’m writing after multiple negative experiences with Sacramento Airport’s traffic operations staff (SMF Operations). They are consistently rude and unnecessarily aggressive. I understand the importance of controlling traffic relative to departures and arrivals, however, it is unacceptable and unnecessary for these employees to be as rude and aggressive as they consistently are. I am wondering if these persons are hired with afore knowledge of their inability to perform their duties without any public service etiquette at all. I would rather travel to the South Bay Area to fly than to fly out of local Sac International in order to avoid having any encounters with these employees whatsoever. I do not appreciate being verbally assaulted by these employees and this is something that definitely should be addressed and changed.

Easy to Navigate airport with a simple layout. Not many restaurants/food places were open due to COVID. Tons of seating available. Easy train connection between check in area and gate area. Extremely short security lines.

What a horrible experience. Rental car shuttle line had hundreds in line. Took forever to board. Bus driver was singing and doing hand gestures, I felt unsafe. At airport security, TSA had a hundred people in line. Meanwhile 5 agents and a dog are standing around at the front of the line. The young agent ordering us through the xray took lessons on TV from a nazi program. Overall, a very trying time getting out of Sacramento.

My home airport, so I know it rather well. While not being a hub (or even a terribly important spoke) for any airline, it's quite practical and typically less stressful than other NorCal alternatives. The new terminal is nice, if a bit over-sized for itself, I'm a fan of the giant red rabbit (why not be different?), the old terminal is still quite functional, clean and serviceable. Decent selection of restaurants/coffee shops, etc. in both. A few words of caution for those who don't use the airport regularly: It's not far from the city, but it is in the middle of an empty field, so no hotels nearby, etc. If you have a very early flight, stay at a hotel and use Uber or equivalent - don't plan on staying at airport. Taxis are a total scam from SMF and usually take longer than needed: use Uber or similar, Blue vans are usually good if you have time to spare. TSA seems to be improving, but can still be a bit nightmarish, especially in the older terminal and on Monday mornings and Friday afternoons, or at holidays.

Last year I flew from Saint John Airport on my way back to Toronto. Although the airport is quite small but the service is fast and very friendly. Check in staff at Air Canada counter was very friendly and even the security staff were courteous to all passengers. As soon as boarding was announced we embarked the aircraft followed by a short walk as there are no air bridges used at this airport.

Almost a shambles. Wait an hour a half for boarding pass / to check in luggage, a further hour through customs. 6 flights going out only two desks open, then a further 20 minutes in passport control. So badly managed and very badly understaffed.

Visiting the island for the first time, I was impressed on how modern and functional the airport was. First they send you to the "Egates" which does not make sense as you will line up again for them to check the "airport tax". The officer will ask you how long are you going to stay and stamp you in, if you do not have bags, you're outside the airport in seconds! Taxis will ask you 20 euros, if you have time and a tight budget, outside on the main highway there is a bus stop, but do not count on when a bus will show up, it depends on your luck. On the way out the lines move quick, security is also quick, immigration will snap your photo again and stamp you out. The sole complaint is about the annoucements volume, it is ridiculous. Overall Sal island is to be visited once in a lifetime I would say.

This airport is good but there is no wifi and check in desk is one. There air two shops and one cafe. The best thing is that there is an outdoor square and a fountain after passport control. There are 8 international gates. The gates area is modern.

Sal is a great small airport which is easy to use, lots of signs and decent food options. Good taxi services and shuttle buses to hotels. Clean and airy and bright. Would recommend. Aeroplanes park very close and many airlines fly to Sal which is useful. Friendly staff.

It's a very small airport which is both a good and a bad thing. There are no terminals as such and so it can be relatively quick to get from check in to departure gate that's if the luggage belts aren't broken. As it stands it's quite a pain free experience but the airport won't be able to cope with many more flights. Usually there are about 3/4 international flights a day carrying 150 - 300 customers per flight and then the 2/3 internal flights which carry around 70 pax. You can smoke after check in and there's a small bar each side offering mainly light snacks. Sometimes security check passports before check in sometimes they don't but I don't really understand their purpose in the main hall way which most airports would allow anyone access to.

By developing nation standards not a terrible airport but not a great one either. Check-in is slow food options are almost non-existent and security screening is on the lax side. There aren't close to enough seats in the departure lounge if there are two planes leaving and smoking is allowed inside the terminal. There are no real departure gates and planes are very close to the door but you must still be bussed to the plane instead of walking about 100 meters. On the up side the taxi drivers aren't pushy and give honest prices.

Modern airport - departure and arrival were quick, efficient and smooth. This not a big nor busy airport so there is never any big queues. Immigration police cordial and friendly. Almost feels like there is too much airport staff for volume of passengers particularly when departing - staff in the multiple cafés looked bored. I appreciated the clean toilets and multiple drinking water fountains where you could fill up water for free. Duty Free felt was the biggest letdown, very generic and poor. Not much local Dhofari or even Omani products, I think it could be better used to sell the country and region one final time before visitors leave instead of overpriced cheap souvenir tat or the usual generic Toblerone you can find at any airport in the world. Even local products like the luxury Amouage perfumes were at the usual price with no deals which was a shame.

Excellent location. Good services. I appreciate the airport but maybe it is necessary to improve the check-in services during the night time. Sometimes the terminal electronic system does not work and personnel seem to have problems with the check in.

The new expensive remodel and redesign of Salt Lake International was a total waste! The uber drivers mow have to stop downstairs versus directly bringing you to your terminal. Now you have to walk to a stair stack labyrinth maze. The ceiling signs do not help, and you always have to end up finding an attendant to guide you. Even security check entrance is a small tiny nook walkway obscure on the 2nd floor away from the 3rd floor checkin to which sends you on another walking journey. The airport is a disaster and who ever conducted the remodel floor plan should be barred from construction. Stay far away from this horrible airport.

Signs are all at 1 level in a line. Unable see what is in the terminal or find services. No service animal relief areas could be located in B terminal. We found was extremely hard to locate in A terminal. Airport employees couldn't tell us exactly where the service animal relief area were. We were told somewhere in A terminal by 4 employees. Bathrooms were unstocked and unclean. If you don't fly Delta, you are in a terminal which you have to walk under the tarmac to get to. This walkway was intentionally made just several feet short of being required to have a tram. They focused their upgrade to include a cardio workout. Fact: This isn't a gym, it is a transportation hub. They focused their upgrades in art installations. Fact: This isn't a museum. It is a transportation hub. The art installations actually block transportation signs from being seen when exiting to baggage. Fact: Good transportation hubs make it easy to get from point A to point B. With clear signage, easy to find facilities and travel needs. Clean facilities and as someone with accessibility needs i can easily say those with accessibility needs have been neglected. This airport provides a landing for airplanes and is a difficult transportation hub to traverse and find essential services. I travel all over the world 50-75% of the year. This airport it #1 on my worst airport list.

Bring your sneakers because you will be walking forever to get anywhere in this airport. Horrible experience both arrival and departure. I couldn’t find gate B for JetBlue, walked so far I almost missed my flight. Horrible design. No signage or help to get to the right gate. No employees to help answer questions . I will avoid this airport at all costs. 1/2 a mile to get from TSA to my gate. Insanity!
B Terminal is very hot. Like they're trying to save money on air conditioning. Restrooms are not clean - dirty seats. Paper Towels on floor.

Horrible arrival experience every time I've flown into Salt Lake City. Sat on the tarmac for 30 minutes at 1130 pm at night. Excuse was they didn't have a gate.  I saw plenty of gates available in the B concourse. If I had another airport to choose from to depart out of I would use it. SLC has expanded to make more money and shows their greed. Maybe they should hire more people to help run the airport.

Terribly designed airport. It took an hour to get from my gate to baggage claim and get my bags. I assumed the very long terribly designed path from gate to baggage claim would allow my bags to get there before me. I was wrong. The long walk was rewarded with a very long additional wait for my bags.

The absolute worst airport in terms of check in, baggage check and security I have experienced. Have flown out of this airport multiple times and never had a good experience. Arrived over 2 hrs before scheduled departure and almost missed my flight. There are simply not enough personnel working baggage check and security, not to mention the security line is basically overrun by Clear. If we didn’t have family in Utah, I would never set foot in this airport again.

This airport is a guaranteed waste of time. Domestic flights connecting east to west or vice versa are often dropped off on the tarmac in terminal A with 20 minutes to exit the plane, wait until you load on the lethargic bus driver inch to the ramp for not the terminal and sprint a mile to terminal D—for instance. Good luck making your connection. Between the way they have connections physically spaced and how closely they are scheduled, it’s like they are actively working to prevent connections. I am rescheduling all my flights to avoid this airport.
Worst airport for people who have a hard time walking. No moving sidewalks or tunnel shuttles. No quick places to buy food in Southwest terminal.

This is a beautiful airport with a great selection of food & shopping. Unfortunately that is where it ends. I think it must have been laid out by a 5 year old. Getting to my Southwest gate from the car rental I had to change floor levels 5 times. Security is a complete mess and so disorganized. The different gate terminals are so long and the distance is ridiculous. I could never take an elderly parent to visit.

To suggest that this is an international airport is really stretching the imagination. The departure area is so small and the security area is so limited, that people have to enter by flight number. Airside has no facilities whatsoever and queuing times mean there is no opportunity to look at shopping or food options landside. There is one small shop airside that calls itself duty free. This is a hideous joke. In Salvador town you can purchase one litre of 51 cacasa for 11 reales, in the duty free shop 300 ml costs 20.00 reals. Overall I have had better service and facilities from my local grass strip that has a tea caravan next to the field. If you have any choice fly from anywhere else except here.
Chaotic lines at check-ins (GOL and Avianca) no idea how to organize slow and uninterested. After security fully overcrowded hot not enough seats and little options to have something to eat.

Although there is little traffic at SSA there will always be long lines. This is especially true for international flights. Although there may be only one international flight leave in 3 hrs immigration will take 1 hr. And beware of the arrival of 2 international flights within 1 hr. You will see the typical Brazilian chaos!

Travellers arriving into SSA on international flights beware: most of the cash machines in the airport for some unfathomable reason cease service at 23:59.
