Security line was quick and efficient. Passport control was also light in traffic and staff were polite as is often the case in Brazil. Not too many shops but the terminal is manageable and not huge so walking distance is good. What lets Guarulhos T3 down a bit is the signposting needs to be better. The Free WIFI was great.

Organizational mess! Interactive signs show wrong info or not info at all. Voice information are only in Portuguese and gate service does not speak English. Near gate 226 5 buses stay all the time near the doors running inserting its fumes constantly inside the terminal. Ecology.

The new terminal 3 is finally a leap to the 21st century, e-gates for brazilians make the process stressless and quick, food and drinks limited but good options (margaritaville, starbucks, pizza hut, subway etc...). They take all cards but very expensive though. Air con is really strong, I would bring a sweater if I were you, staff are ok but only speak portuguese, foreigners be aware. They have installed electric outlets everywhere, very nice, even in european airports you struggle to find it. Overall good experience. The new metro does not arrive at airport, you have to take a bus to the terminal, it is a waiste of time, take the direct bus instead, much quicker and convenient.

A post-modern airport with many good restaurants and very spacious and comfortable environment. Inside the departure area you have an amazing view of the aircrafts. The seats are very ergonomic and delightful. All the airports areas are very clean and hygienic. On the other hand, there are not many signals explaining the directions for each of the airport's areas and facilities.

It's a small modern airport with a really nice look. On arrival there were some 200 people arriving from Lisbon. So lines for immigration and visa counters looked really long at first. However, it took only 30-40 minutes to clear immigration and collect baggage. As there is only one or less international flights per day there is no bank at the airport and the ATM wasn't working. You can still pay with euros for taxis if needed and there is an official list of taxi fares posted close to one of entrances. On departure for domestic flights everything worked well. There are some small shops and a café with normal prices in the main hall. There was nothing opened on departure hall as you enter it only before flight departure. They probably open the small cafe for international departures. The strangest thing was that there was no security control at all before domestic departures. I have no idea if it's usual or not but many locals were surprised. It's easygoing life on the islands but it seemed too chilled for me.

Being in this airport was so much fun. From the royce chocolate factory to different shopping areas, there are lots of thing to do. I arrived 3 hours early, but still did not have enoungh time to explore the airport. The immigration was systemized and there were almost no lines. Although it is not a 5 star airport I think it has to be one of the best in the world

I have been to some of the world's best 5-star (SIN, ICN, HKG, HND) airports, but Sapporo's New Chitose tops them all. Why? So much to do and enjoy - Airport History Museum, Royce Chocolate World factory, open-air Observation Deck, Movie Theatre, Onsen, Sky Museum (interactive airline stuff for kids and adults), Hello Kitty Theatre, Hotel, amazing number and variety of food court options. Aside from these "frills", New Chitose excels in what really matters to travelers. Despite huge crowds (Sapporo-Tokyo is one of the world's busiest routes) terminal is spacious and easy to navigate. Efficient check-in counters-one dedicated to just school groups. Spotless restrooms, plenty of seats in departure areas, Easy to use, frequent (every 15 minutes) JR train connections (39 minutes) to Sapporo Station. Polite, hard-working security teams, Short waits on the runway for takeoffs.

The queuing time was fast. But free wifi was poor, rather it didn't work at all. Not suitable for work. The screen shows departure flights by gate, each screen shows only the departure flights from the nearest gate. For example, if your flight departs from gate A and you are at gate F, you will not find your flight on the screen near you. So you have to run around to every gate in hope that the screen on those gates will show your flight.

This airport has frequent JR rail connections to Sapporo making it very convenient. Huge shopping area and many places to eat and drink. Support staff was very friendly and helped me make a free Wi-fi connection as well as find me a restaurant that serves vegetarian food.

Very good facilities as there are plenty of shops and restaurants. Great transport connection particularly as the JR station is just at the basement. However capacity at the international terminal seems to be pretty constrained. There can be very very long queues at both check-in and security when a few flights depart at around the same time.

I've flown through this airport 2 or 3 times now and it's always a good experience. It's a lovely modern building the staff are very helpful security/customs/immigration has always been quick and painless. It only takes 40-50 mins by train they have a decent airport hotel located in the domestic arrivals terminal and it's always spotless.

SIN-NAR-Sapporo-NAR-SIN trips for last two years Sapporo New-Chitose impressed me. Comfortable massage chairs located around airport dining options fair but still better than others small and somewhat ageing but still cosy. Check-in fast for domestic. Glad to go there again.

Shin-chitose airport is really effective! A lot of souvenir shops and wonderful musiam in the airport. A brand new international terminal will be open in 2010. Great hotels and various amusement things are worth of expecting.

A modern and convenient airport in Hokkaido Island. There is a direct train service from the Sapporo train station to the basement of the New Chitose Airport station. The only negative point about the airport is there are too many shops selling the same local stuff.

Sapporo's New Chitose airport is very effective and user friendly facility. Located somewhat far from Sapporo it is perfectly linked to the city and the region by rail. Quick check-in quick baggage delivery good choice of food outlets landside but not a lot of things to do airside. The train station is underground as almost everywhere in Japan. All in all very good. 5 star.

This is a pretty nice small airport where you can find anything you would expect from it. There are flaws like anywhere else. They definitely need more staff which is obvious. The offering of time killers are updated with new shopping places, but still have to work on it. My main issue was the parking which was pretty expensive so I had to search around for other solutions, since the parking at the airport ended up more expensive than my Wizz Air ticket. I use Google and found a private parking spaces but you can also look for others, I suggest this one definitely. Overall it is a decent airport that keeps on upgrading every year I visit it.

A small airport yet convenient for the amount of flights they receive. Check-in is mostly fast and efficient yet you can't use any online check-in yet due to restrictions by law. The airport has 2 jetbridges and 5 gates, the 3 others are used for walk or bus boarding. Border control is friendly and efficient. The airport has 1 duty free store but not much other facilities. Beware of taxi drivers demanding outrages prices for a trip to the city center. 15 KM should be more than enough. There's a bus service to the city center but timings are a bit off.

Sarajevo Airport is very small and very manageable. After you enter the main building there are check ins. Afterwards you have to go to the first floor where is one departure hall with 9 or 10 departure gates. There is plenty of seating, they also have big beanbags for seating, which can be quite fun and relaxing. There is only one bar with snacks and one shop. If you are travelling with children, the signs for baby changing room is misleading - after you follow the signs, there is no baby room. You have to follow the signs for the bathroom for disabled. If you wait for a long time, you might get very bored.
Small airport, small queue size, fast passport processing airport.  Staff are reasonable, but not a single smile. Smoking is unrestricted. Taxi service available outside gate.

Not much to complain about nowadays there is bus service offered by Centrotrans bus company and GRAS as well from airport to down town. Personnel at check-in counter need to be more friendly for example our flight to GOT via BUD was cancelled by Malev but we were issued tickets to fly with Austrian and people at check-in counter were making faces exhaling loudly while printing boarding passes for flight via VIE.

Very small but clean and cozy airport with only 3 gates. Going through the passport control and customs was a breeze. I do agree with the previous comments about taxis. There is no public transportation from the airport to the city so unless someone is picking you up or you're picking up a rental you're forced to take a cab which will routinely rip you off and not even turn on the meter. For a 10 minute ride I was charged 25.00 marks (currently USD $16.30)! If you can arrange some type of transportation other than the taxi my advice is to do so.

Small very clean and efficient from security check through check-in immigration and baggage claim. But it's not really a hospitable place: there's no restaurant only three cafes offering the same things (little or no food); a very modest and unappealing duty-free shop and a newsstand selling only local-language press. If you have to spend time here you're out of luck. Don't take the airport taxis which all overcharge; instead call the official city cabs by dialling 1515 they arrive quickly and charge the (relatively low) official rate.

Its very small but convenient airport. There is small duty free area and coffee bar in upper floor after immigration and also one coffee bar before immigration. Toilets are clean. Immigration procedures on arrival and on departure are simple and fast.

I have arrived and departed SJJ several times in the first half of 2007 and find very little to criticise . It is fairly small and not very busy so check-in luggage handling passport checks etc. tend to work quickly and effectively. I have only encountered helpful and friendly staff in all areas. One criticism is that there is no public transport to the airport except taxis - and you should agree the price before you get in. I did once walk from the nearest tram stop probably about 1.5km not recommended even with only hand luggage particularly when it starts to pour with rain halfway!

It is very clean and the toilets are cleaned by the crew literally every 20 minutes. I was stranded in this airport for more than 6 hours due to fog which Sarajevo suffers during the winter months of December to February. It is funny kind of similar to the rest of Sarajevo in regards to hospitality. They are either very friendly with a big smile or just very ]rude and disinterested. For example the people at currency exchange information desk baggage claim and check in just couldn't stop smiling. But the people at the security and ticket counters were rude. Ticket counter agents any request such as air fare inquiry schedules etc. creates extra stress for them that they make you feel guilty for being a human being! For instance the lady at the Croatia Airlines ticket counter all I wanted was the air fare from Sarajevo to Munich and she rudely yells at me and say we do not sell tickets from Sarajevo which doesn't make any sense to me whatsoever.

The security staff do not speak clearly, and some speak too fast. Speaking clearly to customers should be top priority. Also, they could be more patient in telling people to remove clothing. The instructions for the circular scanner were vague and resulted in a humiliating pat down.

Saskatoon airport is small and simple to get around. The signs pointing to the right place are just perfect! Renovations were being done at this time - but it was still super easy to be there and get to my flight on time!

Spent a few hours at Saskatoon Airport for a layover. Comfortable seating and general overall layout. Decent selection of food and drink for a smaller airport. I enjoyed the interactive flight map. Friendly and helpful staff. Loved the amount of window space. Nice airport.

This small airport is relatively good but lacks selection of retail and food options. The website is poorly maintained and customer service email is not monitored. There is currently construction but information is not readily available on what the upgrade entails. The check in counters are in need of an upgrade.
Clean efficient airport small but with nice stores. A variety of airlines and it is never busy.

Small clean airport. Close to the city centre. If one arrives for a later flight in the evening arrive with a full stomach as nothing is open after 20:00. It is an efficient small airport with quick security. The TV is still on at full volume in the departure area.

Recently used Saskatoon Airport and found it to be a generally pleasant experience. Quick security clearance is a plus as are the airport greeters who proved friendly and helpful. Aside from the din created by a blaring TV set in the WestJet departure area YXE is a fine airport to use.

Shoutout to Veronica, ground transportation dispatcher. After a very long day of travel from Nova Scotia I finally arrived at Savannah airport a little after midnight only to find that no Uber or Lyft rides were available and there was a very long line at the taxi stand. When I got to the window where Veronica was managing a list of ride requests, I learned that the wait was 1 to 2 hours. Empty taxi's dribbled in and veronica, always with a smile bellowed out the next name on the list is all directions. People were growing impatient with the pace and the next taxi to show up was a mini van. After exchanging a few private words with the driver, Veronica changed strategies, put her list down and bellowed anyone going to "fill in the blank", in my case downtown, "hop in". I got a ride with 2 other fares in a van after only 1/2 hr wait. Way to problem solve Veronica. Everyone wins including the taxi driver who made a few extra$$. In case anyone wants to know the issue was related to a train stopped across the main roadway access for over an hour.

SAV Airport is the only place to rent cars from, the process seems seamless but it’s not. For people coming from a flight directly to the airport it is but for locals it can be a headache with the parking of their actual vehicles. The woman at Thrifty counter was beyond helpful she made this experience so seamless and easy. The lady at the exit point for ticket collecting was rude and unprofessional. I’m usually a nice person but she had the nerve to say this is why people need to know how to read when we were trying to exit following the directions given to us since we had to cross load our vehicles. I’ve never felt so insulted.

Coming from a large airport (Chicago) I was expecting better service and cleanliness in Savannah, GA. The security employees were pushy. Unfriendly, and rude to my three young sons as they were walking thru security. We arrived at our gate, only to find food and wrappers all over the ground. It was filthy. For a Saturday, we were surprised to find restaurants closed. I'd choose O'Hare and it's massiveness and cleanliness over this airport.

I had requested assistance the night before our flight. There was no one to meet us when we initially arrived to head to Las Vegas and even though our entire flight there and back home the other airports had someone to meet us. When we flew back home no one was there to meet us and we had to wait for them to find someone. From now on we will choose another airport to fly out of and into.

I loved Savannah but will never return because I never want to step foot in this airport again. Not only was every single food option closed at 8pm, the vending machines were broken as well. Literally the worst airport ever. Never coming back to Savannah.

❌Not Verified|  Baggage arrived on an earlier flight, no baggage claim personnel present at the office until numerous phone calls and asking for help. 30 minutes later a lady arrived who was not helpful and kept saying she could not release my bag to me without the claim ticket which I had in my hand. After a few minutes of asking what I needed she finally actually looked at the claim ticket saying I’m sorry that’s all I need.

This is one of the nicest airports I have visited. The staff are all helpful and cheerful. The security system is quick and efficient and the seating areas are comfortable and spacious. The woman playing piano in the area prior to security really sets the tone. The whole expereince was professional, polite and efficient.

Flew in to Savannah/Hilton Head International 29 September 2014 and departed 13 October 2014. Once again an absolute pleasure to use. My wife and I use this airport frequently when we travel to Hilton Head Island South Carolina. On arrival my wife goes straight to the car rental desks (about 25 yards from baggage reclaim) and I get the baggage from the belt. Baggage retrieval usually takes 10 minutes or so and by this time the car rental formalities have just about been completed. The cars are just outside the Terminal doors and in about 20 minutes we are on the Interstate. On departure checking in with United Express is a breeze after handing back the rental car and then there is a very pleasant courtyard with retail / café outlets before going through security. Even through security there are a surprising number and variety of eating and drinking outlets with a few retail shops. Usual caveat - if you have a late departure they may not all be open. If only all Airports were this charming and nice to use.

Chicago O'Hare to Savannah and return 9 October. Have used Savannah / HHI International for many years when flying to Hilton Head Island SC. A really very pleasant little airport serving mostly Delta and United Express internal flights. Friendly check in staff quick luggage retrieval and absolutely the best Car Rental desks - just 50 yards along the same floor from Luggage Retrieval with the cars park right outside the Terminal. This is a relatively small International Airport but there is a pleasant courtyard with a couple of shops and eating choices with lots of tables and chairs and a great information desk. Once through security there is a surprising range of nice eating choices BUT of course they may not necessarily be open for a late night departure. Have used many USA Airports over the years but this (and Reno/Sparks in Nevada) is the gem - would unhesitatingly recommend.

The airport seems to focus on appearance instead of focusing on problems with delays. The parking at the airport is a challenge the machine sometimes does not take your credit card and never gives out a receipt. Staff is friendly but cannot control the type or outdated equipment that they have to work with.

Sawyer is a small airport in the Upper Peninsula of Michigan with flights to Detroit and Chicago provided by Delta and American respectively. There is a small store selling Northern Michigan University paraphernalia, some basic snacks, and coffee. The major car rental firms have desks in the terminal with the cars parked just outside. The parking is excellent - you walk out of the terminal into the parking lot. Less than a minute's walk from the airport entrance to the security check area. The terminal has excellent free wi-fi service, courtesy Northern Michigan University. Very friendly and efficient staff. Taxi service is available to the city of Marquette, about 15 miles away.

This is Tel Aviv domestic airport with only regular flights to Eilat. Just one big room with enough seats for about 30 people or so and a small cafe all next too check-in areas. Do not let the tiny size fool you though; security was absolutely out of control bordering surreal absurdity; even with my Amercan passport with no questionable background or former travelled countries they just could not comprehend why a single man would take a day trip to Eilat questioning me over and over and then giving me a full-scale strip search and not even allowing me to take my wallet (!) with me in the plane. Word of caution if you're a single man do not take day-trips; travel with a group and stay overnight.

Terrible airport all around. Not only are the signs confusing, the staff is rude and communicates poorly without specific instructive for where to go. And this is for checking in at 6am and already the airport is crowded and a mess. We also had to take a bus to our plane.

This is the most dirty airport I ever been to. Garbage left on ground around chair area. While my staying there from 6 am to 12 pm, no one come to clean. Waiting Seat around window are so chill. Global entry is useless for connecting fly in this airport.
The employees working baggage claim are all sitting in the customer seats including the disability seat charging their phones and will not move.

Horrible rental service. Avis had 1 person for over 50 customers. Enterprise had no one at the counter & budget was closed. Had a reservation and still had to wait an hour in line after my flight (F9 1723) was delayed 65mins. Horrible trip to the airport.

First time at this airport. What a disappointment after such a great cruise vacation. Long line backed into traffic just to get to departure gates. When we tried to check our bags at the kiosk, it wouldn't work so, we waited in line 15 minutes to get assistance only to be told that Seattle doesn't allow bags to be checked more than 4 hrs before flight. What the heck!! So now we're stuck standing with 4 pcs of luggage because AA pushed our flight back by 2 hrs. No place to sit! The 3 or 4 small eateries were quickly taken up with people dragging lg suitcases who refused to give up their seat once they finished eating. The area near luggage check quickly got overcrowded with people pulling many large suitcases. To have this "4-hr" policy & no general seating (handicap only), makes no sense. Once we finally checked the bags & went to TSA, another nightmare. An hour + at least in line. One of the employees directing people said the reason for the madness was 2 cruise ships just disembarked with 10,000 ppl. Miami doesn't have an issue. Workers are rude & not enough body scanners. I and my carry-on went through the metal detector only to be told that because my knees set it off, I should now go to the line 4 lanes over with a full body scanner. Crazy!! Put scanners at all the TSA lanes! Once we got to our gate (escalator was broken), it was dirty, torn seats and smelled. Only 1 working bathroom in that concourse & it was nasty with no soap in any of the dispensers (women's). The air at the terminal was stagnant & warm. Due to the construction, I don't think there was any ventilation. The icing on the cake is when I overheard an annoyed pilot speaking with a flight attendant saying how much he hates flying into this airport. If you can avoid this airport, do it!

Late arrival due to fog. Global Entry couldn't read my info. Re-screening after customs is understaffed and slow. Reader boards are not working right, and don't match boarding pass gates. My assumption is that checked luggage will not make it to my destination with my connecting flight - it never has when passing through customs. Just avoid this airport if you can.
Completely over crowded, not enough seating. Air is stagnant, hot, smelly. Food is outrageously overpriced and very low quality. Seating, when you find it, is dirty and old.

Arrived on United flight early Saturday afternoon. The walk to baggage claim was long and confusing. Waited about 30 more minutes for bags to arrive. Arrival/pickup area outside was chaotic, traffic was 4 lanes deep, and stretched out from the terminal building. Departed on red eye Monday Morning. Kiosk check-in stations did not work, United rep confirmed they don’t work. TSA lines were very long, and TSA directions were not clearly posted or announced. There were not enough baggage totes to use for the X-ray machines. Long lines and confusing getting through TSA. Again the walk to the United gate was very long.

SeaTac now rivals LAX in terms of chaos, in my opinion. We waited in a line of 100+ people for the shuttle. (After spending about 20 minutes trying to even find where to go). There was no signage and the path to get there is a construction zone right now; we had to weave around various obstacles. We got on the 4th shuttle after about 30 minutes of waiting. Then we had to wait 45 min in line to actually get the car that I had already paid for and had already pre-checked in for (well that’s Budget’s fault, not SeaTac’s). Between these issues and taxiing on the runway, I didn’t leave the airport until 3 hours after touching down. I also had a bad experience last year when flying out of SeaTac, I almost missed my flight despite arriving 90 minutes early because of their “spot saver” program. People are allowed to just cut in line for the security check. This is not the regular pre-check program, this is just people who know about the app before they arrive to the airport and can sign up to skip in line

This airport is a joke. So spread out. Poor/confusing signage. So difficult to move around the airport to gate locations. The "train" system is a farce. Takes so long to get between terminals. I suppose if you use the airport a lot you "know" the in's and out's of how it operates. If you are a first timer I am afraid it is an airport to lay down and avoid if you can. Took us 1.5 hours from time we arrived at the airport to get to the gate in the "S" terminal. TSA was slow, transiting inside the airport was slow. Then we missed the flight by 2 mins. That's another issue with Frontier! If you do have to use this airport I suggest you add at least 1.5 hours to what you normally expect at other airports. When we arrived it was no better. Took so long to get from the arrival gate to the off airport rental car location. The place is a mess and who ever designed it needs a head read. It's just nasty. Seems whoever owns this place is more focused on building a sprawling ediface than serving the people that use it. So sad in a first world country to have to endure a place like this. It would be interesting stat to know how many people have missed flights from Sea Tac in last 3 months? A lot would be my opinion.

Small regional airport and the only airport in Malaysia not managed by MAHB. About an hour bus ride from JB Sentral if you are coming over from Singapore. Decent F&B offerings such as Starbucks, KFC, Marrybrown, secret recipe etc, along with a smattering of other retail shops. AirAsia self check in kiosks are available at the airport, with other airlines flying from here being Malindo air, Jin air, Malaysia Airlines and Firefly. Free wifi is available and the airport doesn't operate for 24 hours although you can still enter and leave the airport even when it's "closed". Most of the times you have to walk on the tarmac to the aircraft.

A small airport, with around just 5 gates. When I arrived immigration had only 3 people in charge. Many restaurants around and wifi is fast which really helps to order uber. One problem is the check in counter (baggage drop), with only 1 counter open and a long queue. Really need to improve cleanliness.

Again and again Gimpo airport disappoints. Airport security is announced as open from 6am but as usual no one is here before 6h10 creating long lines to get your passport and ticket checked before security screening. It is a poor service. If you cannot open at 6am announce it. Gave 1 star as this waiting time is not acceptable
As usual Gimpo security check is failing. Long queue as they do not know how to manage it. They should open more security check point during peak hour.
Long queues to get through immigration, and then a very long walk to the metro. The airport looked reasonable enough with sufficient shops/eateries etc. Arrival was ok but could have been better.

Conveniently located close to Seoul center but experience is consistently sub-par and quite a shame for the image of Korea. Security lines are poorly managed, extremely long with many positions checked (staff probably understaffed). It’s been going on for YEARS. The lines for unpacking liquids / laptops are quite long but there’s a single staff at the end of it handing baskets one by one to passengers so that only one passenger at a time can unpack and prepare for security. That whole process is dumb (that’s it how they do it at Incheon so also by Korean standards it’s weird) and consistently slowing down the lines.

Totally outdated airport. After check in you have to watch a screen to see if your luggage is security cleared. Boarding pass security check: long lines up to 40 minutes. Security up to 20 minutes. A real nightmare. It is a shame for Korea image

The worst airport experience I have ever had. The waiting time for the passport check was almost 2 hours. A lot of people had a hard time standing in line for that long. Even old people had to queue and were unable to sit down. They could also not use the priority line, because you have to have a special medical card for that.

Smaller more convenient airport for Seoul. Arrivals process quick and easy, short walk from the aircraft to Passport Control. Down a set of steps to Baggage Reclaim, Bags come reasonably quickly. There are toilets within Baggage Reclaim. Customs check and then the main Arrivals area. The walk to the metro/train was quite a long way but all flat to push baggage carts. Ticket machines that take cash. Express train to Seoul Station and other metro trains to most points within greater Seoul. A quick and easy way to get into South Korea.

The airport was well connected with the public transportation (bus, subway) and even linked to a shopping mall. Staff was friendly and professional. In overall, the signs were clear with both of English and Korean listed with fast and free WiFi. The international terminal, however, was a bit boring, not as busy as the domestic one.

Gimpo international is not good. Crowded check in, long line for ticket control. Longer line for security check Passport control ok. This airport is a second tier quality. Especially compared to Haneda.

It is a privilege to be able to travel via GMP in Seoul. Not because the airport is extraordinary but because it is within the city of Seoul and much closer then the island of Incheon. GMP can be be reached by metro. It is a domestic and an international airport, the international connections are through towards Asian destinations. GMP has the Advantages and the disadvantages of an old city airport: easy to reach, more efficient security procedures but old facilities (like lounges).

I had lose my hand carry luggage during the security check due to my own negligence. I only realized it after boarded to my flight ( Singapore airline SQ601 on 14th Feb). I highly appreciated Incheon airport ground staff and Singapore airline staff professional service, quick response and putting customer satisfaction at high priority as they managed to quickly locate the luggage, ensure me the luggage will be sent back the by the next available flight and I could proceed returning Singapore as per plan. Two staff members (I'm not sure if he's Incheon airport staff or Singapore airline staff ) I would like to mention in particular who had responded very fast and given me great support at the boarding gate, Mr. Kang and Mr. Lee=. Both their effort was sincerely appreciated.

Terminal 1 Check in good but long delays/lines to check passport and boarding pass up to 90 min Security and immigration. The experience in this long lines are like a third world country. Incheon airport authorities should be ashamed to offer such a poor experience. And as it takes so much time , no time for shopping.

I fly a lot, and this airport has become the worst I have ever experienced in terms of delays accessing departure lounge. At the beginning December, we waited 2 1/2 hours to get through baggage inspection, and beginning January 2025 we are again awaiting over one hour to get to baggage inspection. For an airport that used to post being the best in the world, it has really descended to the depths of the worst in a short period of time. Note for business class passengers; there is no fast track lane.

The security clearance was horribly slow with extremely long queues, which required 1 to 2 hours to clear (terminal 1, departure gate 2, 2pm). There were so many passengers but only 3 security lanes were functioning. This is probably the culprit. This is incompetence on the part of the airport. Read that Incheon airport is ranked 3rd best airport. Is this a joke? This is absurd and is not in keeping with the experience. There were many shops and restaurants at the airport but this was completely moot, when all the time was spent queueing at the security clearance with no time for shopping. What a farce.

Incheon Airport generally has a nice and clean layout, making navigation straightforward. However, my experience today at Security Lane 2 was quite disappointing. Out of the three passport scanner machines, only one was operational, causing severe delays. I joined the queue at 1:45 PM and only cleared security at 3 PM, taking over 1 hour and 15 minutes to get through. For an airport of this reputation, such inefficiency was unexpected. Thankfully, I had arrived early for my 4:40 PM flight, or I might have missed it. While the rest of the airport experience is great, the management should urgently address such issues.

Departing from Terminal 2. Lots of space, light and helpful signaling. Security was well organized and relatively fast moving, but the queue was huge. Actually, three queues, one for facial ID, one for carry-on security checks and the final one for passport control. The automatic passport check did not work for us, maybe because we had not come to the country through this airport, and there were moments of confusion among us and the supervisor. The terminal itself is a bit aseptic, Impersonal, and way too long. Food options could be better. And a bit of color or additional greenery would have been great.

Really long security lines in the morning, no staff to manage it all, no priority security lines for business / elite passengers and overall a really chaotic and stressful experience even for frequent travelers. It’s a shame that in a country like Korea they don’t seem to do anything about this mess.
Decent airport but inadequate for a country such as South Korea. The airport has the most ridicolous control queuing system: you unnecessarily have to queue for almost 2 hours. Avoid if possible.

Checked in at 8 am on Sunday morning. The security lines were never ending at every security station in Terminal 1. New scanning machines for bags and humans but still hopeless slow putting people through. Over 40 minutes to get through to passport control. Allow yourself plenty of time.

Incheon has become one of the worst airport. Easy to check in but if your flight is in the morning be prepared to wait over 40 min at security control. Definitely they are ill prepared. They should open it earlier and have a better indication on waiting time. Korean airports authorities are not know to be clever.
The main pro of flying out of Sevilla Airport is that it is a small airport and close to the city center. The main con is that it is a dirty airport - toilets are shockingly neglected.

Positive departure experience at Seville airport on Oct. 4, 2024 for a domestic flight. After reading previous reviews, I was wary of flying out of this airport, but our experience was perfectly good. Before the security checkpoint, we found a pleasant café for lunch. Going through security was quick and easy. Restrooms were clean and a cleaning person was busy at work keeping them so. A push button rating system for the condition of the restroom was outside the door, so perhaps Aena has received the message from prior reviews and is trying to do better. No complaints at all about this airport.

I had a smooth experience in the airport until I had to go to toilet. They are super dirty. Went to check different ones and none of them had paper. Very unhygienic. Make sure to have some tissues before you visit the restrooms.

This airport is terrible. No working charging stations, the toilets are very dirty. Moreover, screens of for example Burger King are not working, leading to long waiting times. I prefer to never travel over this airport again.

At the airport as I am writing this review. I haven’t come here with high expectations knowing it is a smaller airport and so I am not disappointed by the few shops and services. However, I am hugely disappointed by the state of it - especially when it comes to cleanliness! My very first impression when I got out of the taxi and approached the entrance was, that, despite Spain being in the European Union, they clearly don’t respect the laws that are there to protect non-smokers from the cigarette smoke. Designated smoking areas should be at least 5 meters away from any entrance. The further the better! Yet, here you are greeted by huge smoke clouds as you are trying to make your way into the building. I don’t care if smokers kill themselves by I find it utterly unacceptable that everyone else should breath in the smoke and is disrespected by smokers, let alone airport management. My second impression was even worse: after check-in and before heading to the security check, I needed to use the toilet which was close to the entrance. Boy, did I regret entering that space!! Based on the lack of toilet paper in both 2 (!) toilets, and the rubbish left everywhere and the toilet seat that was clearly dirty, the lack of hand washing liquid, it was clear that this room was not visited by cleaning personnel for (very) long. In general, the whole airport that I walked up and down many times was in desperate need of scrubbing! The other toilet I used also was lacking handwashing gel and the floor was covered with toilet paper, also piling up and falling down from the overflow bin. I sat for over an hour in the big hall by gate B13 to charge my phone, during this time I noticed a lot of dust and other dirt gathering under the seats, and while 2 cleaning ladies showed up during this time, they only poked with their mops under one or two rows of seats, then left, not touching the rest of the area. No tables were cleaned, no plastic bottles that were left behind by lazy passengers were collected. Later, after another walk around I ended up at Gate 14 where I wanted to continue charging my phone at the long table which has many plugs fixed in it, but sadly, none of them were accessible, all were closed and I couldn’t manually open their lid, so I walked back to my previous charging table where i am right now and where the built in plugs are willed with dust, dirt, crumbles. Based on what I have seen so far, I must say that, this airport is pretty neglected and badly maintained. For me, it was truly disappointing, I will probably not return, although I’ve had a wonderful 3 days in town. Should have taken the train on the way back to Barcelona, too!

Had a lovely trip to Seville with wife and baby daughter only to be tainted somewhat by horrific treatment at passport control. After passing through the passport machine we were verbally attacked by a guard whom was shaking with rage. We do not speak Spanish and attempted to calm him but he was completely overwhelmed with anger. We still are unsure the cause of his meltdown but he probably should find a calmer job where he could work away from the general public. Awful airport also, stinks to high heaven.
The best assistance so far, for arrival and departure. For someone who has less mobility and needs a wheel chair. Superb and faster assistance. Everything in place on time!

We came in from Marrakesh. Time 15:20h Walked to passport control. Waited, Waited, Waited, Some douanier really impolite. Two hours later we were outside. Why so irritated and why so understaffed? Automatic passport control units not open until 16:00h. Why? Why keep 2-300 people waiting, standing up, old people included? Shame on you. And if you had good reasons, explain. Just explain. Do it.

First time using this airport, it is modern, has plenty of seats, good signals and clear information, security is also a breeze. You can only reach this airport by bus or taxi. Plenty of food options, but very expensive for Spanish standards, even more expensive than Madrid's or Barcelona's airport. But now what shocked me most as people have mentioned it in here, the total lack of cleaning, I can not explain why, but this airport is filthy. Toilets, floor, seats, all dirty, litter all over the place. I could not believe it.
Very easy to reach and easy to move around inside terminal. Clear signs, polite and friendly staff. Plenty of seats by gate.

A small, very basic airport with basic facilities so do not expect a lot. On the landside, the check-in counters are not air-conditioned so expect to stay in line while hot air irritates you (unless you love hot air). Other than that, on the landside there are a few currency exchanges and car rental booths, a small souvenir shop, a pharmacy, and a few eateries (a bar, a coffee/snack shop, and a Burger King), and that is it. Almost no seating for passengers (except a few on the domestic side) so passengers will have to either purchase something from one of the eateries or pass through security to find somewhere to sit. On the other hand, on the airside there are two nice facilities on the first floor of the international waiting area: a rum bar operated by Takamaka Rum Distillery and a lounge operated by Air Seychelles (basically the only lounge in the airport's international terminal so all business class passengers will have a "class reunion" there). Apart from the rum bar and lounge, however, the waiting area on the ground floor is once again pretty basic with only a few duty-free shops. Queuing times at arrivals immigration have improved over the past as Seychelles now requires all passengers to pre-declare their travel plans digitally, but make sure to have enough time for security and departures immigration as the airport's capacity is still limited to process large planes. Finally, do not fully trust the departures/arrivals screen as flight updates may not be reflected timely.

This is one of the worst airports I have ever seen, and I have been in more than 80. Very very long lines, I waited 1hr 10min to pass the arrival border check and 1h 30m to check in at Qatar Airways counter on departure. There is no organization, “smart” people just skip the line, honest people complaining all the time and the airport staff doesn’t care. Covid social distancing and face covering rules enforcing is inexistent. Unfortunately, things were so stressful that I am never coming to Seychelles ever again and I don’t recommend anyone to.

Very small airport, very few amenities. Only counter-printed boarding passes are accepted, neither mobile nor self-printed boarding passes are accepted at the airport. No self check in kiosks are provided, check in desks open 3 hours before departure. Waiting area for check in is actually not an enclosed room but open, and thus not airconditioned. Immigration has only very few counters, thus large queues are to be expected. Immigration requires a precise address of hotel/location on the Seychelles. Security does neither care for tablets, nor for liquids. No airbridges are provided, all boarding and deboarding is only on the trarmac. Would generally avoid this airport.

I had forgotten what the airport was like but it was great, very small and compact, no air bridges to aircraft just a quick walk across the airfield. Immigration was very easy and efficient as international flights seem to land one at a time. The luggage was swiftly off the aircraft and 20 minutes you are in your taxi off to your Hotel. Check in again was very quick, we arrived very early and were first in the queue, your taxi drops you off curbside and you walk about 40 paces and the check-in is in front of you. Immigration was very quick 5 minutes and you are airside, very limited space and a sad sight of a Burger King! Fortunately, we went upstairs to the Business/First Lounge shared by most airlines, it was empty when we arrived but filled very quickly, good tea and coffee, a bit limited offerings but ample really. Called when the flight was boarding, chaos downstairs but they were calling priority boarding and eventually all went as planned.

This is a small but friendly airport. The check-in area is not air conditioned and is hot. Check-in was efficient, immigration and security were efficient with hardly any queues. In departures there were two food and drink outlets, a duty-free shop and several other shops. Boarding was efficient.

I was flying LGW-DXB-SEZ-PRI and then PRI-SEZ and SEZ-DXB. The international terminal is small and dated, but is clean inside. Queuing times aren't too long for international arrivals, and the luggage arrived quickly. Check in queues were short and staff were friendly, considering I checked in at 5 am. The domestic terminal is very small, but the queues were short and it was 15 minutes before departure check-in time. The waiting area wasn't very clean but it was ok for the short wait. The luggage return was non-existent, a hole in the wall that your luggage was put through. Overall, small airport, but friendly staff and short waiting times.

Old airport - looks like a 1970s relic - which it is! Only used for transfer which was so simple - just a short walk. In that sense convenient but not much to do air side and unable to comment on passport or check in services. Staff pleasant and very helpful. So my one hour in the Seychelles was smooth and pleasant. Departure area air-conditioned which was handy in 31c humid outside temps.

Arrived on almost full Emirates flight to an airport arrivals area that was flooded with passengers. No orderly lines for immigration. Arrivals area was hot no air conditioning no fans even the air was still and hot. Very uncomfortable. A local music group was set up just inside the door in the arrivals area with the loudest music it was not the greeting many wanted. People standing in front and behind were commenting on the volume. Local Seychellois arriving pushed their way to the front ignoring foreign passengers and making fellow passengers feel unwelcome. When they were challenged their attitude was indifferent. Police and immigration officers just watched on and ignored this problem. Immigration processing time was extraordinarily slow. Random bag check was a faux pas. After being asked a series of questions and then being told to put bag through scanner I noted there was actually no one observing the monitor! Departing Seychelles was slightly easier. But again the processing time to get tickets and check bags was so slow. The bag check and line up area is open air. Upon going through to immigration and security I noted two of the immigration officials on the Internet looking at everything but what they were supposed to be doing. The whole experience was not impressive. Quite an embarrassment for such a beautiful country.

A small but pleasant airport. On arrival customs officer friendly and smiling. Luggage delivered quickly and duty free shops in the arrival lounge. On departure staff pleasant including the security check. Just be aware that the domestic terminal is very small and offer very few seating possibilities before check in.

This airport continues to improve as it gets more and more traffic. Air Seychelles are the ground handling company and they have built an excellent lounge for premium passengers. It really is very very nice. The shopping improves with every visit and the space available keeps increasing in size for passengers to stroll. That with the friendly and helpful staff makes it a winner.

Airport is easy to reach by metro, train and taxi. Check in area and departure area have been perfectly clean. In the check in area only few shops and restaurant available, departure area have more choice but I did not use them as I used the lounge. Check in went fast and efficient, same for security check. Staff was professional.

The traffic of Hongqiao Airport is very convenient. It is very close to Hongqiao high speed railway station. There are two subways and many airport buses. There are many self-service check-in machines in the check-in area of Hongqiao Airport, which is very convenient. There are many counters open at the manual check-in, so there is almost no need to queue up, but the service attitude of the staff is general. The queuing time of airport security check is too long. There are many restaurants after security, with free wifi. Airport Arrival triage is very good. People without checked luggage can take another channel to leave quickly. But it's not good to wait a long time for luggage. The design of the arrival exit is narrow and crowded.

This is the second airport in Shanghai and has a train station next to it. Traffic can be very bad here, especially during holidays so recommend giving yourself some extra time or take the subway. Security is just ok, does move slow often and not many lanes open. Restaurants are better here than PVG and there are options on the other side of security. Shops are plentiful and appear to be good for alcohol, candy, perfumes, and Chinese goods. The only large issue is the lack of jetway use. This airport likes to make passengers take a bus, especially when arriving here. Even if it rains they still make you go outside. Not sure why when jetways are open but it’s happen 6 times for me out of the 10 times I’ve used this airport. Also I would avoid flying into this airport at night because they will make take a bus and it adds about 30-45 minutes on to your travel time. Bags arrive at a good rate and there are taxi stands outside. Just avoid the people asking to give you rides, just like most airports, they will charge you more and technically are breaking the law by being there. I always just ignore and go outside to taxi lines, which move quickly. Tip: Avoid travel during Chinese vacations. This will save you loads of time because when Chinese travel they all use train, next door, and taxi lines are ridiculously long.
The set of counters of Cathay Dragon was a bit out of order, since every counter was excessively full due to the great number of passengers (Business Class and Marco Polo Club and Oneworld Members).

I arrived at T2 Terminal Hongqiao. Used the Sky Priority Customer Service. Lovely, helpful staff who helped me with my oversized baggage. I was stressed about it, and the team helped me without a problem. Then even showed me clearly were to go, as well as showing me were Sky Priority Lounge was. I couldn’t be more grateful for their good service.

Flew Shanghai to Tinajin. Although crowded at times in the summer heat, everything went well. Check-in queues were very long. I was lucky to check in at one of the numerous golden pass counters as have been invited by my companion. Although Hongqiao is for domestic flights, it is not difficult for a foreigner like me to have the right orientation. Airport is clean and very clear and correspond to high international standards.

Shanghai Hongqiao Airport is a good airport by Chinese Airport standards, but is not up to International Airport standards. Overall experience of the airport was pretty average-ish. The only plus value of this airport is the accessibility to Shanghai Railway Station and two Shanghai metro lines. Not recommended for stays of more than 1 hour.

I arrived at the airport from London Heathrow and travelled via Beijing. On arrival at Terminal 2 it was nearing 10 pm and I had been travelling for over 18 hours. I wanted to get a taxi to the hotel and go to bed. However none of the ATM's in the terminal accepted any of my debit cards. I have had trouble in the past in rural areas but never at an international airport. I was told to go to terminal one which had international arrivals and try there. Fortunately the shuttle bus was free and I go to terminal 1. Only one of the ATM's there (which also happened to be the last one I tried) accepted my card (with one other machine down.) At other Chinese airports (Beijing and Xi'An Xingang) they have always had ATM's from the big four banks - Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, Bank of China, China Construction Bank, Agricultural Bank of China. I have never had a problem getting cash from these banks. I would also note that the underground station just outside terminal one has multiple big four ATM's and is an excellent way to travel into the city. I finally got to my hotel at midnight, I wrote to the Airport while in China but never received a response.

I took the subway from my hostel to the 1st terminal of Hongqiao airport, the airport is pretty close to the downtown, however the subway is quite far from the airport and there was no exit inside the airport. The food choice in the airport was insufficient. Airport staff were very unhelpful. I tried to find a place to return my metro card and get back the deposit, but the subway staff refused to handle it for me. When I tried to seek help from airport staff, they either do not know where to do the return or told me to go back to the subway station which is quite far from the airport. Inside the airport, the air-conditioning system was very bad. The direction to the check-in counter and the boarding gates was unclear and insufficient. Not enough facilities in the airport, for example ATM or bank counters.

Overall, Shanghai Hongqiao is a good airport if you are flying domestically. There is not much you can do inside the terminal. There are not many restaurants and shops there. On the up side, you don't need to arrive too early for departure because wait times are typically not terrible. Arrival can a bit painful, since you may have to walk pretty long distances to get to the exit. Shanghai Hongqiao Railway Station is adjacent to the airport and they are connected indoors, thus if you need to make a transfer between a flight and high speed train, it will be easy.

We had a really bad experience transiting through Shanghai airport and would strongly recommend that people (particularly those with small children) do not transit through here. We had read bad reviews in advance of booking our flight but stupidly chose to book anyway because of the well-priced fares. We really doing regret this. We spent around two hours queuing for and waiting for our new boarding passes to be issued in essentially a corridor. There was no order or obvious system in place and the whole experience was very frustrating. We also had to give mobile numbers to allow the airport staff to search our bags. Worst of all, we left a bag in the airport and it has mysteriously and completely disappeared. It contained some jewellery and we told the airplane staff where it was. The staff claimed to try to look for it but we have heard nothing from them to date.

Why does China insist on building huge airports with no ac? When will the country understand it is impossible to use 95% of the apps. This is supposed to be a modern country. I have seen the world and only China makes it impossible to move around or get things done.

I have done my fair share of travelling – this is hands down the worst airport out of the ones I've been to. Rude and incompetent staff. Had such an awful experience I will avoid flying through China in the future. At least through Shanghai. China is also one of the countries I haven't travelled to yet and now have absolutely zero desire to. There are so many nice countries with lovely people in the world. There is no need to travel somewhere with people so rude. Awful first impression. Avoid Pudong airport at all cost. The people there have no idea what they are doing, are unhelpful and will treat you like trash. On a side note, it's also a huge, mostly empty airport. Very few shops and eateries.

I read a huge amount of negativity about this airport prior to my trip there, it was a five hour transit stop going from London to Bangkok. I was certainly concerned reading all the previous reviews. However I didn’t experience any real issues. The airport is very large so easy to find a quiet spot, there are plenty of power outlets, and getting online is extremely simple, you just log on and take a pic of your passport. Granted, you won’t be able to do very much online unless you’ve got one of the VPNs that work behind the great China firewall, but if you have an iPad with a couple of movies downloaded the time will soon pass. There was a reasonable amount of shops open both for coffee and souvenir shopping. The train that you’ll need to take to get to your gate is frequent, clean and fast. Overall I’ve been to more interesting airports but my message would be don’t stress out reading the negative reviews, I had no issues whatsoever.

We were transiting through to Tokyo from London Gatwick. Immediately upon arrival, we were herded into a corridor with lots of other people trying to transit to other flights and given zero information. After some time, which we could have spent navigating the Airport independently, we were herded to the transit section. This whole process was a massive time suck and not needed, it felt like they didn't trust foreigners to navigate the airport on their own. The whole feel of the place is very eery. We both felt on edge as they monitor everything with an excessive amount of cameras watching/recording you constantly. We had to endure so many painfully long queues that seemed illogical. We were getting a transfer but we had to go through the exact same processes we had already cleared 12 hrs prior in London Gatwick. Our liquids and hand luggage was intensely scrutinised, even though, again, we were cleared at London Gatwick. We had to constantly show our boarding pass, provide lots of personal information and photos constantly, and it all felt quite invasive. It felt like a massive overkill. We thought having a layover of 2.5 hours would be plentiful, however we ended up, after enduring the most surreal and stress inducing transfer we've ever been through, with only 15 mins to catch our flight. It seems, judging from previous reviews, I was lucky to be able to buy 3 drinks prior to getting our flight, as we were desperately thirsty, using my card, but, again, I had to sign things, and it was a very elongated process. I am dreading our return journey. No one speaks English, they seem unconcerned about time pressures with flight transfers, and while we saw quite literally over 20 members of staff congregating at various points in the airport, they have minimal staff processing flyers. The presence of so many staff loitering around is also intimidating, as is very intensive security procedures I.e. everyone goes through the metal detector gate but noone escapes a pat down. It so excessive and massive overkill. You cannot access the "free wifi' unless you are prepared to give more personal info, like your phone number or passport details with current photo, and if you do take that deal, everything is blocked unless it's a Chinese website, so massive issues of censorship here, which is deeply uncomfortable. I would not recommend unless you are into the vibe of a dystopian escape room.

Quite terrible huge but hollow terminal, has 1 cafe that sells food, most shops closed, numbers of gate have no logic. Basically no wifi - 90% of sites and apps are blocked. Reasonably clean, as its empty lots of space to sit (or lay down) and one particular employee was helpful to get me on next flight while I missed my original all in all. Really below average airport.

The worst international airport I’ve ever travelled through - literally no restaurants open or places to get food. The staff are very abrupt and unfriendly, and the whole experience is weird. Also, we’d booked our seats ahead of time through China Eastern and upon checking in were rudely told we have middle seats for our 13 hour flight and they declined to change our seats to what we had booked. I would strongly suggest transiting through another airport. I’ve been to remote airports in developing countries with better airports…

This whole airport experience was a complete and utter joke. The debacle began the second we left the plane, where we were subjected to long queues and no apparent wifi connectivity. The staff slap a sticker on you without consent and herd you like cattle to the transit area. The best description of the transit area is a skeleton. Yes, it is modern and clean with the initial appearance of many shops and restaurants, but spend more than 5 minutes there and you will realise there is hardly anywhere to eat, where the food is inedible, and there is hardly anywhere to shop, and the staff don't speak English. So, to pass the time, we decided to splurge on entry into the airport lounge. However, we were told (in broken English) that they only accept Chinese yuan for entry. Slightly annoyed, we asked where we could withdraw cash or exchange foreign currency, the staff member advised there was no ATMs nor currency exchange outlets in the airport. So if you want to spend more than 5 minutes in a place with barely any edible food, a smoking room resembling a scene from Black Mirror (Gulag-like environment covered with security cameras) and that simply makes you hate life, then I recommend a transit at Shanghai Pudong.

Recently had a stopover at Shanghai Pudong for a Tokyo-London flight. Arriving at Pudong at around 11pm we were greeted with chaotic scenes. At no point were we told that we needed to go through immigration, get a transit visa, pick up our luggage, and go through the whole check-in/immigration/security check procedure again (thanks air China for not making any effort to explain this process). To make matters worse. We spent an hour in the wrong queue. The whole process was a joke. The 200+ passengers in the very slow line (there were only 2 desks open) weren't allowed to proceed to baggage collection until every passenger had been processed. We were just told to wait 'over there'. Rude/short tempered staff who couldn't speak much English throughout. A 4 hour transit time left us with about 45 mins to spare before boarding. We couldn't buy any drinks and the WiFi was only available to Chinese (more about this later). On the return flight we were given boarding passes for the onward connection to Tokyo. Thinking we were in for an easier time was nothing short of wishful thinking. Same again really, except we didn't have to go through immigration. One desk open, told to wait by the toilets. Once the whole flight had been processed we were allowed to proceed through yet another security check where my duty free purchases from London were scrutinized. Don't bother with the 'free' WiFi. You have to scan your passport at a terminal (another queue) and once connected, the internet doesn't work. The few minutes we had in the duty free area wasn't enough to get some drinks and the stores only accept Chinese currency. On top of it all, one of my suitcases hadn't arrived in Tokyo. Terrible experience. Never flying Air China or transiting through China again.

The staff acts like they understand English but they don’t, like this they sent us to the transit area while we wanted to explore the city seen our long layover. There was no way to get back to the immigration section and when we asked for help the staff was rude and not helping at all. Internet doesn’t work either so this is definitely the worst airport experience ever!

Shannon airport is my favorite airport. I use it a lot. My Ryanair flight to Faro was delayed last Sunday for nearly 2 hours. (Due to the late arrival of the incoming flight). During my stay in the departure lounge there were numerous announcements over the speaker system. The clarity of the woman announcer was appalling due to her poor diction, poor accent and speed of speech.  Another passenger who was returning to Singapore from Shannon via London Heathrow complained that she could not make out any of the announcements either. Its only a small point but it needs attention.

I arrived yesterday morning at 6.30 am for a Ryanair flight to Faro departing at 7.20am. I had no luggage to check in. To my surprise there were hundreds queuing at the desk with one lady checking boarding cards. There were obviously a few more flights departing early yesterday. At the security check in one lady decided to take her tea break leaving one man to check all cases etc. No consideration given to passengers trying to get to the departure gates. Luckily I just made the flight and was the last one to board. Management need to monitor this situation and react when staff decide to leave their posts. Never had a problem like this before at Shannon.

I normally look forward to travelling from this airport, it's usually a calm quiet airport with friendly staff. However our experience going through the security check was anything but that this time around. A lady working there was very bad mannered and seemed to have a very bad attitude. I would expect that kind of attitude from staff at busier airports, but not at Shannon Airport. Felt very upset and disappointed generally. Hope this woman either changes her attitude or changes her job.

I had a flight from Malaga to Manchester via Shannon,  My first flight was delayed and my second was boarding when we landed. I just want to thank the staff, particularly at passport control, the lady was amazing and rushed me straight through. The security and boarding staff were excellent too. All made sure I made the 2nd flight in order to get back to home to my mother who was and still is gravely ill. Without their kind actions, I'd have missed the connecting flight. So thank you all the staff for your compassion and haste! I'll do the overall rating - but - in all honesty I was not in the right state to pay much attention.

Small airport in the West of Ireland. People and staff very friendly. New bathrooms in lounge. Food expensive. Duty free was very big but there are no bargains for people travelling to US as items like perfumes are actually more expensive than sites in US.  We used to get bargains in duty free, but not any more.

Very efficient from arriving on stand, getting though immigration baggage and leaving in the hire car in less than an hour. Departure was a breeze. Only minor issue was Wi-Fi only seemed to work once you go through security. Much prefer Shannon to the chaos that is Dublin.

Such a comfortable and convenient airport to use. The relaxed feeling that I experienced was something you don’t normally feel in airports. Everything and everyone seemed to be at a relaxed pace and the friendliness of the immigration staff was very pleasant. The baggage arrived promptly and even the customs staff seemed very friendly as I passed by. At the exit to the car park I was asked by a couple of international visitors if I could assist them as they lost their car park ticket. I went with them to the car park and visitor reception desk and the two ladies there were very understanding and helpful. There were hand sanitising dispensers and hand towels available throughout the concourse and what is different about Shannon airport is that the sanitising foam dispensers were well stocked compared to other airports that all seem to have the dispensers but they are all empty.

I would like to express my extreme gratitude to staff who managed to retrieve some personal items belonging to my son & I which we left onboard plane on flight in from New York early last Wednesday morning. Due to their quick actions, we managed to reclaim these items from the plane before it headed out to Heathrow on next flight. They were extremely efficient & very friendly, two great ambassadors for Shannon airport. We are very grateful to them both for their assistance in turning what could have been a holiday disaster into a very pleasant experience with Shannon airport. They both deserve special recognition for their excellent customer skills.

I just booked through this airport in October on my way to Australia. It was such a dream, no queues, friendly efficient staff. Luggage scanned without having to remove Ipad, small bottles etc. It must be one of the better airports in the EU.
The pleasant experience of arriving and departure in Shannon Airport was above all else. Efficiency, professionalism courteous. Dublin needs to take a look and see how it’s done. Well done Shannon.

We had to return early from a holiday in Dubai, and it was considerably cheaper to fly from Sharjah than from Dubai! Sharjah is a relatively small airport, but has a reasonable duty free area, a food court with a number of very reasonably priced outlets, and very friendly staff. It was very clean, and staff were constantly and vigilantly cleaning the public areas. Unfortunately the check in desk for Pegasus was very slow, and boarding was slow as well. Nevertheless a stress free experience. Would definitely use Sharjah again.

Absolutely zero customer service from airport staff they just pointed to me to the direction of the gates to be opened for my flight, I wasn't sure the number, one guy said just go down, while hurriedly walking away, I had to follow him to ask the number, horrible customer service attitude shouting instructions at passengers, dirty lounge somewhere in the basement where they ask you to stay if the layover is long. Everyone speaks hindi or Arabic and don't understand English.

I was travelling from Sharjah to Mumbai and staff at the check-in and screening process at gate no 22 were very rude to me. They told me if I am pregnant it's my problem and not theirs, I am an idiot to travel and refused to help me at check in. Also staff were asking me to pay extra for help, my experience was really bad at Sharjah airport and won't recommend anyone to travel from Sharjah airport.

I would like to bring to notice the poor information network the airport transfer desk holds. I had arrived at Sharjah from Milan via Pegasus airlines. From Sharjah I had another flight with Air Arabia to final destination Trivandrum in India. I was told at transfer desk while collecting boarding pass that my luggage would automatically be transferred even though the airlines were different. I tried mentioning that my airlines are different and maybe I have to collect my luggage and re-check-in. They said no need to worry and I was puzzled. However I decided to believe the airlines authority and went ahead. When I reached my final destination in India I was told my baggage did not arrive as it was with Pegasus Airlines in Sharjah. As a student who is visiting his home for two weeks after more than two years it's a terrible incident to happen. What makes me sad is that I repeatedly tried to confirm and I was told that my luggage would be automatically transferred.
It’s a very very crowded airport. There is no good restaurants here. There is no place to sit and relax, no shopping area also. Please don't book your tickets from this airport.

I've had multiple bad experiences at this airport and this time I've chosen to point it out. My problem is the rude attitude of airport staff and customs officers. They are very rude to everyone including children and the elderly.

The worst experience ever had was Air Arabia. Actually, my mom and sister came on a visit visa for the first time and during their departure while entering the Airport they started facing issues. My mom is a senior citizen so, we prefer a wheelchair for her. Could you imagine they started harassing my sister about why our mom was using a wheelchair? Is she a covid patient? Now, this is not a question to be asked as they don't know that without a Covid Negative report they are not allowing passengers to board the flight. At the time of weighing luggage, my sister was informed to put all the luggage including hand luggage and purse and was informed that it was overweight by 7 kg. They don't have the right to do this, it's simple they were trying to get money from people who are on a visit visa. Lastly, not using good language nor good services at all. Though we paid for a wheelchair there was no staff member available for that. My sister and mother had the worst experience ever. For visit visa people, I would suggest never going for Air Arabia. Worst staff I have seen in my life.

I passed by this airport on 11th October night with long lay over for the connecting flight in the morning of 12th Oct. A couple of days before boarding the flight at New Delhi, when contacted Air Arabia customer care office in India, I was told that a long lay over at Sharjah airport is not a problem as the airport has good lounges and an Airport transit hotel. I wrote an email to the hotel but no response was received. To my surprise when I arrived at Sharjah airport, I found that there is only one lounge but that was also closed. Airport transit hotel was also closed. I asked the staff where to pass this long lay over in the absence of lounge and transit hotel. They said I can sit the whole night in the food court, which has only hard uncomfortable plastic chairs. So was the case of chairs placed in two waiting areas of the airport. All chairs were so hard that it caused severe pain after sitting for a long time. I had to sit for 10 hours on those most uncomfortable chairs just to catch my connecting flight. To pass the time I used my laptop and mobile phone to chat. After some time batteries were drained and I needed to charge it again but could not find any electric sockets around so contacted airport staff. They rudely told me that there are only 3 sockets at the airport to connect and charge laptops or mobiles. I searched them and found all those 3 places crowded with other passengers charging their devices. No televisions were provided in the waiting area or food court. I noticed a passenger querying a ground airport staff about a designated place for smoking. Staff replied to him rudely that he cannot smoke inside the airport. Airport staff were extremely rude and their behavior was so annoying. Almost all staff at the airport whether they were wearing a shirt mentioning “May I help You” or otherwise, were extremely impolite and unprofessional in their behavior. In my last 30 years of travelling around the world I have never come across such a bad airport management in a capital city of any country. To my experience this airport should be avoided as far as possible and to be used only exceptionally for short lay over, say 1-2 hours to catch a connecting flight. Air Arabia airline too should be avoided.

Very narrow airport inside with few facilities. Very crowded airport that is being used mainly by Air Arabia. The outer design of this airport is good though. Rude and not courteous airport staff. All of the staffs speak either in Arabic or in Hindi! Very unclean toilets and insufficient in number. Insufficient seating arrangements. Very few airport shops and very costly. Boarding bridges are not available. Difficult to get wifi. I will try to avoid this airport in future.

Very narrow airport inside with few facilities. Very crowded airport that is being used mainly by Air Arabia. The outer design of this airport is good though. Rude and uncourteous airport staff. All of the staff speak either in Arabic or in Hindi! Very unclean toilets and insufficient in number. Insufficient seating arrangements. Very few airport shops and very costly. Boarding bridges are not available. I will try to avoid this airport in future.

We had a horrible experience at this airport due to staff. The staff literally will scream in your face, snatching and wrenching documents out of your hand, and are aggressive and rude. Despite absolutely wonderful stays in local resorts and spending our money happily in Egypt- this airport is a complete NO and we will never return. Egypt should be ashamed of Shark El Sheik airport.

Worst airport experience to date. Beggars posing as staff providing unwanted 'help' and then demanding tips. Extremely rude staff. Unbelievably disorganised. 3 flights all boarding at the same time from the same place, massive queues, chaos and delayed flights. Despite a wonderful time staying in Sharm the airport experience has meant I will not returning.

Incredibly rude, aggressive, threatening security, very intimidating (all of it unnecessary) for returning holidaymakers to UK. Gruff, barked orders, in your face attitudes (from male and female security staff) accompanied by very bad tempered, high handed sneering. Lovely holiday ending with dreadful experience. It was like they hated us and wanted to frighten and control. Reminiscent of camp commandants. We were two old aged pensioners either an autistic son. Three xray machines and body searches. Over the top. We won’t be going back to Egypt.

Worst airport experience of our lives and we travel quite a bit. The way in which the female security “pat” down women really needs addressing. The whole airport is a complete filth hole with rude staff. We had to check in at the easyJet desks and queued for almost 2 hours because of the incapable staff. Toilet facilities are filthy. Something also needs to be done about the people touching and moving luggage and then demanding payment. I can honestly say I will be r return here and that’s mainly due to this horrific airport experience.

I used the Pearl Assist Meet & Greet Departure Service at Sharm El Sheikh on a hectic late night departure, I paid extra for this service and was greeted outside terminal 1 departure by a male and female staff member. Upon handing over my passport and ticket confirmation my young family our check-in luggage, hand luggage was promptly put on waiting trolleys and we queue jumped the initial x-ray scanner queue, queue jumped the check-in counters where the pearl assist team completed all formalities - we were only asked to stand close enough that the check-in agent could confirm our identities. We then queue jumped the ridiculously long immigration, passport control queue and taken to the VIP counter where we had a jovial conversation on our heritage with the 2 star senior officer in English and the paperwork, passports were all handled by the pearl team who fast tracked us to the final x-ray scanner before departure gate area where they left us, we only had to remove our shoes here and our hand luggage went through a breeze, the security agent was a senior gentleman who was smiling and playful with my young children asking their names and greeting them with a hello. The toilets are at the bottom of the left-side escalator and I used the disabled toilet, tipping the lady 50 egyptian pounds, I used translator on my phone to ask her to please wipe the surfaces or the door, sink, taps, toilet and flush with anti-bacterial wipes I brought with me - which she did and was happy to take my money. We used the sanitised disabled toilet and found there was soap in the dispenser and toilet roll in there too, the floor had just been mopped clean, too.
