We visited the duty free shop and found the prices were high so did not purchase anything e.g. 250g Haribo Travel Edition was USD$6 and only purchased a 50cl water bottle and 130g paprika pringles for 300 egyptian pounds which was reasonable cost. At this point we realised we had left a bag behind somewhere which contained heirloom toddler blankets and memory foam pillows for the night flight, I used the lift near the toilets to the 2nd floor to reach the Pearl Lounge, explained I had booked Meet & Assist, described my bag and a lovely girl called Bessant in the lounge took down my whatsapp number and said she would do her best to find my bag and let me know before my flight departs as to whether they find it or not. Within 15 minutes, she message me from the Pearl Lounge Whatsapp account to tell me they had found my bag, found me in the terminal and escorted me back to the final X ray area where I was able to collect my missing bag. I left this area to enter the gate 8,9, 10 area where my UK bound flight was departing, upon entering this area my passport was checked again and there were random searches taking place, these were not as intrusive or discriminatory as those i've experienced in Tel Aviv airport but they were thorough and diligent checking random passengers for every pocket, bag crevice, device and my person but I did not have to strip down naked or made to feel inhumane in my treatment and boarded the plane via a bus, I had to leave the child stroller on the tarmac outside the plane area but it had a tag on it, upon taking my seat the airside controller came to me at my seat and politely asked me for boarding card and wished me well. The flight departed 20 minutes late because of a shortage of tractors would be only criticism but overall, a pleasant experience with support from pearl assist.

The worst airport I’ve ever been to, and I’ve travelled a lot! Horrible rude staff. Lots of queuing, forms to fill in and lots of security checks which is fine, but the staff made it a horrible experience, constant eye rolls, staff shouting telling people to hurry up, excessive pat downs including on my 1 year old child - even touching round his mouth with a disgusted look whilst saying “very rashy” because he has dribble rash from teething. Toilets filthy with no toilet roll in any cubicle. Will never travel back to Sharm El Sheikh purely for the fact I never want to experience this airport again in my life. Awful.

I totally agree with all the other reviews about this airport. The attitude of the airport staff is completely disrespectful. We are all aware that security is of the utmost importance when travelling, however the staff at the airport treated passengers with a total lack of respect. Staff appeared overwhelmed and disinterested, queues were long and while going through the 5 security checks there was no basic courtesy shown. We had never been to Sharm before and had just come from a wonderful week at a 5 star hotel and to be treated in this way has left a lasting impression. Foreign visitors must make a massive contribution to Egypt's economy but the attitude of airport staff, the last people we will see on a visit, completely undermines friendliness and kindness shown by staff working long hours in the hospitality industry. We have travelled all over the world and this airport is the worst by a long way.

The security police were so awful. Would not come back to Egypt just because of this airport alone. The security police (especially on the women's side) were so rude! She insulted everyone who greeted her with a hello or just smiled. I was a victim of her. I said hello to her and smiled and she just kept sending me back and forth through the body scanner and smirked insultingly. I got frustrated and told her that I don't understand what I need to do (I went through the scan about 7 times for no reason) and she told me to get in the back of the line just for smiling. She checked all the women and then just ignored me for around 15 minutes and then checked me and pushed me to get lost or she will "show me where the prison is". So if you are a woman please don't talk or smile while waiting in the security checks because all the women I was on the plane with had the same issue with the same rude security woman. Also, the toilets are disgusting. No toilet paper, dirty, no soap. Just ruined a whole trip.

Worst experience of my life, after a lovely holiday this airport has definitely put me off ever returning. On arrival you go through passport control and one security check which is fine however when returning there are about 10 security checks each time if you are female you get completely touched up in a ‘body check’ as someone who is under 18 this left me feeling violated and very uncomfortable there. There is no sense of order and queues are awful, if you are planning on going there arrive very early. After going through loads of rounds of the exact same security checks you get to duty free and the terminals, these are very unhygienic with an inside smoking lounge with no door or separation from rest of airport, there are bugs and roaches all over the floor the toilets look like they have never been cleaned. When entering the gate there was ‘random security’ checks these were no random at all as everyone who got sent into the line was definitely under the age of 25 where everything gets taken out your bag and rummaged through and you and your belongings get swabbed you are then expected to clear out the area with all your belongings that have been thrown all over the table quickly. This airport is absolutely vile, there are staff everywhere with guns which would be terrifying for families with young kids. There is no WiFi available. I would try to avoid this airport at all costs.

The arrival hall was very good. Quick and easy to navigate. No issues. The departure hall is a different story. Rude police looking for a fight .. corrupt staff asking you to pay to get through quickly. Shocking service and not representative of the airline standards. I was shocked how much the security police looked for trouble.

Shenyang airport traffic is not very convenient, only airport buses and trams (especially few flights), no subway. After entering the terminal, the design is more atmospheric. Except for China Southern Airlines, other airlines can only check in 90 minutes in advance, which is not good. In addition, there are few automatic check-in machines, so the queue at the manual check-in place is serious. Security is fast and funny. There are a lot of rest areas and mobile phone charging areas after security check. WiFi is fast. The fly in the ointment is that there are a few restaurants. In addition, there are many turntables at the baggage claim area, and the luggage will arrive soon. The guidance signs are perfect.

Shenyang is my "home" airport. The recent move to the new terminal is a big improvement, although there is no smoking room. Food and beverage shops ok, but overpriced. Check in always quick and efficient. Same can be said for passport control and security. Lounges for frequent fliers are nice with (if depart around midday) a decent lunch. Delays are not very frequent here and if there are delays they are always caused by traffic control. Warm in winter and cool in summer. Clean toilets. Good signs and all within walking distance of 10 minutes maximum.

Terminal 3 in now already in operation for more then a year. Spacious clean clean toilets food and drink very limited. Still impossible to find Diet drinks or have a decent coffee. No smoking room. Announcements in English poor not understandable and very limited. Underground parking is a long walk from the Dep/Arr area. A real nuisance in this airport is the fact that priority handling of Gold members of any airline is not honoured. Finding a taxi is sometimes also a challenge. There is a new rail line now connecting the airport with the city but have never tried.

Only used this airport in transit to/from Frankfurt/Qingdao so this is a comment on the transit facilities. Speedy visa check and immigration service quick security check and throughout friendly English speaking staff. Excellent signage to transit space which features plenty of seating souvenir and duty free shop coffee bar and small children's play area. In transit one is issued a transit card which has explicit instructions on how to proceed.

Showing its age quite badly even though a relatively modern airport. It does not look like the roof structure has been cleaned since it opened. Distinct lack of departure information boards on the departures level (only one it seems) but otherwise departures is quite easy to navigate and security check area is right next to the gates. Arrivals is a challenge especially if you are looking for the tax stand. An extension is under construction which creates limitations.

It's very convenient to get to/from Shenyang city centre. The nearest boading gate only meters from security check and the airport is full of shops and restaurants - chinese style. But it's sad to see the airport is kind of showing it's age now - only completed in 2002 or so. I think this is due to the fact that the construction quality is not up to standard. The new T2 is adjacent to the abundant T1 which is now looks like a ghost airport terminal itself. Apart from that SHE is an airport which is being well used.

I would agree with the comments on poorly lit baggage area in arrivals. It still appeared that there was some work going on increasing the size of the terminal. Very modern and clean easy access to city. Only disappointment was price of food and beverages once airside - compared with landside Chinese prices for sometimes same product.

Very clean and modern airport. New terminal added in 2002. New access highway to Shenyang. Limited air traffic with few delays. Baggage area is poorly lit. Not sure why? As the Chinese economy grows who knows what will come of this airport. Right now it's a clean. well run airport albeit with little air traffic. Interesting for an American to see Air Koryo planes and personnel at the airport.

Flew from Johannesburg to Schenzhen, connecting flight to Chengdu. Before we landed, stewardess announced that if we are connecting to another city must wait in the transit area. Arrived at Baoan airport, asked the security people where to go or where to go to the transit area, keep pointing to the queue. Nobody speaks English! Asked nearly everybody in the queue, not interest. Eventually got through to customs, asked again where Transit area is, just say 4th floor. Went to 4th floor, don't see any transit area, went to Information Counter, nobody speaks English. Very hesitant to help. Again asked everyone if they speak English so they can translate for me, nothing. Went back to Information again, the lady took me to Check in counter, issued me with a ticket, kept saying must check in. Asked what must I do, she eventually wrote on her phone "your luggage has no business here" so said I know but I did not collect my luggage because in all my other international flights, your luggage gets put on the next plane on your connecting flight. My luggage from JHB has got a big yellow tag with "TRANSFER" attached. So I presumed that it will be put on the plane to Chengdu. Meanwhile by now I am stressing out because my luggage was not collected downstairs. Was told to go to ground floor to collect my luggage, went into the lift, it only went to the 2nd floor, ran around and can't find a lift going down. Went to the 4th floor again and asked the lady to help me. They do not seem interested. I kept asking and asking people standing around too. Nobody is interested in assisting. One security man was standing there so I kept asking him and he said to follow him, we went to a restricted area, waiting for a while and eventually he managed to get my luggage to me. I had to run and check the luggage in again, nearly missed my connecting flight. There should be English speaking staff at the Information Counter. Was so frustrating too, checked in my luggage, I asked where is Gate 3, the girl working behind the counter said "Read". You are already in stress mode and must still get staff working there to be so unfriendly, unhelpful, don't even smile. Staff should be more helpful, at least speak some English, its customer service. WiFi services does not work, Terminal signs and directions is non existent, long queues, Airport staff is not friendly, not helpful, don't speak English. Will not go there again.

A nice looking building and okay for domestic flights I have taken from here. However the international section is really poor and lacking facilities. No proper food and drink options, shopping is atrocious, and seating is quite cramped. Impossible to find charging points and seats offer no power. For a city such as Shenzhen I would have expected much better and certainly something that shows the hi-tech image of the city. WiFi is a joke and cannot be accessed unless you have Chinese mobile or find a wifi machine that are hidden away.

Shenzhen is only my 4th Chinese airport but it is much nicer than Beijing Capital, Shanghai Pudong and Linyi. Although it is still not at Hong Kong's level either. It was a pleasure to see the epidemic of bland airport design that has gripped the world's airport in recent years, has not infected Shenzhen. Yet improvement is still needed for directional signage and in English speaking ground staff and the WiFi access (but that is a problem in all Chinese airports if one does not have a Chinese registered sim card it is impossible to get WiFi).

I had a bad experience in Shenzhen airport after taking a flight from Tokyo via Incheon. The airport was large and there were a huge number of passengers from about 3 or 4 flights arriving at the same time. However, at the entry zone, there were only three opened gate which means I had to queue in a very long line. It took around 2 hours for finishing all procedure and go out of this airport. Moreover, airport staff only speak a little bit English and they did not help me for taking a train from airport to city center. Although I exchanged Chinese money, it could not use for buying train ticket because the automatic ticket machines only accept the smaller value money (which was so strange). When I asked staff, they could not answer in English and also did not help me anymore since I could not speak Chinese.

Arrived in transit from Sydney on the way to Amsterdam via Beijing with China Southern Airlines. On the way to Australia I traveled via Chengdu and Guangzhou with no problems. After a nine hour flight from Sydney we arrived in Shenzen expecting to sail through customs and relax before heading onto Beijing. How wrong could I be. Despite the China Southern staff at Sydney getting me to sign a transit visa (two hour turn around in Shenzen) all passengers going to Beijing were held in a "Holding area" with no drinks or smoking facility from when we landed. My hold luggage (that had been cleared in Sydney and I did not expect to see again until Amsterdam) was then presented to me and I had to open it to find a cigarette lighter was causing a problem? Ok sorted bags re loaded and then I was ushered through another security check and had to run the length of the airport (and it is no small airport) to catch my connecting flight despite arriving two hours earlier. Utter shambles and if I ever travel that way again Shenzen is on my "definite give it a miss list".

Brand new airport. On the positive side, for Chinese standards it certainly is well-designed and well-connected. Bright and clean check-in area. Good choice of restaurants and cafes both before and after security controls. As to the negatives: the security controls are quite inefficient and slow, the airline lounges are all quite poor and certain gates (from 30/35 upward) are very far (up to 20min walking).

Modern and clean airport. The transit is really strange (like you have to get into China and leave China again). Came from Beijing to Singapore via Shenzhen. Convenient airport, lot of shops (reasonable price airports), many eateries (Western, Chinese). Easy to find your way to the  gate. Ground staff do not smile.

Excellent new terminal spacious and with lots of check-in counters. Flew China Southern to Nanjing and the check-in was swift as was security. All passengers get patted down regardless of whether you beep or not which was a bit of a nuisance. Beyond security good amenities and restaurants. We had an early morning departure and the terminal was very busy but it is definitely large enough to handle the number of people. One downside is we got a bus to the plane which took 20 minutes.

Beautiful terminal and concourses in the new terminal. Light and airy honestly the airport I would most enjoy waiting around in for a flight delay. Also good food and shops and a general uplifting feeling. Also the bus transit link back to Hong Kong was fast and efficient. Going through security screening was a bit of a line but the check procedure was quick enough.

The new terminal is amazing but the ground transport options are disjointed until the new direct train line is completed also there are few options for early morning departures. The communal areas are massive well lit and free flowing. Many shops allow for casual browsing. First Class Check In for Shenzhen Airlines was more like a 5 Star hotel in a segregated area.

Shirdi is a small regional airport with about 8-10 movements per day. Located about 15km south west of Shirdi there is nothing outside the airport other than two ATM’s and very little inside. The only commercial outlets are two small kiosks selling some food and drinks. This is not an airport to kill time in easily unless you bring your own entertainment. There is just one gate, no lounges, and the seating in the departure lounge is not really sufficient at peak periods. The air con works well, and free wifi is provided without any need for vouchers, codes etc, although it is quite slow. Also for some reason the terminal wasn’t built next to the apron meaning you have to bus to and from the aircraft.

A small airport - maybe 600 or 700 passengers a day I am guessing. Fifteen flights a day: AA to CLT and DFW. DL to ATL. And UA to DEN and IAH. The plusses: Fast. From drop off to gate in maybe 10 minutes max. Friendly staff, especially at TSA. "Small town" helpfulness: had a cell phone left on a plane returned to the check in desk before I got there to ask for lost and found. Nice, new departure hall and baggage claim. Very airy with lots of light. Low cost parking for friends picking me up. The minuses: The airfares! They border on extortionate. Many times cheaper to fly from MIA to Europe than to Shreveport. And UA, AA, and DL always seem to have the exact, same air fare. The local chamber of commerce should work on that. Concourses are dated. Industrial carpeting (remember that?). Looks like they have not been refreshed since the 1980s. Odd / quirky amateur art and movie posters and house plants (maybe a positive?). No discount carriers like Spirit, Jet Blue, Frontier or SWA. No mainline jets, just smallish regional planes.

Flew to/from Shreveport on United Express. After picking up my check-in luggage from baggage claim, I went outside the terminal and did not find any Taxis. When I did spot a Taxi, the driver asked me to call his company, reserve, and then they would dispatch someone to pick me up. In short, taking a taxi from Shreveport Airport takes significantly longer than most airports. When returning, I arrived at Shreveport Airport 3 hours early due to potential delays at the airport. Apparently, there was no one at the United ticket counter. When an agent came, she told me that I arrived "too early". Overall, the security lines at Shreveport are short, boarding areas are compact, and dining options are limited after security. The primary reason why I can't recommend this airport is due to the serious inconvenience caused to passengers who can't find any cabs readily available at Shreveport Airport.

I only went to this airport to return a car rental and it was not the most user friendly place. I would love to have flown into this destination but they do not allow airlines such as Southwest, causing fares to be much higher. It is far cheaper to fly to Dallas or Little Rock and rent a car. We have family in the area. I would have chosen this airport at least a dozen times if low cost carriers were allowed. SHV is missing out on many passengers.

I was flying out of Shreveport to see my daughter for a couple of days and did not check a bag. I was only taking a carry on. I have flown 4 times, each from a different airport, in the last 6 months. When I was going through security at Shreveport on Friday night around 8 pm, they were making everyone take everything with any liquid, gel, or paste out of your bag, no matter the size. I let them know that I had nothing more than 3 ounces but was still made to remove my cosmetic bag from my carry on and place it on the conveyor. I had not had to do this any of the other airports and is obviously not the norm. It caused a huge bottle neck of people trying to get through security to their flights. It seems they're making their own rules in Shreveport.

Its a newly built airport in Sialkot, operates international flights to various destinations around the globe. Staff are local and helpful. Entrance to the airport car park may take a bit longer but that is due to security checks at the entrance as the airport is located near Sambrial city and security staff allows only one attendant with each passenger. (some locals use this opportunity as a picnic spot which is unnecessary).

A small airport serving the Transylvania town of Sibiu. It's a walk boarding only one, constructed new in an off the shelf design (barebone). Operation is fast and efficient, staff is a bit reserved but friendly and professional. Romania is now a Schengen country, so no more border control to most EU flights. Airside there's one food and beverages shop and one duty-free. Both are nothing to rave about. There are taxis to the city and a modern bus which is cheaper.

Unprofessional and shocking airport staff. I have flown from many different airports and my experience was one of the worst I have ever had. 1) We only had around 1-2kg additional weight for the hand luggage and had to pay 69$. At this airport there is zero tolerance. The staff makes you weigh everything you bring on the plane and it cannot exceed a gram over 7kg. Upon trying to find a solution, the staff were incredibly rude, unprofessional and treated us very disrespectfully. Frankly they just ignored you and did not respond to any questions and even laughed at you. I have never experienced such a condescending attitude from the Check-In staff. Also we learned this is the airport policy and AirAsia is usually more tolerant at all other airports we flew from (Singapore, Bangkok, Kuala Lumpur). Absolutely unreasonable. 2) The airport does not allow local food stands for the local taxi drivers near the airport. If they don‘t pay for the overpriced airport food, they cannot eat during the day. The old airport apparently put much more effort into treating the taxi drivers fairly. 3) Very rude and cold staff at the entire airport from immigration to the shops. No one says hi, thank you - nothing. The airport did not at all reflect the great experience we had in Cambodia, with incredibly friendly people. It is a shame that this is the last experience you have when leaving the country. I am sincerely shocked!

Horrible passport control. If you arrive without a visa, you'll find yourself in a big mess trying to fill out either a paper form or using one of their online tablets, half of which don't work. No signs to clearly explain what to do. Long lines. They really only want your money. There are about 7-8 guys behind the glass shuffling passports along until you finally get yours back with a stamp after paying $30 cash only. Then back to another line where the immigration guys are woefully slow. Woefully. Then there's a ridiculous 50km taxi ride into town. Why did they need to build this so far away? Makes no sense.

Very modern, lots of space etc. Luggage arrived from aircraft quickly. Still the very antiquated way of processing visas, ie 3 windows, 3 queues to suffer, fortunately we were at the front, then queue up again for immigration. The really bad bit about this airport is its distance from Siem Reap itself, nearly 50kms. $35 usd by car and nearly an hours drive. A nice new road leading from the airport that then connects to the bumpy, ramshackle main road for the rest of the journey. For most tourists, the old airport was far more convenient, by a big margin.

My experience at the new Siem Reap Airport surpassed all expectations. The staff’s friendliness and proactive assistance elevated my journey. Navigating immigration was not only expeditious but also conducted with an admirable level of efficiency. The airport’s outstanding features, combined with the exceptional service, created an atmosphere of ease and comfort.

This review is about the new Siem Reap International Airport, that began operations on 16 October 2023. It was my first time at this airport and was taking the long 1 hour trip by the post office bus. Besides a big, nice golden Buddha statue, there is nothing decorative (cultural, paintings, etc.) at this new airport. Despite having an invitation to a lounge, the lounge was not in operation yet. There is only one coffee ‘facility‘, where people must queue up. Only one (Chinese) restaurant was open, but who to eat dim sum for breakfast? The staff overall seemed distant and immigration staff only became friendly after I began speaking in Khmer. I know that this is a new airport but maybe the airport authority can pick up some ideas from this review. t was also very hot inside

Both arrivals and departures in the new airport are very good. The arrivals visa control is very aggressive and unfriendly. The passport control is far too slow. Departures is good but far from friendly. I have an airport lounges pass but, was told sorry we haven’t signed an agreement yet. So you have to pay $37 USD each. The water dispensers only give hot and warm water, why no cold water?

Lovely little airport. Check in was very quick as was passport control and security. Good selection of shops after security. Airport was very clean including the toilets. A couple of dining options available and a drinking water dispenser provided to top up your bottles. Mineral water can also be purchased for US$1. Plenty of seating available by the gates. On departure there are no gates just a short walk to the plane. All in all a great little airport!

The staff at this airport have to be the friendliest and most helpful airport staff I have ever met. My fiend and I arrived at the airport leaving for Vietnam with an hour and a half until our flight, thinking all of our documents were in order. Turns out we had both entered incorrect information on our travel visas by mistake, and this mistakes would not be overlooked by Vietnam country officials, rendering the visas void, and us unable to travel. We were traveling on New Years Day, so the visa office at the airport was closed. The staff were extremely helpful with our situation. They assigned us a personal check in clerk who stayed with us through the whole ordeal and was calm and reassuring the entire time. He contacted an emergency visa officer who drove from his home to the airport and issued us emergency visas on the spot (albeit for a large fee but this was expected). Since it was a holiday they did not have any visa issuers on site. They allowed us to check in even though we did not have the correct visas in place knowing that the visa officer was on the way. Once we had our visas, we had about 20 min until the plane left. The check-in clerk ran us all the way through the airport, moved us to the head of the security line, got us right up to the front of any queue we encountered, and got us on that plane. He was running like his life depended on it. It was amazing to watch and experience. We got on the plane with 5 min to spare. We are eternally grateful to that check-in clerk, the visa officer, and all the staff we (briefly) encountered. The onus was definitely on us for messing up our visas, but they helped us all the way regardless. Most wonderful people I've ever met at an airport. 10/10 would recommend.

I arrived from Phnom Penh and then departed to Bangkok. On arrival at the domestic airport there was no air bridge, and it was a very short walk to the main building. It took a while for the luggage to come out but luckily the arrival area was not crowded. Departed from the international terminal to Bangkok. The terminal was new and clean and check in staff very friendly and helpful. There was only one security line open but the queue wasn't too long. After security there were few shops and a great Plaza Premium Lounge (if you fly Bangkok Airways they also offer their own lounge). The Plaza Premium lounge was quiet, well design and spacious. Overall a great and smooth departure experience.

Let me begin by saying that what my girlfriend and I experienced on Friday March the 7th at the Siem Reap airport was so wonderful that I want to give detains as to what I mean. Let’s start with the fact that we were scheduled to fly that morning from SR to Newark Airport connecting first in Hong Kong. We arrived at the airport, checked our bags—and found our flight from Hong Kong to Newark was cancelled due to the snow storm in the NY City area near Newark. Frustrated as were, we decided we wanted to see if we could stay another day in SR. But we figured we’d never be able to get our checked luggage off the plane. Then I looked online and saw our airline, and every other one we checked, were not flying back to Newark until Sunday! That was a huge problem for us, and left us feeling semi-frantic. And that’s where the people in the terrific staff in SR terminal took over. First, one manager somehow managed to get our checked luggage off the plane to Hong Kong. Then, another staff member advised me to call the Phnom Penh office of my airline, to check and see if by any semi-miracle of a chance there was a flight available from Hong Kong to Newark sooner than Sunday. Sure enough, someone in that office was somehow able to book us on a flight out of SR on Friday instead of Sunday—which was truly a godsend for us. What a fantastic idea it turned out for us that that staff member recommended our calling the Phnom Penh office! And then, when my girlfriend became fully frantic because she couldn’t find her carry-on bag, another staff member walked around the terminal with her and eventually and fortunately was able to locate it. Let me add too that all of these airport-terminal “guardian angels” did all of this for us in a truly friendly, patient and understanding manner. We profusely expressed our gratitude to each and every “angel” — and knew upon returning we had to post this summary of our deeply appreciated experience at the SR airport. Thank you all very much again! PS: to top it off, because of all you, we were able to spend nearly two extra, terrific days in the Siam Reap area than originally planned!

This airport operates the shortest duration flights in Nepal to and from the capital Kathmandu. The aircrafts that it receives is mostly ATR 42/72 operated by domestic carrier Buddha Air or Jetstream/ ATR operated by Yeti Airlines. The airport has very basic facilities, a small hall with few check in counters dedicated to the domestic carriers, a common seating area, to accommodate 50 to 70 people, few toilets before and after security checks. Luggage is delivered on trolleys, one canteen outside, small parking area outside, one short runway for about 20 take offs and landing combined. Very basic of airports one could imagine.

On our departure from Simferopol to Moscow we were very pleased with friendly and efficient service at the check-in and the information desks. But upstairs in the waiting area we were struck by absolutely different attitude. The attempt to have some drinks before boarding finished with success only at the third cafe. Its name somehow "Happy potatoes"? Sorry, not very sure. But I am absolutely sure about the names of the cafes where we were met with rudeness and unhelpful attitude. The names of those cafes are: "Sky-bar" and "Наша ферма". We were flying on the 1st of July. Such a shame to be let down by such a beautiful airport.

It is five years since I have been to the Crimea. The airport terminal is new and quite spacious. The arrival area worked well and I had free WiFi while I waited for my luggage to arrive from the plane. As far as departure was concerned there were plenty of check in counters and the areas were quite well sign posted in Russian and English. There are good areas for food and souvenirs (both before and after the security clearance). It is an airport which seems to work quite well and is a big improvement on the old terminal.

Simferopol Airport in 2016 has one brand new pier and the other two renovated. All look extremely busy at peak season but very well organised, clean, bright, well air-conditioned, spacious and friendly for travelers. Large and convenient parking available. Airport's transfer options include shuttle buses, taxis and even trolleybuses - there is the longest (86 km) trolleybus line in the world between Simferopol Airport and the coastal city of Yalta on the Black Sea. There were no queues at the entrance and pretty short ones at registration desks. There could be more seats available at the lounge area than the airport now has. Security officers are polite and efficient. It was a pity the airport still had outdoor boarding halls but we were assured that it was a matter of time - a year or two. Overall it is an easy airport to use. It will be nice to come back here later.

It is difficult to find polite words to describe how bad this facility is. Very long queues on domestic check in and security. Staff are incompetent and have no understanding of what they are there for. They insult you not because they are rude people but because they think that this is what their duty is. The airport is split onto three buildings: international departures (new but badly kept) international arrivals (old soviet style building shabby looking) domestic departures (new but not looked after) and small uncovered facility of baggage claim for domestic arrivals. You are bussed to and from planes which are parked within 70-100 meters from the building and it takes 10 minutes because buses stop at arrival and don't open door till they see that passengers inside are getting sick of unnesessary wait without air conditioning. Toilets with holes in floor instead of normal toilets. No words to describe how they smell. Overall impression is shame for what is a gateway to a major Ukrainian resort. No normal food bars are specialaized on feeding people with alcohol.

Poor domestic and international terminals due to inattentive and almost hostile services though domestic terminal is more pleasant in style. Expect very long queues on domestic departures both during check in and security control. On international departures I have come across numerous very nasty passport control policewomen. It is better to wear a face with no emotions and not to answer back even if you feel you are being insulted and walk away once your passport is stamped. On international arrivals you can save almost 30 minutes if you grab an immigration form early and get in the queue before filling the form since incoming arrivals passport control is much slower than you will see anywhere in the western world. You can fill your form in the queue on a magazine.
On a Scoot Flight from D49 we could not find any food or drink outlets between D30 and D49, and that is a long way. The airport has obviously grown so big that it has become unwieldy.

Singapore airport is magnificent and extremely well-maintained with its facilities, gardens, waterfalls, etc., but arriving in the country has been made very difficult for Nordics. There is no one at the immigration department, upon arrival you first have to fill out a variety of information in English on a small computer, which can take up to an hour. If the machine accepts everything, be happy. There was no one to assist you in the queue of dozens of people at the machines. And if you are accepted, you go to another automatic machine, where you present your passport and other necessary documents. Your bag has been spinning for a long time waiting for you to pick it up from the belt. When leaving the country, everything seemed to be OK, but then the departure security check began, which was anything but friendly. The border control officers, who were clearly enjoying it, gave orders and ripped off the jackets of older people who did not obey at the same second. A military-style, manly, arrogant woman took my passport and boarding pass away because they noticed my diabetes pills, everything was drugs to them. Then I was ordered aside and subjected to various tactile tests with a digital device. They couldn't, didn't care to read prescriptions. Overall, it had the feel of being in the military chain of command.

My husband and I are transferring today to the USA. We got off our plane from Bangkok and wanted to see the waterfall in the airport. A wonderful, kind and very helpful Changi Service Ambassador Tan Mey, showed us the way to see the waterfall. The train T2-T3 takes you past the waterfall. You can see it after 11am.

I want to express my disappointment regarding my recent experience with the early check-in process at Terminal 1 on December 7, 2024 at around 1.00-2.00 PM, for Thai Airways flight TG408. Upon arriving at the early check-in counter around 1:30 PM, I was met with an unexpectedly rude and unprofessional attitude from the staff member. After weighing my luggage and confirming that it was within the allowed limit, I was surprised when she immediately sent my luggage away without allowing me a chance to verify the weight or receive a luggage tag. When I attempted to ask questions, I was met with dismissive responses such as, "It's already inside, you go inside yourself,", "It's your problem now; find your own solution." "You dont like, you can report to any department you like, I dont care" This lack of communication and support was not only frustrating but also felt disrespectful. Given that there were only 2-3 passengers at the counter at that time, I found it particularly concerning that I was treated this way. Unfortunately, this incident did not end there. Upon arriving in Thailand, I discovered that my luggage had gone missing. I had to wait for the airline to search for it, which added significant stress to my travel experience. As a frequent traveler who has always appreciated Changi Airport's reputation for excellent service, I never expected to encounter such a level of rudeness and disregard. I believe that customer service training and staff management should be prioritized to ensure that all passengers receive the respectful and attentive service they deserve.

Worst customer service I have ever experienced. Half of the staff don’t know where the services such as early check in, baggage etc are. They then have the nerve to give you attitude for asking. Staff are eating food at work without any sign saying the desk is closed. Then talks to customers as if we are in the wrong for disturbing them. First class airport? More pretentious with poor service!

Check in smoothless, immigration great, lounge perfect. When you arrive at the gate here comes the security check. All X-ray, staff do NOT take care of your stuff. You fold your jacket you find it in a wreck when you pick it up. Put your expensive bag in a tray they take it out and put it directly on the conveyor belt. Really this is not acceptable for Singapore I have a 2 stars not for all airport staff but security staff. They need to care more

Electronic passport control did not work at T3. Staff were slow to rectify Phone charge and electrical sockets did not work. Christmas music only 6 bars repeated nov 8 with bad Jazz chords. Very annoying and frustrating all around

Nice and clean airport with good overall services, except passport control. Like in all major airport passport control is automated, and the machine did not recognize any person of our group (which entered Singapore in the same airport the day before). We were held between the automatic gates for 1 or 2 minutes before being directed to the manual control. Even an airline staff of some Asian airlines was held "captive" for 2 minutes. It's very strange that in a tech city like Singapore automatic passport control is so bad

We visited Changi airport both on outbound and return journey's to USA and Europe. The airport is outstanding and easy to see why ranked as 1st or 2nd best in airport rankings. Very large but very well laid out and excellent presentation with multiple facilities and services throughout. Convenient skytrain services and travel walkways to gates and between terminals. Myriad of high end stores and food outlets etc. Well posted advisory signage and notification boards. We deliberately scheduled in 2 x 12 hr stops at Changi between flights on the outbound and return trips and took advantage of the airside hotel which can be booked in 6 hr lots. The Aerotel is on the air side of the airport so no need to pass through customs. They also provide a meal with the booking - not inexpensive but worth looking at. Rooms are spacious and very quiet. Service is professional and friendly.

Terrible food choices only two places to get coffee or breakfast in T1 about a mile apart and very long queues Singapore has a coffee culture but this doesn’t exist at the airport and doesn’t seem to offer any real breakfast options when a lot of people will be travelling early in the morning. No modern water dispenser filling stations to fill your own bottle airside only outdate water fountain that cannot fill a bottle, very poor service. Changi tries to have a beat in class reputation but it’s really failing on food options

I would like to convey my heartfelt thanks to Sharon and Gayithri who were on duty at the information counter at Seletar Airport, Singapore on the eve of CNY 2024, reunion evening. They both have gone out of their way, above and beyond their normal duties in helping me to get a taxi. My flight arrived at 4.10pm. I tried to get a ride to no avail. I decided to wait it out at the airport cafeteria, after which I thought to try again, this time at the taxi stand. When I exited the building, however, the taxi stand seemed empty. The police security on duty suggested I ask for help at the information counter (by arrivals) and I did that. Sharon and her colleague persisted and helped me to get a taxi, all the way from 5.30pm until I finally got into the taxi just short of 6:10pm, which by the way stopped right in front of the arrival entrance so that I didn't have to walk far. I am most grateful and wish to commend Sharon and Gayithri for their exemplary service. I will always remember, especially Sharon, for her kindness and the personal service extended to me, a foreigner who had just arrived Singapore and had turned to her for help.

Such a cute and well designed airport! I am very impressed the moment my flight from Malaysia landed. I realized this airport is mainly used for private jets and my flight from Malaysia operated by Firefly. Facilities look new and very well maintained. Immigration process is very smooth, as well as luggage delivery. It's great to know there's another alternative to fly into Kuala lumpur.

A lovely small airport once enter the departure area left hand side is check in counter straight went to immigration counter, have your luggage security check and holding room and board. Only one small dining place found in this area and right hand side is arrival area with toilet in the middle. Once inside the gate hold room the airport free Wi-Fi is not signal well. Currently the only commercial flight using this airport is Firefly’s service to SZB airport. A more easy and faster way to the KL city area.

Not to be confused with Singapore Changi [SIN] this is a much smaller airport serving 1 commercial airline (Berjaya Air) and some chartered flights. The airport started as a pre-WW2 British military base. Some of the original architecture is still around: The waiting area is in a renovated bunker! There are separate arrival and departure halls. There are no cafes here just vending machines. In the departure hall there is a small waiting lounge for passengers taking the commercial flights mainly to Pulau Redang and Pulau Tioman in Malaysia. Customs clearance is fast and efficient. There are no connecting bridges; passengers board the flights by walking straight up to the plane.

Two years on from my last report and improvements continue to happen. The check in area has been updated making for a comfortable experience and the new TSA security area is large and works efficiently. A new hotel is now connected directly to the terminal. Staff, as usual, friendly and helpful. Forced to deduct one point for the lack of baggage carts. If they are there they are well hidden.

Have been travelling to/from this smallish regional airport for around 15 years. Have seen a lot of improvements over this time. The latest development has provided pax with good eating/drinking facilities airside. On arrival baggage claim is handy to car rentals whose parking lot is only a short walk. Departure is easy with security
queues usually short and its staff efficient and pleasant. Gate lounges have plenty of seating and well placed monitors have the latest flight information. Overall clean facilities and friendly mid west staff. Always a pleasure to use this airport.

One of the worst airports I’ve ever visited! Our flight was delayed 1.5 hours and we were left to sit at the gate without any air conditioning, nor beverages, nor food! We weren’t even allowed to get something to drink! This is unacceptable and I would not recommend Sitia airport to anyone!

We left Skiathos on Friday 30 June after a reasonable arrival at the airport and a wonderful holiday. It was exceptionally hot, with temperatures reaching 30° C. So queue to check in (despite having printed boarding cards beforehand), then another queue to drop off the hold luggage, then another huge queue, outside in the baking sun with the queue snaking around the building to go through security (only a couple of scanners available) and passport control. Once airside, all seats were occupied with many passengers sitting on the floor. You guessed it - long queue for the toilet, longer queue for refreshments. Absolutely horrendous experience which will deter me from ever visiting this beautiful island again. No point in trying to beat the crowds by arriving early, as access to the departure lounge will be refused, as it becomes so crowded.

Skiathos Airport is one of the smallest airports. The arrivals area has one luggage belt and you are outside in no time. Departure area as well is very small and the same staff that are checking your bags at the departure hall before you check in, are also the security staff. So when they are done in one part of the hall they go to the other part where they open the security checks. It looks funny, since they are jumping up and down the hall, but airport is really very small and very manageable. There is no playground for children and toilet facilities are basic. There is only one shop at the departure hall where check ins are. Everything is very relaxed. They have no fingers, so expect to board the plane on foot from the boarding gate. Walking distance to the airplane is a few hundred meters.

The small airport of Skiathos in Greece receives very few flights a day, fortunately for us tourists. It descends directly from the aircraft steps and you can walk comfortably hall for baggage claim after less than 50 meters. Given the few flights arriving at the waiting time for baggage is really ridiculous. Inside the airport is just a small shop with a bar and cafeteria. I must say that the organization of the desk is not exactly the best, in my case there were two flights in that time slot and then the 300 passengers were to form a single line across the airport to access the desk checkin in which there were only 2/3 staff. Once you checked in to access the waiting room for boarding where there is a small duty free selling tobacco, magazines and souvenirs of the island. There are sufficient seating for passengers waiting. You can arrive directly with the car just outside the principal hall of arrival/departures. So small but functional thanks to the reduced number of flights.

Horrendous. Bought priority boarding with Wizz. There was absolutely no distinction between priority and no priority. Families with prams and little children were among the last ones to board “thanks” to the disorganisation of the airport. Instructions were shouted in Macedonian and no English. I feel robbed and Wizz should feel robbed as well. This is no airport experience I would feel ashamed to fly there. Travesty!

This airport is owned by Turkish Airlines via TAV. Macedonians have no option but to increasingly use Istanbul connecting flights to get out or go home, with prices increasing due to the monopolistic nature of the operation. Fly Dubai and Qatar no longer fly due to challenging conditions being imposed by TAV to serve their IST hub, which is a massive graveyard of an airport. Macedonian politicians are corrupt and have accepted the status quo for bribes, and are happy to see the people they represent struggle to get out of Macedonia via IST, while paying more. The airport itself is much better than it used to be, but is akin to a giant toilet, with uneducated staff and 3rd world toilets and service. All employees are ruling party members and there for that reason. I hate coming back home for this very reason. Once you get to the towns and nature in Macedonia - you will love it - but have the same awaiting you on your return. Thank you TAV, Turkish Airlines, and Macedonian Politicians for making my journey home as miserable as possible every single time.
Very disappointed I was looking for some books to buy and the selection was a joke. A few books only. This is a disgrace compared to Athens airport or any other airport whatsoever.

I experienced the best customer service at Skopje Airport. During security I found out that my phone was missing. I left my phone at the selfservice check in machine on the other side of security. But they helped me out! They called their colleagues and eventually found it, brought it back to me. I felt trustful through the whole process and really really het. Thanks a lot!!

The safety control was awful because of the security staff working there. We had a bottle of alcohol in our bag which they informed us was not legal to take on the plane. We were trying to decide and view our options, and there was nobody else around so there was no rush needed. While we were discussing and questioning our options one of the staff tried to throw away our bottle without even asking us, and when we stopped him doing so other guards got included and they were being aggressive and tense for no reason at all. We were right in front of them, there was no way for us to sneak in and yet they acted like we were guilty of something. We tried to communicate like civilized beings but their response was yelling and being aggressive. In the end they threw it away, not allowing us to check it in our baggage. Totally ruined our moods and travel with their unnecessary rudeness and behaviour. Apparently they were waiting for us to offer them money but we did not want it. Wish there was anything that could be done. Do not recommend.

The airport staff are extremely rude and imperious! On checking in the agent made me walk approx. 100m with heavy bags, although the passengers lanes were not clearly defined and absolutely nobody was in front of me in the queue! They don't really understand what is customer service by it's definition and very far from understanding that they are there to help not to humiliate people. Very far from some internationally accepted standards! It's a disgrace how they treat people. I don't think that I will fly there again. It's better to fly to the nearest airport rent car and visit Skopje, if you really have to.

The airport is small yet very well organized. There is every service available that a person would require even for a long wait - restaurant - ATM's - banks - PO - as far as airport seats go I was able to sleep on these in more comfort than others. I've been through many airports and can honestly say that I'm impressed.

Skopje is a small airport but quite spacious, you can see that there are not many people flying international. But there are some coffee shops, burger king and car rentals. The only shuttle bus goes every hour. The toilets could be cleaner, they were dirty even, when there weere almost no people.
A smallish airport with limited facilities but clean and comfortable.

The new terminal is just a large barn. A few shops and very little duty free. Airport staff disinterested rude and officious. Border police just as rude demanding some sort of photocopied form from me which I did not have. Yes I do speak Macedonian and I still could not work out what he was after. Just as well we were leaving.

Sligo is a tiny airport but check-in and security were a breeze and there is a comfortable bar while you wait. After security passengers are penned in a gate which has no facilities and little comfort.

I have flown from Sligo airport a few times in the past. A very clean and well maintained airport and a pleasure to fly from. Very freindly staff and parking very cheap and beside the terminal. Security fast and efficient. Cafe- bar and toilets are open to left of check in area. Sligo airport in a sense can now be called an international airport because of new flights to Manchester in the UK. Expansion of the runway is in the pipeline and the airport hopes to have a new route to London in the future. Aer Arann serves the airport with all flights a good airline with cheap return flights and usually always on time. Always a taxi near by the main entrance and bus service available from strandhill town into Sligo city centre that is about 5 miles away. Road network is basic but acceptable. Overall a pleasant airport.

Outstanding views when arriving in on a fair weather day. Pass through Airport in little time due to size of airport. Friendly staff and facilities need to step up with any increase in flight/passenger numbers. Sligo City is only 5 miles form the airport or Euro10 taxi Journey. Area beside airport is popular for running golf surfing and sea sports with international surf competitions held regularly.

I have always found flying to/from Sligo Airport a pleasure. On a sunny day as one flies over Sligo Bay and comes into land is spectacular. The airport is tiny with two flights per day to Dublin and two flights per day from Dublin. It is served by Aer Arann. The airport has has complimentary newspapers at the check in desk adn there is a little bar where a range of refreshments are served. The staff are friendly and the service is first class. There are no luggage carousels in the airport so all luggage is left in the Baggage Reclaim by hand. One can be in the car after collecting their luggage in under a minute. It could do with better signposting though and the roads to get to it are not the best but all in all a superb airport.

4 benches for arrivals at the terminal. People sit on the ground and I understand them. You should be ashamed or why do it when you have comfortable chairs in offices. What do you care that there are people with small children.

Arrived in full Plane and just two passport controls open. Taxi driver try to rip you off so be careful. They do have a lovely airport park with pond but you cannot get down to it on foot which makes no sense at all. Would be nice if they made access to it from the shuttle train side.

If you ever wondered what it would be like to walk into a parallel universe where everyone is having a bad day every day, Sofia Airport is your ticket to that adventure. I step off the plane to be greeted by the most unfriendly and rudest staff I’ve ever encountered. Immigration at Sofia Airport deserves a special mention. These guys are clearly operating under their own version of Schengen rules – possibly sourced from an alternate dimension where logic and common sense don’t exist. It’s like they’re playing a game of “How confused can we make this traveler?” And let's talk prices. They’re right up there with other major airports, but the friendliness? It’s nowhere to be found. It’s like paying for first-class service and getting a seat in the luggage compartment. In conclusion, there’s absolutely no reason to come here or transit here unless you have a particular fondness for being insulted. If that’s your thing, congratulations, you’ve just found your worldwide number 1 destination. So if you're into adventures of the unfriendly kind, pack your bags and head to Sofia Airport. Just don't expect any warm welcomes or helpful staff. You've been warned!

I would not call Terminal 1 of Sofia Airport a terminal for international flights! This (T1) is more like an intercity bus station - unclean, with insufficient seating, with only 3 (three!) kiosks called (I don't know why). Duty free, provided that the prices in them are equal, and in some cases even higher, than those in stores in Bulgaria! Boarding organization is bordering on ZERO! The so-called "gates" are indicated by some signs, but in no way are they separated into separate areas! Не бих нарекъл Терминал 1 на летище София терминал за международни полети! Това (Т1) по-скоро е нещо като междуселска автогара - непочистено, с недостатъчно места за сядане, само с 3 (три!) павилиона, наречени (не знам защо). Duty free при условие, че цените в тях са равни, а в някои случаи дори и по-високи от тези в магазините в България! Организацията по качването в самолетите граничи с НУЛА! Т. нар. "гейтове" са обозначени с някакви табели, но по никакъв начин не са обособени в отделни зони!
Really rude staff in different positions, from check in to security. It is the worst airport I have ever visited. And definitely ruined their country's image.

If you enjoy dealing with "customer service" staff who spend the entire interaction staring intently at the floor - during check-in and AGAIN at the gate, then this is the airport for you! Uncouth all around. Two anaconda-like queues at passport control. The silent officer stared into my eyes so many times while fiddling with my (EU) passport, I felt like I was FBI Most Wanted. Just a necessary evil, this airport.

I am happy to say that I didn't encounter any problems with the staff at Sofia Airport, though I did create a problem of my own. I assumed that Ryanair used Terminal 1 and only realized my mistake after 10 minutes of failing to find my flight on the departure board. There are no signs to Terminal 2, and it is a rather convoluted walk through a car park and along a couple of busy roads. The walk took me 30 minutes, with only minimal luggage. When I rechecked Google Maps later, the route offered was close to two hours. (I read online that there is a shuttle bus every 30 minutes, but I didn't see any sign of that, either.) Once I was in the right terminal, the security and passport lines moved at reasonable speed, and the staff were professional, if not overly friendly. My arrival was also fine, though I did get stuck in a passport queue when the unfriendly immigration officer took against the passenger ahead of me.

It was the worst experience I’ve ever had at an airport. A security agent who checked our IDs was super aggressive for no reason, and swore at us in Bulgarian thinking that we wouldn’t understand him.  I have seen a few aggressive officers around in my life, however I’ve never been sworn at for no reason, so that was a shock, and I can’t believe that people like him are allowed to do jobs like this and are not fired. I then wanted to report him, however I was told that I needed to get out of the airport, report him, and then go through security all over again, and I didn’t have time to do this. I would like to mention here that all airport staff we encountered were absolutely horribly rude and unhelpful. They all need proper training.

OK. First impressions on arrival were neutral. A somewhat dated airport by appearance, linking to reflections of the 1970s where I was a youngster. Anyway, as a frequent air traveller with Partially Restricted Mobility (PRM) I am acutely conscious of the fact that having metal inside my body following reconstructive surgery is likely to activate the security metal detection archway. So it happened at Sofia Airport. Despite showing a medical card and explaining my medical situation I was then forced through the default procedure adopted by less progressive countries. So, in this case remove shoes and jumper; despite both being clothe. Of course this does not stop the activation on reentering the archway. So, with PRM I have to remove footwear (I have restricted mobility) and suffer the indignity of further removal of clothing (in public) which exposes sensitive (to me) tissue scarring, and then repeated attempts to not activate the machine. Do I need to go thro’ naked? Why is the default not to immediately use the handheld metal detector for people with declared PRM? At progressive airports this has been my experience and avoids embarrassment, whilst treating PRM people with dignity. Of course, ideally fully body X-ray machines would completely eradicate this issue. Shame on you, Sofia Airport security staff. Don’t just default to basic principles; have a progressive and appropriate security protocol for passengers with PRM.

The worst airport in Europe. Bad customer service, waiting time terrible. I am at terminal 1 and the priority line is served by only person only for all flights and economy is moving faster with two people at the check in. Toilets are so dirty. Disgusting!

A very easy and pleasant airport to use. On arrival, I was able to exit the terminal in less than five minutes. In the arrival concourse is a staffed information booth, a shop (closed when I arrived at night) and rental car booths. Taxis waited outside, I called a Uber. Departure was likewise very easy. I printed out my boarding passes from a machine. The shop (gifts, snacks, and reading materials) was open - University of Notre Dame paraphernalia was noticeable. TSA security check was unhurried and polite. After security, there are a couple of good places to eat and drink. The bathrooms were clean. The concourse was airy with high ceiling and glass panes that allowed you to watch tarmac and runway activity. The airport is about a 15 minute drive from downtown South Bend.

No facilities open on a Saturday evening after 7pm, except the toilets. Calling Southampton airport International is a big mistake when only regarding the destinations. I am disappointed about the service for food and that the self service automat only have the usual bespoke selection of chips and chocolate. Really bad service and outdated non compliant care for your visitors.

It does not matter how you look at this place the saying you cannot polish a turd reflects the airport 101%. Everybody staff wise encountered departing and arriving clearly have nothing but disdain for the passengers traveling through the place. Car parking at £55.00 for the day is nothing short of a rip off. Using the airport in this instance was Hobson's choice as it has the only early morning flight to Jersey. Awful.

Dreadful - it’s hard to know where to start from the barking security guy, to the fact that with queues stretching out to the hallway they only had one of the two security lines open. Or how about the way that staff ran around from one departure gate to the other without letting anyone know information or how about the bus driver who insisted on chatting to his mates whilst we all waited or how about the spitfire lounge where staff kept sending people back to get their table number without telling anyone you needed it when ordering. It’s an embarrassment

Poor departure information updates. Arrived early for flight to Jersey as flight was showing on time. Only when we passed through to air side did the flight show a 90 min delay. When speaking to the air crew they advised that it they knew the were delayed long before due to 'operational' reasons. Thanks for wasting my valuable time Southampton.

No information on website for arrival details of plane therefore cannot time arrival at airport to greet passengers arriving. Telephone call to contact number on website 0344 481 7777 doesn’t help, automated service that despite what you say directs you to lost baggage? I visit most airports on a daily basis greeting passengers, Southampton is terrible, no information and nowhere to get the information from. Sort it out Southampton, never experienced this in any other airport!

No staff available on arrival to claim missing baggage. Suggestion: a board with information and email contacts in case your baggage is missing in the baggage area. The only staff member in the airport said it was not her job (she was in the lost and found department), suggestion: train staff in signposting - if it’s not their job train them how to referral to the responsible person. Never say to a customer: ‘it’s not my job’ - my suitcase arrived to the airport. I have to chase airport staff - finally I’m told it is booked with a courier. That’s a week ago, sorry not impressed. Especially as I’m not getting a response or an action plan from the airport - SOU airport do not have a chance in the competitive airport business with this level of service.

Despite being quiet on both the outward and inbound journeys after the pandemic you would half expect them to have got their act together with some decent facilities and delivered some much needed staff training in the area of basic communication skills and customer service. But no, still the same rude miserable offering. The airport needs to look at its car parking charges as they are almost as bad as energy bills! The cost of parking here must be one of the biggest disincentives to flying from Southampton airport. Would I really recommended flying from here to anybody, well the answer is not really unless your travel is for business purposes and the bill is picked up by your customer or the trip is to the Channel Islands and other a long drive to London not much choice really.

Terrible airport. I flew from here 20x times in late 2021. Every single flight was departing late. Normally because the staff from Swissport manning the gates appear to be in no rush to do anything and are only resourced to board one aircraft at a time! Information boards at the airport never provide any information further to that on your ticket unless the flight is cancelled. I've seen bags get loaded onto the wrong aircraft about 15% of the time, causing delays. Altogether rubbish and awful food availability while you wait!

The saddest thing about Southampton Airport is not that it is a small airport, with all the limitations that can be expected of an airport of its size, its the incredibly poor service and jobsworth attitude of the staff. If something can be done badly, or in a way to make your journey worse - that is how they will do it. From the miserable forced parking for drop off, to massive over-charges for a minor amendment to a ticket, or the smallest hand baggage limitations known to man - with zero tolerance, they all add up to an impressively rubbish experience. All delivered by staff who genuinely appear to enjoy making your experience miserable. Clearly this is an airport that only survives due its location, convenient for many in the South, but it shouldn't be like this. They should visit London City airport to see how a small airpot can be an utter joy.

I recently had a return trip from Southampton airport for a trip to Amsterdam, flying with Flybe. The trip didn't start very well, as I realized upon arriving at the airport at 5.30 a.m. that had overbooked for the short stay parking by a week. I asked the two employees at the information desk who I could contact to change my booking or get a partial refund and was given a card with customer services number - which didn't open until 9 a.m. (by that time I was already in Amsterdam). Then proceeded to queue for luggage check-in for about 30 minutes - which for such a small airport is quite a long time. I called the customer service number as soon as the call center opened and was told to send an email with my request to a different department, which I did and didn't think anything more of during my trip. Upon my arrival back to Southampton airport, I noticed that my luggage had been very badly damaged during the trip back and went straight to the help desk, where a gentleman wrote down some information and gave me a leaflet with information for "lost/late luggage" - again, didn't think anything of it, as I was told someone would contact me soon and it was by that time almost 11 p.m. A week later and I've called customer services twice about the refund (each time being given a new email address to send my request to), not heard anything about replacing the luggage, and no idea when I'll be able to get anything sorted because the different departments apparently don't speak to each other. Generally, not too happy.

Why only open the departures area at 3 am? People are sleeping on the floor. In my opinion this is absurd and makes no sense at all. Also there is no free WiFi. I knew Southend was a low cost airport but this is too much to handle, I would avoid transiting here.

There are no signs to the drop off point and people are forced to use the short stay for a £3 charge which is increased by £1 if people are only staying for less than 10 minutes which will apply if they are only dropping off. When I called to enquire about dropping off I received an automated service telling me it would help for queries that the website couldn't help with, however, it then kept referring me to the website but didn't give me an option to find out about dropping off. Additionally, when I selected another option to speak with a person it stated that it didn't understand my query despite giving me the option to speak with someone. Finally, when I shared this feedback I was forced to enter personal details that were excessive under GDPR requirements. Regrettably a poor and seemingly corrupt and dishonest service!

Handy and efficient airport and friendly service. However complete disregard of Government standards in respect of refunds (Coronavirus). Car park booked and paid for in advance on non flex basis. Refund refused despite HM Government Competition and Markets Authority direction. Beware sharp practice.

There are zero positives about this airport. In summary, the staff are rude and unresponsive, the entire airport smells of rotten eggs, is dirty and the runway has many potholes. The pilots even look depressed that they have to fly there. I'm hoping it'll be wiped out by COVID so we can demolish it and start anew.

I am disabled and was given a wrist band saying support and assist. Absolutely no assistance was given. Also at gate I was called back to security. I was told security needed to check my hold bag. Every item was removed, my clothes were falling on the floor. I had 2 new, in box nerf car launches for my grandsons. It says on Ryanair website not to carry nerf guns in hand luggage. As I said they were in my hold luggage. They were taken from me. As I said items were falling on floor. My clothes were then just stuffed back in my case. When I reached my destination items missing, electric adapter, socks, underwear and child's sweater. I did email security with my complaint. As I expected no reply. Very bad experience.

Non è stato rispettato il mio diritto a rifiutarmi di sottopormi al body scanner, ne sono stato avvisato o informato dell'esame in questione. L'aereoporto chiude la notte, il volo alle 6 e nessun mezzo per arrivare a quell'ora. Chiusi fuori al freddo e le intemperie senza un posto dove sedersi riparati. -  My right to refuse to undergo the body scanner was not respected, I was advised or informed of the exam in question. The airport closes at night, the flight at 6 and no means of arriving at that time. Locked out in the cold and bad weather without a place to sit sheltered.

I was disgusted by the way I was treated as someone who needed help to access the plane. As a full time wheelchair user I was belittled and made to feel a nuisance by staff who didn't know what equipment to use and the safest way of using it. I was eventually, after a lot of arguments, forced to try and walk to my seat as there was no suitable transfer chair available that would fit into the aircraft. At one point the staff actually tried to manhandle me, despite me telling them that to do so would cause me immense amounts of pain and damage. All of this was despite having booked full assistance and carriage of my electric wheelchair in advance.

Absolutely terrible airport. Rude staff, security was a complete joke, rude arrogant staff again and everywhere you go outside people are trying to fine you for all sorts of parking or driving violations. Never again.

My son dropped me off at the terminal entrance. I hopped out immediately and he left straight away. I was filmed by the (Stasi?), my son issued with a £60 fine rapidly escalating to £100. Bye bye Southend Airport. See you in another life maybe, but certainly not in this one. Stansted from now on. Same for all my family members. Enjoy your short-lived £60 gain. You are the loser ultimately. Enjoy your ill gotten gains. Your future cannot be good using such dishonesty on customers. Other customers be warned. Avoid this airport at all costs! Signed: "Once Bitten......."

Used Luton airport 10 days ago without a problem. Because I use a medical urine bag it shows up when I pass through the scanner, meaning I am subjected to being frisked. This is embarrassing enough, but Southend security decided to cause me even more embarrassment by taking me to a side room and taking a swab to test for explosives. Over the top security for a near 80-year-old. Last time I use this airport as apart from the above problem the set up is getting worse as the traffic increases
Worst Airport food and coffee i have ever experienced at the café top of the escalators. Nice new building and fast and efficient check in. Just woeful coffee

Miserable staff, making us walk around twice just because we took a shortcut where there was no queue. This bully ruined our last day in Croatia and we like to spend money and travel the world. We will not be returning to Croatia. That person should be sacked for being sad and miserable, making people do things just because he is a queue staff, he should go to school and get better job if he doesn’t like this! We will spend our money in a different country next time.

The rudest customer service ever. They all look miserable and take it out on passengers, maybe if they crack a smile once in a blue moon. If they’re miserable at their jobs maybe they should just leave. What a sad way to end a nice holiday with your miserable sad staff.

Really disappointed with Split airport. Firstly there were no trays to pass our items through security. All the trays were stacked up on the other side and the attendant didn’t think to send any back causing unnecessary waits. Then the concession stand charged us €50 for 2 burgers, 3 fries and 4 soft drinks. They then charged us €1 each per sachet of condiment. That’s right. €1 euro for ketchup. What a rip off. Unfortunately, Croatia has become a bit “money grabbing” recently and this attitude will not be tolerated long by savvy travellers.

Misleading and subpar. My luggage got lost and at the counter where I reported it they told me that the luggage should arrive the day after. They gave me a receipt with their contact phone number and a website address to check on the status. What do you know - it's been 48 hours after arrival already, no sign of luggage, the website address printed on the receipt doesn't exist, and nobody is answering the phone. Terrible service, especially knowing that the local economy and people's livelihoods rely on tourism.

Plainly disability access does not apply to those in the EU. Paid a premium for business only to find the only access to the business lounge is two flights of stairs. The lounge itself is spacious as it offers little. Food is available by going back down the stairs to the main terminal. Or you can have a prepackaged croissant. Staff are between invisible and totally disinterested.

The Croatian people are wonderful until you arrive or depart from Split airport. Check-in are rude as are the servers upstairs in the café restaurant. I was last here in 2019 and it has not improved. There is no comfortable seating areas to relax and the so called premium lounge is a far cry from premium .Even before I got to the terminal I returned my car to Goldcar which is 300 metres from the terminal. I asked for someone to drive me to terminal, I’m 73 with arthritis and the temperature was 36 degrees. Very unhelpful. I was forced to walk by the terminal, I felt physically sick. The terminal is a huge empty space, very little facilities. So I decided to go to café upstairs, small tables and very uncomfortable chairs. The food was limited and not at all good. Rolls in Tuna. Ham and cheese and breaded chicken. The servers were abrupt and lacking any kind of customer service. Overall a terrible experience. Split airport needs some class. Whoever the managers are there they need to get their act together.

No water fountain after security. €3.50 for a bottle of water. €17.50 for my family of five. We really liked Croatia but there are so many times I feel we have been ripped off on this holiday. Oh yes and the airport staff are rude. Also the bag drop is poorly organised. With the space, staff and machines they have other airports process 10 times as many people in a 10th of the time. The airport building is amazing looking btw.

What a great experience visiting Split and I fell in love with Croatia - so sad when we got to the airport to discover all the charger ports to charge a phone simply does not work - not the plugs clearly made available nor the usb ports. Well bad luck I thought - though strange so many are out of action. Went on to look for a water fountain - none found - ok - ill buy a bottle of water (sad it will create plastic waste - hey ho) one place only selling water with a massively long queue - Hang on Ill ask 2 nice friendly looking ladies clearly airport staff …”excuse me I asked - is there perhaps a water fountain?” No came the answer … “you can drink water from the taps in the toilets - its drinkable” - clearly she found that very amusing as she laughed to her colleague and walked off.
