I then asked another airport staff member and he told me the same - I then asked if they do not find many people ask him for a water fountain - yes he said but our managers know this and they said that they will not allow water fountains. So sad how much waste water bottles are created and so sad that a great time in Split is now tarnished by a silly water fountain - but more so some of the rude staff at the airport - my advice - Split airport management - your culture of your company stink - look in the mirror to what cause this!

Absolutely the rudest airport staff I ever came across in my travel experience. I was catching a flight from Split to London Luton on 24th of October at 22.25. When I approached the check-in desk the lady was talking and laughing on the phone with her friend for at least few minutes while I was just standing there and waiting for her finish. After she finally was done, she told me that my flight is full and that she will need to take my bag. I had a speedy boarding ticket with EasyJet and a large cabin bag to take on the flight for which I payed £40 pounds. Anyways, I gave away my bag, and after boarding the flight I saw that it is actually half empty! I approached EasyJet flight attendant and told her my situation, she was in shock and said that they had no right to take my bag even if the flight would be full because I am in S1 category and that I will be getting a full refund for that. On top of that my bag arrived in horrible condition, it is quite pricey and now EasyJet will have to provide me with compensation for mistakes of Split Airport staff. I had such a wonderful time in Split and it is very unfortunate that my holiday ended with such bad experience.
Brand new airport, very wide halls, built for large increase in passenger load, very spacious, short TSA lines.

First of all the washrooms are junk, not at all clean, no hygiene. Lounge is also not satisfactory, chairs are bad, normal pvt bus stand is better than this, you will loose your appetite once you get to know the price of edibles. In my opinion Cochin airport is far far better.

Very sad to see the condition of this airport. When we arrived no idea on which belt the baggage will come, no display for that, have to check both belts simultaneously, after that no queue management for vaccination verification, after lots of hassle came out of terminal. Same hassle for departure too, security checks starts 1-2km before terminal, have to go through checks just after entering the campus and there is sometimes a heavy traffic jam. Then the terminal is crowded, no good options of food and also not so clean wash rooms, and as the cherry on the cake no wifi, already prepaid sim didn't work in Kashmir and no wifi at airport, not sure government seriously wants tourist to visit Kashmir or not.

Pathetic service, no support in boarding pass, baggage check-in, when your internet service is low, travelling first time, make sure you arrive at least 4 hours prior to your journey, as airport has no help, nor are the SpiceJet employees friendly.

Srinagar Airport is quite an experience but then so is the whole of Kashmir for Europeans travelling there. The airport is currently in the process of being rebuilt so arrivals are processed in what can only be described as a shed. Departures use the half-finished terminal where it is impossible to hear announcements due to the deafening construction noise. There is dust and noise everywhere although it looks as if it might be quite nice when it's finished! Be prepared to be repeatedly screened monitored searched and grilled every couple of steps along the way by a mixture of airport staff troops and military police and don't expect them to be polite or friendly - they are not.

On the understanding that Srinagar being the capital of Indian- administered Kashmir is at the centre of one of longest running conflicts in the world then one should expect a particularly unique experience regarding airport security. Srinagar airport in this respect does not disappoint. On arrival (on Jet Airways from Delhi) one is immediately struck by the fact that this is a military airfield masquerading as a civilian airport. MiG fighters and helicopter gunships abound at the far end of the airfield and all buildings are camoflauge painted. The odd civilian Boening 737 looks incongruous. For arriving foreigners you are accosted by a security official (fairly politely it must be said) to fill in a long registration document. He then accompanies you out of the arrival and baggage collection hall on a dirt track to the carpark to ensure you are being met by whoever you had claimed you were on the form. Only then can you be on your way. If you are not being met I am not sure what your fate would be. Departure though is an object lesson in airport security. The first hurdle is a kilometer or so before the airport terminal where you are stopped at a roadblock and put your luggage through an x-ray machine. Entering the airport (and only passengers are allowed not guests or friends) you again put bags through another x-ray sceeening. Then you are allowed to go to check in after which you must as a foreigner fill out another lengthy departure registration form for the police. No hand luggage whatsoever is allowed on Delhi bound flights so all you can carry is what you can fit in your pockets (therefore travel with a multipocket vest or similar to maximise carry on potential). Hand carried clear plastic water bottles do suprisingly seem OK though to carry on. The waiting area after check in is basic but OK as long as you don't mind being stared at suspiciously by numerous armed army and poice men. Then there is another long queue for a more detailed security check which involves turning out all pockets and being individually scanned. Finally you are through to the actual departure area but this is not the end. After being released to go out on foot to your waiting Boeing you again go through another security check; all pockets and a patdown before eventually you board the plane. Great views of the Himalayas to the north on the flight out but since cameras are not allowed on board the memories stay in your mind and not on film.

Worst airport employees I’ve ever experienced. Everyone was rude especially the TSA - if you ask a question be prepared to be yelled at in a rude tone. Signs said if you have any questions ask the employee so I did and he yelled “read the sign” in the rudest way you can imagine. Very unprofessional and acted like he didn’t even want to be there I don’t know how some of these people still have a job. From now on I’m either driving to my destination or a different airport. Also not enough seating in the waiting area for people waiting on flights.
The restrooms were horrible, dirty and no paper towels, disgusting, the attendant was outside the door with her phone. Men’s restroom smelled of urine.

This place is way undersized for the traffic it has. The restaurant selection is a joke. The main food court has been closed for months. Restrooms are dirty and small. Southwest needs to find a better Midwest hub

Was the worst experience of my life. Wasn’t even welcomed by the staff entering the airport plus I was trying to get all of the tags on the luggage’s and they just scolded us instead of helping us at the entrance.

Always a nightmare getting bags from baggage claim. I've never waited lass than 45 minutes for my bag, and usually it's at least an hour. Also, not enough seating. So many people have to stand or not on the ground while waiting for their plane. Absolute worst airport.

I recently had an unforgettable experience at the St. Louis airport that I felt compelled to share. It's not often that you encounter such exceptional customer service and genuine compassion in the service industry, but my encounter with two outstanding Huntleigh USA Corporation employees truly left me in awe. I found myself in a predicament when I was running late due to an unfortunate accident. Time was against me, and I was beginning to feel the stress and anxiety that comes with the fear of missing an important event. That's when Arlando Bolden and his colleague came to the rescue, turning my stressful situation into a heartwarming display of care and professionalism. Despite our best efforts, we arrived at our destination just a few minutes late. At this point, I had resigned myself to the possibility of missing my commitment, but Arlando and his coworker had other plans. They went above and beyond to ensure that I could still reach my destination. First and foremost, they helped me with the necessary arrangements, taking into consideration my convenience. This act of kindness was a relief in itself, but what truly touched me was their willingness to guide me personally. They recognized that my nerves were getting the better of me, and their calming presence made all the difference. Arlando Bolden deserves special recognition for his outstanding service and compassion. His dedication to his job and the well-being of customers is commendable. He was not just a helping hand but a beacon of support during a stressful moment. I am incredibly grateful to Arlando and his coworker for going the extra mile to ensure that I made it to my destination smoothly. Their actions exemplify the exceptional service that Huntleigh USA Corporation is known for, and I cannot thank them enough for their kindness. Huntleigh USA Corporation has earned my utmost respect and gratitude through this experience. They proved that they care deeply about their customers and are willing to do whatever it takes to make their journeys as pleasant as possible. I wholeheartedly recommend Huntleigh USA Corporation to anyone seeking reliable, compassionate, and customer-centric service. Thank you, Arlando Bolden, and your colleague, for restoring my faith in the kindness of strangers and for demonstrating the true spirit of customer service.

Probably the best example of "afraid to lay off useless people" I've seen in any airport. The check-in line for Southwest had to be a hundred people long with what appeared to be enough employees to shorten the line considerably. But no, they just stand around talking to each other with the occasional barking of doing everything yourself. Security was a joke, nobody around to tell you what to take out and leave in the bag - until after it's gone through the X-ray machine, then they tell you and call you back. Great examples of "not my job".

What a horrible airport. In all of my years traveling for business I have never seen such a disorganized mess of an airport. Security line literally out the door. No one seemed to know what was going on. TSA was terrible. I wish I could avoid this airport. If it wasn’t for work I would never fly here again. Stay away.

I travel frequently both internationally and domestically, and St Louis Airport provided one of the smoothest travel experiences I have had to date. Staff were efficient and seemed to actually care about their jobs, food and beverage options were plentiful, and the terminal was easy to navigate. The security process was also extremely efficient and well-staffed. The only negative thing I have to say about this airport is that the seating areas at the gates could have been cleaner, as chairs had dirt and particles of who knows what all over and in between them. However, not all of the seating was like this, and it didn't bother me as there were many cafes and bars to hang out in. Overall one of the better airports I have been through, and I have been through countless. Great job STL!

I have never been so angry. Because the security guard at the terminal two arrivals area couldn’t be bothered to do his job and manage traffic, people were parking and staying in spots long before their family arrived. This led to such a long line behind them that it took over an hour for my daughter to get through to pick me up. There was plenty of space at pick-up, but nobody could get through the single file line because of the idiots parking rather than driving around again. Had the guard just done his job it would have been fine.

The arrival at the airport was chaotic. The departure was even worse. There was no organization of how to get through the check points. Lines to and from the check points were at times in the same area creating a traffic jam that none of the staff seemed to know how to correct. People in line were constantly having to deal with baggage handlers going against the flow of people in line, creating much tension. The security people were rude and uncaring and did not seem to have any idea on how to handle the check point. Parcels that were put on the scanning belt were shoved through without any concern that the passengers were held up for a pat down thereby risking items being lost. Airport personnel were constantly telling people to hurry up with no clear direction as to the seating area or how to get out to the plane. I will never visit St. Lucia again.

Arrived at 2pm on 20th October, queued for 2 hours in a massive tent. Only 3 people checking passports / covid stuff, couldn’t move any slower if they tried (another flight had landed at same time) really bad experience with young children. On departure, we arrived exactly 3 hours before departure - big queue at BA bag drop desk - nobody there. Waited a further 20 minutes as almost queuing out of the door, ground staff finally put in an appearance. When got to the front of the queue, told not allowed to fly! Didn’t have NHS covid travel pass (I had been given a letter proving double vaccinated as my data was incorrect and could not be fixed simply) letter not acceptable, disgusting service, no help, advise, assistance in how to fix issue, genuinely worst ‘service’ ever. By speaking to customers, advised me to travel as ‘unvaccinated’ but had to rush to get private covid test $100 and change letter. They genuinely tried their best to stop me from flying. Made it with 10 minutes to go. ‘Computer said no’ at its very worst.

St. Lucia airport is very poor and this is all for all employees attitude, they will throw away your belongings very rudely such as perfume or lotions that are too big to travel. Just toss it right in the trash can in front of your face. Half the employees send us in a direction where we can smoke a cigarette before flying, then when we reach outside we told no smoking allowed in very rude tones. No air conditioning and they rush you through the lines with the rudest attitude.

Flew to Barbados from "Vigie Airport" last month. Staff were ok. It was clean. Rituals only place to get food and it's overpriced and thank goodness LIAT was on time as the departures lounge has almost nothing.

I must say St Lucia is a very beautiful place to visit but when it comes to traveling from Castries Airport it can be a killer. I was traveling to Barbados with LIAT and I must say the terminal was clean but very very small. Back then American Eagle (Executive Airways) was flying from San Juan to St Lucia and back. So we got the news that the LIAT flight to Barbados was delayed due to the rain. As I proceed to the departure lounge I was shocked by how it looked. The amount of people who were in the small little terminal. Both the Barbados and San Juan flight was delayed. It was such a disaster. But within an hour and some I boarded the dash 8 planes and was on my way to paradise. Got to BGi 2 hours late though.

Very small airport but well located just on the core of the capital. Immigration is ok and customs quick there's a cheap coffee shop before security as someone said before you're out of the airport in minutes.

I arrived at the George Charles Airport after a flight from Bridgetown Barbados. It is a really small airport conveniently located near Castries. The airport can only handle smaller aircraft (turboprops) the main international airport is in the south of the island (UVF). Aircraft arrival at the platform is greeted by local spectators at the airport fence. Arrival hall is a single room that contains one baggage belt and two customs positions. Obviously you're out of the airport in minutes.

We arrived 5 days ago at night and the rental car situation was an absolute mess. When we showed up at the airport today during the daylight, it wasn’t much easier to figure out the mess outside. The Allegiant check in staff seemed overworked and grumpy. The airport needs some serious traffic flow help inside and outside.

Airport still "under construction". It looks just like it did when I flew into and out of in April of 2017. Passengers for 3 departing planes are all herded into a very small room. Very few chairs and much confusion. When will it be finished? And then passenger must walk outside through rain/etc to board planes and walk up steep ramps! Very poor! Only saw one womens bathroom with only 3 stalls.

What great TSA staff have at St Pete-Clearwater Airport. The lines moved smoothly and additional lines were opened when it became crowded. The food court consists of one small shop where the food is OK. Looking forward to going through this airport again on Sunday.

Like Punta Gorda, Florida, this airport is serviced by Allegiant Airlines. The physical building and TSA staffing can not handle the volume of passengers. When flights are departing/arriving, every inch of the building is full of people. It is a fire hazard and impossible for people to move through the terminal. As a result, one needs to plan for spending hours there to get to your gate and then the flight will most likely also be late in departing. If you need to check luggage, it is even more of a nightmare. Parking and signage is also inadequate.

In need of an upgrade. The main check-in hall is wide. In and out traffic are separated. Queues, at customs or security are rather quickly passed through. Departure gates are old and lack space. I counted only 3 seats with access to a power plug on the main floor, which consist in about 10 gates! Only good food is the Teremok just outside of the arrival building, you can find western junk food inside but not russian fast food. Toilets were not clean according to standards. Access to the airport would clearly benefit from a connection to the metro. WiFi says it's connected but it's not. After trying 3 times internet finally works!

Absolute terrible experience with this airport, it takes ages to get through customs. We have been in a queue of 1.5 hrs in order to transfer to the next flight. It took 2 hrs to check the passports of 50 people, they did not check the luggage. All in all a massive let down when you arrive at 4am and you have to stand for 2 hrs just to get in.

A quick efficient security check just inside the door; then you're in a big lobby and go to a check-in counter (which you must do, at any rate for a flight out of Russia, even if you printed a boarding pass on-line [so don't bother]). There are plenty of shops and places to eat both before and after formal passport control and formal security (each of which involved less than 15 minutes queuing). Quintessentially Russian, the passport officer never smiled, but he was efficient and in no way discourteous. Restrooms are clean and well-maintained. I awaited boarding in a nice lounge (but almost all the newspapers to read are in Russian, which I can't read). Ample seating area at gate. My flight to Paris had boarding via a jetway.

Pulkovo new terminal is reasonably good and modern. Easy to navigate both on arrival and departure. Visa checks are very complex in Russia and Pulkovo stands up to the job with lots of passport check desks, queue cleared in less than 5 mins both ways. Departures hall has restaurants, cafes, shops, signage is good. However, the airport still has long way to go. There are very few air bridges - majority of planes sit on the tarmac and require shuttle bus to the terminal. Connections to the city centre belong to previous decade - you have to take bus that takes you to the metro, then ride the metro for several stops. Ending up having to take a taxi, which has some risks in Russia if you aren't familiar.

Pulkovo airport is one of the worst airports I have ever been to. First of all, there are no self kiosks anywhere, so even if you don’t have luggage you have to wait for the check in counters and they only open two hours before the flight. (International flight). We had to wait on our feet for a long time and its exhausting. The personnel in general were not friendy or helpful, they like to ignore you a lot. They are uneducated and very rude. Almost no one knows English and they don’t care about this. They act as if everyone should know Russian. Police at the passport checks don’t even understand basic words like yes and no. They can’t commumicate with you. An airport and personnel like this doesn’t suit such a beautiful place like St Petersburg. It feels like a local airport. One suspects how this airport could be an international airport that is hosting the world cup this year. It would be an ok local airport but it doesn’t deserve to be called an “International airport”.

I haven't been to this airport in years and I must say it has changed a lot for the better but still has a long way to go. The arrival zone is small and grey with a few rows of very old and dirty seating. The only colourful spot was a red warning sign right in the middle about taxi fraudsters. The washrooms have probably seen better days and could use some maintenance. We waited quite a bit for our luggage, but after that everything was pretty quick, no big lineups at the passport checks and we were out in no time. The best part of this airport is its exterior, looks nice and modern. The departure zone was a bit strange. You can get a luggage cart at the airport entrance but you won't get far with it. They run the luggage through the scanners right at the entrance, even before the registration desks, and you can't get the carts past the scanners, so after the bags are scanned you're stuck without a cart and have to carry your bags to the airline counter. There are self check-in kiosks but only the third one I tried actually worked, the passport scanner still didn't work and I had to type all the information myself but at least it printed the boarding passes for me. But even with the boarding passes you still have to stand in the airline registration line where they check in the bags, take the boarding pass you just printed away and give you a different one. Staff at the check-in counter were very nice and helpful. There were a couple of cafes and a restaurant but the service at the restaurant was very slow. Security and passport checks were a bit slow but not too bad, no super big lineups there. There was some shopping in the duty-free zone. The duty-free zone was actually not too bad, albeit relatively small. The flight left on time.

International arrivals at St Petersburg airport are at the newer terminal which is spacious but simply decorated, probably below the standard of a modern airport, but international flights are not too frequent and it is never congested. On your first arrival you may feel uneasy, but it is smooth if you know your way. To book a taxi, it is good to book inside with taxi stands which charges a reasonable standard fare of under 1000 ruples to town, and if you do not have the currency you may even charge your fare on a credit card. The train is not recommended as it terminates far from town. To go to the airport, book a taxi but specify the use of a metered city taxi, or you pay double (if not specified, hotels will book you a non-metered taxi and if so agree on a fare first). The airport is inadequate in facilities such as shopping and food outlets but is not bad.

Beware of taxi scams. There is an official taxi desk on coming through customs which will give you the taxi number plate, colour and make of car, name of driver and price of trip. On exiting, a man looked at my paperwork for the car and claimed it was his car. By the time my suitcases were loaded in his car, it was too late to back out (I hadn't checked the number plate). I was then taken to my destination and charged five times the quoted price according to a 'taxi meter' on his mobile phone. I refused to pay and photographed the number plate - he stopped me from photographing him. Will notify the police although suspect they won't be interested.

From the city to the airport in 20 minutes. The new terminal is fine. Beautiful geometric lines used in the design. Check-in for flight did not take too long. The old building renovated and converted into a zone of local flights. There are many shops and cafes. There was a small queue of pre-control before departure.

This is ridiculous. 1st time trying out Allegiant Air at St Pete (PIE) airport and I would never recommend it! This is the first and last time I will be here. The air conditioning doesn't accommodate the number of people you check in and wait standing in line with no AC no seating (except wheelchairs which I'm sure they charge extra for). Supposed to board at 6am still standing in line with no AC at 6am. So many people that the door outside remains open so more hot air pours in. I'll take Tampa Intl from now on.

This place does not have air conditioning. So if you're delayed you will wait in extreme heat. I just spent 5 hours there. I'm in shock that no one was hauled away on a stretcher from heat exhaustion because it was dangerously hot in there. While we waited in our sweatbox inside our checked luggage that we had to carry thru TSA ourselves sat outside in the hot sun. Don't be fooled by thinking the US Virgin Islands are related to the US somehow and the airport will follow suit. That airport is like any other 3rd world country airport. Awful.

If I could give this airport zero stars, I would. The worst airport I have ever been to in my entire life. Our flight was delayed twice just like other airlines as well because for some odd reason the customs line was backed all the way out of the airport past Spirit’s outside check in. It was horrendous. The delayed flight didn’t really bother me because everyone was in the same boat. We arrived 3 hours and 20 minutes early and we literally needed all of that time. They said they were going to hold flights, but so many people missed their flights because of the ridiculous line. They made the process so confusing. If they had signs and warm and welcoming people in the front, it’ll be smooth-going. You’re literally scared to ask a question because they might bite your head off. It’s like, they have an attitude and make you feel dumb as if we are supposed to already know. People are asking questions because we’re all confused. Between customs and TSA, those were the rudest people I have ever met in my life. They were so mean and nasty to people. I felt so bad for the people they ridiculed and embarrassed in front of everyone. We met a guy in line that went through the 2 hour line before us, he went outside to get fresh air because it was so hot in the airport, and guess what? They literally made him go through the entire 2+ hour process all over again. Wow! I would’ve cried. When you’re coming into the island, it’s all welcoming and they have music playing, but when you’re leaving, it’s like the slums and feels so gloomy, dark, and depressing. The airport is already undeveloped, hot, and outdated, but can you imagine spending all this money during your vacation on this expensive island then, get treated like crap when we’re leaving? That was absolutely heartbreaking. I didn’t expect top notch service because a vast majority of people we met were not very nice outside of the airport, just on the island itself, but overall, I’ve never been so ready to get on a plane in my life. I will not recommend this vacation spot to anyone honestly. I’m glad I went and saw the beauty of the island especially the beaches, but the treatment these people give you, is just horrible. It makes you not want to visit there. Unfortunately, the mean people outweigh the nice ones. I’m good. I’m glad I went, but never again.

This is the worst Airport I ever been to, and to tell you truth, it would be helpful if they gave people more jobs to make this environment less stressful. It took 3 and a half hour to get through TSA. So makes sure if your flying out of St Thomas to arrive 4hrs before your flight because they will leave you. A lot of people were rude that works there, especially TSA, I now know what it's like to be treated like an immigrant. I pray their whole process gets better.

This is the worst, nastiest, pathetic airport I have ever visited. It's absolute amateur hour and all is designed for the convenience of the workers - nothing for the actual passengers. No air conditioning! You must lug your own bag, that you've just checked, through security and then put it on the belt yourself, while some employee just stands there. Insane. Many of the employees can barely hide their disdain for the tourists. Half the ceiling tiles are missing, shops still boarded up a year after the hurricane. And the airport was awful long before the hurricane.

Food in the airport was extremely overpriced. Even though the area had recently went through a hurricane the lack of interest in making repairs or working on repairing the airport was not present. The areas that were damaged were simply covered over with plastic.

Cyril E. King Airport in St Thomas is a dirty, ugly and deteriorating airport! What a way to welcome people to the Virgin Islands. Did you look around? No wonder the welcome girls hand you rum when you pick up your bags, they're trying to blur your vision. I've never seen so many employees doing nothing - someone hand them a paint brush.

Reflecting Newfoundland as a whole, everyone seems friendly at this fairly small airport, and it has the advantages that one does not have endless walking to do inside or out: Parking and rental car lots are not far from the (single) terminal. And it’s an easy drive downtown, or to elsewhere; roads are not crowded. As in Toronto, it's hard to imagine why there are no signs posted at security about what must be taken out of bags and what not, what to do about belts and shoes, and so forth. These should be in multiple languages and in large type and repeated before and throughout the security lines. It’s as if it never occurred to airport managers that passengers include novice travelers, people who don’t hear well, and people who have trouble with spoken English or French. There should also be tables before the lines so that people can organize their things in accord with the procedures. Why don’t airports take these obvious, easy steps to reduce the stress a bit for both passengers and airport employees? The terminal has some of the usual problems of so many airports, such as not enough airside food capacity for the crowds. If you arrive at the gate an hour before your flight, by the time you get through the long Tim Horton’s line, you may not have time to finish your sandwich or your coffee. Gate seating was better than some airports but still left many people standing.

The restaurant closes at 19.45, or after the last Oslo flight takes off (?!) very sad for all of us who are going to Bergen, Norway's capital, in 2 hours. Incomprehensible and extremely poor service.  Serveringen stenger kl 19.45, eller etter at siste Oslo fly tar av(?!) veldig synd for alle oss som skal til Bergen, Norges hovedstad, om 2 timer. Uforståelig og særdeles elendig service.

Poor supervision for security area. 15 minute wait for security check with information board indicating that it would be 5 mins. 2 security lanes were open, one fast track and one non-fast track; but not both utilised when no fast track passengers were waiting. Considerable frustration for all of us in the queue and suggest airport places more supervision in this area.

I fly from this airport regularly. They've done a lot of work on it recently but it's still freezing in a lot of places. No point in it being beautiful if people are miserable from the cold. It's cold for half of the year. Don't plan on spending long in it if you have a choice. Instead walk to the nearby hotel which is cozy.
Arrival into Stavanger was quick and efficient. Hardly anyone there which was surprising after just leaving Heathrow. Departure was okay. Hardly any seats. Not a lot of facilities.

Stavanger is a comfortable and bright regional airport. Arrival is hassle-free with short walking distances and quick luggage delivery. Departure is easy too with self-service check-in machines. Although I flew on a busy Sunday afternoon waiting time to clear security control did not exceed 15 mins. However the departure lounge clearly lacks seating areas. An airport bus connects the airport with the city centre every 20 mins; note that it only accepts cash and no credit cards.

Stavanger airport Sola is a small airport like the one in Bergen and Trondheim. Not many international flights but quite many domestic. The terminal (there is only one) is 20 years old but they have started to upgrade everything. All in all a comfortable airport.;

Stewart Airport in Newburgh, NY, is simply good! I love to use this airport and often choose international carriers based on their landing at Stewart. My experiences with Play Airlines  have also been great. Lorraine in check-in is a gem and keeps things running smoothly. It is wonderful that the airport keeps adding domestic flight carriers, as well. Now, travel is possible from Stewart International to Charleston, SC. No other airport is as easy to navigate as Stewart International. The atmosphere is pleasant, the staffing is top-notch, and the TSA agents are respectful and helpful. The entire process, from check-in to boarding, is smooth and efficient. International arrivals are quick, and I’ve never had an issue with my luggage. I highly recommend Stewart Airport to anyone who wants a simple, hassle-free international travel experience.

In my life, I have been fourtunate enough to travel extensively. I've flown into and out of various airports throughout Africa, and other parts of the "developing" world, and I can say without a doubt that Stewart International Airport is the worst airport I have ever been to. Before leaving for Norway, my family and I decided to get a meal before the flight. This was our first mistake. When we tried to order subs, we were told they were not only out of the meats and vegetables we wanted, but also the sub rolls. "No big deal", I thought. I just want a sub and don't really care what kind it is. I saw that another employee was slicing turkey and asked for it on my sub. Only to be rudely told that they were out, even though it was literally two feet away. This sheer incompetence displayed by the staff seemed to be the airport's only unifying factor. The line to clear security was roughly 45 minutes, something that is ridiculous considering the number of TSA agents there. In addition, I was shocked by how rude, and downright nasty the TSA were. I have only had positive experiences with TSA in the past, and was very disappointed with how our experience went. Our return flight was somehow worse. There were only two automated check in kiosks, and surprise, when people started using them one broke. The airport's response, do absolutely nothing. This whole process took over an hour, partly because we had to wait for the customs officers to show up. Bear in mind, the airport knew a flight was coming in and should've had plenty of time to prepare and make the process as efficient as possible. In fact, I consider myself lucky. Somehow, on a non-stop flight, the staff managed to loose six bags! In conclusion, it seems that the only criteria to get a job at Stewart airport is to be inept, lazy, and rude. I strongly discourage anyone thinking of flying in or out of the airport.

Attention Norwegian! Ground check-in crew are completely rude. We have never flown with Norwegian before and didn’t know what the personal item procedure was for the cabin. Staff rolled her eyes and was chewing gum out of the side of her mouth. No need for that what so ever, regardless of whether it was our first time or not. When asked why the flight was delayed, I got a snarky answer back, saying it left Dublin late, again eyes rolled. Not happy with your level of customer service.

❌Not Verified|  I loved this airport. I have travelled to NY many times before always into JFK. Now that I have discovered the wonderful Norwegian Airlines I arrived and departed NY via Stewart International. It is a relatively small airport but efficient and confident. There is no masses of hurrying crowds which are the tension you get at large international airports. The airport is surrounded by greenery, when you leave the terminal there is a brief walk across to pick up rental car, taxis or the shuttle bus - so relaxing. For the journey home everything was relaxed, fast and efficient. As I mentioned it is a small airport, the bar, café shop and duty free is in a small area. Some people might want more but I found it more than enough. All hands are on deck in the airport to get everyone on their way home. Great little airport and great flights and price by Norwegian Airlines.

Stewart Airport is a great little airport providing service for New York's Hudson Valley Rockland County Westchester County and northern New Jersey. Parking terminal security everything is convenient and easy. The only problem is that the commercial service has dwindled down to only a few flights each day: a few flights to Philadelphia and Detroit for connections on USAirways and Delta plus a couple of nonstops to Florida on JetBlue. It's really a shame because the next-closest airports Westchester County and Newark are overcrowded difficult to park and chaotic.

Small airport in Orange County NY that is a welcome alternative to Newark & other airports if you can get a flight. Fare was hundreds less flying to PHL & connecting to IND rather than nonstop from EWR but lots of time spent sitting in airports. It is clean & staff are pleasant but not much to do. Wish there were more nonstops out of this airport to major cities but I hear it is great if you are going to Florida.
Very rude security employees at terminal 2. Never have I ever been treated the way I was by the lady. She was unprofessional, rude and just horrible!

Airport departure hall going to London (gate 86) does not have any water available either to buy or in fountain. We had to use the water from the toilet tap which is unacceptable and not up to standard. This poses a health risk.

Just getting worse and worse. The airport is dirty, expensive, getting out to the airport with shuttle is a rip-off, the luggage security check takes forever and the staff is unfriendly. Another funny thing in Arlanda is that you are not allowed to buy alcohol bottles in the shop of the airport if you fly within the EU. The last thing: they are removing most chairs so the only place with sitting available outside the gate is the paying coffee place.

Worst airport I have ever experienced for passport control and security checks. Ridiculously understaffed resulting in huge queues and waiting times. Staff just stand around and do absolutely nothing to try to bring some sort of organisation to the chaos. Would avoid this airport at all costs. Only positive is that food prices are reasonable.

My daughters and I flew out of terminal 2 on December 28 on a 6pm flight from Stockholm to LHR. We had a horrible experience. We are all veteran travelers. My daughters are both emerald status with American Airlines and I am United global services (have been for many years). We have now made a pact to avoid this airport at all costs.  The security process alone was horrible. My older daughter is breastfeeding and had pumped about 20 ounces of milk that she was keeping cold with ice. The staff treated her and us like criminals. We had to dump the ice. We had to allocate out the breast milk among the three of us. I then had to throw out my liquids because the breast milk counted against my allocation. No smiles no apologies. Just treated us like we were dirt. In other airports there is a policy for breastfeeding mothers - this one they just said this is Sweden. This is our policy. Then we get through and there is no way to get ice on the other side. Fortunately we got to the lounge and a nice gentleman helped us get ice. But what about other women who don’t have lounge access? The shops were also few and extremely low end. To add insult to injury passport control is some of the worst I’ve ever seen. There is one person sitting reviewing passports manually and physically stamping them. On the way in it took us 45 minutes to get through when we deplaned. On the way out it took 20. Have they not heard of electronic entry? There are no shops on the other side of passport control. Just hard uncomfortable chairs, and dirty toilets. Boarding is similarly manual Avoid at all costs. Horrible facilities and horrible staff

Dreadful experiences from the start of the travel and ending of the travel in Sweden. Avoid Arlanda Airport at any cost. Let me start with the passport control at Terminal 2 - two lanes, one for EU and one for non-EU. You wait for ages because the immigration officer is taking each passenger 5-20 minutes asking non-essential questions. Officers are cold, rude and unapologetic. The check-in staff at the airport stared at me when she looked at my passport. And then checking every single page of my passport to see if I have a visa to travel to the country - they need to understand about the passenger's nationality with a sense. Don't just assume the passenger needs a visa to travel to a non-EU country within Europe. The security staff at Terminal 2 are unpleasant - all staffs are cold and rude. All of the EU airports I have never experienced in terms of clear bag rules. I have used the one from the Heathrow Airport and then the security staff yells at me and throws the new bag to re-pack in a narrow clear plastic cover.  Very limited food facility and the lounge access. It needs some ample amount of improvements from efficiency to staff professionalism. Worst airport experience. I have experienced this twice now and will now travel to the country by taking a train. Avoid at any cost.

Absolutely awful. No signage. Contradictory instructions from the staff. They took my liquids at a transit security desk. We were then taken to terminal 2 and ended up in an area with no restaurants. Chocolate and crisps and fizzy drinks in a vending machine. Really appalling service. Unacceptable.

Absolutely awful. No signage. Contradictory information from staff. A transfer bus to terminal 2 that took us to an enclosed area with only chocolate, fizzy drinks and coffee in a vending machine. No restaurants. Unacceptable.

Worst arrival for a UK flight. Took 50 min to go through the passport control as they only had two border checks open. As soon as the EU passengers passed, they just closed the other booth. The whole plane had to wait for ridiculous delays with checks. Easier to get into Hades.

Expensive transfers to airport. The airport itself has decent facilities plenty of toilets, seats and wifi is adequate. Security wait times have improved from disaster of 2022. Be prepared to wait in long lines on arrival at immigration. There are no e-gates and seems short staffed especially at night. Overall the airport is OK but has areas of improvement

Stockholm Bromma is a small airport. It's very clean and the service was efficient. Great proximity to the city centre. Landing, baggage collection and exit was super easy. Taxi driver able to wait right by the carousel so there is no confusion about meeting places.

The airport is very small, and virtually all of its flights are internal Swedish flights. Firstly, the airport doesn't open until 10:30 am on Sundays, if you show up earlier you will be waiting outside until it does, which in winter in Sweden will not be much fun. Secondly, the first shuttle bus from Stockholm city centre to Bromma doesn't leave Stockholm until 11:20 am on Sunday, and it takes about 25 minutes. (By contrast shuttle buses to Arlanda leave every 15 minutes all day). These factors are well worth bearing in mind for arriving/departing Bromma. The lounge is also closed on Sundays. The airport has a small selection of coffees and cakes, and a very small and not particularly extensive souvenir shop, possibly because the primary users are Swedish people on internal flights.

A small but very nice airport just 8 km from the city center. The distances are short check-in hassle free and handling staff very friendly. I was very happy to hear international traffic had been approved about a year ago. Nowadays there are international flights to Brussels and Copenhagen. I really support the development of this airport because of the proximity to the city center the short distances and a problem free handling.

We had used this airport before. This is a tiny airport 1 hour drive from Stockholm. We have even lived there and have couple of friends there. This latest experience was something different. We are travelling back home to London and have completed our passenger locator forms, we have a copy of two vaccinations in The UK and we both work for NHS. Upon our arrival the gate is protected by armed policemen and a complete difficult character security guy. He reads our passenger locator form line by line. He sees that we have chosen exempted because we have business in The UK. He asks us to back off and puts us in a corner. After 20 minutes he is coming back with printed documents indicating we should show that we have more than 500 employees. We tell him we can book the tests now in front of him. He warns us all the time to back off and screams. The police there is touching her weapon and shows us she is ready to use it. The security guy is telling you got 5 minutes. I ask them to calm down. Internet is slow and they are not happy to help and rather hostile. Then they tell us the gates are closed. It was still 30 minutes left and this is a tiny little airport. Anyway we miss our flight because of that hostility. I’m not sure what is going on with Sweden but it’s not a good sign to see. I’ll probably will be reluctant for a very long time not wishing to visit Sweden and never gonna use Västerås Airport.

Superb airport. Small. Friendly service. No queuing went through security in under 2 minutes. Fast free wifi with constant connection and no connectivity issues. Burger and chips SEK 85. 50cl beer SEK 65. Decent viewing facility but minimal air traffic to view.
Wonderful airport with great hospitality only wish some other airline other than Ryanair flew into there from the UK.

This is a nice little airport as previously stated and one minor comment which persons using it for the first time should appreciate is that there is no ATM or machine for buying tickets for the connecting buses into Stockholm although the information desk is helpful and do accept most credit cards. They will try to assist in anyway possible. So be prepared.

I am a big fan of this airport. It has only four or five check-in desks and lots of plants and pine furniture in the small departure hall. It feels quite homely. The staff at check in and at the small cafe have always been pleasant when I have flown from here. I have also flown from Vasteras when the weather conditions have been dreadful - very cold and heavy snow - and everything at the airport and the shuttle bus from Stockholm have functioned with typical Swedish efficiency.

Stockholm Västerås is a tiny airport located around 80 minutes' drive west of Stockholm. The name is therefore misleading as Västerås is a "proper" medium-sized town in its own right. The place has a very friendly easy-going feel to it. There is very little to do save buy a cup of coffee or something stronger if that's to your taste. but then I have never had course to spend more than 90 minutes at the airport. There are special very efficient buses to Stockholm and elsewhere which connect with incoming and outgoing Ryanair flights. It is also possible to take a regular bus into Västerås. A totally hassle-free calm place to begin or end a journey.

I was there on February 28 around 2.30 pm. The conditions I found there were outrageous. I have never encountered such dirt. The tables were not cleaned after previous people. The tops had dried drink marks and were sticky. There were food marks on the couches. The floor was dirty, there were pieces of food on it. You couldn't even sit on the seats, which were very dirty. The coffee maker was in terrible condition. The coffee spout has not been cleaned for a long time. It was very dirty, with traces of dried coffee and milk. I didn't dare to drink coffee from such a machine. I spent five minutes in this lounge, mainly documenting what I found there. I was also ashamed of my traveling companion, whom I invited with me to this lounge.

Unfortunately, the airport is not good to travel from or transfer. Even though the security check was quite fast for multiple flights around the same hour, it was hard to find a seat or area to rest while waiting for the plane. And the staff are not very nice to passengers asking for directions. Toilets in and out the check-in area are dirty, and so small you can't enter with small bag when you travel alone its problematic as you can't leave the bag out with someone else. I don't recommend this airport.

The arrival at the airport was fine, but departure was atrocious. Getting through security was good but the departure lounge was bad. The kitchen had run out of burgers, which for the price were disgusting. The toilet was dirty and untidy. When called to our gate there was confusion about where to queue, when finally someone came he was a very untidy gent with a dirty shirt who was quite rude. All in all it was not a great experience. I won’t be rushing back to fly there again. My advice is to pay more and fly to Arlanda.

This is a basic airport, very small and expensive with only a few stores both landside and airside. However, security is quick, there is seating and charging points available in the cafe. The connections to public transport are poor, you will need a taxi to take you to Nykoping railway station, or take the coach, however this is expensive and can take up to two hours. There are indoor smoking booths near the gates.

Stockholm-skavsta is an absolutely appalling airport. At least £100 to get to Stockholm. Staff are rude. Takes ages to get through security. Don't bother with the airport lounge. You are offered a bag of crisps and revolting coffee. The whole thing is a nightmare from beginning to end. Use one of the other airports!

Pretty poor airport. Lack of almost all facilities except a single store, ATM and toilets. There's free wifi but you only get half an hour. You can buy beer from the store but you "aren't allowed" to drink it on the seats immediately outside. Coach to Stockholm city centre is a typical tourist trap rip off - just catch the local 515 bus (27 SEK) and then a train from Nyköping (94 SEK, possibly cheaper, if booked in advance). Calling this 'Stockholm Skavsta' airport is the equivalent of a 'Birmingham London' airport. Needs to be better signposted. You may also get harrassed by border/airport security like I did if you only have hand luggage because apparently that looks suspicious. Just save yourself the effort and fly to Arlanda (main city airport) instead.

The building, staff, services, and everything you see there is unlikely to be part of an international airport, especially in the northern Europe. It was undoubtedly the worst place to build a commercial airport. Very far from the city center and not very convenient to commute. More importantly, the amount of unfriendliness one experiences is beyond description. I did know that Sweden had introduced ID check even for European passengers. I was holding my passport as we entered the airport and suddenly a group pf officers appeared in front of us. One of them approached me and stood in front of me. He didn't say anything but he was only staring at me. I gave him my passport and ID. I'm sure he didn't know the difference, as he was looking at all pages and visas for a long time. Without saying a word, he gave them back after 5 minutes. Other staff were not better.

This is the worst airport I have been to. Not once have I got a smile from the staff in about 100 trips. Security is super slow queue for 70mins. The "new built terminal" has steps to enter and exit making it very hard for elderly. You even have to pay if you want to stop and drop off a passenger. I have been to lots of airports but this takes the price!

This airport is nowhere near Stockholm. I was charged 1300SEK (About Â£110) to get a taxi into central Stockholm as it's 105 kms away. There are no taxis available on the rank outside and calling for one on the phone on the wall took forever and when they arrive they park up across the road and it's up to you to go and ask each driver and they arrive it they are there for you. The bags did come out very quickly but this is a very small plus considering the distance the airport is from the real Stockholm. I will be flying with SAS next time as I will save a small fortune for getting to and from Stansted and to and from Stockholm airport.

As has been noted Skavsta Airport is really Nykoping airport under another name but as long as you factor in the 80 minute bus ride into central Stockholm it is a viable alternative for getting to the Swedish capital. As these 'peripheral' airports go it isn't that bad. On arrival the bags arrive fairly quickly and it was a short walk to the bus. These run frequently and apparently wait for the incoming flights which is important of you are scheduled to arrive late. Three buses an hour leave Stockholm's central bus station for the journey back to Skavsta. Returning to the airport check-in is a bit of a slap-dash affair. There are a number of check-in machines which print boarding passes and baggage tags for both Ryanair and Wizzair flights. However if you have luggage you have to join the bag drop queue which is just about as long as the conventional chaeck-in queue. Most of the machines were unservicable when we arrived anyway. There is catering both landside and airside. Remember that this is Sweden - prices are very steep. There is a small duty free shop and well that's about it really. There are five gates two of which require passing through passport control and are used by flights to the UK. There is nothing the other side apart from a few chairs so you are probably better waiting to go to your gate for as long as you are comfortable in doing so. Overall it might not win any awards but it does the job.

Because I arrived by train I spent a long time at the airport before taking the plane. I appreciated being able to wait while working on the platform on the first floor. It's quiet, holds along the wall. On the other hand, the layout is more than basic, and it would deserve to landscape this place and make it more comfortable and with more outlets associated with the tables. It is not at all pretty to see. Everything is well signposted to access the boarding gates, toilets, check-in counters. Real improvement to be made after security for catering and accessible power outlets. Indeed the choice of food is more than summary at the only restaurant in place. Only bread-based food and very rare, more than mediocre salads. Plots with sockets on the boarding floor are extremely rare and many people jostle to get there. The beverage dispensing machines can be used with a credit card, but do not dispense card tickets, which does not allow for an expense report. Very detrimental to business travelers like me.  Parce que je suis arrivée en train j'ai passé un long moment à l'aéroport avant de prendre l'avion. J'ai apprécié de pouvoir attendre en travaillant sur la plateforme au premier étage. C'est calme, des prises le long du mur. Par contre l'aménagement est plus que sommaire, et cela mériterait de paysager ce lieu et le rendre plus confortable et avec plus de prises associées aux tables. Il n'est pas du tout joli à voir. . Tout est bien signalé pour accéder aux portes d'embarquement, toilettes, comptoirs d'enregistrement. De vraies amélioration à faire après la sécurité pour la restauration et les prises de courants accessibles. En effet le choix de nourriture est plus que sommaire au seul restaurant en place. Que de la nourriture à base de pain et de très rares salades plus que médiocres. Les plots avec prises à l'étage d'embarquement sont ultra rares et bcp de monde se bouscule pour y accéder. Les machines de distributions de boissons peuvent être utilisées avec carte de crédit, mais ne distribuent pas de tickets de carte ce qui ne permet pas de faire une note de frais. Très préjudiciable pour les voyageurs business comme moi.

Arrived to airport before 4 am, as it is said on their website it is open from 4am. So waited outside in freezing December for more then one hour. This information must be crystal clear, changed on the website or they should really open the airport terminal at 4 am.

I travel a lot. So I can benchmark. Our flight of 1155h to Brussels got cancelled. Communication of the staff at airport: almost nothing. When asked questions: they answered in a very impolite way. We had to queue for 45min to get rebooked; at the desk: 1 person had to handle 22 people. Two of her colleagues were laughing in the office behind, not helping at all. Restaurant Le Zinc next to the counter: absolute terrible experience. Rude, incompetent, bad. They did not accept the vouchers given by the airline for compensation. New flight at 1510h to Brussels. Delayed again. Staff: rude and impolite. Not even an apology. Level of English: to cry. Conclusion: one of the worst experiences ever in an airport. You should be ashamed!

Strasbourg airport is a nice enough regional airport, but I do not recommend it for transit passengers for the following reason: It is not designed to deal with them, despite many regional flights using it as a changeover location. You have to pass customs and security when arriving, then go straight back through at the departures end of the airport. With a typical transit flight having 30 minutes between your arrival, and your next flight departing (so your connecting flight is officially already boarding the moment you land) this can be a challenge. Thankfully, the security check to get to the gates is quick and efficient. I made my connection, though I wonder if I would have if my connecting flight hadn't been delayed. I was surprised that on my return flight to Amsterdam, I was required to pass customs, even though France and The Netherlands are both Schengen countries. Access to the gate was blocked until someone came to man the border control area, 15 minutes after passengers were asked to proceed to the gate. No staff had any idea why, so there was much passenger confusion.

Strasbourg is a nice and convenient regional airport. Baggage claim is quick. The information desk is friendly and helpful. A covered walkway links the terminal to the train station. Travel to downtown Strasbourg costs €220 one-way and takes 10 mins - while trains run frequently weekdays service is much more reduced during the weekend (only one or two trains per hour). Beware that the ticket machines accept coins or French credit cards only and that the airport station is called "Entzheim Aeroport" and not Strasbourg Aeroport! Upon departure check-in and security screening are hassle-free. For a longer wait there is a so-called relaxation area on the 1st floor above the information booth - few people know about it although the area has comfortable seats working tables and power sockets! On the downside there is no airconditioning there so that the area can be quite warm.
Disrespectful security staff, refusing to speak English and showing ostensible non kindness. Treating EU citizens as terrorists on a Sunday morning at 9am. Worst experience in an airport.

I have used dozens of airports for work, and I have never encountered staff as rude and disrespectful as those at Stuttgart Airport. Today, the staff I tried to ask questions to (one at the tax refund section, one security officer, and another general staff member) not only failed to assist me but also responded rudely. One even made fun of me with his colleague, assuming I didn’t understand German. I find it difficult to understand why they treated people so aggressively instead of simply doing their job. It seems like the airport staff haven’t received even the most basic training in human relations that should be expected

Horrible place. Airport staff at the security check imposing questionable rules and when questioned about the exact rules (is it one liter bag or one liter of liquids (up to 100ml each) combined?) calling on the security and acting very rude. Staff refused to give their names, HIDE their badge while talking to me and refused to provide any email or phone for complains. Police threating me to refuse me entrance to my flight even though all I asked for is additional information and I was not rude or aggressive. Just horrible and disgusting customer service

The worst airport my family has ever visited. Passports were checked at least 6 times before even reaching the gate. The screening process is horrible. Remember to pull your electronics out because they will not tell you to do so, expect you to know without signs telling you, and then rip through all of your things in a side screening. They do not follow their own policy for liquids. My family had the right size bags (1L) and the appropriate sized liquid containers. They allowed my wife to have her items through and refused my daughters things without giving a reason. It was completely due to the size of the bag somehow, even though it was correct. They forced her to throw her prescription skin care to be thrown away. Then two US military members also went through and they had the exact same bags and they forced them to go buy bags in the airport that were the same size as the bags they had to take their items with them. They were then harassed by security trying to determine if my wife was trafficking our kids. They took my 14 year old daughter away from my wife, went to a cubicle, and frisked her because the woman agent said the clothing fabric on the back of her dress was weird but then continued to frisk her everywhere. This all without my wife there in her presence. She began questioning her and asking if 14 year olds are allowed to live with their parents still in the US. Long story short. I would never fly into Stuttgart again if you can avoid it. Check your bag and dont carry on any liquids because they will find a way to throw out all your stuff even if you follow their published guidelines.

Isn’t it fascinating that you can buy any spirit in a one liter bottle but water only in 0.3l bottles. I asked and the not so friendly stuff assured that the whole airport just sells little bottles, at the gates that is after security check. Oh and when I asked why she cleverly replied just because. I have never seen an airport that poor with food and beverages. Don’t come hungry or thirsty!!!

Worst airport I have ever experienced in a wealthy, industialized nation and city. The home of the likes of Mercedes and Porsche; and this is the calling card?! Really. No separate Business Class queues. No Business lounge. No quiet places to get some business done. Yet one must be here 3 hours early to endure this ordeal. What a shame. Decent shops (if I were into shopping). Clean and decent eateries.

Treated badly by the Security! Why are they so rude and disrespectful? I just left for my trip to Mallorca this month. I noticed just how rude the security people are at Stuttgart airport. I used to travel quite a bit for my job and have experienced many airports and I would have to say that these people are by far the rudest security people that I have ever encountered. The female officer in charge spoke German without asking me if I could understand it or not. She showed me that I had to place my shoes on a little step in German. I tried to do what she showed me but she started screaming at me then showed only the bottom (soles) of the shoes without any possibility to hold myself for securing this position. Especially, I objected to an "unusual" pat down I received at a checkpoint. Apparently, this female officer is getting ruder, since 2020. So say an increasing number of travelers, citing their own experiences of being harassed and harangued by the screeners who are supposed to be helping them. I realize that these people deal with thousands and thousands customers everyday and I am sure that some of these customers have attitude problems, but shouldn't air travelers also be treated respectfully and compassionately? I recommend the security screeners to be trained in "general" etiquette, including subjects such as effective communication, common courtesies and appropriate language use. The agency also has a customer service branch responsible for tracking the complaints and working with appropriate personnel to resolve grievances.

Security rude and disrespectful. I am a senior and passed through security as usual. Generally I am very pleased that the security check is made as it gives a feeling of safety while flying. Much to my regret and have to say some negative comments regarding the check I had to run through. The start was very normal but continuation was pretty rude as the woman in charge spoke German without asking me if I could understand it or not. She showed me that I had to place my shoes on a little a little step than she asked something in German I got as she was asking me to take off my shoes for inspection, which I did. Than she started screaming at me and wanted me to put on my shoes again and show only the bottom (soles) of the shoes without any possibility to hold myself for securing this position. I am a frequent flyer and this was the first time I had this type of rude behavior toward a senior.

This airport is a hell for people traveling with children. Never mind the time of the day, if you are traveling with children brace yourself to go through a nightmare. There are no fast lanes for families with babies and the people working at the security check are rude and merciless. I do not say it because of a bad experience: I have traveled to/from Stuttgart several times. Today I am writing because it was just the last straw. Very rude and painfully slow. 45 minutes in the queue with a baby just to pass and have all our suitcases checked by a rude woman, which took up another 15 minutes - pathetic! One of the worst airports I’ve been to while traveling with children! They need either more security gates or more efficient (and nicer) staff. 45 minutes of queueing is just not acceptable in a developed country! And as I say it is not just a punctual thing, it is always like that!

Really nice, modern and clean airport. The shopping options after the security check are limited, but food and beverages are no problem. The security staff is friendly, especially during the more quiet times. The possibilities for transit stays are limited but it's good for departure or arrival.

I do not know even where to start, the worst airport I have been in my life. First, the wifi connection comes and goes very bad quality and you Will not be able to do any meeting with this connection. It is the first time I see an airport close doors at 00.30, worst part is that no one informs you about this when you book your flight, so if you have early departure you have to rush because on top of It they are late for opening. Saff at the airport giving different information about opening time, one told me 3.30, another told me 4am and last one 4.30, but they opened doors 4.50, not even a word of apologies for being late.

It doesn't even look like an airport. More like a shopping mall. Lots and lots of restaurants and shops, but hard to find check-in counters. They are located in the distant corner, not close to the departures, like it's not the main thing here. Only after you get to the waiting area, you see that this is the airport - nothing inside, just a couple expensive shops with awful food and high prices. Well, at least there is 7-11 in domestic departures. Boarding is a mess. Lots of planes, lots of people, no information. They check the ticket and say: go right. On the right you see a hundred people and 5-6 planes. Everyone is running around because they don't know which plane do they need. Just a terrible experience. From check-in to boarding.

I can't remember when the last time I was here, but nevertheless it was a pleasant surprise to use the airport again. Many places to have food and the atmosphere was pleasant. Just one thing that I disliked was the toilet in the common area. It was really smelly and should be dealt with immediately.

I used the Subang Skypark Terminal for the first time on 14th October 2018. An encounter with a rude staff member at the baggage screening area spoilt the experience for me. At about 9.30 am, I queued up to place my carry-on luggage into a tray for screening. Assuming that the contents of the tray (with my identification documents) would be visually inspected and the tray moved along the conveyor belt by a staff, as required in many airports around the world, I proceeded to walk through the metal detecting arch. I was stopped by a female officer in her 20s who in an aggressive voice, asked, “Mana IC? [Where is your (Malaysian) identification card?]”. I returned to my tray to get my identification card and then walked up to the same officer who said loudly, in the earshot of everyone at the screening area , “Siapa tolak beg u? [Who is pushing your bag?]". I was startled by the hostility and before I could make some sense of the situation, she yelled in a louder tone at me, “One by one!”. To provide context, I am a Malaysian national who has lived abroad for 16 years. It was my fourth day back in Malaysia after several years and I was not familiar, especially as a first-time user of the Subang airport, with the current local procedure or practice at the baggage screening area. Regardless of this, the officer’s aggression was uncalled for. I am writing this not to shame, but to stress and remind of the importance of a professional, polite and courteous service and conduct, especially for people-facing roles in airports. Security check work may be hard and stressful, but that does not excuse rude behaviour loaded with a baggage of anger, prejudice and presumptions by a person in uniform. I urge the management to work with the relevant departments and authorities to improve staff training in professionalism and etiquette.

This is my second trip using this Airport. This is a far superior experience when compared to the main international airport KLIA especially at the immigration Department. The staff are friendly and helpful. It took us less than 10 minutes to clear immigration and custom. The airport is clean and free wifi is provided. I would highly recommend this airport if you are travelling within Malaysia or South East Asia.

This used to be the 'old' airport for all departures from KL, but after this trip I realised this airport isn't old at all. In fairness, the upgrades have given Subang a good uplifting and made the airport hassle-free for passengers. There's a good restaurant upstairs serving hot food. We didn't have any difficulty getting to the gate and we got there with time to spare. Signage was good, airport check-in and security not too difficult to clear. For local and regional departures, Subang would be the airport I will consider from now on.

Arrived on an ATR operated flight to Subang airport. Small, cramped, and nothing worth remembering. 2 baggage belts in arrivals, but seems like it needs a few more. Too many shopping kiosks in the hall outside, and a few untrustworthy taxi operators. City connectivity is very poor.

Not enough ticket agents to handle queue. More security guards standing around talking than ticket agents to help. Carrying luggage from basement on overloaded elevator to 5th floor then down for boarding pass where there were one sometimes 2 boarding pass agents while I queued up. By the time I negotiated the airport I missed my flight. Malaysian Air scheduled 1.5 hours between flights. Not nearly enough time for getting baggage going up 5 floors then down for the boarding pass. International flights a passenger needs at least 3 hours especially at Kuala airport. Extremely poor customer service and organization. Not yet arrived into the 21st century.

Modern and easy to use. No queues to speak of. Firefly the main user are efficient and a cheaper alternative to flying Malaysian out of KLIA. However beware transfer times from downtown KL especially during morning and evening peak times even more so on Mondays/Fridays. Although nearer to the city centre than KLIA it can (and did in my case) take longer to get to Subang - 75 mins - than it would have taken to get to KLIA.

Nice little airport but one drawback. The luggage storage is discontinued. That could cause a problem as Berjaya flights have only 10kg of baggage allowance. I was lucky not to pay for the other 10kg in my suit case but that might be due to the low season.

Sukhothai Airport about as nice an airport as you'll ever find anywhere. It is tiny, really well maintained, and most enjoyable to use. I think it hosts two small plane flights a day (by Bangkok Airways, which also owns the airport), maybe a few more flights. There is one gate. A small complimentary buffet with coffee, tea, banana, sticky rice, cookies and such is at one end. The waiting area is a traditional wood roof, no walls, with wood benches to sit and huge AC machines to help cool. You get to the aircraft on an open air trolley, riding past lily ponds with statues and manicured hedges. There a few local items for sale, and some Bangkok Airline bling. Everyone was pleasant and helpful. The Sukhothai airport zoo is next door, featuring some giraffes and zebra. It was not open both when we arrived, and left, but we could see the animals through a fence. Across the way is what seems to be a dinosaur museum, with many life-size dinosaur statues outside.

An airport is usually a necessary evil. This one is different; it makes you feel good. It is a facility owned by Bangkok Airways and is a small, efficient and charming outfit. To/from the plane you are transported by small, open, electric buses to the arrival/departure hall. These are roofed but in the open air surrounded by a neat park. On arrival, luggage arrived in minutes and delivered to the small arrival hall. Check-in and security took minutes without any shortcut but with customer attention and care. The pasture hall has no shopping (Great) but serves some complimentary snacks. Restrooms, as indeed the entire facility, was spotlessly clean. A true "feelgood" facility. Other Bangkok Airways facilities in Thailand follow the same attractive concept.

Sukhothai Airport owned by Bangkok Boutique Airlines is a great little secret gem not to be missed. Due to its size you feel like a celebrity. A flower festooned approach greeted by security officers in their shorts and old colonial hats checking in outdoors the open feel the gardens water dripping from the roof to keep customers cool. The check in staff all line up and 'wai' you to send you off and the ground staff at the aircraft do the same. Priority boarding for monks of course. Exotic and fabulous with the usual Bangkok Airlines free drinks and snacks.

Small island airport servicing mostly domestic and oil industry with the occasional international flight. Airport is clean well laid out with a small adequate cafe however the security leaving is completely over the top I could understand it if I was coming to the Isles given the oil industry and drug problem but leaving? There were about 12 people on our flight had to walk through all the crowd control barriers that had been erected as if they were expecting 1200 people into the security area had to take of jacket sweatshirt shoes socks hair clips was then frisked with a detector wand came through Heathrow during the Olympics the security we experience in Shetland was 10 times more than Heathrow not sure if it is because the staff are bored or they think an airport security badge gives then delusions of being members of some super swat team.

Delightful little airport serving virtually all Shetland passengers. Internal flights from Aberdeen Edinburgh Glasgow Orkney and (twice a week) STN plus occasional scheduled flights to Bergen and Faroe. Terminal has a restaurant tourist office bookshop and car hire. Everyone is friendly even though they have significant disruption from time to time when fog closes down operations. The only gripe is that public transport to Lerwick is not frequent enough to meet all flights. But overall just like the rest of Shetland it is a refreshing change form the 'me too' culture of most of Europe.

Passport control on arrival was fast and friendly. The baggage reclaim did take a while as the luggage is brought from the plane in lots of small batches, so if you're unlucky and your bag is in one of the later batches, you'll need to be patient. Customs control is also quite long and is quite different from what one expects as staff will check phones, cameras etc. The staff were all polite though and smiling and treat your belongings carefully. Departure is similar and there is a rather strange system of customs officers checking declaration forms over the shoulder of the check-in staff processing your flight! The airport itself is spotlessly clean, spacious and has all the shops and cafés you need, all fully staffed by friendly personnel.

The airport was not busy when we arrived but this did not stop it taking 65 minutes to pass through immigration and collect bags. Facilities are what you expect from an airport about 50 years out of date and did not expect anything different I guess. Found the staff to be unfriendly and there were no painted on smiles available here.

Pyongyang airport in North Korea is small and almost empty with very few flights and few passengers. It is to easy find the guides you need for your visit in North Korea. You don´t have to look for them they wait for you and find you after the passport visa and customs control. The document check and the customs control are surprisingly smooth and fast. It takes about 20 minutes to pass the airport building including the controls. The officials are friendly or at least not un-friendly as you might expect in this extremely closed communist country. You have to deposit your mobile phone at the customs control but it can be kept by the guides during your visit and you get it back when you leave the country.
