Brace yourself for a 3rd world experience at this airport; every time I use it I swear and declare I would sooner travel a further hour away to Brisbane airport to experience what you would expect in a 1st world country : we had a herded arrival into the crowded public waiting area for departures; heaving with people and observing no seating places vacant into the equally crowded baggage collection area; greeted with a big sign on the wall from the Sunshine Coast council saying we are working on improvements (same sign that has been there for 5 years with NO sign of improvement as evidence; only change is parking fees which have doubled in that time and take you further away to park). Then, yes, a 55 minute wait for baggage; it is not worth coming here nor is it worth it feeding back to the council as it gets you nowhere

Sunshine Coast Airport (MCY) services mainly flights to Sydney (SYD) and Melbourne (MEL) with some services to Adelaide (ADL) and seasonal international services to Auckland (AKL) New Zealand. A new low cost airline will soon be operating from the airport which will make flights north to several cities in Queensland and other flights to Melbourne and regional New South Wales and regional Victoria. The airport terminal is located in Marcoola about 10 mins north of Maroochydore. Private Airport transfer services, Taxis, Ubers and public buses service the airport however the public bus system does not run a timetable that would service all arrivals or departures. Paid short term and long term parking is available with some of the long term parking having sails to provide limited protection from the elements. There is also an off-site private parking business within the airport precinct that offers secure indoor and outdoor paid parking. The terminal has Check-in counter areas for airlines at the northern end and a covered breezeway then leads to security screening and the departure area at the southern end of the terminal. The luggage carousels for arriving passengers luggage are also located at the southern end of the terminal along with rental car counters, toilets. Luggage sometimes can take a while to arrive on the carousels as it appears the incoming aircraft is unloaded and the bags for the departing flight are then loaded, before the arriving flight luggage is finally brought into the terminal and loaded onto the baggage carousel. The departure area has food outlets that sell food and drinks at the usual airport prices as well as a few shops, including a surf shop and a news agency (books newspapers etc). The northern end of the departure lounge also operates as the international departure and arrival area when the seasonal Auckland flights are operating, at other times it forms part of the domestic departure area. Gates serve both as Arrival and departure gates and their are currently no aerobridges so you will walk down stairs onto the tarmac and into the terminal. Facilities are available for disabled passengers who cannot utilise the stairs. The airport at times can be very busy especially if flights are delayed, otherwise their is plenty of seating. As most flights are coming from Sydney and Melbourne weather or other delays can have a knock on effect causing delays to outbound flights. The real advantage of using this airport is avoiding around a 1hr 30 min trip to Brisbane Airport on a good day when there are no traffic delays or accidents on the M1 to Brisbane Airport, The airport is expanding and the terminal facilities will improve as part of the expansion project. Overall a very good airport experience.
Airport was so dirty, food scraps everywhere. Bins overflowing, no hand sanitiser available. Couldn’t wait to get out of there. Absolutely horrible !

This is a small regional airport with maybe a dozen flights a day, so maybe it does ok, but a booming population and tourism means that it can get crowded. On arrival, walk through the main hall full of departing passengers and then crowd around the tiny baggage carousel - you really have to shove people out of the way when you see your bag. On departure, check-in and security were fast (despite no self-check-in kiosks) but you then have to walk back outside to access departures, then there's a few cafes, shops and a bar in the departure hall. Prices seem even higher than normal for airports. There's an attempt at an observation deck but it has poor views and seems meant for smokers. No airbridges and you can get long walks to the plane in the unpredictable Queensland weather. Still, the airport's much more convenient for this area than Brisbane Airport, there's plenty of parking (long-term for $15 a day or even less - you can look it up on the website but the booking function doesn't seem to work), and there's a great approach over the water (probably for noise abatement) then a hard turn at 500ft to line up with the runway 30 seconds before landing.

Most things and services at this airport are good except the WIFI. I use this airport twice a week. The free WIFI is not operational. Waiting 10 minutes to log on, then dies faster than loading a single web page. Dogs could get the mail quicker than this service! The WIFI is as slow as dialup before dialup was invented. WWW used to be for waiting, waiting, waiting. Here it is NNN, nothing, nothing, nothing. If it can't be provided, don't advertise it.

The airport is a charming little place up on the Sunshine Coast. There are only about 10 flights a day going to Sydney and Melbourne. It has recently been upgraded and expanded the gate area is much bigger and has food outlets and toilets. It opens up on to the runway and provides nice views. It's an easy airport to handle as it isn't too big to get lost in but isn't so small so as to feel cramped. The butterfly sanctuary between check-in and security (which must be walked through as it is on the pathway) is a lovely touch and provides a unique atmosphere. The ground staff are very friendly. If heading up to the Sunshine Coast it is often cheaper and quicker to fly direct rather than to Brisbane and by far it is an easier airport to use!

Aeroplane landed at wrong terminal without telling any passengers. Plane was already delayed and this added to the delay as we were put on shuttle to domestic terminal. Also meant baggage was late arriving. No correct signage of which correct carousel to collect baggage from. Got into a Grab car (Asian Uber) at the airport and our driver was quickly stopped by local airport taxi workers. They snatched her keys from the engine and her phone from her hand. There must have been 7 men at this time. Horrid experience. If Grab drivers are not allowed in the airport then the police should be involved, not local thugs. Absolute disgrace.

Arrived from SIN to T2 Taxi time to gate was quick. Despite the reputation in advance, the Immigration process was very efficient (please learn Changi) presumably because I had got the right visa. And then it was off to get my bags, bags got there quickly. Customs was a bit shambolic as people were pulled aside. I got through quickly and then all hell broke loose as I entered the terminal building. Lots of hustling on taxis etc, but went to the Bluebird desk and no taxi unless I took a great deal on an upgraded taxi. So I took it, absolute bedlam outside with significant risk of being run over. On way back chaos to get into the terminal. More security before I checked in. Check-in queues Ok. Head upstairs and I am now in a parallel universe. The exec lounge is dreadful and sits outside the final security cleared area so no thoughts of going for a walk to do shopping. Get through into departure area gates and there is minimal seating, minimal shopping, certainly no bar and very basic food outlets. In my opinion, this airport is very basic, quite functional but on departure, you want to minimise time spent there

The airport is clean, the public facilities are quite well maintained, the internet connection is above the average airport in Indonesia. The building looks ancient and the cigarette room is inadequate, this is the airport with the fastest internet connection in Indonesia I've ever visited.

It was a nightmare experience at Surabaya airport. Arrived Terminal 2 at 9.35pm and it took me 45 mins to queue up at the immigration counter. After immigration, the baggage claim and the exit area was very crowded and unorganized. It was totally a mess. There were people in the crowd, banging me using the trolley just because I was walking too slowly and they were in a rush. I went out from the international arrival exit, wanting to find something to eat but all shops were closed and the terminal looked drab. My departing flight is in the early morning, it was another chaotic process to even enter the terminal building. And also took me very long time to clear the departure immigration. I wanted to have my breakfast in the airside but the airside is crazily small, and only Starbucks was opened at that timing. This was a nightmare experience and I will avoid this airport in the future.

Surabaya is my hometown airport. I was really happy when Terminal 2 opened but I think they could improve the facilities such as food and stores. Surabaya is a simple airport - the terminal is quite clean, toilets huge, spacious check in and waiting room. I spend a lot of time here but I have never used the WiFi so I don't know about the speed. Airport staff are attentive.

Surabaya airport is a very quick and efficient airport. On arrival the visa on arrival queue was very short, immigration there was a short wait of about 5 minutes, by the time I was done with both the bags had already arrived. Probably one of the quickest experiences for me from exiting the aircraft to curbside. Similar experience on departure quick efficient checkin with Cathay Pacific, short lines at security and immigration. The terminal is spacious and has a lot of natural light from the full height windows on either side, the restrooms were very clean. Food options are limited to a Burger King and Starbucks. the duty free has a good selection for a small airport. The premier lounge which was in a temporary set up was the only disappointment. Chose to sit at the Starbucks instead. Free wifi at the airport is also quite good.

I'm a British expat who has been living in Surabaya since July 2013. I regularly use this airport. The new terminal 2 was opened almost 2 years ago yet they still seem to be adding amenities to it that should have been there at the start like it only recently got a money changer whereas terminal 1, which is now exclusively for domestic travel had them before international flights moved to terminal 2 and still has them today. Also for ages this airport lacked ATMS though they have just been added. Most recently I took a round trip to Krabi via Kuala Lumpur on AirAsia. I took the 5.40am flight to KL from terminal 2 and queuing at check-in seemed disorganised and uncoordinated. I then arrived at immigration around 4.20am and the immigration desks were closed and unmanned. It took until after 4.30am before immigration staff turned up. This seemed very unprofessional since such long queues were forming for early morning flights to Kuala Lumpur on an A320 and the China Airlines flight to Singapore which is a large A330. On my way back we parked at an Airbridge but because it was in the domestic wing of terminal 2 we had to walk down steps from the terminal and get a bus to international arrivals, which was annoying and this is not the first time this has happened. Terminal 2 has some decent facilities like a Carl's jr, Burger King outlets in domestic and international arrivals and Starbucks but its management seem to be poorly organised and have no idea of the concept of the planning. Nevertheless it lacks an airport bar where passengers could enjoy an alcoholic beverage before the flight and if such an addition was made, I'd give food and beverages 5 stars. Another positive was that on my way back to Surabaya, immigration queues were very short but this was due to the fact I was sitting at the front of the last international flight at night.

We had a very pleasant experience at Surat Thani Airport. Queuing time was slow but staff were helpful. The airport is very far from the city and the port. Food was good and you can buy a small bottle of water for 11 baht and a packet of chocolate for 15 baht. It is a cheaper advantage instead of flying into Koh Samui. I highly recommend Surat Thani Airport.

We had quite a lot of time to kill in this airport and it didn't disappoint! There was a restaurant right in the middle of the terminal that was delicious and decently priced! Unfortunately the wifi was not working no matter how many times we tried, but they had this nice area called the library we sat in that was pleasant and helped the time pass!

Small international airport (International flights limited to a few charters from China). Arrival hall (domestic) has only one conveyor belt which did not work on the day I arrived, so luggage were brought in very swiftly by handcart. Taxi and shuttle bus available to city center 30km away. Domestic departure hall is adequate and departure gates have sufficient seating, a coffee shop and wifi.

Very basic domestic airport. Probably the most basic I’ve ever experienced. Probably built late 60s early 70s and left. Old Lino on the floor, broken last I’d strips where your luggage goes straight to the tarmac, one coffee shop. Surprisingly the toilets were very clean even with fresh flowers. Nothing airside, just uncomfortable plastic chairs. I felt offended in that only non Caucasian people were scanned with the wand. Did not seem right or fair. Boarding of course was by steps. Despite its limitations it was ok. Just annoyed when those with too much baggage holds up the rest as they argue about it.

Is a small airport, clean, in the most northern part of the world where you can reach like normal tourist. The walking to/from the airport is always in a open space, not airport finger, be prepared for temperatures below 0 9 months of the year. The baggage claim is in normal time, no so slow, but no so fast. There are taxi to the city center and the bus waiting for all passenger. There are two bus with different routes, you need to ask which one is for the your hotel. The new security check point for taking the airplane is getting a little bit slowly, but after the waiting area is nice, the same like in many years, the store is nice and the staff is great.

Apparently the world's most northerly airport. Rather informal as you might expect, but struggling to cope with the surge in tourism to Svalbard/Spitsbergen. Predictably every arriving flight (there are about 4/5 a day at this time of year, amazingly) from either Oslo or Tromso is turning straight round and going back - no surprise 'cos there really isn't anything beyond LYR. But this means that the same staff who are supposed to be doing check-in for departures are also coping with the arrival, luggage queries, etc. Add to this a shared arrivals/departures hall and a very modest security screening provision, and you get endless and confused queues, frustrated pax etc. As and when you finally get airside the departure gate hall is surprisingly spacious and calm, with a little cafe etc. The only advice is to keep calm. It's in no-one's interest to leave you behind, as that would only add to issues on the next flight, and in our experience, despite the apparently endless queue and slow processing (many passengers are transferring at Oslo so that adds complexity) everyone got on the plane and we left on time.
Poorly organised and toilets and cafe dining tables filthy disgusting. If this is Australia’s premier airport what must international tourists think. Lift your game Sydney!

This was the busiest I had ever seen Sydney Airport but things ran smoothly, the staff were very efficient getting everyone through security and was very impressed to how friendly the security staff were, that is really appreciated. I was also impressed when my flight with Air New Zealand was ready to board they called the Business class passengers first and policed it by checking everyone's boarding pass, which is good as one pays a lot more money for Business Class so should have the privilege. When departing Auckland it wasn't policed hence so many more people were in the line. An impressive airport overall.

Way too much retail space that passengers are forced to walk through, when all you want to do is get as quickly and conveniently as possible onto your flight. Made a huge mistake in stopping to get food at the McDonald's International Airport Airside II (upstairs) - eat in service - as the Big Mac was the smallest and thinnest patty I have ever encountered. It, and the chips, were cold. Not even slightly warm. They had clearly been cooked much earlier and the serving staff had not even bothered to re-heat them. There was also much too much sauce on the burger making its contents slip and slide around while trying to bite into it, and, causing the tomato and lettuce and sauce to mess all over my hands, my clean top, and surrounding areas! I was a mess by the time I had finished. An all round sloppy, disgusting meal, and a disgrace to the McDonald's name and reputation.  We had to sit at a table where used and dirty containers and serviettes were left by previous customers, and during the approx. 35 minutes we were there no one cam to clean up. The floor under our table and in the surrounding area was also littered with food. The ladies bathroom near the gate used by Jetstar (Sydney to Auckland departures) was disgustingly filthy. The handbasins were the worst. As I was walking out I saw a woman walking in and I immediately realized she was there to inspect the bathroom. So I stood and watched her as she did a very cursory look around the toilet and basin areas, then walked past me and out. The toilet paper dispensers (fixed to the wall) are too low to the ground and this makes removing toilet paper from them very difficult. We were disgusted that we would have to pay AU $5 to use a cart to transport our luggage from where the Uber dropped us off into the departures hall check-in counter.

The airport looks worn and uninviting. Signage is abysmal and staff are just not interested in the flying customers. Departures are better than Arrivals. You end up walking literal miles. This trip return from Fiji was like the airport didn't want to see us. The auto kiosk scanning did not work meaning having to go to end of line of human checking. There is no joy in Sydney airport. It was far superior in the recent past. When you exit and look for taxi it is difficult to find. Uber gets precedence and is very slow.

We were on a flight from Christchurch in New Zealand to Germany with a stopover in Sydney. There we had to go through security again, which did its job with unbearable arrogance. Some people had to take everything out of their bags, take shoes apart, throw away unopened sweets. My sand[!] from the beach was taken away from me, others had to throw away shells and small stones. I didn't see the point. Friendly requests were rudely rejected. My conclusion: I will definitely not be coming back.  Wir waren auf dem Flug von Christchurch in Neuseeland nach Deutschland mit Stopover in Sydney. Dort mussten wir nochmals durch die Sicherheitskontrolle, die mit einer unerträglichen Arroganz ihren Job verrichtete. Die Leute mussten z. T. alles aus ihren Taschen packen, Schuhe auseinander nehmen, verschlossene Süßigkeiten wegwerfen. Mir wurde der Sand[!] vom Strand abgenommen, andere mussten Muscheln und kleine Steinchen entsorgen. Ich habe den Sinn nicht erkannt. Freundliche Anfragen wurden barsch abgewiesen. Mein Fazit: Ich komme bestimmt nicht wieder.(more…)

Was not impressed with food service and attitude. Ordered 2 glasses of wine at Mike Kitchen. Charge AUS$58. Is this reasonable? Can get 2 bottles for this price? Was then told could not take wine into food court where we wanted to get something to eat. Could not get food at Mikes Kitchen as kitchen was going to close in 10 minutes. Was not permitted to bring food from another outlet to have with my wine! Shortly after wine was served was asked to hurry up as premises was about to close. We were not advised hen purchasing wine that we would have to hurry up and drink! Do not use Mikes Kitchen. And then in a rush to buy food went to KFC where the very young staff had no interest in serving me and I was then told that most menu choices were unavailable and only "zinger" burgers were on sale. My wife does not eat any spicy food. Will avoid Sydney Airport on future visits to Australia or bring my own sandwiches and but wine in duty free. Sadly spoilt an otherwise great visit to Australia.

Horrific lines at every women's toilet! People were discussing how bad it was in the line. Also, not enough seating while waiting for your flights. McDonald's was a nightmare. Such a shame to sour a lovely trip to Sydney. You can do better!

We arrived at this disgraceful airport called Sydney airport. It was like a rugby scrum. There were only six automated passport check ins. The Border security force are lazy. It was a nightmare trying to get to immigration. Hundreds of passengers all in a mess. The staff all pretending to work. We have been through so many many airports in South America and I can tell you they could teach this country and the airports on how to manage passengers. It was a nightmare. We missed our connecting flight. Then had to run to domestic to get booked on to a later flight.

Signage is never updated of the nearly 4 hours delay even until boarding time. Announcement was unclear of further delays. Staff weren’t very helpful in providing clear information and blames airport or delayed arrival of delay. Could be better trained in dealing with situation. Toilets in airport dirty and messy. Long long queues to enter departure hall. Overall rather disappointed with our national airline and busiest airport.

Worst airport experience ever, asked 5 people how to get to terminal 2 from international, every answer different. Most of the ground staff ignored arrivals or were terribly rude. Walked through duty free on arrival, absolute chaos. Got picked out for security check, luggage etc. rudest man i have ever met practically yelling at me to put my suitcase on conveyer for 2nd review, could not lift my suitcase. Marked as heavy. Had 2 hours to get from international to terminal 2, finally found virgin connections cues a mile long, told to go outside to catch but for T@ bus full. finally got to T@ Virgin ground staff behind counters clearly stressed this was 8.15am, cleaners blocking walk ways every where, went through departure security check and got singled out for wand test. walkways again crowded with cleaners. had to go to gate 31, no signage for gate 31. Absolute disgrace.

The staff was very rude. It was like they were inconvenienced. Was very dissatisfied with the whole experience. Everything from check in and through security. You would think they would be people friendly.

This airport is horrible. TSA is unorganized and slow. Please do not underestimate this small airport please get there 2 hours early maybe 3 because TSA will slow you down. I’m not sure who is in charge of TSA but you need have better protocol. I almost missed my flight.

Over an hour wait at a one baggage carousel to receive luggage absolutely unacceptable. This place is a joke for all the money that they invest into it. Strongly recommend avoiding this airport at all costs if you are able to.

The airport layout is horrible. The elevators don’t match to all parking levels. Staff unable to give basic directions about location of airport services. Over 40mins wait for baggage. Gates not identified for arriving planes. Just exiting parking garage is confusing.

The service is absolutely awful! I cannot express how rude and inconsiderate these people are. If I had a choice I’d never use this airport again, unfortunately I don’t have a choice. Extremely disappointed.

Waited 65 minutes thru security yesterday and was closed out of my 11.43 to Charlotte after finally getting to the gate at 11.40. Get there 2 hrs early these days. TSA painfully slow. No sense of urgency or willingness to help. Horrible. Cost my company thousands in missed meetings. Complete joke.

Having lived in the area all of my life, I've flown out of Syracuse Hancock for years. It is a smallish regional airport with a few places to eat. The bathroom facilities are abundant and clean while gate areas are somewhat outdated and a little shopworn. The airport is divided into two main departure/arrival wings; previously each had its own TSA screening area. Recent renovations resulted in consolidation to a single TSA screening area with capacity to manage both gate wings. Because I was not aware of the renovations, I took my usual path to my assigned gate only to find that I had to backtrack to the TSA area and then back out to the gate. Perhaps further renovations (and/or improvements in signage) could result in more a more direct and efficient pathway to TSA. Once through the mostly efficient TSA process, the walk to the gate was fairly quick and straightforward. TSA lines can be long (but not like LAX, DCA, etc.) during peak periods so be prepared. Parking is adjacent to the terminal with very reasonable rates. I've left my car there for a few days at a time without concern. While sometimes flights are less expensive out of nearby cities (Rochester, Buffalo, Albany for example) I choose to fly out of Syracuse because it is so accessible. Lastly, the "Syracuse" illuminated sign on the gate area has welcomed passengers for decades with its comforting deco appearance!

Small and always a risk for bad weather but they do an amazing job clearing the snow (closed less than 24 hrs per year despite getting more snow on average than any comparable city). Rarely any delays at counters or security. Free WiFi. Not much in the way of food or shopping. No public transportation into Syracuse (taxi only).

I flew in from TRF 4th July and returned 7th. Inbound went well (no passport control between Norway and Poland) luggage came fast and no delays getting out of the airport. On departure things were not that smooth baggage system failed but much worse was the queue through security. Our departure was at the same time as a Ryanair flight to Dublin and it took the best part of 1.5 hours to pass. Staff was not rude but in dire need of learning how to smile and treat people nicely. Pity since the facilities are quite nice once you get through security. When boarding the plane there was no one leading the way from the terminal so we had to find the plane more or less on our own. Hardly satisfactory from a security point of view. All in all it wasn't that bad. Szczecin Solidarity is one of the smaller regional airports and as such rather new to international traffic. I think they have come a good way and knowing the Poles I suspect they soon will do the required adjustments.

Flew from here to STN and the service to get through passport control and security check is abysmal. Only 1 gate for each open and with 2 full Ryanair flights (STN & DUB) boarding at the same time I queued for 78 minutes to get through. Security staff who look like armed forces personnel are extremely surly and work to a go slow. If flying from here check in well early and go through passport check and security as soon as possible.

I have been using this airport for about 3 years now and found it to be a right pain sometimes. First the good points: not far from Szczecin town centre (30 mins by bus or car) it has a good bar (sells nice beers!). Now the bad points: very slow moving queues when arriving here. They dont make much of an effort to get you through passport control quickly. Bags sometimes take a long time to arrive (even though only 1 flight arrives!). When leaving SZZ the army personnel that check you are quite surly and unhelpful. You have to remove your shoes and belts!. There is no organised queue system for Ryanair flights just a free for all. Waiting lounge is very small. Can get very overcrowded when a flight is late. Overall needs improvement and the staff need to be more cheerful. 2 stars max for now.

Szczecin's Solidarity Airport is one of the smaller regional airports in Poland. The car/taxi ride from Szczecin takes a bit longer than expected but once there you will find a pleasant airport located in a wood away from the city. It has only a small terminal but it is very modern fresh and complete with all facilities (bookstalls shops cafés etc that open also for early morning departures - I'm told there is a small hotel nearby. The staff is helpful. Only a handful of flights depart each day so the terminal does not get crowded and the atmosphere is casual and relaxed. And the security check was very thorough which I appreciated.

A tip when arriving. Get to the baggage belt as quickly as possible and stand next to the baggage entry point. If you don't then you end up having to fight off the fake (they look like maintenance staff) porters who grab the bags off the belt and then demand bakshish to hand over your luggage. Departure is a real trial. As others have said there are no announcements and no departure or arrival boards. Two three or four flights depart within a short period of each other and the departure lounge is packed. You have no real idea what flight the man at the gate is calling and everyone pushes forward wondering if it's theirs.

Its a small airport and there is a queue when you depart but it moves quickly they seem very efficient and polite and do the best they can. Seating did get very tight just before the flights were called but the toilets were new clean and quite impressive for an Egyptian airport. Snacks were expensive but what you expect at the airport. Duty free seemed extremely cheap and I have been at many worse European airports.

This airport is very bad. If you fly with Thomsons they have 3 flights arriving within 20 mins of each other. Massive queues to get through the one gate. On return they have the same 3 flights Gatwick Manchester and Birmingham all checking in at the same time. Once through you are greeted with a poor departure lounge - not enough seats. You can only use local currency Refreshments are the dearest you have ever seen. Toilets a joke. Most passengers have had a long transfer before reaching this nightmare. I thought Sharm was bad but its positively luxury compared to Taba.

There is not enough seating if two flights are departing within a short space of time. The prices for snacks and drinks are exorbitant - more expensive than London Gatwick. The toilet facilities are appalling - hold your breath and get out quick. One outside a janitor gives a square of toilet paper and holds his hands out for a tip! Would travel through this airport again but would be a lot more prepared!

Small airport with arrivals and departures in this one terminal single story building. It appears to be geared towards purely charter airlines for those wishing to visit some of the nearby Egyptian resorts but is close enough to be used as an alternative to gain entry to Israel at the Taba crossing point. Very limited in regard to facilities. In departure it has two toilets one small duty free shop selling tobacco and alcohol two "snack bars" and a couple of "shops" selling typical tourist tat. Only one gate. No announcements and no boards to look for flight information. You are called forward for departure. Typical Egyptian officialdom why have two people to do a job when ten can do it ? Security checks are worrying. Big gaps that really need to be addressed which if someone was so minded could lead to a significant incident without too much effort.

Tabriz airport is small but efficient. You can't expect an international airport will all the duty-free etc. It's built for domestic flights but still offers a few flights to regional capitals and holiday destinations. Tabriz airport is the home for ATA airline which is a private Iranian airliner. Direct Istanbul-Tabriz flights are very convenient and as I said with minimal bureaucracy at the airport. The airport itself is tidy but with a limited choice for customers. The transit hall and the check-in area relatively small but they meet the purpose. The selection of food and beverages is limited though there a few nice souvenir shops. Tabriz is known for good food, Dry Nuts, Sweet shops which are all available at the airport.

Tabriz is a small, modern airport with easy access from city center. Taxi costs only 5 Euro. I was at the airport 2.5 hours before flight and there have been only one other flight in this period. I was almost alone there and already start to worry as the check in for my flight starts only 90 minutes before departure. They have plenty of souvenir shops and one cafeteria. Multimedia screens helps to kill the time. All went smooth and fast. No smoking rooms and wifi available.

TPE airport is decent overall, but the shopping area feels pretty messy. Layout is kind of disorganized, and it’s not always easy to find what you’re looking for. Also some stores seem cramped, and isn’t a clear flow to space. It would be a lot better if they improved the arrangement and made it more convenient to navigate.

I had an excellent experience at Taoyuan Airport. Very impressed with the smooth and efficient baggage handling process. The staff were incredibly helpful, offering assistance with moving my luggage at the baggage carousel. It made the entire process much easier and stress-free. Really appreciated the level of customer care and attention to detail in ensuring that everything went smoothly. I’m highly satisfied with the service and would definitely recommend it

Arrived in terminal 2. The facilities were quite outdated and the queues for immigration were quite long. I departed from terminal 1. The security lines were short, but the food options are extremely limited. Also, the airport is designed quite inefficiently. I was overall quite disappointed.

Taoyuan International Airport provides a comfortable travel experience, with modern and clean facilities and very friendly and professional staff.  However, it's worth mentioning that security and check-in queues do tend to be slightly longer during peak hours, which may impact some travellers' schedules. It is hoped that there will be further improvements in the future to provide a smoother traffic experience

This airport is ridiculous. The main waiting gates are on a lower level and they block off the gate with ropes so passengers have no where to sit! It is the craziest thing I have seen. We had dozens and dozens of people, old people, kids, whatever, standing or sitting on the floor while an empty waiting gate was roped off for who knows what reason.  I will never fly through Taipei again.

The airport was a bit far from the city but well connected to the public transportation with clear signs and direction. It was, in general, clean. Queuing time at the immigration was not too long for us. As many other Asian international airports, TPE was full of restaurants, and a shopping paradise for passengers to kill waiting time. Each boarding gate had a different theme, and sometimes did not have enough seats for everyone.

This airport is very nice, clean and efficient. The staff at the airport are also very kind and welcoming. I remember I was a little late to my flight and only had around half an hour to the flight from the check-in area. They really got me in and out very fast and I had around 10 minutes to spare. Very thankful for that.

Excellent airport and decent size - it is not as huge as other asian mega hubs but it means getting in the out of the airport is very quick. From touching town to the taxi it took 30 mins maximum. Signposts are very clear and there are so many staff to help you - all very friendly. The airport is dated and is due for a refurb yet it is spotless. Departure experience was also great. Check in was easy, immigration and security very fast and smooth (despite not having priority lane for business class custmers). There are some interesting shop aside the global boutique and plenty of seats to rest. There are even "free lounge" area which is like a living room. Airlines lounges in TPE aren't good quality with the exception of Cathay Pacific but there are a lot of F&B offers especially in Terminal 2.

Very poor experience on guiding. Although the security check and customs clearance were smooth, there are too many promotional messages on the ceiling block and guidance signs in the middle of the way to the boarding gate As a result, I almost couldn't get on the plane
There is very good food and Wifi Internet. The duty-free shop has all kinds of brands and it is cheaper than neighboring countries. The immigration inspection is  fast and not difficult.
It is located in the city center and easily accessible by buses and MRT. The size is not big. Signposts are clear. Employees are friendly and helpful. The ambience is clean.

Queuing time was 45 minutes long to get through. The staff were unhelpful. I cannot imagine a single person in that exceedingly long queue thought there was not a better way to do this process. If you can avoid transferring flights at this airport, do so. It is inefficient. I keep thinking they'll correct it but in seven years, it has remained the same.

What to say. I transit every year in 6 or 8 airports and first time here as first time with EVA Air. May be I have been spoiled by traveling with SIA or Qatar Airways but here it looks like a 1980 flashback. Dark, old and odd! First and last time.

Songshan is the most convenient airport if you are heading to Taipei. It is centrally located in downtown Taipei and has direct access to the MRT (subway) system. It is smaller than Taoyuan International Airport, the main international airport of the island but you are literally 10-15 minutes from the city center. Songshan mainly serves domestic flights within Taiwan but has direct flights to Tokyo (HND, NRT), Seul Gimpo and Shanghai (PVG, SHA). Taoyuan will have a direct connection to Taipei Main Station before the end of 2016 served by a High Speed Subway system (Taoyuan Airport MRT). The MRT claims to reach Taipei in about 36 minutes. There are two terminals, the first one is for domestic and the second one is international. Both terminals are in the same building but after clearing immigration you are separated. This could be a little bit bothersome because the stores are different. I have been to both the domestic (Kinmen - Taipei) and international (Taipei - Shanghai) and I find the international to have a better design but smaller choice of shops. Due to its small nature, I have rarely experienced lanes going longer than 15-20 minutes. It is my go to airport as I am largely based in Taipei when I am there.

I arrived here from Tokyo Haneda. Two other flights arrived at the same time, so there was a queue at immigration, which took 15 minutes. My baggage was waiting for me at baggage claim. Although older and smaller than TPE, this airport is super convenient for visitors to Taipei. Fewer passengers, decent shopping, very close to downtown and served by a metro line. I flew out of Songshan to HND once before and was surprised at how easy it was to deal with.

Decided to fly via Kinmen to mainland China instead of HKG. This required using Taipei's older Songshan Airport instead of Taoyuan Airport. Access to the airport is very quick and easy using the Taipei Metro direct to the front of the airport, something that Taoyuan is yet to get. I used the Domestic Terminal, which is odd in many ways as the domestic arrangements in Taiwan do not follow an international standard. For a start there is a 10KG limit, despite the airline's website saying 20KG was okay (the error was simply a copy and paste from the airline international sister airline and followed international rules). The Check-In counter were arranged in small islands however after getting your boarding pass, you then had to go to another counter along the airside wall for your baggage. While the queue was almost non-existent, why it can not be done at the same counter at the same time defies logic. Baggage tags simply state the name of your destination in English and Chinese, no bar codes and no straight forward ability for transferring to other flights. Due to the limited space on the airside gates, passengers are asked to wait in the Check-In Hall where there are amble lounges and 7Eleven convenience store. When your flight number appears above the Security Door, you can then proceed through to your gate. Flights are very frequent and regular, so this was not a great issue and waiting by the gate or the lounge makes little difference. Overall it was efficient and quick, despite it's quirky nature. On my return flight, the baggage hall housed two belts and the bags appeared quickly enough and I was through and on the metro back into Taipei in little time.

As a frequent traveler, this is the worst airport I’ve ever been in. Flights are perpetually delayed with no information given to passengers. Luggage has been left on the tarmac twice and not put on the plane. TSA is horrendously unprofessional. Searched through my entire luggage and strip searched me with no information given as to why I was being subjected to this. After requesting a private room for the degrading pat down, they made me remove my pants to examen my knee brace and then the TSA agent opened the door to the screening room before I was dressed. If I didn’t have to frequently come to Tallahassee for family I would boycott this airport. This is the worst excuse of an airport I’ve ever seen.

I live in Tallahassee and have used the airport (aka TLH) for more than 30 years. TLH is a very expensive local domestic airport to use. It very small for an American capital city. However it is accessible to most people who live within 50 miles of Tallahassee. The current facility is a significant upgrade over our old airport but not worthwhile for the airport construction price paid maintenance costs and amenities provided. Unfortunately I would have to recommend that travellers drive from either Atlanta or Orlando rather than rely on timely and enjoyable arrival/departure from TLH.

A very tiny airport not worthy of a city that hosts FSU and the state capital of Florida. Pretty far from city limits and costs an arm and a leg to fly into. I suggest JAX instead. The terminal is clean but thats because there is only a few square feet of actual "terminal." Not many eating selections to choose from. Long term is more expensive than it should have been.

I have been routinely flying from this airport for more than a decade and if there were any other airports in the country I would never use this one again. The only good thing about the airport is that it is fairly modern. Other than that, the service is absolutely atrocious and makes me cautious and embarrassed to invite anyone to visit the country. Staff are snappy and arrogant, refusing to answer questions, or if they bother to acknowledge your presence, you get a snarky remark spat at your face. Also, the only airport in Europe where I have experienced hands being literally shoved down my trousers. This is why I try to wear dresses whenever I’m forced to use the airport. Can’t imagine any other country allowing this kind of physical harassment. What a sad and embarrassing state of affairs.

Delightful little airport with helpful staff, unique concepts of design and little corners of comfort everywhere. There are games for children. Café was like a living room and I enjoyed my experience in this sparkling clean airport.

I had gotten through the security where the person in charge had me throw away my cosmetics (all correct sized 100 ml) because it didn’t fit properly into the minuscule plastic bag. Had I know there is a stone age policy (proven not necessary to observe in most modern airports around Europe), I would have placed my cosmetics in the luggage. I throw it out and gave a terrible review.

The absolute worst airport in Europe. If Estonia had any other international airports I would not be travelling from Tallinn. I have been to this airport more than a dozen times and not a single time have I experienced friendly service or respectful staff. Everyone who works here seems to think they are better than those disgusting passengers. Perhaps the most hopeless part is security - the only place where someone has put their hand in my trousers without warning, small items that are permitted at airports in the UK/Germany/France/Sweden/Finland/Netherlands are confiscated, and the security gates that beep at every other person are a whole new level. When you ask for an explanation they don't even look at you, and snap something along the lines of, "none of my business". One time a security guard even laughed at me when I was about to miss my flight because they were scanning half the bags twice. During the Covid-19 pandemic social distancing is not followed whatsoever. My partner was put in a cold, crowded room an hour before departure, and more recently security staff was not wearing masks nor gloves when they went through your hygiene products. Disappointing and disgraceful.

2 arrivals and one departure. Arrival is one part and departure is the other. Super efficient, clean and pleasant. Taxis out front. Departure area maybe could use more seating. Interesting there was a ping pong table there and it was quite popular. It has a relaxing feel about it. Probably one of the nicest airports anywhere. Arrival has a store where you can buy a bus card and load it for say or 3 days travel.

You can find following information on the internet: "Tallin airport will never be the largest in the world but it can be the world's cosiest airport". And basically, it's true. It's really small airport with size of average regional airport. And also it's very colorful inside. A lot wooden elements, patterned carpets and space for kids makes this airport very friendly for travellers. However due to the small size it can be a bit tight during peak hours. I've located two lounges there, one in shopping area and second between gates (not sure). I was able to use Bussines lounge in the shopping area.

Tallinn is my favourite airport of all airports I've been to. It's so small, lovely, and there are never crowds flowing around. There are about 18 gates. The Business Lounge is quiet and comfy and there's always enough food. Its main difference is the low ceiling compared to other airports. There aren't many restaurants or shops but the Tax Free Shop has almost everything needed for your flight. Staff very friendly and Wi-Fi works well.

Overall I like Tallin airport - it is small and efficient. It has many nice features. However, security check was inefficient in my case. My checked in luggage was stopped and turn upside down. Nothing was found. I was left with a mess and no apologies. When sitting at the gate I could smell everything that was being fried in the nearby bar. Also, they have TVs at the gate that are noisy and annoying.

Super tiny Airport like a bus terminal in my town, but it was a quite clean and cozy place. Location is nice - not far from city and you can get there from city center by local bus for about 1.5 euro. There were nice sofas inside and the toilet was neat and clean.

A nicely laid-out airy and spacious airport with excellent facilities and courteous staff a proper Estonian showpiece. With TLL only 5-6 km from the city centre taxi fares are very reasonable. Security was efficient and from a UK perspective refreshingly unofficious.

They were incredibly rude at TSA by the Southwest gate. They wouldn’t let me on to pick up my sons even though I had a gate pass. They said the machine couldn’t recognize my ID, despite me flying all the time. My ID and appearance match up. Finally a supervisor came over, after 20 minutes, looked at me, and said ok. The gate guy yelled to not get depressed over missing picking up my sons

The customer service at this airport is the worst I have ever experienced. The staff just seem to shout instructions which are very unclear. I don’t think I have ever come across such a rude check in staff as the lady that was checking in the BA flight to London on 31st May at F gate. We were business class and we had our passports and e tickets. She shouted at us to leave the queue as we had the wrong tickets ( or that is what she thought ) we were confused as had used them earlier, she made us feel awful and when we said we had both e tickets and paper she said we had to use paper, with that she snatched them out of our hands, rolled her eyes and huffed, she then passed them on to a colleagues whilst we stood there waiting for one of them to give back both our tickets and passports. There had been no communication or advise when we checked our luggage in that you had to have a paper boarding pass. In this day and age it seems very out of date. I felt like I was being told off, awful experience. Collecting and returning car hire was good although a pain that you have to get two separate trains but pretty quick Also if you like a wander around shops this is not the airport for you.

The customer service was absolutely terrible during security. They yelled at everyone going through and we’re not giving clean instructions and then proceeded to get mad if you got confused. I am an anxious flier and this made it so much worse. The rudeness ruined my whole experience. Absolutely do not recommend.

Worst airport for customer service. Automated boarding pass scanners don’t scan right and when you have an issue you can’t find an employee in sight and when you find one they do not care one bit. Don’t ask for a manager because they will start saying that you the customer is being disrespectful.

Immigration hall is far too small and the number of agents processing arriving passengers was far too few. There were only two agents processing arrivals (no kiosks available) yet about a dozen standing around with their thumbs hooked in their armored vests doing nothing but chatting with each other. Fortunately almost all the passengers on the flight I arrived on were American citizens and it seemed somewhat resigned to being treated with disdain by the immigration and customs agents. It's a pity if first time arrivals from a foreign country experience a "welcome" as such.

Nice airport. However, poor signage for pickup by Lyft or Uber. Baggage clam then have to go back upstairs to get picked up. Very poor design. A lot more walking for disabled. Any very confusing for someone not accustom to the area. Very disappointed in the design.

Tampa International Airport is huge and very confusing that I ended up going to the wrong direction upon exiting. I ended up in the sky center. I asked one of the people who I assume work there because he has an ID and he happily helped me and walked with me back to where I supposed to go. He worked as a chef in PF changs yet, he helped me. He was waiting for his ride after a long busy day at work, yet he got up and assisted me. Thank you Sir for going above and beyond. There really is hope in humanity.

TPA is the cleanest airport I have been in compared to ATL and BOS. This time I lost my ID and was frantic. The TA were so nice and said that it happens more than you think. There was a slight delay on Jet Blue but they made it up in the air. I prefer Jet Blue cuz I have never had a problem. Only once flying into Newark but it wasn't the airlines fault. Our flight was diverted because their was an explosion at Newark so all flights were diverted to LGA and JFK. Luckily I wound up in PA somewhere and they had to get us a hotel. Missed the wedding shower cuz then pilots were on overtime. Big mess. Finally I got to Newark and rented a car. Was glad to get back to Tampa.

Airport staff offered no assistance with flight cancellations or my wheel chair due to a significant injury to my foot. Personnel stood by while party struggled managing luggage, a 3 year old and my disability.

Incredibly rude TSA employees throughout the entire check-in process. Going through security is the absolute worst. Every employee was rude. TIA service is terrible all around anymore. They used to be very polite.

The airport is extremely small smaller than most bus stations. Services are extremely basic. On the landside there are only a small waiting room (maybe 20 chairs) and one info desk. Nothing more. Not a single ATM! (make sure you do have some cash when arriving here). On the airside there is a small cafe upstairs and a bit larger waiting room (maybe 30 or 40 chairs but still small). And only one gate. Out of the gate you walk straight to the airplane - no apron transport cause it is so small. However I can say that my experience with it is almost only good. Everything worked efficiently security is quite thorough (on the arrival there was even a police dog) but it was correct and did not make unnecessary complications. Security queue was well organized and it waiting was not too long. A bit of a hassle in the boarding queue where the staff opened an additional check and some people from the back of the queue managed to get in front. But all in all no big problems efficient procedures on arrival and departure baggage claim was also prompt. I can imagine that it might be a bit different in the high season when there are more people.

Is this an airport? Very crowded regional airport for cheaper airlines but not really worth the savings. No seating no signs under staffed queues for everything noisy and not very air conditioned the queue for our flight ended up in the gift shop and with little staff on hand arguments broke out. After paying extra to get to Tampere from the Helsinki airport we would recommend paying extra money to use Helsinki Vantaa.

Flying cheap is always a compromise and the departures' facilities at Tampere are no exception. On my journey the overcrowding and under-staffing resulted in long long queues for everything (check- in security loos etc) Babies cried and cried angry voices cursed Ryanair scrums formed - all rather stressful and unpleasant. Very few seats around most had to use the floor. p.s. be aware that in Finland the expensive taxis are more expensive on Sundays and in the evenings.

Clean and efficient nice ground staff home-made pies in the cafe upstairs. You feel you are welcome. Then 1 sq foot or less per person when Ryanair process their passengers from 3 flights at the same time through the only gate. Just don't get into that huge black hole after the check-in - - that's not the entrance but the place to drop your luggage in. A bit confusing. But the good thing is that upon arrival you walk no more than 100 yards from the plane through the custom and luggage reclaim to the coach/taxi. Beware there is no ATM around. Nice service but very basic facilities.

Diabolical shambles of an airport with very poor organisation and too many flights for it to cope with. Food offering airside is also abysmal. Flight queues intermingle and announcements are inaudible.

I am a tour operator. I organize itineraries and lead groups, mostly in Morocco. I recently had a group of 24 US university students and 2 staff arriving at the Tangier airport on Vueling flight VY7635 on Friday morning, 17 February, 2023. The flight was due in at 09:00 and arrived at 09:15. It took the group until 11:10, just under 2 hours, to get through the immigration process. I was waiting for them in the arrivals area. I had phone contact with the staff. They told me there were 3 agents working, when there is room for more to work. People waiting were getting so frustrated that they were applauding sarcastically whenever a person got through. As soon as my group was together in arrivals, I welcomed them to Morocco and immediately apologized for the miserable welcome they had received. I had to change the morning's itinerary and drop an activity. I was back in the aiport a few days later to see the group off and I had time before my own departure, so I sought out the airport manager who directed me to fill in a suggestions/complaints form--it was obvious he was not interested in hearing from me. I told him anyway. I have also sent a complaint to ONDA, the national airports authority in Morocco, and they have responded saying just about nothing. Morocco wants tourists and the money they bring, but they treat visitors to a first impression of incompetence, indifference and a lack of respect. Marrakech airport used to have people wait for up to an hour for immigration clearance and they got better. I hope Tangier airport can improve, too. They really ought to be ashamed.

International Arrival at Tashkent is fine. Bus from plane to terminal. Very quick and smooth passport control, no landing card needed, no forms to fill in. Baggage Reclaim was slow for some reason. Money Exchange in Baggage Reclaim Hall along with local mobile SIM Cards. Baggage X-ray and then walk in fenced off compound to where taxis and buses await - the usual scrum of offers of taxi etc. Domestic Departures in separate building which is older. X-ray and show ticket/E-Ticket to get in then 6 Check-in desks. Security scanning of hand luggage basic, water is allowed to go through. Departure Hall has 4/5 "gates" for bus loading of planes. There is a small cafe serving drinks/snacks and seats. International Departures is in a separate building, scanned to get in and lots of Check-in Desks. Only 1 Money Exchange that was reluctant to exchange Uzbek Soms but did so - very important as there is nowhere to do so after passport control! Check-in show as no on-line check-in, everyone has to check-in to get a Boarding Pass. Passport Control quite quick and Security OK. International Departures has a mix of shops selling local items and usual big brand alchol/cigarettes price in USD or EUR, prices OK. A few cafes that were priced in local currency, Euros or US Dollars. Many departure screens and quite a lot of seating. Only a couple of air bridges so most planes land on remote stands served by buses.

I am a U.S. citizen who was departing Tashkent airport for NYC on October 15th 2023 at 6:45 am on HY101 flight. The customs lady started berating me for having a 1 kilo or 2 pounds over the limit for my checked baggage. When I offered to pay for the extra, she ignored my offer and kept berating me in Russian for not knowing customs rules. Then, she asked me to put my carry on on the weights and continued to berate me for having another 1 kilo over the limit for my carry-on. She finally let me go! Absolutely unprofessional and unethical treatment of foreign tourists!  I will never go back!

This airport is really lame. When you arrive, you see throngs of people swarming the ticket counter with nobody outside the queue trying to control the crowd. You have to have your bags scanned on entry, at customs and at security. You also need to have a printed copy of your electronic visa to show passport control. Once behind security, there is only one shop, the duty-free shop. But that’s in name only. All the wine is twice as expensive as on the street. The conversion from Euros to USD is terrible, and it’s a must if paying by card. It’s best to try and push back and tell them how much it should be in USD using the current rate. Meanwhile, there is no business lounge for carriers besides HY, and there are no jet bridges, just old buses. There is no free Wi-Fi. Uzbekistan is trying to make a name for itself, but the departing experience is like something out of Midnight Express. I might never be back.

Strict levels of security bordering on the obsessive. Luggage is scanned twice. You are searched even if the metal detector does not go off as you pass through it. It is understandable. Beware of possible rip-offs at the Duty-Free Shop. They can give you the wrong conversions from euros to Uzbek sums if you want to pay in local currency.

Tashkent Airport has become very efficient on the international side. Immigration and customs both on the way in and on departure were quite user friendly. Not a lot of shops and restaurants but that was not inconvenient. Readers should be aware that the domestic terminal is on the other side of the runway and it could take up to 30 minutes to connect from one side to the other side using a taxi.

Tashkent airport is one of the least welcoming ever but at least there are soviet-era aircraft to look at. When I arrived, There was just a walkway leading from the gate to the immigration, which took a while but was acceptable. Then there was security. It is like Ataturk airport, only more strict. Once you approach the terminal, you pass through a metal detector. Then once you enter the terminal, am etal detector. When Checking in, the attendant at the counter seemed to be too focused on the job at hand, he didn't really hear my requests up until I got my boarding pass. Then, departure security the staff yelled at me for not putting my wallet into the x-ray machine, since I thought that it was only carry-on baggage. After that, immigration. Another person travelling in our group took so long, when we asked why, he said "The officer just kept checking and checking and checking." Then departures was welcoming. And then the cobus to take us to the plane had no air conditioning, so it was scorching.

Date 15th Aug. Time 2000 hours. Flight 2250 hours. First state - The entry to airport is thru one small gate only. The security was struggling with 200-300 passengers at a time. No sun shade. It took 30 minutes to enter first stage. Second stage is on upper floor. No issue but only one gate. For Boeing wide bodied check in staff only 2. How can they manage 200 plus passengers. It took 40 minutes to get boarding pass as one check in staff closed the counter leaving a long queue for the only one checkin staff. Third stage is customs, I have seen customs only during arrivals. But it is in Departure also at Tashkent. It took 30 minutes. Fourth stage is Immigration. Counters are but staff is very slow. Took another 30 minutes. Fifth stage is security. Open shoes, take shoe cover. Took 20 minutes. At last we reached Gate B2 just 25 minutes before departure time.

Departure was fairly easy and quick and there was an English guide for completing the customs form. You can only spend local money in the cafe or burger place but duty free only accepts dollars and euros. Escalator up to departures and not big inside but okay and clean. Arrival is very slow - so be patient. There is no queuing at passport control so I just took a seat on the side and waited until only a few people left and was much easier. At customs you need to complete two forms and I couldn't see an English guide (whereas there was one in departures) so ask a local or fill it in best as you can and customs officers will help with rest. There is a separate queue for tourists and they speak a little English make sure you keep the second copy as you will need it when you come to leave the country. Taxi ride into centre around 15000 Som i.e. $5 but you'll need to haggle a lot. Overall it's a fairly small airport and arrival does take a long time but it seems they are trying to improve things all the time.

Clean airport. Fairly good coffee and muffin place inside. The cafe takes Som or $US. Power for charging stuff in the cafe. Duty free a bit sad.3 separate security screenings but all fast enough. 60 minutes from kerbside to airline gate better than many "civilised" airports. Bags checked there arrived ok at destination on time after 3 flights. Take off 90 minutes late without explanation. The indicator board was never altered. The information desk had no better advice. Maybe the airport could insist airlines provide up to date information. The waiting masses were getting restless. One announcement was made in a language that may have been Korean but none of the Korean passengers could understand it. It was not English or Uzbek.

Tashkent Airport can be difficult to navigate. Regulations are strictly enforced especially at departure. Upon arrival I noticed that the people do not observe lines and not speaking Uzbek or Russian can be a disadvantage. Make sure that you fill out and keep all official forms you receive! There is one for each hotel you stay in and there are matching customs forms for arrival and departure; you need to list valuables and cash and produce both forms when leaving the country. Departure gate is a floor below the departure area. There is now an escalator and carts are available for taking bags from the entrance gate to the escalator but only passengers may enter the departure gate. Good luck if you have more than one or two bags! There are no porters or at least not when I was there. I had forgotten about the customs forms after I had to repeatedly insist to the airline representative that I was allowed to check in more than one bag and the customs official said I could not take my money out of the country without submitting both forms. You will have to remove your shoes and socks and put on blue plastic booties before going through security. The airport personnel were courteous and even friendly but it was clear that no exceptions would be made.

Taupo is a tiny regional airport servicing the central North Island of New Zealand. When I say tiny, I mean tiny, arrivals, departures, check in, security, lounge and facilities are all in one room. It's serviced by the regional arm of Air New Zealand and is a a great option for getting into the Heart of "Lords of the Rings" country. There's rarely any queuing, the staff are very friendly helpful and polite. Bags are delivered just a few minutes after stepping off the plane. Food and drink options are limited. There's a cafe, but it seems to closed more often than open.

I forgot my prescription glasses in the Duty Free in Tbilisi. Following a few emails to the Duty Free department, I received a positive response that they were found. Two ladies did everything in their power to have them returned to me. I can't fault these people, they showed care and sympathy to my problems. They are Natia and Inna. Thank you so much.

Rude treatment of elderly passengers. This is not our first time visiting Tbilisi. It was always great. This year I decided to meet my elderly parents in this city. We were flying from America, they were from Belarus. We had a great time and were inspired by the beauty of Georgia, its hospitable people, unique culture and great food. But all of this was crossed out at the airport. Both of my parents are over 80 years old and it shows. At the security screening they were never offered help or possibility to skip the line. Moreover, they were rudely searched and groped, and my father was taken to a separate office, where he was forced to take off the hernia belt, which he never takes off and cannot put back on on his own. We got to the airport more than two hours before the flight time. However, because my parents cannot walk quickly all of this screening took a lot of time. They were at the security line past the boarding time. Even after their names were announced on the PA system several times, they were not allowed to go through passport control without standing in line. As the result, they were forced to run as fast as they could to get on the plane. My parents are very kind people, they never complain about anyone and try to stay positive. But I see that for a couple of days now they have not been able to recover from this stress. I am shocked by this attitude of the airport security and border control staff.  I am very sorry that airport services demonstrate such treatment towards guests of their country.

The first interaction with the airport staff (immigration) on arrival was terrible. The lady was rude and unpleasant, treating me and my passport disrespectfully by throwing it and removing seals from the pages reserved for visas without any communication. When I asked her to kindly stamp on a used page with sufficient space for the Georgian stamp (as I had limited empty pages), she simply said "NO" without any elaboration. She then tried to talk to me in a language other than English (I assume Russian, but I am not sure) and expected me to understand. Her overall attitude was rude, and her tone of voice was unfriendly and irritated. I have traveled to more than 60 countries and have never been treated with such disrespect.

The staff at the airport is perhaps the rudest I’ve encountered in my life. They haven’t been properly trained on how to treat visitors. They yell and talk to people like they are dogs. The country was a wonderful place to visit full of good people, however the men checking your bags are hateful, condescending and outright disrespectful. I don’t mind it I can take it but to talk to my wife the way they did is unacceptable. Low quality, ignorant staff, it’s a horrible representation of such a beautiful country to deal with these people.

Staff are very rude. They checked me thoroughly and ask to open my bag and not to touch anything, i was just standing there and they are also checking the other passengers coming, after 15 mins i ask the security if i can go and get my bag she said “oh, yes you can, i forgot”.  She made me wait for nothing. They have an overpriced for their food inside the airport. I will share this experience to my colleagues and other friends.

The airport is clean, very functional and not too big to the point it becomes customer unfriendly. As expected most products available to buy are well overpriced. Passport control and security was a breeze.

Small airport with no arrival duty free shop. Passport control staff attitude towards me was unacceptable. Had a valid 2-year multiple entry Schengen visa in my passport, but they  asked me to show them the money I had with me, along with my return ticket and my hotel reservation.  While leaving the country, I noticed filthy toilets and very few options of restaurants.

Modern airport generally fine. On arrival the taxi situation is uncontrolled resulting in rip-off cabs (I ended up angrily being demanded 100 GEL on arrival in Tbilisi for a 20 GEL journey). They seem to try to block Bolt which doesn’t seem to work. On departure good luck finding a coffee for less than $6 in any café - seems to be run by a cartel.
Awful experience, staff are very unprofessional and rude. They behave in a very bad manner, not making you feel welcome at all. Immigration officers are very nasty and unfriendly.

Reading all the bad reviews I cannot help but agree on how rude and unprofessional the airport staff is. Check in staff eating pumpkin seeds, security staff with a massive ego, and immigration officers acting in a disrespectful manner. Even the food and beverage staff have no clue about service and hospitality. Being such a beautiful tourist destination, you would think service is a priority, but we found it very disappointing. Good food, great nature, and not the warmest people.

I'm a Honduran guy who lives in Tegucigalpa, home of Toncontin International Airport, I am a frequent flyer of AA so I have to use my hometown airport frequently (travel 1-2 times a year). I bet many have seen Toncontin Airport on many documentaries where they call it one of the most dangerous in the world. Maybe that's true, the runway is short but in terms of the airport itself, it has easy access and a large parking area, you don't have to walk that far to get to the airline stands due to the fact that it is a small airport. The flow of people is small, therefore you won't have to deal with long lines. There is a foodcourt on the second floor and a mall just a street away (yep, after check-in you are able to get out of the airport again because you have to go through the security check point until almost the boarding door). In the terminal there aren't many duty free stores, there are some kiosks where you can get some Honduran food. 1 VIP lounge is available but no one uses it. To finish, only 3 bridges are available that connect the airport to the airplane door, so in many cases especially on small flights, you will be requested to go through some stairs that will take you to the runway where you will have to walk to get to your planes.

Terrible management in this airport, all European flights are during the nights, the queues for luggage last at least 1h 30. Too few staff members in the middle of the night, exhausted travellers. Nobody to help, I have never seen such a bad management. Only the business lounge is great, for usual travellers there is no consideration.

If you're coming from a western country, be aware that this airport functions a bit differently than what we're used to. First, you and all your bags have to pass through security (bags in the scanner + you in a light body search), and then you enter the hall where the airlines check in counters are. You do not need to present a boarding pass to enter this first hall, meaning you can come in with a friend or family member who isn't flying. This hall has some chairs, toilets and 2 or 3 shops. After you check in and drop your bags with your airline, you proceed to immigration. At this point, you can only get through if you have a valid boarding pass. You get to a second hall with the duty free and a couple more shops and restaurants. Last, you move to the area where your gate is. There's different areas with different gates each with their own security line, if you go to the wrong gate area (like I did) you need to ask airport staff to escort you out so you can go to the correct area. This security check is the same as the first one, bags on the scanners and you get a light body search. Then you proceed to your gate's waiting area, where you have toilets and 2-3 shops. No one ever checks for liquids or electronic equipments and I even had my own bottle of water in my bag when I went through both security checks. Men and women have different security lines so that man are searched by a male officer and women searched by a female one. As for facilities, there were enough chairs for everyone but chairs were not the most comfortable. If you like shopping in airport this is also not the best place, not enough offer of shops and even the duty free doesn't have much to offer. The airport is generally clean and there are western toilets, plus free water. On arrivals, immigration lines are often under staffed so prepare for waiting 30mins +. If you're looking to exchange money at the airport, you need go back the stairs after you collect your luggage because the money exchange counter is on the departures floor.

The airport is outside the capital and it could be a 90 minute drive depending on the traffic. Aesthetically it's not the nicest facility and in some places it seems like a warehouse. The security is really good and the immigration formalities for Iranians are fine. I'm not entirely sure how immigration is for non Iranians but I heard that it's alright but they have their own line which could take them longer to clear immigration if the line is long. The customs formalities are alright, I never had any problems as a regular traveler there. The toilet facilities are not so clean but there is almost always an attendant there cleaning the place and offering to watch your bags in return for a small tip. The staff in general are pleasant enough. The duty free isn't the best in the world but the prices are reasonable. Good opportunity to buy some Iranian products as gifts for friends and family. The eating options are pretty good with two open air cafes after passport control with deserts and sandwiches and beverages at reasonable prices. There's a decent fastfood restaurant in the international departure area and the prices are alright there too. If you have a long transit, there is a mosque at the departure terminal where you can prey, relax and even take a nap. There's no public transportation to and from the airport so the only way to get there is by car. A taxi to Tehran for Iranians is about 30 USD. I heard the business class lounge is good as well as the VIP terminal. Wi-Fi is basically non existent for passengers. Enjoy your time in Iran!

Arrival was super speedy, world class speed by the immigration guy. Airport facilities (money changer) is up until the time we arrive in there (early 11pm ish local time). Kudos to the landside staff. However departure is a different story, travelers are mire with last minute opening of AAX counters where usually it opens three hours ahead of time however at IKA it opens 1.5 hours before departure time. For non Iranians, immigration queue is super long with one female officer working only, we had to queue for more than 30 minutes just to clear our passport. Before immigration the seats are not enough to contains all the travellers and after the immigration there isn't any trolleys to move the luggage of us. Good part about IKA, you will feel safe in the airport with thorough checks and the presence of officers in military fatigue, the security here is top notch. After immigration there are sleeping benches at the most behind of gates. Improvements to be done, add more chairs before the immigration, speed up the passport clearance and introduce trolleys after immigration.

Greatly improved airport, with better immigration facilities on arrival, fast track lane for business passengers on departure (entrance into departure hall, entrance to immigration), much faster retrieval of luggage and more smiling people. The departure zone after security has been revamped and is now more frendly too.

As I was travelling in Emirates Business class from Tehran, I was able to use the VIP terminal just around the corner of the main terminal. It was very clean, stylish and modern for Iranian standards. Emirates passengers got to use the whole second floor which provided a good buffet, nice leather seats, clean prayer room and very clean toilets. The customer service and security checks were also quite decent despite being busy during the day.

Long queing times Tehran Imam Khomeini airport, rude and unfriendly staff. Not worthy of such a friendly and hospital country. Waiting times have been extraordinary long. We had to pass 4 diffrent security and xray scans to board the plane. Unfriendly and stressed staff all over the airport!

Tehran IKA Airport looks like an isolated domestic terminal rather than international. Arrival immigration is small and if two or more flights arrive at the same time, it will be chaos. Baggage conveyor belts are limited to three which seems no maintenance has been performed for a long time. At the same place the toilets are dirty most of the time. The departure section is little better in comparison of Arrival. Wi-fi is free but could not be used at all. Passengers security checks are conducted two times! Departure section is a little bit organized. The airport website is just in Persian language! Finding a car park is so hard. At the time writing review, no public transportation except taxi are accessible. In comparison of other region airport like Dubai, Qatar and Istanbul airports, IKA is messy.

For a city of this size Tehran Imam Khomeini airport is quite small. Overall a modern airport but immigration procedure at arrival took a long time. Also a bit chaotic at baggage claim as the space on the belt is tight if a B747 arrives. At departure all went fine, but the food in the restaurants was awful.
