Even in duty free no alcohol was avaiaible and there are no smoking rooms after security check. No free wifi available.

I have traveled a few times there and had no problem but this time I missed my flight due to the malfunction of the airport. The flight information board doesn't work properly any more and they only announce your flight once so be careful. Pay your exit tax (?!) in a bank before you go to the airport. Don't rely on the bank there like me. The cashier was serving one of us form the queue and 10 passport from a travel agency without our knowledge so some people from the queue were missing their flight.  The police or security office weren't helpful and were nasty. It seems as if the Airport site doesn't let you to write a review since it's getting probably lots of bad ones. Hopefully they sort the airport out soon.

Tehran Merhabad is the old main airport of Tehran. Easy access from city center. Before security check there are plenty shops and restaurants, after security check the choice is lower. Long queue and chaotic scenes at check in, also at first security check before entering the airport. Second security check was taken a bit easy, they not even use hand held dedectors. No wifi available, smoking rooms after security check available. Waiting area after security looks like a bus station.

Very modern newly built structure with passport control relatively smooth (I expected tighter go-through experience). If you think of your immigration check at JFK going through passport check at IKA is a walk in the park. I had carryon luggage so I rushed through exit with one more X Ray control to go. Nothing major but of course avoid to bring in alcohol. Departure was early in the morning. Very congested security check before you check in: you have to squeeze all your luggage and metal stuff under the x ray and then your physical check is very slow. If you fly economy not much to do in the airport. Couple of good coffee shops with plenty of tables and seats few duty free shops. There is one nice handicraft shop tough. Careful about public announcements that are delayed. Flights were announced departing when I had seen them happily taking off 10-15 minutes earlier. Smoking area is below the main floor with very nice view of the apron. No internet available in the public space. Once you move to your departing gate there is another security control. The boarding area is okay with nice reclined seats overlooking the runway and one small coffee shop. Overall a nice airport with huge room for improvement given the beautiful building and the fair share of international traffic.

Departing on 8am flight to Kerman. All bags X-ray'd before you enter the terminal. There was one queue for my flight and only one person checking everyone in but she was fantastically efficient and once at the head of the queue the process must have taken only 30 seconds. Amazingly people behind me were thrusting their tickets at her whilst she was dealing with me. Airside departure lounge was full and despite a lot of seats very few free. There seemed to be about 6 flight leaving at the same time as mine. The lounge reminded me of a 1970's bus depot. Plenty of shops around to get souvenirs and snacks although I didn't use them. It is a small affair and all gates are in the one area. Toilets were grim with long queues. Go before you arrive! Flight information screens toggled between English and farsi but the English version stayed on screen about 5% of the time. It seemed I was the only European person there. Suddenly the screen above the departure door flashed up for my flight. Bus to the plane for an on time departure. On the return journey bus journey back to the terminal and baggage re- claim was very fast. I was out of the airport within 20 minutes of landing. Some taxi offices in the arrivals building. Overall Mehrabad is a place to catch a domestic flight no more no less. A long delay would be a nightmare here. The transfer to the international airport is about an hour through heavy Tehran traffic.

Although the computer information screens are in Farsi and English I would advise completely disregarding the English information. Flying from Terminal 2 to Esfahan on Iran Air the computer screens read "Delay without estimate" next to my flight. An hour after the scheduled departure time this suddenly switched to "boarding". When I enquired I was told I was too late to check in. By this point the info screens were showing "Await further information" on my - now departing - flight. Moral of the story? Ignore the screens and be at a check in desk - any check in desk - an hour before your flight is leaving and stay there until someone gives you a boarding card. Don't take no for an answer and don't ask the airport info desk - they're nice but clueless - speak with the airline. Airport itself is fine but frequently descends into chaos that only a minimal amount of planning or thought would avoid. You quite often see hordes of staff racing around and shouting trying to resolve a confused multi- flight boarding situation when it would have taken just one of them to head off the problem with clear directions half an hour earlier. Would strongly recommend arranging for your hotel to send a car to pick you up on arrival. It is not possible to figure out how the airport taxi system works without practice - and often its the last thing you need when you've just landed. Taxi touts (attempting to charge a 150% markup on the maxmimum rate) are common. Ensure a fare at the start and don't let him drive off until you're satisfied.

Mehrabad airport is an old and small airport that shows its age. The tarmac is worn out and inside terminal 2 is very dark and boring . Duty free shops are expensive and there's not a good eatery at the gates. Also I noticed security was taken easier than other airports given that I walked through the metal detector and it beeped but nobody apparently cared. I also noticed that their body search was very basic. On another occasion upon return I walked into the Homa class lounge without having proper authority and no one seemed to care. In the lounge although nice looking there was nothing special. All in all it's a tolerable airport but far from being a world class gateway. I am hoping to see the brand new airport opened in my next trip to Iran this summer.

Tehran Mehrabad Airport is what you expect. Very basic very 70's and just not that great. It's not modern shopping facilities are limited and eating and drinking is minimal also it's very crowded at certain times (especially around midnight). I always wondered why Iran didn't put some money in airport improvements. Because as we all know an airport is the first and last thing visitors to the country usually see. It turns out that they didn't improve the airport because they were quietly building a super modern airport (Imam Khomeini International Airport) that will be fully operational in 2004.

I had a fantastic experience at Ben Gurion airport. From the moment I arrived, everything was smooth and efficient. The check-in process was quick, security lines were well-organized, and the staff was friendly and professional. The terminal was clean, spacious, and well-maintained, with plenty of seating areas to relax before my flight. I was especially impressed with the variety of shops and dining options—there was something for everyone. Free Wi-Fi was fast and reliable, making it easy to get work done while waiting. Boarding was handled efficiently, and overall, the experience was stress-free and friendly. I highly recommend this airport for its excellent service and organization. Looking forward to flying through here again!

Traumatising experience in this airport last friday. Everything was ok when we arrived but it was a whole different story when we left Israel. The first security check before checking in our luggage is simply ridiculous. We got interviewed by a very young girl who was clearly having fun torturing us with the most stupid questions (who packed your bags, did you leave your bags unattended, what did you do with your bags since you finished packing) it was endless. She went to see what seemed to be her supervisor many times with our passports surely with the hope of delaying us more. But they seemed to tell her off and she finally let us go. She put a number on the back of our passport and after checking in our bags we got sent to the infamous (line 1) very strict bag searching security check. Rude staff there again,  who will shamelessly open all your bags and go through all your stuff. We arrived 7 hours prior to our flight and were at the gate 30 minutes before boarding. What a joke.

Disrespect to high level among the security staff. I was not treated like a human, but rather a criminal. All I had was a short layover, and still stood in an interrogation with 3 different woman who were wielding their powers over me. It took over an hour to answer questions and un pack and repack my bags. I had good experiences previously, but honestly, that whole situation makes me not excited to travel back again.

The security is so rude and disrespectful. I arrived at the airport at 18:05 for a 19:35 flight, due to getting stuck in traffic for many hours (because of a holiday in Israel which I did not know about). I was really stressed that I was going to miss my flight. First, security acted like they had never seen dual passports in their life before (I have German and South African), then the head security lady came to ask me the most useless and pointless questions, stressing me out more about missing my flight. She was clearly having an ego trip and told me she won't speak to me until I calm down, while I was calm the whole time, I just did not know the answers to the questions she wanted (such as the name of the uncle of my friend - I do not speak Arabic so I cannot remember his strange name?). Then she was on the phone for ages, wasting my time, and came to ask me more useless questions like with who I stayed with and the names of other family members, asking me why I drove with the uncle instead of my friend (and not believing me when I said because my friend was working). I finally got her to let me through after showing her Whatsapp messages with my travel agent who was reasurring me I would still make my flight. I felt personally violated and disrespected. Then at security they pulled me aside the the extra intense security check.  They ripped all of my personal belongings out with absolutely no care, my underwear everywhere, and my nice new handbags getting manhandled. I had packed everything so meticulously so that I could fit everything in and was left with my things strewn around and told to repack after about 30 minutes of them treating me like vermin. I had enjoyed Israel, but I will never be back due to the slowness and rudeness of the staff here.

I'm flying back with Air Canada via TLV Airport with my poor dog checked downstairs in a cargo. The Air Canada flight AC081 got 1 hr generously delayed. However, nobody bothered to notify us regarding the delay and I was forced to check in my dog in a cargo department as if now 3 hrs before the flight! This is absolutely unacceptable and inconsiderate from Air Canada crew as well as chaotic airport staff. While I'm on a plane, nobody seems to know when will we depart and the crew is extremely rude. Everyone making others at guilt, just so not to accept responsibility. Unfortunately, this is the cruel reality of super packed plane, delayed flight and very unpleasant and unprofessional team. Very disappointing

We were told we need to be at the airport 5 hours before our flight. We arrived from Jerusalem to Tel Aviv airport by train and took a 15 mins bus to terminal 1. The security check-in process at the departure door was surprisingly fast. And the bags checks were pretty fast too. They opened up a separate area for a faster bag check process. The whole process only took 45 mins and we have 4 hours now to kill at the airport. Note that this was a 10pm flight and we arrived at 6pm on Monday.

Just to counterbalance the other reviews. We had a 6.00am flight. We arrived at the airport at 2.45 and were completely through check-in and security by 3.30. We checked luggage. It would have been 20 minutes faster with just carry on.

First and foremost most of the staff firstly spoke only their language, if you are working in an international environment mostly an airport you are expected to speak to the passengers in the international language. And even after in speaking the the security staff that check the hand carry before the passport control they would respond in Hebrew as if that helps in providing information needed. The security was unreasonable, before even check-in to the counter there is a security that has a long line after that you have to spend time again on the check in counter but the worst part of is when you are entering the security check as they would look into your boarding pass and put you in a line where you have to wait based on the departure time of your flight. It’s unreasonable to be in a line that almost not move unless its 1.5 hrs before the boarding. The security staff are rude and not at all responsive to why there's a moving line and there's a line that is not moving at all. After that there is a random check that you have you bring out everything on your hand carry, remove shoes check every inch of what you have and worse part that they do is i have some chocolates coming from Tbilisi as i travel to Georgia before coming to Israel. The security officer poke all the chocolates that i have with a push pin which is very unhygienic as its from a cork board or where they pinch all this push pin in the area. I have traveled to almost every continent of the world but this airport would have been the worst airport staff I have every encountered.

Allow 5 hours to get through this airport. They tag anything that is not a standard wheel bag as oversized so every other passenger has to go through the over sizes luggage area. When I was there, the line was at least 50 people and there were 4 workers in the area. Three stood around talking while one worker worked through the line in the slowest possible manner I can imagine. I have been standing in the line for 30 minutes and there are still 10 people ahead of me. Check in was no different. There were only 4 people in front of me but it took 40 minutes to get me. I am anticipating security to be the same but since I have had so much time in this line, I figured I would write this review.

Tel Aviv should be renamed Tel Avoid! Staff are rude, not helpful. Try to avoid helping in any way. One occasion witnessed one person asking for help after they’ve checked through & was advised to go all the way back. Simply because the staff couldn’t understand English. Get some real workers in and be kind

Tenerife South Airport is the most stressful airport to arrive or depart from. The security queues are beyond ridiculous. Expect to stand for hours with no consideration for the elderly, children or those who would find it painful to stand for long periods of time. Either this country really doesn’t want tourism (which is one of its main forms of income, so would be a stupid idea ) or the airport itself is run by idiots. Note to anyone departing: The minute you know what area (A,B or C) you should be - head there immediately and join the queues (especially on a Friday). As someone that owns an apartment in Tenerife, I travel to this airport regularly but it has put my elderly parents off from coming and it upsets me that because of your lack of care, assistance and bad management they are missing out on enjoying some much needed winter sun. Come on “who ever is in charge” - sort out the problem at security!

I had an awful experience with the security staff. I was pulled aside after going through the scanner. I had already removed everything from my pockets, jewellery, watch etc and this had been scanned. I understand this is normal procedure and some people get asked extra questions. But I struggle to believe how this proceeded was normal. I was not told anything but instead had to wait to the side of the scanner and not able to proceed. Security staff would not talk or even look at me. 15 minutes passed and my friends who had progressed were waiting and concerned. One, who is a native Spanish speaker tried to approach but was ordered not to approach I thought a bit forcefully. After another few minutes a different security staff member tried to reassure me and said I was being selected for a random search and would be taken to a different location for a search. They tried to make a joke out of it but I was not happy and quite anxious. After a few more moments they pointed to three bags and said "these are yours?". These were not my bags. I was then told to go to a different carousel. The security staff at this counter was far ruder and barked orders at me. She advised my bags had been scanned and due to the scan they needed to be searched. They presented three bags, but these were also not my bags! They then asked me to go to my friends who were with my bags, bring them back and then they'd be searched. I complied and the whole bag was opened on the counters to be searched and swabbed. They said I would also need to remove my belt for it to be swabbed - but I wasn't even wearing a belt as I had already removed it for the scanner! After this they swabbed the waist of my trousers after processing the results allowed me to proceed. I was very agitated by this. I did nothing wrong but was treated like a criminal. I was told conflicting information including this being a personale / strip search, a random search, then it being a search because of my bag, was asked about 6 different bags that weren't mine (and I didn't see their owners being searched). I don't understand the logic. Nothing was explained to me. The whole process was very unpleasant

From going into departures the man at check in never spoke and did not ask any security questions, not sociable at all. Did not stop there, also in E Gates they were talking to people aggressively who were having difficulty using the new system. Not going on holiday for that.

It’s been years since I last visited Tenerife, and as a family that travels frequently, we’ve experienced airports both big and small. Tenerife South, however, ranks as the most grim and awful airport we’ve ever encountered. Every single staff member—from check-in and shop assistants to passport control and duty-free employees—was astonishingly rude and unhelpful. We attempted to reclaim tax on some expensive purchases made in Tenerife, but were sent back and forth across the airport by various Aena staff who had no idea where the customs office was located. We walked the entire length of that dreadful building three times before giving up, after encountering a particularly unpleasant woman at the Menzies desk, who barked and gestured wildly at us when we asked for help. Upon arrival (on Christmas Eve), it took three hours to clear passport control, causing us to miss our evening reservations. On the return journey, all flights were paused or cancelled due to a private jet losing a tyre on the runway. While unexpected issues happen, there was absolutely no communication regarding gate changes. The Aena app was uselessly out of date (thankfully the EasyJet app wasn’t), and the staff were as miserable and rude as ever. The experience was so stressful and unpleasant that I have no desire to return to Tenerife. There are plenty of other destinations that value and welcome tourists. The airport’s design—an endless, dreary corridor—only adds to the ordeal.

I’ve been through this airport many times but this was awful. We travelled at 4-30pm on 18/12/24. They took my wife’s passport to stamp and left it their side and she had to lean through to retrieve it and they sniggered and lugged between themselves. When we went through a young child was crying to use the bathroom and her mother went back to get her, an officer grabbed her and pushed her in the back even though she was protesting.

I usually travel to Tenerife South and North airports several times a month. The most important thing for me is the fastest way thru security and food services. On both airports usually time waited for security screening is less than 10 min (average time 3-5min), staff polite and very helpful. The food and services offered in Tenerife South is much better than the older airport in the north of the island. I have used both airports VIP lounge. They are nice, have lots of food and drink and usually are ok. Sometimes during peak season can be a bit crowded or even full.

The rudest security staff I have ever met, whilst going through the scanner, we were told to go back and separate laptops etc, which is fine, except the woman saying this to me got up to my face and said "English, look at me while I tell you". I said to her that I had heard her the first time she said it, I was amazed at her rudeness and arrogance, I get it that going through security is a bit stressful, but some of their staff make it a horrible experience. Its about the third time I have encountered rude security at Tenerife airport.

I found at least 2 female staff members extremely rude at Tenerife South Airport ... never experienced this at any other airport! I was treated like I had done something wrong. I am a 62 year old disabled women and was getting very anxious because of the chaos there. Because I didn't understand what was being said to me due to a hearing problem the female staff member became increasingly rude and separated me from my husband and carer also my Grandson, whom has needs too! She said I had to go through the on my own and I struggled. This was such a stressful and horrible experience for us, I don't want to go away again.

Went to information for some help. 5 women standing around talking. Didn’t even stop when I stood there waiting for someone to acknowledge me. Then when I asked the question the just pointed towards the cafe where I had already been and asked. So unhelpful and uninterested is an understatement. Actually I found that rude. Maybe they should try a bit harder to help someone instead of having a paid mothers meeting!

I live in London, Moldovian nationality with Resident to live in UK. The immigration officer was weary friendly. I went to Tenerife for 5 days for holiday with my daughter. When I was boarding the plane the lady didn’t want me to board. She was very rude and unprofessional . She was asking me why I’m flying to England without a visa. Then I start to explain to her and show my passport and all documents. She was saying that my visa is false. It was not her job to check all these. It was very stressful for me and my daughter. Then immigration officer came to her and told her that she was wrong.  She was very rude and said many bad words in Spanish to me. Not happy with the situation.

The airport is rather old, but not badly maintained. It is clean. Signs are clear, given that the configuartion is very unusual: being in a slope, it is three floors high, the gates being in the middle floor. There could me more variety when it comes to shops. Security was just surprinsingly slow: manned by police, trays handed to people one by one, making it all very slow. Not practical at all.

A small airport used mainly to service tourists going to Ngapoli beach. Immigration on entry is unusually time consuming with officials taking a long time to inspect each passport. Baggage is taken outside airport where it is collected by either passengers or more usually by staff from the hotels booked by passengers. Works well. Departure is chaotic. Check-in manually with printed passenger list. Effective but slow. There is no scanner at the airport and all luggage checked by hand. Some are checked in minute detail while others igored. The departure area small but adequate for the size of airport. Spectacular location on ocean edge.

Over the years I have traveled to and from Thessaloniki countless times. However, tired of the absolutely INSANE prices that you have to pay for the smallest thing as soon as you go through security. Having to pay close to €6 for a bottle of water is not justifiable. As you are not allowed to bring water into the departure hall, you are at the mercy of the sales points that are there. Thinking that a family of four should pay €24 for each bottle of water?! Sharpening! I think the prices at this airport are unreasonable at all, but the price they charge for water should be banned | Genom åren har jag rest till och från Thessaloniki otaliga gånger. Har dock tröttnat på de absolut HUTLÖSA priserna som du får betala för minsta lilla så fort du är igenom security. Att behöva betala närmare 6€ för en flaska vatten är inte försvarbart. Då man inte får ta med sig vatten in till avgångshallen är man utlämnad till de försäljningsställen som finns där. Tänker att en familj på fyra personer ska betala 24€ för varsin flaska vatten??!! Skärpning! Jag tycker att det överhuvudtaget är oskäliga priser på denna flygplats, men priset de tar för vatten borde vara förbjudet

I chose Thessaloniki as my holiday destination because I heard a lot of good things about it. In fact, I really had a great experience in the city, as well as where I was staying. Obviously, wherever I shopped or visited before, the people were fine and decent, but the moment I arrived at the airport this evening, everything changed. Unfortunately, the airport has very poorly trained staff, who are not willing to explain to the passengers what is the matter with the check-in. I, for example, had a very bad experience!!! I would ask in advance that the ladies in charge of this area inform themselves well and, in turn, be patient with all the passengers! I think they may have been taken of this job, because through it they have contact with such and such people, but we are not obliged to put up with their faces either!!! I also work with people and I know it's hard, but despite all that, I try to be patient with everyone because that's what I'm paid for! And it's not ok to write one on the receipt and charge you another higher amount. The rest of the pennies where do they go??? I'm asking for a friend. It's a shame that there is no emphasis on hospitality, responsibility and fairness!!! Honestly, I'm left with a bitter taste!!! So, dear Thessaloniki airports, soon we won't see each other again. Am ales ca destinație de vacanță Thessaloniki pentru că am auzit multe lucruri faine despre el.De altfel chiar am avut o experiență super făină în oraș, cât și unde am fost cazată.Evident că și unde am mai făcut cumpărături sau vizitat ceva oamenii au fost faini și cumsecade, însă în momentul în care am ajuns în aeroport în această seară totul s -a schimbat.Din păcate aeroportul dispune de personal foarte prost pregătit,care nu-i dispus să le explice pasagerilor care e treaba cu chek-inul. Eu spre exemplu am avut parte de o experiență ft proastă!!!Aș ruga în prealabil ca doamnele care se ocupă de aria aceasta să se informeze bine și la rândul lor să aibă răbdare cu toți pasagerii!!!Le cred că poate li s a luat de acest job , deoarece prin intermediul lui au contact cu fel și fel de oameni,dar nici noi nu suntem obligați să le suportăm figurile. !Și eu lucrez cu oamenii și știu că e greu ,dar cu toate astea încerc să am răbdare cu toată lumea că pentru asta sunt plătită!Și nu-i ok să scrie una pe chitanță și să-ți încaseze altă sumă mai mare !!!Restul bănuților unde se duc??? Întreb pentru o prietenă Păcat că nu se pune accent pe ospitalitate,responsabilitate și corectitudine. Sincer vă spun am rămas cu un gust amar!!! Deci , dragă aeroportule din Thessaloniki prea curând nu ne mai revedem.

I recently arrived at Thessaloniki Airport with my 15-month-old child in a carrier, expecting a smooth transition after a long journey. Unfortunately, my experience was far from satisfactory. Upon arrival, I had to collect my luggage, which included a travel case with two bicycles, a stroller, and regular luggage. Managing all of this alone was already challenging, but it became nearly impossible when I tried to get a trolley. To my dismay, I discovered that trolleys could only be accessed with a coin, which I didn't have. There were no machines to obtain coins, nor were there any employees willing to assist or lend a coin. Despite my obvious struggle and the presence of a small child, no staff members stepped in to help. The lack of basic assistance and the unavailability of a simple solution to access a trolley made the situation extremely stressful and frustrating. This level of service is unacceptable, especially for an international airport that should be equipped to handle the needs of travelers, including those with young children and large luggage. I hope the management takes steps to address these issues and improve the overall experience for future passengers.
No announcements for the flights, a few sockets for charging mobile, bad behavior, new building but a lot of things are out of order.

A moderately sized airport some 15km away from the city center. It's clean and modern and during the off-season security check was very fast and efficient. Duty-free shopping is in abundance and has some good offers. Staff is very friendly, far nicer than what you experience at other airports. All arrivals and departures are busboarding only as there are no jetbridges. Connection to the city is by taxi or bus 01X which cost only 1,80 euro.
Good airport, no delays - it was fairly quiet when I travelled. Security and passport checks all done efficiently. Staff were polite and helpful.

The Fast Track for Business Guests is used by employees of the airport who think they have the right to move forward without asking. I have been flying out of SKG many times this year and this seems to be routine practice to have the paying customers wait in line since the employees consider themselves as being entitled to have priority. Fraport should definitely change this practice!

Despite enjoying a very relaxing holiday in Greece, the experience was ruined by rude immigration staff at Departures. As I walked through the metal detectors, the alarm did not go off. I think this upset one of the immigration officers so she then rudely said random selection. The man politely swabbed my hands but did not like the fact that I was collecting my belongings. This is because I knew that the result would be negative. The woman was very unpleasant. In the departure area the airport is very clean and the shops are kept tidy. There was enough seating in the gate area.

Airport is clean, has good shops, great seating area and has clear signs. However, the thing that annoyed me the most was the fact that in the entire terminal you could literally (i counted) just find a total of five power outlets -that should really be something to be improved, so watch out for that.

The airport is much better than before after the construction of the new terminal and the renovation of the old one. Much cleaner, more shops, better signage etc. However the passenger experience is affected by the lack of jet bridges and the use of buses for going to and from the aircraft. The buses are hot in the summer and cold in winter and they are probably unsafe during the pandemic. If jet bridges cannot be added, then passengers should be allowed to walk to and from the aircraft with buses used only during poor weather. The external spaces also need some greening up and better maintenance.

I feel compelled to write this review because the bathrooms at this airport when I flew out this morning 19th Sept 2018 about 6-7am are easily the worst I have seen in my entire flying experience of ten years. The ladies bathroom close to gates 102 was not only stinky, every single stall was clogged and unflushed. It is disgraceful for an international airport to maintain such pathetic standards. I have seen the railway stations at Tianjin better maintained. There were zero staff taking care of maintaining the restrooms. This being an international airport, I was so horrified to see this level of callous treatment of passengers. When they announced my flight would be delayed. I really prayed that it wouldn't be too long. The airport guys ought to be ashamed!

I was twice in Tianjin Airport. First time it was domestic flight, the second time it was an international one. I was positively surprised about the airport and its open and bright architecture. No signs are missing, very straightforward, as well as very good shopping and food opportunities. I flew the second time with Air China and I would have appreciated it, if the airline provided permanent open check-in desks but they didn't. So if you are too early as I was that time you have to wait until the desks are open to drop your Bagage. All in all a quite good experience.

All flights are delayed from Tianjin airport. No information about departure time. Lounges are uncomfortable. Check-in for International bad design and only open 2 hours before a flight. Would recommend to go to Beijing although as most Chinese airlines/airports they will have delays but at least you have something to look at there.

The most terrible airport I have ever had the displeasure of visiting. Stuck here for 5 hours when flight was delayed a fate I wouldn't wish upon my worst enemy. The entire terminal was ridiculously hot no AC in the summer! The excess of people plus the sunlight streaming in from the glass walls made it unbearably hot. Bathrooms were okay in terms of cleanliness but because there are so few stalls expect to wait in line. The one restaurant served terrible overpriced food. Noodles there were foisted from an instant noodle packet. Just awful. The stores have no variety. You want in-flight snacks? Too bad the only thing they have curiously is chocolate. I ate so much chocolate I was sick. The VIP/first class lounges are a joke. They're temporary spaces with temporary walls enclosing the size of a closet. You can see the whole room just passing by. The lounges probably were a closet in a past life that were hastily assembled to be a "lounge" at the last minute with little standards of or consideration in quality. They just stuck a few couches in a closet. Worst of all there are no working outlets in the terminal so good luck if you want to charge your laptop tablet or phone. There is a stand with adapters for charging phones but it's only compatible with weird Asian phones. The few outlets on the wall don't work. Overall it was a horrible experience. Again the entire place was hot enough to kill you.

The International Terminal seems and feels like a temporary after thought. There is a major expansion of another terminal building next door so maybe proper facilities may exist later. As it is the check in area is separated totally from the rest of the airport requiring everyone to show ID to walk through a door to go through a customs area before actually checking in for the back end of the row of counter. Then you retrace your steps to access the immigration area before the typically cramped security screening which only had two of the four points on duty leading to a long wait in line. Once through the main terminal area is obviously a temporary scenario by the way the duty free shop acts to block access to the other gates. However the toilets were clean and respectable the food and beverage were not too bad and the shops were okay to browse through.

The new terminal is a big step up compared to the old one but still it does not give the passengers a warm feeling. It's big and but feels small crowed and untidy comparing to Incheon Int'l airport. Most of the facilities are not well designed. Signs are confusing and some do not make sense. Most staff are unfriendly. International departure area is not an open design: passenger need to go through a door to check in at the counter and if you want to come out you have to go through the same door again totally unnecessary. Seems that the Chinese has long way to catch up with the world standards.

Arrival from and departure to Shanghai. I hadn't been to Tianjin for 15 years it's now one of those standard new Asian airports : all sweeping steel and glass and marble. It's easy to navigate and check-in and security are quick and efficient. There's cheap Internet access airside (landside too but it was down) and reasonable food options on both airside and landside. There's lots of room and seating and airport as a whole and the toilets are clean. A metered taxi to or from the city is around RMB 60. My only criticism would be the flight announcements: they have one of those computers that says "Fliight xxx from xxx to xxx is now checking in at gate xxx". I don't know why these computers have the "From xxx" bit in China: you're in Tianjin (or wherever) so it's pretty obvious where the flight is from. The computer couldn't pronounce Tianjin which made this even more irritating: you'd have thought they could find a computer that could pronounce the name of their own airport. But otherwise it was lovely.

The airport is mostly new after months of renovation and expansion. As usual now both domestic and intl passengers undergo passport control and customs either departing or arriving. Make sure when departing to get your tourist permit and your passport stamped. Immigration personnel were friendly but the lady at Customs wasn't. I usually get immigration cleared at the land border point when coming from San Diego but the office at the border closes at night TIJ Immigration is 24/7 so no worries for late night/early morning flight. Check-in is a bit messy - though not slow - with Volaris the largest tenant but otherwise smooth with other carriers. If you fly Aeromexico well let's say I've enjoyed better lounges than theirs at terminal A. Better spend time at the terminal's Starbucks. Food is the airport biggest failure (small gates too perhaps) I believe with nothing other than the aforementioned cafe and some overpriced bad tasting and cramped "restaurants". Terminal B isn't any better at food; its upside is a great local wine shop. Free wifi available everywhere.

I arrived on a national flight from Guadalajara. The gates of the Tijuana Airport are quite modern with jetways at each gate. There are restaurants and shops along the concourse. It was necessary to have my passport checked by an immigration officer who saw it was a US passport and waved me through without looking at it. The customs inspection was minimal. The baggage claim area is OK. When I checked in for my departing flight I found passengers were required to go through screening and customs inspection to enter the check-in area. It is possible to exit and go outside while awaiting boarding time after you check in. The street entrance to the airport is under construction and it is necessary to walk past the boarded-off areas to enter the terminal. There is a bus station at the airport right by the terminal for shuttle buses to CA. Overall this airport is not bad and will be very good once construction is completed.

Having used Tijuana many times in the past I was surprised while using it recently after a 5 year break. The renovations are still under way but it is a clean modern and efficient airport that works well. The queues are generally quick and the staff know what they're doing. With some great connections to mainland Mexico and a couple of new discount airlines using the airport it is a great alternative to SAN. Only annoying bit is the lack of any decent food and beverage once you're through security. Over priced and average. The upside is you can check in for most flights in Mexico up to 45 minutes before take off so basically you can just walk through security and to the gate.

Very Crowded check in and long security lines. However once past security it was a very clean and nice airport. Not enough seats in the gate area however. Just know where you are going and leave plenty of time before your flight.

Timimoun airport is a small terminal serving a very small number of flights daily, but this does not explain the lack of any facilities for passengers apart from dirty toilets. You can not buy anything here - no food, no drink, not even a bottle of water. Stock up on food and water as the Air Algerie flight will likely be delayed for a couple of hours or cancelled altogether. No shop. No kiosk. No cafeteria - nothing. The town is 15 minutes away. Hard metal seats will add to the long waiting hours.

Very very weak services with luggage on arrival. 2 airplanes worth of people waiting for one rail of luggage under the pretext that it is under construction (even though one already arrives at the supposed new terminal). All in all a very poor service for a new and modern airport.

A small airport divided into 3 mini terminals: domestic, international arrival and international departure. Border control was fast and efficient, despite the large amount of passengers. The terminals itself are clean and well maintained but rather 90s looking. Access to the aircraft is by bus boarding only. There are many taxi's to the center but negotiate well. A few busses are available too but look like from a museum.

Poorest airport from all the airports in the country. I saw airports outside EU from really poor country’s that they are way over them. Unprofessional and rude staff from check in till you enter in the plane. Dirty and unorganised. For the food and beverage they see themselves at least Paris or another great airport among EU elite. Nightmare airport to be avoided.

Good, small airport. The staff is not friendly at all. First, nobody smile in that airport and when i pass the gate they dont greeting, (at the search point and passport point). One guy he just pointing me by hand what to do and chewing gum in your face.

One of the poorest services you will ever receive at an airport! From the security guy at the parking are, to the security staff and the shop assistants at the shop on the ground floor, they all yell at you and treat you with disrespect and arrogance. Unacceptable.

Small airport, short ways to the gates, but very unfriendly staff. Today I was yelled at because there was some metal applied to my shirt. After checking everything several times I had to go to a cabin and undress myself. The staff member was arrogant and did not speak in a way that I would call appropiate. As I regulary fly from this airport I have often at times had similar problems. On the other side everything can easily be found at the airport and cheap food can be purchased.

A pleasant but very small airport. I took the number 4 bus from the town, out to the airport. Bus tickets should be bought from a kiosk - these are usually located near tram stops. It was a short 30 minute ride to the airport. It's a bit of a comically small airport, with a handful of check in desks. With hand luggage only, I went straight to security (2 lines available). The security guard told me (incorrectly) by liquids bag was oversized so I had to dispose of some items. Not a problem given it was the end of my trip but a little annoying given there was not a legitimate issue. Security was quick nonetheless There aren't many facilities in the airport. A couple of small shops are there, not extortionately priced. There is no drinkable tap water to fill bottles. There are not many toilets. Seating could be tight if there were multiple flights. Communication for boarding was clear and we departed as scheduled.

It is a small airport operating both line and low cost flights. The security check and the boarding went very fast, the waiting areas are ok. The quality of the sound system is low, it is difficult sometimes to understand the announcements, especially those in English.

Primitive airport. I was told to go to the airline’s office so they can verify airport check in was included in my booking even though I was showing staff proof I had a priority booking which included this service. Staff is rude and unhelpful. The airport is crowded, clearly operating beyond capacity. Absolute nightmare! Impossible to avoid since it’s the only airport in the country so practically a monopoly.
Phenomenal airport, the best I ever experienced in Europe or anywhere else. Just the material definition of how an airport should be. Well done Albania.

The staff at security are super rude. No manners, no ethics. I was wearing heels, which obviously I had to remove for the control process, so I asked for plastic bags. They started laughing as if it was a shame to ask for them, and replied to one another: Signorina want plastic bags hahaha and then replied to me: Guess what we don't have and you have to walk barefoot like it or not or you can go back home. The tone was unacceptable and as I saw they harassed with their manners and lack of ethics all the women in security check. Someone has to do them some training, we do need to deal with their frustration.

I had extremely bad experience in this airport. The staff is very rude and unfriendly, the passports check are very, very arrogant, can you say good morning that don’t reply to you you say thank you they don’t reply to you and they have a really nasty attitude! Going through security check they kept my keychain no explanation no so I ever I don’t know what keychain could be a threat at the airport or the airplane for the matter of fact, I’ve been all over the Europe with that keychain hanging in my backpack never had a problem, not even a question, here no, that was a big problem you can’t have it.

A small airport serving the capital. It's a bit of a chaotic place, long queues, staff aren't the friendliest and generally messy. The terminal itself is clean tho and seating is comfortable. As it's the only major airport in the country, this it what they can offer. Taxi trip to the center is 1200 lek.

This airport is one of the worst airports I have ever had to travel to. As far as airports go, its infrastructure is mediocre at best. However, what really makes this pathetic excuse of an airport stand out are the police and airport staff. They are unbelievably rude and arrogant! I have travelled to the US before which is infamous for having strict airport staff and security who take their attitude too far - however Tirana airport takes the crown here! Once we landed and were shepherded to the terminal, I was accosted by what looked like a teenager in civilian clothing who started finger calling me and frantically pointing over to the queues. When I asked him what he wants me to do, he simply replied (shouted) 'just go' and waved me over to Customs! Upon making my way over to border control, I greeted the Customs officer 'Good Evening' - no response. Grabbed my passport, scanned it, once done, he simply slammed it down on the desk in front of me and simply stared back at me. At this point, I did not know what to do. I politely asked him, 'Is there anything else I can help with', to which he simply responded with a very stern 'No - go'. After I retrieved my baggage (which took a very long time to arrive, giving that we were the only late night flight arriving), I noticed people being ushered towards a scanner by people in civilian clothing with a 'Police' badge dangling from their necks. Once approached by the alleged 'police officer' he asks for my passport again (again no polite communication, just very stern shouting and ordering), and proceeds to ask me me personal and intrusive questions about how much money I have, where I work, as well as very random and trivial questions about where my birth place is located, which I found to be very inappropriate and infuriating giving that such questions are meaningless and mean nothing in the picture of airport security. Once he was done, he simply flicked the passport back to me with no 'Thank You' or 'Have a good evening'. Overall, if you would like to know what its like to be a free, law abiding citizen, but treated like a criminal, this airport will provide that experience for you! And the worst thing about it is, you cannot even complain to anyone, nor is there any sort of medium to submit complaints. Vile place and awfully rude people!
Clean, easy to navigate, reasonably priced for an international airport. weak wifi signal. Security staff not very polite. The airport was easy to access.

Visited Tirana on 12/12/18 and departed on 12/17/2018. Both the arrival and departure experiences were smooth. There was a slight delay at passport control on arrival as the scanner was not working at the booth where we presented our passports. This is a neat and bright medium sized airport. There is a lot of seating at the departure gates. There is a nice Business Lounge that we accessed through our Priority Pass card. The staff are friendly and professional. Check in was effortless. There is no online check in for TIA, so one has to check in at the counter. Wi-Fi is available however it appeared to be spotty. We did not have to wait very long for our luggage to arrive in baggage claim. There are no jet bridges at TIA. All passengers are bussed to and from the terminal to the aircraft.

I was disappointed. I knew that Albania is a not so developed country, but I expected that at least the airport would come up to European standards. I failed. Checkin and passport control were okay. Security very eagerly took the small bottle opener which was easily allowed at other airports. There are a few shops outside, so it is worth buying things and drinking there before security check, because inside there are only very limited facilities, and they do not accept credit/bank cards. All prices are displayed only in Euros, which is strange in a country where Lek is the official currency. Wi-fi was okay, I cannot complain about that. Travellers have no other option than this airport, so let's hope Albania will step on the road to modernity soon. If more tourists come, a better equipped airport will be necessary.

Arrival was great with no queues and security quick and easy. Luggage arrived on carrousel very quickly. Departure less good with long queues at security and long waits. Fortunately plenty of seats in departure lounge. Not much to do in lounge and poor range of food outlets. WiFi free but non-existent and unable to connect.

The airport has got very poor quality of housekeeping service. Our flight was at 10:30 pm and we arrived airport around 8 pm. To our surprise there were lots of mosquitoes at seating place. After complaining to airport authorities they have given us number to call housekeeping incharge. He arrived there after more than half an hour. And he blindly said us that either we have to seat in front of AC flow or bear the mosquitoes as he cant do fogging. He just given us this excuse and walked out from there. I have observed few foreign traveller also there.

Tiruchirappalli Airport is a rather small airport, not modern and sophisticated. Main lobby is poorly lit. Bathrooms are smelly and stained. Refreshment stalls are fair. Certainly needs more improvements.

The worst of the worst. Plenty flights delayed. No communication from any staff. Totally overpriced coffee shop. Long lines going nowhere. An excuse for an airport. The first and last time I will visit this excuse of an airport.

It’s fine to arrive at this airport, but departing from it is horrendous! We arrived 3 hours early for our flight and only just made the flight due to horrible crowds, no staff or organisation, absolutely no visible system in place. The airport had far too many flights than it can actually cope with so it’s a dreadful experience. Try to avoid by flying from a different airport.

This is a seriously bad airport, honestly the worst I have ever visited. It is far too small for the number of flights it serves, with poor facilities. All staff I dealt with were fine, it's the physical building and facilities that are lacking. The loo is dirty and smelly, the café too small and had run out of a lot of drinks and foods on the menu. The space for queuing for security and passport control is hot, cramped and crowded, as is the airside space. I loved Tivat town, but please sort out the airport!

My recent visit to Tivat Airport left me utterly disappointed and frustrated, to say the least. From the moment I arrived until the moment I finally boarded my flight, the experience was nothing short of a chaotic nightmare. Understaffed and Overcrowded Upon entering the airport, it became immediately apparent that the facility was severely understaffed. There was only one person checking flight tickets, leading to an outrageously long queue that snaked through the terminal. To exacerbate matters, there was also just one queue for both hand luggage and personal control, causing massive congestion and delays. No Relief from Crowds and Heat The airport quickly filled with travelers waiting in line, and the atmosphere became stifling. There was a complete lack of adequate air conditioning or ventilation, making it unbearable to stand in the packed queues. The lack of seating aggravated the situation, leaving elderly passengers and families with young children particularly vulnerable and uncomfortable. Unprofessional and Unhelpful Staff Adding insult to injury, the airport staff were shockingly unprofessional and downright rude. They displayed a complete lack of courtesy and seemed indifferent to the plight of passengers struggling with the chaotic conditions. Requests for assistance were met with dismissive gestures or simply ignored, further deepening the sense of frustration among travelers. Overall Impression In summary, my experience at Tivat Airport was one of the worst I have encountered in my travels. The combination of understaffing, overcrowding, lack of basic amenities, and unprofessional staff created an environment that was not only unpleasant but also distressing. For an international airport, these conditions are simply unacceptable and reflect poorly on the management and operational standards. If you have the option to avoid Tivat Airport or choose an alternative route, I strongly recommend doing so.

Tivat Airport is a nightmare. Small, hardly any staff, overcrowded, hot and no wifi. It took nearly 2 hours of solid queuing with only 1 check in desk, 1 person checking passports. Unable to move due to the entire airport full of passengers. Avoid if possible.

I would like to thank two ladies at the Check In who were simply awesome. With hundreds of people around them - they saw I was very late (due to traffic, my fault completely). They conducted my registration and took me through lines I was late was my flight to Brussels Thank you very much Tivat Airport.

What a dump. Queues going in all directions. From outside you have to get through the queue to security to access the gates. Your own boarding pass is not acceptable they throw it back at you and give you one of theirs. People queued 10 wide to get through security manned by 1 person. The gate number on the boarding pass is not the one used. The airport departure lounge was pouring with rain inside. No information and nowhere to get out of the way.

Tivat Airport is the busier of the two international airports in Montenegro. It serves the coastal area of the country. The airport seems to have two terminals of which I only saw one. The airport caters mostly for charter flights from European countries as well as Russia and Israel. On arrival, all passengers can make their way to the terminal. In Tivat, no buses are used. The baggage claim went pretty quickly, but they do not adhere to the priority labeling on the baggage. Within 5 minutes after leaving the aeroplane, I was outside. A week later, I checked in early for my Lufthansa flight to Munich, so there was no crowd at the check-in counter and at the security and passport control either. At check-in, I was misinformed about the possibility of using the airport lounge. It proved that Lufthansa – as one of the few airlines serving Tivat Aiport – has no contract with the lounge. The things you can do in the waiting area are very limited. There is one large duty-free shop in the departure hall but no café or snack bar where people can buy some food or refreshments, which is a real shame. However, I later noticed that some fellow passengers had gone through security control with their drinks, which means Montenegro’s authorities do not stop you from taking drinks from outside on board. Good to know for the next time! Boarding went swiftly and again all passengers were asked to walk the short way to the aeroplane.

I could not believe this was the first time I had arrived and departed from Tokyo Haneda Airport. When I first arrived, immigration was straightforward, and I was very impressed. When I was leaving, check-in was also pretty straightforward, and the whole Terminal 3 was massive, with great lounges, shops, and food. Plus, I got to do plenty of plane spotting from lounges.

ANA is using Terminal 2 for some international flights. The inside is new, ANA lounge is spacious. But if you do not have access to lounge the F&B is very limited. Shopping almost inexistant. This terminal is really small and most flight has to be boarded by bus. Really not acceptable for an international airport. Terminal 3 is far better

We were travelling with a baby. Immigration was efficient although the agents were quite slow in processing us. Everyone was quite helpful in ushering us to the priority or special assistance lines. Customs was difficult due to the difficulty of the machines reading our passports. Getting it to scan and verify your QR code is hit or miss. On departure, everything was quick and everyone was helpful again. The only issue is that it seems to be way too hot everywhere. Even the nursing rooms are like saunas. I am giving it a 6 because of how uncomfortably hot it is.

Haneda is a nice airport but immigration is hell, long lines, clearly show the Japanese slowness to adapt to any increase of the #of arrival If you fly in while low traffic. It is one of the best airport but not today as I will be losing 40 minutes to pass immigration.

Clean but queues are atrocious. Particularly immigration. 5 border agents for 1000+ people. Unfathomable that Japan thinks this is acceptable. They have 2x the number of desks for foreigners than residents, but literally 10x the wait times. It send the message that “we don’t want foreigners here”. Honestly would consider not going to Japan again because this 2+ hour wait has happened multiple times.

Toyko's 2nd airport, smaller and closer to the city. Arrival process OK but suffered from being rather manual with queues for immigration and then passport control despite offering "on-line" advanced registration. Baggage reclaim quite quick. Excellent transport links by bus, train or taxi, clear signs in Japanese and English. Ticket Machines for trains ONLY take cash but do give change and are fantastic value for money. Leaving Japan the process is very speedy with Bag Drop etc and then Security and automated passport gates. There is a cafe on the Arrivals Level if you arrive too early to check-in or are waiting to be picked up on arrival. Within the terminal is the usual array of shops and eating places focused more on the regional/local travellers rather than the full Duty Free range of goods you might find elsewhere in the region. Reasonable seating near the departure gates and overall quite quick turnround of planes.

Passengers entering Japan are encouraged to complete an online Visit Japan questionnaire with all personal data apparently to facilitate and speed up arrival at Haneda. It is a complete and utter waste of time, and the Japanese Immigration system has travelled back to a period that is beyond silly. All "Foreigners" (announced at a high volume) have to attach themselves to a snaking line that makes no sense. Any benefits afforded to Business Class travel are not provided at this airport: "you are a foreigner". My travelling companion, who is Japanese, sailed through to baggage collection within minutes, whereas I, a "foreigner", traipsed through 45 minutes of nonsense before reaching an immigration officer, having diligently completed the "Visit Japan" online site and obtained my QR code. A complete and utter waste of time, and utterly pointless. Please someone, at Visit Japan and or Immigration, review what this is about. Please someone at Visit Japan and or Immigration, go and have a look onsite and see what utter nonsense you have created. Please someone at Visit Japan or Immigration provide a benefit to those of us who have paid Business Class fares and receive no Fast Track facility, which is the norm in airports across the world. Truly frustrating and disappointing.

Departing from Terminal 2 for a domestic flight. The airport was well connected with the public bus and train. The terminal, in general, was clean, modern and efficient. Check in was fast, and completely automatic via machines, with ground staff was ready to help. Surprising no long queue at the security and everything was smooth. There were numerous comfy seats available for passengers. Shopping and dining were also really good, and at reasonable price.

Terminal 3 International. The arrivals hall was a long walk from the gate to customs and immigration – but aided by moving walkways and wide corridors. Baggage collection was very rapid, and despite the enormous volume of passengers, clearance through immigration was super-efficient with lots of staff ushering passengers to the right lanes. Departure was a similar experience, with long queues being very effectively managed by extremely helpful staff. The free wi-fi is fast and effective throughout the airport. Most of the food and beverage options “land-side” are for Japanese or Asian food – all of which are a bit pricey. There is also a very good outdoor viewing deck (a rarity these days!) Airside, there are lots of shops and food outlets – much more than the land-side offerings. Importantly, the terminal offers a large, open space with heaps of charging stations and comfortable seating. PA announcements are clear and in multiple languages. One word of caution: walking from the central area to the boarding gates can take as much as 15 minutes, so factor this into your timing.

I want to make a sincere gratefulness to your information service staff. I recently lost my passport on 23:55 4 Feb 2024 and boarding pass before the security check. Since it was late at night and the information kiosk on departure lobby was closed, I called the hotline (2132), a kind lady staff (name as Kuje?) who checked for me again and again if any lost report. She also suggest me to contach to related staff. THE PASSPORT WAS FINALLY FOUND. Thank you (Kuje San). いつもありがとうございます! I hope this message could be read by you. Cheers from Hong Kong!

My mother and I experienced Tokyo Narita International Airport. Good service, the staff smiled when my mother and I went in to buy things. When I transited at Tokyo Narita International Airport. To return to Lax International Airport to continue studying I did not know where to go. There were two guides, very polite, the first staff held a map. The second staff asked me if I needed a car to gate 57B. At that time, I was at gate 27 because flight NH 834 Ana Airlines departed from Ho Chi Minh City to Tokyo Narita International Airport. I will come back many more times because the staff is very good.

Easy to access by train. Plenty of shops and eateries, even convenience store! Lots of toy machines. Clean and enjoyable to wait for our departure. Signs are clear. You can enjoy lunch while watching the airplanes take off. We’ve got our last minute omiyage shopping like handkerchiefs, japan only cute snacks and satisfying lunch.

The Narita Express train from Tokyo is an excellent means of getting to the airport and comes straight in to the terminal. Narita airport was rather quiet when we travelled though it so maybe we were lucky as there were no queues at all in security nor immigration. Plenty of shops for last minute gifts. The terminal is light and airy and everything well signposted. More than happy with our experience.

As a first-class passenger traveling from Tokyo's Narita Airport to New York, I must commend the airport for its exceptional services and facilities. Narita Airport truly impressed me with its cleanliness and efficiency. One notable aspect was the cleanliness of the airport premises. The terminals and waiting areas were spotless, creating a welcoming atmosphere for passengers. This made my travel experience more comfortable and enjoyable. Moreover, Narita Airport offers a wide array of shops and boutiques. As a first-class passenger, I appreciated the convenience of having access to high-end retail stores, duty-free shops, and a variety of restaurants and cafes. This allowed me to shop for last-minute gifts and indulge in delicious cuisine before my flight. One feature that stood out to me was the availability of card payment options at vending machines throughout the airport. Being able to purchase drinks and snacks with ease using my credit card was incredibly convenient and time-saving. Another commendable aspect was the priority boarding privilege extended to first-class passengers. The expedited security and boarding process ensured a seamless and stress-free journey, allowing me to relax and settle into my premium cabin with ease. In summary, Narita Airport exceeded my expectations as a first-class traveler. Its cleanliness, diverse shopping options, card payment convenience, and priority boarding made my journey to New York truly exceptional. I highly recommend Narita Airport to fellow travelers seeking a top-notch airport experience.
Worst organization at Singapore Airlines check in, more than an hour for a luggage drop off. 3 people to check but let everyone in. People spend their time negotiating with customers.
Everything was efficient in the immigration but there was a slight delay before baggage started showing up in the carousel. I still managed to receive my luggage at the end.

Horrible airport design. Absolute nightmare flying out of here. All the food is a very long walk from most gates and the entire floor is carpeted which makes moving your luggage a hassle. Can’t think of one redeeming quality of this airport.

Departing from this international airport post Covid is a nightmare with everything closed including the immigration check-in for departure and arrivals unless it is after 8am and before 9pm. I am not kidding when I say that there are no shops (not even duty free) or eateries open during those closed times. I was unfortunately stuck here cos of flight diversion on 1 Jan 2023. Normally I would stay at the airport since it's just 1 night. Non-Japanese were asked to fend for themselves with no assistance provided whatsoever by the staff. To put salt to wound, the non-Japanese passengers were only told that there are no overnight accommodation arrangements made after the Japanese passengers were dealt with, which was by that time, around 8.30-9pm (which was how I saw that the entire airport was unmanned from 9pm). So in short, avoid this airport if you need an early or late flight out cos you might just not be able to make it with their limited staffing.

The only reason I used Narita Airport was because none of the Middle Eastern airlines fly to/from Haneda anymore and Cathay Pacific wasn’t the best option price wise this time around otherwise. I always choose to fly to/from Haneda instead due to close proximity to Tokyo City Center and its much better layout. Check-in staff were extremely nice and polite but they lacked flexibility and didn’t let me take my other carry on to the plane instead, they had me check it in and pay a huge sum of money although it wasn’t a full flight. Airside, everything was closed although it was it was still 8PM. There was only one souvenir shop and there was no money exchange (except for the one in the check-in area Landside). An international terminal should have these things available for passengers at least until midnight.

I've flown via Narita Airport before and always found it to be excellent, especially the connection between Terminals 1,2 and 3 via the free shuttle bus. This review is specifically about Terminal 3, which serves only a handful of regional airlines like JetStar Japan, Spring and Jeju Air. Pre-pandemic it was a functional, but drab location. By comparison, the new Terminal 3 is absolutely stunning, easily the most spacious (per number of airlines served) I've ever seen. There are huge seating areas, several appealing food outlets, a bookstore, and a Lawson's convenience store. The beautiful art work complements the peaceful, relaxed atmosphere - an immediately noticeable contrast to the crowded scene at most of the world's terminals. I really didn't want to depart! Congratulations to those responsible

Toluca Airport located about 45 minutes away from Mexico City is a nice alternative to Mexico City Airport. It mainly has flights within Mexico and limited service to the USA (Florida, Las Vegas, Houston). The best thing about this airport are the short lines. Check in and security took less than 10 minutes. Its small, but has a new feeling to it and covers the most basic needs. It has a few shops and a Food court consisting of Subway, Domino's, hamburger joint and smoothly. All seems clean and tidy. Boarding is done via Airplane stairs and several ground transport options exist to Toluca and Mexico city
Arrived on full QF91 from Sydney on 22 April. Fantastic new airport that does credit to New Caledonia. Clean modern and very quick from a full plane to bus transfer to Noumea.

I passed through this airport in July 2012. They had done a lot of improvements since the first time I flew through in 2011 and I know that it's not totally finished now. The price of food and beverages is pretty expensive. The airport looks good and clean. The staff are professional.

Tontouta Airport is a building dating back to the 1970s offering basic facilities. However it is undergoing an amazing expansion and facelift which looks promising : modern with pleasant architecture and more user-friendly. The new airport should be completed by 2011. On arrival pax climb down steps and cross the air-parking zone to enter the airport. There are five-six immigration booths open per flight however the quarantine service is small and slow. Tontouta airport is a no smoking area. The departure hall is of reasonable size for the current traffic and the ground staff is friendly. The café is expensive and basic but it could be worse. The whole airport is a free WI-FI zone. On departure after checking in the luggage pax often wait long minutes in a line to perform the immigration and security controls. The police and security staff are usually friendly enough though cruelly lacking the ability to communicate in English! The boarding lounge where the gates are located is well air- conditioned  though boring. The main features being a largish duty-free shop and a café on the 1st floor. The business class lounge is comfortable and obviously more interesting. There is a post-office and a bank in both arrival and boarding lounges for money exchange however the only ATM distributor is in the main hall across from the souvenir shop.

Tontouta is a fairly basic international airport. There are no skybridges so on arrival you descend the stairs and cross the tarmac to the single terminal and vice versa on departure. Customs and immigration are fairly straightforward although a little bit of French will help. The airport is a long way from Noumea so it is best to arrange a transfer with your hotel pre booking before you leave is the best. Arc en ciel was the best company we thought. Heading back out is always a nightmare at Tontouta there is no order for anything. Customs is always straightforward when departing. Only a small duty free on the other side and only 1 cafe. not much to do. There are no tv screens or monitors for the flights. You just have to rely on the French announcements and a piece of paper at the gate. Overall was a good experience and a very good airport for a small tropical island.

I've travelled through Tontouta a few times now and have thought the place relatively unremarkable. Basic with few luxuries and an unfortunate distance from Noumea township NOU finally earned a brickbat on my last visit. Security screening caused the delay of two very busy flights to SYD and Tokyo. Appallingly slow and with little or no organisation it's a wonder pax remained calm and good-natured as they crushed in against the one tiny door. With Tokyo pax getting priority my QF92 to SYD left a full hour late wholly as a result of this woeful process. Only one of the two X-Ray machines were in operation because apparently of a lack of trained staff. When I reported it to airport officials the response was "Oh!".

Not a great airport but not the worst either. The only really bad aspect is the cost of food and drink - 17 Australian dollars for a stale sandwich and two cokes at a self-service cafe is over the top. The fact that smoking is allowed is also a black mark. Make sure you have arranged a transfer to and from the airport because there are few taxis and the ride is not cheap because of the distance from Noumea.

Tontouta is a fairly basic international airport. There are no skybridges so on arrival you will descend the stairs and cross the tarmac to the single terminal and vice versa on departure. Customs and immigration are fairly straightforward although a little bit of French will help. The airport is a long way from Noumea so it is best to arrange a transfer with your hotel this will cost XPF2500 (EUR 21.57) payable to the driver in cash. I did not see any ATMs in the arrivals area so it would be as well to buy some francs before you arrive. New Caledonia Tourism also has links to a number of transport companies that provide airport transfers. The airport is a smoking zone and many passengers take advantage of this. When you depart your hotel should recommend you leave for the airport three hours before your scheduled flight. Again it will be a XPF 2500 (cash) bus fare to the airport. There is no additional departure tax as it will have been collected by the airline when they ticketed your flight. At the airport you will need to fill in the departure card before you approach the customs area and there are no pens anywhere. Customs and security are uneventful. Just through security you can turn to the left and go up the stairs to the two airline lounges - Air Calin and Air France. Air Calin's Hibiscus Lounge is very small and basic whilst the Air France's Salon looks much larger and has nice tub style leather chairs. I was flying Qantas and they use the Air Calin lounge. There is one duty free store airside on the left after the stairs to the lounges. There is really only one gate area although there are a number of "gates" - doors to the tarmac. At the far end of the departure area you go up the stairs to the public bar and cafe. The boarding procedure is very relaxed and does not take that long.

Tontouta International Airport is located 45km outside of Noumea. If you catch a cab to the airport be prepared to pay for a two-way journey as cabbies are not guaranteed a return fare back into town. There's no point turning up early for your flight. The airport only operates when flights are due to arrive/depart. Check-in counters the small souvenir shop and cafe don't open till 90 minutes prior to scheduled departures. Duty free shopping is only available air-side which can only be accessed 60 minutes prior to departure. Surprisingly smoking is permitted in all parts of the terminal. In summary Tontouta is a very basic facility offering very basic services. On a more positive note all the airport's ground staff were exceptionally friendly helpful and good- natured including check-in agents security immigration and customs officials.

Terrible experience and an awful time. Lack of communication and understanding. Cancelled my next flight mid air. Will never fly Air Canada again. After the cancelled my flight the rebooked it for two days later and gave me thirty dollars for food. I will never go to Canada again. Getting baggage was extremely frustrating for me and my young kids. The employees were very incompetent and inexperienced in their work.

Terrible airport. When I travel, I try to avoid Toronto, dirty rough carpet, hard to wheel with a wheelchair and being disabled. Westjet asks when you travel if you have any special needs, I travel Priority so I can sit more at the front and avoid the hassle of bothering employees, the distance between gates is long and not easy for someone in a wheelchair, however, there is no help from the airline WestJet and having a hard time to wheel with the carpet. Terrible airport. Avoid and avoid. Not worth it to transit by.

What an airport. Clean, easy to navigate, comfortable and customs and security are solid. Landing in this airport coming back from the United States was just as good as when I left. The one thing that would be nice is having preclearing for US customs which would have saved me time once I landed in the United States.

The arrival process at YTZ is very smooth, quick and easy. Unfortunately, the same can't be said for the departure process. As traffic from the airport has increased, the lounge can no longer accommodate all of the passengers. It is very rare that I am able to find a seat. Equally unfortunate are the constant announcements directing passengers to exit doors and gates. These two things combined make for a very loud, stressful experience.

The Pick up and drop off area at this airport is ridiculously small for the number of passengers currently passing through. Parking and pick is basically total chaos at this airport, the rude and aggressive parking "security" guards do not make matters any better. If you are driving seriously consider an alternative.

Toronto City Center, while dwarfed in size by nearby Toronto Pearson Airport, provides an exceptional experience for travelers. Most notable is the terminal cafeteria stocked with free coffee, soft drinks, and light snacks. In an era where nothing seems to be given out for free in air travel, it is refreshing to see this at City Center. The terminal is designed differently than those at most other airports. As opposed to separate waiting areas for each gate, there is one central waiting area which serves every gate (the airport has 10 gates). At first glance, the sight is a bit jarring, but travelers will feel at ease as they settle in to the comfortable seats with their free snacks. City Center is also recommended because of its location. Views from within the airport and during approaches are beautiful as the airport is situated over water (Lake Ontario). Meanwhile, the airport is very close to downtown Toronto, making transport to and from the airport quick and cheap.

Upon arrival to Billy Bishop there were no wheelchairs. My husband used a luggage cart for mobility through the tunnel. We registered as needing assistance. We also submitted doctor form. Cancellation was given way later than seems appropriate. It was a very stressful experience for ourselves and others.

Passed through Toronto City Centre Airport on a recent trip from Chicago to Quebec. It is a small airport so very easy to navigate.
