The worst is boarding - Passengers are checked for boarding in up to 20 minutes before they can actually board the flight. After going through boarding, passengers do not actually board but they have to walk down two flights of stairs carrying their hand luggage and then they wait outside for up to 20 minutes. Next, passengers walk up the steps carrying their 10 kilo hand luggage to board the plane. Meanwhile the brand new walkways that can take passengers directly from the terminal into the plane (avoiding walking down and up stairs and waiting outside) are idle. I have been to Torino 4 times since September and the walkways have never been used! People talk about the difference between the North and South in Italy however I see the same incompetence from North to South. Italy has one if the World's most significan historic and cultural heritages but the culture of incompetence permeates Italy.

Absolutely horrible experience every single time. If you do not arrive 3 hours ahead you will miss your flight. No one is willing to help as most of the people who work in this airport are soulless robots and instead of going with common sense they side with policy. Never in my life have I been met with so much unprofessionalism.

Small super convenient airport. It’s small but efficient. Has one food counter with the really good food, Better than most airports. Have to walk out on tarmac to plane. Arrival and exiting are quick and easy. Wait about 10 minutes to 15 minutes for bag and out the front door in 20 steps. Outside attendant are great. The give directions and keep pick up lines organized enough. Gets a 10 for Convenience.

Ladies toilets were bad, flush were not working. Female assistance were cleaning toilet just before entry only for Foreigners, why? I am from Mumbai and highest contributing tax payer of India for so many years. But then why service is bad for Indian citizens.
Poor spacing, poor food choices, poor temperature maintenance, suffocating. The impression of a beautiful city fades away once you spend some time in the airport

Positive: very clean toilets. Fast check-in, service, X-ray scan, security. Bad: restaurant is closed. The 3 coffee shops have identically printed menu (ie same items and prices). Talking to the manager I learnt that ALL 3 cafes are owned by same person. So the choice is limited and prices are higher than other airports. Looks like the coffee shops are probably owned by the son of some MLA. Why is Udaipur airport authority giving the contract for 3-4 coffee outlets to one owner.

Air Conditioning does not seem functional, the temp was less than 10 degree and was very cold. Flight got delayed and the display screens were not commanded properly. Big queue at Checkin and staff was too slow.

This airport is situated good one hour away from Udaipur. Small and basic airport. Nothing at arrival hall, not even a tea/snack shop. Toilets need to be more clean and hygienic. Only 2 baggage belt on arrivals so easy to get baggage, also very short walk from aircraft to baggage to exit. Wifi is of no use, either it won't connect and if connect won't be working properly. Few chairs available near baggage belt. Uber/Ola available from airport also a prepaid taxi counter for booking. No public bus available to city from airport. If not travelling with heavy baggage then can walk to highway and then wait for bus going towards Udaipur.

What a miserable little airport. First up you show your ticket and passport to someone at the door. Then step in and put luggage on a belt to be scanned where again you show passport and ticket. Then you take luggage to the check in desk. Show ticket and passport. Plus credit card that you booked with. Then a line for bag check. Bags on a belt while you stand under a sign for women (one) or men (four). You get called into a booth that has curtains (help where is my bag?). You are patted down and a metal detector scan all over. Super sensitive even for my underwire bra. My wrist went off (operation years ago). I had to explain that in detail. The whole procedure was not done in a friendly way. Then quickly rush back to the belt where all my valuables were in my bags. The waiting area is dull with nothing to do. One small store open airside. Even the smoking room was closed. I was happy leaving this airport.

It is a modern airport built about a year or two ago. Though small and only flying out domestic flights it is air conditioned and has a two shops and a restaurant. Security and checkin was efficient and modern. There is not a lot to do so if you get there early I hope you have a book to read.

An almost new airport that is reasonably efficient up to and including the security checks. Security checks are stringent unlike those at some other Indian airports. The "no batteries" rule in hand luggage is strictly enforced. Past security there are no facilities at all except a small shop. And if there is air conditioning it didn't work. So eat and drink before going through security. Only one gate of the three (on the ground floor) is operational and there is no seating at all upstairs.

Quaint little airport. Easy check in with Nok Air (2 hours prior earliest). Few basic shops and Thai restaurants but nothing significant. Many seats but don't sit on the monk's seat by accident like I did because the English sign is written incorrectly, should say "Reserved" not "Please Offer" (see picture attached). Efficient AC and lots of adjacent parking just 20m from terminal, an easy ride.

This is a very comfortable and affordable airport. There are a number of shops on the ground floor with very reasonable prices also Thai massage at the end of the ground floor again with very reasonable prices. They've replaced the lounge chairs in the past two years and the new chairs are nicely padded. The only negative is that you will likely have to walk across the tarmac to board your plane. No problem in the winter but I'm not sure how that works during the rainy season.

Small functional regional airport with all necessary amenities including nice buffet restaurant on upper level free parking outside and no airport entrance charge for vehicles. I even checked in with Nokair with less than 30 mins to departure as my Thai friends decided to stop off at the market on the way to go All passengers are expected to stand up for the national anthem when it is played by loudspeaker twice daily - a quaint touch.

They took everyone's passport and boarding passes in the transit desk without an explanation. They showed us to an elevator and up to the second floor. The guy at the desk said he will bring the passports up later. We kept waiting. When no one came after 20 something passengers and more than half an hour i went back down to ask when to get our passports back and they said they will be delivered at the boarding, which for me is 5 hours later at 8a.m! Instead of trying to get some rest i am waiting to get my passport and boarding pass back in the middle of the night, which is kept in a stack of other passports and boarding passes!

I had to use the transit hall twice, once on my way to Seoul, and once the way back. It was to be honest a very bad experience, as the availability of food counters was very limited in terms of opening hours and the types of food, the staff did not speak almost any English, and many of them were very unfriendly and even rude, and this is not just towards me, but towards all other passengers as well. When I or some other transit passengers that I met there asked simple questions to the so-called information desk, the employees just walked away without saying anything, and I have never seen something like this before. The seating is available, but is very limited, as they consist mostly, of plastic "benches" that are really uncomfortable. The toilets were also very dirty, and sometimes so dirty that it was impossible to use. I would definitely avoid this airport in the future. There is only one departure "gate" and all passengers have to go through there, while the shouting staff direct people into the accurate aircraft from there.

Arrivals experience was very easy - only a short queue at passport control, and bags arrived quickly. Watch out for the unlicensed taxi drivers touting for business, and head straight for the green taxis on the rank to the left of the terminal door. On departure, check in opened early and had no queue, again no queue for security or passport control. Only a small airport, but plenty of seating available, and a couple of cafés and bars. There's a small smoking room. Lots of duty free shops - unlike main western airports, these are several independent stores all selling similar items but different prices, so shop around for the best deals. On the downside, despite having 4 air bridges they are all accessed by a single gate which can get confusing if more than one flight is boarding at once.

A small airport, but still outdated with minimum amenities, manned by communist era employees. I would still consider all these tolerable, if the whole departure/boarding process was not a tragicomic procedure. Although the airport boasts 4 jetties, they all share one entry from the departure hall, and if there are more than one flight taking off at the same/similar time, the chaos ensues, as both planes passengers storm the single gate to get to their jetty, there is no order or info given as to which particular plane is loading, and at the gate throngs are sorted out by the personnel! It was hysterical, shoving, pushing, being pushed back by the airline personnel who scream for the other plane's passengers, etc etc.. Beautiful country with very nice people, so a bit of an adventure does not mar the travel experience. The airport is very soon to be replaced by a newer, hopefully much modern version.

Very pleasant experience. The airport was very clean and up to a great standard. It looked like a new development. The airport staff are very polite. Passport control a breeze, especially for families with small children. The baggage arrived in good time. I could not find an ATM or a currency exchange counter though. Had to go downtown to get local currency.

Time travel back to circa 1960: the building the service the ambience is completely mid-20th century. Check-in is completely disorganized - there was no line for business class you simply had to shove aside others on the line while shouting "business class". Business class lounge looks exactly like a not-too-classy bar from Eastern Europe in the 1950s. Shops are like souvenir shops at a cheap tourist site. But it is not a very busy airport so you pass through everything fairly fast. Fun in strange sort of way. They are building a modern airport for UB so you better go now if you want to experience it before the airport is retired.

Departure: MIAT Airline check in requires credit card verification from traveller. This can be a problem if you book your flight through a travel agent as the credit card details wont match. Very limited number of shops and lounge availability (I suggest eating before you get to the airport). Arrival: Slow customs officers for a small airport. Allow 1 hour from landing to clear customs and collect bags (there is only 1 baggage carousel and travellers to UB often have a lot of luggage). Wifi in arrivals area is unreliable and Taxis will most likely not use the meter unless prompted.

Very small airport. One baggage carousel. Very quick customs and immigration line. Old Russian-style concrete architecture. Departure area similarly small. There is a business class "lounge" but not much on offer. There are a few stores in the departure area where you can get snacks drinks and souvenirs. There is a small room for smokers. Very basic but functional. Customs and immigration again very quick on departure.

What an experience Genghis Khan (ULN) proved to be! I arrived with my small group at 06.00 for an 08.15 MIAT flight. Several full flights and 4 staffed check-in desks. No queuing system exists - pushing and shoving is standard. Check-in staff vanish leaving empty desks. No management and nobody can answer questions. We started queuing at 06.00 and we were finally checked in at 08.00. Other than the check-in hall and a blur of corridors as I ran to the aircraft I saw nothing of the airport. Recommendations? Time the patience of a saint and stand your ground! Oh and a small child seems to be a golden ticket the the front of the "queue".

There's nothing quite like a small airport to really make commercial flying enjoyable. Parking is very simple and convenient, it's like parking at your local grocery store - right at the entrance to the terminal. It's also inexpensive at $9 a day (ironically, if you're able to fly to this airport with a light aircraft, parking a single engine private plane here is only $5 a day). Food and shopping options are limited in the terminal, but Irving's bagels and sandwiches are tasty and reasonably priced. There is a portion of the terminal where you can sit with family members while waiting for your flight. Remember those days when you could walk up to the gate and meet someone? You can essentially still do that here because of the way the terminal is designed. There are only three gates here, and they're all in one large room past the TSA checkpoint. Because of the low volume of travelers here, the TSA facility is small, and the line moves quickly. The rest rooms are very clean. The only drawback is it's sort of hard to find on the road. Signage on the local major roads is inadequate. As is the signage at the parking lot.

Small airport in Uzbekistan, mainly used by tourists following the Silk Road. A few fights a day to Tashkent and one to Istanbul also flights to Russia and Saudi Arabia. Arrival at remote stand and walk about 100 yards to the terminal. A single baggage carousel and a few seats in the Arrival Hall. Toilets available. Departures done in separate, newer building. Airport is of the Soviet Union design but had a refurbishment about 20 years ago. Car Park at the front of the terminal building.

Flew in and out on my way from Asia to Europe with China Southern. The airport was fine, not great. There is a mix of staff who speak no English, basic English and good enough English. Also could not go through the international departures security until 2 hours before the scheduled flight departure time even though I've said I would like to use the first class lounge which is at the airside. WiFi is available, however, can only be used with a Chinese phone number to log in.

Well organised for the transit process. Airport service persons picked us up at the exit and allocated us in a special area. There are free services for water, wifi access and breakfast. A lady registers and reminds each of the customers in the waiting area for boarding. Very good experience!

I had an early morning flight from Terminal 2 to CKG. Arrived early due to the scheduled shuttle from my hotel. The security arrangements here are very tight but not overbearing. Check-In was simple enough, while I virtually had to empty my carry on of all electronic items for separate scanning. Once through, I headed to the Hainan Airlines lounge, but it only opened at 6am, so I waited for 30 minutes. Then I had a wait until 6.30am until breakfast was served, but it was plentiful and delicious. My aircraft was at a distant stand, so I had to board a bus but the boarding process was smooth and simple.

I was on a trip from Korla, which is in the northwest of China, to Sydney Australia taking transition stops at Urumqi and Guangzhou. The transition experience at Urumqi was smooth and impressive. The staff were very friendly and helpful. They respond quickly to the customer's needs and patiently explain procedures to follow. I will definitely to recommend friends to take transition stops at Urumqi Airport in future.

Small airport and gateway to the Antarctica. Ushuaia is a tourist destination and claimed by Argentina to be the southernmost city in the world. Check in is straightforward on street level. You go up a flight of stairs for security check and to your gate. Ample sitting space. There were a couple of small shops selling souvenirs. Jetways to aircraft. On the main floor there is a large duty free shop selling the usual "international" brands of chocolates, perfumes, and liquor. Also a cafe for food and drinks. Arrival is straight forward. Luggage arrived quickly in baggage claim and put through a casual security check. Taxi dispatcher at exit arranges for passengers to get into vehicles for their respective hotels. English widely understood by airport workers. They are also very helpful. The town is very close by - visible from the entrance to the airport - aned reached in 10 minutes. The airport caters to the huge tourist flow there. Views from the airplane while landing and taking off are dramatic with scenes of the Tierra del Fuego archipelago spread out. Window seat is a must. Nearly all the flights to Buenos Aires from Ushuaia are to the capital city's domestic airport which is far away from the airport that caters to international flights to the U.S. and Europe.

Ushuaia copies El Calafate in the design and in doing a lot of things right for a small regional airport - but it doesn't do it as well. The good things include using airbridges even for small regional jets (helps get you out of the cold wind), fast check-in and security staff, a nice clean terminal, lots of meter taxis (less than $200 to most of town). However, there were fewer toilets, badly organised cafes with limited food, flight info was often wrong, and the wifi was unusable most of the time.

Flew in and out of here on our way to a ship. Arrival was straight forward and baggage arrived quite quickly. There was a customs check on arrival for plant material even though this was a domestic flight. Departure check-in was fast the departure gates are upstairs although we did not find any signs to tell us. At the time of writing the airport tax is 13 pesos. There is free wifi internet available at the airport a cafe with not too high prices but little public seating. Although a modernish building users will notice that the roof leaks in numerous places quite badly.

Small modern wood-paneled regional airport. Helpful tourist info desk located just before you exit the building. Airport is located close to the town on what was apparently a bird nesting area so taxi rides are cheap. I arrived in Ushuaia by plane and departed by ship so cannot comment on check-in procedures and facilities.

This month, I flew out of new Terminal at Vadodara Airport using three different airlines (Jet Airways, Air India, and IndiGo). Despite having built new Jet Bridge, Vadodara Airport just doesn't utilize them. I was transported from terminal to aircraft using shuttle bus on all occasions. The new terminal still uses many of the old processes (ex: check-in bags are scanned before check-in). On one occasion, I couldn't enter security screening for 11 am Jet Airways flight because the security personnel were short-staffed. Immediately after security screening, there is no place to sit and organize your belongings. The boarding area is very small. The dining and shopping options are limited. The terminal does have a nursing room for mothers. During boarding, the ground staff doesn't utilize the PA system, so passengers struggle to hear the boarding announcements. Overall, the new terminal at Vadodara Airport just doesn't feel like a new, world-class terminal.
Horrible experience. Extremely rude and unprofessional staff. Zero costumer care and support. Very angry and unfriendly. The worst airport experience in my entire life.
Rude, unfriendly staff. I had a quick query and was just told move on. However quick and efficient getting through scanner etc. Very poor signposting

I recently had an extremely disappointing experience with the security staff at Valencia Airport. The service was abysmal, with staff displaying bad attitudes, rudeness, and a complete lack of communication regarding the security process. It was embarrassing to witness such incompetence from what should be a well-managed team. In particular, the lady operating the X-ray machine on the morning of March 16th made me walk through the security line twice due to her inefficiency, i was not the only one this happened to as she continuously rolled her eyes as if it wasn't self inflicted. This kind of treatment is unacceptable and reflects poorly on the airport's professionalism and customer service standards.

A moderate sized airport with fast security processing times, decent duty-free shopping and enough seats with a power socket. Signaling isn't the clearest however as the airport was build in 3 steps. Half of the gates are bus boarding only. It has a convenient metro connection to the city center. Wifi was quite good and staff friendly and helpful.

The worst airport staff I have ever seen. They only speak Spanish (or incomprehensible English) and are very inefficient and unprofessional. At the security check, they took out every single item from my backpack for no reason at all, and it took me 15 minutes to put everything back in place to make the contents fit in my backpack. They also made me go through some additional checks, again totally unjustified, and all the time they treated me with utmost disrespect and harshness. The extra security checks might be justified, it is good to be extra careful, but the disrespect and harshness a foreigner is exposed to at this airport is something that needs to be changed. Nobody has the right to treat someone with such cruelty just for being a foreigner. It was the first and definitely the last time I took a flight from this airport and I do not recommend it to anyone.

There was no access to toilets for more then 45 minutes in departures hall. We had a delay, it was very busy  and a very unpolite lady was cleaning toilets. More than 20 people waiting in line who had to catch a plane and not able to use the toilets.

I am 76 and have a hip replacement. Yesterday evening I went through the security scan. I was flying to Heathrow, flight BA 0445, May 17th, 20.50. The alarm went off and I explained my hip replacement. This was ignored. I was man handled and treated very roughly and rudely. The security man even pulled back the back of my trousers and looked down them. I was humiliated and disrespected in front of passengers. After I asked him for his number and name. I did I was unhappy about how I had been pushed about and treated. He put his face into mine and gave me a very threatening point with his finger. I am a respectable professional man. I also served 10 years in the police. I do not deserve to be treated in this discriminatory way and I hope my complaint will be heard.

Terrible airport. Very small. The air inside was horrible. It was so hot in the entire airport. It shocked me that there were no stations for refilling your water bottle. Also Wi-Fi connection was very poor. The most bizarre situation occurred when there were closed both (yes, there are only two) toilettes for women. Cleaning ladies just closed it and cleaned it for 30 minutes! There was queue of approximately 50 women. Our flight Is delayed. We don't know why or for how long. According to information board we are already in the air. Boarding didn't even started.

Beware of the awful Ryanair hostesses. The airport is small but fine. The real hustle are the Ryanair hostesses at the gate. Truly horrible experience. Make sure you stuff your pockets with any excess item, they will charge you almost 50 euros for a tiny purse without giving you the time to reorganize your backpack. Even threatening that you will miss your flight if you don't pay. Terrible.

On the 20th of November 2021 I was on the phone to my friend who was having issues with a passenger locator form for arriving in Scotland. The way the staff at the check in desk spoke to my friend was a down right disgrace and in other airports would such mannerisms be accepted! The staff would not provide any help to my friend and would also not speak to myself over the phone who had flown out of the airport 3 days prior! This is an absolute disgrace and as an airport you should take immediate action! Only for a kind passenger who over heard the matter would still not be sorted! Then proceeded to go to security where the security decided the throw about two expensive laptops! 0/5 experience! Would love to see their reaction if we treated them the same in any of our UK airports!

Small airport if there are more than 2 flights leaving at the same time the boarding area becomes really small with only two gates available. Impossible to buy water after security check only an automatic machine but quickly empty. However check-in quick and professional.
A very tiny airport at 10 km to Valladolid. Only a little number of flights a restaurant and a drinks and snacks machine. Clean safe and quiet.

Small airport 20 mins from city centre Good coach links to other major cities. Very clean. Very limited resources and facilities. Raciones and Tapas not recommended! Prioritised boarding non existant so booking in 'rush' a total waste of time. Don't try to enlist help from other check in desks even if they are empty as they stick 125% to the rules!

A tiny little airport with probably only a handful of flights a day as such security and passport control get somewhat overloaded as does the departure lounge when a full flight is due. a small restaurant/bar is there as is a small shop which was closed for lunch when I was there.

International flights from Shanghai. Have to go out and come back in even without luggage. Normal transfer procedure does not apply. It is all verbal. No lounge sign anywhere except on lounge. Signs are badly marked.

The airport advertises Verified Traveller program and has signage but this option didn’t exist, I was shunted into regular lineup. When I asked the security guard about it he shrugged, told me to empty out everything and looked away until I started doing it. As I was packed for the express line and they are very old school, wanting belts etc off, laptops in their own tray, I ended up using 4 trays. Grateful I didn’t have kids with me.

My recent experience at Vancouver International Airport was nothing short of a nightmare, thanks to the appalling behavior of the airport security staff. As an avid traveler who flies almost monthly, I've never encountered such disrespect and incompetence anywhere else. Upon passing through security for my flight to Los Angeles, I was subjected to an unnecessarily intrusive inspection of my toiletry and makeup bag by a particularly rude security agent. This individual meticulously scrutinized every item, treating me as though I were a criminal rather than a paying passenger. Despite adhering to all liquid and gel rules with clearly labeled travel-sized products, he insisted on removing each item, meticulously examining them, and transferring them into a clear plastic bag. This absurd process dragged on for a staggering 20 minutes, leaving me stranded at the security checkpoint while other travelers breezed through. When I dared to question the purpose of such excessive scrutiny, the agent responded with unwarranted aggression, shouting at me in a manner that suggested he owned the airport and I was some sort of threat. His colleague, instead of diffusing the situation, also joined in to defend his unacceptable behavior. I was given an ultimatum: either discard my makeup or check my bag, neither of which was necessary had it not been for the agent's rude conduct. Thankfully, a supervisor intervened after my confrontation with the agent and escorted me to a separate area to reorganize my belongings. While the supervisor was at least understanding and tried to calm me down, the damage to my experience had already been done. Upon returning for a second security check, I was greeted by yet another unpleasant surprise—a different agent aggressively slapped my suitcase onto the belt for another round of screening. This agent proceeded to meticulously search through every pocket and zipper of my suitcase, despite my prior clearance and the absence of any suspicious items. Her dismissive attitude towards my situation and lack of consideration for my time was downright infuriating. Overall, my visit to Vancouver was overshadowed by this deplorable experience at the airport. The blatant disregard for passenger dignity and the ineptitude displayed by the security staff tarnished my impression of an otherwise pleasant city. Vancouver International Airport, you have a lot to improve in terms of customer service and professionalism. Until then, I will be reluctant to fly through YVR again, and I certainly won't recommend it to fellow travelers seeking a stress-free journey.

This is the worst service oriented airport I have ever experienced. I was selected for a 'random customs check' which took time and sent me out into the beginning of the security area with a connecting flight to catch in half an hour. I went to the Information desk who then gave me a green stamp on my boarding pass and told me that would allow me to get to the front of the security line. I showed the boarding pass with the green stamp to the security person who was dismissive, did not look or read my boarding pass and said: "You go to end of line." Worrying and stressed I did so. I ran to my flight and barely made it on without a chance to use the washroom or get a bottle of water. This airport has the worst care for people I have ever experienced, and I fly all over Canada and the US. I will now fly via Calgary to return home to Kelowna.
Took an hour for luggage to start coming on the belt. No other belts even operating, completely ridiculous. If you can’t handle the luggage don’t take a flight in.

I was travelling with my carry on baggage and personal item only. As an experienced traveller I was aware about liquid and gel rules and packed them in my clear bag ahead, and placed in the bin. I was surprised when one of the staff has decided to check my bag. She was extremely slow and arrogant. She didn’t ask any permission, just opened a bag and without comments began to open all items one after another, checking and reading labels of my cosmetics and medicine. She started to place in the clear bag everything- cream (25g), eyelash, lipstick. When I asked when it became a rule she laughed and said 16 years ago.  I am not arguing with the officer in the morning flight but I think that it should be respected environment. If I breach any rule, explain why so I would not do it again. I never ever had any issues with those items in the baggage. And I would accept it if not the tone and the face. Train your officers on how to provide a customer service or at least be tolerant and professional.

First time traveling with our skis, we arrived at the airport 3 hours before our flight & barely made the flight. The 1 screening point for skis / oversized luggage had hundreds of us & it took nearly 2 hours to get through it. It was ridiculous. I will never again go through Vancouver airport. The security lines are ridiculous long even with Global entry. The mornings are so slow and the agents so grumpy that we opted for the afternoon flight. Hundreds of us were panicking over making our flights.

This is one of the worst experiences at an airport. First you have to take your bags to a security check yourself after check in at the counter. Normal bags one place oversized in another. The line to scan your oversized bag was at least half an hour long with one old slow scanner. This is a ski destination so there’s a lot of people with oversized bags. So guess what happens. Then the global entry has a super long line and literally no one in the other lines because they only have one lane open for the Nexus line. You would think they would look at what is happening and open another line, but again just no thought from the people running the place. Then of course there is no one world lounge for an international airport. 0 Stars for this airport!

I was with my mother at the entrance of the airport. There was a young man named William. He asked us if we needed help and I couldn't believe he helped us to get a wheelchair immediately. That was awesome customer service compared to my experience in LA airport.
In desperate need of a cleaning especially when hygiene has escalated from the Covid epidemic. Appears dust has been collecting since initial construction

Flight was delayed 7 hours and representatives are running away from passengers asking for help. They overprice necessities like bottles of water so everyone in this delayed flight is stranded here with no food or water, and representatives are ignoring us. No one speaks English and those who do refuse to help. Very disappointing

We have traveled through Varadero airport on a number of occasions in the past. In some respects not much has changed. I'm pleased to see more x-ray scanners at security. This alleviated one of the major and very uncomfortable bottlenecks. My concern and a very unpleasant discovery when we arrived home was that our checked luggage had been opened and a number of items stolen. It's sad that Cuba has become another place where you need to be alert. Please take care of what is placed in the checked luggage.

Arrival. Slow staff, 50 min waiting line for clearance. Completely spoiled staff. Staff demonstrated full ignorance to the time matter. Demonstratively search 85 plus years old women with hand metal detectors. Poor women barely couldn't stand on her feet. Departure. The same as slow as possible staff, doing as little as possible with demonstrative I do not care attitude. Confiscated umbrella from retirement age women. Refused to give written confiscation notice, and when protested, all 10 officers on the place told her that they do not speak English. Is Varadero International Airport, or place where law and order does not exist. What a shame. Spoiled vacation. Spoiled image of Cuba.

Varadero is a small airport catering mostly to vacationers from North America, Europe and some neighbouring country. It has only 4 airbridges. When my flight (AC from Toronto) arrived, we had to wait for about 10 minutes on taxiway until some other aircraft left. After deboarding, it was smooth. Only 3 mins wait at immigration. Right after immigration, you have to go through security, which I found odd for incoming flights. But the officers were quite relaxed. Baggage was already out when I arrived at the belt. Airport staff unload it from the belt and demand a baksheesh for that. Outside arrival is a small taxi stand and a currency exchange. When departing, check-in was quick and efficient (AC, but handled by local airport staff). Long lines at immigration as three international flights were departing shortly after another. Officers fairly slow (though friendly), it took us 40 mins to clear. Security check behind immigration was quick. Departure hall offers sufficient seating, a few snackbars as well as duty free and souvenir shops where you can blow your remaining CUCs. Airport was fairly clean and overall well maintained. There is no wifi.

Utter absence of thought, empathy and planning would synthesize our experience. We initially headed to the 'departures' sign to find it locked with a sign on the door pointing to another building. Upon reaching the second building, another arrow pointed to a third building and entrance to 'departures', leading to a 20-minute initial meandering, which could have unsettling and anxiety-provoking effect on passengers. There is no information board so you would have to be physically alert to movement to figure out which gate you would be flying from. The experience with border control was very similar: we headed through to the baggage control desk to be informed that we needed to return to a different desk for initial Covid screening and issuing of new boarding passes (the ones we had already printed were deemed unnecessary). The professional conduct of these staff officials leaves a lot to be desired. Remnants from communist eras, these privileged state representatives impose an extremely offensive, authoritative and subjugating tone in the way they demand, command and threaten passengers. The screening of passenger locator forms and codes was precipitated by sharp military style commands and requests to provide multiple proofs of having booked and pre-paid for post-arrival Covid tests, which was completely unnecessary and evident within the passenger locator forms only. The tone was humiliating and demanding, rather than humane and down-to earth. The exact justification for this was that staff needed to inspect all possible evidence to ensure I was not lying. Needless to say, my family had all the necessary provisions and the accusation inflicted pain and public insult. Similarly, the passport control officials demanded all of our dual citizenship documents, checking each and every page and reading all of the information in a silent passive-aggressive way. When asked for explanation, they said that they had the right to request all documents and that this would make the procedure easier for them. My experience was that the customer officials were deriving pleasure from inflicting fear and a sense of humiliation onto others. I am utterly disgusted with the professional conduct of both customer support passport control staff and the border police officials at this airport. The attitude is in the 'how', class-based and passive aggressive and might not be felt by citizens of other countries. However, my family was left feeling humiliated and insulted by this demonic chain of proteges who are occupying key administrative and representative positions. I would not recommend the experience and would advice to avoid this airport at all cost.

Ok, not much to do, but not bad queues. Very small and modern airport. Has a smell of cigarettes in the gates where S7 fly. There is an outdoor bar in the summer and has very expensive duty free. There is also a McDonalds and a coffee store (both expensive).

I flew from and to Varna Airport in April. The airport is good, but the lounges were closed early in the morning. There is only 1 duty free shop and the prices there are good. One bad thing is that boarding the plane is always by bus, otherwise it is a good experience.
The airport is new, modern and colorful. Everywhere is clean. There are nice looking green areas with flowers and trees outside. The employees were polite and smiling.

Terrible place. On arrival waited 50 mins around a baggage claim carousel that displayed the flight for it to change to the other one (yes only 2 claim belts in an arrivals hall) So not a problem you may think wrong. Literally hundreds of people (One full British flight and one full Russian flight) shoved in one room waiting for their luggage at the right belt then for it to be switched at the last minute is not a good combination. On return flight check in speedy and good overweight baggage didn't stir an eyebrow (to my advantage) but then the fun commenced. A queue stretching around the departure lounge and back again for security checks and the reason one person at the control desk. There were at least 7 flights due to leave according to the flight board. Everyone queuing to get through but the queue just grew longer and longer as the names of flights were shouted out to try push past everyone in an attempt to make their flight (we arrived in ample time thanks to our tour operator). Utter unorganised chaos. And all this in sweltering heat as very little in the way of air-conditioning.

Much the same to report as Tony Maddern - I agree with all his comments. Baggage claim is still taking a long time considering the short distance from the aircraft and minimal schedules. Priority baggage tags don't seem to be recognised either. The two baggage carousels are positioned on either side of the walk route to arrivals so if there are a lot of people they end up blocking the path! There is a handy radiation monitor just above the exit from baggage claim - useful if you're about to sit in the sun (I presume it was UV radiation)! A clarification on the taxis - unlike Sofia that have fixed fares the taxis in Varna and particularly those at the airport are allowed to charge by the meter AND the meter can run at whatever rate the driver chooses as long as it's displayed on the window of the taxi. So before getting in any taxi check the rate displayed on side or on the wind screen. 0.29 Level per km seems ok but many taxis at the airport will charge three times that amount per km! Even Costa Sands resorts should only cost 20-35 Leva let alone Varna City. If departing from the airport be aware that there aren't any eating establishments - so if you'll be hungry get something before you get there! Overall not an amazing airport but it much better than many others of it's age! And if there is only one flight departing from your terminal it shouldn't take too long to pass through security.

Varna airport is interesting. Aircraft are parked on stands about 200m from the airport. An old truck with airstairs pulls up beside the plane and you get off and wait 5 - 10 mins in a really modern bus. The immigration hall serves its' purpose but once you get into the baggage hall that's where it gets interesting. 21st century technology beside old world equipment. It looks like they have just decided to put things in there without any real thought or planning. There are 2 baggage belts which seem to have been cut into the floor. The baggage hall is about 10m X 10m and looks like it has been built to handle 2 flights and there are only a couple of toilets in the baggage / arrivals hall. I think that 40 mins was far too long to be waiting for my bags considering that my flight was the only one at the airport. As you leave the baggage hall into the arrivals area it's just like anywhere else - scrum of people keen to get you into their taxi. A word of warning about taxis though. It's about a 15 - 20 min drive into Varna. (about 15km). The taxi drivers are always keen to rip you off and have a trick of pressing the meter button 2 or 3 times depending on how much they want to rip you off by. A taxi fare into Varna should only cost about 20 - 35 leva.

Poor connection to cities like Trieste. Be careful if you wish to take a connection by bus to Trieste, as there are very few schedule options and ITABUS will not allow you to buy the ticket on the spot even if the bus is empty (I don't know if Flixbus has the same procedure). You should always buy the ticket online beforehand, otherwise you will be left standing there and likely have to wait four or five hours until the next bus comes (which is what happened to me when they refused to let me buy a ticket for the 8am bus). The default answer from the staff is that tickets can only be purchased online, but on ITABUS IG page they say it is possible to purchase also by calling their phone line. Also, the bus stops of ITABUS and Flixbus are not indicated, but they stop in the parking lot in front of the regular shuttles that connect to Venice city centre (as of november 2024). If you are left waiting there, at least inside the airport there are mobile charging stations and there is wifi.

One of the worst airports in the world in terms of customer care - absolute zero - queues at checks - inconvenient and very expensive car parks - obstructionism to shuttles - boarding with buses that leave you endlessly huddled in the heat.

For the first time I have ever seen an airport’s gates and the stores are closed. There is not event any vending machine just for water. It is 3 am in the morning and my flight is at 6. Even the screens are shut down. If the airport will not be open than why there is a flight.

I am writing to express my heartfelt gratitude to the staff of "Lost & Found" at the Venice airport. At arrival at Venice Marco Polo airport, my suitcase was lost. The staff there was very helpful throughout the process in my application and delivery of my suitcase to my home address. The luggage was delivered within 38 hours. So, I was delighted with the service and want to give credit to staff and delivery. Thank you!

It took 2 hours 20 mins to clear immigration. For over 700 passengers there were only 6 immigration officers. This is a joke! They want us to come and spend money and give us such a horrible experience from the time we land. In this horrible immigration area there was no place to eat or have a coffee or smoke. We stood in the line for 140 minutes. Then when we came out our bags were not yet there on the belt and we had to wait another 20 mins for the bags. Furthermore the free wifi never worked.

Long queues for everything. Once you clear security then you go passport control after there is no lounge. The lounge is located between security and passport control. So even if you buy the lounge service you cannot access it once you are past passport control. As they won't let you go out. And if you spend more time Lounge then the line for passport control will be so big that you might not be able to catch your flight. Better arrive 4 hours earlier if you want to use the lounge so that you can get some extra time .

Worst airport I’ve ever experienced. Signage is completely lacking as far as telling you where particular airlines are located for check in. All you see is signs for “check In 1-40” or “41-99”. But no airlines attached to those numbers.  Plus check ins are in first and second floor. So we saw signs for checkin second floor and went up. Walked around entire floor and not seeing our airline asked where easyjet was and was told first floor. What??? Ok back to first floor and again only numbers no names. Finally find easyjet. All self bag check lanes closed and checkin line for boarding passes closed. What?? Stand in line for an hour until someone wakes up from their nap and attends the lanes to check people in and check bags in. Slow. Finally to security. Slow and rude personnel. Thru security and into gate areas. Gates not posted until about 30 mins before flight. Signage to get to gates confusing and inconsistent. Finally to gate. Boarding at 2:10 pm for 2:50 flight but as of 2:30 still no person at gate to attend to passengers. Food options ok but limited. For those traveling in from Venice, from arrival at noon by water bus to checking in and getting thru security it was one hour twenty minutes. Awful. People say Paris Orly and Charles De Gaulle are worse- no way. We did both in the past two weeks and they were fine comparatively.

Had to wait 30 min for the buses to arrive to the plane and take us to the airport. The flight was already 15 min late, I do not know why the buses were so slow and late. We waited in the plane with very suffocating dry air and it was very hot. The real time it would take us to come from the plane to the airport would be no more then 5 min. A very big disappointment, and was a first one for me.

I was there to help my mother during her travel home. She had surgery few weeks earlier and was somehow unstable in her feet, so she was holding on my arm all time, and we were walking slowly toward the security checks. We didn't ask for any kind of assistance, but the security open up a line just for us, and one of the security even held my mother and accompanied her through the security gate, while I was unable since getting through security myself. The place was crazy busy, and finding these people so aware and helpful surprise me. Also going through the check in and accessing the gate was quite easy.

I found this airport to be surprising good for a European airport. Getting through the airport was smooth and the terminal was busy but not crowded. The Marco Polo Lounge was again very pleasant, one of the best I have been to in Europe, it even has an outside terrace with views of the apron which is a rare treat. My only complaint would be the strange approach to the use of airbridges, there were so many available and yet slow and cumbersome bus boarding seems to be standard operating procedure at VCE, strange.

They asked me to buy a ffp2 mask (almost 6 euros for a pack, no single mask available) because they said I couldn't fly with my surgeon mask. Then they let embark everyone and even the cabin crew didn't have the ffp2 mask! The flight was 2h25 minutes late and all they gave us was a 4€ voucher when all the sandwiches prices are over 5 euros. Not enough sitting places in the airport.

Reopened after one year and a half, the Treviso airport (which is also my "home" airport, being close to where my family lives) is supposed to be a convenient choice for tourists and business travellers willing to visit Venice, which bills it as its second airport despite it being quite far from it. Still, Treviso is a wonderful little city which might deserve a short stop and which is well connected to Venice as well. The issue stems from the way the airport is kept: a very tiny terminal way too close to houses and factories, which appear even closer during the landing, without any amenity, notable shop or restaurant. Seats are few and the design is old and absolutely counterintuitive, and nothing was done to improve it during the long lockdown. In other words, just a very cheap option, not just in terms of airlines flying there.

If you imagine the trip from hell then times that by 3 then you have Treviso Airport. This is a largely dysfunctional, lethargic and poor quality airport. Staff don’t appear to have any idea what is going on. Security doesn’t fill me with any confidence and once you’ve made it through the never ending lines into departures you are faced with the lack of seating. Multiple people sat on the ground in a small terminal. Late flight topped it off. Never again.

This was the worst airport ever. Not enough seating, people sit on the floor everywhere. Ridiculously long queues. So disorganised. All flights are delayed by at least 30 minutes. Definitely too loaded for its capacity!

Nice quiet airport, however departing to East Midlands yesterday was unbearable. Crowds were left waiting in a very humid area at the bottom of the stairs, no air con on. Passengers were all complaining about the chaos and safety. Minimal seating. Most were standing.

This tiny little airport couldn't be any more crowded or inadequate for its traffic. Underseated, understaffed. And the most frustrating thing is the amount of space wasted on trying to sell perfume and other duty free (when no one cares to buy it), while people are all crowded around sitting on the floor in the terminal. Food costs were highway robbery (even in comparison to other airports) and lines were so long it was frightening. The only good part was the security agents who were friendly and less stressful than in most airports.
Good little airport, takes very little time to get through to the gate, not much seating at the gate so don’t go through too early. Good shop. What more do you want?

No sense of organisation. Only few staff for security control and loads of departures at same time slot. People arriving to this huge queue 5-10 minutes before flight departure knowing that will be fast tracked without paying. If I knew better I would do the same and arrive late to the airport.

Treviso airport is utterly chaotic. Possibly the worst I have ever been through. Staff impatient and rude, exit to departure gates totally inadequate for the amount of people travelling at busy times. We almost missed our plane despite the fact we were at the airport two hours before our flight left - the queue was simply at a standstill. I will never ever go to this badly organised airport again in my life. Marco Polo is much better!

Awful airport. Just not up to the job. Unable and seemingly unwilling to cope with the passenger numbers passing through. We use Ryanair alot but having experienced this dreadful airport twice I'm afraid our next trip to Venice will be with another airline which used Marco Polo Airport as we are not prepared to suffer Treviso again.

Veracruz International Airport is small and clean airport. The problem was that, after passing the check in, and entered the departure hall, there are no duty frees, or shops- and my problem no smoking lounges. One small store is accepting only pesos and there are absolutely no souvenirs.

This was the worst airport I have ever been to. Firstly, the check-in line was being operated by one person when the line needed a minimum of three members of staff. Secondly, the staff on check-in and security were extremely rude. The security line was poorly managed. Only one security scanner was being used and staff was on the side to cover a security scanner, there was a minimum of a 20 minutes waiting time so there should have been more than one line working. Multiple people were able to skip the queue by going through open points that should have been closed and monitored by the person that was supposed to be "managing the line". The gate was poorly managed just like everything else was and to very little surprise the volume of people couldn't be controlled. Overall the airport was awful, and I wouldn't recommend this to my worst enemy.

Arrival, no issue, cannot complain. Departure an absolute joke. How can this airport belong to Schengen airport and European standard is beyond me. You better arrive 4 hours before to get through security or else buy fast track and you can wait only an our. Staff, including security staff, that has no clue what they do, rude, shouting, will not provide any information, feels like year 1950 that no digital screens exist, one could continue on and on .. really, really bad airport.

This is the worst airport I have been to. Dirty bathrooms, rude staff, no seating, no wi-fi, no charging stations, and no check-in until one hour before departure, which shortens the time to get through security and to boarding.

Dreadful airport if you can avoid it - do so. Far too small to cope with the number of people using it. Because building work is going on TUI have an air conditioned tent in the concourse where you check in and get your luggage weighed you then drag your luggage to the baggage drop off point in the terminal. You then queue up for an hour to get through security - too few security guards on duty. We had to be pulled put of the queue and fast tracked as we would have missed our flight they were so slow. You then have to go through passport control where two men were stamping the passports at snail pace we along with 20 other people just made our flight even though we were there 2 and a half hours before departure .

We lost our stroller during our flight from Turkey to Milan. The stroller was sent to the Verona airport since it the closest to us. We called the number provided to us on Saturday 16 March 2024. The operator a female was very rude and basically hang up on us when we were just trying to find out the hours of operation. She refused to give her name and was very unprofessional. She should not be holding a position of customer service.

We were warned by Tui rep that there were construction works ongoing for the forthcoming winter Olympics in Cortina but that's no excuse for this shambles of an airport. On arrival there's a trek from bus park to a large white tent to check in luggage, but no , you get a boarding card and a security tag and then another trek to the actual departure area where baggage is checked in for the flight. Facilities pre passport control basic and overcrowded. Passport control chaotic with long queues stretching back through the shops/ food outlets. Typical arrogant Italian border police on the desks. At gates very limited seating and floor area for amount of passengers. They then open gates and herd you out to a covered area to stand baking in 38° heat for 20 minutes to wait on the bus transfer to plane. Must be the worst airport I've experienced ever.

This has to be the worst airport I have been to, limited seating. Ridiculously expensive for everything, staff rude and unhelpful, Que to go to the gate was 1.40 hours and reached the length of the airport. Put me off traveling to verona again.

Queues at passport control of over 1 hr with 1 police officer checking 300 passenger ridiculous! Disorganized! Automatic passport check with digital passport not working! Deserves to be closed and not used for passenger if they can’t staff it!

We travelled to Gatwick, London with EasyJet. It took almost 2 hours to reach the Departure Gate. No staff were visible. Information was lacking. No seats at check in area and few at the gate. Overcrowded and inefficiently managed airport.

NotVerified|  How this airport has changed since we last used it 9 years ago! Arrivals wasn't too bad with the inevitable queues, but Departures was another story. We arrived by taxi at 9.35 am for a 12.15 flight, and checked in straight away with TUI with no waiting. Then the queuing began - straight to Security and joined a long queue: there were 9 lanes, (A to I), but only 4 were in use. Several earlier flights were called through so we didn't move at all. After about an hour we were through and straight into another queue for Passports. This went straight through Duty Free but moved so slowly that we took turns to visit the shop, buy very expensive water and visit the toilet. Again they were not using all available lanes. Once at the gate it was heaving with frustrated people but we did manage to find a seat. We were put on a very hot bus and kept waiting on there for ages before being transferred to the aircraft. Why is this airport so understaffed? If all the lanes had been used it would've been much better, although the waiting areas at the gates are far too small for the number of people using them at busy times.

When I arrived at the airport on August 3rd, 2022 (flight FN 8506) one officer stopped me and asked me for the Payment Confirmation of my Visa, I showed to him on my phone and he said that was not valid if was not printed and I had to pay it again. Finally I didn´t pay but when I asked others they said that he was trying to get money from them too.

Excellent small airport which is newly built, few flights in the afternoon when it is at its busiest! It is located way out of town hence you need to have pre booked transport to reach the town as no public transport is available. The building is air conditioned which is a relief from searing heat. The washrooms needed a bit of TLC. The shopping was expensive as is the case at any international airport. Food options are plenty. Aircraft turn around time is quick. Overall a good airport. WiFi is free for one hour.

Victoria Falls boasts a nice, new terminal building that is uncluttered and pleasant. I arrived for a flight to Addis Ababa and was immediately impressed with the pleasant surroundings of the terminal and its air conditioned comfort. Check in procedures were swiftly handled and passengers then move on to clear security and immigration, which are straight forward, save for the fact that one has to deal with the nuisance of removing his shoes at security. Following security, one takes an elevator up to the departure level where there a number of shops - very expensive shops - and food outlets. All of these were clean and presentable. Restroom facilities were well-maintained and clean. Boarding was accomplished via an air bridge directly into the plane. Surprisingly, Victoria Falls International Airport is very straight forward and easy to negotiate. Staff are friendly and helpful. I feel that anyone traveling through Victoria Falls airport will have no difficulties or issues.

Small airport and rather run down but being refurbished with new buildings and new runway to take bigger planes. Walk to terminal. Staff very helpful. Best to be at front of plane if you need to purchase Visa as can take a time. Need to pre-book transfers to hotels as a long way out of town and no public transport. Check in easy although staff seem unable to book people or their baggage onto connecting flights so if going via Johannesburg you will have to enter the country via Immigration collect bags clear customs and recheck them at the International desks and then go through security and Immigration again! Can take 90mins so allow time for that to happen. Departure lounge basic and small no lounge for premium customers. A few shops and one bar. Short walk to plane on the airport.

It is a small airport located about 20km from the town. No public transport so you will have to arrange your own private transport. If you require a visa to enter the country be prepared for a long line. There are only a couple of shops landside none airside. The departure hall is small and dark with a small cafe-bar.

Quite small with no cover if it's raining. If it's an option make sure you have your visa organized in advance otherwise expect to wait a while in the cramped arrivals area with no fans or air conditioning. Luggage is simply left on the floor. The entire airport is out-dated but most people coming here would expect that.

A very small airport no airways you walk on the tarmac to the terminal if (like most people) you need to buy a visa there is a line manned by only 2 people and no organization at all then the customs man grunts at you or makes you open everything!! but then you are out and in one of the most beautiful places on earth.

This airport is head and shoulders above any other airport I have been to, and I've been through a few. Every person I interacted with form check in to security to service staff were all over the top friendly with great senses of humor. The security line is the fastest I have ever seen, I have never waited in a line here even during the holidays, maybe 5 minutes max. The gates are clean and modern, tons of outlets and different seating arrangements, lots of space for only having 13 gates. 4. Loads of parking for an airport of this size, I was able to park my car like 50 meters from departures and left it there for a week I know how infuriating flying can be, especially when things go wrong, but it goes a long way when people are so friendly. This is my favorite airport and I go out of my way to fly out of here 10/10 please give these people the recognition they deserve

The security screening at your airport is tedious and slow. I arrived 2.5 hours before my flight in order to be within the 2 hour window recommended by the airline. The security screening line took 25 minutes to clear. I had arrived from Calgary International Airport where security screening was accomplished without any delay at all. You have three lines available for security screening and only one was in use forcing people to wait. This situation has not improved since my last visit to your facility. Please do something to fix this problem.

We could not check in online as we had paid for our dog crate. Upon arrival at YYJ all of the machines were down. The line up was extremely long. One WestJet attendant to service a number of people from departing flights and cancelled flights. Priority first we were told line up, we did with numerous other people. People kept coming to the priority line even though they were not we were still told to wait. Rules are rules Priority first then baggage tags, then this horrendous line up. Now 2 people behind the counter. 2 hour wait to finally check in. Finally a third attendant arrived otherwise plane was not loading as all passengers were inline. Arrived in Calgary, dog was well taken care of, lost our bag. Have filed lost bag report, 24 hours later and nothing. Keep checking and nothing.

Foodservice options are very limited. We went to only one before security and with 90 minutes to departure and no line-up, they could not guarantee service. The only service after security has long line ups, cramped seating for 40 only.

Victoria Airport on arrival the terminal was easy to find, clean and well laid out. Friendly and helpful staff, who went out of their way to guide you, check-in was a breeze, and no surprises with our luggage. Even the customs staff shared some humour with us. On the other side of security it was just as impressive with clean well laid out waiting areas and washrooms. Water fountains available that you could fill up your water bottle from and not have to pay the rip off price for bottled water like at other airports. We will definitely use this airport again in the future.

I had an appalling experience in Victoria International Airport. We were flying with Pacific Coastal airlines to Vancouver YVR airport, and the security lines took forever. My father and I waited a tedious 30 minutes in the queue for a 5 minute flight to Vancouver. We had several trays of stuff and a man thought I dropped a SD card and when he took it up from one of my trays and asked me all the security people turned to me, glaring for no reason. The four trays blocked the traffic of baggages coming through the X-ray machine so out of respect I put them all onto one tray and moved away, and a security personnel said kindly to place it on a table. However as I was worried that we'd miss our flight as the security was taking forever to screen my father I was talking in a loud voice as he was across the room and all the security were busy looking at me and it just took forever. If you are flying from YVR to Victoria I highly recommend not using YYJ, as the security is appalling. I flew the seaplane to Victoria Downtown and there were no security measures, so that is a much better choice. However the terminal was well set out and we could find our way easily.

Small airport that's been recently renovated. Modern look but limited services. Especially the free wifi. May as well not even have it. On a quiet day with few Travellers I was not able to even do a simple google search.
I visited Victoria BC two weeks ago and for a small international airport I enjoyed the experience. Security was quick the facilities were good and check-in was quick. I recommend this airport!

Excellent small regional airport spotlessly clean with very friendly staff - slight oddity that the baggage reclaim belts are in the arrivals hall but I was out within 10th mins of the plane touching down and you can't get much better than that.

Although it is a regional airport it handles two international arrivals: Seattle and San Francisco. As I avoid YVR Immigration like a plague (I spent over 3 hours in one of my latest arrivals) I prefer Victoria to get into Canada and then go to Vancouver. You can take a taxi cab to the ferry terminal (would not work on late flights though) and be in Vancouver in less than 2 hours enjoying one of the most scenic rides you will ever find in a ferry. Immigration in YYJ is short and pleasant. You get your bags in less than 5 minutes (usually) and go through customs in less than 10. Overall great airport to get to Canada. Coming out is also simple and effective. Short lines and great staff.

Not meant for passenger comfort! Vienna Airport is for sure the worst in the region and that by design, dark, cramped, unfriendly staff, incompetent management which after COVID 5 years later is not able to produce contact free bathrooms, no space for passengers to wait and relax, a power outlet to charge your phone is nearly impossible, waiting areas are like it is 1968, and don't get me started on the endless dark and cramped corridors. The management screams here incompetence, going overboard on advertising and try to squeeze a buck out of the passengers before they leave. My recommendation avoid at all cost use Bratislava or transit in another airport, Vienna does not like nor want you there!

My trip to the airport was ruined by the unexplained policy to evict all passengers waiting for our flight from our waiting place at our gate. This decision was baffling, as no other airport before has ever required passengers to vacate the most logical and comfortable waiting place to board with little alternative.

Very confusing for connecting passengers, luggage not checked through to our final destination. Ask Austrian service desk staff member about where to pick up luggage and she replied that she did not check it in! Not very helpful. Eventually she gave us the information we we’re seeking Self luggage checkin did not work / print bag tag. Staff at security screening very disorganised, staff lady shouted at us for touching the wrong tray and then gave us a long lecture about why we should only touch the bag trays we are using. No direction from staff at security on what they wanted passengers to do. Duty Free seems to be Duty Plus- more expensive than buying outside of airport! Overall based on experience at Vienna airport would avoid if there is an alternative hub for transfer. Of course Vienna itself is fabulous.

The worst airport and the most confusing one I used for transfer. The layout is really bad and signage so confusing. When we came out of an airplane to transit and catch another airplane we had to go again thru security and we had to discard the water we had. The worst thing is they know about this issue and don't do anything about it as this has happened before.  The lounges are so far away you just don't bother.
Often late in dispatching luggage, especially on weekends. Crowds of people waiting for no good reason. Often too few immigration officers at border control. Overall tiring exercise

It is a nice airport but I was shocked to discover you need 1 euro coin to be able to use the luggage trolley. I had 4 luggages and I carried a toddler. It was impossible to carry all my bags after picking them up, and my child. I asked a security person for advice or a "fake coin", eventually for help. He told me to go to Exchange stand, I explained None of my countries I live in uses Euros. He said it is my problem. If it wasnt for some Czech passengers who heard me talking Czech to my child, and who offered their help, I dont know what I would do. It's incerdibly rude from the airport management to require coins to use the trolleys. I haven't experienced this on any other international airports. Also, the toilets for people with babies are always occupied by people without kids and there is only one such toilet. I think your trolley system should be reconsidered! As the current situation makes the travel experience for people with kids and many luggages simply horrible. Not to mentiom the rude security employee.

It is extremely difficult to find your way around the airport due to lack of signages and there is no staff to help you. They could have added direction signages every few meters. Because of absence of signs You panic as you do not know where to go. Toilets are very few. Seating is very less. Confused pax are milling about every where. Lounges are not in the proper convenient places. Duty free shopping is very limited and more expensive than even in other cities of Europe. Don't expect to get any good duty free deal here.

Dreadful experience with airport security.  A security officer doesn’t speak English well enough. She harassed my husband saying ‘you must put your bag there’ . He has no clue unloading our stuff from the bins after security checkpoint. There are 5 bins with pieces of our luggage and he only unloaded 2 of them. After a minute she returns and this time she is really angry. Says I told you to put your bags there. It appears she wanted me collect empty bins and put them into the special cart. So there are 2 questions: - Are really passengers responsible for loading bins into the airport carts? Why is passenger isn’t allowed to take all his pieces out of bins first? 2My experience with the same officer. My backpack was selected for additional screening. Normal operating procedure, right? After finding nothing restricted in the backpack, she demanded to show her my purse. It had already cleared the security by the way. But even that wasn’t enough. She demanded I should unzip my under jacket. She also said she needed to see my waistband. I had none. At this point I asked he if I could keep my pants.  If it’s not a passenger harassment, I don’t know what it is.

After arrival from Doha we had to to wait ages on a passport control. It is a real joke Vienna airport doesn't have E-gates, at least for EU passport holders. Airport staff more than unfriendly. Immigration officers were extremly slow, and we almost lost our connection flight to Prague even when we had hour and something transfer time. Very bad experience.

Its a maze, if you want to miss you flight because of bad design and bad employee managment this is you airport. The employees are nice and friendly enough, but since i almost didnt get my flight 2 out of 2 times I can't say anything about the wifi, food or shops. The directions are horrible, the number of employees are used the wrong way and all in all i am just happy i am leaving the airport and i will avoid it in the future.
Contrary to another review there are good facilities after passport control. Including shops, Bistro and cafe. Very clean and definitely not a shed.

Very basic all the way. Very few shops or coffee places. Passport and check in was fine but once through that it was bit like waiting in a big shed. Finally found a food court to get a meal but was so badly signed most people did not know where it was and that's a shame as the food was good. Only give minimum time to be there if at all possible.

Nice little airport; small and quaint and delightful to use. All staff were extremely pleasant and I will definitely plan to use this again when next flying to Laos. Two downsides, toilets and airport internet connection. Toilets smelly, they should be on a continuous cleaning schedule. Internet very poor, low bandwidth and annoying log-in process including a compulsory (and multiple) viewing for 7 seconds of the Lao Telecom advert then a 30 second video. As the airport filled up for its one flight per hour the internet became impossible to use, see photographs. Apart from that, excellent and I will definitely use again.

Wattay International Airport in Vientiane is a simple and pleasant airport. Perhaps the ease of travel is due to its tiny size, at any given time, there will only be a couple of flights on the docket so checking in for your flight is very quick. One does not need to arrive too far in advance of their flight. The departure terminal contains decent seating with a couple of large televisions (they were showing muay thai boxing when I was last there). The arrival experience is also positive, with a reasonably short visa on arrival line (and pretty relaxed officials), eliminating a potential source of stress on the final leg of one's trip. My favorite aspect of this airport is the walkway between the plane and the gate. It is elevated and fully exposed to the outdoors so that travelers get a blast of fresh, warm air to set the tone for their stay in Laos.

Singapore to Luang Prabang via Vientiane. As this is the capital airport of Laos, my expectation was way better than this. However, I was very disappointed. The terminal was dirty, especially the toilet. Upon arriving in Vientiane before heading to Luang Prabang, the ground staff was unable to handle our group properly. We waited for 30 minutes just for the ground staff to bring us to the domestic terminal. The domestic terminal is insanely small and dark and we experienced elactricity cut off while transiting for our returning flight back to Singapore.

Wattay International Airport is small and friendly easy to access from Vientiane and nevertheless very easy to get around. The staff are friendly and quick and this includes the Immigration officers and just about every person who you come in contact with while you are there. The facilities are in perfect accordance with the size of this airport: you won`t find any gourmet restaurant here but there is a little bit of everything including a very nice duty-free shop. This is a very comfortable arrival and departure airport as laid-back and relaxed as Laos itself. Arrived mid-November departed mid-December.

Domestic Terminal is older than the International Terminal and was clearly "the" airport in the past. Only few in and out on domestic flights. The planes are parked on the apron and usually passengers walk to and from. Arrivals is through the single gate to the Baggage Spur not a circular belt so things can pile up if there is a lot of luggage. There are toilets before the Arrivals Hall. The whole terminal is a single story with Arrivals at one end and Departures at the other end. There are no facilities in the Departure Lounge after Security. Within the terminal there are a couple of shops selling snacks and souvenirs and a Money Changing booth. The whole experience is pretty good not many flights and a generally relaxed friendly attitude. You would not believe you were in the Capital City.

Late flight out on New Year's day. I love this small airport it's quick to get though and friendly. A surprisingly well stocked duty free shop with a good choice. A small cafe before boarding. I imagine it's how airports were 40 years ago and is a pleasure to travel through.

The international terminal is small and because of that there are no endless walks which is great. The visa on arrival staff were very quick and it only took a few minutes to be processed then it was the same going through immigration. Our bags were waiting for us in the baggage hall after immigration then it was over to the taxi desk and straight into cab and on to our hotel. On departing once again immigration was very quick then we had a short wait in the departure lounge which was very nice with a few shops and a good cafe.

Arrived from Bangkok on Thai flight and still bussed to the terminal in June 2009. Queues for visa on arrival handled relatively quickly and luggage handling dealt with promptly and efficiently. Friendly staff with a relaxed atmosphere.

Expecting the worst but a great surprise. It was a new building and super clean. Great welcome by the airport staff and especially the Passport Control, proud of their airport and their country and genuinely do their best to make it a painless process. On departure the check in staff were efficient, cheerful, and helpful. A very pleasant little cafe for snacks and once again through to more smiling passport control.
The staff forced me to throw away small tube of crème because it did not fit into their plastic bag. One week ago I passed the security check with exactly the same items, at the same airport.

The security staff were extremely rude, I travel through here often and always had a good experience before. They were so blunt with everyone, the way they were speaking to us, when translated, sounded like ‘you will move along’ & ‘you will open your bag for me’. No please not thank you - nothing. Something has gone very wrong in their recruitment policy (or internal affairs) - the majority of staff were like this. This reminded me how horrible customer service was used to be in Lithuania 20 years ago.

The airline counter had not opened when I arrived and was able to find a seat until it opened. The Finnair desk was staffed with English speaking agents who issued me the boarding pass for my flight to Helsinki and also for my onward journey from there. I was directed to the priority security lines which were only a few feet away. The security check was a breeze. I was the only person in this line. Right in front was an elevator to take me to the business lounge which was a perfect place to relax and catch up on my emails.
