The exit from the security area also leads to shops which one has to pass through before reaching the gates. The airport is dated. After the boarding passes were checked at the gate we walked down flights of concrete stairs to the tarmac where a bus was waiting to take us to the ATR 72 propeller aircraft parked remotely in mid field. We boarded the plain by stairs through the rear. The airport was easy to use though I hope the stairs will be replaced by jetways soon.

I read online before getting to Vilnius that a taxi from the airport to the hotel was not expensive, less than €15 and warned of using a meter when I got to the taxi stand there were not people nor cabs. Started reading the notice for tourists, which said a taxi should cost 18-20€, it had rates per km. At that time a taxi drives by and asks me if I want a taxi. I got in and asked him if he is using a meter and he said yes. Get to my hotel and he tells me its 30.30€. The reason for the difference is he doesn't work for the airport and it was a holiday (Sept 15). I travel all the time and never heard an argument the prices posted at the airport is for taxis working for the airport. I felt cheated and not a good way to go to a new country to visit it. The note posted for tourists should warn tourists about cheaters. If someone needs I have picture of his plate and the driver registration. This is not the way to treat and protect tourists. Besides this issue, my stay was good.

At the arrival, I had an issue with mí luggage. The employees in the luggage office were helpful.  The airport is small, but well equipped. At the departure, only the security control was slow a bit. Somehow they rescanned my electronic devices, from the hand luggage. The departure terminal was small, cozy, the staff in one of the café were friendly. The plane took off in time.

The airport is small and clearly arranged, basically there is hardly anything to complain about. The toilets unkempt and bad smelling. Loudspeaker announcements in English with a completely incomprehensible sound quality (loudspeaker) and at such a speed that all the passengers just looked at each other questioningly. However, the reason for the rating is the security staff: we only speak mediocre English. You are instructed to take off your shoes, stand to one side, pull up your pullover to do a routine drug check, all in a barracks tone of absolute unfriendliness. The word please seems to be completely unknown. An impossible way, even if security is necessary. We have never experienced that anywhere on numerous trips. By the way, our suitcase came back with 2 broken wheels.  Der Flughafen ist klein und übersichtlich, im Grunde genommen gibt es kaum etwas auszusetzen. Die Toiletten ungepflegt und schlecht riechend. Lautsprecherdurchsagen auf Englisch in einer völlig unverständlichen Klangqualität (Lautsprecher) und einer Redegeschwindigkeit, dass alle Passagiere sich nur fragend anschauten. Der Grund der Bewertung ist jedoch das Sicherheitspersonal: Wir sprechen nur mittelmäßiges Englisch. Man wird angewiesen die Schuhe auszuziehen, sich an die Seite zu stellen, der Pullover wird hoch gezogen um einen Drogen Routinecheck zu machen, das alles in einem Kasernenton mit absoluter Unfreundlichkeit. Das Wort Bitte scheint völlig unbekannt zu sein. Eine unmögliche Art, auch wenn Sicherheit notwendig ist. Das haben wir auf zahlreichen Reisen so noch nirgendwo erlebt. Unser Koffer kam übrigens mit 2 abgebrochenen Rollen zurück aufs Band.

The airport was great: with chill music, clean spaces and nice atmosphere overall. We were departing in the early morning, flying to Kyiv, but still almost everyone stayed professional and kind (despite the early hour). The only thing that disappointed us was two workers at the passport control gate. We were talking to them in English, gave our passports, but they did not even say hi. Just went with the “маску снимите» (take off your mask) as a form of greeting, when they saw our document and realized we are from Ukraine. First of all, even if it was easier for them to talk to us in Russian, it would have been nice not to hear such rude words and intonations. Secondly, and most important, not every citizen of Ukraine knows or wishes to speak in Russian. Which we clearly demonstrated by talking to the workers in English first. Their responses and the looks they were giving us were not professional.  Again, everything else was perfect and we enjoyed this little time we had at the airport.

On June 2020 airport started renovation of taxiways, as well as the installation of a new apron. The inside of the airport is very clean, it is easy to orientate, the construction of a new terminal will begin. The runway lighting is bad but will also be updated soon. I very much hope that everything will be fine and that it will be easier and safer to travel.

Strange airport. Only saw the arrival side due to bus arrival from out of town. Departure area a bit dreary at the check in. I experienced no lines. Seating is terrible throughout. Unlike others, I had no issue at security. Going past security, it was a lot more pleasant. I ate at one place. However seating at the gate are was terrible. It is a hodgepodge of mostly old and some renos done in the gate area. They could use a new airport building for sure but apart from the seating, I had no real issues

Worst airport security I have experienced in traveling across over 80 countries. As other reviews have suggested, the attitude and "work quality" of the security personal at this airport is completely unacceptable and a complete insult to anything to do with tourism , hospitality or simple being human. As a family of 7, all of us were harassed through the security gates, 3 items were confiscated, all 3 items were already with us through our travels to Milano and Brussels the previous days. The items were a toothpaste that was not marked for volume (it was a regular tube, 75ml I would say, but as the marking of the volume was already faded, they just throw it away, because nothing say "have a nice day" than taking a toothpaste from a traveler). It was a lighter that was not loaded (it was bought empty) but with a price tag of 40 EUR, I must assume they "liked" it. They said it's a "blue-flame" lighter despite the fact that they couldn't light it up once (tried it over and over just to prove their point). The 3rd item was a perfume, that was indeed 125 ml (it was half full, but yes, I know, legally it should not be taken on board if the original load is over 100ml). Two things that became obvious through the process: 1. The staff members are far more happy if they find something (they also sent bags through the scanner 3 times, just to find that empty lighter). The motivation behind that - I let you have a guess. 2. The staff members have thug mentality, they take pleasure of bullying people, make inside jokes within each other on their language, and talk to passengers (including my elderly parents) like dogs. Disgusting, vile, unreasonable behavior. Left the country after a beautiful holiday with a bad taste in our mouth.

SAS misplaced my luggage. While the agent at the airport was relatively helpful, when we called regarding the status of my lost luggage, the person on the phone was less than helpful. In fact, she was basically clueless. Other than that, when we departed Visby, we experienced an efficient process.

Quiet regional airport. Train available from the city which is quite convenient. A few shops and cafes in the domestic gates and these mainly sell local souvenirs and foods. Security setup is a bit dysfunctional but as there aren't many passengers it's not at all hurried. Flight was quiet so quick boarding.

Super fast from plane touching down to exiting the airport; at most 15 minutes, including walking, passport control, waiting for luggage. Entrance hall of the airport had all services necessary for a new traveller: tourist info on city and region, taxi, public bus, train station all nearby and easy to access. Money exchange booth and ATM also on the spot.

Airport security was very tight. Everyone entering the airport, regardless of by car or by train, had to be x-ray checked. The check in counter was very slow and inefficient, so queue was long and slow moving. Adding all these, and the super slow passport control, it took a long time to get through the airport and to the gate. Its shopping options, were extremely limited. Russian dolls accounted for a big chunks of items in the most shops. Food and drink options were equally limited, if not less. As for other amenities, there were almost none. Airport overall though, was very clean. And because it was small, it was easy to move from point A to point B, including to/from parking.

Vladivostok is a fairly modern airport, built in the last 10 years it has lots of space for check in and a decent departure area. There is one major problem though, there is limited foreigh language support if you are a non Russian speaker. If you have problems with your baggage all the forms are written in Russian with no translation, all the support staff only speak Russian. The people at check in have limited English language skills - enough to check people in, but I estimate 95% of staff in the airport only speak Russian. If you dont have any issues when you fly into or out of Vladivostok then it is a nice airport to travel through, but if you do have any problems it can be a nightmare to try to find any people willing to help you - they just dont care if you have an issue.
Stay away in the Covid situation. Masks are not enforced even though fines are announced constantly. The majority of travellers and even staff are not wearing them. No social distancing either.

Arrived early for check in and flew through very quickly as it had not yet offically opened. Unlike last year when I was a little late and it took more than 30 minutes while my Passport was checked and rechecked. Immigration was quick (took about two minutes) and the security check was also quick. I came through here last year and had to be pushy to get both to Passport Control and then through Security as otherwise qiven the queues I would have missed my flight). The airport is quite spacious and there are a few shops. I went straight to Turkish Airlines Lounge and stayed there until it was time to board the place. This was straightforward. This was my third time going through Vnukovo and the experience was similar to that of my first time.

Vnukovo Airport. Waiting for baggage, almost 1 hour now and haven't get it yet. No extra infornation from airport officials. In combination with absence of smoking rooms everything becomes so-called great. I'll consider another airport the next time. Though ceiling is ok.

Once you get over the endless checks of ticket/passport/etc then the airport building itself is quite pleasant. Sailed through passports (with another check of passport/ticket straight after prior to security) and security then into a vast hanger of a terminal. However it looks half finished with most shops still boarded up. Almost no power points anywhere in the terminal and seemingly no Wi-Fi either. No simple shop for water/sweets/etc which is a bit unusual!

Excellent security. Left my laptops by mistake at security and went to my plane. I noticed once in the plane. While I couldn't deboard the staff and pilot called security and they were found and brought to lost and found. A friend picked them up 3 days later.

Travelled via Vnukovo for Champions League final. Bright modern airport which is being expanded. As always the local staff could do with some charm school training but on a normal day It beats the other two airports hands down. 2 specific points: the chocolates in Duty Free are usually months past their sell-by date so check each packet; and for the princely sum of £15 ea (in Roubles or Dollars) you can pay for access to the business lounge where wine is free (but beer isn't) and the sandwiches are odd - and you can smoke in there as well.

Having travelled to and from Vnukovo twice (both times flying on German Wings from Berlin) it is an infinitely better introduction to Moscow than Sheremetyevo. Immigration on the way in was as foreigner friendly as anywhere else in Russia (huge lines officious officers scrutinising every last page of your passport and visa) but everything else is great. The new international terminal is very modern lots of glass. On departure Germanwings flights depart from a gate area in the depths of the basement (or so it seems) but facilities including duty free and food are good if expensive by Russian standards. There is a branch of SberBank in arrivals but the rates are awful so try not to change too much here (just enough to get into the city centre). As for travel to Moscow the best bet is the shared taxi (transit van) to Yugo Zapadnaya metro and then take the metro. These services leave from just outside the domestic terminal (right next to the international one).

You might use Moscow Vnukovo when flying to cities within the CIS on regional airlines or catching a charter flight to Turkey Egypt etc. The airport is located south-west of the city it takes about 20 minutes and 25 Roubles to/from Yugo Zapadnaya metro station by minibus in normal traffic; taxi drivers ask the usual extortionate rates as in Sheremetyevo. The building is very small and displays a bizarre mixture of typical drab Soviet facilities and shiny renovated areas that you could almost call Scandinavian. Arriving at about 5 a.m on a red-eye flight I was greeted by a pack of stray dogs roaming the street outside the terminal but then I was able to wait for the first bus into town while having an excellent cappuccino in the new cafe inside the arrival area with plenty of seats and cheerful service from the very friendly staff. Immigration is the same as everywhere else in Russia even though this was the only place where I was asked to produce a copy of my invitation and health insurance. On an afternoon visit the departure sector which is located on the same level as the arrivals was almost deserted. Services on offer are scarce: one exchange office with ridiculously short opening times one Atm one cafe a couple of windows selling airline tickets and providing general information in Russian exclusively. Everywhere around the airport there are obvious signs of big renovation works going on I'm really curious to see what comes out of it in the future. All in all one of the most relaxed ways to/from Moscow and Russia.

Old style basic airport with Soviet overtones. Arrivals is limited with a single baggage carousel. Check over your baggage before leaving the airport as your baggage tag will be taken from you and checked against your luggage as you leave the building. Departures has a rather casual feel to Security checks - not convinced how thorough they actually are. Only a single departure lounge witha small snack bar vending machines and a newspaper stand. I would not want to be stuck here with other departing flights as there is limited seating. If you want a meal go upstairs before you check-in to a small snack bar - ask for the menu as it is not obvious that meals are provided.

Waco Regional is not a bad airport overall. They only have one flight which is to Dallas but I have heard rumors that United Express is resuming flights to Houston. The reason I have given it 8 stars is because their flights are always delayed or late. My advice to travelers flying into Waco is to have patience. The baggage claim takes a while. The car rental facility is not bad for a small town. Overall I think the airport shows good quality.

Very nice very small domestic regional airport. I arrived from IAH (Houston) on a tiny little Saab 340 and I collected my luggage and was outside in about 5 minutes! I also departed there for IAH with eventual connection to LHR and was surprised by the very welcoming attitude of the Continental staff. The security staff seemed less happy to be working but I was through in under 3 minutes. It's a nice little airport with a nice little cafe and a few static displays to look at. It's also used by USAF so it's common whilst waiting for your flight to see an F/A 18 land or depart.

This is the home of Regional Express (rex) and is a significant number of services offered by QantasLink. However despite this there are no lounge facilities and there is only one general store/cafe/newsagent/everything else in the terminal that operates limited hours. The facilities were all  and the concept of crowds and queues appears to be a foreign concept as only small planes operate to this small country airport. Its clear that recent terminal renovations have geared the terminal up for larger aircraft with room for security screening. In doing so extra facilities would need to be added (premium lounge tea/coffee making facilities). All in all an easy airport to use (realistically it's just a room with a few side rooms) and would happily use it again.

Wagga Wagga is a regional airport serving a town of 70000. All was good except that our flight was delayed due to Sydney weather (that's not an issue) but the snack bar closed during the 2 hour wait. There is a soft drink vending machine but nothing for food or snacks. Oddly there were instant coffee and sugar sachets on the tables but no hot water. Large plasma screens whiled away the time and there were enough seats to stretch out and have a nap. It's the home base of REX (Regional Express Airline) - a snack machine and hot water would be good.

I used Wakkanai Airport to fly out to Tokyo Haneda. It is located about 30 minutes away from Wakanai city. There are only four flights per day by All Nippon Airlines - two in and two out to Haneda and a city in Hokkaido. The three storey building is clean modern and spacious. Check-in is on the ground floor second floor is the arrival and departure gates and third floor is the viewing gallery. Gift shop and a small restaurant are on the second floor just next to the security/departure. The airport is on an open field with no other buildings nearby. Wakkanai Park which the Japan Cup - sled dog racing - is held here annually in the winter is opposite the airport. Like most Japanese regional airports Wakkanai airport is very much under utilized. The ground staff are polite and efficient.

Arrival process was very chaotic. Two immigration officers working for 2 planes that landed simultaneously. Luggage arrived 40 minutes after arrival, which is unacceptable for such a small airport, considering that it was also recently refurbished. Check in is just as tedious at this airport.
I've flown through roughly a hundred airports, and this is the only one that disallows me to take my wine bottle opener on board. Outrageous.

Due to flight cancellation due to heavy fog in Poznan, I had to use Warsaw Chopin airport. The airport seats are hard and too cold no cushion. At night nowhere to sleep, lights are too bright. Other aspects like staff courtesy commendable. Food is fine.

Actually this is the worst airport I've ever experienced, I was first greeted to getting yelled at by TSA for not listening to them when they weren't even speaking English so I didn't know what they were saying, and then my flight got delayed by 6 hours, but because it appeared many flights suffered the same fate, we were  laying on the cold, concrete floors covered in junk with overfilled bins. I realized then that there is basically no space in this airport, barely any food options or anything, and it's just a horrible experience. Only redeeming factor is that the wifi is good.

This is the second time in the last month that my fully functional suitcase handed to the luggage arch, has been destroyed by the staff, who probably throw them, this is a scandal, If someone doesn't want to work they shouldn't destroy someone else a property. Does anyone even control this?? I'm talking about flight today from Warsaw to Gdansk and the same happend with another suitcase day 29.08.2024.

This for sure my worst transit experience over many dozens of terminals where I stopped by. Never seen this extreme rude attitude from airport staff. Toilets have no running water in the taps but innondated on its soil. LOT staff are unsmiling, military ordering passangers what they have to do. The terminal has not enough space to sit. In sum, this airport is an ugly face for the country. In any case, I will never go through this airport again!

Very depressing airport building. Unfriendly staff. Screaming officers. Toilets not clean. Food lousy. Very outdated. Half an hour extra delay because the plane was half loaded, staff left while the suitcases were on the platform. Fortunately only transfer. Will never come here again and choose another route.

Unfriendly place, expensive overrated and untasty foods, much staff missing in offices, intended to help passengers, no place to stay overnight for reasonable price (I do not count the expensive Marriott across the road), only one spot to charge phone, but no USB port there.

Gate 45, there is little shop called 1minute. There is an unpleasant lady working there, cannot speak English and not even trying to be nice. She was super mean with my little daughter because she was holding something we would buy a minute later. In my opinion in such as international airport they should have pleasant people working to give nice experiences to people or at least kids. The minimum should be that they speak little bit of English.

Control and security staff are rude and intolerant to kids. Lady at the control gates was so rude to my daughter which had issues to scan the ticket, didn’t allow me to help to translate and and ashamed small child that she doesn’t understand foreign language. Very unpleasant experience

Security guys did not speak English. They were very unprofessional for one tool they took everything, did a complete mess from the bag 3 times and did not let to show even that it was. The tool was on the side pocket 20 min scanning the bag, while the told was on the side pocket, horrible. Not even decent place to make the check on the middle of the line, shouting on me for the skate tool like a committed the crime, the tool was not even sharp.

Terrible airport. There is not enough space to sit down, you have to sit on the floor. Smoking room with the door open, so everything smells like smoke. The toilet smells like a public toilet. Very unpleasant staff. I wish you would start changing things because it's a horrible experience.

Horrific experience. A very crowded airport and very few seats. The staff is rude. Toilets are dirty and the worst of all the water is scalding hot. Can't wash hands properly, my child could not wash hands at all. Very little soap.

Small airport not staffed to cope with volume of passengers, long queues for security and even worse for passport control. It took over an hour to get through both checkpoints. We nearly missed our flight to Manchester arriving at the terminal 1hour 25 minutes before flying at 13.30. There was another Ryanair flight to Stansted leaving at 13.40, with only 3 passport booths open to cope with over 350 passengers.

Why would an x-ray security guard be so rude? He asked where I came from and I answered Norway. Surprised by the answer, he asked again with contemptuous facial expressions, "Norway?" I think he didn't like my appearance because I wasn't blonde and blue-eyed. His repulsive and sarcastic looks, his looking at my appearance and asking me again if I was from Norway. Are these behaviors really humane? Why do you marginalize people? Who are you to judge someone else by their appearance? Almost all the comments I read are full of negative experiences. I hope an official takes these complaints into consideration. I will not use this airport again.

This review is about the security staff, which is being particularly rude during luggage check. I forgot to put the perfume into a see-through bag so when I got it out of the backpack he took it and started screaming at me “what is this?!” as if I was committing and offence, then he threw it against the tray on the counter which could have easily brake the glass bottle. I consider this behaviour as unprofessional and unacceptable.

Worst airport I have ever flown from. It's tiny, not fit for purpose (they had to build a restaurant outside), not enough seating area, staff (especially security) are not trained to do their job, they can't speak English, they are rude and arrogant and will shout at you in Polish (?). Airport is equipped with outdated security tools, it feels like 2002 just after WTC attacks, be prepared to take off your shoes, belts, jewellery, take out your laptops, phones, keys, throw away all your drinks, and get shouted at in Polish.
Worst airport ever. Small, dirty, very expensive. But the worst thing is the staff who work there. Rude, aggressive.
Uncomfortable, poor facilities, dirty and crowded. Dirty smelly toilets. Such a shame at the end of our trip as for the rest of it, I found Poland to be so clean and pleasant.

Very unpleasant and rude member of staff with an attitude during airport security process. I witnessed him making rude comments to the person in front of me such as “if everybody was taking as long as you we would have been here all day” and telling him to hurry up. Then was again making unpleasant unnecessary comments when it was my turn.

This was our second time using the airport, both extremely disappointing and frustrating. We have travelled to many other airports in the past and never been treated as bad as this airport. I understand that travelling can be difficult and dealing with customers is not an easy task, but the way those people treat others is unreal. I wouldn't dream to speak to an animal the way they spoke to us. All because we couldn't buy a plastic bag (as the machine wasn't working). I will definitely make everyone aware to never use this airport in the future! Worst experience ever!

A very pleasant airport. Modern, spacious, very quiet - the building has good acoustics to dampen internal and external noise. Tasty food, free drinking water - you need to bring your own bottle. Also interesting, in the general area of the terminal you can spend time in the Flyport - an interesting educational area about aerospace. Efficient service, smiling and helpful staff. All in all, highly recommended.

Very nice new airport approx 100 km from Warsaw. The airport is easy to navigate, the staff is very helpful. There was no queue to check in or security control, so it was good for family travel. We  ate a dinner in the airport's restaurant: the meal was tasty and there was a large selection of food for children. There is also a small playground for kids - nice thing if you have some time to spend. The airport is very clean and quiet - the terminal has a very good acoustic capabilities and there was no noise when we were waiting for the flight. On the arrival journey everything was very quick, just few minutes from the airplane doors to the luggage claim and city exit. The car parking is just in front of the terminal building, it's much cheaper than at Warsaw Chopin airport, there's also a bus station just next to the terminal.

This is a very large and well maintained airport located in Virginia. Given the size of this airport with its main terminal and then midfield terminals, give yourself plenty of time to get to your gate(s) especially the midfield terminals. On arrival I had to take the mobile lounges to the main terminal. The mobile lounges have frequent service from midfield terminal to main terminal. No more than a 5 min wait. Restrooms in baggage claim are were very clean. Departure was from Terminal C which necessitated using the labyrinth of escalators to get to the AeroTrains which run underground. When I lived in Centreville VA, Dulles was my airport of choice over Reagan National

Dulles Airport is located in Virginia and bit far from Washington DC. Very large and well-maintained airport, very clean. Few sitting places. Immigration process takes long time. Boarding bridge works as bus to the airport terminal. Taxi and bus services are there.

Having read reviews here I expected a nightmare, but everything went very smoothly. Terminal A seems to be new and very efficiently organised. Staff friendly and helpful and lines short. It was a quiet period, so it might be different at Thanksgiving and other busy times.

The worst airport in the world. Us Customs and Border Protection - who manages this institution?  1 h 45 min waiting on passport control. In Los Angeles it was more than 1 hour. They don't treat tourists seriously but we, the tourists spend our money there. Fortunately on my list only San Francisco is left. Then I will avoid travelling to this country. There are more interesting places in the world.

Going to Washington Dulles Airport is easy when departing and arriving, regardless of connections—good staff, lounges, and great AeroTrains and Mobile Lounges to connect different terminals. They have good food in various terminals and airline lounges.

This airport is the worst design for an airport. Who cares if it’s architecturally significant? Always horrendous traffic to drop off or pick people up. The over the top threatening ways the traffic police rushes passengers and treats them like criminals is not seen anywhere else in the world and I’ve traveled aboard a lot to see family and seen it all. They need to move some of the airlines to a separate building to spread out the load of cars and people. Try to avoid this airport at all cost, it will ruin your travel experience every time. Not to mention having to walk through a maze for miles in addition to taking ground transportation or tram.
Very poor range of restaurants. I did not even look at any shops, they all looked uninteresting. The airport is cold, the toilets without soap. Terrible place.

I made the mistake of flying international out of Terminal 1 at Dulles. Thursday evening flight, I arrived at 4 pm. There are meant to be four restaurants, but two of them (Wolfgang Puck and an oyster bar) were boarded up closes. Carrabas was open until they told me the bar was closed. Bracket was the only place to get a beer left, and they have exactly zero electrical plugs. On a long international flight, you need power. I ended going to Volo Vino which had a plug (horray!) but not beer or spirits, just wine. I knew Dulles was a terribly managed airport, but this experience takes the cake. There were thousands of people in the terminal and nearly zero places to sit down and eat. Don’t ever ever fly international in or out of Dulles. It’s like it’s stuck in time from 1960. The reason I rated it 1 instead of 0 or -3 is because it was clean. There are plenty of places peddling their wares of course, but that’s about it. If you do get stuck flying out, you might consider bringing along a Sherpa and some oxygen. It’s not the airport staff’s fault either, it’s management.

After long trip from Copenhagen we about 200 passengers were directed to funny “bus” - packed to the limits and very hot. We did arrival at what looks like United Airlines hub. We are Global Pass/TSA members so we got our face screen and after we had to pickup our luggage to place it back on the conveyor for transfer? There was no screening, no one checking why we had to do this? After we were directed to TSA check - why? We did our Global check which should include TSA? After a long wait we arrived in terminal where we had to walk fast the full length of terminal to catch our connecting flight. There was no place to sit and most of the restaurants had long waiting lines. For anyone specify for one’s arriving for the first time in USA this Capitol airport is total embarrassment! It looks old, dark and dirty. Airport management needs to invite Secretary of Transportation to visit this place as a regular passenger without any preparation for his visit.

Worst airport WiFi. Has been the same since 2010 - no improvements. No cell coverage so WiFi is the only option - and it’s horrible. Plan on no connectivity and if you get it - it’s a bonus. Bring a hard cover or paperback book or a pillow and you will be happy. Plan on answering email or making a call & you will be sadly disappointed. If I could give a negative 1,000 rating I would. This is the 21st century. WiFi is cheap - use the surcharges to fund an upgrade. Your customers, employees, and vendors will be thrilled !

Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport  is a well-designed and highly efficient airport that makes traveling a seamless experience. The terminal layout is intuitive, making navigation easy and stress-free. With a wide range of dining and shopping options, passengers have plenty of choices to enjoy before their flight. The airport is clean, modern, and offers a comfortable atmosphere with ample seating and well-maintained facilities. Security is well-managed, ensuring a safe and smooth travel experience. Whether you’re on a quick layover or starting a journey, DCA provides convenience, comfort, and efficiency at every step.

Upon arriving to airport, it took a significant amount of time for operations to have a crew park the plane. This caused several people to miss their connection. The valet checked bags took more than 20 minutes to be returned. The gate attendant had to call operations in order for anything to be accomplished. Our departing aircraft had to call 3 times for a pushback from the gate in order to taxi. DCA is amazingly inefficient.

This review is limited to Terminal 1. This terminal is very convenient as all of Southwest's gates are in one location which means connection times of 45 minutes is more than enough to catch connecting flight. As I had a very short layover, I did not access Wi-Fi. The terminal was crowded mid-morning but there's plenty of seating. The bathrooms are very clean.

Having lived in northern Va most of my life I remember when Dulles airport was built. The plan at that time was to close National airport for a number of reasons but unfortunately it was never closed. Now, although the terminal has been renovated the entire facility is out of space, it is jammed into a virtual labyrinth of ramps and access roads. For that reason I despise flying in/out of DCA. Car rentals are underground and that process is complicated. Once someone figures out how to escape the airport invariably you end up in heavy traffic often at a standstill. Dulles is so much easier. Ground transportation to DC and elsewhere in No Va is much easier on the dedicated Dulles access.

I used this airport several times past few years. This time I was traveling to Greenville, SC. I found the Airport was improving in terms of services and facilities. This airport is not too large one, but it has all basic facilities. Moreover, it is located in the central of Washington DC.

This review applies only to Terminal 1 (Arrival & Departure). For one of the busiest days of the travel season (Sunday after Thanksgiving), the terminal was busy but surprisingly uncrowded. From the boarding areas, there are views of the airfield and parking apron. Seating is plenty though at busier times there can be a dearth of seating. Food options are limited given the size of the terminal. To order food, the iPads which contained flight info, links to newspapers and magazines have been eliminated. U now have to us a QR code to scan the menu from your phone. WiFi service is excellent. Easy to connect and fast. There was barely a wait to go through security with TSA-Pre. The bathrooms on both arrival and departure were clean with an attendant cleaning the bathrooms frequently. Terminal 1 lacks a lounge, nonetheless its a good terminal.

This review applies to Terminal 2 only (American Airlines). Transited through a rather busy Reagan National. There are great views for the airfield from the D concourse, terminal building and E concourse. The walk from the end of D concourse to the end of E concourse is rather long and with only a 40 minutes connection, I made it to the connecting gate in E concourse with 10 minutes to spare. Overall, a good airport and terminal to transit through.

I was disappointed in the fact that I wished to purchase an alcoholic beverage during my layover with Southwest Airlines and found out that the only purchase option was with a smart phone. I don't have that type of phone and there wasn't an available restaurant that could accommodate me. I feel that was discrimination for the public that doesn't use that type of phone. What are you doing to accommodate that portion of the population? We're not all what you would like. if you want us you need to make it easier.

Arrived in time but getting a gate took an hour, and same happened when going from Washington to New York. This has got to be the worst airport. Waiting on the tarmac for an hour both ways is preposterous.

I live in Alexandria, VA. I do not travel very often but I made a trip to Tampa, FL. this past Memorial weekend. My review or complaint is about the public restrooms service in DCA, small spaces, uncleaned, sinks clogged, broken faucets, no refilled soap dispensers, no coat/purse hooks, in resume a restroom service failure. DCA is the capital airport! What a shame! When I was in Tampa Airport waiting for my flight back to DC, I used the restroom, it was almost impeccable, also I saw an airport staff with a checking list. Time to improve DCA authorities!

Flew Waterford to Birmingham on 18th January 2015. Nice little airport staff very friendly. Small cafe before departure excellent coffee and light snacks. Security and boarding very well handled. An enjoyable experience.

WAT-BHX. Car Park in airport a total mess no spaces. Airport staff outside terminal smoking. Security staff friendly however departures hall hot and stuffy. Little shop had a lot to offer and friendly staff. Will use Aer Arann again but not Waterford Airport. Five euro charge to depart a cattle mart.

First time to use this Airport and I have mixed feelings.The poor signage makes this a difficult airport to find on a first trip. However it is a rare pleasure to be able to park mere yards from the terminal! Mind you at 8Euro a day it is far from cheap. Yet the automated pay machines do not accept 50Euro notes or Laser debit cards. Staff are very friendly and the small size of the building is makes a pleasant change from most other airports. At present catering is limited to drinks and snacks. Beware of one outrageous thing: each passenger is required to pay a fee of 5Euro at check-in to fund the future development of the airport. Nowhere during the booking process is this mentioned. Furthermore when other busineses plan expansions there is no requirement for current customers to pay upfront. I would have thought that as with most business plans additional facilities would be funded from the additional revenues received.

A great small airport. Staff pleasant even down to the security staff which makes a pleasant change from the usual bored/rude staff in most airports. Free internet in departures and from landing to leaving teh front door only 10 mins. A bus to the city would be good.

What a lovely little airport. Check in staff very helpful. top security must say and very good information desk. Pity about the facilitiess and layout of the airport despite the levy charge. Fast punctual service and with a smile.

There is only 2 check in desks in the whole airport. One small tea stand and thats about it. So if you want something more than a sausage roll. Very basic facilities at this airport no automated baggage belt only a roll along one. Pity there is not a bus service from Waterford city to it. A taxi costs 15 euro from the city to the airport. Aer Arran is the only airport using this airport due to the size of its runway.

There is no AC, no available seating, unhygienic toilets, dirty floors and rude staff. The passport control officer was extremely strict like her life depends on whether my backpack fits inside the frame or not.

It is an efficiently run small low cost carrier hub. As long as you consider it as such it is appropriate and convenient. I see it more as a kind of bus stop for airplanes to a limited number of countries. Parking is great and affordable an in walking distance to the 'terminal'. Guess total distance from car door to plane door is appx 250 metres. Services are limited and food/shops overpriced. Big airport prices here on this small airfield. Boarding procedures, check in and security OK. Kind staff.

The worst airport I’ve ever experienced! Just chose it because it’s the closest to my living place in Germany but I’ve experienced the biggest rudeness and boorishness from both the control personnel but even more from the woman working in the bar close to the gate, who she doesn’t know how to manage customers and really rude. Also the shop doesn’t have food so you’re obliged to spend 20€ for two sandwiches!

Parking in front of the aiport and you can almost board your plane. Small, short ways, no waiting times at security and passport control, quiet (since our flight was the only one departing), ridiculous airport prices and good seating. Weeze is the prototype of a convenient regional airport (though I don't know how it would be in summer) and I like it very much. Equally easy when returning. One minus: I think the parking fee is too high.

The service at the airport was very poor and the airport itself was not clean. Moreover, it was impossible from the airport to find a connection to the Netherlands despite being only a few kilometres away from the Dutch border. The airport staff was unfriendly and gave me wrong directions to the station of Weeze.

We fly frequently from Weeze Airport. If you know all it's flaws it's doable, but I would not recommend it to anyone. First: why is it called Dusseldorf Weeze? I heard from many people that they were at the wrong airport. Dusseldorf is not even close to Weeze. Second: If you have to drop someone off or pick someone up (5 min) you already have to pay 2 Euro to even get on the terrain. Third: Parking is ridiculously expensive. And you have to calculate half an hour extra to find a parking spot. Last: My latest experience was very stressful. I had a declaration from my doctor that I am pregnant. Ryanair would not let me through because it did not say 'fit to fly'. After tears and a few calls to my doctor they finally let me through, almost missing the flight and causing a lot of stress. Must say the airport staff were very friendly. Now: My parents just missed their flight. They had to pass security before 8.25. They were there at 8.27 (because of the parking problems). Ryanair were okay with letting them on the plane, but the airport staff were not. There was even a family with small kids and a baby whose luggage was already on the plain. It took more time to get the luggage off than let those few people through.

Niederrhein is losing some of its advantages as a small airport. Parking cost today are on the same level as Schiphol. (Not so ) funny experience: For going to the gates after security you are forced to take the steps to the first floor going though the shop and then go down again another step arriving just a few feet away from the first stairs just separated by locked glass doors.

Why is this airport called Dusseldorf Weeze by Ryanair? It's extremely far from Dusseldorf and buses only go every hour. If you want to go by train the bus to the train station also just goes every hour so I had to take a taxi to get to Dusseldorf. Airport is okay before the security but after security there's no good food to buy only very expensive donuts and bread rolls and it was very cold. The boarding system is terrible; we had to wait outside in the cold after showing our boarding pass. Never ever do I want to fly on this airport again if I have to go to Dusseldorf!

This airport is mainly used by the low cost carrier Ryanair and the package of both is simply unacceptable. Rude and money chasing airport staff - 2 Gates open for 12 flights. During the peak summer months the complete infrastructure is far away of providing a minimum service to customers. But for those only flying once a year and focussed only on minimum price this may be still an option.

The airport is OK though its parking facilities are horrible. I entered a crowded parking place with hundreds of cars parked anywhere outside the indicated positions. After quite some time and not finding a free space I also parked my car in the shoulder. Two weeks later the parking was still crowded with cars parked anywhere but my car was gone. It was towed away and I had to pay a serious fine to get it back. Completely arbitrary and unclear policy. Very customer unfriendly. Avoid Weeze if you need to park your car.

A small airport staffed with helpful friendly people. Since it is not usually a "layover" airport the restaurants and shops are limited but adequate for the size of the airport. Every time I travel through it seems the level of English and/or Korean spoken by staff increases. Money changing capabilities are limited.

Weihai Airport is an efficient modern airport that contains international and domestic flights within the same building. Arrived at WEH Airport from ICN. Left the aircraft via air-bridge. I was pleasantly surprised by with number of counters opened at passport control that handled the passengers very quickly. After clearing immigration I waited for less than 5 minutes for the luggage. Arrived back at WEH a week later for flight to ICN. The check in staff understood English and took to effort to confirm the destination of my ticket and luggage. Security and passport control was also a quick and efficient process. I was amazed with the facilities at the airport terminal given the small number of international flight currently being handled by Weihai. The departure hall included duty free and other shops restaurants and television for the passengers. The Airport was modern and clean. The staff were friendly. The process of arrival and departures seemsed less stressful and time consuming than larger airports. Also being a smaller airport there was plenty of parking and no traffic congestion to and from the airport.

Staff tried to say we had made a mistake assigning our kids regarding our only infant. How ever we booked our travel flights to New Zealand and around New Zealand under one booking with no problems until we reached leaving New Zealand on our last flight. One and half hours to check in bags.  Customs hold up with both parents, with no thought on who would supervise our young children. Airport is shockingly unorganised and staff are not aware of the live environment. More than happy to go through procedures, obviously if their are children involved there needs to be a little more planning and patience.

I waited at the airport for a long time because my flight was delayed for over three hours in the evening. The incredibly nasty security woman continued shrieking "oy oy oy" as I waited in line, not realizing that she was calling for me to put my luggage in for scanning. She even said, "Stop petting my dog," to her coworkers while being boisterous. These personnel seemed unfriendly, therefore I hope they are taught in effective communication with us passengers.

What a joke of an International departure area. Not enough seating, only one area to buy hot or cold drinks and only one person serving. Line of 10+ waiting to be served. Only 1 lot of toilets - long line for ladies. Only a few seats with an outdoor outlook - so depressing - wish I had stayed in the domestic terminal longer. Will avoid this airport at all times from now on.

Very rude airport security staff as they allowed only one 200ml milk sachet for my 2 year old toddler. They said only one milk sachets allowed for 3 hour duration. Who are they to decide how much food should a baby drink. I had an additional 3 more 200 ml sachets. Both Sydney airport and Wellington airport as per the formal guidelines allow unlimited food for the baby. Literally the worst baby friendly airport I have seen. What if the flight is delayed before take off or before landing. Nobody wants a crying baby on the plane for sure. While the same quantity of milk was allowed inside new Zealand while returning back to Australia they asked to throw the milk out.
Checked in this morning lady on the customer service floor was extremely helpful and professional couldn't do enough for us.

What a terrible “International” airport. Disgusting. You should warn passengers before they go through security and go and spend two hours sitting in the international airport from the domestic. Nothing to do! Nothing to eat. One small cafe, one subway with one person working and serving at the same time and broken fridge and no cold drinks. Inadequate seating, poor facilities and lay out. Absolutely the worst airport I have been to.

A disappointing review from the one (Blue Lady) food stall I used. Overheated milk, tough food, and a poor response from staff who seemed focused on themselves their music rather than their customers. The big screen update was slow (had to check with the airline gate, whose response was timely). Airline security staff (numerous members) gave a poor impression of their professionalism when on a break.

Plane arrival NZ 254 2.45PM. Time cleared customs and immigration 5.00pm. Over 2hrs. Enough said, totally unacceptable. The flow on effects multiplied, pick up, transfers, hire cars. Thanks Wellington, really smashed our family of 6 day. Useless WIFI to fix above.

I was flying home to Queenstown on 14/1/23 for a 8.30am and was lining up at security with Christchurch and Auckland flights they had one security line working. Christchurch flight was first and people were panicking as they were calling out the final calls. There was a man on security checking people and screaming at the customers, I’m 50 years old and have never in my life experienced a rude aggressive man like this before, my 11 year son has autism and he yelled at him to get through the screen, my husband had to tell the man to calm down as my son cried, I honestly don’t know why nobody on the security said anything to him. A Chinese family in front of us were screamed at as well. I totally understand the short staff issues but please have a nicer friendly people in security as this is part of New Zealand.

Ridiculous. It took 30 mins to get through security. Totally inadequate capacity. I was already in the queue when the first boarding call was made. Twenty minutes later I was still miles from the security inspection area when the final boarding call was made. What a joke.

Wenzhou Airport is for me one of best airports in China. The New terminal 2 is very big and very beautiful, the check-in, security check and boarding is fast and easy. At this airport they start the automatic check-in and it is fantastic and very simple. The airport staff are kind and happy to serve you.
The new terminal is really fresh and at the domestic departure, some airlines merge in the same area and you can check in at any queue. Everything looks good.

This is a great airport and the T2 terminal is newly established, everything inside this airport are symbols of a modernized airport. Staff were friendly and helpful in helping directing me to the baggage claim area upon arrival as well as help me check in efficiently (by asking my seat preference, which I haven’t experienced during check in before). Only disadvantage would be the Wi-Fi in the airport, when I arrived in the airport I do not have a Chinese mobile phone, and in order to connect to the airport WiFi I need to have a valid Chinese phone number so I could receive verification code, unlike my transfer flight in Guangzhou where I could simply connect to the WiFi using my WeChat account. Overall my experience with WNZ is great, but please fix the WiFi issue so international traveler can connnect to the WiFi.

This is a wonderful airport. Staff providing good services to pick up luggage when arriving. It has a good transportation centre with taxis, bus routes to downtown, and shuttle buses to other cities near Wenzhou. Many shops in the airport selling products with affordable prices. Wifi is fast. This airport is expanding to have another much larger terminal by 2017.

The worst airport in America. Even the basics are impossible. Flights delayed only to be cancelled - rebooked on a flight with no chance of getting your bags. Incompetency from this airport and its staff.

I am deeply disappointed in what Westchester Airport has become. I have flown out of this airport hundreds of times as a business and recreational traveler going back to when it was a single counter and one desk for all of the airlines. While excited to see its growth, my recent trip on January 23rd left me flabbergasted with what I saw and was subjected to. We arrived at Westchester airport at 5.50am on January 23 for a 7.10am flight and didn’t get through the horribly backed up security line until 7am, so we just made our flight. We were luckier than those booked on other flights that were actually left behind. When we arrived the line was backed up to the coffee shop and the pre-check/Clear line was wrapped around the baggage carousel. It was ridiculous. Travelers 2 rows ahead of us had been in line for over an hour since security was barely moving. I inquired with the TSA representative standing in front of the pre-check line why the third belt wasn’t running and was informed it was allegedly “broken”. Although in my travels I don’t ever remember seeing all 3 belts open even when security is backing up. By the way, it was still “broken” when we arrived 1 week later. The attitude of the TSA worker was nothing short of atrocious and exacerbated the problem. As I mentioned, the line was sluggish at best. To complete one lane took over 20 minutes. It wasn’t until passengers started getting very heated with the TSA agent in front of the pre check line that they did something about it. That’s right, they called the police. Didn’t try to remedy the problem, just called for back-up. Her attitude was terrible and she took no action to resolve the problem. When I had spoken with the TSA Agent I had asked why there was a such back up, she informed me that it was now the way the airport was operating and they are leaving 20-30 paid passengers behind daily because they cannot get them through fast enough. This is unacceptable. People had arrived with plenty of time before their flight and were left behind only to be rescheduled. What are you doing to remedy this with TSA? As the 100+ people in line were becoming more and more heated and vocal, the line suddenly sped up a bit. They delayed one flight by 15 minutes and still left about 25 passengers behind. Another flight to Ft Lauderdale did the same. We were fortunate that we made our flight. Does this not present a security issue with unattended bags being loaded and sent on plane without its owner? As I was going through security there were 4 TSA agents huddled in the back laughing, joking and mimicking a passenger that was upset about a 2 hour wait in the security line and missing their flight. Again, unacceptable! I now know why there was a delay, they were all busy chatting in the back near the office instead of helping to move the lines. Needless to say, I am more than disappointed with airport’s lack of remediation for these TSA issues they apparently are aware of and the policy changes. I am someone who chooses this airport as my primary and have added to its growth by continuing to fly out and recommend that people to utilize this wonderful airport. I feel for the gate agents that now have to deal with irate passengers on a daily basis. I’m also concerned about the safety of all passengers with unattended bags being flown. I do hope you’ll receive this with some gravity as this was one of the worst airport security experiences I have had world-wide.

This is the worst airport I have ever been to in my life. The lack of post-security amenties makes it even worse. It is bland and there is almost nowhere to sit in the "gate". It is convenient to land into, but it is a nightmare to fly out of. You are better off going to JFK or LGA.

Worst TSA experience ever! I am a corporate pilot flying for a fractional ownership program, with Known Crew Member (KCM) status. I airline weekly, sometimes multiple times a week to commute to wherever one of my company’s airplanes happens to be. Even before my company had KCM, as I would go through TSA at dozens of airports (big, small medium) I would just show them my flight crew badge, place my bags “between the bowels” not take my electronics out, and walk through the metal detectors instead of having my body bombarded by radiation through the X-ray machine. Also, I’ve never had to throw out water which is huge, when you’re flying somewhere to pick up a plane to fly late into the night. (As I happen you only be doing today). Today while airlining from HPN to ATL to pick up a plane, TSA Made me go through security twice (shoes off and electronics out) shot me through with radiation (twice) and dump out my 3 bottles of water, patted me down twice, and swabbed my hands and tested it! What should have been 10 minute process turned into a 30-40 minute process! This is insane! This never happens at other airports, big or small, KCM or not. This is totally unprofessional, and someone in management needs to retrain their agents. Treatment like this can easily cause a pilot to miss their flight, creating major problems for flight companies.

Most of the staff were okay. One lady in particular was very pleasant but there was a gentleman at the checkout desk who was unecessarily rude and unprofessional. When I handed him something he practically grabbed it out of my hand. Then, when I thought I was done with him my sister and I are waiting to board the plane. I was tired so I didn’t notice that he was putting suitcases to the side to put under the plane. Even still, it’s not the customers duty in my opinion to be on top of those things. If I was in his position I would’ve kindly alerted the customer that I was collecting the bags. Anyway, my sister noticed so she hands him my suitcase and when she did that that’s when I realized so I handed him mine. Instead of leaving it there he makes a comment about my sister being more attentive than me. True or not, I think it’s out of line to be making those kinds of snide remarks to customers and if you’re going to have a personal conversation with customers I feel that it should at least be something nice. But, that was just the one person so I hope it’s only him.
I really love this airport! It is small and very quick. Regular security is quicker than TSA Pre! The Airport has nice entertainment, and its a nice regional airport.

Although Westchester County Airport is awfully small compared to JFK or Bradley, it is amazing. It has car rentals, an actual baggage carousel, five airlines going in and out of there, local planes accepted too, and even have 8 gates. This is so much better than some small airports I've been to.

Nice little airport, there are barely any food options, just a sushi bar, diner, 2 convenience stores (all pre security) the only thing that is post security is a tiny place that has yogurt and granola bars to eat for breakfast. No information regarding departing flights. Very small, cramped and crowded waiting area. Upon arrival it took 20 minutes from stepping off the plane to being in my car which includes getting 3 checked bags.

Ideal location only short haul flights offered. Terminal needs drastic expansion. Too many flights departing at the same time causing people to be packed like sardines in one terminal. They need to invest and modernize.

Great restaurant upstairs that serves main course meals and happy to work in your time frame for your flight. Modern building and brilliant to depart and arrive from if you live anywhere nearby. Just make sure you check the kind of aircraft being used for your flight. If you do NOT want to be on a small regional or propeller plane your choices are limited! Nothing better than arriving at HPN and getting home locally in under 15 minutes!

Very small Airport on the Northern German Island of Sylt. During Summer Season served by Lufthansa and Air Berlin with flights to major German Cities. Only a handful check-in Counters and during busy hours on weekends - which means 4 or 5 planes within a couple of hours - long lines. Upon Arrival only one Baggage Belt and Baggage Claim Area crowded. But due to the small size of the airport and short distances from the planes to the Baggage Claim Area baggage arrives very fast. Staff very friendly and efficient; waiting lounge can get very crowded during peak hours. Small shops and one nice Cafe/Restaurant. Short distance to Parking Area; Delivery service by Rental Car Companys. No public Transport. Overall a different but nice experience. And flying to Sylt gives You a great chance to visit the island even from Southern Germany for only a few days.

Vast upgrade from the previous terminal. Far more space at check-in counters, baggage claim, and security. Baggage service is efficient. Ample seating in the gate areas. But there are few food options, especially if you are on the concourse after 5 p.m.

I have no complaints whatsoever about the new airport in Wichita. Lobby is wide and bright with helpful staff at the information desk. There is a wonderful exhibition on the aviation history of Wichita on the second floor. Go to the airport early so that you can read all the displays. Not a wide assortment of food choices, but good enough. Car rental area is well organized and staff is well-trained. A most pleasant experience there. The signage for getting to the city center and on the highways could be better, but I think that is the responsibility of the city, not the airport. A very pleasant airport to use.

Nice, friendly airport.  Quick check in usually, efficient security screening, everybody keeps moving.  Gates are easy to find/navigate.  Short on food options, nice bar after security near Gate 4.  Good coffee/bagel bar near Gate 2.  The new airport is about finished.  Will be nice to see the improvements.  Eisenhower is the new airport name - excellent choice.

Got to be one of the world's smallest airports. The terminal is the size of a large living room. You can literally drive up to the front door and walk in. This made the airport very efficient and easy to use but don't bank on having a gourmet burger before your flight! You will have to make do with a snickers bar and an Irn Bru from the vending machine. To be fair it was very clean and is a good hub for the northern extremities.

I absolutely love the Wilkes-Barre/Scranton International Airport. Small enough to accommodate us easily, friendly staff, and yet large enough for us to easily reach any destination. We especially love the fact that they now have Breeze Airlines which will allow us to increase our travel from this airport. Great move on both parts.

Great airport for small aircraft (Twin Otter/Cessna) used primarily for safari transfers. Courteous and friendly staff/security as well as satisfactory washrooms and a nice snack bar. Wilson airport is a welcome change from the chaos of Jomo Kenyatta. Note - due to its small size, there is no souvenir or duty free shopping.

It’s clean, staff are pleasant enough but the seating is awful. There are only two bars/restaurants - both of which are packed all day. The lounges have been “closed for refurbishment” for months with no sign of opening. Nobody seemed to know why. Awful place to spend 2-3 hours when we’re back we will go to Walvis Bay!

Staff are extremely rude. Airport staff also confiscated a normal lighter which is allowed on your person, and instructed me to place it in my check-in baggage. Airport has a monopoly on shuttle services with price fixing. They banned all taxis and have a full monopoly, overcharging for a 45km trip. A trip that would normally cost R90/N$90/US$6, costs R380/N$380/US$25. Total ripoff and not African prices, especially for locals like myself.

Check your Covid test proof requirements carefully to void this chaos.  I entered Windhoek Airport on 10th Feb and left 22nd Feb 2022. On arrival at Windhoek Airport, before customs, I was asked for Panabios Covid test results. I had everything else including vaccination certificates, the RSA Lab negative Test results - all were unacceptable. Queues of arriving passengers on the Airlink flight also did not have this Panabios hardcopy report. All without the Panabios proof were then required to establish internet connection using phones, download the Panabios App, retrieve their results, and present this to the authorities with a bar coded reference number. Chaos ensued as some passengers did not have internet on phones, many others could not get into the App, remember, or get passwords etc. etc. Unnecessary frustration, irritation and anxiety occurred as a result. Clearly the Panabios requirement was poorly - or not communicated to passengers before they left. Then on my return, I diligently got the Panabios report in hard copy, presented it to Airlink check-in staff who said it was not acceptable - they wanted the lab report NOT the Panabios document. I did not have it in hard copy and they did not want to accept my phone lab report email as evidence, so once again I ended up messing around until eventually I was able to get a lab report printed through the Airlink office. OR Thambo wanted the Lab report, NOT Panabios. The lack of consistency in terms of the Covid proof of testing is unnecessarily frustrating. If Windhoek requires something different to RSA, can we at least be better informed. Recommend passengers download and copy both the Panabios and the Laboratory proof of negative status to avoid this frustration..

What a horrendous experience (again). Getting through WDH airport has now become a mission and I'd suggest to anyone planning a trip there to bring a camping chair, sandwiches and something to drink, because you'll spend up to 2 hours getting in and out of the airport. A new immigration system is to blame I understand. Forget trying to do a day trip to Windhoek, what with the queues and the lengthy drive into town, you'll probably only get an hour's work done. This airport does nothing to enhance the image of what is otherwise a very pleasant country to visit.

Windhoek is a small airport with an increasing number of flights. Facilities are limited but everything you need is there and seemed sufficient for numbers passing through. Arriving early, departing late on Air Namibia from/to FRA arrival took less than an hour and departing security was a reasonable time. Staff were efficient and friendly. Much easier to pass through than major airports.
Windhoek airport is small but clean and really well organized. The only restaurant at the check in area is situated at the Arrival area, food is fresh and delicious. Facilities are quite good.

On arrival we had a long wait in the queue at 3pm. It appeared as though most of the staff were on lunch. We had a few elderly people in the queue who had difficulty standing for so long. On departure a female staff member had an earpiece for a cell phone in her ear was enjoying her conversation and laughing. Barely greeted me and almost threw passport at me. Very hostile attitude. Officials generally were unfriendly. Two toilet seats were missing in the ladies toilets in the general area.

Windhoek Airport is nearly 50km away from the city. Most people will arrange for private transport although there is supposed to be shuttle bus operators. It is not very big and there is a decent selection of shops air-side. The waiting hall is spacious enough most of the time. The problem is during peak periods (notably in the early morning when a bunch of flights leave around the same time or when the Windhoek-Frankfurt flight leaves) that it falls short. The immigration counters and the single x-ray machine (the second machine appears to be for show only) backs up considerably.

Again in WDH July 2009 no changes at the airport. Lost and Found queue very slow go there as soon as possible when you realize that your luggage is lost. Immigration very slow too. Note that you have to fill up a form after security control when departing (it takes some more minute and you need a pen!).

The main lounge is quite large and it is clean and bright. There are some shops vat refund (enter the "Custom Office") tables outside the airport to enjoy last minutes of Namibia. Not many flights but in the evening there are departures to Germany and South Africa at the same time and the departure lounge is really too small for all passengers leaving! Expect to sit on the floor so wait in the main lounge until is possible. Duty free is expensive a poor bar and a very small gift and diamonds(!) shop. There are only 5 or 6 gates but often the screens show the wrong flights! There is a smoking area often crowded too!

Why don't you have more people de-icing the planes? Do you not know that it is cold and snows in Winnipeg? Flight delayed at least an hour because you don't have enough staff. Ridiculous and totally incompetent.

It is October 10, 2019, 7.00 pm and we have been waiting for one hour to be deiced on the Delta flight 2840 to Minneapolis. We are not deiced yet and there are very very few trucks deicing the planes. This should not be happening in the city that of all the cities in the world has to be ready for events like this. It was known for a number of days that the snow was on the way and this kind of delay is unacceptable and will lead to a number of passengers not making their connecting flights. At the end someone should be responsible for this mess so that it does not happen again.

Nice lay out. I got to the airport in the morning. I just had a bit of some confusion as it was my first flight. The automated ticket booths were convenient and quick. Security was a breeze. No queue, the security personnel were nice and polite. I didn't feel intimidated. The gates are lined up along the back of the building nicely. The Tim Hortons was next to my gate. Washrooms are clean. They even provide you with sanitizing wipes and cleaner to wipe the seat. The stalls are private with no big gaps in the stalls. There's tables with outlets to charge your phone. Coming back, it was alright. The luggage carousels are at the main floor where the front doors are.

Winnipeg to Abbotsford. I flew with Swoop for the first time and I absolutely loved it. There were no delays and Winnipeg airport was not busy. The signs were easy to follow. Airport crew were very friendly.

On arrival into Winnipeg on a WestJet 737, in parallel with three other similar, fully loaded planes, I discovered that the contracted only available taxi supplier, Unicity, had no cars available. I waited, alongside approx. 45 others for one hour before we were all picked up. The support from Airport Staff was just not nice and in the end my call to the taxi company was "the first they'd heard of the demand/need for cars. If you are arriving into my fine city home, send someone to get a taxi while you wait for luggage, you won't regret it.

I fly out of Winnipeg many times. Although it's not the best in terms of stores and flight choice, it is very spacious, bright, and traveler friendly. It's one of the nicest airports I've traveled through. Massive glass windows give a wonderful view of the planes and surrounding area. Check in is usually quick and easy, although the self serve machines are useless. Lots of parking and room to drop off as well. Security is quick and simple dropping you in the middle of the terminal. Moving around isn't hard either since it only takes 5 mins to walk the entire terminal length. The only issue I have with this airport is that there isn't many food and store options. The "food court" has a Pizza place and sandwich store, along with the necessary Tim Hortons (3 in the airport). They sell some snacks at the usual travel stores though quite expensive. Wifi and staff are great along with bag claim/customs being quick to get through. Overall great airport!

Much nicer than the concrete block that was YWG, open and bright. Staff were friendly, check-in a breeze and clearing security has never been a problem for me. Despite being an International Airport it is small, even if you have to walk the furthest distance (Gates 11, 12) you can be out of the Airport in 5 minutes if not waiting for checked baggage. International travel out of YWG is quite limited so the International secure side is small, MAYBE 4 gates, with just a couple Restaurants including the "required" Tim Hortons kiosk. Others have complained of the lack of moving sidewalk but don't let that concern you, as I said the longest walk is less than 5 minutes from gate to exit so a moving sidewalk would actually be pointless. While shopping and Restaurants are an improvement over the old Airport, they are still very limited when compared to most other International Airports. YWG serves it's purpose but it won't wow you.

This is a good smaller airport to fly in and out of. The terminal is new and it shows. Also staff are friendly and helpful. This terminal is also well located as it is actually on the outskirts of the city, not outside of the city. In addition it is served by local transit. However, there is one accessibility issue. While the lanes for commercial providers are covered and wide, there is only a 2 lane uncovered pickup area on the arrivals level for private vehicles. This results in congestion during heavier arrival times.

I have been to over 50 countries and usually fly standby which means I spend many a day and night in an airport. Some are more secure than Winnipeg and some are much less secure. Not once have I ever been kicked out of an airport secure zone on an over night layover. So now I have to stay up an additional 9 hours to ensure my bag and passport do not get taken. Ridiculous.

This is my home airport, whilst small, it has a basic array of services and amenities you would expect from a larger airport. The terminal looks pretty fresh and is thoroughly modern. There isn't much landside although there are a couple of shops and restaurants for basic needs. The security areas move promptly and the transborder security is easy to get through because there aren't that many US departures. Once you're airside, the domestic/international area is quite good with a decent array of shops and restaurants. This is a small airport so you're out of luck if you're hoping for luxury goods, but you can find many of the basic items you might need. The seating areas are bright with plenty of glass to let in the prairie sunshine. There are two lounges including a small but comfortable Maple Leaf Lounge. Transborder is a different story. While it's an improvement over the tiny TB area in the old terminal, it's still a very small space with only one restaurant (TGI Fridays) and a Tim Hortons kiosk that only sells coffee, donuts and not much else. Baggage claim runs efficiently although it's not in a secure area which always makes me nervous. Customs tends to process people quickly. Transportation is easy with a good array of car rentals onsite and very convenient bus transportation downtown. The airport is not that far from the city centre, so a bus is actually a pretty good option. Also, there is free WiFi and washrooms are generally clean and well kept, if somewhat small. There are three airport hotels a short walk outside, and at least two of them have restaurants. All things considered, Winnipeg Airport delivers what you would expect it to.

Unbelievably rude and incompetent staff. I was travelling to London Stansted on the 28th of September. Ladies at the gate on the Ryanair, especially one (I’m afraid I don’t have her name-unfortunately), extremely unprofessional and rude. Quite a lot of passengers were upset. I would suggest change of staff, otherwise the reputation of the airport and airlines will dramatically change. I will never use this airport again.
Rude, surly staff. Camera at immigration doesn't work properly. Even trying to find out how to complain was an unpleasant experience.
Horrible treatment given. Staff are not adaptable and were not empathetic or considerate. Just wanted to be difficult and unhelpful. On the other hand security checks were very nice.

Our flight from Athens (23.10.19) was delayed 2 hrs and redirected from Kraków due to the fog, so we landed at Wroclaw airport at night. We had to wait for a replacement service to take us to Balice. We collected some “tickets” from the check in counter to be allocated on the one of three buses going to Kraków. We were waiting for that transport for over an hour without any information when they would eventually arrive to pick up the passengers, not even sure if we have time to go to the toilet. None came to us to give us any information about the busses and when I finally decided to go to the toilet I met a member of the airport personnel, who gave us the tickets before, and I asked how long it would take to wait. He answered without hesitation than it’s only 20 more minutes. So why did we have to wait for that whole hour guessing the time with no clue? When the buses finally arrived the drivers had no idea what to do with those “tickets”, people rushed pushing to get inside. The ticket system didn’t work at all! Such a joke! The driver shouting at people in Polish, disorientated foreign passengers didn’t understand a word. When a lady started talking to him in English to asked a question about stopping in Katowice, he answered ironically in Polish “We are in Poland, we speak in Polish. Not English”. A person who works with foreigner passengers, really? Terrible customer service, no help at all for non-Polish speaking passengers! So disrespectful! Not even mention the airport staff (a young man in his 20s) who was shouting at us in English (at last!) “You bought tickets to Balice airport, you’ll go to Balice!”. I tried to explain him that I had asked someone at the airport about this possibility and they had said something different. Such a lack of communication between the staff members! Such a chaos and mess! At last we ended up on the bus going to Kraków. Not even mention that the journey was horrible because a group of noisy youngsters laughing and shouting at night (midnight till 3 am) while people kept asking them politely for 3 hours to speak quietly because of late hours and tiredness. Such a disrespectful behaviour talking back rudely to the passengers. And again no help at all from the driver. At least we got to Kraków safety, such a memorable journey! Wroclaw airport should really retrain their staff in customer service and basic English if they want to serve properly passengers from all over the world. Sort to say, but it was such a bad experience!

The scale of Wroclaw Airport is small but lovely. There is a lack of USB sockets in the waiting room and lack of seats for people who want to wait at the arrival gate. When it is peak season, it might be difficult to wait comfortably.

The main idea of this airport is to delay and inconvenience. Deboarding your plane via finger you then make two steep flight of stairs. No lift or escalator can be used due to layout of non-Schengen arrivals. Stairs only. Then non-EU passport holders are welcomed to the long line served by just one officer for all who arrived.
