EU passports are served by two officers who are now doing nothing since no people are in the corresponding line. The only non-EU officer works as slowly as he can spending 4-6 minutes per head. It either means that border control are unable to comprehend that arriving plane can bring 180 pax, or they just enjoy seeing that every chance to make things worse is fully used. Disgrace.

It either means that border control are unable to comprehend that arriving plane can bring 180 pax, or they just enjoy seeing that every chance to make things worse is fully used. Disgrace.

Arrival to Wroclaw Airport was fine I pre booked my airport assistance and he was there when the aircraft landed got me through passport control and out to me my booked taxi. It was on my departure that I experienced very very poor service (I have used the very twice for good reason). It was 04:00 and we waited until 04:35 for the check-in to open to deposit our case. We also had a walking frame on wheels for me and my pair of crutches. On putting the case on the belt I was told that it was over 15kgs. I explained that I had in fact paid for 2 pieces of luggage one at 15 kgs and another at 20 Kgs the check-in clerk still was trying to charge me for the case which weighed in at 20 kgs. The staff would not have it that I had paid for two cases but was only checking in one piece. Her colleague reiterated that she must charge us and I asked to see the manager who arrived and was incredulous that the clerk was trying to charge for a piece of luggage that was already paid for and that was clearly on her screen as being prepaid. That hurdle over next was my walking frame and crutches I was told that I had to take both through security which is odd because at airports the walking frame usually goes via extra large luggage portals. Never mind I went to security and of course it would not fit through the scanner no matter which way they tried. This was not my fault although I was made to feel that it was my fault lots of dirty looks etc and so on and so forth. Then came the body check - I will always set off the alarms at I have replacement hips and knee. The alarm went off and without asking I was then ordered to remove a cardigan (I had already removed my coat) I was then asked to take my hair down as I had it on top in a bun and remove all hair clips at no time was I given the opportunity to explain about my metal joints and once again I was made to feel guilty for the walker not going through the scanner. The treatment of a disabled person in Wroclaw airport is nothing short of scandalous the security. Do not get me wrong I support everything they do and what they are trying to achieve to keep us safe but really did I deserve such a woefully embarrassing experience - I think not. For sure I will not be returning to Wroclaw again.

I've been to Wroclaw Airport 4 times. It's fast, convenient, beautiful airport, doesn't matter if it is arrival or departure. The variety of shops and restaurants is adequate and the prices are normal airport prices. A very clean terminal that is one of the prettiest terminals I've been to. Toilets are very clean. Only problem is absence of air conditioning in buses between terminal and airplane, it's very disappointing and uncomfortable in summer.

I travelled all around the world. I saw many regional airports. Wroclaw/Breslau was excellent. Everything went quickly. Staff were really helpful no queues. Brilliant seats before departure. No problem with luggage. One minus - no good access to the city transport. You must take a taxi to drive to the center.
Small airport, which makes everything easier. But going through security was a hassle with lines (nothing compared to Beijing, though!). Don’t expect much of it, given the size. Very clean!

Generally efficient and courteous staff. However, security will not allow aerosol cans either in the cabin or checked in. There is no explanation for this. I have flown into and from airports in China and around the world and never had this problem but for some reason, Xi’an Airport has this policy. So be prepared to lose your aerosols, even if in checked baggage. Very limited F&B airside. Airport is at least one hour drive from centre of city. Take a high-speed train to/from Xi’an if you can.

Xi'an is a modern Airport. Quite good landside and airside retail and F&B in T3. Priority check-in is difficult to find in T3 (it is at the far-left check-in island N). English proficiency of ground staff is poor. Long queues at security. As as with every Chinese airport, security channels are terrible with lack of space to un-pack and re-pack hand luggage. Information on displays is not clear. Last time I traveled through Xi'an, passenger security check was not very thorough. Bottles of water in my bag passed without notice.
Airport very cold. No restaurant, no coffee shop and no drinks machine. 1 smoking area very far from from the gate. The announcements are not understandable. Very bad experience.

Flight from Xi'an to Beijing. T3 is huge but only few entertainment facilities and shops. A long queue in security check only 6 passageways are available. Staff in security check are rude and impolite. After the security check my paper bag was broken and no any staff apologized for it. The toilets are extremely dirty. Very bad experience and I will not go to Xianyang airport anymore.

I departed on 16th April 2014 and was lucky to make my flight. I was part of a tour group and as there were many groups trying to leave at the same time and not enough check in staff to process the travelers I made my flight with 3 minutes to spare.

Last time I was in Xi'an Xianyang airport was in 2011. I have visited many times before. There was always a Scrum outside the airport building for tickets and to board the airport buses for downtown. Returned this year 2013 a lot has changed with the airport and getting tickets for the buses. You now go to a ticket booth inside the building. Then a waiting room for your respective bus. What an improvement!

Domestic flight to Chengdu. Check-In OK and Security quick. Interestingly no need to remove laptops or belts for scanning but 100ml fluid requirement enforced. Airside a new "wing" has been built and some gates are quite a walk from the Security Check Area. Very difficult to find Departure Gate information once airside no screens as you enter and despite lots of TV screens with advertising very few with the actual flight information. Reasonable signs showing which direction each gate is. A reasonable selection of typical airport shops offering the usual variety of gifts alcohol cigarettes and snacks. Overall airport clean and tidy.
Went through there domestically June 10 and June 12. Everything seemed to work the airside men's rooms left something to be desired. All else worked including the air-conditioning.

I've been though both international and domestic terminals. The ground staff are very efficient I have to say. It looks like the ground handing agents are China Eastern Airline and Xianyang airport. However there is one thing I don't really like which is the VIP lounges are on the other side of the main terminal. Last time when I was travelling from XIY to AKL I went to the on the VIP lounge it was very inconvenient. What I mean is you can't check your bags in at VIP lounges and staffs in VIP lounge are not friendly at all I hope this is not a Chinese thing.

Very bad check-in: huge queue at Xiamen Airlines, but only one counter open, apart from courtesy Desk and check-in without luggage. Unpleasant security people: my checked-in suitcase had to be opened to check on my Swiss Army knife, and this was coupled with a long waiting time. Very limited choice of goods in duty free area, general atmosphere similar to hospital morgue.
The size is not big. Passengers can walk around easily. Signposts are clear. Employees are friendly and helpful. The efficiency of the immigration is good. It is clean and modern.
No free WiFi at airport and if you want WiFi have to OTP a Chinese mobile number which we foreigners do not have yet! Can the airport do something about the free WiFi?

Transferring at Xiamen airport is a hot mess. You need to go through immigration, exit the secure area, check in again from the outside, and go through security a second time, even if you're not even stopping in China. At immigration, they stopped most of the foreigners and questioned them intensely before letting them through. My husband was questioned for over an hour before we could go on to our connecting flight. He's lived in China for 12 years; they already have all of his information on file. But they questioned him anyway, sometimes asking the same question three or four times. Not sure if it was incompetence, lack of training, some new system, or a mandate to heighten security, but either way, it was not okay. Another family connecting from our flight was also stopped for over an hour. The husband got through, but they held the wife and their baby at the immigration desk for an hour and a quarter. They were literally going from Bali to Seoul and had nothing to do with China, but they stopped them and questioned them, collected all ten finger prints from each of them, made them submit to facial recognition photos, etc. It was a total abuse of privacy. The search at security is also an invasion of privacy. I went through the scanner and didn't set it off - I avoid wearing metal on flights to save time. But I was manually searched with a scanner anyway. She felt me all over my body and even pinched me all over - my arms, my legs, hips, stomach, extremely invasive, especially considering I had just come from a connecting flight and had already been through security. This airport is incredibly inefficient and treats passengers like livestock. Don't transfer through here unless you have 3+ hours of layover time to spend on going through the insane process.

Actions speak alot. And to log in and post a review is alot to me. Anyways, the employees are severely understaffed for the amount of passengers there are. If you are departing from Xiamen, 50% you can expect them to fly a plane, halfway turn back and tell you theres a weather issue, then take the entire passengers on 4 busses to a hotel whom they promised us was free, then start charging the folks in the back of the line for a room. I paid for the hotel btw after employees suggested us to wait till the end. I did check the forecast for the city we were landing at and it was clear at 0% humidity with 1mph winds at 66 degrees fahrenheit. In my mind, there was an underlying motive for the delay. The airport, customs, wait line queues, incosistent boarding gate changes, and management are enough for me to choose a different place. Expect to jog or run or feel rushed when transferring. Flights are very often delayed. My rating is 4/10. You get what you pay for. This quote resonates deeply. Maybe I will mellow out with time because I am still shocked at my experience. But my 20hr flight turned into a 55 hour flight. So I could have reasons for writing a post. And I am sorry for sharing my experience.

I was pleasantly surprised I didn't run into any issues the other reviews described. Yes, I did need to go through immigration again but there were absolutely no lines at 7pm on a Thursday. Every counter or checkpoint I went through whisked me through quickly and efficiently. I had plenty of time to sit down for dinner before my flight and check out some of the shops. The airport is clean and modern. Some of the seating areas at gates are not that comfortable (average), but some looked better.

This is the worst airport I’ve ever been to. I was only making a transfer back to my home country. Waited 2 hours to go one floor because they were too lazy to open the gates the the line of people going out the door. They separated my brother and I whom I was traveling with, so I had to explain we would like to be seated together. Then I was searched 2 extra times. The staff is extremely rude, racists (they hate Americans) and they also searched me as I was getting on the plane, although they already lifted my shirt up in front of everyone previously. If I had more time and I wasn’t just in transit, I would’ve complained then. But, honestly this airport doesn’t work. The atm they have was never available the two times I arrived in August and then again in November. They are poorly equipped and have a bad attitude.
Horrible airport with no options. Rude uncaring and pushy staff. No padded seating. Random bag searches aimed to make you buy a new ticket.  NO wifi

Having read earlier reviews of Xiamen Airport, I wasn't looking forward to going there and changing from international to domestic. First, whatever the airline tells you at your point of departure, you will have to re-check your bags on to domestic flights, and vice versa from domestic to international. From international to domestic, the signage isn't helpful. After collecting your bags go upstairs to the domestic check in area and re-check your bag at the transfer desk of your airline. Transferring from domestic to international, if the international check in section isn't open you just have to hang around until they open the doors. There are plenty of cafes and noodle bars. Once through the security screening go to the check in desk for your airline and re-check your bag in. In fact, at my point of departure (Changsha) they managed to check my bags through to Amsterdam but when I went to the check in desk to pick up my boarding pass for the next leg, there was my bag waiting for me to check it in. Apart from all that the airport is spacious and pleasant. Lots of shops and cafes. All the people I approached for assistance spoke good English.

I knew that Xiamen is known for being not so passenger friendly when it comes to transfering and long stayovers. I read that most of the time they won't transfer your bag onwards, meaning that you would have to go through customs and claim your bag on landside. Knowing that, I was pleasantly surprised that there was ground staff waiting for all transfering passengers at the arrival gate where my KLM flight rolled in to. They guided me all the way through security and told me that I wouldn't have to reclaim my bag at first but in the end thay said I needed to. The airport itself is quite clean and has a simple layout, although I had only seen terminal 4 (int'l flights). All the signs were in english too. So from then on it was playing the waiting game. I must say that that the amount of shops and only 1 cafe wasn't to nice. Nothing to kill time unless trying something to eat. Only staff at the gate could speak proper English. I was surprised by the drinking water fountains to be found everywhere on the airport. After waiting for 10 hours was able to check in for my flight to Sydney. Once boarding commenced there was a problem with a lot of carry on bags, so that took a while. After boarding was finished everything was ready to go until the captain made an announcement that we were going to be delayed by almost an hour due to traffic. Once the flight departed it was a pleasant journey onwards to Sydney, where we arrived on time.
Lacking warmth, lacking some basics, lacking good English-communication skills from personnel.

The airport of Yangon was very clean, with good air-conditioning, the queue for the visa was not long, so it was fast, the belt with the bags was easy to find. Good impression when you arrive. Has also a really good conection with bus to the city center.

I arrived today from Heho with a sick child, probably from food poisoning and was helped like I never thought I could. We were taken charge of by a great team of officers, nurse, doctor that took us to the airport clinic and took care of my daughter. Everyone has been great and we are really grateful to each of you. They will recognize themselves.

I arrived at Yangon airport about 8.30am today (1 Dec 2018) and proceeded to be processed through security X-ray machines. I was in a hurry and thus quickly picked-up my luggage, but forgot and left my phone, wallet and spectacles behind. It must have been about 20 minutes later at the airline check-in when I realized my mistake. I was in panic and so backtraced my steps. However, I requested the wrong counter for my belongings. But the officers were very helpful and apologetic that they could not find my belongings. I then remembered the correct counter (near row D), and there the security officers were able to retrieve my belongings very quickly. I believe they had followed strict procedures and had kept my belongings safe while awaiting my return to claim them. After a simple verification, I have all my items returned in good order. I wish to thank security staff for their prompt and helpful assistance and making my return trip pleasant.

This airport has undergone a transition from ugly duckling to something of a beautiful swan. Spacious, beautifully furnished, comfortable are just some of the words that come to mind. There is plenty of signage and even passengers on discount airlines are treated as if they are appreciated. Although it doesn't have a butterfly garden, I would compare this in ambiance to Singapore Changi, on a much smaller scale of course. Burmese charm is everywhere. The CIP lounges are spacious, well stocked, well staffed and offer a good selection of local and international snacks. I wish every airport in Asia was more like this one.

I have travelled to Yangon many times in the past and this was the first time I used the new airport extension. On arrival luggage has to go through baggage scanner (just like some airports in Middle East). Guests are also able to enter the airport too until immigration and passport control. The airport is very large and spacious, there are international branded shops and some that sell local products. The products in the convenience store were not over priced. The airport facilities are better than in some western European cities.

This review is for Terminal 1. Terminal 2 is dramatically different. RGN has undergone vast changes during the last 10 years. There remain remnants of the underdeveloped facility that once was, but the outside world has arrived in Yangon, and at least as far as the airport is concerned, it is a good thing. Customs/Immigration at both arrival and departure is reasonably fast. On the absolute worst day, you might wait 30 minutes, but an average wait will be 10 minutes or less. Lines at check in counters move quickly, which is terrific. Departure lounges are a lot nicer than they once were. Now they sport clean, comfortable spaces, dependable WiFi, and food that works in a pinch. Restaurants in the airport are not great, but if you want a decent cup of coffee, some KFC, a Burger King something or other, you’ll be ok. Souvenir and duty free shops still have a long way to do. Alcohol and cigarettes are fairly priced. There are perennially empty luxury clothing brands without customers. There are a couple of small boutiques selling attractive textiles, carvings, local bath products, delicious local coffees, etc. Services are generally more than adequate in the pre-departure areas. There is a bag wrapping counter for flimsy luggage, convenience stores, plenty of seating, free WiFi, etc. Taxis downtown should be priced out before you leave. Money Change desks offer the exact same rate as all the other places in the country, so there’s no reason to hold on to your foreign currency. The airport is still a work in progress, but leaving and arriving in this amazing city is a lot less unpleasant than a few years back.

Yangon International Airport has 3 Terminals. 1 and 2 for International Flights and 3 for Domestic Flights. This is the review for Terminal 3 (Domestic). This Terminal 3 is a new build and many upgraded from the old terminal. The airport is very clean and you can find the check-in counter very easily. After check-in the 2nd floor is for departure and the 3rd floor is for lounges. The departure hall is very large and can buy goods and many restaurants which already open early morning 4:00 a.m. The gates numbers are easily to find.

Yangon is a relatively small airport. It’s setup is strange in that you are required to pass through security just to access the check-in counters. Once in, it appears you can’t get back out, so if you’re there early, you have to wait in an area with no services and no WiFi until your counter is open. Air is circulated by fans only, so it gets pretty warm. They take security very seriously. Luggage is scanned three times, as are people. We flew out of T2, which has 5 gates, so lines were pretty much non-existent. Immigration took about 30 seconds. We used the Priority Pass Lounge, which was pretty sad and very cold, so we ventured out about half an hour before boarding. Shopping was sparse, as was food and beverage. Toilet facilities were basic, but generally clean. Gate services were good. I recommend it because it’s the only game in town.

Hugh brand new terminals both International and Domestic. Check in was the usual full baggage screening but the lines were not long. Once at check in again everything was easy, as we were a group of 7 our tour guide checked all the bags as we just sat and waited, all very efficient. Airport vast and very clean, once in departure lounge on upper level there were shops for snacks and good coffee or tea. Announcements made over loud speaker system but very difficult to understand.

Yangon Terminal 2 is very nice. It is not too large, immigration may be slow but they are friendly. Atmosphere is modern, clean and nice, including good restroom. Check in counter are totally empty at the time of my departure. Once can spend 5 minutes for check in process and wait at a few nice cafe they have, noted that you can't find anything to eat after passing immigration.

Yaoundé Nsimalen is the worst obstacle course I have encountered. Not content with the regular three hurdles of check-in, passport control and security, airport authorities have added multiple stops with random officials asking to see this or that document. It starts at the airport entrance, where you are required to show your ticket to enter. Before reaching check-in, your passport is taken from you and you are required to produce the visa for your flight destination, even though you may be stuck in the queue some distance from his desk. The journey from check-in to security involves filling in a departure form (available from an unmarked desk), producing proof of yellow fever vaccination (even though LEAVING the country), then showing boarding card and passport to another random official. Security is inefficient and random. Passport control involves waiting for a passport official to turn up (often only one booth is occupied). Once you´re through, you´re not done: you will be asked for your passport a couple more times, as well as your boarding card. There is a small restaurant on the air side, but little prospect of accessing it, since it would mean negotiating the dragon at the gate entrance again. On the positive side, thanks to the friendly Brussels Airlines staff member at check-in, who made all the difference in an otherwise frustrating experience.

Yaounde is extremely disorganised and dysfunctional. It's hot and humid and there is no A/C. Upon arrival all flights exit through one security area. At this point a lady from the Ministry of Health stops random passengers checking their Yellow Fever certificate. At the customs desk lines form for visa stamps this is extremely slow. Getting baggage out of the airport is also chaos as airport staff want to check baggage tags against passenger. Again not everyone is stopped. I wouldn't recommend a taxi there are a lot of touts. Departure is equally frustrating no clear signage so always confusion. Need to pay a departure tax. Then you go to a window in the departure hall and give the CFA to a woman who will stamp your ticket. After this you need to fill out a departure form and have your passport stamped. Once you arrive at your gate your hand-carry luggage is hand checked as are you. Then you can proceed to your flight. There are no announcements so make sure you know where you're going! Not the worst airport I've been to but difficult all the same.

Yaounde airport is remarkably large clean and well-organized for a central African airport with so little traffic. Immigration is a bit confusing because they want to see your Yellow Fever card before passport control and they ask in French. but after figuring that out Passport and Customs are easy with minimal lines. Little bit of a mob coming out and I always recommend arranging for one's hotel or host to have a driver to meet you in a country like this. Departing through NSI is very confusing. Unless you are a diplomat you have to pay a CFA10000 ($40) departure tax. At one end of the ticket counters are a couple of guys behind a ticket counter who are actually exchanging dollars/euros/francs etc for CFA's. Then you go to a window behind them to give the CFA10k note to a woman who will stamp your ticket. Then you can pass the first control to go upstairs to the gates. Someone inspects your carry-ons for size and number before you get to Passport Control. After ppt control you're stuck with little or no shopping and a small bar. My flight on Swiss arrived on time but left 50 minutes late because it took so long for ground grew to load cargo and by the response of the airport staff that was normal. No announcements nothing. Security very tight with hand checking of all carry ons after x-ray. Still everyone professional and did not seem dangerous or seedy.

Horrible customer service at FlyOne and Sixt car rental. If you have to go to Yerevan, avoid this airline and rental car company. Immigration was fine, but quite demanding about my previous countries visiting, but at least they were polite and reasonable. But the sassy clerk at Flyone was rude and the crooks at Sixt will not refund your payment if you don't read all the tiny fine print buried in the policy details.
Their airport is pragmatic, on the right size to be passenger friendly and with all major needs served like SIM cards and ATMs available. Beware of overpriced rides to the city center or your hotel.

The man working at the check-in desk is very rude and doesn't have any positive attitude which is a must for a person working in the customer service field. Besides he was unaware of the rules and regulations established by Transavia Airlines. He was trying to take 60 EUR for 10 kg of baggage insisting that I was not allowed to have it together with the 5 kg backpack. In general, most of the workers at Zvartnots airport are bad-mannered and do their best in order to get on people's nerves and make your registration much more complicated. They mostly look like cold fish than human beings working in customer service.

I had almost the same story with one review below. I had bad experience with passport control rude woman where she ask me where do you go, I said Dubai, when you arrive to Armenia then from where did you come from, which country, then she said give your visa to Dubai. I said I got already my boarding pass I couldn't get my boarding pass with Emirates if I was not resident or have valid visa to Dubai, so I show her my residence where it was on my previous passport then she took it and start checking 1 paper by 1. Then she took my both passports inside and I had to wait more than 30 minutes standing next to passport control and then was around me 5 police looking at me and ask me questions.

The main airport of Armenia has been completely rebuilt and the old Soviet style one is no longer operating. The new terminal is clean and modern, duty-free shopping is in abundance. As most fights arrive at midnight border control takes at least 30-60 min. During covid times all boarding passes need to be printed so take extra time in mind. Taxi's easily overcharge, 3000 dram should be more than enough. Overall a good experience.

I must say that in my experience the staff at the security check are doing a great job. I was flying back to Moscow from Yerevan on Tuesday 29th October. The staff were very welcoming, polite, and helpful! Moreover, while passing the security check I realized that I lost my cross, the thread on which it hung was torn, and after passing the security check I informed the security staff about it. They were very helpful and helped me find my lost cross.

Most incompetent staff at the security check, and a supervisor, who was very rude, apparently thinking he was a customs zar in the Sovjet times. They would not security check our hand luggage, as they said it was too big. In other airports this is a question which the respective airlines decides. The fact that we had arrived with the same airline with the same luggage made no impression. The problem increased when they refused to acknowledge our electronic phone boarding card, as they apparently had never had seen such a thing before. The public information system is not being updated, as the departures shown are the same as when we arrived here 3 hours ago, and all of them should have left some time ago. Our airline staff has not yet come, so instead of going to the business lounge as planned, we are still sitting in the departure hall on the solid steel chairs. This is a regretable bad last impression of the otherwise friendly and helpful Armenian people. 12th Oct 2019, 01.06 hours

I am an Australian but of Indian heritage. Upon my arrival I were asked to provide more Australian ID's and more question were asked to me about India than Australia. Immigration officer even asked me if I have any friends in Pakistan. The same behaviour pattern was followed upon my arrival. The immigration office checked my passport from every possible angle and checked at least 5 times under UV light. Customs were no different. Super dissatisfied with the quality of service. It seems like the last time any airport staff smiled was 20 years ago. Very sour experience. Never returning back.

One of the better airport experiences in recent times. This may be due to this airport not being the big hub type with all its unpleasant experiences that come with it. But from curb to boarding everything went smoothly. Friendly bar tenders, check-in agents, emigration officer and security staff. A pleasant surprise. The building appeared very well designed. For urban explorers, there's the old brutalism style icon of soviet times next door to explore from outside. Only downside is the air conditioning in the air side waiting area, too windy and cold.

The best airport in the Middle East and Europe. Staff service is very good. Check-in procedure was fast and efficient. The airport amentities are quite good, good cafes to eat something, Segafredo for coffee. Duty Free is really very big and the selection is quite large.

First impressions of the airport when entering are pretty good, there was staff at the entrance that were eager to help. However, the check in counter is then a different story. Security behind the luggage x day scanner at check in was rude and disrespectful at best. Both the person in front of me and I were unaware that we packed a portable charger in our check in, that was our fault, fine. But the security staff then shouted at us to open our luggage, he then proceeded to throw things in our luggage all over a table without a single touch of care. He then swore at us in front of everyone and pronounced that the other person and I were idiots. How this airport can put up a four star plaque with confidence is beyond my belief, I have never encountered such a toxic person in the air travel industry. For reference this was on 18/07/2021 in the evening at check in counter 10.

A small domestic grade airport that is being doubled in size. Check-in seemed to serve just China Southern flights. Was on a flight to Shenzhen, via Xiamen. After a month of traveling, this was the only airport in China that made me take my boots off to be scanned. There was several food outlets and coffee choices available but I 
did not look closely at them.

I've been to this airport several times. And as time passes by, I think this airport needs a major facelift. Terminal A was okay, clear signs but the layout was all over the place, two waiting halls in two seperate areas which is quite confusing. There were a good selection of F&B stores, the shops were good but they offer a small, thin magazine at exorbitant fares. Waiting times were good for departure but not for arrival. One baggage claim filled with 4 arrivals in one? Ridiculous. Taxi drivers would have shouted anything at you just to ride their taxi which is very expensive (a 3.75 mile drive costs US$7) Terminal B was the worst part. Leaking ceilings, queues a bit disorganized, and looks like a budget terminal or like a terminal that was converted from a conference centre. Good thing that this airport has a BRT and Railway station. Wi-Fi was quite fast. But the terminal building itself, I think, needs a major facelift.

There are 2 terminals, terminal A for most domestic flights (Garuda Indonesia, Lion Air, Wings Air, Citilink), and terminal B for international flights and other domestic flights (Sriwijaya Air, NAM Air, Air Asia and Express Air). Terminal B is smaller than Terminal A, but the facilities are quite good. The security staff and ground staff are good. There are some shops that sell food and drink with reasonable prices. There are also some toilets and ATM for the passengers. Some minor issues are the lack of electrical socket for charging your gadget. The seat in the waiting room is adequate in quality and quantity. There are some traditional Javanese ornament in the airport.

The Airport has two Terminal, old Terminal for Domestic only is called Terminal A, and the new one for Domestic and International is called Terminal B. There's no different security check for Domestic and International at Terminal B. First security check before check-in, second security check for boarding gate, then for International Departure you need a third security check, usually you need only two security checks. It's tiring with all the queuing. No food and drink shops at international departures.

This is one of the worst airports in the world (domestic terminal). Not only is it filthy, crowded, and utterly disorganized, but if you arrive at any time after 9pm you cannot even buy a bottle of water anywhere in terminal b. There are also no water fountains. Your flight will also be delayed, and boarding zones will be ignored so you will push and shove and wait a long time to get an the plane. Even at the airport in Port Harcourt, Nigeria, you can buy a bottle of water. That airport is a tent. This one has many vendors, but they were all closed.

This is the worst international Airport I have come across. Everything was so cramped in the arrival hall through immigration and up to exit that I was concerned about the safety of my family. Any kind of commotion can lead to a stampede. Similar experience while departing (I was going through domestic departure so no immigration) - A single check-in counter and a cramped waiting hall. One must also be careful about the Taxi services as the official taxi counter is quite a distance from the international exit. There are several other Taxi services waiting to fleece the first timers. Opt for the Rajawali Taxi.

A small airport with a single crowded waiting room. Only one restaurant and its food is expensive. The check in area and the arrival area is very crowded. I would recommend using Adi Sumarmo Airport nearby when visiting Yogyakarta.

Pleasant but rather old-fashioned airport. Most of the traffic is domestic and the terminal copes well with this. A good range of shops/refreshments in the departure lounge area which is well organised. You are very close to the aircraft (including the runway) so it does not feel claustrophobic. My only gripe would be the totally constant announcements of both arriving and departing traffic needed because the information on the boards was unreliable. No airbidges so you walk to the planes but this did make for speedy boarding. We had prearranged transport so I cannot comment on local transportation but it does have a train station which is rarity in Indonesia!

This small airport is totally overwhelmed by the amount of traffic it handles. For international passengers after checking in and paying the departure tax you proceed to a waiting room prior to passing immigration and security. You are basically waiting for a prior international departure to clear the next holding room. Once the prior international flight has departed you then proceed through immigration and security. The next small holding room only has capacity to deal with one flight at a time and there are absolutely no facilities in the holding room other than restrooms. If you're hungry or want to do some last minute shopping visit the few meager concessions in the check-in hall first.

Noticed some improvements from last visit about 3 years ago. Basically it is the same structure but only interior is much fresher. I noticed some new shops inside and outside. Inside the arrival hall there is a traditional Javanese music band playing live music with traditional Javanese instruments. It is quite a welcoming nice charm. There is dedicated taxi stand outside the domestic arrival hall. Get a voucher and walk to the taxi pier. It is quite organized.

Very small nice airport. There is no shops at all no airco check in was OK no queues at immigration. The only downside is to get to town was quite difficult as when I was there there was no any taxi's or buses so had to wait for almost 1 hour!!! Staff was friendly but facilities poor.

Yuzhno-Sakhalinsk is an old Soviet style airport, built I believe 70 years ago when air travel wasn't too common. Both domestic and international check in areas are very cramped and not big enough to cater for the B777's that arrive. Queues can sometimes be seen coming out of the main entrance as people try to check in to their flights and as with all Russian airports you have to go through security checks before entering the check in areas which slows entry into the airport down. The check in staff speak limited English and are fairly inflexible to help people. If you are flying direct to your destination great, if you have connections it significantly slows the process down and the majority of the time the staff can't (and won't) check bags through to your final destination and wont provide you an onward bording pass. There is very limited seating and refreshments in the check in and pre-departure lounges and almost no facilities to buy anything before you fly. There is a tiny 'cafe' in the domestic departure area and a slightly larger cafe in the international departure area with a small duty free shop selling very expensive duty free goods. There are no airbridges connecting to planes so all boarding means a bus trip to the plane or a walk to the plane. This slows boarding down considerably too. International arrivals is one of the worst I've experienced - it is paper based and slow. Even with a flight of 100 people if you are foreign it could take up to 1hr to get through immigration as preference is always given to local Russians. There is a newer domestic arrivals hall with 1 baggage belt which is a huge improvement on the previous hall, but still poor compared to any other airport I've travelled through. Overall, if you have to fly to Sakhalin you have no choice but to use the airport, but if you had a choice you wouldnt use it. They keep saying they will improve it but in the 3+ years I've been traveling through Sakhalin I've seen very few worthwhile improvements.

This airport is in dire need of an upgrade. There is a tiny check in area (we flew domestic today) with 4-6 check in desks but there are no lines or barriers and in typical Russian style there is no coherent queue. People are lining up all over to get in the correct queue. Upstairs there is a nice cafe called Lime which does decent coffee although double the usual cost. Still it is the only decent place to sit and wait. Then you go through another security check into a waiting room (full no seats left) then downstairs again to board the actual flight. This downstairs waiting room was also packed so we stood for about 30 mins in total with our squirmy 3 year old. All announcements were exclusively in Russian and we had to guess when our flight was called. No provision for families travelling with small kids that we were aware of.

Getting out of the airport arriving from a domestic flight without baggage is very quick - just walk across the tarmac and out the gate. Departure is very chaotic and confusing. If leaving on business class on a domestic flight you should go through the international departures entrance but there is nothing to tell you this. Once inside there is very little indication of where to go to check in or to board and the monitors providing information about the flights are only in Russian. My departure was delayed by two hours but this wasn't clear to me and I was getting worried trying to work out where I should be thinking I was about to miss my flight.

Rod Hocking seems to have had a particularly tough passage through UUS - it's usually not that bad. If you're arriving from outside Russia it's important to get close to the front of the plane. Inbound immigration can be lengthy and the form will be in Russian. (Cabin Crew may have an English crib-sheet). After immigration you have to register with with the Police and the baggage does take some time to come through with no priority for Business Class. I don't know why they didn't use the carousel when Rod arrived - there is a small one in international arrivals. And you will have to show your Bag Tag before you can exit. All pretty slow and not very organised and usually very crowded. You just have to be patient and rarely will you be out of the building within an hour of landing - 1.5 hours would be average. On international departures arrive early (at least two hours before departure). Airport Tax is RR600 and has to be paid before you can check-in. Outgoing Immigration is more spacious than incoming and there is a bar in the departure area which may or may not be open. You're going to have to walk to the plane so in winter you need to wrap up. Yes UUS is bit chaotic and far too small for the current passenger traffic but it does work (just about). Don't expect it to be efficient don't be late or in a hurry - and be patient.

Yuzhno -Sakhalinsk (UUS) On a trip ICN/UUS/ICN had to pass thru the airport twice. On the way in those passengers in the know bunched up at the door of the aircraft and ran for the entrance hall. Those (like me) who hadn't a clue about what was coming walked normally and were confronted with chaos. I know the Russians are paranoid about security but this was ridiculous took over 3 hours to clear a 737 load; fortunately we were the only aircraft on the ground at the time. The fire truck took about 5 minutes just to start lucky (there were no fires). The baggage hall was interesting all baggage arrived on a tip-truck which backed up to a slide (and you guessed it) up-ended the tray and baggage into the room (no carousel). Customs Hall is something else one over eager passenger put his head around the door before he was called; flashing lights and sirens erupted. You didn't need to speak Russian to get the gist of what he was told. Fortunately I had a Company courier waiting for me outside with a name board. On the way out similar system. this time however the flight was delayed due to heavy snow. No information given by staff no flight info boards all passengers JUST WAITED. In my case it was about 8 hours; this must be a fairly common occurrence in January as the same courier was with me and refused to leave until the aircaft was actually on the ground (most impressed). Food was available for purchase at a cafeteria acceptable (by Russian standards) but certainly not flash the stairs leading up to it were a bit scary their condition screaming for maintenance (won't happen). Seating inside the departure area is simple but acceptable. Overall the airport is (only just) OK.

Airport terminal is new. I have arrived late - after 22.00, so we were only passengers in the terminal. I had to wait for more than 15 minutes for my baggage, which was odd because only 20-ish passengers were waiting for the baggage. There were very few to no staff members which was almost disturbing. Overall experience: Fine, but it could be much better.
This is horrible, there are not enough seats at the airport, people are sitting on the floor everywhere even though there is plenty of space to install more chairs. Toilet is broken.

I am a frequent traveller to/from Zagreb airport and find the experience consistently disappointing. Taxi service - a rip off! Airport staff are unhelpful, rude, probably underpaid and definitely in the wrong customer facing jobs. Very poor food/drink choices also - way overpriced. Today, I ordered something to eat from the pub menu, the staff member told me they don't have food and pointed at the place behind me to go there. I mean, I could see couple of people half finishing a burger & chips! Admittedly, there was a queue, he was on his on at the bar so, maybe he just couldn't be bothered. He served 'randomly picked' tea bags to a customer in from of me, who clearly ordered English Breakfast tea (from the printed menu on every table!), the gentleman corrected him and pointed out this is not what he wanted. The staff member replaced it with another random picked tea bags, shrugged his shoulders as if to say - take it or leave it. The customer was an English person, he accepted the wrong tea bags - completely rising a above it. The abrupt and unfriendly approach needs to be addressed at every level and people (from security, check in, shops, eating/drinking places) dealing with the public at this airport should be educated in providing the basic customer service. They need to be reminded they are not doing passengers a FAVOUR, it is their job. It's a disgrace.

This airport is called international but service is ridiculous. We checked in 2 hours before our flight and only one line for security check was opened. There was several flights around same time. People were stressing out they will not catch their flight. If you want to call yourself international airport you need to provide more efficient passenger flow. Second line was opened only after people started to complain. Extremely disappointed.

Airport is nicely designed but poorly managed. It gives one feeling that the airport staff collectively, from check-in desk to security check-in are either totally disengaged with the customer or on the other end of the scale, utterly rude in typical post communist fashion. Client service and politeness, friendliness is somewhat of a mystery in Zagreb. Which is really pity as it has a lot to offer. The Airline Club Lounge is dark, uninviting, poor choice of food as well as poor choice of drinks. Croatia could and should do better as it has a lot to offer, instead it is rather depressing to be there presently as a tourist.

Awful experience. Drop off area is awful and barely sufficient for small traffic Zagreb airport has. Connections to the city comparable to Tirana and Skopje. Public transportation bus every 30 min. The only place where one can get fresh water is after security check but it is not working for days. The water on the pipes in the toilet is smelly (I would say on purpose so the duty free can sell more). Toilets always have wooden piece on the entrance door and are open. Toilets are smelly and poorly maintained. Queue for security check requires you to walk around for 60 meters althought there are barely 5 passengers in the queue. One can feel that the management of the airport is very bad. Passengers are on the last place.

Arrogant, unprofessional and rude passport control police officers, without a smile or greeting. Do not expect anything better. Welcome to the Balkans. Although they think highly about them selves being western European country, with western standards, they are far, far away from the west.

The special assist for disabled passengers is terrible. Passengers are removed from the aeroplane and asked to walk through baggage and passport control. We were two disabled passengers and when I stated that we required wheelchairs we were told that it’s not a long walk. Having used this airport many times I know this to be untrue and insisted on wheelchairs and assistance to which he rolled his eyes, tutted, and replied “There are only five if us and seven wheelchairs!” To which I replied “Well you better go and get them then”. The first passenger was attended to after 10 minutes. I waited half an hour. Once escorted to the Cafe Nero at the exit I ordered a coffee from the bar and when I asked if they could carry it outside to a table (5 metres away) they, yet again refused, even though I had a walking stick and a small bag. By the time I got to a table I had spilled half the coffee. One cannot help but feel that disabled passengers are considered a nuisance here. Very disappointing

Zagreb Airport is a small but clean airport. The airport staff were generally friendly, helpful and efficient. Moderate queuing time. Seating area was a bit crowded during busy hours and lacking charging sockets around seats. Fast and free WiFi.

Been waiting in line for passport control for two and a half hours. Worst experience I have had. Only one controller for the whole queue. Some official kept coming with other passengers "hand in hand" and placing them in front of the queue. And to make things even worse, that single controller kept leaving his work post every now and then.

Overall: Modern looking airport, but inefficiently designed. Inefficient and incompetent customer service (with an average IQ of about 70). Recommendation: If you want to travel to Zagreb, use Graz (Austria) airport and rent a car; or land in Vienna and take a 1.5hr, super modern, rapid and inexpensive train to Graz and then rent a car. If you travel to Istra (northern Croatian coast), take a direct plane to Pula (Istra) or Trieste (Italy). The less money you spend at Zagreb airport (and Croatia in general), the better you'll feel. (1) No access to free phone service. For example, if you are from outside of the EU, and do not have local cell phone service, and need to call airline company to change the ticket, you can't! There are also no tellers where you can go and ask to use a phone. (2) Wi-fi is disastrously slow. At 0.5-1.5 Mb/sec, this speed is insufficient to browse internet, change your ticket online, or make a wi-fi call. (3) Foreign airlines have no permanent tellers, so after check-in is closed, there is no way to get in touch with that specific airline. (see 1 and 2 above). (4) The local personnel behind "information desk" (ID) gives incorrect or misleading info. I was late for a check-in, and teller told me to walk across the airport to talk to some other person, who then referred me back to the Information Desk. This roundabout, circular walking of customers from one teller to another, without anyone assisting the customer is a signature of Croatian bureaucracy! (5) Car rentals are found out in the open, a 10 minute walk from the airport. There is absolutely no overhead protection at any of the rental agencies. If it's raining, you'll be soaked wet, as will your luggage. (6) Beyond coffee/drinks, there aren't any healthy food options, so if you're stuck at the airport, your best option is to fast. Munich and Vienna airports have excellent super/mini-markets. (7) Check in is a bit chaotic, with local travelers acting like they grew up in a barn (pushing, not knowing how to form a line), and local employees not being able to issue clear instructions. (8) Almost the only way to and from the airport is by car. There is no rail between the airport and the city. (compared to Paris, Vienna, Munich etc..). There's a bus service between main train station in Zagreb and airport but the service is unreliable and irregular. On a positive note: (1) It's a modern looking airport (2) Waiting lounge outside on a terrace has with big, comfortable cushions. (3) Premises are clean.

Absolutely joke! Not enough shuttle busses to get passengers off planes and then onto planes - gridlock! Flights with similar flight departure times given gates next to each other so absolute chaos for seating etc. So slow getting passengers boarded so inevitably leading to late departure times

Delayed 4 hours, not a fault of the airport but had to get water. Our six euro voucher from Tui barely covered a bottle of water as the café only put out Evian to purchase. Reading the list of drinks which should be available, there should have been bottled water at just over one euro but they hid that behind the counter out of sight and had none out on display. I asked for the cheaper water and the staff behind the counter seemed really put out that I asked and took forever to get it and I could see the staff talking about me as they were looking at me/the water and looked really fed up I asked for it and just raised their eyebrows - they still didn't put any out on display despite having plenty as my husband also had to ask for one later in the day - obviously they do not want us to buy their cheaper products and there was simply no other option to get water anywhere else.

Was booked in as requiring Disabled Assistance with processing through departures. Due to the Covid problems & paperwork required to depart the airport after our holiday. The company I booked and payed for (the Covid day 2 test), failed to give me a code for the Passenger Location form). I spent 3days of our holiday just trying to get this code. (Without this form we could not fly home). Finally just before pickup time I finally got this code and partially film 1 of two of the forms. I thought that's great & can finish the two at the airport. How wrong I was & got to the stage they were calling us on the speakers. I cannot thank the two young Special assistance girls at the desk. We managed to board the plane 10 mins before take off time. Had they not been so understanding and helpful we would not have flown home. Zante Airport, you have 2 brilliant workers on the Disabled Special Assistance.

Had assistance at airport on the whole this was ok. Was taken through cheack in then to duty free and on to gate through the last passport cheack to the gate area. Normally you are told to be back at the gate if you go shopping 40 mins before flight but when we went to go and get our duty free we were told we were not allowed back into airport so me and my party could not get anything. I told the assistant I wanted duty free but she took no notice and did not explain the situation to us.

Wow. We were amazed at the transformation of this airport in the space of 1 year since being taken over by a German company. Previous check in desks removed and brand new ones on a different wall, far more. Check in was seamless and plenty check in desks. A new security area which was quick and smooth, apart from the aggressive female member of staff shouting at passengers and rolling her eyes, brand new duty free area. Such an improvement. Heraklion airport in Crete could take some tips. We were stesssed thinking about our return journey but the airport has vastly improved. Arrival area is also spacious and easy. All toilets in the airport have been renewed.

This was the last time we put our foot on this airport. Of 20 toilets, there was one with door (but there was no paper, and did not lock + that there was feces on the wall) The airport is not made to handle the number of passengers is today. Does the fact that tour operators must make more demands, otherwise it is they who are losing customers in the end. Never more Zakynthos Airport.

I have never experienced anything like this before. Zakynthos airport is a dump. Far too many passengers for its capacity. Toilets dirty, no locks on doors, no hand dryers, not enough seats. You have to check in even though we already had done on line and had printed boarding passes in our hands. After a 40 minute wait for that we had our baggage labels put on and had to take our cases and join another queue to put them through a scanner. This had a bored girl "watching" the screen. Security quite quick but then a very small waiting area for all the flights with not enough seats and more dirty toilets. Duty free prices a joke, as were prices for food and drink. We couldn't wait to get on the plane and out of there.

Zakynthos is a grotty airport. The toilets are horrendouse with many not working and dirty. The whole place needs a make over, I don't think I've visited a worse airport. Duty free is a laugh, the perfume I wanted on the plane was £29 and they wanted €57 in the "tax free" shop - rip off.

Arriving from Gatwick at 10am was a bit of a nightmare lots of queues 3 flights arriving about 10 minutes apart. The baggage reclaim decided to stop working for a good 20 minutes and when it started again he conveyor belt was not going round but the luggage was still coming up cue everyone doing the airport's work to get the luggage round the conveyor belt. People were standing on top of the luggage belt to make sure the luggage could manually go round because otherwise the suitcases just jammed up. We asked several people for some help that worked at the airport only to get ignored. Our return to Gatwick was definitely easier though. We were checked in through security in no more than 30 minutes. Which left us plenty of time to relax in the spacious seating area. It's very open lots of windows and shops (slightly overpriced but what do you expect?) We boarded and flew home quickly!

Things have improved vastly since the new terminal opened and the new baggage claim is very good far faster than Edinburgh or Glasgow. Return journeys can be a bit of a pain but the new departure lounge is reasonably good. Airport staff we've found to be generally polite and helpful. Our tips for a happier return trip: Buy any food or drink in your resort. Don't be in a rush to go through security to the departure lounge - it's much nicer outside or in the check-in hall. If you smoke there is a smoking room in the departure lounge. Think about investing in a portable balance for weighing your baggage as if you are overweight it could cost you.

The staff of Zanzibar Airport, pretending that items in the luggage are illegal, requested money from me. When I told him that the items are not illegal and I don’t want to give him money, he insisted to gave him anything, it doesn’t matter what. The shocking and humiliating surprise wat at home when I discovered that, after my departure from the security area, that the employee re-open my luggage, took some personal items from which were in it. Unfortunately, I experienced such negative and humiliating experiences both when I arrive and I depart from Zanzibar.

New international terminal is ok but nothing special, 6 departure gates in total so not very big. On arrival most people did VOA - visa on arrival, so queue to get it and then another queue to pay it took quite long. On departure check-in and security went smoothly, on airside there were only one shop and a café open so there wasn't much to do. Wifi is free but works on/off, not good for streaming anything but good enough for basic surfing. At least terminal is new and clean with decent air conditioning.

The airport is very chaotic, on arrival we stayed in a long queue, after some time the airport staff came to let us in, the whole document check took a lot of time, onle 2 offices for 300 people. At departure, we were 20th in the chech-in line, and it took us 2 hours to chech- in our luggage. This resulted in a delay of our departure time of chourse. I don't know if the issue was with the airport staff or the charter company ( Animawing) as the other queues went faster. They mixed the tickets from 2 different destinations for the same company, then they searched for our names on printed sheets. At the immigration check , they took all my fingerprints but none of my husbands. Security check was the lowest ever possible. This was my worst airport experience so far.

Where shall I start? How about with the fact that in order to board my outbound plane, which I had a confirmation code for and a receipt, they claimed "There was no reservation." This resulted in visiting four "offices" and "officials". I was at the point of missing my flight and therefore my safari. I am embarrassed to admit I burst into tears. When I produced a $100 bill, they "found" my reservation. I was routed through Zanzibar on another portion of my trip to Africa and another mess! The rude gate agent would not listen to me when I said that my flight was called-I missed my flight and guess what? Yep - more $$$$$. I was also ripped off by the airport money exchange, their transport to the resort, and phone data purchase. Never, ever, ever will I go back to this island and I tell everyone of my experiences. This is a stupid and short-sighted way to treat tourists. For a temporary "win" they lose any future business and with media, it is an ignorant thing to do because the message gets out to the world.

Unpleasant. When I was there, hundreds of passengers were crammed into a stifling room without air conditioning. It's the kind of heat you can't imagine unless you experience it. (The small duty-free shop is air-conditioned so I spent a lot of time examining bottles of spirits and picking through trinkets.) Arrival wasn't much better. There were three different entry forms on offer and the staff member I asked said I should fill in all three. It turned out only one was right.

The infrastructure is poor as expected. However, this can be managed if the weather is not hot. What makes the airport one of the worst is the staff. Unfriendly service almost everywhere especially in the lounge. This is better than the ground floor service (still bellow any standards). The airport is pretty chaotic and the security is more than questionable.

I did not experience any line ups or other issues experienced by others. The whole check-in process was easy and the staff was helpful in checking our bags all the way back to Canada. We visited the lounge upstairs but the lounge was very outdated with stale food. Not recommended but it is better than downstairs waiting lounge.

The worst airport I have ever seen! No organization, huge queue, everyone asks for money, temperature inside is so hot you can’t imagine. I asked to switch on the aircon and they laughed at me for my request. Never again.

Horrible airport, everything is chaotic and people constantly want money for everything. The security searched my husband’s bag (checked luggage) and decided that a mosquito repellent and a deodorant must go to rubbish cause of the inflatable liquid sign on them! You must be joking! When I explained to her the toiletries and personal care items are allowed and she could as well take another 5 items from my suitcase following her logic thinking, she said I need some education! Who is the one who needs education? Can’t even do her job properly. Or maybe she wanted me to “buy out” the items I was about to lose? Hah! The funny thing is that everybody who wants to visit Zanzibar will have to go through that horrendous experience as there is no alternative airport. Good luck to whoever is flying in the future.

I am lucky to have travelled to many remote places with small airports. Zanzibar is the worst airport I have ever visited. Arrival meant waiting for luggage in a barn in tropical heat as bags were hauled in 2 by 2. Departure started with queuing outside the airport for half an hour in heat for all passengers to put all their luggage through only 1 scanner. The entrance for this allowed only 1 person at a time to sort their stuff. Inside was hot, dirty and provided no information on flights. No one knew when planes were going or seemed to care. It would have made a good comedy sketch but this is an international airport handling thousands of passengers.

Zaporizhia airport (Ukraine) is probably the most original and exotic airport I flew to and from. The airport serves a million people city, and is unbelievabely small. It did not see any main restructuration and reconstruction since the middle of soviet era, and this airport is a real step back in times (but it will change by 2020). I have nothing bad to say about this airport, because it is impossible to compare with european standards. The terminal consist in a small building, where everything is included into a very small space. It deserves a visit. Landing in Zaporizhia is landing in the 50's. You walk to the terminal from the aircraft, then you pick up your lugguage straight on the tractor (no conveyor). For check-in, you also bring you baggage straight to the tractor because there is no conveyor as well. Then, there is a very small cafe, and a unique passport control, and you arrive in a waiting room that you've never seen before. To go to the plane, you walk down outside stairs, and walk to your aircraft again. A very interesting experience!

Modern but slightly odd airport. Arrival was easy with aircraft arriving early bags almost beating the passengers to the terminal and out of the building even before plane was due to land. Baggage collection area was big and empty being at odds with the rest of the rather cramped airport. Bus to the city centre was a "local" ie a very zigzag route via shopping centre railway station and just about everywhere else. Took 45 mins compared with 15-20 for a taxi but at less than 2 euros it was entertaining interesting from a people watching viewpoint and worth the inconvenience. On return to the airport we took a taxi from the hotel in the centre and it was only 17 euros compared with the 20 -25 euros that others were suggesting. In the terminal I noticed that the landside area is very narrow and could get crowded if the numbers at the airport increase. The departure lounge is also pretty small and  oddly enough is accessed straight through a bottleneck of the only shop /cafe (very small). Then there was passport control followed by 180 passengers waiting for the plane but with only about 150 seats. All in all modern but surprisingly small.

Pretty new terminal opened about a year and half ago. Its an improvement on the old terminal. Not many flights and 90% of them from Ryanair. Basic regional airport that does the job (not huge lines to check in or pass security). Dont go through security unless your flight its about to depart since in the air side there is only a little bar/cafeteria and two vending machines. not too many seat if there are two flights at the same time. In the land side good bar and resto. Bad Bus connection to the city and expensive taxi service (25 EUR to centre). So overall small nice airport that allows you to show up 1h before your flight departs without risk of missing the plane!!

Nice experience at Zhengzhou airport. I departedto Guangzhou and then to Vancouver. The service at Zhengzhou was very good. Staff are very friendly and efficient. They made my trip much easier. Great experience.

Zhengzhou is a dusty rural/ industrial city in central China so it’s hard to see why it has an “international” airport at all. I havn’t been called comrade once in my seven years living in China but I suspect the bad treatment experienced by the poster below is reserved for residents of HK Macao and Taiwan Province who have their very own queue at all airports. Aren’t they lucky! My most recent visit to ZZ confirmed my impression of a well run clean and shiny new airport. As with most Chinese airports the departures area is big open with a sweeping roof while arrivals seems small dark and pokey by comparison. The airport (and the city as a whole) seems to be swamped with coffee shops mostly local brands with “western” food on the menu. At the airport they are quite expensive but at least one promised free internet access so it’s not all bad. The best value food was in arrivals- Dicko’s a Chinese fast food chain. Only other options for eating are continence stores throughout the terminal with over prices snack food. Once airside the only choice is the expensive coffee shop mentioned earlier- at a higher price. The usual situation for restrooms in China- BYO paper but otherwise they are relatively clean and efficiently run but expect to have to put up with the smokers.

A couple of points firstly there is now a new terminal so most of the tips above do not now apply. Agree about the prices for coffee etc they are outrageous! They now handle more international flights for example to Bangkok so I would like to think they are better equipped for international flights now. I have Never been stopped by the immigration people. I find them very friendly. Last point the taxis. There is no doubt they are expensive. They are on the clock but from the airport the clocks run fast. From my old apartment it was 33km to the airport and on one occasion 54km back! Better to pay 15rmb for the bus directly outside the airport then get a taxi from the Aviation hotel in the city. Hope this helps.

Zhengzhou airport is about a 45 minutes ride from the city center. It is a 2 hours flight from Hong Kong or 1 hour flight from Beijing or Shanghai. The only regular international flight it has is from Hong Kong. That means all the immigration and custom officers there handles only China Southern flight in and out 4 times a week. They have the leisure of taking more time to examine the passports and the contents. I almost always get searched going through the Custom. One time the officer was looking for the magazines movies the other time they were looking at my milk powder as well as the dried meats. Next to me was a woman with a baby. They were trying to take away her milk powder. They reason they gave was that these US made milk powder may not conform to the Chinese standard. If you are a tourist you immediately feel you came back to the Mao's age where you are being called comerade. There is a regular airport bus on the ground floor that goes to the city center. The cost is $15 Yuan. The regular airport taxi usually costs around $100 Yuan. (The regular taxi costs around $65 Yuans. The trip to the city is a nice one with all the date trees on both sides of the highway. There are two Chinese restaurants on both sides of the Departure Hall. If you want a tasty regular noodle choose the right one. If you want regular Chinese dishes choose the left one. The price is reasonable. Checking in is easy as all flights are well segregated. The departure lounge is bright and clean. There are massage chairs in every gate. If you have time use them. The cost is $5 Yuans every 15 minutes. They even give you the bottled water free. The small shops are nice since they sell local items like dates peanut biscuit and nice paintings. There is a coffee shop at the far right. I ordered a regular black coffee there and it costs $30 Yuans a big wipe-off. No wonder they do not place any menu on the table.

Traveled to Haikou from this airport as there were no flights from Macau to Haikou. It is a fairly large airport with a small aviation museum in the departures hall. However the airport was a bit old and wasn't very clean. Overall it was quite a good airport with interesting activities to pass the time

Travelled domestically to this airport to avoid the higher airfares charged to travel directly to Macau or Hong Kong. It was neat but showing some wear at the edges. We were the only aircraft at the terminal so was able to move through quickly. Was confronted by a barrage of taxi touts upon leaving the airport. It is a long way out of Zhuhai & Macau some 40 minutes for the 40km & the road was a giant construction zone for most of it.

Bad even for an intentionally low cost airport, taking into account it has been launched quite recently. Bad connection to the city, very few sitting places in departure hall, pathetic choice of shops and food / drink points, uncomfortable toilet.

Airport was working smoothly for arrival and departure, with no appreciable delays. No queues at immigration or security, indeed not that many passengers around. A marked improvement from earlier trips.

We have travelled extensively through dozens of airports but this one is the least attractive, from the boring exterior to the basement type interior. Although we skipped the horrendous check in and security lines because we were business class we still had to endure passport control, crowded trains and escalators. This airport makes it questionable that we will ever visit Switzerland again.

We reached TSA at a time when we had 15 minutes to make it to our next flight (if you ask why the rush, it is because our previous flight got delayed). We ask people online to let us go ahead of them so that we can catch the flight. They all were nice and let us go to the front of the line. Two of our bags got signaled as needing more search. I approach one of the security workers and explained our situation. She ignored me totally. Then another security officer started helping us. It took him over 10 minutes searching through both of our bags, as slow as he could be, told us we should have known the rules (granted we went through TSA in JFK, Vienna with the same bags). He took out containers that had much less quality than 100 ml, he took out our stuff into a bin and made both bags a big mess throwing our stuff back in. We told him he could take whatever containers out, we didn’t care, All we needed was to be done with the process and catch our plane. Yet, he went at his same very slow pace.  When I told him that this experience and his treatment would make us never come to Switzerland again, he said “That would not be a shame.” The real shame was the attitude of security officers at such a major airport. And we actually ended up missing our plane, by a couple of minutes.

On 5th September 2024, around 8:45 am , I went through security check at Zurich airport. I was wearing a religious bangle, that I am not supposed to take off. I was stopped and I let the security agent know that - am not able to take if it off. In all other airports I am given a pat down and let go. This time the security agent said that I am lying and that there is no religion like that. She asked me what religion I was and I told her. She said it doesn't exist. I am still in shock. How can an employee speak to anyone that way when I was doing everything she said. How can she talk about anyone’s religion in such a derogatory manner. It seemed like she just didn’t want to do a pat down and and was feeling lazy so she wanted to be miserable and talk bad about someone’s religion. At this day and age this act of religious discrimination is simply unacceptable. I hope strict action is taken.

We queued 15 minutes to get down one escalator If you’re at E gate leave plenty of time! Passport control was equally as bad - poorly organised and long queues even if EU resident Good luck if you have a connection here!

Zurich Airport Saga continues. Stay away from this airport, as clearly is a mess. As noticed already by several here, there is a high chance you will queue for hours because their ticket access system is down and they have to manually scan boarding passes. Did you hear about backup systems or BCP plans? Clearly not! There were only two people scanning and the longest queue I saw in my life in an airport - why not have 4 or more people scanning? Epic narrow minded security - I had 2 small bags with maybe 400 ml in different small containers. Only 1 bag is allowed?! A week before same airport no problem. Clearly security missed some school classes - you make me wait for more than an hour to scan boarding pass, after brilliant security makes even a worse experience. I think you should close the airport and go for training to Singapore or Middle East - you make your customers feel so miserable!
The worst organized airport ever experienced, along with Geneva airport. Incompetence, lack of friendliness, and huge and unmanaged lines. Incapable of directing passengers

My flight was from Vienna to Zurich and then I had a flight from Zurich to Miami. Unfortunately the flight from Vienna took 15 minutes and I had only 40 minutes to transfer instead of 55 minutes. I arrived at one terminal and had to move to the other terminal which is far enough and I was flying all the way to make it. Saved myself and the airline the trouble of having to rebook the next flight and in case it is full it is a lot of trouble. At passport control there were big queues. Many people are travelling on holiday. I went up to a group of policemen who were "keeping order" - they were talking among themselves all the time. Is it possible to give me priority because I missed my flight. They said it was not possible and that I had to get in line. After waiting in line for 5 minutes I noticed an automated passport control where there was no need to wait, where the machine let me through in 2 minutes. I am an EU citizen so my check was minimal and the policeman's question was from whom did I answer. The problem I see is that the police are there to maintain order but they are mainly there for us passengers and the fact that they were not interested in helping or explaining or directing me correctly I see in their lack of understanding of what they are there for. I am sorry about this situation because I travel through Zurich very often and this experience has had an unnecessary negative impact on me, I hope that someone will address this comment and take steps to fix it so that the airport staff understands what they are there for and who they are there to serve.

No seats available while waiting for your gate. You can only sit in a coffeeshop and consume. Travellers sit on the floor or lean on bannisters which makes the place look untidy. Old, tight toilets where it is difficult to take your hand-luggage. Shops are banal: duty free, luxury, watches and chocolate, no fun stores. Gates are dark and with low ceilings. For a fast bag drop you need to print all by yourself - no thought for older travelers who cannot do this and need to take the slow track. Security check are underestimated and with long queues  I doubt that this is the 8th airport in Europe

Extremely disappointing experience! My family and I were taking our connecting flight to Toronto. Arrived at Swiss Air departure gate E26 after having already gone through a passport control in the same airport while transiting from the other flight. At the gate very few seats exist. Hundreds of people are lined up parallel and away from gate E26 for (at that time) unknown reason. While going to the washroom I noticed they were actually lining up to some improvised booth in the middle of the hallway with a hand-written sign that read "Passport Control". I and my family stayed put knowing we already had our passports checked before and assuming these folks are probably taking some charter flight. We barely ever heard any announcements from the PA system which was extremely muffled and easily overcome by the screaming of the tens of children and phones playing national media. When Swiss E26 gate started boarding they all ran to line-up to so we barely caught our places toward the end of the line.
